title: Jagan refuses to allow niece’s wedding at family compound amid dispute with sister Sharmila
description: The relationship between the siblings is said to have deteriorated after Jagan Mohan Reddy became chief minister
content: Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP) chief YS Jagan Mohan Reddy has refused to allow his niece’s wedding at the family compound, Yelahanka Palace, in Bengaluru in November amid a property dispute with his sister YS Sharmila, people aware of the matter said.Sharmila’s daughter, YS Anjili Reddy, got engaged to Somala Raghurami Reddy, who lives in the United States, on September 24. People aware of the matter said Sharmila, the Andhra Pradesh Congress chief, wanted to have their wedding on November 25 at Yelahanka Palace.An aide to Sharmila said Jagan Mohan Reddy conveyed to her through their mother, YS Vijayamma, that he would not allow the wedding at Yelahanka Palace.“This has come as a big shock to Sharmila, as she had distributed wedding invitations to relatives, political leaders and prominent personalities. Now, she is compelled to look for an alternative venue for the wedding,” said the aide.The aide quoted Jagan Mohan Reddy telling Vijayamma that the property was registered in the name of his mother-in-law, Bharati Reddy. “Vijayamma tried to persuade him to reconsider his position, but he was firm on his stand,” Sharmila’s aide said.He added that Sharmila is now left with no alternative but to scramble for another suitable venue. “She has already sent invitations to top Congress leaders in the high command, besides chief ministers including D K Shivakumar of Karnataka and A Revanth Reddy of Telangana, and former Tamil Nadu chief minister M K Stalin. She has to look for another suitable venue to ensure security and logistical requirements associated with their attendance,” he said.Jagan Mohan Reddy and Sharmila have been involved in a dispute over family properties, including shares in Saraswati Power and Industries Ltd, for the last five years. The issue is pending adjudication in the National Company Law Tribunal.People close to Sharmila said the late former Andhra Pradesh chief minister Y S Rajasekhar Reddy wanted his son and daughter to receive equal shares in the family’s properties. He arranged for separate residences for them in Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Idupulapaya.In Hyderabad’s Lotus Pond locality, their residences are next to each other. Sharmila continues to live in her house there. Similarly, separate residences were reportedly constructed for the siblings at Idupulapaya, the family’s native place.Jagan Mohan Reddy is said to have stopped visiting his residence there. Sharmila reportedly stays at hers when she visits Idupulapaya.In Yelahanka, the family reportedly has two houses constructed next to each other for the siblings across approximately 20 acres. “But the house given to Sharmila was not registered in her name. Rajasekhara Reddy used to stay there whenever he visited Bengaluru. Jagan also has been staying in his palace at Yelahanka during his weekly visits,” Sharmila’s aide said.Rajasekhara Reddy’s death in a helicopter crash on September 2, 2009, left the division of the family’s assets unresolved, leading to disputes between the siblings. The aide said Jagan Mohan Reddy is denying Sharmila a share in the Bengaluru property.Sharmila played a key role in the YSRCR and undertook a foot march when Jagan Mohan Reddy was in jail between 2012 and 2013. She campaigned for the party before the 2019 elections.The relationship is said to have deteriorated after Jagan Mohan Reddy became chief minister in 2019. Sharmila was distanced from the party as disagreements over the division of family assets strained relations.Sharmila floated a party in Telangana before joining the Congress in 2024 and becoming its chief in Andhra Pradesh. She has been attacking her brother politically since.

title: Meghalaya’s hills hum with a hidden world of bees key to honey economy, crop pollination, conservation
description: Meghalaya’s rich bee diversity, traditional beekeeping, planned Bee Museum stress efforts to promote honey production, pollinator conservation, rural livelihood
content: Meghalaya’s hills are home to a diversity of bees, from honey-producing species to lesser-known pollinators that help sustain farms and forests. As research begins to map this hidden wealth, the state is looking to put its honey on the global map, raising questions about conservation, traditional knowledge and the future of rural livelihoods.Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma highlighted this potential on Tuesday while inaugurating an Apiculture Multi-Facility Centre-cum-Processing Unit at Mellim in Rerapara block of South West Garo Hills. He said the government was considering a Bee Museum and Interpretation Centre to showcase Meghalaya’s honey, explain how it is produced and help market premium local products. “Honey from Meghalaya has been termed as the best in the world and there is potential if it is produced and marketed properly,” Sangma said. He envisaged a facility “where organic and best honey can be sold and digital interpretation of honey production can be shown”.“Meghalaya’s organic honey, if supported with scientific beekeeping, processing and branding, can become a major rural enterprise and take Meghalaya to the world,” he added.The ₹1.52-crore centre at Mellim will support honey collection, processing, bottling, testing and marketing, as well as bee-box manufacturing. Under Apiculture Mission 2.0, the state is working across all 12 districts through 87 clusters, covering 6,491 beekeepers. The programme has provided 32,455 bee boxes and 6,491 equipment sets. The 39 clusters covered under Phase III produced 157.69 metric tonnes of honey in 2024–25.But building a successful honey industry will require more than processing facilities and better marketing. It will also depend on healthy habitats, flowering plants and farming practices that allow bees to thrive.Mapping Meghalaya’s hidden bee diversityA national assessment of pollination services recorded 62 bee species in Meghalaya, including 48 free-living and 14 cleptoparasitic species. These account for about 7.49% of India’s recorded bee diversity. A separate taxonomic study by researchers at the Indian Agricultural Research Institute documented 108 bee species across 30 genera in agricultural ecosystems in seven districts of the state. The studies used different methods and covered different areas, so their findings are not directly comparable. Together, however, they highlight Meghalaya’s importance as a habitat for bee diversity and the need for further research and conservation.Bees do far more than produce honey. As pollinators, they help plants reproduce and support the production of fruits, vegetables and seeds. In agricultural landscapes, their activity can influence crop yields and the health of ecosystems.Researchers at the ICAR Research Complex for the North Eastern Hill Region in Umiam studied insect pollinators visiting cucurbit crops, including ridge gourd, sponge gourd, pumpkin, teasel gourd, chow-chow, bottle gourd and cucumber. They recorded 25 pollinator species belonging to three insect orders: Hymenoptera, Diptera and Lepidoptera. Hymenoptera, which includes bees and wasps, accounted for 80% of the relative abundance recorded.Bumblebees were abundant on ridge gourd, pumpkin and sponge gourd, while carpenter bees were also observed on sponge gourd. Indian honeybees visited cucumber and chow-chow.“Native bees are equally contributing to pollination service so conservation of these bees is also a demand of nature,” the researchers wrote.The findings also have practical implications for farmers. Knowing when pollinators are most active can help farmers avoid spraying pesticides during peak activity, reducing the risk of harming insects that contribute to crop production.Traditional knowledge keeps the hives aliveLong before scientists began systematically documenting Meghalaya’s bee diversity, local communities had developed their own methods of keeping bees and managing their relationship with the land.Documentation by the North East Society for Agroecology Support (NESFAS) describes traditional apiculture practices among Khasi and Garo communities. In Daribokgre and Tosekgre in West Garo Hills, households use traditional wooden boxes to rear Apis cerana indica, locally known as Bija kol.In Khapmaw, traditional and modern methods coexist, with bees housed in hollow wooden boxes called Ksing pyllun. In Borgang Marngar in Ri-Bhoi, communities capture wild bees, while in parts of East Khasi Hills, wild colonies are transferred to wooden cabinets. These practices reflect generations of knowledge about bees, farming and the natural environment. They could also help guide sustainable beekeeping as the state expands its apiculture sector.In Daribokgre, near Nokrek, citrus cultivation and beekeeping are closely linked. The area has around 20 varieties of wild and domesticated citrus. NESFAS has documented that 14 of the 15 farmers in an Agroecology Learning Circle there also keep bees. The bees forage on orange flowers, helping pollinate the trees, while honey provides an additional source of income.Community facilitator Sengte Marak has described the connection: “We rear bees for honey and also because bees have been found to increase fruit production, and both of these are important sources of income for our livelihood.”Lotsing M Sangma, a farmer and beekeeper from Daribokgre, has kept bees for 17 years and maintains around 50 hives across his farm, orange orchard and kitchen garden.“Beekeepers are also vegetable farmers in Garo Hills,” he said.His experience shows how beekeeping can complement a diversified farming system, supporting crop production while providing an additional source of income.From awareness to actionFor Phang Roy, founder of NESFAS, protecting pollinators requires public awareness, scientific documentation and farming practices that safeguard their habitats.“The first concrete step is to raise awareness on the importance of pollinators beyond bees by documenting and mapping their roles within ecosystems,” Roy said.He suggested turning scientific findings into accessible educational material to help schoolchildren understand pollinator diversity and its role in maintaining healthy ecosystems. In the longer term, he said, pollinator conservation could be incorporated into the school syllabus as part of environmental education.Roy also stressed the need to promote sustainable, locally appropriate beekeeping as demand for local honey grows and apiculture offers new livelihood opportunities for rural households.However, he cautioned that the expansion of monocropping and the intensive use of chemical fertilisers and other agricultural inputs threaten pollinator populations and the livelihoods that depend on them.“Raising awareness of these threats is essential to encourage farming practices that protect pollinators while supporting local livelihoods,” he said.For NESFAS executive director Pius Ranee, conservation must be built on trust, shared responsibility and cooperation between communities and the government.“Bees have a unique relationship with human beings, built on care, patience, and trust,” Ranee said. “The trust they place in us is a powerful reminder of our responsibility to protect and nurture the natural world.”He called for stronger collaboration among farmers, community institutions and government agencies. Farmers could adopt pollinator-friendly practices, communities could draw on indigenous knowledge and collective action, and the government could provide policy support, technical assistance and resources.“Ultimately, caring, sharing, and trust must be the guiding principles of this collaboration, ensuring that both people and pollinators thrive and that our landscapes remain productive and healthy for future generations,” Ranee said.Beyond honey: Protecting the landscapes that sustain beesMeghalaya’s expanding apiculture infrastructure offers an opportunity to improve honey production, quality and market access. The Integrated Bee Development Centre at Sambrak in North Garo Hills already provides training, testing, processing, hive manufacturing, storage, retail and information services. The proposed Bee Museum and Interpretation Centre could complement these efforts by bringing public education, honey interpretation and marketing together.But a successful honey economy will require more than branding, processing facilities or the distribution of bee boxes. It will also depend on protecting native bee species, maintaining diverse flowering plants, managing colonies responsibly and reducing harmful pesticide exposure.Scientific research can help identify bee species and their ecological roles. Government programmes can provide infrastructure and technical support, while indigenous knowledge can guide practices suited to local landscapes.Meghalaya’s bees are part of the natural systems that sustain crops, forests and rural livelihoods. A museum could introduce visitors to this largely unseen world, but protecting the habitats in which bees forage and ensuring that communities continue to benefit from them will be the more enduring task.Meghalaya may not be discovering its bees so much as learning to document what its communities have understood for generations.

title: ‘Protests achieve nothing’: Amit Shah takes dig at Rahul Gandhi, says Congress won't win polls even in ‘30 years’
description: Launching a scathing attack on the Opposition, Shah said that the Congress party would not be able to win elections in 30 years due to its “negative politics”.
content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday said "protests and demonstrations achieve nothing", stressing that political leaders should focus on public welfare.Speaking at an event in outer Delhi to launch and inaugurate 33 Delhi Jal Board (DJB) projects worth ₹8,941 crore, Shah hit out at the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over their allegations of “vote chori” and discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, accusing them of using “political jugglery and mobocracy” to challenge the people’s mandate. He warned that the parties risk losing their remaining political ground unless they focus on governance.“You cannot use political jugglery and mobocracy to defy the mandate of the people. If you want to win elections, go among the people to understand their problems. These protests and demonstrations will not achieve anything. Implement schemes for people’s welfare wherever you have been elected, otherwise you will be wiped out from the remaining places,” Shah said. Shah accused the opposition of repeatedly questioning electoral outcomes whenever the BJP wins, alleging that the “vote chori” narrative was an excuse to cover up electoral defeats. “A new game has begun in Delhi. As BJP governments are being elected, they are making excuses of vote chori. They say the BJP is not coming to power by popular vote but by vote theft. In reality, you want to save the votes of infiltrators by making these allegations of Vote chori,” he said.He cited the Congress’s electoral defeats across states over several decades, arguing that the party had been rejected by voters even before the BJP came to power nationally in 2014. He also pointed to the opposition’s victories in Kerala, Himachal Pradesh and Telangana, arguing that the same electronic voting machines (EVMs) and Election Commission were in place when those parties won.“Whenever you lose, you criticise the Election Commission. When courts rule in your favour, they are good; otherwise, they are bad,” Shah said.Shah repeats ‘30-year claim’Predicting that the BJP would remain in power for 30 years, Shah said the opposition’s negative politics would prevent it from returning to government. He urged Congress and AAP to concentrate on improving governance in states where they still hold power. "When I say BJP will be in power for 30 years, they again reiterate allegations of vote theft...I want to tell you that Amit Shah was born here, stays here, and will die here...I don't need to visit foreign countries every six months. I am saying you won't form government for 30 years, based on your negative politics," he said.Shah blames Congress, AAP for Delhi’s environmental challengesTurning to Delhi’s environmental challenges, Shah blamed successive Congress and AAP governments for allowing sewage and industrial waste to enter the Yamuna. He said the Centre, Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh were now working together on a time-bound plan to clean the river.“We will come before the people in May 2029 with a clean Yamuna,” he said, adding that a three-year action plan had been drawn up to provide sewer connections to every household and ensure clean water reaches every home. He said the newly launched projects would play a critical role in achieving the target.Shah also targeted AAP over Delhi’s landfill sites, claiming that more than two crore tonnes of waste had been removed and 100 acres of land cleared. He said the sites would be transformed into gardens within two years. Taking aim at AAP’s government in Punjab, Shah accused it of failing to curb drug abuse and asserted that the NDA would form the government in the state by 2029 and dismantle the drug trade.

title: Tiger Shroff firing suspect left Bihar two years ago, worked as a cook, bike-taxi driver: Police
description: Only three months ago, he moved to Mumbai, where he worked as a cook at a restaurant and later as a bike-taxi driver and delivery partner, the police said.
content: One of the three suspects arrested for firing at Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff once worked with a catering agency in Delhi, then as a cook in Mumbai, before becoming a driver with an app-based bike-taxi, Bihar Police said.The suspect, 22-year-old Hrithik Kumar alias Roshan, studied till the intermediate level and left his house in Bihar’s Begusarai two years ago in search of work. He first found a job with a food catering agency in Delhi. Only three months ago, he moved to Mumbai, where he worked as a cook at a restaurant and later as a bike-taxi driver and delivery partner, the police said.Kumar was allegedly riding the two-wheeler when his accomplice fired shots at Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening, police said. The actor escaped relatively unhurt, while his driver and a bystander were injured. Two alleged operatives of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, claimed responsibility for the attack. The suspects were nabbed from Kota station in Rajasthan a day later.Also read | Tiger Shroff shooting accused had a short fuse, say neighbours Begusarai superintendent of Police Maneesh said Kumar has two younger brothers and sisters.The suspect’s family and friends said he is very particular about his appearance and fitness, and had even gained attention on social media with videos of intense workouts and his tattoos.“Last I knew, he was working with a catering agency in Delhi and also wanted to marry a woman from Rajasthan. He had even visited Surat to purchase wedding-related items along with the woman’s father,” Kumar’s mother Sanyukta, who stays in Dumri locality, said.Also read | Tiger Shroff shooting case: Shooters surveyed Salman, Aamir Khan, Ranbir Kapoor’s houses too, say police“We know that he last visited Surat railway station with the woman on October 17 and last spoke to him at around 2pm that day. His mobile phone went off after that,” she added.The parents of the suspect run a tea-cum-cosmetic stall at Pipra Chowk. His mother claimed he was innocent. “My son is innocent. I cannot believe he is a criminal and was part of the firing at the actor,” she said.Kumar’s maternal uncle Chhotu Mehta also said the family had not been in touch with him for the last few days. “We are currently unable to get clear information about his whereabouts and his situation in Mumbai,” he said.Also read | Salman Khan was original target, Tiger Shroff an ‘easy second choice’ for Lawrence Bishnoi gang: Mumbai Police sourcesEarlier, Kumar’s neighbours at Mumbai’s Gilbert Hill, where he rented a room for around six months, said he had acquired a reputation for picking fights. They said even seemingly minor disputes over parking his electric scooter or water spilling near his doorway could trigger angry confrontations.“Roshan was extremely aggressive and was always ready to pick fights. He would argue with neighbours over issues such as water being spilled near his door or someone parking their bike in the spot where he parked his vehicle,” said Mohammed Azhar, a construction site worker who lives nearby.

title: ‘They’re just pictures of Indian flag': Raihan Vadra questions removal of protest photos from Delhi exhibition
description: Vadra alleged that Bikaner House officials asked him to remove two photographs of the Indian flag from his exhibition, which he refused to do.
content: Visual artist Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, on Thursday questioned the Bikaner House administration's move to remove 70 photographs documenting recent protests in Delhi from his solo exhibition just hours before its scheduled opening.Vadra alleged that Bikaner House officials asked him to remove two photographs of the Indian flag from his exhibition after he had already set aside pictures containing overtly political slogans. He said officials argued that the context of the Delhi protests made the photographs political and subsequently asked him to remove more images after inspecting the exhibition for a second time.ALSO READ: 'Raihan was under lot of pressure': Robert Vadra, Priyanka Gandhi on son's Delhi exhibition row "I said, ‘But they are just pictures of the Indian flag. I do not think there is anything in your policy that says photographs of the Indian flag have to be removed’. At that point, I firmly told them to put their demand in writing if they wanted me to remove the photographs of the Indian flag. They did not send me anything in writing," news agency PTI quoted Raihan Vadra as saying.He alleged that officials later removed one flag photograph themselves while he was at home preparing for the exhibition's opening, adding that he had recorded the incident on video.'Most art is political, right?'Criticising the decision, Raihan Vadra said an art institution should not prohibit political content, arguing that political expression is integral to artistic practice.“I had to tell them that an art institution should not have such a policy. I mean, most art is political, right? You cannot function as an artistic institution and then say that political content is not allowed,” he said.Raihan also questioned the timing of the decision, claiming he had shared the exhibition layout with the administration on October 15 and received a response.“You’re telling me just four hours before my show that you couldn’t see the layout. Now, 70 photographs have to be removed. What am I supposed to do?” he said.He added that the photographs represented three years of his work and criticised the expectation that he remain silent over their removal.“Three years of my work is now just sitting in a corner, and the walls are empty,” Raihan said.Vadra wondered if there was a political motive behind the action as he said, “I've done many shows here, and I have great relationships with everyone who works here. I don't know if there was any pressure or anything from anywhere else. I know that it was the management here that decided to take that decision. I don't know if it's been done with a political motive.”Acknowledging that he has the “unique opportunity to take a stand” as an artist given his family background, Vadra said, Public institutions like Bikaner House, Travancore Palace, and other big art fairs and public institutions have a responsibility to the ecosystem that holds them up: the artists, the galleries, the curators. Without that, this is just a bunch of restaurants.""Those people have to be responsible, and they cannot put a curb on our freedoms of expression on artists, just because it doesn't suit them," he was quoted as saying by ANI.(With PTI inputs)

title: Sit-ins, mass cease-work mark 3rd day of protest amid Manipur ethnic violence spike
description: A committee formed in connection with the killing of three Meiteis urged people to observe a day’s mass cease-work
content: Hundreds of protestors on Thursday staged sit-ins amid a day-long mass cease-work call following two days of street protests in Imphal valley districts against the killing of three Meitei farmers three days earlier amid a spike in ethnic violence in Manipur.A 45-year-old Kuki man collecting bamboo shoots was killed, and at least six Kuki houses were set ablaze after the three Meiteis were killed in an ambush on Monday. The ambush was the first incident of violence between Meiteis and Kukis after July 13, when armed Kuki groups attacked Meiteis in Bishnupur’s Torbung Bangla. In the last few months, at least 50 people have died in the state, mostly in Naga-Kuki clashes.A committee formed in connection with the killing of three Meiteis urged people to observe a day’s mass cease-work and stage sit-ins in their respective localities, offices, educational institutions, and marketplaces. Marketplaces, including Khwairamband Ima, opened around 9.30am before businesses were made to shutter.Shutdowns paralysed much of Manipur on Tuesday and Wednesday when at least six protestors were injured as police dispersed a mob when protestors tried to storm a stadium to meet chief minister Yumnam Khemchand.Protestors blocked the Imphal-Dimapur national highway at Khurai Lamlong junction. An altercation between security forces and protestors in Khurai Lamlong forced police to fire tear gas, mock bombs, and stun grenades to disperse the crowd and clear the highway. The protesters retaliated with slingshots and threw stones instead of clearing the highway.The protesters have refused to take the bodies of the three slain Meiteis until all involved in the killing are held. Meitei protesters on Monday left two bodies in front of the main gate of the Chief Minister’s residence to protest the failure to protect civilians after suspected armed Kuki militants carried out the ambush.Security forces fired tear gas shells to disperse the mob that breached security outside the residence and parked a truck carrying two bodies.The families of the victims claimed that the attackers belonged to the Kuki community.The ethnic clashes in Manipur first broke out between the dominant Meitei and tribal Kuki communities in May 2023 and have left at least 360 people dead since 2023. A breakdown of law and order led to the creation of ethnic enclaves, displaced around 55,000 people, and left 49,000 missing.On May 13, four people, including three church leaders, were killed in a twin ambush in Kangpokpi. On the same day, 48 civilians from the Kuki and Naga communities were taken hostage from both groups.Two days later, 14 people from each community were released. But 14 Kukis and six Nagas remained in captivity. After 27 days of protest and appeals for unconditional release of the hostages, 14 Kukis were released on June 9. But on June 10, mutilated bodies of six Naga hostages were recovered, fuelling tensions.

title: BJP launches 15-day campaign to counter opposition’s SIR protests in Bihar
description: The campaign will feature rallies, press conferences, youth and student dialogues and outreach to civil society groups to defend its position on electoral processes
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Thursday launched a 15-day campaign, ‘Loktantra Bachao, Bheedtantra Hatao’ (Save Democracy, Remove Mobocracy). The campaign which began on Thursday will continue till November 5. The campaign will feature rallies, press conferences, youth and student dialogues and outreach to civil society groups to defend its position on electoral processes and counter the opposition’s allegations over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, senior party leaders said on Wednesday.On Wednesday, BJP state president Sanjay Saraogi and state organisation general secretary Bhikhubhai Dalsania reviewed the campaign strategy with state office-bearers.The campaign will focus on electoral roll accuracy, protection of voting rights, accountability of political parties and public confidence in democratic institutions.The BJP has accused opposition parties, particularly the Congress and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) CPI(M), of spreading misleading claims about electoral rolls and undermining trust in the electoral process.Also Read: CJP news LIVE updates: Das, Ranka summoned for Jantar Mantar trespass probe; new anti-ECI march calledThe campaign’s outreach will extend to social media, influencer engagement under the theme ‘Ghuspethiya Hatao, Loktantra Bachao’ (Remove infiltrators, save democracy), and the distribution of publications, booklets and other publicity material.Saraogi said the BJP will reach people across Bihar to strengthen democracy, ensure the integrity of electoral rolls and protect constitutional values. The campaign is intended to present the party’s position on these issues and challenge the opposition’s claims, he said.The party aims to counter what it calls misleading claims by the opposition and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the revision exercise, which has triggered protests over the deletion of large numbers of voters’ names from electoral rolls.“We have been asking the opposition to give us even one name that has been wrongfully deleted from the electoral roll during the SIR. They have not been able to provide one and are unnecessarily trying to mislead people over the SIR,” BJP media in-charge Danish Eqbal said.Also Read: ‘Har gali Jantar Mantar’: Dipke, Bora among those invited to Friday’s anti-EC march; no police nod soughtHe claimed that those whose names had been deleted were either deceased, registered as voters at multiple places or had shifted elsewhere.The opposition has argued that the exercise has led to the deletion of crores of voters’ names, raising concerns over the integrity and inclusiveness of electoral rolls and casting shadow on the manner in which public representatives were elected in a democracy.

title: Jamia Millia Islamia cancels its 106th Foundation Day celebrations amid protest over students' union
description: The protest demanding the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union, which was dissolved in 2006, entered its 10th day on October 22.
content: Jamia Millia Islamia has cancelled its 106th Foundation Day celebrations, citing ongoing protests on campus over the demand to restore the students' union.The celebration, dubbed ‘Talimi Mela’, was scheduled from October 29 to November 1 at the campus in New Delhi to showcase the university’s cultural and educational heritage.“The protesting students have not yet agreed to the proposed resolution, and normalcy has not yet been restored on campus. In view of this, and keeping the safety and well-being of our students, guests and participants foremost in mind, it has been decided with deep regret to cancel Talimi Mela 2026, scheduled from 29 October to 1 November 2026,” JMI’s Dean of Students’ Welfare stated this in an internal communication dated October 21, addressed to heads of departments and deans. The protest demanding the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union, which was dissolved in 2006, entered its 10th day on October 22, following the start of an indefinite hunger strike by five students—Ebin Basil, Mohd Jasim Khan, Rehan Haider, Rehan Pawar and Faizan Ali Khan—on October 12. Since then, a series of demonstrations has been held on the JMI campus.What has happened so far?Over the past ten days, JMI has taken several measures in response to the ongoing campus agitation. The university shut down the Dr Zakir Husain Library and the Old Library for a day, citing security concerns. It initially constituted a high-level committee to engage with the protesting students and address their concerns.On October 21, the university also announced the formation of a five-member committee to draft a constitution for the students’ union, which has been suspended since 2006 amid growing demands for its restoration. Additionally, JMI had suspended three students in connection with the agitation. However, in a notification issued on October 21, the university said it would review disciplinary action taken against students involved in protests between October 12 and 21.Meanwhile, the protesting students issued a statement demanding that JMISU elections be conducted by a student-constituted election commission, that all disciplinary action linked to the ongoing agitation be revoked in writing, and that the Chief Proctor and Security Adviser be removed from their posts. The protesters also called for regular medical monitoring, access to ambulances, and protection from intimidation for students on hunger strike.“The students of Jamia will not be intimidated by deadlines or threats. Our protest is peaceful and democratic, and the hunger strike continues,” the statement read.

title: How to download e-Aadhaar online: From OTP authentication to PDF password
description: Download your e-Aadhaar online using UIDAI's official portal. Learn about OTP verification, authentication requirements and the PDF password format
content: A physical Aadhaar card is not the only way to access your Aadhaar details. The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) allows residents to download an electronic version, known as e-Aadhaar, through its official website. The document is digitally signed and password-protected. It can be downloaded as a PDF, stored electronically or printed when required. The process involves entering your Aadhaar details and completing an authentication step. Here is how to download e-Aadhaar, what you need before starting and how to open the downloaded file.Where can you download e-Aadhaar?You can download your e-Aadhaar through the official website of the Unique Identification Authority of India. Visit the UIDAI website and navigate to the Aadhaar download service. You can also access the download facility through the official myAadhaar portal.Keep your 12-digit Aadhaar number, Enrolment ID or other accepted identification details ready, depending on the option you choose. You will generally need access to the mobile number registered with your Aadhaar to complete OTP-based authentication. How to download your e-Aadhaar1. Visit the official myAadhaar portal2. Select the option to download Aadhaar3. Choose the appropriate identification method, such as your Aadhaar number or Enrolment ID4. Enter the requested details and complete the security verification displayed on the screen5. Request an OTP and enter the code sent to your registered mobile number6. Submit the details after verifying that the information is correct7. Download the resulting e-Aadhaar PDF to your deviceThe precise options displayed may vary depending on the service and authentication method available. The UIDAI also documents the use of a time-based one-time password, or T-OTP, generated through the application for supported services.What authentication is required?OTP verification is a key security measure when downloading e-Aadhaar through the online portal. The code is sent to the mobile number registered with your Aadhaar and is used to verify access. If you no longer have access to that number, you may be unable to complete the usual OTP-based process. Check UIDAI's official guidance for available alternatives rather than relying on unofficial websites or third-party services.Never share your OTP with another person. Use only official UIDAI services when entering your Aadhaar details. What is the password for e-Aadhar pdf?The downloaded e-Aadhaar PDF is password-protected. According to UIDAI's guidance, the password combines the first four letters of your name in capital letters and your year of birth in YYYY format.For example, if your name is RAHUL KUMAR and your year of birth is 1998, the password would be RAHU1998.If the file does not open, check the spelling of your name as recorded in Aadhaar, use capital letters for the first four characters and enter the full four-digit year of birth.Is e-Aadhar valid?Yes. UIDAI states that e-Aadhaar is a digitally signed electronic document and is legally valid for use in the same way as the Aadhaar letter. Its digital signature and QR code can help verify its authenticity. Keep the PDF secure, particularly if it contains personal information. If you need to share Aadhaar details, consider whether the receiving organisation requires the complete document or whether an alternative, such as masked Aadhaar, is appropriate.Sourceshttps://uidai.gov.inhttps://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.inhttps://www.uidai.gov.in/16-english-uk/aapka-aadhaar/40-e-aadhaar-service.html

title: Busted by a secret video: 2 Bihar GRP cops hold back seized liquor, arrested
description: They were arrested after a passenger, who had recorded the two seizing the 36 bottles packed in four bags on the train, released the video
content: A havildar and a woman home guard personnel of the Government Railway Police (GRP) in Bihar have been arrested after they seized 36 bottles of liquor from a passenger but did not report the seizure, police said on Thursday.They were arrested after a passenger, who had recorded the two seizing the 36 bottles packed in four bags on the train, released the video. As senior police officers learned of the seizure, they checked the CCTV footage at Hajipur Junction station. The claims checked out.Muzaffarpur Rail superintendent of police (SP) Beena Kumari said Havildar Narendra Kumar Singh and Archana Kumari, a home guard personnel, were arrested under the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act.The SP said 36 bottles containing 27 litres of liquor, which were packed in four bags, have been retrieved from the two personnel.She said Havildar Singh, Kumari, and two other personnel were assigned to escort the Amritsar–Saharsa Garib Rath Express on the Chhapra–Hajipur route. During the journey, the two spotted the contraband in a coach at Chhapra station and seized the bottles. They unloaded the consignment at Hajipur Junction but did not inform the local GRP police station or deposit the seized liquor.But a person had secretly filmed them seizing the liquor.The Hajipur GRP initiated an inquiry and scanned CCTV footage from the station. Upon questioning, both accused confessed to concealing the liquor and led police to the four bags.Narendra Kumar Singh had been posted at the Hajipur GRP station for two years and was due to retire next year. Archana Kumari (24) had been attached to the GRP a year ago.

title: Bypoll to Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha seat vacated by L Murugan on November 12: Election Commission
description: Murugan's term was due to end on April 2, 2030.
content: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Thursday announced that the bypoll to a Rajya Sabha seat from Madhya Pradesh vacated by former Union minister L Murugan will be held on November 12.The seat fell vacant on October 14, a day after Murugan, the Union minister of state for information and broadcasting and parliamentary affairs, quit the Council of Ministers and sought to give up his Rajya Sabha membership. His term was due to end on April 2, 2030.Murugan was a Rajya Sabha member since September 2021 and was re-elected from Madhya Pradesh in April 2024. He is a former Tamil Nadu BJP chief and joined the Union Cabinet in July 2021.In his resignation letter, Murugan said he wanted to return to the grassroots and work full-time to strengthen the BJP in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.Also read | Murugan’s resignation letter: Praise for Modi’s Tamil outreach, from Sitharaman and Jaishankar to Thirukkural and SengolHe also spoke about what Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership meant for him. “It has been the greatest honour of my life to serve India and Tamil Nadu under your leadership. I do not come from a political family. I come from a very poor family,” he wrote. His parents, who worked as daily wage labourers and cattle grazers, “continue to lead a simple life in Konur village”, he said.Murugan credited Modi and the BJP’s culture of recognising grassroots karyakartas and giving him opportunities far beyond his expectations. He described every responsibility he received as “an expression of your trust” – from the National Commission for Scheduled Castes to the Rajya Sabha and the Council of Ministers.Also read | ‘Want to strengthen BJP in Tamil Nadu’: L Murugan resigns; 3rd Union minister to quit in 4 monthsThe notification for the bypoll will be issued on October 26, and the last date for filing nominations is November 2. Scrutiny will take place on November 3, and candidates can withdraw by November 5.Voting will be held from 9am to 4pm on November 12, with counting at 5pm the same day. The whole process must be completed before November 16.

title: PM Modi likely to visit Bihar in November, Vikramshila University foundation stone on cards
description: The proposed Vikramshila Central University is planned near the site of the ancient Buddhist learning centre at Antichak in Kahalgaon, Bhagalpur district.
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to visit Bihar on November 20 to lay the foundation stone for the proposed Vikramshila Central University at Kahalgaon in Bhagalpur district, along with launching infrastructure projects, senior BJP leaders said on Wednesday.The proposed visit is expected to coincide with the completion of one year of the NDA government in Bihar following its victory in the 2025 assembly elections. To be sure, the NDA has been in power in Bihar since 2005.“The Prime Minister’s visit to Bihar in November is tentative. Official confirmation is awaited,” BJP media in-charge Danish Eqbal said.During the visit, the Prime Minister is likely to lay the foundation stones for several infrastructure projects, including roads and railway schemes, an official said.Among the projects under consideration are the proposed Gorakhpur-Siliguri, Raxaul-Haldia and Patna-Purnia road corridors, along with a couple of railway projects sponsored by the Centre. The state’s Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur road project is also among those likely to be included in the programme, the official said.Reviving the ‘Vikramshila legacy’The proposed Vikramshila Central University is planned near the site of the ancient Buddhist learning centre at Antichak in Kahalgaon. The ancient learning centre was established in the ninth century AD during the reign of the Pala dynasty.In a July 2025 reply to Parliament, the Union education ministry said the Bihar government had offered around 205 acres of land in the Antichak and Malakpur areas for the project.Chief minister Samrat Choudhary announced in June that the state would work towards reviving Vikramshila’s legacy. In July, he said the proposed Central University would be established on around 200 acres.

title: From required documents to appointment process: A step-by-step guide on the process to apply for Indian passport
description: Learn how to apply for an Indian passport, prepare documents, pay the applicable fee, book an appointment and complete police verification
content: For Indian nationals to travel abroad, a passport is required. As per the ministry of external affairs, the blue book serves as a travel and identity document for eligible Indian citizens.The MEA operates the Passport Seva system, which allows applicants to submit forms, pay fees, book appointments, and track their applications online.Here's a look at all you need to know in order to apply for a passport in IndiaWho can apply for an Indian passport?Any person who is an Indian citizen under the applicable provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955, may apply for an Indian passport, subject to the rules governing passport issuance and any applicable legal restrictions.Indian citizenship may be acquired through birth, descent, registration or naturalisation, depending on the circumstances and the provisions of Indian law. Nevertheless, the rules differ according to when and where a person was born, their parents’ citizenship status and, in certain cases, other legal conditions. Being born in India does not automatically confer citizenship in every circumstance, particularly for those born on or after 1 July 1987.Applicants must also meet the requirements of the particular passport service they seek. Adults applying for their first passport, parents applying on behalf of minor children, and individuals seeking a reissue may need to provide different documents to establish their identity, address, date of birth or citizenship, as applicable.Those applying for the first time must submit a new application, while existing passport holders may need to apply for a reissue if their passport expires or their personal details change.A reissue is for someone who already holds a passport and needs a new one due to an expiry, changes to personal details, damage, loss or other eligible reasons. The documents and procedures can differ for adults, minors and applicants with special circumstances.Eligible citizens can visit the official website at https://www.passportindia.gov.in/ to apply for a passport according to their requirements.Which documents are required?The documents required depend on the type of application and the applicant's circumstances. Commonly required documents may include:1. Proof of address2. Proof of date of birth, where required3. Documents supporting identity or other particulars, where applicable4. An existing passport when applying for a reissue5. Additional documents required for the relevant categoryThe official Passport Seva website provides instructions and document-advisory information for different types of applications. Applicants are required to carry the original documents requested for verification, and multiple copies of the same as specified in the instructions. How to apply online and book an appointmentThe application begins on the Passport Seva website.1. Register as a new user on the official portal.2. Sign in and select the fresh-passport or reissue service.3. Complete the application form with your personal and address details.4. Review the information carefully before submitting it.5. Pay the applicable fee through the available payment facility.6. Book an appointment at an available Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) or Post Office Passport Seva Kendra (POPSK).A PSK or POPSK is an authorised centre where passport applicants attend appointments for document checks and other application formalities. Appointment availability depends on the centre and the dates offered through the portal. Keep your application reference details and appointment confirmation. How much does a passport cost?Passport fees depend on the type of service, booklet size, validity and whether the applicant qualifies for the normal or Tatkaal process. Tatkaal is an expedited service intended for eligible applicants who require faster processing. Additional charges may apply, and not every application qualifies.Passport application fees were revised, with effect from July 1, 2026, according to the official Passport Seva website. Because the fee schedule was revised, applicants should use the official Passport Seva fee calculator to confirm the amount payable.The calculator helps determine the fee for the selected application category. Check the amount before payment and retain the transaction confirmation.Police verification and application trackingAfter the appointment, the application proceeds through the checks required for the particular case. Police verification may be required to confirm details such as the applicant's identity and residential address.The sequence and timing can vary according to the application category and the passport authority's assessment. Applicants should provide accurate information and respond promptly to requests for additional documents or verification.To track the application, visit the Passport Seva portal and select the status-checking facility. Enter the requested application reference details to see the latest status. Submitting a form or attending an appointment does not guarantee immediate passport issuance. Follow the official instructions until the application is completed.

title: BJP accuses Annamalai of 'double standards' on SIR as he slams response to CJP protests
description: Annamalai's remarks came amid the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were released on Wednesday after seven days in custody.
content: After former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader K Annamalai launched a tirade against the Centre over the crackdown on protests against the ongoing Special Intensive Revision, the party hit back at him for switching his earlier stance on the SIR. Annamalai, who slammed the government and police response to protests and the detention of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists, was accused of double standards as BJP claimed he had earlier defended the electoral roll revision exercise.Annamalai's criticism of the BJP-led government came months after he left the party in June this year. In an X post on Wednesday, the former Tamil Nadu BJP president alleged that those raising their voice against the government could be "jailed indefinitely" or "labelled anti-nationals or foreign agents". His remarks followed the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were released on Wednesday after seven days in custody. Annamalai further said that while he did not approve of the tactics used by CJP, he was "completely" in support of the questions they want to raise in regards to the electoral process.He was met with a sharp response from Tamil Nadu spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy, who accused Annamalai of double standards on the issue of SIR. Thirupathy also condemned Annamalai's questions against Delhi Police, saying he should understand the demands of maintaining law and order as a former IPS officer. Defending police action, the BJP leader said, "Annamalai's questions deliberately blur the line between peaceful protest and deliberate law-breaking."Annamalai slams Centre's response to protests Annamalai, who was an IPS officer before he joined politics, has backed the citizens' right to protest and question the government. "In 2011, the then Chief Minister of Gujarat, Narendra Modi, stated that if his hands had not been tied, he would have gone to Delhi and waged a war against the Central government. In my opinion, what the Hon PM said then was absolutely right, and there is nothing wrong about it".Referring to Das and Ranka's arrest after they trespassed into the Jantar Mantar area despite the place being de-notified as a site of protest, Annamalai said, "Today, you could be jailed indefinitely; your surety bonds could be rejected; and, surprisingly, a Special Executive Magistrate will play circles around you when he/ she is empowered to deal with preventive bond cases.""If you question the violation of due process of law in a democracy, you would be called names, and a barrage of attacks would follow, including being labelled a Foreign Agent," Annamalai said in his post.Clarifying that he does not agree with CJP's tactics, Annamalai backed their right to protest. "I might not agree with the tactics of the CJP, and I think many of theirs are misguided. But if you ask me whether they have a right to oppose/argue/protest on an issue that they think is important, I would categorically say - YES," he said."So, I would like people to ask the questions again, even if it makes some of them uncomfortable, and I wish the Central Government would answer them instead of resorting to whataboutism," he argued.The former BJP leader also criticised the labelling of protesters as "anti-India" and "foreign agents", calling it a "tiring and boring" narrative.Training is guns on the Centre, he said, "FCRA is controlled by MHA. All agencies don't report to the opposition parties in the country. All the embassies outside are equipped with enough people to track any Indian national in hand in glove with foreign enemies. It's honestly very tiring and boring to see all protests and statements against the central government being called as anti-national and funded by forces outside."I have a feeling the central government forgets it's been in power in Delhi for 12 plus years and still manufactures an enemy at all times to keep itself relevant. Sadly, that's a pity!"BJP hits back at AnnamalaiThe BJP on Wednesday hit back at former party leader Annamalai over his criticism of the Centre's handling of protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), accusing him of inconsistency and overlooking alleged violations of the law.BJP spokesperson Thirupathy said Annamalai had previously defended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, arguing that fake voters needed to be removed, but had now backed concerns raised by the Congress and CJP."Today, after quitting the BJP, the same Annamalai has switched sides," Thirupathy said, adding that his questions "deliberately blur the line between peaceful protest and deliberate law-breaking".Tamil Nadu BJP leader Vinod Selvam also issued a point-by-point rebuttal, defending the government's responsibility to maintain public order. "The Modi government has a responsibility to maintain public order. It cannot suspend that responsibility whenever those facing action happen to oppose BJP," Selvam said. He added, "Peaceful protest deserves protection. Alleged violations deserve examination."

title: Yes Bank-DHFL case: Bombay HC sets aside ED’s attachment of assets worth ₹25 cr
description: The Bombay High Court said it found no basis for the attachment, as all involved transactions were legal
content: The Bombay High Court has set aside an appellate tribunal’s April order for continuing the Enforcement Directorate (ED)’s provisional attachment of assets worth ₹25 crore belonging to Pune businessman Avinash Bhosale and others, as part of its money-laundering probe related to the allegedly suspicious transactions in 2018 between Yes Bank and Dewan Housing Finance Limited (DHFL).The court on Wednesday said it found no basis for the continuation of the attachment, as all involved transactions were legal and could not be considered as proceeds of crime in the case.On April 1, the tribunal under the Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act continued the provisional attachment of a Pune land parcel attached for the value of Rs. 14.65 crore under the title of Samit Realty Private Limited and a plot in Nagpur, valued at ₹15.52 lakh, in the name of Bhosale’s wife, Gauri.Bhosale, Gauri and Samit Realty Private Limited challenged the tribunal’s order on the continuation of the attachment. The ED opposed their plea for the release of the attached properties.Bhosale was named as an accused in the ED’s third supplementary charge sheet in the Yes Bank–DHFL case initiated in 2020.In its October 2022 charge sheet, ED alleged that proceeds of crime worth ₹3,983 crore originated from YES Bank, wherein the monies were sanctioned and disbursed to DHFL during April-June 2018 against investments including DHFL’s debentures and grant of loans. The ED alleged that proceeds of crime worth ₹164 .64 crore were received by Bhosale and/or his entities (Nibhodh Realty) and through transactions related to consultancy and ABIL Dairy, which received ₹25 crore.The high court referred to these transactions and said each was an independent transaction with an independent corporate entity and none of them is, by any stretch of imagination, illegal. “We find there is no nexus between them,” said the court, setting aside the appellate tribunal’s order.“We find no basis for the continuation of the attachment of the said two properties by the Appellate Tribunal. Having concluded that all the transactions were legal transactions and could not be construed as proceeds of crime, we find no basis for continuing the attachment of the properties.”The court cited ED’s allegations related to Yes Bank’s transactions involving investment and loans to DHFL. It added that the receipt of these monies by DHFL, whether as an investment or as a loan from YES Bank, cannot be faulted in law. The court said that they were official banking transactions and cannot be construed as proceeds of crime.The court said subsequent disbursement by DHFL to other legal entities cannot be construed as illegal transactions either, as they too are recognised lawful transactions. “The entire basis of the investigation therefore proceeds on erroneous hypothesis, and the transactions cannot be treated as illegal, as alleged by the ED,” the court said.The court cited ED’s contention that in July 2018, DHFL allegedly lent ₹600 crore to DOIT Urban Ventures, allegedly the family entity of Yes Bank’s founder Rana Kapoor, by way of a kickback. It added that this contention is wholly unfounded.“A loan transaction cannot, in the first place, be termed as a kickback, and there is no basis for such an allegation. A loan transaction may be extended with or without appropriate security, and it is entirely for the lender, in its own commercial wisdom, to decide whether to lend monies to an individual or entity.”

title: Sonia Gandhi makes Instagram debut, shares first look of upcoming memoir ‘Belonging: A Journey Of Love’
description: In her first post, Sonia Gandhi described the memoir as a story of “love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong”
content: Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi joined Instagram on Wednesday, sharing the first look of her forthcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, in the presence of her friend Manju Dubey.The 79-year-old Congress leader’s debut on the platform marks her entry into a social media space widely used by young people, particularly Generation Z. Instagram has increasingly become a communication channel for Indian politicians, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, to share public engagements, political messages and glimpses of their personal lives.In her first post, Sonia Gandhi described the memoir as a story of “love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong” and said she looked forward to sharing it with readers. She also pointed out photographs of her daughter and Vayanad MP Priyanaka Gandhi.“Hello everyone, I’m truly grateful to share this moment with you all; the first look of Belonging: A Journey of Love. It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” she wrote. Instagram’s visual format has made it an important platform for politicians seeking to communicate beyond conventional speeches, press conferences and party statements. Modi and Rahul Gandhi have used the platform to share political events, public interactions and personal moments, while several other leaders have expanded their social media presence to connect with younger audiences.Sonia Gandhi’s entry comes ahead of the memoir’s worldwide release on November 10 by Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of Penguin Random House.The memoir traces her journey from childhood in post-war Italy to her life in India, including her romance with Rajiv Gandhi during their time at Cambridge and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband.The book has also drawn attention over a reported disagreement between Sonia Gandhi and Penguin Random House India (PRHI) concerning its contents.HT had earlier reported that the proposed publishing arrangement with PRHI fell through after Gandhi refused to alter or remove references to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Chinese intrusions.A person familiar with the matter said Gandhi maintained that the memoir was her story and that she would not allow distortions to her account of her life.PRHI issued a statement following media reports that it had withdrawn from publishing the memoir in India. Later, HarperCollins finalised an agreement to publish and distribute the Indian edition. The memoir revisits the personal experiences and tragedies that shaped Sonia Gandhi’s relationship with India. Despite her decades-long presence at the centre of national politics, she has largely maintained a private public persona.Her son, Rahul Gandhi, recently expressed pride in her decision to share her story. On the birth anniversary of Rajiv Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition said he was happy that millions of people would be able to read his mother’s account.“I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story,” he said, adding that he imagined his father looking down proudly at Sonia.Sonia Gandhi, who served as Congress president for nearly two decades across two terms, is expected to offer readers a personal account of her journey into the Nehru-Gandhi family and the experiences that shaped her public life.With the worldwide release approaching, attention will remain on the memoir’s contents and the final form of its Indian edition.

title: 'Raihan was under lot of pressure': Robert Vadra, Priyanka Gandhi on son's Delhi exhibition row
description: Raihan Vadra had alleged that the management of Bikaner House had objected to photographs depicting protests by young people in Delhi.
content: Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Thursday voiced support for her son, Raihan R Vadra, after he alleged that authorities had asked him to remove certain photographs related to the Delhi protests, including an image of the national flag, from his exhibition scheduled to open on Thursday at the Bikaner House in the capital.In a post on X, Priyanka shared a message about freedom of expression, saying that those in positions of power weaken their own authority when they fear others expressing themselves. “When someone with power becomes afraid of the expression of another, he doesn’t know it, but he has already lost the very power he is trying to protect. You stand for what is true and everything beautiful will find its way to you. I am proud of you, always will be” her post read. Reacting to the incident, Robert Vadra, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra’s husband and Raihan’s father, said his son had faced considerable pressure to remove the photographs just two hours before the exhibition was scheduled to open. “There was a lot of pressure on him to remove everything, and this happened just two hours before the opening of his exhibition. It was shocking because the authorities had received the PDF file a week in advance and had been informed about the exhibition” he said. Describing the last-minute intervention as shocking, Robert questioned why the situation had changed without any explanation. He also praised Raihan for going ahead with the exhibition despite the removal of several photographs, adding that the invited guests had attended the event.Noting that Bikaner House comes under the Rajasthan government, Robert said politics should not be mixed with the creative world and stressed that everyone should be allowed to express themselves in a democracy.Priyanka and Robert's reaction comes after Raihan alleged that the exhibition management sought to remove specific photographs. "Five hours ago, the management of Bikaner House compelled me to remove most of the artworks from my exhibition, 'No Idea Is Final,' which is scheduled to open this evening at 7 pm. The images in question depicted protests carried out by young people in Delhi. Evidently, the management found the content of these images 'objectionable.' They also instructed me to remove two images featuring the Tricolour," the statement read.Also Read: Priyanka Gandhi's son Raihan alleges Bikaner House pulled down his protest pics ahead of exhibitionRaihan said he had declined to remove the photograph featuring the Indian national flag, adding that the exhibition would continue with a limited selection of works for now. He said he would seek an alternative venue to showcase the complete collection of photographs documenting the protests.“I have refused to do so; I will not remove the image of the Indian flag. For now, the exhibition will proceed in a limited capacity, but I will look for an alternative venue where I can display the entire collection of photographs related to the protests,” he said in the post.

title: 'Har gali Jantar Mantar': Dipke, Bora among those invited to Friday’s anti-EC march; no police nod sought
description: Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita that was imposed during the earlier protests continues to remain in force in the New Delhi district.
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, student leaders Neha Bora and Aishe Ghosh, and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan are among the prominent figures invited to a march in the Capital on Friday to "restore democracy", demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and press for the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Actor-activist Prakash Raj, farmer leader Rakesh Tikait and author Tushar Gandhi have also been invited for the march that is also scheduled to be held in other parts of the country. The marches – organised by People Against SIR, a week-old alliance of students, farmers and civil society groups – have been planned without police permission and are likely to run into trouble given the recent crackdowns on similar protests, including those by CJP, held without nod. To be sure, section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) that was imposed during the earlier protests continues to remain in force in the New Delhi district.Also read | 'Har gali Jantar Mantar': Farmers, women, youth form joint platform against SIR"The People's March to Reclaim Democracy will not request police permission anywhere," the platform had said in a statement on October 18. It also warned the police, paramilitary personnel and prison authorities against using force on peaceful protesters. The platform has planned a “No SIR” campaign under the slogan “Har Gali Jantar Mantar, Har Gaon Jantar Mantar, Mera Ghar Jantar Mantar”.The alliance said it has also invited the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA). To be sure, there was no immediate comment or confirmation from the invitees on the march till the time of filing this report.Also read | No Jantar Mantar protest call until it remains de-notified: CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka to courtAccording to the platform, the march in the Capital is scheduled to be held from Bangla Sahib Gurdwara in Connaught Place to the Election Commission’s office near Patel Chowk. If police block the route, the protesters will hold a "People's Parliament" and disperse after singing the national anthem, the group said.There was no immediate comment from Delhi Police at the time of filing this report. Under section 163 of BNSS, public meetings or assembly of five or more people, processions, demonstrations, picketing or dharnas, shouting of slogans or making of speeches, carrying firearms, banners, placards, lathis, swords, sticks, brickbats, or similar articles are prohibited without prior written permission.The People Against SIR group was formed on October 14 at Surjeet Bhavan in New Delhi by groups representing farmers, workers, women, students, Adivasis, Dalits and minorities. The platform has alleged that the SIR exercise is illegal and demanded the voter lists be reset to their pre-2024 version and updated through social audits as laid down in the Election Commission Manual and CAG guidelines.Also read | Jantar Mantar played host to varying degrees of discontentIt has listed six “immediate” bottomlines and a second set of “key” demands. It has sought the removal and prosecution of Kumar, whom it referred to as “Gyanesh” and also sought revocation of the Election Commission of India’s legal immunity. "Gyanesh Kumar has violated his Constitutional pledge and must be prosecuted," the statement said.Several people among the invitees were earlier detained for holding similar protests against Kumar. On October 10, Dipke and other CJP members – Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka – were held ahead of their march at Jantar Mantar – now a denotified protest zone. About 41,000 security personnel turned the Capital into a fortress to thwart the planned protest, launching an unprecedented clampdown that saw the detention of 7,000 people and left large chunks of Delhi deserted.Dipke was released on Saturday and Das and Ranka were released on Wednesday.Also read | Terms of Trade: Why Jantar Mantar matters for IndiaBora – president of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) – was also detained as she gave a call to protesters to regroup at Dilli Haat on October 10. Security forces stopped the group on Sri Aurobindo Marg and put the leaders in a bus. Protesters blocked the bus with the leaders and stopped it from moving, and an hour-long scuffle followed. Ghosh was also held near Bangla Sahib that day. Bhushan was also detained by the police. They were later released.Days before on October 6, INDIA bloc MPs, including Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, were detained as at least 300 lawmakers from the INDIA bloc marched from Parliament to the Election Commission.The Election Commission and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have rejected the charges related to SIR. On October 10, BJP spokesman Sambit Patra called the protesters "anarchic elements".

title: Loan fraud case: Three arrested for duping public of ₹100 crore in Chennai
description: According to police, the trio lured Manivannan by promising to secure a business loan for industrial development in exchange for an advance payment as a service fee for them
content: Three persons were arrested for allegedly cheating people in Tamil Nadu and in Keralam by collecting over ₹100 crore promising to secure loans, police said on Thursday.Acting on a complaint from a city-based businessman N Manivannan, the Central Crime Branch police arrested the key suspect ‘Lion’ Muthuvel alias Muthukrishna alias B M Chettiyar and two of his associates.According to police, the trio lured Manivannan by promising to secure a business loan for industrial development in exchange for an advance payment as a service fee for them.The three individuals collected an advance of ₹2 crore obtained signatures on cheques and blank papers but failed to arrange the loan as promised. Besides, they were demanding additional money by threatening Manivannan, police said.Also Read: Financial fraud in Ludhiana: Identity swap leaves labourer saddled with ₹19 lakh loanA special Central Crime Branch team was formed to probe the case which led to the arrest of 48-year-old Muthuvel, his accomplices, B Jagan (44) alias Gurubaran and A Thirukumaran (51) late on Wednesday.“Further investigation revealed that the gang by adopting similar modus operandi had cheated the members of public of over ₹100 crore by promising to secure loans and several cases were pending against them in various police stations including in Dharmapuri and also in various police stations in Keralam,” the police said.On completion of the investigation, the three were produced before a local court and were remanded to judicial custody.Chennai City police commissioner A Amalraj urged the members of the public to approach banks for obtaining loans and advised not to get cheated by paying commissions to such fraudulent middlemen and financiers.

title: India corrects UN rapporteur on Dawood Ibrahim, points to Pakistan: ‘He resides where bin Laden was found'
description: Indian diplomat Raghoo Puri said that Dawood is a wanted criminal in India and, according to the UN's listing entry, was living in Pakistan.
content: India on Wednesday strongly hit out at UN rapporteur Ben Saul over a counter-terrorism report and called for high standards of impartiality after the document described underworld don Dawood Ibrahim as the leader of the “India-based” D-Company criminal gang with terrorist ties.In a report titled “Distinguishing organized crime from terrorism to protect human rights”, released in July, special rapporteur Ben Saul mentioned Dawood Ibrahim's ‘D-Company’ as “India-based”. Notably, special rapporteurs do not receive direct payment from the UN and are expected to carry out their work independently of the organisation.ALSO READ | India slams UN over ‘selective targeting’ after experts flag crackdown on protestsIndia affirms Dawood Ibrahim residing in PakistanRaghoo Puri, India's First Secretary at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN, expressed “serious concern” over the Special Rapporteur “releasing reports with factual inaccuracies while not being held accountable for them”.Puri said that Dawood is a wanted criminal in India and, according to the UN's listing entry, was living in Pakistan.He said the report noted that the Security Council had listed the head of D-Company in 2003 over links to Al-Qaeda. However, he argued that “this line paints a very different picture from the actual reality”. Puri said D-Company and its listed leader, Dawood Ibrahim, had been wanted in India over terror attacks since 1993. “This is clearly written in the narrative summary of reasons of listing under the 1267 sanctions regime.”“Not mentioning this fact is regrettable, and such incompetence on the part of special mandate holders does this organisation tremendous harm,” Puri added.He told the assembly that Dawood had been wanted in India well before the 2003 listing. He said Dawood was listed during this period for his links to Al-Qaeda and Osama bin Laden while operating from outside India.‘He resides where bin Laden was found’Dawood remains a wanted criminal in India to this day, Puri said, adding that Dawood “resides in the same country where Osama bin Laden was found and neutralised”, referring to Pakistan.Osama bin Laden, the mastermind behind the 9/11 terror attacks of 2001 that killed nearly 3,000 people in the US, was found and killed in a fortified compound in Pakistan's Abbottabad.Notably, India has repeatedly told the international community that the al-Qaeda leaders who planned and directed the 9/11 attacks in the US were not found hiding in an ungoverned border region but in a fortified compound in a settled and guarded area of Pakistan. In September this year, India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Harish Parvathaneni, told the UN assembly that al-Qaeda leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in populated areas rather than remote hideouts.India slams Pakistan’s remarks on KashmirPuri also responded to remarks made by the Pakistani delegation and reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh were integral parts of India."It seems to have become fashionable for sponsors of terror to use human rights and the framework of counterterrorism to justify their misdeeds. The human rights framework cannot be the refuge of the perpetrators of terror and those who propagate radicalisation and extremism. Terrorism can never be justified," he said."Regarding the statement just made by the delegate of Pakistan, everyone in this room knows that what has been mentioned against my country, including about the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, is pure propaganda made for very narrow political gains. And these have been on account of the actual rulers of Pakistan, which is its military,” he said.He added, “I would like to reiterate for the record that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are inalienable parts of India, have been so, and will always remain so.”India hit out at UN over ‘selective targeting’ earlierOn Tuesday, India said that human rights should not be used to exert political pressure or to single out countries after more than 20 UN human rights experts in Geneva raised concerns over what they described as a "repeatedly heavy-handed police response" to youth-led protests in the national capital.Barkha Tamrakar, deputy secretary in the ministry of external affairs, delivered India's statement at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee. “India engages with international human rights mechanisms, but such engagement must be based on dialogue, consultation, cooperation, with non-selectivity and transparency as guiding principles,” she said.Tamrakar said India was ready to address specific cases backed by proper documentation through established channels. However, she opposed any "attempt to convert unverified allegations, incomplete statistics or a report that contains no India country observation into a negative characterisation of the world's largest democracy".The response came after criticism from UN experts over the Indian police's “heavy-handed” handling of youth-led protests in Delhi and other areas over the past three months. They called on the authorities to protect peaceful demonstrations and ensure justice for alleged human rights violations during these and earlier protests.Last week, India rejected as “hearsay” a report by a UN human rights expert that referred to a “satirical political movement” formed by young people in the country and alleged that its members had faced retaliation. New Delhi urged the expert to “verify” the claims before “vilifying issues based on unverified allegations.”With inputs from agencies

title: Annamalai says CJP has right to protest in India, disagrees with its tactics
description: Former IPS officer Annamalai had earlier also said that CJP's protest tactics were “misguided”.
content: Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai on Friday said his organisation, We The Leaders, does not support the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) because of differences in their objectives, but backed the group's right to protest.“If you ask whether our ‘We The Leaders’ will support the CJP party, we will never do so. Because our goal is different, and their goal is different. However, if you ask whether the CJP party has the right to protest in India, yes, it does,” he said at an event on Thursday.Annamalai had earlier described CJP's protest tactics as “misguided”, while asserting that the group had the right to oppose issues it considered important.“As I mentioned yesterday, I might not agree with the tactics of the CJP, and I think many of theirs are misguided. But if you ask me whether they have a right to oppose/argue/protest on an issue that they think is important, I would categorically say — YES,” he said in a post on X on October 21.Also Read | ‘Does BJP want Opposition votes to split?’ Annamalai backs CJP's right to protestAnnamalai's remarks come amid a row over the Delhi Police's handling of CJP's protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Speaking to reporters in Chennai earlier this week, the BJP leader criticised the police for detaining protesters, arguing that the action could strengthen the group's leadership rather than weaken it. “To arrest them for a violation and again to drag them in terms of how they spend their time in jail, that is only going to make the leaders of CJP stronger. I'm afraid of it. The Delhi Police are doing a real disservice,” he said.A day after making these remarks, Annamalai said he had faced social media trolling over his comments.
