He also questioned the restrictions on protests at Jantar Mantar and raised concerns about the powers exercised by police officials in cases involving preventive detention.In a series of questions, Annamalai asked how long an assistant commissioner of police could continue to exercise powers as a special executive magistrate to decide whether a person should be placed under preventive detention.CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by the Delhi Police and spent seven days in custody following an order by a special executive magistrate's court.The former IPS officer also questioned whether any action had been taken over the alleged use of pellet guns by the Delhi Police or other alleged violations of standard operating procedures during protests linked to the NEET controversy.He also referred to the burning of a cockroach effigy during Dussehra celebrations, saying he had looked into who was responsible for the incident and the publicity it received.“I also recently saw a cockroach effigy burned as part of the Dussehra celebrations. Out of curiosity, I tried to find out who is giving this free publicity at a national level. No surprises here. It was led by a BJP MLA, Ashok Goel,” he said.

title: Threat email to Mumbai Mayor names Amitabh Bachchan, Diljit Dosanjh concert
description: The email threatens to target Bollywood Superstar Amitabh Bachchan as well.
content: A threat email was received by Mumbai Mayor on Friday threatening to target her office and Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh India Tour event at Mahalaxmi Racecourse in the city on November 27. The email also threatened to target Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan.Meanwhile, the Delhi Police denied permission for Diljit Dosanjh’s concert in the Capital on October 30, citing security concerns, according to a letter the police wrote to ticketing partner BookMyShow, HT reported earlier.ALSO READ: 6 schools receive bomb threats; investigators say emails a hoaxHowever, as of Thursday evening, the ticketing partner had not removed the show listing from its app or website. Dosanjh’s Aura India Tour concert was scheduled at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. In a letter to BookMyShow, the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (South District) stated, “With reference to your application, I am to inform you that your request for organising Diljit Dosanjh’s Aura India Tour Delhi at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on 30.10.2026 has been examined by this office. In view of the specific threat-related inputs, coupled with the multifarious security and law and order commitments arising out of the ongoing festive season and other important law and order concerns, the same cannot be acceded to.”ALSO READ: Diljit Dosanjh warns fans against volunteer scam ahead of Delhi concert, urges fans not to share personal dataDeputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal confirmed that permission was not granted, but refrained from sharing more details.A senior police officer, who did not wish to be named, said apart from the “festive rush”, one of the reasons is a hoax bomb threat e-mail received by multiple schools in Delhi on the morning of October 15. One such e-mail, seen by HT, warned students not to attend Dosanjh’s concert on October 30.The hoax e-mail also had pro-Khalistani slogans. Six schools received the e-mail, including The British School, Mount Carmel, Ahlcon International School, and Ahlcon Public School.Meanwhile, Dosanjh or his team has not yet commented on the development.

title: Ghaziabad: Cop thrashes minor inside GRP station, video goes viral; probe ordered
description: Ashutosh Shukla, superintendent of police at GRP (Moradabad), said the constable seen in the video clip has been transferred to police lines and an inquiry ordered
content: A constable of the Government Railway Police (GRP) has been removed from active duty after a video clip showed him beating a 15-year-old boy at the Ghaziabad railway station, a senior police officer said on Friday.Ashutosh Shukla, superintendent of police at GRP (Moradabad), said the constable seen in the video clip has been transferred to police lines and an inquiry has been ordered into the entire episode.The video, possibly filmed by a passenger, shows a uniformed man repeatedly hitting a teenager with a stick inside the GRP police station at Ghaziabad station’s platform No. 3.HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the clip.Shukla told HT that the incident took place late Thursday night. The teenager had been accused of stealing belongings of a passenger at the railway station and was picked up by GRP personnel.“The erring personnel is a constable, and he has been sent to police lines. An inquiry has also been initiated into the matter,” Ashutosh Shukla, superintendent of police at GRP (Moradabad), told HT on Friday.Manoj Chaudhary, station house officer at the GRP police station, said the teenager in the video was one of two boys who came to the station last night from Delhi and were loitering on platforms 3 and 4.“They picked a passenger’s bag who was sleeping under the stairs. When he noticed, he shouted for help, and the constable on duty chased the boys and nabbed them. They were brought to the police station. The constable thrashed one boy aged 15 when he was filmed,” Chaudhary said.However, the passenger whose bag they had taken didn’t want to pursue the case. “Thereafter, the boys were allowed to leave,” he said.“The erring constable was sent to police lines, and an inquiry was ordered by senior officials. The inquiry will be conducted by a circle officer (GRP),” Chaudhary added.

title: Parliament's monsoon session yet to be prorogued, raising doubts over winter sitting
description: The government has kept everyone guessing but defended the decision, pointing out there is no illegality or irregularity.
content: The Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13, has yet to be prorogued. While the constitutional validity of the decision cannot be challenged, it has raised questions about whether the upcoming Winter Session of Parliament will be on track.The delay in proroguing the House has exacerbated friction between the government and the opposition and set off speculation that a special session could be in the offing to pass the crucial 131st Constitution Amendment Bill and the Delimitation Bill, which are required to roll out the 33% reservation for women in legislatures.The government has kept everyone guessing but defended the decision, pointing out there is no illegality or irregularity. In a detailed letter to Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge on Monday, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said there was no impropriety or irregularity in Parliament not being prorogued since the monsoon session ended in August, as there was “no constitutional requirement” prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die.Will there be a Winter session of Parliament?Typically, there are three sessions every year, starting with the Budget Session, which begins at the end of January and winds up by April; followed by the Monsoon session that begins in July and extends till August; and the Winter session that begins in November and winds up with the calendar year in December. This calendar is conventional and not constitutionally bound.According to people aware of the details, if the government does not recommend proroguing the House to the President, the upcoming session will be considered part of the Monsoon session. Simply put, there will be no Winter Session.“If the House is not prorogued, then it is considered a continuation of the previous session…” said a person familiar with Parliamentary procedures.Article 85 of the Constitution, which lays down the rules for convening sessions, does not specify any cut-off date for proroguing the House. It only prescribes that the gap between two consecutive sessions of Parliament cannot exceed six months. This means Parliament has to meet at least twice a year.“The three sessions are a convention, not a rule…There have been instances in the past when one session was skipped on account of an exigency; the most recent example is that of 2020, when COVID was at its peak, and the Winter Session could not be convened,” said the person quoted above.In the past, Parliament did not convene for the Winter session four times since 1952: in 1975, during the Emergency; in 1979, because the Lok Sabha had been dissolved; in 1984, after the assassination of the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi; and finally in 2020, owing to the pandemic.The procedurePer Article 85(2)(a) of the Constitution, the President has the power to prorogue either House acting on the recommendation of the Union Cabinet.The tenure of a session ends with the House being adjourned sine die by the Presiding Officer- Speaker of the Lok Sabha or Chairman of the Rajya Sabha- which is followed by the parliamentary affairs ministry sending a proposal to the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs (CCPA) to prorogue the House. This proposal is then sent to the President by the Union Cabinet. The House is prorogued once the President signs the order, and a notification is issued.The government has defended the delay, pointing out that there are several instances in the past when the House was kept unprorogued for as many as 87 days.Former secretary general of the Lok Sabha and Constitutional expert PDT Achary, however, said the government needs to explain the reason for the delay. “For better and smooth parliamentary functioning, the government must tell the Opposition why it has not recommended the proroguing… In the past, when the House was not prorogued, there were reasons for it, and those were stated,” he said.

title: Red Corner notice against Russian woman who fled India with son despite joint custody order
description: Police also informed the court that they had sought her extradition through the ministry of external affairs (MEA) and the Indian embassy in Moscow.
content: A Red Corner notice has been issued against Russian national Viktoriia Basu, who allegedly left India with her minor son last year after the Supreme Court granted joint custody to both parents, Delhi Police told the Saket court on Thursday.Police also informed the court that they had sought her extradition through the ministry of external affairs (MEA) and the Indian embassy in Moscow.Notably, a Red Corner Notice is a request to law enforcement agencies worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, surrender or similar legal action. Each member country decides whether to make an arrest under its own laws.What is the case about?An FIR was registered at Delhi's Defence Colony police station in 2025 following a complaint by Saikat Basu, who married Viktoriia in 2017. The couple's son was born on October 29, 2020.Viktoriia, who came to India in 2019, approached the court in 2023 seeking full custody of her son after the marriage broke down.After attempts to reconcile the couple failed, the Supreme Court approved a shared-custody arrangement in May, allowing each parent to spend three days a week with the child. It also extended Viktoriia's visa and directed Delhi Police to keep her residence under watch.However, on July 7 that year, her husband informed the court that she had gone missing with their son. This led to a search by law enforcement agencies and intervention by the MEA.The matter is pending before the Saket District Court. On Thursday, Delhi Police filed a status report before Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Deepakshi Rana.Seeking more time, police told the court that a formal extradition request had been sent to the ministry of home affairs (MHA) for action through the MEA and the Indian embassy in Moscow. The request seeks to trace Viktoriia, the main accused in the FIR registered on the basis of Saikat Basu's complaint.Police said they were examining the documents submitted by the complainant to determine the further action required.What Russian embassy said earlierIn November last year, the Russian embassy said it was in close contact with Indian authorities over the matter.The Russian embassy “implements its priority duties to ensure and defend rights and legitimate interests of Russian citizens in full accordance with the Indian legislation”, the statement said. “With regard to the matter of Ms Basu, we maintain close contact with the competent Indian authorities,” it said.Police had also submitted evidence alleging that two Russian embassy officials, Albert Shtoda and Arthur Gerbst, helped arrange a vehicle for Viktoriia when she went missing on July 7. The vehicle reportedly took her to the India-Nepal border in Bihar, from where she travelled to Russia via Sharjah.With inputs from agencies

title: Bengaluru hit by magnitude 3 earthquake, disaster agency says no need to panic
description: The epicentre was located north of Timmojanahalli village in Tubagere Gram Panchayat limits of Doddaballapur taluk Bangalore rural district.
content: An earthquake of magnitude 3 struck Bengaluru on Friday morning. As per the National Centre for Seismology and the Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC), the earthquake struck at 9:01am today with its epicentre located north of Timmojanahalli village in Tubagere Gram Panchayat limits of Doddaballapur taluk, Bangalore rural district.According to KSNDMC, the tremors may have been felt within a radius of 20-30 km from the epicentre. However, the seismic intensity was low, and the earthquake was not expected to cause damage to the local community.The epicentre falls in Seismic Zone II, and KSNDMC said there was no need for panic given the low magnitude and intensity of the earthquake.This is a developing story.

title: Andhra: Low pressure over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into cyclone by Oct 26
description: Andhra: Low pressure over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into cyclone by Oct 26
content: Amaravati, A low pressure area has formed over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal and is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by October 26 before moving towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts, the Meteorological Department said on Friday.The system, which formed at 5.30 am under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the southeast and adjoining east-central Bay of Bengal, is likely to persist over the same region and intensify into a depression on October 24, it said.The weather system is likely to intensify further into a deep depression on October 25 and into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26. It is then expected to continue moving west-northwestwards and intensify further towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts over the subsequent two days, the Meteorological Department said in a release.Meanwhile, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has forecast scattered heavy rainfall across the state over the next four days under the influence of the northeast monsoon.SDMA Managing Director Prakhar Jain said cloudy weather, moderate rainfall and lightning were likely on Friday.He advised people to remain alert and take necessary precautions, warning them against standing under trees or near large hoardings.Moderate rainfall accompanied by lightning is likely at isolated places in Vizianagaram, Manyam, Alluri, Kadapa, Annamayya, Chittoor and Tirupati districts on Friday, he said.Light to moderate rainfall accompanied by lightning is likely at isolated places in Srikakulam, Polavaram, Visakhapatnam, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Markapuram, Prakasam, Nellore, Nandyal and Sri Sathya Sai districts. Light rainfall is likely in the remaining districts.For Saturday, moderate rainfall accompanied by lightning is forecast at isolated places in Alluri, Krishna, Bapatla, Nellore, Kadapa and Chittoor districts, while light to moderate rainfall is likely in the remaining districts, Jain said.Rainfall recorded until 5 pm on Thursday included 87.5 mm at Alivelumangapuram and 50.4 mm at Obulavaripalle in Tirupati district, 57.2 mm at Dagadarthi in Nellore district, 53.3 mm at Kavali and 51.5 mm in Chittoor Urban. Pennepalle recorded 45.7 mm of rainfall, Renigunta 41.2 mm, Puttur 40.5 mm and Naidupeta 38.4 mm, he said.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Keralam offers to host Raihan Vadra's photo exhibition without exceptions amid Bikaner House row
description: The offer came a day after Raihan said the administration of Bikaner House in Delhi demanded that he take down several photographs documenting protests.
content: Keralam Chief Minister VD Satheesan has said that the state is "happy and proud" to host the "No Idea is final" photography exhibition of Raihan Vadra, son of Wayanad MP and Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.The offer came a day after Raihan said the administration of Bikaner House in Delhi, where the exhibition is ongoing, demanded that he take down several photographs documenting the protests in the national capital over the past six months. He claimed that some photographs which were demanded to be taken down even included those of the tricolour. CM Satheesan, in a post on X, wrote, "Kerala would be happy and proud to host Raihan Vadra's No Idea is Final exhibition in its entirety. No exclusions, no exceptions."Who said what on the rowAfter the order from Bikaner House, Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said that she was proud of her son. "When someone with power becomes afraid of the expression of another, he doesn't know it, but he has already lost the very power he is trying to protect," she wrote, in a snide comment at the BJP-led Union government.Meanwhile, Bikaner House said the photographs "found to be inconsistent with the policy" of the venue were removed. The administration claimed it sought the removal of some of the photographs because they had “political messaging.”Bikaner House is owned by the Rajasthan government, currently led by the BJP.

title: Siddaramaiah sting operation case: News channel head seeks anticipatory bail
description: Police said Rakesh Shetty, the channel head, was taken into custody and brought to Bengaluru for questioning
content: A Bengaluru court will on Friday take up a news channel head’s anticipatory bail application in connection with a purported sting operation targeting ruling Congress leader and former chief minister Siddaramaiah.Police said Rakesh Shetty, the channel head, was taken into custody from a hotel in Mysuru on Wednesday night and brought to Bengaluru for questioning early on Thursday. Shetty, who had been staying at the hotel for four days, was questioned and asked to appear for further questioning.The Bengaluru court adjourned the hearing in Shetty’s anticipatory bail application to Friday.Karnataka’s Cyber Crime Division has been investigating the case over the past week after Siddaramaiah filed a complaint over the purported operation and the circulation of a video.Siddaramaiah this month moved court seeking to restrain media organisations from publishing details of, or broadcasting videos linked to, the sting allegedly carried out at the behest of his successor, DK Shivakumar, to force the former to step down as Karnataka chief minister in May.Siddaramaiah’s resignation ended months of uncertainty over the Congress leadership transition and cleared the way for his then deputy and challenger Shivakumar to assume office.Siddaramaiah described the circulation of the videos on social media as false propaganda intended to damage his reputation.Siddaramaiah acknowledged being aware of sting operations in Karnataka and called for those responsible to be identified.Union minister and Janata Dal (Secular) leader H D Kumaraswamy alleged Shivakumar used the purported sting operation to force Siddaramaiah out of office. Kumaraswamy alleged that Siddaramaiah was called to Delhi for discussions on Cabinet expansion but was instead confronted with “compromising material” purportedly obtained through the sting operation.He said the ruling Congress leadership and a media organisation were allegedly involved.Kumaraswamy demanded Shetty’s arrest and sought a special investigation team probe. He submitted complaints to top police officers, identifying Shetty as the prime person behind the purported sting operation.Kumaraswamy alleged that the operation was part of a conspiracy targeting Siddaramaiah. The allegations are under investigation.Shivakumar rejected the allegations against him, saying attempts were also made to trap him through sting operations after he became chief minister. He said he possessed photographs and documents identifying those allegedly involved and warned Cabinet colleagues and government officials to remain vigilant.In May, Siddaramaiah said he stepped down as the chief minister acting on directions from the Congress leadership but will remain active in Karnataka politics.Siddaramaiah, the state’s longest-serving chief minister, took over after the Congress won its biggest victory in a generation in Karnataka in 2023. Siddaramaiah’s government remained mired in tensions over the chief minister’s post.

title: Bharatiya Kisan Union leader Rakesh Tikait stages sit-in after finding Ganna Bhawan locked
description: The sit-in preceded Friday’s proposed farmers’ mahapanchayat, where participants are expected to press for higher sugarcane prices and other demands.
content: Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) leader Rakesh Tikait staged a sit-in outside the gate of the Ganna Kisan Sansthan (Ganna Bhawan) in Dalibagh on Thursday after finding the institute locked.The incident took place when Tikait reached the institute ahead of Kisan Mazdoor Mahapanchayat scheduled on Friday. Finding the gate closed, Tikait and his supporters sat on the ground outside the gate itself.After the protest, the administration started the process of opening the gate, sources said. The gates were opened at around 8pm, said Alok Varma, district president of the BKU.Also Read | Ministers hold talks with BKU leaders, promise time-bound action on demandsThe sit-in was linked to Friday’s proposed mahapanchayat of farmers at Ganna Sansthan. The proposed Mahapanchayat is expected to see participation of farmers from Western UP, Terai and Central UP. It is being seen as a show of strength by the BKU faction led by Tikait ahead of 2027 assembly polls.Sitting by the roadside, Tikait said that if the gate is not opened, the panchayat will be held on the road itself. “If you lock the gate of the institution for farmers, where will farmers go? We will hold the panchayat here on the road,” Tikait said.BKU workers said mahapanchayat has been called to raise key demands: increase sugarcane price to ₹500-600 per quintal, immediate clearance of pending dues by sugar mills, increase in circle rate for land acquisition and legal guarantee for MSP.Also Read | Demanding higher MSP, debt relief, BKU Ekta Ugrahan activists stage widespread protestsThe Dalibagh-situated Ganna Kisan Sansthan is a traditional venue for farmers’ meetings in Lucknow and is linked to sugarcane farmers’ interests.Police force was deployed on the spot as Tikait’s sit-in drew a crowd of supporters. Officials said that the situation is under control and permission for Friday’s panchayat is being examined. Tikait, who has been mobilising farmers over cane price and payment issues ahead of the crushing season, said farmers are being forced to protest for basic demands.“Cane price has not increased in proportion to cost. Mills owe crores. Farmers want MSP guarantee and fair circle rate for land,” he said.

title: US national Mathew Vandyke appears before Delhi court in Myanmar arms training case
description: The six Ukrainian nationals arrested along with Mathew VanDyke on March 13, however, have not returned to India.
content: US national Mathew VanDyke, who was allowed to return to his home country for a month, returned to India and appeared before a Delhi court on Friday, people familiar with the development said.The court had directed VanDyke, in an order last month, to appear before it within 72 hours of returning to India, one of the persons said. “He is currently completing formalities in the court,” the person said, requesting anonymity.The six Ukrainian nationals arrested along with VanDyke on March 13, however, have not returned to India.Last month, a Delhi court allowed VanDyke and the six Ukrainian nationals to return to their respective countries on the condition that they would rejoin the investigation. The seven were arrested in March under stringent provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), which the National Investigation Agency (NIA) subsequently dropped in its chargesheet filed in September.In the chargesheet, the NIA charged the seven accused only under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, an offence that can be compounded. VanDyke paid the compounding fees for the alleged violations under the Act and was granted default bail by the court last month.The agency had said last month that its investigation under the UAPA was continuing.The six Ukrainians are Hurba Petro, Taras Slyviak, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Marian Stefankiv, Maksim Honcharuk and Viktor Kaminskyi.The NIA had earlier alleged that the seven accused illegally entered Myanmar through Mizoram without valid travel documents and participated in a pre-scheduled training programme for ethnic armed groups operating in Myanmar that were fighting the country's military junta.According to the agency, the seven imparted training in drone warfare, drone operations, assembly and jamming technology to members of Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups, including the Chin National Front (CNF) and the Kachin Independence Army (KIA), over nearly three months.The NIA also alleged that VanDyke and the others received logistical support from CNF members and that the mission was financed through funds arranged by a commander of a Myanmar-based rebel group.

title: Row over ITBP chief's Arunachal 'face-off' remark, Congress questions govt
description: In an address to the troops, ITBP director general purportedly said "there was a face-off at different locations" in Arunachal, "which is still continuing".
content: A political row erupted on Friday over Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) chief Shatrujeet Kapur's purported remarks that the Shaurya platoon, an elite unit of the force, is successfully dealing with a “face-off in Arunachal Pradesh”.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh accused the government of remaining "silent on this grave issue". There was no immediate reaction by government officials or the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).In his address to the troops in Rajasthan's Alwar at a felicitation ceremony on Thursday, ITBP director general Kapur purportedly said: “In recent days, there was a situation in Arunachal Pradesh where there was a face-off at different locations, which is still continuing. There our Shaurya commando teams did really exceedingly well."A video clip of his remarks is circulating widely online. The central armed force, which is tasked with guarding and patrolling the Line of Actual Control (LAC) between India and China, released the footage on social media late on Thursday night but later deleted it. HT has reached out to ITBP for comment. This article will be updated when there is a response.Kapur did not explicitly name who the face-off was with but added, “ITBP started as a mountain guerrilla force, but since 2004 we have been guarding the Indo-China border."Since July, there have been reports of a standoff with Chinese troops in the remote Taksin area of Upper Subansiri district. Asked about this in a press conference in August, foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the state of border affairs has ramifications for overall India-China ties, adding that the two sides have agreed to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to “avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation” along the border.Congress asks questionsAfter portions of Kapur's remarks appeared online, the Congress party sharpened its attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his government.“While on one hand, the Prime Minister, who bows to China, continues the ongoing saga of making concessions, in the meantime, the Director General of the ITBP has commended the force's performance in the recent clashes with the Chinese PLA within Indian territory in Arunachal Pradesh, which is absolutely justified,” Congress leader Ramesh said in a long post on X."...what kind of nationalism is this softness toward China and the growing economic dependence?" he asked, accusing the government of being “silent” on the matter. The government has in the past rejected the Congress's allegations of bowing down to Beijing, saying it was committed to protecting India's borders.At the same time, BJP functionaries have accused the Congress of politicising national security issues. They have also hit back at the opposition party, saying Jawaharal Nehru ceded ground to China.India and China have attempted to rebuild their relationship after reaching an understanding in October 2024 to end a military standoff in Ladakh that lasted more than four years and took ties to a six-decade low. Chinese President Xi Jinping made his first visit to India in seven years to attend the BRICS Summit on September 12-13, and held a bilateral meeting with PM Modi to review ties.Speaking at an Asia Society event in New York in late September, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said India-China ties were better today than they were a couple of years ago.ITBP chief's advice In Alwar, during his address at the felicitation ceremony, ITBP chief Kapur also advised the troops to avoid drinking alcohol and getting “honey trapped” on social media.“Those who make reels should be careful. I would say avoid social media. Our adversaries keep an eye on your social media accounts. Even when you share one photo on your profile, they get a lot of information. Do not talk to people you do not know. Use social media and apps, but don’t get used,” he said.

title: Kolkata Durga Puja stampede: SIT zeroes in on narrow exit point, dimly lit pathway
description: A six-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) is probing the October 17 stampede that killed 19 people
content: The six-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the October 17 Kolkata stampede that killed 19 people has zeroed in on the narrow exit point and the dimly lit pathway at the Chor Bagan Durga Puja pandal, even as the eighth accused arrested in the case was due to be produced before a court on Friday, a day after his arrest.A surge in crowds amid heavy rain triggered the stampede at one of the popular Durga Puja venues, in cramped north Kolkata, as crowds jostled through a narrow bylane.Retired Calcutta high court judge Anindita Roy Saraswati, heading the SIT, said the stampede did not happen inside the pandal but at the exit point. “We found the lights to be dim, as people had complained,” she said outside the pandal on Thursday.She added that the pandal was kept in the same condition as it was during the incident. “We have to find out how the whole thing happened and who was responsible.”A police forensic team visited the stampede site on Thursday to create a 3D map. A drone was deployed for aerial videos of the pandal and the roads around it.A police officer, who inspected the site, said that the families of those killed and the 25 injured people alleged that the emergency gate, which was otherwise used for VIP movement, was locked. “The exit path used by common visitors was around seven feet wide, which was extremely narrow. The exit route was further narrowed by outdoor units of the air conditioner machines installed inside the pandals and food stalls set up on a road.”The officer added that visitors had to use a five-feet-wide and seven-feet-high circular ramp to get a 360-degree view of the idol inside the pandal. “[They had to] climb down the ramp before leaving the pandal. There was no second path.”The officer said the ramp was intact during the police inspection. “It seems people panicked and ran for safety because someone announced that the pandal, of which the ramp was an integral part, was collapsing.”Sanjib Raha, a puja committee member, was arrested from Nadia on Thursday and brought to Kolkata.A second officer said Raha was identified as one who made the announcement that triggered the panic.Another person, Kushal Majumdar, was detained for questioning in the case on Friday. A second officer said inquiries indicate that Majumdar also made announcements on October 17.All the accused arrested in the case have been booked under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)’s Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), 110 (attempt to commit culpable homicide) and 3(5) (crime committed with common intention).The seven accused, including Raj Kumar Sewda, the puja committee secretary, and Santanu Dubey, the vice-president, were remanded in 10-day police custody.The stampede triggered a political row as there has been no recent history of people dying in a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in West Bengal.The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which came to power in West Bengal for the first time five months ago, has drawn flak from the opposition over the stampede.The Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC) and the Left parties targeted chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, especially because his nephew, Depdeep Adhikari, was involved in the puja as its patron along with BJP’s north Calcutta chief Tamoghna Ghosh and the party’s lawmaker Vijay Ojha.Suvendu Adhikari visited the families of those killed on Tuesday and Wednesday and distributed compensation. The state government has promised a job for one member from each family.Suvendu Adhikari said nobody would have died had someone not announced over the loudspeaker that the pandal was about to collapse. “The incident happened because of human error and not because a crowd entered the pandal to take shelter from rain,” Adhikari said on Wednesday.MAITC lawmaker Kunal Ghosh alleged that efforts to shield those responsible for the tragedy have started. “We appeal to the SIT chairperson to question all people associated with the puja after they are taken into police custody. Otherwise, the truth will never be revealed.”

title: CPI(M) MP seeks independent probe into SBI customer data exposure, writes to FM Nirmala Sitharaman
description: On October 21, SBI informed the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange that it had suffered “an incident involving the loss of certain data.”
content: CPI(M) MP A A Rahim wrote to Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, seeking an independent investigation into the reported exposure of 3,897 State Bank of India (SBI) customer records on the dark web.He urged the state-run bank to notify affected customers directly and asked the Centre to take urgent measures to safeguard them, in addition to “strict accountability” for security lapses.“Wrote to FM Nirmala Sitharaman on the alarming exposure of SBI customer data on the dark web. I urge an independent probe, direct notification to affected citizens, and strict accountability for security lapses,” Rahim said in a post on X, sharing the letter dated October 21.The SBI data exposure On October 21, SBI informed the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange that it had suffered “an incident involving the loss of certain data,” with 3,897 customer records containing personal information identified in a larger trove of about 3.75 lakh records on the dark web.The exposed information reportedly included registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and Customer Information File (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata linked to loan records and other files. The bank said it learnt of the incident on October 16 through its threat intelligence provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In).What the CPI(M) MP said in letter to SitharamanIn his letter, Rahim said the incident raised concerns about the adequacy of data protection and cybersecurity safeguards at public-sector banks. He stressed the need to ensure that institutions entrusted with citizens’ financial security adequately protect their personal information.“While the bank has indicated that its core operations remain unaffected, the absence of disruption to banking services does not diminish the seriousness of the potential compromise of customers’ personal information,” Rahim wrote, stressing that the incident’s implications extended beyond its impact on the bank’s operations.He urged the finance ministry to ensure a comprehensive and independent investigation, with clear timelines to identify the source and extent of the suspected breach. “SBI should take immediate steps to directly notify all affected customers through accessible channels for reporting suspected fraud, and extend appropriate assistance to those at risk,” he added.Rahim warned that customers whose personal information had been exposed could face identity theft, targeted phishing, impersonation and financial fraud. “Customers must not be left exposed to fraudulent calls, impersonation and other forms of exploitation without timely information and adequate institutional support,” he wrote.

title: Two workers die of asphyxiation due to gas leak in Telangana’s pharma factory
description: The plant manufactures active pharmaceutical ingredients and drug intermediates, and also takes up contract manufacturing services.
content: Two workers died of asphyxiation following an alleged gas leak at a pharmaceutical factory in Telangana’s Sangareddy district on Friday morning, police said.The incident took place at a popular pharmaceutical manufacturing unit at Gaddapotharam village of Jinnaram mandal. The plant manufactures active pharmaceutical ingredients and drug intermediates, and also takes up contract manufacturing services.The workers were identified as Sudarshan and Balaji from Andhra Pradesh. The full names and the ages of the deceased have not yet been given.It is not immediately known how many workers were there at the plant.Also Read: UP man reports wife’s ‘sudden death’, arrested after autopsy reveals plot“We have launched an investigation to ascertain how the accident occurred and what caused the gas leak,” a police official said. Further details are awaited.Similar incidentMeanwhile, fire broke out at another pharmaceutical unit in Andhra Pradesh’s Anakapalli district in the early hours of Friday, triggering panic among the workers.The fire mishap occurred in the production block of Unit-15 of Aurobindo Pharma plant in Parawada Pharma City on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam at around 5:30am.“No injuries or casualties were reported in the incident and the fire was quickly brought under control by the fire extinguishers,” the police said.As flames rapidly spread, employees were alarmed and rushed out of the premises fearing for their lives. Fire personnel, who were alerted to the incident, rushed to the spot and managed to bring the flames under control after considerable effort.Also Read: Chandigarh: Mystery shrouds death of Chhattisgarh bizman at Sector 17 hotel roomA short circuit or a chemical reaction is suspected to have triggered the fire. Officials have launched an investigation to establish the exact cause of the incident.Andhra Pradesh home minister Vangalapudi Anitha spoke over the phone with the Anakapalli district collector and superintendent of police and enquired about the circumstances that led to the fire and the prevailing situation at the industrial unit.The home minister also directed officials to expedite the response and relief measures at the site, an official statement said.

title: Class 3 student crushed by reversing school van Uttar Pradesh's Naini
description: Residents reportedly assaulted the driver before handing him to police. Officials said the van appeared to be operating without a required helper.
content: An eight-year-old girl was killed Thursday afternoon after being run over by her school van in Naini, shortly after arriving home. The accident sparked outrage among local residents, who allegedly assaulted the driver before handing him over to the police.According to family members, the victim, Taswani Udyanshi Pathak, a Class III student of Delhi Public School, reached home in the school van at around 3:30 pm. After exiting the van, she reportedly became trapped when the strap of her school bag caught in the vehicle’s door. The driver, assuming the child had already reached safely, allegedly reversed the van without checking, pinning her between the vehicle and the boundary wall of her home.Neighbours and passersby, alerted by the screams of other children inside the van, rushed to the scene and extricated the girl. She was rushed to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival.Also Read | MCD again floats tender for Naini Lake revival project pending since 2015The victim was an only child of her parents. Originally from the Mirzapur district, the family resides in Prayagpuram, Naini. Taswani lived with her grandparents, Surendra Pathak, a retired section engineer, and Kadambini Pathak. Her father, Manish Pathak, works in a private firm in Delhi, while her mother, Aarti Dubey, is a government school teacher posted in Gorakhpur.The tragedy has devastated the family. Her grandparents and uncle, Pushpendra Pathak, were left inconsolable, while her parents travelled to Prayagraj immediately upon receiving the news.Naini SHO Avinash Singh confirmed that the driver, identified as Satyapal, has been taken into custody. He noted that the body has not yet been sent for a postmortem, as the family is awaiting the arrival of the parents. Formal legal action will proceed once a complaint is lodged.Also Read | Delhi: Naini Lake set for major facelift as residents complain of ageing infraRecalling the incident, her grandmother, Kadambini Pathak, who was waiting at the gate, described the harrowing moments. “Taswani got down from the rear of the van and was trying to free her bag strap, which had caught in the door. Without checking if she was clear, the driver suddenly reversed at speed. She was crushed between the van and the wall. We screamed and tried to stop him, but it was too late,” she said.Meanwhile, ARTO (Enforcement) SP Singh stated that preliminary findings indicate the van was operating without a helper, despite regulations mandating an attendant in vehicles transporting schoolchildren.“The absence of a helper appears to be a serious lapse,” he said.

title: Gujarat bars outsiders from govt schools without principal’s nod; Congress alleges cover-up
description: Gujarat Cong spokesperson Manish Doshi the restrictions would not address teacher shortages, the condition of classrooms or the lack of facilities in schools.
content: The Gujarat government has barred outsiders from entering government school premises without prior written permission from the institution’s head and made the principal’s written approval mandatory for any photography or videography involving students or teachers.According to the state education department circular dated October 21, all visitors must log their details in an entry register. Access to classrooms, laboratories, libraries, playgrounds, and toilets where students are present would require prior written permission. Also, they must be accompanied by school officials at all times during the visit.The department has cited the government’s responsibility to protect children under the principle of in loco parentis, under which the state assumes responsibilities similar to those of a parent. The circular also cites safety guidelines issued by the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and a Supreme Court verdict recognising privacy as a fundamental right.“Photography, videography, interviews, audio recording or live-streaming of students, teachers or school activities shall not be carried out without the prior written permission of the Principal. Such activities may be permitted only for lawful purposes,” the circular said.Unauthorised entry, refusal to leave, unauthorised recording or obstruction of school activities must be reported to the local police and the relevant education authorities. The circular refers to applicable laws, including the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act and the Information Technology Act for possible legal action.“Any external person shall obtain prior written permission from the principal or head of the Institution to enter the school premises. Only government officials who are duly authorised.... to perform their official duties shall be exempted,” the circular said.To be sure, the Rajasthan government and several districts in Uttar Pradesh have issued similar orders over the past three months prohibiting outsiders from entering government schools. Rajasthan issued the restriction ahead of much-publicised visits by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders to government schools in the state under its “School Theek Karo” (fix schools) campaign.The Gujarat directive triggered sharp political reactions, with the opposition Congress accusing the state of using child safety as a shield to block public scrutiny of decaying school infrastructure.Gujarat Congress spokesperson Manish Doshi said the government had no right to hide administrative failures in the name of child safety, adding that restrictions on cameras would not address teacher shortages, the condition of classrooms or the lack of facilities in schools.Doshi claimed that around 40,000 teacher posts in the state were vacant and about 42,000 classrooms were dilapidated. He also claimed that around 3,000 schools operated with a single teacher, serving more than 80,000 students, while around 14,500 schools had students from multiple grades studying together.On the government citing the need to protect the privacy of students, Doshi asked if the same considerations would apply when students attend government programmes or their photographs were used for publicity.

title: No dilution in prescribed standards: NMC on denotification of medical education regulations
description: No dilution in prescribed standards: NMC on denotification of medical education regulations
content: New Delhi, The National Medical Commission has asserted that the de-notification of the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 will not dilute prescribed standards of medical education and are intended to remove overlapping procedures.The Commission, which is the statutory body for medical education in the country, had on October 14 denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations .The denotification "does not, in any manner, dilute the prescribed standards of medical education or the regulatory oversight exercised by NMC," a statement by the Commission said.Under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, the Undergraduate Medical Education Board and Postgraduate Medical Education Board are primarily entrusted with prescribing academic standards, minimum requirements and educational norms.The Medical Assessment and Rating Board , under Section 26 of the Act is specifically empowered to assess and inspect medical institutions, verify compliance with prescribed standards and initiate appropriate regulatory measures against institutions found deficient, it stated.The regulations had introduced a parallel mechanism of institutional evaluation, annual renewal and enforcement through UGMEB and PGMEB, resulting in overlapping regulatory functions, the statement.Following judicial observations and a detailed examination of the statutory framework, the Commission decided to remove this duplication and align regulatory responsibilities with the provisions of the NMC Act, it stated.The requirement of Annual Disclosure Reports remains mandatory and medical colleges will continue to submit annual disclosures concerning faculty, infrastructure, clinical facilities, patient load and other prescribed parameters, it emphasised.These disclosures remain available for scrutiny and verification through the statutory assessment and inspection mechanisms of MARB. Therefore, any suggestion that annual disclosures would become merely unverified claims is misplaced, the statement said.Further, all existing minimum standard requirements relating to faculty, infrastructure, clinical material, teaching facilities, attendance and academic standards will remain fully applicable.The MARB retains its statutory authority to conduct assessments and inspections, including where necessary without prior notice, and to take appropriate action against non-compliant institutions under the NMC Act and Regulation of the Establishment of Medical Institutions, Assessment and Rating Regulations, 2023, the statement said.The de-notification also safeguards actions already taken, liabilities incurred and proceedings initiated under MSMER-2023. The decision neither provides immunity for past violations nor exempts medical colleges from future regulatory action, it stressed.The only procedural change is the removal of the additional annual renewal requirement under MSMER-2023.Medical colleges remain subject to mandatory annual disclosures, prescribed minimum standards, institutional assessment and statutory enforcement."NMC remains committed to maintaining the highest standards of medical education while ensuring that regulation is transparent, effective and free from unnecessary duplication. Regulatory simplification must not be mistaken for regulatory relaxation," it stated."The NMC has removed an overlapping process, not the safeguards that protect the quality of medical education," the statement added.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Karnataka asks hospitals to reveal medicine purchase prices, display procedure costs
description: The measures are intended to give patients a clearer account of medicine costs and bring greater transparency to hospital billing.
content: From November 1, patients at hospitals across Karnataka will be able to see what hospitals paid for medicines as well as their maximum retail prices, under new billing requirements announced by the state government.Karnataka health and family welfare minister U T Khader said in Bengaluru that hospitals in the state will have to record both figures on patient bills and use the disclosed prices while charging for medicines. Medicine price lists will also have to be displayed in prominent public areas, particularly near registration counters.The measures are intended to give patients a clearer account of medicine costs and bring greater transparency to hospital billing.The government is also considering greater disclosure of procedure costs. Hospitals could display prices for major medical procedures on notice boards, while charges for other procedures could be maintained in a ledger that patients could consult when required, Khader said.The proposed rules will not require private hospitals to adopt the rates charged at government facilities. Instead, Khader said private hospital charges could vary depending on the amenities and level of treatment provided.“We are not expecting the pricing at private hospitals to be on par with the price set at government hospitals, but the rates could be fixed based on the amenities provided and the level of treatment at the hospital,” he said.The government’s proposed changes will therefore cover not only the disclosure of medicine purchase prices and MRPs on bills, but also the public display of medicine prices and, potentially, procedure charges.No punishment for violation yetThe state has yet to decide what action hospitals could face for failing to comply with the new requirements. The Health Department plans to meet private hospitals shortly to discuss and finalise the terms and conditions.“The punishment for violating the rules would be discussed,” U T Khader said.He said the government did not want regulations to make healthcare businesses financially unviable, while arguing that tighter rules were necessary. “We do not intend to push the healthcare business into loss, but some stringent rules and regulations will have to be put in place,” he said.Minister blames foreign investment for rising healthcare costsKhader said the government was concerned about the rise in healthcare costs and, in his view, linked part of the increase to the entry of foreign investors into the healthcare sector. “According to my observation, after foreign investors have entered the healthcare market, the prices have gone up tremendously. We will discuss and see what best can be done,” he said.

title: ‘You are responsible for this mess’: Piyush Goyal slams West over carbon emissions, climate finance failures
description: Goyal reminded the developed countries of the pledge to provide financial and technological support to developing nations under the Paris Agreement
content: Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal blamed developed countries for contributing a disproportionately large share of global carbon emissions while failing to honour the climate finance commitments they made at COP21 in Paris in 2015.Speaking at a roundtable during the Berlin Global Dialogue, Goyal said Western countries were largely responsible for the environmental damage caused by ozone layer depletion and carbon emissions. He also told the roundtable that India's contribution to global carbon emissions was only three to four percentage points lower than Europe's, despite India having a population of 1.4 billion and accounting for 17 per cent of the world's population.Also Read | Emissions didn't spike in 2025. That doesn't mean climate crisis has been stopped in its tracks"Who's responsible for this mess in the first place? Where did the ozone layer get damaged? Who sent all that carbon into the atmosphere? I represent 17% of the world's population, but my contribution to global carbon emissions is less than 3%. You (Europe) represent probably 3% or 4% of the world's population, yet your contribution to those carbon emissions—or this mess—is humongous. The problem was caused by you," Goyal said. Goyal said India's per capita carbon emissions remain significantly lower than those of Western countries, arguing that Europe’s per capita emissions and environmental impact are seven to eight times higher than India's.“Even today, as we sit here, my per capita contribution to carbon emissions is probably less than 10 per cent or 15 per cent of yours. Even today, Europe's per capita contribution to carbon emissions—and its per capita environmental impact—is probably seven or eight times that of India,” Goyal said.Also Read | If current policies continue, warming could reach 2.8°C within this century: UN reportWhat happened to $100 billion climate finance pledge, Goyal questions?Goyal also reminded the developed countries of the world about the pledge to provide financial and technological support to developing and vulnerable nations under the Paris Agreement. He said that as per the agreement, developed countries were to assist developing countries with climate finance worth $100 billion but not a ‘dime of it’ has been received."At the Paris climate conference in 2015, when the whole world came together, it was Prime Minister Modi who brought the Global South together and encouraged countries to commit to addressing climate change at COP21. It was agreed that the developed countries, who have enjoyed the fruits of messing up the climate for so many decades, will pay a greater price, and will support the developing and less developed countries, as well as island nations in the Pacific and the Caribbean...Just $100 billion a year. That was the commitment," Goyal said.Also Read | Ahead of COP31 next month, what has India committed to and what does it expect?“Eleven years later, we haven't seen a nickel or a dime of that. It's all promises. The larger question that the European Union and CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) have failed to answer,” Goyal added.India reportedly recorded a decline in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in 2025 compared to the previous year, breaking a prolonged trend of rapid growth, according to the United Nations Environment Programme's (UNEP) annual Emissions Gap Report released on Wednesday. The decline was attributed partly to weather-related factors and partly to structural shifts towards renewable energy.The report noted that while India remains the world's third-largest emitter of greenhouse gases, its per capita emissions are less than half the global average and significantly lower than those of China and the United States, the two largest emitters, which reportedly recorded an increase in total emissions last year.

title: Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 to focus on promotion of classical text Thirukkural
description: The sangamam will bring around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu to Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya
content: The fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS) will focus on the promotion of the classical Tamil text Thirukkural, and 1,000 students selected through a test from colleges across the country will receive a month-long internship and a ₹10,000 stipend each to study it.KTS will bring around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu to Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya for cultural, academic and spiritual exchanges from November 28 to December 12.KTS is organised under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB) programme to reinforce the historical and cultural connections between Kashi (Varanasi) and Tamil Nadu, two ancient centres of learning. Launched in October 2015, EBSB aims to enhance interaction and promote mutual understanding between people of different states and Union Territories (UTs).The government pitches the initiative as a way to strengthen national unity through shared cultural heritage, with a particular emphasis on engaging young people with classical knowledge traditions.Union education minister Pralhad Joshi, who launched the KTS 5.0 registration portal on Thursday, said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasised that India is one when “divisive forces” try to divide India along regional lines and on other issues. “...the Vishnu Purana, which is 5,000 years old, conveys that India is one. It was one in the past, it is one today, and it will remain one in the future,” Joshi said at the portal launch.He said the event would help participants explore the historical links between Kashi and Tamil Nadu.The theme“Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen,” or “Let us study the Thirukkural,” will be the KTS 5.0 theme. The classical Tamil text comprises 1,330 couplets on virtue, wealth and love, and is widely regarded as a source of ethical and moral teachings.Joshi said awards have been instituted to encourage 1,000 students chosen to study the text through structured learning, research and campus activities.According to the KTS website, the interns will read Thirukkural in a language they know and submit a research paper through their college on its moral values. “The Central Institute of Classical Tamil (CICT) will give a one-hour online orientation and a 20-minute question session.”Students will be grouped into about 20 batches of 50, by the language they choose. “In their own college, under a guiding teacher, each student will give a one-hour presentation and learn and teach at least 10 important couplets, in Tamil and in translation. Learning material will be placed on the CICT website,” says the website.Tamil scholars will visit schools and colleges in Varanasi to introduce students to the text through orientation modules, interactive sessions and quizzes as part of KTS 5.0. The National Book Trust, in collaboration with Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya, will also organise school activities focused on reading, storytelling and creative engagement.National Educational Technology Forum chairman Anil Sahasrabudhe said the fifth KTS edition aims to reconnect the social and cultural bonds between Kashi and Tamil Nadu that have existed since ancient times. He said the activities would help students learn about the Thirukkural’s values and the historical links between the two regions, reconnect with their cultural roots and develop a sense of pride in India’s heritage.The Union education ministry said KTS 5.0 will leverage technology to make the teachings of the Thirukkural accessible to a wider audience across India.The ministry is organising the event in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, the CICT, Banaras Hindu University, and the Uttar Pradesh government.Dinesh Patel, a Varanasi schoolteacher who has been involved in activities during previous editions, said the initiative provides an opportunity for people from the two regions to understand each other’s traditions and faith.“The idea is to foster mutual love and goodwill and help people understand each other’s culture,” Patel said. He added that cultural familiarity could encourage trade, citing the popularity of Banarasi silk sarees in Tamil Nadu.Patel said students participate in quizzes and other competitions, with activities organised at school, block and district levels. He added that winners are felicitated. Patel said such engagement allows students to learn about the other region beyond the exchanges involving visiting delegates.A national outreach initiativeThe first Kashi Tamil Sangamam was held in 2022. The initiative’s concept note described it as Modi’s “brainchild” seeking to celebrate the historical connections between Kashi and Tamil Nadu and bring their cultural traditions into contemporary educational and public discourse.The four previous editions facilitated an exchange of knowledge, language and traditions. The fifth edition builds on that approach by combining visits and cultural interactions with a nationwide educational initiative centred on the Thirukkural.Eligible applicants from Tamil Nadu can register on the KTS portal from October 22 to November 13 under the categories of students, teachers, writers and media professionals, people from agriculture and allied sectors, professionals and artisans, women, and spiritual leaders.

title: Himachal local fund accounts committee emphasises transparent use of public money
description: Himachal local fund accounts committee emphasises transparent use of public money
content: Una , Ensure timely utilisation of public funds and prioritise resolution of pending audit paras, Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly's Local Fund Accounts Committee Chairman Sanjay Rattan has said.During a meeting here on Thursday, he stressed the need for transparency in use of public funds and said there should be no unnecessary delays in resolving pending financial matters, a statement issued here on Friday said.The meeting, held at the Zila Parishad auditorium and attended by committee members and MLAs Inder Dutt Lakhanpal, Malender Rajan, Kuldeep Singh Rathore and Vivek Sharma, reviewed pending audit paras, financial management, and utilisation of public funds across departments.The chairman directed that audit paras that can be resolved by December 31 be identified, and time-bound action be taken to settle them. He further instructed that information requested by the committee be provided within one month and that updates regarding audit paras be communicated to respective directorates periodically.Rattan said public funds should not remain unutilised unnecessarily. Development projects and public welfare schemes must be completed on time so that the general public can reap the benefits.He directed officials to submit utilisation certificates on time, maintain accurate financial records and avoid delays in resolving pending audit paras. He emphasised that ensuring the benefits of government schemes reach eligible individuals and providing better facilities to the public should remain a top priority.The chairman also advised officials to maintain coordination with local MLAs to accelerate development projects. If any change or conversion is required for a project, consult the concerned MLA and take necessary action in accordance with rules, he said.The meeting also reviewed cases involving recovery of long-pending rent and penalties related to commercial premises and shops owned by urban local bodies.The chairman said the committee would recommend to the government the implementation of a 'one-time settlement' scheme across the state to facilitate recovery of outstanding dues. The final decision in this regard will be taken by the government.Rattan also instructed the principals of colleges in the district to submit a detailed report to the committee within 15 days, outlining the funds available in the Student Welfare Fund and how these funds are being utilised for the benefit of students.He said the fund available in educational institutions including colleges, polytechnics, and ITIs should be utilised for purposes such as student welfare, development of libraries, and provision of better facilities.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Delhi’s AQI remains ‘poor’; minimum temperature recorded at 19°C
description: According to the Air Quality Early Warning System, Delhi’s air quality is likely to remain poor till October 25.
content: Delhi’s air quality remained in the poor category as the minimum temperature was recorded at 19°C on Friday. The air quality index (AQI) stood at 223 (8am).Out of 57 air quality monitoring stations, 19 recorded air quality in the moderate zone while the rest were in the poor category. An AQI between 201 and 300 is classified as poor under the Central Pollution Control Board’s scale.The air quality reading comes amid the seasonal deterioration in pollution levels amid impending onset of winter and meteorological conditions favouring the accumulation of pollutants. According to the Air Quality Early Warning System, Delhi’s air quality is likely to remain poor till October 25. The outlook for the following six days also indicates that the city is unlikely to see an immediate improvement.Also Read:New GRAP actions failed to curb Delhi-NCR pollution in 10 of 12 episodes, reveals studyAccording to India Meteorological Department (IMD) data, Safdarjung, Delhi’s base weather station, recorded a minimum temperature of 19 degrees Celsius, 1.8 degrees above the seasonal average. The minimum temperature at the Ridge station settled at 19.2 degrees Celsius, 0.7 degrees above normal.Lodi Road recorded a minimum temperature of 18.6°C, 2.6°C above normal, while Ayanagar registered 19.1°C, 1.9°C above normal. Palam recorded the lowest minimum temperature among the five stations at 18.3°C, 0.5°C above normal.Also Read: Himachal to remain dry till Oct 25, mercury set to rise: IMDThe maximum temperature on Thursday was 32.5°C Celsius at Safdarjung, 32.4°C at Lodi Road, 31.7°C at Ayanagar, 31.5°C at the Ridge and 29.9°C at Palam.No rainfall was recorded at any of the five weather stations in the 24-hour period ending at 8:30am on Friday.Stubble burning dataAccording to the Decision Support System for Air Quality Management in Delhi, developed by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune, stubble burning contributed an estimated 7.4% to Delhi’s PM2.5 concentration on Thursday. Its contribution rose to 15.9% on Friday.Satellite monitoring detected 114 paddy residue-burning events across six states on Thursday, including 36 in Punjab, one in Haryana, three in Uttar Pradesh, 56 in Rajasthan, 11 in Uttarakhand and seven in Madhya Pradesh. No fires were detected in Delhi.Between September 15 and October 22, satellites detected 1,507 crop-residue burning events across the six states and Delhi. Punjab accounted for 510 events, followed by Madhya Pradesh (400), Rajasthan (308), Uttar Pradesh (193), Uttarakhand (83), Haryana (12) and Delhi (one).Transport remains highest contributorThe transport sector was the largest contributor to Delhi’s pollution, accounting for 17.32% of the estimated concentration, followed by other sources at 17.28%, according to the Decision Support System.

title: Anti-CEC protests LIVE: Marches called across Delhi, Bengaluru, other cities; suspense over Dipke's participation
description: Anti-CEC protests LIVE: The ‘People Against SIR’ group will hold nationwide marches today, with demonstrations scheduled to take place in the afternoon in New Delhi, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Jaipur and several other regions across the country.
content: Anti-CEC protests LIVE: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders have been invited to join a march on Friday, organised by People Against SIR – a week-old alliance of students, farmers and civil society groups — from Bangla Sahib Gurdwara in Delhi's Connaught Place to the Election Commission’s office near Patel Chowk. The march has been called to "restore democracy", demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and press for the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The demonstrations are scheduled for the afternoon in New Delhi, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Jaipur, and several other regions across the country.Among the prominent figures invited to join the march include CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, actor Prakash Raj, student leaders Neha Bora and Aishe Ghosh, senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, farmer leader Rakesh Tikait and activist Tushar Gandhi.‘Har Gali mein Jantar Mantar’"The People's March to Reclaim Democracy will not request police permission anywhere," the platform had said in a statement on October 18.It also warned the police, paramilitary personnel and prison authorities against using force on peaceful protesters.The platform has planned a “No SIR” campaign under the slogan “Har Gali Jantar Mantar, Har Gaon Jantar Mantar, Mera Ghar Jantar Mantar”.The People Against SIR group was formed on October 14 at Surjeet Bhavan in New Delhi by groups representing farmers, workers, women, students, Adivasis, Dalits and minorities.The platform has alleged that the SIR exercise is illegal and demanded that the voter lists be reset to their pre-2024 version and updated through social audits as laid down in the Election Commission Manual and CAG guidelines.CJP's Ranka, Das likely to get fresh summons todayCockroach Janta Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will be issued fresh notice to join the police probe in the two cases against them after they failed to appear earlier, officials aware of the matter told HT.A senior police officer said that the Delhi Police crime branch had issued a notice to Das, Ranka, and CJP member Ajinkya Shinde to join the probe on Thursday.Why CEC Gyanesh Kumar is under fireCEC Kumar is at the centre of a controversy involving the Election Commission following an investigative report by The Indian Express that claimed Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months regarding decisions and procedures linked to the SIR exercise.The Election Commission has rejected these allegations, saying that major decisions, including the SIR of electoral rolls, had been taken unanimously by the full commission.RTI reveals Cabinet Secretariat sent election commissioners’ letters to CECThe Cabinet Secretariat forwarded the letters written to the Cabinet Secretary by election commissioners Sukhbir Sandhu and Vivek Joshi about the alleged misconduct of senior deputy election commissioner (DEC) Maneesh Garg to the office of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, in addition to sending them to the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), according to information obtained through a Right to Information (RTI) application.A document released in response to the application shows that on August 3, the secretariat proposed seeking CEC Kumar's opinion on the letters.Another, on August 4, noted that the letters from the commissioners were in their individual capacity and not a formal communication from the Election Commission of India.The only response to the two commissioners was an acknowledgement that their letters had been received. The acknowledgements dated August 5 were copied to the secretary, department of personnel and training (DoPT), the establishment officer in DoPT, and the principal private secretary to the chief election commissioner.

title: Delhi Police arrest content creator Amir Shokeen over alleged racial jibes against Tripura man
description: Union minister Kiren Rijiju called for strict action, while Tripura DGP GS Rao said a state police team would travel to Delhi to assist the investigation.
content: The Delhi Police on Thursday arrested content creator Amir Shokeen for allegedly using racially derogatory remarks against a man from Tripura in a clip which surfaced on social media.In the 52-second clip, Mohammed Amir alias Amir Shokeen was seen standing holding the man’s hand while throwing racial jibes at him, which were met with laughter by Shokeen’s companions.Deputy commissioner of police (north) Niharika Bhatt said that Shokeen was arrested from north Delhi’s Sadar Bazaar on Thursday evening. . Union minister Kiren Rijiju took to X on Wednesday and promised strict action against Shokeen. “People who tolerate such wicked behaviour in the society are also responsible for the spread of hatred,” he wrote.Also read: In South Delhi, racial abuse didn't come from strangers. It came from my neighboursCreator booked under four provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya SanhitaThe Delhi Police charged Shokeen under sections 192 (malignantly or wantonly do an illegal act that provokes someone), 196 (Promoting or attempting to promote enmity, hatred, or ill-will between different religious, racial, language, regional groups), 352 (Intentionally insulting someone), and 353 (circulating false statements, rumors) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).A senior police officer said that Shokeen already faced at least five criminal cases on charges of causing hurt and molestation and was listed as a repeat offender at Sadar Bazaar police station.Also read: Approach Centre for ‘racial slur’ as hate crime: SC“During interrogation, it was revealed that the video was filmed in Ahmedabad about a month ago. He claimed it’s a scripted video but it has been found to be a lie,” the senior police officer added.Shokeen posted an apology video on Instagram on Tuesday and reiterated the claim that the video was scripted. He has 142,000 followers on Instagram and makes what he claims are “funny videos”.Tripura DGP GS Rao said that a team would head to Delhi to aid the Delhi Police probe.

title: Telangana to host first state-organised defence and aerospace expo, curtain-raiser on Saturday
description: The main event, scheduled from December 7 to 9 will bring together the aerospace, space, defence, and internal security sectors on a single platform.
content: Telangana is set to host Raksha Expo 2026—India’s first defence and aerospace expo organised by a state government—with the curtain-raiser scheduled to be held in Hyderabad on October 24.The main event, scheduled from December 7 to 9 at Bharat Future City, will bring together the aerospace, space, defence, and internal security sectors on a single platform to promote domestic manufacturing, innovation, and investment.“The nature of conflict is changing. Conventional methods of warfare and statecraft now operate alongside drones and new-age missiles. Telangana must be the centre of this revolution. We must be the largest contributors to India’s national and internal security,” Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy said.“Telangana must become the largest contributor to the mission of securing India’s national and internal security. I am confident Telangana will help make India a global defence superpower,” he said.The programThe curtain-raiser is expected to bring together more than 80 leaders from over 70 organisations, including global original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and Indian defence and aerospace companies. Companies represented include Airbus, Boeing, Tata Lockheed Martin, Safran, Rolls-Royce and GE Aerospace, among others.Union defence minister Rajnath Singh has been invited to inaugurate the main expo. The state government has also planned a roadshow in New Delhi on October 29 to build participation ahead of the December summit.The expo will be held as a flagship event alongside the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026. Its programme will include exhibitions, live technology demonstrations, drone shows and a planned air show on December 9.Business-to-business and business-to-government meetings are expected to connect manufacturers, startups, and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with government representatives, security agencies, and international investors. The aim is to enable supplier partnerships, joint ventures, technology transfer, and indigenous co-development.Hyderabad’s existing aerospace and defence ecosystem will be central to the showcase. The city is home to more than 12 Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) laboratories and defence public sector enterprises, as well as private manufacturers such as Tata Advanced Systems, Adani Defence and Bharat Forge. The Telangana Rising 2047 linkThe state’s aerospace network has produced 400 Apache helicopter fuselages. It also serves as the global single source for C-130J Super Hercules empennages— the structure at the rear of an aircraft responsible for aerodynamic stability.The event is also linked to the state’s Telangana Rising 2047 vision, which seeks to position Telangana as a major economic and manufacturing hub and achieve the status of a $1 trillion economy by 2034.“Hyderabad has powered India’s strategic programmes for decades, from missiles and fighter aircraft to satellites and secure communications, and is home to nearly 30 per cent of the country’s defence and aerospace industry,” said chief secretary Sanjay Jaju.The event comes amid a push to strengthen domestic defence manufacturing and reduce vulnerabilities in global supply chains. India’s defence production reached a record ₹1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, while defence exports touched ₹38,424 crore. Telangana’s aerospace exports also rose from ₹15,900 crore in 2023-24 to ₹30,742 crore in 2024-25.

title: Food Department seeks delinking of ration cards from Ayushman Bharat
description: The department highlighted ration cards are not a formal eligibility criterion for the Ayushman Bharat scheme
