content: The Department of Food and Public Distribution has flagged the use of ration cards for identifying families under the Ayushman Bharat health insurance scheme, saying the practice can create operational difficulties and effectively make the document compulsory for beneficiaries.In a letter to the Cabinet Secretary in September, the department highlighted the issue of ration cards being used to establish family identity under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), even though they are not a formal eligibility criterion for the scheme, a government official said.“We have only informed the Cabinet Secretariat that the ration card is not an eligibility criterion,” the official said, adding that the problem arises during implementation at the ground level.The move raises questions about how beneficiaries are identified under a scheme intended to cover the bottom 40% of India’s population. While requiring ration cards can exclude eligible people who do not possess them, removing the linkage could also make it harder to identify poor households covered through ration-card databases, experts argue.The scheme provides health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family a year for hospitalisation. Its original beneficiary base was identified using the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) of 2011, alongside other applicable eligibility categories and state-specific arrangements.The National Health Authority (NHA), which implements the scheme, began integrating the SECC beneficiary database with the National Food Security Act database in 2022 to make it easier to identify eligible families using ration-card numbers. The food department asked states and Union territories in January that year to share ration-card data, along with corresponding Aadhaar details, with the NHA.Ration cards can help establish family composition and verify beneficiary details. However, the food department’s concern is that this operational practice can make the document appear compulsory even for someone who qualifies for Ayushman Bharat but is not eligible for a ration card or has not obtained one.“If somebody in a family is seriously ill and does not have a ration card, they may be asked to get one immediately,” the official said, describing the administrative difficulties this creates for beneficiaries and government technical teams.The problem is not limited to people without ration cards. A significant number of households that possess ration cards remain outside the health insurance scheme, highlighting the gap between food security coverage and health insurance coverage.A chapter titled Government-funded Health Insurance: Does Coverage Mean Care? published in Realising Rights: A Handbook of Welfare in India, highlights this gap in section 10.3, which examines the exclusion of needy households from government-funded health insurance schemes.Based on the National Sample Survey’s Consumer Expenditure Survey for 2022-23, the chapter estimates that more than 60% of priority ration-card holders in rural areas and 70% in urban areas are not covered by government-funded health insurance schemes. Among Antyodaya ration-card holders, the exclusion rates are 72% in rural areas and 80% in urban areas.These figures suggest that possession of a ration card does not automatically translate into health insurance coverage. They also show why ration-card data cannot, by itself, establish eligibility for Ayushman Bharat.Rajendran Narayanan, economics professor at Azim Premji University, said around 67% of Indian households have ration cards, while Ayushman Bharat is intended to cover the bottom 40% of the population.“There are several people who are entitled to ration cards but still don’t have them. ...several others who have ration cards but are still out of PMJAY coverage,” he said.Mandating ration cards for access to PMJAY could exclude poor people who qualify for subsidised foodgrain but have not obtained the document, Narayanan said. However, he cautioned that delinking the two databases could also reduce the scheme’s reach if alternative systems to identify eligible households are not put in place.“While mandating ration cards for PMJAY may not be a good idea because many poor who are eligible for rations don’t have ration cards, delinking ration cards from PMJAY is likely to further decrease the coverage of PMJAY,” he said.The food department’s concern is that the existing arrangement has turned a document used only for administrative convenience into a requirement for accessing healthcare.The official said states were developing their own social registries to establish family-level records, which could offer an alternative means of identifying beneficiaries. Updated census data could also help address gaps in existing databases, the official said.

title: In a first, UN's Loss and Damage Fund sets aside $21.6 million for Nepal for Bhote Koshi disaster
description: It is the first time money has been allocated to or set aside for a country since the fund's creation and marks a pivotal point.
content: For the first time since it was operationalised at COP 28, the United Nations’ (UN) Loss and Damage Fund has provisionally approved $20 million plus $1.6 million in oversight fees for Nepal on Thursday for the damage caused during August’s Bhote Koshi River floods, which killed at least 1,000 people and left over 5,000 missing. The Board for the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) met at an “extraordinary meeting” on Thursday to address a formal climate-emergency funding request from Nepal for $20 million over a four-year period.This accounts for only around 0.7% of the costs estimated to be incurred by Nepal during the disaster. However, it is the first time money has been allocated to or set aside for a country since the fund's creation and marks a pivotal point in developing countries' efforts to access climate finance for disasters.The Loss and Damage Fund was set up to provide financial assistance to developing countries that are especially vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change – helping them cope with unavoidable economic and non-economic lossesExperts said Nepal will still have to formally apply for this funding, and the Board will consider the request at its next meeting in December. This is the maximum amount that can currently be requested for a single project.The funding is expected to cover about 0.7% of the costs of the August Nepal floods, which preliminary estimates suggest could be around US$2.56 billion. The co-chairs received a communication from the Government of Nepal via its senior signatory national focal point on August 31. Within the communication, Nepal requested that the Board “take a special decision to respond rapidly, directly and effectively in accordance with its Governing Instrument”.Applications and contributionsSo far, developing countries have submitted 176 applications to the fund, totalling $2.8 billion, a separate analysis by Carbon Brief shows.As of March 15 this year, the Loss and Damage Fund had received $822.06 million in pledges from 27 countries, with total grant contributions currently standing at $ 629.70 million. The largest contributors include the UAE ($100 million); Germany ($98.4 million); France ($ 53.07 million); the United Kingdom ($ 52.15 million); Spain ($ 44.01 million); and Australia ($ 34.11 million).Harjeet Singh, Global Convenor, Fill the Fund campaign and Founding Director, Satat Sampada Climate Foundation, said Thursday marked a historic day in responding to Nepal.“No country should have to endure a catastrophe and wait seven weeks, through historic letters and relentless pressure, just to unlock the Fund’s first-ever emergency meeting. We must set up a permanent rapid-response system that moves support in days, not months,” he said.Why it is a milestoneFor India and other developing countries facing similar climate-induced disasters, this remains an important milestone in accessing disaster finance, experts said. Anjal Prakash, Professor of Public Policy at FLAME University and an IPCC author, said Nepal’s allocation was an important recognition of the need to pay for climate justice.“However, setting money aside is not the same as delivering it. At just 0.7% of estimated losses, this support exposes the enormous gap between climate impacts and available finance. The priority must now be rapid disbursement, with transparent safeguards that enable rather than delay assistance. We need a permanent emergency window, simpler access procedures and predictable contributions from wealthy countries,” he said, stating recovery support should reach affected families, restore essential services and protect livelihoods without adding to national debt.“Ahead of COP31, the test is delivery- whether this decision becomes a reliable system that responds to vulnerable communities at the speed and scale their losses demand, rather than another symbolic financial commitment,” he added.

title: Banquet halls, farmhouses in Delhi must obtain event-wise liquor permits: Excise dept
description: The move is aimed at streamlining the approval process as establishments prepare for a busy season of weddings and festive gatherings
content: P-10 Permit Required for Liquor ServiceAhead of the upcoming festive and wedding season, the Delhi Excise Department has directed banquet halls and farmhouses hosting weddings, parties and other social functions to obtain a P-10 permit for serving liquor, with a fee of ₹15,000 per event.In a public notice issued on Thursday, the department announced a special registration camp from October 27 to November 16 to facilitate one-time registration of banquet halls and farmhouses on the E-Abkari portal.The move is aimed at streamlining the approval process as establishments prepare for a busy season of weddings and festive gatherings.Also Read:Haryana excise policy: No liquor sub-vend to be allowed in villages with 500 or less peoplePermit Fees and Requirements“It is hereby informed that all banquet halls and farmhouses hosting marriages, parties, events or other social functions in Delhi are required to obtain a P-10 Permit for each event for the service of liquor at the premises. A separate permit shall be obtained for each hall/space where liquor is proposed to be served.The prescribed fee for the P-10 Permit is 15,000 per event in the banquet halls/ farmhouses,” read the public notice.Registration and ComplianceThe department said one-time registration would facilitate instantaneous approval and issuance of P-10 permits for subsequent events. A separate permit will be required for every hall or space where liquor is served.The department underlined that submitting an application alone does not authorise the purchase or service of liquor. Establishments must obtain a valid permit for the concerned event and maintain records of the permit, along with bills or invoices showing that the liquor was purchased from a licensed liquor vend in Delhi.Also Read: Delhi ban, ₹3,000 crore payout: Absolut vodka maker punished in mega casesThe department has advised all banquet hall and farmhouse owners and operators to ensure compliance, warning that violations will invite action under the applicable provisions of the Delhi Excise Act and Rules.

title: 21,900 digital arrest complaints registered till Sept: MHA to SC
description: More than 21,900 complaints of digital arrest fraud involving over ₹647 crore were registered in the first eight months of 2026 from January 1 to August 31, according to a status report filed by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) before the Supreme Court, which took suo motu cognisance of the menace a year ago
content: More than 21,900 complaints of digital arrest fraud involving over ₹647 crore were registered in the first eight months of 2026 from January 1 to August 31, according to a status report filed by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) before the Supreme Court, which took suo motu cognisance of the menace a year ago.The court took suo motu cognisance of the matter on October 17, 2025, after receiving a letter from a Haryana-based senior citizen couple who were cheated of over ₹1 crore by fraudsters posing as Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and Enforcement Directorate (ED) officers. The accused kept the couple under digital arrest through WhatsApp calls and video conferences, using forged Supreme Court orders to intimidate them.At the time, the court was informed of 123,672 complaints involving ₹1,935 crore registered from January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024.In 2025, the complaints came down to 58,239 involving ₹1,211 crore between January 1 and December 31.The latest report, filed on October 7, details measures being taken by law enforcement agencies, banks, telecom companies and social media platforms to curb the fraud, recover victims’ money and prevent further losses.Reporting and recoveryA Grievance Redressal Portal (GRP), launched by the home ministry in February, became fully operational across the country in April 2026. As of September 30, it covered 109 banks and 1.28 lakh branches across states and Union territories.The task of giving publicity to the GRP has been entrusted by the court to all states, UTs, state legal services committees, and high courts. The latest status report indicates that out of 93,041 grievances received on the portal in relation to cybercrimes and cyber frauds, the concerned law enforcement agencies have acted upon 60,638 grievances.On August 4, the top court had directed that similar to I4C, there should be a State Cybercrime Coordination Centre (S4C) for better coordination and expeditious action on complaints. Except for Jharkhand, all states have established S4C, the status report stated. An online zero FIR mechanism for cybercrime complaints is also being rolled out, with Himachal Pradesh, Lakshadweep, Manipur and Nagaland yet to operationalise it.Under the e-Zero FIR, the number of complaints have seen a sharp rise from 2% to 8% across all states and UTs.A Money Restoration Portal (MRP), launched in April, has facilitated refunds to victims, the report said. Of more than six lakh refund or restoration requests, law enforcement agencies issued 4.69 lakh orders, resulting in the restoration of ₹332.7 crore, of which ₹112.96 crore were restored by the banks to the victims.Banking safeguardsThe Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is seeking to amend its existing instructions on ‘Operations of Bank Accounts and Money Mules’ under which the banks are mandated to undertake due diligence measures and monitor the transactions meticulously to identify accounts which are operated as ‘money mules” and take action as per a draft SOP being prepared by RBI.To operationalise the draft RBI SOP, its integration is necessary with the GRP and MRP. The tentative timeline for its operationalisation is December 2026, subject to completion of the requisite technical development, integration, testing and implementation processes, the report submitted in court stated.The RBI had informed the I4C and the inter-departmental committee (IDC) examining the issue of digital arrests that enhanced measures are being examined to prevent such frauds from taking place. It is in discussion over implementing the delayed transaction safeguard or the lagged credit mechanism as a means to protect customers from losing their money.While some banks have supported the initiative, others have adopted a view that it may inconvenience customers and its effectiveness may diminish over time given the evolving nature of frauds. The overall cost-benefits analysis of implementing the proposal is being examined.The RBI issued the ‘Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’ on June 24 which extends a compensation mechanism for small value fraudulent electronic banking transactions (EBT) and shortens the complaint resolution timeline. The instructions, that will take effect from January 1, 2027 shorten the complaint resolution timeline from 90 days to 45 days in case of domestic fraudulent EBTs and 60 days for cross-border fraudulent EBTs.A genuine individual victim lodging a complaint regarding fraudulent EBT involving gross loss up to ₹50,000 can receive a compensation of 85% of the net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is less, only once during the victim’s lifetime. To qualify for such compensation, the fraud must be reported to the bank and NCRP or the helpline 1930 within five calendar days of occurrence of fraud.Some banks have also implemented additional technological interventions which include UPI payee or keyword blocking; disabling mobile banking while a call is active; WhatsApp-based dispute mechanisms; in-app fraud reporting with immediate debit freeze; and enhanced due diligence workflows for flagged beneficiary accounts.Other measures which are underway include real-time branch alerts for suspected digital arrest situations, behavioural biometrics and common customer risk scoring, and enhanced real-time monitoring of suspected beneficiary accounts.Investigation and preventionThe Supreme Court has directed the CBI to investigate digital arrest cases involving fraud of ₹10 crore or more. Since December 1, 2025, the agency has arrested more than 49 people and filed charge sheets against over 140, the report said.The top court had on August 4 asked the Centre to consider a suggestion made by amicus curiae and senior advocate NS Nappinai for introducing a mechanism such as “kill switch” which is a mechanism for automatic disconnecting long duration audio/video calls.The latest report submitted in court states that a similar facility has already been implemented by all major telecom service providers and the duration of the call ranges up to 180 minutes at maximum.Since digital arrest cases involve video calls of long duration with the victims, the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) held a meeting last month with Meta and Telegram to discuss the technical feasibility of introducing kill switch. WhatsApp and Telegram raised practical concerns on its implementation even as it supported the need to have a graded approach.The court will take up the matter on October 29. The inter-departmental committee examining digital arrest fraud is also preparing a proposal on victim compensation and shared liability.EOM

title: Sonia joins Instagram, shares first look of her upcoming memoir
description: Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi joined Instagram on Wednesday, sharing the first look of her forthcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love
content: Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi joined Instagram on Wednesday, sharing the first look of her forthcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.The 79-year-old Congress leader’s debut on the platform marks her entry into a social media space widely used by young people, particularly Gen Z. Instagram has increasingly become a communication channel for Indian politicians, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.In her first post, Sonia Gandhi, who served as Congress president for nearly two decades across two terms, described the memoir as a story of “love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong” and said she looked forward to sharing it with readers. “Hello everyone, I’m truly grateful to share this moment with you all; the first look of Belonging: A Journey of Love. It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” she said in the post.Sonia Gandhi’s entry comes ahead of the memoir’s worldwide release on November 10 by Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of Penguin Random House.The memoir traces her journey from childhood in post-war Italy to her life in India, including her romance with Rajiv Gandhi during their time at Cambridge and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband.The book drew attention over a reported disagreement between Sonia Gandhi and Penguin Random House India (PRHI) concerning its contents.HT had earlier reported that the proposed publishing arrangement with PRHI fell through after Sonia Gandhi refused to alter or remove references to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Chinese intrusions.A person familiar with the matter said Sonia Gandhi maintained that the memoir was her story and that she would not allow distortions to her account of her life.PRHI issued a statement following media reports that it had withdrawn from publishing the memoir in India. Later, HarperCollins finalised an agreement to publish and distribute the Indian edition.Her son, Rahul Gandhi, recently expressed pride in her decision to share her story. On the birth anniversary of Rajiv Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha said he was happy that millions of people would be able to read his mother’s account.“I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story,” he said, adding that he imagined his father looking down proudly at Sonia.

title: YS Jagan Mohan Reddy refuses to allow niece’s wedding on family property citing security concerns
description: In the letter, the YSRCP chief cited security and privacy risks from guests, event staff and the circulation of photographs, suggesting alternative venues.
content: Hyderabad: Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP) chief YS Jagan Mohan Reddy has refused to allow his niece’s wedding at the family compound, Yelahanka Palace, in Bengaluru in November amid a property dispute with his sister YS Sharmila, people aware of the matter said.Sharmila’s daughter, YS Anjili Reddy, got engaged to Somala Raghurami Reddy, who lives in the United States, on September 24. People aware of the matter said Sharmila, the Andhra Pradesh Congress chief, wanted to hold their wedding on November 25 at Yelahanka Palace.An aide to Sharmila said Jagan Mohan Reddy conveyed to her through their mother, YS Vijayamma, that he would not allow the wedding at Yelahanka Palace.“This has come as a big shock to Sharmila, as she had distributed wedding invitations to relatives, political leaders and prominent personalities. Now, she is compelled to look for an alternative venue for the wedding,” the aide said.The aide quoted Jagan as telling Vijayamma that the property was registered in the name of his mother-in-law, his wife Bharati Reddy’s mother. “Vijayamma tried to persuade him to reconsider his position, but he was firm on his stand,” the aide added.Jagan Mohan Reddy subsequently explained his position in a letter dated October 9, 2026, which the YSRCP disclosed and HT has seen. He cited security and privacy concerns arising from the movement of a large number of people and the possibility of photographs and videos of the premises being circulated.In his letter, Jagan said hosting a wedding of this scale would involve several service providers, including catering staff, decorators, event managers, videographers and photographers, besides guests entering and leaving the premises.“Most of these people will be unfamiliar to the family and that the circulation of photographs and videos of the property and surrounding areas could pose serious security risks,” he wrote.Jagan said the decision had not been easy, as he had seen Anjili, whom he referred to as Jili, grow up in the bungalow and wanted the best for her. However, he said the security and privacy concerns could not be ignored.“I would have done the same, even if it were for Harsha or Varsha (Jagan’s daughters),” he said, adding that the event would attract considerable and unnecessary attention because he currently lived at the property.“I was hurt that, despite me communicating the very real privacy and security risks through various people, you still went ahead, ignoring my disapproval and concerns,” he wrote.Jagan urged Sharmila to choose another venue, suggesting a convention centre or a destination wedding, as had been done for her son Raja’s wedding. He also offered his Lotus Pond property in Hyderabad as an alternative. “The offer remains open,” he said, adding that he wanted Anjili’s wedding to be a memorable occasion.Sharmila’s aide said, “She has already sent invitations to senior Congress leaders, besides Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar, Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy and former Tamil Nadu chief minister M K Stalin. She would now have to find another venue that could accommodate the security and logistical requirements associated with their attendance.”Jagan Mohan Reddy and Sharmila have been involved in a dispute over family properties, including shares in Saraswati Power and Industries Ltd, for the last five years. The issue is pending adjudication before the National Company Law Tribunal.People close to Sharmila said their late father, former Andhra Pradesh chief minister YS Rajasekhara Reddy, wanted his son and daughter to receive equal shares in the family’s properties. He arranged separate residences for them in Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Idupulapaya.In Hyderabad’s Lotus Pond locality, their residences are next to each other, and Sharmila continues to live in hers. Separate houses were also reportedly constructed for the siblings at Idupulapaya, their native place.In Bengaluru’s Yelahanka, the family reportedly has two houses built next to each other across approximately 20 acres. “However, Sharmila’s house was not registered in her name. Rajasekhara Reddy used to stay there during his visits to Bengaluru, while Jagan has been living at the palace during his weekly visits,” her aide said.Rajasekhara Reddy’s death in a helicopter crash on September 2, 2009, left the division of the family’s assets unresolved, leading to disputes between the siblings.Sharmila played a key role in the YSRCP and undertook a foot march when Jagan was in jail between 2012 and 2013. She campaigned for the party before the 2019 elections.Their relationship reportedly deteriorated after Jagan became chief minister in 2019, with disagreements over family assets straining ties. Sharmila later floated a party in Telangana before joining the Congress in 2024 and becoming its Andhra Pradesh chief. She has since been attacking her brother politically.

title: Procedures to be followed if fresh impeachment motion against CEC filed: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla
description: The Opposition has been leading protests against Kumar and has met President Droupadi Murmu, demanding his removal and the repeal of a 2023 law.
content: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Thursday said any fresh impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar would be examined as per the laid-down procedures, amid Opposition protests demanding his removal over alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“We will follow the process when the motion is moved. Just as there is a procedure for the impeachment of judges, there is a process laid down for the CEC too… It will be followed if the opposition moves a motion,” Birla said at a press conference ahead of the 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum, which India is hosting. Opposition's demands and campaignThe Opposition has been leading protests against Kumar and has met President Droupadi Murmu, demanding his removal and the repeal of the 2023 law that provides immunity to the CEC and Election Commissioners. It has accused the CEC of the “unilateral and arbitrary exercise of the collective powers” during the ongoing revision of electoral rolls.Under the law, the CEC can be removed by Parliament through a process similar to the impeachment of a Supreme Court judge. The CEC or an Election Commissioner may also resign by submitting a written resignation to the President.On the petitions seeking the disqualification of rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), Birla said the matter was being examined. “The petitions are being heard in the (Supreme) Court and they are also being heard in my court… Both sides are being heard and the proceedings are underway. As soon as we receive their response, we will expedite the process,” he said.Also Read I Slapped with defamation notice by top cop in Bihar, RJD MP seeks Speaker Om Birla's interventionA TMC faction led by its national general secretary, Abhishek Banerjee, had petitioned Birla seeking the immediate disqualification of the rebel lawmakers, arguing that their merger amounted to “voluntarily giving up party membership”.Birla also expressed hope that the two-day Brics Parliamentary Forum, beginning October 26, would adopt a joint declaration by consensus and discuss issues of global concern, including terrorism and climate change.“I hope there will be a detailed discussion on this issue within BRICS as well,” he said.

title: Cong is fine when it wins, blames BJP and EC when it loses: Bhupender Yadav
description: Union minister and senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader Bhupender Yadav on Thursday said the Opposition’s intent in raising questions about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is not to correct irregularities in the poll process, but largely to destabilise Indian democracy
content: Union minister and senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader Bhupender Yadav on Thursday said the Opposition’s intent in raising questions about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is not to correct irregularities in the poll process, but largely to destabilise Indian democracy.In an interview to HT, he said the Opposition’s bid was to discredit constitutional bodies, and discussed why the Mamata Banerjee government was ousted from West Bengal after 15 years in power. Edited excerpts:What is the government’s response to the Opposition’s serious charges of irregularities against the election commission over the conduct of SIR ? The Opposition is frustrated with repeated losses in state after state. The Congress doesn’t believe in EVMs (electronic voting machines), which were introduced by them. They don’t believe in Parliament, in the Supreme Court when the verdict is not to their liking. They don’t believe in EC if the poll result is not to their liking.But the Congress has still not been able to invalidate the process of SIR.It won in Kerala, and supported the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) that won in Tamil Nadu. It has not explained how, if the SIR is so wrong, did the party win the elections. If the SIR was flawed, then why accept the result and the victory? They accept victories, but blame EC and the BJP for defeats.They have made several allegations of irregularities against the CEC over how SIR is being done?They filed a case in the Supreme Court. The judgment clearly upheld and validated the proceedings of SIR, which is not being held for the first time. Between 1951 and 2004, it was conducted eight times and the current cycle which started in 2025 is the ninth. Of these eight-and-a-half cycles have been conducted during their tenure. Under Rule 25(2) of Registration of Electors Rules, during SIR, the electoral roll is to be prepared afresh for the correction of electoral rolls and the purpose is to update the voter list.The Congress’s aim is to shoot and scoot. EC asked them to submit a signed affidavit with the complaints so that the cases could be investigated. Rahul Gandhi or their BLAs (block level agents) never signed any affidavit. The President of India asked them to submit proof. They are yet to do that.The dynasts in the Congress believe they have a right to rule. Since they are unable to win fair and square, they want to discredit institutions and push people to take to the streets for a regime change. Indian democracy is far too strong and people are way too mature to fall for these gimmicks.You were the election-in-charge in West Bengal, where the BJP swept to power with a huge mandate for the first time. Almost 2.2 million people were disenfranchised in the state and filed petitions. Opposition leaders alleged that the exercise was rushed and opaque and targeted minorities and the marginalised.It was the so-called INDI alliance that asked for SIR, alleging voter rolls had issues. EC acted promptly and ordered SIR. In some states they won; in most states we won. They couldn’t digest this and started alleging foul play. It all started with blaming EVMs. In West Bengal, SIR was conducted by EC and monitored by the Supreme Court. And it was the TMC that won the 13 seats where the maximum number of voters were deleted.Mamata Banerjee lost because of a huge anti-incumbency wave and people had faith in the leadership of PM Narendra Modi ji to provide good governance.What about the voters who were barred from voting after EC marked them for discrepancies?During SIR, EC first publishes a draft roll. It is bound to issue a notice to anyone whose name is deleted. The reasons for deletion are death, migration, duplication, or wrong information. The appeals of those who were excluded are pending before the appellate tribunal created by SC. If people come forward to give their documents, I am sure EC will take corrective measures.Economist Surjit Bhalla in an analysis of SIR in Bengal said the 2004 electoral rolls had 28 million more names than the estimated adult population, an excess of 4.4% and in 2014, the roll was 3.1% higher than the adult population. We did not allege any electoral fraud, or question EC.The TMC appointed BLAs in every booth and government machinery was there, but where is their complaint? You participated in the exercise, used the state machinery in your favour, used muscle power and even then when you failed, you are blaming the Election Commission and SIR.It is not correct that only the minorities were left out; many Hindus who should have been protected by the provisions of the Citizenship Amendment Act were also excluded due to Mamata Banerji’s negligence.The BJP believes every eligible citizen should be able to vote. EC is mandated to ensure every eligible citizen has the right to vote and to ensure the removal of those who aren’t. Our institutions must be empowered to discharge their duties, not discredited because someone did not get a poll result they desired.What were the key factors for the TMC’s loss?Mamata Banerjee lost the election because of arrogance, anti-incumbency, social unrest, and the politics of appeasement. If you fail in the eyes of the public because of your misgovernance, you cannot pin the blame on concocted reasons, especially those that imperil your Constitutional institutions.The post-election scenario was intriguing. How did the 20 lawmakers reach out to the BJP and what were their concerns?Mamata Banerjee lost the confidence of Bengal’s voters and her own party. The anti-incumbency was both within and outside of the party. She came to power in Bengal against the authoritarian rule of the Left. Over time, she became an authoritarian CM. People felt suffocated and so did the people in her party.Adding to that the fact the TMC was not a party rooted in ideology, Mamata gave preference to family over senior party members. There was always disgruntlement in the party.There is another set of assembly elections coming up. In Uttar Pradesh, which is crucial for the BJP, the Opposition’s main planks are vote chori, chanda chori in Ayodhya and anti-incumbency.The BJP is working hard on the ground, the organisational activities as decided by the national president, Nitin Nabin, are underway. The improved law and order situation in the state, the credibility of chief minister Yogi Adityanath and the leadership of PM Modi are there for all to see. There is no impact of the Opposition’s attempts to create any narrative. What matters is how in the last 12 years governance has become the main poll plank.Look at states such as Telangana where the Congress and Chhattisgarh where the JMM also announced social welfare schemes but corruption hampered delivery. The NDA, on the other hand, has been successful in the delivery of pro-poor schemes.In the past 12 years, the BJP-led NDA government announced and successfully implemented pro-poor policies. In the second term, major reforms through legislative action such as the GST rollout, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, Direct Benefit Transfer happened. In the third term there is a more proactive push for reforms, the PM has called it the “reform express”. So, this is the core of Indian politics now. The issues raised by the Opposition are just to discredit constitutional bodies, which are highly respected worldwide.

title: Two DNA tests confirm sexual assault by 4 in Delhi's Swaroop Nagar gangrape case
description: Delhi Police said that the body of the girl was highly decomposed and these scientific tests were essential to link the victim to the accused.
content: Delhi Police conducted two rare tests of forensic DNA profiling to establish the alleged involvement of four accused in the gang-rape and murder of a 16-year-old girl in outer Delhi’s Swaroop Nagar, with a Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL) report confirming the presence of “human semen” and “a mixed male DNA profile corresponding to four males on swabs collected from the victim”, officers aware of the findings said on Thursday.Police said that the body of the girl was highly decomposed and these scientific tests were essential to link the victim to the accused.“They are essential when the DNA is possibly contaminated and when there is a possibility of multiple DNAs. Hence, the exhibits were sent to Central FSL in Chandigarh,” the officer said.Also Read | 3-star tattoo, sustained CCTV scanning help police solve Delhi gangrape-murder caseA police officer aware of the matter said that the report found that the Y-chromosome short tandem repeat (Y-STR) profiles of all the four accused strongly matched the mixed male DNA profile recovered from the victim’s swabs, corroborating the allegations of sexual assault, a police officer said.“The CFSL report has been received. It confirms the presence of human semen on the victim’s swabs and a mixed DNA profile corresponding to four different males. The Y-STR profiles of all the accused show a strong match with the male DNA recovered from the victim. The findings support the investigation and corroborate the involvement of the accused,” the officer said.How Y-STR analysis worksA FSL official explained that Y-STR analysis examines genetic markers on the Y chromosome, which is passed down the paternal line.The technique is particularly useful in sexual assault investigations where samples contain a mixture of DNA from a female victim and multiple male contributors.“It helps investigators identify and compare male DNA profiles, although it may not distinguish between men belonging to the same paternal lineage. The four males in this case were not related,” the official said.Also Read | Woman can face gang rape charge without personally committing the act, says Delhi HCInvestigation and chargesheetDelhi Police submitted a 365-page chargesheet in the case on October 12, which details the investigation into the alleged sexual assault and murder. The chargesheet includes statements from 54 witnesses and mentions a gait analysis conducted on the accused, officers said earlier.Gait analysis involves studying a person’s walking or running pattern, usually through video recordings, to assess whether their movements correspond with those captured in surveillance footage. The technique can help investigators examine whether a suspect’s physical movements are consistent with those of a person seen at a crime scene.The incident took place on September 11, and the girl’s highly decomposed body was found in a field in Khadda Colony, Swaroop Nagar, on September 13. Four teenagers, three of them minors, were apprehended in connection with the case.Also Read | Fake cop behind Delhi teen’s rape near Kalkaji Mandir arrested after encounterAccording to the chargesheet, the accused allegedly raped the girl, stabbed her multiple times and dumped her body after deciding to kill her because she had threatened to report the sexual assault to the police.The investigation initially faced difficulties because the body was severely mutilated, with the skull and rib cage exposed and the right arm severed. Investigators were initially unable to establish the deceased’s gender.A breakthrough came when an assistant sub-inspector noticed a tattoo of three stars in a row on the victim’s left arm. While one team checked missing-person records, another collected CCTV footage from the surrounding area.Investigators eventually traced footage from around 3.30am on September 11 showing a delivery tempo approaching the spot, switching off its headlights for around 15 minutes and then moving away. A distinctive design on the vehicle helped police trace it to its owner and identify the alleged driver, who subsequently disclosed the identities of his associates, according to the chargesheet.The chargesheet also includes the postmortem report, which police said confirmed forceful penetration and multiple stab injuries.

title: India, Poland pledge to deepen ties in defence, nuclear energy
description: New Delhi India and Poland on Thursday agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk focused on leveraging the economic growth of both countries to achieve the shared target of doubling trade from the current level of $6 billion by 2030
content: New Delhi India and Poland on Thursday agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk focused on leveraging the economic growth of both countries to achieve the shared target of doubling trade from the current level of $6 billion by 2030.Bilateral ties got a major boost with Modi’s visit to Warsaw in 2024, the first by an Indian PM in 45 years, and defence and security have emerged as a key area for cooperation as Poland is currently engaged in the largest military modernisation campaign in Europe by spending almost 5% of its GDP on its armed forces against the backdrop of the war in Ukraine.Modi described his discussions with Tusk as “excellent” and said on social media the two leaders discussed bolstering cooperation in trade, investment, defence, nuclear energy, space and critical minerals. Regional and global issues also figured in the talks, and Indian officials said the Polish side appreciated India’s recent proposal for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire.“Today, we agreed to deepen our cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to partner with India in co-development and co-production,” Modi said at a media interaction with Tusk.Tusk added, “We are very aware of political threats and the need to become independent as much as possible in the area of…minerals and strategic resources…to make sure that Poland and India are independent in those areas.”India and Poland, Modi said, have emerged as centres of growth and technology at a time of uncertainty and change. “Last year, Poland’s GDP crossed the historic milestone of $1 trillion…Meanwhile, India recorded an impressive growth rate of 7.8% in the last quarter,” he said, noting that the proposed India-European Union (EU) trade deal will open new opportunities for India to export machinery, chemicals, plastics and engineering goods to Poland.“At the same time, we will seek new investments from Poland in sectors such as railways and mobility, advanced manufacturing, food processing and biotechnology,” Modi said, adding that Tusk is accompanied by a large business delegation that will focus on developing trusted supply chains to achieve the shared goal of doubling trade by 2030.The two sides will also develop new partnerships in critical minerals and coal gasification using Polish expertise, and establish a bilateral “startup bridge” to build on cooperation in AI, cybersecurity and fintech, Modi said.The business delegation of almost 100 Polish companies will participate in two business forums in New Delhi and Bengaluru to explore collaboration in defence, agri-tech, food processing, pharmaceuticals, mining, technology and infrastructure. Two-way trade is currently worth $6.3 billion, and Indian investments in Poland have grown to $3 billion, with Indian IT companies having a significant presence.Tusk noted the two countries were able to build synergy as they have no conflicts of interest or historical issues that divide them. He also lauded Modi’s role on the global stage, describing it as a “beacon of hope” at a time of destabilisation and political uncertainty.He pointed to growing defence cooperation between the two sides and said: “Our drones were very useful…recently and I am convinced that cooperation in satellites and drones has helped our countries in times of political tensions and crises.”Tusk’s comments were an apparent reference to the use of Polish loitering munitions or drones by India’s military against Pakistan during Operation Sindoor, last year’s campaign that targeted terrorist infrastructure on Pakistani soil in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack. Poland’s WB Group supplied 100 units of Warmate loitering munitions to the Indian Army in 2022, and Polish officials said earlier this year that the army had signed three more defence contracts.Poland is also eyeing tie-ups with Indian manufacturers of munitions to replenish ammunition stocks depleted by supplies provided to Ukraine since the start of the Russian invasion in 2022. However, some Polish firms have concerns about India’s long-standing military ties with Russia, and New Delhi and Warsaw are finalising an agreement on secure information exchanges to boost defence industrial cooperation.Sibi George, secretary (West) in the external affairs ministry, told a media briefing the two sides are working on an agreement on mutual protection and exchange of classified information that is expected to build on the growing trust between India and the EU in areas such as defence and technology. With both countries eyeing joint development and production of military gear, it is important to have agreements to put in place trust and confidentiality, he said.The two sides also agreed to establish a defence industry dialogue and a counter-terrorism dialogue, George said. The security and defence partnership concluded by India and the EU earlier this year provides an additional framework for strategic cooperation with Poland in defence, counter-terrorism, technology, cybersecurity, space and shipbuilding, he said.Modi also referred to his discussions with Tusk on regional and global issues and said: “Whether in Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace.”George said Poland was “very appreciative” of India’s approach for a diplomatic solution to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and Modi’s recent call to Russian President Vladimir Putin to move from “endless war to the end of war”. He added that India has shared ideas with Russia and Ukraine, including the safety and security of commercial shipping, exports of grains and energy, and “non-attack possibilities”.Modi and Tusk both highlighted people-to-people ties, including the role played by the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur in providing refuge to thousands of Polish children and families during World War II, and the assistance provided by Polish authorities in evacuating thousands of Indian students from Ukraine in 2022. Poland is currently home to around 30,000 Indians, including 3,500 students.

title: India-US trade deal in ‘last stage’, says EAM Jaishankar: ‘It’s never done until it’s done’
description: The trade deal figured in Jaishankar’s meeting with Rubio this week after the secretary of state visited India for the second time in less than five months.
content: The India-US trade agreement is in its “last mile” but “it’s never done till it’s done”, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Thursday about efforts by the two countries to find common ground on the deal they have negotiated for more than a year.US secretary of state Marco Rubio and commerce minister Piyush Goyal too have spoken of the two sides moving towards the final stages of the trade deal, he said at a session at the NDTV World Summit.“But…often the last mile or the penultimate miles do pose their challenges. I think the [negotiating] teams are working through them now,” Jaishankar said. “If you’re asking me to tell you what exactly those challenges are, I’m sorry I won’t. That’s for the negotiators to sort out.”Also Read I US ‘very close’ to India trade deal; energy needs considered in Russia sanctions waiver: Marco RubioS Jaishankar addresses India-US tiesThe trade deal figured in Jaishankar’s meeting with Rubio in Mumbai this week after the secretary of state visited India for the second time in less than five months. Bilateral ties have been hit by the Trump administration’s unpredictable trade policies, immigration restrictions that have impacted Indian professionals and growing ties between Washington and the Pakistani military leadership.Jaishankar said he failed to understand criticism by opposition parties of his visit to Mumbai to meet Rubio, which Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had described as a “summoning”.“They have something against Mumbai. It’s our financial capital, it’s our Bollywood capital. It has got so much going for it. Maybe Mumbai doesn’t like them, I have no idea why they have this reservation,” the minister said. Jaishankar listed examples of Indian leaders travelling out of New Delhi to meet foreign dignitaries, including two instances involving Congress leaders – former PM Indira Gandhi met Pakistani leader Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in Shimla in 1972 to sign the Simla Agreement, and Union minister Salman Khurshid hosted a lunch for then Pakistan PM Raja Pervez Ashraf in Jaipur in 2013.“We are adults, let’s have an adult conversation,” he said, taking a swipe at Rahul Gandhi.On Pakistan and terrorismJaishankar also spoke on the issue of Pakistan-backed terrorism and said India does not want to wait for the US and other countries to understand its concerns on terror. He emphasised that the world takes note only when a country responds to terrorism, and India has done so through Operation Sindoor and the Balakot air strikes.While India desires good relations with Pakistan, it is unwilling to overlook terrorism to achieve this, he said. He responded to a question on Pakistan’s military leadership wooing the Trump administration in the US and the perception that Washington hasn’t fully understood New Delhi’s concerns on cross-border terror by saying the issue is much broader.“If Washington understood it so well, why didn’t we act in 2008, when 26/11 happened? And when we did act, we didn’t act because Washington understood it, we acted because we understood it,” he said. “First of all, forget about somebody else getting terrorism right. Get it right yourself. If you don’t have the clarity of thought, the conviction to fight back against terrorism, don’t think somebody else is going to do that job for you.”Also Read I ‘India diversified imports, but hard to pivot in one day’: Marco Rubio explains why US waived some Russia energy tariffsIndia’s counter-terror policy has evolved and this was evident in the response to cross-border terror with last year’s Operation Sindoor, the Balakot air strikes in 2019, and the surgical strikes across the Line of Control in 2016.“The evolution is that if terrorism goes on, it will not be business as usual. It is not, you will take a break and then say, ‘Okay, now it has been a long time. Let me get back to talking to them again’, which is what the pattern was,” he said.“The 26/11 attacks should serve as a reminder of the enormity of what is being done to us and the necessity for us to respond. And when you respond, the world will take note. When you don’t respond, the world will play games.”When Jaishankar was asked if India, which has made it clear that terrorism and talks cannot go together, still wishes to have better relations with Pakistan, he said the reality was Islamabad was using terrorism as state policy.“Of course we want good relations with Pakistan, we want that with all our neighbours but will I overlook terror for that? I will not. The government is very clear,” he said. “The national mood on Pakistan changed after 26/11. Till then, there were people who would keep making these arguments. After 26/11, only the government of the day made the argument.”United Nations and protestsJaishankar responded to another question on whether the UN has “double standards” on protests in different countries by saying that the answer is “pretty obvious”.The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and UN human rights experts have expressed concern over the government’s handling of protests associated with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and other groups.“That is a bigger issue because you get into what the UN is, what positions they take, and so forth. Let’s be straightforward about it, I am making this assessment and observation about what is happening across multiple countries and societies. This is not a comment specific to India, the Indian subcontinent or France,” Jaishankar said.“We have seen that in many cases, when these moments occur, there is external encouragement and external support. There is a set of actors who see this as a tool of influence to advance their agenda. It is not a secret – even those who do it openly admit to it, they are not hiding it,” he said.Also Read I 'Very close, some items left': Marco Rubio optimistic about India-US trade dealJaishankar also spoke about his choice of streaming shows based on diplomacy and how closely they reflect realities. He said he watches The Diplomat on Netflix but noted that the series presents diplomacy in a distinctly American way.“I’m watching The Diplomat but I want to say one thing. No value judgement here but The Diplomat is very quintessentially American. Even then, when you make these shows, you make them because you want to dramatise things,” he said. “If I made a real show about how diplomacy works, people would go to sleep.”Jaishankar added, “I look at it with a somewhat critical eye. I relate to some of it. I looked at the ambassador having reflux and told myself, ‘Okay, that problem I know.’ So the point is, I travel, I read, I do everything which you guys do. But it’s always a bit of a busman’s holiday. When you look at some of these things that are in your line of work, you can’t disconnect from that line of work.”.”

title: Defence PSU showcases India-made munitions at Prague show amid scrutiny after official's arrest
description: A CBI probe and arrests in the alleged corruption case linked to a ₹500-crore ammunition contract have cast a shadow over Munitions India Ltd (MIL).
content: Munitions India Ltd (MIL) is showcasing indigenous military products at a leading trade show in Prague, Czech Republic, to attract foreign buyers and boost exports, officials aware of the matter said on Friday. This comes even as the recent arrest of a senior executive in an alleged bribery case has put the state-owned company's internal oversight and accountability under scrutiny.The Pune-headquartered defence PSU manufactures a wide range of ammunition, including tank rounds, bombs and rockets.MIL, Yantra India Ltd and Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) are among the Indian companies showcasing defence and security technologies at the Future Forces Exhibition and Forum in Prague from October 21-23, the officials said.The probeA Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe and arrests in the alleged corruption case linked to a ₹500-crore ammunition contract have cast a shadow over MIL, one of the country’s best-performing ordnance units, which has also strengthened its presence in overseas markets. MIL executive director Anil Kumar, his brother B Harshavardhan and private defence firm SMPP Ltd CEO Ashish Kansal were arrested on October 14.MIL is set to face a clean-up and a renewed push for accountability following the corruption allegations, HT reported last week. The Department of Defence Production is closely tracking the case.The case may have raised reputational concerns for the company, but allegations against one executive do not establish corporate wrongdoing, the officials said, asking not to be named.Private defence firm may face actionSMPP Ltd could face suspension or be debarred from government contracts under the country’s defence procurement rules. However, its name was missing from the defence ministry’s latest list of firms debarred from government business or suspended for corruption and unfair practices in securing military contracts.Issued on October 19, five days after the CBI made the arrests, the list names 22 firms—none new. The list is periodically reviewed, leaving SMPP Ltd in line for a possible listing in the next update, the officials said. It manufactures ammunition, loitering munitions, bullet-proof jackets and helmets.Rules allow the government to suspend business dealings with any entity pending a full inquiry into corruption allegations. It can also suspend business dealings with a firm the moment it refers any complaint against it to the CBI or any other investigating agency, or when it receives intimation regarding the initiation of a criminal investigation against that firm. The suspension period ordinarily does not exceed one year. But in exceptional cases involving national security, the government may order a longer ban.MIL posted highest profitAccording to official data, MIL posted a profit after tax of ₹1,250 crore in 2025-26, the highest among the seven defence companies carved out of the erstwhile Ordnance Factory Board (OFB) five years ago. The seven firms, including Yantra India Ltd, Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Ltd, Troop Comforts Ltd, India Optel Ltd, Armoured Vehicles Nigam Ltd and Gliders India Ltd, together posted a profit of ₹2,801 crore.MIL’s exports stood at around ₹4,000 crore last year. Boosting defence exports is a key government priority. India has set a target of achieving ₹50,000 crore in defence exports by 2029-30.The PSU reported record revenue of ₹10,954 crore in 2025-26, up 33% from the previous year. Its order book was the largest at ₹42,864 crore, while the remaining six firms together accounted for ₹57,111 crore as of April 1, 2026, according to the data.

title: PM Modi says United Nation's limitations 'clearly visible' amid changing world order
description: PM Modi called for stronger institutions, a greater voice for the Global South and international cooperation.
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has described the current global situation as a "world between orders," saying the limitations of the United Nations and the global institutions are increasingly visible in the face of today’s complex challenges.Addressing the NDTV World Summit on Thursday evening, the Prime Minister called for stronger institutions, a greater voice for the Global South and international cooperation, stressing that global decision-making must evolve with changing realities.Describing the current global situation as a "world between orders," PM Modi said, "We have to understand two things: First, why is the world's order changing, and why is the old global order unable to provide solutions to today's challenges? And second, what is India's role in this changing world"."The Second World War taught the world a big lesson," he added.Modi further highlighted that the UN was founded on the principles of dialogue, cooperation and peaceful dispute resolution but noted that changing global realities and increasingly complex challenges have tested the existing world order.ALSO READ: PM Modi says Congress tarnishes India's image abroad: 'They seek intervention in internal affairs'United Nations' limits 'clearly visible'"The world understood that world systems cannot run solely on the basis of power and interests. Dialogue is necessary, cooperation is necessary, and the resolution of disputes is also necessary. This sentiment laid the foundation of the United Nations (UN). For decades, the UN played its role in promoting global cooperation and peace. But with time, the world kept changing. New aspirations emerged, new economies and new powers arose. The challenges before the world became much more complex than before," he said at the NDTV's event."The United Nations and other global institutions have had their historical role, but in the face of today's challenges, their limits are clearly visible. Now new powers are emerging, new voices are demanding their place, and new challenges are demanding new solutions," Modi further remarked."The changing world order calls for stronger global institutions, a greater voice for the Global South and international cooperation that stands firm in times of crisis," he said, highlighting the need to reform global governance.‘Trade, technology, sea routes being weaponised’PM Modi also noted that trade, technology, and sea routes, in particular, are "being weaponised", in a reference apparently to the ongoing US-Iran war in West Asia and other such conflicts.He referenced ancient Indian economist Chanakya, too, citing his Sanskrit mantra 'apranitah tu matsyanyayam udbhavayati', which translates to 'when the law of punishment is kept in abeyance, it gives rise to Matsya Nyaya (law of the sea)', meaning the strong shall swallow the weak.Jaishankar had earlier called UN ‘gridlocked’Earlier this month, external affairs minister S Jaishankar had also criticised the functioning of the UN.ALSO READ: Movements seeking improvements necessary in democracy, but Congress destroys even them: PM ModiHe had said the United Nations needs urgent reform, arguing that the global body has increasingly failed to play a meaningful role in decisions on major international crises, including conflicts in Ukraine and the Gulf. Jaishankar made the remarks while responding to a question during an interactive session at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in Delhi, news agency PTI reported.He was asked about the future of the UN and multilateral institutions amid growing questions over their effectiveness in addressing global challenges."Where the UN is concerned, I think it's obvious to everybody by now that the UN is gridlocked. If you look at the big issues of the day, whether you look at the conflict in the Gulf, whether you look at the conflict in Ukraine, whether you look at other issues in Africa, whether you look at Covid, actually, the United Nations has been largely irrelevant to the decision-making," Jaishankar said."I think, again there's a widely held view that a lot of it is because the (UN) Security Council is gridlocked, that the Security Council no longer represents the entirety of the global interest," he said.

title: No building plan approval for painting: NDMC issues list of works exempt from permits
description: NDMC clarified that the exemptions do not permit unauthorised construction, additional floors, setbacks and other statutory conditions
content: Repairs such as plastering, painting, flooring, roof replacement and alterations to doors and windows will not require prior building plan approval, the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) has clarified in a public notice listing works exempt from permission under the Unified Building Bye-Laws for Delhi, 2016 (UBBL-2016).The notice, issued on October 22 also exempts specified public utility structures, including public toilets, traffic and police control rooms, air purification systems, vertical gardens, dhalaos and solar panels, from building permits, subject to prescribed conditions.The move comes a day after NDMC chairman Manoj Kumar Dwivedi said a lack of awareness and clarity was often prompting building users to apply for permissions for work that did not require them. In some cases, he said, they faced harassment at the hands of enforcement officials.Also Read: MHA asks MCD for audit plan covering every building in cityDwivedi said the civic body would distinguish structural additions and alterations from routine maintenance and non-structural renovation, clarifying which works were exempt and which required prior approval. He also announced plans for an awareness campaign to ensure residents were not inconvenienced or confused by compliance requirements.Works and structures covered by the exemptionsThe list of exempt works includes plastering, cladding and patch repairs; re-roofing at the existing height; flooring and re-flooring; repairs to damaged bricks, stones, pillars and beams; and internal partitions permitted under the bye-laws. Owners can also undertake whitewashing, painting and false ceiling installation, provided the ceiling is not used to create a loft or mezzanine.Also Read: NDMC closes Central Park for ‘administrative’ reasonsOther exemptions cover boundary walls permitted under the bye-laws, parapets, sunshades up to 75cm wide within the owner’s land, landscaping and public art. Installation or relocation of fixtures and equipment is also permitted if it does not encroach on another person’s property or public land. Installation of lifts in existing low-rise residential plotted buildings is among the listed exemptions.Conditions and limits on exempt worksHowever, the exemptions come with conditions. Works must comply with applicable structural stability and fire safety requirements and cannot encroach on public land or obstruct fire tender movement. Heritage buildings remain subject to heritage conservation permissions wherever required.Also Read: Water supply to south, central Delhi may be disrupted due to annual canal maintenanceUnder the notice, qualifying public utility structures measuring up to 25 square metres and executed or promoted by government agencies for public safety, health, pollution control, transport, water supply, sewage disposal and solid waste management do not require building permits.NDMC clarified that the exemptions do not permit unauthorised construction, additional floors, changes in land use or violations of sanctioned plans, setbacks and other statutory conditions. Owners, architects and engineers will remain responsible for structural defects arising from exempt works.

title: Govt to tighten learner’s licence requirements
description: The Centre has proposed making several driving-licence services free and tightening the requirements for obtaining a learner’s licence, as part of a wider overhaul of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989
content: The Centre has proposed making several driving-licence services free and tightening the requirements for obtaining a learner’s licence, as part of a wider overhaul of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. A draft notification published by the Union road transport and highways ministry late on Wednesday. proposes raising the pass mark for the safe-driving tutorial assessment from 60% to 75%, while making the tutorial at least 30 minutes long.The draft rules propose waiving fees for services accessed through online Aadhaar authentication. Changes to a driving licence holder’s name or other particulars would also be free, while updating an address, mobile number or email ID would attract no fee.The proposals are part of a wider revision of licence application procedures, identity requirements and licence formats. Under the proposed changes, applicants would have to complete the safe-driving tutorial within 15 days, against the existing seven-day period. The pass mark would rise to 75% from 60%, and the minimum tutorial duration would be 30 minutes. The draft proposes ending exemptions for people with older learner’s licences and those with driving-school certificates, requiring them to undergo the prescribed tutorial and test.The ministry has proposed a revised list of documents for establishing an applicant’s address, age and identity. Address proof could include Aadhaar, voter identity card, passport, e-ration card, government-issued service photo identity card, pensioner or freedom fighter identity card, or a pension payment order. Electricity and household gas bills would be accepted if they were not more than three months old. Foreign applicants would also have to provide proof of their legal presence in India.For age or date-of-birth proof, the proposed list includes a passport, a marksheet or certificate issued by a recognised educational institution showing the date of birth, a birth certificate, and specified government-issued service or pension documents. Aadhaar, a valid Indian passport, an e-ration card, specified service or pension documents, and a permanent account number (PAN) would be accepted as identity proof.The draft also proposes making laminated or polyvinyl chloride (PVC) cards the prescribed format for driving licences, with separate formats for Indian and foreign nationals. Applications to change licence particulars would have to be filed online with supporting evidence. Licensing authorities would have 15 days to approve or reject such applications, recording reasons for rejection. Address-change applications would be deemed approved if neither accepted nor rejected within 30 days.A person surrendering a vehicle category on a driving licence permanently would not be eligible to obtain a learner’s or driving licence for that category for one year. The category would be automatically deleted from the licence within seven days of the application.The draft also proposes revised application forms and photograph specifications for online applications, including a maximum file size of 1 MB, a plain white background, the face occupying 70% of the frame, and a specified image resolution. Proposed form changes include making blood group details mandatory and collecting mobile and emergency-contact numbers. The learner’s licence format would specify validity of six months from the date of issue and allow corrections to discrepancies, including date of birth, through a written request with original documents before applying for a driving licence. The draft will be considered after the 30-day period, and the proposed rules would come into force upon final publication in the Official Gazette, unless otherwise specified.“The proposed reforms are a welcome step towards making driving licence services more accessible, transparent and citizen-friendly. Raising the pass threshold for the safe-driving assessment from 60% to 75% is also a positive move, as driving must be treated as a responsibility that requires demonstrable knowledge of road safety, not merely a procedural entitlement,” Piyush Tewari, Founder & CEO, SaveLIFE Foundation said. However, he said the real test of these reforms will be whether they produce safer drivers on our roads. “A higher pass mark alone is insufficient unless the assessment meaningfully evaluates understanding of traffic rules, hazard perception, vulnerable road users and safe driving behaviour. Equally important is ensuring that practical driving tests are rigorous, objective and free from human discretion or manipulation.”He said India must move towards a licensing system where obtaining a driving licence is convenient for those who are competent, but difficult for those who are not. “Ease of access must never come at the cost of road safety,” Tewari said.

title: Google, Telegram asked how they handle CSAM
description: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) on Thursday met with Google and Telegram representatives to understand how they detect and report child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on their platforms, an NCPCR official told HT
content: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) on Thursday met with Google and Telegram representatives to understand how they detect and report child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on their platforms, an NCPCR official told HT. The meeting comes amid the commission’s ongoing inquiry into Meta, after a BBC Eye investigation found Instagram advertisements that directed users to Telegram channels allegedly selling CSAM.Google was asked how it handles CSAM on YouTube and its other platforms, and the commission also asked Telegram about its content moderation policy, the official said. The commission wants a detailed response from both platforms and will send both a questionnaire on Friday and seek written responses, giving them 10-12 days to reply. After studying the answers, NCPCR will call another meeting.The commission also questioned why the companies had not, until recently, been reporting such cases to Indian agencies. “They were reminded that the law of the land must be followed,” the official said. This comes after Meta and Google in September announced that they will begin reporting to the Cyber Crime portal maintained by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Telegram told the commission that it is already reporting to I4C.This also comes as the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has submitted a draft of an SOP on CSAM to the Supreme Court, after it asked the ministry to implement its 2024 judgment in the Just Rights for Children Alliance v S Harish, which requires social media intermediaries to report such material to law enforcement. The SOP will explain how an intermediary must report CSAM, where to report it, and what the process will be.Until now, Google and Meta reported detected CSAM through the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), which forwards reports to law enforcement agencies around the world. The government’s position is that platforms must report such cases directly to Indian law enforcement agencies, and it has called children’s online safety “non-negotiable”.

title: SC points out vacation listing loophole, urges uniform rules for HCs
description: The Supreme Court has recommended that high courts adopt a uniform approach to listing cases during court vacations, cautioning that litigants should not be prejudiced by an inadvertent act of the court -- an order that came after it examined a video recording of a disputed bail hearing that took place during the Karnataka High Court’s winter break last year
content: The Supreme Court has recommended that high courts adopt a uniform approach to listing cases during court vacations, cautioning that litigants should not be prejudiced by an inadvertent act of the court -- an order that came after it examined a video recording of a disputed bail hearing that took place during the Karnataka High Court’s winter break last year.In an unusual exercise, a bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu went through a pen drive containing the video recording and transcript of the December 26, 2025 hearing to examine conflicting claims over whether a government counsel had been given an adequate opportunity to oppose bail. The bench’s scrutiny of the material eventually led it to flag a broader procedural issue concerning the urgent listing of matters when high courts are on vacation.In its October 16 order, the court said that when a high court directs a matter to be listed “two weeks hence”, and the day following the expiry of that period falls during a court vacation, the registry should ordinarily calculate the two-week period by excluding the vacation. This would help ensure that matters are not listed during a vacation merely because a deadline happens to expire while the court is in recess.The court, however, clarified that this approach would not apply where the bench specifically directs a matter to be listed on a date falling during the vacation or orders its listing before the vacation bench. The arrangement would also remain subject to the relevant rules framed by individual high courts.“These observations, aimed at serving the interest of justice better, are essential to secure uniformity as well as to ensure that litigants are not prejudiced due to an inadvertent act of the court,” the bench said.The recommendation is significant because vacation benches are intended to address urgent matters that cannot wait until regular court sittings resume. Where listing directions intersect with court holidays, the calculation of deadlines can determine whether a case is heard during the break or after reopening, potentially affecting both parties seeking urgent relief and those entitled to oppose it.The recommendation arose from an appeal by a senior intelligence officer of the Directorate General of Service Tax Intelligence against a Karnataka high court order granting bail to Mohammed Kamran, accused of causing a loss of more than ₹43 crore to the exchequer through alleged fraudulent input tax credit claims and invoices issued without the supply of goods.The department alleged that its arguing counsel was unavailable when Kamran’s bail petition was heard during the winter vacation, that a request for adjournment was rejected and that it was denied a proper opportunity to present its case. Kamran’s counsel disputed this account, maintaining that a lawyer representing the department had appeared and addressed the court on the merits.To resolve the conflicting versions, the Supreme Court, by an order dated September 10, permitted the department to file an additional affidavit and allowed Kamran to respond. With his reply, Kamran submitted the pen drive containing the recording and transcript of the hearing.The examination of the video-recording revealed that the department was not entirely unrepresented, as the lawyer who appeared did make some submissions on the merits. However, he had also sought an adjournment because the department’s standing counsel had been engaged to appear in the matter. When the request was declined, the lawyer chose to assist the court by opposing bail.What weighed more heavily against Kamran was the manner in which he secured an expedited hearing while pursuing parallel legal remedies. After filing a bail petition in the high court on December 9, 2025, he moved the sessions court for bail the following day. On December 22, he also filed a writ petition challenging the legality of his arrest and seeking, among other reliefs, release from custody. The writ court refused interim relief that day. Later the same day, a memo was moved seeking urgent listing of the pending bail petition, which was heard on December 26 during the winter vacation.The bench noted that Kamran did not disclose to the single judge that the writ court had refused his request for interim release. Nor were the parallel proceedings and the rejection of bail by the sessions court adequately brought to the judge’s attention.The court described this conduct as forum shopping and an abuse of the process of law, stressing that pursuing remedies before different judicial fora without adequate disclosure could undermine the integrity of judicial proceedings.The court also questioned the vacation listing, observing that the earlier direction had not specified a date falling during the winter break, nor had the single judge directed that the matter be placed before the vacation bench. The petition should ideally have been listed after the high court reopened, it said.“To have obtained listing of a petition, without adequate notice to the appellant, was clearly an attempt to steal a march by even misleading the Court,” it observed.The Supreme Court stopped short of cancelling Kamran’s bail outright.
