Instead, it set aside the portion of the high court order disposing of his criminal petition and revived the matter for fresh consideration by the single judge. Kamran will continue on interim bail on the existing terms until further orders. The department was given two weeks to file its counter-affidavit and Kamran one week thereafter to file a rejoinder. The high court was asked to decide the petition, preferably by the end of 2026.

title: Andhra Pradesh revises urban local body election schedule after Supreme Court directive
description: The Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission revised the urban local body election schedule and reopened nominations for 48 hours in four areas.
content: The Andhra Pradesh state election commission on Thursday announced a revised schedule for the elections to urban local bodies in the state, following the Supreme Court directions which came on Wednesday on complaints that some candidates were prevented from filing nominations due to law-and-order problems.According to the fresh notification released by state election commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha, the polling for 100 ULB, including 13 municipal corporations, will be held on November 1 and counting of votes will take place on November 3.With regard to four urban local bodies – Kadapa Municipal Corporation, Rajampet Municipality and Mydukur Municipality in YSR Kadapa district, and Tirupati Municipal Corporation in Tirupati district, where there were allegations of violence and disturbances in the nomination process, the nomination process would be reopened for 48 hours.Also Read | Andhra loses Supreme Court battle over 34% Backward Classes quota in local pollsIn these four places, fresh nominations will be received on October 23 and 24 between 11 am and 3 pm at the locations already notified by the respective Returning Officers/Election Officers. Besides existing nomination centres, candidates can submit their nomination papers at Collectorate premises designated by respective Collectors and district election authorities.The APSEC observed that in these four urban local bodies, candidates willing to contest had allegedly been intimidated or attacked, their nomination papers torn, or other adverse circumstances had prevented them from filing nominations. Now, the candidates will be allowed to file fresh nominations.The commission clarified that the facility to withdraw nominations will be allowed on October 25 only for candidates filing fresh nominations during the extended period.

title: Entry restrictions, WhatsApp group: Delhi traffic police plans to curb air pollution
description: The plans and their implementation strategies were discussed during the inter-state coordination meeting that the Delhi Traffic Police held on Thursday
content: Creation of a dedicated WhatsApp group to improve multi-agency coordination and enforcement, diversion of non-complaint inter-city and inter-state buses at Delhi’s borders, ensuring entry restrictions of vehicles registered outside Delhi and setting up joint enforcement teams at the city’s borders for coordinated action are some of the measures that the Delhi Traffic Police have decided to implement to curb air pollution.The plans and their implementation strategies were discussed during the inter-state coordination meeting that the Delhi Traffic Police held on Thursday with other concerned stakeholders, including the city’s civic agencies and police authorities of the neighbouring states. The objective of the meeting was to ensure effective implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) and directions issued by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), said deputy commissioner of police (traffic) SK Singh.Chairing the meeting, special commissioner of police (traffic) Ajay Chaudhry emphasised on improving coordination between all stakeholders and for that he directed that a dedicated WhatsApp group be created and all concerned officials be added to it.Also Read: Delhi’s air quality remains ‘poor’ for second consecutive day; no relief expected in coming daysBus diversions and vehicle entry restrictions“The WhatsApp group will facilitate real-time sharing of CAQM directions and updates on action taken by various agencies. It will also help monitor actions taken by the concerned departments,” a senior officer, who attended the meeting, said, asking not to be named.Special CP Chaudhry also asked the officials to ensure preventing the entry of non-compliant inter-city and inter-state buses into Delhi, and such public transport vehicles must be diverted at the borders itself, as their diversion after entering Delhi leads to traffic congestion and additional air pollution.“As per the applicable directions, only electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) and BS-VI diesel buses are permitted in Delhi subject to the prescribed conditions. Also, entry restrictions applicable to vehicles registered outside should be ensured from November 1 to January 31 next year, subject to notified exemptions. Prominent display boards should be installed at Delhi borders clearly indicating that prohibited vehicles, including non-exempt vehicles not meeting the prescribed emission norms, will not be allowed to enter Delhi,” Chaudhry said in the meeting.Joint enforcement and dust controlWhile setting up joint enforcement teams at the borders for effective implementation was planned, the traffic police have also asked the concerned authorities to strictly enforce no-entry timings, check non-destined and overloaded vehicles, and take action against vehicles transporting construction and demolition (C&D) material in violation of prescribed norms.Also Read: Delhi govt’s winter action plan targets sources at correct time, but mirrors GrapThe civic agencies have been asked to expedite ongoing construction works, minimise dust generation and undertake regular water sprinkling on roads and at construction sites. Public awareness regarding GRAP measures, CAQM directions and vehicle entry.“Vehicle owners are advised to ensure valid Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCC), wherever applicable. We will also be focusing on public awareness regarding GRAP measures, CAQM directions and vehicle entry restrictions. The measures are aimed at curbing vehicular emissions and reducing pollution in Delhi,” added DCP Singh.

title: RTI reveals Cabinet Secretariat sent election commissioners’ letters to CEC Gyanesh Kumar
description: The July 29 letters alleged that senior deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg issued a work-allocation order without consulting the commissioners.
content: The Cabinet Secretariat forwarded the letters written to the Cabinet Secretary by election commissioners Sukhbir Sandhu and Vivek Joshi about the alleged misconduct of senior deputy election commissioner (DEC) Maneesh Garg to the office of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, in addition to sending them to the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), according to information obtained through a Right to Information (RTI) application.A document released in response to the application shows that on August 3, the secretariat proposed asking CEC Kumar for his opinion on the letters. Another, on August 4, noted that the letters from the commissioners were in their individual capacity and not a formal communication from the Election Commission of India. The only response to the two commissioners was an acknowledgement that their letters had been received. The acknowledgements dated August 5 were copied to the secretary, department of personnel and training (DoPT), the establishment officer in DoPT, and the principal private secretary to the chief election commissioner.Hindustan Times first reported on October 3, the details of the letters and the fact that they had been forwarded to DoPT, but the RTI reply shows that the CEC was also sent a copy. HT also reported that the Cabinet Secretary did not act on the letters because they had not been written by the Election Commission, but the two commissioners in their individual capacity.Also read: How ECI identifies, removes duplicate electoral roll entries Secretariat flags risk of interference in constitutional bodyThe documents released under the RTI Act to transparency activist Commodore Lokesh Batra (Retd.) show that in its note dated August 4, the secretariat noted that any step that could be “construed as interference” in a constitutional body. It also recommended that the matter be placed on record with DoPT for future decisions on the officer concerned, Garg.Batra filed his application on September 24.The nearly identical letters were sent to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan on July 29. Sandhu’s letter was accompanied by the copy of an order issued by Garg on July 28 allocating work to himself and other EC officials, including director general IT Seema Khanna and DEC Sanjay Kumar.Also read: Any fresh impeachment motion to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar will follow due process: Om BirlaDispute centred on routing of IT department filesAccording to a Hindustan Times report dated October 3, the commissioners were concerned about Garg’s decision to change the routing of files of the IT department under Khanna. The files had earlier gone to Kumar.In their confidential letters to the Cabinet Secretary, the commissioners said Garg was given additional charge of the Administration Division on July 28, while DEC Bhanu Prakash Yeturu was on leave until August 9. Within hours, they said, he issued a work-allocation order covering officers senior and equivalent to him. The letters said the commissioners were not consulted on the decision. Both cited Sections 18(1) and 18(2) of the 2023 CEC/EC Act. Joshi added that a file he asked for from the Administration Division was not provided.Also read: UN experts slam India’s ‘heavy-handed’ crackdown on youth-led protestsRTI response lists acknowledgements and endorsementsIn reply to Batra’s question on “steps taken,” the Cabinet Secretariat’s information officer listed the acknowledgments and endorsements.The letters, and the response, are significant because Khanna and the IT department are at the heart of a controversy after an investigation by the Indian Express said that the new IT protocol/system put in place by Khanna and approved by the Election Commission, shut the database of electors (the rolls) from the very people responsible for adding or deleting names, Electoral Registration Officials (EROs).The Express investigation also reported that there were differences between the election commissioners , and that Joshi and Sandhu had disagreed several times with CEC Kumar. The Election Commission has denied this and said that all decisions were either unanimous or taken by a majority in keeping with the rules.

title: Alternative routes turn bottlenecks as RTR flyover closure triggers 18km jam from Delhi to Gurugram
description: The reroutes, announced by the Gurugram traffic police, were supposed to ease congestion on NH-48 by directing traffic to Dhaula Kuan in Delhi.
content: Repair work on the Rao Tula Ram (RTR) flyover on the Outer Ring Road in south Delhi spiralled into a massive traffic jam on Thursday, with congestion stretching nearly 18 kilometres from Dhaula Kuan to Udyog Vihar in Gurugram and thousands of commuters bearing the brunt of diversions on one of the National Capital Region’s busiest corridors.On Thursday, the RTR flyover remained shut for a second consecutive day, forcing vehicles travelling between Delhi airport, Gurugram, Dwarka and south Delhi to take alternative routes.Also Read I Cracks repair work force closure of RTR flyover, triggers traffic snarlsThe closure triggered a cascading traffic backlog on the Delhi-Gurgaon Expressway and roads leading into Gurugram, leaving commuters facing sharply increased travel times.RTR Flyover closure creates traffic woesMany took to social media to share videos of the congestion and complain about the disruption. “Gurgaon New Delhi connectivity is broken for the past 48 hours. Traffic Police nowhere to be found,” a motorist posted on X. Another commuter posted, “Taking 2.5 hours to reach from Gurugram to central Delhi because the Vasant Vihar flyover is closed. Please help.”The RTR flyover has been shut since early Wednesday, after Delhi traffic personnel observed cracks at two locations on the flyover on Tuesday night and informed the Public Works Department (PWD) about it, seeking necessary repairs. The repair work is expected to be completed by October 26, and vehicular movement on the flyover is likely to resume by October 27.Until then, traffic from the Delhi airport, Gurugram, and Dwarka, heading to Vasant Vihar and Chirag Delhi, has been diverted onto the service road adjoining the RTR flyover and other alternative routes. In an advisory, Delhi Traffic Police said, “The flyover has been closed for repair work, and the entire traffic has been diverted onto the adjoining service road. Consequently, traffic is heavy, and the queue is extending considerably behind the flyover. The flyover will remain closed until completion of the work, and traffic is expected to remain heavy during peak hours.”Gurugram reels from diversionsGurugram traffic police said congestion worsened Thursday morning due to restrictions on the entry of heavy vehicles into Gurugram between 8am and 10am via NH-48 and the Dwarka Expressway. Traffic movement was severely affected from Rajiv Chowk to 32nd Avenue, on NH-48 towards Jaipur, near Leisure Valley Park, and from Iffco Chowk to Udyog Vihar Phase 4. Vehicular movement on MG Road towards the Iffco Chowk metro station and near Sikanderpur moved slowly, and the backlog cleared up by around 11.30am, police said.Also Read I Entry restrictions, WhatsApp group: Delhi traffic police plans to curb air pollutionOn the Faridabad-Gurugram road, vehicles moved bumper to bumper on a three-kilometre stretch from the Ghata T-Point to Valley View Estate leading to Gurugram.Traffic inspector Tanej Pal said the congestion was caused by the diversion and worsened due to a vehicle breakdown.Vandana Sharma, a Noida resident, said that due to severe congestion, it took her 70 minutes to reach Gurugram.

title: eMudhra shuts global website certificate business after key flaws exposed, calls scrutiny ‘disproportionate’
description: The vulnerabilities came to light after an independent cybersecurity researcher discovered that several of eMudhra's key certificates could be attacked.
content: Digital security firm eMudhra will reportedly withdraw from the global website security certificate business after major browser makers, including Google, Apple and Microsoft, withdrew trust in its certificates over vulnerabilities that triggered cybersecurity concerns worldwide.The company announced its exit on Thursday, news agency Reuters reported. eMudhra said the attention on social media had resulted in disproportionate scrutiny of a business that contributes just 1 per cent of its revenue.The company's SSL/TLS certificates encrypt communications between websites and users to protect data from unauthorised interception. eMudhra's customers include IT majors Infosys and TCS, as well as government agencies. Its certificates also protected critical websites, including India's income-tax portal. The vulnerabilities came to light over the weekend after an independent cybersecurity researcher discovered that several of eMudhra's key certificates could be attacked.Also Read | Centre orders probe as Bengaluru firm eMudhra's key-making error leaves holes in web securityThe company said it had revoked eight certificates but maintained that its infrastructure had not been compromised and no data breach had occurred, reported Reuters.Investors have reacted sharply to the disclosure, with eMudhra's shares falling 40% over the two days following the revelation.The flaws originated in eight cryptographic keys generated by eMudhra in April last year. The keys were inadvertently shortened by the company's software, making them significantly weaker, co-founder Kaushik Srinivasan told Reuters.Cryptographic keys are strings of characters used by encryption algorithms to secure data. When these keys are too short, they can become easier for attackers to crack, potentially compromising the security of encrypted communications.Also Read | From eMudhra to Bank of Baroda: 5 major data breaches in recent times“A single compromised certificate authority can impersonate any website,” said Lukasz Olejnik, an independent consultant and visiting senior researcher at the Department of War Studies at King's College London.The ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) on Thursday said it had “taken serious note” of the incident and set up a special team to investigate. The ministry said the impact on Indian websites and applications had been “very limited and for a very short interval”. It also accused some social media accounts of “fear mongering” about the incident.

title: Arrivals of Indian students in US on visa plunge by 39% amid immigration crackdown
description: Visa delays, stricter screening and uncertainty over post-study work are among the factors consultants say are discouraging students.
content: Arrivals from India on US student visas fell 39% in August from a year earlier, the third straight annual decline in the month that usually sees the biggest influx of foreign students ahead of the fall semester.The US Commerce Department’s International Trade Administration (ITA) recorded 25,321 such arrivals on F and M category visas in August, down from 41,540 a year earlier. That was the lowest August figure since 2020, when pandemic travel restrictions held arrivals to 2,908, and 73% below the August 2023 peak of 93,833.The slide began under Joe Biden, with a 20.3% fall to 74,825 in August 2024, but has accelerated since US President Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025. August arrivals fell 44.5% in 2025 and another 39% this year, leaving them 66.2% below the 2024 level. In that time, his administration has expanded social media screening of student visa applicants, finalised a rule, since blocked by a court, ending open-ended admission for foreign students, and proposed steep fees on their post-study work. Study-abroad consultants cite visa appointment and processing delays, stricter screening and uncertainty over post-study work among the reasons for the fall.Also Read | Trump administration revokes over 300,000 visas as immigration checks tightenVisa Processing, Screening and DataF-1 visa processing was hit by significant delays in 2025. The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said in a Rajya Sabha reply on April 2 that 12,776 F-1 visas were issued to Indian nationals in June and July 2025, down 69.1% from 41,336 a year earlier, and that expanded US screening and compliance measures had affected issuance. The US State Department has published monthly issuance data only up to February 2026, so no comparable figure is public for this summer.Under State Department guidance issued on June 18, 2025, applicants for student and exchange visitor visas were required to make their social media profiles public for review.The ITA counts entries rather than individuals, includes dependants on F-2 and M-2 visas, and records arrivals by country of residence. Its August and September figures are preliminary. The data do not show how many visas were issued, how many students enrolled or why arrivals fell. The US Embassy in New Delhi and the ITA did not immediately respond to HT’s queries.Also Read | Rubio says US immigration curbs not aimed at India, blames 'mass migration' for visa crackdownArrivals and Visa Refusal RatesArrivals also fell 17.3% year-on-year in June and 30.6% in July. September arrivals rose 5% to 12,285 from 11,700, a gain of 585 that offset little of August’s shortfall of 16,219, and remained 37.5% below September 2024’s 19,641. From June to September, arrivals totalled 53,714, down 28.2% from 2025 and 59.7% from 2024.An April paper by US-based education company Shorelight, using government data obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request, found the F-1 visa refusal rate for Indian applicants rose from 36% in fiscal 2023 to 53% in 2024 and 61% in 2025.Consultants Cite Costs and UncertaintyConsultants also cited higher rejection rates, employment prospects and the rising cost of education, which together, they said, were prompting students and families to reconsider their plans. Vinu Warrier, managing partner and founder of eduVelocity Global, said US universities’ admission timelines had not been delayed. “US universities continue to follow their usual admission timelines, with no significant delays reported,” he said.Anil Wagde, a core team member at Global Empower Network, which advises students on studying abroad, said students had complained about a lack of visa-stamping appointments. “There are some students who have now started postponing their travel to later semesters due to delays in visa issuance,” he said.A spokesperson for IDP Education, an international education services firm, said appointment shortages and higher rejection rates were affecting students’ travel plans, while proposed changes to Optional Practical Training (OPT) and a new Duration of Status rule were prompting families to weigh costs against future employment prospects. “Fluctuations in the dollar exchange rate are affecting affordability, leading families to focus more on return on investment (ROI) when planning their education,” the spokesperson said, adding that students were reviewing their options amid the policy uncertainty.Also Read | US legal immigration falls by half under Trump as visa restrictions hit 91 countriesProposed OPT Fees and Duration of Status RuleOPT lets F-1 students work in their field during or after their degree. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed on October 8 that institutions pay $70,000 per student for a first OPT period and $30,000 for each later one. A separate DHS rule, finalised on July 17, would replace Duration of Status, under which students are admitted without a fixed end date, with fixed periods of up to four years. A federal court in Massachusetts blocked it on September 14, a day before it was to take effect, and the government has appealed.Vinu Warrier said inconsistent policies on academic visas, temporary work visas and green cards were eroding confidence in the US as a study destination. “The biggest reassurance you would need is stability, certainty,” he said.Consultants said some students were considering alternatives such as Germany, the Netherlands, France, Spain, Singapore, Hong Kong and Japan, while others were weighing private universities in India or waiting for greater clarity over visa rules and job prospects.

title: Supreme Court calls for setting human trafficking apart from voluntary sex work
description: The National Judicial Academy has been asked to frame guidelines for magistrates, while the Centre must submit a fresh compliance report before the next hearing
content: The Supreme Court has moved to protect adult women engaged in voluntary sex work from being subjected to the same legal process as victims of human trafficking, directing the National Judicial Academy to frame a uniform protocol for magistrates to determine whether rescued women were forced into commercial sexual exploitation or were engaged in the work voluntarily.The court said magistrates across the country must be trained to conduct a mandatory “threshold inquiry” into the circumstances of every adult woman rescued during anti-trafficking operations, even if she claims that her work is voluntary. The exercise is intended to distinguish genuine trafficking victims requiring protection from adult sex workers who should not be subjected to intrusive judicial proceedings or compelled into rehabilitation merely because they were at the site of a raid.The directions, issued recently by a bench of justices JB Pardiwala and R Mahadevan, build on the court’s May 29 judgment in a 2004 public interest litigation filed by NGO Prajwala. The court has now sought to ensure that its extensive victim protection framework is implemented uniformly, acknowledging that judicial directions often risk remaining confined to judgments without any reliable assessment of their impact on the ground.Also read: Govt ends segregation of sex workers, brothel-keepers from female prisoners“Once these directions are committed to the paper in the form of a judgment, the matter marks its abrupt end,” noted the bench, expressing concern that courts often have no means of knowing whether the frameworks they prescribe are making a measurable difference in people’s lives or what obstacles are impeding their implementation.The latest order followed a compliance review in which the court found that several states and Union territories had yet to implement four additional directions issued in May. It also asked the Union government to obtain detailed compliance reports from all stakeholders involved in the victim protection plan and directed the petitioner and the Centre to suggest concrete mechanisms to track its progress and effectiveness.Senior advocate Aparna Bhat, appearing for Prajwala, submitted a detailed compliance table identifying the responsibilities assigned to the various stakeholders under the May judgment. The bench commended the exercise, saying it would help monitor compliance with its directions. Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati presented the Centre’s status note on steps taken so far.Also read: ₹48 lakh forfeited">Nurpur drug trafficker’s assets worth ₹48 lakh forfeitedMagistrates must distinguish consent from coercionThe central concern behind the latest directions is the danger of treating all women found during anti-trafficking raids as a single category, irrespective of whether they have been trafficked, are being coerced into sex work or have chosen it voluntarily.In its May 29 judgment, the Supreme Court held that the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, or ITPA, must not be used to subject adult voluntary sex workers to the same rescue, custody and rehabilitation procedures meant to protect victims of trafficking. It underscored that prostitution, in itself, is not an offence under the law and that voluntary adult sex workers must not be arrested, penalised, harassed or victimised during raids merely because they are found in a brothel.Drawing on the Law Commission’s 64th report and its earlier ruling in Budhadev Karmaskar Vs State of West Bengal (2022), the court said the statutory framework was never intended to interfere with the lives of adults who engage in sex work of their own volition. The Law Commission specifically reasoned that the question of rescuing a woman does not arise when she is engaged in prostitution voluntarily.The May judgment noted that the existing framework under ITPA sections 15, 16 and 17 could bring a wide range of women within the same process, from those trafficked against their will to those who had chosen sex work for themselves. A mandatory preliminary judicial determination was therefore necessary to prevent voluntary adult sex workers from being drawn into a deeper inquiry into their age, character, antecedents and family circumstances, which could keep them away from their lives and families.Also read: How SC reimagined the fight against human trafficking? Threshold inquiry must assess consent, coercion and safety risksUnder the framework laid down by the court, a magistrate must examine the rescued adult woman’s consent and wishes, her account of whether her work was voluntary, the social worker’s assessment, the possibility of threats, coercion, force or undue influence, and any safety concerns that could expose her to immediate danger or re-trafficking if released.The inquiry is mandatory even when a woman says she is engaged in sex work voluntarily. The court has cautioned that traffickers may tutor or intimidate victims into claiming that their work is voluntary, or into refusing rehabilitation, to ensure their return to the trafficker’s control. Magistrates must therefore assess the totality of the circumstances rather than treat a statement of consent as conclusive.At the same time, the court made clear that the possibility of coercion cannot become a justification for indiscriminate detention. The May judgment held that a victim’s consent must be the primary consideration in decisions on long-term custody in a protective home or restoration to her family. A magistrate may depart from her expressed wishes only in exceptional circumstances, such as when her safety is at risk or her consent is found to be the product of coercion, tutoring or undue influence, and must record reasons in writing.Also read: Darren Indyke, Epstein’s longtime lawyer, sued over alleged sex trafficking cover-up at New Mexico propertyAHTUs as police stationsThe court also stressed that rehabilitation cannot be imposed against a victim’s will as a matter of routine. The State’s obligation is to provide the support and means necessary for rehabilitation, while respecting the individual’s choices, dignity and circumstances.To translate these principles into consistent judicial practice, the bench has now requested the National Judicial Academy to prepare comprehensive guidelines for magistrates conducting the threshold inquiry. Prajwala may assist the academy in framing the protocol, which is intended to ensure that the May judgment is implemented in both letter and spirit across the country.The directions concerning the threshold inquiry and primacy of consent apply to adult victims of trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation. Child victims are governed by the separate procedure under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, through child welfare committees.Also read: Courts can’t suggest custodial quizzing, says Supreme CourtAnti-Trafficking Units and Compliance MeasuresThe court also directed all state and Union Territory governments to give Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) the status of police stations by issuing appropriate notifications in accordance with law. The Union government has been asked to take up the issue with all states and Union territories and ensure that the notifications are issued at the earliest.The direction seeks to give effect to a measure already contained in the May judgment. Formal notification of AHTUs as police stations is important to ensure that specialised units tasked with investigating human trafficking can function within a clear legal framework, rather than have their role undermined by gaps in their formal status and authority.The court’s broader intervention arose from Prajwala’s plea seeking a dedicated investigating agency to tackle cyber-enabled human trafficking and sexual exploitation, alongside a victim-oriented approach under the ITPA. The NGO had argued that the existing law did not adequately address the rehabilitation of rescued victims and risked clubbing them with those responsible for the offences.Also read: Supreme Court directs mother to take 7-year-old daughter back to US by Dec 31 in custody disputeIn its May judgment, the Supreme Court had laid down an extensive victim protection plan under Article 142 of the Constitution and dealt with the proposal for an Organised Crime Investigation Agency. It had also made recommendations for the Union government’s consideration.The court has now directed the Centre to ensure that all states and Union territories fully comply with four additional requirements set out in the May judgment -- notifying recognised welfare institutions and organisations for the purposes of the ITPA; preparing state-wide lists of eligible social welfare workers for advisory boards and magistrates’ panels; designating a police nodal officer; and designating a government nodal officer. The bench said these arrangements were essential for implementing the victim protection plan at the ground level.The Union government has been asked to file a fresh status report by the next hearing on December 14. Prajwala is also expected to inform the court about the progress made by the National Judicial Academy in preparing the magistrates’ protocol, while both sides must propose practical ways to monitor compliance and measure the plan’s real-world impact.

title: Benjamin Netanyahu invites PM Modi, Smit Machchhar to light torch at Israeli Independence Day event
description: Modi reiterated India’s support for dialogue and diplomacy, while both leaders also reviewed their countries’ strategic partnership.
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Israeli counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday discussed recent developments in West Asia, which have witnessed an escalation in hostilities in recent weeks, and emphasised the need to urgently restore peace and stability in the region.Netanyahu, who dialled the Indian PM, said on social media he had invited Modi to join Indian pilot Smit Machchhar — currently recovering in a hospital in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) after being injured while foiling an attempted hijacking last month — to light a torch on Israel’s Independence Day in May next year.Modi’s social media post and an Indian government readout on the phone conversation made no reference to this issue.In his social media post, Modi said he received a call from Netanyahu and they “exchanged views on recent developments in West Asia and underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region”. They also reviewed the “sustained momentum in our bilateral ties and reaffirmed our commitment to further strengthening” the bilateral special strategic partnership.Also Read | Watch: Ahead Of Elections, Netanyahu Says Israel And US Have 'A Job To Finish' In IranModi reiterated “India’s call for dialogue and diplomacy as the way forward”, the Indian readout said.Netanyahu's Invitation to Modi and MachchharNetanyahu said in social media posts in Hindi and Hebrew that he invited Modi to “light a torch together with the heroic Indian pilot on the Independence Day of the State of Israel”. He added, “Modi thanked me for the invitation and said that on the ground and in the air, India and Israel fight terrorism together. He expressed his appreciation for the courageous and long-standing relationship between us.”Netanyahu’s invitation follows Israel President Isaac Herzog’s recent invite to Machchhar to visit the country to be given the Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism, the highest honour for bravery by civilians.Also Read | Netanyahu warns future US president could be hostile to Israel, eyes close ties with IndiaThe Hijacking Attempt and Machchhar's BraveryMachchhar was severely wounded while trying to stop his Omani co-pilot from attempting to hijack a Flydubai flight with 174 passengers that was going from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30. He sustained injuries to his head and neck when he was attacked with an axe, but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing crew members and passengers to overpower the co-pilot.The aircraft made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, and Israeli officials have said the co-pilot intended to crash the aircraft. Modi and Netanyahu have lauded Machchhar for his bravery.Also Read | JD Vance sidesteps Netanyahu's endorsement ahead of Israel elections, says Trump's backing ‘most influential’Election ContextPeople familiar with the matter said Netanyahu’s social media post appeared to have been made with an eye on Israel’s general election on October 27, the first since the military campaign in Gaza and the country’s wars with Iran and Lebanon.

title: Congress a ‘parasite’, defaming India abroad: PM Modi hits out at Opposition amid anti-EC stir
description: Modi called for reforms to global institutions, greater representation for the Global South and international cooperation focused on humanity.
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched a frontal attack on the Congress on Thursday, calling the opposition party a parasite and accusing it of damaging India’s international standing by criticising the country on foreign platforms.Addressing the NDTV World Summit, Modi also called for reforms in global institutions, including the United Nations, to reflect changing geopolitical and economic realities, argued that the emerging world order must give the Global South greater representation, and said the global balance of power had changed significantly since World War II but the mechanisms governing international decision-making had failed to keep pace.“When the entire world is in search of a new order, some people are dreaming of disorder in India. Today, when there is so much disorder in the world, a strong picture of India should be presented to the world, but these people are interested only in ruining the reputation of the country. These people go abroad and defame India. They ask foreigners to intervene,” he said.“I don’t know how long the Congress will continue to put the country at stake for the launch of its failed product. Sriharikota does not see as many launches as the Congress tries, unsuccessfully, to launch its leader in a year. The party can do what it wants to ruin itself; we have no issue with that. But to save one family from the stain of failure, the Congress is now putting India’s achievements, India’s greatness and its development at stake,” he added.Also Read | PM Modi, Polish PM Donald Tusk agree to deepen cooperation in defence, space, nuclear energyHe also questioned the Congress’s leadership and electoral prospects, arguing that the party’s approach was undermining legitimate criticism of the government by allowing political rhetoric to overshadow substantive policy debates.“The Congress has become that parasite that does not want to let anyone succeed. The dimagi Naxals (intellectual Naxals) have taken over the Congress’s brain and hence it has lost the ability to think. The people who used to wreak havoc in the jungles have entered the Congress and are trying to destroy the country,” he added.He said the Congress was hurting even other opponents of the government. “The voices of those who want to oppose the government in a democratic manner are being suppressed... We have seen in Parliament how talented young MPs in the Opposition want to speak and criticise the government, but the Congress does not let the House run so that others do not get a chance. Because the Congress wants to keep only one person in the limelight,” he said.Also Read | CM Modi to PM Modi: A tale of continuity and evolutionProtests and the Political RowThe remarks came amid protests by the Cockroach Janta Party and the Opposition seeking the removal of Kumar and scrapping the controversial special intensive revision. The Bharatiya Janata Party has alleged the protesters are trying to destabilise constitutional bodies to deflect attention from their own political and electoral failures.Modi Calls for Reform of Global InstitutionsIn his speech, Modi also spoke about the changing world order. “The challenge is how to make such an order in the changing world in which new personalities get a place, global institutions are more influential, and there is a strong sense of unity among the nations,” he said.Modi argued that emerging economies and new centres of power needed a greater role in international institutions, warning that outdated arrangements risked weakening their ability to address contemporary challenges.The PM said global interconnectedness through trade, technology, maritime routes and cultural exchanges had also created new avenues for geopolitical competition. “Trade is becoming a means of weaponisation. Technology is becoming a new area of competition and conflict. Sea routes are becoming the centre of geopolitical tensions,” he said.Referring to the Covid-19 pandemic, Modi said the crisis exposed the limitations of international cooperation. Countries prioritised their own interests, undermining global trust, he said.Recalling his 2020 call for “a new world order for the collective well-being of humankind”, Modi said international arrangements must put humanity at their centre rather than allow narrow national interests to dominate.“India is a guarantee of stability,” Modi said, linking the country’s approach to international affairs with its historical experience and civilisational values.Also Read | Movements seeking improvements necessary in democracy, but Congress destroys even them: PM ModiModi cited India’s response to the Covid-19 pandemic, including the supply of vaccines and medicines to countries in need, as an example of international cooperation during a crisis.He also pointed to India’s presidencies of the G20 and Brics, saying the country had helped secure consensus among members despite differences over key issues and expectations of disagreements over summit declarations.The PM highlighted advances in green energy, artificial intelligence, digital payments and entrepreneurship, alongside developments in nuclear energy, hydrogen-powered transport and preparations for a digital census. He also referred to India’s non-fossil fuel electricity capacity as evidence of progress in the energy transition.Turning to sporting achievements, Modi mentioned India’s 85 medals at the Asian Games and progress in women’s cricket and boxing.

title: Chennai YouTuber arrested for allegedly abetting suicide of influencer
description: The accused allegedly posted defamatory videos targeting the influencer and threatened him in an attempt to extort money, a police official said.
content: A Chennai-based YouTuber has been arrested for allegedly extorting and threatening a 27-year-old social media influencer who was later found dead at his residence, police said on Thursday.The influencer, who hailed from Puducherry and had more than 1.4 million followers, was found dead at his rented home in Chennai on October 20. Police are investigating the death as a suspected suicide.The accused, Jason Samuel Vijayakumar, 30, allegedly posted defamatory videos targeting the influencer and threatened him in an attempt to extort money, a police official said.The accused also allegedly got the influencer's social media accounts blocked by Meta, the official said.According to the police, the influencer was facing pressure over his financial advice content, which he was allegedly accused of sharing without a licence from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).“He was under severe mental stress due to this and allegedly died by suicide by hanging himself at his residence on October 20,” the official said.A case was registered at Kanathur police station under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with abetment of suicide, following a complaint by the victim's father.Police said witness statements and documents collected during the investigation pointed to Vijayakumar's alleged role in the circumstances leading to the death.Vijayakumar was arrested on Thursday and remanded in judicial custody by a judicial magistrate after being produced before the court.

title: Power supply hit in Gurugram, Faridabad and Nuh as workers strike over privatisation
description: A strike by DHBVN workers disrupted power across three Haryana districts from Wednesday night, generating more than 3,000 complaints in 12 hours.
content: A strike by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) workers plunged Gurugram, Faridabad, and Nuh districts into darkness since 10 pm on Wednesday, affecting thousands of consumers and industrial units.The power department received more than 3,000 complaints of outages within 12 hours of the strike, an official said on condition of anonymity on Thursday.Also read: Power department staff begins 3-day strike against private discom in Gurugram, Nuh The employees had announced the strike to protest against the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission's decision to grant a parallel electricity distribution licence to a private company for Gurugram and Nuh districts.Gurugram Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh held a meeting with the employees till late at night, urging them to reconsider their decision. However, the talks proved inconclusive, and no agreement was reached to end the strike.Several industrial units in Gurugram came to a standstill due to prolonged power cuts, with many owners complaining of potential losses running to crores of rupees.Also read: Drought, water shortage: K'taka CM says people should be 'mentally' preparedDeepak Maini, an industrialist and the chairman of the Progressive Federation of Trade and Industry, said there had been no power supply at Gurugram's Sector-37 since 10 pm on Wednesday.Maini also expressed concern that any delay in the restoration of power supply could adversely affect production and business activities.He said that the availability of finished goods and the timely delivery of supplies could also be affected."Power cuts at industrial units have brought machinery and production to a halt, impacting business operations. With operations suspended across hundreds of units, the risk of losses has increased," Maini said.Also read: Haryana:Backdoor privatisation of power sector will be resisted, says AIPEF chairmanApart from Gurugram, industrial units in Kadipur and Basai were also affected by power cuts.Several residential colonies in Gurugram had to switch to generators as inverter backups ran out, residents said.In many areas, the breakdown of the power supply led to a shortage of drinking water. Residents say they are managing using water stored in tanks but claim that it will last only a few hours.Also read: States asked to assess resources before clearing data centres"Electricity and water are both essential services. Where is the government? Residents are held hostage by DHBVN staff. There has been no power since 10 pm yesterday. Either the government should settle employees' demands or depute the Disaster Management team to restore the supply. Officers are also showing helplessness. In such a situation, how will we come up with a solution?" said Shiv Kumar Sharma, a resident.In Faridabad, people in the New Industrial Township-2 area hit the streets, demanding restoration of power supply. They said the power cut also impacted water supply.Upon hearing information of a road blockade, police arrived at the scene and pacified the protesters, after which they were dispersed.Also read: Ludhiana industrial feeders face 5-hour cuts amid power shortageIn Nuh district, the power outage severely affected life in several areas, including Punhana, Nagina, and Firozpur Jhirka.Despite several attempts, the Superintending Engineer of the Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN), Operation Circle Gurugram-I, could not be contacted.

title: ‘Rahul Gandhi should become PM’: Revanth Reddy's appeal in Telangana
description: Reddy said the country was at a critical juncture and urged members of the Nehru family to take responsibility for its future.
content: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Thursday called for Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, to become prime minister, saying his leadership was necessary to secure justice for backward classes and steer the country towards progress.Addressing the 174th birth anniversary celebrations of Panduga Sayanna Mudiraj, a figure associated with the struggle for backward-class rights, Reddy said the Nehru family chose other leaders to head the government despite having opportunities to take the top post after Rajiv Gandhi's death, news agency PTI reported."Rahul Gandhi should become prime minister if justice is to be done to the backward classes. They could have become (PM) long ago had they wanted it. After Rajiv Gandhi's death, Congress came to power many times," he said.He also appealed to people to set aside their differences and make a positive choice when the next Lok Sabha elections are held.Telangana government considers Mudiraj community's BC-A statusReddy said his government was committed to strengthening the political representation of all backward-class communities. He announced that a cabinet sub-committee would be formed to examine the demand for including the Mudiraj community in the BC-A category.The community currently falls under the BC-D category in Telangana. According to Reddy, the matter would be taken up at the next cabinet meeting, with officials and legal experts consulted before a decision is made.He also asked Backward Classes Welfare Minister Ponnam Prabhakar to engage with other backward communities, including Gangaputras, who are already classified under BC-A, to address concerns about the distribution of reservation benefits.Revanth Reddy highlights caste survey and welfare measuresReferring to the caste survey conducted by his government, Reddy said the findings had enabled different communities to raise their concerns more effectively.He also highlighted the government's food distribution programme, contrasting it with the subsidised rice scheme introduced by former undivided Andhra Pradesh chief minister N T Rama Rao.While Rama Rao had launched a scheme providing rice at two rupees per kilogram, Reddy said his government was supplying fine-quality rice free of cost to 3.48 crore people through the Public Distribution System (PDS).He added that his government was continuing policies pursued by former chief ministers N Chandrababu Naidu and Y S Rajasekhara Reddy in undivided Andhra Pradesh, as well as K Chandrasekhar Rao after Telangana was formed.Statues of Telangana figures planned at Tank BundReddy also announced plans to install statues of prominent Telangana personalities, including Doddi Komuraiah and Panduga Sayanna, at Tank Bund on the banks of Hussain Sagar lake.Recalling Sayanna's legacy, he said the social figure had stood up for marginalised people when feudal landlords encroached on their lands during Nizam rule.Reddy said Sayanna was arrested by the Nizam's police, after which the queen of Wanaparthy Samsthanam, a feudal estate, paid a substantial amount to secure his release.He said Sayanna was killed unjustly and noted that songs celebrating his contributions continued to be sung during agricultural activities such as sowing, even more than a century after his death.(With inputs from PTI)

title: Upper caste activists gherao HP Secretariat; demand UGC notification rollback, Swaran Aayog
description: Panchayat and Rural Development Minister Anirudh Singh was deputed to talk to the protesters on Thursday.
content: Hundreds of Swaran (upper caste) community activists demanding the rollback of the UGC notification in January and the enactment of a Swaran Aayog gheraoed the Himachal Pradesh Secretariat on Thursday, prompting the police to resort to mild use of force.Protesters linked to the Rashtriya Devbhoomi Party and allied associations attempted to breach the state secretariat as the 21-day, 600-kilometre foot march 'Swarn Samaj Ashwamedh Nyay Yatra' reached the state capital Shimla.As the traffic came to a standstill in Chota Shimla, police deployed water cannons and used mild force to disperse the demonstrators.Panchayat and Rural Development Minister Anirudh Singh was deputed to talk to the protesters on Thursday. A meeting between the chief minister and the leaders spearheading the demonstration has also been scheduled for Friday.Rumit Singh Thakur, president of Rashtriya Devbhoomi Party, which organised the foot march, said the yatra received an overwhelming response, and called it a "victory for the entire society".He said they are grateful that no case was registered against the protesters.Also Read: Supreme Court directs UGC to issue public advisories on fake institutions after Etah medical college caseAlleging that both the BJP and the Congress governments in Himachal Pradesh have failed to address the issues raised by his party, Thakur cautioned that no political party would be able to win the 2027 Assembly elections without the support of Swaran Samaj, as the community constitutes a huge section of the state's population and wields tremendous influence in the society.He said Cabinet Minister Anirudh Singh was deputed to hold talks with the protesters, and this was no mean feat as he represents the government.Mahipal Singh Makrana, president of Rajput Karni Sena, which is also associated with the agitation, said, "Our main demand is rollback of the University Grants Commission (UGC) notification and the enactment of a law for Swaran Aayog."He said the provision of 15 per cent reservation for Scheduled Castes, 7.5 per cent for Scheduled Tribes, 27 per cent for Other Backward Classes and 4 per cent for Persons with Disabilities was a cruel joke on the Swaran Samaj and it will not be brooked.The University Grants Commission notified the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026 on January 13 this year to curb discrimination in Indian higher education. A Supreme Court bench stayed the operation of these regulations on January 29, 2026, observing that they appeared vague and were susceptible to misuse.Swaran Aayog refers to the demand of the upper caste community to constitute a state-level commission to study and address the economic, educational, and social challenges faced by economically weaker sections among members of the general category.Also Read: UGC-NET Row: NTA removes over 50 staff, fills 10 new leadership rolesMakrana further said, "We have been on the road for the last eight months, and such yatras are planned in all states. Four states are already covered; other major states would be covered in the coming days. A massive protest will be held in Delhi on January 10."He added, "These reservations have blocked the future of our children, who will not be able to get access to higher education institutions."Talking to mediapersons after receiving a memorandum from the agitators, Minister Anirudh Singh, who hails from a Royal family, said that in his personal opinion, an Aayog should be constituted for the Swaran community.The Himachal Pradesh government listens to the demands of all sections of people, he said, adding that the chief minister will meet leaders of the agitation on Friday.

title: Power department staff begins 3-day strike against private discom in Gurugram, Nuh
description: The Haryana Bijli Karamchari and Engineers Joint Sangharsh Morcha called for a strike after the power sector regulator granted a licence to a private firm.
content: Around 40,000 electricity department employees on Thursday began a three-day strike against the entry of a private power distribution company in Gurugram and Nuh, leading to disrupted supplies in several residential and industrial areas due to unattended breakdown complaints.The Haryana Bijli Karamchari and Engineers Joint Sangharsh Morcha called for a three-day strike after the state's power sector regulator, HERC, on October 19 granted a licence to a private company to supply electricity in Gurugram and Nuh districts along with the existing state-owned discoms.Around 40,000 electricity department employees have joined the strike, which saw a widespread impact across the state, disrupting electricity supply, water services, industrial production and several essential activities, the forum of employees' union said in a statement. Also read: ESMA: Chandigarh prohibits power firm staffers from going on strike for 6 monthsThe HERC, in an order dated October 19, granted a parallel electricity distribution licence to Eleven Power Private Limited for 25 years in both revenue districts under Section 14 of the Electricity Act, 2003.The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC), a three-member statutory body, is responsible for regulation of the power sector in the state. The state government, on the recommendation of a selection committee, appoints the chairperson and members of the commission.On Wednesday, Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini said the state government will represent the employees' case before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) against HERC's decision.Also read: Will challenge HERC’s decision to grant licence to pvt firm: SainiSaini said the government is ready to engage lawyers trusted by the power workers' unions to pursue the case.Saini also held a review meeting with administrative secretaries to assess arrangements for the three-day strike.Meanwhile, the Joint Front, representing the striking employees, said that with almost the entire workforce participating, numerous 33 kV and 11 kV feeders affected by breakdowns remained out of service.Electricity supply was disrupted in several urban and rural residential areas. Industrial production was also affected due to the disruption of power supply to industrial feeders.Electricity complaint centres, substations and offices at the sub-divisional, divisional and circle levels were largely deserted, the forum said.Also read: Haryana milk strike enters second day, milk supply remains unaffectedMost constituent organisations of the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, along with Sarv Karamchari Sangh Haryana and workers' organisations, including CITU, AITUC, INTUC, extended support to the strike and organised demonstrations at various locations.Subhash Lamba, vice president of the Electricity Employees Federation of India (EEFI), and Shailendra Dubey, Chairman of the All India Power Engineers Federation (AIPEF), also opposed the parallel distribution licence and expressed solidarity with the striking employees.Senior leader of the Joint Front, Devender Singh Hooda emphasised that electricity employees and engineers were not striking for higher salaries or allowances. Their struggle, he said, was aimed at protecting electricity distribution from privatisation and safeguarding the interests of farmers and ordinary consumers.Expressing regret over the hardships faced by consumers, he said the employees' struggle was intended to ensure access to affordable and reliable electricity for all.He appealed to farmers, consumers and the public to support the movement and press the government to revoke the parallel distribution licence.He warned that handing electricity distribution over to private companies could make power increasingly unaffordable for farmers and economically weaker sections in both rural and urban areas.Lamba of EEFI alleged that the Haryana government was attempting to undermine the strike by bringing technical employees and supervisors from neighbouring states, including Punjab and Himachal Pradesh.Questioning the government's position, Lamba asked: "If the chief minister and the energy minister oppose privatisation and stand with electricity employees, why is a parallel distribution licence being granted to a private company in the first place?"He argued that if legal obstacles stood in the way of stopping the licensing arrangement, the government should explore appropriate legal and legislative measures to resolve them, noting that the BJP governs both Haryana and the Centre.The EEFI leader said that the government must demonstrate its opposition to privatisation through concrete action rather than statements or assurances.Also read: Punbus, PRTC contractual workers continue strike as talks with govt failOn Thursday, Haryana Energy Minister Anil Vij said the strike is unnecessary as it is HERC's decision to grant a parallel electricity distribution licence to a private company.Vij said that he himself is against privatisation because so much public money and infrastructure have been invested, and employees' jobs are at stake.Therefore, the government opposed the move firmly, but the decision went against us. The government is now appealing against that decision in APTEL and is trying to obtain a stay against the regulatory commission's order as soon as possible, he said.He told the employees to leave the path of strike and join duties. "If you want to give any advice to our lawyer while preparing the case, give it. If you want to appoint your own lawyer, do so. Or if you want to suggest another lawyer, tell us, and we will hire that lawyer."Also read: Haryana sanitation workers extend strike, plans jan nyaya panchayats

title: Gangster who claimed responsibility in Tiger Shroff firing case named wanted accused
description: Pandit, a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, who had allegedly claimed responsibility for the on Tiger Shroff, has been named as a wanted accused in the case.
content: Gangster Anil Pandit, who had claimed responsibility for the firing on Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff has been named as a wanted accused in the case, police told a court on Thursday as it remanded four arrested persons to police custody till October 26.Pandit, a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang who is said to be operating from the US, had allegedly claimed responsibility for the October 18 attack on Shroff in a social media post.Also read: The firing on Shroff was carried out at Pandit's instructions, and he has been named as a wanted accused in the case, the police told the court. The Crime Branch of Mumbai Police on Thursday produced Kunal (21) and Sumit (19), both hailing from Haryana's Sonipat district, and Radha (23) and Babita (23), both from Uttar Pradesh, before the Esplanade Magistrate's court here. The firing on Shroff was carried out at Pandit's instructions, and he has been named as a wanted accused in the case, the police told the court.The investigators sought police custody of the four arrested accused, stating that they had actively participated in the conspiracy with those held earlier in the case.These four accused had supplied a weapon to the shooters, the police said.Also read: Tiger Shroff firing: Two women among four accused sent to police custody till Oct 26Kunal and Sumit collected a pistol and 20 rounds from Amritsar on Anil Pandit's instructions, while Radha and Babita travelled to Mumbai and handed over the weapon to other conspirators, the police said.Defence lawyers Ajinkya Mirgul and Satyavrat Joshi opposed the demand for custody, arguing that there was no material against these four accused and they had been arrested on mere suspicion.After hearing both sides, the court remanded the four accused in police custody till October 26.At least two men fired shots at Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area on the evening of October 18 before fleeing on a motorcycle. The actor escaped relatively unhurt, while his driver and a bystander were injured.Also read: Tiger Shroff firing suspect left Bihar two years ago, worked as a cook, bike-taxi driver: PoliceThe motorcycle was later found abandoned in suburban Andheri.Mumbai Police have registered a case of attempt to murder and arrested a total of 10 persons so far.On Wednesday, the court remanded Rehan alias Sukka, from Sonipat in Haryana; Ritik Kurmi alias Roshan, originally from Begusarai in Bihar and living in Mumbai; and Phool Singh from Haryana to police custody till October 31.Also read: After attack on Tiger Shroff, Maharashtra govt cracks down on bike taxis

title: PM Modi says Congress tarnishes India's image abroad: 'They seek intervention in internal affairs'
description: PM Modi also accused the Congress of undermining movements that sought to hold the government accountable and push for reforms.
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday took a jibe at the Congress, accusing the party of creating disorder and tarnishing India’s image abroad. He added that Congress leaders seek foreign intervention in India’s internal affairs, putting the country at risk to revive the political careers of its “failed leaders.”Addressing the NDTV World Summit 2026, PM Modi said, “Sriharikota sees fewer launches than the number of times Congress tried to launch its failed leaders in a single year.”"The Congress family has become a burden on its own party. Even the party’s own senior leaders admit to this,” he added.The BJP has time and again accused the Congress and LoP Rahul Gandhi of disrespecting India abroad. In 2023, the BJP slammed his speech at the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom. During his address there, Gandhi had alleged that Indian democracy was under attack and that the Opposition was facing “constant pressure” through what he described as unreasonable criminal cases.‘Congress has become a parasite’: PM ModiPM Modi, at the Summit, also accused the Congress of undermining movements that sought to hold the government accountable and push for reforms. He added that such movements were necessary in a democracy, alleging that the Opposition party was destroying them.“Movements that naturally seek to highlight the government’s shortcomings and bring about reforms in the system are also necessary in a democracy. But the Congress destroys these movements as well. It has become a parasite that does not want anyone else to move forward,” he said.He further accused the Congress party of sidelining young opposition leaders and keeping only one person in the limelight.“The Congress does not allow others to get an opportunity. It wants to keep only one person in the limelight and does not listen to the voices of young leaders in the opposition.”

title: ‘Congress is fine when it wins, blames BJP and EC when it loses’: Bhupender Yadav amid SIR row, anti-CEC stir | HT Interview
description: Bhupender Yadav defended the Election Commission’s SIR exercise, citing pending appeals by excluded voters.
content: Union minister and senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader Bhupender Yadav on Thursday said the Opposition’s intent in raising questions about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is not to correct irregularities in the poll process, but largely to destabilise Indian democracy.In an interview to HT, he said the Opposition’s bid was to discredit constitutional bodies, and discussed why the Mamata Banerjee government was ousted from West Bengal after 15 years in power. Edited excerpts:What is the government’s response to the Opposition’s serious charges of irregularities against the election commission over the conduct of SIR?The Opposition is frustrated with repeated loses in state after state. The Congress doesn’t believe in EVMs, which was introduced by them. They don’t believe in Parliament, in the Supreme Court when the verdict is not to their liking. They don’t believe in EC if the poll result is not to their liking.But the Congress has still not been able to invalidate the process of SIR.It won in Kerala, and supported the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) that won in Tamil Nadu. It has not explained how, if the SIR is so wrong, did the party win the elections. If the SIR was flawed, then why accept the result and the victory? They accept victories, but blame EC and the BJP for defeats.Also read: ‘Protests achieve nothing’: Amit Shah takes dig at Rahul Gandhi, says Congress won't win polls even in ‘30 years’They have made several allegations of irregularities against the CEC over how SIR is being done?They filed a case in the Supreme Court. The judgment clearly upheld and validated the proceedings of SIR, which is not being held for the first time. Between 1951 and 2004, it was conducted eight times and the current cycle which started in 2025 is the ninth. Of these eight-and-a-half cycles have been conducted during their tenure. Under Rule 25(2) of Registration of Electors Rules, during SIR, the electoral roll is to be prepared afresh for the correction of electoral rolls and the purpose is to update the voter list.The Congress’s aim is to shoot and scoot. EC asked them to submit a signed affidavit with the complaints so that the cases could be investigated. Rahul Gandhi or their BLAs (block level agents) never signed any affidavit. The President of India asked them to submit proof. They are yet to do that.The dynasts in the Congress believe they have a right to rule. Since they are unable to win fair and square, they want to discredit institutions and push people to take to the streets for a regime change. Indian democracy is far too strong and people are way too mature to fall for these gimmicks.Also read: HT interview: Congress not coming forward to talk on delimitation, says Kiren RijijuYou were the election-in-charge in West Bengal, where the BJP swept to power with a huge mandate for the first time. Almost 2.2 million people were disenfranchised in the state and filed petitions. Opposition leaders alleged that the exercise was rushed and opaque and targeted minorities and the marginalised.It was the so-called INDI alliance that asked for SIR, alleging voter rolls had issues. EC acted promptly and ordered SIR. In some states they won; in most states we won. They couldn’t digest this and started alleging foul play. It all started with blaming EVMs. In West Bengal, SIR was conducted by EC and monitored by the Supreme Court. And it was the TMC that won the 13 seats where the maximum number of voters were deleted.Mamata Banerjee lost because of a huge anti-incumbency wave and people had faith in the leadership of PM Narendra Modi ji to provide good governance.What about the voters who were barred from voting after EC marked them for discrepancies?During SIR, EC first publishes a draft roll. It is bound to issue a notice to anyone whose name is deleted. The reasons for deletion are death, migration, duplication, or wrong information. The appeals of those who were excluded are pending before the appellate tribunal created by SC. If people come forward to give their documents, I am sure EC will take corrective measures.Economist Surjit Bhalla in an analysis of SIR in Bengal said the 2004 electoral rolls had 2.8 crore more names than the estimated adult population-- an excess of 4.4% and in 2014, the roll was 3.1% higher than the adult population. We did not allege any electoral fraud, or question EC.The TMC appointed BLAs in every booth and government machinery was there, but where is their complaint? You participated in the exercise, used the state machinery in your favour, used muscle power and even then when you failed, you are blaming the Election Commission and SIR.It is not correct that only the minorities were left out; many Hindus who should have been protected by the provisions of the Citizenship Amendment Act were also excluded due to Mamata Banerjee's negligence.The BJP believes every eligible citizen should be able to vote. EC is mandated to ensure every eligible citizen has the right to vote and to ensure the removal of those who aren’t. Our institutions must be empowered to discharge their duties, not discredited because someone did not get a poll result they desired.Also read: INDIA bloc plans next round of protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in early NovemberWhat were the key factors for the TMC’s loss?Mamata Banerjee lost the election because of arrogance, anti-incumbency, social unrest, and the politics of appeasement. If you fail in the eyes of the public because of your misgovernance, you cannot pin the blame on concocted reasons, especially those that imperil your Constitutional institutions.The post-election scenario was intriguing. How did the 20 lawmakers reach out to the BJP and what were their concerns?Mamata Banerjee lost the confidence of Bengal’s voters and her own party. The anti-incumbency was both within and outside of the party. She came to power in Bengal against the authoritarian rule of the Left. Over time, she became an authoritarian CM. People felt suffocated and so did the people in her party.Adding to that the fact the TMC was not a party rooted in ideology, Mamata gave preference to family over senior party members. There was always disgruntlement in the party.Also read: PM Modi says Congress tarnishes India's image abroad: 'They seek intervention in internal affairs'There is another set of assembly elections coming up. In UP, which is crucial for the BJP, the Opposition’s main planks are vote chori, chanda chori in Ayodhya and anti-incumbency.The BJP is working hard on the ground, the organisational activities as decided by the national president, Nitin Nabin, are underway. The improved law and order situation in the state, the credibility of chief minister Yogi Adityanath and the leadership of PM Modi are there for all to see. There is no impact of the Opposition’s attempts to create any narrative. What matters is how in the last 12 years governance has become the main poll plank.Look at states such as Telangana where the Congress and Chhattisgarh where the JMM also announced social welfare schemes but corruption hampered delivery. The NDA, on the other hand, has been successful in the delivery of pro-poor schemes.In the past 12 years, the BJP-led NDA government announced and successfully implemented pro-poor policies. In the second term, major reforms through legislative action such as the GST rollout, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, Direct Benefit Transfer happened. In the third term there is a more proactive push for reforms, the PM has called it the “reform express”. So, this is the core of Indian politics now. The issues raised by the Opposition are just to discredit constitutional bodies, which are highly respected worldwide.

title: Movements seeking improvements necessary in democracy, but Congress destroys even them: PM Modi
description: PM Modi accused the Congress of keeping only one person in the limelight and ignoring the voices of young opposition leaders.
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday accused the Congress of undermining movements that sought to hold the government accountable and push for reforms.At the NDTV World Summit, Modi said such movements were necessary in a democracy but accused Congress of undermining them. He also criticised the party for disrupting Parliament and claimed “dimagi naxals” had taken control of their minds.“Movements that naturally seek to highlight the government’s shortcomings and bring about reforms in the system are also necessary in a democracy. But the Congress destroys these movements as well. It has become a parasite that does not want anyone else to move forward,” Modi said."Dimagi naxals have seized control of Congress's mind to such an extent that Congress has lost the ability to think for itself. Those who used to destroy in the forests are now infiltrating Congress and are engaged in the complete ruin of the country,” the PM said.He accused the Congress of sidelining young opposition leaders and keeping only one person in the limelight. “The Congress does not allow others to get an opportunity. It wants to keep only one person in the limelight and does not listen to the voices of young leaders in the opposition,” he said.His remarks come amid a series of protests in Delhi over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, demands for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and restrictions on the right to demonstrate. Modi's ‘angoor khatte hai’ jibe at CongressModi also mocked the Congress’s attempts to promote its leadership, comparing them with rocket launches from Sriharikota.“I don’t know how long Congress will continue putting the country’s interests at stake to launch its failed product. In a year, there are not as many launches from Sriharikota as the number of failed attempts Congress makes to launch its leader,” he said.He also accused the party of putting India’s reputation at stake to protect its leadership. “Congress can continue on its path of decline; we have no problem with that. But to protect its family from repeated failures, it is putting the country’s reputation on trial. The grapes are so sour that Congress is trying to cut down the very vine that bears them,” Modi said.Rahul Gandhi leads protests against CEC, SIRCongress leader and Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi has led protests against Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls this month. The Congress and other opposition parties have alleged irregularities in the electoral process and demanded accountability from the Election Commission.On October 6, Gandhi joined INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Trinamool Congress leader Derek O’Brien and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, in a march towards the Election Commission’s office. They demanded Kumar’s resignation and opposed the SIR exercise. Police stopped the march and detained several opposition leaders after a confrontation at the barricades.During the protest, Gandhi climbed a police barricade and held a placard that read, “Gyanesh, it’s done bro!” He later posted the same message on X, adding, “It’s time to resign.”On October 12, Gandhi led another INDIA bloc demonstration, called the “March for Democracy”, towards the Supreme Court. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Samajwadi party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other opposition leaders also joined the march.The protests form part of the opposition’s “vote chori” campaign, which alleges irregularities in the electoral process. The Election Commission has said the SIR exercise aimed to update voter lists, remove duplicate and ineligible entries, and ensure that eligible voters remain on the rolls.Student groups, including AISA, and youth organisations have protested in Delhi over the SIR exercise, alleging that 13 crore eligible voters’ names could be deleted and demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.On October 10, police barricaded Jantar Mantar, forcing CJP and student protesters to gather at other locations, including Connaught Place and Raj Ghat. Police dragged and detained protesters and journalists.Demonstrators also opposed the removal of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and the shift to alternative venues that require booking fees. SFI, DYFI and IYC also held protests, demanding accountability from the Election Commission and space for peaceful demonstrations.

title: Delhi HC refuses to stay release of Sourav Ganguly-inspired film Doosra
description: The Delhi high court declines to stay the release of Doosra: India’s Other Freedom Struggle after Sourav Ganguly and Luv Films challenge its release.
content: The Delhi high court on Thursday declined to stay the release of “Doosra: India’s Other Freedom Struggle”, a Hindi sports drama inspired by former India cricket captain Sourav Ganguly, which is scheduled to hit theatres on Friday.“I have said no stay, so the film can go on,” Justice Dinesh Bhatt said.The court was hearing a petition filed by former India cricket captain Sourav Ganguly and Luv Films LLP to restrain the release of the film, citing the unauthorised use of events from the former cricketer’s life, particularly his captaincy in the NatWest cricket series final and his shirtless celebration at Lord’s.The suit, argued by senior advocate Balbir Singh, alleged that Doosra amounted to the unauthorised commercial exploitation of Sourav Ganguly’s personality rights and infringed Luv Films’ exclusive contractual rights over his proposed biopic.It contended that the film used the former cricketer’s name, image, likeness and iconic cricketing moments without his consent or a licence.According to the suit, Ganguly entered into an agreement with Luv Films on August 5, 2021, granting the production house exclusive rights to develop, produce and commercially exploit audiovisual content, including a biographical film based on his life and cricketing career.Luv Films claimed to have made substantial investments in the authorised biopic, titled Dada – The Sourav Ganguly Story, which is scheduled for release on May 14, 2027.The suit further stated that the trailer and promotional campaign for Doosra, launched on October 12, prominently referenced
