Ganguly’s leadership of the Indian cricket team and its historic victory in the 2002 NatWest Series final at Lord’s.It also cited an October 13 interview in which Deo discussed how the 2002 final and milestones in Ganguly’s career had influenced the film’s fictional character, Tara.However, Deo’s lawyer Saurabh Kirpal argued that the movie was not a biopic of former India captain Sourav Ganguly, but the story of a girl from Rajasthan who draws inspiration from him. Kirpal further submitted that the filmmakers had obtained a licence from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to use footage from the NatWest Series, contending that Ganguly had no rights over the footage itself.The matter will be heard again on Friday.

title: Govt proposes mandatory automatic emergency braking in new car models from October 2030
description: The road ministry's draft rules propose AEBS for new car models from October 2030 and all existing models still in production from October 2032.
content: The Road Ministry has proposed mandating Advanced Emergency Braking Systems (AEBS) for all new car models starting October 2030 to curb road accidents.The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), in a draft notification dated October 19, 2026, said that for pre-2030 still-in-production models, AEBS would be mandatory from October 2032.Also Read: MoRTH pushes for an intelligent and clean constructionAEBS provides automatic braking in the event of failure of the driver to respond to emergency situations to either avoid a crash or reduce the impact of a collision."Provided that, M1 category of vehicles manufactured on and after 1st October 2030 in the case of new models and 1st October 2032 in the case of all models shall be fitted with Advanced Emergency Braking System, conforming to AIS-185, as amended from time to time," the draft notification said.Also Read: MoRTH mandates automatic load covers for tippers, dumpers from April 2027The government has mandated multiple measures, especially focused on braking systems, to enhance the safety of medium and heavy-duty vehicles.To enhance brake performance, a revised braking standard has been mandated for trucks effective October 1, 2027.Also Read: ‘Results visible next winter’: MoRTH secy on Delhi-NCR fleet renewal schemeBraking systems have been advanced with the mandatory implementation of electronic stability control systems (AIS 162) for trucks from October 1, 2027, which provide stability, especially in the event of braking at curves.The draft rules will be taken into consideration after the expiry of thirty days from the date on which the copies of this notification, as published in the Gazette of India, are made available to the public.

title: ‘Was Indira Gandhi summoned?’: Jaishankar questions criticism over his Mumbai meet with Marco Rubio
description: Reiterating his argument, Jaishankar asked why meetings held outside the national capital should be viewed as a sign that a leader had been summoned.
content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Thursday questioned the criticism surrounding his meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Mumbai, responding to Rahul Gandhi's description of the visit as a “summons”.Speaking at the NDTV World Summit, Jaishankar said he could not understand why the meeting had triggered such a reaction. He also questioned the criticism of Mumbai as the venue for the interaction with the US official.“I failed to get it,” the minister said, adding, “They don't like Mumbai. They have something against Mumbai. It's our financial capital. It's our Bollywood capital. It has got so much going for it. Maybe Mumbai doesn't like them. I have no idea. Why they have this reservation,” Jaishankar said.Also read | Marco Rubio’s visit: Catalyst for a new era of diplomacyJaishankar added that if travelling outside Delhi to meet a foreign leader or counterpart was considered a summoning, he could cite several such instances. He referred to former prime minister Indira Gandhi's visit to Shimla to meet Pakistan's then president Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, questioning whether she too had been summoned on that occasion.His remarks came in response to Rahul Gandhi's characterisation of his Mumbai visit to meet Rubio as a “summoning”.Jaishankar cites Indira Gandhi's meeting with BhuttoThe 71-year-old minister argued that travelling outside Delhi to meet foreign leaders was not unusual. He cited instances from the Congress's own history to counter the criticism.Also read | ‘Very, very close’: Marco Rubio on India-US trade deal after meeting with EAM JaishankarJaishankar referred to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's meeting with Pakistan's Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in Shimla in 1972, where the two leaders signed the Shimla Agreement. He also mentioned former External Affairs Minister Salman Khurshid hosting a lunch for Pakistan Prime Minister Raja Pervez Ashraf in Jaipur.“If going out of Delhi to meet a foreign leader or a foreign counterpart is summoning, I can give you a lot of examples. Mrs Gandhi went to Shimla to meet Bhutto. Was she summoned? Salman Khurshid went to Jaipur to meet a Pakistan PM; was he summoned?” he asked.Earlier, on October 16, Rahul Gandhi took a swipe at the government over US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s meeting with government officials in Mumbai, claiming that officials of the external affairs ministry were “confused” over it.“Mr Rubio has summoned his employee to Mumbai. Modi ji, your officials in the External Affairs Ministry are confused about what’s going on. You might want to explain. Unless, of course, you want me to,” Gandhi said in a post on X.

title: At least 6 killed, 40 injured as passenger bus crashes into tree in Chhattisgarh’s MCB district
description: Six people were killed and 40 injured after a bus crashed into a roadside tree on the Manendragarh-Kelhari road in Chhattisgarh’s MCB district. CM Vishnu Deo Sai announced compensation.
content: At least six people were killed and 40 others injured after a passenger bus carrying 46 people crashed into a roadside tree in Chhattisgarh’s Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur (MCB) district on Thursday, police said.The accident took place shortly after noon near the Semarmathani turn on the Manendragarh-Kelhari road when the bus was travelling towards Kelhari, a police officer said, adding that four of the injured were in critical condition.Superintendent of police (SP) Ratna Singh said passengers told her that the driver lost control of the steering, following which the bus crashed into the roadside tree.“Six passengers, including four women, died in the accident. Around 20 people, including the driver, suffered serious injuries, while another 20 sustained minor injuries,” Singh said.Police identified the deceased as Panchram (70), Madhu and Neha, all three residents of Rojhi village; bus owner Sipahi Lal from Kelhari; Sangeeta from Gudru village in Kelhari; and Sukaron (80) from Kelhari.The injured were taken to hospitals in Manendragarh and Chirmiri. Two seriously injured passengers were referred to Ambikapur for better medical treatment, while two others were shifted to the district hospital in Chirmiri, police officers said. Chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai expressed grief over the deaths and directed the district administration to ensure proper treatment of the injured. The state government will provide ₹5 lakh each to the families of the deceased and ₹50,000 each to those injured, Sai said.Police said an FIR will be registered and action will be taken against those found responsible after the investigation.

title: ‘Resolve things through dialogue’: Uttarakhand CM speaks to Mika Singh amid Daler Mehndi's event row
description: The controversy centres on a public confrontation between Uttarakhand cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal and singer Daler Mehndi during a Navratri event.
content: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami spoke to singer Mika Singh over the phone on Thursday amid the controversy surrounding his brother, singer Daler Mehndi, and state cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal. Dhami said “any misunderstanding or difference of opinion should be resolved through dialogue and in a cordial atmosphere”.Officials aware of the matter said Dhami emphasised the importance of communication and mutual understanding during the conversation.“Uttarakhand has always followed the principle of ‘Atithi Devo Bhava’ and welcomed guests with warmth and respect,” the chief minister said. He added artists from across the country and the world are welcome in the state and are be treated with due respect. “In ‘Devbhoomi’ Uttarakhand, artists from across the country and the world are welcomed and respected wholeheartedly. The state government remains firmly committed to honouring art, culture and artists,” Dhami said.Earlier in the day, during a press conference, Dhami had said he would speak to both Mika Singh and Daler Mehndi over the controversy, which has drawn attention across the country. Asked about the confrontation between Uniyal and Daler Mehndi, Dhami said the minister had already addressed the matter.“Look, I believe that since there was likely pressure from the public at the time—and the honourable minister, Subodh Uniyal, stated yesterday that he was unaware of Daler Mehndi’s poor health—the minister himself has already come forward to address it,” Dhami said.The chief minister said the artists involved were accomplished personalities and stressed that Uttarakhand respected writers, artists and scholars.“Given the circumstances that arose due to public pressure at the time, and since the minister has already issued a statement clarifying that he had no such intent, I believe it is time to bring this matter to a close,” Dhami said.Asked about Mika Singh’s appeal to him to take action against Uniyal, Dhami said he would speak to both brothers. “I will first speak with Mika. I will also speak with Daler Mehndi. I will talk to both of them—I am friends with both,” the chief minister said.What happened at the Kunjapuri MelaThe controversy erupted on Sunday night, October 18, at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair, popularly known as the Kunjapuri Mela, in Narendra Nagar, Tehri Garhwal district, where Daler Mehndi was performing as part of the Navratri celebrations.Cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal walked onto the stage, interrupted the singer and publicly reprimanded him, accusing him of lip-syncing instead of singing live and claiming he was unable to speak or perform properly. Uniyal also alleged that Mehndi was under the influence of alcohol and reportedly pointed out that he had received an advance payment of ₹35 lakh.The minister later defended his actions, saying an artist who was unwell or unfit to perform should have declined the engagement. There has been no verification to establish that Mehndi was intoxicated.Mika Singh seeks apologyOn Wednesday, Mika Singh appealed for an apology in an Instagram post, thanking singers, fans, friends, family and well-wishers for their support.“My point is simple: Daler Mehndi ji does not drink alcohol, and making such allegations against him is completely wrong,” Mika Singh wrote.He questioned the public reprimand of a renowned artist on stage, drawing a comparison with how scolding a child in school or college can become a major issue.“I believe an apology is due. The person responsible should acknowledge that the allegations about Daler Mehndi ji drinking alcohol were wrong and apologise for the way he was treated,” he said.

title: PM Modi, Polish PM Donald Tusk agree to deepen cooperation in defence, space, nuclear energy
description: India and Poland agree to deepen defence, space and nuclear energy ties, with PM Narendra Modi and Donald Tusk targeting a doubling of bilateral trade to $12 billion by 2030.
content: India and Poland on Thursday agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk focused on leveraging the economic growth of both countries to achieve the shared target of doubling trade from the current level of around $6 billion by 2030.Bilateral ties got a major boost with Modi’s visit to Warsaw in 2024, the first by an Indian PM in 45 years, and defence and security have emerged as a key area for cooperation as Poland is currently engaged in the largest military modernisation campaign in Europe**, spending** almost 5% of its GDP on its armed forces against the backdrop of the war in Ukraine.Modi described his discussions with Tusk as “excellent” and said on social media that the two leaders discussed bolstering cooperation in trade, investment, defence, nuclear energy, space and critical minerals. Regional and global issues also figured in the talks, and Indian officials said the Polish side appreciated India’s recent proposal for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire.“Today, we agreed to deepen our cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to partner with India in co-development and co-production,” Modi said at a media interaction with Tusk.Tusk added, “We are very aware of political threats and the need to become independent as much as possible in the area of…minerals and strategic resources…to make sure that Poland and India are independent in those areas.”India and Poland, Modi said, have emerged as centres of growth and technology at a time of uncertainty and change. “Last year, Poland’s GDP crossed the historic milestone of $1 trillion…Meanwhile, India recorded an impressive growth rate of 7.8% in the last quarter,” he said, noting that the proposed India-European Union (EU) trade deal will open new opportunities for India to export machinery, chemicals, plastics and engineering goods to Poland.“At the same time, we will seek new investments from Poland in sectors such as railways and mobility, advanced manufacturing, food processing and biotechnology,” Modi said, adding that Tusk was accompanied by a large business delegation that would focus on developing trusted supply chains to achieve the shared goal of doubling trade by 2030.The two sides will also develop new partnerships in critical minerals and coal gasification using Polish expertise, and establish a bilateral “startup bridge” to build on cooperation in AI, cybersecurity and fintech, Modi said.The business delegation of almost 100 Polish companies will participate in two business forums in New Delhi and Bengaluru to explore collaboration in defence, agri-tech, food processing, pharmaceuticals, mining, technology and infrastructure. Two-way trade is currently worth $6.3 billion, and Indian investments in Poland have grown to $3 billion, with Indian IT companies having a significant presence.Tusk noted that the two countries were able to build synergy as they have no conflicts of interest or historical issues that divide them. He also lauded Modi’s role on the global stage, describing it as a “beacon of hope” at a time of destabilisation and political uncertainty.He pointed to growing defence cooperation between the two sides and said: “Our drones were very useful…recently and I am convinced that cooperation in satellites and drones has helped our countries in times of political tensions and crises.”Tusk’s comments were an apparent reference to the use of Polish loitering munitions or drones by India’s military against Pakistan during Operation Sindoor, the campaign launched last year that targeted terrorist infrastructure on Pakistani soil in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack. Poland’s WB Group supplied 100 units of Warmate loitering munitions to the Indian Army in 2022, and Polish officials said earlier this year that the army had signed three more defence contracts.Poland is also eyeing tie-ups with Indian manufacturers of munitions to replenish ammunition stocks depleted by supplies provided to Ukraine since the start of the Russian invasion in 2022. However, some Polish firms have concerns about India’s long-standing military ties with Russia, and New Delhi and Warsaw are finalising an agreement on secure information exchanges to boost defence industrial cooperation.Sibi George, secretary (West) in the external affairs ministry, told a media briefing that the two sides were working on an agreement on mutual protection and exchange of classified information that was expected to build on the growing trust between India and the EU in areas such as defence and technology. With both countries eyeing joint development and production of military gear, it was important to have agreements in place to ensure trust and confidentiality, he said.The two sides also agreed to establish a defence industry dialogue and a counter-terrorism dialogue, George said. The security and defence partnership concluded by India and the EU earlier this year provides an additional framework for strategic cooperation with Poland in defence, counter-terrorism, technology, cybersecurity, space and shipbuilding, he said.Modi also referred to his discussions with Tusk on regional and global issues and said: “Whether in Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace.”George said Poland was “very appreciative” of India’s approach to finding a diplomatic solution to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and Modi’s recent call to Russian President Vladimir Putin to move from “endless war to the end of war”. He added that India had shared ideas with Russia and Ukraine, including the safety and security of commercial shipping, exports of grains and energy, and “non-attack possibilities”.Modi and Tusk both highlighted people-to-people ties, including the role played by the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur in providing refuge to thousands of Polish children and families during World War II, and the assistance provided by Polish authorities in evacuating thousands of Indian students from Ukraine in 2022. Poland is currently home to around 30,000 Indians, including 3,500 students.

title: Any fresh impeachment motion to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar will follow due process: Om Birla
description: The Opposition has been leading protests against Kumar and has met President Droupadi Murmu.
content: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Thursday said any fresh impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar would be examined in accordance with the laid-down procedures, amid Opposition protests demanding his removal over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“We will follow the process when the motion is moved. Just as there is a procedure for the impeachment of judges, there is a process laid down for the CEC too… It will be followed if the opposition moves a motion,” Birla said at a press conference ahead of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum, which India is hosting.Follow here for live updatesOpposition demands removal of CECThe Opposition has been leading protests against Kumar and has met President Droupadi Murmu, demanding his removal and the repeal of the 2023 law that provides immunity to the CEC and Election Commissioners. It has accused the CEC of the “unilateral and arbitrary exercise of the collective powers” during the ongoing revision of electoral rolls. The Opposition has made two attempts to remove Kumar. The notices submitted in the first attempt were rejected by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, while those submitted in the second attempt are pending.Under the law, the CEC can be removed by Parliament through a process similar to the impeachment of a Supreme Court judge. The CEC or an Election Commissioner may also resign by submitting a written resignation to the President.Responding to speculation that the government may convene a special session of Parliament to introduce and pass the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill and the Delimitation Bill to implement 33% reservation for women in legislatures, Birla declined to comment on whether such a session was planned.He said the process of proroguing Parliament was explicitly laid down in the Constitution and that there had been instances of long intervals between the adjournment of a session and the proroguing of the House.“This is not the longest duration (between the adjournment and proroguing)... Article 85 of the Constitution clearly states the rules for proroguing the House,” he said.Also Read | Monsoon session adjourned in August, it still hasn’t officially closed: What that means for Parliament and governmentParliament adjourned on August 13The Monsoon session was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has not yet been prorogued. Article 85 empowers the President to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament, or dissolve the Lok Sabha, on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers. While it requires that no more than six months elapse between two sessions, it does not specify a deadline for proroguing a House.According to a person aware of the details, the government needs to give 15 days’ notice before convening a full session and at least three days’ notice for a special session. Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said earlier this week that there had been several instances in the past when both Houses had not been prorogued for extended periods, including for periods of up to 87 days.Also Read | INDIA bloc plans next round of protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in early NovemberDisqualification petitions against rebel TMC MPsOn the petitions seeking the disqualification of rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), a registered, unrecognised regional party, Birla said the matter was being examined.“The petitions are being heard in the (Supreme) Court and they are also being heard in my court… Both sides are being heard and the proceedings are underway. As soon as we receive their response, we will expedite the process,” he said.A TMC faction had petitioned Birla under the leadership of its national general secretary, Abhishek Banerjee, seeking the immediate disqualification of the rebel lawmakers, arguing that their merger amounted to “voluntarily giving up party membership”.Birla also expressed hope that the two-day BRICS Parliamentary Forum, beginning October 26, would adopt a joint declaration by consensus and discuss issues of global concern, including terrorism and climate change.“India’s position has consistently been against terrorism, and we have always condemned it at every level. I hope there will be a detailed discussion on this issue within BRICS as well. Terrorism must end in every country,” he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend the event and meet leaders of visiting delegations, Birla said. While Saudi Arabia and Ethiopia are yet to confirm their participation, 18 countries have submitted suggestions for the forum, which will be taken up during the deliberations.

title: Houthis say they tried to rescue 14 Indians from boat in Red Sea, allege attack by Saudi Arabia
description: Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the boat was attacked close to the Bab el-Mandeb strait, a key global shipping route.
content: Yemen’s Houthi rebels on Thursday said they were trying to rescue 14 Indians aboard a boat that came under attack near Jabal Zuqar island in the Red Sea. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the boat was attacked near the island, close to the Bab el-Mandeb strait, a key global shipping route, Reuters reported.He blamed Saudi Arabia for the attack.This comes amid fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Two people were killed, including one Indian national, and eight were injured, including two Indians, HT reported earlier. ALSO READ | ‘Unacceptable’: India slams Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia, moves to help stranded pilgrims Saudi Aramco asks staff to evacuate headquartersSaudi state oil giant Aramco has asked employees to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely, six people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday. The reason for the evacuation remains unclear.This follows a series of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, targeting energy infrastructure and airports. Houthi spokesperson Saree said the group launched attacks on Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu and the Saudi defence ministry in Riyadh. Saudi authorities have not confirmed the claims.The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted drones over Riyadh and Medina on Thursday.India condemns attacks on Saudi ArabiaIndia on Thursday condemned the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and expressed solidarity with the kingdom.ALSO READ | Indian national among 2 killed in attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Fahd airport“We strongly condemn the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oilfield in the Eastern Province on October 21,” the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement.The ministry described the attacks as “completely unacceptable” and called for them to stop immediately. It also expressed condolences to the family of the Indian national killed in Dammam and wished those injured a speedy recovery.The Indian embassy in Riyadh is in touch with Saudi authorities and providing assistance to affected Indian nationals.India working to bring back stranded pilgrimsIndia is also working with airlines and tour operators to facilitate the return of pilgrims stranded in Saudi Arabia after Indian carriers suspended flights amid the escalation in hostilities.External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said around 3,000 stranded Indian pilgrims had returned to India on available flights over the previous week. More than 10,000 other pilgrims had also returned during the same period.ALSO READ | Brent crude oil hits highest since May as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia fuel global oil supply fears“Arrangements are being discussed to facilitate the return of other Umrah pilgrims at the earliest,” Jaiswal said.He added that Indian missions in Riyadh and Jeddah, with the support of community volunteers, were providing assistance to the pilgrims.Oil prices rise amid fears of supply disruptionThe escalating conflict has unsettled energy markets, with Brent crude futures rising to $111.88 a barrel on Thursday after touching $112.55 earlier in the session, their highest level since May 18.Saudi Arabia’s benchmark stock index fell 2.5% on Thursday following reports of the evacuation at Aramco’s headquarters, according to LSEG data.The renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has ended a United Nations-brokered truce that largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022.

title: ‘Deprived of democracy’: Wangchuk says cancelled home ministry meeting has broken Ladakh’s trust
description: Sonam Wangchuk accuses the Centre of denying Ladakh democracy after a home ministry meeting was cancelled.
content: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Thursday accused the Centre of keeping Ladakh “deprived of democracy” and treating it as a “controversial area” by keeping it a Union Territory without a legislature.The statements came after a Union home ministry meeting scheduled for Thursday with Ladakh leaders in the national capital did not take place. Wangchuk said the cancellation, with no reason given, had prompted the region’s leadership to consider taking its case to the United Nations".Also Read | ‘Undeclared emergency’: Sonam Wangchuk slams Centre over leaders’ arrest in Delhi‘Meeting is not happening’: Wangchuk“We were told with complete determination that we will meet in Delhi on the 22nd of October,” Wangchuk told the media in New Delhi. “We made our plans and bought our tickets. Today I am here, and the meeting is not happening. The country should know how the hopes of Ladakh have been ruined again and again.”The stalemate is the latest turn in a long dispute over Ladakh’s political future. The region has been a UT without an elected assembly since 2019, governed by a lieutenant governor. Talks with the home ministry resumed after violence and arrests in Leh on September 24, 2025, and Wangchuk said he spent six months in jail in Jodhpur. The Leh Apex Body (LAB) and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) have since pressed for statehood or, failing that, a UT with a legislature and constitutional safeguards.The government has not publicly explained why the October 22 meeting was called off, and its version was not available at the time of publication.The talks between the government and leaders of the UT have gone through three rounds this year.

title: ‘Nothing wrong with regime change’, Neha Bora tells Delhi HC; cops counter her
description: Neha Bora was detained during a protest at Mandi House last week and released after approximately 12 hours.
content: There is “nothing wrong" in regime change in a democracy, All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora's lawyer told the Delhi High Court on Thursday. The submissions came after the Delhi Police's counsel alleged she was part of a gathering where people called for a change in government. The court was hearing her plea challenging a Delhi Police notice asking her to furnish a ₹10,000 “peace bond”. During the hearing, the Delhi Police alleged that Bora was part of a gathering where activist Prashant Bhushan called for “regime change.”As Bora's lawyer defended the call for a regime change, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Delhi Police, said, “Regime change will happen by votes, not by lumpen elements congregating in New Delhi.” ALSO READ | 'Not involved with CJP's protest call': Neha Bora to Delhi HC on Oct 16 detentionThe Delhi High Court later reserved its verdict on Bora’s plea. Justice Prasad said the order would be pronounced at 6 pm on Friday.The petition challenges a notice issued by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) in New Delhi district on October 17, the day Bora was released after being detained during a protest on October 16. The notice directed her to appear before the magistrate and execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 with one surety.Delhi Police cites alleged repeated violationsDuring the hearing, Sharma argued that the notice was issued after an independent assessment of the material available to the authorities.The ASG told the court that the complete records had been placed before the magistrate before the notice was issued. He alleged that Bora had repeatedly violated restrictions, citing 12 instances of violations.The law officer also alleged that Bora was part of a gathering where statements calling for regime change were made alongside Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders and activist Prashant Bhushan.ALSO READ | AISA president Neha Bora moves Delhi HC, challenges police notice to execute bond“There is nothing wrong in regime change in a democracy,” Bora’s counsel, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, argued. Sharma opposed the submission, reiterating that regime change must happen through votes and not through “lumpen elements” gathering in New Delhi.The ASG said that the case involved substantial material and that the proceedings were preventive in nature, aimed at maintaining public peace. He said the authorities had considered information from a police sub-inspector, past FIRs and the prevailing situation before issuing the notice.Sharma also disputed Bora’s contention that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were not in force in the relevant area. He alleged that police personnel were outnumbered during the incident and that Bora did not stop when asked to do so.The court questioned whether there was material beyond the kalandra -- a police report placed before the magistrate in preventive proceedings -- to support the notice. The ASG subsequently handed over additional documents to the bench.ALSO READ | Who is Neha Bora? AISA president at centre of anti-CEC, SIR protests breaking internetThe court also asked whether a lawyer could represent Bora before the magistrate. Sharma said she could appear herself, attend with a lawyer or send a lawyer to represent her.The Delhi Police maintained that the notice had not itself resulted in a bond being executed or any penal consequences being imposed, and that Bora had been given the option of appearing through counsel.Court flags implications for personal libertyDuring the hearing, the bench raised concerns about the stigma attached to proceedings that require a person to furnish a bond for good behaviour.The court observed that Bora’s grievance stemmed from being treated as someone likely to disturb the peace and being asked to undertake to behave properly even before the proceedings had concluded.“Concern of the petitioner is that I am already branded as a bad boy and asked to say you shall be a good boy,” the bench observed, as per LiveLaw.Why Neha Bora challenged the noticeIn her petition, filed through advocate Abhik Chimni, Neha Bora argued that the notice was ambiguous, factually incorrect and violated her fundamental rights under Articles 19 and 21 of the Constitution.She contended that the notice did not provide sufficient material to establish the likelihood of a breach of peace. It also did not specify the period, occasion or event in connection with which such a breach was apprehended, her petition said.Representing Bora, Sankaranarayanan also said that she was not involved in the separate protest called by the CJP at Central Park in Connaught Place on October 16.“She is not involved with the CP Central Park call, and she was dealing with her own call at Mandi House,” the senior advocate told the court.The police notice cited alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests near Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders, and allegations that Bora had instigated people to join a protest at Connaught Place.What happened on October 16Bora was detained on October 16 after starting a flag march with AISA activists from Mandi House demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar for irregularities in the voting system. She was released at around 6 am the following day, after being held for approximately 12 hours.The developments came amid protests by the CJP, founded by Abhijeet Dipke. The party’s co-convenors, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had been arrested after unfurling the national flag at Jantar Mantar and were subsequently sent to five days of judicial custody, that later extended to two more days. Dipke announced a flag march at Connaught Place following their arrest.(With inputs from Shruti Kakkar)

title: Karnataka CM Shivakumar orders probe after police stop 3 Dalit ministers at Mysuru Palace Dasara puja
description: Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar orders an inquiry after police stop three Dalit ministers at Mysuru Palace during Dasara puja, triggering a political row over social justice.
content: Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar on Thursday ordered an inquiry into the stopping of three Dalit ministers by police at Mysuru Palace during the Nandi Dhwaja puja, after the BJP and Janata Dal (Secular) accused the Congress government of insulting Dalit representatives and questioned its commitment to social justice.Superintendent of Police C B Rishyanth, deployed for security at the celebrations, stopped ministers Shivaraj Tangadagi, P M Narendraswamy and K S Basavanthappa, who were following Shivakumar for the ritual preceding the Mysuru Dasara procession on Wednesday.Shivakumar, however, intervened and allowed the ministers to enter.Kannada and culture minister Tangadagi challenged the officer when he was stopped. “I am the Culture Minister,” he said before moving past the officer, according to a video of the confrontation that was widely shared.Rishyanth subsequently stopped Narendraswamy and Basavanthappa. A video of the exchange circulated widely on social media.The chief minister directed chief secretary Shalini Rajneesh to investigate the incident, identify the officers responsible and submit a report. He said action would follow against those found guilty.In a statement, Shivakumar described the incident as “extremely serious” and the officials’ conduct as “condemnable”.“I consider the incident where police officials prevented Ministers Shivaraj Tangadagi, P.M. Narendra Swamy, H.C. Balakrishna, and K.S. Basavanthappa from entering the puja premises during the Nandidhway Puja at the Mysore Palace premises to be extremely serious. The officials’ arrogant behaviour in denying entry even to ministers is condemnable. Immediate intervention was made, and arrangements were provided to allow the ministers to enter the puja premises,” he said.He added that maintaining discipline while respecting elected representatives was every official’s responsibility and that the government would not tolerate overreach in the name of authority. The chief minister’s office (CMO) statement named four ministers as having been denied entry, although Balakrishna was not visible in the circulating video.Basavanthappa said the ministers had not been informed of any restriction on their movement. “We would have known if there was any such protocol. There was no restriction on the movement of ministers. I do not know why we were stopped despite the officers knowing that we were ministers,” he told reporters.The Opposition alleged that the ministers had been singled out because they were Dalits. Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy demanded to know whether police officers had been instructed to prevent their entry.“Why was there an attempt to obstruct the entry of ministers Tangadagi, Narendraswamy and Basavanthappa? Was it solely because they are Dalits? Were there any such instructions to officers?” he asked.He accused the Congress government of failing to practise the equality and social justice it advocates. “I have called this government anti-Dalit several times. There is suspicion in this incident too, as all three ministers were Dalits,” he said.BJP leader R Ashoka also questioned whether the officer had acted on instructions from senior officials and demanded that Shivakumar take responsibility for the incident.The JD(S), in a post on X, accused the Congress of using Dalits as a vote bank and humiliating them after coming to power. It asked why the ministers accompanying Shivakumar had been left behind rather than escorted into the venue.“If ministers themselves are subjected to such treatment, what would be the plight of ordinary people under your administration? Is this your social justice? Is this your Ambedkarite ideology? Is this your faith in the Constitution written by him?” the party asked.Deputy chief minister G Parameshwara cautioned against assigning a caste motive before the circumstances were established. He said the police might have been enforcing security restrictions at an event attended by large crowds.Calling it “cheap thinking” to give such incidents a caste angle without knowing the facts, Parameshwara defended the possibility that officers were following instructions from their superiors.“There may have been instructions that no one other than the chief minister should be allowed beyond a particular point. I do not have the exact details. But if the police acted on

title: 'We should understand them': Ex-Army chief Naravane on Gen Z's approach amidst recent protests
description: Advocating for patient listening and empathy, he added, "We should try to understand them.
content: Emphasising the need for constructive engagement rather than outright dismissal, former chief of the Indian Army, General Manoj Mukund Naravane (Retd), on Thursday weighed in on recent statements made by Gen Z concerning "regime change," remarking that having a "different way of thinking does not mean they are wrong."Speaking to ANI, the former Army Chief stressed that society and authorities must make a genuine effort to understand the perspective, grievances, and confusion of the younger generation through regular dialogue."The younger generation has a different way of thinking. However, having a different way of thinking does not mean they are wrong," Gen Naravane (retd) said.Also Read | Row over Gen Naravane's memoir raises the question: Should Army prioritise merit over seniority?Advocating for patient listening and empathy, he added, "We should try to understand them. Once we understand them, understand their problems and difficulties—if we listen to them and understand them—only then can we resolve and fix the confusion and issues they face. Therefore, engaging in dialogue with each other and listening to one another is very essential."The “regime change” row erupted after senior advocate Prashant Bhushan described the ongoing agitation against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as a “fight for regime change”. All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora also referred to the Gen Z-led movement in Bangladesh while talking about 'regime change'.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had accused the Congress and its allies of using youth-led protests in Delhi to spread "anarchy" and seek a Bangladesh-style change of government.Union Minister Kiren Rijiju accused opposition figures and external actors of attempting to foment violent street protests in India similar to those seen in Bangladesh and Paris.Pushing back, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor emphasised that analogies comparing India’s democratic protests to violent European riots were completely baseless.Speaking to ANI, Tharoor said, "I think that India is not Bangladesh and India is not France… We only believe in peaceful protest… What we are calling for is free and fair elections… It's a constitutional issue. It's not an issue of trying to topple a regime or anything like that.”Also Read | ‘On our radar as threat’: Ex-army chief MM Naravane calls China India's competitor, Pakistan a security challengeEchoing similar sentiments, Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera also accused the ruling party of recycling a "dangerous trope" to communalise domestic discourse and discredit legitimate grievances regarding electoral integrity and education."Comparing India and Europe is comparing apples with oranges," Khera said, stating that the narrative was an attempt to portray Europe as a cautionary tale to villainise Indian minorities.RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat also denied the term, stating that “regime change has neither happened nor will it happen,” while referring to protests in France and developments in Albania, Nepal and Bangladesh. (ANI)

title: HT Evening News Brief October 22: India condemns Houthi attacks in Saudi, Diljit Dosanjh concert denied police nod in Delhi and more
