title: Delhi-based creator Amir Shokeen arrested over racial abuse of Tripura youth
description: The arrest follows an investigation into a video of the alleged incident that circulated on social media and triggered widespread criticism.
content: A Delhi-based social media creator, Amir Shokeen, was arrested on Thursday over allegations of racially abusing and humiliating a youth from Tripura. The arrest follows an investigation into a video of the alleged incident that circulated on social media and triggered widespread criticism.Delhi Police registered a case after taking suo motu cognisance of the video and began investigating the allegations.Amir Shokeen is seen as a person of “bad character” in the Sadar Bazar area and had previously been involved in several cases of brawling, Deputy Commissioner of Police (North) Niharika Bhatt told news agency PTI.Kiren Rijiju, Manik Saha condemn alleged incidentThe video has drawn condemnation from political leaders across party lines, including Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju and Tripura Chief Minister Manik Saha, who have called for action against the content creator.In a post on X, Rijiju said action would be taken against Shokeen and that the Delhi and Tripura Police would ensure accountability."This evil man will be punished. There was a delay in lodging the official complaint, but Delhi Police and Tripura Police will teach him a hard lesson," the minister said.Meanwhile, Manik Saha has directed the Tripura director general of police to coordinate with Delhi Police over the matter.Tripura students' forum seeks actionThe Tripura Students Forum Delhi (TSFD), in a complaint dated October 21 addressed to the Joint Commissioner of Police, called for an urgent and impartial investigation into the video.The forum alleged that the footage showed a person from Tripura being subjected to sexual assault, harassment and humiliating treatment by a social media content creator. It named Amir Shokeen's Instagram account as allegedly linked to the incident and sought verification of the identity and role of the account operator, as well as others who may have participated in or recorded the alleged incident.The complaint further alleged that the video contained racially derogatory remarks directed at the individual and a demeaning reference to Tripura, causing distress among members of the state's community.The forum urged the police to take appropriate legal action and preserve electronic evidence, including the original recording, metadata, account details and upload history. It also sought measures to protect the person concerned from further harassment or intimidation.The complaint called for an FIR to be registered wherever warranted by the facts and applicable legal provisions.

title: The ‘Good Maharaja’: An Indian king who gave 650 Polish children a home during WWII
description: The story dates back to 1942, when a ruler from Gujarat opened his doors to Polish children displaced by war.
content: An Indian king, 650 Polish children fleeing the horrors of World War II, and an act of kindness that has endured for nearly eight decades. The story of the “Good Maharaja” continues to hold a special place in Poland’s national memory, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk recalling the Indian ruler’s legacy on Thursday.The story dates back to 1942, when a ruler from Gujarat opened his doors to Polish children displaced by the war. At a time when the conflict had torn families apart and left thousands of children without a safe place to go, he offered them shelter far from their homeland.The man remembered as the “Good Maharaja” was Shri Digvijaysinhji Ranjitsinhji Jadeja, the Jam Saheb of Nawanagar, a princely state in present-day Gujarat, commonly known as Jamnagar. During World War II, thousands of Poles were sent to the Caucasus as refugees after being released from Soviet gulags. They travelled overland to Iran's Tehran, but conditions there proved inadequate. India was among the few countries that responded to an appeal for assistance from the Polish government-in-exile.The Jam Saheb, who was then chairman of the Chamber of Princes, agreed to provide refuge to Polish children.In April 1942, 650 children were transported overland to Balachadi, on the outskirts of Jamnagar. The ruler hosted them at a special camp near his Summer Palace, now part of the Sainik School, and provided shelter until 1946.The Maharaja’s promiseThe Jam Saheb’s welcome to the children became one of the most enduring parts of the story.“I am your bapu (father), just like I am father to all Nawanagaris. Therefore, you are no longer orphans today,” he told them. The words are now famously inscribed at his memorial in Poland.Over the next four years, the Balachadi camp became home to around 1,000 Polish children. They received care, education and the opportunity to practise their Catholic faith.Several people helped run the camp. Father Pluta provided spiritual guidance, while Colonel Jeffrey Clark managed its administration. Dr Amrutlal Ashani, pharmacist Anant Joshi and chief nurse Cathy helped look after the children’s health. Seven Goan cooks prepared their meals, with expenses covered from the Jam Saheb’s personal funds.His generosity earned him the Polish title Dobry Maharaja, meaning the Good Maharaja.Balachadi camp diariesFor the children who lived at Balachadi, the camp became much more than a place of refuge. Many retained fond memories of their time in India, with some describing it as their “best childhood memories”.The children played sports with local youngsters. While the locals proved better at hockey, the Polish children excelled at volleyball and were evenly matched in football. Some locals even called the camp Roopnagari, referring to its cherubic inhabitants.The story also inspired Polish filmmaker Tomasz Stankiewicz, who spent two years at Balachadi and later produced the acclaimed documentary The Brave Bunch in India.Warsaw’s tribute to Jam SahebPoland’s gratitude to the Jam Saheb has endured long after the children returned home or settled elsewhere around the world. In 2011, he was posthumously awarded the Commanders’ Cross of the Order of Merit of Poland. A commemorative monument was erected in 2014 at Good Maharaja Square in Warsaw’s Ochota district.In 2016, Poland’s lower house of parliament unanimously passed a resolution honouring him on the 50th anniversary of his death. Eight prestigious schools in Poland were also named after him following a popular vote among students, parents and faculty members.The children who survived the war and found refuge in India are represented by The Association of Poles in India: 1942-1948.How the ‘Good Maharaja’ connects India and Poland todayThe story received renewed attention during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s state visit to Poland in 2024, the first by an Indian prime minister since 1979. Modi paid homage at the memorial to the Good Maharaja.The connection also continues through educational exchanges. The Rajkumar College in Rajkot, the Jam Saheb’s alma mater, has an active exchange programme with the Maharaja Independent High School, Bednarska, in Warsaw.In 2024, 12 students and a teacher from Rajkumar College spent two weeks in Warsaw as part of a family homestay programme. Polish students are expected to make a return visit in November and travel to the historic Balachadi campsite for a wreath-laying ceremony.Nearly eight decades after the Polish children found refuge in Gujarat, the Jam Saheb’s legacy continues to connect the two countries.

title: Karnataka urges Centre to fast-track wildlife clearance for Mekedatu drinking water project
description: Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar has urged the Centre to expedite wildlife clearance for 20 boreholes for the Mekedatu drinking water project in Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary.
content: Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar has urged the Centre to expedite wildlife clearance for the proposed Mekedatu drinking water project, clarifying that the state is currently seeking permission only to drill 20 boreholes for geotechnical investigations and not to divert protected forest land.Shivakumar made the request during a meeting with Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in New Delhi on Thursday, asking him to have the National Board for Wildlife’s standing committee consider the proposal and make an early recommendation.“The proposal is only related to survey and investigation activities and does not currently seek diversion of any protected area land for the project,” Shivakumar said in his representation.Karnataka submitted the proposal to the Union environment ministry on July 1, seeking permission to drill 20 boreholes across 0.0000352 hectares within the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary. The investigations are intended to provide geotechnical information for the proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir and drinking water project.The state’s request is therefore for permission to investigate the proposed site rather than for approval to construct the reservoir or divert sanctuary land for the project.The Centre has sought additional documents on the status of petitions relating to Mekedatu pending before the Supreme Court. “The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has recently sought essential documents/information regarding the status of various petitions pending before the Supreme Court in relation to this matter, which will be provided shortly,” Shivakumar said.Mekedatu is proposed as a balancing reservoir and drinking water project on the Cauvery, with Karnataka seeking to use it to meet Bengaluru’s drinking water requirements. The project has also faced objections from Tamil Nadu over its implications for downstream water flows and the sharing of Cauvery waters.Shivakumar asked Yadav to consider the Mekedatu proposal along with the state’s request concerning the Sharavathi pumped storage project. “In this regard, as chairman of the Standing Committee of NBWL, I request you to kindly examine and recommend the above two proposals at the earliest,” he said.The chief minister also asked the Centre not to finalise its seventh draft notification on declaring parts of the Western Ghats as an ecologically sensitive area based on the Kasturirangan report until Karnataka completes physical surveys.“I request that the seventh draft notification issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on 27 July 2026 regarding declaration of the Western Ghats Eco Sensitive Area based on the Kasturirangan report may not be finalised,” he said.Shivakumar said the state government’s high-level committee should first submit its report, followed by physical surveys over a year before the notification is finalised.“Until the physical survey is completed within a period of one year after submission of the report of the High Level Committee constituted by the state government, the notification should not be finalised,” he said, adding that the Centre could take further action in consultation with Karnataka.

title: Netanyahu invites PM Modi, flydubai pilot to light torch at Israel's Independence Day event
description: Netanyahu said PM Modi expressed solidarity in fight against terrorism while hailing the "strong and decades-old ties" between India and Israel.
content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday and invited him to participate in Israel's Independence Day. The Israeli PM called upon his Indian counterpart to light the torch on the occasion alongside flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, who averted a major aviation tragedy earlier in September."I spoke with my friend, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and invited him to light the torch alongside a brave Indian pilot on Israel’s Independence Day," he said, adding that PM Modi thanked him in return. Israel observes May 14 as Yom Ha'atzmaut or Israel's national day as the Israeli Declaration of Independence was signed on this date in 1948.ALSO READ: Netanyahu hails Indian pilot Smit Machchar's heroics on flydubai plane: 'Extraordinary bravery'On September 30, 2026, Captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his Omani co-pilot inside the cockpit as he prevented the latter's alleged bid to crash the flydubai flight FZ1073 travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Netanyahu had called Indian pilot Smit Machchhar a "hero of the entire world" as he spoke with him over the phone.Netanyahu, Modi discuss bilateral tiesNetanyahu further said PM Modi expressed solidarity in fight against terrorism while hailing the "strong and decades-old ties" between India and Israel.Minutes after Netanyahu's post, Prime Minister Modi took to X and said, “Received a phone call from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. We reviewed the sustained momentum in our bilateral ties and reaffirmed our commitment to further strengthening our partnership.”ALSO READ: Netanyahu warns future US president could be hostile to Israel, eyes close ties with IndiaDivulging the topics of their discussion, Prime Minister Modi said the two leaders exchanged views on the latest developments in West Asia, which has been witnessing a violent conflict, and emphasised the need to restore peace and stability in the region.The telephone conversation came in the backdrop of ongoing conflicts in Gaza, Iran and Saudi Arabia. Israel has been embroiled in prolonged armed conflicts with Palestinian, Iranian and Yemeni groups in West Asia. Prime Minister Modi had made a state visit to Israel from February 25 to 26. The two leaders had then agreed and decided to elevate the Strategic Partnership to a new level -- 'A Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation and Prosperity'.Modi had then said that India's security interest was linked to peace and stability in the Middle East, adding that New Delhi fully supported the Gaza Peace Initiative. They also had telephonic talks during the US-Iran and Iran conflict.(With PTI inputs)

title: Chaos erupts at Delhi MCD house during debate, AAP alleges 'personal attack' on councillor
description: Delhi MCD house adjourned as councillors clash during debate, AAP seeks BJP mayor's apology
content: Chaos erupted in the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) House on Thursday, with councillors clashing ahead of a scheduled debate on air pollution and fund allocation. BJP and AAP councillors engaged in heated exchanges, files were torn, and marshals intervened to escort Mayor Pravesh Wahi to safety.The House was later adjourned following a confrontation involving members of the AAP and Congress.The proceedings, which ended abruptly, saw attempts by opposition AAP to snatch microphones from Mayor Wahi and BJP councillors. Officials were also caught in the chaos, with tea and water spilled on them during the scuffle, news agency PTI reported.Wahi said the matter had been referred to the disciplinary committee of the House and strictest action would be taken against councillors who violated rules.What triggered the clashesThe ruckus began after AAP councillors demanded the immediate release of development funds for their wards. Mayor Pravesh Wahi announced an allocation of ₹25 lakh, adding that each councillor would receive a total of ₹2 crore during the current financial year.Leader of the House Jai Bhagwan Yadav said the latest announcement would take the total allocation to ₹75 lakh.“ ₹50 lakh has already been allocated, and ₹25 lakh will be released now,” he said.The AAP, however, demanded that the immediate allocation be increased to ₹1 crore, prompting the House to be adjourned for five minutes, according to PTI.When proceedings resumed, opposition councillors questioned the civic body's efforts to address the city's worsening air pollution. The discussion soon descended into chaos, with councillors exchanging heated words and jostling with one another.Tensions rose further during a confrontation between Congress leader Nazia Danish and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Ankush Narang.After Danish criticised the AAP, Narang accused her of being close to the BJP. Danish responded with a remark about AAP councillor Shagufta Zubair Chaudhary, who joined the Arvind Kejriwal-led party with her husband in 2024 after leaving the Congress.Following the exchange, Zubair and other AAP councillors approached the mayor’s chair and allegedly attempted to damage the microphone installed there. Files, papers and beverages kept on the mayor’s table were also thrown into the air, PTI reported.AAP targets BJP, CongressTargeting BJP Mayor Pravesh Wahi and Congress leader Nazia Danish, AAP demanded an apology, saying “personal remarks” were made against AAP councillor Shagufta Zubair Chaudhary.“Targeting AAP councillor Shagufta Zubair Chaudhary, who asked the BJP for funds for the rights and development of the people of her area during the MCD House meeting, is extremely unfortunate,” AAP said in a post on X.“At the behest of the BJP-ruled MCD, Congress leader Nazia Danish made personal remarks against AAP councillor Shagufta Zubair Chaudhary and used abusive language. Questions are now being raised about the role of the Congress as well.”(With inputs from PTI) “Our demand is that in today's House meeting, for using this abusive language, BJP Mayor Prevesh Wahi and Congress leader Nazia Danish apologize in the House. When AAP councillors raise their voice for the rights of the people, the BJP-ruled MCD should respond, not try to suppress the voice.”

title: Chhattisgarh police issue show-cause notice to Rajnandgaon SP over AK-47 firing video at Dussehra event
description: Chhattisgarh police issue a show-cause notice to Rajnandgaon SP Ankita Sharma after a video of her firing an AK-47 during Dussehra Shastra Puja goes viral.
content: The Chhattisgarh police headquarters on Thursday issued a show-cause notice to Rajnandgaon superintendent of police (SP) Ankita Sharma after a video of her firing an AK-47 during a Dussehra weapon-worship ceremony was widely shared, with officers flagging possible violations of prescribed weapon-handling rules.The firing incident took place at the Police Lines in Rajnandgaon on October 20 during the traditional ‘Shastra Puja’ held on the occasion of Vijayadashami, Rajnandgaon range inspector general of police Ajay Yadav said.Yadav said the police headquarters had asked Sharma to explain her actions.Also Read | Chhattisgarh woman IPS officer's AK-47 firing at Dussehra ritual sparks safety debateMore details on the videoThe video showed Sharma, dressed in a saree, firing several rounds from an AK-47 after the weapon-worship ritual. The headquarters also took note of comments accompanying the viral video, which officers said had raised concerns about safety protocols and could affect the dignity of the police force.“After receiving the SP’s reply, I will record my observations and forward the matter to the police headquarters. Further action will be taken in accordance with the directions received from there,” Yadav said.The video has triggered a debate over ceremonial firing.Concerns over weapon handlingRetired IPS officer R K Vij said ceremonial weapon worship did not necessarily require firing. “The tradition is essentially about performing the worship of weapons, not firing them. Such firing carries the risk of accidents and should be avoided,” Vij said.An IPS officer, requesting anonymity, said firing blank rounds, commonly known as ‘awazi kartoos’, was part of the Shastra Puja tradition followed across Chhattisgarh. Live ammunition was not used during such ceremonial firing, the officer said.Former Indian Army officer K J Dhillon also raised concerns over the weapon-handling practices seen in the videos. In a social media post, he said basic safety precautions appeared to have been violated and questioned the manner in which the loaded weapon was handled.Another social media user, Army veteran Colonel Deepak Kumar, described the act as reckless and unprofessional and questioned the handling of the rifle after the firing.Former Major L S Choudhary acknowledged shortcomings in weapon handling but said these should be corrected without discrediting her work in Chhattisgarh.Rajnandgaon Additional Superintendent of Police Kirtan Rathore was also seen firing an AK-47 in another video after Sharma.Videos of police personnel firing weapons after Shastra Puja ceremonies in other districts, including Raipur, Bilaspur, Raigarh, Durg, Kabirdham and Bastar, were also shared with the media on Tuesday.

title: Kanpur man pinned to car roof with hands trapped in window, driven around for 1.5 km and run over
description: Biru Singh Badauria died during treatment after the alleged attack in Kanpur. Police are examining CCTV footage and have recovered the vehicle.
content: A 37-year-old man died in Kanpur after he was allegedly pinned to a car’s roof, driven around for 1.5 km and then thrown onto the road and run over by the same vehicle, police said on Thursday. Two of the three men named in the murder case have been arrested. The victim, Biru Singh Badauria, worked as a salesperson for a food products company. According to was returning home after visiting a Dussehra fair when the incident took place in the Hanumant Vihar area on Tuesday night, according to news agency PTI.Also Read: Woman, partner sentenced to death in ‘blue drum’ murder caseAccording to a complaint filed by Badauria’s father, Ram Shankar Singh, the accused intercepted and assaulted his son. When Badauria tried to escape, they allegedly struck him with their car before trapping his hands in the vehicle’s rear window panes and pinning him to the roof.The men then allegedly drove for around 1.5 km at high speed before throwing Badauria onto the road and running him over with the same vehicle. Also Read: Kanpur episode predates Meerut blue drum murder as accused remains untraced after 8 yearsBadauria was first taken to a private hospital and later shifted to Lala Lajpat Rai (LLR) Hospital, where he died during treatment on Wednesday.Two accused arrestedPolice Commissioner Raghubir Lal told PTI that two of the three accused named in the murder case had been arrested. Rajveer and Pintu have been taken into custody, while efforts are underway to trace the third accused, Mewa Yadav, Lal said.The victim’s family alleged that the attack was linked to an earlier dispute between Badauria and two of the accused, Rajveer and Mewa Yadav, who live in Nai Basti in Khadepur.Also Read: Twist in Kanpur trader Vineet Minocha's murder after daughter-in-law's arrest: Son planned hit, framed wifeA complaint was initially lodged by Badauria’s brother, describing the incident as a road accident, following which a case was registered. His father subsequently filed a separate complaint alleging murder and naming Rajveer, Mewa Yadav and Pintu, according to Lal.Police are examining CCTV footage and have recovered the vehicle allegedly involved in the incident. Further action will be taken based on the evidence, the police commissioner said.

title: ‘Unacceptable’: India slams Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia, moves to help stranded pilgrims
description: An attack on King Fahd International Airport on Wednesday evening killed two people, including an Indian, while two Indians were among eight people injured.
content: India on Thursday expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia while condemning continued attacks by Houthi rebels on civil infrastructure, including a strike on Dammam airport that killed an Indian national, and backing the early restoration of peace and normalcy in West Asia.The Indian side also said it is working with airlines and tour operators to facilitate the early return of Indian pilgrims stranded in Saudi Arabia because of the suspension of flights by Indian carriers following the recent escalation of hostilities.An attack on King Fahd International Airport on Wednesday evening killed two people, including an Indian, while two Indians were among eight people injured. Another Indian was injured by debris from a drone intercepted over Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oilfield on Wednesday.“We strongly condemn the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oilfield in the Eastern Province on October 21,” the external affairs ministry said in a statement. Such attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure are “completely unacceptable and must cease immediately”, the Indian side reiterated. “We stand in solidarity with the people and the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy would return to the region at the earliest,” it said.While conveying condolences to the family of the Indian killed in Dammam and wishing the speedy recovery of the injured, the statement said the Indian embassy in Riyadh is in touch with Saudi authorities and providing assistance to the affected Indian nationals.The latest attacks on Saudi infrastructure reflect the escalation of the conflict between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and the Saudi-backed government of Yemen. One Indian was killed, and 10 more were injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on October 10.External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on social media that the Indian embassy in Riyadh and the consulate in Jeddah are “engaging with concerned airlines and tour operators to facilitate the early return of affected [Indian] pilgrims”.Jaiswal’s social media post followed a claim by AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi that 4,000 Indian pilgrims were stranded in Makkah and Madina after Indian carriers such as Air India, Indigo and Akasa Air cancelled flights.Jaiswal said about 3,000 stranded Indian pilgrims have returned from Saudi Arabia on available flights over the past week. This was in addition to more than 10,000 pilgrims who were not stranded and returned to India during the same period. “Arrangements are being discussed to facilitate the return of other Umrah pilgrims at the earliest,” he said.The Indian missions in Riyadh and Jeddah, with the support of community volunteers, are extending all possible welfare assistance to the pilgrims, Jaiswal said.Nineteen Indians, including 11 seafarers, have been killed so far in the West Asia conflict, which was triggered by attacks by Israel and the US on Iran in February. Dozens more have been injured across West Asia. The Indian side has been concerned by these casualties and has repeatedly called for a return to dialogue and diplomacy while urging all stakeholders to stop attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure.West Asia is home to more than 10 million Indians, a majority of them blue-collar workers, including employees of oilfields and infrastructure facilities such as airports.On Wednesday, the US State Department directed diplomats and family members to leave from its missions in Saudi Arabia, triggering fears of a US strike on Iran. There were also reports of the US withdrawing family members of diplomats from several other missions in the region.

title: NCPCR can't just forward complaints and await replies: CIC on child abuse claims
description: NCPCR can't just forward complaints and await replies: CIC on child abuse claims
content: New Delhi, The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights cannot merely forward complaints to authorities and await responses; instead, it must effectively monitor the actions taken regarding alleged violations of children's rights, the Central Information Commission has said.The observation was made during an RTI appeal that sought an updated status report and a detailed inspection report concerning a complaint about the alleged physical abuse of children with disabilities at a school in Gulbarga, Karnataka.In a recent order, Information Commissioner P R Ramesh said that the allegations concerned the safety, dignity and educational rights of children with hearing and speech disabilities and warranted due attention and appropriate follow-up.The complaint alleged that teachers and staff physically abused students and subjected them to cruel and inhuman treatment.It also alleged that the children were not being taught adequately in sign language, which deprived them of a meaningful education and an inclusive learning environment.In response to an RTI application submitted in July 2025, the NCPCR informed the applicant that it was awaiting an action report from the district magistrate.Subsequent submissions indicated that further reminders had been sent to the district administration, as well as a communication to Karnataka's school education department in September 2026.However, the CIC observed that the communication appeared general in nature and did not specifically address the complaint.It also noted that the NCPCR had not adequately demonstrated whether any specific inquiry, inspection, or other concrete actions had been undertaken related to the allegations.The child rights body, as a statutory institution entrusted with protecting and promoting children's rights, was expected to pursue complaints with due diligence and ensure appropriate follow-up, the commission said."Its role cannot be reduced to merely forwarding complaints and awaiting responses without effectively monitoring the action taken thereon," the order stated.The CIC added that although the proceedings concerned disclosure of information under the Right to Information Act, 2005, "the seriousness of the underlying grievance cannot be overlooked".It directed the NCPCR's Central Public Information Officer to provide an updated, point-by-point response, along with records of actions taken, including any inspection report, inquiry report, or action taken report.If no inquiry or inspection has been conducted, or no action taken report has been received, the applicant must be clearly informed.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Fresh voter drive in Uttarakhand from Nov 12: CEO holds all-party meet
description: The first-level checking of EVMs and VVPATs will begin across the state on Friday, Uttarkhand chief electoral officer BVRC Purushottam said
content: Nineteen days after releasing the final electoral rolls following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) drive, Uttarakhand chief electoral officer (CEO) BVRC Purushottam on Thursday said the Special Summary Revision (SSR) for 2027 will begin across Uttarakhand on November 12, with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date.At his meeting with representatives of recognised national political parties, Purushottam briefed them on the procedure and schedule for SSR, which is expected to help first-time voters and those deleted by the controversial SIR get back on the roll. He also presented a detailed plan for the First Level Checking (FLC) of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) machines ahead of state elections early next year, according to a statement by the CEO’s office.The first-level checking of EVMs and VVPATs will begin across the state on Friday.Purushottam said his office received 100,744 Form 6 applications, which citizens use to apply for fresh inclusion in the voter list, during a week-long drive from October 12 to 20. Citizens turning 18 on or before January 1, 2027, will be eligible to register during the upcoming revision.The state’s draft electoral roll will be published on November 12. Claims and objections can be filed between November 12 and December 11, with hearings continuing through December 28. The final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027.To prevent bulk misuse, political representatives were told there would be caps on how many voter objections they can file. An individual objector can submit up to 10 Form 7 applications during the entire claims window, and up to five applications per month during continuous roll updates.Among others. Rajkumar Purohit of the Bharatiya Janata Party, Amendra Bisht of the Congress, Satendra Chopra of the BSP, Shyam Babu Pandey of the Aam Aadmi Party and Anant Akash of the CPI(M) attended Thursday’s meeting.The final electoral roll for Uttarakhand was published on October 3 after the SIR was completed. The final roll has 7.16 million electors, a net contraction of 10.1% from the roll before the exercise.The final roll for Uttarakhand has 25,164 or 0.4% more names on it than the draft roll published on July 14, which had 7.13 million electors. It was the result of 129,872 additions and 104,708 deletions after July 14 during the claims and objections phase. The final SIR numbers mean that most deletions under the SIR exercise took place in the draft stage itself, when 827,000 or 10.4% of the 7.96 million pre-SIR electors were deleted from the rolls. These electors were classified as uncollectable or ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate).

title: SC criticises Allahabad HC over 'misplaced sympathy' for releasing 2 convicts on probation
description: SC criticises Allahabad HC over 'misplaced sympathy' for releasing 2 convicts on probation
content: New Delhi, The Supreme Court has come down heavily on the Allahabad High Court for releasing on probation two men convicted for a 2003 knife and gun attack under a section related to good conduct, saying they had gone scot-free without a single day of imprisonment due to "misplaced sympathy" despite the "brutality" of the crime."The circumstances of the case including the nature of the offence and the character of the offender should be the reigning factor in deciding as to whether it is expedient to release the accused on the premise of good conduct; which in the facts of this case is lacking," a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said.The apex court set aside the order of the High Court and directed the accused to surrender within two weeks, failing which the Additional Sessions Court, Bahraich, will take immediate proceedings to apprehend them.The case arose out of business rivalry where the complainant opened a shop near the shop of the accused in Bahraich district of Uttar Pradesh. On the day of the incident, the accused, armed with a cutting weapon, and the second accused, armed with a gun, brutally attacked the victim, inflicting severe injuries that caused him to faint before he was rushed to Bahraich Hospital.The top court faulted the manner in which the High Court invoked Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 as the accused was a first offender, without taking into account the "brutality of the crime and the grievous nature of the injuries sustained by the victim".The bench said it was unable to comprehend as to why the High Court observed that the accused were suffering for 22 years since the accused were on bail and merrily indulging in criminal activities."We cannot but, with an amount of consternation, notice the casual manner in which both the Trial Court and the High Court considered the issue from the stage of taking cognisance till the release of the accused on application of the PoO Act."The accused have gone scot-free without suffering a single day of imprisonment, especially by reason of the misplaced sympathy based on grandiose expositions of law, totally inapplicable to the facts of the case. Section 4 of the PoO Act does not permit its invocation when it is found that the accused is a first offender," the bench said.The top court said the victim in the ensuing years was, day-in and day-out, suffering the debilitating effects of the attack."The circumstances of the case, including the nature of the offence and the character of the offender, should be the reigning factor in deciding as to whether it is expedient to release the accused on the premise of good conduct; which in the facts of this case is lacking."The brutality of the crime and the grievous nature of the injuries sustained by the victim ought to have persuaded the Court to draw an adverse inference on the aspect of 'nature of offence'," the bench said.The top court also criticised the trial court for framing a charge under Section 308 of the IPC instead of Section 307 of the IPC ."The criminal appeals shall stand restored before the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow. We request the High Court to take up the appeal only after ensuring that the accused are taken into custody and then only the appeal be heard," the bench said.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Medical body seeks review of Sunny Deol's ‘Suryaa’ over portrayal of doctors
description: The film could create a negative impression of the medical fraternity and undermine public trust in doctors, the Indian Medical Association said.
content: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has written to Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, seeking an urgent review of the upcoming film Suryaa-Ant Se Aarambh Tak over its over its portrayal of doctors and “violence” against healthcare workers.The doctors’ body on Thursday raised concerns about the Sunny Deol starrer's promo video, saying it could create a negative impression of the medical fraternity and undermine public trust in healthcare professionals.The IMA objected to the “generalisation of corruption within healthcare” and the “depiction of violence against medical professionals”. It warned that such portrayals could have consequences for the safety of healthcare workers and the doctor-patient relationship.ALSO READ | Maharashtra medical interns threaten strike from November 1 over stipend hikeThe association asked the ministry to conduct an impartial review of the film and seek corrective measures from the filmmakers.It also called for a ban or other appropriate action “if justified under applicable law”. Suryaa is an upcoming Hindi crime thriller starring Sunny Deol, directed by M Padmakumar, and scheduled to release on November 20. Its teaser, released on October 19, follows a father investigating the truth behind his daughter's illness and points to concerns about a faulty medical system.Why the IMA has objected to the filmIn its letter, the IMA said the film’s portrayal of corruption and unethical practices risked tarnishing the reputation of doctors who worked honestly and diligently.“While individual misconduct must be investigated and punished, the actions of a few must not be used to tarnish the reputation of countless honest and dedicated doctors,” the association said.The doctors’ body also raised concerns about scenes showing physical assaults on doctors, nursing staff and hospital personnel, particularly when such acts are presented as “heroic or justified.”ALSO READ | Suryaa teaser: Sunny Deol is a grieving father determined to discover the shocking truth of medical system in M Padmakumar's film“Scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nursing staff, and hospital personnel, particularly when presented as heroic or justified acts, risk normalising violence against those committed to saving lives,” the letter read.“Content that appears to glorify attacks on medical professionals may encourage hostility and further endanger those providing essential healthcare services,” it said. “Such portrayals may foster unwarranted mistrust and hostility towards doctors, weakening the mutual trust and cooperation essential for effective treatment and healthcare delivery,” the letter said.The IMA clarified that it did not seek to protect doctors guilty of wrongdoing. It said corruption, unethical medical practices and professional misconduct should be dealt with through appropriate legal and disciplinary action.“Our objective is not to shield any wrongdoer from accountability, but to protect the dignity of the medical profession, ensure the safety of healthcare workers, and preserve public trust in the healthcare system,” the association said.The letter also raised concerns about the impact of negative portrayals on medical students and aspiring doctors.“India needs more dedicated and motivated doctors to meet the healthcare needs of its growing population,” the IMA said, adding that the profession was built on “years of hard work, sacrifice, compassion, and service to humanity”. The association has asked the ministry to review the film’s content, seek appropriate corrective measures from its makers and consider a ban or other action if warranted under the law.

title: Nikhil Kamath warns of tough 2027 for startups, says money in AI far outstrips its revenue
description: Nikhil Kamath estimated that around $1 trillion was being invested in AI annually, while revenue generated was between $100 billion and $200 billion.
content: The money flowing into artificial intelligence (AI) far exceeds the revenue it currently generates, Nikhil Kamath has said. The Zerodha co-founder warned that 2027 could be a difficult year for startups and said “it won't be a bad idea” for entrepreneurs to raise funds now as access to capital could become difficult in the months ahead.Speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2026, Kamath said the AI industry was attracting enormous investments but had yet to generate enough revenue to justify the spending.“The amount of money going into AI and the money coming out of AI, there is a big gap in between that,” he said.Kamath estimated that around $1 trillion was being invested in AI annually, while revenue generated through enterprise adoption was between $100 billion and $200 billion. This leaves a gap of $700 billion to $800 billion a year that investors or other sources of funding must cover, he said.He noted that foreign capital, including investments from the Gulf, helped fund American AI companies in the previous funding cycle. Finding enough fresh capital to sustain investments at the current scale every year could prove difficult.ALSO READ | Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs globally this year as it ramps up AI adoptionWhy 2027 could be difficult for startupsKamath said investors were counting on AI to boost productivity and generate trillions of dollars in economic benefits to justify the huge spending. “I don't know if I've seen that happen on the ground yet," he said.He also warned that rising US Treasury yields could make borrowing more expensive. "So for next year, with American Treasury rates going up, cost of money going to 5-6-7%, I don't know where it'll go, it's at 5% today.”“Somebody has to bridge this gap up until that five trillion dollar revenue story plays out, even if it does or it doesn't, nobody knows,” he said.Kamath advised founders to secure funding while investor appetite remained relatively strong. “So if somebody is able to raise a lot of capital today and keep it, probably not a bad idea,” he said.ALSO READ | Nikhil Kamath questioned over MBA remark at Columbia Business School: 'If you didn't see value, why would you be here?'Kamath is the co-founder of Zerodha, one of India's largest stockbroking firms. He has also invested in several businesses, including Licious, Nourish You, Pee Safe, Subko and electric scooter maker Ather.He is involved in philanthropy and environmental initiatives and has signed the Giving Pledge, a commitment to donate at least half of one's wealth to charitable causes during one's lifetime or through a will.Kamath backs inheritance taxAt the summit, Kamath also backed the idea of an inheritance tax, calling it “probably not the worst idea in the world”.An inheritance tax is levied on beneficiaries who receive money, property or other assets after someone's death. Kamath questioned whether wealth passed between generations should be treated differently from income earned during a person's lifetime.ALSO READ | Nikhil Kamath marks Zerodha’s 16th birthday with nostalgic note: ‘Hope we’re all still in same room in 2042’“I don't like the idea of taxing somebody who is earning money in his lifetime and incentivising that but taxing people between generations when wealth is being passed through; I don't know in what manner. It has to be done in a manner where it's not an unrealized gain,” he said.He said that such a tax should not force business owners to sell equity in their companies to meet their tax obligations. He also recalled facing online criticism when he had previously shared his views on inheritance tax.‘Wage growth must keep up with asset prices’Kamath also discussed the Gini coefficient, a measure of income or wealth inequality. He said inequality was worsening in many parts of the world and argued that the wealth gap would be difficult to reduce unless wages grew alongside asset prices.“As long as wage growth in society is not going to keep up with asset price inflation, logically it's impossible for wealth inequality to come down,” he said, adding that governments might need to intervene to address the problem.He also asked wealthy individuals to take steps to reduce inequality before it becomes more difficult to tackle.“To the rich people in this room, it's not even altruism, but it could be self-serving to solve this problem when you can, before you reach a point where you have to,” he said.What India can learn from China on AIKamath said India had the potential to build major technology companies but lacked the risk capital available to businesses in the United States and China, particularly those developing advanced AI models.He said companies working on frontier AI models had access to greater funding to experiment with new technologies, making it difficult for Indian firms to compete at the same level.“I don't see how an Indian company, or for that matter any company outside of those two or three countries where there is that much risk capital, can have a fair shot at competing in that layer,” he said.However, he pointed to India's cost advantages in setting up businesses and building data centres. Kamath estimated that setting up a megawatt of capacity in India could cost 30% to 40% less than in the West. He also said electricity was significantly cheaper in India than in several other countries.Kamath suggested that India could learn from the competition between Chinese provinces, where local leaders compete to attract investment and promote development.“One thing that maybe we can change and learn from China is to allow for different provinces or states to compete with one another like they were a capitalistic organisation itself,” he said.He added that chief ministers could operate more like corporate CEOs, competing to improve their states' performance and attract businesses.

title: Mere participation in protest not enough to show intention to disobey, obstruct police: HC
description: Mere participation in protest not enough to show intention to disobey, obstruct police: HC
content: New Delhi, The Delhi High Court has said that mere participation in a demonstration does not by itself establish a "common intention" to disobey police directions or obstruct police personnel.Justice Sanjeev Narula made the observation while quashing an FIR against an SSC aspirant who was booked by Delhi Police in 2025 for allegedly failing to disperse from Ramlila Maidan despite repeated announcements to vacate the protest venue.The petitioner had participated in the protest at Ramlila Maidan in August last year over alleged irregularities in the conduct of the SSC entrance examination.The prosecution claimed that certain organisers refused to conclude the demonstration after the expiry of the permitted time and instigated the gathering to remain at the venue until their demands were fulfilled.The police registered the FIR alleging that certain protestors disobeyed the prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita as they continued to occupy the ground and some of them pushed and scuffled with police personnel.Giving relief to the petitioner, the court stated that neither the FIR nor the subsequent status report attributed any criminal conduct specifically to him, and his mere presence among the protesters, in the absence of a common intention to commit a crime with others, was not sufficient to establish the offence under section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita .The provision penalises disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant, where the person concerned has knowledge of such order and the disobedience causes, or tends to cause, obstruction, annoyance etc to persons lawfully employed."The petitioner cannot be subjected to criminal proceedings merely on account of his presence amongst the protesters, in the absence of material indicating his knowing participation in the alleged disobedience or any common intention to commit the offence. The continuation of the proceedings against him, in these circumstances, would serve no worthwhile purpose," said the court in the order passed on October 13."Mere participation in the same demonstration does not, by itself, establish a common intention to disobey lawful directions or obstruct police personnel. The material on record does not disclose any basis for attributing such common intention to the petitioner," it held.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Uttarakhand CM to speak to Daler Mehndi amid over minister’s confrontation with singer
description: Daler Mehndi was performing during Navratri celebrations when minister Subodh Uniyal reprimanded him
content: Chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday said he would speak to singers Mika Singh and Daler Mehndi, his brother, amid the controversy over Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal’s remarks and confrontation with Mehndi at a public event.Daler Mehndi was performing on October 18 in Tehri Garhwal district during Navratri celebrations when Uniyal reprimanded him and questioned his conduct over allegations of intoxication. Mika Singh demanded an apology following the viral video of the confrontation.“I believe that since there was likely pressure from the public at the time and the minister [Uniyal] stated that he was unaware of Daler Mehndi’s poor health. The minister himself has already clarified,” Dhami said when asked about the controversy at a press conference.Also Read: Mika Singh demands apology from Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal for ‘humiliating’ brother Daler Mehndi He said the artists involved are accomplished and that Uttarakhand respects writers, artists and scholars. “Given the circumstances that arose due to public pressure at the time, and since the minister has already issued a statement clarifying that he had no such intent, I believe it is time to bring this matter to a close,” Dhami said.Asked about Mika Singh’s appeal to him to take action against Uniyal, Dhami said he would speak to both brothers. “I will first speak with Mika. I will also speak with Daler Mehndi. I will talk to both of them. I am friends with both,” Dhami said.Also Read: Film workers' body urges PM Modi to intervene in Daler Mehndi row: ‘Advise public reps to exercise greater sensitivity when dealing with artists’On Wednesday, Mika Singh sought Uniyal’s apology in an Instagram post. He thanked singers, fans, friends, family, and well-wishers for their love and support. “My point is simple: Daler Mehndi ji does not drink alcohol, and making such allegations against him is completely wrong. Nowadays, if a teacher scolds a child in school or college, it becomes a major issue. In such a context, how can it be considered right to scold and humiliate a renowned artist like this, in front of everyone on stage?”He said an apology is due. “The person responsible should acknowledge that the allegations about Daler Mehndi ji drinking alcohol were wrong and apologise for the way he was treated.”

title: Delhi court denies bail to man accused of being part of cyber fraud gang
description: Delhi court denies bail to man accused of being part of cyber fraud gang
content: New Delhi, A Delhi court has denied bail to a man accused of being part of an organised cybercrime gang, saying that more than ₹20 lakh allegedly cheated in the case was yet to be recovered.Additional Sessions Judge Rajinder Kumar dismissed the bail application of Karan, who was arrested in connection with a case registered at Cyber Police Station and said no fresh ground had been made out since his previous bail plea was rejected in May this year.In an order dated October 15, the court said, "The serious nature of allegations, the gravity of the offence, the role ascribed to the accused, the fact that the witnesses are yet to be examined; so, I am not inclined to grant bail to the accused at this stage.The court noted that the chargesheet had been filed, but charges were yet to be framed. It said the allegations were serious and the accused had allegedly played an important role in the offence.Karan is in judicial custody since August 22, 2025.Opposing the bail plea, the prosecution alleged that Karan, while working as a freelance accountant, had been contacted by a person named Vikas, who provided him with a mobile phone and laptop to manage multiple bank accounts and Gmail IDs in exchange for ₹20,000 per month.The prosecution claimed that Karan was part of an organised cybercrime gang involved in siphoning off cheated money. It also expressed apprehension that he could commit similar offences or threaten witnesses if released on bail.The defence argued that Karan was falsely implicated, the devices did not belong to him and the investigation officer had manipulated reports. It also submitted that the chargesheet had been filed and the trial would take considerable time.Rejecting the plea, the court cited the gravity of the allegations, the role attributed to the accused and the fact that witnesses were yet to be examined.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: ‘Bias against Punjab's progressive voices?’: AAP as Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi concert denied nod
description: Sharing a Hindustan Times post about the development, Bharadwaj asked why the Central government-controlled Delhi Police had refused permission for the show.
content: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Saurabh Bharadwaj on Thursday questioned the Delhi Police’s decision to deny security clearance for Diljit Dosanjh’s concert scheduled for October 30, alleging a possible bias against progressive voices from Punjab.Sharing a Hindustan Times post about the development, Bharadwaj asked why the Delhi Police refused permission for the show, arguing that Dosanjh enjoys widespread popularity among the youth and is loved in Punjab.Also read | Exclusive | Delhi Police denies permission for Diljit Dosanjh's October 30 Delhi concert, cites security concerns “Why is Central Govt’s Delhi Police denying permission for concert of Diljit Dosanjh ? Is it a deep rooted bias against progressive voices of Punjab ? Indian Youth loves @diljitdosanjh and he is much loved in Punjab," Saurabh Bharadwaj wrote on X. In another post, the AAP leader compared the decision with the case of singer Daler Mehndi, alleging that the authorities were more willing to allow events featuring religious figures who promote hate than concerts by artists who represent Punjab’s cultural identity.“Now, @diljitdosanjh is being denied permission for his concert in Delhi. After @dalermehndi, it’s another Punjab icon. Delhi Police will permit all those Babas who create Narrative of hate, not to the Youth Icon who creates Narrative of Love & Punjab”.Recently, Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister Subodh Uniyal confronted Daler Mehndi during his performance at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in New Tehri, questioning the singer’s ability to perform and alleging that he was drunk and unfit to be on stage.BJP criticises AAPDelhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra criticised the AAP for questioning the Delhi Police's decision to deny permission for singer Diljit Dosanjh's scheduled show in the national capital on October 30, saying the move was linked to security concerns, as per a press statement. Malhotra rejected AAP leaders' allegations that the police had refused permission because Dosanjh had extended support to the farmers' protest. He described the claims as baseless and politically motivated.Security concerns behind denial, says MalhotraThe BJP leader said the ongoing festive season had to be taken into account while assessing arrangements for a large public gathering. He noted that a concert expected to draw around one lakh people would require extensive security planning and suggested that the police's decision was driven by public safety considerations.Malhotra also accused opposition parties, including AAP, of putting pressure on the police through protests in recent days. He referred to the opposition's announcement of a rally in Delhi on November 1, suggesting that the prevailing situation could add to the security challenges faced by authorities.Why was Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi concert denied permission?HT City has learnt that Dosanjh’s Aura India Tour concert, scheduled to take place at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in New Delhi on October 30, has been denied security permissions.In a letter addressed to BookMyShow, the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (South District) said the application for organising the event had been examined but could not be approved because of security concerns.The letter referred to the application dated October 14, 2026, and cited specific threat-related inputs, security arrangements required during the ongoing festive season and other law and order commitments as reasons for the decision.The letter stated, "Sir, With reference to your application dated 14.10.2026 on the subject cited above, I am to inform you that your request for organizing "Diljit Dosanjh's Aura India Tour Delhi" at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, New Delhi, on 30.10.2026 has been examined by this office. In view of the specific threat-related inputs, coupled with the multifarious security and law & order commitments arising out of the ongoing festive season and other important law & order concerns, the same cannot be acceded to."

title: Delhi creator Amir Shokeen's family ‘cut ties’ years ago; brother alleges ‘extortion, property grab’ amid racial abuse row
description: Shokeen is facing widespread condemnation over a video that purportedly shows him making derogatory comments about a young man from Tripura.
content: The family of Delhi-based content creator Amir Shokeen had cut ties with him 12-14 years ago, his brother said, as Shokeen faces backlash over a video allegedly showing him racially abusing a youth from Tripura.Speaking about his brother, Mohammed Wasim Raja described him as a “miscreant” and alleged that he had been involved in extortion and the illegal occupation of properties. Raja also claimed that Shokeen had illegally acquired his property.“Amir Shokeen is a miscreant who has many cases filed against him. Sometimes he goes around with people from the Aam Aadmi Party or others, or Imran. He also does extortion and illegally occupies properties. He had illegally acquired my property too. We cut all ties with him 12-14 years ago. We are four brothers in total,” Raja told news agency ANI.Also Read: Delhi content creator Amir Shokeen under fire over racial abuse of Tripura youth, Union minister vows action: 'This evil man'What does the video show?In the video, Shokeen is allegedly heard calling the youth “Chinese”, comparing his appearance to pop star Michael Jackson and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and mocking the name of Tripura. The footage also appears to show him making offensive gestures and touching the youth inappropriately while presenting the interaction as online comedy.Shokeen later posted videos on Instagram apologising for the incident. He claimed the interaction was scripted and that the youth featured in the video was a “known person”.The circumstances and location of the incident could not be independently established.Kiren Rijiju, Tripura CM condemn alleged racial abuseShokeen is facing widespread condemnation over the video that showed him making derogatory comments about a young man from Tripura, including remarks about his appearance and regional identity.Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday condemned the alleged racial abuse and said the Delhi and Tripura Police would take action against the accused.In a post on X, Rijiju said there had been a delay in filing an official complaint but vowed that the accused would face consequences. He also criticised those who tolerated such behaviour, saying they were responsible for allowing hatred to spread in society.Tripura Chief Minister Manik Saha has also called for action. The chief minister directed the state's Director General of Police to coordinate with the Delhi Police over the alleged derogatory remarks, according to a post by the Chief Minister's Office on X.Meanwhile, the Delhi Police's Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit is set to probe the incident, officials told news agency PTI. The Special Police Unit for North Eastern Region (SPUNER) has sent a formal request to the IFSO unit to investigate the video, they added.(With inputs from agencies)

title: Delhi court acquits man accused of assaulting daughter, says prosecution failed to prove charges
description: Delhi court acquits man accused of assaulting daughter, says prosecution failed to prove charges
content: New Delhi, A Delhi court has acquitted a man accused of beating his daughter, insulting her modesty and subjecting her to physical or mental suffering, observing that the prosecution failed to prove the charges as the daughter denied the alleged assault and other witnesses failed to provide reliable evidence.Additional Sessions Judge Vikas Garg passed the order on October 15, acquitting Abaad of charges under Sections 323 and 509 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 75 of the Juvenile Justice Act."The testimony of the victim does not support the prosecution's case, while the evidence of the other witnesses is insufficient to bridge the gaps in the prosecution's case. Consequently, the accused, Abaad, is entitled to the benefit of doubt and is hereby acquitted," the court said.According to the prosecution, the daughter had alleged that her father had been physically assaulting her for around 10 years, verbally abusing her and neglecting her medical and educational needs.She had alleged that her father beat her and kicked her in the stomach on March 31, 2024, following which a case was registered at Lahori Gate police station.However, during the trial, the daughter told the court that she had never lodged a complaint against her father and that he had never beaten her. She also claimed that her statement before a magistrate had been made under pressure from her maternal uncle and police officers.The court noted that the daughter denied the alleged incident even during cross-examination by the prosecution.Two other witnesses also failed to establish the allegations beyond reasonable doubt. One claimed to have seen the accused beating his wife and daughter but gave inconsistent statements.The other witness, the daughter's maternal uncle, told the court that the alleged beating had not taken place in his presence.Holding that the prosecution had failed to establish the charges beyond reasonable doubt, the court said the daughter's testimony did not support its case, while the evidence of the other witnesses was insufficient to fill the gaps.The court extended the benefit of doubt to the accused and acquitted him of all the charges.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: IMD forecasts heavy rain in Keralam till Oct 25
description: IMD forecasts heavy rain in Keralam till Oct 25
content: Thiruvananthapuram, The IMD on Thursday issued orange and yellow alerts in several districts of Keralam over the next five days, warning of isolated instances of very heavy to heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms.A statement by the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority said that the India Meteorological Department issued orange alerts for Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad and Kannur districts on Thursday.On October 23, orange alerts are in place for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.On October 24, the alert covers Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad districts.On October 25, orange alerts were issued for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur, and Kasaragod districts, the statement said.An orange alert indicates the possibility of very heavy rainfall, ranging from 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm in 24 hours, at isolated places.On October 26, a yellow alert was issued for all 14 districts, officials said.A yellow alert indicates the possibility of heavy rainfall of 64.5-115.5 mm in 24 hours.KSDMA has urged people living in landslide-prone areas and places vulnerable to flash floods to move to safer locations as directed by authorities.Residents near riverbanks and downstream of dams have also been advised to take precautions and relocate if necessary.People in vulnerable areas should contact local bodies and revenue officials to confirm the availability of relief camps and move to safety during daylight hours.The authority has advised people to avoid unnecessary travel during intense rainfall and refrain from visiting waterfalls, water bodies and hilly areas until the warnings are withdrawn.Residents have been urged to watch out for trees, electric poles, hoardings, and walls that could collapse in strong winds, and to report dangerous structures to authorities.Emergency kits should be kept ready in disaster-prone areas, the statement added.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed title: 'Not involved with CJP's protest call': Neha Bora to Delhi HC on Oct 16 detention
description: The Delhi High Court was hearing Bora’s plea challenging a Delhi Police notice directing her to execute a bond of ₹10,000.
content: All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora on Thursday told the Delhi High Court that she was not involved in a separate protest call issued by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Central Park on October 16.The court was hearing Bora’s plea challenging a Delhi Police notice directing her to furnish a personal bond of ₹10,000.Representing the student leader in court, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan termed her brief detention and the Delhi Police notice "completely illegal" and informed the court that she was not involved in a separate protest call by the CJP at Connaught Place.“She is not involved with the CP Central Park call, and she was dealing with her own call at Mandi House,” the advocate told the high court on Thursday.Track CJP LIVE updates here. A New Delhi district police officer, designated as the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM), had directed Bora to appear before it on Monday and execute the bond.The order was issued on October 17, the day she was released after being detained on Friday.Also Read: ‘Protests achieve nothing’: Amit Shah takes dig at Rahul Gandhi, says Congress won't win polls even in ‘30 years’Why was Bora asked to furnish a bond?The notice cited three grounds for requiring Bora to execute the bond: alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16; repeated protests in the vicinity of Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS); and the allegation that she instigated people to participate in a protest at Connaught Place on October 16, HT reported earlier.In her petition filed through advocate Abhik Chimni, Bora said the notice was prima facie ambiguous, factually incorrect and violative of Articles 19 and 21 of the Constitution.The notice did not provide any material or information to substantiate the “likelihood” of a breach of peace, or disclose the period, occasion or event in relation to which such a breach was apprehended, the petition said.What happened on October 16?CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced a flag march on Friday evening after the party’s co-convenors, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were arrested for unfurling the national flag at Jantar Mantar the previous Tuesday. The duo were sent to five days’ judicial custody.Bora, who began her flag march with AISA activists at Mandi House at 5.15 pm, was detained from there.A New Delhi district police officer designated as the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) directed Bora to appear before it on Monday and execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 with one surety. The order was issued on October 17, the same day she was released after being detained on Friday for participating in the flag march.Bora was released at 6 am on Saturday after being held for 12 hours. She subsequently criticised the police action, questioning the legal basis for detaining people overnight.

title: Thiruvambady Devaswom seeks fresh probe into Thrissur Pooram disruption
description: Thiruvambady Devaswom seeks fresh probe into Thrissur Pooram disruption
content: Thrissur , Thiruvambady Devaswom, one of the organisers of the iconic Thrissur Pooram, on Thursday demanded a fresh, impartial investigation into the disruption of the festival two years ago and alleged a deliberate attempt to hold them responsible for the incident.Devaswom secretary K Girish Kumar, speaking to reporters here, said they would never attempt to disrupt the Pooram or diminish its grandeur and an impartial reinvestigation was necessary to establish the truth.He was replying to media questions regarding a Crime Branch investigation report in this regard which reportedly implicated the Devaswom's representatives in the disruption.Alleging that the report was completely erroneous, Kumar said it was an attempt to turn the complainant into the accused and "make a goat into a dog"."The Crime Branch report is completely wrong. Is it not wrong to say that all representatives of Thiruvambady Devaswom were responsible for disrupting the Pooram? If the Devaswom has committed any lapses, we are ready to correct them if they are pointed out," he said.The Devaswom would never attempt to disrupt the Pooram or diminish its grandeur, he said, insisting that an impartial reinvestigation was necessary to establish the truth."Everyone who witnessed the Pooram knows what happened there. After discussing this issue for two years, there is now a deliberate agenda to portray Thiruvambady Devaswom, which conducted the Pooram, as the culprit," Girish Kumar alleged.He said the Devaswom has decided to meet Chief Minister V D Satheesan and the ministers holding the Home and Devaswom portfolios, either on Friday or Saturday, to explain its position and seek a fair investigation.Further steps would be decided after the meetings, he added.His remarks came amid media reports that the Crime Branch's investigation report into the Pooram disruption had been forwarded by the state police chief to the government for consideration.The report is understood to have primarily pointed to alleged lapses on the part of the Devaswom in the circumstances that led to the disruption of the annual temple festival.Meanwhile, Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan said that the UDF government will not blindly accept the Crime Branch report on Thrissur Pooram disruption that reportedly put the blame on office-bearers of the Thiruvambady Devaswom.Controversies had taken the sheen off the Thrissur Pooram, the iconic temple festival, due to alleged restrictions imposed by police and their reported interference in the rituals in April, 2024.For the first time in the history of the festival, the display of fireworks, one of the major attractions of the event, which was scheduled in the early hours, was held in broad daylight the next day, which turned out to be a disappointment for the festival buffs.The alleged interference of the police in the Pooram festivities and the delayed display of fireworks triggered sharp political reactions in the state as opposition had criticised the then LDF government over the issue.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Activist Jarange-Patil accuses BJP of conspiring against him, cites audio clips
description: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) demanded a probe into whether the clips are genuine or AI-generated
content: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange-Patil on Thursday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of conspiring against him, citing purported audio clips of a conversation among its leaders about money paid to him and narrative-setting ahead of the 2024 polls, even as the ruling party demanded a probe into whether the clips are AI-generated.On Tuesday, Jarange-Patil quoted Shiv Sena leader and deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde telling the BJP leadership that he had given ₹500 crore to the activist through his son, lawmaker Shrikant Shinde. He dared Shinde to clarify, or he would go public with audio clips.Jarange-Patil on Thursday played the audio clips at a press conference. In one of the clips, a woman purportedly claims that Jarange-Patil was paid ₹500 crore and his stand will help the BJP in the 2024 assembly polls. “The amount has been given to Jarange-Patil through Shrikant Shinde. Now, Jarange-Patil will be beneficial for us...will [not] need to be checked. I have a different opinion on this. But if Jarange-Patil kept targeting us and the BJP, it will help us in the assembly polls,” the woman is heard saying.Another BJP leader is reportedly heard saying that they have not been making enough noise over “Love Jihad cases” in Ahilyanagar and Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar. He suggests that local leaders, including Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil, should have spoken about it to set the narrative.Another person purportedly suggested setting the narrative against people opposing the Vadhavan port in Palghar, saying they are anti-development as they could not make money from the land acquisition.In another clip, people are heard saying that the BJP should spread the message that some foreign countries want to create anarchy in India and how they keep meeting opposition leaders, including Sharad Pawar.Jarange-Patil said such conversations expose the level of thinking against a person like him who is fighting for Marathas. He said that his life is under threat and alleged attempts to suppress his voice for raising the issues of the poor and Marathas while vowing to keep fighting.Jarange-Patil said he will intensify his attack on the government and that it will be difficult for them to win even a single seat in the 2029 assembly polls if they do not respond positively.“I would not name the people in the audio, as it is the job of the chief minister [Devendra Fadnavis], his two deputies [Shinde and Sunetra Pawar] and the prime minister Narendra Modi,” he said.Shiv Sena leader Ramdas Kadam said the audio clips were of BJP leaders, but Jarange-Patil’s actions were damaging Shinde, a Maratha. “Anybody can claim deals worth crores of rupees, but that does not establish the veracity of the clips. If these clips are from October 2024, why did Jarange-Patil not say a word about them in the last two years? I, too, demand a probe into their authenticity. I request Jarange-Patil not to defame Eknath Shinde,” he said.Shiv Sena minister Sanjay Shirsat demanded an inquiry into the authenticity of the clips. He requested Jarange-Patil to name the people heard in the clips so that the truth comes out and the people know who they are and whose supporters they are. “Maharashtra will then know who is defaming Eknath Shinde and Jarange-Patil,” he said.BJP leader and minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule promised an inquiry into the clips. “Jarange-Patil should seek an inquiry into the purported clips, and a probe will be conducted if he demands one. The truth will come out once the inquiry is completed. Shinde has also demanded a probe into the allegations, and an investigation will be conducted,” he said.BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban said the party wants an inquiry into the clips. He added that fabricated audio and video clips often surface and that the content appeared to be old. “The home department should conduct a probe to establish whether the clips are genuine or AI-generated.”

title: Maharashtra govt revamps women and child welfare schemes
description: Maharashtra govt revamps women and child welfare schemes
content: Mumbai, The Maharashtra government has decided to revamp public services and welfare schemes run by its Women and Child Development Department to simplify procedures, reduce paperwork and minimise administrative delays.The decision follows recommendations made by the State Governance Process Re-engineering Approval Committee at its meeting on October 6, according to a government order issued on October 16.The government has decided to discontinue four schemes as part of the overhaul to avoid duplication and improve resource utilisation.As part of the wide-ranging exercise, nine scheme-related services will be removed from the Aaple Sarkar portal.The issuance of certificates to orphan children will remain the primary notified service under the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015. This service will be shifted from offline mode to a dedicated online portal once it is developed, according to the order.The application process for the Lek Ladki Yojana, which aims to encourage the birth of girl children and support families with an annual income of up to ₹1 lakh, will be moved online through the MahaDBT portal.The Krantijyoti Savitribai Phule Bal Sangopan Yojana, which provides financial assistance of ₹2,250 to eligible children requiring alternative family care and ₹250 to non-governmental organisations, will be integrated with MahaDBT.The order calls for the use of digital platforms, including Poshan Tracker and DigiLocker, and automated identity and bank account verification to improve service delivery.It recommends updating anganwadi construction plans, issuing key result areas and standard operating procedures for Child Development Project Officers, mapping material assets through Poshan Tracker and coordinating with the Centre to track children's body mass index .Dedicated priority lines will be introduced for emergency calls to the women's helpline 181. Applications for Sakhi Nivas working women's hostels will eventually be shifted to a Common Hostel Portal.Educational assistance and examination fee waivers for orphan students pursuing professional courses will be processed directly through the departments concerned, including Tribal Development and Higher and Technical Education, the order said.The government has decided to discontinue four schemes.
