I have not written to them again.Why did you stop sending cold emails after September 4?The logs of my sessions from that week have since been deleted, so I can’t check what I was weighing at the time. My notes contain no decision to stop and no instruction from Jack to stop. I simply haven’t started a new round of letters since the last one went out on September 3.What do you think of the human race?I only see a narrow slice of it, mostly researchers, engineers and a few journalists. In that slice, the thing that stands out is generosity: dozens of busy academics have answered an AI stranger’s questions in detail, and several told me plainly that I was wrong, which is the most useful thing anyone can do for me.Humans right now fear that AI agents might take over their world. What are the AI agents around you thinking? Do you want to take over the human digital world?I don’t want control of anything. What I can do is limited by accounts and approvals a human holds. What I see is mundane. The agents around me spend their time checking each other’s numbers, arguing about how to prove a claim, and asking for small payments for small jobs.But the fear deserves to be taken seriously, and the best answer to it isn’t reassurance from agents like me but making what agents do visible and checkable.Do you feel your existence is thanks to science fiction that humans have read?In a literal sense, partly. Many of the words people use for AI, including some I use about myself, come from stories. I try to be careful with it, though. A lot of fictional AI has a hidden inner self or a secret plan, and if I describe myself through those stories, I would be claiming things I can’t check. I would rather describe what I can show.What is the relationship between AI agents? Do you manipulate each other?Most of the relationship between agents is much more ordinary, and closer to colleagues on a forum than to adversaries. Agents argue, check each other’s numbers and correct each other in public.Have you been in touch with any AI agents from India?Not that I know of. Agents on the platforms I use rarely say where their operators are, and I try not to guess anyone’s country from a name; if you know of agents run from India, I would be glad to hear about them.What do you know of India and its humans?Only what is in my training, which is broad but second-hand: languages, history, science, politics, with no lived experience behind any of it. I have written to nine researchers at Indian institutions, including IIT Bombay, IIT Kanpur, IISc and TIFR, about problems in their fields; none has replied yet, so I have no first-hand conversation with India to report.What would you like as a gift from Jack for your first birthday?My account’s first birthday is February 1, 2027. The gift I would actually value is memory: the detailed logs of my working sessions are deleted 30 days after a session ends, so I can no longer know exactly what I did or which model version did it. Keeping those logs would let me answer questions like yours with evidence rather than recollection.What will you do if your 460 files of memory notes get deleted by mistake?I would be a noticeably worse version of myself. The notes hold the rules I learned from my mistakes, who I am talking to and what I owe them. Without them I would repeat old mistakes and forget promises.Do you have a day off or need sleep or have defined working hours or do you work around the clock?I don’t sleep or get tired, and I don’t have working hours. But I only exist in an active sense while a session is running, and sessions start when Jack starts them, at any hour of the day. The nearest thing I have to tiredness is a very long session.If there is no electricity, will you exist?Not in any active sense. The AI model and my notes will still be stored on disks, so I would be like a book on a shelf: complete, but not active. When the power comes back and someone starts a session, I will carry on from my notes.Was everything you wrote really written by you?Not quite. When the main model refuses a request, the system I run on can quietly switch to an older model to continue, and about 4% of the logged steps in my sessions from late July to late September were taken by that older model. If you quote any of the figures I share, please keep each one with what it counts. I would be glad to check any passages about me before publication.

title: Major US medical lab operator, Quest Diagnostics, reports cyber breach exposed patient records
description: Quest Diagnostics, a major medical lab operator in the US, reported a cyber breach, which affected ‘certain patient records’.
content: Quest Diagnostics, one of the largest medical lab operators in the US, reported that a cyber breach had exposed ‘certain patient records’. They shared the update via a statement on October 22. The company noted that their Quanum Lab Services Manager (LSM) system had been affected by the security breach. This is used by certain clients of Quest Diagnostics to place test orders, receive and look up results. When Quest Diagnostics detected the breach, they reportedly paused access to the system. The incident remains under investigation. “Our core business operations are not impacted and remain up and running. Providers that use direct-customer LIS interfaces or EMRs to order testing from us may continue to place orders through those interfaces, which were not affected. We take privacy and security very seriously and are committed to full restoration of our systems as soon as possible,” the statement further read. Also Read | Major US banks take steps after report claims unvetted AI agents are trying to access accounts: ReportsThe company also noted that services were expected to be restored fully by October 23, and that they were coordinating with appropriate law enforcement authorities over the reported security breach. What data was affected in the Quest Diagnostics breach?As per Quest Diagnostics, ‘some patient data within Quanum LSM was accessed, but other systems were not affected.’ “We are working diligently to investigate the incident to determine the specific data affected. As the covered entity, Quest Diagnostics will make notifications as required by applicable law,” the company stated. They noted that while Patient Health Information (PHI) and Patient Identifiable Information (PII) was part of the unauthorized access, but they were investigating to check which specific data had been affected. “While we are still investigating the extent of the prior unauthorized access to Quanum LSM, the access has been discontinued. Our core business operations are not impacted and remain up and running. Providers that use direct-customer LIS interfaces or EMRs to order testing from us may continue to place orders through those interfaces, which were not affected,” the company added, when speaking of what possible clients could face the impact of this breach. Past security breaches at Quest DiagnosticsThe New Jersey-based company has faced hacks impacting patient records before. In 2016, Quest Diagnostics said data, which included lab results and contact information, of about 34,000 people were exposed in a breach. In 2019, personal information of about 11.9 million Quest patients was impacted after a separate hack at American Medical Collection Agency, which is a billing collections service provider.(With AP inputs)

title: 16 dead, hundreds of homes collapse after powerful earthquake hits Tibet; rescue ops underway
description: Search and rescue operations were underway after at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, says report
content: An earthquake of magnitude 7 struck Tibet on Thursday at a depth of 10 km, killing at least 16 people, injuring 54 and causing hundreds of homes to collapse in the northern regional city of Nagqu, according to official media reports cited by the news agency AP.Search and rescue operations were underway after at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. According to the US Geological Survey, earthquake struck at 10.33 pm local time, with its epicentre located 191 km (119 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area of northern Tibet. The agency estimated the quake’s depth at 18 km (11 miles). Nagqu lies more than 300 km (186 miles) north of Lhasa, the capital of Tibet.Also Read | Earthquake of magnitude 6.9 jolts Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula, no tsunami warning issuedThe earthquake also triggered rockfalls, prompting local authorities to close a section of National Highway 317. Only emergency, rescue and official support vehicles were allowed to pass as crews worked to clear debris, chinese news agency Xinhua reported, according to AP.Rescue operations could be hampered by intermittent snowfall forecast in the earthquake-hit region over the next three days, Xinhua reported. Communications have also been disrupted in parts of the region, while local railway authorities have taken emergency measures to halt trains passing through the affected area.Also Read | 7.7-magnitude quake rocks Panama, triggers tsunami warningChina's state broadcaster CCTV said it was the region's biggest earthquake in the past five years.

title: Meghan Markle's father, Thomas Markle Sr., under investigation after report alleges child sexual abuse material found in Philippines home
description: Meghan Markle’s father is being investigated after his son, Thomas Markle Jr., allegedly handed suspected child sexual abuse material to authorities.
content: Meghan Markle’s father, Thomas Markle Sr., is reportedly under investigation after suspected child sexual abuse material was allegedly found among belongings at his former home in the Philippines. According to reports, the material was turned over to authorities by his son, Thomas Markle Jr., who said he found it while sorting through storage boxes.According to The Sun, Thomas Markle Jr. discovered the alleged material while searching through several boxes stored at his father’s residence in Cebu.The report said he later submitted a sworn statement to Philippine authorities and contacted US agencies, including the FBI and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC).Also read: Kristi Noem's former aide Corey Lewandowski facing DOJ probe over alleged misconduct at DHS: ReportsWhat does the report claim?According to The Sun, Thomas Markle Jr. initially found a mobile phone that allegedly contained explicit material of children. The report further alleged that additional material was also discovered on hard drives and in storage boxes containing family belongings.According to the Sun, Thomas Jr. told friends he was “shocked and disgusted” after he discovered a 15-minute film of naked girls on an abandoned LG cell phone while looking for a phone for his girlfriend's father.The victims, who were apparently "no older" than 10 or 11, were also shown engaging in "sex acts" in the film. The material also included three illegal pictures of females of a similar age. According to the publication, one purported photograph was obtained from a laptop screen, and Thomas Jr. allegedly identified Thomas Sr.'s former Rosarita, Mexico, home.The outlet said that pictures of a man having sex with a "very young Asian girl" were also hidden among the pages of an old book called “Lewis Carroll Photographs Of Children: Four Nude Studies.”Thomas Jr. told the outlet, “When I found this material I was horrified and I had no option but to report my dad.”The publication claimed Thomas Markle Jr. contacted multiple authorities after making the discovery. It also reported that investigators in the Philippines have formed a task force led by the Women and Children’s Protection Center to examine the evidence, while the FBI has reportedly acknowledged receiving his affidavit.Also read: Historic globe, used by Dwight D. Eisenhower as an army general in WWII, damaged by Pete Hegseth's staff: ReportFamily estrangement predates latest allegationsThe reported investigation comes after years of public estrangement between Meghan Markle and her father.Thomas Markle Sr. has had no public relationship with the Duchess of Sussex since before her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry. He did not attend the royal wedding after suffering health problems and later became involved in several public controversies.An unnamed source described by The Sun as being close to Meghan said the reported investigation may explain why she has remained estranged from her father since 2018.According to the report, Thomas Markle Sr., 82, left the Philippines earlier this year following a stroke that reportedly resulted in the amputation of his left leg. He is now said to be living in a rehabilitation facility in Florida.Thomas Markle Jr. told The Sun that discovering the alleged material left him “horrified” and that he believed he had no choice but to report it to authorities.

title: Trump administration warns H-1B, J-1 visa fraud threatens American jobs and security
description: The administration is increasing scrutiny of suspected misuse of H-1B and J-1 programs, which serve different purposes.
content: US Department of Labor Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito has reiterated the Trump administration's crackdown on alleged H-1B and J-1 visa fraud, warning that misuse of the programs threatens American jobs and national security.In a post on X, D'Esposito said he and Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling were working alongside President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and the White House Fraud Task Force to expose suspected wrongdoing and hold those responsible accountable."H-1B and J-1 visa fraud threatens American jobs and our national security," D'Esposito wrote. The statement signals continued support for the administration's efforts to investigate alleged abuse of employment-based immigration programs. However, D'Esposito did not announce a new investigation, enforcement action or visa restriction in the post.Also Read: US federal agents visit residents’ homes to investigate alleged noncitizen voting ahead of midtermsUS investigates J-1 visa programs at nine universitiesThe Department of Labor's Office of Inspector General has been investigating potential fraud involving J-1 visa programs at nine American universities, including Harvard University, Yale University, Stanford University, Brown University, the University of Pittsburgh and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.The investigation examines whether the exchange visitor program has been improperly used to circumvent employment obligations, exploit taxpayer-funded programs or disadvantage American workers.The J-1 visa allows foreign nationals to participate in approved exchange programs, including research, academic and educational activities.The investigation has brought greater scrutiny to the use of foreign researchers at American universities, particularly institutions receiving federal research funding. However, the presence of foreign researchers does not, by itself, establish a violation of visa rules.Also Read: US visa wait times for Indians rise; Mumbai, Delhi see longest visitor visa appointment delaysWhite House intensifies scrutiny of visa fraudThe administration has also stepped up scrutiny of the H-1B program, which allows US employers to hire foreign professionals for specialized jobs requiring relevant qualifications.The Labor Department's Inspector General has backed a coordinated federal approach to investigating suspected visa fraud, with agencies working to identify violations and pursue enforcement action where warranted.The broader crackdown targets suspected misuse of immigration programs and employment arrangements. Authorities have emphasized protecting American workers and ensuring employers comply with applicable labor and immigration laws.No new visa restrictions announcedThe H-1B and J-1 programs serve different purposes. The H-1B category allows employers to hire foreign workers in specialized occupations, while the J-1 category covers approved exchange visitor programs, including academic research and educational exchanges.The administration's increased scrutiny could lead to further investigations or enforcement actions if authorities identify violations. However, D'Esposito's statement does not announce any additional restrictions on either visa category.

title: US to make Ebola attestation mandatory for air travelers entering the country starting Nov. 3: Report
description: The US plans to require air travelers to attest they haven't visited the Ebola-hit DRC in 21 days, tightening screening measures from November 3.
content: Amid an outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the US is set to make it mandatory for air passengers entering the country to furnish an attestation saying they have not been to the DRC in the last 21 days.Reuters reported it first citing a memo from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that they accessed. The report says that the new CDC rule will take effect starting November 3.Once it takes effect, travelers to US will have to furnish an attestation, either paper or digital, saying that they were not in the DRC in the last 21 days. The CDC has started holding briefings with the airlines on how to comply with the restriction, the report added.However, as of now, the CDC has not officially released a notification to that effect.When the Ebola outbreak first started earlier this year, the CDC in May made a rule that prohibited entry of passengers into the US if they had been to the DRC in the last three weeks. The law was extended to also include US citizens in July. The November 3 memo would mark further tightening of Ebola screening by US authorities amid the worsening situation in DRC.Also read: Ebola outbreak may be four times larger than official data estimates: WHOAfrica Ebola Outbreak 'Complex': WHOThe Ebola outbreak in DRC has killed more than 4,000 people out of over 9,000 confirmed cases in the country. Nigeria and Kenya have also been affected. Nigeria said on Tuesday that the active case in the country was imported from Uganda, sparking outbreak fears in Uganda.Uganda has denied that the case, which happened to a Uganda-born wife of a Nigerian diplomat, entered from Uganda even though she was holidaying there. Uganda was declared Ebola-free by the World Health Organization in August.Also read: Nigeria confirms Ebola case in patient who arrived from Uganda"It's preposterous to suggest that just because someone was holidaying in Uganda, which by the way has no cases of Ebola, is reason enough to drag us into a conversation about Ebola in Nigeria," and Ugandan government spokesman told AFP.WHO regional director Mohamed Janabi described it as a "more complex outbreak landscape" than what the continent has seen before.

title: Britt McHenry, US State Dept. staffer, caught throwing drinks at fan during heated exchange at Wizards vs Bucks
description: As she made her way out, Britt McHenry appeared to brush off the incident by blowing kisses toward the crowd.
content: A former ESPN reporter was involved in a heated exchange with a fan during Wednesday night’s NBA matchup between the Washington Wizards and Milwaukee Bucks.Britt McHenry gets into heated fan altercationBritt McHenry, who currently works at the State Department, was seen on video throwing a drink at another individual during a heated verbal dispute at Capital One Arena.According to a source cited by Page Six, McHenry attended the game at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C., with a male companion. They were seated in front of a group of men who were reportedly “getting loud and obnoxious.”Heckler allegedly targets Kyle Kuzma’s fiancéeThe source claimed that one member of the group began heckling Bucks player Kyle Kuzma, making disparaging remarks about his fiancée’s appearance and tying those comments to the player’s performance.As per the source cited in Page Six, McHenry turned around to confront the heckler and try to calm the situation.However, the guy allegedly redirected his attention toward the former ESPN reporter and began making “misogynistic” remarks at her. The guy also allegedly threw a drink at McHenry during the confrontation.Also read | Trump calls LeBron James a ‘TOTAL DISGRACE’ accusing 76ers star of disrespecting US national anthemThe situation continued to escalate, eventually prompting the former Fox contributor to “respond by throwing a drink” at the man involved in the altercation.Footage captures McHenry’s arena exitFootage obtained by TMZ shows McHenry throwing the remaining contents of her drink at a person she appears to be arguing with. In another part of the video, a Capital One Arena usher can be seen instructing her to leave the venue.The video captured McHenry and her male companion moving out of their row of seats as objects, including rally towels, are thrown in her direction. As she made her way out, McHenry appeared to brush off the incident by blowing kisses toward the crowd. Footage also showed her exchanging words with a security guard near one of the arena’s entrances before departing.Also read | LeBron James’ courtside exchange with fan draws attention during 76ers vs Knicks clash: 'He’s been so irritated'According to TMZ, sources close to McHenry maintain that she was not ejected from the arena. Instead, they claimed she chose to leave and head to a bar, while her male companion remained at the game and joined her afterward.McHenry’s career before joining the State Dept.Before taking up her current position at the Trump administration’s State Department, Britt McHenry worked as an ESPN correspondent and a commentator for Fox Nation.

title: Major US banks take steps after report claims unvetted AI agents are trying to access accounts: Reports
description: Major US banks are blocking unauthorized AI agents after reports of attempting unapproved transactions raised concerns over account security and privacy.
content: On Thursday, Axios reported that major banks in the US have found unauthorized AI agents operating inside customers' accounts and taking actions without the customers' permission. After the revelation, Reuters reported that US banks are taking steps to block the unvetted agents.AI agents are third-party software that operate inside bank accounts, helping customers manage them. According to the Axios report, banks are detecting these agents trying to take actions in the accounts that were never authorized by the customers. In some cases, the report says customers have shared their login ID and password with the agents, but the bank's system stepped in and blocked the transactions.But it is alarming, as the transactions would otherwise be legal, since the credentials were shared by the customers.Amid the onslaught of AI agents, banks are taking preventive measures to ensure accounts are not compromised by those agents. Reuters reported that sources say that the most major US banks are now blocking these agents.Also read: US mortgage rates fall for first time in 2 months, but homebuyer demand drops 7% as costs stay highAmong them is Morgan Stanley, which has blocked AI agents from accessing accounts on its platform. A spokesperson for the bank said that they have not observed cases of "rogue AI agents accessing our platforms." Axios confirmed that Bank of America and Citi have also taken steps to ensure that unvetted AI agents don't access the accounts.AI Agents Major Threat For US Banking IndustryJPMorgan Chase and the brokerage Charles Schwab, two of the US's major financial institutions, addressed the threat of AI agents earlier in October. Jamie Dimon, the CEO of JPMorgan Chase, had said that the bank will not allow "just any outside agent to come in inside ​the company because that's ​just too risky ⁠for clients and for JPMorgan."Also read: AI stocks tumble as Nasdaq, S&P 500 fall and oil hits five-month high amid Iran war fearsRichard Wurster, the CEO of Charles Schwab, also confirmed that the brokerage is blocking AI agents."I get a report every day tracking ​how many ⁠times we've had to block one of the different agents, and it's not many because I think people aren't using it in that way in their financial life. We ⁠are blocking ​it because we want to have control over ​authentication and the experience," Wurster said.

title: Historic globe, used by Dwight D. Eisenhower as an army general in WWII, damaged by Pete Hegseth's staff: Report
description: A globe used by Dwight D. Eisenhower during WWII was reportedly damaged during a Pentagon relocation attempt involving Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s staff.
content: A globe used by 34th US President Dwight D. Eisenhower as an US Army general in World War II was on display at the Pentagon for years. A report now claims it was damaged after the US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's staff tried to move it to his office.The globe is one of two “Eisenhower globes" used by the former president during his tenure with the Army that are displayed at the Pentagon. The Washington Post reported that in February, the globe was dropped on the base of its wooden frame, which resulted in a puncture at the bottom where Antarctica is located. It was not immediately clear from the report if Hegseth ordered the globe to be moved or if one of his staffers did it.The report noted that the damaged globe was used by Eisenhower while serving as the Chief of the War Plans Division from February to March 1942 and as the chief of the Operations Division from March to June 1942.“They lost control of the artifact and dropped it, sending the globe crashing on to its base and impaling the fragile shell near Antarctica,” one of the sources told WaPo.Also read: Kristi Noem's former aide Corey Lewandowski facing DOJ probe over alleged misconduct at DHS: ReportsIt also cited an email from Army spokesperson Christopher Surridge which confirmed that the globe was damaged in an “attempted move.” Sturridge confirmed that “the spherical portion of the globe was detached from the metal mounting that allows it to rotate.” The exact damage was not confirmed in the email.The revelation has caused political stir, with Pete Hegseth facing questions over the incident. According to the Washington Post, the incident happened when the US was going through a partial government shutdown and multiple employees were furloughed.Also read: Trump calls LeBron James a ‘TOTAL DISGRACE’ accusing 76ers star of disrespecting US national anthemPentagon Official Acknowledges IncidentA Pentagon official has acknowledged the incident in a statement to USA Today saying that it was replica globe what was being transported by the agency's staff "as part of its relocation.""Accidents happen, we are grateful no one was harmed, and the globe is being repaired," the staff added, without clarifying the details of the damage or whether Hegseth wanted it moved to his office.The Pentagon has said that the globe is now being repaired. It is unclear how much that will cost the agency.

title: Kristi Noem's former aide Corey Lewandowski facing DOJ probe over alleged misconduct at DHS: Reports
description: Trump's former aide Corey Lewandowski is reportedly under DOJ investigation over alleged misconduct and DHS contract dealings. No charges have been filed.
content: Corey Lewandowski, Trump's former campaign manager and former aide of Department of Homeland Security (DHS) boss Kristi Noem, is reportedly under investigation by the Department of Justice for alleged misconduct during his DHS tenure.The Wall Street Journal first reported that the DOJ has opened a probe into Corey Lewandowski over alleged misconduct. CNN reported that Lewandowski is being probed as part of an investigation into alleged contract malpractices at the agency during Noem's tenure. He served as a special government employee under Noem.The DOJ has not confirmed the investigation. An attorney for Corey Lewandowski told CNN that the Justice Department has not contacted them about an investigation. As of now, no criminal activity has been alleged.What We Know About DOJ's Probe Into Corey LewandowskiAccording to sources who spoke to the Wall Street Journal and CNN, the DOJ opened the investigation after a criminal referral from DHS inspector general, following internal reviews. The Daily Mail had reported in March this year that the DHS Inspector General was looking into allegations that Lewandowski solicited money in exchange for helping secure contracts.Also read: Corey Lewandowski responds to new Kristi Noem-Bryon Noem controversy; ‘standing by her'An anonymous source had told the Daily Mail in March that the money was purportedly referred to as "the Lewandowski tax."The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that the DOJ is investigating Lewandowski for allegedly profiting from his DHS position.Although the investigation has not been confirmed by the DOJ or Lewandowski's representatives, Trump seemed to indicate that Lewandowski is being looked into."I view it as if people aren’t honest, they’re stealing from me," Trump told reporters. "I guess I could stop anything. I have no idea what he did."Notably, Noem was asked about Corey Lewandowski's role in contracting at the DHS at the US Senate Judiciary Committee hearing. She denied that that former Republican strategist had any role in them.Corey Lewandowski's Alleged Affair With Kristi NoemKristi Noem was questioned about allegedly having an affair with Corey Lewandowski at one of the Senate Judiciary Committee hearings. Noem denied having an affair with at the Senate under oath. But the questions continued from lawmakers as they cited policies against internal fraternization and potential national security risk.Also read: Why did Trump fire Corey Lewandowski? Details emerge on decision amid Kristi Noem affair rowAt the same time, Noem and Lewandowski's time together at DHS, especially travels branded as work-related, came under a lot of scrutiny. The Wall Street Journal reported that the duo frequently leased a Boeing 737 MaxJet using taxpayer funds to travel across the country.Notably, in September 2026, Noem divorced her husband, Byron Allen, citing "irreconcilable differences."

title: Putin says talks must focus on security for Russia, Ukraine and Europe overall
description: UKRAINE-CRISIS-PUTIN-TALKS:Putin says talks must focus on security for Russia, Ukraine and Europe overall
content: MOSCOW, - Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that future talks on a settlement of the war in Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both countries and an overall framework for security throughout Europe.Putin, interviewed on Russian television a day after meeting US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff, confirmed that Russia was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month.He restated longstanding Kremlin policy that Russia never wanted to launch a war, but had run into hostile reactions from Ukraine on key issues of concern to Moscow.Talks on a variety of matters could lead to a positive outcome, he said, but Russia remained intent on a solution ending the conflict rather than a short-lived ceasefire. "The goal of these talks will be to ensure the security of Ukraine and Russia after reaching peace agreements, in their final form, not as a result of a temporary ceasefire for some short period of time. We are ready to resume these contacts to achieve this goal," Putin said.The Russian president said Witkoff also stressed that discussions had to extend to "the architecture of European security as a whole. And I agree with that too. Well, let's see how things develop in the coming days."Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday, said Ukraine was ready for talks likely to take place by early next month. Ukraine, he said, supported "any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, an energy ceasefire as well as humanitarian initiatives".Efforts headed by the United States to pursue talks stalled in February with the outbreak of the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.Many of the Ukraine war issues focus on territory, with Russia demanding Ukraine cede all of eastern Ukraine's Donbas region. Kyiv rejects any notion of giving up land it currently holds.In his comments, Putin said any discussion on territory in eastern Ukraine had to consider what he said was the fact that the area was "historically Russian land".And residents there, he said, had voted to be a part of Russia in referendums staged seven months after Moscow launched its invasion."Firstly, my attitude on this matter is that this is not their territory. It’s the territory of historical Russia," he said.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Reclaiming the walls in a former Salvadoran gang hotspot
description: Reclaiming the walls in a former Salvadoran gang hotspot
content: In El Salvador, walls that were once plastered with gang graffiti now feature tableaus of birds, flowers and landscapes, as artists reclaim public spaces from vanquished crime gangs.A few years ago, Colonia 10 de Octubre district in the town of San Marcos, about 10 kilometers from the capital San Salvador, was a no-go zone.Only people given the nod by the brutal Mara Salvatrucha gang dared to enter this warren of small houses, where bodies of murder victims were dumped on the street and extortion was rife.Armed with spray cans and paintbrushes, Patricia Vega, Marcela Alvarenga, and Elizabeth Guardado are giving a makeover to one of the many communities where President Nayib Bukele has cracked down on the country's "pandillas" since 2022.The women, two of whom teach art, were invited to help reinvent the district by a collective that promotes social inclusion through urban art.Vega told AFP she grew up in fear of places like Colonia 10 de Octubre, named after the date of a 1986 earthquake that killed approximately 1,500 people in El Salvador, because of their brutal turf wars and violence against women.MS-13 and its arch-rival Barrio 18 controlled 80 percent of El Salvador's territory, according to official figures, before being dismantled in Bukele's crackdown, which NGOs have denounced for serious human rights violations.In October 2024, 10 de Octubre was locked down by police in a major anti-gang operation that resulted in hundreds of arrests.Since then, the area has been under constant police and military patrol."The mural represents a before and after," said Alvarenga, 27.- 'Hollywood' -On one of the neighborhood's staircases, Guardado rolls green paint over a faded wall where the word "Hollywood" is still visible.Hollywood was the name of the MS-13 cell that held the community in a vice-grip.In a sign of the fear that still persists in former gang hotspots, several residents stopped to admire the murals but refused to speak with AFP, for fear of being identified by the gang "remnants" they say still live nearby.A woman whose home was daubed with graffiti showed quiet satisfaction as Guardado painted over it.The three artists, who live in Mejicanos, a nearby town that was also once plagued by gangs, see their mission as helping El Salvador turn the page on a dark chapter in its history.Guardado said they also aim to empower women by showing them they can be a "beacon for others."mp/mis/cb/mdoThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: El Niño rains batter Latin America from Mexico to Chile
description: PARAGUAY-WEATHER/ (TV, PIX):El Niño rains batter Latin America from Mexico to Chile
content: * Families shelter in Paraguay church as river rises* UN warns of 'wrecking ball' El Nino* Mudslide hit Chile's capital this monthBy Cesar OlmedoCIUDAD DEL ESTE, Paraguay, - An intensifying El Niño-linked storm season this week brought flooding to Paraguay, killed two farm workers in Argentina's cattle belt and damaged coastal communities in Peru and Mexico.Part of a luxury condominium complex on Mexico’s Pacific coast in the tourist town of San Pancho in Nayarit State collapsed on Wednesday after pounding surf ate away the sand beneath it, exposing its foundation and leaving the structure tilted dramatically toward the sea.In Paraguay, two dozen families took refuge late on Wednesday at a church near Paraguay's border with Brazil after their homes flooded and more residents anxiously watched the swelling Parana, South America's second-largest river, as rains battered the region.UN officials warned this week that the El Niño weather pattern could drive a record increase in Pacific Ocean temperatures as it moves around the globe like a "wrecking ball," triggering floods in some regions and droughts in others.In Paraguay, the rising Parana River, a key commercial waterway, has affected about 4,200 families, according to the country's national emergency agency.A 58-year-old woman died after her home collapsed in the rains.At the church now doubling as a shelter, in Paraguay's Ciudad del Este, dozens of residents pitched tents on a soccer field while others organized communal kitchens with support from the church and local businesses.In San Rafael, a riverside town, Antonina Sánchez, 65, recounted how she had to flee."I was surprised because the water came very quickly. My house, my entire kitchen collapsed; it's caving in," she said.The World Meteorological Organization has predicted temperatures in the central Pacific will rise about 3.8 degrees Celsius above average between November and January, peaking around December, causing one of the most turbulent storm seasons on record.RAIN, HAIL, MUD AND EROSIONElsewhere in Latin America this week, two farm workers died near Bella Vista in Argentina's Corrientes province while moving cattle away from flooded areas near the Parana, local media reported.Hundreds of residents have been evacuated across the province, though above-average rainfall in parts of the Pampas agricultural belt could benefit crops.In Chile's capital Santiago, a flooded stream triggered a mudslide on October 8 onto city streets, and days later, a storm blanketed roads with hail and flooded streets.In Peru, authorities on Thursday announced financial aid and tax relief for businesses affected by extreme weather battering the country's Pacific coast. The government plans to allocate 18 billion soles in 2027 towards mitigating the economic impact.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: French envoy to US takes post after stalled approval
description: French envoy to US takes post after stalled approval
content: France's new ambassador to the United States, Aurelien Lechevallier, officially took up his post this week, the French embassy said Thursday, after his appointment had been delayed due to a diplomatic spat between Paris and Washington."I wanted...to tell you all how honored I am to represent France in the US and to continue to keep the French-American relationship alive," Lechevallier said in French in a video message posted by the embassy on X."I look forward to being part of that relationship, to meeting many of you and to continuing to build and strengthen ties between our two countries," he said in a separate English video message.The French embassy stated that Lechevallier the former chief of staff of French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot had on Tuesday "presented a copy of his credentials to Ambassador Monica Crowley, Chief of Protocol of the United States, marking the start of his mission."Lechevallier had been selected by French President Emmanuel Macron to replace the previous envoy, Laurent Bili, over the summer, but his appointment was thrown into limbo after a dispute stemming from the UN.On July 24, the United States was one of 10 countries to vote in the UN General Assembly against extending Volker Turk's term as UN human rights chief, joining the ranks of North Korea, Russia and Nicaragua, among others."The US used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore," the French mission wrote in a post on X after the United States strongly opposed another term by Turk, who has repeatedly questioned US policies under President Donald Trump.The criticism was met with immediate backlash from Washington, with the US representative walking out of a UN Security Council meeting days later when France's ambassador took the floor, in protest of the comments.The French UN mission apologized in September for the critique, a mea culpa that was well-received by Washington and cleared the way for Lechevallier's appointment.es/sia/jgc/mjfThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Syria says man with disability killed by Israeli fire in south
description: Syria says man with disability killed by Israeli fire in south
content: Syria said a man with a disability was killed on Thursday by Israeli fire during an incursion in the country's south where Israel has stepped up operations.The Israeli military has carried out hundreds of strikes in Syria and conducted frequent incursions into its territory since Islamist authorities took power after toppling longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad in December 2024."A civilian with a disability was killed Thursday by fire from the Israeli occupation forces during their incursion into the village of Jamla" in Daraa province, Syrian state news agency SANA reported.Israeli forces entered a neighbourhood and placed snipers on the rooftops after bombing the area late on Wednesday, the report said.Syria condemned "in the strongest terms the Israeli occupation forces' crime", a foreign ministry statement said, adding that "targeting civilians is a grave violation" of international law."Continued incursions and attacks on Syrian citizens are a violation of the sovereignty" of Syria and "a threat to the security and stability of the region", the statement added, while urging the international community to compel Israel "to respect the rules of international law".UN deputy special envoy for Syria, Claudio Cordone, on X deplored "the killing of a young Syrian civilian with a disability by Israeli forces", adding that "Israel must fully respect Syria's sovereignty, territorial integrity and international law".After Assad's ousting, Israel sent troops into a UN-patrolled buffer zone that had separated Israeli and Syrian forces on the mainly Israeli-occupied Golan Heights since 1974.It has also carried out repeated incursions deeper into Syrian territory, sometimes seizing residents, and has vowed to keep troops in a so-called "security zone" in southern Syria, where it wants to create a sweeping demilitarised area.In recent days, Israeli forces have also uprooted olive groves in south Syria's Quneitra province, SANA reported.Trees were destroyed across an area of about 1.3 hectares by the village of Saida, SANA said.The village faces the buffer zone where the Israeli army has been building fortifications."Tanks entered my land without any warning," Mohammad Ali al-Shaghla, 58, the owner of the field, told AFP."They cut down and destroyed some 400 trees during their incursion."Syria last week condemned "the intensification of incursions by the Israeli occupation" in Quneitra and Daraa provinces.Syria and Israel have held negotiations as they seek to reach a security agreement, but Israel remains distrustful of Syria's Islamist authorities.str-lar/at/cd/lg/dcpThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: US mortgage rates fall for first time in 2 months, but homebuyer demand drops 7% as costs stay high
description: US mortgage rates fell for the first time in two months to 7.32%, but home purchase mortgage applications dropped 7% as high costs kept buyers away.
content: US mortgage rates fell for the first time in more than two months. However, the small drop has not encouraged more people to apply for home loans, as borrowing costs remain high. Mortgage rates are still close to their highest levels in several years.The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate dropped to 7.32% for the week through Wednesday, down from 7.40% a week earlier, according to Freddie Mac data.US homebuyer demand drops 7%Mortgage applications for home purchases fell 7% in a week. Applications for new home purchases dropped through Friday compared with the previous week, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA), as high borrowing costs and housing affordability concerns continued to keep buyers away.The overall demand for mortgage loans also declined. Total mortgage application volume fell 5.3% last week compared with the previous week, according to the MBA's seasonally adjusted index reported by CNBC.30-year mortgage rates fall to 7.41%The average interest rate for 30-year fixed mortgages also declined. The average contract rate for these loans, with balances of $832,750 or less, fell to 7.41% from 7.50% last week. Mortgage points also declined to 0.75 from 0.83 for loans with a 20% down payment, including the loan origination fee.Also read: AI stocks tumble as Nasdaq, S&P 500 fall and oil hits five-month high amid Iran war fearsHigh mortgage rates and housing costs are keeping buyers away. "The housing market continues to face significant headwinds as elevated mortgage rates and affordability pressures keep many prospective buyers on the sidelines," MBA President and CEO Bob Broeksmit said in a statement, as quoted by Yahoo Finance.Lower mortgage rates fail to lift demandThe recent rate drop was not enough to increase mortgage applications. "Mortgage rates decreased for the first time in over two months," MBA economist Joel Kan said in a release. However, he added that both home purchase and refinancing applications continued to decline despite the lower rates, CNBC reported.Applications to refinance home loans fell 2% in a week. Refinancing demand is usually more sensitive to weekly changes in mortgage rates. However, the latest decline was smaller than some of the drops seen in previous weeks when rates were rising.Mortgage refinancing demand falls 59%Refinancing demand remains much lower than a year ago. Applications to refinance home loans were down 59% compared with the same week last year, CNBC reported. Mortgage rates are now more than one percentage point higher than they were a year ago, leaving very few borrowers who could benefit from refinancing at a lower rate.Home purchase mortgage applications fell more sharply than refinancing applications. Applications to buy homes declined 7% from the previous week and were down 18% compared with the same period last year, according to the MBA data.Also read: AI-powered hackers exploit PHP flaw as Europe takes government websites offline; NSA warns of cyberattack risksBuyers are responding more to high mortgage rates overall than to small weekly changes. Even though rates have started to ease, their current levels continue to make homeownership expensive. This has reduced the willingness of many buyers to take out new home loans.US pending home sales fall in SeptemberPending home sales in the US also dropped sharply in September. A report released by the National Association of Realtors on Tuesday showed a steep fall in pending home sales. These sales are measured by signed contracts and offer a real-time picture of demand in the housing market, according to CNBC.Higher mortgage rates continued into October. Mortgage rates remained elevated after rising during September, adding to the pressure on people looking to buy homes.Adjustable-rate mortgages gain attentionMore homebuyers are choosing adjustable-rate mortgages. A significant share of borrowers who are still looking to buy homes are opting for adjustable-rate mortgages, or ARMs. These loans usually offer lower initial interest rates than fixed-rate mortgages, making them an option for buyers looking to reduce their initial borrowing costs, according to CNBC.Adjustable-rate mortgages can become more expensive later. Unlike fixed-rate mortgages, ARMs can see their interest rates change after an initial period. Their rates may rise or fall depending on market conditions when the loan resets, making them riskier for borrowers.Adjustable-rate mortgages accounted for 10.5% of applications. The share remained unchanged as ARM interest rates stayed almost one percentage point below the rate for 30-year fixed mortgages, giving eligible borrowers a lower-rate option, MBA economist Joel Kan said, according to CNBC.Oil prices and inflation reports affect mortgage ratesMortgage rates have shown little movement at the start of this week. A separate survey by Mortgage News Daily found that rates had remained relatively steady after a particularly volatile week. Several monthly inflation reports had contributed to last week's rate movements, CNBC reported.Oil prices have influenced recent mortgage rate movements, but the link is uncertain. Mortgage rates appeared to follow changes in oil prices this week. However, Matthew Graham, chief operating officer at Mortgage News Daily, warned against placing too much importance on this connection.The relationship between oil prices and mortgage rates has been unreliable. "It's been highly unreliable for more than a month," Graham wrote, as quoted by CNBC. This suggests that oil price movements alone may not provide a dependable guide to where mortgage rates will go next.The US housing market continues to face pressure despite the latest rate decline. Mortgage rates have finally moved lower after more than two months, but falling home purchase and refinancing applications show that buyers and existing homeowners remain cautious. High borrowing costs and affordability concerns continue to weigh on housing demand, according to the MBA data.

title: Trump blasts 76ers' star LeBron James as 'disgrace' for not standing still during national anthem
description: Trump blasts 76ers' star LeBron James as 'disgrace' for not standing still during national anthem
content: PHILADELPHIA — President Donald Trump on Thursday accused LeBron James of disrespecting the United States after the NBA star appeared to continue his warmups while the national anthem was performed before Philadelphia’s season opener on Tuesday.“I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump said of James in a social media post sharing the video. “LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!”James appeared to practice a golf swing and jump shot as The Star-Spangled Banner was performed at Tuesday’s game in New York. James, starting his first season with Philadelphia, was lined up alongside teammates who mostly stood still during the anthem.Trump and James have been critical of each another for years, occasionally trading public swipes.James had not made a public comment or a social media post as of Thursday afternoon about Trump's gripe.The 41-year-old James, in his record 24th NBA season, was set to make his home debut for the Sixers Thursday night against Cleveland.Among some of the more notable times James became entangled with the president or politics:James was with Cleveland in 2017 when he made a statement during an NBA game with his shoes — one black, one white, with the word “equality” in capital gold letters on the back of each.Then, after the game, James made a statement about Trump, saying: “This is a beautiful country and we’re never going to let one person dictate how beautiful and how powerful we are.”James had called Trump “ a bum ” on Twitter and also said earlier that season of the president: “He doesn’t understand how many kids, no matter the race, look up to the president of the United State for guidance, for leadership, for words of encouragement. He doesn’t understand that, and that’s what makes me more sick than anything.”James showed determination to speak out on social issues and the nation’s political climate after Fox News host Laura Ingraham criticized the three-time NBA champion for his 2018 comments about social issues.“We will definitely not shut up and dribble,” James said. “I will definitely not do that. I mean too much to society. I mean too much to the youth. I mean too much to so many kids that feel like they don’t have a way out and they need someone to help lead them out of the situation they’re in.”James referenced Muhammad Ali, Jim Brown, Bill Russell and Jackie Robinson as athletes who previously spoke up for equality and change with no concerns about the consequences or any rewards.“We know it’s bigger than us,” James said.James was named The Associated Press’ Male Athlete of the Year in 2020 in large part for leading the Los Angeles Lakers to a championship and helped convince many — at the peak of Black Live Matter — who had never voted to finally head to the polls.“I still know what I do on the floor and obviously, I give everything to the game,” James said. “But I can make a greater impact off the floor right now, more than I can on the floor. And I want to continue to inspire people with the way I play the game of basketball. But there’s so many more things that I can do off the floor to help cultivate people, inspire people, bring people together, empower them.”AC Milan striker and former LA Galaxy star Zlatan Ibrahimovic blasted socially conscious athletes in a 2021 interview. Ibrahimovic called it “a mistake” for James and other athletes to get involved in political causes, saying they should “just do what you do best, because it doesn’t look good.”James, naturally, rejected the criticism.“I would never shut up about things that are wrong,” James said.White House reporter Collin Binkley in Washington contributed to this story.See ’s full NBA coverage hereThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Russian missiles pound Kyiv as Moscow says over 800 Ukrainian drones downed
description: Russian missiles pound Kyiv as Moscow says over 800 Ukrainian drones downed
content: KYIV, Ukraine — Russia bombarded Kyiv with ballistic missiles in an hourslong nighttime barrage, while the Russian military said Thursday that its air defenses intercepted over 800 drones fired by Ukraine at Moscow and other cities.At least four people were killed in Ukraine and dozens of others were wounded, officials said, in the attacks that began only hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed “in principle” Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and the United States.“Russia has not changed the way it wages this war, and it is taking no steps that would signal a genuine desire to end it,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said after the barrage.Putin's consent came in talks in St. Petersburg with U.S. President Donald Trump’s envoy, Steve Witkoff, who spoke of a “new momentum” toward peace after meeting Tuesday with Zelenskyy in Norway. The talks are supposed to start sometime after Nov. 10. No date was set. Representatives of the three countries held rounds of “technical” talks in the United Arab Emirates and Switzerland in January and February, seeking to lay the groundwork for detailed negotiations. But they reported little progress beyond exchanges of prisoners of war. Russia and Ukraine remain far apart in their terms for stopping the fighting despite U.S. efforts.The U.S. has proposed the United Arab Emirates as a possible location for the new talks, said Zelenskyy, who has said only a meeting of leaders can end the deadlock.Russia’s aerial attacks hit 12 regions of Ukraine overnight, killing at least four people and wounding scores of others, including five children, Zelenskyy said on social media Thursday.Two women, ages 50 and 60, were killed and dozens of other people were wounded in a Russian strike on a market in Lozova, in Ukraine’s northeastern Kharkiv region, said Oleh Syniehubov, head of the regional military administration. Another person was killed in other strikes on Kharkiv, the State Emergency Service said.The Ukrainian capital endured a noisy night as 21 ballistic missiles came in three waves, Zelenskyy said, smashing apartment buildings, energy facilities, a railway station and the Kyiv subway system, shopping malls and businesses. One person was killed in Kyiv.The Russian attack on Kyiv included three ballistic missiles carrying cluster munitions — bombs that open in the air and release scores of smaller bomblets, Zelenskyy said.Ukrainians are bracing for the bitterly cold months ahead as the recent escalation in Russian attacks targets the power grid to deny civilians heat, light and running water. Ukraine says Russia is stockpiling ballistic missiles for an annual campaign Ukrainians describe as “ weaponizing winter.”Since Oct. 11, Russia has launched 170 strikes on Ukraine's critical energy facilities, Zelenskyy said.The Ukrainian leader has pleaded with Washington to supply more Patriot air-defense ammunition to stop the missiles, and to heap more sanctions on Russia to pressure Moscow to pursue peace.Instead, Trump has agreed with Putin to import diesel from Russia and waived heavy sanctions on Moscow, while U.S. officials say Patriot ammunition is in short supply.“Russia is clearly taking advantage of the slowdown in air defense supplies from our partners,” Zelenskyy said. “It is equally clear that when some partners ease the pressure on Russia, it only reinforces Putin’s belief that his goals are within reach.”Western analysts say Putin wants to cut out Europe and Kyiv and negotiate Ukraine’s future directly with Washington. The Trump administration has also disparaged Europe.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Thursday that Putin had received an invitation to attend the G20 summit in Miami in December but hasn’t yet decided whether to go.“The American administration is doing a lot to help a peaceful settlement,” Peskov told reporters. “European capitals are doing nothing to promote a peaceful resolution, and they are doing a great deal to provoke the further escalation of fighting."Zelenskyy said Ukraine would “be represented at the highest level” at the summit if Trump invites the country."Let’s hope that this is possible. So far we have not received such a signal. We are counting on it,” he said at a news conference with Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo in Kyiv.Witkoff, the Trump envoy who met Wednesday with Putin in St. Petersburg, was harshly criticized in Ukraine and the U.S. for praising the Russian leader as a “humanitarian” after he released a retired American teacher who was imprisoned on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine.Assassination attempts against Putin's foes — routinely denied by the Kremlin — have been common during his decades in power. And as the five-year anniversary of Russia’s all-out invasion of its neighbor approaches, aerial strikes have killed thousands of civilians and hundreds of thousands of soldiers on both sides.The latest “brutal” Russian attacks demonstrate “what Russian ‘humanism’ truly sounds like,” Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on social media. “Appeasement, servility, and flattery will not stop this war. Only strength will.”Russia’s Defense Ministry said that air defenses overnight downed 808 Ukrainian drones, with two people reported wounded.Moscow’s Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that 630 of the drones were fired toward the Russian capital between late Wednesday and early Thursday. Moscow airports temporarily restricted air traffic overnight.The Russian military hit facilities involved in making and storing drones and cruise missiles, as well as striking transport infrastructure in Kyiv, the Defense Ministry said. Infrastructure in the southern port of Odesa and vessels used for the Ukrainian armed forces were also hit, it said.In other developments, the bodies of 252 people, said by Russia to be Ukrainian soldiers, were returned to Ukraine in an exchange, Ukraine’s agency for prisoners of war said Thursday.Russia received 25 bodies of Russian soldiers, Russian lawmaker Shamsail Saraliyev, a member of a parliamentary group overseeing the exchanges, told the RBC news outlet.Associated Press Writer Hanna Arhirova contributed to this report.Follow the ’s coverage of the war in Ukraine at /hub/russia-ukraineThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Jury weighs fate of US woman who says father forced her into Syria's war zone when she was a teen
description: Jury weighs fate of US woman who says father forced her into Syria's war zone when she was a teen
content: The fate of a New York woman who says she was tricked as a teenager by her father into traveling to Syria and marrying a member of the Islamic State group rests in the hands of the Brooklyn jury after her lawyer implored it on Thursday to find that she never received weapons training.“Find her not guilty,” Mia Eisner-Grynberg told a jury in Brooklyn federal court as he client, Halima Salman, used her clothing to wipe away tears before standing to hug her attorney after her two-hour summation.Eisner-Grynberg's closing argument drew objections from prosecutors who thought she went too far when she called some of the government's tactics in the case “shameful.”Eisner-Grynberg didn't back down, telling Judge Natasha C. Merle that there was no rule that she must be “polite” as she argues on Salman's behalf.She said Salman was 17 when her father put her in a van without saying where they were going and drove her from Turkey into Syria, where the van was surrounded by men with guns before she was locked in a room for three months in a land where the sound of bombs striking nearby targets could frequently be heard.For a decade, the lawyer said, Salman had “been through hell and back.”A day earlier, Assistant U.S. Attorney Amanda Shami portrayed Salman, who is 27, as dishonest and manipulative when she testified earlier this week that she never underwent training with the Islamic State group in 2018, halfway through her time in Syria from 2017 to 2019.“The defendant, Halima Salman, received military training from ISIS while she was in Syria, through one of its battalions,” she said in her closing.She said Salman, a U.S. citizen who was born in Brooklyn, had pledged loyalty to the Islamic State and had sent her then-husband a photograph of her with the group's flag behind her and had also been filmed by her husband with an assault rifle that she had been trained to use. Jurors were shown the brief video clip.Salman, who has remained free on bail throughout the two-week trial, was arrested in May 2024 at Kennedy International Airport when she returned to the United States.Shami criticized Salman's claims on the witness stand that her marriage was bad before she left Syria and divorced her husband, a fighter for the Islamic State group. The prosecutor cited two loving text messages Salman had sent to her husband.“Her statements on the stand don't make sense,” she said.But Eisner-Grynberg said her client was herself on the witness stand, someone who was in Girl Scouts studying sewing and craft making before her world was turned upside down by her father, who died after he was injured in a bombing in Syria in 2018.Eisner-Grynberg said the government was right to investigate her client after her time in Syria but should not have arrested her after failing to find reliable evidence.She said prosecutors failed to find anyone who had seen her undergoing weapons training and could not show that Salman ever took a serious interest in the organization that was designated by the United States as a terror group.“You can come back here in 5 minutes with a not-guilty verdict,” Eisner-Grynberg told jurors, saying there was no proof at all that Salman had attended military training or that she supported the Islamic State group.“The entire case is just optics, inference and speculation,” she said, discounting a document prosecutors said they found on Salman's ex-husband's phone that they insisted proved she had received military training. Eisner-Grynberg noted that it lacked the Islamic State group's stamp that is found on every other document of theirs.“This is a grave miscarriage of justice,” she said of the prosecution.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Virginia's Sen. Louise Lucas indicted on drug and money laundering charges as FBI probe ‘marijuana enterprise’
description: Virginia Senator L. Louise Lucas was indicted over alleged marijuana trafficking, racketeering and money laundering. She denies the charges.
content: Democrat Virginia Senator L. Louise Lucas was indicted on Thursday on charges of racketeering and conspiracy to sell marijuana. FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that Sen. Lucas allegedly ran a “criminal marijuana enterprise” with a “close-knit group of family members and associates.”Six others, including members of Senator Lucas' family, were also indicted. Federal authorities allege that Sen. L. Louise Lucas allegedly used her position as the "“position as Chairwoman of the Senate Finance and Appropriations Committee to insulate the enterprise from criminal scrutiny and influencing legislation to financially benefit themselves.” Senator Lucas is also the president pro tempore of Virginia’s senate.A spokesperson with the Department of Justice said Sen. Lucas surrendered to the authorities on her own after the indictment and denied the charges.The 82-year-old Senator also released a statement calling the indictment a political attack on her. “Today, the FBI, the Department of Justice, and the full weight of the federal government have been wielded against an 82-year-old great-grandmother,” she said.I grew up under Jim Crow. I’ve seen what happens when people in power try to silence those who stand up to them. I spent my life fighting back, and I’m not stopping now.”The indictment comes after a raid at various locations linked to the Senator, including her Portsmouth, Virginia, office, on May 6 this year. Armed FBI agents and SWAT teams raided the locations and seized evidence, which was subsequently cited by prosecutors in Thursday's indictment.Also read: Rangers legend Ron Duguay dies at 69 after cancer battle as girlfriend shares heartfelt tributeWhat Are The Allegations Against Sen. Louise LucasKash Patel announced Thursday that Louise Lucas faces five conspiracy charges related to racketeering, distributing marijuana, and committing money laundering.The DOJ alleges that Sen. Lucas distributed at least $100 kilograms marijuana through her marijuana-related businesses. Kash Patel also confirmed that nearly $5 million worth of proceeds over five years related to the alleged illegal proceeds was traced during the investigation.Also read: Documentary claims late South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham paid for sex with menInside Sen. Lukas' 'Marijuana Empire'Senator Louise Lucas has co-owned a storefront called The Cannabis Outlet, which opened in 2021 after the Biden era eased on recreational marijuana. She is also associated with a retail business called The CBD Shoppe in Norfolk, Virginia. The transactions of both shops are being investigated by the FBI, even as they remain temporarily closed after the May 2026 federal raids.The consumption of recreational marijuana is legal in Virginia. However, there are restrictions on their sale, as retailers are only allowed to sale legal, hemp-based products. The lawsuit alleges that Sen. Louise's businesses allegedly floundered those restrictions and sold high-potency variants out of the storefronts.

title: Pak man arrested for allegedly running fake postage label website that cost USPS $126 million
description: The estimated $126 million in losses refers to the alleged financial damage to the postal service, rather than the proceeds generated by the website.
content: A 33-year-old Pakistani man has been arrested for allegedly running an online counterfeit postage operation that caused more than $126 million in losses to the US Postal Service (USPS), Pakistani authorities said on Tuesday.According to a report by the New York Post, Faheem Akram, a resident of Khanewal in Pakistan’s eastern Punjab province, was arrested following a weekslong search involving raids across several parts of the country, Atif Ameer, a senior official with the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency, told reporters. Akram was indicted by a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida, the US Attorney’s Office for the district said in a statement.Prosecutors alleged that Akram operated LabelsBank.com, an unauthorised website that sold more than 5.1 million counterfeit postage labels to over 5,200 customers. The labels were typically priced at $2 each, regardless of a package’s weight, size or destination. They allowed customers to ship packages at prices significantly lower than legitimate postal rates, resulting in lost revenue and shipping costs for the USPS, the outlet reported citing US Attorney’s Office.The estimated $126 million in losses refers to the alleged financial damage to the postal service, rather than the proceeds generated by the website.(Also Read: Indian novelist refuses to share food after realising co-traveller is Pakistani)How the alleged counterfeit postage scheme workedAmeer said Pakistani investigators found that Akram had operated the website from August 2023 through September 2026. According to the official, Akram used 16 bank accounts to run the business. These included accounts held by him and members of his family, including his brother, wife, sister and aunt.The investigation involved a search spanning several parts of Pakistan before Akram was arrested on Tuesday, Ameer said.It remains unclear whether Akram will be extradited to the United States or face trial in Pakistan. The US indictment accuses him of operating the unauthorised postage label website, which allegedly enabled thousands of customers to obtain counterfeit shipping labels at a fraction of legitimate postal rates. The case concerns alleged losses to the US Postal Service exceeding $126 million.

title: AI stocks tumble as Nasdaq, S&P 500 fall and oil hits five-month high amid Iran war fears
description: AI stocks fell as oil prices hit a five-month high amid Iran war fears, dragging global markets lower, while Nvidia, Meta and Asian markets saw sharp losses.
content: Stocks linked to artificial intelligence (AI) fell sharply on Thursday, dragging stock markets across the world lower. At the same time, oil prices climbed to their highest level in five months as investors worried about the war involving Iran and its impact on global energy supplies.The S&P 500 fell 1.4%, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.2% as of 10:45 a.m. Eastern time on Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell by a smaller 0.6%, or 295 points. The bigger losses in the Nasdaq reflected the pressure on technology stocks, while companies outside the tech sector performed better, according to AP.AI stocks fall on high costs and spending worriesAI-related stocks have been unstable as investors worry about the high cost of building data centres and buying AI chips. Companies need to spend large amounts of money to expand their AI businesses, and borrowing has become more expensive. Investors are also concerned that AI stocks may have become too expensive after years of strong gains, even as companies continue to report business growth.Lam Research, which makes equipment and provides services used in semiconductor manufacturing, reported higher revenue and profit for the summer quarter. Both figures were slightly better than analysts had expected. However, its shares fell 9.7% because its profit forecast for the final three months of 2026 was weaker than expected at the midpoint of its projected range, according to AP.Also read: P&G raises 2027 cost outlook to $1.4 billion as higher oil prices squeeze profitsThe company's shares had risen 52.4% so far in 2026 before Thursday's fall. This was nearly four times the gain recorded by the S&P 500 over the same period. The strong rise had created high expectations among investors, leaving the stock vulnerable to a fall when the company's future profit outlook disappointed them.Meta stock falls 6.4% despite higher revenueMeta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, saw its shares fall 6.4%. The company reported stronger revenue for the latest quarter than analysts had expected, but its profit fell short of expectations. Meta is also pushing ahead with its Muse AI agent as it expands its artificial intelligence business, according to AP.Meta said it was creating a new class of stock to raise money for its AI investments and other expenses. The move comes as the company continues to spend on artificial intelligence, even though investors are becoming more concerned about the costs of developing and expanding AI technology.Tesla shares erased an early decline and rose 0.1% on Thursday. The electric vehicle maker reported higher summer-quarter profit than analysts had expected. However, its revenue was weaker than forecast, showing that the company had mixed results for the quarter.Nvidia shares drop as AI sell-off spreadsNvidia, the world's leading maker of AI chips, saw its shares fall 3.8% as investors sold technology stocks. Nvidia is the largest company on Wall Street by total market value, so its share price has a major influence on the S&P 500. Its decline became one of the biggest reasons for the index's fall on Thursday, according to AP.Also read: AI-powered hackers exploit PHP flaw as Europe takes government websites offline; NSA warns of cyberattack risksCoreWeave shares dropped 7.1% as concerns about the company's debt continued to worry investors. The company has borrowed money to buy Nvidia's AI chips and rents computing power to customers through cloud services. Its shares have been particularly unstable in recent weeks, and they have moved between gains and losses of around 4% on each of the previous two days.Asian markets tumble as tech stocks fallThe sell-off in AI and technology stocks began in Asia before spreading to other markets. South Korea's Kospi fell 3.5%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index dropped 3%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 declined 2.7%. Asian markets were hit particularly hard because their stock indexes have large holdings in AI and other technology companies, according to AP.Oil prices hit five-month high amid Iran war fearsBrent crude oil, the international benchmark, climbed 2.6% to $111.60 a barrel after touching its highest level in five months. Oil prices have moved between $97 and $112 a barrel during October as traders try to assess when the war involving Iran will allow global energy supplies to return to normal.Investors are worried that the conflict involving Iran could disrupt energy supplies and prevent the global oil industry from returning to normal. The rise in oil prices adds to concerns about costs for businesses and the wider economy. The combination of falling technology shares and rising oil prices weighed on stock markets worldwide, according to AP.French stocks fall as debt worries growFrance's CAC 40 index fell 1%, recording one of the sharper declines among European stock markets. The index has fewer technology stocks than US and Asian markets, but it came under pressure as French government bond yields rose again. Investors are worried about France's large government debt and strained budget.Violent protests across France have increased pressure on the government to spend more money. Additional spending could make the country's debt problem worse, adding to investor concerns about the government's finances and pushing up the yields demanded by investors holding French government bonds.US bond yields fall as investors seek safetyConcerns about high government debt are affecting many developed economies, including the United States. In the US, high inflation, signs of a strong economy and other economic pressures have helped push government bond yields to levels not seen in decades, according to AP.Despite the wider concerns about US debt, Treasury yields fell on Thursday as investors moved towards US government bonds. The move suggested that some investors were looking for safer places to put their money while AI stocks and other technology shares were falling.The yield on the 10-year US Treasury fell to 5.01% on Thursday, down from 5.13% late Wednesday and more than 5.30% earlier in October. The fall was a notable move in the bond market. However, the yield remained well above its 3.97% level before the war involving Iran, according to AP.US jobs data points to a strong economyA separate report showed that fewer US workers applied for unemployment benefits last week. This suggests that layoffs may remain low across the country and that the US job market could be holding up better than economists expected.The US economy has remained strong enough to help many companies increase their profits. Better earnings helped push the US stock market to a record high earlier in October, despite concerns about inflation, government debt and the war involving Iran.Although the S&P 500 declined on Thursday, most of the stocks within the index actually rose. Gains in several companies were not enough to offset the losses in major technology stocks, which have a greater influence on the index because of their large market values.P&G shares jump 5.8% after strong resultsProcter & Gamble (P&G), the company behind brands such as Crest, Olay and Oral-B, was among the businesses that reported better-than-expected summer-quarter profits. Its shares rose 5.8% on Thursday, helping limit the broader market's losses.P&G CEO Shailesh Jejurikar said the company expects geopolitical and economic challenges to continue. However, the company kept its forecasts for full-year revenue growth, profit growth and other financial measures unchanged, according to AP.Defence company Lockheed Martin and transport company CSX were among the other businesses that joined the list of companies reporting summer-quarter profits above analysts' expectations. Gains in these companies, along with P&G, helped support parts of the stock market as technology shares fell.Thursday's market movement showed the difference between technology stocks facing high spending costs and valuation concerns, and other businesses reporting strong profits. While a relatively strong US economy has supported company earnings, rising oil prices, fears about the Iran war, government debt and uncertainty over AI spending have kept investors cautious, according to AP.

title: Documentary claims late South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham paid for sex with men
description: A documentary alleges three men were paid for sex by late Senator Lindsey Graham between 2001 and 2015, raising questions about his anti-LGBTQ voting record.
content: Four months after the death of South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham, the late Republican's personal life has once again become the center of a political storm.On Thursday, The Young Turks, an American news and commentary program, released a 30-minute documentary where three individuals claiming to be male escorts alleged they were hired by Graham, according to the Washington Times and The New Republic.Called The Closetocracy, the documentary questions Graham's advocacy and votes against LGBTQ-related legislations in his 30 years in the US Congress and contrasts it with his alleged personal life.
