A website has also been created called The Lindsey Graham Files, which visually documents the allegations and their timeline in detail.Ht.com could not independently verify the authenticity of the allegations.Lindsey Graham never talked about his personal life in detail despite public scrutiny over the years. Back in October 2018, after actor Chelsea Handler publicly accused Graham of homosexuality, he told TMZ in an interview at the Reagan National Airport: "To the extent that it matters, I’m not gay."And these comments… I don't think they reflect well on her and I don't know how it makes us a better country, but it's up to her, not me," he had added.Also read: Did Iran's closest ally just 'assassinate' US senator Lindsey Graham? Laura Loomer drops bombshell | VideosWhat Are The Allegations Against Lindsay Graham?The Closetocracy makes several allegations against late Lindsey Graham. It features testimonies of three individuals claiming to be male escorts alleging they were hired for sex by Graham between 2001 and 2015. They appeared in the documentary with their faces and identities revealed. They never met each other but described the same person, it alleged.The first, Kevin, alleges in the documentary he was paid $120 by Graham in 2001 in Arizona for sex. The individual claims he was only 17 when the alleged incident happened. Next, there is an individual called Jesse who claims that he allegedly had a paid sexual encounter with Graham at The Beacon and a Days Inn in Washington, in 2012 and 2014. Finally, Cory claims he was allegedly paid $1,500 by the late Senator on November 11, 2015, to have sex at The Mayflower Hotel in Washington.

title: P&G raises 2027 cost outlook to $1.4 billion as higher oil prices squeeze profits
description: P&G raises its 2027 cost outlook to $1.4 billion as oil prices and freight costs rise, putting pressure on profits despite strong quarterly sales.
content: Procter & Gamble (P&G), the company that makes Tide detergent and Pantene shampoo, warned on Thursday that rising raw material, energy and transportation costs could reduce its annual profit by more than expected. However, strong demand for its beauty and home-care products helped the company report better-than-expected sales for the first quarter.P&G now expects higher costs to reduce its fiscal 2027 profit by around $1.4 billion, up from its earlier estimate of $1 billion. The company raised its cost estimate as higher oil prices and other rising expenses put pressure on its business, according to Reuters.P&G faces higher costs in 2027P&G Chief Financial Officer Andre Schulten said during a media call that pressure from high commodity prices is expected to increase over the next two quarters. This means the company could face even higher costs in the coming months.P&G's results will help show whether strong spending by US consumers can continue despite another period of rising prices. Higher fuel and food costs are putting pressure on household budgets and encouraging some shoppers to choose cheaper products, according to Reuters.Also read: AI-powered hackers exploit PHP flaw as Europe takes government websites offline; NSA warns of cyberattack risksOil prices push up business costsRising commodity prices have become a growing concern for companies across different industries. Consumer goods companies and airlines are also facing higher expenses as oil price changes following the US war on Iran push up fuel and transportation costs.Despite the higher cost pressure, P&G kept its fiscal 2027 financial forecasts unchanged. The company expects organic sales growth of 1% to 3% and core earnings of around $7 per share, according to Reuters.P&G profit margins face pressureArt Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth, said rising commodity prices are making it harder for companies to pass higher costs on to customers. As a result, companies may have to absorb more of these expenses themselves, reducing their profit margins.P&G's core operating margin fell by 80 basis points in the quarter ended September 30. This happened despite the company saving 250 basis points through productivity improvements, including efforts to make its supply chain more efficient under new CEO Shailesh Jejurikar.Higher fuel costs raise transport expensesHigher fuel prices have increased transportation and freight costs for companies that sell packaged consumer goods. A shortage of truck drivers on some routes has added to the pressure, a P&G spokesperson told Reuters.Also read: US Treasury yields fall as investors track Middle East tensions, await US jobless claims dataUS retail diesel prices reached a record $6 per gallon in September after the US war in Iran and have remained high. These elevated prices have added to the cost of moving goods, increasing pressure on companies such as P&G.P&G is negotiating with suppliers and improving its transportation routes to control expenses. The company also plans to continue investing in new products and product innovation while trying to manage rising costs, a company spokesperson told Reuters.P&G sales beat market estimatesDespite these challenges, P&G reported a 4% increase in first-quarter net sales to $23.28 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $22.80 billion. The figures were compiled by LSEG. P&G shares rose about 2% in premarket trading on Thursday following the company's quarterly results, according to Reuters.The company's beauty business recorded higher sales volumes, supported by demand for more expensive hair-care products. Consumers continued spending on personal care even as higher fuel and food costs put pressure on their household budgets.P&G's overall sales volume increased by 2.4% in the three months through September, while prices rose by around 0.4%. This indicates that the company sold more products, while the average increase in prices remained relatively small.Swiss consumer goods company Nestle also reported better-than-expected organic sales growth on Thursday, supported by stronger sales volumes. Its results showed that demand for products from major consumer goods companies remained steady despite cost pressures, according to Reuters.P&G reported first-quarter core earnings of $2 per share, beating analysts' expectations of $1.88 per share, according to Reuters. In August, P&G announced plans to buy supplements maker Thorne. The move was aimed at tapping into growing demand for health and wellness products as the company looks to expand its business in this market.

title: Earthquake of magnitude 7.0 strikes Tibet
description: A magnitude 7 earthquake struck Tibet at a depth of 10 km, according to the German Research Centre for Geosciences.
content: An earthquake of magnitude 7 struck Tibet on Thursday at a depth of 10 km (6.21 miles), according to the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ).The epicentre was located in a county in Nagqu, northern Tibet, at a depth of 10 km, data from the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC), cited by Reuters, showed. The average elevation within 5 km of the epicentre is approximately 4,864 metres.Also Read | China closes 3 Tibetan schools in Golog, claims government-in-exileTremor felt in surrounding areaThe tremor was clearly felt in the surrounding area, CENC said. The epicentre was located around 400 km from Lhasa, the Tibetan capital, at 32.40 degrees north latitude and 93.79 degrees east longitude.The Tibetan Plateau is prone to powerful earthquakes because it lies in a region where the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates collide, generating significant seismic activity.

title: AI-powered hackers exploit PHP flaw as Europe takes government websites offline; NSA warns of cyberattack risks
description: AI-powered hackers exploit PHP2Shell flaws as Europe takes government websites offline, prompting urgent security patches amid rising cyberattack risks.
content: Government websites across Europe were taken offline on Wednesday as cybersecurity experts raised concerns about serious security flaws in PHP, a programming language used by millions of websites. The move came as the US National Security Agency (NSA) warned organisations to install security updates immediately or take their servers offline.The security scare highlights how artificial intelligence (AI) is helping hackers find and exploit software weaknesses much faster than before. Vulnerabilities that once took weeks or months to discover and exploit can now be used within hours, cybersecurity experts told CNBC.Matt Suiche, a researcher at cybersecurity startup Tolmo, said the level of urgency around these threats was something new. He said AI tools are now helping both cybersecurity teams and attackers, making it easier for hackers to find weaknesses and act quickly, as cited by CNBC. PHP is a programming language created in the 1990s. It helps websites process requests and run functions on their servers. According to W3Techs, PHP is used by just under 70% of websites whose server-side programming language is known. AI tools help find PHP2Shell vulnerabilitiesIn mid-August, researchers at AI company Calif and Google's cybersecurity firm Wiz identified vulnerabilities affecting PHP installations that handle web requests. The researchers used AI tools to help find the weaknesses, according to CNBC.Also read: US Treasury yields fall as investors track Middle East tensions, await US jobless claims dataCalif's researchers used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model. The Wiz team used its Wiz Atlas security AI agent, Google's Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. These tools helped researchers examine the software and explore different ways the security flaws could be exploited.The security flaws allow hackers to remotely run code on affected PHP servers without logging in or proving their identity. This could allow attackers to steal data, access sensitive information and potentially gain control over parts of a vulnerable system, according to CNBC.PHP security patches released earlyThe PHP Foundation had planned to release fixes for the vulnerabilities on Thursday. However, information about the flaws began spreading through online forums before the planned release. The situation became more urgent after Calif accidentally published a video showing a proof-of-concept exploit on Tuesday.Calif's video demonstrated a chain of steps that could be used to exploit the vulnerabilities. Although the video was later removed, the information had already raised concerns about the risk of other people developing working attacks.The foundation fast-tracked the security updates and released them at 10 a.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday, a day earlier than planned. The US National Security Agency issued its warning shortly before the patches were released, according to CNBC.By then, code claiming to exploit PHP2Shell on any server had already been published on GitHub, an online platform for sharing and storing software code. GitHub is owned by Microsoft. The appearance of this code added to concerns that attackers could quickly try to use the vulnerabilities against exposed servers.Also read: World’s largest sovereign wealth fund loses $30 billion in Q3 as bond returns fallElizabeth Barron, executive director of The PHP Foundation, told CNBC on Wednesday afternoon that the organisation was closely monitoring the situation. She said there was no evidence of working exploits at that point, describing the generated examples that had appeared as incomplete, misguided and non-working, according to CNBC.AI-powered hackers develop working exploit quicklyMatt Suiche said his team at Tolmo was able to develop a working exploit in under 24 hours. He said AI made it relatively quick to reproduce the vulnerability in a local environment. Before today's more powerful AI models, the same work could have taken his team several weeks.Amazon Threat Intelligence said on Wednesday that it had identified an attempt to exploit PHP2Shell on Saturday. The activity was detected through its MadPot telemetry network, which uses digital decoys to identify and study suspicious connections and potential cyberattacks.PHP Foundation admits security failureMihail Kirov, a product security engineer at Tolmo who previously worked at Quarkslab, said he was part of a team that discovered a vulnerability with the same root cause as PHP2Shell two years ago. Kirov said The PHP Foundation had been alerted to the earlier flaw, but a fix was not released at the time, according to CNBC.In a blog post published on Wednesday, the foundation described the delay in addressing the earlier issue as a “structural failure.” It said the problem was caused by decisions made by its security team and a lack of resources, according to the foundation's blog post.The latest research showed how quickly AI tools can help security researchers explore possible weaknesses. Calif's researchers identified two vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity. Kirov said large language models allow researchers to examine many different angles much faster.Older government websites face greater cyber risksCybersecurity experts warned that fixing the flaws does not automatically reveal whether a server was attacked before the updates were installed. Organisations may have to investigate their systems separately to find out whether attackers accessed sensitive information.Neatsun Ziv, chief executive of cybersecurity company Ox Security, said organisations could struggle to identify suspicious requests if they had not already installed an application security platform before an attack. Without such monitoring, some attempts to exploit a vulnerability may go unnoticed, according to CNBC.Suiche said a company might realise it had been hacked only after its valuable data appeared for sale on the dark web. His comments highlight the difficulty of identifying a breach when organisations lack strong monitoring and security systems.Suiche said PHP is a legacy server language and some organisations using it may not have sophisticated security measures in place. He pointed out that city governments and other public agencies often use PHP and may have websites that have not been updated for 10 years, according to CNBC.Suiche warned that older government websites can contain or provide access to critical data. This makes the security flaws especially concerning because a successful attack could put sensitive public-sector information at risk.Anthropic's Mythos AI model raises cyberattack concernsCybersecurity experts say the threat has grown as more powerful AI models have become available. The technology can help attackers analyse software, identify vulnerabilities and develop ways to exploit them much faster than traditional methods.Anthropic, the company behind Claude, released its powerful Mythos model to a limited group of companies and government agencies in April 2026. The aim was to allow selected organisations to test its cybersecurity capabilities and ensure that appropriate security measures were in place before a wider release, according to CNBC.Neatsun Ziv said hackers previously needed weeks to discover a new vulnerability and exploit it across the internet. That timeline later fell to days and, since the arrival of the Mythos era in April 2026, can be as short as hours, he told CNBC.The PHP2Shell vulnerabilities have raised concerns because PHP is widely used, the flaws can allow remote code execution without authentication, and AI can speed up the process of turning a weakness into a working attack. The incident underlines the need for organisations to install security updates quickly, monitor their servers and check whether their systems were accessed before the fixes were applied.

title: US Treasury yields fall as investors track Middle East tensions, await US jobless claims data
description: US Treasury yields fall as investors track Middle East tensions, rising oil prices and US jobless claims data for clues about the economy and interest rates.
content: US Treasury yields fell on Thursday as investors kept a close watch on rising tensions in the Middle East and waited for fresh US jobless claims data due later in the day. The decline in Treasury yields also came amid a broader move away from riskier assets in stock markets.The 10-year US Treasury yield dropped by more than 7 basis points to 5.0732%. The 10-year Treasury yield is an important benchmark for borrowing costs in the US, including mortgage rates, auto loans and credit card debt, according to CNBC.US Treasury yields fall across maturitiesThe 2-year US Treasury yield also moved lower. It fell by more than 5 basis points to 4.7654%. This yield is closely linked to investor expectations for short-term interest rate decisions by the Federal Reserve, the US central bank.The 30-year US Treasury yield declined by 6 basis points to 5.3751%. Longer-term Treasury yields can also react to geopolitical developments and changes in investor sentiment, according to CNBC.Other US Treasury yields also recorded declines. Market data listed the 10-year yield at 5.048%, down 0.098 percentage points, while the 2-year yield stood at 4.736%, down 0.087 percentage points. The 30-year yield was at 5.359%, down 0.078 percentage points.Also read: World’s largest sovereign wealth fund loses $30 billion in Q3 as bond returns fallYields on shorter-term Treasury securities also fell. The one-month Treasury yield stood at 3.98%, down 0.003 percentage points. The three-month yield fell to 4.156%, down 0.013 percentage points, while the six-month yield declined to 4.34%, down 0.027 percentage points. The one-year Treasury yield dropped to 4.458%, down 0.041 percentage points, according to the market data provided by CNBC.US jobless claims data in focusInvestors are waiting for US initial jobless claims data. The US Labor Department is scheduled to release the figures later on Thursday. The report will show how many people filed for unemployment benefits for the first time, giving investors another indication of the health of the US labour market.Economists expect 200,000 Americans to have filed initial jobless claims. The estimate, based on a Dow Jones poll of economists, is for the week ended October 17. Investors will assess the figures for clues about labour market conditions and the possible direction of US interest rates, according to CNBC.Middle East tensions weigh on market sentimentRising Middle East tensions have also put pressure on market sentiment. Treasury yields fell as investors adopted a more cautious approach amid geopolitical uncertainty and weakness in stock markets.Investors are monitoring developments in the Middle East alongside incoming US economic data. The combination of geopolitical risks, rising oil prices and uncertainty about the labour market is shaping market sentiment as investors assess the outlook for the US economy and interest rates, according to CNBC.Also read: Brent crude oil hits highest since May as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia fuel global oil supply fearsOil prices rise amid Iran strike concernsOil prices climbed sharply as concerns about a possible escalation in the Middle East grew. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 2.81% to $99.96 a barrel in early trading on Thursday, moving closer to the $100 mark.Brent crude, the global oil price benchmark, also rose. Prices increased 3.33% to $112.44 a barrel on Thursday.The rise in oil prices followed a report about possible renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran. The New York Times reported on Wednesday, citing unnamed US officials, that the US and Israel were considering restarting strikes on Iran in a “short but intensive” operation after next month's US midterm elections.What falling Treasury yields meanA basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point. One basis point equals 0.01 percentage points. Treasury yields and bond prices move in opposite directions, meaning bond prices generally rise when yields fall and decline when yields rise.

title: UK man fined ₹2.8 lakh after throwing parking ticket at female officer's face
description: The case was heard at Truro Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday. Lang did not attend the hearing and was found guilty in his absence.
content: A UK man was recently fined £2,270 (around ₹2.8 lakh) after throwing a parking ticket at a female civil enforcement officer’s face and later crumpling it up and throwing it towards her.According to a report by Metro, Stephen Lang, 58, from Cornwall, was initially issued a parking ticket for parking outside a marked bay. However, instead of accepting the ticket, he removed it from his vehicle’s windscreen and threw it at the officer's face before walking away.Moments later, Lang approached the officer again as she retrieved the ticket from the ground and attempted to put it back on his vehicle. He removed it once more, crumpled it up and threw it in the officer’s direction.The incident was captured by the officer’s body-worn camera and CCTV cameras covering the car park.According to Cornwall Council, Lang was initially found guilty of littering on November 20, 2025. He was issued a £250 (Around ₹32,000) Fixed Penalty Notice, which he failed to pay despite receiving a reminder and a warning that the matter could be referred for prosecution.The case was heard at Truro Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday. Lang did not attend the hearing and was found guilty in his absence.(Also Read: ₹1.5 lakh traffic fine from Switzerland a year after vacation: 'Any way to appeal?'">Indian tourist receives ₹1.5 lakh traffic fine from Switzerland a year after vacation: 'Any way to appeal?')Court orders the man to pay £2,270The court ordered him to pay a £250 fine, £1,920.90 in costs and a £100 victim surcharge, bringing the total amount to £2,270.90.Cllr Thalia Marrington, Cornwall Council’s cabinet member for community safety and public health, condemned Lang’s behaviour. “It is both unacceptable to litter and to be aggressive to an officer doing her job,” she said.“We will not tolerate any abuse towards our officers,” she added.Notably, the UK fine for street littering is a default £100 Fixed Penalty Notice (FPN), which local authorities can set between £65 and £500. Civil penalties or FPNs for throwing rubbish out of a car also range up to £500.If an FPN is ignored or the case is contested in magistrates' court, the maximum fine climbs up to £2,500.

title: World’s largest sovereign wealth fund loses $30 billion in Q3 as bond returns fall
description: Norway’s $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund lost $29.7 billion in Q3 2026 as rising interest rates hurt bond returns, despite small gains in stocks.
content: Norway’s sovereign wealth fund, the largest in the world, reported a loss of nearly $30 billion in the third quarter of 2026. The loss came as rising interest rates reduced the value of its bond investments.The fund recorded a loss of 278 billion Norwegian kroner ($29.7 billion) during the July-September quarter. Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM), which manages the fund, said rising interest rates weakened returns from its fixed-income investments. The fund is worth around $2.3 trillion, according to CNBC.Norway sovereign wealth fund loses $30 billion in Q3Bonds were the main reason behind the fund’s weak performance. Its fixed-income investments, which include government and corporate debt, delivered a negative return of 3.5% in the third quarter. NBIM’s management said this was a key reason for the overall decline.Rising government bond yields hurt the global bond market during the quarter. Yields surged as major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, began raising interest rates. Concerns about inflation and rising government debt levels also put pressure on bond markets.Rising interest rates hit bond returnsNBIM Deputy CEO Trond Grande said the fund’s overall return was close to zero but ended slightly negative. He said higher interest rates led to weaker results from its fixed-income investments, according to a statement cited by CNBC.Also read: Brent crude oil hits highest since May as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia fuel global oil supply fearsFixed-income investments make up just over one-fourth of the fund’s total portfolio. Around 70% of its fixed-income holdings are invested in government bonds, while the remaining portion is invested in corporate debt. The fund holds 1,664 bonds across 51 countries.The fund had also announced plans to reduce its US Treasury holdings. In September, NBIM said it wanted to cut its investments in US government debt as part of a broader plan to reduce its allocation to government-issued bonds, CNBC reported.US stock market returns remain mixedStock investments delivered a small positive return during the quarter. Equities account for 72% of the fund’s portfolio and returned 0.5% in the third quarter. However, the gains were not enough to offset the losses from bonds.The fund has investments in around 7,100 companies across most countries. It holds stakes equivalent to about 1.5% of all listed companies worldwide, making it the world’s largest single investor.Global stock markets also had a mixed third quarter. In the US, the S&P 500 rose 2.03%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.9%. The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite gained 2.2% during the three months ending in September, CNBC reported.Also read: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs as AI-led cost-cutting drive expands after mixed Q3 results and trading revenue fallsThe gains in US stocks were much slower than in the previous quarter. The average change across the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nasdaq Composite was around 0.6%. This marked a slowdown after the three indexes recorded double-digit gains in the previous quarter.Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft among top holdingsThe fund has major investments in some of America’s biggest technology companies. Its holdings include a $65.4 billion stake in Nvidia, along with investments in Apple, Alphabet and Microsoft. These large stakes give NBIM significant voting power in companies and influence over investment trends, CNBC reported.Returns varied widely across different stock market sectors. Grande said equity returns were close to zero overall, but energy companies performed the best. Utilities and real estate companies, which are more sensitive to interest rates, recorded declines.Rising oil prices helped energy stocks during the quarter. Oil prices surged as the US-Iran war continued, supporting the performance of energy companies. NBIM has investments in major energy firms, including Exxon Mobil, Shell and Chevron, CNBC reported.Fund reports record first-half profit of $185 billionNBIM’s chief executive had earlier warned investors against expecting another period of unusually strong stock market gains. In an interview with CNBC in August, CEO Nicolai Tangen said investors should not expect returns similar to those seen in the first half of 2026.The warning came after the fund recorded strong gains in the first half of the year. NBIM reported a return of 12.95% for the first six months of 2026, generating a record first-half profit of nearly $185 billion.The fund’s other investments also delivered positive returns in the third quarter. Real estate investments returned 0.4%, while renewable energy infrastructure investments generated a return of 7.5%, according to CNBC.Norway established the sovereign wealth fund in 1998 to invest revenue generated from the country’s oil resources. The fund invests across global financial markets and other assets to manage Norway’s oil wealth over the long term.

title: Italy truckers’ protests over diesel prices disrupt food transport as vegetables rot; farmers warn of losses
description: Truckers in Italy continued to block roads in the country’s south, with fishing fleets in the port of Ancona also idled to protest high diesel prices.
content: Truckers in Italy continued to block roads in the country’s south on Thursday, with fishing fleets in the port of Ancona also idled to protest high diesel prices.The decision to continue the demonstrations despite pending aid for truckers has worsened the pain for farmers, their lobby group Confagricoltura said in a statement. Disruptions focused on buffalo mozzarella have spread to seasonal vegetables and fruit such as tomatoes, which are rotting due to a lack of transport, it said.“The trucker blockages, which are still ongoing in various regions in southern Italy, are bringing agricultural companies to their knees, with economic damage that risks becoming irreversible,” Confagricoltura said in a statement. “We can’t afford to destroy food and revenue. Normalcy needs to be reinstated immediately.”Also Read | Indian embassy in Italy issues advisory, urges citizens to avoid protest sites, crowded areasPM to consider aid for truckers, farmersPrime ⁠Minister Giorgia Meloni, who took office exactly four years ago, has sought to accommodate the truckers while separately cracking down on young protesters in Milan who have raised a range of grievances. Her cabinet is scheduled to meet on Thursday to approve new measures to help truck drivers and farmers.In the Adriatic port of Ancona, fishing fleets were also idled to protest higher diesel fuel, Corriere della Sera reported. Truckers have also kept a blockade in Gela, Sicily, in place, the newspaper said.On the A1, which leads to the mozzarella center of Caserta motorists were stuck in traffic near the city of Naples after truckers restricted access.Truck blockades disrupt food transportThe unrest in the south runs parallel to a series of protests in the north which led to looting and rioting in Milan in recent days.Also Read | From France to Italy: Looting, vandalism prevails across Europe as rising cost of living stirs unrestEarlier this week, Meloni announced measures aimed at stemming further violence amid concern over another round of demonstrations scheduled for the coming weekend.In Milan, where the protests were particularly violent, the government plans to deploy 500 military personnel until the end of the year. Protesters also plan to target Naples, Corriere reported.

title: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs as AI-led cost-cutting drive expands after mixed Q3 results and trading revenue falls
description: Barclays plans to cut 5,000 jobs as it expands AI-led cost savings, after reporting mixed third-quarter results and a 19% fall in fixed-income trading revenue.
content: British bank Barclays Plc has announced plans to cut 5,000 jobs, or about 5% of its total workforce, as part of a wider effort to reduce costs and improve efficiency using technology and artificial intelligence (AI). According to Barclays' third-quarter earnings statement, the bank is focusing on simplifying its organisation and making its operations more efficient.Barclays job cuts: 60% of layoffs to hit support teamsAbout 60% of the planned job cuts will affect support functions, including developers. Barclays had already cut around 1,000 jobs during the first six months of 2026. The remaining cuts are expected to take place before the end of the year. According to Bloomberg, Barclays employed around 93,000 people globally at the end of 2025.Barclays Chief Executive Officer CS Venkatakrishnan said the bank plans to use AI on a large scale but stressed that the technology is only one part of its cost-cutting strategy. “We will employ AI at scale,” he said. “But AI is the icing on the cake, not the cake.” Venkatakrishnan made these remarks during a call with reporters, according to Bloomberg.Barclays Q3 results miss estimatesThe announcement came as Barclays reported its third-quarter earnings on Thursday. The bank's results missed several analyst estimates, with weakness in its investment banking business offsetting stronger performance in some other areas. The bank's bond traders recorded a particularly sharp decline in performance during the quarter, while its equities trading business delivered strong growth. Also read: eBay layoffs 2026: Company to cut 1,000 jobs in second round of workforce reductionsBarclays' revenue from fixed-income and currency trading, also known as FICC, fell 19% year on year to £1.01 billion ($1.4 billion) in the third quarter. The result was below analysts' expectations compiled by Bloomberg. According to the bank, the decline reflected lower client activity in interest-rate and credit markets, as well as further difficulties in September due to the broader economic environment.Barclays bond trading revenue falls 19%Venkatakrishnan described the investment bank's FICC performance as “somewhat disappointing” during a call with reporters. The weakness in bond trading reduced the impact of a strong performance in equities, where revenue increased significantly during the quarter.Barclays' equities trading revenue jumped 47% year on year, almost matching the £1.01 billion generated by its fixed-income and currency trading business. The equities division recorded its strongest performance since at least 2009, the year after Barclays acquired the North American business of Lehman Brothers.JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs face bond trading pressureThe weakness in fixed-income trading was not limited to Barclays. Other major US banks, including JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs and Bank of America, also reported declines in fixed-income trading revenue. Revenue at these banks' fixed-income desks fell by as much as 17% year on year as they dealt with the impact of rising interest rates.Barclays Q3 profit rises 12% to £2.3 billionBarclays' investment bank reported total income of £3.13 billion in the third quarter, slightly below expectations. The bank's overall group income also came in below forecasts, despite an increase in pre-tax profit. According to CNBC, group income stood at £7.4 billion, compared with analysts' estimate of £7.61 billion.Also read: Brent crude oil hits highest since May as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia fuel global oil supply fearsBarclays' pre-tax profit increased 12% year on year to £2.3 billion ($3.1 billion) in the third quarter, matching forecasts compiled by LSEG. However, the bank's performance varied across its businesses, with weakness in investment banking affecting the overall results. According to CNBC, the bank's net interest income remained broadly unchanged at £3.91 billion.Barclays cuts costs by £201 millionBarclays has been under pressure to control expenses after reporting higher-than-expected costs in its half-year results. The bank had announced a fresh cost-cutting programme in February, and investors have been watching whether it can deliver the promised savings. According to Bloomberg, the latest job reductions form part of its broader effort to improve efficiency and manage spending.The bank reduced costs by £201 million in the three months through September. It plans to cut costs by a further £300 million in the final quarter of 2026. The additional savings are part of Barclays' continuing drive to lower expenses and create more room for investment.Venkatakrishnan said Barclays was on track to meet its existing targets for 2026 and remained committed to its longer-term plans. “With one quarter to go before the end of our original three-year plan, we have either achieved or are on track to achieve all of our 2026 group targets,” he said. He added that the bank remained confident in its 2028 targets. Barclays shares fell after the results were announced. The stock traded as much as 2.4% lower as the London market opened.

title: Trump-pardoned January 6 US Capitol rioters file lawsuits seeking taxpayer-funded payouts
description: Nearly 200 people are suing for compensation, including dozens convicted of attacking or impeding law enforcement.
content: Police guarding the US capitol against riots on January 6, 2021, as Congress certified the 2020 election results, were punched, shoved, dragged down steps and pulled into the crowd. Some officers were hit in the face with bear spray, struck with flagpoles or had their shields and batons used against them.Now, dozens of people pardoned by President Donald Trump after convictions for assaulting or interfering with law enforcement that day are suing the US government for millions of dollars, alleging mistreatment by prosecutors, federal agents and prison officials.At least 199 people file lawsuitsThe number of civil lawsuits seeking taxpayer compensation filed by those covered by Trump’s sweeping executive clemency for Jan. 6 prosecutions has jumped since the summer, court records show. At least 199 people have filed Jan. 6-related cases and more are expected. Fifty-three of the plaintiffs so far were convicted at trial or pleaded guilty to “assaulting, resisting or impeding” officers.As these cases unfold in court, justice department officials will have to publicly pick a side on an issue that carries political baggage. Settlements — especially for police assault cases — could trigger blowback from Republicans who took the rare step of criticizing Trump for pardons that they saw as conflicting with their party’s pro-law enforcement stance.Also Read | Natalie Harp update: More than 150 January 6 posts show fierce Trump loyalty, ‘We love you’If the department fights these cases, on the other hand, Trump will have to answer to a part of his base that has held up the prosecutions of nearly 1,600 people in connection with Jan. 6 as a paramount example of Democratic “weaponization” of government power against conservatives. The capitol breach took place as lawmakers met to certify Joe Biden's electoral win after Trump unsuccessfully tried to overturn the results.Lawsuits could lead to taxpayer-funded payoutsSettlements or court-ordered compensation would be paid from what’s known as the Judgment Fund, a permanent source of public money approved by Congress. The fund has already been tapped by the Trump administration for controversial million-dollar payments to settle litigation with Trump’s allies and political supporters, including in cases the government previously fought involving conservative activist Michael Flynn and former Trump campaign adviser Carter Page.The Jan. 6 plaintiffs are relying on a decades-old process under US law for demanding financial recompense from the government. Objections from top Senate Republicans this summer led attorney general Todd Blanche to scuttle plans for a special $1.8 billion fund for victims of alleged government “weaponization” that was expected to handle Jan. 6-related issues. Critics accused the administration of trying to create a separate track for these types of claims to avoid public scrutiny of payouts of taxpayer dollars.Lawsuits could lead to taxpayer-funded payoutsFormer federal prosecutors who handled these cases slammed the idea that Jan. 6 defendants are entitled to compensation. Michael Romano, who served as a deputy chief of the Justice Department unit that handled the prosecutions, said that they secured convictions “in overwhelming numbers because they were guilty and we had the evidence to back it up.”“We heard people say they were maliciously prosecuted or targeted for their political beliefs at the time we were bringing these cases,” Romano said. “It wasn’t true then and it isn’t true now.”Trump has expressed support for Jan. 6 defendants but hasn’t committed to compensating them. Asked over the summer if people who assaulted police should get paid, he didn’t offer a full-throated endorsement but didn’t knock down the idea either, telling NBC News, “I wouldn’t be inclined to say so, but I have to see it.”In response to questions about Jan. 6 compensation claims, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said in a statement that “the only pardons anyone should be critical of are from” former President Joe Biden and “extreme liberal Democrat governors.”The justice department hasn’t signaled how it intends to handle the new crop of Jan. 6 cases. In recent weeks, government lawyers have asked judges to extend deadlines, saying they need more time to review voluminous court filings. A department spokesperson declined to comment on pending litigation.At least five of the Jan. 6 plaintiffs are former clients of the department’s third-ranking official, associate attorney general Stanley Woodward, whose law practice included criminal defense before Trump appointed him. In response to a question about whether Woodward is recused from Jan. 6 matters, the department shared a statement that he 'complies with all ethics advice.'Justice Department outlines possible legal defencesJustice department lawyers have argued for judges to toss out a handful of early Jan. 6-related lawsuits that were filed before the caseload exploded this summer, including one filed by five defendants from the high-profile prosecution against former members of the Proud Boys extremist group; four of them were convicted of seditious conspiracy against the US government and the fifth was found guilty of other offenses.These cases preview defenses that the government could raise if it decides to push back, including that the US generally can’t be sued for prosecutors’ “discretionary” charging decisions, that claimants missed the two-year statute of limitations and that grand jury indictments create a “presumption” of probable cause that’s difficult to overcome.Thomas Ranieri, a lawyer representing the five plaintiffs in the Proud Boys case, said in an email that there haven’t been settlement talks with the government. He said that the Justice Department was “not sympathetic to the harm done to my clients” but had “litigated the case professionally.”Also Read | Marco Rubio’s visit: Catalyst for a new era of diplomacy“The real problem is that the laws related to constitutional violation claims like these give the government far too many protections,” he said.The justice department typically defends both current and former officials or agency employees who are sued over work they did in their government roles. Former attorney general Merrick Garland, who is named as a defendant in many of the Jan. 6 lawsuits, has brought on his own counsel, court records show. His attorney Beth Wilkinson declined to comment.Plaintiffs allege mistreatmentThe Jan. 6 plaintiffs broadly contend that they were targeted because of their support for Trump. Many cases feature specific allegations of wrongdoing by prosecutors and investigators, including claims that guilty pleas were coerced or that evidence was misleadingly presented in court. Some individuals held in jail after their arrest or who served sentences at federal prisons claim they were mistreated, assaulted or received poor medical care.Two of the plaintiffs in the Jan. 6 lawsuits weren't charged but alleged they were wronged by federal officers investigating their family members. One man was convicted of threatening a lawyer associated with the Jan. 6 investigation. The rest were charged or convicted in connection with the events at the Capitol.Two lawyers are handling the bulk of these cases, Peter Ticktin and Alexander Lonstein. Ticktin, a conservative activist who for years has promoted discredited and unproven 2020 election fraud conspiracy theories, said he expects to file lawsuits on behalf of more than 400 people.Ticktin said that his clients convicted of assaulting or interfering with police were wrongly accused and that he wouldn’t represent someone who committed such a crime. He expressed confidence they could overcome arguments the government may raise about US immunity for prosecution decisions, the two-year limit for filing claims and other defenses.“Maybe the individuals that did this may have some insulation so we can’t sue them individually, that doesn’t mean that the government can just ignore the fact that these things happened,” he said.Lonstein, who represents more than two dozen Jan. 6 plaintiffs, said in a statement that property damage and violence “should rightfully be condemned,” but the “law requires that justice be applied equally and proportionately.” The Biden administration “weaponized the justice system against these everyday Americans, with unconstitutional charges, harsh and excessive bails, and disproportionate sentences; the egregiousness of which was eclipsed only by the squalid conditions of our client’s confinement,” he wrote.The Jan. 6 lawsuits are being brought under the Federal Tort Claims Act. The law requires individuals first to file a claim with the agency at issue. That review isn’t public. If the claim is denied or the agency doesn’t respond within six months, the person can sue. That puts the claim – and whatever the government does in response – on a public court docket.In response to questions from senators about Jan. 6 this summer, Blanche said in a written response that every claim brought under the tort law 'is reviewed on the merits' and that any settlements are 'made only in the best interest of the United States.' As of July, Blanche said he wasn't aware of the department settling any Jan. 6-related claim.Judgment fund payments are listed in a public database, although the administration is facing a lawsuit that accuses officials of failing to disclose all of the required information. The justice department contends the challengers lack standing to sue and disputes that the treasury department has an 'independent obligation' under a federal recordkeeping law to release certain details about payments.Michael Gordon, a former Jan. 6 prosecutor, said that the Capitol attack “was the most filmed, documented crime scene ever” and that the plaintiffs face a high procedural bar for suing the federal government, let alone proving their allegations. Settlements also would create challenging precedents for the Justice Department going forward, he said. Gordon and Romano previously sued the department over the 'anti-weaponization' fund plan.“They would be somehow saying that prosecutors who followed the law and juries who applied the law did something wrong,” said Gordon, who also is among a number of former government lawyers and FBI agents suing over their firings under Trump. “If it’s, ‘Okay we’re going to pay anybody the president pardons,’ that becomes a gateway for corruption.”

title: Indian-origin pharmacist, employee jailed for 6 years for NHS fraud worth 1.3 million pounds in UK
description: The Patels, who are not related, were both found guilty of three counts of fraud by false representation and two counts of converting criminal property.
content: An Indian-origin pharmacist and his employee have each been sentenced to six years' imprisonment over an NHS prescription fraud worth an estimated 1.3 million pounds.Jignesh Patel, 46, and Rahil Patel, 42, were sentenced last week following a three-week trial at Southwark Crown Court.The Patels, who are not related, were both found guilty of three counts of fraud by false representation and two counts of converting criminal property.Also read: Indian-origin UK police officer charged with attempted rape, intentional strangulation"This was committed out of greed, and you were equal partners in the serious fraud designed to make you a lot of money," Justice Cole said at the sentencing hearing last Friday."This was a thoroughly impressive investigation, expertly presented on all sides," he said.The National Health Service said the NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA) investigators will now use their powers under the UK Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (POCA) to recover these lost funds.Also read: Chicago sex assault suspect described as ‘South Asian male with dark complexion’"Jignesh Patel and Rahil Patel worked together for several years, obtaining drugs using false prescriptions and selling them on to European pharmaceutical wholesale businesses," said Ben Harrison, Head of Operations and Engagement at the NHSCFA."Our expert investigation team followed the evidence, both in the UK and Europe, to bring these individuals to justice. This case demonstrates that there is no hiding place for those who seek to defraud the NHS," he said."We will actively pursue any criminals that seek to defraud the NHS of vital funds and every pound stolen from the NHS is a pound that cannot be spent on frontline services, and the NHSCFA is committed to pursuing those responsible," he added.As a pharmacist who owns Wise Pharmacy in north London and a pharmaceutical wholesale business called Actipharm Limited, Jignesh Patel came under the NHSCFA radar for dispensing high-cost drugs, normally only issued in a hospital environment.Following anomalies in the expected prescribing data, NHS Clinical Commissioning Groups obtained copies of the prescriptions and checked them with the named general practitioners (GPs). These checks identified that there was no documentation to support the patients' clinical need for the drugs and confirmed they had not been prescribed.Enquiries by the Local Counter Fraud Specialist (LCFS) identified seven high-cost medicines being dispensed by Wise Pharmacy which would not normally be expected in primary care. The drugs were Sprycel, Noxafil, Atripla, Eviplera, Tobramycin, Truvada and Viread.The NHSCFA obtained all the prescriptions dispensed by Patel's pharmacy for the period January 2015 to November 2017. Examination of these prescriptions identified 1,639 false prescriptions in the names of 24 GPs for 440 individual patients and 6,983 dispensed items. The GPs named as prescribers were interviewed and confirmed that they had not issued the prescriptions, the NHSCFA said."The reimbursement value for the drugs listed on the false prescriptions paid by the NHS to Wise Pharmacy was in excess of £1.3 million," it stated.Also read: ₹98 lakh pharma fraud case after 13 years; accused held from Surat">Delhi Police solves ₹98 lakh pharma fraud case after 13 years; accused held from SuratEvidence from European wholesalers was obtained through European Investigation Orders (EIOs) submitted by the UK's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) to prosecutors in the Netherlands, Germany and Belgium in November 2018.In May 2019, NHSCFA presented the investigation and its evidential requirements to German authorities at Eurojust in The Hague.In March 2020, Danish police, assisted by NHSCFA, attended a Copenhagen wholesaler. The evidence linked drugs obtained by Wise Pharmacy through false prescriptions to their subsequent sale by Actipharm to European wholesalers.Jignesh Patel was arrested on December 6, 2017, and 190,000 pounds in cash was seized during a search of his property.In the UK, the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) regulates the distribution of drugs and requires wholesale businesses such as Actipharm to employ a Responsible Person (RP). An RP is responsible for ensuring that the conditions under which a licence was granted have been, and are being, complied with.Also read: One more arrested in interstate counterfeit drug racket"At the time of these offences, the RPs for Actipharm were Jignesh Patel and Rahil Patel. As Responsible Persons for Actipharm Ltd, they were responsible for accurate record-keeping and had knowledge of where the pharmaceutical drugs were obtained from and which companies they were sold to," the NHSCFA said."The investigation established that Actipharm was selling Sprycel and Noxafil to other wholesale companies despite not having purchased them, meaning they could only have been obtained through Wise Pharmacy," it added.Rahil Patel was interviewed under caution on February 14, 2020, and text messages between him and Jignesh regarding the purchase of false prescriptions and drugs formed part of the evidence at their trial this month.Also read: Bribes, fake degrees: Anatomy of a pharmacy racket

title: Women are protesting around Poland for free access to legal abortions
description: Protests across Poland challenged the government’s record on abortion access, despite two bills passed by parliament.
content: Women planned street demonstrations in more than 20 Polish cities and towns on Thursday to protest the lack of access to free and legal abortion.They're accusing Prime Minister Donald Tusk's liberal government of failing to fulfil its promise to relax Poland's strict abortion laws, and protesting even though the parliament passed two bills on Tuesday aimed at easing abortion rules. The measures are likely to be vetoed by the conservative president, Karol Nawrocki.Passing the draft laws now, a year before the next parliamentary election, is a case of "token gestures" rather than a genuine effort to reform abortion law, said Zofia Marcinek of the Abortion Dream Team, a reproductive rights activist group in Warsaw.Also Read | Poland holds suspect in alleged assassination plot against PM TuskShe said the liberal government knew the draft laws stand no chance of withstanding Nawrocki's veto, and has merely tried to create the impression of taking action because it needs women's support to win elections next year.Most abortions are performed secretlySince 1993, legal abortions have been allowed in Catholic Poland only in cases of severe fetal abnormality, risk to the mother's life and health, or the pregnancy being a result of rape or incest.Polish women have been pushing for the legalisation of abortion ever since, including in a nationwide wave of demonstrations of women wearing black called "Black Protest," which began in 2016.Rather than being liberalised, Poland's abortion laws were tightened further, banning abortions of fetuses with congenital defects in 2020 under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government.Despite the laws, abortions remain common in Poland, an overwhelming majority of which are carried out by women at home using pills obtained from outside the country. Women who undergo abortions, including by taking pills, do not face criminal responsibility under Polish law. But people helping them, including doctors and family, can potentially be prosecuted.And abortion remains a taboo subject in Poland, which now has one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws, with only Malta imposing stricter limits.Also Read | Trade, defence to be in focus of Polish PM’s India visit from Oct 21Activists accuse Polish government of disinformationTusk's pro-European coalition won the 2023 election in part on a promise to liberalise Poland's abortion laws. But in 2024, Tusk said his government wouldn't be able to overcome the likely veto of a conservative president. Instead, measures were introduced to prevent hospitals from refusing to perform legal abortions on religious grounds."The state will increasingly effectively stand on the side of the woman when she is making dramatic decisions in her life," Tusk said in 2024 when he announced the measures.Polish hospitals performed 573 abortions in the first half of 2026, compared to 452 in the whole of 2022 before Tusk came to power, according to data from the national health fund. But activists say tens of thousands of abortions happen yearly outside of hospitals.Activists organising Thursday's protests are claiming the Tusk government has betrayed Polish women -- and that Tusk's claims that women's access to abortion has improved during his administration have actually complicated getting care for some women."The government's promises act as a type of disinformation," Marcinek told the AP. "Women getting pregnant hear the prime minister say that everything is ok, that there is access to abortion, and then they end up in the hospital and see that is not the case. So they come to us when it's very late and very complicated and expensive to help them."Meanwhile, international donors are less interested in supporting Polish women's rights because they mistakenly believe things have improved, Marcinek said.Watch | Zelensky’s Ukraine under scrutiny? Poland busts alleged $86 million money-laundering ringActivists dispense abortion pills outside parliamentIn 2025, the Abortion Dream Team opened an " abortion clinic " across from the parliament building in Warsaw where women can get information about their options, or even take their abortion pills in the company of supporting activists.This September, the activists also launched a parcel locker dispensing abortion pills at the same location, nicknamed "Abortomat."The dispenser is operated by the international feminist non-profit Women Help Women. It enables women needing abortions to get the pills the next day, rather than wait for up to two weeks for home delivery, Marcinek said."There are also people who cannot safely order such pills at their own address, for example because of an unsupportive family or abusive partner," she said. "These women can get a pin number and pick up the pills in the machine the next day.""In Poland, assisting with an abortion is a criminal offence. Even passing the pills from hand to hand can be considered a crime," the Abortion Dream Team wrote in a statement. "That's why we're hacking the Criminal Code and bringing abortion into the 21st century."

title: Brent crude oil hits highest since May as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia fuel global oil supply fears
description: Brent crude hits its highest level since May as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, Strait of Hormuz tensions and oil supply disruptions fuel market fears.
content: Brent crude oil prices rose to their highest level since May on Thursday after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group carried out more attacks in Saudi Arabia. The attacks raised fears that the conflict in the Middle East could spread further and disrupt oil supplies from one of the world's most important oil-exporting regions.Brent crude futures rose by $3.35, or 3.08%, to $112.17 a barrel by 0818 GMT on Thursday. This was the highest level since May 18. Brent prices had touched $112.55 a barrel earlier in the trading session. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also moved higher. WTI crude rose by $2.68, or 2.76%, to $99.83 a barrel, according to Reuters.Brent crude oil prices rise amid supply fearsOil market analysts said efforts to reduce tensions in Ukraine and the Middle East were not convincing enough to calm the markets. Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and its oil infrastructure were raising concerns about oil supplies, despite reports that Middle Eastern crude exports had recovered to levels above those seen before the conflict, PVM Oil analyst Tamas Varga said.Varga also said he did not expect the conflicts to ease before the US midterm elections. He said this could keep oil prices high in the coming weeks, according to Reuters. Despite the security concerns, Middle Eastern crude oil exports remained high. Morgan Stanley analysts estimated that crude oil exports from the region stood at around 17 million barrels per day last week.Also read: Oil prices jump over 2% as Iran-US tensions deepen and crude inventories fallThe United States has also taken steps to protect its diplomatic staff in the region. The US State Department ordered some diplomats and their family members to leave American missions in Saudi Arabia. It also plans to withdraw family members from several other US diplomatic missions across the Middle East, US officials told Reuters.Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia raise oil concernsYemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group attacked several targets in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday. At least one person was killed and eight others were wounded at a civilian airport in Dammam, while two people were killed in a drone attack on a Saudi oil field, Reuters reported.The attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil infrastructure have added to concerns about possible disruptions to oil production and exports. Any further escalation could make it harder to maintain stable supplies from the region, which plays a major role in the global oil market. Meanwhile, explosions were heard in Sirik in southern Iran on Wednesday, Iranian media reported.Strait of Hormuz attacks threaten oil suppliesIran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday that its forces had tracked four vessels involved in what it described as illegal oil transfers in the northern Gulf. The navy said all four vessels were hit simultaneously and caught fire on Wednesday.The IRGC Navy also said three other vessels had collided with mines west of the Strait of Hormuz. It warned the US military that continued provocations could lead to a wider response against American military bases in the region, Reuters reported.The Strait of Hormuz remains a key concern for oil markets because of its importance to global energy shipments. Attacks on vessels and further military escalation in the area could threaten the movement of crude oil and add pressure to prices.Also read: US Treasury yields hold steady as investors await economic data ahead of Fed rate decision on October 28Libya oil supply disruptions add to market pressureOil supply disruptions are also continuing in Libya. A valve on an oil pipeline connecting the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to the Zawiya port has been shut, reducing production at both oilfields, the head of Libya's National Oil Corporation told Reuters.The US administration is also taking steps to address rising fuel prices. The Trump administration is offering to loan out nearly one-third of the country's 1-million-barrel emergency heating oil reserve as it seeks to contain prices that have surged amid diesel shortages.The diesel shortages have been linked to the US-Israeli war with Iran and the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine, according to Reuters. Higher fuel costs have added to pressure on governments and energy markets as supply concerns continue.Ukraine peace talks in focus as oil prices riseSeparately, Russian President Vladimir Putin met US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday. The meeting focused on efforts to end the war in Ukraine, as Washington renewed its push to stop Europe's deadliest conflict since World War Two, Reuters reported.The Kremlin said Putin had agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy also expressed support for the talks and said he hoped they would begin as soon as possible, according to Reuters.However, uncertainty over the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine continues to weigh on the oil market. Fresh attacks, threats to shipping routes and disruptions to production have increased concerns about the reliability of global crude supplies.Brent crude's rise above $112 a barrel reflects these growing supply concerns. Traders are watching developments in Saudi Arabia, Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and Ukraine closely, as any further escalation could push oil prices higher, Reuters reported.

title: Paris police bans protests around presidential palace, other high-profile areas for 12 hours
description: A Paris police decree barred protests in parts of the city Thursday, citing student demonstrations and the possibility of actions targeting symbolic sites.
content: Paris Police banned protests and demonstrations in some areas of the city on Thursday, including around the presidential palace, along the Champs-Elysées and near other tourist sites, citing the risk of violence.The police force issued the ban in a decree published on its website late Wednesday. Several other cities around France also prohibited protests, Agence France-Presse reported, with larger demonstrations planned for Saturday.Protests across France this past weekend drew more than half a million people and degenerated into violence, vandalism and looting. Since then, French officials have acknowledged failures in law-enforcement and rolled out tougher security measures, as well as pledging aid for businesses affected. Also Read | Indian embassy issues advisory for nationals in France amid violent protests: ‘Remain vigilant and exercise caution’ Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has promised “massive” security measures for next weekend’s demonstrations.Thursday’s ban in Paris is in force from 8 AM to 8 PM.The police decree refers primarily to student protests, which have been running since mid-September and stem from complaints about overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and the system used to allocate university slots. Several demonstrations “in sympathy” with high school student have also sprung up, including one that forced the Louvre museum to close on Monday.Also Read | French protests highlight deep, historical faultlinesThat action was referred to directly in the decree as part of the justification for Thursday’s ban: “Spontaneous actions are also possible on a scattered basis throughout the capital, targeting centers of authority or sites that serve as symbols, which could have international reverberations, similar to the one carried out by students at the Ecole du Louvre just recently.”Early on Thursday, before the ban came into effect, several student were dragging green recycling bins toward the front door of a university in Paris’s 6th arrondissement, a frequently used method of blocking access.

title: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs globally this year as it ramps up AI adoption
description: The banking group said it has already cut around 1,000 positions, with a further 4,000 job cuts expected to be completed by the end of this year.
content: Barclays is cutting around 5,000 jobs globally by the end of 2026 as it increases its reliance on artificial intelligence (AI).According to a report by the BBC, the banking group said it has already cut around 1,000 positions, with a further 4,000 job cuts expected to be completed by the end of this year. The reductions amount to around 5% of its global workforce, with most of the affected roles falling within operational and support functions.Barclays Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts were linked to the bank’s investments in technology to simplify and improve its operations. He stressed that while AI would play an increasingly important role in the business, it was not the sole driver of the changes.“We will employ AI at scale,” Venkatakrishnan told Bloomberg, adding, “But AI is the icing on the cake, not the cake.” He explained that building the necessary technological infrastructure was essential to unlocking the benefits of AI, adding that such investments were driving most of the efficiency gains seen so far. “I’ve often said that it is the icing on the cake – it’s not the cake – because you need to do the infrastructure build to get the benefits of AI,” he said.(Also Read: eBay layoffs 2026: Company to cut 1,000 jobs in second round of workforce reductions)Support functions, developers among roles affectedAround 60% of the planned job cuts are expected to affect support functions, including developers, according to a report by Business Insider.The cuts are a part of Barclays’ three-year cost-cutting programme, which has focused primarily on its UK retail banking operations, although its investment banking division has also been affected."With one quarter to go before the end of our original three-year plan, we have either achieved or are on track to achieve all of our 2026 group targets. We are confident in and committed to the 2028 targets that we laid out earlier in the year," Venkatakrishnan said in a statement.The banking group also revealed that it made a profit of £2.3 billion for the three months to September. The figure was higher than the profit recorded during the same period a year earlier, but slightly less than forecast.

title: 'Blessed to join Hindu New Yorkers': Zohran Mamdani on joining Navratri celebrations
description: Zohran Mamdani said it was an “honour” to come together in joy, faith, and community in temples across the city.
content: New York city mayor Zohran Mamdani on Thursday said he was “blessed” to join the Hindu New Yorkers in Queens to celebrate Navratri, Durga Puja, Dashain, and Vijayadashami.“This week, I was blessed to join Hindu New Yorkers in Queens celebrating Navratri, Durga Puja, Dashain, and Vijayadashami. We danced garba, performed aarti, witnessed Sindoor Khela, and honored the Goddess Durga,” he said in a post on X.Acknowledging the attempted mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois last week, Mamdani said, “It was an honour to come together in joy, faith, and community in temples across our city — especially after the attempted mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois last week. May we all join together in our shared responsibility to stand against hate and care for one another.”In pictures and videos shared by Mamdani and social media users, he can be seen participating in garba with members of the Indian diaspora community and joining prayers and other festive rituals at temples. Shooting attempt at Hindu temple in IllinoisHis remarks come after an alleged mass-shooting plot at a Hindu temple in Illinois. Nineteen-year old Alexandros Paporakis was arrested on October 11.A cashier at Taco Bell from Palatine, Illinois, allegedly told one of his co-workers that Sunday was going to be “a special day.” He has been charged with one count of making a terrorist threat and one count of unlawful possession of weapons.Investigators allege that Paporakis planned to target Indians at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Temple in Aurora, located about 65 km west of downtown Chicago. He focused on the temple for around two months, according to prosecutors.Prosecutors also alleged that Paporakis attempted to carry out the attack on October 11 but his rifle malfunctioned when he tried to shoot a man from a car. Paporakis called one coworker earlier in the day Sunday, saying that his gun had jammed and he left “super fast” without being seen, the Associated Press reported.Paporakis openly identified as a white supremacist at work and told them he couldn’t wait to kill Indian people, prosecutors from the Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office were quoted as saying in an AP report.In an eight-page document sent by Paporakis to his co-worker, he described Indian, Jewish and African American people as “subhumans” and outlined a plot to kill as many of them as possible, according to a court document cited by The Associated Press.When he turned up at the temple, it was filled with people while he was planning to “kill a significant number of Indians," NBC Chicago quoted a police official as saying.

title: Christina Munn-Holliday: Search underway after Texas mom crashes car on Louisiana bridge, walks away and disappears
description: Christina Munn-Holliday, 22, disappeared after authorities said she crashed her car on one of Louisiana's longest bridges, walked away and vanished.
content: A search is underway for a Texas mother who disappeared after authorities said she crashed her car on one of Louisiana's longest bridges, walked away and vanished before troopers arrived. 22-year-old Christina Munn-Holliday was reported missing to the Harris County Sheriff's Office on September 30 after a reported hit-and-run crash on I-10 in Iberville Parish, Louisiana, according to KPRC.Christina went missing after she had dropped her children off with her parents on September 29 and left for Louisiana in a gray late-model BMW. Her family later stopped hearing from her.The crash occurred early September 30 on the Atchafalaya Basin Bridge near the Whiskey Bay exit, WBRZ reported. Christina was last seen after a two-car crash. Troopers and Iberville Parish deputies arrived and found one occupied vehicle and a second empty car belonging to the young mom.Read More | Nancy Guthrie case: Ex-FBI agent reveals what made Savannah Guthrie's mom ‘even more vulnerable’ to an attack"It's a very strange case," Iberville Parish Sheriff Brett Stassi told WBRZ. "We don't know if she was picked up, we don't know if she walked away, we don't have any idea where she went that night or where she is today."The bridge stretches about 18 miles over remote bayous and swamps between Lafayette and Baton Rouge. Witnesses said that they saw Christina walk away from the scene.Investigators believe Christina was traveling to Baton Rouge. Her cell phone last pinged at the crash site.Christina Munn-Holliday’s family speaks outChristina’s relatives reportedly said that traffic camera video showed her driving fast on the bridge, per WBRZ. They believe someone may have been chasing her on I-10."Why was she on the bridge? I don't know. For her to not be there when the police arrive says a lot because you can't walk that bridge without being seen," Robert Munn, Christina's father, told ABC 13.Authorities have not confirmed this theory. Christina’s disappearance is being handled as a missing person case.Read More | What makes Nancy Guthrie's disappearance unusual? Explaining how the case differs from other missing person cases"We also are leaving open the options that she was picked up, could have been kidnapped," Stassi told WBRZ.Christina’s family is offering a $20,000 reward for her safe return. A GoFundMe has been launched to help the family in their search.Robert has been sharing regular updates on social media, seeking the public’s help in finding his daughter.“PLEASE HELP BRING MY DAUGHTER HOME,” he wrote in one Facebook post. “If you have my daughter, please know that our only concern right now is getting her home safely. You don’t have to explain anything or face anyone right now. Please let her go safely at the nearest gas station or public place and allow her to contact her family. No questions. No confrontation. Just let her come home.”

title: Thales boosts sales forecasts as defense, aerospace orders surge
description: Thales lifted its sales projections for the year as orders at its defense and aerospace units surged in the first nine months.
content: Thales lifted its sales projections for the year as orders at its defense and aerospace units surged in the first nine months.The French aerospace-and-defense group had expected sales this year to grow between 6% and 7% organically, a closely watched rate that shows performance at constant scope and exchange rates. Thales said Thursday that growth should be in the upper end of that range, and potentially above.The rosier forecasts came as Thales posted nine-month sales of 16.42 billion euros, equivalent to $18.44 billion, up 7.6% in reported terms and 8.1% organically. Analysts had forecast sales of 16.33 billion euros, according to a market consensus provided by the company.Thales, whose operations give it wide exposure to defense, aviation, space exploration and cybersecurity, continues to benefit from healthy demand for military equipment as geopolitical tensions remain high.The group reported orders of 19.12 billion euros, up 14% in reported terms and 15% organically. Analysts had forecast orders of 18.58 billion euros, according to the consensus. Thales’s defense business, which remains the largest contributor to orders, brought in nearly 11.32 billion euros in bookings, up 14% both in reported terms and organically.Thales bagged an order from the Romanian government for the supply of 12 GM200 MM/A radars as well as orders from two undisclosed European countries for air-defense equipment. A Middle Eastern country also contracted Thales to supply vehicular and portable military radios.The company said demand was particularly sustained in the naval domain. It secured a new tranche under a multiyear contract for the support and maintenance of Australian Navy vessels as well as another contract under a French program for the development of four nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarines.Thales’s aerospace business fared too, with orders up 29% organically to 5.01 billion euros. Thales Alenia Space—a joint venture between Thales and Italy’s Leonardo—last month signed an agreement with French satellite operator Eutelsat to supply payloads—equipment that satellites carry to perform their mission—for 330 low Earth orbit satellites.The company said it continued to expect an adjusted earnings before interest and taxes margin between 12.6% and 12.8% this year.Write to Mauro Orru at mauro.orru@wsj.com

title: Florida cop arrested for allegedly stealing dead man’s identity, taking over his home
description: The Florida cop is facing five felony charges following an investigation.
content: A Florida police officer was arrested after allegedly impersonating a dead man whose body he found during a welfare check in 2022. The authorities claimed that he used the deceased man's identity for years to take control of his home.According to a news release by the Broward County Sheriff’s Office, Lauderhill Police Officer Brian Louis Sguros forged documents, paid utilities, and used law enforcement databases to orchestrate a property theft scheme before his arrest on multiple felony charges.“According to investigators, Sguros filed paperwork with BCPA in Feb. 2025 stating his possession of the property dated back to Aug. 2022, just weeks after West’s [Dennis West] death.”What are the allegations?The police stated, “The investigation revealed that the Lauderhill Police officer assisted on a welfare check of a Lauderhill resident in 2022 and, after finding the individual deceased of natural causes, created a complex scheme to take control of the individual’s home.”The department added that Sguros responded to the welfare check call on July 11, 2022 at 4551 N.W. 12th Street in Lauderhill.“The resident, Dennis West, was deceased inside the home. Following his death, detectives say Sguros became involved in West’s post-death affairs.” The cop even visited the Broward County Medical Examiner’s Office posing as West’s friend and told the authorities that he had no living family.The investigators say that they didn’t find any evidence suggesting Sguros and West were friends. Further, they said that Sguros’ claim that West had no living family was untrue.The investigation revealed that “Sguros paid the taxes and utilities at the home in West’s name.” He allegedly used “West’s identification to make it appear that West was still alive to get the city of Lauderhill to issue a permit to facilitate repairs.”The authorities believe that he forged West’s signature on the permit, adding that Sguros got information about the dead man using his access to law enforcement databases.What charges is he facing?He is facing several felony charges following the joint investigation conducted by the Broward Sheriff’s Office and Broward County Property Appraiser’s Office Crimes Against Property Unit.“On Oct. 20, 2026, Brian Louis Sguros was arrested on charges of official misconduct, criminal use of deceased personal identification, criminal use of personal identification information, offense against computer user and unlawful use of two-way communication device.”"What's so upsetting is officers are supposed to uphold the law, and instead he's defrauding people," Broward Property Appraiser Marty Kair told CBS News."If you have a property, do a will, name heirs," Kair said. "It's much less likely your loved ones will be defrauded."Sguros left the Broward County Jail after posting his $25,000 bond. The investigation into the matter is underway.

title: Security flaws in PHP programming language sparks worldwide concerns
description: According to Alphabet-owned security firm Wiz, the PHP language powers around 70 percent of the websites in the world.
content: A flaw discovered by artificial intelligence in the PHP programming language has triggered a wave of shutdowns of various websites and government servers across the world.On Wednesday, cybersecurity experts discovered a pair of vulnerabilities, dubbed PHP2Shell, with the help of AI models.What is PHP?PHP, which is a recursive acronym for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, is a free, open-source, server-side scripting language designed specifically for web development. This programme serves as the invisible engine behind a website.
