Created in 1995 and initially called 'Personal Home Page', PHP is known as the the server-side language and is responsible for assembling content and delivering pure HTML code to the respective browsers. PHP is commonly used for content management systems, major tech platforms such as social media websites, and e-commerce applications.Also Read | Weak web IDs and a decade-old PHP flaw. The week the internet's plumbing showed its cracksAI models and research flag serious security flawsResearchers at security firm Calif, working with OpenAI, reported the first flaw on August 11."Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory," said OpenAI in a statement.According to Alphabet-owned security firm Wiz, the PHP language powers around 70 percent of the websites in the world.It is also the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others on the internet. The flaw by Wiz was first reported on August 24.With world leaders shutting down websites amid the panic, here's a look at the latest developments -PHP security vulnerabilities | Top updatesGovernment websites taken offline across the world: Authorities in Europe, Asia and other continents have temporarily taken certain government websites offline to protect against newly discovered security vulnerabilities. The concerns also resulted in a rare public warning from the United States National Security Agency (NSA), UK's National Cyber Security Centre, and CERT-EU'Most severe flaws ever seen': In a statement addressing the vulnerabilities, nonprofit group PHP Foundation said on Wednesday that the flaws were among the most severe it had encountered. The group also called on website administrators to update their code immediately.Vulnerability 1 - CVE-2026-109618: As per the PHP foundation, CVE-2026-109618, or Remote Code Execution (RCE) via OOM corruption, is among the two critical remote code executive vulnerabilities found. This issue can result in the PHP leaving partially initialised internal data behind and later treating it as valid, corrupting memory.Vulnerability 2 - CVE-2026-109619: The other error is CVE-2026-109619 or RCE via stale global state. As per the non-profit group, a fatal error at the wrong point in the PHP could leave internal state pointing to memory that belonged to a previous request. Both of these vulnerabilities have a score of 9.2 on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS).

title: US federal agents visit residents’ homes to investigate alleged noncitizen voting ahead of midterms
description: A DHS operation targeting alleged noncitizen voting had agents visiting residents’ homes across several states.
content: Federal agents from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) have been knocking on residents’ doors across several US states to question people about their immigration status and whether they have registered to vote or cast ballots in past elections, according to a CBS News report.The operation aims to investigate potential noncitizen voting ahead of the November 2026 midterm elections. DHS has alleged that as many as 250,000 noncitizens could be illegally registered to vote, although election experts have disputed the accuracy of the figure. According to the Department of Justice, 156 people have been charged with voting-fraud-related offences since the beginning of the Trump administration. The US has around 227 million registered voters.The presence of armed federal agents at homes has raised concerns among civil rights advocates and legal experts, who warn that the operation could intimidate eligible voters and discourage participation in elections.“What we're seeing now is the federal government is inserting itself into the state process for verifying their voter roles in an unprecedented way,” Jessica Marsden, a lawyer for Protect Democracy, which is suing the federal agency over the campaign, told CBS News.Also Read: US visa wait times for Indians rise; Mumbai, Delhi see longest visitor visa appointment delaysHundreds of agents assigned to voter fraud probeThe home visits intensified in September and continued through the past weekend, according to CBS News. Internal documents reviewed by the news organization indicate that hundreds of agents were reassigned from other cases to investigate alleged noncitizen voting.The initiative, described in an internal directive as a “Criminal Voter Fraud” operation, includes field reviews in at least six states: California, Georgia, Missouri, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wisconsin.Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), which is conducting the visits, is an enforcement arm of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Its work typically involves criminal investigations into offences such as drug smuggling, money laundering and child exploitation.On Monday, the Justice Department announced that DHS agents in California had arrested more than 20 people, all green card holders, over allegations that they had illegally registered or voted. One case involved a 72-year-old man from Belize accused of voting illegally in four elections. The allegations have not been established in court.Also Read: US launches nationwide operation targeting undocumented immigrants accused of SNAP fraudData matching raises concernsAccording to CBS News, investigators draw on government databases, voter rolls and other datasets before attempting to match names against citizenship information held by US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).A USCIS whistleblower said in September that employees were asked to review voter information for tens of thousands of people, including citizens, with a target of 40 subjects per day.DHS defended the process, saying investigations were conducted professionally and that there was no quota for determining criminality.On October 21, Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson, the ranking member of the House Homeland Security Committee, urged DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin to halt activity he said could intimidate the public during the midterm election season.

title: Is Netflix losing the plot?
description: The rise of YouTube has shifted the ground under the streamer’s feet
content: Last week Netflix unleashed a round of bloodletting in Hollywood reminiscent of a Quentin Tarantino film. The streaming giant fired about 6% of its staff, the biggest round of lay-offs since 2022, and purged some of its most senior creative executives. The aim, no doubt, was to assuage investors’ concerns about the effect of a drought of hit shows on its revenue. But alas, à la Tarantino, the plot thickens.Its quarterly results on October 20th showed what a funk Netflix is in. The company reported year-on-year revenue growth of 11.8% in the quarter ending in September, and forecast that in the final three months of the year the figure would fall to 11.5%, down from 17.6% in the same period in 2025 (see chart). The news sent Netflix’s shares sliding. Its market value has fallen by almost half in the past year.A company that once looked so unstoppable that it was valued as a tech firm now disappoints shareholders with the regularity of a stodgy media company. Some wonder whether it will next break its promise to keep revenue growing by double digits into 2027. The bigger question is whether its co-chief executives, Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters, are capable of changing the script.Their approach to a year of anaemic viewership, a shortage of zeitgeisty shows and a weak showing in American television’s Emmy Awards is to blame their underlings. Bela Bajaria, Netflix’s head of content, got the sack, along with two other senior executives. Ms Bajaria, who spent nearly ten years at Netflix, was replaced by Peter Rice, a newcomer formerly at Fox and Disney.Netflix will be hoping that Mr Rice can raise the flagging hit rate of its shows with American viewers. The trouble, however, is that Mr Sarandos still holds overall responsibility for the company’s content strategy. “Why fire Bela and not Ted?” asked LightShed Partners, a firm of analysts.Lacklustre content is not the only reason for investors’ disgruntlement. During the past year Netflix tried and failed to acquire the film and TV studios of Warner Bros Discovery, a Hollywood colossus, losing out to Paramount Skydance, a smaller Tinseltown rival. Some consider the endeavour to have been a misguided distraction that signalled a lack of confidence in Netflix’s prospects. “They never really gave a good reason for it,” says Tom Harrington of Enders Analysis, a media-research firm. “If you want more movies, just make more movies. You don’t need to buy this giant thing.”Mr Sarandos tried his best on the earnings call to persuade investors that, despite weakening growth and Netflix’s attempt at a colossal acquisition, there was “no need for a fundamental shift in strategy”. Yet the entertainment business is in the midst of upheaval. As the pioneer of streaming, Netflix used to set the pace for others to follow. Now YouTube does. According to Nielsen, a market-research firm, for the past four years more people have streamed YouTube than Netflix on their TVs. As the video-sharing platform’s most successful creators move up market, they are increasingly invading Netflix’s territory. And on mobile, YouTube, TikTok and Instagram each grab far more attention than Netflix.Like other streaming services, such as Disney+, Netflix is reacting. It has introduced short-form videos suitable for the vertical format of smartphones, has wooed some YouTube creators and is expanding its efforts around live entertainment, including sports. But it is getting harder for Netflix to stand out, and its response to the new competition looks increasingly haphazard. “It’s YouTube panic,” says Mr Harrington of Enders.For all that, Netflix’s great strength is its capacity to make money from streaming. As Maria Rua Agouti of Omdia, another research firm, puts it: “People watch YouTube but they pay for Netflix.” For now, YouTube’s subscription business is still relatively small.Netflix also still has high hopes for its effort to sell ads, which it initiated during its previous slump in 2022. Yet that sideline—which is Mr Peters’ responsibility—has lately been disappointing. On the earnings call Mr Peters said that he expects ad revenue of $2.7bn this year, below the $3bn previously forecasted, owing to delays in the adoption of new ad products. If YouTube and others continue to steal viewers’ attention, hitting such targets will only get tougher. Mr Peters, like his co-chief, offered no indication of a shift in approach. Eventually investors may demand a different kind of bloodletting.

title: Ilhan Omar says 'not to my knowledge' when asked if she's related to ex-husband in first interview after DC raid
description: Ilhan Omar spoke out for the first time after her Washington, DC, house was raided, saying that allegations that she married her brother were “insane.”
content: Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) spoke out for the first time after her Washington, DC, house was raided, saying on Wednesday, October 21, that allegations that she married her brother were “insane.”“Not to my knowledge,” Omar responded, when asked by MS NOW’s Chris Hayes if there was any “weird kernel of truth” to the claim that she married her brother.The allegations that Omar and her ex-husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, tied the knot in a failed effort to get him a green card originated on a “Somali blog.” The claims spread after “right-wing conspiracy theorists” latched onto it, Omar said in the interview.“Somebody put in there that, you know, he had to have been my brother or something to that effect,” she said. Omar claimed that bloggers “went and like found random people who are like .. ‘She introduced him to us and said he was her brother,’ which is, you know, insane.”Alleged documents previously indicated that Omar suggested she and her husband had a combined net-worth of some $30 million. She later claimed that it was a mistake and revised it down.On being asked about her current financial situation in light of those documents, she described herself as “working class” and living “paycheck to paycheck.”“I have a Toyota Camry that’s from 2016. It’s our only car. I rent my DC place and my Minneapolis place, and so I mean, I don’t know, that sounds like not the majority of Congress, but there’s some of us that don’t come from wealth and don’t have wealth,” said Omar.Omar also said that she has no plans to continue to live at the DC home which Homeland Security Investigations agents searched.Also Read | Ilhan Omar citizenship row: Trump officials found no evidence of wrongdoing in 2019 review, report says“I can’t continue to live there, so we have to figure out where to move to,” she said, adding that her address was made public and “with the death threats that I deal with, it’s no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids like visiting off and on, having people track them.”Omar also asked her supporters to donate to her re-election campaign so she could “fight Trump and his administration for trying to intimidate me and so many other people right before the midterm elections.”What Ilhan Omar said about the raidTalking about her initial reaction to the DC raid, Omar said she thought “something was on fire” when federal agents banged on her door.“I thought something was happening to the neighbors. It sounded like an urgent evacuation sort of situation,” she recalled.Omar said that agents “went room by room” and “took 17 items,” including her cellphones, her daughter’s old cellphone, her husband’s notebooks, a Somali phrase book and a camera.Omar dismissed claims that investigators obtained her DNA during the search. Sources earlier told the New York Post that federal prosecutors might use DNA evidence to try to prove that Omar committed immigration fraud. People familiar with the investigation said that the feds used whistleblowers, government records and now obtained DNA in an effort to substantiate allegations that Omar and her family members, like her father, defrauded immigration authorities.“I would have seen if they did take anything that had contained DNA,” she said.She praised HSI agents for leaving the home tidy after completing their search.“They did a really good job in putting everything back in its place,” she said. “They actually even folded some of my clothing that were not folded.”Also Read | Obama condemns probe into Ilhan Omar, says Trump administration is using federal power to intimidate herOmar went on to describe the raid as “intrusive but polite,” adding they “left the house in good shape.”Tom Homan has said that the feds have built “a strong case” that could result in the Trump administration seeking to denaturalize Omar. The congresswoman has lived in the US since her family emigrated from Somalia in 1995.Sources previously said that immigration fraud pertained to either Omar or her father, Nur Omar Mohamed, allegedly misrepresenting the future congresswoman’s birth date in order for her to become a US citizen when her dad naturalized in 2000.Defense attorneys Amy Jeffress and Joshua Matz wrote that the feds refused to comply with a magistrate judge’s “special requests” for executing the search warrant at Omar’s home and even flouted DOJ policy by conducting it close to an election.“President Trump has made no secret of his desire to target Representative Omar for criminal investigation and deportation as retribution for her political advocacy,” they said.In response, a DOJ spokesperson said that the letter was “riddled with false allegations and inaccuracies.”“Our attorneys and law enforcement partners complied with all court orders and legal obligations, as they always do,” the rep added. “Leaking a letter to the press right after sending it is not good faith. It is a publicity play.”

title: IT firm ConnectWise hit by China-linked hackers in targeted global attack, says Microsoft
description: The hackers, which Microsoft tracks as Storm-0940, used an open-source penetration testing framework called ARTEX to carry out the campaign, said the statement.
content: A Chinese state-aligned hacking group used an AI-driven penetration testing tool to compromise IT services firm ConnectWise as part of a campaign that targeted hundreds of organizations globally, Microsoft said on Wednesday.Based on Microsoft's analysis and evidence available to ConnectWise, "it appears that a China state-aligned group was responsible for the attack on ConnectWise Cloud Backup," ConnectWise CEO Manny Rivelo said in a separate statement.Rivelo said ConnectWise "contained the affected application connections and are restoring services in controlled phases," and that "those actions do not remove unauthorized access that may have already been established within individual customer tenants, which require separate review." Also Read | Govts in Europe take down sites, US urges fix after AI discovers flaw in programming language PHP A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington said China "opposes and fights hacking activities in accordance with the law. At the same time, we oppose smears and attacks against China under the excuse of cybersecurity issues."The hackers, which Microsoft tracks as Storm-0940, used an open-source penetration testing framework called ARTEX to carry out the campaign, Microsoft said.There are multiple tools used to conduct penetration testing, a form of legitimate testing of the security of networks or services. ARTEX allows users to use any AI model to automate a variety of penetration testing tasks and can be configured to run autonomous tasks, including reconnaissance and data exfiltration, Microsoft said.The attack targeted organizations across a variety of sectors, including aerospace, defense, automotive, chemicals, energy, financial services, government, legal, manufacturing, media, military, semiconductor, software, technology, think tanks and non-profit organizations, Microsoft said.While the majority of targeting was not successful, Microsoft said, Storm-0940 achieved privileged cloud persistence — or high-level access that could continue even after cleanup efforts — at many organizations in a brief time.

title: Iran claims it struck 4 oil ships in Persian Gulf, 3 others hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
description: The IRGC's statement came amid heightened tensions over maritime movement through the strategically important waterway.
content: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy has claimed that it struck and set fire to four ships carrying oil cargoes in the northern Persian Gulf, while three other vessels collided with mines in the western Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state media, Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB).In a statement issued on Thursday, the IRGC Navy said the four ships had previously crossed an “illegal route” despite warnings to the maritime companies operating them.“Following previous warnings to the offending maritime companies, who had been deceived by the invading US military and had crossed illegal routes, Navy fighters, by observing and pursuing four offending ships, which had previously crossed the illegal route, discovered them transferring oil cargoes in the middle of the northern Persian Gulf, where all four ships were hit simultaneously and caught fire,” the statement said, as reported by IRIB.Also Read I Trump's eldest son Don Jr. breaks with POTUS as Iran war's effects haunt Republicans before midterms: Report The IRGC Navy also claimed that three other vessels had struck mines in the western Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday night and were stopped.The statement came amid heightened tensions over maritime movement through the strategically important waterway, through which a significant share of global oil shipments passes.Iran blames Washington for ‘encouragement’Reiterating its control over the strait, the IRGC Navy said its personnel continued to manage maritime movement with the support of the Iranian public.“With this enormous national support, the IRGC Navy sailors continue to manage and control the Strait of Hormuz,” the statement said.The Iranian force also blamed the United States for the reported maritime incidents, accusing Washington of encouraging vessels to navigate through "illegally mined passage"."The insistence of the arrogant US regime on inciting ships to pass through the illegally mined passage has increased maritime incidents day by day," the statement said. Issuing a warning to Washington, the IRGC Navy said the confrontation could expand if the situation continued."The aggressive US army should know that if this trend continues, the scope of the confrontation will be extended to the aggressive bases in the region. This is a serious warning," it added.The statement did not identify the vessels involved or provide details about their ownership, the extent of the reported damage or any casualties.Trump tables Iran negotiationsThe claim of strikes on the ships came as US President Donald Trump on Wednesday (local time) said that the United States is not negotiating with Iran and "something" will happen "fairly soon."Speaking to American news network NewsNation's White House correspondent Libbey Dean, Trump was asked about developments in negotiations with Tehran; Trump initially acknowledged some activity but indicated that the outcome remained uncertain.“A little bit, but we'll see what happens,” Trump said when asked whether negotiations with Iran were ongoing.Asked whether he was done negotiating with the Iranian government, Trump said, "No, I think we're not negotiating...we are going to have something, one way or the other. It'll happen fairly soon."Also Read I ‘Not negotiating’: Trump says 'something will happen fairly soon' with Iran, as US mulls fresh strikesIn the interview, Trump also highlighted the situation between Washington and Tehran as "a little conflict against Iran" and said the United States was performing well on both military and economic fronts."I think our sanctions ended the real deal over there. But we're doing very well militarily and financially against Iran," he said.Trump did not specify what action or development he expected to take place “fairly soon” or provide a definitive timeline for the next steps in the US approach towards Iran.Threat of fresh strikesAll the developments come amid the report by The New York Times that the United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the American midterm elections, while Tehran has threatened to unveil a weapon it calls the "father of all bombs" amid escalating tensions in West Asia.According to The New York Times, the US and Israeli militaries have developed specific plans for a short but intensive operation targeting Iran’s energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and missile and drone arsenal. Citing US officials and other people briefed on the deliberations, the report said the two militaries have stepped up exercises, including flying aircraft over Iraq to practise strike manoeuvres.Amid the possibility of renewed strikes, Iran has warned that it would respond to any renewed military action. According to Iranian state-affiliated media outlet Student News Network (SNN), IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said, "The United States has the ‘Mother of All Bombs.’ We will show them the ‘Father of All Bombs,’ and it will definitely be something new for them."But Tehran has not provided details about the weapon or clarified what the threat entails.The warning follows reports that US President Donald Trump has considered using the 22,000-pound GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), known as the "Mother of All Bombs", against Iran’s deeply buried Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility.According to The New York Times, the United States is assembling a substantial military force expected to be fully in place by early November, including three aircraft carriers, thousands of Marines, fighter jets and Special Operations forces. Officials have cited political considerations, including Trump’s earlier pledge not to strike Iran before the midterm elections, as reasons the operation could be delayed.Also Read I More Oil Is Now Coming Out of the Persian Gulf Than Before the Iran WarIranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, has highlighted the situation as a major challenge for Tehran. In an address to the Iranian Parliament, Pezeshkian said, "The memorandum of understanding we signed was very good; we hadn't given anything. The current situation is neither good for us, nor for the region, nor for the world."He added, "We are in a super-challenge, not a challenge. America didn't think we would stand firm despite the pressure and war, but we stood firm, and we will continue to stand firm."The New York Times report said Washington was seeking to use the prospect of renewed military action as leverage in negotiations over Iran’s nuclear programme and control over the Strait of Hormuz. However, Iranian negotiators have resisted making concessions on the nuclear issue, insisting that the matter be deferred until later in the talks.As military preparations and diplomatic efforts continue, the possibility of renewed strikes has raised concerns about a wider regional conflict, with uncertainty persisting over Trump’s final decision and Iran’s potential response.

title: Tesla logs surge in European monthly sales
description: Elon Musk’s electric-vehicle maker kept gaining ground in a region where Chinese rivals are also growing strongly.
content: Tesla’s European sales surged last month, showing that Elon Musk’s electric-vehicle maker keeps gaining ground in a region where Chinese rivals are also growing strongly.New-car registrations for Tesla models, a reflection of sales, jumped 72.5% on year in September to 68,776 units across the European Union, the U.K., Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, according to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association, an industry body also known as ACEA.Growth picked up noticeably last month from a mere 4% increase in August, which tends to be a slow month for car registrations since many dealerships in Europe close for the summer holidays. Higher registrations show that drivers in Europe are embracing Tesla despite stiff competition from Chinese rivals.Chinese carmakers have experienced a meteoric rise in the continent in recent years thanks to their relatively cheap lineups of electric and hybrid vehicles, denting sales for well-established domestic auto groups such as Volkswagen and Renault.ACEA reported a nearly 99% surge in BYD registrations last month to 49,953 vehicles. SAIC Motor’s registrations grew nearly 24% to 41,987 units, while Leapmotor logged a more than fourfold increase to 14,594 vehicles. In contrast, Germany’s Volkswagen recorded a 2.9% decline in sales to 308,474 units, while Renault’s fell 0.7% to 114,726 vehicles.Tesla’s growth comes as the company seeks approval for its full self-driving technology in the EU. In April, the Netherlands became the first country in the bloc to greenlight the system that helps drivers change lanes and navigate around other vehicles and objects. FSD doesn’t make vehicles fully autonomous and is meant to be used only with a fully attentive driver, according to Tesla’s website.Since then, some EU member states including Lithuania, Estonia and Denmark, have recognized the Dutch approval, allowing Tesla to roll out FSD in those countries while EU authorities review an application from the Netherlands Vehicle Authority to make FSD available across the bloc.The market for battery-electric vehicles grew nearly 60% in Europe last month. Registrations of hybrid-electric cars gained 5.3%, while plug-in-hybrid models were up 24%.ACEA said monthly passenger-car registrations increased 10% in Europe as a whole and 9.3% in the EU, with sales up 9% in Germany, 12% in France and 9.8% in Italy.Write to Mauro Orru at mauro.orru@wsj.com

title: Laura Danbom: Amazon employee accuses senior executive of raping her on NYC business trip, claims company failed to perform full investigation
description: Laura Danbom alleged that she was raped by a senior executive during a business trip to New York City. She also claimed that the company told her to keep quiet.
content: An Amazon employee has alleged that she was raped by a senior executive during a business trip to New York City. She also claimed in a lawsuit that the company told her to keep quiet about the alleged incident and even neglected to perform a full investigation of the allegations.The alleged victim, Laura Danbom, works at Amazon’s Seattle headquarters as a marketing and operations manager for Amazon Web Services. This week, she sued the e-commerce giant for allegedly subjecting her to a hostile work environment and violating Washington State’s Silenced No More Act, per the New York Post. The act protects victims who speak up about workplace assaults from retaliation.What was the alleged incident?The alleged rape happened on October 27, 2023. At the time, Danbom had traveled to New York with a group of colleagues including Michelangelo Simonte, who is a top-performing advertising executive in her division. He was based in Madrid, according to the complaint. Simonte still works for Amazon at its Madrid offices.The group went to an Amazon-hosted open bar event that evening, and then continued the gathering at karaoke bars. The suit filed in state court in Seattle revealed that all of it was paid for by Amazon.That evening, initially, Danbom and Simonte “flirted,” “joked” and “got along,” according to the complaint. Later in the night, Simonte “kissed her,” and “persuaded Laura” to let him accompany her to her hotel room, per the complaint.Also Read | What did Letitia James say about alleged Cornell gang rape? Why New York AG faces bar ethics complaintDanbom was staying at the Hyatt Place at 140 W. 24th St. in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood, a representative for the plaintiff said, which is where things allegedly took a wrong turn.“In Laura’s hotel room, during the early morning hours, Simonte raped her,” the complaint alleged. “Before the rape started, she said no. During the rape, Laura asked him: ‘you realize this is,’ and Simonte finished her sentence saying ‘rape? Yes.’ He ignored her protests. He raped her.”Danbom reported the alleged incident to the New York Police Department the next day. She handed the officers a condom Simonte had left behind, the complaint said. She also submitted a rape kit.Subsequently, a detective monitored a phone call between Danbom and Simonte for a potential confession. During the call, Simonte said he was “200% sure” that they never had sexual intercourse, according to the complaint. However, he contradicted himself in a police interview later, admitting that he was too drunk to remember.Danbom’s attorney Jay Free said that the NYPD refused to refer the case to local prosecutors, and that police said they had exhausted all investigative avenues. The complaint accused police of failing to interview the witnesses Danbom reported the rape to immediately after it occurred, including another Amazon employee.Two days after the alleged rape, Danbom told Amazon’s human resources department about her experience, and also several friends and her therapist.Allegations against AmazonDanbom told the New York Post that Amazon investigated the allegations, put Simonte on a monthslong leave of absence, but eventually decided that he did not violate its policy. The company said that Danbom’s account of what happened was “unfounded due to lack of evidence,” and amounted to a “he said, she said” situation, according to the filing.Danbom accused Amazon of closing its investigation without speaking with witnesses who could corroborate her account and “without gathering evidence that was there for the asking,” the complaint stated.Also Read | Cornell president Michael Kotlikoff breaks silence on alleged gang rape of student, ‘My heart aches when I think of…’The complaint alleged that during Amazon’s investigation, the company “asked inappropriate and re-traumatizing questions that suggested Laura did not do enough to stop the attack, including challenging Laura on whether she yelled ‘no’.”“Before the rape began, she said no. No means no,” the suit added. “This is shameful questioning by a leading employer in 2024.”The suit further claimed that the company said it would reopen the case if New York prosecutors brought charges against Simonte. The company also asked Danbom “not to speak about Simonte’s rape at work saying the allegation was ‘highly confidential,’” according to the filing.“It prevented me from warning other women who might interact with him at events,” Danbom told the New York Post.The filing claimed that Danbom was told that her role would not change at Amazon and that she would be required to “work with Simonte directly, by phone, by email and in remote meetings.”“We take any allegation of this nature extremely seriously, and we have zero tolerance for workplace sexual misconduct or violence of any kind. We thoroughly investigate each report we receive and take appropriate action, up to and including termination, against those who are found to have violated our policies,” Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in a statement.“We have robust policies and trained investigators in place to ensure each concern is heard and addressed with the proper care. While we don’t have more to share about the specifics of this pending litigation at this time, we continue to follow our rigorous processes and to hold all employees to the same high standards,” she added.Danbom said that she took two leaves of absence after the incident. After as many as ten job applications within Amazon, she was transferred to a different position where she would not interact with Simonte back in 2024.“It was really an escape,” she said. “The position was a lateral move. I was on a path for a promotion and had to walk away from that.”The complaint is now seeking “lost wages, including front and backpay, lost bonuses and other benefits of employment, in an amount to be proven at trial.”

title: Millennials’ success deserves a toast (not the avocado sort)
description: How a “lost generation” found itself
content: Millennials, born between the early 1980s and mid-1990s, had a brutal coming of age. Many graduated in the wake of the global financial crisis. Youth unemployment rose above 50% in some parts of Europe, leading to talk of a “lost generation”. Living with their parents and deprived of the prospect of owning a home, they were lectured by unsympathetic elders not to spend so much money on brunch.Today millennials, aged around 30-45, have dramatically turned their fortunes round. They earn more than any other recent generation did at the same age, and are catching up in terms of home-ownership. At the same time, millennial-era culture is enjoying a revival in television, music, gaming and even fashion, where their notoriously tight trousers are cool once again.Dig deeperSome of this is simply the way of the world. As generations age, they get better jobs, earn more and buy homes. Millennials are not the first lot to reach middle age and revive the culture of their youth. The 1970s witnessed a 1950s revival, with a rock'n’roll renaissance, “Happy Days” and “Grease”. In the 1990s bell-bottoms and tie-dye emerged from the back of wardrobes. Nostalgia reliably runs on a two-decade timetable.Yet the millennial comeback is different. True, part of it is luck. The generation’s early economic misfortune was later counterbalanced by serendipity, when the covid-19 pandemic triggered the early retirement of many older workers. The result was a senior-management vacuum—filled by millennials.A bigger part of the story, however, is innovation and hard work. The leading lights of the tech industry, which has created enormous wealth, include many millennials. They account for more than twice the share of America’s billionaires that Gen X did at the same age. Tech’s next great leap, artificial intelligence, is likely only to strengthen their position. The bosses leading the revolution, such as Dario Amodei, Mark Zuckerberg and Sam Altman, are themselves millennials.Tech has also boosted millennials’ cultural comeback. Online platforms encourage people to bathe in the content of their youth. YouTube and Spotify are nostalgia machines. Services like Netflix, with their vast libraries, introduce new generations to millennial hits like “The Big Bang Theory”, from 2007, which is the fifth-most streamed series in America this year. Meanwhile, social media have terrified Hollywood. Hence all those sequels and reboots—safer bets than original projects. “The Devil Wears Prada 2” is one of the world’s highest-grossing films this year.Even those who dread the return of skinny jeans should cheer the millennial revival. The generation’s economic story shows that “lost” cohorts can find their way. Policymakers should note that millennials’ prospects improved thanks to markets and events, not the state-funded rescue that some once called for. As AI causes alarm about young people’s job opportunities, the millennial bounce offers a cautious cause for optimism.Millennials’ cultural comeback has lessons, too. Many will look at the glut of 1990s reboots, such as a new “Baywatch” series, and feel that Hollywood’s creativity needs saving. But once more, technology is helping. The infinite breadth of online platforms means that you have plenty of alternatives if millennial favourites are not to your taste. And the vast back-catalogues stored on these platforms mean that the hits of every era are available to everyone. Twenty years ago, one generation bore the brunt of the financial crisis. Today, all generations should celebrate the millennials’ deserved rebound.Subscribers to The Economist can sign up to our Opinion newsletter, which brings together the best of our leaders, columns, guest essays and reader correspondence.

title: Roche posts higher sales on growth scross pharma, diagnostics units
description: Roche reiterated its full-year guidance and said it is prepared to launch its giredestrant breast-cancer pill later this year.
content: Roche Holding reported higher sales for the third quarter on growth in its pharmaceuticals and diagnostics units, as the drugmaker works to secure approval for its new breast-cancer and multiple-sclerosis pills.The Swiss group said Thursday that third-quarter sales came to 16.13 billion Swiss francs ($19.57 billion) compared with 14.92 billion francs for the same period last year. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha had forecast quarterly sales at 15.78 billion francs.Roche said sales grew 7% when excluding currency changes, with increases in both its pharma and diagnostics divisions.Higher sales for top-selling drugs such as Ocrevus for multiple sclerosis, Hemlibra for hemophilia, and Vabysmo for eye diseases helped Roche’s core pharma business deliver top-line growth of 8%, the company said. Meanwhile, the group’s diagnostics division posted a 5% rise in quarterly sales, with demand for core lab and pathology systems offsetting a hit from China’s healthcare-pricing reforms.Roche reiterated its full-year guidance, which calls for increases in both sales and core earnings per share when excluding currency movements.The company said it is fully prepared to launch its giredestrant breast-cancer pill later this year, and is nearing approval of its fenebrutinib tablet for multiple sclerosis.Write to Adrià Calatayud at adria.calatayud@wsj.com

title: Indian national among 2 killed in attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Fahd airport
description: Attack on Dammam Airport: The airport has been targeted in the past during a wave of Houthi missile and projectile attacks on major airports across Saudi.
content: Two people were killed, including an Indian national, in an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's eastern oil city of Dammam, the country's general authority of civil aviation said on Thursday, as strikes by Yemen's Houthis intensify. The other victim was a Saudi citizen, the authority confirmed.Eight others were injured, including nationals of India, Yemen and Bangladesh, as well as a Saudi resident of Bangladeshi nationality.The Indian embassy in Riyadh said it was gathering more information about the incident and reaching out to the affected families. “Our thoughts and prayers are with the family and loved ones of the deceased and we wish speedy recovery of the injured,” it said in a statement posted on X. Saudi's King Fahd airport attackedAuthorities were assessing the damage caused by the attack, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. Airport operations had resumed, and air traffic was back to normal. Saudi Arabia has come under near-daily attacks by Iran-backed Houthi forces this month, including a strike on Riyadh's international airport that was the kingdom's deadliest in years.On Wednesday, the Saudi energy ministry said falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility had killed 2 people and injured 2 others.US issues travel alert, India urges nationals to take precautionsThe US ordered non-essential embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, the state department said."Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," state department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a social media post explaining the decision.On Sunday, the Indian embassy had urged Indian nationals to follow the latest safety instructions issued by Saudi authorities for people who receive emergency alerts.The guidelines, shared on social media, advise people to stay calm, follow official instructions and move immediately to the nearest safe place inside a building. People have also been told to remain inside their homes or buildings until it is safe to leave. MEA condemns attacksReacting to the attacks on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said attacks on "civilian and critical infrastructure are completely unacceptable". The MEA called for immediate cessation of such strikes while expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia. "We stand in solidarity with the people and the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy would return to the region at the earliest," the MEA said.The ministry further said the Indian Embassy in Riyadh was in touch with the Saudi authorities and will provide all possible assistance to Indian nationals affected.Houthi-Saudi conflictHouthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities and civilian infrastructure have intensified in recent weeks, forcing Riyadh to close its main airport.According to an AFP tally based on official figures, attacks on Saudi airports have killed 22 people this month.The attacks come after a years-long truce in Yemen's civil war collapsed in July. The Iran-backed Houthis are fighting the Yemeni government, which is supported by a Saudi-led coalition.The Houthis announced a maritime blockade targeting Saudi Arabia and began attacking its ships, territory and oil facilities. In September, they launched a major offensive and captured areas along the Red Sea coast that had been under government control.In response, the Saudi air force has repeatedly carried out strikes on areas controlled by the Houthis, who hold much of Yemen.With inputs from agencies

title: Pentagon allows DHS to test military-grade heat ray for potential use at US-Mexico border
description: A Pentagon memo authorizes DHS to borrow a military heat-ray system for seven months beginning in September and develop potential border-use tactics.
content: The Pentagon has authorized the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to test a military-grade heat ray and develop tactics for its potential use along the US-Mexico border, according to a memo obtained by CNN.The memo, signed by US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth last month, authorizes the temporary loan of one Active Denial System (ADS) to DHS for seven months starting in September. The system uses electromagnetic waves to create an intense burning sensation on the skin without physically touching a person.The weapon is designed to make people move away from the beam. According to the US military, its effects can feel like a blast of heat from opening a hot oven, with the resulting sensation typically lasting 10 to 15 minutes.The DHS request did not specify where or how the system would be tested or how it might eventually be used in border operations.How the heat ray worksThe Active Denial System fires an invisible beam of electromagnetic energy that can reach a little more than half a mile, according to the US military.Also read: US secures $5 million settlement after Instacart accused of favoring visa holders over American workersThe beam heats the surface of the skin, causing an intense burning sensation intended to make people move away from the affected area. Military officials have described the effect as producing an instinctive urge to escape the beam.The US military briefly deployed the system to Afghanistan nearly two decades ago but ultimately did not use it in active combat operations. Officials also considered using it for crowd control at US facilities abroad where terrorist detainees were held but did not proceed.The proposed border use would mark an unprecedented step in deploying the technology for US border operations.Concerns over safety and legalityUS border officials have discussed the possibility of using the system to disperse crowds and discourage crossings in areas with high numbers of attempted illegal crossings. However, concerns over its effectiveness, legality and potential harm have complicated earlier discussions.One concern is that people could be injured indirectly if the weapon causes them to flee into dangerous areas or water. Officials have also considered the possibility that its use could increase the need for rescue operations.A former Customs and Border Protection official told CNN that authorities would need to weigh the cost, training requirements and policies against the potential benefits.Border officials examined the technology in the El Centro sector, which covers about 70 miles along the US-Mexico border, several years ago. The discussions included whether it could discourage people from crossing a nearby river or push them out of the water.In 2018, Customs and Border Protection officials also considered using the system against migrants, but then-Homeland Security Secretary Kirstjen Nielsen rejected the proposal.Also read: US launches nationwide operation targeting undocumented immigrants accused of SNAP fraudDHS to oversee testing and tacticsUnder the Pentagon memo, DHS will be responsible for operating the system and developing tactics, techniques and procedures for its use. The memo states that the system will not be operated by Department of War personnel.At the end of the seven-month loan period, DHS can request additional use of the system for border operations, depending on its needs, a defense official told CNN.A Customs and Border Protection spokesperson said the agency was continually evaluating new technologies to improve operational effectiveness and strengthen its capabilities.The Pentagon referred CNN to DHS when asked for comment. The report did not specify a testing location or confirm whether the heat ray would ultimately be deployed against migrants.

title: Japan’s mission to Mars’s moons takes off
description: It will collect samples and search for signs of ancient life
content: ORBITERS, LANDERS and rovers have travelled to Mars, but none has returned. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) intends for that to change. On October 20th its Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission lifted off from Tanegashima, an island in southern Japan. The probe will spend the next year travelling to Mars, where it aims to land on Phobos, the larger of the planet’s two moons, collect at least ten grams of rock and dust, and return the haul to Earth in 2031. Planetary scientists hope the mission will resolve a long-standing puzzle: how Mars’s moons were formed—and, in the process, reveal much about the planet itself.Phobos and Mars’s other moon, Deimos, are small, respectively about 22km and 12km across, and look like lumpy potatoes. That might suggest they are asteroids that were captured by Mars’s gravitational field after straying too close. Captured asteroids, however, usually have tilted, elliptical orbits, whereas both moons follow nearly circular paths around the planet’s equator. That hints at another possible origin: a giant collision that threw debris into orbit that later gathered into moons.JAXA has spent over a decade developing MMX, working with the space agencies of America, Europe and Australia. The mission builds on Japan’s record of returning samples from space. Its Hayabusa mission collected small amounts of grains from Itokawa, an asteroid which comes close to Earth, and brought them home in 2010. Its successor, Hayabusa2, brought back five grams of material—well above the mission’s target—from Ryugu, another near-Earth asteroid, in 2020. The samples proved rich in water-bearing molecules and organic compounds, offering clues to how asteroids may have carried the ingredients for life to Earth.MMX’s mission is more demanding. Phobos’s surface gravity is roughly one-2,000th of Earth’s, but it is 40 times greater than Ryugu’s. That is strong enough to pose a crash risk for a delicate spacecraft, explains Erik Asphaug, a planetary scientist at the University of Arizona. The Hayabusa missions also followed a “touch-and-go” method in which the spacecraft briefly kissed the asteroids. In contrast, MMX will land on Phobos and extract samples from beneath its surface.And MMX’s makers want to do a lot more during its three years orbiting Mars. An instrument called MEGANE (pronounced “meh-gah-neh”, like the Japanese word for spectacles), developed by NASA, will measure gamma rays and neutrons given off when cosmic rays hit Phobos, thus revealing its chemistry. A small European rover will explore its surface. After departing Phobos, MMX will conduct fly-bys of Deimos to observe it, too, up close.If the samples make it safely back to Earth, scientists reckon they might settle which of the two origin stories is true. If Phobos is a captured asteroid, its rocks may resemble meteorites from elsewhere in the solar system. If it instead formed after a giant impact, it will contain melt fragments generated by intense heating.Whatever Phobos’s history, its proximity to Mars means it should also have collected material blasted off the planet by asteroid impacts. Martian debris should make up about 0.1% of the samples MMX collects. Scientists already have Martian meteorites, but these are mostly hard volcanic rocks that survived the journey through space and Earth’s atmosphere. Sara Russell, a planetary scientist at the Natural History Museum in London who will help analyse MMX’s samples, hopes the mission could recover softer sedimentary material. “That’s the material where we might see biosignatures,” she says, offering clues to whether Mars was once habitable.There is reason to wonder. Ancient riverbeds and lake deposits suggest Mars once had liquid water and a thicker atmosphere. Unlike the planet itself, its moons have undergone little geological change. They may therefore have preserved fragments of that distant past like a time capsule, says Elizabeth Tasker, an astrophysicist at JAXA. The two small moons could thus help answer a much bigger question: whether life existed on the red planet.

title: JD Vance’s visit to Cincinnati Bengals practice facility draws attention after players accused of ‘ignoring’ VP
description: A video from Vice President JD Vance’s visit to the Bengals’ practice facility appeared to show most players walking past him.
content: US Vice President JD Vance’s visit to the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice facility on Wednesday drew attention after a video appeared to show most players walking past him without acknowledging him.Vance, a lifelong Bengals fan, visited the team’s practice facility in Kettering, Ohio, while in the area following a campaign rally in nearby Sharonville. He was accompanied by a large police presence as he toured the facility and greeted players.An 18-second video filmed from an office window showed Bengals players walking towards the locker room as Vance stood nearby. Most appeared to pass him without stopping, while one player shook his hand. The footage circulated online, prompting comments from fans about the players’ apparent lack of interaction with the vice president.ALSO READ: US launches nationwide operation targeting undocumented immigrants accused of SNAP fraudJoe Burrow says he did not meet VanceBengals quarterback Joe Burrow was asked about Vance’s visit after practice. He said he did not get an opportunity to interact with the vice president.“He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn’t get to (talk with him),” Burrow said, as per reports.He added that there were “a lot of people around”.Burrow also spoke about the attention the team receives from visitors and fans, saying, “That’s what I love about what I do is it brings a lot of people together.”He added that people take time out of their day to watch the team and the work he puts in.ALSO READ: Texas GOP candidate Brandon Herrera sparks backlash over joke about sending kittens to Chinese restaurantsBengals prepare for Ravens gameVance’s visit came as the Bengals prepare for their next game against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.Cincinnati entered the game with a 3-2 record, while Baltimore stood at 4-2.The video did not establish why most players did not stop to greet Vance, and the report did not indicate that the players had deliberately avoided him.

title: University of Utah issues campus alert amid reports of threat, person ‘brandishing a firearm’ detained
description: The University of Utah has issued a campus alert amid reports of a threat incident. Here's what we know.
content: The University of Utah issued a campus alert amid reports of a threat incident. The alert asked students to “stay in your room or area.”A person “brandishing a firearm” was reportedly later detained.The initial alert read, “Emergency personnel are on scene for an unverified threat incident in the area of: B46 LASSONDE STUDIOS 1701 E STUDENT LIFE WAY AND SURROUNDING BUILDINGS. Expect a heavy police presence and potential disruption to campus activities.”Also Read | ‘Forever in Our Hearts’: Sandy Hook victims honoured as surviving peers graduateIt added, “If you are in or near the area, HOLD in your current room or area. Do not enter or exit the building or surrounding area. Clear hallways and follow instructions from law enforcement.” “Remain in place until an ALL CLEAR message is issued,” the alert further said.Latest updateThe University of Utah later shared that an “all clear” message was eventually issued.“An individual brandishing a firearm has been detained. The area around LASSONDE STUDIOS is safe. The HOLD for police activity has been lifted. No injuries were reported. Officers from University Police and Salt Lake City Police responded quickly and located the individual who is detained. The item was determined to be an Airsoft rifle,” said the alert.Also Read | Minneapolis school shooting: Robin Westman wrote about what he wanted to wear during attack, ‘I look pretty’It added, “Normal activities may resume. Police will remain in the area as the investigation continues. Additional updates will be provided as needed. Please report any suspicious activity to University Police at 801-585-2677.”The University of Utah Department of Public Safety says of the alert system, “The University of Utah’s Campus Alert System is designed to reach everyone on campus in the best way possible during an emergency. Most alerts are sent via email, and are color-coded according to level of importance for quick identification.”

title: US Rep Ilhan Omar to move out of Washington DC home after federal agents’ search, says raid made her feel unsafe
description: Ilhan Omar revealed she was rattled by the search weeks out from the Nov. 3 midterms, which will decide control of the House and Senate.
content: US Rep. Ilhan Omar will move out of her Washington, D.C., home that federal agents searched last week, she said Wednesday, noting that attention brought on by the raid has made her feel unsafe there.Federal authorities are investigating potential fraud in her family's immigration paperwork and have issued grand jury subpoenas to some of her relatives, a person briefed on the investigation told The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss an ongoing investigation.Also Read I Ilhan Omar update: Trump says Democrat ‘could be in jail’ as family is seen at home amid DNA investigation Omar, who was born in Somalia and is a naturalized U.S. citizen, said Wednesday in her first interview since the search that she is “confident in the fact that I didn’t do anything wrong.” Omar rattled by home searchThe progressive Minnesota Democrat has been a frequent critic and target of President Donald Trump, who has on multiple occasions pushed for the prosecution of his perceived political enemies.In the interview with MS NOW, Omar said she was rattled by the search weeks out from the Nov. 3 midterms, which will decide control of the House and Senate. She is running for reelection in a deep blue district centered in Minneapolis and is expected to retain her seat.Omar recalled waking around 6 a.m. to Homeland Security investigators banging on her door with a warrant. They searched for four or five hours and seized 17 items, including phones, notebooks, a Somali language children’s book and a vintage camera that her husband had received as a gift, she said. The Justice Department has shared few details about the case other than saying it was a criminal investigation.Omar came with her family to the U.S. at age 12, after they obtained asylum. She became a U.S. citizen five years later, in 2000.“It would be a huge undertaking to, I suppose, indict a 12-year-old for so cleverly conspiring to defraud immigration services to come to the United States. I'm sure there are a lot of smart 12-year-olds, but that seams like a leap,” she said in the interview.Also Read I Ilhan Omar's first married name ‘Ilhan Nur Said Elmi’ on DOJ doc reignites debunked marriage claimThe search drew sharp condemnation from congressional Democrats, who also questioned the timing. The Justice Department has historically avoided overt investigative actions involving candidates in the immediate run-up to an election.Omar said the agents were “intrusive but polite,” logging the items they took and putting back everything else in its place.

title: Pak army chief, Maldives president discuss defence cooperation
description: Pak army chief, Maldives president discuss defence cooperation
content: Islamabad, Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu discussed ways to strengthen defence cooperation and institutional ties, as the two countries seek to expand bilateral engagement.Munir, who also serves as Chief of Defence Forces , called on Muizzu in Islamabad on Wednesday during the Maldivian president's three-day visit to Pakistan, according to a statement issued by the Pakistan Army.The meeting covered "matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment and avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation", the statement said."Both sides underscored the importance of strengthening defence cooperation, institutional linkages and professional exchanges," it said.Munir highlighted the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and the Maldives and reaffirmed Islamabad's commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation and promoting regional peace, stability and security through constructive engagement.Muizzu's visit is the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, marking a renewed high-level engagement between the two countries.The meeting between Munir and Muizzu assumes significance for India given the Maldives' strategic location in the Indian Ocean and its importance to New Delhi's maritime security interests.India has traditionally been a key security and development partner of the archipelago, providing assistance in areas such as maritime surveillance, defence training and capacity-building.Maldives occupies a special place under 'Neighbourhood First' foreign policy of India, which aims at bringing stability and prosperity in the Indian Ocean Region .Both nations are also key players in maintaining the safety and security of the IOR, contributing to India-led Security And Growth for All in the Region vision.Pakistan's outreach to Male comes amid India's efforts to strengthen its engagement with Indian Ocean neighbours and safeguard its strategic interests in the region.Pakistan and the Maldives on Wednesday also signed 20 memorandums of understanding to strengthen cooperation in various fields, including defence, maritime security and artificial intelligence.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: ‘Not negotiating’: Trump says 'something will happen fairly soon' with Iran, as US mulls fresh strikes
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told parliament that the confrontation with Washington had placed Tehran in a “super-challenge”.
content: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said that the United States is not negotiating with Iran and "something" will happen "fairly soon," Speaking to American news network 'NewsNation's White House correspondent Libbey Dean, Trump was asked about developments in negotiations with Tehran, Trump initially acknowledged some activity but indicated that the outcome remained uncertain.“A little bit, but we'll see what happens,” Trump said when asked whether negotiations with Iran were ongoing.Asked whether he was done negotiating with the Iranian government, Trump said, "No, I think we're not negotiating...we are going to have something, one way or the other. It'll happen fairly soon." He added that some people expected developments to take place after the US election, saying, "Most people think, seem to think it's after the election, and we're going to see what happens."Trump also praised his administration's approach towards Iran, stating, “But I will say this: what we've done with Iran is amazing.”Also read: 'No enriched nuclear material will leave Iran': Tehran tells Pakistan army chief Asim Munir amid US peace deal deadlockIn the interview, Trump also highlighted the situation between Washington and Tehran as "a little conflict against Iran" and said the United States was performing well on both military and economic fronts."I think our sanctions ended the real deal over there. But we're doing very well militarily and financially against Iran," he said.Trump did not specify what action or development he expected to take place “fairly soon” or provide a definitive timeline for the next steps in the US approach towards Iran. But this comes amid the report by The New York Times that the United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the American midterm elections, while Tehran has threatened to unveil a weapon it calls the "father of all bombs" amid escalating tensions in West Asia.According to The New York Times, the US and Israeli militaries have developed specific plans for a short but intensive operation targeting Iran’s energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and missile and drone arsenal. Citing US officials and other people briefed on the deliberations, the report said the two militaries have stepped up exercises, including flying aircraft over Iraq to practise strike manoeuvres.Also read: US official denies Iran's claim that American forces targeted Konarak naval base: 'Inaccurate, as usual'US War Secretary Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel this week to discuss potential renewed strikes, according to the news report. Some US officials believe another round of "attacks" could push Iran’s economy to the brink and force Tehran to make diplomatic concessions after nearly eight months of conflict.Amid the possibility of renewed strikes, Iran has warned that it would respond to any renewed military action. According to Iranian state-affiliated media outlet Student News Network (SNN), Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said, "The United States has the ‘Mother of All Bombs.’ We will show them the ‘Father of All Bombs,’ and it will definitely be something new for them."But, Tehran has not provided details about the weapon or clarified what the threat entails.Also read: IRGC drops bombshell before US midterms: Hormuz now 100% close, missiles more deadly & longer range?The warning follows reports that US President Donald Trump has considered using the 22,000-pound GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), known as the "Mother of All Bombs", against Iran’s deeply buried Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility. According to The New York Times, the United States is assembling a substantial military force expected to be fully in place by early November, including three aircraft carriers, thousands of Marines, fighter jets and Special Operations forces. Officials have cited political considerations, including Trump’s earlier pledge not to strike Iran before the midterm elections, as reasons the operation could be delayed.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, has highlighted the situation as a major challenge for Tehran. In an address to the Iranian Parliament, Pezeshkian said, "The memorandum of understanding we signed was very good; we hadn't given anything. The current situation is neither good for us, nor for the region, nor for the world."He added, "We are in a super-challenge, not a challenge. America didn't think we would stand firm despite the pressure and war, but we stood firm, and we will continue to stand firm."Also read: Oil prices jump over 2% as Iran-US tensions deepen and crude inventories fallIran’s representative to the United Nations also alleged, as cited by the SNN, that "Starlink has been used to identify and target in military attacks against Iran...The country's space and scientific infrastructure has been targeted in attacks."The New York Times report said Washington was seeking to use the prospect of renewed military action as leverage in negotiations over Iran’s nuclear programme and control over the Strait of Hormuz. However, Iranian negotiators have resisted making concessions on the nuclear issue, insisting that the matter be deferred until later in the talks.As military preparations and diplomatic efforts continue, the possibility of renewed strikes has raised concerns about a wider regional conflict, with uncertainty persisting over Trump’s final decision and Iran’s potential response.

title: Soviet space dogs Veterok and Ugolyok spent 22 days in orbit in 1966, revealing the effects of prolonged spaceflight
description: Soviet dogs Veterok and Ugolyok spent 22 days in orbit in 1966, helping researchers examine how prolonged spaceflight affected living animals.
content: Veterok and Ugolyok were launched aboard the Soviet Cosmos 110 spacecraft on February 22, 1966, and returned safely to Earth on March 16, after 22 days in orbit. The mission examined the effects of prolonged spaceflight, including exposure to radiation from the Van Allen belts. Scientists tracked the dogs’ vital functions, recorded their radiation exposure, and assessed their physical condition after landing.The objectives and findings of the mission are documented in NASA’s historical publication Astronautics and Aeronautics, 1966. The records describe the flight and the medical observations made during and after the mission. The findings also showed why researchers needed to examine the animals after their return, rather than treating survival alone as an indication of the mission’s success.Long trip through Earth’s radiation beltsThe Soviet Union launched Cosmos 110 on February 22, 1966, with Veterok and Ugolyok aboard. The spacecraft returned on March 16, completing 330 orbits around Earth during its 22-day mission. On each orbit, the spacecraft passed through the Van Allen radiation belts, regions above Earth where charged particles are trapped by the planet’s magnetic field.Radiation exposure was another focus of the experiment. NASA’s historical account records that Cosmos 110 carried 300 thermoluminescent dosimeters to measure radiation doses in relation to spacecraft shielding, along with 10 sets of nuclear emulsions to help determine the composition of the radiation encountered. This equipment allowed researchers to collect data on the radiation environment during the flight.The spacecraft also carried equipment to monitor the dogs’ health. Electronic sensors continuously recorded blood pressure, pulse, and respiration, allowing researchers to observe physiological changes during the mission. One dog underwent tests to assess cardiovascular responses, while the other served as a control for comparison. Both were secured in harnesses, and a pneumatic device delivered food paste directly into their stomachs.The dogs experienced difficulties coordinating their movements during the initial stages of weightlessness. Head rocking was observed, indicating changes in their motor coordination. The physiological monitoring also allowed researchers to track cardiovascular responses during the flight. These observations showed that the effects of spaceflight could extend beyond the immediate challenges of adapting to weightlessness and could be assessed through changes in the animals’ physical condition. Results of the medical examinationsAfter the spacecraft returned to Earth, researchers examined Veterok and Ugolyok to assess the effects of their extended time in orbit. The findings recorded in NASA’s Astronautics and Aeronautics, 1966, including its May 16 entry, noted elevated pulse rates and dehydration. The examinations also identified changes in the dogs’ skeletal systems, including calcium loss.NASA’s historical account, A New Beginning, reports that the dogs’ motor systems took eight to 10 days to return to normal after the mission. Their recovery illustrated the difficulties of readjusting to Earth’s gravity after an extended period in space. The observations also showed that some effects of spaceflight persisted after the spacecraft had landed.The historical record further notes that Soviet doctors observed an increase in the red blood cell sedimentation rate and white blood cell counts on the fourth or fifth day after the dogs’ return. The report associated these changes with the animals’ readjustment to normal gravity. These post-flight findings provided additional information about how the body responded after an extended mission.Together, the radiation measurements, continuous physiological monitoring, and post-flight medical examinations gave researchers a more detailed picture of the effects of prolonged spaceflight. The different stages of observation helped scientists identify changes that could not have been assessed through the successful recovery of the animals alone.Veterok and Ugolyok’s 22-day mission allowed researchers to document physical effects associated with prolonged spaceflight, including changes in motor coordination and physiological responses. The findings, preserved in NASA’s historical records, contributed to scientific investigations into the challenges of keeping living organisms in space for extended periods.

title: Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general seeking a seat in the US Senate
description: Texas attorney general Ken Paxton is set to face Democrat James Talarico in the 2026 US Senate race.
content: Warren Kenneth Paxton Jr. is currently representing the Republican Party in the 2026 US Senate race in Texas, where he will be competing against Democratic nominee James Talarico. With President Donald Trump backing Paxton, Republicans seek to retain the Senate seat in Texas. Having served as an attorney general, he has emerged as a prominent person in Texas politics.Paxton began his political career in the Texas House of Representatives where he represented parts of Collin County. He was then elected to the Texas Senate in 2012 where he represented District 8. Paxton then took office as Texas attorney general and became the 51st person to hold this position.Early life, education and familyBorn in December 1962 in Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota, Paxton's father worked for the United States Air Force. He later attended Baylor University, where he earned a bachelor’s degree in psychology in 1985 and an MBA in 1986. Paxton also served as Baylor’s student body president. He went on to earn his law degree from the University of Virginia School of Law in 1991. Paxton is married to Angela Paxton, who he met in Baylor University as a student. Angela is a member of the Texas State Senate. After 38 years of marriage, she filed for a divorce alleging adultery. However, she continues to support his political campaigns. Paxton, 63, is a father to four children named Tucker, Abby, Mattie and Katie. He also has five grandchildren.Policies and initiatives by PaxtonKen Paxton strongly opposes his opponent James Talarico who he calls as “the most radical candidate in Texas history”. He continues to claim that Democrats have made Texas their “top target”. Describing himself as a “fearless conservative”, he made election integrity his major focus. He defended the voter-roll verification system for Texas including the use of the federal Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) database to verify voter eligibility.Paxton also launched an investigation to determine whether doctors or vaccine makers received financial benefits for recommending vaccines for children. His office sent requests for information to more than 20 healthcare providers, insurers and pharmaceutical companies, including UnitedHealthcare and Pfizer. Paxton also took legal actions against COVID-19 vaccine mandates. His office represented Texas Governor Greg Abbott in a case challenging the Joe Biden administration’s vaccine mandate for Texas National Guard members. A federal appeals court ruled in favor of Texas, saying that the federal government could not punish non-federalized Guard members for refusing the mandate.His office also focused on combating human trafficking. Through thorough investigations and legal actions. Paxton’s attorney general website claims that the Human Trafficking and Transnational/Organized Crime division of his office works with prosecutors, supports the victims and provides them training. His office has also filed lawsuits against hotel companies for charging hidden fees and showing misleading prices.Also Read | US passport records in voter verification? Trump administration pushes new election data planKen Paxton: Immigration, jobs, trade and tariffsImmigration and border security have been integral parts of Ken Paxton’s policies. In the past, he has challenged federal immigration policies and advocated for a larger role of Texas when it comes to border enforcement. His office also defended the Senate Bill 4 which aims to protect the citizens of Texas by tracking and punishing federal immigration crimes. He also supported the construction of the US-Mexico border wall.Paxton keeps reinforcing his promise of reducing taxes, cutting regulations and keeps encouraging Americans to manufacture more. His campaign promises to create more American jobs and expand domestic energy production. His “Protecting the Texas Promise” plan also proposes tax deductions for healthcare expenses and home purchases, as well as an increased child tax credit. He also promised to restrain government spendings.Paxton aligns himself with President Donald Trump’s “America First” legislation that prioritizes American workers and businesses. However, tariffs have not been a major part of his campaign platform. He said tariffs were not the main issue affecting his campaign and instead pointed to the Iran war, gas prices and diesel costs as greater concerns.Paxton’s stance on Iran war and artificial intelligencePaxton faced criticism over his stance on the US-Iran war after a leaked audio from a private meeting showed him saying the war was hurting Republicans in the midterm elections. He also said that decisions made in Washington were outside his control, despite his close association with President Donald Trump. He also acknowledged in the audio that he cannot control or stop the war saying “I don’t make decisions”. Publicly, he has defended President Trump’s military action against Iran, saying he believed Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon.Paxton has also raised concerns about Chinese AI companies and data security. In 2025, his office launched an investigation on DeepSeek over its privacy practices and possible violations of Texas privacy law. His office also banned DeepSeek from devices used by its employees and sought information about the app from Google and Apple. Paxton said the investigation was aimed at protecting the personal data of citizens of Texas from potential risks linked to the Chinese AI company.Also Read | Trump’s RNC convention speech beaten by Jimmy Kimmel’s James Talarico interview in views; check numbersKen Paxton's controversiesPaxton faced criticism due to his enforcement of abortion laws in Texas that ban nearly all abortions except when the mother has a serious medical emergency that risks her life or could severely damage her body. In September 2026, the family of Tierra Walker, a Texas woman who died in 2024 due to complications during pregnancy, sued Paxton and other officials, alleging that abortion restrictions in Texas contributed to her death. The lawsuit claims Walker was denied an abortion despite serious health complications.In 2015, a Texas grand jury accused Paxton of felony securities fraud charges. He resolved the case in 2024 through a pretrial agreement that required him to perform community service, complete ethics classes and pay about $300,000 in restitution. He did not admit guilt. In 2023, the Texas House impeached Paxton due to allegations including bribery, abuse of office and misuse of public resources. The Texas Senate acquitted him of the charges in September 2023, allowing him to remain in office. He was also accused of using his office to benefit real estate developer Nate Paul, leading to an FBI investigation. Additionally, he has also faced criticism due to his alleged extramarital affair that led to his divorce in 2025.Also Read | Why is Trump returning to Texas? Paxton Senate race becomes key 2026 midterm testNet worth and what lies aheadAccording to Forbes, Ken Paxton’s net worth is estimated at around $13 million. As per Federal Election Commission data, Ken Paxton’s campaign raised about $9.25 million between April 1 and June 30, 2026. Individual donors accounted for about $9.02 million of the total.
