His campaign reported about $7.49 million in spending and $1.76 million in cash on hand at the end of the reporting period. With years of experience in the state politics of Texas, Paxton is set to face his Democratic opponent James Talarico for the US Senate seat.-By Tanisha Sharma

title: Bacteria that causes deadly Legionnaires’ disease discovered at LA Medical Examiner’s Office, employee tests positive
description: The bacteria, Legionella, was detected in a cooling system at the office near downtown Los Angeles.
content: The airborne bacteria that causes deadly Legionnaires’ disease was discovered at the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office. An employee has tested positive for the disease.NBC 4 reported that the bacteria, Legionella, was detected in a cooling system at the office near downtown Los Angeles. The identity of the worker who tested positive has not been revealed. The person’s condition also remains unknown.Officials have yet to publicly establish whether the employee’s infection was connected to the contaminated system.“The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health was notified of one Los Angeles County employee who tested positive for Legionnaire’s Disease,” a department spokesperson told NBC.Also Read | What is cyclosporiasis? Parasite behind severe diarrhea outbreak across US states; symptoms and causes explainedThe discovery was made in May 2026. At the time, the bacteria was found during maintenance work. Officials said that employees in the affected buildings were notified later in the year. The county has not reported any other infections involving people with shared exposure to the employee.“To date, no additional cases have been identified with shared common exposures to this individual,” officials said.County health officials have described the bacteria as “commonly found in building plumbing systems, especially in older buildings.” County officials stressed that healthcare providers must report “symptomatic cases.” They have also asked public health authorities to monitor high risk settings.What is Legionnaires’ disease?Legionnaires’ disease is a serious form of pneumonia. It is caused by the Legionella bacteria, and individuals can get infected by breathing in contaminated water droplets or mist, which can originate in cooling equipment and building plumbing systems.According to the Cleveland Clinic, “Symptoms include high fever, cough, diarrhea and confusion. You can get Legionnaires’ disease from water or cooling systems in large buildings, like hospitals or hotels. Legionnaires’ disease can be life-threatening.”Also Read | What is Vibrio vulnificus? 6 die in Louisiana from eating oysters contaminated with flesh-eating bacteria“Legionnaire’s disease is uncommon. Around 10,000 people in the U.S. are diagnosed with it every year,” it adds.The CDC says about reporting cases, “If someone is diagnosed with Legionnaires' disease, the healthcare provider or lab that did the testing will report the case to the local or state health department. People can also report their case by contacting the health department of the state where they believe they were exposed. The health department will determine if an investigation is needed.

title: Researchers tested a two-stage process to turn dog feces into hydrogen and methane, but found single-stage processing more economical
description: Researchers tested ways to recover energy from dog waste, finding that methane offered most of the energy and simpler processing had economic advantages.
content: Dog droppings are a common urban waste problem, and disposing of them can create challenges for owners and municipal cleaning agencies. Scientists are studying whether this waste can be used to recover energy rather than simply discarded. One such study by Karla Cruz-Torres, Martín Barragán-Trinidad, and Dulce María Arias-Lizárraga, published in the Biochemical Engineering Journal on Feb. 1, 2026, examined whether dog feces could be used to produce hydrogen and methane through biological waste processing.The team conducted experiments comparing single-stage and two-stage processing technologies using wet dog feces, both with and without acid pretreatment. The researchers investigated whether producing two fuels from one waste stream would deliver enough additional energy to justify the extra costs. Their results showed that although the two-stage process could generate both fuels, single-stage processing of untreated wet feces offered the best balance between energy recovery and cost among the methods tested.How the two-stage process worksTo produce biofuels, the researchers used anaerobic digestion, a biological process in which microorganisms break down organic material without oxygen. The process releases biogas containing methane and carbon dioxide and can be used to recover energy from organic waste. In the two-stage system, the first stage, called acidogenesis, involves the breakdown of organic matter and the production of hydrogen. The remaining organic material then undergoes anaerobic digestion in the second stage, producing methane.This arrangement allows researchers to investigate whether two fuels can be recovered from a single waste stream. However, an additional treatment stage also brings extra operating demands that can affect the system's overall efficiency and cost. Comparing the two-stage setup with a simpler digestion process helped the researchers assess whether the additional steps offered an economic advantage.The team also tested dilute-acid pretreatment, which changes organic material before biological processing. Although pretreatment improved energy recovery in the two-stage system, it did not reduce the cost of producing methane. This distinction matters because an increase in energy output does not necessarily translate into a cheaper or more practical process.The study's techno-economic analysis indicated that the two-stage process did not provide the best economic balance. The authors found that single-stage anaerobic digestion using fresh, untreated wet dog feces was the most economical option among the methods tested under the experimental conditions. Why methane mattersThe results indicated that methane accounted for more than 85% of the energy recovered in the scenarios analyzed by the researchers. Hydrogen contributed only a small share, making its recovery economically inefficient when the additional processing costs were considered. The findings suggest that producing more types of fuel does not automatically make a system more cost-effective.Energy used to control temperature and mix the material was another important consideration. These operations help maintain biological activity, but they also consume energy and increase operating costs. A fuel-producing process must therefore be evaluated against the resources it uses, rather than by measuring fuel output alone.The authors suggested that low biogas yields may have been linked to insufficient acclimatization of the microbial inoculum, the community of microorganisms used to initiate digestion. If these organisms are not adequately adapted to the feedstock, gas production may be limited. This possibility also leaves room for further investigation: the economic ranking reflects the conditions tested and does not establish that single-stage digestion will always outperform a two-stage system under different operating conditions. Research into microbial adaptation and process stability could help determine whether yields can be improved and how that might affect the cost comparison.The experiments evaluated controlled processing systems rather than a ready-to-use domestic technology. Any future application would need to account for collection, handling, treatment, equipment, energy use, and operating costs.The authors recommended a life cycle analysis to assess the process's environmental effects, including resource consumption and the impacts associated with recovering energy from dog waste. Such an assessment could help determine whether the potential benefits outweigh the environmental costs. For now, the study suggests that dog feces can serve as a feedstock for bioenergy, while single-stage digestion appears more economical under the conditions examined.

title: In 2021, NASA sent microscopic tardigrades into orbit to examine their responses to spaceflight across generations
description: NASA’s Cell Science-04 experiment sent tardigrades to the space station to investigate the genes behind their survival in stressful space conditions.
content: A minute creature that is capable of forming a tight ball in difficult conditions has been chosen as an object of study to understand how living creatures cope with space. Tardigrades, whose name means “slow walkers” and which are also called “water bears” owing to their appearance under a microscope, are small invertebrate animals famous for their ability to withstand various forms of stress, including desiccation and freezing. The tardigrades were transported to the International Space Station by SpaceX’s 22nd commercial resupply mission on June 3, 2021.NASA’s mission report described this experiment as one of a series of scientific investigations carried out in the orbiting laboratory. Known as Cell Science-04, the study examined how tardigrades respond to stress factors in outer space, as well as changes in genetic activity across several generations.Why did NASA use microscopic water bears?This experiment aimed to answer a broader question: How do organisms react when changes in their habitat affect their cells? It is not easy to replicate these conditions in laboratories on Earth. By using a small organism that has already demonstrated its resistance to stress, scientists can study the mechanisms behind that resilience. NASA’s Cell Science-04 research overview identifies the experiment’s central objectives as characterizing short-term and multigenerational survival and identifying genes involved in adaptation to stressful environments. The investigation used Hypsibius exemplaris, a tardigrade species suited to laboratory research. Scientists planned to examine how its gene expression changed after exposure to spaceflight conditions and compare those changes with results from control samples maintained on Earth.Gene expression is the process by which cells use information encoded in genes to make molecules necessary for their activities. Variations in gene expression can provide information about an organism’s response to stress. Researchers also planned to apply RNA interference, a process used to inhibit specific genes, to determine whether candidate genes played a role in the tardigrades’ stress tolerance.Researchers compared the animals’ initial reactions with those observed after extended periods in space. In a NASA podcast interview, principal investigator Thomas Boothby explained that the team intended to study the first generation after about a week and another generation that had been maintained in space for roughly two months, representing approximately four generations. What can scientists learn from the experiment?An organism’s immediate response to spaceflight may differ from changes that develop over time. Studying successive generations allows scientists to investigate these differences. However, changes observed across generations do not, by themselves, prove that a trait is hereditary or that later generations adapt better.NASA also explained the potential relevance of this research to astronaut health in its article on microscopic organisms and spaceflight. Studying how tardigrades protect themselves from harsh conditions could help researchers identify biological mechanisms worth investigating for the protection of astronauts during extended space missions. The research, however, did not establish that these mechanisms could directly protect humans.The potential applications remain research objectives, not proven medical benefits. Tardigrades and humans differ substantially in their biology, so a mechanism that helps a microscopic animal cope with stress cannot automatically be applied to astronauts. Researchers would need to establish which processes matter, determine whether similar mechanisms operate in humans, and test any proposed protective measures.For NASA, the experiment formed part of a broader effort to understand how space conditions affect living systems at the cellular and molecular levels. That knowledge could inform future research as space agencies plan missions that keep crews away from Earth for longer periods. Understanding biological responses to microgravity and other spaceflight stresses is one step toward identifying risks and investigating ways to reduce them.The tardigrades taken to the space station were not simply organisms accompanying a cargo delivery. They allowed scientists to study changes in gene expression in response to the stresses of spaceflight and examine how those responses might differ across generations. Cell Science-04 was designed to improve understanding of tardigrades’ biological processes in space. Whether the findings can eventually help researchers develop ways to protect astronauts remains an open question.

title: ‘Look at the person, not the party’: Tony Kozycki, Georgia Democrat running for Congress, to voters
description: In an exclusive interview with HT.com, Democrat Tony Kozycki discusses the case that pushed him into politics, his views on the Iran war and more.
content: Tony Kozycki, a Democrat running for Congress in Georgia’s 7th District in the upcoming November midterms, has a simple message for voters: look at the person, not the party. The combat veteran and immigration lawyer is challenging Republican Rich McCormick. In an exclusive interview with HT.com, he spoke about his rival, the Iran war, politics and his life at home.Speaking about his message to voters, Kozycki said, “Look who they are. Look what they’re telling you and actually vote on people and not party right now.”How Kozycki’s family shaped his path to politicsKozycki said he was not ready for this. “Honestly, I think if I didn’t get involved in Godfrey’s case, I’d be coaching my son’s baseball team right now,” he said. He had even paused a public leadership course at the Harvard Kennedy School to run.He said his story starts with his mother. According to Kozycki, she was a Puerto Rican girl who grew up in inner-city New York at a time of bias and racism. She later joined the US Army. He said she was one of the first women to lead troops on the demilitarized zone in Korea.After leaving the Army, she went to law school while he was in elementary school. Those years were hard, according to Kozycki, and the family needed government help.The family then moved to LaGrange, a small town in Georgia, where his mother became a public defender. Kozycki said she defended people who could not afford a lawyer. “When we walked into the grocery store and you saw the folks behind the counter know who mom was, it meant so much,” he said.Kozycki said his mother encouraged him to join the military. He went to the US Naval Academy and served in the military. After that, he went to law school and started a small law firm in Atlanta with his mother and his wife, who are both attorneys. Their firm does a lot of immigration work. He is also a father of two, aged 9 and 12.Also read: John Hauer agrees with Trump on this hot-button issue as Kansas Libertarian gears up for midterm Congress raceThe case that pushed himKozycki said the turning point was the case of Godfrey Wade, a fellow veteran. According to reports, Wade is a US Army veteran who was deported to Jamaica in February over a bounced cheque from almost 20 years ago, while his appeal was still going onKozycki said he reached out to his own congressman, expecting help. “I thought, yeah, we’re all military veterans. Let’s fix this,” he said.That did not happen. “At the very least, I expected him to try or at least pretend to care,” he said. According to Kozycki, he kept speaking to the office week after week and month after month, and they kept saying they were not interested.He said the frustration became too much. He started talking to his wife about needing “somebody different”. Then he asked himself a question. “If I don’t want to do it myself, then why would anybody do it?” he said. And then, he and his wife decided they needed to do this work “on a bigger scale”.Also read: Indiana candidate Jaime West admits to drinking before viral rant against MAGA: ‘I had 3 beers’What he says about his opponent Rich McCormickKozycki said McCormick does not know the people of the district. “The guy that I’m challenging, Rich McCormick, he doesn’t represent this district,” he said.According to Kozycki, McCormick talks mostly about border security, as if Kozycki wants open borders. Kozycki said that is not true. “I think we need secure borders,” he said. He also said dangerous criminals who are not citizens should be removed if the law requires it.But Kozycki said McCormick misses one point: the law also says people must get a fair hearing. He said someone like Godfrey Wade is entitled to “due process” and “the rule of law”.Kozycki also said McCormick has no real answers for voters. According to him, McCormick’s only reply is to call him a communist. “He just wants to scare you into thinking that I’m a communist,” Kozycki said. He pointed to his own record in reply. “I fought in three wars for this country. I’m a small business owner,” he said.Kozycki also said big tech is funding McCormick’s campaign, so McCormick does not listen to people on data centers. As per him, the community is not against data centers, it only wants a fair deal.Kozycki also said, “Rich McCormick has had serious character flaws". He alleged that McCormick has had affairs and “has gone through several wives”. He also said McCormick is tied closely to Donald Trump and Stephen Miller, and that Miller’s idea of how an American should look is “a white nationalist idea”.HT.com could not independently verify these claims.What Kozycki says about the poll numbersAccording to Kozycki, his campaign’s poll shows McCormick at 46 per cent and him at 43 per cent.Kozycki said the numbers give him hope. “If we can get our message in front of voters, I think that’s what it shows. We can win this race,” he said. He said the seat was not seen as close a year ago.He also said McCormick is taking voters for granted. “McCormick isn’t even campaigning. He’s saying he’s going to beat me by double digits,” he said. According to Kozycki, a leader has to come back every two years and earn the vote.Then he made a prediction. “And I think it’s going to be a big shock to Rich McCormick on November 4th when he lost his job,” he said.Kozycki's views on the Iran warKozycki said the Iran war is costly, but money is not his main worry. “It’s not dollars and cents. It’s American lives that are going to be at risk,” he said.According to Kozycki, McCormick wants a ground invasion. He said this would cost “another trillion dollars at a minimum because that’s what a forever war would look like.”He said the war feels personal. He spent his young adult life in a war in the Middle East. “I watched my daughter’s first steps while I sat on a Zoom call in the desert. I missed her first Christmas,” he said.“We can’t throw them into a war without a plan, without objectives, and without an exit strategy,” he said.Instead of a ground invasion, Kozycki said the US should go back to its allies. “America’s greatest strength is the alliances that we’ve built,” he said. He named India and NATO as good partners.

title: Most businesses worry about SIM fraud, don’t think SIM binding will stop it: Survey
description: The SIM-binding directive, which will come into effect from January 1, requires messaging accounts to be linked to physical SIM cards for traceability
content: Nearly nine in 10 small businesses are worried about fraud linked to SIM cards, but most of them do not believe that tying messaging apps to SIM cards will make platforms safer, according to a survey of over 350 small firms by tech policy think tank Esya Centre.The survey covered 353 businesses across 17 cities, most of them small firms. About 87.2% said they were concerned about SIM-related fraud, while 81% said SIM binding did not offer security benefits. Separately, in a survey of 2,033 consumers across 18 cities, 59.2% said SIM binding would not make messaging platforms safer.Both surveys were done between February and April 2026.The survey report comes two months before the December 31 deadline for apps such as WhatsApp and Telegram to follow SIM binding rules notified by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) ends. The initial deadline for SIM binding was February-end 2026. As first reported by HT on March 30, it was extended till December 31, 2026, following requests from companies.The SIM-binding directive, which will come into effect from January 1, requires messaging accounts to be linked to physical SIM cards for traceability and mandates that web sessions be logged out at least once every six hours.The Esya Centre report argued that much of the online fraud happens through phishing, stolen passwords, malware and hijacked sessions, something SIM binding does not directly address.It also cited a study by the Indian School of Business, which found that telecom companies often don’t verify details given by SIM buyers against government databases such as Aadhaar, and that agents sometimes skip identity checks while issuing SIM cards. The report said fixing these gaps could do more to reduce fraud.The survey report also voiced operational concerns. Of the businesses surveyed, 83.5% said delays and mistakes would become likely, and about 41% of consumers said they would consider buying an extra SIM card. These figures are what people expect to happen, not what has already happened.SIM-binding directionsThe guidelines on SIM binding were issued under the Telecom Cyber Security Rules in November 2025 and sent to companies providing app-based communication services in India, including WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Arattai, Snapchat, Sharechat, Jiochat and Josh.DoT has said some of these apps let people use the service even when the SIM card linked to their mobile number was not in the phone, and that this was being misused to commit cyber frauds by entities located abroad. Under the directions, the apps have to make sure that the SIM card was in the device and connected with the mobile number used to identify the user. The app should not work without that specific and active SIM.If the app has a web version, the user should be logged out regularly, no later than every six hours, and should be allowed to link the device again by scanning a QR code.The directive faced pushback from the industry, with several messaging platforms raising concerns about how practical it was to implement it and what it would mean for user experience. Companies said that enforcing continuous SIM binding, especially across multiple devices and web logins, would need significant changes to how their apps are built, along with coordination with operating system providers.

title: Apple iPhone Duo goes on sale in India at ₹2.99 lakh, buyers throng stores on launch day
description: The iPhone Duo has gone on sale in several markets, including India, drawing interest from Apple customers, resellers and early adopters.
content: Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, went on sale in India on Friday, drawing customers to physical stores to experience and buy the new device on launch day. Priced at over ₹2,99,900, the phone has seen strong demand, with limited pre-order supplies and long delivery timelines pushing more buyers towards Apple stores, including its outlet in Saket, Delhi. Giving his first impression of the iPhone Duo, a customer, Rahul, says, “It is an amazing phone. Its best feature is multitasking. I have bought the 512 GB version of the phone for around ₹3.24 lakhs.”With launch-day supplies expected to be limited, buyers without pre-orders are hoping to get their hands on the device at their nearest store.Also read: Apple iPhone Duo review: Boldest iPhone since the iPhone X, with a dash of funLimited supplies bring back Apple store queuesEven in United States, at Apple’s flagship store on Fifth Avenue in New York City, dozens of customers without pre-orders had gathered by Thursday evening. Similar queues were reported in parts of Asia and Australia, according to news agency Bloomberg.Apple has set aside a limited number of devices for customers who want to buy the phone in person. However, those hoping to take one home on launch day face uncertainty because pre-orders have already placed significant pressure on available stocks.The launch has attracted attention because of the Duo’s high price. Depending on the configuration, the phone costs as much as ₹4,49,900 for the version with 2 terabytes of storage. Despite the premium pricing, early adopters, resellers and regular Apple customers have shown considerable interest in the device.Also read: Apple's iPhone Duo goes on pre-order in India today: Check price, offers, top featuresA major design shift for the iPhoneApple is not the first company to introduce a foldable smartphone, however, the design is still attracting buyers with a refined device designed for its existing customer base.The launch comes as other smartphone makers, including Samsung Electronics, have also increased prices. Higher costs for memory chips and other components have added to the expense of consumer electronics, making premium devices even more costly.Also read: iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, and Apple Watch 12: Apple’s John Ternus era beginsDelivery delays highlight production challengesCustomers placing fresh orders through Apple’s website, the delivery is expected during the second half of January. Some people who ordered earlier, however, have received revised estimates indicating that their phones could arrive in November or December.Also read: Apple's iPhone 16 gets a major discount at Amazon Great Indian Festival: Check price, discount offersThe lengthy waiting period reflects the manufacturing challenges. The device uses an advanced hinge mechanism and new display technology. Production is also concentrated in a limited number of facilities in China.(With inputs from Bloomberg and ANI)

title: The internet is under attack, and we have very few answers
description: A surge in cyberattacks on banks and millions of websites, leaves us with more questions than answers as October poses a stark test for general preparedness from AI-powered cyber threats
content: Something quite unprecedented is unfolding on the internet. It affects almost everyone who uses the internet, has online banking accounts, has ever made a digital payment on any website, has a smart home system, uses cloud storage, or does online shopping. That essentially means everyone.A lot continues to unfold. In just the last few days, India’s largest bank, the State Bank of India (SBI) warned that almost 4,000 customer records were leaked to the dark web. Microsoft warned that a Chinese group called Storm-0940 is using artificial intelligence (AI) penetration to automate attacks targeting hundreds of organisations globally using a cloud backup service called ConnectWise.There is a race to patch PHP, or Hypertext Processor, an open-source programming code used by millions of websites globally. Hackers have used AI agents to drive a cyberattack on 16 banks and investment companies in Korea. US banks including JPMorgan, Bank of America and Wells Fargo sounded the alarm earlier today that AI agents are now operating inside customer banking accounts as they scramble to block their actions (they fear unauthorized money movement).No wonder cybersecurity experts are dubbing this ‘Black October,’ following warnings that AI-driven cyberattacks were imminent. Former OpenAI researcher Joshua Achiam sounded the alarm over the wave of various cybersecurity incidents earlier this week in a post on X. “Feels like March 1, 2020 for Cyber. Not normal, something is happening. Internet lockdowns in a couple of months?” he wrote on October 21. That may seem far-fetched for now, but the scale and diversity of cyberattacks is worrying.The latest concern focuses on the PHP vulnerability called PHP2Shell, which would allow hackers to steal sensitive data or take control of unpatched servers. The interesting thing is that the vulnerability was revealed on social media on Wednesday, before the patch was readily available for every developer and IT department to install. Repercussions have been immense. Many websites were taken offline as a precautionary measurePHP has been around since the 1990s, helping to build websites, and is still widely used today to work behind the scenes to collect information and generate content that is seen on web pages. At this stage, it is difficult to gauge the scale of patching by websites, till official confirmations come through.Matthew Prince, Co-founder & CEO of Cloudflare, says the PHP2Shell exploit was drawing attention from hackers almost immediately. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the Cloudflare network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post-announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now,” he says, in a statement.Industry-wide collaborations and an inflection pointAI company OpenAI had worked with maintainers, researchers, and security providers to address critical vulnerabilities in PHP, using the GPT-5.6 Sol model as part of the Patch the Planet initiative. Of course, they’re expected to push a case for their AI models as cybersecurity tools.“Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory. It highlights how AI can uncover security flaws with internet-scale impact, but the same capabilities can also help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits,” they say.Wiz Research, a cybersecurity firm explains that their own autonomous AI agent called Atlas alongside Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, was used for the vulnerability search. They say AI helps adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts. “This significantly lowers the barrier to scaling attacks across different deployments,” the company says in its research.“Using Gemini 4 Argon, the team at Wiz has shown why frontier AI is a game-changer for cyber defense. For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex. We’re pleased to see Gemini 4 Argon help defenders bridge that gap, finding vulnerabilities and helping patch them,” says Raluca Ada Popa, Head of Gemini Security, Google DeepMindThe timing is where things get interesting. Amazon Threat Intelligence identified a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt dating to Oct. 17 in their telemetry, four days before the public disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 vulnerabilities.“The exploit attempt originated from an IP address associated with a commercial anonymization network. While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure,” says CJ Moses, CISO of Amazon Integrated Security.A smart home conundrumIf you think cybersecurity vulnerabilities such as PHP2Shell are a headache for IT admins in organisations and businesses, you’d be wrong. For consumers, their photos, music, data backups, online games, network-attached storage and all smart home accessories can potentially be at risk.“The vulnerability allows an attacker to steal authentication tokens from server memory. These tokens essentially act like electronic passes, telling a website that the user has already signed in. As a result, an attacker may be able to access someone else’s account without entering a password or a two-factor authentication code, putting messages, documents, delivery addresses, order histories and other confidential information at risk,” explains cybersecurity firm Kaspersky.Home cloud storage devices such as consumer NAS or network-attached storage services have become popular in recent years. They are vulnerable, which means your login credentials and the data in those accounts, is to. Popular NAS makers including Synology have confirmed these vulnerabilities impact their products such as Mail Station and Synology Calendar. They have released fixes for all affected products.The overall patch landscape for smart home devices such as smart TVs, appliances, gaming services and other devices remains unclear.Here’s what you can doFor most consumers, this may be a revision in the practice of keeping the software and firmware on their devices updated to the latest versions released by manufacturers. Kaspersky researchers say most people reuse the same password, or variations of it, across multiple websites. If an attacker finds one of those passwords on a vulnerable server, they may be able to compromise your other accounts as wellIt is important to stay away from websites that a consumer isn’t familiar with, and stick to regularly used and trusted ones—particularly if it involves signing in with your Google account or Apple iCloud credentials, or making a transaction using a credit card or bank account.This is particularly relevant for online banking websites and apps—if a financial services platform’s data is leaked as part of the ongoing vulnerability, hackers may try to communicate with an account holder in what may seem to be genuine-looking emails or messages to elicit more information—such as bank account credentials or credit card specifics.Last but not least, setting up two-factor authentication (2FA) will go some way in mitigating attempts to gain unauthorised access to your online accounts if credentials do get accessed by hackers as part of their data haul from any website.

title: Swiggy shares hit record low as wider Instamart losses fuel profitability concerns
description: Swiggy's stock was down 6.20% at 198.30 rupees in early trade, set for its worst day on record, if the current momentum persists.
content: Shares of Swiggy fell to a record low on Friday after the Instamart operator posted wider losses in its quick-commerce business, keeping the focus on profitability in the competitive segment following rival Eternal's results this week.Swiggy's stock was down 6.20% at 198.30 rupees in early trade, set for its worst day on record, if the current momentum persists.Also Read | Sensex 400+ points higher after 3 straight loss sessions; eMudhra among stocks in focusEternal and Swiggy have been rapidly expanding their networks of small warehouses, known as dark stores, as the segment has emerged as a key growth driver for both companies even as spending on expansion and competition have put profitability in focus.Instamart's adjusted core loss widened to 8.95 billion rupees in the second quarter from 8.49 billion rupees a year earlier.Jefferies said Instamart's losses are a key concern for investors, adding that the current price does not fully reflect the value of Swiggy's food-delivery business and cash holdings.The brokerage maintained its "buy" rating but reduced its target price to 330 rupees from 435 rupees.Also Read | Jio Platforms IPO fully subscribed in 100 minutes of openingEmkay said sustained double-digit sequential net order value growth in Instamart, along with improving customer retention, monetisation, and store utilisation could help assign a higher valuation for the stock."We see Swiggy as a strong FD (food delivery) franchise with operating leverage and QCom as an optionality," Emkay said.The brokerage maintained its "buy" rating but cut its target price by 11% to 310 rupees.

title: Sensex 400+ points higher after 3 straight loss sessions; eMudhra among stocks in focus
description: Nifty and Sensex have declined about two per cent each so far this week, with sentiment weighed down by a surge in Brent crude oil futures to $113.5 a barrel.
content: Sensex and Nifty opened higher on Friday after three consecutive sessions of losses, although gains were expected to be short-lived amid surging oil prices in the backdrop of escalating tensions in the Middle East.GIFT Nifty futures were trading at 22,830.50 at 7:42 am, signalling a positive opening for the benchmark Nifty 50, which closed at 22,687.65 on Thursday, according to a Reuters report.The Nifty and Sensex have declined about two per cent each so far this week, with sentiment weighed down by a surge in Brent crude oil futures to $113.5 a barrel amid concerns over further energy supply disruptions following Houthi attacks on top oil exporter Saudi Arabia."Recent price action suggests buyers are attempting to defend lower levels, but sellers continue to emerge on rebounds, keeping the market bias cautious," Reuters quoted as saying Hitesh Tailor, technical research analyst at Choice Broking.Asian markets opened lower, dragged down by technology stocks after Wall Street equities fell overnight.The Nasdaq slumped more than 2%, while Meta shares fell nearly 8% after the Facebook parent reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade, driven by expenditure related to artificial intelligence.Foreign portfolio investors were net buyers of Indian stocks on Thursday, with inflows totalling 10.22 billion rupees ($107.79 million). Domestic institutional investors also purchased a net 16.14 billion rupees worth of stocks, according to provisional data from the NSE."Domestically, near-term market direction will depend on quarterly earnings delivery, as investors react to management commentary on demand outlook for coming quarters," said Vinod Nair, head of research at Geojit Investments.Colgate-Palmolive India will be in focus after reporting an increase in quarterly profit, supported by demand for its toothpaste portfolio.Swiggy plans to expand the presence of its quick-commerce business, Instamart, after the company reported a bigger-than-expected loss in the September quarter.Stocks to watcheMudhra: The company exited the website security business after flaws trigger global alarm. Its shares have fallen 36 per cent over two sessions.Hatsun Agro: The company reported a 5.5 per cent year-on-year increase in second-quarter profit to 1.16 billion rupees, while revenue rises about 20 per cent.HPCL: The company reported a nine per cent decline in September-quarter profit, as higher tax expenses and a sharp surge in oil prices squeezed the fuel retailer's margins.(With inputs from Reuters)

title: Sensex falls 460 points, Nifty declines 123 points as Saudi attacks fuel oil price concerns
description: From rising crude oil prices to caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision, here are the key factors behind the stock market decline.
content: Equity benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty declined in intraday trade on Thursday, dragged down by selling in power and metal stocks, a surge in crude oil prices amid escalating tensions in West Asia and caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy decision.The 30-share BSE Sensex fell 460.30 points to settle at 73,249.39. The NSE Nifty 50 dropped 123.70 points to close at 22,687.65.ALSO READ: Indian national among 2 killed in attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Fahd airportEarlier in the session, Sensex fell 523.54 points, or 0.71%, to 73,186.15, while the NSE Nifty 50 declined 181.50 points, or 0.80%, to 22,629.85 around 2 pm. In the morning trade, the Sensex had plunged 678.90 points, or 0.92%, to 73,030.79, while the Nifty dropped 250.90 points, or 1.10%, to 22,568.10.Here are the key factors weighing on the stock markets: 1. Crude oil prices surge amid West Asia tensionsRising crude oil prices remained a major concern for investors, with Brent crude trading above $112 per barrel amid escalating hostilities in West Asia and renewed attacks involving Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia.The latest escalation has heightened concerns over the security of energy infrastructure and potential disruptions to oil supplies. The Houthis have claimed multiple attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s energy and aviation infrastructure, including an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and airports in Riyadh and Dammam.ALSO READ: Apple iPhone Duo review: Boldest iPhone since the iPhone X, with a dash of funThe conflict has also disrupted air travel and prompted security advisories for foreign nationals. Earlier attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport led to flight disruptions, while the US tightened travel restrictions for its government employees in parts of Saudi Arabia amid heightened security concerns.The developments have added to concerns over the wider regional conflict and the risks to energy supplies. For India, which depends heavily on imported crude oil, a sustained rise in prices could increase the import bill, put pressure on the rupee and complicate efforts to contain inflation.2. Mid- and small-cap stocks face a valuation resetThe sell-off extended beyond heavyweight stocks, with mid- and small-cap indices declining more sharply than the benchmark indices, indicating broader weakness across the market.The Nifty 100 declined 1.01%, while the Nifty 200 fell 1.09% and the Nifty 500 dropped 1.12%. Selling pressure was more pronounced in the mid- and small-cap segments, with the Nifty Midcap 50 slipping 1.36%, the Nifty Midcap 100 falling 1.39% and the Nifty Smallcap 100 declining 1.45%.The broader market’s underperformance reflected investors’ cautious stance amid geopolitical uncertainty, elevated oil prices and concerns over valuations.3. Investors cautious ahead of US Fed meetingInvestors remained cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision following its October 27-28 policy meeting. The decision could influence foreign investment flows into Indian markets.If the US Fed keeps interest rates high, investors may prefer to put their money in the US, where they can earn better returns on relatively safer investments. This could lead to more foreign investors selling Indian shares, putting further pressure on the stock market.High US interest rates can also strengthen the dollar against the rupee, making imports such as crude oil more expensive for India. This could add to inflationary pressures.On the other hand, signals of a possible rate cut could encourage investors to put more money into markets such as India.Foreign capital outflows have already crossed ₹3 lakh crore this year, adding to the pressure on domestic equities.4. Rupee weakens against US dollarThe Indian rupee snapped an eight-session-long winning streak and fell 44 paise to close at 94.82 per dollar, reversing some of the optimism generated in the previous session by hopes of a potential India-US trade agreement.Elevated crude oil prices remain a key risk for the domestic currency, as higher oil import bills increase demand for dollars and put pressure on India's external balances.Measures by the Reserve Bank of India to regulate dollar purchases, including dedicated banking arrangements for oil-marketing companies, have offered some support. However, sustained geopolitical tensions and expensive crude could continue to weigh on the rupee and investor sentiment.

title: Apple iPhone Duo review: Boldest iPhone since the iPhone X, with a dash of fun
description: The long wait exemplifies patience as the iPhone Duo comes together, while an obsession with finer details remains quintessentially Apple.
content: Folding and unfolding an iPhone. It has been a considerable wait, and there is inevitably a lot to unpack from this moment. Apple’s decision to bide its time and spend years refining every element of what is now its first foldable iPhone has sent expectations soaring.The iPhone Duo is certainly the boldest iPhone in years. I would place it in the same elite category as the iPhone X, launched in 2017. This is designed to be an aspirational iPhone, one that showcases what Apple is capable of today and offers a glimpse of where it is headed. The evolution of iOS 27 for the inner and outer displays is quite something. Apple has even moved away from the rumoured name, iPhone Ultra, in favour of iPhone Duo.The overall footprint and form factor take some getting used to. You will have to retrain your muscle memory, whether it is the way you pull the phone out of your trouser pocket or the habit of holding it between your ear and shoulder while multitasking. I am referring specifically to its shorter vertical length, a consequence of the passport-style design.You get the typically exquisite craftsmanship expected of an Apple product. There is a titanium frame, Ceramic Shield on the front and back glass panels, and a precision-engineered hinge that holds the phone at virtually any angle at which you unfold it.The hinge is exceptionally smooth. As you begin unfolding the iPhone Duo, there is relatively little resistance, which gradually increases as the main foldable display opens out and becomes flatter. This should help protect the screen during everyday use. And, for once, here is a foldable phone that unfolds completely flat, rather than leaving even a barely perceptible gap. The iPhone Duo is also more pocketable than its form factor might suggest. Apple says the antenna splits are reinforced with ceramic fibre inserts that are three times stronger than the Grade 5 titanium alongside them.When unfolded, all four corners are rounded, creating the visual symmetry Apple appears to be aiming for. When folded, however, the outer display presents two rounded corners on the right and two right-angled corners on the left, where the hinge sits. Samsung takes a different approach, retaining right-angled corners on all four sides, folded or unfolded, on the Galaxy Z Fold8. Two different approaches to the same design challenge.This is a first-generation product, something that is easy to forget given the refinement across the board. That, however, does not excuse the areas where the iPhone Duo warrants closer scrutiny. Last year's iPhone Air, which I had described as a hint of Apple's future playbook, may well have offered the first clues to the foldable. Look at the camera island and the sculpting of the frame, for instance.Fusion of perspectivesSince we are on the subject of the camera island, let us talk about the 48-megapixel Fusion main wide camera and the 48-megapixel Fusion ultra-wide camera.Photography and video recording are excellent, as you would expect from an iPhone. Compared with the Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max, which uses different main and ultra-wide sensors, the iPhone Duo holds its own in daylight, indoors and in low light. That is a testament to Apple's imaging algorithms.I set the camera to capture pixel-binned images at 24 megapixels. These retain more detail than 12-megapixel pixel-binned images, making them better suited to editing.Photographic Styles, now in their third iteration, are fun to experiment with, particularly on the larger 7.6-inch folding display. Smart focus tracking and Dual Preview, which lets subjects see the frame on the outer display, have genuine practical value. I did not need to use Kid Cue, since my child is old enough not to need a visual prompt to hold their attention. For many parents, however, this feature could be invaluable.That said, the telephoto camera, or rather the lack of one, deserves attention. Not everyone needs a telephoto lens or takes pictures that require significant zoom, but optical zoom can be extremely useful for certain photos and videos, as it is on the iPhone 18 Pro Max.The iPhone Duo offers 2x optical zoom through its main Fusion camera. Beyond that, up to 10x, the zoom is digitally enhanced. This can work in some situations, but if photography involving distant subjects is a significant part of your usage, it is a compromise you will have to accept. I hope the next-generation iPhone Duo adds a telephoto camera or replaces the ultra-wide camera with one, if space constraints permit only two rear cameras. The primary sensor also offers three focal-length options: 26mm at 1x, 28mm at 1.1x and 35mm at 1.3x. Tap the 1x toggle to switch between them and experiment with different perspectives.The iPhone Duo has two front-facing FaceTime cameras: one on the outer Super Retina XDR display and another beneath the inner Super Retina XDR display. The outer camera sits within the vertically positioned Dynamic Island. It is a 12-megapixel sensor with Center Stage, which keeps you in the frame during video calls. The camera is positioned towards the top-right corner rather than in the centre.The camera hidden beneath the foldable screen is another story.Neither camera supports Face ID, so the iPhone Duo relies exclusively on Touch ID. The fingerprint sensor is integrated into the power button. After a week of using the phone, I still occasionally find myself staring at the screen, wondering why it is not unlocking, before remembering that I need to use the fingerprint sensor.Hot tip: Disable the Rest Finger to Open setting for faster Touch ID unlocking. It is not as fast as Face ID, but comes close.Two canvases, real symmetryApple's first foldable iPhone follows what is popularly known as the passport-style design. It offers three distinct ways to use the device: the outer display, the inner foldable display in landscape orientation, and a portrait layout reminiscent of the iPad mini.iOS 27 does a considerable amount of work behind the scenes to make the two screens, with their different aspect ratios, work seamlessly as apps switch between them. Apple has repositioned interface elements to make better use of the available screen space and keep controls within easier reach.The dock, for instance, sits vertically on the right, while Control Centre can be accessed from lower down the screen. Users no longer need to stretch their thumbs all the way to the top-right corner.The passport-style design is a key choice. The inner screen's landscape orientation is better suited to watching videos in the 16:9 aspect ratio or thereabouts. It is also wider than the book-style foldables such as the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra and the Vivo X Fold6. This gives apps that run side by side more room to breathe, making split-screen use more practical. The 7.6-inch inner Super Retina XDR display has a resolution of 2670 x 1878 pixels, higher than the Galaxy Z Fold8's 2448 x 1848 pixels. Its nano-texture matte coating serves two purposes: it conceals the crease down the middle more effectively than any foldable display I have used so far, and it gives the screen a paper-like appearance while reducing reflections.Apple has succeeded on both fronts.The crease is virtually invisible under most viewing conditions. You have to look at the screen from an angle, particularly against a dark background, to make it out. On competing foldables, the crease is often much more noticeable.My biggest concern with the nano-texture coating is its long-term durability. How well will it withstand daily use, dust particles and the occasional pressure from a fingernail? The coating will face considerably more wear and tear on an iPhone Duo than it might on an iPad Pro. The silver lining is that the cover layer is replaceable, at a cost of ₹5,900.The 5.4-inch outer Super Retina XDR display has a resolution of 2034 x 1398 pixels, compared with 1972 x 1248 pixels on the Galaxy Z Fold8. It lacks the matte coating but delivers the bright, rich and well-balanced visuals you would expect. It is an inviting introduction to the iPhone Duo before you unfold it and appreciate the larger screen.The squarer outer display is perfectly usable for many apps. However, the keyboard layout and the positioning of certain interface elements will take some getting used to, even if you are switching from another iPhone. At times, the dock and certain app-specific elements on the right can feel as though they occupy too much space. Safari, for instance, could offer a more immersive browsing experience. Mail could benefit from a floating compose button that leaves more room for the inbox. In Messages, opening the keyboard to type a reply leaves you with, at most, a couple of messages visible in the chat history.These are largely matters of adjustment. The outer display is certainly not a compromised half-phone, despite what its dimensions might suggest.The inner display, meanwhile, is fantastic to use. Typing long emails, drafting documents and even working on spreadsheets should be a pleasure.Both screens follow the same broad approach to aspect ratio: shorter and wider. This is why many interface elements that traditionally sit at the top or bottom of the screen have been moved to the sides, freeing up vertical space.The trade-off is that buttons are not always where your fingers expect them to be. You will need to retrain your muscle memory, and a few accidental touches are inevitable along the way. That is part of the learning curve.Performance, battery life and no compromisesThe iPhone Duo shares the Apple A20 Pro chip and 12GB of memory with the iPhone 18 Pro series. The chip also appears to be tuned similarly for the foldable.In synthetic benchmark tests, it significantly outperforms the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in single-core and dual-core performance, as well as graphics. It is encouraging to see Apple maintain parity on this fundamental aspect of performance, especially when Android foldables have often lagged behind their conventional flagship counterparts in either camera capabilities or processing power. As expected, the hardware and iOS 27 are well optimised to work together. Even apps that have not yet been updated for the iPhone Duo scale well, and performance is not a deterrent.The iPhone Duo is an eSIM-only device. If you are moving from a physical SIM on an existing iPhone, you can transfer to an eSIM directly during the data transfer process. Alternatively, you can use the apps of Airtel, Reliance Jio or Vi to generate the required QR code.No operator in India currently supports the iPhone Handoff feature, which allows the same mobile number to work across two iPhones.Battery life will depend on how you use the iPhone Duo, including how much time you spend on the larger inner display versus the outer screen. The number of pixels illuminated, and for how long, naturally affects consumption.During my week of testing, the phone averaged around 6.5 hours of active screen time between a full charge and 30% battery remaining, with heavy usage as my primary phone. The iPhone Duo uses a split-cell battery architecture, with a primary and a secondary cell combining to offer a capacity of almost 5,000mAh. These are encouraging numbers, particularly because most users should find that the phone gets through a day of heavy use with reasonable ease.Choices and directionThe wait for a foldable iPhone is finally over. As a complete package, no other foldable quite matches the iPhone Duo. But this is far from an affordable proposition, bringing us back to the original point: this is an aspirational iPhone. Prices in India start at ₹2,99,900, a figure that is not to be taken lightly.Apple has not simply taken a foldable form factor and installed iOS 27 on it. The company has made a range of software changes, some more visible than others, to make better use of the available display space and improve usability.This is one of those rare reviews in which I am assessing not just the physical product but also the journey that led to this moment, and the direction Apple might take from here.The Apple iPhone Duo is the most fun I have had with a foldable phone so far. Android foldables have often leaned towards a more serious approach, attempting to justify the form factor as a category worth paying a premium for. Apple, by contrast, has embarked on its foldable journey with a bold and playful approach.It is not trying to replace an iPad, nor is it positioning the phone as a substitute for a Mac. That distinction is precisely what makes the iPhone Duo interesting.The phone has its shortcomings, and that is part of the learning curve for a first-generation product. Many third-party apps still need to be optimised for the iPhone Duo's combination of displays and repositioned interface elements. That is typical of a first-generation product. The phone is also expected to support the Apple Pencil with iOS 27.2, anticipated in about a week's time.Ultimately, Apple has made most of the right hardware choices and paired them with software that gives the iPhone Duo a distinct identity. It occupies an interesting space between the iPhone and the iPad mini, offering flexibility without necessarily trying to replicate either device.The question is whether you can find enough practical utility in that combination to justify carrying it in your pocket, especially at this price.

title: Sensex falls over 600 points as Middle East war keeps oil above $110; inflation worries mount
