title: Baffling Tata Play Smart, Vi prepaid family & gauging Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6
description: Beyond the regular noise, a closer look at personal technology. 22 October 2026.
content: Opening thoughts. A few days ago, there was some excitement about a Vi prepaid family plan. This is essentially the first of its kind in India, but it’s a concept familiar to postpaid users who have increasingly bundled multiple connections into a family plan to save some money. That was my expectation when I heard about the Vi prepaid family plan. Alas, as you understand most things, this becomes more an exercise in wondering what really was the need for this prepaid collective? I’ll explain why.Three key elements define the Vi prepaid family plan proposition, which can hold up to four members.First, a member of a prepaid family plan can share data with another member of that group. But this is limited to 500 MB of available data at a time through the Vi App, once a day, up to twice a week and a maximum of four times in a calendar month. The transferred data is valid only for that particular date. While this would be handy to get a UPI payment through if a user is running low on data, I’m not entirely sure how far 500MB gets in this era.Vi says that each member of a prepaid family will be able to get discounts of up to 10% on every recharge. I am not sure how that is quantified—is it on the price of the recharge pack, the duration or some other metric? Vi hasn’t said, and I don’t have the humans required to create a prepaid family pack.Vi also says prepaid family users will get ‘exclusive benefits’, but that also remains unquantified regarding the specifics of what these would be.Basically, this is an attempt by Vi to add stickiness and loyalty to the prepaid connection proposition (loyalty is usually more associated with postpaid users). It may well work out for them if the recharge discounts aspect is well implemented—those discounts will go a long way in adding a proposition of value, and keeping users on the network. What this needs is a lot more. Curated recharge packages that offer better pricing or bundled inclusions would be a start. And logically, how about a prepaid recharge plan that incudes up to four users within the same fold, with the overall data and calling minutes pool shared between them? That will simplify pricing, and convenience.Previously, on Wired Wisdom: Microsoft’s Edge tactics, assessing Samsung Galaxy S26 FE, XECH and Siri AIEDITOR’S MARGIN: TATA PLAY SMART AND AN IPTV QUESTIONI don’t like to encounter otherwise easily avoided complications. Subscriptions, particularly. I’m pretty certain you’d have similar views too. A few days ago, direct-to-home (DTH) company Tata Play launched its Tata Play Smart service which streams Live TV channels on smart TVs via their app (so far, Live TV channels were only on the Tata Play mobile app), without needing a DTH connection or a set-top box (STB). The idea is appreciated because, while they’re technically not terming this as IPTV (or internet protocol television), it’s routed the same way via any broadband connection without restrictions.Tata Play needed this diversification, and the logic is understandable. User preferences are changing to on-demand viewing rather than just linear TV broadcasts, and secondly, viewing across a variety of devices instead of just on a TV via an STB. Though that conventional proposition still remains very relevant for many users, that volume is reducing. The TRAI Pay TV data indicates this trend. DTH had 48.56 million subscribers in India in June this year, down from 49.05 million in March, and a significant reduction from 56.07 million in June last year. Tata Play is the leading DTH player in terms of active subscriber base, followed by Bharti Telemedia.But I want to point out a few things about the implementation. And from the outset, it is important to note that for now, there is no clear guideline that Tata Play or any IPTV platform must charge separately for streaming Live TV channels to a smart TV. This seems like a revenue stream, and no revenue stream shall be left untapped. There are two distinct ways of looking at this—as an existing Tata Play DTH subscriber, and as a new subscriber simply signing up for Tata Play Smart streaming. I sit in the former (and have been a Tata Play subscriber ever since 2006; they were called Tata Sky then), and despite existing relationships, using Tata Play Smart for streaming Live TV channels on a smart TV such as a Google TV-based smart TV requires an additional subscription starting at ₹199 per month for a single-language set of channels, and ₹99 per month additionally for every language set you add. These channels are available to stream without this subscription on the mobile app. That is incredibly confusing for most customers, and unnecessary friction in the overall experience.If you aren’t a Tata Play DTH subscriber, you’ll need the subscription to even view Live TV channels on the mobile app.And to that point, Tata Play says the service streams more than 500 Live TV channels. Great number to have and a lot of potential. But here’s the reality. None of Sony’s sports channels are listed (Sony and Tata Play’s issues aren’t new, but do consumers really care about the tussle?) and that is a big miss. For instance, key upcoming cricket including India’s tour of New Zealand, as well as the UEFA Champions League football, are on the Sony Sports channels. In the English movies and entertainment section, well-known channels including Star Movies and Star Movies Select, Sony Pix, and Colors Infinity are missing. These are just some examples.Potentially, Tata Play Smart could have been the answer to a seamless Live TV platform without requiring a DTH connection. For now, it isn’t exactly there. It could be, if developed carefully. I cannot comment on streaming quality or stability because, as a Tata Play HD+ user, I refuse (maybe it’s just me) to be arm-twisted into paying additionally for a service which subscribers should get irrespective of.The answer actually could come from an app that has surprised me in recent weeks. It is called VZY, and it has OTT plans (including 23 OTTs such as JioHotstar, Zee 5, Sony Liv and more), standalone Live TV plans with more than 200 channels (for ₹179 per month), and a bundle of both depending on how a subscriber wants to configure the subscription tenure. This has the full gamut of sports channels, including some Sony Sports ones (complications galore, like I said). Some movie and entertainment channels are missing here too.What this market really needs is a complete Live TV streaming app—an affordable subscription, that works across devices and broadband networks and doesn’t have any complication between TV and mobile apps. It’s been tried before by JioTV+ and JioTV but they only work on a Jio network. And Airtel’s Xstream IPTV service has DTH-like subscription package structures, which are comparatively more costly.The latest, on Neural Dispatch: Sonos and Plaud define AI utility, Adobe’s report, and Microsoft sells a solutionTECH SPOTLIGHT: XIAOMI’S MIJIA AIR PURIFIERI’ve said it time and again. Get ready, because the pollution season is upon us. Indoor air purifier purchases are best done in advance because once the AQI deteriorates rapidly, you’ll find the good ones out of stock more often than not. Xiaomi’s smart move ahead of the winter is to try something new, with elements that have previously worked well for them. The arrival of their Mijia smart home brand is marked by a familiar product, the Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 (alongside an intriguing Mijia Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact). The Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 is priced at ₹17,999 which if I’m not mistaken, makes this the most expensive air purifier in Xiaomi’s recent lineup. The replacement filter, which you will need a few months down the line, costs ₹3,499. This is the logical successor to the Smart Air Purifier 4 which itself has been a very reliable performer over the years. The key upgrade is the ‘Pentaclean’ technology. It works with monitoring, with the new 5-sensor AQI monitoring collecting data for PM1 particles (this is rare in purifiers), PM2.5 particles, dust, temperature and humidity. It is also dictating the filtration process, which now has a primary filter for larger particles, a Xiaomi High-Efficiency Filter, UV-C sterilisation, negative ionisation and activated carbon.I had the chance to test this as the AQI began to significantly deteriorate in the NCR, which gave us a good barometer of how the new filter packaging in particular is a step forward from something that was already so good. In the same bedroom where the Smart Air Purifier 4 was, the Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 held the AQI at a slightly lower (read, better quality) reading through the day and night. And it does so while staying quite silent at fan speed 1 as well as in sleep mode. You will notice the fan at higher speeds, but those moments may be necessary to quickly clean indoor air after a spurt of outdoor pollution enters.The UV-C module, which is still rare in home air purifiers, is an effective way of countering airborne viruses that inevitably wriggle between even the densest of filters. The Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 maintains an overall AQI around 15 with all metrics (PM 2.5, PM1 and Dust) on the LCD display in green. It brought the indoor AQI from around 230 to 50 in about 7 minutes in auto mode. And if you are someone who likes to maintain things as they are supposed to be, the detachable top cover makes it much simpler to clean the duct and fan blade every once in a while.

title: 2 senior HDFC officials leaked confidential data, bank's internal probe shows
description: The executives oversee certain key businesses and functions at the bank, according to the people, who asked not to be named, discussing confidential matters.
content: An internal probe by HDFC Bank Ltd. — India’s largest by market value — found evidence that two senior executives disclosed confidential business strategies and possible market-sensitive information to outsiders, according to people familiar with the matter.The executives oversee certain key businesses and functions at the bank, according to the people, who asked not to be named, discussing confidential matters.Also Read | HDFC Bank cuts over 3,300 jobs as automation drive gathers paceHDFC identified the executives during an internal investigation that began after some leaders grew concerned about the possibility of information being leaked, the people said. The probe is still underway as the bank continues to examine whether the information was misused, the people said.An HDFC Bank spokesperson acknowledged an internal review, but didn’t comment on its findings or the executives involved. “In line with our policies, an internal review into this matter is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts,” the spokesperson said by email. “Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings, once the review is complete.”The bank said it was committed to upholding the highest standards of ethics and governance and takes reports of potential violations seriously.The review comes at a sensitive moment for HDFC Bank, which has a market value of about $115 billion and has spent three decades cultivating a reputation for conservative management, strong internal controls and consistent profitability. The lender is preparing for its first outsider chief executive following boardroom disputes and management departures. Its share price has declined about 28% this year.Also Read | Anup Bagchi choice for HDFC Bank CEO signals regulatory slant for fresh bloodThe probe and its findings were reported to senior management, including some members of the board, earlier this year, the people said. Both executives have since been formally informed of the findings, and it wasn’t immediately clear what disciplinary action will be taken, the people said.The findings add to the challenges confronting Anup Bagchi, a veteran of rival ICICI Group, who is set to become HDFC Bank’s chief executive on Oct. 27.In recent months, internal divisions in HDFC have played out publicly. In March, then-chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned abruptly, citing differences between his personal values and certain practices at the bank. An independent legal review commissioned by the lender subsequently said his concerns were not substantiated.Also Read | Who is Anup Bagchi? 5 things to know about HDFC Bank’s incoming CEOBagchi’s appointment follows the surprise decision of Sashidhar Jagdishan, the incumbent chief executive, not to seek another term. Jagdishan is stepping down after six years at the helm.Kaizad Bharucha, deputy managing director and one of the bank’s longest-serving executives, has also asked to leave at the end of December.Founded in 1994, as the country opened its financial sector to private competition, HDFC Bank grew into a preferred investment for international fund managers seeking exposure to India’s rising incomes and expanding consumer credit.

title: Google rolls out new Gemini tools to help small businesses manage marketing, finances
description: Google is rolling out Gemini features that help entrepreneurs manage branding, create marketing content, analyse finances and connect business apps.
content: Google has announced new tools in its Gemini artificial intelligence (AI) assistant for small businesses, including a dedicated business landing page that brings together brand development, financial analysis and customer insights, aiming to reduce the time entrepreneurs spend on routine tasks.The new features will allow business owners to connect Gemini with Google services such as Google Business Profile, Google Ads and Google Workspace, as well as third-party applications including Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho and Xero, according to a blog post by Google.Also Read: From assistant to agent: Google brings Gemini Spark personal AI agent to IndiaThe business landing page will serve as a central hub for managing daily operations, while new features will allow users to upload their websites, brand kits, fonts and colour palettes to establish a consistent brand style within Gemini.Combined with Google's Nano Banana 2.1 image-generation model, the platform can create visual material for product launches and marketing campaigns while retaining the specified brand style. This is intended to help small businesses generate consistent marketing assets without repeatedly providing their design guidelines.Also Read: Google takes aim in frontier AI race as Gemini 4 Argon leads in benchmarksGemini will also help business owners analyse financial information by turning spreadsheets, receipts and purchase records into visual summaries and interactive models. The tool is designed to make financial information easier to understand and help entrepreneurs draw insights from their business records.Google said tens of millions of small business owners are already using Gemini to develop product ideas, manage customer feedback and analyse business performance.The company highlighted examples of entrepreneurs using the technology to support their operations. In France, a ceramicist uses Gemini to write product descriptions, newsletters and social media content, saving two to three hours daily.Also Read: How Google is giving Indian farming an AI upgrade to help grow better cropsIn Maharashtra, farmer and content creator Santosh Jadhav used Gemini to assess soil suitability for ginger cultivation, calculate seed requirements and prepare an investment budget despite having no formal training or local mentors.Google said the business landing page, marketing and finance features, and new app connections would begin rolling out globally to all Gemini app users in the coming days.The rollout expands Gemini's intended role from an AI assistant for individual tasks to a tool that can support multiple aspects of running a small business, including marketing, financial analysis and customer engagement.

title: PM Modi calls for youth empowerment, preservation of India’s cultural heritage | India News
description: Recalling his association with the mission’s founder, Swami Chinmayananda, PM Narendra Modi described an emotional experience at the event. | India News
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday called for the empowerment of the youth and the preservation of India’s cultural heritage, while urging spiritual and cultural organisations to contribute to India’s ambition of becoming a developed nation by 2047.Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, PM Modi linked India's goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047 to the centenary of the Chinmaya Mission, which will also fall that year.The three-day gathering to mark 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission has brought together more than 9,000 participants from India and abroad.Modi said the mission’s centenary and India’s 100 years of independence should advance together. He urged spiritual organisations to work towards national development and social unity, saying India must address emerging challenges and build public awareness around the goal of a developed nation.Modi recalls his association with Swami ChinmayanandaRecalling his association with the mission’s founder, Swami Chinmayananda, the prime minister described an emotional experience at the event, where technology recreated his interaction with his spiritual mentor.“It felt as if I had gone back 33 years in time,” Modi said, recalling his guru’s affection and blessings.He said he met Chinmayananda in Chicago in February-March 1993 to invite him to the centenary celebrations of the World Parliament of Religions. The spiritual leader accepted the invitation and promoted the event in the US, but died in San Diego on August 3, weeks before the gathering in Chicago on September 11.Recalling their last meeting, Modi said youth empowerment and building a strong India were central to Chinmayananda’s vision. He also highlighted an initiative in which young people travelled nearly 40,000 km over about 300 days, reaching more than 100,000 people, and congratulated those involved.Connecting the mission’s milestone with the idea of Amrit Kaal, Modi said the Upanishadic concept of being children of Amrit represented enduring consciousness and cultural continuity, rather than physical immortality. He said India’s civilisational strength stemmed from its commitment to truth, knowledge and enlightenment.Spiritual progress and human welfareModi said Chinmayananda sought to link spiritual progress with human welfare and national self-respect. Through the Gita Gyan Yagna, he took the teachings of the Vedas, Upanishads and other scriptures to the public, making Indian philosophical traditions more accessible.The prime minister credited the mission’s educational institutions and cultural activities with introducing Indian values to younger generations. More than 100 institutions run by the mission, he said, were combining modern education with Indian values.He cited the National Education Policy as an effort to integrate India’s knowledge traditions, mother-tongue instruction, modern science and emerging technologies into education.Modi also recalled Chinmayananda’s support for the Vivekananda Rock Memorial in Kanyakumari, saying the spiritual leader made the first financial contribution to the project. He highlighted the development of cultural and religious centres, including Kashi Vishwanath Dham, the Ram temple in Ayodhya, and sites at Kedarnath and Badrinath.Modi says restoring India’s cultural heritageThe prime minister said India had recovered more than 650 stolen ancient artefacts over the past 12 years, describing the recovery as part of efforts to restore the country’s cultural heritage.He also cited International Yoga Day as an example of Indian spiritual traditions reaching a global audience.Concluding his address, Modi said the Chinmaya Mission’s global network of acharyas, spiritual practitioners and volunteers could contribute to the country’s transformation.With the mission set to complete 100 years in 2047, he said its centenary journey and India’s pursuit of Viksit Bharat shared a common objective.

title: Asian Para Games: Mona Agarwal wins second gold, sets world record in 50m Rifle 3 Positions SH1 final | Hindustan Times
description: Mona produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang, who claimed the silver medal.
content: Indian para shooter Mona Agarwal clinched her second gold medal at the 2026 Asian Para Games, setting a world record in the women's 50m Rifle 3 Positions SH1 final on Friday.Mona produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang, who claimed the silver medal. The Indian shooter had earlier won gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day of the Games.Avani Lekhara, the other Indian competing in the final, narrowly missed out on a podium finish, finishing fourth. She had been among the top two after the prone position but lost ground in the standing series.On the opening day, Mona and Avani had secured a one-two finish in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event. Mona won gold with a score of 250, setting an Asian Para Games record and surpassing Avani's previous mark of 249.6 from the 2023 Hangzhou edition.India's para athletes and shooters enjoyed a productive Day 5, with the country adding several medals across disciplines. In para badminton, Nitesh Kumar won gold in the men's singles SL3 final, while Pramod Bhagat won silver. Naveen Sivakumar also secured gold in the men's singles SL4 event after defeating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in the final.In para archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men's recurve doubles event.Sandeep claimed gold in the men's 400m T64 final, with Ajay Kumar taking bronze, while Haney secured gold in the men's javelin throw F37/38 final.India also collected silver medals through Thulasimathi Murugesan in women's singles SU5 (badminton), Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan in women's singles SH6 (badminton), Pooja Jatyan and Bhawna Choudhary in women's recurve doubles, Parmod Bijarnia in men's 1500m T46 and Nimisha Suresh in women's long jump T47. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa won bronze in the men's doubles (MD4) para table tennis.India had a total of 103 medals, comprising 27 gold, 33 silver and 43 bronze, and were fourth in the standings at the time of writing, with China leading the table with 354 medals.India are now targeting a tally beyond their previous best of 108 medals, achieved at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games as competition continues in Aichi-Nagoya.

title: Centre extends deployment of 273 CAPF companies in Delhi till Oct 31 amid flash protest fears | Latest News Delhi
description: Centre extends deployment of 273 CAPF companies in Delhi till Oct 31 amid flash protest fears  | Latest News Delhi
content: New Delhi, The Union home ministry has extended for the second time the deployment of 273 Central Armed Police Forces companies in the national capital till October 31 in view of the possibility of "flash protests" by political and other groups, official sources said on Friday.The companies were brought to Delhi for the protests by the Cockroach Janta Party earlier this month.The Ministry of Home Affairs directed the Delhi Police and the respective CFs on October 22 to coordinate the deployment, the sources told PTI.The extension was approved at the request of the Delhi Police, they said, adding that a similar extension had been sanctioned in mid-October.Officials said the Delhi Police had informed the ministry that there was a possibility of flash protests being undertaken by political and other outfits in various "sensitive" locations of the city. The extension of the deployment was essential in order to ensure proper law and order, they said.The MHA has approved the request, the sources said.Of the 273 companies that will continue to remain deployed in Delhi alongside the local police, 125 are from the Central Reserve Police Force , including 20 women personnel units; 20 from the Rapid Action Force ; 46 from the Border Security Force ; 39 from the Indo-Tibetan Border Police ; 31 from the Sashastra Seema Bal ; and 12 from the Central Industrial Security Force .A CF company has a sanctioned strength of 100 personnel, but its effective operational manpower is about 70-72 personnel.Parts of Delhi witnessed CJP protests on October 9 seeking the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Opposition parties subsequently staged protests with the same demand.The CJP also held a 'Lehra Do Tiranga' demonstration on October 16.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Three-year-old girl killed in attack by stray dog in MP’s Ratlam | Hindustan Times
description: The child’s parents were away in Rajasthan for work, while her grandparents were working in agricultural fields when the attack took place.
content: A three-year-old girl died after being attacked by a stray dog in Madhya Pradesh's Ratlam district, officials have said.Manisha Bhabhar, the daughter of a labourer couple, was mauled by the canine while playing in the courtyard of her house, within the jurisdiction of Deendayal Nagar police station, on Thursday evening, they said.The child was rushed to the district hospital by her relatives, but doctors declared her dead after examination, said officials."The dog had badly bitten the girl on her head and back, leaving deep wounds at both places," Jeevan Chauhan, a doctor at the hospital, told PTI.Also read: Gzb: 4-year-old dies from injuries suffered from stray dog attackDeendayal Nagar police station house officer Anurag Yadav said they had received information about the girl's death following a stray dog attack.An autopsy would be conducted on her body, and the police would investigate the incident, he said.Raju, a neighbour who took the girl to the hospital, said her grandparents were working in agricultural fields at the time of the incident, while her parents, both labourers, were away in Ajmer in Rajasthan for work.The seriously injured girl might have died on the way to the hospital, he added.

title: TN: Heavy downpours cause waterlogging, flooding, teen killed in wall collapse | Hindustan Times
description: TN: Heavy downpours cause waterlogging, flooding, teen killed in wall collapse
content: Chennai, Heavy showers caused localised waterlogging in lower areas across Tamil Nadu and districts such as Madurai and Virudhunagar, known for extreme heat, received bounteous rain, bringing down the temperature in the region.Dindigul, Erode, Perambalur, Ariyalur, Tiruvarur, Theni and many interior districts as well received heavy rain.A 17-year-old girl died, and her mother was injured after a wall of their rented house collapsed due to heavy rains at Mettumalai near Sattur in Virudhunagar district, police said on Friday.The deceased was identified as Muthuchelvi, a Class 12 student. Her mother, Solaiyammal, who sustained injuries in the incident, was rescued from the debris and admitted to the Sattur Government Hospital.According to the police, the incident occurred on October 22 night while the family was sleeping. Sattur and its surrounding areas had experienced heavy downpours for over five hours prior to the collapse.The girl's father, Selvam, who works at a printing press in Sivakasi, lived in the rented house with his wife and two children.Following the collapse, neighbours immediately alerted the Sattur Town Police. Police personnel rushed to the spot, rescued the injured woman, and recovered the teenager's body. The body was subsequently sent to the Sattur Government Hospital for a post-mortem examination.Meanwhile, the water level in Tamil Nadu's 89 reservoirs stood at 27.9 per cent of their total capacity as on October 22, retaining 62.53 TMC against a capacity of 224.3 TMC. The storage rose by 1.02 TMC in the last 24 hours, but remained 134.4 TMC below the corresponding period last year, sources said.The IMD warned that under the influence of Thursday's upper-air cyclonic circulation over Southeast and adjoining Eastcentral Bay of Bengal, a low pressure area formed over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal at 5.30 am on Friday. It is most likely to persist over the same region and intensify into a depression on October 24. Thereafter, it is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression on October 25 and into a cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by October 26 morning.It would then continue to intensify further and move west-northwestwards towards North Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha coasts during the subsequent 2 days, a bulletin said.An official said that there was no direct threat from the persisting depression to Tamil Nadu. However, northern districts of the state may experience continued rain until October 26 due to existing atmospheric circulation. The arrival of the cyclone is expected to draw moisture away, leading to a decrease in rainfall across the state after October 26.Rainfall activity may resume in the first week of November after the storm makes landfall, he said.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: SS Rajamouli: ఒక్క హాలీవుడ్ మూవీ అయినా చేస్తా.. ఆర్ఆర్ఆర్ తర్వాత ఎన్ని ఆఫర్లు వచ్చినా అందుకే చేయలేదు: రాజమౌళి | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: SS Rajamouli: బ్రెజిల్‌లో జరిగిన 50వ సావో పాలో అంతర్జాతీయ ఫిల్మ్ ఫెస్టివల్‌లో పాల్గొన్న ఎస్.ఎస్. రాజమౌళి.. అక్కడ లైఫ్‌టైమ్ అచీవ్‌మెంట్ అవార్డు ('లియాన్ కాకాఫ్' అవార్డు) అందుకున్నారు. 'RRR' విజయం తర్వాత హాలీవుడ్ నుంచి తనకు అనేక ఆఫర్లు వచ్చాయని, కానీ తాను ఎందుకు వెళ్లలేదో రాజమౌళి వెల్లడించారు.
content: SS Rajamouli: తెలుగు చిత్రసీమ ఖ్యాతిని ప్రపంచం నలుమూలలా చాటిచెప్పిన దర్శకధీరుడు ఎస్.ఎస్. రాజమౌళి. 'ఆర్ఆర్ఆర్' (RRR) సినిమాతో ఆస్కార్ వేదికపై భారతీయ జెండాను ఎగురవేసిన తర్వాత.. ఆయన నెక్స్ట్ ప్రాజెక్ట్ ఏంటి? హాలీవుడ్‌లో సినిమా చేస్తారా? లేదా? అనే అంశాలపై అంతర్జాతీయ స్థాయిలో ఆసక్తి నెలకొంది.తాజాగా బ్రెజిల్‌లో జరిగిన 50వ సావో పాలో అంతర్జాతీయ ఫిల్మ్ ఫెస్టివల్‌కు హాజరైన రాజమౌళి.. స్థానిక బ్రెజిలియన్ మీడియా ('ఒమెలెట్') కు ఇచ్చిన ప్రత్యేక ఇంటర్వ్యూలో తన హాలీవుడ్ ఎంట్రీపై సంచలన వ్యాఖ్యలు చేశారు. మహేష్ బాబు, ప్రియాంకా చోప్రా ప్రధాన పాత్రల్లో వస్తున్న తన అత్యంత ప్రతిష్టాత్మక చిత్రం 'వారణాసి' (Varanasi) షూటింగ్ కేవలం 10 రోజులు మాత్రమే మిగిలి ఉందని క్లారిటీ ఇచ్చారు."కనీసం ఒక హాలీవుడ్ సినిమా అయినా చేయాలనుంది!"హాలీవుడ్ వర్కింగ్ కల్చర్, అక్కడ ఉండే నెట్‌వర్కింగ్, ప్రొడక్షన్ నిర్మాణం గురించి రాజమౌళి ఎంతో ప్రశంసాపూర్వకంగా మాట్లాడారు. "నాకు హాలీవుడ్‌లో కనీసం ఒక సినిమా అయినా చేయాలని ఉంది. అక్కడ ఉండే పక్కా వర్క్ ఎథిక్స్, వర్క్ స్ట్రక్చర్ నుంచి నేను నేర్చుకోవాల్సింది చాలా ఉంది. హాలీవుడ్ ప్రొడక్షన్‌లో పనిచేయడం నాకు ఎంతో ఇష్టం" అని రాజమౌళి తెలిపారు.అయితే 'RRR' తర్వాత వచ్చిన అవకాశాలను ఎందుకు తాను పక్కన పెట్టాల్సి వచ్చిందో వివరిస్తూ.. "'RRR' గ్లోబల్ హిట్ అయ్యాక హాలీవుడ్ ప్రముఖ నిర్మాణ సంస్థల నుంచి నాకు చాలా ఆఫర్లు వచ్చాయి. అందులో కొన్ని ఆఫర్లు ఇప్పటికీ ఓపెన్‌గానే ఉన్నాయి. కానీ 'RRR' సమయానికే నేను నా డ్రీమ్ ప్రాజెక్ట్ 'వారణాసి' (Varanasi) ప్రీ-ప్రొడక్షన్ పనుల్లో నిమగ్నమై ఉన్నాను. నా మైండ్ ఒకేసారి రెండు ప్రాజెక్ట్‌లపై దృష్టి పెట్టలేదు. ఒక పని పూర్తయ్యాకే మరో పని గురించి ఆలోచించడం నా అలవాటు. 'వారణాసి' పూర్తయ్యాక హాలీవుడ్ ప్రాజెక్ట్ గురించి ఆలోచిస్తాను" అని రాజమౌళి తెల్చిచెప్పారు.కేవలం 10 రోజుల షూటింగ్ మాత్రమే బాకీసూపర్ స్టార్ మహేష్ బాబు, గ్లోబల్ స్టార్ ప్రియాంకా చోప్రా జోనస్, పృథ్వీరాజ్ సుకుమారన్ ప్రధాన పాత్రల్లో వస్తున్న భారీ యాక్షన్ అడ్వెంచర్ డ్రామా 'వారణాసి'. ఈ సినిమాకు సంబంధించి అభిమానులకు మైండ్ బ్లాకింగ్ అప్‌డేట్ ఇచ్చారు జక్కన్న.ఈ ఎపిక్ యాక్షన్ అడ్వెంచర్‌కు సంబంధించిన ప్రధాన షూటింగ్ దాదాపు పూర్తయిందని, కేవలం మరో 10 రోజుల షూటింగ్ మాత్రమే మిగిలి ఉందని రాజమౌళి ధృవీకరించారు. భారతీయ ఇతిహాసాలను తెరపై ఆవిష్కరించే క్రమంలో తాను గతంలో ఎప్పుడూ పూర్తి సంతృప్తి చెందలేదని, కానీ 'వారణాసి' రూపంలో విజన్‌ను సరికొత్తగా ఆవిష్కరిస్తున్నానని వెల్లడించారు.2027 ఏప్రిల్ 7న 'వారణాసి' వరల్డ్‌వైడ్ గ్రాండ్ రిలీజ్విజయేంద్ర ప్రసాద్, ఎస్.ఎస్. కాంచిలతో కలిసి రాజమౌళి స్క్రీన్‌ప్లే సమకూర్చిన ఈ చిత్రాన్ని కె.ఎల్. నారాయణ, ఎస్.ఎస్. కార్తికేయ అత్యంత భారీ బడ్జెట్‌తో నిర్మిస్తున్నారు. ఎం.ఎం. కీరవాణి సంగీతం అందిస్తున్నారు.భారీ వీఎఫ్ఎక్స్ (VFX), అంతర్జాతీయ స్థాయి యాక్షన్ స్టంట్స్‌తో రూపొందుతున్న ఈ ఎపిక్ వరల్డ్-ట్రాటర్ ఫిల్మ్‌ను 2027 ఏప్రిల్ 7న (ఉగాది పండుగ కానుకగా) ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా వేల థియేటర్లలో విడుదల చేయడానికి మేకర్స్ తేదీని ఇప్పటికే అధికారికంగా ఖరారు చేశారు. 'వారణాసి' పూర్తయిన తర్వాతే రాజమౌళి డైరెక్ట్ హాలీవుడ్ ప్రాజెక్ట్ వైపు అడుగులు వేసే అవకాశం కనిపిస్తోంది.

title: Punjab govt moves resolution against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over SIR issue | Hindustan Times
description: Finance minister Harpal Cheema leads motion demanding impartial inquiry into special intensive revision exercise and alleged voter deletions.
content: Chandigarh: The Punjab government on Friday tabled an official resolution moved by finance minister Harpal Cheema, calling for an independent inquiry against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the administrative decisions governing recent voter registration updates.Presenting the motion, Cheema accused the BJP of snatching citizens’ right to vote. “In Delhi, the BJP came to power last year through vote chori (theft),” Cheema alleged during his address on the assembly floor.According to the resolution, the House expressed concern over incidents of citizens allegedly being deprived of their right to vote, demanding that constitutional protections for the voting rights of all eligible citizens be ensured. It calls for the establishment of an independent, impartial, and credible investigative mechanism to inquire into alleged irregularities concerning the electoral process and voter lists under the leadership of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, aimed at bringing the truth to light and fixing administrative accountability.The resolution seeks a non-partisan judicial investigation to determine whether procedural violations, administrative changes, or unauthorised deletions compromised voting ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.Central to the motion are serious allegations surrounding the Election Commission of India’s special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. Official figures published following the SIR drive reveal that over 13.6 lakh names were removed from Punjab’s final electoral roll, reducing the state’s total electorate from 2.14 crore down to roughly 2.01 crore voters.While the Election Commission maintains that these removals were conducted transparently to purge duplicate records, deceased individuals, and permanently relocated citizens, the resolution highlights persistent claims that eligible citizens were systematically excluded without adequate verification. Critics also cite contentious additions to Form 6 registration processes and disputed voter notices on the ECINET portal as key indicators of central overreach and procedural bias.Prior to the legislative action, street demonstrations were held in Chandigarh on October 10, during which senior AAP leaders—including Cheema and former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia—were detained by police while demanding the CEC’s removal and an immediate halt to SIR operations. The opposition Congress in the state has also staged separate protests, demanding a return to pre-revision voter lists.Punjab’s resolution follows similar action in Kerala, where lawmakers passed a motion challenging the constitutional validity of the Election Commission leadership’s voter revision methods.

title: Advance Dental Export Is Revolutionizing Dentistry by Bridging the Gap Between Dental Labs and Modern Technology | Hindustan Times
description: Advance Dental Export’s Ultimate Smile Design concept focuses on planning smiles around individual patients rather than using a template.
content: For decades, the relationship between a dentist and a dental laboratory was largely transactional. A case was sent to the lab, a restoration was manufactured, and the finished prosthesis was sent back to the clinic. Somewhere between those steps, however, something important was often missing: conversation.There was limited opportunity to discuss the patient's expectations, understand the dentist's clinical approach, plan the case together or translate an idea into a precise restorative outcome. The laboratory was often expected to make the restoration, rather than become part of the thinking behind it.But dentistry is changing.As digital workflows, CAD/CAM, intraoral scanning, digital treatment planning and advanced manufacturing become increasingly integrated into modern digital dentistry, the role of the dental laboratory is changing with them. Today, a dentist doesn't simply need a laboratory that can manufacture a crown, bridge or veneer. They need someone who can understand the case, communicate clearly, interpret the dentist's vision, solve technical challenges and contribute to the outcome.This is the shift Advance Dental Export (ADE), Surat has been building toward - from a dental laboratory to a dental technology partner for modern dental practices.Founded by Haresh Savani in 2009, Advance Dental Export has grown around a combination of craftsmanship, personalisation, digital technology and collaboration with dental professionals. Its philosophy goes beyond just manufacturing dental prosthetics. Because a smile is never just a restoration from a laboratory. It is an outcome created for a person.The Dental Laboratory Is No Longer Just a ManufacturerThe modern dental case at ADE begins long before a restoration reaches the patient's mouth.It can begin with a conversation.What does the dentist want to achieve? What does the patient expect? What does the clinical situation allow? What aesthetic details matter? What needs to be communicated between the clinic and the laboratory before anything is designed?These questions can fundamentally change the way a case progresses.Think of it like building a house. The final structure may be what everyone sees, but the outcome depends on everything that happened before the first brick was placed - the plan, measurements, materials, decisions and people involved.Dental restorations are no different.Digital dentistry has made this relationship even more connected. ADE works with digital workflows and supports major scanning and CAD/CAM ecosystems, including 3Shape, iTero, Cerec Connect, 3M ESPE and Carestream. Its capabilities span digital design, custom milling and digitally manufactured restorations.But technology is only one part of the equation.ADE's larger proposition is what happens when technology meets interpretation, communication and craftsmanship.The result is our laboratory that does not simply receive instructions - it embraces change, takes on complex challenges and works towards finding the right solution for the case.From Sending Cases to Collaborative Case PlanningOne of the biggest changes in modern dentistry is the movement from case submission to case collaboration.At Advance Dental Export, the relationship extends beyond fabrication to areas such as diagnostic wax-ups, implant planning, custom abutments, denture bars, shade analysis and custom milling.This becomes especially important when a case is complex or highly aesthetic.Because the dentist may know the patient clinically, while the dental technician brings another layer of expertise - the ability to interpret materials, morphology, proportions, contours and fabrication possibilities.When these perspectives meet early, the restoration becomes less about following an order and more about building an outcome together.That is also why communication matters.ADE itself has emphasised the importance of structured communication and collaboration between dentists and laboratory technicians, recognising that better communication can improve workflow and restorative outcomes.Because a smile that is created is not just about how it looks.It is about how it fits, how it functions, how it feels - and how closely it reflects the treatment vision.Where ADE Meets Ultimate Smile DesignIf the future of dentistry is about thinking beyond what a laboratory can make, Ultimate Smile Design (USD) is a clear example of what that thinking can create. Ultimate Smile Design is ADE's premium smile-design concept.Built around the idea that a smile should be considered before it is treated, it brings a design perspective to dentistry - looking beyond individual teeth to how shape, proportion and expression come together as a whole. The result is not a smile selected from a template, but one developed with intention around the person it belongs to.For ADE, USD is a reflection of its belief that the future of dentistry will belong to those willing to rethink the process, not simply refine the product.Technology That Connects the Clinic and the LaboratoryDigital dentistry has changed not only how restorations are manufactured, but also how people work together.Digital impressions can move from the clinic to the laboratory without the limitations of traditional physical workflows. Digital designs can be reviewed, modified and translated into manufacturing instructions. CAD/CAM allows restorations and components to be produced with a high degree of digital precision.Advance Dental Export has built its workflow around these developments, including digital scanning, CAD/CAM design, 3D printing and custom milling. It also works with authentic implant manufacturer hardware and custom CAD/CAM abutments, supporting implant cases while helping preserve manufacturer warranty requirements.But this changes the question dentists should be asking.It is no longer simply:“Can the lab make this restoration?”It is:“Can the lab understand my case, work with my workflow and help me take the outcome further?”For a technology partner, the answer has to be yes.Precision Still Needs PeopleFor all the progress in digital dentistry, there is one thing technology cannot replace: judgement.A scanner can capture data. Software can generate a design. A milling machine can manufacture with remarkable consistency.But someone still has to understand what the numbers mean.Someone still has to recognise when a contour needs refinement, when an aesthetic detail feels off, when a material is right for the case - and, just as importantly, when something simply shouldn’t be done. Because knowing what to change is important, but knowing what to leave alone can be just as valuable.That is where ADE's team of experienced dental professionals and technicians becomes central to its model.Technology creates possibilities. People turn those possibilities into outcomes.And perhaps that is the real evolution of the dental laboratory.It is no longer technology versus craftsmanship.It is technology with craftsmanship.Building a More Connected Dental PracticeFor dentists, the value of a technology-enabled laboratory is ultimately not about having more machines.It is about having fewer gaps.Fewer gaps between the clinic and laboratory.Fewer gaps between the treatment plan and the final restoration.Fewer gaps between what the dentist envisions and what the technician creates.That is where a strong laboratory partnership can make a difference.The modern dentist is also becoming increasingly conscious of differentiation. Patients are looking for personalised treatment, greater predictability and experiences that feel considered rather than standardised.And for a dentist, standing apart is not always about offering more.Sometimes, it is about doing the same thing differently - and doing it better.That requires the right clinical expertise, the right technology and, increasingly, the right people behind the scenes.Advance Dental Export: Building the Future of Digital DentistryAdvance Dental Export's evolution reflects a larger transformation taking place across dentistry - and ADE is emerging as a flag bearer of that change.Its current ecosystem reflects that scale: 500+ local partners, 750+ qualified professionals, 20+ countries served, 120,000+ cases and 12,000+ trusted dentists, backed by more than two decades of experience in the dental industry.But numbers alone do not explain the shift.The bigger story is what those relationships represent: a growing ecosystem where dentists, technicians and technology work more closely together, while keeping the patient at the heart of every outcome.For Haresh Savani, the journey has been about evolving from a dental laboratory into a trusted provider of dental prosthetics and solutions for dental professionals. His vision today goes further - towards empowering dentists through solutions that bring together artistry, efficiency and predictability, while continuing to embrace emerging technologies and new possibilities in dentistry.And the patient remains an important part of that journey. After all, every case begins with a clinical need, but ends with a person who has to live with, feel confident in and experience the result.That is why the next generation of dental laboratories will need to think differently.Not simply:“What can we manufacture?”But:“What can we create that makes a difference?”Because the future of dentistry will not be shaped by dentists, laboratories or technology working in isolation. It will come from bringing these forces closer together - with the patient at the centre.For dentists looking to distinguish their work, elevate the patient experience and deliver outcomes that reflect their own clinical vision, the laboratory partnership becomes more than a backend function. It becomes part of how they practise differently.And that is where Advance Dental Export sees its role: not simply keeping pace with the evolution of dentistry, but helping lead it.ADE is at the forefront of this new era - one where the laboratory moves closer to the practice, the practice moves closer to the patient, and better possibilities begin with bringing the right people together.For dentists ready to think beyond the conventional laboratory relationship, the next chapter of dentistry is already underway.Note to readers: This article is part of HT's paid consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. title: The new career paths opening up for architecture and engineering students | Hindustan Times
description: India’s growing data centre, sustainability and digital construction sectors are creating new career opportunities for architecture and engineering graduates.
content: Ask a final-year architecture or engineering student where they see themselves in five years, and the answer is still often “a design firm” or “a site.” Both remain valid. But the biggest hiring growth is now elsewhere.1. Data centres: the fastest-growing building typeIndia’s data centre capacity stood at 1.6 GW in June 2026 and is projected to reach 6 GW by 2029, requiring about $110 billion in investment. The spending is revealing: $18 billion goes to mechanical, electrical and plumbing infrastructure, against $4 billion for the real estate construction itself. The jobs are therefore concentrated in MEP design, power systems, cooling, and commissioning. Mumbai alone holds over half of India’s operational data centre inventory. indias data centre capacity expected to jump to 6 gw by 2029 20260902131252 +2Roles: data centre MEP engineer, cooling design engineer, commissioning engineer, critical-facilities project manager.2. Sustainability: from certificate to careerIGBC now reports over 20,000 registered projects covering 16.33 billion sq. ft. Each one needs people who can model energy use, specify materials and document compliance. The focus is also shifting from individual green buildings to net zero buildings and resilient infrastructure. constructionworldconstructionworldRoles: IGBC or LEED accredited professional, energy modeller, embodied-carbon analyst, ESG consultant for developers.3. BIM and digital deliveryIndia’s public capital expenditure is set to reach ₹12.2 lakh crore in 2026-27, and large projects such as metros, airports and expressways increasingly depend on digital coordination. One verified example is NCRTC’s rapid rail project, which has publicly disclosed its use of BIM. A formal national standard is still missing: BIS has not published a dedicated IS standard on BIM, so firms follow ISO 19650 and client requirements. Graduates who understand these frameworks can fill a real gap. ₹12.2 Lakh Crore CapEx: How Budget 2026 Is Accelerating BIM Adoption in India +2"> ₹12.2 Lakh Crore CapEx: How Budget 2026 Is Accelerating BIM Adoption in India +2Roles: BIM coordinator, BIM manager, information manager, 4D/5D planner, digital twin specialist.4. Other fast-growing areasPrefab and modular construction: design-for-manufacture engineer.Facility and asset management: smart-building and operations specialist.Computational design: parametric and generative design specialist.Reality capture: drone and laser-scan surveyor for progress monitoring.What students should do this yearLearn one BIM platform (Revit or Navisworks) and complete at least one coordinated multi-discipline model.Take one sustainability credential such as IGBC AP or LEED Green Associate.Pick up one analysis tool, such as EnergyPlus, IES-VE or Python for building data.Intern in a different discipline from your own, so you understand how structure, MEP and architecture constrain each other.Attend industry events where project teams discuss real problems. Some, like the IGBC Green Building Congress in Mumbai on 26 to 28 November, are open to students.A cautionNot every boom creates permanent local jobs. One analysis note that large data centres may create only about 1,000 permanent jobs per site and consume substantial land, power and water. The strongest careers will go to those who can design and deliver these facilities efficiently, not only operate them. diggThe bottom lineThe profession is moving from drawing and supervising to modelling, measuring, and integrating. Students who combine sound fundamentals with digital and sustainability skills will find more entry points than any previous generation.By Roy Aniruddha, Founder and Chairman, TechnoStruct Group

title: ఐఐటీ హైదరాబాద్‌లో 'గుడ్‌నెస్‌'పై భారతదేశంలోనే మొట్టమొదటి అకడమిక్ కోర్సు | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: IIT Hyderabad Goodness Course : విద్యార్థులు కేవలం విద్యా, వృత్తి నైపుణ్యాలపై మాత్రమే దృష్టి పెట్టడం కాదు. మానవీయ విలువలను కూడా సరిగా అర్థం చేసుకోవాలనే ఉద్దేశంతో ఐఐటీ హైదరాబాద్ కొత్త కోర్సును తీసుకొచ్చింది.
content: ఐఐటీ హైదరాబాద్ కేవలం విద్య, వృత్తిపరమైన నైపుణ్యాలకే పరిమితం కాకుండా విద్యార్థులలో మానవతా విలువలు, సామాజిక బాధ్యత, వ్యక్తిత్వ వికాసాన్ని పెంపొందించే దిశగా ఒక చారిత్రాత్మక అడుగు వేసింది. దేశంలోనే తొలిసారిగా "మంచితనం" (Goodness) అనే అంశంపై క్రెడిట్ పొందేందుకు వీలుగా ఒక ప్రత్యేక అకడమిక్ కోర్సును ప్రారంభించింది."గుడ్‌నెస్: క్యారెక్టర్, రెస్పాన్సిబిలిటీ అండ్ హ్యూమన్ ఫ్లోరిషింగ్" (Goodness: Character, Responsibility and Human Flourishing - LA2270) పేరుతో ఈ ఒక క్రెడిట్ (1-Credit Elective) ఆప్షనల్ కోర్సును అధికారులు ప్రవేశపెట్టారు.ఈ కోర్సును బి.టెక్ ఫస్ట్ ఇయర్ నుంచి ఫైనల్ ఇయర్ వరకు, బి.డిజైన్ (BDes) చదువుతున్న విద్యార్థులందరూ ఎంచుకోవచ్చు. దీనికి ఎలాంటి ముందస్తు అర్హతలు అవసరం లేదు. ఐఐటీ హైదరాబాద్ విడుదల చేసిన ప్రకటన ప్రకారం, ఈ కోర్సు ప్రారంభమైన వెంటనే 140 మందికి పైగా విద్యార్థులు దీనిలో చేరడం విశేషం.ఈ కోర్సును ఇన్‌స్టిట్యూట్ ఆఫ్ గుడ్‌నెస్ ప్రతిపాదించగా ఐఐటీ హైదరాబాద్ దీనిని ఆమోదించి అధికారిక అకడమిక్ క్రెడిట్ కోర్సుగా అమలు చేస్తోంది.కేవలం ఆదాయం, పదవులే విజయం అనుకునే ఈ రోజుల్లో అసలైన మంచి జీవితం అంటే ఏమిటి? సమాజం పట్ల ఒక వ్యక్తికి ఉండాల్సిన బాధ్యతలేంటి? అనే అంశాలపై విద్యార్థుల్లో ఆలోచన రేకెత్తించడమే ఈ కోర్సు ముఖ్య ఉద్దేశం. మొత్తం 7 సెషన్లలో సాగే ఈ కోర్సులో పలు అంశాలను కవర్ చేస్తారు.గుడ్‌నెస్ ఇండెక్స్ ఫ్రేమ్‌వర్క్: మంచితనాన్ని అంచనా వేసే విధానం.హ్యూమన్ ఫ్లోరిషింగ్: జీవితంలోని శారీరక, మానసిక, భావోద్వేగ, సామాజిక మరియు ఆధ్యాత్మిక పరిమాణాలు.క్యారెక్టర్ ఇన్‌ఫ్రాస్ట్రక్చర్ అండ్ డెవిడెండ్: వ్యక్తిత్వ నిర్మాణం, దాని వల్ల సమాజానికి జరిగే ప్రయోజనం.పర్సనల్ సోషల్ రెస్పాన్సిబిలిటీ: వ్యక్తిగత సామాజిక బాధ్యత.వికసిత్ భారత్ : మంచితనానికి, నవ భారత నిర్మాణానికి ఉన్న సంబంధం.విద్యార్థులకు ఏదో ఒక నిర్దిష్టమైన సిద్ధాంతాన్ని రుద్దకుండా, మంచితనాన్ని విమర్శనాత్మకంగా పరిశీలించడం, రోజువారీ జీవితంలో దానిని ఎలా ఆచరణలో పెట్టవచ్చో తెలుసుకోవడానికి ఈ కోర్సు తోడ్పడుతుంది. కేవలం థియరీగా నేర్చుకోవడమే కాకుండా రాబోయే రోజుల్లో తాము ఎలాంటి భారతదేశాన్ని నిర్మించాలనుకుంటున్నారనే అంశంపై విద్యార్థుల రిఫ్లెక్షన్‌తో ఈ కోర్సు ముగుస్తుంది.సాంకేతిక పరిజ్ఞానంతో పాటు సామాజిక స్పృహ ఉన్న ఉత్తమ పౌరులను తీర్చిదిద్దడంలో ఐఐటీ హైదరాబాద్ చేపట్టిన ఈ ప్రయోగం దేశవ్యాప్తంగా విద్యావేత్తల ప్రశంసలు అందుకుంటోంది.

title: Scientists discover yak-like Ice Age mammal in Siberian cave through DNA analysis | Trending
description: A Siberian cave known for its Denisovan remains has yielded a new discovery, a previously unknown Ice Age mammal closely related to modern yaks.  | Trending
content: Scientists have identified a previously unknown Ice Age mammal closely related to modern yaks by analysing ancient DNA recovered from tiny bone fragments in Siberia. The discovery was made at Denisova Cave, a site famous for revealing evidence of an extinct human lineage called the Denisovans. Ancient DNA reveals a distinct mammalAccording to Reuters, researchers examined 20 bone fragments, including 14 recovered from Denisova Cave and six from other sites in the surrounding region. The remains were too small and fragmented to reveal the animal’s identity through their physical features alone.The breakthrough came from genetic analysis. Scientists generated 20 ancient genomes and found that the animal belonged to a distinct bovine lineage that began diverging from the ancestors of modern yaks around 400,000 years ago.The researchers have provisionally called the animal “Yak X”. They have not assigned it a formal scientific name because the available bones do not provide enough anatomical evidence to establish its identity through conventional classification.(Also Read: Airbnb bans hosts from asking guests to strip beds, wash dishes and do other time-consuming chores)“It is unusual, especially to recognize a large mammal species from small, unidentifiable fragments,” evolutionary geneticist Love Dalén told Reuters. Dalén is a senior author of the study published in the journal Current Biology.What did Yak X look like?Although its exact appearance remains uncertain, researchers believe Yak X probably resembled a modern yak more closely than a bison because of its evolutionary relationship with the animal.Yaks are sturdy, horned bovines known for their long fur and ability to survive in cold, high altitude environments. Today, wild yaks are mainly found on the Tibetan Plateau.According to a study published in Current Biology, the genetic evidence also suggests that Yak X experienced a population decline during the Ice Age. The lineage eventually disappeared, although scientists cannot establish the precise circumstances of its extinction.Did Denisovans hunt Yak X?Yak X shared its habitat with several well-known Ice Age animals, including woolly mammoths, woolly rhinoceroses, steppe bison and aurochs, the extinct wild ancestors of modern domestic cattle.(Also Read: Ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt says AI could leave companies needing ‘a couple of thousand’ fewer workers)The Centre for Palaeogenetics research team said the discovery adds to evidence that the Altai region was home to a wide diversity of mammals and ancient human relatives.Denisovans, an extinct human lineage first identified in the cave in 2008, also lived in the region. Researchers believe they may have hunted Yak X, though this remains unconfirmed.

title: My 20s were avoidable: Comedian Sumukhi Suresh on exploring dating, female friendship in 'Hoemonal' | Bollywood
description: My 20s were avoidable: Comedian Sumukhi Suresh on exploring dating, female friendship in 'Hoemonal'  | Bollywood
content: New Delhi, Comedian Sumukhi Suresh was just coming out of a long-term relationship when she got the idea for "Hoemonal", her new Netflix special, which she describes as a "chick-flick" about a conservatively-raised woman.A multi-hyphenate artiste, Suresh is known as a writer, comedian and actor who switches easily between her different identities. The special, she said, is about women like her, who are earning money and now feel "guilty about spending it"."I think 'Hoemonal' on Netflix is a proper comfort chick-flick/rom-com that you will watch and keep watching. It's about a conservatively-raised girl because I was raised very conservatively. I was with someone for a really long time. And then that ended."And suddenly I was like, 'Oh, I have to start dating'. And I have never experienced those things. So, it is a conservatively-raised girl failing to be a hoe while managing her hormones," Suresh told PTI in an interview.In the over-one-hour-long show, the comedian talks about breaking up, spectacularly failing to figure out dating apps, female friendships and how she was raised to be a "sindoor chaser".Suresh said when she was asked what her target audience for the special was, she said "25 and above" but those in their 20s are also welcome."I think my 20s were very avoidable. I actually started enjoying life at 30. I feel like most women are living their 20s in their 30s. The earlier idea was that you study, graduate, have a job and then any minute you will find someone or you will be partnered up. And then a good chunk went, 'Maybe I don't want to.' And then you start building your life... So, I feel like I was a teenager, then I came directly to my 30s," Suresh said.The comedian, who wrote and starred in the popular two-season comedy drama series "Pushpavalli" in 2017, said she loves the energy of live performances."I have too much fun on stage. The dissipation of my energy into the audience is my favourite thing to do. With 'Hoemonal', every audience has been genuinely beautiful... Usually, specials are done under a special time frame but I was like, 'I will take as much time as I want.' I think this show became what it was in 2023-2024 when I got my producer Kim Sharma on board," Suresh said.The comedian said Sharma built the show into a business IP, taking it from a 1,000-seater venue to selling 5,000 tickets for a performance in Bengaluru."And these things, as much as it may seem like they are not important, they are a boost for a comedian and artiste. It almost gives you a responsibility. Now, every time you go on stage, you have to perform properly for it to continue. So, it's been a fun journey."The show, she said, evolved through her stage performances as it is not set on specific punchlines."I don't really write... I do stand up where I perform again and again until it becomes the piece it is. So, basically it's the reverse process of putting it together. First, you have to throw yourself to the deep end. I made the mistake of trying to write my last special and then realised, 'No, I'm someone who loves performing.' So, I found the show in its performance," she explained."'Hoemonal' has laughter, romance, happiness, sadness and tears. It is a roller coaster of those emotions. So at any point if I give you a joke, you will snap out of it. It needs to seem like your best friend or sister is standing in front of you and she is having a meltdown and you're like, 'this girl is crazy'. So, you have to give the story of what happened."Similarly, her show "Pushpavalli" was born out of her love for fiction and writing."For me, to think that I'm doing something unique as a female comedian, I needed to know what the industry was. And I never did. I was working for a food safety lab. When I entered this, I didn't even know whether this space was male-friendly or female-friendly."All I wanted was to act in a show. And they were like, 'Hey, you can't be a lead.' I'm like, 'Oh, but why?' They're like, no one writes for someone with my body frame. I was like, 'What's body frame? Cast me anywhere.' So, they were like, 'You write a show'. I said, 'Okay, then I'll write a show.' I didn't have time to understand the uniqueness of the situation," she said."Pushpavalli", about a woman who falls for a guy during a chance encounter where she mistakes his kindness for love and starts stalking him, was written by Suresh with Ayesha Nair and Naveen Richard. It was a success and opened doors for other acting and writing opportunities for her.Since "Pushpavalli", Suresh has worked with writer-director Vikramaditya Motwane on "CTRL" and is collaborating with filmmaker Tushar Hiranandani and producer Rhea Kapoor on different projects. She has also acted in "The Royals" and Vir Das' "Happy Patel: Khatarnak Jasoos".She is currently shooting for Ekta Kapoor-produced "Ragini MMS 3" that features Tamannaah Bhatia and Nargis Fakhri.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title:
AI compute is the new oil—and needs a new market | Technology News
(HT Tech)
description: Financial firms race to create instruments to trade processing power | Technology News
content: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE is changing many things about the modern world. Language is no exception. The word “compute”, for instance, used to be regarded as a verb. Today even grammar pedants grudgingly accept it as a noun, referring to the processing power generated by advanced chips. This new, non-verbal compute is the fuel of a technological revolution.Demand for processing oomph has surged, and it is in short supply. About $360bn was spent on AI compute last year around the world, according to Boston Consulting Group, about 50% more than on copper. By 2030 BCG expects $2.3trn in transactions, roughly the size of the global trade in crude oil today.For all its impressive size, however, the compute market lacks sophistication. The “hyperscalers” (a still somewhat arcane piece of IT jargon for a handful of giant cloud-computing providers including Amazon, Google and Microsoft) and frontier AI labs (such as Anthropic and OpenAI) make deals for tens or even hundreds of billions of dollars of compute. But such arrangements are unavailable to thousands of smaller firms. Buyers and sellers also have few of the derivatives that in established markets allow them to hedge their exposures and speculate.The compute supply chain, then, looks ripe for marketisation. In the most simple form, chipmakers (like Nvidia and AMD) sell advanced AI semiconductors to equipment manufacturers (such as Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprises), which package the silicon into racks and servers to sell to data-centre operators. Besides the hyperscalers, these include a few large “neoclouds” (one more linguistic innovation, denoting independent providers like CoreWeave and Nebius) and hundreds of smaller, less well-known firms.The operators, in turn, rent out access to compute to customers for a fixed period, often several years. Customers range from the hyperscalers (which supplement their in-house compute with rentals) to startups running open-source AI models.So far, so simple—in theory. In practice, things quickly get complicated. That is because compute is heterogeneous: different chips are sold in different servers, at different locations, for different time periods. Matching buyers and sellers is finicky. Every business that needs processing power has a “compute guy” (or several) buying second-hand capacity through an opaque network of middlemen. Many of these informal brokers, some shadier than others, tout their offerings through messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram. The whole thing looks less like trading a high-tech commodity and more like peddling illegal drugs.In a market that is so fractured and immature, providers and purchasers alike prefer the safety of long-term contracts. On paper, these guarantee capacity to users and revenues for themselves. In reality, given how fast the technology and the market of AI are evolving, it is hard to tell how much such deals are worth: today’s buyers and sellers may not be around in a few years to honour their commitments. The surging yields on CoreWeave’s bonds highlight the uncertainty. Who will make a killing? And who may not make it at all? With lenders struggling to price risk, many smaller operators buying and renting compute face double-digit interest rates.Fortunately for everyone involved, proper markets are being built around the compute supply chain. Some budding bourses, such as Compute Exchange, list GPUs (the increasingly familiar shorthand for graphics-processing units, AI’s silicon workhorse) by location, rental duration, price and availability. Titans of global derivatives trading, including CME Group and the Intercontinental Exchange, hope to launch their own compute futures. They have teamed up with startups pioneering compute indices, pegged to the rental price of popular AI chips. They await regulatory approval.Rather than wait for exchange-traded derivatives to be approved, some compute-market pioneers are creating over-the-counter instruments of the sort common in credit and foreign-exchange markets. In March a startup called Anera Labs arranged a six-figure pilot trade for June with FalconX, a cryptocurrency broker, based on the future rental price of Nvidia’s popular H100 GPUs.Luxor, another startup, offers operators swap-like contracts that guarantee fixed cashflow per server, per hour. If the spot price for compute is below the price agreed in the swap, the operator is paid the difference. If the spot price is higher, it is the operator that pays. This payment, explains Ethan Vera, one of the firm’s co-founders, may for example be made through a revenue-sharing arrangement. Luxor’s bespoke derivatives are modest for now, in the tens of millions of dollars, but the potential is vast.As American exchanges await the thumbs-up from regulators, upstarts are getting off the ground elsewhere. From its exchange in Bermuda, Architect Financial Technologies, founded in 2023, offers futures in compute linked to the value of chips in America. The firm has also recently launched a platform where model-makers bid to provide “inference”—the useful output produced by an AI model in response to a prompt—rather than the underlying compute capacity. Brett Harrison, the company’s founder and boss, believes that inference may prove easier to standardise than compute.Given the uncertainty surrounding the all-new market, it is attracting risk-takers. Many, including Mr Harrison, spent time in crypto, once the most compute-intensive enterprise out there, which attracted financial engineers trying to turn processing power into a tradable asset. Mr Harrison was president of FTX US, the American arm of the crypto exchange founded by Sam Bankman Fried, resigning two months before the parent firm’s bankruptcy amid fraud in November 2022. Luxor once primarily served bitcoin miners. One of Anera’s co-founders, Vishwa Naik, was a crypto entrepreneur. (CoreWeave and some other neoclouds also began life as crypto-mining businesses.)AI’s finance brosAs opportunities grow, established financial companies are taking more of an interest. DRW and Jump Trading, two large market-makers, have both invested in Silicon Data, the compute-focused research firm with which CME hopes to launch its futures. Each market-maker has also assembled its own team to trade the new commodity. This month Jump Trading acquired Ito Markets, a compute-trading startup, whose founders will lead its efforts to break into the new industry.David Olsen, Jump’s investment chief, points out that the market will grow more rapidly with the right institutions, such as clearing houses that limit the risk of blow-ups by ensuring that contracts are honoured by both sides of a trade. “We’re a long way from that,” he acknowledges, echoing many in this industry who think it may take years or even decades for the market to mature. “But”, he adds, “we want to be part of that discussion.”His desire is unsurprising. After all, with surging demand for what remains a scarce commodity, and with so many businesses around the world exposed to it, the prize is enormous.Mr Naik of Anera, who in his pre-crypto days was an oil trader at Reliance Industries, an Indian conglomerate, likens today’s moment in the compute market to the last days of the “seven sisters”, a cartel of Western giants that ruled the global petroleum trade between the late 1920s and the 1970s. Their chokehold was broken by nationalisation (in many exporting countries) and the rise of the open oil market (just about everywhere). As governments covetously eye the AI labs and ventures like Anera attempt to create a market from scratch, you do not need to squint too hard to see a similar future for compute.
