title: Woman dies after kite string slits throat in Karnataka's Hubballi | Bengaluru
description: Woman dies after kite string slits throat in Karnataka's Hubballi  | Bengaluru News
content: Hubballi , A 38-year-old woman died after a sharp kite string allegedly got entangled around her neck and slit her throat while she was riding a two-wheeler in Hubballi city, police said on Friday.The deceased was identified as Vidya Manjunath Gowdar, a resident of Bharat Nagar in Old Hubballi. She was working as a laboratory technician at a hospital, they said.The incident occurred on Thursday near Shivashankar Colony on Karwar Road, within the limits of Old Hubballi police station, when she was on her way to work, police said.According to police, the kite string allegedly got entangled around her neck, causing her to lose control of the two-wheeler and fall on the road. She sustained severe injuries and died on the spot.Hubballi-Dharwad Police Commissioner Borase Bhushan Gulabrao said teams had been formed at all police stations to identify and seize banned Chinese manja being sold in the city.Criminal cases would be registered against those selling the hazardous string, while action would also be taken against those found using it, irrespective of whether they were students or adults, he said.In the case of minors, action would also be initiated against their parents for allegedly endangering public life, the commissioner said.The police had earlier conducted social media awareness campaigns urging people not to use Chinese manja and to opt for regular kite string instead, he said.Appealing to people to report instances of people using the hazardous string through the police's social media handles, Gulabrao said teams would respond immediately and seize the material."Your fun should not take the life of others. Celebrate responsibly," he said.Meanwhile, doctors at the hospital where the victim was employed demanded stringent punishment for those responsible and urged the authorities to take effective measures to prevent such incidents in the future.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: శుక్రాదిత్య రాజయోగంతో మూడు రాశులకు నవంబర్ 6 లోపే జాక్‌పాట్.. కెరీర్‌లో ఊహించని మార్పులు! | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: జ్యోతిష్య నమ్మకాల ప్రకారం, సూర్యుడు, శుక్రుడు తులా రాశిలో సంచరించడం వల్ల శుక్రాదిత్య యోగం ఏర్పడిందని ఈ కథనం పేర్కొంటోంది. అక్టోబర్ 17 నుంచి నవంబర్ 6 వరకు ఈ యోగం ప్రభావంతో కొన్ని రాశుల వారికి అనుకూల ఫలితాలు కలుగుతాయని జ్యోతిష్య అంచనాలు చెబుతున్నాయి.
content: గ్రహాలు ఎప్పటికప్పుడు వాటి రాశులను, నక్షత్రాలను మారుస్తాయి. అలాంటప్పుడు శుభ ఫలితాలను, అశుభ ఫలితాలను చూస్తూ ఉంటాం. ఒక్కోసారి కొన్ని రాశుల వారికి మంచి జరిగితే, ఒక్కోసారి సమస్యలను ఎదుర్కోవాల్సి ఉంటుంది.నవంబర్ నెల కొన్ని రాశుల వారికి అదృష్టాన్ని తీసుకురాబోతోంది. ఈ రాశుల వారు శుక్ర రాజయోగంతో అనేక విధాలుగా ప్రయోజనాలను పొందబోతున్నారు. మరి, నవంబర్ నెలలో శుక్రాదిత్య రాజయోగంతో ఏ రాశుల వారికి బాగా కలిసి రాబోతోంది? ఎవరు ఎలాంటి లాభాలను పొందుతారో ఇప్పుడు తెలుసుకుందాం.అక్టోబర్ 17న సూర్యుడు తులా రాశిలోకి ప్రవేశించాడు. శుక్రుడుతులా రాశిలో సంచారం చేస్తున్నాడు. దాంతో శుక్రుడితో కలిపి రాజయోగాన్ని ఏర్పరిచాడు. ఈ సంచారం నవంబర్ 6 వరకు ఉంటుంది. దీని కారణంగా కొన్ని రాశుల వారు భారీగా లాభాలను పొందబోతున్నారు.అక్టోబర్ 17 నుంచి నవంబర్ 6 వరకు ఈ రాశుల వారికి బాగా కలిసి రాబోతోంది. ఈ సమయంలో కష్టపడినా ఫలితం రాకపోయినట్లయితే, నవంబర్ 6లోగా మీరు శుభవార్తలను, తగిన ఫలితాలను చూడొచ్చు.మేష రాశిమేష రాశి వారికి ఈ యోగం శుభ ఫలితాలను అందిస్తుంది. సానుకూల మార్పులను చూస్తారు. కెరీర్‌లో కూడా అద్భుతమైన మలుపులు ఉంటాయి. నిరుద్యోగులకు కొత్త బాధ్యతలు వస్తాయి. ఈ కారణంగా పని ప్రదేశంలో ప్రశంసలు పొందుతారు.భారీగా ఇన్వెస్ట్‌మెంట్ల నుంచి లాభాలను పొందే అవకాశాలు కూడా ఎక్కువగా కనిపిస్తున్నాయి. వివిధ మార్గాల ద్వారా డబ్బు సంపాదిస్తారు. ఆర్థిక పరిస్థితి మెరుగుపడుతుంది. వ్యక్తిగత జీవితంలో కూడా మార్పులు ఉంటాయి. రిలేషన్‌షిప్ మరింత మధురంగా మారుతుంది.తులా రాశితులా రాశి వారు నవంబర్ 6లోపు అద్భుతమైన ఫలితాలను చూస్తారు. అవకాశాలను కూడా ఈ సమయంలో విజయవంతంగా పూర్తి చేస్తారు. సమస్యలన్నీ కూడా ఇట్టే పరిష్కారం అవుతాయి. సరైన నిర్ణయాలు తీసుకుంటారు. జీవితంలో సానుకూల మార్పులను చూస్తారు.ధనుస్సు రాశిధనుస్సు రాశి వారికి అద్భుతమైన సమయం. ఈ సమయంలో ఈ రాశి వారి అదృష్టం డబుల్ అవుతుంది. వ్యాపారస్తులకు కూడా ఇది శుభ సమయం. కొత్త ప్లాన్‌లను విజయవంతంగా పూర్తి చేస్తారు. కెరీర్‌లో కూడా ఓ మెట్టు పైకి వెళ్తారు. ఉద్యోగం మారాలని అనుకుంటున్నట్లయితే, ఇది సరైన సమయం. మంచి అవకాశాలు వస్తాయి. సరిగ్గా ప్రణాళికతో పనులు చేస్తే అవకాశాలు పెరుగుతాయి. అనుకున్న వాటిని విజయవంతంగా పూర్తి చేయొచ్చు.

title: Missing 7-year-old girl found raped, murdered in Chhattisgarh's Korba; one held | Hindustan Times
description: Missing 7-year-old girl found raped, murdered in Chhattisgarh's Korba; one held
content: Korba, A seven-year-old girl who went missing three days ago was found raped and murdered in Chhattisgarh's Korba district, leading to the arrest of a 42-year-old man tracked down by a police sniffer dog, an official said on Friday.The body of the child, who went missing while running an errand at a grocery store, was found in the bushes behind a poultry farm in the Rajgamar police chowki area on Thursday morning, the official said.He said that the girl's father had reported her missing on the evening of October 19, informing the police that his daughter had not returned home from the shop.The girl's father, a native of Faguram village in Sakti district, had moved to Rajgamar with his four children four months ago, and he worked at a poultry farm to support his family, the official said.Police launched a search to trace the girl. However, on Thursday morning, they received information about a body lying in bushes behind the poultry farm, and a forensic team and a police dog were also called in to assist the investigation, he said.During the probe, the police sniffer dog traced the accused's house in the Ravanbhatha locality of Rajgamar. Based on the clue, police tracked down and arrested the accused, identified as Ajay aka Amit Chauhan from Devmati Para in the Bango police station area, 60 km away, the official said.Korba Additional Superintendent of Police Lakhan Patle said that the accused had two wives and had come to visit his second wife in the Ravanbhatha locality on the day of the murder.Chauhan spotted the victim alone, and He allegedly sexually assaulted and killed her, and fled the scene, Patle said.The accused confessed to the crime, and further investigation is underway, police said.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Ranabaali box office collection day 7: Vijay Deverakonda, Rashmika Mandanna film yet to cross  ₹45 crore; sees further dip | Hindustan Times
description: Rahul Sankrityan's period action drama Ranabaali, featuring Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna, opened to lukewarm reviews.
content: Rahul Sankrityan’s period drama Ranabaali, starring Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna in lead roles, was released in theatres on October 16. The film, which opened to lukewarm reviews, crossed the ₹40 crore mark in India before the end of its first week. Ranabaali has shown a dip in collections on Thursday.Ranabaali box office collectionAccording to the trade website, Sacnilk Ranabaali collected ₹2.98 crore net in India on Thursday, taking its domestic total to ₹45.03 crore. It showed an occupancy of 28.35 % from 21112 shows. Ranabaali registered an opening of ₹9.25 crore last Friday. It dipped and then held steady, collecting ₹7.30 crore and ₹7.50 crore on Saturday and Sunday, respectively.On Monday, Ranabaali collected ₹5.40 crore, then spiked on Tuesday due to Dussehra, bringing in ₹7.10 crore. On Wednesday, it collected ₹5.50 crore. With the weekend approaching, it remains to be seen whether the film will see a spike in collections. Despite competition from Jailer 2’s Telugu-dubbed version, Ranabaali has held steady for the most part. For context, Deverakonda’s previous film, Kingdom, had brought in ₹46.15 crore in seven days after its release. The Family Star made only ₹18.25 crore, and Kushi brought in ₹41.52 crore.About RanabaaliRanabaali is directed by Rahul Sankrityan, produced by Mythri Movie Makers, and presented by T-Series Films. It stars Deverakonda in the titular role and Rashmika as his wife, Jayamma. Arnold Vosloo plays the film’s main antagonist as Sir Theodore Hector. Set in 19th-century South India, it tells the story of a famine caused by colonial rule that left many dead. Ranabaali fights back against the British to keep his people alive.After the film’s release, Rashmika, who worked alongside Allu Arjun in Sukumar’s Pushpa films, compared her husband’s performance to his. “When I was seeing Ranabaali be Ranabaali, there’s a full difference between Vijay and Ranabaali. Completely. Even on set, when I would speak to him off shooting, there’s one sense of Ranabaali. I’m like, where is Viju? You know?” she said. She also added, “It took me time, but I understood with what gravitas he’s performing, at what level he’s performing it. When you do some characters, they just consume you fully. Every cell of you feels those emotions, that performance. So, I watched all that. This was a very new experience for me.” Ranabaali grossed ₹59.65 crore worldwide in six days of its release.

title: India v NZ: Naman Dhir and the value of arriving ready | Cricket
description: At Bengaluru, and now at Christchurch, Dhir feels like a batter not intimidated by the absence of time  | Cricket
content: The curious thing about Naman Dhir is how little time he seems to need to switch on. In a format in which the first few deliveries can determine whether a batter is going to have an innings or merely appear in one, Dhir has begun to make a virtue of skipping the preliminaries. He arrives, takes stock, and starts hitting. It can be untidy at times, and sometimes it can border on the spectacular. But it is increasingly proving to be useful.At Christchurch against New Zealand on Thursday, India needed 55 from five overs just after Dhir walked in during the 15th over of a chase of 226. Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma had laid the platform, and Shreyas Iyer had taken on the business of keeping the chase together. But Iyer would soon fall, leaving India needing 16 from 11 balls and little time for a new batter to settle down. Already in the swing of things, Dhir prevented that chaos.Also Read: Cricket gave me money and peace, says spinner Bhargav Bhatt at 100 His unbeaten 42 — from just 15 balls — was not an uninterrupted exhibition of clean hitting. That is part of what made it interesting. Dhir cut Mitchell Santner behind square, slog-swept him towards cow corner and watched Nathan Smith's attempt at a catch end in a six.Against Nathan Smith, an outside edge flew towards short third, where Lockie Ferguson failed to complete a difficult chance. Then, another top edge cleared short fine leg. A strain of luck ran through his innings, helped a bit by New Zealand's poor fielding as well.But fortune is not the same as passivity. Dhir gave himself opportunities to score, forced the fielders into action and ensured that the situation never became an excuse for hesitation. It was the kind of busy ending that a team ideally seeks to deflect from the fact that they had lost a cluster of wickets cheaply after such a start that should have guaranteed a comfortable win.Efficient way, for sureThe final over was an appropriately messy conclusion. Matt Henry missed his yorker and offered a full toss, which Dhir lofted over mid-off for four despite losing his bottom hand. Then came a short ball, a top edge and six over Tim Seifert. Dhir's finishing was hardly a portrait of technical perfection, but it was an efficient way of ending a game.There is a distinction worth making here. India possess big hitters of the ball. What they need, particularly in the middle and lower order, are players in the mould of Rinku Singh who can do it without requiring a long introduction. A batter arriving with 30 balls remaining can’t always afford the conventional business of taking a few deliveries to settle in. Dhir seems to understand that exceptionally well.His brief innings against West Indies in Bengaluru last week offered an even more concentrated illustration. In a match reduced to nine overs per side, India were 88/4 with 17 balls remaining when he came in to hammer 24 from six deliveries, including three sixes and a four. Using his height and high grip, he chose deep square-leg, mid-off and long-off for the three boundary hits off Keemo Paul before thumping Shamar Springer over long-off for another six.It’s not simply that he swings hard. Dhir’s height and reach give him access to different areas, while his willingness to attack early puts pressure on a bowler who might otherwise spend the first few deliveries establishing control. The risk is obvious—a batter who begins at full throttle can run out of options as quickly as he runs out of deliveries. The reward is that he can make a small opportunity count, which is all that matters in T20.The numbers support the impression, though they should be handled with some care. In overs 16 to 20 of T20 matches, Dhir has scored 341 runs from 167 balls, with 10 dismissals. His strike rate is 204.19, with 34 fours and 19 sixes. The sample is limited, but the numbers can’t tell us how he will respond when the pitch is slow, when the bowling is disciplined or the target requires calculation rather than assault.They do, however, tell us that Dhir’s instincts are currently extremely valuable. The next step is to discover how much lies beyond that instinct. For now, Dhir has offered two useful glimpses—at Bengaluru and Christchurch—of a batter who doesn’t appear intimidated by the lack of time. That is reason enough to keep Dhir in the loop.

title: Netflix Today: నెట్‌ఫ్లిక్స్‌లో ఈరోజు థ్రిల్లర్ మూవీస్, సిరీస్ జాతర.. మలయాళ, తమిళ, హిందీ థ్రిల్లర్లు, క్రైమ్ థ్రిల్లర్లు | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: Netflix Today Releases October 23rd 2026: నెట్‌ఫ్లిక్స్ లోకి ఈరోజు అంటే అక్టోబర్ 23న థ్రిల్లర్, క్రైమ్ థ్రిల్లర్ సినిమాలు, వెబ్ సిరీస్ జాతర ఉంది. మలయాళ థ్రిల్లర్, తమిళ బోల్డ్ మూవీ, హిందీ క్రైమ్ థ్రిల్లర్ సినిమాలతోపాటు ఇంగ్లిష్ వెబ్ సిరీస్ కూడా వచ్చింది.
content: Netflix Today Releases October 23rd 2026: ఓటీటీలో వీకెండ్ ఏం చూడాలా అని పెద్దగా ఆలోచించాల్సిన అవసరం లేకుండా నెట్‌ఫ్లిక్స్ శుక్రవారం (అక్టోబర్ 23) ప్రేక్షకులకు మంచి కంటెంట్ తీసుకొచ్చింది. అందులోనూ థ్రిల్లర్ అభిమానులకైతే మంచి విందు భోజనమే. మరి ఈరోజు వచ్చిన ఆ మూవీస్, వెబ్ సిరీస్ ఏవో ఇక్కడ చూడండి.1. మలయాళం టైమ్-లూప్ థ్రిల్లర్ 'ధూమకేతు' (Dhoomakethu)మలయాళంలో విమర్శకుల ప్రశంసలు అందుకున్న వినూత్న టైమ్-లూప్ కామెడీ థ్రిల్లర్ 'ధూమకేతు'. సజిన్ గోపు, నిఖిలా విమల్ జంటగా నటించిన ఈ మూవీ అక్టోబర్ 23 నుంచి నెట్‌ఫ్లిక్స్‌లో స్ట్రీమింగ్ అవుతోంది. మలయాళంతోపాటు తెలుగు, తమిళం, కన్నడ, హిందీ భాషల్లో అందుబాటులో ఉంది.తన పెళ్లి రోజే హత్యకు గురయ్యే హీరో, మళ్లీ మళ్లీ అదే రోజు ఉదయానికి చేరుకోవడం, తన చావు నుంచి తప్పించుకోవడానికి చేసే ప్రయత్నాలు ప్రేక్షకులకు పుష్కలంగా నవ్వులు, థ్రిల్‌ను పంచుతాయి. అసలు అలా ఎందుకు జరిగింది? దాని వెనుక ఉన్న అసలు కథేంటి అన్నది ఈ మూవీలో చూడొచ్చు.2. కీర్తి సురేష్ 'డోరతీ' (Dorothy)జాతీయ అవార్డు గ్రహీత కీర్తి సురేష్ నటించిన ఇంటెన్స్ తమిళ సోషల్ క్రైమ్ డ్రామా 'డోరతీ'. 1990ల కాలం నాటి గ్రామీణ నేపథ్యంలో సాగే ఈ కథలో కుల వివక్ష, సమాజంలో మహిళలు ఎదుర్కొనే అణచివేత, పాత ఆలోచనలను ధిక్కరించే ఇద్దరు చిన్ననాటి స్నేహితుల పోరాటాన్ని కళ్లకు కట్టినట్లు తెరకెక్కించారు. తెలుగులోనూ ఈ మూవీ చూడొచ్చు.3. లూపిన్: పార్ట్ 4 (Lupin: Part 4)గ్లోబల్ వైడ్‌గా కోట్లాది మంది వీక్షకులను సొంతం చేసుకున్న ఫ్రెంచ్ మిస్టరీ రివేంజ్ థ్రిల్లర్ 'లూపిన్'. ఒమర్ సై (Omar Sy) ప్రధాన పాత్రలో నటించిన ఈ ఫ్రాంచైజ్ 4వ భాగం అక్టోబర్ 23న స్ట్రీమింగ్ కు వచ్చింది. అర్సేన్ లూపిన్ అనే జెంటిల్‌మన్ దొంగ ప్రేరణతో అస్సానే దియోప్ తన తండ్రిపై పడిన నిందను తొలగించుకోవడానికి, శత్రువుల కుట్రలను ఛేదించడానికి చేసే కొత్త మిషన్ ఈ పార్ట్ 4లో చూపించబోతున్నారు.4. మనోజ్ బాజ్‌పాయ్ 'గజబ్ రాత్' (Gajab Raat)బహుముఖ ప్రజ్ఞాశాలి మనోజ్ బాజ్‌పాయ్, నుస్రత్ భరుచా, సాఖిబ్ సలీమ్ ప్రధాన పాత్రల్లో నటించిన బాలీవుడ్ క్రైమ్ సస్పెన్స్ థ్రిల్లర్ 'గజబ్ రాత్'. ఒకే ఒక్క రాత్రి వేళ పోలీస్ అధికారి తీసుకునే ఓ తొందరపాటు నిర్ణయం ఎంతటి అనర్థాలకు దారితీసింది? సస్పెన్స్, డార్క్ కామెడీతో కూడిన ఆ రాత్రి మిస్టరీ ఏమిటనేది ఈ సినిమాలో ఉత్కంఠభరితంగా ఆవిష్కరించారు.5. సర్వైవింగ్ హరికేన్ ఓటిస్ (Surviving Hurricane Otis)2023లో మెక్సికోలోని అకాపుల్కో నగరాన్ని వణికించిన భయంకరమైన 'కేటగిరీ-5' హరికేన్ 'ఓటిస్' ఆధారంగా రూపొందించిన నేచురల్ డిజాస్టర్ థ్రిల్లర్ మూవీ ఇది. ఊహించని విధ్వంసం మధ్య సాధారణ ప్రజలు తమ ప్రాణాలను కాపాడుకోవడానికి, కుటుంబాలను కాపాడుకోవడానికి చేసిన పోరాటాన్ని ఈ సినిమాలో కళ్లకు కట్టినట్లు చూపించారు.

title: Wooden Street Highlights Thoughtful Furniture Choices for Delhi Homes This Festive Season | Hindustan Times
description: Wooden Street’s festive message focuses on furniture choices that remain useful beyond the celebrations, including durable sofas, dining tables and storage.
content: New Delhi: As households prepare for festive celebrations, furniture and home furnishing brand Wooden Street is highlighting the importance of comfortable, functional and thoughtfully selected furniture. With family gatherings and celebrations bringing additional activity into homes, the brand's furniture offerings address a range of everyday furnishing requirements, including seating, dining and storage.The festive calendar, stretching from Dussehra and Karwa Chauth to Dhanteras and Diwali, often brings increased activity into homes. Family gatherings, celebrations and visits from relatives place greater demands on living rooms, dining areas and bedrooms. For many households, this period also provides an opportunity to reassess their furniture arrangements and identify areas where additional seating, storage or more practical furniture could improve everyday convenience.Understanding the Changing Needs of Delhi HomesFrom apartments in Dwarka and builder floors in Rajouri Garden to independent residences in Greater Kailash, Delhi homes vary considerably in size, layout and furnishing requirements. However, the need to balance comfort, available space and functionality remains common across different households.During festive gatherings, living rooms frequently become shared spaces for conversations, celebrations and family activities. Dining areas accommodate additional guests, while bedrooms may need to serve visiting relatives. These changing requirements can highlight the importance of furniture that supports both regular household routines and occasional gatherings.The brand's festive furnishing approach places emphasis on evaluating existing furniture, available space and everyday household requirements before making new purchases..Rather than focusing exclusively on extensive home renovations, the campaign's positioning centres on selecting individual furniture pieces that complement existing interiors and address practical household requirements.Combining Online Convenience with In-Store ExperienceFurniture selection involves several considerations, including dimensions, materials, finishes, comfort and suitability for a particular room. While online platforms allow customers to explore designs and compare options, physical store visits can provide a clearer understanding of how individual products look and feel.Customers exploring the furniture market in Delhi can consider Wooden Street's furniture offerings across categories such as sofas, beds, dining tables and storage solutions.An in-store experience allows buyers to assess seating comfort, examine finishes and understand the proportions of furniture before making purchasing decisions. Such considerations become particularly important in urban homes where available floor space and room layouts influence furniture selection.Homeowners can also begin their search by exploring options through Wooden Street's online furniture platform, which features furniture across multiple categories.Preparing room measurements, identifying preferred designs and establishing a budget before visiting a store can help customers narrow their choices and make more informed decisions.Creating Comfortable Spaces for Festive GatheringsFestive preparations often involve rearranging existing furniture to accommodate visitors and create a welcoming atmosphere. Maintaining clear pathways, introducing flexible seating arrangements and using practical storage solutions can help households manage additional activity without overcrowding their interiors.A well-planned living room can accommodate family gatherings while continuing to serve everyday needs. Similarly, an appropriately sized dining table can support both regular meals and festive occasions.Materials, colours and finishes also contribute to the overall appearance of a home. Wooden furniture, for instance, can complement traditional decorative elements such as brass lamps, festive textiles and floral arrangements while remaining suitable for contemporary interiors.The emphasis is on creating spaces that reflect individual preferences without compromising functionality.Furniture Choices Beyond the Festive SeasonAlthough festivals frequently encourage households to refresh their interiors, furniture purchases are generally long-term decisions. Factors such as durability, maintenance, comfort and compatibility with existing furnishings remain relevant after the celebrations conclude.Replacing an ageing sofa, choosing a dining table suited to available space or introducing additional storage can address everyday household requirements beyond festive gatherings.Wooden Street's festive furnishing message connects seasonal home preparations with longer-term furniture planning, highlighting the importance of comfort, practicality and thoughtful design.As Delhi families prepare to welcome relatives and friends during the festive period, Wooden Street's campaign places attention on practical furnishing decisions that support comfortable living.The underlying message is that a festive home refresh need not involve replacing every piece of furniture. Thoughtful additions and suitable arrangements can help create spaces that remain welcoming, functional and comfortable long after the decorations have been packed away.Note to readers: This article is part of HT's paid consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. HT assumes no editorial responsibility for the content, including its accuracy, completeness, or any errors or omissions. Readers are advised to verify all information independently.

title: Ryan Gosling revives band Dead Man's Bones after 17 years, to release new music on Oct 27 | Hollywood
description: Ryan Gosling revives band Dead Man's Bones after 17 years, to release new music on Oct 27  | Hollywood
content: Los Angeles, Hollywood star Ryan Gosling won over audiences with his musical performances in "La La Land" and "Barbie", and now he has revived his band Dead Man's Bones, which will release new music on October 27.The band, comprising Gosling and musician Zach Shields, shared an announcement video on Instagram, featuring a haunting voice reciting a poem about ghosts, shadows and the night before a young girl announces the release date.The upcoming release will mark the duo's first new music in 17 years, following its self-titled debut album in 2009.Gosling's partner, actor Eva Mendes, had hinted at the band's return through recent social media posts. In one of the posts, she had written, "Trying to summon new music from Dead Man's Bones".Following the announcement on Thursday night, she wrote, "He came through on his promise to me."As a movie star, Gosling has featured in critically acclaimed films and commercial blockbusters such as "The Notebook", "Blue Valentine", "Drive", "The Big Short", "La La Land", "Blade Runner 2049", "Barbie" and most recently "Project Hail Mary".But music has been an important part of some of his most recognisable screen performances. In Damien Chazelle's 2016 musical "La La Land", he played jazz pianist Sebastian opposite Emma Stone, performing songs including "City of Stars" and "A Lovely Night".The film earned him a Golden Globe Award for best actor in a musical or comedy.He returned to the musical spotlight in Greta Gerwig's 2023 blockbuster "Barbie", in which he played Ken and performed the popular song "I'm Just Ken".The track became one of the film's most talked-about moments and Gosling had performed it live at the Oscars ceremony to a standing ovation in 2024.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Cricket gave me money and peace, says spinner Bhargav Bhatt at 100 | Cricket
description: The domestic spin legend from Baroda talks about how advice from Adam Gilchrist helped find peace.  | Cricket
content: In 2013, Bhargav Bhatt dared to dream. Two members from the national selection committee alerted the Baroda orthodox left-arm spinner to stay in shape ahead of the new home season of Test cricket. R Ashwin was India’s lead spinner but Ravindra Jadeja was still finding his feet. Pragyan Ojha’s bowling action was under a cloud and Harbhajan Singh had by then lost his place.Despite picking up a 7-fer against the visiting West Indies in an India A bowling attack that also comprised Zaheer Khan and Mohammed Shami, Bhatt’s phone didn’t ring. He would go on to tour Australia for three-day matches, also featuring South Africa, and do well. Years went by. Bhatt continued to pick a load of wickets on the Ranji circuit, but the national call-up never came.On reaching the milestone of 100 first-class matches, the 36-year-old spinner reminisces about his peak years. For every domestic cricketer who successfully graduates to the international level, countless others don’t. Bhatt is also likely to miss out amid the intense competition among left-arm spinners, even though he has begun the new Ranji season brightly with 17 wickets in 2 matches.“When I was playing under Adam Gilchrist for Kings XI Punjab in IPL, he told me one thing: ‘Ask yourself what you are doing to become better’,” Bhatt said. “He told me, ‘The opportunity will come if it has to’. That’s how I have always played my cricket.”Bhatt was noticed by IPL scouts for the 2011 edition - played 17 matches across 3 seasons - after a stellar Ranji season when he finished as the highest wicket-taker. He was yet to get a taste of T20 cricket.“My debut match against Pune Warriors was low-scoring and Gilchrist never gave me the ball. They had mistakenly named me as a wicket-keeper in the TV gfx and I thought, maybe the captain felt I couldn’t bowl,” said Bhatt."A couple of matches later, Gilchrist came up to me and told me I would be used in the Powerplay against Rajasthan Royals to counter Rahul Dravid and Shane Watson. That’s when I first learned how tactics work at the highest level. The captain wanted to protect the mystery around my newness as no one had seen any visual of me bowling previously in white-ball cricket.”T20 cricket took some mental adjustment for Bhatt. It took him time to understand that going for 35 runs in 4 overs wasn’t necessarily too many runs conceded.“But IPL also made me a better bowler,” he said. “Bowling with boundary dimensions in mind, using angles, and bowling with different speeds is what I learned. IPL also took away all fear because I was bowling to the best batters in the world and that too in the Powerplay.”It also helped him improve in red-ball cricket. “Earlier, people liked it if you flighted the ball,” Bhatt said. “Today, if you flight the ball for an entire over, there are enough batters who will take it on. So you learned to change your speeds and add more revolutions to the ball. Despite cutting the flight, get the ball to dip. Get drift, you learn all the time.”In his early days, Bhatt remembers how he would long to run into a senior spinner like Murali Karthik, Sunil Joshi or Harbhajan, just to brush up on finer aspects of spin bowling. “Today, whether it is (Manav) Suthar, Harsh (Dubey), or Sai Kishore, we are always catching up: say in competitions in Chennai before the domestic season. We are like a spinners’ club, bouncing off ideas,” he said.For his 390 first-class wickets, some remain more special. “There was a match against Mumbai and I had high fever. Yusuf Pathan told me not to take the field,” he said. “But how could I not, when Sachin Tendulkar was soon to arrive at the crease and Wasim Jaffer was at it? Yusuf told me if I took the field, I would have to bowl all day. I managed to bowl and got Sachin paaji out at slips.”A career full of domestic grind on different pitches, conditions, weather and opposition makes you a complete spinner. Sledging the batter only got him fines, the ones where he outfoxed batters playing mind games are the ones he remembers best. Nothing equates to playing Tests for India, but even Ranji Trophy can be a very competitive field.“Against Mumbai, I bowled to Ajinkya Rahane, Shreyas Iyer, Rohit Sharma and others. Got them out. That was tougher than India A,” he said.“Cricket gave me everything in life. It brought me both money and sukoon (inner calm). It helped me make new friends. I shouldn’t be expecting more,” he philosophises. “I know the size of the country where I am performing. There are so many spinners and I can only have control over my own bowling, not the competition. Until I play, all I strive for is to be the best bowler I can be.”

title: Chaos in Punjab assembly over Mansa anti-drug activist’s murder; Cong MLA suspended | Hindustan Times
description: Opposition protests Parvinder Singh Jhota’s killing with ‘Laanat Patra’ before staging walkout; AAP retaliates over 1984 riots and Akali ties.
content: Chandigarh: Ruckus erupted in the Punjab assembly on the second day of the session on Friday over the murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa on October 13.As the day’s proceedings began, Congress legislators raised the issue and demanded the resignation of chief minister Bhagwant Mann. Wearing black scarves, Congress members entered the well of the House, raising slogans and carrying a poster titled ‘Laanat Patra’ (Letter of Shame), accusing the Aam Aadmi Party government of failing on law and order, drug control, and gangsterism.Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan asked members not to disrupt Question Hour, but Leader of the Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa and other Congress MLAs urged the Chair to accept their letter. Several AAP members countered with slogans before Sandhwan directed everyone to return to their seats.Finance minister Harpal Cheema targeted the Congress over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and attacked newly appointed Punjab Congress president and Jalandhar Cantt MLA Pargat Singh over his past association with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), alleging the drug menace took root during the SAD’s rule.Congress members continued raising slogans before staging a walkout at 10.34am.Following the walkout, Congress MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira was placed under suspension for the remainder of the session. Cheema moved the suspension resolution, citing Khaira’s use of unparliamentary language against the Speaker, disregard for the Chair, and disruption during the Jhota murder protest.The resolution was passed in the absence of the Opposition.The assembly session, which began on Thursday, concludes on October 27.

title: Cyclone Warning : అక్టోబర్ 26 నాటికి తుపాను.. 27 నుండి ఆంధ్రాలో భారీ వర్షాలు | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: IMD Cyclone Warning : అక్టోబర్ 26 నాటికి తుపాను ఏర్పడే అవకాశం ఉందని భారత వాతావరణ శాఖ వెల్లడించింది. అక్టోబర్ 27 నుండి కోస్తాంధ్రలో భారీ వర్షాలు కురవనున్నాయి.
content: తూర్పు-మధ్య, దానిని ఆనుకుని ఉన్న ఆగ్నేయ బంగాళాఖాతంలో అల్పపీడనం ఏర్పడిందని ఇది అక్టోబర్ 26 ఉదయానికి పశ్చిమ-మధ్య బంగాళాఖాతంలో తుపానుగా బలపడే అవకాశం ఉందని భారత వాతావరణ శాఖ తెలిపింది. ఆ తర్వాత ఈ వ్యవస్థ ఉత్తరాంధ్ర, దానిని ఆనుకుని ఉన్న దక్షిణ ఒడిశా తీరాల వైపు పయనించే అవకాశం ఉందని అంచనా వేసింది.విశాఖపట్నంలోని ఐఎండీ తుపాను హెచ్చరిక కేంద్రం విడుదల చేసిన ప్రత్యేక ప్రకటన ప్రకారం.. గురువారం ఆగ్నేయ, దానిని ఆనుకుని ఉన్న తూర్పు-మధ్య బంగాళాఖాతంలో ఏర్పడిన ఉపరితల ఆవర్తనం ప్రభావంతో శుక్రవారం ఉదయం 5:30 గంటల సమయంలో అల్పపీడనం ఏర్పడింది.'గురువారం ఆగ్నేయ, దానిని ఆనుకుని ఉన్న తూర్పు-మధ్య బంగాళాఖాతంలో ఉన్న ఉపరితల ఆవర్తనం ప్రభావంతో అక్టోబర్ 23 ఉదయం 05:30 గంటలకు తూర్పు-మధ్య, దానిని ఆనుకుని ఉన్న ఆగ్నేయ బంగాళాఖాతంలో అల్పపీడనం ఏర్పడింది. ఇది అదే ప్రాంతంలో కొనసాగుతూ అక్టోబర్ 24, 2026న అల్పపీడనంగా బలపడే అవకాశం ఉంది. ఆ తర్వాత ఇది పశ్చిమ-వాయవ్య దిశగా పయనిస్తూ అక్టోబర్ 25న తీవ్ర అల్పపీడనంగా, అక్టోబర్ 26 ఉదయానికి పశ్చిమ-మధ్య బంగాళాఖాతంలో తుపానుగా మరింత బలపడే అవకాశం ఉంది. ఆ తర్వాత మరింత బలపడుతూ రాబోయే రెండు రోజుల్లో పశ్చిమ-వాయవ్య దిశగా ఉత్తరాంధ్ర, దానిని ఆనుకుని ఉన్న దక్షిణ ఒడిశా తీరాల వైపు కదిలే అవకాశం ఉంది.' అని భారత వాతావరణ శాఖ తెలిపింది.ఈ వాతావరణ ప్రభావంతో రాష్ట్రవ్యాప్తంగా విస్తారమైన వర్షాలు కురిసే అవకాశం ఉందని ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ రాష్ట్ర విపత్తు నిర్వహణ సంస్థ మేనేజింగ్ డైరెక్టర్ ప్రఖర్ జైన్ తెలిపారు. ప్రజలు, రైతులు ముందు జాగ్రత్తలు తీసుకోవాలని ఆయన సూచించారు. మత్స్యకారులు వెంటనే తీరానికి తిరిగి రావాలని విజ్ఞప్తి చేశారు.భారత వాతావరణ శాఖ (IMD) అమరావతి కేంద్రం వెల్లడించిన వివరాల ప్రకారం.. అక్టోబర్ 27 నుండి తీర ప్రాంత ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌లోని కొన్ని చోట్ల భారీ నుండి అతి భారీ వర్షాలు కురిసే అవకాశం ఉంది. అక్టోబర్ 27, 28 తేదీలలో అల్లూరి సీతారామరాజు, కాకినాడ, తూర్పు గోదావరి, డాక్టర్ బి.ఆర్. అంబేద్కర్ కోనసీమ, ఏలూరు, పశ్చిమ గోదావరి, ఎన్టీఆర్ జిల్లాలు, యానాంలో భారీ నుండి అతి భారీ వర్షాలు కురిసే అవకాశం ఉంది. ఉత్తరాంధ్రలో భారీ వానలు పడొచ్చు.విశాఖపట్నంతో సహా మరో 10 జిల్లాల్లో అక్కడక్కడా భారీ వర్షాలు కురిసే అవకాశం ఉన్నందున అప్రమత్తంగా ఉండాలని అధికారులు సూచించారు. ఎల్ నినో సంవత్సరాల్లో, రుతుపవనాల అనంతర కాలంలో బంగాళాఖాతంలో ఏర్పడే తుపానులు ఎక్కువగా 17 డిగ్రీల ఉత్తర అక్షాంశానికి దక్షిణంగా తీరాన్ని దాటుతాయని నిపుణులు పేర్కొన్నారు.గురువారం నెల్లూరు, ప్రకాశం జిల్లాల్లో భారీ వర్షాలు కురిశాయి. తిరుపతి జిల్లాలోని తొట్టంబేడులో 40.2 మి.మీ, నెల్లూరు జిల్లాలోని రాపూరులో 40 మి.మీ వర్షపాతం నమోదైంది. గురువారం పగటిపూట నెల్లూరులో 22 మి.మీ, కావలిలో 15 మి.మీ, కడపలో 13 మి.మీ వర్షపాతం నమోదైనట్లు ఐఎండీ అమరావతి కేంద్రం తెలిపింది.మరోవైపు నమోదైన ఉష్ణోగ్రతల వివరాలు చూస్తే.. కర్నూలులో అత్యధికంగా 35.3 డిగ్రీల ఉష్ణోగ్రత నమోదైంది. అదే సమయంలో ఒంగోలు, నర్సాపురం, నెల్లూరులలో ఉష్ణోగ్రతలు సాధారణం కంటే 3.9 డిగ్రీల నుండి 4.6 డిగ్రీల తక్కువగా నమోదయ్యాయి. అమరావతిలో 33.5 డిగ్రీల, విశాఖపట్నంలో 32.7 డిగ్రీల ఉష్ణోగ్రతలు నమోదయ్యాయి.శనివారం కోస్తా ఆంధ్ర, రాయలసీమ ప్రాంతాల్లోని కొన్ని చోట్ల ఉరుములు, మెరుపులతో కూడిన వర్షాలు పడే అవకాశం ఉంది. ఈ సమయంలో గంటకు 30 నుండి 40 కిలోమీటర్ల వేగంతో బలమైన గాలులు వీచే అవకాశం ఉందని వాతావరణ శాఖ పేర్కొంది.

title: Think pink salt, table salt, and rock salt are healthier options? Here’s what you should know about their iodine content | Health
description: Planning to switch from table salt to pink salt or rock salt? Here’s what you need to know about each's iodine content.    | Health
content: Most of us choose salt out of habit or because it’s already in the kitchen. But with pink Himalayan salt and black salt showing up in more homes, it’s worth asking whether they do the same job as the plain packet salt we grew up with. When it comes to iodine, the answer mostly comes down to one thing: has the salt been iodised or not? In an interview with HT Lifestyle, Dr Tushar Tayal, associate director, internal medicine, CK Birla Hospital, Gurugram, explained the difference in iodine content and its impact on health.​Also read | Always add extra salt to your meals? It is risky: Here's what it actually does to your body over timeWhy does your body need iodine?According to Dr Tayal, our thyroid uses iodine to make two hormones, T4 and T3. These hormones set the pace of your metabolism, help keep body temperature steady, and support how your organs work. In children, they also shape growth and the development of the brain and nervous system. That’s why iodine matters so much during pregnancy and the early years of life. “A shortage in pregnancy can affect the baby’s development. In adults, a long-term shortage can lead to an underactive thyroid or goitre, the swelling at the front of the neck,” highlighted Dr Tayal.The body can’t make iodine, so it has to come from what we eat. This is exactly why many countries, India included, promoted iodised salt: it’s a cheap, simple way to prevent deficiency across a whole population.Table saltDr Tayal highlighted that of the three, regular table salt is the safest bet for iodine, as long as the packet says “iodised.” A small, controlled amount of iodine is added during processing, so ordinary meals cover a good part of your daily needs.How much iodine you actually get depends on how much was added, how the salt is stored, and how it’s cooked. Still, it’s the easiest option to rely on. One thing to watch: not all table salt is iodised, so read the label rather than assuming. You won’t be able to taste the difference either way.Pink Himalayan saltPink salt is often sold as the purer, more natural choice, thanks to its colour and trace minerals. But the pink shade comes from those minerals, not from iodine. Unless the packet specifically says it’s iodised, the iodine in it is likely to be too little and too inconsistent to count on.The same goes for the idea that it’s healthier overall. Those trace minerals are present in tiny amounts, and pink salt is still sodium chloride, so it adds just as much sodium to your meals.Rock saltRock salt is a staple during fasts and in a lot of traditional cooking. Because it’s mined rather than processed, it usually isn’t iodised unless the manufacturer has added iodine on purpose. Its mineral makeup changes depending on where it comes from, but that doesn’t guarantee any useful amount of iodine. If you swap your regular salt for rock salt in everyday cooking, your iodine intake can quietly drop, especially if you don’t eat many other iodine-rich foods.How to make sure you’re getting enough?“The simplest fix is to buy salt labelled iodised and use it sparingly. Most adults need about 150 micrograms of iodine a day, and the requirement goes up during pregnancy and breastfeeding,” highlighted Dr Tayal.Salt isn’t your only source. Milk and curd, eggs, seafood and some fortified foods all contribute, though the amounts vary. If you’re vegetarian, and especially if you avoid dairy and eggs too, it’s worth paying closer attention to where your iodine is coming from.Note to readers: This article is for informational purposes only and not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always seek the advice of your doctor with any questions about a medical condition.

title: CM Saini to meet unions amid strike by employees of state-owned power companies | Hindustan Times
description: Power outages were reported as employees  went on strike against distribution licence to a private firm
content: Chief minister Nayab Singh Saini has called a meeting in Panchkula on Friday with representatives of the four unions amid a three-day strike by employees of state-owned power distribution companies against the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC)’s order granting a 25-year parallel distribution licence to a private company in Gurugram and Nuh.Power outages were reported across Haryana, including Gurugram, as striking employees of Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited (DHBVNL) and Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited did not undertake repair work, or feeder cables were shut down.The two companies supply power to southern and northern Haryana. The striking employees have either turned off their phones or stopped attending to calls from residents to restore the power supply.A DHBVNL official said the meeting was called as Saini does not want the common people to suffer due to the strike. “The representatives of the unions will attend the meeting in Panchkula, following which the further situation on the strike will become clear,” he said.Haryana Power Engineers Association general secretary Ravinder Ghanghas confirmed that they received a message from the state government on Friday morning for the meeting.“We are waiting for the confirmation on the time of the meeting, which is expected to take place in the PWD guesthouse in Panchkula. It may take place any time before or after lunch,” he said. He added that the course of their strike will depend on the meeting outcome.Haryana energy minister Anil Vij said the government is ready to discuss all options. He appealed to the employees to end the strike and return to duty as people took to the streets in Gurugram, Faridabad and other places against the outages, which left many with no water.Vij said the options include action under Section 108 of the Electricity Act, 2003, which empowers the Haryana government to issue written policy directions to the HERC on matters related to public interest. The government can override the HERC’s order granting the parallel-distribution licence to the private firm, energy department officials said.

title: Rakul Preet Singh talks her fashion evolution and everyday dressing mantra: ‘I didn’t really have an idea of what my style was’ | HT Exclusive | Fashion Trends
description: Rakul Preet Singh opens up about her evolving personal style, fashion journey and the everyday wardrobe essentials that make her feel confident and comfortable.  | Fashion Trends
content: Fashion is as much about self-discovery as it is about keeping up with trends. For actor Rakul Preet Singh, personal style has been an evolving journey of understanding what feels authentic to her, both on and off the red carpet. She shares with HT Lifestyle insights into her fashion journey, from her everyday dressing choices to the little details that influence how she puts a look together. (Also read: Rani Mukerji’s metallic grey saree look with bold statement glasses at Sabyasachi’s Diwali reception is a lesson in modern festive dressing )Rakul Preet Singh on finding her personal styleReflecting on how her style has changed over the years, Rakul says, “I think I've just understood my sense of style a little more.” Looking back at her early days in the industry, she admits, “When I started out in the industry, I really didn't have an idea of who I am, what is my style, what is style on the whole. And I think it's been an evolving process over the years.”When it comes to getting ready in a hurry, Rakul keeps things simple and fuss-free. Her five-minute outfit formula is all about wardrobe staples that never go out of fashion. “Denim, a tank top and sneakers, that's it,” she says, summing up her go-to look in a few words. Why comfort is key to Rakul's fashion choicesFor Rakul, versatility is just as important as style. Asked which item she would happily repeat across different festive looks, she points to footwear. “I think I could repeat my footwear, like a comfortable pair of footwear.” Her answer highlights the value of investing in pieces that combine practicality with everyday appeal.And how does she make sure a pair of shoes feels as good as it looks? Rakul's approach is refreshingly straightforward. “I walk, I jump, I hop around, and I make sure that I'm able to feel the comfort even if I'm walking around and dancing.”For Rakul, personal style is ultimately about discovering what works for you and finding the right balance between looking good and feeling comfortable.On the work frontOn the professional front, Rakul Preet Singh is set to play Surpanakha in Nitesh Tiwari’s much-anticipated two-part epic Ramayana, with the first instalment scheduled for a theatrical release on November 5, 2026. She was also seen in De De Pyaar De 2, the sequel to her 2019 romantic comedy, alongside Ajay Devgn.

title: Doctor explains how modern work habits affect metabolic health and changes to make | Health
description: Focusing on work often forces one to cut corners with maintaining healthy habits like getting enough movement and eating on time, cautions Dr Niraj Kumar.  | Health
content: Metabolism is the total work that the body does to keep an individual alive. It is not just about eating right and exercising, even though they play important roles in maintaining a healthy metabolism. According to internal medicine expert Dr Niraj Kumar, the daily habits of an individual have an equal impact on their metabolism.Also Read | Medical oncologist debunks 3 breastfeeding myths; explains how it does not prevent breast cancer“For most working professionals, lunch happens between meetings, physical activity is limited to travelling to work, and sleep depends on work,” shared the physician with HT Lifestyle. “It becomes easy to overlook these regular activities while concentrating on your deadlines. However, they can affect how the body handles blood sugar, appetite, and energy in the long term.”How does a modern workday affect metabolism?Speaking of metabolic health, Dr Kumar highlighted the increasing risk of diabetes among Indians. Citing the International Diabetes Federation's 2025 Diabetes Atlas, he shared that an estimated 90 million Indian adults aged between 20 and 79 were living with diabetes in 2024.“The condition has several causes, including genetics and age, but physical inactivity and dietary habits are factors people may be able to address,” noted Dr Kumar.Highlighting modern office habits, Dr Kumar stated that sitting for most of the working day leaves little opportunity for movement.“Muscles use glucose for energy, and regular physical activity helps the body maintain blood sugar,” he explained. “When movement is consistently limited, insulin resistance can become a concern, particularly when other risk factors are present.”According to the physician, eating habits can suffer for similar reasons. During a busy workday, some people skip lunch and snack through the afternoon, and some end up having dinner much later than they had planned.“A study published in Cell Metabolism found that late eating increased hunger and altered appetite-related hormones in adults with overweight or obesity. It also reduced waking energy expenditure,” noted Dr Kumar.Making room for healthier habitsDr Kumar acknowledged that it is not possible for many to completely break free of their current work habits and start following a strict, healthy routine. However, one can try to change their patterns.“Getting up from the desk regularly, taking a short walk during a break, carrying a balanced meal to work and keeping a consistent bedtime are manageable starting points,” stated the physician, adding that the World Health Organisation recommends 150 to 300 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity a week for adults.The physician cautioned that metabolic disorders can stay undiagnosed for a long period of time. Therefore, he recommended regular screening for blood sugar levels, blood pressure and cholesterol, with the schedule varying based on one’s age, medical background and risk factors.“While it might be difficult to avoid work stress, eating whenever time permits and regularly cutting back on sleep should not become the default. Small changes to these routines can help support better metabolic health over time,” noted Dr Kumar.Note to readers: This article is for informational purposes only and not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always seek the advice of your doctor with any questions about a medical condition.Dr Niraj Kumar is a Senior Consultant of Internal Medicine at ShardaCare - Healthcity, with over 15 years of clinical experience.

title: LuLu leases hypermarket space at Greater Noida Mall for 15 years at nearly  ₹51 crore | Real Estate News
description: Greater Noida: LuLu International Shopping Malls Private Limited has leased approx 62,035 sq ft of carpet area on the lower-ground floor of I-Thums Galleria   | Real Estate News
content: LuLu International Shopping Malls Private Limited has leased approximately 62,035 sq ft of carpet area on the lower-ground floor of I-Thums Galleria in Greater Noida for 15 years, at a total rent of nearly ₹51 crore, according to documents accessed by Propstack.The documents show that the lease provides for a monthly rent of ₹45 per sq ft for the retail area and ₹20 per sq ft for the back-of-house area, taking the initial monthly rent to approximately ₹26.41 lakh.The leased premises comprise 56,035 sq ft of retail carpet area and 6,000 sq ft of back-of-house area. The premises were scheduled to be handed over by March 31, 2026, with rent commencing after a 240-day fit-out period or on the store’s opening date, whichever is earlier.The documents showed the company has deposited ₹1.585 crore as a security deposit, equivalent to six months of the initial lease rent.Key details of LuLu’s Greater Noida hypermarket leaseThe lease provides for a 9% rent escalation every three years. It also includes 10 car parking spaces and 100 two-wheeler parking spaces at no additional cost.The agreement specifies a three-year lock-in period for the lessee and a 15-year lock-in period for the lessor. In addition to rent, the company will pay monthly common area maintenance (CAM) charges of approximately ₹12.11 lakh to the maintenance company, the documents showed.Earlier this week, LuLu Group announced the opening of a new 1-lakh-sq-ft hypermarket in Greater Noida, strengthening its presence in Uttar Pradesh and the Delhi-NCR region. Company sources told Hindustan Times that the 1-lakh-sq-ft figure refers to the hypermarket’s larger, super built-up area, which includes common areas, while the registered lease covers 62,035 sq ft of carpet area.The UAE-based retailer is targeting an investment of ₹2,500 crore to establish 25 outlets across Delhi-NCR by 2030. The expansion will include a mix of hypermarkets and smaller daily-concept stores, depending on the catchment and population of each location, a senior company executive told Hindustan Times.Also Read: LuLu opens 1 lakh sq ft hypermarket in Greater NoidaRaja Seetharaman, co-founder of Propstack, said LuLu Group’s entry into Greater Noida reflected the growing interest of institutional and large-format retailers in NCR’s expanding suburban markets.“Anchor commitments of this scale reflect sustained confidence in organised physical retail, especially in high-density residential corridors where consumer spending is maturing rapidly,” he said.Also Read: ₹2,500-crore investment, targets 25 outlets across Delhi-NCR by 2030">LuLu Group plans ₹2,500-crore investment, targets 25 outlets across Delhi-NCR by 2030With operations across more than 35 countries, a network of over 285 retail stores and 24 shopping malls, LuLu continues to expand its presence in India through shopping malls and hypermarkets, the company said in a statement.

title: All the trends, twists and double takes we saw at Lakmē Fashion Week | Hindustan Times
description: From swishing fringes to ornamental brows, designers experimented with movement, texture and proportion at the recently concluded Lakmē Fashion Week x FDCI.
content: Lakmé Fashion Week x FDCI had its share of statement-making clothes, but the season's talking points went beyond the collections. Fringe swung, velvet made a plush comeback and peplums played with proportions, while sculptural face masks, lace eyebrows and spooky beauty looks brought the unexpected to the runway. We pick the trends and quirks that stayed with us.When in doubt, add more fringe Fringe brought plenty of movement to the runway. At AM:IT by Amit Aggarwal, it swung from skirts, bags and separates, adding texture to the label’s high-voltage neon palette. It also appeared at The Fifth Season: A Fashion Story from Ladakh, where fringed hemlines moved with the models. The showcase brought together Charkha Ladakh by Rigzin Yangdol, Changra Ladakh, Zilzom and Namza, drawing on the region’s textile and craft traditions.A bib statement TIL by Ankur Verma reimagined the humble bib with jewelled necklines and jacket-like interpretations, while AM:IT by Amit Aggarwal saw bright colours with woven surfaces, long fringes, knots, and pom-poms. At Shahin Mannan, bibs were layered over dresses and lehengas and styled as saree blouses.Velvet crush The plush textile brought depth and richness to occasionwear. At Manish Malhotra’s Luxury Prêt 2026 showcase, velvet appeared alongside intricate embroidery, sculpted bodices and relaxed tailoring with crimson and jewel tones. Velvet also featured in The Fifth Season: A Fashion Story from Ladakh, adding another layer of texture to the regional showcase.Menswear loosens up At the Arvind x Ashish N Soni show, cowl necklines and relaxed folds softened silhouettes, offering alternatives to rigid collars and conventional fits. Manish Malhotra balanced embellished jackets and structured pieces with fluid draping. It was less about abandoning the bandhgala and more about widening the options beyond sharp, stiff or closely fitted lines.Peplum gets playful The peplum found fresh expression through sculpted waists and exaggerated proportions. Sara Arjun closed Anushree Reddy’s Maya showcase in a powder-blue strapless gown with an embroidered peplum and mermaid hem. Namrata Joshipura also experimented with sculptural shapes and hemlines, bringing a sharper eveningwear sensibility to the mix.The quirky things we spottedFunky socks on the runway Printed socks earned their place in the styling at Pearl Academy’s First Cut showcase. Paired with sneakers and floral details, they added a dash of fun to the looks.Lace on the eyebrows At Duja’s show at R|ELAN Circular Design Challenge, lace detailing framed the brows. The ornamental shapes drew attention to the upper face, offering an alternative to the usual brushed-up brows and graphic eye makeup.Halloween glam HUEMN’s beauty looks leaned dark and dramatic, with red accents and experimental hair and makeup. The effect felt distinctly Halloween-ready, with the beauty direction adding a theatrical edge to the clothes.Woven face masks Anurag Gupta’s sculptural masks covered models’ faces, bringing an eerie edge to the runway. Part protective armour, part wearable sculpture, the masks were an extension of the clothes.

title: Airbnb bans hosts from asking guests to strip beds, wash dishes and do other time-consuming chores | Trending
description: Airbnb will ban hosts from asking guests to complete time-consuming cleaning tasks — including stripping bed linen, taking out the trash and washing dishes  | Trending
content: Airbnb will ban hosts from asking guests to complete time-consuming cleaning tasks — including stripping bed linen, taking out the trash and washing dishes — under new rules coming into effect on November 20.The updated guidelines apply globally to bookings covered by the platform’s policy. They aim to make house rules clearer and prevent guests from being asked to carry out extensive cleaning despite paying for their accommodation.Airbnb has faced complaints from travellers who have been charged cleaning fees and still been expected to complete a list of chores before checking out.In a policy update on its website, the company said hosts would “generally” no longer be allowed to ask guests to perform tasks that “require significant effort or time or would typically be performed by a cleaner”.What chores can Airbnb hosts ask guests to do?Under the revised rules, hosts cannot require guests to strip beds, take rubbish offsite or wash and put away dishes. However, they can ask visitors to leave used dishes in the sink.(Also read: ₹1.05 crore apartment after guests leave: 'This isn’t a hotel room'">Airbnb host shows state of ₹1.05 crore apartment after guests leave: 'This isn’t a hotel room')The guidelines also state that hosts cannot introduce new house rules or requests after a booking has been made. Guests must be able to view all applicable rules when they make their reservation.Airbnb will review requests that do not comply with its policy. Hosts will be required to remove such requests or appeal the decision.The platform has also clarified that cleaning fees should cover routine cleaning between stays. Hosts cannot impose additional charges on guests for failing to complete checkout tasks listed by the host.Airbnb updates house rules for hostsAlongside the restrictions on cleaning chores, Airbnb has revised how hosts communicate their property rules.Hosts can now choose from seven standard categories of house rules, covering check-in and check-out times, the number of permitted guests, smoking, pets, quiet hours, and commercial filming and photography.These rules must be displayed in full when guests make a booking. They will also appear on property listing pages, in the Trips section of the app and in reservation reminders.(Also read: Goa Airbnb host says guests trashed flat, then said: ‘Isme kya badi baat hai’)Hosts can continue to make other reasonable requests, depending on local conditions. For instance, they may ask guests to limit shower time in areas facing water shortages or dispose of rubbish in animal-proof containers.The updated policy also prohibits hosts from restricting access to amenities advertised in their listings or charging guests fines and penalties. Airbnb's AirCover programme already provides protection for hosts against damage caused by guests.“Hosts are generally not allowed to impose fines or other penalties on guests. AirCover provides protection for hosts in the rare event that their place or belongings are damaged by a guest during an Airbnb stay,” the updated policy states.Airbnb says new rules will be easier for guestsIn a statement shared with Euronews Travel, Airbnb said: “House rules help guests understand what hosts expect, but we've heard from our community that they can be confusing, onerous and hard to manage.“So we've redesigned them to make them easier to discover and clearer to set, alongside a new policy that keeps requests reasonable, with no surprises.”(Also read: Guest slapped with $10,000 bill over selfie at vacation rental: ‘Complete nightmare’)The changes follow growing criticism from travellers over demanding checkout instructions, particularly when they have already paid cleaning fees. In recent years, some guests have also shared their experiences of strict house rules and detailed post-checkout inspections on social media.Airbnb said the updated guidelines are intended to ensure that guests know what is expected of them before booking, while allowing hosts to set reasonable conditions for their properties.

title: The workforce numbers that leave Indian seafarers exposed as attacks spread from Strait of Hormuz to Red Sea | HT Explainers
description: Houthis said they are rescuing 14 Indian sailors from a yacht attacked off Yemen. The Indian Mission in Yemen said it was ascertaining what had happened. | HT Explainers
content: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Thursday that their forces were rescuing 14 Indian sailors from a yacht that had come under attack near Zuqar Island in the Red Sea, the latest in a run of incidents at sea since the war in West Asia began in February.New Delhi has not confirmed the account. The Indian Mission in Yemen said on X that “apparently there were Indian nationals (sailors) on board a yacht”, and that it had reached out to different parties to establish what happened. “Given the prevailing conflict situation exact information is not currently available,” the Mission added.Indians have been hit harder than most. About one in eight of the world’s merchant seafarers are Indians. Over a dozen Indians have been killed in the Gulf and the Black Sea by the end of July, and the Red Sea is now a third conflict zone. The three theatresUS and Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28, and by early March, tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman that is the only sea route out of the Persian Gulf, had almost stopped, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the Paris-based body that tracks energy markets for its member countries.Ten Indian seafarers were killed in West Asia between the start of the conflict and July 30, Kirti Vardhan Singh, the minister of state for external affairs, had told the Rajya Sabha.In June, three Indian seafarers were killed when the tanker MT Settebello was struck off Oman. On July 12, the Cyprus-flagged container ship GFS Galaxy was attacked near Omani waters. An Indian engineer went missing and was later confirmed dead. On the night of July 20, an Indian second engineer was hospitalised after the Kuwait-flagged Kaifan was hit at Limah Anchorage off Oman.In the Black Sea, where merchant ships have come under fire in the Russia-Ukraine war, five Indian seafarers were killed within two days in July. On July 18, the Omorfi was attacked in what the external affairs ministry described as Russian territorial waters, and one of its three Indian crew members was killed. The next evening, the Golden Leo was attacked while leaving the Ukrainian port of Odesa. Four of the five Indians in its 17-strong crew were killed, and the fifth was hospitalised in a critical condition.In the Red Sea, the Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia on July 20. They then claimed attacks on vessels, and Saudi Arabia responded with air strikes.Why Indians are so exposedIndia is the second-largest source of merchant seafarers after the Philippines, according to the Seafarer Workforce Report 2026, published in June by the Baltic and International Maritime Council (BIMCO), a shipowners’ association, and the International Chamber of Shipping (ICS), the industry’s trade body. India supplies 311,936 seafarers, 12.16% of a global workforce of 2.57 million. Among officers, the senior ranks who navigate, command and run the engines, its share rises to 13.41%. About 750,000 Indian seafarers are registered with the country's shipping regulator, of whom about 320,000 are actively employed.Indians were also the seafarers most often abandoned last year. Under international labour rules, a crew counts as abandoned when the shipowner stops paying wages for two months or more, cuts off food and supplies, or refuses to pay for the journey home.That happened to 1,125 Indian seafarers in 2025, according to the International Transport Workers' Federation (ITF), the global union body for transport workers. They made up 18% of a record 6,223 seafarers abandoned worldwide, and Indians were the worst-affected nationality, as in 2024.Most of the ships involved, 82%, flew flags of convenience, which means the vessels were registered in a country other than the one their owners operated from. The ITF said the Indian government had announced “blacklisting” measures at the end of 2025 against ships with a record of repeat abandonments.India’s responseIn July, after a string of attacks in and around Hormuz, India’s shipping regulator, the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), told ship owners, ship managers and licensed recruitment agencies to avoid putting Indian seafarers on ships sailing through the strait.Beyond that, the government relies on what Singh told Parliament was a “structured, multi-layered mechanism, consisting of regular advisories, setting up additional emergency helplines and 24x7 control rooms, and evacuation operations as necessary”.The external affairs ministry's Rapid Response Cell coordinates with the armed forces and other departments. On July 30, the ministry said its own digital emergency response system for evacuations was in final trials.The shipping regulator runs a 24x7 communication centre, and in early September, it launched e-Navik 24x7, a digital grievance system that gives a seafarer’s complaint a ticket number, covering cases from unpaid wages and abandonment to detention, death and missing seafarers.Manoj Yadav, general secretary of the Forward Seamen Union of India, had told HT last month that the regulator issues new circulars and policies every month, but what matters is action.Also read: Indian proposal for Ukraine truce ‘most comprehensive’, says Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii SybihaPM Modi’s Brics proposalAt the Brics summit in September, Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed a shared safety net for seafarers. “Seafarers contribute significantly to global trade, but they often lack support in difficult times," he said, proposing a Seafarers Emergency Support Network.It would, he said, “connect maritime authorities and missions in the respective countries” and provide “assistance with distress alerts, medical assistance, information to families, and evacuation”.Modi placed the proposal under the second of three tests he set out for reforming global governance. “Humanity will only gain confidence in global institutions if they are capable of effectively addressing problems,” he told Brics leaders. “We must pay attention to the speed, scale, and last-mile impact of our collective response.”Russia and Iran, both Brics members, are parties to the conflicts in the Black Sea and the Gulf in which Indian seafarers have died.

title: Reforming pay structures in the social sector will benefit everyone | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Mangesh Wange, CEO and Board Member, Swades Foundation.
content: For most young professionals, compensation is the primary filter when evaluating a job. When the pay is low, capable, driven talent rarely considers a career in non-governmental organisations (NGOs). Yet, society expects this sector to solve the world’s most complex challenges such as poverty, water scarcity, education gaps, health care and the climate change.This tension spans the broader public service landscape. In India, public school teachers routinely manage classrooms of over 50 students while earning a fraction of what their corporate counterparts make, driving high absenteeism and learning deficits. On World Teachers’ Day, UNESCO projected a global shortage of 44 million primary and secondary teachers needed to meet the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), identifying uncompetitive salaries and poor working conditions as primary drivers of attrition.This holds true for the development sector as well. A study by the Centre for Social Impact and Philanthropy (CSIP) at Ashoka University and the Indian School of Development Management (ISDM), covering over 10,000 social sector employees, found that total compensation in the Indian development sector is 58% lower than in the for-profit sector.Development cannot run on passion alone. While it is absolutely essential to commit to the sector, passion does not pay bills. The sector requires skill, intellectual capacity and a workforce equipped to navigate community trust, bureaucracy, infrastructure gaps, and policy constraints over the long term. Modern non-profits operate in an increasingly complex landscape with high expectations around compliance, reporting, and statutory deliverables adding immense operational pressure. Therefore, organisations must recruit specialists across finance, IT, monitoring systems, HR, and fundraising. These roles increase overhead but are essential for building resilient institutions.When salaries remain subpar, high-performing professionals migrate to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) roles, consulting firms, or corporate positions that pay market rates and non-profits are left in a perpetual cycle of recruitment and training, incurring high hiring costs and losing institutional memory while operational continuity suffers and community relationships weaken. Part of the issue lies in funding structures. A report by The Bridgespan Group highlights that Indian non-profits face chronic underfunding due to the under-reimbursement of indirect costs, with many donors allocating just 4% to 10% for overheads such as salaries, capacity-building, and systems. Donor restrictions force administrative budgets to a breaking point: Every rupee or dollar is expected to fund visible outputs like building classrooms or distributing field kits, while investments in workforce and infrastructure are squeezed. Funders expect detailed impact metrics, documentation, media visibility, and strict compliance, yet rarely provide the financial backing required to pay the talent performing this work. While transparency in the sector is routinely championed, we must be equally transparent about the fact that many NGOs cannot pay their staff what they deserve.Solving this crisis requires a fundamental shift in how we view compensation.First, grantmakers and corporate CSR foundations must replace rigid overhead caps with flexible, unrestricted funding models that explicitly allocate 10% to 20% of project budgets toward talent, operational infrastructure, and staff well-being. Second, non-profit leadership and donors must collaboratively establish cross-sector compensation benchmarks that index NGO salaries to fair market rates. By funding the organisational backbone with the same rigor as field outputs, the social sector can build durable institutions capable of retaining the talent needed to solve our world's greatest challenges.Third, supporting non-profit manpower and capacity building through their L&D teams on pro bono basis. For sustainable solutions and impact, strengthening the delivery systems and organisations is the first step which we all should consider.Until funding models adapt to cover true operational costs, the sector will continue to starve its most valuable asset--its people.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Mangesh Wange, CEO and Board Member, Swades Foundation.

title: Rubio’s visit: Rebuilding strategic trust | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by KS Tomar, strategic affairs columnist and senior political analyst, Shimla.
content: India faces a difficult diplomatic balancing act: It needs the US as a partner in technology, defence and the Indo-Pacific, but cannot allow its national interests to become casualties of President Donald Trump’s transactional diplomacy. The tariff offensive, pressure over Russian oil purchases and Washington’s engagement with Pakistan have exposed the fragility of a partnership built over three decades.US secretary of State Marco Rubio’s recent visit, his second to India in five months, offered New Delhi an opportunity to repair strained ties without surrendering strategic autonomy. With trade negotiations showing signs of progress and some punitive measures eased, the question is whether diplomatic warmth can deliver durable gains or merely a temporary reprieve from American pressure.Rubio conveyed that Washington continues to regard its partnership with New Delhi as strategically significant, while energy cooperation is emerging as another pillar of mutual interest. The visit’s deeper significance lay in indications that the American administration may be reassessing its engagement with India.Experts say Rubio’s visit was driven mainly by US commercial interests—expanding markets for Venezuelan crude, with India as a key buyer. Though India buys cheaper oil from Russia and Iran, Washington may pressure it to switch, leveraging Ambani refineries to process the crude and turn diplomacy into a strategic energy deal.For India, the relationship extends beyond access to the American market. It encompasses defence modernisation, advanced technology, investment, supply-chain diversification and cooperation in balancing China’s growing Indo-Pacific influence. A prolonged trade dispute could damage business confidence and complicate strategic coordination.New Delhi must seek more than temporary tariff relief. It needs predictable rules, fair access for Indian exports and protection against unilateral economic measures used as instruments of political pressure. A partnership cannot remain dependable if commercial concessions are periodically threatened by decisions in Washington.External affairs minister S Jaishankar’s engagement with Rubio, including their interaction alongside UAE foreign minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed, demonstrated India’s willingness to maintain dialogue despite serious disagreements. New Delhi has neither abandoned its American partnership nor accepted that cooperation requires unquestioning alignment.Energy remains a crucial test. India’s purchases of Russian crude reflect considerations of price, availability and national energy security. A country with enormous development needs cannot treat affordable supplies merely as instruments of another country’s geopolitical strategy.India’s sophisticated refining industry, including the Jamnagar complex, can process diverse grades of crude. But this flexibility should not become an expectation that India will automatically accommodate American energy priorities.Washington, too, has reasons to avoid destabilising global oil supplies. Higher fuel prices carry domestic political costs for Trump, particularly ahead of the November mid-term elections. India should use this convergence to pursue pragmatic energy cooperation while diversifying suppliers and avoiding excessive dependence on any one country.The principle is clear: India can cooperate with Washington on energy without surrendering its freedom of choice.The most persistent strategic disagreement concerns Pakistan. Jaishankar’s emphasis on zero tolerance for terrorism reinforced India’s position that security cooperation cannot be measured solely through trade, energy or defence transactions.Rubio’s defence of continued American engagement with Pakistan, citing its nuclear status and geographical significance, exposed the divergence. Washington may view engagement as a means of managing regional risks, but New Delhi remains concerned that diplomatic accommodation gives Islamabad strategic space without ensuring accountability for terrorism.India should not expect one visit to eliminate this difference. It must insist that American engagement with Pakistan be assessed against tangible counterterrorism outcomes. Diplomatic contact is not the same as responsible conduct.For New Delhi, this disagreement directly affects the credibility of a partnership Washington itself considers important.Quad provides another measure of whether the relationship can withstand immediate disputes. Rubio’s indication that a leaders’ summit is expected before year-end in Manila, alongside the ASEAN conference, keeps the Indo-Pacific agenda in view.India values Quad because it advances regional cooperation without obliging members to enter a formal military alliance. Its relevance lies in practical coordination on maritime security, technology, resilient supply chains and regional stability.Sustained American commitment matters as China expands its economic, technological and military influence. But India’s participation does not imply automatic alignment with every American preference. Quad’s credibility depends on shared interests and continuity, not the absence of bilateral disagreements.Rubio’s most consequential role may begin after his return to Washington. With direct access to Trump, he can explain why pressuring India risks undermining wider American objectives. India is a major market, an important defence and technology partner, and a consequential actor in Asia’s balance of power.Yet Rubio’s influence should not be exaggerated. Trump’s decisions reflect domestic political calculations, personal instincts and a negotiating style that treats economic pressure as leverage. Rubio’s assessment cannot guarantee a lasting policy change.India must combine diplomatic engagement with a clear-eyed assessment of American unpredictability. It should welcome cooperation without assuming strategic convergence will override transactional considerations.The immediate priorities are a balanced trade agreement, greater certainty over tariffs, sustained energy cooperation and continued momentum in Quad. The longer-term objective is a relationship in which disagreements do not routinely threaten wider strategic cooperation.India should judge the Rubio visit by outcomes rather than diplomatic optics. The test is whether Washington recognises that a confident India will cooperate where interests converge while retaining the freedom to differ where they do not.Rubio has opened a window for repair. Turning it into a durable reset will require American predictability and Indian firmness. New Delhi’s goal is not to win Trump’s favour at any cost, but to ensure that partnership with Washington strengthens rather than constrains India’s strategic choices.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by KS Tomar, strategic affairs columnist and senior political analyst, Shimla.

title: Punjab launches SANGAT mental health clubs in 40 colleges to prevent drug abuse | Hindustan Times
description: Punjab has launched SANGAT mental health clubs in 40 colleges, linking peer support with substance-abuse prevention under Yudh Nashean Virudh.
content: The Punjab government has launched SANGAT mental health clubs in 40 colleges across the state to promote youth wellbeing, encourage early intervention and help prevent substance abuse under its campaign, Yudh Nashean Virudh.The initiative, led by the Department of Higher Education in partnership with the Aditya Birla Education Trust (ABET), aims to create supportive campus environments where students can recognise signs of emotional distress, seek appropriate assistance and discuss mental health concerns without stigma.Education minister Harjot Singh Bains and former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia interacted with student participants during the launch at Plaksha University in Mohali. Discussions focused on the role of educational institutions, families and peer networks in encouraging young people to seek help and addressing the stigma associated with mental health challenges and substance use.Bains said SANGAT had been designed by young people for young people to promote peer support, mental wellbeing and healthier choices. He emphasised the importance of guidance and mentorship, adding that helping someone move away from harmful influences was more important than stigmatising them for their circumstances.Neerja Birla, founder and chairperson of ABET and Mpower, said emotional distress, untreated mental health concerns and substance use could intersect, making sustained preventive efforts and early intervention important. She commended the Punjab government for bringing together government departments, civil society organisations, educators, healthcare professionals and community leaders to strengthen prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration efforts.Actor Aparshakti Khurana also highlighted the need for supportive spaces where young people could speak openly about their struggles and seek help without fear of judgement. He said friends, families and educational institutions had an important role in ensuring that young people felt heard and understood. Nikhil Taneja, co-founder and chief of Yuvaa, also participated in discussions on youth mental health. Punjabi comedian Manpreet Singh, known as The Comic Singh, performed at the event.Under the programme, 25 students from each participating college will receive 14 hours of Youth Mental Health First Aid training and certification. The training will help them recognise emotional distress, provide initial peer support and guide fellow students towards professional assistance when needed.The clubs will organise campus activities to encourage conversations about emotional wellbeing, discourage substance use and promote early identification of concerns. The programme is being implemented by Mpower, an ABET subsidiary, under its Counselling and Outreach for Peer Empowerment framework.The state government said SANGAT was part of its wider efforts under Yudh Nashean Virudh to address substance abuse through prevention, awareness, peer support and collective responsibility.

title: Yogi Adityanath highlights role of public servants in effective governance | Hindustan Times
