description: Yogi Adityanath said governance should be judged by its impact on citizens, stressing that accountable public servants are vital to delivering schemes.
content: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday said the effectiveness of administration should be measured by the positive changes it brings to people’s lives, emphasising the role of public servants in ensuring that government schemes reach those most in need.In a post on social media platform X, the Chief Minister extended his wishes for Sadhana Shrankhla-2026, a two-day regional programme being launched in Lucknow with the participation of eight states and four Union territories. Union minister of state (independent charge) Jitendra Singh is scheduled to attend the event, according to the state government’s statement.The CM said public servants were among the most important drivers of change and that efficient, sensitive and accountable administration was essential for translating the promise of good governance into public welfare. He said government programmes could benefit people at the last mile only when the administrative system functioned effectively and remained responsive to their needs.The Chief Minister also criticised the governance record of Uttar Pradesh before 2017, alleging that family-based politics, appeasement and corruption had adversely affected administrative efficiency and work culture. He said crime, the influence of mafias, policy apathy and a crisis of identity had constrained the state’s potential.Referring to initiatives such as Mission Karmayogi, CM Yogi said the central government, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s guidance, was seeking to give a new direction to administrative work culture. He claimed that Uttar Pradesh had moved beyond its earlier image as a “BIMARU” state over the past nine-and-a-half years and was working to redefine its administrative, economic and institutional structures.The Chief Minister said the state was pursuing the principle of “minimum government, maximum governance” and remained committed to inclusive development and the goal of a developed India.Sadhana Shrankhla-2026 is intended to carry forward this administrative reform agenda. He wished participants success and said public servants had a key role in ensuring that governance commitments translated into tangible improvements in citizens’ lives.

title: Nepal MP’s upcoming India visit will be a real test | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Brabim Karki, columnist and commentator, Nepal.
content: Nepal Prime Minister (PM) Balendra Shah is preparing to visit India towards November, nearly eight months after taking office in March, and this would be his maiden bilateral foreign trip as PM. There are reports that two governments have already swapped lists of projects to inaugurate and agreements to sign.There are serious issues to raise with the Indian counterparts: The boundary, air routes for Nepal through India, and the trade imbalance. The visit is worth making, but it will be worth remembering only if it moves those three issues. Geographically landlocked, Nepal remains fundamentally bound to India, through which the vast majority of its trade, fuel imports, and future revenues must flow. Among the critical infrastructure projects slated to break ground, a new petroleum pipeline from Siliguri to Jhapa carries the most immediate promise for ordinary citizens; fuel transported via pipeline bypasses the volatile logistics of tanker trucks and the perennial threat of blocked border roads. Yet the true engine of long-term economic sovereignty lies in Nepal's unharnessed rivers. India's state-owned NHPC has heavily invested in mega-projects like West Seti (750MW), Phukot Karnali (480MW), and Seti River-6 (450MW). This shows that Nepal possesses the liquid assets, New Delhi needs power and no other regional partner can enter that equation.Reports indicate that the most of bilateral mechanisms between New Delhi and Kathmandu have yielded tangible monuments to cooperation like the Nepal Police Academy in Panauti and the critical bridges over the Mahakali River in Darchula. Yet, while technocratic committees can successfully engineer a bridge, they lack the mandate to redraw a contested border or fundamentally restructure the terms of trade. Such structural shifts require political will, the kind forged only when PMs execute decisions. A brief three-day State visit offers a rare window for this high-level arbitrage; Kathmandu must seize the moment to advance these deeper structural demands, and New Delhi must be prepared to accommodate them.Delhi has its own reason to listen. India's pitch to its neighbours is that it delivers: Roads, pipelines, power. The project list suggests that, in Nepal at least, it often does. Nepal buys far more from India than it sells back. It wants better access to air routes through Indian airspace. These are matters for negotiation, and they can be settled at modest cost to both sides. Settle them, and the issues become easier to raise. India also gains. A Nepal that earns more from its exports and its rivers is a steadier neighbour on an open border.His upcoming visit to New Delhi will serve as a crucial test of whether this diplomatic approach can yield concrete agreements on infrastructure, reconstruction, and the structural disputes that have long hampered bilateral relations. While breakthroughs on the first two fronts remain comfortably within reach, it is the third by which the success of the entire visit will be measured. Resolving long-standing boundary disputes, securing vital entry routes through Indian airspace, and correcting a trade imbalance that skews in India's favor are not tasks that can be delegated to bureaucratic working groups; they demand a PM willing to articulate them and a counterpart ready to listen constructively. New Delhi has a profound self-interest in doing so: An economically resilient Nepal that derives robust revenues from its own exports and unharnessed rivers makes for a far more stable neighbour along an open border. (The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Brabim Karki, columnist and commentator, Nepal.

title: Ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt says AI could leave companies needing ‘a couple of thousand’ fewer workers | Trending
description: Eric Schmidt has shared his vision of how AI agents could reshape businesses.  | Trending
content: Artificial intelligence could change how companies are run, and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt believes the shift could be bigger than many workers expect. As AI agents become more capable, business leaders could use them to monitor projects, track decisions and oversee operations in new ways.Speaking on the In Good Company podcast, Schmidt explained how AI could reshape corporate leadership and the way large organisations function.How AI agents could change CEO jobsSchmidt believes future CEOs could use AI assistants that monitor activity across their companies and flag issues that require their attention. These tools could track project progress, identify inefficiencies and check whether decisions align with a company's stated values, according to Business Insider's report.(Also Read: ₹240 crore in UAE lottery says ‘excitement has faded’ after buying cars, properties, gold">Indian winner of ₹240 crore in UAE lottery says ‘excitement has faded’ after buying cars, properties, gold)He recalled how his days as Google's chief executive were often consumed by meetings, sometimes lasting 12 hours a day, five days a week. AI platforms, he suggested, could reduce what he described as the “coordination tax”, the time and effort spent collecting updates, passing information between teams and keeping projects on track.Schmidt also shared an example of two founders who use an AI assistant every Friday to identify activities within their company that conflict with their values.In another instance, an executive reportedly created an AI version of himself to guide an employee, monitor progress and answer questions. Schmidt said the arrangement concerned him because it could feel abusive, although he acknowledged that it could speed up decision-making.(Also Read: Scottish museum removes Egyptian mummies from exhibition over lack of ‘consent from the deceased individual')Why AI could put coordination jobs at riskSchmidt suggested that businesses with thousands of employees could need fewer workers as AI takes over administrative and coordination tasks. For a company with 10,000 employees, he estimated that AI could eliminate the need for “a couple of thousand people”.He also cited the example of a friend whose rapidly growing company cut 20% of its workforce, including employees he described as “glue people”, who helped with planning and coordination.However, Schmidt did not suggest that every job would disappear. He said companies would continue to need people who develop products, generate sales, engage with regulators and lead teams.For employees whose roles are affected, he argued that companies should manage transitions “legally and humanely”.Schmidt warns companies have little time to adaptThe former Google chief executive also highlighted the speed of competition in artificial intelligence. He argued that AI development cycles move faster than earlier technology battles, leaving companies with little time to adjust before competitors introduce newer models.Rejecting the idea that AI is merely a bubble, Schmidt pointed to Anthropic's rapid revenue growth as evidence of growing commercial demand.

title: Prolific Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan added to India A squad for two games against New Zealand A | Cricket
description: In the ongoing Ranji Trophy, the 21-year-old left-hander has scored two centuries in as many games.  | Cricket
content: Jharkhand batsman Shikhar Mohan has been rewarded for his stellar show in domestic cricket with a place in the India A squad for four-day games in New Zealand.In the ongoing Ranji Trophy, the 21-year-old left-handed batsman scored centuries in both rounds. Against Kerala, the opener smashed 143 off 196 balls with the help of 18 fours and two sixes as Jharkhand picked up three points on the basis of their first-innings lead.Then, in the second game against Maharashtra, he scored a very important century under pressure in the second innings. Jharkhand trailed by 358 runs and stared a big defeat in the face, but Mohan’s 127 helped them avoid it as Jharkhand picked up a point. Mohan, who made his first-class debut last year, has been prolific in the 12 matches that he has played so far, scoring 1,109 runs at a solid average of 61.61. India play two Tests in New Zealand after five T20Is and five ODIs. Quite a few Test regulars are in the India A squad like KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Dhruv Jurel, Rishabh Pant, Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan, Washington Sundar and Akash Deep. These three 4-day games are part of India’s preparations for the Test series. Mohan will be available for selection after the first game.The India A-New Zealand A series kicks off on Saturday at Lincoln, followed by matches in Christchurch (October 31-November 3) and Lincoln again (November 07-10). The first Test between India and New Zealand starts in Wellington on November 19, followed by the second at Christchurch on November 27.India A squad:Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, R Smaran, Kumar Kushagra (wicketkeeper), Dhruv Jurel (captain and wicketkeeper), Washington Sundar, Auqib Nabi, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj, Manav Suthar, Mukesh Choudhary, B Sai Sudharsan, Yash Rathod, Mukesh Kumar, Rishabh Pant (subject to fitness), Shikhar Mohan (for 2nd and 3rd games)

title: BIMSTEC and India’s search for a more effective regional order | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Janvi Singhi.
content: The Bay of Bengal is central to India’s economic connectivity, maritime security and engagement with Southeast Asia. Yet, despite its strategic significance, regional cooperation remains constrained by political instability, inadequate infrastructure and weak economic integration. The first Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Home Ministers’ Meeting, held in New Delhi on October 13, 2026, offers an opportunity to examine a larger question: Can India transform regional diplomacy into an institutional framework that delivers tangible outcomes?The meeting’s Delhi Declaration reaffirmed the commitment of the seven member States i.e Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand to combat terrorism, drug trafficking, human trafficking, cybercrime and transnational organised crime. However, the adoption of a declaration is only the beginning. BIMSTEC’s credibility will depend on whether these commitments translate into coordinated action, measurable progress and sustained regional cooperation.For India, BIMSTEC connects two central foreign-policy priorities: Neighbourhood First and Act East. Its membership creates a bridge between South and Southeast Asia, offering opportunities to integrate India’s northeastern states with regional markets while strengthening maritime cooperation across the Bay of Bengal.The grouping also provides a practical platform for regional engagement amid the persistent difficulties facing the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC). However, BIMSTEC should not be judged merely by its ability to function without Pakistan. Its strategic value must rest on what its members can collectively achieve, rather than on the limitations of another institution.The central challenge is that geographical proximity has not translated into economic interdependence. Intra-regional trade remains below its potential, cross-border infrastructure is incomplete, and negotiations on a BIMSTEC free trade agreement have progressed slowly. Without reducing these barriers, the organisation risks becoming a forum for diplomatic coordination rather than a driver of regional integration.The October meeting provides a timely basis for strengthening regional responses to transnational threats. Terrorist networks, illicit financial flows, narcotics trafficking and human trafficking exploit jurisdictional boundaries and differences in enforcement capacity. Addressing them requires more than political agreement.India should prioritise operational mechanisms, including designated national contact points, secure intelligence-sharing procedures, joint training and effective mutual legal assistance. Regular implementation reviews should distinguish between agreements signed, procedures established and outcomes achieved. Security cooperation must also respect due process, domestic law and human-rights obligations, particularly in investigations involving trafficking victims and vulnerable communities.The same logic applies to disaster management. Cyclones, floods and other climate-related emergencies affect countries across the Bay of Bengal, making early-warning systems, coordinated relief exercises and shared emergency protocols areas where cooperation can produce immediate public benefits. These initiatives would strengthen BIMSTEC by demonstrating that regional institutions can address problems that individual governments cannot manage efficiently in isolation.Security cooperation alone cannot sustain a regional order. BIMSTEC must also make cross-border economic activity easier, cheaper and more predictable. India’s Northeast is crucial to this objective. Its location offers opportunities to connect domestic production centres with Bangladesh, Myanmar and Thailand. Yet projects such as the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway and the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project face implementation challenges, including delays and insecurity in Myanmar. Roads and ports cannot generate their intended economic returns if border procedures remain cumbersome or transport networks fail to operate reliably.India must, therefore, approach connectivity as an integrated programme rather than a collection of infrastructure projects. Physical links need efficient customs systems, compatible standards, reliable logistics and clear administrative responsibilities. Progress should be measured through indicators such as transit times, trade volumes and the actual utilisation of transport corridors.The proposed free trade framework also requires renewed attention. Negotiations on tariffs, rules of origin, customs cooperation and non-tariff barriers are essential to converting geographical proximity into commercial opportunity. Smaller economies must see credible benefits, while Indian industries must be prepared for greater regional competition.India’s economic weight gives it an important role in BIMSTEC, but asymmetry can also generate concerns about unequal influence. Smaller member states have distinct economic priorities, domestic constraints and external partnerships. Their sustained participation cannot be taken for granted.India should build confidence through consultation, transparent project implementation and a willingness to accommodate the priorities of other members. It should also support a public implementation scorecard, coordinated through the BIMSTEC Secretariat, covering connectivity, trade facilitation, security cooperation and disaster preparedness. Such a mechanism would clarify responsibilities, expose delays and improve accountability.Fiscal discipline is equally important. Rather than expanding the agenda indiscriminately, India should prioritise a limited number of feasible, high-impact initiatives with clear timelines and identifiable benefits. Public resources should address infrastructure and institutional gaps that private investment cannot adequately resolve, while commercially viable projects should attract business participation.BIMSTEC offers India an opportunity to shape a more functional regional order, but institutional effectiveness cannot be assumed from strategic intent. Its success will depend on whether member States can sustain cooperation despite political changes, administrative constraints and competing priorities.India should measure progress not by the frequency of meetings or the number of declarations adopted, but by stronger economic links, effective security coordination and tangible benefits for citizens across the region. The real test of India’s regional leadership is whether it can help build a BIMSTEC that delivers collectively, not merely deliberates diplomatically.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Janvi Singhi, senior research fellow, IndiaForth, and research associate, Asia-Pacific Bureau, Organisation for Threat Assessment and Peacebuilding (OTAP).

title: Hello Meghalaya: hyperlocal and highly successful | Hindustan Times
description: On Meghalaya’s state-backed OTT platform that has built a huge following while also creating opportunities for young creators
content: The global media landscape is changing rapidly, with regional cinema reaching audiences far beyond traditional geographies. Hollywood is no longer the sole centre of global entertainment, audiences increasingly seek stories rooted in specific cultures and places. A Korean film can win Best Picture at the Oscars, a South Indian film reaches North India, and a K-Pop song becomes a global hit. This is particularly significant for India’s Northeast. Nagaland filmmaker Theja Rio’s debut Angh, rooted in Konyak culture and set in 1960s Nagaland, won the Platform Prize at the Toronto International Film Festival, the only Indian film in its Platform competition. Against this backdrop, Meghalaya’s state-backed OTT platform, Hello Meghalaya, launched two years ago, has built a following while creating opportunities for the state’s youth.When I went to Meghalaya last year for the Shillong Literary Festival, I was pleasantly surprised to see that the state supports emerging artists, and not just those who practice traditional art forms. Unique in its social structure, demographics, terrain and history, the state has centuries-old storytelling traditions, one of the world’s last surviving matrilineal cultures, and is one of India’s youngest states, with nearly 50 percent of its population under 20 years of age. Hyperlocal media cannot be ignored anymore. Close to six lakh people have already downloaded the Hello Meghalaya app and more than 20,000 daily active users engage with Khasi, Garo and Pnar stories. Free access lets a filmmaker in Shillong, a band in Tura, or a home chef in Jowai publish and earn without traditional gatekeepers. With over 2,000 pieces of content and 380+ creators and filmmakers, the app has become a functioning creative marketplace. “Earlier we didn’t have a platform where people could post their content. Hello Meghalaya gave a voice to the talented artists of our state. Before this, artists couldn’t speak in their own language on a big platform like this one,” says award-winning filmmaker Dominic Sangma.Not just an appHello Meghalaya seems to be a part of a wider creative-economy strategy combining film grants, tourism incentives, music programmes and national showcases. Last year, grants were awarded to 47 filmmakers in Shillong. The grant offers up to ₹35 lakh for established feature filmmakers, ₹25 lakh for other features, ₹20 lakh for web series, and ₹5 lakh for emerging filmmakers.The Meghalaya Film Tourism Policy 2025 also tries to further the state’s filmmaking culture by offering single-window clearances and subsidies up to ₹1 crore for qualifying national and international productions, which will also be hosted on Hello Meghalaya if dubbed in Khasi, Garo or Pnar. Telugu feature Baa Baa Black Sheep, shot entirely in Meghalaya in 25 days, employed nearly 2,000 local youth, demonstrating the potential economic impact. “An initiative will work only if it sustains. I hope that’s the case here as well. Hello Meghalaya has given space to both mature filmmakers and newer talent which makes it even more special. Anybody can watch it as you don’t have to pay any money for it. This makes it accessible even to people living in remote villages,” says director and producer Tyrel Lyngdoh.Bringing Meghalaya together, live Hello Meghalaya also live streams cultural, sporting and other public events like Shad Suk Mynsiem, the Khasi spring thanksgiving celebration, Wangala, the Garo Festival of the Hundred Drums celebrating the harvest, Chad Sukra, a Pnar festival centred on community and togetherness, and the Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival, among others. It also streams government programmes, the Shillong Premier League, Meghalaya State League, kickboxing, MMA, archery, basketball, arm wrestling and Meghalaya Games 2025.In June 2026, the inaugural Hello Meghalaya Music Awards recognized the work of several musicians. Reble (Daiaphi Lamare), the Shillong rapper who gained wider recognition through Dhurandhar, received Icon of the Year, while Eastern Brook, a band of visually impaired musicians, received Best Inspirational Song. At the same event, the state’s chief minister Conrad K Sangma announced the setting up of a Film City and Film Institute in Shillong and a Music Institute in Tura, signaling a long-term effort to make creative careers viable livelihoods.From regional stories to global audiencesIndia’s media landscape is changing: regional content is no longer confined to regional audiences, and Meghalaya is positioning itself within that transformation.The next phase is stronger links with national and international distributors, streaming platforms and creative networks. The state already has filmmakers whose work has demonstrated that its stories can travel. Dominic Megam Sangma’s Rimdogittanga (Rapture) won the National Film Award for Best Garo Film and the Cultural Diversity Award at the Asia Pacific Screen Awards. Pradip Kurbah’s Ri, Onaatah and Ïewduh each won the National Award for Best Khasi Film, while Ïewduh also won the Kim Ji-seok Award at Busan. This year, Pradip Kurbah’s Ha Lyngkha Bneng (The Elysian Field), created from a Hello Meghalaya grant, premiered at the Chicago South Asian Film Festival on September 19, 2026. It had its African premiere at FINIFA’s Main Competition in Agadir, Morocco in early October, and won Best Film, Best Director and the NETPAC Award at the 2025 Moscow International Film Festival.These achievements show that the state’s filmmakers are already producing work that finds audiences and recognition beyond the region. Distribution collaborations can build on this foundation, creating pathways for filmmakers, musicians and other creators to reach national and international audiences.That brings the story back to where it began. As audiences seek specific, authentic, place-rooted stories, Meghalaya can become both producer and exporter of culture.Chittajit Mitra (he/him) is a queer writer, translator and editor from Allahabad. He is co-founder of RAQS, an organisation working on gender, sexuality and mental health.

title: Redevelopment must renew buildings without unmaking communities | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Adrija Agarwal, president, Sattva Group.
content: Across Mumbai, redevelopment is asking entire communities to exchange the certainty of the familiar for a promise about the future. A family may be leaving the home in which two generations were raised. A tenant may be moving away from the neighbourhood that makes work and school accessible. A shopkeeper may be stepping away from customers built over decades. Older residents may be leaving behind neighbours who function as an informal support system.Redevelopment promises safer structures, better-planned homes, improved accessibility and modern infrastructure. Yet residents are not only evaluating the replacement apartment. They are also asking whether they will return on time, whether the new development will remain affordable to maintain, whether local livelihoods will survive the transition, and whether the neighbourhood will still feel like theirs.These concerns are not an argument against change. They reveal the true complexity of redevelopment. It is both a capital-intensive real-estate proposition and a transformation of an inhabited social environment. The former is assessed through title, land potential, FSI, rehabilitation obligations, transit rent, approvals, construction costs, sale inventory and returns. The latter is experienced through relationships, livelihoods, identity and patterns of everyday life. Successful redevelopment depends on planning these two realities together.The scale makes this an urgent urban question. Between January 2020 and March 15, 2026, Mumbai recorded 1,094 redevelopment agreements, unlocking approximately 432 acres and potentially generating about 59,000 sale units, excluding rehabilitation and amenity areas. The city also has more than 13,000 cessed buildings requiring structural assessment and renewal. Redevelopment is therefore not a collection of isolated transactions; it is becoming one of the principal ways in which Mumbai will renew its housing stock and reshape established neighbourhoods.If redevelopment is to create continuity rather than displacement, the conventional feasibility study must become more expansive. Structural condition, ownership, regulatory potential and project economics determine whether a development can proceed. They do not fully explain what must be protected while it proceeds.That understanding begins with observing how the neighbourhood functions. Local enterprises may depend on relationships built over generations. A courtyard, corridor or shaded entrance may enable interaction and informal supervision. Familiar pedestrian routes may connect residents to schools, transport, healthcare, markets and places of worship. Together, these elements form a kind of social infrastructure that makes urban density manageable.The objective is not to preserve an ageing physical form unchanged. It is to identify which functions and relationships should continue after that form changes. This understanding should influence the placement of common areas, pedestrian circulation, retail interfaces, accessibility, phasing and temporary relocation.Resident engagement is consequently most valuable before the project’s principal assumptions harden. Residents are not a uniform stakeholder group. Owners, tenants, young families, older residents and local businesses may experience the same transition differently. Their concerns can range from transit accommodation and school commutes to lease continuity, customer access, maintenance costs and certainty of return.Engagement conducted after the master plan is substantially complete can explain a proposition. Engagement conducted earlier can improve it. It becomes a source of planning intelligence rather than a procedural formality.That intelligence has direct commercial value. Redevelopment involves fragmented ownership, consent risk, regulatory complexity, construction inflation, long cash-flow cycles and reputational exposure. Ambiguity around entitlements, timelines, escalation mechanisms and grievance resolution can compound each of these risks.Clear commitments and transparent communication, therefore, do more than reassure residents. They create more durable consent and greater execution certainty. Trust is not external to the business plan; in redevelopment, it is one of the conditions on which the business plan holds.The same discipline must extend to the design and operating model. Commercial viability cannot be measured only through achievable FSI, the value of the sale component or positioning at launch. It must also account for the performance of the completed development and the ability of returning residents to sustain it.A larger rehabilitation unit is not an unqualified improvement if its maintenance becomes unaffordable. An extensive amenity programme does not create enduring value if it is costly to operate or disconnected from residents’ needs. Efficient layouts, durable materials, passive design, accessible circulation and purposeful shared spaces often create stronger long-term outcomes.These choices are where community continuity becomes tangible. A familiar courtyard may be reinterpreted as a shared terrace or well-planned podium space. Local retail can be integrated rather than displaced. Seating, play areas and pedestrian movement can be designed around actual patterns of use rather than treated as residual elements of the site plan.The same thinking must extend beyond the plot boundary. Additional density creates greater demand for water, energy, waste management, mobility, green cover, public space and social infrastructure. A development may be underwritten plot by plot, but its cumulative effects are experienced neighbourhood by neighbourhood.Sustainability must, therefore, encompass both the environmental performance of the building and the carrying capacity of its urban context. This calls for closer alignment between development potential, infrastructure provision and long-term operating efficiency.The developer’s role is ultimately to reconcile these multiple imperatives: residents’ aspirations, commercial discipline, environmental responsibility and urban capacity. The purpose is neither to hold a neighbourhood in the past nor to maximise built potential without regard to consequence. It is to enable necessary change without discarding the social value accumulated over decades.Redevelopment succeeds when residents return not only to safer and better homes, but to a neighbourhood that remains economically viable, environmentally resilient and recognisably their own. The most enduring projects will demonstrate that modernisation and memory are not opposing forces—and that progress creates the greatest value when communities are carried forward with it.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Adrija Agarwal, president, Sattva Group.

title: Raja Krishnamoorthi warns of rising anti-Indian hate on social media, calls for Big Tech accountability | Hindustan Times
description: US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi accused major technology companies of profiting from anti-Indian and anti-South Asian hate online.
content: US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi has accused major technology companies of profiting from online hatred targeting Indian, Hindu and other South Asian communities, calling on Congress to hold social media platforms accountable for failing to curb hateful content.“Anti-Indian hate is exploding on social media, and Big Tech is profiting from it. These companies have no incentive to stop the hatred they help spread. Congress must hold them accountable,” Krishnamoorthi said in a post on X.In a video accompanying the post, the Illinois Democrat alleged that social media platforms were not doing enough to police their services and cited a rise of more than 240% in posts promoting anti-South Asian hate on X.“The number of X posts, posts on X or tweets, basically touting anti-South Asian hate has increased by more than 240% over a very short period of time,” he said. Krishnamoorthi argued that technology companies lacked sufficient financial incentives to remove hateful content and called for federal action to ensure they faced consequences for failing to address the problem.The congressman did not identify the specific dataset behind the 240% figure in the supplied statement.Anti-South Asian hate raises concerns over social mediaThe remarks highlight concerns about online discrimination targeting Indian Americans and other South Asian communities in the United States. Such content can include racial slurs, hostility towards cultural and religious identities, and claims portraying South Asians as threats to American jobs and demographics.Krishnamoorthi's criticism centers on the role of major technology companies in moderating content on their platforms and whether existing measures are sufficient to address the spread of hate.His call for congressional intervention also raises questions about how the federal government could hold technology companies accountable. However, he did not outline a specific legislative proposal or identify particular penalties in his post.Congressman calls for federal action against Big TechIn his video, Krishnamoorthi said the issue required action at the federal level, arguing that social media companies should face consequences if they failed to act against hateful content.“We have to, at this point, at the federal level, make sure that they face the full consequences of not taking action,” he said.The remarks come amid wider debate in the United States over online hate speech, platform moderation and the responsibilities of technology companies for content shared by users.Krishnamoorthi's central demand was that technology companies be held accountable for their handling of anti-Indian and anti-South Asian hate online.

title: Haryana FDA inspects Gurugram firm over health claims, flags nine food products for suspected misbranding | Hindustan Times
description: According to the FDA, some of the claims appeared to go beyond general nutritional support and could imply the prevention or treatment of diseases.
content: The Haryana Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) raided the premises of a Gurugram-based food brand in Fazilpur Jharsa and flagged nine food products marketed for suspected misbranding on Thursday, officials said on Friday.The inspection was conducted to scrutinise products sold under the same brand, including online claims of relief from nerve and joint pain, constipation management, improved lung function, liver detoxification, blood sugar control, and reduction of skin pigmentation.It was carried out under the directions of FDA Haryana commissioner Dr Manoj Yadav. The team included senior drugs control and drugs control officers from Gurugram, along with food safety officer Dr Deepak.According to the FDA, some of the claims appeared to go beyond general nutritional support and could imply the prevention or treatment of diseases and medical conditions. The inspection The company’s representative was asked to provide scientific evidence and supporting regulatory documents, but the required records were not produced during the inspection, the department said in a press note.The department said a show-cause notice was issued to the firm. Further action will be decided after examining the company's reply and the investigation findings.The matter is being examined under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the relevant rules and regulations, the FDA said.The inspection team also collected nine food samples and nine cosmetic samples for testing and analysis. Documents, including the company's FSSAI licence, GST certificate, certificate of incorporation and details of its current directors, were also collected.The department said the investigation would assess whether the products and their advertised claims complied with applicable regulatory requirements.

title: Next evolution of HR is intelligence, not just automation | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Girish Rowjee, co-founder & CEO, greytHR.
content: For more than two decades, HR technology has helped organisations move from paper-based processes to digital platforms and automation. Payroll moved beyond spreadsheets, attendance and leave became digital, employee records became centralised, and routine processes became faster and more consistent. This took a significant amount of manual work off HR teams.But HR work has changed too. Teams today manage larger and more distributed workforces, navigate complex compliance requirements, respond to rising employee expectations and support business growth, often with leaner teams. SHRM’s 2025 State of the Workplace research found that 62% of HR leaders said their departments were operating beyond their typical capacity, up from 57% in 2023.So, if automation has made routine HR work easier, what should technology help HR do next?The answer is not simply more automation. It is helping HR understand information, spot what needs attention and act on it, while giving teams more time for work that requires human judgement.Human Resource Management System (HRMS) platforms have made many core HR processes faster and more consistent. But HR work goes well beyond transactions. Professionals spend time finding information, responding to queries, interpreting data, following up on processes and making decisions across the employee lifecycle.Much of the information they need already exists within the organisation. The challenge is finding it, connecting it and understanding what it means. For example, a rise in queries about a policy, repeated attendance issues or delays in recruitment could point to a larger problem. Traditional systems can record these events, but the next generation of HR technology should help HR spot these patterns and understand what they mean.This means moving from systems that simply execute tasks to systems that can also help HR understand what is happening and what needs attention. An intelligent HRMS should make it easier to find information, spot patterns and act on them.This is where AI can play a meaningful role. Its value should go beyond chatbots or automating existing workflows. AI can help HR teams spot patterns, connect information across processes and get answers without having to search through multiple systems and reports.Deloitte India reported in July 2026 that more than half of Indian organisations had started integrating AI into HR and work processes, while more than 60% reported a shift from task-based roles towards roles requiring problem-solving and creativity. As routine work becomes more automated, HR professionals can spend more time interpreting information, solving problems and making decisions that require context and judgement.But saving time is only part of the story. What matters is how HR uses that time.When technology takes care of repetitive requests, information searches and routine exceptions, HR can spend more time understanding workforce needs, supporting managers, developing talent and making informed decisions.HR is still, at its core, a people function. Developing talent, supporting managers, building engagement, strengthening culture and planning for the future require more than efficient processes. Technology should take away some of the administrative work and create more room for conversations and decisions that need human judgement.Deloitte’s 2025 research found that 74% of surveyed workers, managers and executives considered prioritising human capabilities to be very or critically important. The goal should not be to make HR less human by moving more decisions to technology. It should be to reduce the operational load so HR professionals have more time for work that needs judgement, empathy and context.The fundamentals of HR technology are not changing. What is changing is what we expect these systems to do with the information they generate. An HRMS should not just store information and manage workflows. It should also help HR make sense of that information and act on it. The next step for HR technology is not more automation for its own sake. It is better information, better context and more time for people.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Girish Rowjee, co-founder & CEO, greytHR.

title: Jio IPO : జియో ఐపీఓ సబ్​స్క్రిప్షన్​కి ఇంకొన్ని గంటలే ఛాన్స్! అప్లై చేయాలా? వద్దా? జీఎంపీ ఎంతంటే.. | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: భారత్‌లోనే అత్యంత భారీ బిజినెస్ డీల్‌గా నిలిచిన రూ.30,213 కోట్ల రిలయన్స్ జియో ప్లాట్‌ఫామ్స్ ఐపీఓ సబ్‌స్క్రిప్షన్ నేటితో (అక్టోబర్ 23) ముగియనుంది. గ్రే మార్కెట్‌లో దాదాపు 22 శాతం ప్రీమియం పలుకుతున్న ఈ ఐపీఓలో ఇన్వెస్ట్ చేయవచ్చా లేదా అనే దానిపై మార్కెట్ దిగ్గజాల విశ్లేషణ ఇక్కడ చూడండి..
content: దేశీయ స్టాక్ మార్కెట్ చరిత్రలోనే సరికొత్త రికార్డులు తిరగరాస్తున్న 'జియో ప్లాట్‌ఫామ్స్' పబ్లిక్ ఇష్యూ (ఐపీఓ) సబ్​స్క్రిప్షన్ ప్రాసెస్ నేటితో (శుక్రవారం, అక్టోబర్ 23) ముగియనుంది. రూ.30,213 కోట్ల భారీ నిధుల సేకరణ లక్ష్యంతో మార్కెట్లోకి వచ్చిన ఈ జియో ఐపీఓకు మొదటి రోజు నుంచే ఇన్వెస్టర్ల నుంచి అనూహ్య స్పందన లభిస్తోంది. రెండో రోజు చివరి నాటికే మొత్తం ఇష్యూ 5.57 రెట్లు ఓవర్‌సబ్‌స్క్రైబ్ అయి మదుపరుల ఆదరణను చాటుకుంది!తెలుగు రాష్ట్రాల్లోని రిటైల్ ఇన్వెస్టర్లు సహా దేశవ్యాప్తంగా ఉన్న చిన్న, పెద్ద మదుపరులు ఈ ఐపీఓలో దరఖాస్తు చేసేందుకు చివరి క్షణం వరకు పోటీపడుతున్నారు. ఈ నేపథ్యంలో ఆఖరి రోజున అసలు బిడ్ వేయాలా? లేక లిస్టింగ్ తర్వాత కొనవచ్చా? అనే అంశాలపై ఆర్థిక రంగానికి చెందిన ప్రముఖ విశ్లేషకులు ఇచ్చిన సలహాలతో పాటు ఇతర కీలక వివరాలను ఇక్కడ తెలుసుకోండి..జియో ఐపీఓకు సబ్‌స్క్రిప్షన్ జోరు..రెండో రోజు బిడ్డింగ్ ముగిసే సమయానికి రిటైల్ ఇన్వెస్టర్ల కోటా 1.54 రెట్లు భర్తీ కాగా, కంపెనీ ఉద్యోగుల విభాగంలో 2.10 రెట్ల దరఖాస్తులు వచ్చాయి. నాన్-ఇన్‌స్టిట్యూషనల్ ఇన్వెస్టర్ల (ఎన్​ఐఐ) కేటాయింపు 5.97 రెట్లు సబ్‌స్క్రిప్షన్ సాధించింది. విదేశీ, దేశీయ దిగ్గజ సంస్థాగత ఇన్వెస్టర్లు (క్యూఐబీ) ఈ ఇష్యూపై విపరీతమైన ఆసక్తి చూపిస్తూ ఏకంగా 13.29 రెట్లు దరఖాస్తులు దాఖలు చేశారు. దీనితో మార్కెట్‌లో జియో ప్లాట్‌ఫామ్స్ ఎంతటి నమ్మకాన్ని సంపాదించుకుందో స్పష్టమవుతోంది.జియో ఐపీఓ గ్రే మార్కెట్ ప్రీమియం ఎంత ఉందంటే..ప్రాథమిక మార్కెట్ వర్గాల సమాచారం ప్రకారం, గ్రే మార్కెట్‌లో జియో షేర్లకు బలమైన డిమాండ్ కనిపిస్తోంది! శుక్రవారం ఉదయం నాటికి జియో ఐపీఓ గ్రే మార్కెట్ ప్రీమియం (జీఎంపీ) రూ.240 వద్ద కొనసాగుతోంది. ఐపీఓ గరిష్ఠ ధర రూ.1,119 ప్రాతిపదికగా చూస్తే, ఇది దాదాపు 21.45 శాతం ప్రీమియంను సూచిస్తోంది. ఈ లెక్కన అక్టోబర్ 28న స్టాక్ ఎక్స్​ఛేంజీల్లో జియో షేరు రూ.1,359 వద్ద లిస్ట్ అయ్యే అవకాశం ఉందని మార్కెట్ వర్గాలు అంచనా వేస్తున్నాయి.జియో ఐపీఓ ఇన్వెస్ట్ చేయొచ్చా? నిపుణులు ఏం చెబుతున్నారు?ఐపీఓ ఇప్పటికే పూర్తిగా సబ్‌స్క్రైబ్ అయినప్పటికీ, సుదీర్ఘకాల దృక్పథంతో జియో ప్లాట్​ఫామ్స్​లో ఇన్వెస్టే చేయవచ్చని నిపుణులు సూచిస్తున్నారు."కేవలం లిస్టింగ్ రోజు స్వల్ప లాభాలు వస్తాయా లేదా అనేది చూసి నిర్ణయం తీసుకోకూడదు. దీర్ఘకాలిక పెట్టుబడి ప్రాతిపదికన ఈ ఐపీఓకు దరఖాస్తు చేసుకోవడం శ్రేయస్కరం. కంపెనీ రాబోయే కాలంలో సాధించే వృద్ధిపైనే ఇన్వెస్టర్లు దృష్టి పెట్టాలి," అని రేలిగేర్ బ్రోకింగ్ సీనియర్ వైస్ ప్రెసిడెంట్ (రీసెర్చ్) అజిత్ మిశ్రా అభిప్రాయపడ్డారు.అంచనా వేసిన ఎబిట్​డాకు కంపెనీ వ్యాల్యుయేషన్ 11.6 రెట్లుగా ఉండటంతో ఇది మరీ చౌకైందేమీ కాదని, అయితే టెలికాం రంగానికే పరిమితం కాకుండా క్లౌడ్ కంప్యూటింగ్, ఆర్టిఫీషియల్ ఇంటెలిజెన్స్ (ఏఐ) వంటి భవిష్యత్ సాంకేతికతలలోకి జియో విస్తరిస్తున్న తీరు సుదీర్ఘకాలంలో మంచి ప్రయోజనాలను ఇస్తుందని ఆయన స్పష్టం చేశారు. ఒకవేళ షేర్ల కేటాయింపు దక్కని పక్షంలో, లిస్టింగ్ రోజున 20 నుంచి 30 శాతం ప్రీమియంతో షేరు ప్రారంభమైతే కొద్దిరోజులు ఆగి మార్కెట్ దిద్దుబాటు సమయంలో కొనుగోలు చేయడం మేలని సలహా ఇచ్చారు."వ్యాల్యుయేషన్స్ ఆశాజనకంగా ఉన్నాయి. సంస్థాగత ఇన్వెస్టర్ల నుంచి బలమైన మద్దతు లభిస్తున్నందున రిటైల్ ఇన్వెస్టర్లు ఈ ఐపీఓలో ఇన్వెస్ట్ చేయడాన్ని పరిశీలించవచ్చు," అని సెబీ రిజిస్టర్డ్ స్వతంత్ర మార్కెట్ నిపుణుడు అంబరీష్ బాలిగా తెలిపారు.భారతీ ఎయిర్‌టెల్‌తో పోలిస్తే జియో పొజిషన్ ఏంటి?ఎస్ఎంసీ గ్లోబల్ సెక్యూరిటీస్ డైరెక్టర్, సీఈఓ అజయ్ గార్గ్ కంపెనీ బలాబలాలను విశ్లేషించారు. జియో ప్లాట్‌ఫామ్స్ దాదాపు 53.3 కోట్ల భారీ కస్టమర్ల బేస్ కలిగి ఉండి, ఆర్థిక సంవత్సరం 2026లో రూ.1.47 లక్షల కోట్ల ఆదాయాన్ని, రూ.30,049 కోట్ల నికర లాభాన్ని గడించిందని ఆయన వివరించారు.ఐపీఓ గరిష్ఠ ధర వద్ద కంపెనీ మార్కెట్ విలువ రూ.10.3 లక్షల కోట్లుగా ఉంది. ఆర్థిక సంవత్సరం 2026 సంపాదన ఆధారంగా జియో ఐపీఓ పీఈ రేషియో 33.3 రెట్లు కాగా, దాని ప్రధాన పోటీదారు భారతీ ఎయిర్‌టెల్ పిఈ రేషియో 40.7 రెట్లుగా ఉంది. అంటే పీఈ నిష్పత్తి ప్రాతిపదికన ఎయిర్‌టెల్ కంటే జియో చౌకగా లభిస్తోంది.అలాగే, 2026 జూన్ త్రైమాసికంలో జియో వినియోగదారు సగటు ఆదాయం (ఆర్​పూ) నెలకు రూ.215.6 గా నమోదు కాగా, ఎయిర్‌టెల్ ఏఆర్‌పీయూ రూ.264 గా ఉంది. దీనిని బట్టి జియోకు మున్ముందు ఆర్​పూ పెంచుకుని ఆదాయాన్ని మరింత పెంచుకునేందుకు పుష్కలమైన అవకాశాలు ఉన్నాయని స్పష్టమవుతోంది."లిస్టింగ్ గెయిన్స్ మాత్రమే ఆశించే వారు లిస్టింగ్ తర్వాత మార్కెట్ సరళిని చూసి నిర్ణయం తీసుకోవడం మంచిది. అయితే లిస్టింగ్ తర్వాత కూడా తక్కువ ధరకే షేరు దొరుకుతుందని గ్యారెంటీ లేదు. కాబట్టి తాత్కాలిక హడావుడిని చూడకుండా కంపెనీ దీర్ఘకాలిక వృద్ధిని నమ్మి ఇన్వెస్ట్ చేయాలి," అని అజయ్ గార్గ్ స్పష్టం చేశారు.(గమనిక- ఇది సమాచారం కోసం రూపొందించిన కథనం మాత్రమే. హిందుస్థాన్ టైమ్స్ తెలుగుకు ఎలాంటి సంబంధం లేదు. ఎదైనా ఐపీఓలో ఇన్వెస్ట్ చేసే ముందు సెబీ రిజిస్టర్డ్ ఫైనాన్షియల్ అడ్వైజర్​ని సంప్రదించడం శ్రేయస్కరం.)

title: మరికొన్ని రోజుల్లో డబుల్ పవర్‌ఫుల్‌గా మారనున్న శుక్రుడు.. వీరికి రెట్టింపు ప్రయోజనాలు | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: శుక్రుడు డిసెంబర్ నెలలో ఒకటి కంటే ఎక్కువసార్లు తన స్థానాన్ని మార్చుకుంటాడు. దీని కారణంగా శుక్రుని శక్తి పెరుగుతుంది. ఇది అనేక రాశుల వారికి వృత్తిపరంగా పురోగతి సాధించడానికి, సొంత ఇల్లు కొనుగోలు చేయడానికి అవకాశాలను కల్పిస్తుంది.
content: శుక్రుడిని అందం, వైభవం, ప్రేమ, సంపద, శ్రేయస్సుకు అధిపతిగా పరిగణిస్తారు. శుక్రుడు తన స్థానాన్ని మార్చుకున్నప్పుడల్లా దాని ప్రభావం అన్ని రాశుల వారి జీవితాలపై కనిపిస్తుంది. డిసెంబర్ 5న శుక్రుడు చిత్తా నక్షత్రం నుండి స్వాతి నక్షత్రంలోకి మారుతాడు. ఆ తర్వాత డిసెంబర్ 22న అది విశాఖ నక్షత్రంలోకి ప్రవేశిస్తుంది. ఈ నక్షత్రానికి అధిపతి గురుడు. ఈ సమయంలో శుక్రుడి శక్తి రెట్టింపు అవుతుంది. అందువల్ల డిసెంబర్ మాసంలో ఏ రాశుల వారి జాతకంలో శుక్రుడి స్థానం బలంగా ఉంటుందో చూడండి.మేష రాశిశుక్ర గ్రహ సంచారం మేష రాశి వారికి అనుకూలమైన మార్పులను తెస్తుంది. ఈ కాలంలో కొత్త వాహనం లేదా ఆస్తిని కొనుగోలు చేసే అవకాశాలు ఉన్నాయి. అలాగే ఆర్థిక పరిస్థితి గణనీయంగా మెరుగుపడుతుంది. మీరు అప్పుగా ఇచ్చిన డబ్బును తిరిగి చెల్లిస్తారు. కుటుంబంలో సంతోషం రెట్టింపు అవుతుంది. అలాగే పని, వృత్తిలో పురోగతికి మార్గాలు తెరుచుకుంటాయి. ఈ కాలంలో వ్యాపారవేత్తలు కొత్త కాంట్రాక్టులను పొందవచ్చు. అలాగే దేశ విదేశాలకు ప్రయాణించే అవకాశాలు ఉన్నాయి. మీరు మీ పనిలో కొత్త బాధ్యతలను విజయవంతంగా నిర్వహిస్తారు.మకర రాశిమకర రాశి వారికి శుక్ర గ్రహ సంచారం డిసెంబర్ నెల అంతా అద్భుతమైన మార్పులను తీసుకువస్తుంది. దీని కారణంగా మీరు మీ వ్యాపారంలో, పనిలో పురోగతి సాధించగలుగుతారు. రైతులు, వ్యాపారవేత్తలు, పారిశ్రామికవేత్తలు ఒక పెద్ద ప్రాజెక్ట్ లేదా క్లయింట్ నుండి ప్రయోజనం పొందుతారు. కళాకారులు, సృజనాత్మక రంగాలలో ఉన్నవారికి ఈ కాలం చాలా అనుకూలంగా ఉంటుంది. ఉద్యోగంలో ఉన్నవారికి ఈ కాలంలో పదోన్నతులు లభిస్తాయి. మీరు పనిలో కొత్త బాధ్యతలు స్వీకరించవచ్చు. మీ ప్రాజెక్టులన్నీ విజయవంతంగా పూర్తవుతాయి. అలాగే ఇల్లు కొనాలనే కల నెరవేరవచ్చు. వైవాహిక జీవితంలో శాంతి, సంతోషం రెట్టింపు అవుతాయి. మీ ఆరోగ్యం మీ అన్ని ప్రయత్నాలకు సహకరిస్తుంది.వృశ్చిక రాశివృశ్చిక రాశి వారికి డిసెంబరులో శుక్ర గ్రహ సంచారం అనేక ప్రయోజనాలను చేకూరుస్తుంది. ఈ కాలం సంతోషానికి నాంది పలుకుతుంది. కొత్త అవకాశాలను అందిపుచ్చుకోవడానికి, మీ వృత్తిపరమైన కార్యకలాపాలలో పురోగతి సాధించడానికి ఇది సరైన సమయం. ఈ శుక్ర సంచారం ఉద్యోగంలో ఉన్నవారికి గణనీయమైన వృద్ధిని, లాభాలను తెస్తుంది. మీరు ఉద్యోగంలో పదోన్నతిని ఆశించవచ్చు. ఇది ఆర్థిక పురోగతిని కూడా తెస్తుంది. సంపదను సంపాదించడానికి, మీ భవిష్యత్తును ఆర్థికంగా సురక్షితం చేసుకోవడానికి ఇది మీకు అవకాశాలను ఇస్తుంది. మీ జీవిత భాగస్వామితో సాన్నిహిత్యం పెరగడంతో కుటుంబ వాతావరణం సంతోషంగా ఉంటుంది. శుక్రుని ఆశీస్సులతో, ఈ నెల ఆర్థిక శ్రేయస్సును మాత్రమే కాకుండా వ్యక్తిగత, వృత్తిపరమైన అభివృద్ధిని కూడా తెస్తుంది. మొత్తంగా ఈ శుక్ర సంచారం మీ జీవితాన్ని మరింత మంచిగా మారుస్తుంది.ధనుస్సు రాశిడిసెంబరులో శుక్ర గ్రహ సంచారం ధనుస్సు రాశి వారికి అనేక ప్రయోజనాలను చేకూరుస్తుంది. ధనుస్సు రాశిలో జన్మించిన వారు తమ అన్ని ప్రయత్నాలలో విజయాన్ని ఆశించవచ్చు. కార్యాలయంలో మీ గౌరవం పెరుగుతుంది. మీ బంధువుల సహాయంతో, మీరు వ్యాపారంలో గొప్ప పురోగతిని సాధించగలరు. అలాగే ఇది మిమ్మల్ని పనిలో ప్రత్యేకంగా నిలబెడుతుంది. సహోద్యోగులతో సంబంధాలు మెరుగుపడతాయి, కార్యాలయ వాతావరణం ఉల్లాసంగా ఉంటుంది. పారిశ్రామికవేత్తలు విదేశాలలో తమ వ్యాపారాన్ని ప్రారంభించడానికి ప్రయత్నించవచ్చు. కొత్త వ్యాపారాన్ని ప్రారంభించాలనుకునే వారికి, లాభదాయకమైన వ్యాపారాన్ని ప్రారంభించడానికి ఇది అనుకూలమైన కాలం. మీరు కుటుంబ సభ్యులు, స్నేహితులతో సంతోషకరమైన క్షణాలను ఆశించవచ్చు. ఈ కాలంలో మీ ఆరోగ్యం పట్ల జాగ్రత్తగా ఉండటం ముఖ్యం.కన్యా రాశిశుక్ర గ్రహ సంచారం కన్యారాశి వారికి అదృష్ట ద్వారాలను తెరుస్తుంది. ఈ కాలంలో మీరు వివిధ కాంట్రాక్టుల ద్వారా అధికంగా సంపాదించే అవకాశాలను పొందుతారు. ఈ సమయంలో మీ ధైర్యం, బలం రెట్టింపు అవుతాయి. అలాగే ఈ సమయంలో మీ పాత అప్పుల సమస్యలు తీరిపోతాయి. వైవాహిక జీవితంలో ఆనందం రెట్టింపు అవుతుంది. మీరు మీ భాగస్వామితో ఉత్సాహంగా సమయం గడుపుతారు. పురోగతికి మీ భాగస్వామి సహాయపడతారు. ఈ సమయంలో, మీరు ఎంతోకాలంగా ఎదురుచూస్తున్న రుణం లభించే అవకాశం ఉంది. మీరు వివిధ కార్యకలాపాల ద్వారా మీ వృత్తి జీవితంలో విజయం సాధిస్తారు. పనిలో మీ పై అధికారుల నుండి గౌరవం పెరుగుతుంది. మీ ఆరోగ్యం బాగుంటుంది. అన్ని ప్రాజెక్టులు సకాలంలో పూర్తవుతాయి.

title: Everyone seems to be ramping up their security”: Ronit Roy | Hindustan Times
description: Ronit Roy says demand for celebrity security is rising after the firing outside Tiger Shroff’s residence, with stars beefing up protection amid safety concerns
content: The firing incident outside actor Tiger Shroff’s residence has once again brought celebrity security into focus, with actors reassessing their safety amid growing concerns. Actor Ronit Roy, who runs a private security agency, has provided protection to several Bollywood A-listers, including Amitabh Bachchan and Akshay Kumar, as well as Saif Ali Khan following the stabbing incident at his residence.Speaking to HT City, Roy (61) says the firing incident outside Tiger Shroff’s residence has once again brought celebrity safety into focus, with demand for professional security rising as actors strengthen existing arrangements and seek fresh protection.“It’s a normal practice for demand to fluctuate. There are times when it picks up and times when things are slow. However, given the current circumstances, everyone seems to be ramping up their security. There is rise in demand for security. Existing security is being beefed up. New security is being given,” he says.Roy points to a shift in how celebrities perceive professional protection, saying clients are increasingly recognising its importance. “Earlier, people would question why they needed such security. Now, they understand what we do and why it matters,” he says.The actor also notes that younger celebrities, including Gen Z, are more receptive to professional security and understand that protection goes beyond physical presence. “They understand that security is not just about having someone with biceps standing beside you; it’s about brains” he says.According to Roy, enquiries have picked up as celebrities take a more proactive approach to their safety. “Everyone is enquiring about security. Celebrities are increasingly taking steps to protect themselves. People are no longer just window-shopping when it comes to security,” he says.The shift suggests that celebrity security is increasingly being viewed as a necessary precaution rather than merely a status symbol, particularly amid heightened concerns over personal safety.

title: JEE Mains 2027 Registration Date LIVE: When will JEE Session 1 application process begin? | Competitive Exams
description: JEE Mains 2027 Registration Date LIVE: NTA JEE session 1 exam registration dates will be released soon. The notice will be available on the official website of JEE. Follow the blog for latest updates on application form and other details.  | Competitive Exams
content: JEE Mains 2027 Registration Date LIVE: The National Testing Agency (NTA has not yet released the JEE Main 2027 registration date. When released, candidates who want to appear for the Joint Entrance Examination for Session 1 can check the notice on the official website of NTA JEE at jeemain.nta.nic.in. The JEE Main Session 1 examination will be held on January 22 to 24 and from January 28 to 30, 2027. The examination will be held in two shifts: the first shift from 9 am to 12 noon and the second shift from 3 pm to 6 pm. Candidates who are applying for the exam should have passed Class 12 or an equivalent exam. The candidates who will appear for Class 12 in 2027 can also apply. For appearing in the JEE (Main) - 2027, there is no age limit for the candidates. The candidates who have passed the class XII / equivalent Examination in 2025, 2026 or are appearing in 2027, irrespective of their age, can appear in the JEE (Main) – 2027 Examination.The exam comprises two papers: Paper 1 and Paper 2A and 2B. Paper 1 (B.E. /B. Tech.) in “Computer Based Test (CBT)” mode. Paper 2A (B. Arch): Mathematics (Part-I) and Aptitude Test (Part-II) in “Computer Based Test (CBT)” mode and Drawing Test (Part-III) in pen and paper (offline) mode, to be attempted on a drawing sheet of A4 size. Paper 2B (B. Planning): Mathematics (Part-I), Aptitude Test (Part-II), and Planning-Based Questions (Part-III) in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode.Follow the blog for latest updates on exam registration, direct link and more.

title: Simple Wave electric scooter gets  ₹10,000 festive discount | Hindustan Times
description: Simple Energy is offering a  ₹10,000 discount on Simple Wave 3.7 kW and 5 kW scooters with TFT displays.
content: Simple Energy has announced a festive-season discount of ₹10,000 on the Simple Wave 3.7 kW and 5 kW electric scooters with TFT displays. The introductory offer is valid until December 31, 2026, and is available across North and East India, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.With the discount, the Simple Wave 3.7 kW TFT variant is available at an effective ex-showroom price of ₹1,64,999, down from its all-India price of ₹1,74,999. Meanwhile, the Simple Wave 5 kW TFT variant is priced at ₹1,79,999 after the discount, against its listed price of ₹1,89,999.The offer is valid from October 1 to December 31, 2026. Interested buyers can avail of the benefit through their nearest Simple Energy touchpoint.(Also read: Simple Wave first ride review: The family scooter I wanted to like more)Simple Wave: Key details Simple Energy unveiled the Simple Wave electric scooter lineup on September 2, 2026. The family-focused electric scooter range is designed for everyday commuting and is offered in multiple configurations, allowing buyers to choose between different battery capacities, display technologies and connected features.The Simple Wave features a 920 mm-long seat and 70 litres of storage capacity. The company says the scooter has been designed with an emphasis on practicality, technology and ergonomics for Indian families.The lineup comprises three variants and six products, catering to different customer requirements. The ₹10,000 introductory benefit, however, is specifically applicable to the 3.7 kW and 5 kW versions equipped with TFT displays.The festive offer gives prospective buyers an opportunity to purchase the electric scooter at a reduced price during the ongoing festive season. Customers can contact their nearest Simple Energy touchpoint for more information about the offer and availability in their city, as the terms and conditions would be available with them.

title: OTT Crime Thriller: కార్ల దొంగతనం నుంచి అతిపెద్ద నేర సామ్రాజ్యం వరకు.. ఈరోజు ఓటీటీలోకి వచ్చిన క్రైమ్ థ్రిల్లర్ ఎలా ఉంది? | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: OTT Crime Thriller: ప్రముఖ ఓటీటీ ప్లాట్‌ఫామ్ అమెజాన్ ప్రైమ్ వీడియోలో ఈరోజు విడుదలైన సరికొత్త క్రైమ్ కామెడీ థ్రిల్లర్ వెబ్ సిరీస్ 'చార్ యార్' (Chaar Yaar). అప్పు తీర్చడానికి మొదలుపెట్టిన కార్ల దొంగతనం.. నలుగురు కుర్రాళ్లను ముంబై నేర సామ్రాజ్యంలో ఎలా గ్యాంగ్‌స్టర్లుగా మార్చిందనేది ఈ సిరీస్ కథాంశం.
content: OTT Crime Thriller: క్రైమ్, సస్పెన్స్ థ్రిల్లర్‌కు పర్ఫెక్ట్ కామెడీ డోస్ తోడైతే వచ్చే వినోదమే వేరు. వీకెండ్‌లో బింజ్ వాచ్ చేయడానికి ఓ మంచి వెబ్ సిరీస్ కోసం చూస్తున్న ఓటీటీ ప్రియుల ముందుకు అమెజాన్ ప్రైమ్ వీడియో తీసుకువచ్చిన లేటెస్ట్ సిరీస్ 'చార్ యార్' (Chaar Yaar). ప్రసిద్ధ యూట్యూబర్, డిజిటల్ క్రియేటర్ పూరవ్ ఝా ప్రధాన నటుడిగా డిజిటల్ తెరకు పరిచయమైన ఈ వెబ్ సిరీస్ ప్రేక్షకులను ఎంతవరకు ఆకట్టుకుందో, బింజ్ వాచ్ చేయవచ్చో లేదో పూర్తి వివరాలతో కూడిన రివ్యూ ఇప్పుడు చూద్దాం.చార్ యార్ స్టోరీ ఏంటి.. వాళ్లు గ్యాంగ్‌స్టర్లు ఎలా మారారు?ఈ చార్ యార్ వెబ్ సిరీస్ కథ అంతా ముంబై నగరంలో నివసించే నలుగురు సాధారణ మిడిల్ క్లాస్ స్నేహితులు.. జై (ప్రేరక్ మెహతా), టోనీ (సైఖిబ్ అయ్యూబ్), సాహిల్ (పూరవ్ ఝా), సమీర్ (నమన్ జైన్) ల చుట్టూ తిరుగుతుంది. అత్యవసరంగా రూ. 10 లక్షల డబ్బు అవసరం పడటంతో, ఈ నలుగురు మిత్రులు ఈజీగా డబ్బు సంపాదించేందుకు కార్ల దొంగతనం అనే అడ్డదారిని ఎంచుకుంటారు.అయితే వీరు చేసే వరుస కార్ల దొంగతనాలు అనుకోకుండా ముంబైలోనే మోస్ట్ వాంటెడ్ గ్యాంగ్‌స్టర్ ఇంతియాజ్ ఇంజనీర్ (సికందర్ ఖేర్) కంట పడతాయి. దాంతో ఈ నలుగురిని తన నెట్‌వర్క్‌లోకి లాక్కుంటాడు ఇంతియాజ్. మొదట భయంతో, అనివార్య పరిస్థితిలో నేరప్రపంచంలోకి అడుగుపెట్టిన ఈ నలుగురు కుర్రాళ్ళు.. ఆ తర్వాత తమ తెలివితేటలతో ముంబై పోలీసులకే సవాల్ విసిరే స్థాయికి ఎదుగుతారు.మరోవైపు లేడీ పోలీస్ ఆఫీసర్ ఏఎస్ఐ సుమతి భాలేరావ్ (సయీ తమ్‌హంకర్) జై నేతృత్వంలోని ఈ గ్యాంగ్‌ను పట్టుకోవడానికి ప్రాణాలను పణంగా పెట్టి ఇన్వెస్టిగేషన్ ప్రారంభిస్తుంది. ఆ తర్వాత ఏం జరిగింది అనేది మిగిలిన కథ.చార్ యార్ ఎలా ఉందంటే?మొత్తం 8 ఎపిసోడ్లుగా రూపొందిన ఈ చార్ యార్ వెబ్ సిరీస్ మొదటి ఎపిసోడ్ నుంచే ప్రేక్షకులను కథలోకి తీసుకెళ్తుంది. హై-వోల్టేజ్ షూటౌట్ సీన్‌తో ప్రారంభమై, ఆ వెంటనే "ఇది కేవలం ట్రైలర్ మాత్రమే.. అసలు కథ ముందు ఉంది" అనే వాయిస్ ఓవర్‌తో గ్రిప్పింగ్ నరేషన్ ప్రారంభమవుతుంది.దర్శకుడు ముంబై నేటివిటీని, ఆ నగరంలోని యాసను, కార్ల దొంగతనం వెనుక ఉండే మాఫియా నెట్‌వర్క్‌ను అత్యంత నిశితంగా తెరకెక్కించారు. ఒకవైపు ఉత్కంఠ రేకెత్తించే క్రైమ్ ఎలిమెంట్స్ నడుస్తుంటే, మరోవైపు నలుగురు స్నేహితుల మధ్య ఉండే హాస్యం ప్రేక్షకులకు నవ్వులు పూయిస్తుంది. అటు పురుషాధిక్య పోలీస్ వ్యవస్థలో ఒక మహిళా అధికారిగా ఏఎస్ఐ భాలేరావ్ ఎదుర్కొనే అవమానాలు, తన సీనియర్లు ఆమెను తక్కువ అంచనా వేసినప్పటికీ శ్రమించి నిజాలను వెలికితీసే సన్నివేశాలు ఆలోచింపజేస్తాయి.ఈ సిరీస్ మొదటి 5 ఎపిసోడ్లు అత్యంత వేగంగా, సీట్ ఎడ్జ్ డ్రామాగా సాగుతాయి. అయితే 6వ ఎపిసోడ్‌కు వచ్చేసరికి కథ కాస్త సాగదీసినట్లు అనిపించినప్పటికీ, క్లైమాక్స్ ఎపిసోడ్లు మళ్లీ మునుపటి వేగాన్ని అందుకుని ప్రేక్షకులకు సంతృప్తికరమైన అనుభూతిని ఇస్తాయి.నటీనటుల నటన అదుర్స్డిజిటల్ క్రియేటర్ నుంచి నటుడిగా మారిన పూరవ్ ఝా (సాహిల్) తన పాత్రలో ఒదిగిపోయి అద్భుతమైన నటనను కనబరిచారు. జై గా నటించిన ప్రేరక్ మెహతా, టోనీగా సైఖిబ్ అయ్యూబ్, సమీర్‌గా నమన్ జైన్ తమ నటనతో నలుగురు మిత్రుల మధ్య ఉండే బలమైన బాండింగ్‌ను కళ్లకు కట్టారు.ఇక సపోర్టింగ్ రోల్స్ చేసిన సీనియర్ నటులు సయీ తమ్‌హంకర్, సికందర్ ఖేర్, చుంకీ పాండే, రాజేష్ తైలాంగ్, దిబ్యేందు భట్టాచార్యలు సిరీస్‌కు ప్రధాన పిల్లర్లుగా నిలిచారు. ముఖ్యంగా డైనమిక్ పోలీస్ ఆఫీసర్‌గా సయీ తమ్‌హంకర్ నటన, నెగెటివ్ షేడ్స్ ఉన్న గ్యాంగ్‌స్టర్‌గా సికందర్ ఖేర్ లుక్ అండ్ మాడ్యులేషన్ సిరీస్‌ను నెక్స్ట్ లెవెల్‌కు తీసుకెళ్లాయి.మీరు ఈ వీకెండ్‌లో ఒక మంచి క్రైమ్ థ్రిల్లర్, కామెడీతో కూడిన వెబ్ సిరీస్ చూడాలనుకుంటే 'చార్ యార్' మీకు పర్ఫెక్ట్ చాయిస్. ఎక్కడా బోర్ కొట్టకుండా సాగే కథనం, అద్భుతమైన నటన, గ్రిప్పింగ్ బ్యాక్‌గ్రౌండ్ మ్యూజిక్ దీని సొంతం. తప్పకుండా మీ వాచ్‌లిస్ట్‌లో చేర్చుకోవాల్సిన వెబ్ సిరీస్ ఇది. అయితే కేవలం హిందీ ఆడియో, ఇంగ్లిష్ సబ్ టైటిల్స్ తో మాత్రమే అందుబాటులో ఉంది.

title: Haryana power employees’ strike disrupts supply across districts, 40,000 join protest | Hindustan Times
description: The state government plans to challenge the 25-year distribution licence granted to Eleven Power Private Limited before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity.
content: Around 40,000 electricity department employees on Thursday began a three-day strike against the entry of a private power distribution company in Gurugram and Nuh, leading to disrupted supplies in several residential and industrial areas due to unattended breakdown complaints.The Haryana Electricity Employees and Engineers Joint Struggle Front called for a three-day strike after the state’s power sector regulator, Electricity , on October 19 granted a licence to a private company to supply electricity in Gurugram and Nuh districts along with the existing state-owned discoms.The impact of the strike was particularly severe in urban areas and industrial feeders, where outages disrupted household water supplies, office work, and students’ preparations for competitive examinations. The strike, called from October 22 to 24, began at 10pm on Wednesday.The employees have warned that they will not attend to routine breakdowns during the agitation, raising concerns over the restoration of supply wherever technical faults occur. With a large section of the workforce joining the agitation, several 33-kV and 11-kV feeders suffered breakdowns.Also read: Power restored in many parts of Gurugram after strike over private licence triggered blackoutsUnions and farmers’ organisations extend support to agitationMeanwhile, constituent organisations of the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, the Sarv Karamchari Sangh Haryana and several trade unions, including CITU, AITUC, INTUC, and AIUTUC, extended their support to the strike and staged demonstrations at various locations across the state.In Rohtak, the district helpline had received 1,022 complaints by Thursday morning, while several villages reported power cuts and faults on urban and rural feeders. In Sirsa, however, officials claimed that alternative arrangements had helped limit the impact. Superintending engineer Ashutosh Kumar Panchal, posted in Sirsa, said staff from other departments had been deployed. Of approximately 900 feeders in the district, 30 were reported to be non-functional at the time of the assessment.In Gurugram, residents of Sector 7 reported outages beginning Wednesday night, with exhausted inverters, disrupted water supplies and internet connectivity problems.In Charkhi Dadri district, the closure of Sanjarwas and Ghasola power houses and faults on 11-kV lines affected electricity supply to dozens of villages. Kurukshetra also witnessed significant disruption, with power cuts affecting nearly half the city, according to local reports.Also read: Power supply hit in Gurugram, Faridabad and Nuh as workers strike over privatisationState activates contingency arrangementsThe state government has activated contingency arrangements to maintain essential services during the strike. The Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (UHBVN) deployed senior engineers from its Panchkula headquarters to monitor operations across Haryana.Meanwhile, the power utilities have also restricted leave for employees and directed personnel deployed in different areas to report for duty. In Kaithal, police personnel were seen handling complaints at electricity offices, while private contractors were being used to repair faulty feeders.Also read: Gurugram on outage alert ahead of power workers’ strikeSaini appeals to power staff to call off strikeMeanwhile, chief minister Nayab Singh Saini held a review meeting with senior officials ahead of the strike and appealed to them to call it off, assuring them that the government stood with them and that the doors for dialogue remained open.The strike has been called in protest against the HERC’s decision to grant a 25-year parallel electricity distribution licence to Eleven Power Private Limited for Gurugram and Nuh districts.The employees’ unions have described the move as indirect privatisation and argued that it could undermine the state-owned power utilities, threaten employees’ interests and increase the financial burden on consumers.Jagdish Nirala, legal adviser to the protesting Front, alleged that the government was pursuing privatisation through the back door. He claimed that handing over distribution in high-revenue areas to private companies could adversely affect consumers and farmers who depend on affordable electricity.The state government, meanwhile, has announced that it will challenge the HERC decision before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL), seeking a stay on the order.Also read: Indian states seek extra power to avoid outages as nighttime supply tightens, officials sayVij calls strike unnecessary, says govt too seeks stay on licence orderHaryana energy minister Anil Vij termed the three-day strike by electricity employees unnecessary, saying the state government was challenging the HERC’s decision before the APTEL.Vij said the government had strongly opposed the licence before the regulator by engaging a senior lawyer but the decision went against it. He maintained that HERC was an autonomous body and the government had not invited applications for privatisation.INLD demands cancellation of HERC’s parallel power distribution licenceFormer Haryana finance minister and INLD patron Sampat Singh also criticised the BJP governments at the Centre and in Haryana for pursuing with privatisation.Demanding immediate cancellation of the licence, Singh urged the CM to invoke Section 108 of the Electricity Act, 2003, to issue a written policy directive in the public interest. He termed the government’s proposed appeal against the HERC order a diversion from the need for immediate intervention.

title: Why education needs an AI evaluation layer | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Swaminathan Ganesan, co-founder & CEO, Smartail.
content: Education has already seen technology transform content delivery, learning management, administration and, more recently, personalised learning and AI tutoring. Yet one of the most important parts of the learning cycle has received comparatively less attention: Assessment—and the teacher at the centre of it.Before a school can personalise learning, it needs reliable evidence of what students have actually understood, where misconceptions exist and where intervention is required. Much of that evidence still comes from tests, assignments and answer sheets.Competency-based assessment is not new in India. The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 has stressed that assessment should focus on testing conceptual understanding, higher-order thinking skills and learning outcomes, not rote memorisation. The next question is whether the technology used to evaluate those assessments is ready for the same shift.Much of the conversation around AI in education focuses on what students are taught. But changing curriculum will only be effective with AI assessment infrastructure.A curriculum might promote critical thought, problem-solving, and advanced application. But if the test can only reward the context of textbook solutions, the education system is still communicating to students that they should have an eye on the exam pattern and answer key. An obvious gap thus exists between what education is attempting to teach and what assessment is able to reveal.A modern assessment system needs to look beyond whether an answer is right or wrong. It should be able to identify:Whether a student has understood the underlying conceptWhere a particular misconception appearsWhether an answer demonstrates reasoning or simply memorisationWhich topics are creating difficulty across a class or cohortWhere a teacher may need to interveneThis is where AI-assisted assessment can move beyond automating marks towards assessment intelligence turning every answer into evidence of conceptual understanding, misconceptions, reasoning patterns and learning gaps.Assessment is also a workload problem. According to OECD's TALIS 2024 data, teachers spend around 9% of their working time, on average, marking and correcting student work. Forty per cent of teachers across OECD education systems report excessive marking as a source of stress. This becomes particularly significant when assessments involve descriptive or handwritten answers. Unlike multiple-choice tests, these responses require interpretation. They also generate large amounts of unstructured information that is difficult to analyse manually at scale.AI can take on some of the repetitive work and help with response analysis, automated test correction, identifying learning gaps and reducing teacher workload. The key is that the teacher does not go away from that process. AI can deliver a first assessment and identify the pattern, but the teacher remains in place for judgement, context and final decisions.This is perhaps the bigger change. A conventional examination produces a score. An intelligent assessment system can potentially produce a learning map.For example, two students may both score 60%. On paper, they look similar. But their answer patterns may tell very different stories. One student may understand most concepts but make calculation errors. Another may remember definitions but struggle to apply them to unfamiliar problems.The mark tells us how the student performed. Assessment intelligence begins to tell us why.A useful AI evaluation system should be able to distinguish between these patterns rather than treating both students as simply “60% performers”. This is where assessment starts becoming an input for personalised learning insights rather than the final step after teaching.AI tutors, personalised learning platforms and generative content tools will continue to evolve rapidly. But all of them eventually confront the same fundamental question: How do we know whether a student has actually learned?Assessment is, therefore, more than an administrative function. It is the feedback loop connecting teaching, learning and intervention.India's assessment reforms already point towards competency-based examination and more frequent measurement of learning. The next step could be building the technology and infrastructure capable of interpreting that evidence at scale.The future of AI in education may not begin with an AI teacher or another layer of generated content. It may begin somewhere less visible but far more fundamental—with an assessment system that understands learning better.The opportunity is not to take the teacher out of assessment, but to put the teacher back at its centre—supported by better evidence, greater consistency and timely learning intelligence.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Swaminathan Ganesan, co-founder & CEO, Smartail.

title: Nepal, a fake name and a taxi switch: How Shraddha Dubey stayed ahead of police before Nagpur arrest | Hindustan Times
description: Lucknow police had said on October 16 that Dubey’s last known location was Nepal, even as the investigation timeline suggests she had returned to Uttar Pradesh.
content: Returning quietly from Nepal on October 16 while police still believed she was abroad, model Shraddha Dubey kept ahead of investigators for four days through calculated moves and deception. Travelling across Uttar Pradesh with her sister and driver, the main accused in cafe owner Shiva Sharma’s death used an alias at an Agra hotel, slipped into Lucknow to sign anticipatory bail papers and ditched a slow cab in Kanpur during a cross-country dash that eventually ended with her arrest in Nagpur.An investigation timeline and route plan, based on inputs given by the influencer to interrogation officers on Thursday at Hazratganj police station, suggested that Dubey, her sister Rashmi and their driver Danish spent around six days in Nepal before returning to India on October 16. Over the next few days, the trio allegedly travelled through Rae Bareli, Agra, Lucknow and Kanpur before taking a route through Fatehpur and Satna in Madhya Pradesh to reach Nagpur.Also read: Cops grill Shraddha Dubey, 2 others; sent to 10-day judicial custody in Lucknow cafe owner death caseThe movements raise questions about how long investigators continued to pursue the Nepal lead after the accused had allegedly returned to Uttar Pradesh.On October 16, Lucknow police commissioner Tarun Gauba told media persons that Dubey’s last known location had been traced to Nepal and that the police were coordinating with Nepal police. A day later, the then DCP (Central) Vikrant Vir said the police were in coordination with their Nepal counterparts.However, according to the investigation timeline shared by a senior officer to HT, Dubey had reached Rae Bareli on October 16, before moving on to Agra the following day.Also read: Model Shraddha Dubey, sister and driver arrested in Lucknow cafe owner Shiva Sharma's death case An assumed name in AgraOn October 17, the accused allegedly checked into a small hotel in Agra, where the name “Devraj” was entered in the register, sources said. The two sisters reportedly entered the hotel with their faces covered and remained inside the room during their 24-hour stay.They resumed their journey on October 18, travelling to Lucknow before heading towards Kanpur. During her brief return to the state capital, Dubey allegedly met a lawyer and signed documents linked to the process of seeking anticipatory bail and surrendering, according to sources. She also gave a video interview to a news agency without disclosing her location, before leaving Lucknow by taxi.Also read: Cafe owner death: Prime suspect model, 2 others brought to Lucknow from NagpurA change of vehicle, then NagpurThe three reached Kanpur on October 18 and stayed there for some time before continuing towards Nagpur via Fatehpur and Satna, Madhya Pradesh, sources said. As the taxi driver was driving slowly, Dubey allegedly abandoned the vehicle in Kanpur and hired another taxi to continue the journey. She eventually reached Nagpur, where she reportedly rented a flat on the 11th floor. The precise date of her arrival needs to be confirmed, with sources placing it around October 19-20.Dubey was arrested in Nagpur on October 20 along with her sister and their driver. The three were subsequently produced before a court, which granted Uttar Pradesh police transit remand to bring them to the state for further investigation.The route allegedly taken by the accused from the Nepal border back into Uttar Pradesh, followed by a journey across central India to Nagpur is now a key part of the investigation into how the group moved between locations before its arrest.
