title: Residents block roads as power strike leaves large parts of Gurugram in the dark | Hindustan Times
description: The strike began at 10pm on Wednesday against the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (HERC) decision to grant a private company a 25-year licence.
content: Residents blocked roads and protested across Gurugram on Thursday night after prolonged power outages disrupted water supply to thousands of households as a three-day statewide strike by power utility employees stalled repairs.Around 150 to 200 residents blocked the main road near Daulatabad flyover. Senior police officers arrived with reinforcements and appealed to protesters to clear the road. Police contacted Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) officials, who restored supply, defusing tensions.Also Read I Outages across Haryana as power staff begin 3-day strikePower workers' strike causes outageAt least 250 residents of Ashok Vihar Phase 3 protested after outages exceeding 20 hours. In Faridabad, residents blocked a road near Lakhani Dharamshala in NIT-2 over outages and unavailable repair teams.The strike began at 10pm on Wednesday against the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (HERC) decision to grant a private company a 25-year parallel distribution licence in Gurugram and Nuh.Four unions representing officers and regular and contractual employees called the strike: Haryana Power Engineers Association, All Haryana Power Corporation Workers Union, Haryana Electricity Board Workers Union and Haryana Power Corporation SC-ST and BC Workers Union. They said the decision threatened profit-making public utilities’ viability and employees’ job security.Haryana energy minister Anil Vij urged employees to resume work and engage with the government. “A strike would have been justified if we did not intend to file an appeal before the appellate tribunal. It will be filed within five to six days,” Vij said. Residents alleged that calls to DHBVN officials, junior engineers and linemen went unanswered, employees refused repairs and phones were switched off. Disruptions were also reported in Faridabad, Nuh, Palwal, Rewari, Jhajjar and Rohtak, where several discom offices remained locked or deserted.Gurugram’s sectors 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, areas along the Dwarka Expressway and parts of DLF phases 1, 2 and 3 reported prolonged outages. Private electricians repaired some localised faults after delays, while several societies relied on diesel generators.Water and electricity woesTilak Adlakha, president of the sectors 3, 5 and 6 RWA, said a fault in the high-tension feeder from Palam Vihar substation left the sectors without power for over 20 hours since Wednesday night.“There is no one available to carry out repairs. Officials are not responding to calls. Families have no water. Those working from home are suffering as there is neither Wi-Fi nor backup power for laptops,” he said.Sumit Pradhan, president of Hari Nagar society’s RWA in Sector 10A, alleged that Kadipur subdivision employees disconnected supply before locking their office on Wednesday night.“At least 10,000 people live here. Families have no water, and women and children are suffering. All employees have switched off their phones. We have been left helpless,” he said.In Garhi Harsaru near Sector 99, resident Angad Kumar said outages exceeded 24 hours, affecting nearly 50,000 people in the area and adjoining localities. Supply failed around 6pm on Wednesday, before the strike, but staff subsequently refused repairs, he alleged. Water supply was disrupted and backup power exhausted, he said.Ravinder Ghanghas, general secretary of the Haryana Power Engineers Association, claimed participation by 94% of DHBVN employees, 90% of Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam employees, 96% of Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited employees and 29% of Haryana Power Generation Corporation Limited employees.He also claimed Haryana’s average evening peak load fell by 45% on Thursday. “No progress has been made in talks with the government. The three-day strike will continue as planned until Saturday night,” he said.DHBVN officials did not respond to calls seeking comment on outages and allegations against employees.

title: Meghana Raj Sarja asked Jailer 2 makers if she'd be like ‘set property’ or get scenes with Rajinikanth; cross-checked offer with Shiva Rajkumar | Hindustan Times
description: Meghana Raj Sarja shot 35 days for Nelson Dilipkumar's Jailer 2 with Rajinikanth but says her scenes were trimmed from the film.
content: Nelson Dilipkumar’s Jailer 2, starring Rajinikanth in the lead role, was released in theatres on October 15 to positive reviews. The film has since become the second-highest-grossing Tamil film of all time, having beaten Vijay’s Leo too. Meghana Raj Sarja, who played a key role in the film, recalled asking the makers, when they offered her the film, whether she’d be treated like ‘set property’ or have scenes with Rajinikanth.Meghana Raj Sarja’s condition to Jailer 2 makersMeghana received the offer to star in Jailer 2 from a member of Nelson’s direction team. While sceptical that it could’ve been a prank, the actor recalled on Rednool’s YouTube channel how she set conditions nonetheless.“I asked her (Bhargavi Kalidas) only one question. See, I will say okay, but you have to be really open about my character. Please tell me if I will be used like set property or if I will be used in a frame with Rajini sir? That was my condition. She was like, ma’am, the entire 25 days you will be with Rajini sir, all your portions are with him. I said I would get back to her. Because once I say okay, what if it was some radio calling me and saying, we pranked Meghana?” recalled the actor. Cross-checking Jailer 2 offer with Shiva RajkumarIn fact, Meghana was so sceptical about receiving an offer for Rajinikanth’s film that she had her father cross-check the offer with Shiva Rajkumar. The Kannada star made a cameo in the film, and Meghana, incidentally, plays his daughter.She said, “Then, I called my father and asked him to find out if the offer was even true. He cross-checked with Shivanna (Shiva Rajkumar) and confirmed to me. Then I called back and said yes. I worked over the span of a year. It was a small role, but we shot for so many other things, which were trimmed. Creatively, they’ve taken a decision. But, I can proudly say I have worked in Jailer 2 for around 35 days over a period of one year.” Jailer 2 tells the story of a retired jailer, Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, who fights to save his family from an idol-smuggling ring. The film has grossed over ₹600 crore worldwide in eight days. Meghana is the wife of the late Kannada actor Chiranjeevi Sarja. She also starred in Amartha this year and has Ottakomban, Sangeetha Bar and Restaurant and Buddhivanta 2 lined up.

title: Post-SIR electoral roll in Uttar Pradesh under first major scrutiny ahead of assembly elections | Hindustan Times
description: The controversy comes months after the SIR led to a substantial reduction in the state’s electoral roll.
content: The electoral roll published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Uttar Pradesh has come under its first major scrutiny, with allegations of altered voter details and duplicate entries prompting the Election Commission of India (ECI) to order a statewide examination of voter lists.The immediate trigger is a Congress complaint alleging irregularities affecting 13,150 voter entries in Pilibhit Sadar assembly constituency, where the party claimed voters’ names were changed while their Electors Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers and serial numbers remained unchanged. The commission has directed district election officers (DEOs) across UP to examine the matter and check voter lists in all assembly constituencies in their respective districts, with reports to be submitted to the chief electoral officer’s office within two days.Earlier, when the Samajwadi Party raised the issue of duplicate voters, the ECI directed the district election officers (DEOs) and electoral registration officers (EROs) to remove duplicate entries from the voter list.UP's election controversyThe controversy comes months after the SIR led to a substantial reduction in the state’s electoral roll, intensifying opposition concerns over deletions and discrepancies. The Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress have repeatedly questioned the accuracy of the revised lists, while the BJP has defended the exercise as necessary to eliminate duplicate entries and ensure clean electoral rolls.In Pilibhit, the ECI has already removed two election officials — an electoral registration officer (ERO) and a voter registration centre (VRC) operator — following a preliminary inquiry by the district election officer. Legal action has also been ordered against them. Further action will follow if the ongoing investigation establishes irregularities, officials said. The district-level reports are expected on Friday.Also Read I BJP mounts all-out voter outreach for UP MLC pollsCongress leader Rajendra Pal Gautam, in-charge of the UP Congress Committee, alleged at a press conference on Wednesday that 13,150 voter names had been altered in Pilibhit Sadar. He further claimed that 884 voters had been removed despite continuing to reside in the constituency and submitting applications confirming their residence, while another 2,600 names had been added despite the individuals concerned allegedly not living there.Together, he said, the discrepancies affected over 16,554 voter entries. The SP said it had raised the Pilibhit issue before the Congress and had submitted a memorandum to the chief electoral officer. Party state secretary KK Srivastava said one of the discrepancies flagged by the SP involved an EPIC number displaying the details of another voter. Srivastava claimed the party had lodged complaints concerning more than three lakh suspected duplicate voters across the state. It had also flagged anomalies involving prefixes and suffixes in voters’ names, he said, adding that numerous complaints and memorandums had been submitted to the ECI. The SP leader questioned whether action against two officials would be sufficient, alleging that similar irregularities could exist elsewhere. These remain allegations and are subject to verification by the election authorities.BJP state spokesperson Dinesh Pratap Singh said a case had been registered in connection with the alteration of voter names in Pilibhit and that the Election Commission was taking appropriate action. The BJP supports the SIR as a necessary exercise to eliminate duplicate entries and ensure accuracy in the electoral roll, he said.SIR's impact on UP's electoral rollThe scale of the revision has added significance to the latest allegations. UP’s electoral roll declined from 15.44 crore voters in the list published on October 27, 2025, to 13.39 crore in the final roll published on April 10 following the SIR — a net reduction of around 2.04 crore names.The draft roll published on January 6 had flagged 2.89 crore voters as uncollectible. These included 1.29 crore who had permanently shifted, 46 lakh deceased voters, 25.4 lakh duplicate entries and 79.5 lakh voters who could not be traced, according to Election Commission data.The final roll contained 13,39,84,792 voters. The subsequent deletions included 3.50 lakh people who did not respond to notices, 3.28 lakh permanently shifted or absent voters, 79,076 duplicate entries, 55,865 deceased voters and 2,269 people found to be either non-citizens or underage, according to the figures provided.Also Read I Reading the tea leaves before the UP electionsMeanwhile, the next phase of electoral roll revision — the Special Summary Revision (SSR) — is scheduled to begin on November 12. The reorganisation and allocation of polling stations will be completed by November 2, while claims and objections can be submitted between November 12 and December 11. These will be resolved by December 28, with final voter roll scheduled for publication on January 4.Chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa has directed district election officers and electoral registration officers to prioritise the resolution of duplicate entries arising from multiple applications by the same voter during the SIR.

title: Tomb of American missionary who influenced the Jyotirao Phule's girls’ education mission found in Pune's Ahilyanagar | Hindustan Times
description: Cynthia Farrar’s educational work in the region bears early influences such as those of Mahatma Jyotirao Phule’s efforts to establish schools for girls in Pune.
content: After nearly five years of rummaging through hundreds of graves and historical records, three history enthusiasts have chanced upon the tomb of American missionary Cynthia Farrar in Ahilyanagar; restoring a missing physical link to a pioneering chapter in Maharashtra’s girls’ education movement.The stone tomb – discovered on October 16 at an old, British-era cemetery near Ahilyanagar fort – bears an inscription commemorating Farrar and her work of 35 years towards the education and spiritual enlightenment of Hindu women. Farrar’s educational work in the region bears early influences such as those of Mahatma Jyotirao Phule’s efforts to establish schools for girls in Pune.Also Read I No chai, coffee or cooked food at Pune railway station grocery kiosksThe trio's breakthroughThe trio of Abhijit Wagh, Bhairavnath Wakale and Asif Khan Dulekhan – members of the Ahilyanagar Itihas Premi Mandal – spent four to five years trying to establish the location of Farrar’s grave. Although historical accounts record her death in Ahilyanagar in 1862, the researchers could not initially trace her final place of rest. They searched a cemetery near Lal taki in Siddharthnagar where the graves of reverend Narayan Waman Tilak and American missionary Samuel Fairbank are located, but Farrar’s tomb wasn’t there.The breakthrough came when the team stumbled upon Farrar’s name in British-era burial records listing 465 people and their burial locations in Ahilyanagar; leading them to the old cemetery near Damdi masjid, close to Ahilyanagar fort.“We had been searching for four to five years. We were looking for information in old books and records, but we could not establish the exact location of her grave. When we found the British records, we got a clear lead and decided to search the cemetery again,” Wagh said. “On October 16, we went to the cemetery and started checking the graves. We searched through around 500 to 550 graves, one by one. At around 10 am, we finally found the tomb. Farrar’s name was clearly engraved on the stone,” Wagh said. The inscription reads, “In memory of Miss Cynthia Farrar of the American Mission born April 20, 1795 died January 25, 1862. For 35 years, she laboured for the education and spiritual enlightenment of Hindu females. Her works do follow her,” Wagh added. Following the discovery, the researchers cleaned the tomb, offered flowers, and paid their respects to Farrar.Khan Dulekhan, president of the Ahilyanagar Itihas Premi Mandal, said, “The inscription on Farrar’s tomb itself mentions that she worked for the education and spiritual enlightenment of Hindu women. Her work was focused on bringing women into education and social progress.”Farrar's work and life historyBorn on April 20, 1795, Farrar arrived in Bombay on December 29, 1827, as a missionary associated with the American Marathi Mission. After working with girls’ schools in Bombay, she returned to the United States in 1837 because of health concerns and came back to India in 1839. She subsequently worked in Ahilyanagar, where the mission had established a girls’ school in 1838, and remained associated with its educational activities until her death on January 25, 1862.Farrar’s work is linked to her association with Jyotirao Phule. According to Khan Dulekhan, Phule’s friend Sadashivrao Govande who worked in Ahilyanagar, learned about the teaching methods and curriculum deployed at the girls’ school and shared the information with Phule. Historian Dhananjay Keer’s biography of Phule recounts Phule’s visit to Farrar’s school in Ahilyanagar with Govande. Historical accounts have associated the interaction with Phule’s subsequent efforts to establish girls’ schools in Pune.Also Read I PM’s Pune visit deferred, metro inauguration date uncertainResearcher Hari Narke has written about Savitribai Phule’s teacher training under Farrar in Ahilyanagar and under another missionary in Pune. Savitribai went on to teach at the schools established by the Phule couple, and became a pioneering figure in women’s education. In his statement to the Hunter Commission on October 19, 1882, Jyotirao Phule recalled that Christian missionaries had established a girls’ school in Pune about 25 years earlier, inspiring him and Savitribai to take up the cause of girls’ education.

title: Rebels, independents add twist to BJP-SP contest in Uttar Pradesh MLC polls today | Hindustan Times
description: Lucknow graduates’ constituency has the largest electorate at 3,13,531, followed by Varanasi with 2,88,622 and Allahabad-Jhansi with 2,64,233 voters.
content: A total of 152 candidates will contest 11 Uttar Pradesh legislative council seats, comprising five graduates’ and six teachers’ constituencies, on Friday, with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Samajwadi Party (SP) facing challenges from rebel and independent candidates across several seats.The SP has fielded two BJP rebels to capitalise on discontent within the ruling party, with the council polls coming ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.The SP has fielded BJP rebel Sanjayan Tripathi from the Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers’ constituency and Akash Agarwal from the Agra graduates’ constituency, seeking to capitalise on discontent within the ruling party.The political stakes are reflected in chief minister Yogi Adityanath’s campaign for BJP candidates across constituencies. Though the elections cover 11 council seats, the outcome comes ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, scheduled for February-March.Graduates' constituencies across stateThe five graduates’ constituencies are Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut and Allahabad-Jhansi. The six teachers’ constituencies are Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut, Bareilly-Moradabad and Gorakhpur-Faizabad.Among the graduates’ constituencies, Varanasi has the highest number of candidates at 24, followed by Lucknow with 16, and Agra and Allahabad-Jhansi with 13 each, and Meerut with eight. Among the teachers’ constituencies, Bareilly-Moradabad has 17 candidates, followed by Gorakhpur-Faizabad with 16, Lucknow with 13, Agra with 12, and Varanasi and Meerut with 10 each.Lucknow graduates’ constituency has the largest electorate at 3,13,531, followed by Varanasi with 2,88,622 and Allahabad-Jhansi with 2,64,233 voters.Also Read I Reading the tea leaves before the UP electionsPolling will be held from 8 am to 4 pm at 2,697 polling stations across 72 districts, excluding Kanpur Nagar, Kanpur Dehat and Unnao. A total of 14,81,310 voters are eligible to cast their votes. The Election Commission has deployed 12,309 polling personnel for the elections.Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa said the Election Commission of India (ECI) had deployed 11 observers to monitor polling. In addition, 1,041 sector magistrates and 456 zonal magistrates have been deployed.Micro-observers and videography arrangements have also been made at polling stations. Security arrangements have been put in place to ensure peaceful polling. Voters must present their voter photo identity cards to establish their identity. Those unable to produce the card can use alternative documents approved by the ECI, Rinwa said.Voting will be conducted under the proportional representation system through the single transferable vote. Voters must indicate their preferences numerically, with ‘1’ mandatory for their first choice.

title: For Harry Brook, record double ton has “no value” after England fail to defend 429 against Sri Lanka | Cricket
description: Harry Brook's double century went in vain as Sri Lanka chased down 430 against England in Rawalpindi.  | Cricket
content: England captain Harry Brook slammed the fastest ODI double century in Rawalpindi, but his knock went in vain as Sri Lanka pulled off a heist on Thursday, chasing down 430 with two wickets left and one ball to spare. With this, the Lankans registered the second-highest successful chase in ODI history.Brook, who broke India captain Shubman Gill's record for the record, said his achievement meant nothing and held no value after England ended up losing the contest.“Yeah, it's nice. But unfortunately, it doesn't mean anything now, being on the losing side. It has no value whatsoever in my eyes,” Brook said at the post-match presentation. Brook, who was eventually dismissed for 202, brought up his double century off 114 deliveries, three balls quicker than Gill's recent knock against the West Indies. He also became the first English batter to score an ODI double century, setting a new record for England's highest individual score in the format and surpassing Ben Stokes' previous best of 182 against New Zealand in 2023.Brook's innings was studded with 21 fours and 10 sixes, as he finished with an astounding strike rate of 174.14. His knock helped England post 429/4 in 50 overs, but the total wasn't enough.Sri Lanka's fightbackFor Sri Lanka, Avishka Fernando (97), Pavan Rathnayake (130) and Dasun Shanaka (97) produced solid knocks to defy England. In the end, Janith Liyanage's unbeaten 61 off 27 balls sealed Sri Lanka's victory in the final over.Sri Lanka needed eight runs off the final six balls. Josh Tongue briefly raised hopes for England, dismissing Dunith Wellalage and Eshan Malinga off consecutive deliveries. But with six needed off two balls, Liyanage smashed a straight six to spark jubilation in the Sri Lankan camp.Brook heaped praise on Sri Lanka, admitting that England were outclassed by a special effort. He added that the team needed to go back to the basics after losing their first two matches of the tri-series.“Incredible game of cricket. I thought both teams were exceptional. Sri Lanka just outplayed us, unfortunately. We couldn't quite hit our straps with the ball and played into their strengths a little bit. And again, they played exceptional cricket to knock off 400. I think you said first time in 20 years is an incredible achievement, so fair play to them,” said Brook."We've got to go back to the drawing board a little bit. No, we know where we've gone wrong. Unfortunately, we didn't execute well enough with the ball," he added.

title: Is your heart playing tricks on you? Cardiologist warns of the silent danger of tricuspid regurgitation you can't afford to ignore | Health
description: Tricuspid regurgitation, often overlooked, can lead to serious complications. Learn about its symptoms, causes, and why early diagnosis matters  | Health
content: Heart valve disease is a common yet often underdiagnosed condition in India, particularly among older adults, with many patients remaining symptom-free until the disease progresses. It can result from rheumatic heart disease, congenital heart defects, infective endocarditis, or age-related valve degeneration.While diseases affecting the aortic and mitral valves are relatively well recognized, conditions involving the tricuspid valve, particularly tricuspid regurgitation (TR), have historically received far less attention despite their significant impact on heart function and quality of life.Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) often coexists with heart valve disease in which the tricuspid valve fails to close properly, allowing blood to leak backward from the right ventricle into the right atrium. Often called a "leaky tricuspid valve," the condition develops gradually and can go undetected for years because symptoms are often subtle or absent early on."As the disease progresses, it puts increasing strain on the heart, causing symptoms such as fatigue, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs or abdomen, and reduced ability to do everyday activities," Dr Sumanto Mukhopadhyay, Senior Consultant and Interventional Cardiologist at Apollo Multispeciality Hospital, Kolkata, tells Health Shots. If left untreated, severe TR can significantly impair quality of life and may progress to complications such as heart failure, liver and kidney dysfunction, and ultimately death.Why is tricuspid regurgitation often overlooked?TR is often called a "silent" heart valve disease because its symptoms develop gradually and are frequently mistaken for aging or other common conditions. People often ignore fatigue, breathlessness, reduced stamina, and swelling until they start affecting daily life. Limited awareness and the need for an echocardiogram to confirm the diagnosis further delay detection. By this time, the disease may have already progressed.TR symptoms are often gradual but should not be ignored. Common signs include poor appetite and progressive weight loss during routine activities, swelling in the legs or ankles, and reduced exercise tolerance. Some patients may also experience a fluttering heartbeat or a pounding sensation in the neck caused by changes in blood flow. When these symptoms persist or worsen, particularly in individuals with existing heart disease or pulmonary hypertension, they should prompt a medical evaluation rather than being dismissed as part of aging.Causes, diagnosis and treatmentTR occurs when the tricuspid valve between the right atrium and right ventricle doesn't close properly, allowing blood to leak back into the right atrium. It often results from changes in the heart's structure or function rather than a defect in the valve itself.Common causes of tricuspid regurgitation include pulmonary hypertension, which can enlarge the right ventricle and prevent the valve from closing properly, as well as left-sided heart disease.Other causes include infective endocarditis, a serious infection of the heart valves, rheumatic heart disease, and congenital heart defects present from birth. Less commonly, the condition may result from connective tissue disorders such as Marfan syndrome, chest injury, or rare conditions such as carcinoid disease.A clinical examination, supported by echocardiography, allows assessment of valve function, determination of leakage severity, and identification of any underlying cardiac conditions. Early diagnosis is important because TR is progressive and can eventually lead to complications such as atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and liver failure if left untreated.“Mild cases may require only regular monitoring, but medications such as diuretics can help manage symptoms,” the doctor says. For severe, symptomatic TR, treatment may involve surgical valve repair or replacement, or minimally invasive transcatheter therapies like TriClip or TTVR for patients at high surgical risk. Early diagnosis and timely intervention can relieve symptoms, improve quality of life, and reduce the risk of heart failure progression.(Disclaimer: This article is for informational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always seek the advice of your doctor with any questions about a medical condition.)

title: ఈ ఏడాది చివరికి కేతువు సంచారం.. ఈ 6 రాశులకు ధనలాభం, ఉద్యోగంలో ప్రమోషన్లు, వ్యాపారంలో విజయాలు! | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: జ్యోతిష్య శాస్త్రం ప్రకారం, 2026 డిసెంబర్ 5న కేతువు కర్కాటక రాశిలోకి ప్రవేశించి, 2028 జూన్ 23 వరకు అక్కడ సంచరిస్తారని ఈ కథనం పేర్కొంటోంది. చంద్రుడి అధిపత్యంలోని కర్కాటక రాశిలో కేతువు సంచారం మానసిక స్థితి, భావోద్వేగాలు, ఆర్థిక పరిస్థితులపై ప్రభావం చూపుతుందని జ్యోతిష్య విశ్వాసం.
content: జ్యోతిష్య శాస్త్రంలో కేతువు గోచారానికి అత్యంత ప్రాధాన్యత ఉంది. గ్రహాల గమనంలో వచ్చే ఈ మార్పులు ద్వాదశ రాశులపై తీవ్ర ప్రభావాన్ని చూపుతాయి. ఈ ఏడాది డిసెంబర్ 5, శనివారం నాడు కేతువు చంద్రుడి రాశి అయిన కర్కాటకంలోకి అడుగుపెట్టనున్నారు.2028 జూన్ 23 వరకు కేతువు ఇదే రాశిలో సంచారం కొనసాగిస్తారు. ఈ ఏడాది దీపావళి నవంబర్ 8న రానుండగా, ఆ పండుగ ముగిసిన తర్వాత ఈ కీలక గోచారం జరగనుంది.చంద్రుడు - కేతువు వైరం: మానసిక స్థితిపై ప్రభావంకర్కాటక రాశి జల తత్వానికి చెందినది. దీనికి అధిపతి చంద్రుడు. జ్యోతిష్య శాస్త్రంలో చంద్రుడిని, కేతువును పరమ శత్రువులుగా పరిగణిస్తారు. చంద్రుడు మనిషి మనసు, మానసిక ప్రశాంతత, భావోద్వేగాలకు ప్రతీక. మరోవైపు కేతువు వైరాగ్యం, మానసిక ఒత్తిడి, అంతుచిక్కని ఆలోచనలకు కారకుడు. అందువల్ల కేతువు చంద్రుడి రాశిలోకి ప్రవేశించినప్పుడు ప్రజల మనస్తత్వంపై, భావోద్వేగాలపై తీవ్రమైన ప్రభావం పడుతుంది.కేతువు ఎప్పుడూ చెడు ఫలితాలనే ఇస్తాడని అనుకోవడం పొరపాటు. కొన్ని రాశుల వారికి ఈ గోచారం ద్వారా ఊహించని శుభ పరిణామాలు ఎదురవుతాయి. ఈ కాలంలో కొందరు మానసికంగా ఒంటరితనాన్ని అనుభవించే అవకాశం ఉన్నప్పటికీ, కొన్ని రాశుల వారికి అద్భుతమైన లాభాలు కలుగుతాయని ఆయన స్పష్టం చేస్తున్నారు.ఈ రాశుల వారికి అద్భుతమైన ఫలితాలువృషభ రాశి:వృషభ రాశి వారికి కేతువు సంచార కాలం ఎంతో లాభదాయకంగా మారుతుంది. జీవితంలో ఊహించని సానుకూల మార్పులు చోటుచేసుకుంటాయి. అకస్మాత్తుగా ధనలాభం కలగడంతో పాటు ఆదాయ మార్గాలు విస్తరిస్తాయి. ఎప్పటినుంచో ఆగిపోయిన పనులు విజయవంతంగా పూర్తవుతాయి. కుటుంబ సభ్యుల పూర్తి మద్దతు లభించడం వల్ల మానసిక ప్రశాంతత దక్కుతుంది.మిథున రాశి:ఉద్యోగ రంగంలో ఉన్నవారికి మిథున రాశిలో కేతువు ప్రభావం అద్భుతమైన ఫలితాలను ఇస్తుంది. వ్యాపారంలో తిరుగులేని విజయాలు సాధిస్తారు. ఆత్మవిశ్వాసం రెట్టింపు అవుతుంది. కార్యక్షేత్రంలో అపారమైన ఫలితాలు దక్కడంతో పాటు ఉన్నతాధికారుల ప్రశంసలు అందుకుంటారు. శత్రువులపై సులభంగా విజయం సాధిస్తారు. చేసే ప్రయాణాలు విశేష లాభాలను తెచ్చిపెడతాయి.కన్యా రాశి:కన్యా రాశి జాతకులకు ఈ గోచారం అదృష్టాన్ని ఇస్తుంది. అకస్మాత్తుగా ఆర్థిక లాభాలు కలుగుతాయి. కొత్త ఆదాయ మార్గాలు తెరుచుకోవడంతో ఆర్థిక ఇబ్బందులు తొలగిపోతాయి. సమాజంలో గౌరవ ప్రతిష్టలు పెరుగుతాయి. ముఖ్యమైన నిర్ణయాలు తీసుకునేటప్పుడు కుటుంబం నుంచి సంపూర్ణ మద్దతు లభిస్తుంది. పెట్టుబడులకు ఇది సరైన సమయం. పాత పెట్టుబడుల ద్వారా భారీ రాబడులు అందుకుంటారు.మరికొన్ని రాశులకు కలిసొచ్చే కాలంతులా రాశి:తులా రాశి వారికి కేతువు కర్కాటక సంచారం ఎంతో మేలు చేస్తుంది. వ్యక్తిగత ప్రవర్తనలో ఆకర్షణ పెరుగుతుంది. మాటతీరుతో అందరినీ ఆకట్టుకుంటారు. కుటుంబ సభ్యుల మధ్య సఖ్యత ఏర్పడుతుంది. ఆర్థిక పరిస్థితి క్రమంగా బలపడుతుంది. వ్యాపార విస్తరణకు అనువైన వాతావరణం ఏర్పడుతుంది. ఉద్యోగంలో పదోన్నతులు లభించే అవకాశాలు స్పష్టంగా కనిపిస్తున్నాయి.మకర రాశి:మకర రాశి వారికి ఈ కాలం ఎంతో అనుకూలంగా ఉంటుంది. ఆత్మవిశ్వాసం పెరిగి కఠినమైన నిర్ణయాలు సులభంగా తీసుకుంటారు. శత్రువుల నుంచి ఎదురవుతున్న అడ్డంకులు తొలగిపోతాయి. కోర్టు కేసుల్లో సానుకూల తీర్పులు వచ్చే సూచనలున్నాయి. వ్యాపారస్తులు కొత్త ఒప్పందాలపై సంతకాలు చేసే అవకాశం ఉంది. ఉద్యోగ మార్పును కోరుకునే వారికి ఇది సరైన తరుణం.కుంభ రాశి:కుంభ రాశి వారికి కేతువు శుభవార్తలను మోసుకొస్తుంది. ప్రముఖ వ్యక్తులతో పరిచయాలు ఏర్పడతాయి. ఈ సంబంధాలు భవిష్యత్తులో ఉద్యోగ, వ్యాపార రంగాల్లో గొప్ప ప్రయోజనాలను చేకూరుస్తాయి. జీవిత భాగస్వామితో సంతోషకరమైన సమయం గడుపుతారు. ప్రయాణాల వల్ల ఆర్థిక లాభం కలుగుతుంది. కుటుంబంలో ఆనందకర వాతావరణం నెలకొంటుంది.

title: Madhuri Dixit’s purple saree has me rethinking festive styling | Fashion Trends
description: Madhuri Dixit Nene, Rashmika Mandanna and Yami Gautam are embracing purple saris. Here is why I love the colour and how I style it.  | Fashion Trends
content: Purple has been my favourite colour for as long as I can remember. So when Madhuri Dixit Nene stepped out in a rich purple Banarasi sari for Vijayadashami, it caught my attention for more than one reason. The look reminded me of a colour I have always loved, but also of how beautifully purple works in traditional Indian wear.Earlier this week, I wore a purple-shaded sari to a Durga Puja pandal. I paired it with a matching V-neck blouse with half sleeves and a small bindi, keeping accessories to a minimum. I wanted the sari to be the focus of the outfit, rather than compete with it through too many embellishments.That is also why I have a soft spot for matching blouses. A coordinated blouse can create a balanced, elegant look without interrupting the colour or the drape of a sari. For me, the V-neck was an especially flattering choice because it highlighted my collarbones, while the half sleeves kept the silhouette classic.With recent celebrity appearances bringing purple into focus, I think the colour deserves a closer look this festive and wedding season. From traditional Banarasi weaves to contemporary colour combinations, there are several ways to wear it without losing the individuality of your own style.Madhuri Dixit Nene’s purple Banarasi sari celebrates traditional craftsmanship Madhuri Dixit Nene has long championed the sari, and her latest festive appearance is a reminder of how traditional textiles can make a statement without needing an unconventional silhouette.For Vijayadashami, the actor wore a purple Banarasi sari from designer Sanjay Garg’s label Raw Mango. The sari featured floral motifs enclosed within paisley-shaped buttas, set against a lustrous purple base with a broad gold-toned border.What makes the sari particularly interesting is its craftsmanship. According to Vogue India’s report, the motifs draw inspiration from inlay work found in Mughal and Rajputana architecture and were created using the kadwa weaving technique, in which individual motifs are woven separately. The result is a textile where the detailing, rather than heavy surface embellishment, creates the visual richness.Madhuri paired the sari with a matching purple blouse featuring a backless design and traditional mid-length sleeves. The gold border on the sleeves echoed the pallu, creating a cohesive finish. Statement earrings, bangles and flowers tucked into her hair completed the look.I particularly like how the matching blouse allows the sari's colour and woven motifs to remain the focus. When a sari already has a rich colour, a striking border or intricate craftsmanship, a coordinated blouse can bring the look together instead of introducing another competing element.It is a styling approach that works beyond designer saris, too. Even a simpler festive sari can look considered when the blouse, drape and accessories feel intentional.Why I prefer a matching blouse with a festive sariMy own Durga Puja look was a simpler interpretation of festive dressing. I wore a purple-shaded sari with a matching V-neck blouse with half sleeves and a small bindi. I deliberately kept the accessories minimal because I wanted the sari to do the talking. For me, the appeal of a matching blouse lies in the visual continuity it creates. The eye moves across the sari without being distracted by a sharply contrasting blouse colour. This can be particularly effective when the sari has an interesting sheen, an unusual shade or a beautiful drape.The neckline matters, too. I personally find a V-neck flattering because it draws attention to my collarbones and creates an elongated line around the neck. That is a preference based on how I like my outfits to look, rather than a rule that applies to everyone. A square neckline, boat neck or deeper round neck can work just as well, depending on the sari, the occasion and individual comfort.Sleeve length is another detail that can change the overall impression. My half-sleeved blouse kept the look traditional, while the matching colour made the outfit feel coordinated rather than overly styled.I also believe accessories should complement the sari rather than automatically be added because an occasion calls for dressing up. If the fabric and colour already have enough visual impact, earrings, a small bindi and a few understated details may be all that is needed.This is not to say contrasting blouses do not work. They can be an excellent way to introduce another colour or give an older sari a fresh look. But a matching blouse deserves just as much consideration, particularly when the aim is an elegant, balanced ensemble.Wamiqa Gabbi shows how purple can work with contrasting colours While I gravitate towards matching blouses, Wamiqa Gabbi offers inspiration for those who prefer to experiment with colour.The actor was spotted on the sets of Kaun Banega Crorepati wearing a traditional green sari with a purple blouse, alongside Rajkummar Rao and lawyer Ujjwal Nikam. The combination reverses the more familiar approach of pairing a purple sari with a matching blouse.What I like about this pairing is that it demonstrates how the same two colours can create different effects depending on which one takes centre stage. A green sari with a purple blouse makes the contrast the focal point, while a purple sari with a green blouse reverses that balance.If you want to try the combination, deeper shades such as emerald or bottle green can complement a rich purple sari. Gold jewellery can help tie the colours together, especially if the sari has a zari border. For a more understated interpretation, keep the blouse relatively simple and let the colour contrast provide the interest.The choice ultimately comes down to personal style. A matching blouse offers continuity, while a contrasting one introduces a deliberate break in the colour palette. Neither is inherently better; the important thing is understanding the effect you want to create.Purple is gaining visibility in celebrity festive dressingPurple has featured in several recent celebrity appearances, offering different ways to interpret the colour for Indian occasionwear. These looks do not establish purple as the season's definitive leading colour, but they provide useful inspiration for anyone considering it for festive dressing.Rashmika Mandanna's purple-and-gold sari At Swadesh's first-anniversary celebrations in Mumbai, Rashmika Mandanna wore a purple crepe sari by Itrh, the label founded by stylist Mohit Rai and designer Ridhi Bansal. The sari featured Chanderi brocade buttas, intricate detailing along the border and pallu, and a heavily embroidered gold blouse.The combination makes a case for purple and gold when you want a more elaborate festive look. The gold embroidery adds richness to the purple base, while the sari's detailing gives the ensemble its occasionwear appeal.For a similar effect, you could pair a purple sari with antique-gold jewellery or a gold blouse, keeping the remaining accessories in proportion to the amount of embellishment.Yami Gautam's coordinated purple silk sari Yami Gautam also wore purple for the Ravan Dahan celebrations at Delhi's Red Fort. Her silk sari, designed by Anita Dongre, featured a royal purple shade and a contrasting gold-toned border. She paired it with a matching blouse and kept the overall styling traditional.Her look is particularly relevant to the matching-blouse conversation. The coordinated blouse allows the sari's colour and border to remain prominent, while understated styling keeps the ensemble from feeling overdone.Madhuri Dixit Nene's purple Banarasi sari Madhuri's Raw Mango sari offers another interpretation, this time centred on woven motifs and traditional craftsmanship. Its rich colour and gold detailing provide enough visual interest without requiring a contrasting blouse.Together, these appearances show how purple can work across different fabrics, silhouettes and levels of embellishment. The shade can feel traditional in a Banarasi weave, dramatic with intricate gold embroidery or understated in a coordinated silk sari.Five ways I would style purple for festive occasionsIf you want to incorporate purple into your festive wardrobe, the starting point does not have to be an elaborate designer outfit. The colour can work across different silhouettes and occasions, depending on how you choose the fabric, blouse and accessories.1. Pair a purple sari with a matching blouseThis is my preferred approach. A coordinated blouse keeps the overall look balanced and allows the sari's colour, texture or border to stand out. A V-neck with half sleeves, like the one I wore for Durga Puja, is one option if you prefer a classic silhouette.2. Use gold to bring out the richness of purpleGold and purple are a natural pairing for traditional occasions. A sari with gold zari can be styled with gold-toned earrings and bangles, while a simpler purple sari can accommodate a more elaborate blouse or necklace. The idea is to balance the embellishment rather than add detail everywhere.3. Experiment with green if you prefer contrastWamiqa Gabbi's green sari and purple blouse demonstrate how contrasting colours can change the mood of an outfit. Try emerald or bottle green with a deeper purple, and consider the sari's border and existing embellishments before adding jewellery.4. Choose lilac for a softer daytime lookIf deep purple feels too bold, lilac and lavender offer a lighter alternative. These shades can work for daytime celebrations in saris, kurta sets and other Indian separates. Silver jewellery, pearls and delicate embroidery can complement the softer palette.5. Let the sari guide your accessoriesA heavily woven Banarasi sari, an embroidered crepe sari and a plain silk sari each call for a different approach. When the fabric and border already provide detail, minimal accessories can create a more balanced finish. With a simpler sari, you have more room to experiment with statement earrings, bangles or a contrasting blouse.Why purple will always have a place in my festive wardrobeFor me, purple is more than a colour appearing in celebrity fashion coverage. It has been my favourite for years, and wearing it to a Durga Puja pandal earlier this week reminded me that festive dressing can be personal without being complicated.My purple-shaded sari, matching V-neck blouse, half sleeves and small bindi were enough to create the look I wanted. I liked the way the coordinated blouse kept the outfit cohesive, the neckline highlighted my collarbones and the minimal accessories allowed the sari to remain the focus.Madhuri Dixit Nene's Banarasi sari, Yami Gautam's coordinated silk ensemble and Rashmika Mandanna's purple-and-gold look offer further inspiration for wearing the colour in different ways. Wamiqa Gabbi's contrasting blouse combination is a reminder that there is no single formula for styling a sari.The takeaway is not that everyone needs to buy a purple outfit this season. It is that a familiar colour can feel different depending on the fabric, blouse, drape and finishing details you choose. Whether you prefer a matching blouse or a contrasting one, the best festive look is the one that feels considered, comfortable and true to your personal style. title: Behind Gurugram’s green cracker displays, a discreet trade takes place in banned varieties | Hindustan Times
description: Customers who specifically asked for traditional crackers were directed by shopkeepers towards a godown tucked away behind the main shopping area.
content: Beyond the broken roads, heaps of garbage and narrow lanes of Gadoli lies one of Gurugram’s busiest firecracker markets, where business is picking up ahead of Diwali. Shops are stacked with colourful boxes of crackers, customers arrive to buy in bulk, and salesmen promise prices that keep buyers coming back.At first glance, everything appears to be in order, with green firecrackers prominently displayed at storefronts. But behind these displays, another trade is flourishing: one where banned, polluting firecrackers are discreetly offered to customers who know what to ask for.During an HT spot check on Wednesday, traders at Gadoli were found selling firecrackers without visible green certification markings, alongside products they advertised as green crackers. As customers moved through the crowded market, several were seen purchasing firecrackers in bulk and carrying them away in large sacks.Also Read | Green only in colour: Firecrackers flood Delhi markets amid festive season, rising AQISome who specifically asked for traditional or polluting crackers were directed by shopkeepers towards a godown tucked away behind the main shopping area.Following these customers, HT entered a poorly maintained godown with exposed brick walls and tall shelves stacked with boxes of firecrackers. Among them were bombs that lacked visible green certification markings. Other varieties were stuffed into large polythene bags, which salesmen opened only when customers asked for particular products. Several men remained stationed near the stock, attending to buyers.Inside, bargaining was brisk. Packets with printed prices of ₹1,400 were being offered for ₹400 to ₹500, while a packet of sparklers was priced at ₹500, bombs at ₹1,000 and flower pots, or anars, at ₹350.“You pick up the crackers you want, the price will be adjusted. I will talk to the owner,” a salesman inside the godown said.Outside, traders appeared confident of a busy festive season this year.“Till Diwali (November 8), we will remain open from 5am until late evening. People from nearby cities come here to buy firecrackers in bulk,” a salesman said.“The number of customers will increase by the end of the week. On weekends, the footfall will rise even more. And as Diwali nears, people will find it difficult to even park their cars. We offer the best rates here; that probably why everyone returns to Gadoli year on year to buy firecrackers,” he added.HT also found that shops and godowns in Gadoli were storing large quantities of firecrackers without any visible firefighting equipment. No fire extinguishers or other immediate firefighting arrangements were seen in the godown or shops the team visited, raising concerns about safety.Also Read | SC against blanket firecracker ban in Delhi-NCR, but asks ‘what's religious about bursting crackers’Sushil Yadav, a resident of Sector 37, said he had purchased green crackers but was also looking for conventional varieties. “I have bought green crackers but Diwali seems incomplete without ladis and firecracker bombs. I can’t find them in a green variant,” he said, adding that such crackers remained popular among buyers, despite the ban and the health hazards.Mamta Singh, another customer browsing the stalls, appeared unconcerned about the restrictions when asked whether she was aware of them. “It’s a matter of just one day. My children want to burst crackers. I grew up burning them,” she said.The sale of polluting firecrackers was not confined to Gadoli.During visits to Sector 56’s Huda Market, Sector 46 Market, Sector 14, Badshahpur and Farrukhnagar, HT found vendors offering traditional varieties discreetly, often keeping their stock beneath makeshift tables or in sacks. Some sold them only to regular customers or those who specifically asked for them.At Sector 56’s Huda Market, several stalls were selling green crackers alongside conventional varieties. Some vendors were also offering unsold stock from last year, promising discounts to interested customers.Genuine green crackers carry certification markings, including the CSIR-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) logo and a QR code that can be scanned to verify their authenticity. Approved green-cracker formulations include SWAS, SAFAL and STAR, which are designed to reduce emissions compared with conventional firecrackers.However, the type or appearance of a firecracker alone does not determine whether it is a certified green product. Varieties such as sparklers and flower pots can also be manufactured using approved formulations, making certification checks essential.There are severe restrictions on the sale of conventional firecrackers in Delhi-NCR and increased enforcement ahead of Diwali.Earlier this month, the Supreme Court refused to impose a blanket ban on firecrackers ahead of Diwali 2026, opting instead for a balanced approach that rejects both a total prohibition and 24-hour unrestricted bursting.Meanwhile, the Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) and Gurugram police have intensified inspections of firecracker markets and storage facilities.This week, HSPCB teams conducted raids at two warehouses in Chandu and Farrukhnagar and sent samples for testing to determine whether the firecrackers complied with green-cracker requirements.“We have intensified our crackdown on illegal firecrackers being sold in Gurugram. Multiple teams have been formed to check and ensure that no illegal firecrackers are stored or sold to customers. Only PESO-approved green firecrackers are allowed in Gurugram,” said Harish Kumar, regional officer, HSPCB Gurugram North.A Gurugram police officer said teams were inspecting warehouses, godowns and shops on the basis of tip-offs to identify and seize illegal firecrackers.

title: Ramayana vs Adipurush: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash-starrer dwarfs Prabhas film, outpaces it by 120% in advance bookings | Bollywood
description: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's Ramayana grossed over twice of what Prabhas' Adipurush had managed in pre-sales in the first 24 hours.  | Bollywood
content: Ticket sales for Nitesh Tiwari’s ambitious Ramayana adaptation began on Dussehra, 15 days before the film's release in theatres ahead of Diwali. Giving the film such a long advance booking window seems to be the makers’ strategy to increase the buzz around it. And early signs indicate that the strategy seems to be working. Ramayana Part One is showing breakneck pre-sales, crossing one lakh tickets with 13 days to go before release.In doing so, it has also outpaced the previous big-scale Ramayana adaptation, Adipurush, which had a grand opening before it crash-landed due to extremely negative word of mouth.Ramayana vs Adipurush advance bookingsAdvance bookings for Adipurush began five days before its release, in line with how most big Indian films do so. The pre-sales Hindi version opened first, followed by the Telugu version a day later. In the first 24 hours, Adipurush sold around 36K tickets for its Hindi version, bringing in ₹1.40 crore in pre-sales. This was a healthy number. As the Telugu advance booking opened the following day, the pre-sales soared.Ramayana has followed a similar pattern. The first day saw ticket sales only for the Hindi version, as the Kannada version opened with just 60 shows across India. Despite that, Ramayana sold over 65K tickets, minting ₹3.13 crore in gross on its opening day. This figure is 123% higher than what Adipurush managed in the same time period. The Prabhas-starrer salvaged its pre-sales with the Telugu advance bookings in the days to come, closing its final figure at a respectable ₹26 crore, with over a million tickets sold. How Ramayana pre-sales are faringRamayana has already reached the ₹6.25 crore mark. The Kannada, Telugu, and Tamil versions have barely begun, contributing just ₹50 lakh to this figure. The Hindi version of Ramayana is already showing occupancy of 15-20% in most major cities, with over 900 screens open. In comparison, the Kannada version has opened in fewer than 100 screens so far and is still doing well, with some centres already reporting up to 72% occupancy for the morning shows. Yash’s star power will help the film soar to greater heights once advance bookings for Kannada and Telugu open fully later this month. All about RamayanaProduced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part film. The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide release on November 5, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will release in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the film in the Hindi-speaking market. The film is also planned for a worldwide IMAX release.

title: 22-yr-old pharmacy employee shot dead by 3 men at friend’s shop in Loni: Police | Hindustan Times
description: The victim, identified as Sonu Khan, a resident of the nearby Chirodi area, was having snacks at a friend’s shop in the market around 9 pm when the attack took place.
content: A 22-year-old medical store employee was shot dead by three bike-borne assailants at Banthla-Chirodi Road in Ghaziabad’s Loni late Thursday evening, police said.The victim, identified as Sonu Khan, a resident of the nearby Chirodi area, was having snacks at a friend’s shop in the market around 9 pm when the attack took place.“While the victim was at his friend’s shop, three bikers arrived and fired shots at him before fleeing. His friend informed his family and rushed him to a hospital in Delhi, where he was declared dead on arrival. The victim sustained at least two bullet injuries,” said Ram Kishan, assistant commissioner of police (ACP), Loni Circle.Khan’s family lodged a formal complaint early Friday morning, following which an FIR under Section 103(1) (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) was registered against four persons.According to the FIR, Khan’s brother said he had gotten into an altercation with the three accused about 10 to 15 days ago over a payment dispute at the medical store where he worked. HT has reviewed a copy of the FIR.“My brother was working at a medical store. A dispute arose when my brother asked them for money. He was at his friend’s shop. When we asked his friend about the murder, he revealed the names of three suspects,” the FIR said.Kishan said the family has raised suspicions about the involvement of the victim’s friend, who had called him to his shop. The friend was called in for questioning, but he has not revealed anything significant regarding the murder.The police officer said the three suspects named in the FIR were on the run and multiple teams have been formed to trace them.The officer, however, underlined that an investigation was underway to establish the exact motive behind the killing.

title: Udta Teer review: This Ayushmann Khurrana spy comedy rarely misses a chance to make you laugh | Bollywood
description: Ayushmann Khurrana leads a lively comedy about a memory-losing Pakistani spy who ends up working for India.  | Bollywood
content: Udta TeerDirector: Akash KaushikCast: Ayushmann Khurrana, Sara Ali Khan, Ram KapoorRating: 3.5 starsI am struggling to recall the last time a film made me laugh as much as Udta Teer did. And none of it relies on double meaning dialogues or cheap innuendo, mind you. If you can sense my excitement already, let's get straight to why this Ayushmann Khurrana starrer simply works.What is the plot of Udta Teer?Directed by Akash Kaushik (who has previously written the screenplays for hits like Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2 and 3) Udta Teer follows Bilal/Vikrant (Ayushmann), who has been working as a Pakistani spy in India's counter terrorism unit. One day, he loses his memory in an accident and ends up working for India instead, dismantling Pakistan's terror network embedded within the system. Akash was bang on when he recently described the film as a "reverse Dhurandhar".Making his feature directorial debut with Udta Teer, Akash proves surprisingly sure footed. Also the film's writer, he keeps the first half tight, with hardly a scene feeling like dead weight. The pacing is spot on, with witty one liners and funny situations keeping the laughs coming. There is Pakistan bashing, but not the chest thumping kind. The humour is far more cheeky than jingoistic. Take Gulshan Grover's character, for instance, who declares that the head of the Pakistani Army never has to bow his head before anyone-- until the President of China calls and he bows his head immediately. A man waiting every day for the Pakistani Army General to give him the time of the day in Gulshan's office, turns out to be the Pakistani Prime Minister himself. All this lands because the film knows exactly where to poke fun, and more importantly, when to stop. After such a funny first half, the second half naturally comes with high expectations. This is where Udta Teer changes gears, and not to its advantage. As the film tries to tie up its plot, the narrative becomes more serious than you might have bargained for, taking some of the fizz out. The momentum built in the first half begins to dip, and you find yourself missing the earlier ability for turning even the most absurd situations into laugh out loud moments.There are also some moments, like the placement of a romantic and patriotic song, which slows down the pace.But does that mean Udta Teer derails completely? Nope. In fact, it leaves you wishing this were the start of a franchise, because there is plenty of potential here. The VerdictA big reason it works is its talented cast, which makes even the most absurd ideas seem normal. From making Rahul Bose dance to It's the Time to Disco while lying in a vegetative state in a hospital, to turning heartrate monitor beeps into the tune of an iconic Dharma song, there is plenty to enjoy. Ayushmann Khurrana is pitch perfect as Bilal, the spy grappling with memory loss. He gets the balance between confusion and comedy just right. The late Mukul Dev gives him tough competition, bringing an effortless sense of humour to his role. Sandeep Anand is hilarious as Bilal's cook, while Suhail Nayyar is equally good as Bilal's best friend. Sara Ali Khan, as Bilal's wife, has a decent role and she does well.The music by Sachin-Jigar is well done, complimented by Amitabh Bhattacharya's lyrics.Udta Teer is the kind of comedy that makes you wish filmmakers would trust good writing a little more often. Its first half delivers the laughs without resorting to cheap tricks, and its cast is more than happy to play along with the madness. The second half could have held on to that for longer, but the film still leaves a good impression. Bilal's loyalties may be all over the place, but the film's intentions are clear: to entertain without insulting the audience's intelligence.

title: Hala mobility : 60 సెకన్లలో బ్యాటరీ స్వాప్, రూ.2కే ఇన్సూరెన్స్! డెలివరీ బాయ్స్‌కు హైదరాబాద్ కంపెనీ ఆఫర్.. | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: హైదరాబాద్‌కు చెందిన 'హాలా మొబిలిటీ' గిగ్ డెలివరీ పార్ట్​నర్స్​ కోసం 'సీడ్' పేరుతో ప్రత్యేక ఈకోసిస్టమ్‌ను అందుబాటులోకి తెచ్చింది. 60 సెకన్లలో బ్యాటరీ స్వ్యాపింగ్, రోజుకు రూ.2కే ఆరోగ్య బీమా, ముందస్తు వేతనం వంటి సదుపాయాలను ఇందులో అందిస్తోంది. ఇవి గిగ్​ వర్కర్లకు ఎంతగానో ఉపగయోగపడతాయి.
content: లాస్ట్-మైల్ డెలివరీ రంగంలో పనిచేసే ప్రతీ డెలివరీ బాయ్‌కి కూడా ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ అనేది కేవలం ఒక ప్రయాణ సాధనం మాత్రమే కాదు; అది అతనికి ప్రతి నిషమం ఆదాయాన్ని తెచ్చిపెట్టే జీవనోపాధి! ఇక స్విగ్గీ, జొమాటో, బ్లింకిట్, జెప్టో వంటి సంస్థల్లో రోజంతా బైక్‌పై తిరిగే గిగ్ వర్కర్లకు కారు లేదా బైక్ ఛార్జింగ్ కోసం గంటల తరబడి వేచి చూడటం అంటే ఆ రోజు సంపాదనను కోల్పోవడమే. ఈ నేపథ్యంలోనే ఈ క్షేత్రస్థాయి సమస్యకు పక్కా పరిష్కారంతో ముందుకొచ్చింది హైదరాబాద్ కేంద్రంగా పనిచేస్తున్న ప్రముఖ ఈవీ స్టార్టప్ ‘హాలా మొబిలిటీ’.తమ వినూత్న 'ఈవీ-యాజ్-ఏ-సర్వీస్' (ఈవీఏఏఎస్) మోడల్‌తో పాటు 'సీడ్' (సస్టైనెబుల్ ఎకోసిస్టెమ్ టు ఎంపవర్ డెలివరీ పార్ట్​నర్స్) వేదిక ద్వారా డెలివరీ భాగస్వాముల దైనందిన సమస్యలను పరిష్కరించేందుకు హాలా సరికొత్త సేవలను ప్రారంభించింది.60 సెకన్లలో బ్యాటరీ స్వ్యాపింగ్: 'ట్విన్‌ఫినిటీ'గంటల కొద్దీ సాగే ఛార్జింగ్ కష్టాలకు ముగింపు పలుకుతూ హాలా సంస్థ 'ట్విన్‌ఫినిటీ' పేరుతో సొంత బ్యాటరీ స్వ్యాపింగ్ నెట్‌వర్క్‌ను అందుబాటులోకి తెచ్చింది. సంస్థ స్వయంగా అభివృద్ధి చేసిన బ్యాటరీలు, స్వ్యాపింగ్ స్టేషన్లు, అడ్వాన్స్‌డ్ సాఫ్ట్‌వేర్ ఆధారంగా ఇది పనిచేస్తుంది.ఈ సాంకేతికత ద్వారా డెలివరీ రైడర్లు తమ వాహనంలోని డిశ్చార్జ్ అయిన బ్యాటరీని తీసి, పూర్తిగా ఛార్జ్ అయిన కొత్త బ్యాటరీని కేవలం 60 సెకన్ల కంటే తక్కువ సమయంలోనే అమర్చుకోవచ్చు. దీనివల్ల ఆర్డర్ల రద్దీ ఎక్కువగా ఉండే సమయాల్లో ఛార్జింగ్ కోసం విలువైన సమయం వృథా కాకుండా తక్షణమే రోడ్డుపైకి వెళ్లే వీలు కలుగుతుంది.గిగ్ వర్కర్ల కోసం 'కవచ్', 'స్వయం'!కమర్షియల్ ఈవీ విభాగంలో కేవలం వాహనాలను అందించడమే కాకుండా, వాటిని నడిపే వర్కర్ల ఆరోగ్య, ఆర్థిక భద్రతకు హాలా మొబిలిటీ ప్రాధాన్యమిస్తోంది. అందుకోసం 'కవచ్', 'స్వయం' అనే రెండు ప్రత్యేక సేవలను 'సీడ్' ఈకోసిస్టమ్ కింద జోడించింది.కవచ్ : రోడ్డుపై నిరంతరం ప్రయాణించే డెలివరీ భాగస్వాములకు రోజుకు కేవలం రూ. 2 నామమాత్రపు రుసుముతో సమగ్ర ప్రమాద, ఆరోగ్య బీమా రక్షణ కల్పిస్తోంది. అత్యవసర వేళల్లో ఆసుపత్రి ఖర్చుల భారం పడకుండా ఇది కుటుంబాలకు అభయాన్ని ఇస్తుంది.స్వయం : రైడర్ల పనితీరు, ఆర్డర్ల రికార్డు ఆధారంగా వారు సాధించిన సంపాదన నుంచి క్రమం తప్పకుండా రావాల్సిన జీతం తేదీ కంటే ముందే కొంత మొత్తాన్ని డ్రా చేసుకునే వెసులుబాటును ఈ సేవ అందిస్తుంది. పండుగలు లేదా అత్యవసర నిత్యావసర ఖర్చులకు ఇది ఎంతో తోడ్పడుతుంది.లాస్ట్-మైల్ డెలివరీ రంగానికి కొత్త ఊపిరి!హైదరాబాద్‌లోని సర్వీస్ హబ్ ప్రాతిపదికన ప్రారంభమైన ఈ ఆవిష్కరణలు కమర్షియల్ ఈవీ నిర్వహణ విధానాన్ని మార్చేస్తున్నాయి. వ్యాపార సంస్థలు ఈవీ ఫ్లీట్‌ను పెంచుకుంటున్న తరుణంలో, వాహనాలు నిరుపయోగంగా ఉండకుండా చూడటమే అసలైన సవాలు. ఈ సవాలకు పరిష్కారాలు తెస్తోంది హాలా మొబిలిటీ.ప్రస్తుతం హాలా మొబిలిటీ హైదరాబాద్‌తో పాటు బెంగళూరు, చెన్నై, దిల్లీ-ఎన్‌సీఆర్, ముంబై, పూణె, అహ్మదాబాద్, జైపూర్, కోల్‌కతా సహా 9 ప్రధాన నగరాల్లో తన సేవలను విస్తరించింది. ఇప్పటివరకు 25,000 మందికి పైగా గిగ్ వర్కర్లకు ఈ నెట్‌వర్క్ ప్రత్యక్షంగా ఆసరాగా నిలిచింది.పర్యావరణహిత విద్యుత్ వాహన రంగాన్ని వాణిజ్యపరంగా మరింత విజయవంతం చేసేందుకు ఇటువంటి సమగ్ర వ్యవస్థలు ఎంతగానో దోహదపడతాయి.

title: MACT orders Serum Institute, insurer to pay  ₹16.72 lakh to mother of 2024 accident victim | Hindustan Times
description: Tribunal member SR Agrawal held that the evidence established negligence on the part of the car driver, belonging to Serum Institute
content: The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Pune, has directed Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its insurer, New India Assurance Company Ltd, to jointly and severally pay ₹16.72 lakh in compensation, with 7% annual interest, to a 65-year-old woman whose 41-year-old son died after being run over by a car following a motorcycle accident near Golf Club Chowk in June 2024.In its judgment delivered on Wednesday, tribunal member SR Agrawal held that the evidence established negligence on the part of the car driver. Serum Institute owned the vehicle involved in the accident.“The material on record establishes that the accident was caused by the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle,” the tribunal observed. It added that the motorcycle skidding and the victim falling on the road did not, by themselves, absolve the driver of the responsibility to exercise due care.The award was passed on a claim petition filed by the victim’s mother, Lata Mohanrao Chavan, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, on October 19, 2024.Also Read | Serum Institute’s Cervavac vaccine receives WHO prequalificationAccording to the petition, Kedar Chavan was riding towards Yerawada Jail Post Office from Golf Club Chowk around 1 pm on June 18, 2024, when his motorcycle skidded. The high-end car allegedly approaching from behind at high speed, hit the motorcycle and ran over him. He sustained multiple injuries and died during treatment at Sahyadri Hospital. Police registered a case against the driver and subsequently filed a chargesheet.The mother stated that her son worked as a delivery executive with a logistics firm and ran a tailoring business. She claimed he earned ₹37,000 a month from both occupations and sought ₹60 lakh in compensation, stating that she depended on his income.Serum institute admitted owning the car but denied its involvement in the accident. The insurer disputed the deceased’s income and the mother’s dependency, denied negligence and alleged that the driver lacked a valid licence and the owner had breached policy conditions.The tribunal noted that neither the driver nor any eyewitness was examined by the respondents to explain the collision. It said motor accident claims are decided on the preponderance of probabilities, rather than the stricter standard applicable in criminal trials.While accepting negligence, the tribunal assessed Chavan’s monthly income at ₹15,000, citing gaps in the employment, income and tailoring-business records. Adding 25% for future prospects, deducting half towards personal expenses and applying a multiplier of 14, it calculated the loss of dependency at ₹15.75 lakh.The award includes amounts for funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of consortium and medical expenses, taking the total to ₹16,72,210. Rejecting the insurer’s policy-breach argument for want of evidence, the tribunal directed both respondents to pay the compensation with 7% annual interest from the date of filing the petition until realisation, along with ₹5,000 towards litigation costs.

title: SAU Inaugurates SAARC–SAU Regional and Transdisciplinary Centre for Precision Nutrition and Health | Hindustan Times
description: The new SAARC–SAU Centre for Precision Nutrition and Health will connect researchers and institutions across SAARC member states.
content: South Asian University (SAU), New Delhi, inaugurated the SAARC–SAU Regional and Transdisciplinary Centre for Precision Nutrition and Health (CPNH) on 9 October 2026, marking a significant step towards strengthening regional cooperation and advancing collaborative research to address anaemia, malnutrition, and public health challenges across South Asia. The Centre has been envisaged and initiated in collaboration with SAARC, UNICEF and the Cornell Joan Klein Jacobs Center for Precision Nutrition and Health, Cornell University, USA.The presidential address was delivered by Prof. K. K. Aggarwal, President of South Asian University. Special remarks were delivered by H.E. Ambassador Md. Golam Sarwar, Secretary General of SAARC; Prof. M. Srinivas, Member of NITI Aayog; Dr. Joan N. Matji, Global Director of Child Nutrition and Development at the Child Survival and Development Centre of Excellence, Nairobi, Kenya, representing UNICEF online; and Prof. K. Srinath Reddy, Chancellor and Founder President of the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI). All were among the distinguished dignitaries who attended the inauguration.The inaugural programme also featured a distinguished lecture by Dr. Saurabh Mehta, Founding Director of the Cornell Joan Klein Jacobs Center for Precision Nutrition and Health at Cornell University. His lecture highlighted the role of precision nutrition, biomarker research, affordable diagnostics, and interdisciplinary collaboration in improving health outcomes.The Centre will focus on addressing challenges such as anaemia and improving nutrition, particularly among adolescent girls, women, and children, through regional research, capacity development, and evidence-based health policies.With South Asian University as its institutional base, CPNH will serve as a regional collaborative hub, connecting researchers, institutions, and technical partners across SAARC member states to advance affordable, context-specific, and scalable solutions for better nutrition and health across South Asia.Note to the Reader: This article is part of Hindustan Times' promotional consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. Hindustan Times assumes no editorial responsibility for the content.

title: సంగారెడ్డి జిల్లాలోని ఫార్మా ల్యాబ్స్‌లో గ్యాస్ లీక్.. ఇద్దరు ఏపీ వాసులు మృతి | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: సంగారెడ్డి జిల్లాలోని ఓ పరిశ్రమలో గ్యాస్ లీకైంది. ఈ ఘటనలో ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌కు చెందిన ఇద్దరు మృతి చెందారు. బాధిత కుటుంబాలకు కోటి రూపాయల పరిహారం ఇవ్వాలని ప్రభుత్వాన్ని బీఆర్ఎస్ నేత హరీశ్ రావు డిమాండ్ చేశారు.
content: తెలంగాణలోని సంగారెడ్డి జిల్లా పారిశ్రామిక ప్రాంతంలో తీవ్ర విషాదం చోటుచేసుకుంది. జిన్నారం మండలం గడ్డపోతారం పారిశ్రామిక వాడలోని సరాకా లాబొరేటరీస్ లిమిటెడ్ ఫార్మాస్యూటికల్ పరిశ్రమలో శుక్రవారం తెల్లవారుజామున ప్రమాదవశాత్తు గ్యాస్ లీకై ఇద్దరు కార్మికులు ప్రాణాలు కోల్పోయారు.మృతులను సుదర్శన్ రావు (27), బాలాజీగా పోలీసులు ప్రాథమికంగా గుర్తించారు. వీరిద్దరూ ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ రాష్ట్రానికి చెందిన వారిగా సమాచారం లభించింది.సరాకా లాబొరేటరీస్ ఫార్మా యూనిట్‌లో శుక్రవారం తెల్లవారుజామున విధులు నిర్వహిస్తుండగా హఠాత్తుగా ప్రమాదకరమైన వాయువు లీకైంది. విషవాయువు పీల్చడంతో ఊపిరాడక ఇద్దరు కార్మికులు అక్కడికక్కడే చనిపోయారు. సమాచారం అందుకున్న వెంటనే స్థానిక పోలీసులు సంఘటనా స్థలానికి చేరుకుని పరిస్థితిని సమీక్షించారు. గ్యాస్ లీకేజీకి గల కచ్చితమైన కారణాలు, ప్రమాద సమయానికి సంబంధించిన పూర్తి వివరాలు ఇంకా తెలియాల్సి ఉందని, పరిశ్రమలో భద్రతా ప్రమాణాలు పాటించారా లేదా అన్న కోణంలో సైతం సమగ్ర విచారణ జరుపుతున్నామని క్షేత్రస్థాయి అధికారులు వెల్లడించారు.పరిశ్రమల్లో వరుసగా జరుగుతున్న ప్రమాదాలపై ప్రభుత్వం దృష్టి సారించడం లేదని, భద్రతా ప్రమాణాలను విస్మరిస్తున్న యాజమాన్యాలపై కఠిన చర్యలు తీసుకోవాలని బీఆర్ఎస్ నేత, మాజీ మంత్రి హరీశ్ రావు డిమాండ్ చేశారు.'సంగారెడ్డి జిల్లా జిన్నారం మండలం గడ్డపోతారం పారిశ్రామిక వాడలోని సరాక రసాయన పరిశ్రమలో గ్యాస్ లీక్ అయి ఇద్దరు కార్మికులు మృతి చెందడం తీవ్ర విషాదకరం. మృతుల కుటుంబాలకు నా ప్రగాఢ సానుభూతి. క్షతగాత్రులకు మెరుగైన వైద్యం అందించాలని, మృతుల కుటుంబాలకు కోటి రూపాయల ఎక్స్ గ్రేషియా ప్రకటించాలని ప్రభుత్వాన్ని డిమాండ్ చేస్తున్నాం. పరిశ్రమల్లో ఇలాంటి ఘటనలు తరచూ జరుగుతున్నా ప్రభుత్వం పట్టించుకోకపోవడం దుర్మార్గం. నాడు సిగాచి.. నేడు సరాక పరిశ్రమలో ప్రమాదం. గత చేదు అనుభవాల నుండి ఈ ప్రభుత్వం ఏం నేర్చుకోదా? కాంగ్రెస్ ప్రభుత్వ నిర్లక్ష్యం అమాయక కార్మికుల ప్రాణాలను బలితీసుకుంటోంది. పరిశ్రమల్లో భద్రతా ప్రమాణాల అమలు ప్రశ్నార్థకంగా మారగా, అధికారుల పర్యవేక్షణ లేకుండా పోయింది.' అని హరీశ్ రావు అన్నారు.ప్రమాదం జరిగిన తర్వాత వచ్చి ఫోటోలకు ఫోజులు ఇవ్వడం తప్ప.. కార్మికుల ప్రాణాలకు భరోసా కల్పించేందుకు మీరు చేస్తున్నదేమిటి? అని హరీశ్ రావు ప్రశ్నించారు. భద్రతా ప్రమాణాలు పాటించకుండా కార్మికుల ప్రాణాలతో చెలగాటమాడుతున్న పరిశ్రమల యాజమాన్యాలపై కఠిన చర్యలు తీసుకునేదెప్పుడు? అని అడిగారు. సరాక పరిశ్రమ ఘటనపై సమగ్ర విచారణ జరిపి, ప్రమాదానికి బాధ్యులైన కంపెనీ యాజమాన్యం పై కఠిన చర్యలు తీసుకోవాలన్నారు. భవిష్యత్తులో ఇలాంటి ప్రమాదాలు పునరావృతం కాకుండా పరిశ్రమల్లో భద్రతా చర్యలు పటిష్టం చేయాలన్నారు. ఉపాధి కోసం వచ్చిన అమాయక కార్మికుల ప్రాణాలకు ప్రభుత్వం భరోసా కల్పించాలన్నారు. సిగాచి ఘటనలో ఇంటి పెద్దను కోల్పోయిన 54 మంది కార్మిక కుటుంబాలందరికీ సీఎం స్వయంగా ప్రకటించిన కోటి రూపాయల పరిహారాన్ని ఇప్పటికైనా అందించి మాట నిలుపుకోవాలన్నారు.

title: Aman Arora accuses Congress of planning to withdraw Punjab welfare schemes | Hindustan Times
description: AAP Punjab chief Aman Arora accused Congress of threatening welfare schemes ahead of the 2027 election, citing remarks by MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring.
content: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Punjab president and cabinet minister Aman Arora on Thursday accused the Congress of threatening welfare benefits in the state, asking the opposition party to clarify whether it would continue free electricity, the ₹10 lakh Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna and financial assistance for women if it wins the 2027 Assembly elections.Addressing a press conference, Arora said remarks by Congress MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring on electricity subsidies and financial assistance for women had raised questions about the party’s position on welfare schemes. He alleged that a Congress government would withdraw benefits currently available to ordinary households and could reintroduce toll plazas and higher electricity and canal water charges.Arora challenged Congress leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, party president Mallikarjun Kharge and Pratap Singh Bajwa, to state whether the schemes would continue under a Congress government. He questioned who would decide which families qualified for assistance if benefits were restricted according to financial need.The AAP leader also asked Congress MPs, MLAs and former ministers to give up subsidies themselves if they believed those who did not need assistance should be excluded. He said he had not seen Congress leaders publicly surrender the benefits while the AAP government continued to provide free electricity and financial assistance to women.Arora referred to the Congress government led by Captain Amarinder Singh, alleging that free electricity for farmers had been discontinued after the party came to power in 2002 and restored around two-and-a-half years later. He also cited the party’s promise before the 2017 Assembly elections to continue free electricity, arguing that voters should assess its assurances against its record in government.The AAP leader said the state government, led by Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, was providing electricity subsidies to households, farmers and industry. He also referred to the monthly financial assistance for women and the health coverage available under the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna.Arora further alleged that a Congress government would impose charges for canal water supplied to agricultural fields, increase electricity costs and discontinue the ₹10 lakh health cover. He urged voters to consider Raja Warring’s remarks when assessing the Congress’s policies ahead of the 2027 elections.The Congress’s position on the continuation of these schemes was not included in the material provided. Arora called on its leadership to give clear answers before seeking votes in Punjab.

title: KENT RO enters home energy market with  ₹250-crore Noida manufacturing investment | Hindustan Times
description: KENT has entered residential energy storage and backup, adding lithium batteries and solar hybrid inverters to its product lineup.
content: KENT New Energy will offer lithium battery storage and power backup systems as the company expands beyond water and air purification. KENT RO Systems Ltd. has entered the residential energy storage and power backup market with the launch of KENT New Energy, backed by an investment of nearly ₹250 crore in a manufacturing facility in Noida.Announced in New Delhi on October 21, 2026, the new division will cater to households adopting rooftop solar as well as those seeking alternatives to conventional lead-acid batteries used in home inverters and uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems.The company's manufacturing facility in Sector 159, Noida, has an installed annual capacity of 3.5 gigawatt-hours (GWh), which KENT plans to increase to 10 GWh over the next six months. Spread across six acres, the facility covers 3 lakh sq. ft. The company sources battery cells from manufacturers including EVE and REPT.The launch extends KENT's presence beyond its established water purification business and its air purifiers and Kühl BLDC fans into household energy management.“We began by helping families access purified drinking water. Now we want to empower them to generate, store and manage electricity in their own homes,” said Mahesh Gupta, chairman and managing director of KENT RO Systems Ltd.Products target solar adoption and power backupKENT New Energy's portfolio comprises lithium batteries and solar hybrid inverters for energy storage, alongside batteries and inverter systems for conventional household backup requirements.For homes with rooftop solar installations, the company has introduced battery storage systems in 5.1 kWh, 11.8 kWh and 16 kWh capacities. According to KENT, the batteries can store electricity generated by solar panels and power drawn from the grid. They are rated for more than 6,000 charge cycles and carry a 10-year warranty.The accompanying hybrid inverters combine solar, grid and battery power. The single-phase range includes 3 kW, 5 kW and 6 kW models, while the three-phase range offers capacities of 10 kW, 12 kW and 15 kW. Depending on the system configuration and connected load, these products are designed to support appliances such as air-conditioners and pumps during power outages.For households using existing inverter systems, KENT has introduced 12V and 24V lithium batteries with capacities ranging from 1.28 kWh to 3.84 kWh. The 12V range starts at ₹22,000. The company states that these batteries have a design life of 10 years, support 90% depth of discharge and do not require water top-ups.The portfolio also includes an all-in-one inverter that combines a lithium battery and inverter in one enclosure, along with the H1 series home UPS. Both product lines are available in 1100 VA and 2400 VA models.Remote monitoring included with solar invertersThe solar hybrid inverters come with a 4G data logger and a five-year data pack included in the price. Through the KENT central command mobile application, installers can monitor installed systems and change settings remotely.According to the company, the system uses mobile network connectivity rather than home Wi-Fi, and data is stored on its servers in India.KENT plans to distribute the products through its dealer network, retail stores and online channels. Solar hybrid inverters and larger battery packs will also be available through solar system integrators and engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) partners. The company said its distribution plans include installer training, professional installation and after-sales support.Residential solar expansion provides market contextThe launch comes as rooftop solar adoption increases in India, creating demand for systems that can store electricity for use outside daylight hours and provide backup during grid outages.According to Mercom India Research, residential consumers accounted for 82 per cent of the 2.7 GW of rooftop solar capacity installed in India in the first quarter of 2026. The government's PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana aims to extend rooftop solar installations to one crore households.KENT's entry into energy storage places it in a market serving both solar-equipped homes and households looking to upgrade conventional backup systems. The company said the new division is intended to expand its role in household energy generation, storage and management.Note to the Reader: This article is part of Hindustan Times' promotional consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand.
