title: Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar review: This Luv Ranjan-coded buddy romance with newcomers is a fun, harmless ride for the most part | Bollywood
description: Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar pairs scenic Dehradun locations, catchy music and appealing newcomers with a familiar school-reunion story.  | Bollywood
content: Pehla Pyaar Doosri BaarDirector: Anuj SainiCast: Sparsh, Alisha, Kunal, Sakshi, Tushar and SargunRating: 3 starsGood looking people, catchy songs, scenic locations and cheesy dialogues. For decades, Indian cinema has relied on this tried and tested formula to tell rom coms, and audiences have rarely complained. Luv Ranjan, however, found his own spin on it 15 years ago, throwing in bickering friends and everyday lingo that made Pyaar Ka Punchnama and Sonu Ke Titu Ki Sweety big successes. Now comes Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar, another attempt to revisit familiar territory. Does it have enough charm to make an old formula feel fresh?What is the plot of Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar?Directed by Anuj Saini, the film follows three school friends- Shivi, Gautam and Vedant, who are now colleagues, all single and still searching for love. A school reunion brings with it a chance of finally confessing their feelings to their respective school crushes. But when it comes to matters of the heart, is a second chance all it takes or are some things best left in the past?For starters, there is an ease to the way this roughly 2 hour 20 minute film begins. Luv Ranjan and Jehan Handa, who have written PPDB, keep things light and tap into what rarely fails: nostalgia. Here, it is the nostalgia of going back to school and meeting classmates you have long lost touch with. Set against the beautiful landscapes of Dehradun, the film is easy on the eyes. The first half of PPDB is a breeze, largely thanks to the chemistry between its three leads. A few dips too surface along the way. But a major problem crops up soon: for all its easy charm, what is the film actually about? The characters go back to school, meet their respective crushes... and then what? The film seems unsure of where to go from there.The second half picks up the pace, and the film finally seems to find some direction. The climax works, wrapping things up on a fun note. The comedy lands more often than it misses, with a handful of sequences likely to draw genuine chuckles. Thankfully, the dialogues steer clear of recycled WhatsApp jokes, giving the humour a more natural feel. A major track feels hard to buy into- a man falling head over heels for a school crush he barely spoke to back in the day, expects her to call off her impending wedding years later, all within two days of the reunion! Nostalgia can make old memories feel special, but it cannot, by itself make a convincing love story. The music by Rochak Kohli is very good, and helps the film a lot. The acting performances by the newcomers- Sparsh Walia, Sakshi Vaidya, Kunal Vaid, Alisha Chopra (as Gehna) and Tushar Chhibber (as Kabir) are good, and lift the wafer thin story. Sparsh's character reminds you of Kartik Aaryan from the first Pyaar Ka Punchnama.The verdictOverall, Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar has its moments. Its characters are busy chasing the people they fancied in school, but the film never quite makes you root for these romances as much as it should. That said, watch it with your friends and the familiar setting might get you talking about the people you fancied and the confessions you never made. Your stories might just be better written than this one.

title: Punjab Congress chief moves privilege motion against Mann, says CM ‘misled’ House on anti-sacrilege law | Hindustan Times
description: The Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed unanimously on April 13, proposes life imprisonment and fines for acts of sacrilege.
content: Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh on Thursday moved a privilege motion against chief minister Bhagwant Mann, accusing him of misleading the House regarding the 2018 Punjab anti-sacrilege bill and backtracking from amending the law.Pargat, who is also the Jalandhar Cantt MLA, alleged that despite a consensus among all legislators on amending the law in the presence of the Akal Takht jathedar, the government was now backing away from its commitment.2026 amendment bill proposes stricter punishment for sacrilegeThe Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was unanimously passed by the assembly on April 13. It includes a provision for stricter punishment, including life imprisonment for any act of sacrilege against the Guru Granth Sahib. It also proposes fines from ₹5 lakh to ₹25 lakh. However, the Akal Takht raised several objections to the law, particularly related to some Sikh terminology, the “custodian” of the religious text and assigning unique numbers to the holy “birs”.“The chief minister had misled the House regarding the 2018 Punjab anti-sacrilege bill and the documents sent by the Punjab Legislative Assembly to the President’s office,” Pargat claimed after submitting the privilege motion against Mann to Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan through the assembly secretary on the first day of the session here.Also read: Akal Takht supreme, but law against sacrilege won’t be diluted: CM Bhagwant MannCongress leader seeks clarity on documents sent to President’s office“The people of Punjab have the right to know the current status of the proposed amendments to the anti-sacrilege law and the actual position regarding the documents sent to the President’s Office in 2018,” he said. The Congress leader said through the privilege motion, he has sought scrutiny of the chief minister’s role and accountability in the matter, so that the rights of the House and the dignity of democratic institutions are preserved.“It is the government’s responsibility to present the facts clearly before the House. If there are discrepancies between the chief minister’s statements and official documents, the matter must be investigated impartially and the truth brought before the public,” added Pargat.He said the assembly is a vital democratic institution where every member has the right to receive accurate information based on facts and official documents.Also read: Chandigarh: Mann to meet 7-member panel to discuss anti-sacrilege law todayCongress accuses AAP government of avoiding consultations with Sikh bodiesPargat alleged that the AAP government was not only avoiding amendments to the law but was also retreating from consultations with Sikh institutions and a discussion on the sensitive issue in the assembly.Pargat said the issue of sacrilege is deeply connected with Punjab’s religious sentiments, faith and the trust of its people. “The government must explain why it is unwilling to proceed in accordance with the consensus reached earlier and what objection it has to an open discussion on the issue in the assembly,” he said.

title: Prabhas Birthday: ప్రభాస్ బర్త్‌డే.. ప్రశాంత్ నీల్ భార్యకు ప్రేమతో కూడిన ముద్దు.. కల్కి 2 సెట్స్‌లో రెబల్ స్టార్ | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: Prabhas Birthday: ఇండియన్ సినిమా రంగానికి తిరుగులేని 'పాన్-ఇండియా' ఐకాన్‌గా ఎదిగిన రెబెల్ స్టార్ ప్రభాస్ పుట్టినరోజు సందర్భంగా సోషల్ మీడియా ఊగిపోతోంది. ప్రశాంత్ నీల్ భార్య లిఖితా రెడ్డి షేర్ చేసిన ఒక ఫోటో నెట్టింట విపరీతంగా ట్రెండ్ అవుతుండగా.. 'ఫౌజీ', 'కల్కి 2' టీమ్స్ ఫ్యాన్స్‌కు ట్రీట్ ఇచ్చాయి.
content: Prabhas Birthday: భారతీయ చిత్ర పరిశ్రమలోనే అత్యంత భారీ క్రేజ్, వేలకోట్ల బాక్సాఫీస్ స్టామినా కలిగిన డార్లింగ్, రెబెల్ స్టార్ ప్రభాస్ (Prabhas) ఈరోజు (అక్టోబర్ 23) తన పుట్టినరోజును జరుపుకుంటున్నారు. పాన్-ఇండియా సూపర్ స్టార్ బర్త్‌డే కావడంతో ప్రపంచ వ్యాప్తంగా ఉన్న ఆయన అభిమానులు సోషల్ మీడియా వేదికగా పండుగ వాతావరణాన్ని సృష్టించారు. తనకంటూ ప్రత్యేకమైన గుర్తింపును తెచ్చుకున్న ప్రభాస్.. తన ఆత్మీయులు, కుటుంబ సభ్యుల మధ్య అత్యంత సాధారణంగా ఈ వేడుకలను జరుపుకున్నారు.ఈ సందర్భంగా ప్రభాస్ సినిమాలకు సంబంధించిన భారీ అప్‌డేట్‌లతో పాటు, ఆయనకు సంబంధించిన ఒక అరుదైన ఫోటో ప్రస్తుతం నెట్టింట హల్‌చల్ చేస్తోంది. అంతేకాదు హను రాఘవపూడి దర్శకత్వంలో రాబోతున్న 'ఫౌజీ' చిత్రం నుంచి స్పెషల్ గ్లింప్స్ అనౌన్స్‌మెంట్, అలాగే 'కల్కి 2' సెట్స్‌లోకి ప్రభాస్ అడుగుపెట్టిన ఆన్-సెట్ విజువల్స్ వైరల్ అవుతున్నాయి.ప్రశాంత్ నీల్ భార్యకు ప్రభాస్ ముద్దు..ప్రభాస్‌తో 'సలార్' వంటి ఇండస్ట్రీ హిట్ అందించిన కేజీఎఫ్ ఫేమ్ డైరెక్టర్ ప్రశాంత్ నీల్ (Prashanth Neel) కుటుంబంతో డార్లింగ్‌కు ఉన్న అనుబంధం అందరికీ తెలిసిందే. ప్రభాస్ బర్త్‌డే సందర్భంగా ప్రశాంత్ నీల్ సతిమణి లిఖిత రెడ్డి (Likitha Reddy) తన సోషల్ మీడియా ఖాతాలో ప్రభాస్‌తో ఉన్న ఒక రేర్ పిక్‌ను పంచుకున్నారు. అందులో ప్రభాస్ ఎంతో ఆప్యాయంగా లిఖిత చెంపపై ముద్దుపెడుతూ కనిపించారు.కెమెరా ముందుకు రాగానే ఎంతో సిగ్గుపడే ప్రభాస్, ఇంత ఆఫ్-స్క్రీన్ ఆప్యాయతను చూపించడం చాలా అరుదు. ఈ ఫోటోను షేర్ చేస్తూ.. "హ్యాపీ బర్త్‌డే అన్నయ్య" అంటూ లిఖిత రెడ్డి క్యాప్షన్ జోడించారు. ఈ క్యూట్ అండ్ అఫెక్షనేట్ పిక్ చూసిన డార్లింగ్ ఫ్యాన్స్ విపరీతంగా లైకులు, కామెంట్లతో సోషల్ మీడియాను హోరెత్తిస్తున్నారు.'ఫౌజీ' గ్లింప్స్ అప్‌డేట్.. హను రాఘవపూడి మ్యాజిక్మరోవైపు ప్రభాస్ పుట్టినరోజు కానుకగా ఆయన రాబోయే చిత్రాల నుంచి మేకర్స్ వరుస అప్‌డేట్లను ప్రకటిస్తున్నారు. సీతారామం ఫేమ్ హను రాఘవపూడి (Hanu Raghavapudi) దర్శకత్వంలో మైత్రీ మూవీ మేకర్స్ నిర్మిస్తున్న పీరియాడికల్ యాక్షన్ డ్రామా ‘ఫౌజీ’ నుంచి ఈరోజు ఒక ప్రత్యేకమైన అప్‌డేట్ రాబోతోంది. ఇది సాధారణ టీజర్ కాకుండా, సినిమా కథా నేపథ్యం, ప్రభాస్ క్యారెక్టర్ వైబ్‌ను పరిచయం చేసే ఒక స్పెషల్ ‘గ్లింప్స్’ అని నిర్మాత రవిశంకర్ ఇప్పటికే వెల్లడించారు.'కల్కి 2' సెట్స్‌లోకి భైరవ.. వైజయంతీ మూవీస్ మాస్ వీడియాఇక గ్లోబల్ వైడ్‌గా రూ. 1000 కోట్లకు పైగా వసూళ్లు సాధించిన 'కల్కి 2898 AD' సీక్వెల్ 'కల్కి 2' (Kalki 2) నుంచి మేకర్స్ బిగ్ అప్‌డేట్ ఇచ్చారు. ప్రభాస్ 'భైరవ' (Bhairava) పాత్రలో తిరిగి షూటింగ్ సెట్స్‌లోకి అడుగుపెట్టినట్లు తెలియజేస్తూ వైజయంతీ మూవీస్ ఒక పవర్‌ఫుల్ ఆన్-సెట్ వీడియోను విడుదల చేసింది. ప్రభాస్ రాయల్ లుక్‌ను సిల్హౌట్ (Silhouette) విజువల్స్‌లో చూపిస్తూ ఫ్యాన్స్ లో క్యూరియాసిటీని పెంచారు.ఈ సీక్వెల్‌లో సుమతి (Sumati) పాత్రలో ఎవరు నటించబోతున్నారనేది త్వరలోనే ప్రకటించనున్నారు. అమితాబ్ బచ్చన్, కమల్ హాసన్ వంటి దిగ్గజాలు తమ పాత్రల్లో తిరిగి అలరించనున్నారు. ఈ చిత్రాన్ని 2028లో ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా విడుదల చేయడానికి నిర్మాతలు ప్లాన్ చేస్తున్నారు. బర్త్‌డే నాడే బ్యాక్-టు-బ్యాక్ మాస్ అప్‌డేట్లు రావడంతో ప్రభాస్ అభిమానుల ఆనందానికి హద్దులు లేకుండా పోయాయి.

title: Video of minor brothers in Kapurthala consuming drugs leads to peddler’s arrest in Punjab | Hindustan Times
description: The case has put the police and civil administration on the back foot at a time when the state government claims to be tackling drug abuse.
content: As the political debate over Punjab’s drug crisis intensifies, two brothers—aged 9 and 12 years—have fallen victim to ‘chitta’ (synthetic drugs) in a Kapurthala village.The issue surfaced on Wednesday after a video showing the 9-year-old openly consuming drugs went viral on social media, forcing the police into action. Subsequent dope tests for both brothers came back positive.Also Read I How many drug peddlers released by police, SAD (PS) questions CMDrug abuse issue in PunjabKapurthala police rushed the boys to the local civil hospital on Thursday. The 9-year-old was later sent to the drug de-addiction centre at the Government Medical College in Amritsar, while his elder brother will receive treatment at the Kapurthala civil hospital. The brothers, both school dropouts, are raised by a single mother who works as a daily-wager.The case has put the police and civil administration on the back foot at a time when the state government claims to be tackling drug abuse on a war-footing through its 60-day campaign, Yudh Nashean Virudh. Bholath deputy superintendent of police (DSP) Sukhpal Singh said a probe was underway to track down the supply chain. “Preliminary investigation reveals that the 9-year-old was hooked onto drugs two months ago,” he said.Police said the village was situated near drug hotspots Naharpur and Lakhan Khurd villages between the Subhanpur-Kartarpur belt.Parental oversight key: ExpertCommenting on the incident, Punjabi University, Patiala, psychology professor Damanjit Sandhu said, “At this age, children lack fully developed decision-making abilities. There is typically no peer pressure among kids this young. Irrespective of socio-economic status—from bureaucrats to daily wagers—parents must monitor who their children spend time with and who influences them.”Sandhu, who specialises in adolescent psychology, said childhood trauma, vulnerability, parental neglect, and immediate social environments contributed to early drug dependence. “Earlier, the focus was on teaching children about ‘good touch and bad touch’. Today, we must warn them never to accept or consume anything given by strangers or acquaintances,” she said.Police have arrested the accused peddler, Paramjit Singh, 32, a resident of New Shanti Nagar in Hoshiarpur’s Islamabad area. He is accused of introducing children to drugs and filming them during consumption.Also Read I Kejriwal questions Amit Shah over drug menace in BJP-ruled statesSubhanpur station house officer (SHO) Amandeep Kumar said the police recovered a mobile phone from the accused containing footage of the juvenile consuming drugs.“In the clip, the accused can be seen handing drugs to the minor and coercing him to consume them. The accused, who is currently in one-day police custody, was staying at a relative’s house in the victims’ village,” Kumar said, adding that the victims identified Paramjit as the person who repeatedly forced them into drug abuse. He added that both the victims will be handed over to the district child welfare committee once treated. A case has been registered under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, and Section 29/61/85 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.

title: మేనకోడలి పెళ్లికి వైఎస్ జగన్ బెంగళూరు ప్యాలెస్ ఎందుకు ఇవ్వడం లేదు? అసలు కారణం | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: కొన్ని రోజులుగా వైఎస్ షర్మిల కుమార్తె అంజలి వివాహ వేదిక గురించి వార్తలు వస్తూనే ఉన్నాయి. బెంగళూరులో పెళ్లికి వైఎస్ జగన్ అనుమతించలేదని చర్చ జరుగుతోంది. దీనికి వైసీపీ నేతలు ఓ కారణం చెబుతున్నారు.
content: వైఎస్సార్ కుటుంబంలో గత కొంతకాలంగా సాగుతున్న ఆస్తుల వివాదం ఇప్పుడు మరో కీలక మలుపు తిరిగింది. ఏపీ కాంగ్రెస్ అధ్యక్షురాలు వైఎస్ షర్మిల కుమార్తె అంజలి వివాహం వేళ.. బెంగళూరులోని యెలహంకలో ఉన్న వైఎస్సార్ కుటుంబ ఆస్తి (ప్యాలెస్) ఉపయోగంపై చోటుచేసుకున్న పరిణామాలు రెండు తెలుగు రాష్ట్రాల్లో చర్చనీయాంశంగా మారాయి.తన కుమార్తె వివాహాన్ని బెంగళూరులోని యెలహంక ప్యాలెస్‌లో జరిపించేందుకు వైఎస్ షర్మిల ఏర్పాట్లు చేసుకోవాలని భావించినప్పటికీ, అక్కడ పెళ్లికి అనుమతించేందుకు వైఎస్సార్‌సీపీ అధినేత వైఎస్ జగన్ మోహన్ రెడ్డి సుముఖత వ్యక్తం చేయలేదని కథనాలు వెలువడుతున్నాయి. ఈ అంశంపై జగన్ వర్గం, షర్మిల వర్గాల మధ్య భిన్నమైన వాదనలు వినిపిస్తున్నాయి.వైసీపీ చెబుతున్న ప్రధాన కారణాలుమాజీ ముఖ్యమంత్రి వైఎస్ జగన్‌ భద్రతా ప్రోటోకాల్స్ దృష్ట్యా, బెంగళూరు నివాసం అత్యంత సున్నితమైన ప్రాంతం. వివాహం వంటి భారీ వేడుక నిర్వహించినప్పుడు పెద్ద ఎత్తున ప్రజలు, రాజకీయ ప్రముఖులు, విఐపీలు, మీడియా ప్రతినిధులు తరలివస్తారు. ఇటువంటి చోట నిరంతరం రద్దీ ఉండటం భద్రతకు విఘాతం కలిగిస్తుందని భావిస్తున్నారు. అంతేకాదు తెలియని వ్యక్తులు కూడా ఇంటిలోపలకి వేడుక సమయంలో వస్తుంటారు. ఇదే సెక్యూరిటీ దృష్ట్యా సమస్యలు సృష్టించవచ్చని వైసీపీ చెబుతోంది.భారీగా వచ్చే అతిథుల వల్ల ఆ నివాస ప్రాంగణానికి సంబంధించిన అంతర్గత విజువల్స్, ఫొటోలు, వీడియోలు సోషల్ మీడియాలో, బయట సర్క్యులేట్ అయ్యే అవకాశం ఉందని, దీనివల్ల ప్రైవసీకి భంగం వాటిల్లుతుందని జగన్ లేఖ ద్వారా వివరణ ఇచ్చినట్లు వర్గాలు చెబుతున్నాయి. అంతేకాదు తాను నివసించేది బెంగళూరులోనే కాబట్టి.. పులివెందుల, హైదరాబాద్‌లోని తమకు చెందిన ప్రాంతాల్లో వేడుకలు నిర్వహించేందుకు తనకు ఎలాంటి అభ్యంతర లేదని జగన్ తెలిపినట్టుగా తెలుస్తోంది. అయితే వెడ్డింగ్ కార్డ్స్ కంటే ముందే దీనిపై చర్చ జరిగింది. అప్పుడే జగన్ ఈ విషయాన్ని షర్మిలకు చెప్పారని వైసీపీ అంటోంది.మరోవైపు వేడుకకు పలు రాష్ట్రాల ముఖ్యమంత్రులు, కాంగ్రెస్ అగ్రనేతలు హాజరయ్యే అవకాశం ఉన్నందున, జగన్ సొంత నివాసంలోనే కాంగ్రెస్ ముఖ్యనేతల సమావేశాలు లేదా రాజకీయ చర్చలు జరగడం వైఎస్సార్‌సీపీ రాజకీయ వ్యూహాలకు, పొత్తుల సమీకరణాలకు ఇబ్బందిగా మారుతుందన్న కోణం కూడా ఉందనే ప్రచారం జరుగుతోంది.షర్మిల వర్గం వాదనమరోవైపు వైఎస్ షర్మిల మద్దతుదారులు ఈ వ్యవహారాన్ని ఆస్తి వివాదం, వ్యక్తిగత పట్టింపులతో ముడిపెట్టి చూస్తున్నారు. వైఎస్ రాజశేఖర రెడ్డి జీవించి ఉన్నప్పుడు పిల్లలిద్దరికీ సమానంగా ఆస్తులు పంచాలని భావించారని, హైదరాబాద్‌లోని లొటస్ పాండ్, బెంగళూరులోని యెలహంక కాంపౌండ్, ఇడుపులపాయ నివాసాల్లో షర్మిలకు భాగస్వామ్యం ఉందన్నది వారి వాదన. భద్రతా కారణాల దృష్ట్యా కుదరదని జగన్ చెప్పినట్టుగా తెలుస్తోంది.గత ఐదేళ్లుగా జగన్, షర్మిల మధ్య సరస్వతి పవర్ అండ్ ఇండస్ట్రీస్ షేర్లతో పాటు ఇతర ఆస్తులపై వివాదం నడుస్తోందని, ఈ వ్యవహారం నేషనల్ కంపెనీ లా ట్రిబ్యునల్ ముందు కూడా విచారణలో ఉందనేది బహిరంగ రహస్యమే. పెళ్లి వేదిక విషయమై ఇరువర్గాల మధ్య విభేదాలు రావడంతో తల్లి వైఎస్ విజయమ్మ స్వయంగా జగన్‌ను ఒప్పించేందుకు ప్రయత్నించినప్పటికీ, ఆయన తన నిర్ణయానికే కట్టుబడి ఉన్నారని వార్తలు వస్తున్నాయి.మరో వేదికఇప్పటికే వివాహ ఆహ్వాన పత్రికలు అందజేసే ప్రక్రియ ప్రారంభమైన నేపథ్యంలో, యెలహంక ప్యాలెస్‌లో అనుమతి లభించకపోవడంతో షర్మిల బృందం బెంగళూరు లేదా హైదరాబాద్‌ పరిసరాల్లో విఐపీల భద్రతకు సరిపోయే ప్రత్యామ్నాయ వేదిక కోసం అన్వేషణ ప్రారంభించినట్లు తెలుస్తోంది.

title: What we know about Shamonda, the livestock virus linked to a human infection for the first time | HT Explainers
description: French reports said the man in his 60s was severely immunocompromised when he died in early October. World Health Organization said it was an isolated case. | HT Explainers
content: France's report on Thursday of the first known human case of Shamonda, a cattle virus spread by biting midges that reached Europe only this summer, has drawn attention to a pathogen known in livestock since the 1960s but never before found in a person.The patient, a man in his 60s from the Lyon area according to the local newspaper Le Progrès, was severely immunocompromised and was being treated for a serious illness when he died in early October, Reuters reported. French authorities suspect he was infected through a midge bite in eastern France, where the virus circulated among animals in spring and summer. The country's health and agriculture ministries said the neurological complications he developed before his death were "very likely linked" to Shamonda, citing preliminary findings.The World Health Organization (WHO) described it as an isolated case. The French government said it had identified no health risk to the general population, and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) is investigating "the potential public health implications of this first human infection", Bloomberg reported.The virusShamonda is an orthobunyavirus, the same type of virus as Schmallenberg, which spread through European livestock from 2011. Within that group, Shamonda is part of the Simbu serogroup, a family of more than 25 related viruses that the immune system recognises in similar ways. Several of its members, including Akabane and Schmallenberg, are carried by insects and can harm unborn livestock.Midges are tiny flies that carry the virus from animal to animal. Cattle are the virus's main hosts, though infections have also been found in sheep, goats, horses and alpacas, according to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH). The midge species behind its spread in Europe is still unknown, Bloomberg reported.First detected in cattleShamonda was first detected in cattle in Nigeria in the mid-1960s. Scientists working in Ibadan described it as a new virus in a 1972 paper on Simbu-group viruses they had isolated there between 1964 and 1969. It has since been reported sporadically in cattle in west, east and southern Africa and in Japan.In 2015 and 2016, researchers studying cattle in southern Japan found 15 calves born deformed after Shamonda infected them in the womb. The calves had arthrogryposis, a condition in which the joints are locked in bent positions, along with damage to the brain and spinal cord. The researchers concluded that the virus should be treated as teratogenic, or able to cause birth defects, in ruminants such as cattle, sheep and goats.The virus was confirmed in Europe in late July, after genetic tests on sick cattle in southern Germany, Switzerland and eastern France.French authorities believe it had been circulating in France since the spring. It has now been detected in 14 countries, among them Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal and Spain.Europe has dealt with a close relative of the virus before. In 2011, farmers and vets in Germany and the Netherlands reported an unidentified disease in cattle, with fever, lower milk yields and diarrhoea. German researchers used metagenomic sequencing, which reads all the genetic material in a sample, to find a new orthobunyavirus in the animals' blood, and first described it as "Shamonda-like" because part of its genome closely resembled Shamonda's.The virus, named Schmallenberg, spread rapidly across much of central and western Europe in the first known outbreak of a Simbu-group virus on the continent.Also read: The science of H1N1The infectionIn cattle, Shamonda causes diarrhoea, weakness and loss of appetite and, less often, fever, French animal health authorities said. A study of nine French dairy farms found milk production fell by up to 75%, Reuters reported.Infection in pregnant cows can cause abortions, stillbirths and brain deformities in calves, according to the Federation of Veterinarians of Europe, Bloomberg reported. Some infected horses have also developed neurological disorders.WOAH says the long-term impact of the European variants of the virus remains uncertain.Countries are not obliged to report Shamonda cases to WOAH, because the virus is not on its list of diseases. The European Union's Animal Health Law does not cover it either, so there is no EU surveillance specific to it. The available data therefore may not give a complete picture of its spread, Reuters reported.The human caseShamonda had never been detected in a human before the Lyon case, despite circulating in Africa and Asia for decades, the French ministries said. The health ministry called it "an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient". Clinical, biological and epidemiological investigations are still under way, the ministries said, and doctors have only this one case from which to gauge how the virus affects people.There is no treatment for the insect-borne orthobunyaviruses that affect livestock, according to a 2022 review of vaccine research published in the journal One Health Outlook. Three vaccines against Schmallenberg have received marketing authorisation for use in livestock, the review added.A vaccine made for one virus in the group may not protect against another, however. In a 2013 study, researchers vaccinated calves against Akabane and Aino, two relatives of Schmallenberg, and then infected them with Schmallenberg. The vaccine did not prevent infection, and the researchers concluded that vaccines for related viruses could not substitute for ones made specifically for Schmallenberg.Also read: Billions of doses later, a Lancet review confirms mRNA vaccine safetyShould people worry?"Based on current information and knowledge of the transmission of closely related viruses, this is an isolated human case and it is unlikely to lead to wider spread at this time," the WHO said.In 2012, researchers at the Robert Koch Institute, Germany's national public health agency, surveyed and tested shepherds who had handled sheep infected with Schmallenberg, including birth products carrying high levels of the virus. They found no evidence that the virus had passed to any of them.But some other viruses in the Simbu group cause human illness. Oropouche, spread mainly by midges, has caused outbreaks in South America and the Caribbean since late 2023, including in places with no previous history of the disease. It has no specific treatment or vaccine, according to the WHO's regional office for the Americas. Shuni, another member of the group, has been found in people with neurological infections in South Africa.As recently as 2023, researchers who had identified the virus in a goat foetus in South Africa wrote that there was no evidence linking Shamonda to human disease, though they said its characteristics needed study because of the risk that it could pass from animals to people.Also read: Zoonotic diseases: A neglected public and planetary health frontierAnimal diseases and a changing climateThe WHO defines a zoonosis as any disease or infection that passes naturally from vertebrate animals to humans. More than 200 kinds are known, and they account for a large share of new and existing human diseases.Covid-19 is the most widely studied recent case. In June 2025, the WHO's Scientific Advisory Group for the Origins of Novel Pathogens (SAGO), an independent panel of experts, said available evidence suggested the virus had passed to humans from animals, either directly from bats or through an intermediate host. (There is a longstanding debate on the origins of Sars-CoV-2, the virus that causes Covid-19, with another side supporting a lab-leak theory.)A 2008 study in Nature of 335 events in which infectious diseases emerged in people between 1940 and 2004 found that 60.3% were zoonoses, most of them originating in wildlife, and that their number had risen over time. Diseases spread by insects and ticks made up 22.8% of the total, and 28.8% in the study's final decade.Researchers have also linked the risk to how people use land. A 2020 study in Nature found that wild animals known to carry pathogens shared with humans were more common on farmland, in cities and on other heavily used land than in nearby undisturbed habitat, with the effect strongest for rodents, bats and perching birds.A 2022 study in Nature projected that climate change will bring more wild mammal species into contact with one another, giving viruses new chances to jump between species. By 2070, it found, warming and land-use change will push mammal species into new combinations, including in densely populated parts of Asia and Africa, leading to about 4,000 new transmissions of viruses between species. The authors found that bats would account for most of this sharing, that the shift may already be under way, and that holding warming under 2°C this century would not reduce it.Since 1998, six strains of bluetongue, a midge-borne livestock disease, have spread across 12 countries and 800km further north in Europe than previously recorded, researchers reported in 2005. They linked the spread to a warmer European climate, which let the virus survive winters better and let its main midge carrier expand northwards, while native European midges began transmitting it too.These studies aren't specifically about Shamonda. Scientists have not established how the virus reached Europe or which midges are spreading it, and WOAH says its long-term impact remains uncertain.

title: Henry Nicholls among 11 international players in New Zealand A squad for Tests against India A | Cricket
description: New Zealand named a strong squad for the three unofficial Tests against India A, beginning October 24.   | Cricket
content: New Zealand on Friday named a star-studded 19-member squad for the upcoming three unofficial Tests against India A. The extended squad features 11 international players for the three four-day matches, with the opener set to begin on Saturday, October 23, in Lincoln.New Zealand A will be led by Canterbury's Rhys Mariu in the first two Tests, while the skipper for the third and final game has not been revealed yet. Adi Ashok, Kristian Clarke, Dean Foxcroft, Matt Fisher, Mitch Hay, Jayden Lennox, Ben Lister, Henry Nicholls and Tim Robinson have all been named in the squad. These players bring a lot of experience to the side, having represented the senior team in the past.Nick Kelly, who is New Zealand's newest centrally contracted player, is also in line to feature in the third match. The A series will run concurrently with the white-ball matches between New Zealand and India.Also Read: Ishan Kishan has groin niggle, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi might play in 2nd T20I against New Zealand: Sitanshu Kotak"We're really looking forward to hosting India A," New Zealand Cricket Head of High Performance Development, Pete Sanford, said in an official statement.“They've announced a very strong lineup, which poses a great opportunity for growth as players to test their strengths against international class. There's a huge buzz around having India on our shores, and I know the squad are raring to get their domestic summer underway,” he added.All you need to know about A seriesThe first unofficial Test will be played at Bert Sutcliffe Oval in Lincoln from October 24 to 27, with the second at Hagley Oval in Christchurch from October 31 to November 3.The third and final match will go ahead at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval in Lincoln from November 7 to 10. India A have named a strong squad for the series, with Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan, KL Rahul, Akash Deep and Washington Sundar among the squad. Rishabh Pant was also named in the team, but a left side strain ruled him out of the first two Tests.New Zealand A squads for four-day matches against India A1st Match: Rhys Mariu (C), Matt Boyle, Max Chu, Kristian Clarke, Dean Foxcroft, Zak Gibson, Mitch Hay (WK), Curtis Heaphy, Simon Keene, Jayden Lennox, Jarrod McKay, Tim Robinson, Fraser Sheat.2nd Match: Rhys Mariu (C), Matt Boyle, Kristian Clarke, Matt Fisher, Dean Foxcroft, Zak Gibson, Mitch Hay (WK), Curtis Heaphy, Simon Keene, Jayden Lennox, Jarrod McKay, Tim Robinson, Fraser Sheat.3rd Match: Adi Ashok, Matt Boyle, Max Chu (WK), Dean Foxcroft, Curtis Heaphy, Simon Keene, Nick Kelly, Ben Lister, Rhys Mariu, Jarrod McKay, Cam Paul, Henry Nicholls, Fraser Sheat.

title: ‘Deprived of democracy’: Wangchuk slams Centre over cancellation of Ladakh talks | Hindustan Times
description: He said Ladakh’s leaders were considering taking their case to the United Nations and renewed calls for constitutional safeguards and elected governance.
content: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Thursday accused the Centre of keeping Ladakh “deprived of democracy” and treating it as a “controversial area” by retaining its status as a Union Territory without a legislature.The remarks came after a Union home ministry meeting with Ladakh leaders, scheduled for Thursday in New Delhi, did not take place. Wangchuk said the cancellation, without an explanation, had prompted the region’s leadership to consider taking its case to the United Nations.“We were told with complete determination that we will meet in Delhi on the 22nd of October,” Wangchuk told the media in New Delhi. “We made our plans and bought our tickets. Today I am here, and the meeting is not happening. The country should know how the hopes of Ladakh have been ruined again and again.”This was supposed to be the seventh round of talks between the Centre and the leaders of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA).At the last meeting in Leh on October 15, the ministry of home affairs had reportedly fixed October 22 as the next date for holding talks in Delhi. The October 15 meeting had remained inconclusive and was dubbed “disappointing” by the LAB and KDA leaders.Also Read | Ladakh administration defends in HC cancellation of land allotment to Wangchuk’s institute“On one hand, China has staked its claim over Ladakh and refuses to accept any changes being made in the region and on the other, our own country keeps betraying the people of Ladakh again and again,” Wangchuk said.He recalled how the BJP had promised constitutional safeguards under the Sixth Schedule and a democratically elected government since 2019 but has not delivered on its promise.“When the people raised their voice and resorted to peaceful protests, they were subjected to brutalities….lives were lost, several others were injured, and many of us were jailed,” he said, referring to September 24 unrest last year that left four civilians, including a retired soldier, dead, more than 80 injured and over 85 arrested.He said that the progress made at the May 22 meeting, when both sides had agreed in principle, had been squandered away at the October 15 meeting.“The hopes of the people of Ladakh are being shattered repeatedly. At the October 15 meeting, the sub-committee of the MHA had squarely backtracked on its words and had suggested an agency, much lower than the existing hill development councils,” he said.Also Read | Sonam Wangchuk backs CJP stir in Delhi, but says he can't attend: 'Hope we won't let Bapu down'Wangchuk also reiterated that the lieutenant governor VK Saxena should refrain from taking big decisions till an elected governance model was put in place.“Now Panchayat polls are going to be held but without any consultation with the people. Therefore, I say that Ladakh has become a black spot in the name of Indian democracy as people there have no democratic rights,” he said.Wangchuk said the LAB and KDA were mulling approaching the United Nations over the declaration on the rights of indigenous peoples, to which India was a signatory in 2007.Also Read | Sonam Wangchuk Drops 24-Hour Ultimatum Video, Threatens Hunger Strike Amid Delhi Detentions“Since Ladakh majorly comprises indigenous people, the UN’s declaration on the rights of indigenous peoples gives rights to the indigenous people of Ladakh to decide their future and rights. We are mulling to take the issue to the UN as well, and we appeal to all the citizens of India to support the people of Ladakh,” he said.

title: Farm fires cross last year’s tally, Punjab's Tarn Taran accounts for half of 454 cases | Hindustan Times
description: The annual farm fire monitoring period begins on September 15, two weeks before paddy procurement starts on October 1.
content: Punjab recorded 50 fresh stubble burning incidents taking the cumulative tally to 454 as of October 21, surpassing the 415 cases reported during the corresponding period last year, according to data from the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB). The state recorded 5,114 farm fires during the entire paddy harvesting season last year.The annual farm fire monitoring period begins on September 15, two weeks before paddy procurement starts on October 1.Stubble burning deteriorates air qualityTarn Taran has emerged as the worst-affected district, accounting for 218 of the 454 incidents, nearly half of the state’s total. Amritsar followed with 125 cases, while Gurdaspur and Ferozepur reported 28 and 23 incidents, respectively.Most fires have been reported from districts where early-maturing paddy varieties were cultivated. Harvesting has only recently begun in several other areas. According to the PPCB data, 83% of the paddy crop has already been harvested in Amritsar and 73% in Tarn Taran. Stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana is among the factors contributing to the seasonal deterioration in air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR), particularly during October and November. With a narrow window between paddy harvesting and wheat sowing, farmers often burn crop residue to clear their fields quickly for the next crop.Agriculture experts expect farm fires to peak in the first week of November as farmers race to complete harvesting and prepare their fields for wheat sowing before the November 15 deadline. Timely sowing is also considered important for achieving optimum wheat yields.Authorities monitor farmer's activityPunjab cultivates paddy across approximately 31 lakh hectares, generating nearly 19.5 million tonnes of straw annually. Harvesting generally begins in mid-September and continues until the end of November. Unlike wheat straw, paddy residue has limited traditional uses on farms, making its management challenging within the short interval between the two crops.State nodal officer at the PPCB Rajeev Gupta said enforcement teams were working round the clock to curb the practice. “Our teams are on the ground working 24x7. We urge farmers to adopt in-situ or ex-situ management of stubble instead of burning it,” he said.Farmer unions, however, argue that most farmers in Punjab are marginal or small landholders who cannot afford the machinery required for stubble management.Also Read I How Punjab cop in anti-drone unit helped smugglers clear 24 drug deliveriesGeneral secretary of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (Dakunda) Jagmohan Singh said managing stubble cost small farmers between ₹3,000 and ₹3,500 per acre, making the process financially unviable for many. “The government should provide an incentive of ₹100 per quintal of paddy to help farmers manage the straw. Those who continue burning stubble despite receiving the incentive should be punished,” he said.Rising farm fires have coincided with deteriorating air quality across the state. Jalandhar’s air quality index (AQI) climbed to 198 on Wednesday from 130 on Sunday. Mandi Gobindgarh recorded an AQI of 177, while Bathinda’s AQI rose to 142 on October 21, according to the PPCB monitoring dashboard. ₹8-lakh fine imposed, 62 FIRs registered across stateEnforcement against stubble burning has been stepped up, although violations continue across several districts.According to a Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) report, environmental compensation totalling ₹8.3 lakh has been imposed in 164 cases, of which ₹4.38 lakh has been recovered. Authorities have registered 62 FIRs under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and made red entries in land records in 130 cases. Such entries restrict farmers’ ability to secure loans against, sell or mortgage their land.Field teams inspected 401 locations, with physical verification confirming crop burning at 168 sites. Burning traces were also detected in two fields classified as non-accidental fire (non-AFL) cases.In Tarn Taran, 28 FIRs have been registered and environmental compensation of ₹4.3 lakh has been imposed in 84 cases, recovering ₹1.8 lakh, while red entries were made in 84 cases. In Amritsar, authorities registered 11 FIRs, imposed ₹2.3 lakh in compensation and recovered ₹2.08 lakh. Red entries were made in 28 cases. The report also noted 193 warning or show-cause notices issued to nodal and supervisory officers.

title: Power restored in many parts of Gurugram after strike over private licence triggered blackouts | Hindustan Times
description: Several residents, however, complained that despite the restoration, the supply was suffering from severe low voltage, leaving them unable to operate household appliances or run water pumps.
content: Power supply has been restored to many parts of Gurugram following widespread blackouts triggered by a strike by state power department employees against a regulatory order granting a 25-year parallel distribution licence to a private firm in Gurugram and Nuh, district officials said on Friday.Several residents, however, complained that despite the restoration, the supply was suffering from severe low voltage, leaving them unable to operate household appliances or run water pumps.Power grid workers and engineers have been on a 72-hour strike starting 10 pm Wednesday to protest an order by the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) granting a 25-year parallel distribution license to a private firm, Eleven Power Private Limited, in Gurugram and Nuh.The city saw blackouts lasting nearly 24 hours after striking workers of the Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) shut down feeders or refused to repair routine line faults.In Sector 10’s Hari Nagar, angry residents went to the residence of Haryana minister Rao Narbir Singh around 9:30 pm on Thursday after DHBVN officials stopped answering phones, said local resident Anita Yadav.The minister wasn’t home. “We vented our ire and asked his aides to intervene to get the power supply restored in our area,” she said.Sumit Pradhan, president of the Hari Nagar Residents’ Welfare Association, said power was restored within 30 minutes of residents raising the issue at the minister’s residence. “Not a single drop of water was available in our homes, forcing people to buy packaged drinking water,” he said.Dinesh Vashist, former president of Sector-3, 5 and 6 resident welfare associations, said power supply in their area was restored after midnight, 26 hours after the outage. Officials said the power disruption was due to a fault in a main high-tension feeder cable supplying power from substation in Palam Vihar which wasn’t repaired till late evening.In some areas of old Gurugram, DHBVN employees restored power supply after the police approached them and warned that they could face legal action if the protests by residents who had blocked roads at two locations against the outage turned violent.Four major power unions including the Haryana Power Engineers Association and the All Haryana Power Corporation Workers Union called the strike against the regulator’s decision in Gurugram, alleging that parallel licensing was a back-door step toward privatisation that would threaten public sector jobs.Chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and energy minister Anil Vij said the state government had no role in the regulator’s decision and would appeal the HERC order to the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity within a week. At a review meeting, Saini said the government was ready to engage lawyers trusted by the power unions to pursue the case and reiterated that the government’s doors are always open for dialogue.Eleven Power, chaired by Sunil Sachdeva, is the first private player granted a parallel power distribution licence in Haryana. The firm plans to invest ₹4,716 crore over five years to build a parallel network, allowing over 8.3 lakh consumers to choose between the private firm and state-run DHBVN.

title: Punjab cop in anti-drone unit helped smugglers clear 24 drug deliveries, arrested by NCB | Hindustan Times
description: Investigators allege the constable used his knowledge of anti-drone deployments to guide smugglers towards safe drop zones for cross-border deliveries.
content: Karandeep Singh, the Punjab Police constable arrested on October 15 by the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) for colluding with drug traffickers, has allegedly told interrogators that he has collected over two dozen consignments of drugs sent from across the Pakistan border since June this year.An NCB officer, who asked not to be named, said Karandeep, who was posted with the force’s anti-drone unit mandated to intercept drugs and weapons smuggled across the Indo-Pak fence, used his operational knowledge of anti-drone deployments in Tarn Taran district to guide smugglers to safe drop zones.Also read: How many drug peddlers released by police, SAD (PS) questions CMPolice tips and arms licence allegedly helped maintain his coverOn two occasions, he did pass on tips to the police that led to drug seizures. Karandeep also applied for, and received, an arms licence for a personal weapon, claiming a threat to his life for helping police bust drug-related cases. An NCB officer said this was designed to to preserve his standing within the police force while he facilitated the trafficking operation.Karandeep was intercepted by the Border Security Force (BSF) in Tarn Taran on October 15 while he was smuggling 15kg of high-grade heroin. The NCB took over the case.The officer said Karandeep had been taking deliveries of drug consignments sent across the border in June. Since August, he also started helping his handlers with safe drop-zone locations. “Based on his communications with Pakistan handlers and the drop zones he sent them for safe delivery, investigators could confirm at least 24 deliveries,” the officer said. The China-made drones used by traffickers can carry payloads of anywhere between 5-15 kg of heroin.Karandeep told his interrogators that he had been a heroin addict, a vulnerability that the trafficking networks exploited to turn him.Also read: Hooked at 9, 12: Video of Kapurthala brothers leads to drug peddler’s arrestEncrypted calls allegedly drew constable into smuggling network“Earlier this year, people contacted him via encrypted calls from Pakistan and lured him into smuggling heroin, for which he received his share of drugs and money. He claimed he did not know how the Pak smugglers knew he was a user and lured him. Pakistani smugglers target such vulnerable people, including villagers. He is still being questioned,” a second officer said.On Tuesday, the local Punjab media reported the arrest of Karandeep’s associate, Lakwinder Singh, a former sarpanch of Rajoke village, a border village, in Tarn Taran. Lakwinder Singh is also in NCB custody.A BSF officer, who asked not to be named, said the force had had Lakwinder on its radar for a long time. Local BSF units had searched his house several times but found no evidence.“He had come under the radar because forensic analysis of a few recovered drones showed their flight paths near or above Lakwinder Singh’s house many times. This meant the drugs, which are always tied to the drone using a hook, were dropped at or near his house. But he always feigned ignorance and BSF teams did not recover anything during searches,” the officer said.Also read: Kejriwal questions Amit Shah over drug menace in BJP-ruled statesRajoke remains a cross-border smuggling hotspotRajoke has been a hotspot of cross-border smuggling in the district.At least 11 drones have been shot down here since 2023, but the instances have declined since 2025. Only one drone was busted from Rajoke this year, in April. Local BSF officers believed at the time that this route was no longer in use.“With the Punjab cop’s and the sarpanch’s arrest, it is clear that the cases had not decreased. They had only become smarter,” he added.Also read: Punjab Police has delivered a decisive blow to drugs: DGPDrug enforcement agencies registered 305 drone-related seizure cases across India in 2025, recovering 468 kg of narcotics. Punjab alone accounted for 298 of those cases and 461 kg of seized drugs, primarily heroin.On September 26, the Punjab police also arrested an inspector posted in the counter-intelligence unit on charges of smuggling 3.35 kg of heroin, 6 pistols and 6 cell phones.

title: శుక్ర ప్రదోష కథ: వ్రత మహిమ ఇదే.. దాంపత్య సమస్యలు తొలగి సుఖసంతోషాలు కలుగుతాయట! | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: హిందూ సంప్రదాయంలో శుక్ర ప్రదోష వ్రతానికి ఎంతో విశిష్టత ఉంది. శుక్రవారం వచ్చే త్రయోదశి తిథిన పరమశివుడిని ప్రదోష కాలంలో పూజించడం వల్ల పాపాలు తొలగి, సుఖసంతోషాలు కలుగుతాయని భక్తుల విశ్వాసం
content: హిందూ సంప్రదాయంలో ప్రదోష వ్రతానికి విశేషమైన ప్రాధాన్యత ఉంది. ప్రతి నెలా వచ్చే శుక్ల, కృష్ణ పక్షాల త్రయోదశి తిథిన ఈ వ్రతం ఆచరిస్తారు. ముఖ్యంగా శుక్రవారం నాడు వచ్చే త్రయోదశిని 'శుక్ర ప్రదోష వ్రతం' అంటారు. ఈ పవిత్ర దినాన లయకారకుడైన పరమశివుడిని భక్తిశ్రద్ధలతో కొలిస్తే సమస్త పాపాలు తొలగిపోతాయని, జీవితంలో సుఖసంతోషాలు వెల్లివిరుస్తాయని భక్తుల విశ్వాసం.సూర్యాస్తమయ వేళ, అనగా సంధ్యా సమయంలో (ప్రదోష కాలం) శివుడుని పూజించడం ఈ వ్రతంలో అత్యంత ముఖ్యం. శివాలయాలను దర్శించి, అభిషేకాలు చేయడం, ప్రదోష వ్రత కథను పఠించడం ద్వారా సంపూర్ణ ఫలితం దక్కుతుంది.శుక్ర ప్రదోష వ్రత పౌరాణిక కథపురాణాల ప్రకారం, పూర్వం ఒక నగరంలో ముగ్గురు ప్రాణ స్నేహితులు ఉండేవాళ్లు. ఒకరు రాజకుమారుడు, మరొకరు బ్రాహ్మణ కుమారుడు, మూడోవాడు ధనికుడి (శ్రేష్ఠి) కుమారుడు. వీరిలో రాజకుమారుడు, బ్రాహ్మణ కుమారునికి వివాహాలు జరిగాయిగానీ, భార్యలను అత్తగారింటి నుంచి ఇంటికి తీసుకువచ్చే కార్యక్రమం జరగాల్సి ఉంది.ఒకరోజు ముగ్గురు మిత్రులు సంభాషించుకుంటుండగా, బ్రాహ్మణ పుత్రుడు నారీల ప్రాముఖ్యాన్ని వివరిస్తాడు. ఈ మాటలకు ప్రభావితుడైన ధనిక కుమారుడు వెంటనే తన భార్యను ఇంటికి తీసుకురావాలని నిర్ణయించుకుంటాడు. ఈ విషయాన్ని తల్లిదండ్రులకు తెలపగా, "శుక్రాస్త సమయంలో వెళ్ళరాదు," అని తల్లిదండ్రులు హెచ్చరించారు. "ఈ సమయంలో పంపడం శుభం కాదు అని అన్నారు.అయితే ధనిక పుత్రుడు ఎవరి మాట వినకుండా అత్తగారింటికి బయలుదేరుతాడు. అత్తగారింట కూడా అందరూ వారిని ఆపే ప్రయత్నం చేసినా పట్టు వీడడు. చివరికి కుటుంబ సభ్యులు విధిలేక ఆమెను పంపుతారు.మార్గమధ్యంలో ఎదురైన విపత్తులునగరం దాటిన వెంటనే వారి బండి చక్రం ఊడిపోతుంది, ఎద్దు కాలు విరిగిపోతుంది. ఇద్దరికీ తీవ్ర గాయాలైనా ప్రయాణం కొనసాగిస్తారు. కొంతదూరం వెళ్లగానే దొంగలు వారికున్న ధనధాన్యాలన్నీ దోచుకుపోతారు. చివరకు భార్యాభర్తలు రోధిస్తూ ఇంటికి చేరుకుంటారు. ఇంటికి రాగానే ఆ ధనిక పుమారుడిని విషసర్పం కాటేస్తుంది. వైద్యుడు పరిశీలించి అతడు మూడు రోజుల్లో మరణిస్తాడని ప్రకటిస్తాడు.ఈ దుర్వార్త తెలుసుకున్న బ్రాహ్మణ కుమారుడు వెంటనే వచ్చి, "మీ కొడుకు శుక్రాస్త సమయంలో భార్యను తీసుకు రావడం వల్లే ఈ ఆపదలు వచ్చాయి. వెంటనే అతడిని భార్యతో సహా అత్తగారింటికి తిరిగి పంపండి," అని సలహా ఇస్తాడు.ధనిక కుమారుడి కుటుంబం ఆ సలహాను పాటిస్తూ కొడుకును, కోడలిని తిరిగి పంపిస్తుంది. అత్తగారింటికి చేరగానే ధనిక పుమారుడి ఆరోగ్యం కుదుటపడుతుంది. శుక్ర ప్రదోష వ్రత మహిమ వల్ల సమస్త కష్టాలు తొలగిపోతాయి. ఆ దంపతులు శేష జీవితాన్ని ఆనందంగా గడిపి, అంత్యమున శివలోకం చేరుకుంటారు.వ్రత ఆచరణ - ప్రయోజనాలుశుక్ర ప్రదోష వ్రతం ఆచరించడం వల్ల దాంపత్య జీవితంలో సమస్యలు తొలగిపోతాయి. జీవితంలో కలుగుతున్న ప్రతికూలతలు నశించి, అనుకున్న రంగంలో విజయం సాధిస్తారని భక్తుల ప్రగాఢ విశ్వాసం.

title: Aamir Khan breaks down in tears talking about career's weakest moments, says he lost relationships, time with kids by working like a ‘madman’ | Bollywood
description: Aamir Khan opened up on the weakest moments of his career in a chat about his life and work at the Singapore International Film Festival.  | Bollywood
content: Actor Aamir Khan was reduced to tears on stage at the Singapore International Film Festival on Thursday as he recalled the weakest moments of his acting career. The actor spoke about how three decades of nonstop work had cost him years with his family.Aamir Khan breaks down talking about careerOn Thursday, at the Singapore film festival, the Bollywood superstar was awarded the Screen Icon Award by renowned Hong Kong-based film director Peter Chan Ho-sun. Later in the evening, Aamir sat down for a chat about his life and work in a conversation session moderated by Singapore comedian Rishi Budhrani.When asked about the weakest moment in his career, Aamir responded, “When I was sitting in COVID, and I was thinking, I said, about 30 years have passed of my life. And it’s okay to work like a madman, completely obsessed with what you’re doing for one year, two years, five years. But if it goes on for 30 years, I mean, you’ve lost your relationships. Your kids have grown up; they’re adults now. So I felt a deep sense of loss.”Aamir then paused while speaking and broke down in tears. The actor then apologised to the audience before gathering himself as the crowd broke into applause. Wiping his tears away, Aamir added that the experience pushed him to make a major change, and that for the last four years he has deliberately carved out time for his family and close friends. “I’m so glad that this thought occurred to me when I was 56 and not when I was 86, when it would be really too late to do anything about it,” he added. Aamir recalls early flopsIn the same answer about his weakest moments, Aamir Khan recounted an earlier low point from the start of his career. After his 1988 debut Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak was a huge success, Aamir recalled signing nine films within six months. However, he realised his mistake once filming began. Aamir said he would come home and weep to his then-wife Reena. The films then flopped one after another, and he was branded a “one-film wonder.”“At that time, mentally and emotionally, I felt like I was in quicksand. I was sinking slowly, and the more I struggled to get out, the deeper I was going,” Aamir added.Aamir Khan at the Singapore International Film FestivalAccepting the Screen Icon Award, Aamir Khan thanked the festival and said that having Chan present it made the moment special. “Filmmaking is a collective art form, and a lot of people contribute to each other’s work,” he said. Aamir last attended the festival nine years ago with his production Secret Superstar. This year, he also has a 25th anniversary screening of Lagaan, his first film as producer, lined up at the festival.

title: Jamia students hold general body meeting, demand restoration of students' union | Education
description: The development comes a day after JMI admin constituted a committee to draft the JMISU constitution and to review disciplinary action.   | Education News
content: Jamia Millia Islamia students held a general body meeting on Thursday at the university's Ghalib lawn, with hundreds participating, to demand the restoration of the students' union, dissolved in 2006, according to a statement from student organisations.The United Students of Jamia, a newly formed body, said several student organisations and students called the meeting to support the ongoing hunger strike and sit-in protest on campus, mounting pressure on the administration to announce the date for student elections.Amit Shah to attend DU's 103rd convocation on November 20The student organisations said the large turnout reflected support for continuing the struggle for the union and that the meeting would take up resolutions on its proposed structure and functioning.The development comes a day after Jamia's administration constituted a committee to draft the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union (JMISU) constitution and to review disciplinary action taken or initiated against protesting students.Rethinking the MBA: Why domain expertise and practical learning matter more than everIn an email to university officials on Thursday, Dean of Students' Welfare Neelofer Afzal said the administration took these two steps after interactions between the vice-chancellor-constituted high-level committee and the protesting students.However, the students had not agreed to the proposed resolution and normalcy had not been restored on campus, she said. Citing the continuing protest and concerns over the safety and well-being of students and visitors, the university has cancelled its annual "Talimi Mela 2026", scheduled from October 29 to November 1.IBPS SO Mains Admit Card 2026 released at ibps.in, download link hereStudents have been protesting since October 12, demanding notice of the JMISU election schedule for the 2026-27 academic session.The United Students of Jamia, a collective comprising AIDSO, AIRSO, AISA, DISHA, DISSC, Fraternity Movement, MSF, SFI, and SIO, issued the press release.

title: 300km of ageing BEST underground power cable network to be replaced after Bhuleshwar fire | Mumbai news
description: According to BEST officials, several sections of the underground network are 70 to 80 years old, with some cables even dating back to pre-independence.  | Mumbai news
content: On Thursday, a fire triggered by a suspected short circuit in Mumbai's Bhuleshwar once again swung the spotlight on the ageing underground power cable network of the Brihanmumbai Electricity Supply and Transport (BEST). A substantial 300 km of the network is in need of replacement, and the process for this has begun.According to BEST officials, several sections of the underground network are 70 to 80 years old, with some cables even dating back to pre-independence. “Following power outages, temporary connections are often provided, increasing the load on existing lines,” said a senior official from BEST. “This can cause old cables to overheat and catch fire. This could also have been a factor in the Bhuleshwar blaze.” Replacement programme likely to take 2-3 yearsThe officials added that damaged sections of old cables were sometimes temporarily repaired by wrapping them with insulating tape. However, excessive heat, the weather, and the electrical load can cause the insulation and cables to deteriorate further, increasing the risk of short circuits and fires. BEST has now initiated a tender process to replace the 300km of underground electricity cables at an estimated cost of ₹200 crore.“The tender is expected to be awarded shortly, with work likely to begin by December or early January 2027,” said another official. “The replacement programme is expected to take around two to three years to complete, with the entire network upgrade targeted for 2029. This is crucial to prevent power supply failures and short circuits owing to overloaded cables.”The BEST authorities stated often temporary cables were connected to the power lines, exacerbating the problem. In several instances, engineers have restored supply by diverting power through alternate cable networks, a temporary measure that can increase the load on otherwise functional cables while leaving the original faults unresolved.BEST has identified nearly 1,200 urgent cable fault locations across South and Central Mumbai, impacting municipal wards that serve around 1.05 million electricity consumers across areas like Marine Lines, Girgaon, Wadala, Dadar, and Zaveri Bazaar. Repairing these sites requires digging three- to five-metre patches at each location to replace temporary wiring used during past repairs. The entire project will take approximately one year to finish.Also Read I ‘This is shocking’: Bombay HC says Mumbai pollution surpassing Delhi, pulls up authoritiesThis effort may require fresh road excavations, including in Bhuleshwar and nearby areas where the BMC recently completed cement-concretization. Because BMC permission to dig up concrete roads is difficult to obtain, many cable faults have remained unresolved; BEST plans to compensate the civic body at an estimated rate of ₹10,000 per metre.Currently, BEST faces over 2,500 unresolved technical and cable fault complaints. The crisis is most severe in South Mumbai’s A, B, C, D, and E wards, where a single fuse control room serves 350,000 consumers. So far this year, BEST has received roughly 7,500 power complaints—up by nearly 1,000 from 2024. To address these challenges, BEST approved recruiting 690 workers to fix faults exacerbated by heatwaves and monsoon waterlogging.

title: Badlapur IVF racket: ED seizes  ₹29 lakh cash, freezes bank lockers, mutual funds | Mumbai news
description: The ED is probing suspected money laundering, seizing  ₹29 lakh and identifying properties and investments potentially linked to the alleged proceeds.  | Mumbai news
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has seized cash worth ₹29 lakh and frozen several bank lockers and mutual fund (MF) investments during searches conducted on Friday as part of its money-laundering investigation linked to the Badlapur human egg trafficking racket.The searches also led to the recovery of incriminating documents and digital devices containing details relevant to the case, according to officials aware of the developments. The agency has identified more agents involved in supplying egg donors, and their roles in the racket are now being examined, officials said.The investigation is based on a case registered by the Thane police against a syndicate allegedly involved in a major illegal fertility scam in Badlapur.Also Read | Supreme Court calls for setting human trafficking apart from voluntary sex workThe syndicate allegedly lured financially vulnerable women towards egg donation, offering them ₹25,000 to ₹30,000 per cycle. It then repeatedly subjected the women to hazardous, unsupervised egg extractions to sell to in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) centres and assisted reproductive technology (ART) banks through agents, who received commissions.The ED is examining the financial transactions linked to the alleged racket. According to officials, Friday’s searches led to the identification of a few immovable properties and investments, involving substantial amounts, which are suspected to be linked to the proceeds of crime in the case. The searches were conducted at 10 premises, including hospitals and IVF centres in Thane, Baramati and Nashik, under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The investigation has revealed the use of forged documents, including Aadhaar cards, PAN cards, affidavits, consent letters, birth certificates, blood test reports, and insurance papers, to conceal donors’ identities, facilitate repeat egg donations, and falsely establish their medical fitness, officials said.“Thereafter, the women were sent to various establishments in Maharashtra and other states for human egg retrieval, thereby exposing them to potential medical risks and circumventing prescribed medical safeguards,” said an ED official, requesting anonymity.Also Read | Child trafficking racket busted in Delhi, 4-day-old infant rescuedThe racket was uncovered on February 19, 2026, when police found that an IVF centre registered in Nashik was allegedly operating an unauthorised facility in Thane without the required licences and approvals. According to investigators, women were allegedly paid between ₹25,000 and ₹30,000 per cycle and recruited repeatedly as egg donors, despite restrictions on repeated donations.The Thane police’s charge sheet in the case names 17 accused, charged with cheating and forgery under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with violations of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act and the Drugs and Cosmetics Act.

title: POCSO survivor cannot be denied compensation solely due to absence of injury marks: Allahabad HC | Hindustan Times
description: POCSO survivor cannot be denied compensation solely due to absence of injury marks: Allahabad HC
content: Lucknow, The Allahabad High Court has ruled that a survivor of sexual assault under the POCSO Act cannot be denied compensation merely because the medical report does not record physical injuries.In the order issued Thursday, a division bench of Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice Amitabh Kumar Rai directed authorities to pay ₹3 lakh to a minor under the Uttar Pradesh Rani Lakshmi Bai Mahila Samman Kosh scheme within 10 days of the production of a certified copy of the order.The court held that the district steering committee's decision to withhold compensation was contrary to law and the provisions of the scheme.Under the scheme, survivors of sexual assault under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act are entitled to compensation of ₹3 lakh. Of this, ₹1 lakh is payable within 15 days of the FIR, while the remaining ₹2 lakh must be paid within a month of the chargesheet being filed.The case relates to an FIR registered at Sarojini Nagar police station in Lucknow on December 7, 2022. A chargesheet in this connection was filed on January 13, 2023.The district committee had withheld compensation citing the absence of medical evidence supporting penetrative sexual assault. The state counsel defended the decision, arguing that the medical report did not record injuries indicating penetration.Rejecting the argument, the high court observed that physical injury is not a necessary condition for establishing penetrative sexual assault under Section 3 of the POCSO Act.The bench held that absence of injury marks cannot, by itself, negate an allegation of sexual assault. Once the FIR and chargesheet indicate an offence under Section 4 of the Act, compensation cannot be denied solely because the medical report does not record injuries.Describing the scheme as a beneficial measure intended to alleviate the trauma and suffering of victims, the court said its provisions must be interpreted liberally.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.
