A civil suit concerning ownership of the property is pending before a competent court.The bench observed that electricity was essential for lighting, water supply, cooking, education, healthcare and livelihood, making access to power an integral part of a dignified life.Setting aside the rejection order as illegal and arbitrary, the court remanded the matter to the executive engineer concerned for fresh consideration.It directed the officer to decide the application in accordance with the law within 10 days of receiving a certified copy of the order. If approved, the electricity connection must be provided immediately, the court said.

title: Bijnor farmer shot dead, body found on tractor | Hindustan Times
description: The motive behind the murder remains unclear, and police teams are investigating the case to identify and arrest the suspects
content: A 50-year-old farmer was shot dead by unidentified assailants in Bijnor’s Chandpur police station area. His blood-soaked body was found slumped over the driver’s seat of his tractor late on Wednesday night, approximately 2.5 km away from his village, said police on Thursday.The motive behind the murder remains unclear, and police teams are investigating the case to identify and arrest the suspects, said Chandpur station house officer (SHO) Sudhir Panwar.The deceased has been identified as Vijaypal Singh, a resident of Kelanpur village. The family had suffered another tragedy just three months ago, when Singh’s younger son died in a road accident. His elder son, Mohit Kumar, 25, is serving with the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) and is currently posted in Lucknow.According to family members, Singh left home at 4 pm on Wednesday to plough his fields. When he failed to return by 7 pm, his wife, Geeta, called him several times, but he did not answer. Relatives and villagers launched a search, eventually finding his tractor on the Kelanpur-Rampur Nazrana link road between midnight and 1 am. Singh was found dead on the tractor seat with multiple gunshot wounds, triggering fear and tension in the area.Investigators said the attackers fired three rounds, two of which hit Singh in the chest and abdomen. A third bullet was found near the tractor. Upon receiving information, local police along with a specialised forensic field unit rushed to the spot to secure the crime scene andKelanpur village pradhan Chaudhary Sanjiv said police were informed immediately after the body was found. The family will file a written complaint once Singh’s elder son arrives from his posting in Lucknow.Chandpur station house officer (SHO) Sudhir Panwar said the body was sent for post-mortem around 5 am on Thursday after completion of inquest proceedings. He said the motive behind the murder was yet to be established and police teams were probing all possible angles to identify and arrest the accused.

title: SHO, investigating SI suspended after high court flags illegal detention | Hindustan Times
description: The matter came to light after the accused’s mother approached the High Court, alleging that her son had been illegally detained at the police station for six days.
content: The Deoria Superintendent of Police, Abhijeet R Shankar, on Wednesday night suspended Salempur police station SHO Vinod Kumar Singh and investigating sub-inspector Deep Narayan after the Allahabad High Court took a serious view of the alleged illegal detention of a man at the police station for six days.The High Court has directed the investigating officer to appear before it on October 23 along with the CCTV footage and relevant records in the case.According to officials, the matter concerns allegations that the man was kept at Salempur police station from August 28 to September 2 following a complaint by a young woman who accused him of establishing physical relations with her on the promise of marriage. Police subsequently registered a case in connection with the allegations.The matter came to light after the accused’s mother approached the High Court, alleging that her son had been illegally detained at the police station for six days.During an inquiry initiated by the Deoria SP, CCTV footage reportedly showed the accused at different locations inside the police station during the period in question. The footage is understood to have played a key role in the action taken against the police personnel.The High Court subsequently directed the investigating officer to appear before it on October 23 with the CCTV footage and relevant records.Deoria SP Abhijeet R Shankar confirmed the suspension of SHO Vinod Kumar Singh and SI Deep Narayan. He said Rahul Singh had been appointed the new in-charge of Salempur police station. HTC

title: 16 arrested in Lucknow gambling den raid,  ₹1.27 lakh cash seized | Hindustan Times
description: An FIR has been registered under Sections 3 and 4 of the Public Gambling Act at Bazaar Khala police station.
content: The Bazaar Khala police arrested 16 men during a raid at a house in Nand Kheda Mill Area, where gambling was allegedly on, and seized ₹1,27,150 in cash, officials said on Thursday.Acting on a tip-off received during patrolling on October 21, a police team led by the assistant commissioner of police (Bazaar Khala) surrounded the house and conducted a raid. According to police, those present allegedly attempted to flee but were apprehended by the team.An FIR has been registered under Sections 3 and 4 of the Public Gambling Act at Bazaar Khala police station.Postal employee arrestedThe Sarojini Nagar police arrested a 24-year-old former branch postmaster, Raunak Shukla, on Thursday in connection with an alleged embezzlement of government and account holders’ money, police said. According to police, an FIR (case number 122/2025) was registered against Shukla under Section 316(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita following a complaint filed on April 4, 2025, by Harihar Nath Tripathi, assistant superintendent of post offices. Shukla had been absconding since the case was registered, and a non-bailable warrant had been issued against him by a court.Man loses money after offering lift to strangerA 55-year-old man allegedly lost some of the ₹1.35 lakh he was carrying after a stranger asked him for a lift on his motorcycle near Vijaypur traffic signal in Vibhuti Khand on Thursday, police said.According to police, Gomti Prasad, a resident of Rahim Nagar, was carrying the cash from the glass shop where he had worked for around 15 years to AU Small Finance Bank in Husadiya’s Patrakar Puram area. Around 1pm, a youth carrying a bag approached him and requested a lift. After getting on the motorcycle, the youth placed his bag across their thighs. Prasad became suspicious when the youth allegedly pressed the side where the cash was kept.The youth jumped off, causing Prasad to lose balance and fall. While Prasad collected the scattered cash with help from workers and a street vendor, the youth allegedly fled with some money. Police are gathering details for further action.

title: College staff not criminally liable for Murud beach drowning: HC | Mumbai news
description: A single-judge bench of justice Milind Jadhav said that third-year college students are mature and possess a reasonable degree of life experience  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: Ten years after 14 third-year students of a Pune college drowned at Murud beach, the Bombay High Court on Thursday quashed criminal proceedings against 17 people, including the institute’s chairman, principal, teachers and non-teaching staff, ruling that they cannot be held “criminally negligent for an unforeseeable event occurring beyond their direct control or operational purview”.A single-judge bench of justice Milind Jadhav said that third-year college students are mature and possess a reasonable degree of life experience. They are expected to understand the distinction between right and wrong and to appreciate the likely consequences of their actions, it added.The court also said that if vicarious liability can be foisted on the institute’s trustees, teaching and non-teaching staff members, similar liability can be imposed on state authorities, which are responsible for ensuring that all public beaches have adequate signage, warnings, and beach safety and rescue measures.The incident occurred on February 1, 2016, when 116 students, faculty, and staff members of the Abeda Inamdar Senior College of Arts, Science and Commerce in Pune went for a picnic to Murud beach in Raigad. In the afternoon, 41 third-year students entered the sea, and around 20 were swept away. Local residents managed to rescue six of them, but the remaining 14 drowned.On April 19, 2016, the Murud police registered an FIR against 17 people for causing death by negligence. Five office-bearers of the educational trust that runs the college, including chairman PA Inamdar, the principal, faculty members, and non-teaching staff accompanying the students, were among those booked.The 17 accused subsequently approached the high court, seeking to quash the criminal proceedings. They argued that there was no evidence to invoke the charge of causing death by negligence against the office bearers, teaching and non-teaching members of the college.Additional public prosecutor Rajeshree Newton opposed the petition, arguing that the accused were directly responsible for ensuring the students’ safety, and the death of the 14 students was a direct result of their negligence. Newton justified the registration of the FIR, stating that the accused ought to have taken precautionary measures, especially when a large number of students went to a spot where there were chances of life-threatening accidents.However, the court refused to accept Newton’s argument, saying that there was no evidence indicating negligence on the part of the staff members that could be said to have resulted in the drowning of the 14 students.The court noted that the third-year students had gone to the beach after lunch at a hotel while the two professors supervising them were resting. The students ventured into the sea, after which 20 of them were swept away by the sea current and 14 unfortunately lost their lives, it added.The bench also said that the mere occurrence of an accident resulting in death or the alleged absence of ordinary care does not by itself render them liable for an offence punishable under section 304A (causing death by negligence) of the Indian Penal Code.

title: RIP roads: Repaired after months, dug up on the morrow | Hindustan Times
description: An HT check finds fresh excavation in Dalibagh, Vibhuti Khand and near EWS apartments; officials blame lack of coordination among road-owning and utility agencies
content: Isn’t it a joy to see a road repaired or remetalled after it lay broken for months?But how often have you had that joy cut short with a government department digging it up right after repairs, to lay pipes or cables?This lack of co-ordination and communication between government departments, leaving damaged stretches behind, points - among other things - towards a wastage of public money.An HT ground check found freshly repaired roads damaged at multiple locations, including Dalibagh, Vibhuti Khand and near the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel EWS apartments. The excavation has undone recent roadwork, with some stretches remaining in poor condition for months. The problem has surfaced even as the state government has directed departments to repair pothole-ridden roads and restore damaged stretches after the monsoon.The recurring practice points to a planning gap: utility agencies often undertake digging after road-owning departments complete repairs, instead of coordinating their work schedules and laying essential lines beforehand.‘Repeated digging wastes public money’Social activist Vivek Sharma termed the situation a departmental failure and said agencies should coordinate before undertaking road repairs or construction.“If departments know that cables, pipelines or other utility lines need to be laid, they should complete the work before repairing the road. A common trench could accommodate these utilities and prevent repeated damage to the road surface,” Sharma said.He questioned why agencies waited until departments repaired roads before starting excavation, when they can complete their work while the roads await repairs.Coordination failure acknowledgedPublic Works Department (PWD) executive engineer for the Lucknow division Satendra Nath said that the department recovers restoration charges during the time any department or agency seeks an NOC. The recovered amount gets utilised for the repair of the road, said Satendra Nath.Another senior PWD official said utility agencies, including electricity distribution agencies and other service providers, often failed to share their plans in advance. Agencies generally apply for permission to dig roads and deposit the prescribed restoration charges, but late applications prevent road-owning departments from incorporating utility work into their repair schedules.Separate utility ducts plannedLucknow Development Authority secretary Sushil Pratap Singh said upcoming and proposed LDA schemes will provide separate ducts for utility lines to prevent agencies from repeatedly cutting into newly constructed main roads.He said the authority was adopting this approach in the Anant Nagar scheme and other projects under development.Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar said that the LMC collects road-cutting charges from agencies seeking permission to carry out work on roads under its jurisdiction. He added that the civic body is responsible for taking necessary action after the work is completed. If any stretch of road has been left neglected, the corporation will take appropriate action.

title: Mumbai gets its first paediatric heart transplant in a public hospital | Mumbai news
description: MUMBAI: In a couple of days, Tanmay Shinde, 17, will walk out of hospital with a second chance at life – thanks to his new heart  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: In a couple of days, Tanmay Shinde, 17, will walk out of hospital with a second chance at life – thanks to his new heart.Tanmay’s surgery – Mumbai’s first-ever paediatric heart transplant in a public charitable hospital – was performed at the Bai Jerbai Wadia Hospital for Children in Parel. While the hospital has been undertaking paediatric renal and liver transplants, this is its first heart transplant since it received its cardiac transplant licence in 2024.The son of a BEST bus conductor, Tanmay was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy and severe heart failure, a condition where the heart muscle is enlarged and weakens, reducing its ability to pump blood effectively. After being diagnosed in December 2015, he had reached a stage where regular medication offered no scope for improvement.Constant chest pain, breathlessness, and fatigue in the last 12 months had left Tanmay frustrated and agitated. Being in and out of hospital had also cost him a year in college. In December 2025, Tanmay’s heart took a turn and he was brought to Wadia Hospital in critical condition. Doctors said a heart transplant was the only way forward.The surgery was performed on October 6, by a team led by paediatric cardiac surgeon Dr Biswa Panda. While the donor heart was being retrieved and transported, the recipient team prepared Tanmay for surgery. The total time from when the donor’s heart stopped beating to when the transplanted heart began beating in Tanmay’s chest was around three hours. The teenager remained in the ICU for a week after the surgery.Wadia hospital has a dedicated paediatric cardiomyopathy and heart failure clinic, where more than 370 children are currently undergoing treatment for cardiac issues. Nineteen of these children are being considered for cardiac transplant. After Tanmay, the hospital has listed three more children, aged between 7 and 15, with the Zonal Transplant Coordination Center (ZTCC) for heart transplants.A major challenge in paediatric heart transplants is the shortage of suitable donor hearts. “Children with severe heart failure may remain on waiting lists because finding a heart that matches their size and medical requirements can be difficult,” said Dr Panda.Child donors are few as most children succumb due to infections, which make their hearts unfit for transplantation. “In case of paediatric patients with dilated hearts, their bodies have created space to fit an adult heart. However, we avoid the hearts of donors aged above 40 for children since hearts above that age are susceptible to coronary issues in a few years time. Also, the parents have to consent to such a transplantation,” said Dr Sumitra Venkatesh, paediatric cardiologist who manages the hospital’s cardiomyopathy and heart failure clinic,Tanmay received the heart of a 22-year-old brain dead donor, “Having seen how organ donation can benefit families, we have decided to donate my own organs and even urge my friends and relatives to do the same,” said the teenager’s mother, Sujata. “We are very thankful to the donor family. My son had become very agitated. However, since the transplant, he has changed completely. Now he is cheerful and has been chatting with the hospital staff,” she added.But the Shindes’ troubles are far from over. Tanmay’s 11-year-old brother Pranav has also been diagnosed with a genetic heart condition and is listed for a cardiac transplant by the Wadia hospital.Tanmay’s father Ashok earns a modest salary as a BEST bus conductor and the family, from Ghansoli in Navi Mumbai, could not afford the surgery. All expenses – pre-surgery tests, the actual organ transfer costs, and the surgery and post-surgery treatments – were paid for by the hospital and its network including crowdfunding, said Dr Panda. The bill – around ₹20 lakh.Dr Minnie Bodhanwala, CEO of the hospital, said, “We hope this surgery will encourage greater awareness of paediatric organ donation and inspire more families to come forward, giving children awaiting transplants a chance at a healthier future.”

title: HC restores 6-year-old’s RTE admission, rejects ‘rigid’ distance rule | Mumbai news
description: A single-judge bench of justice N J Jamadar observed that a “neighbourhood school” described under the Act cannot be construed in a “rigid and pedantic manner”  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: The Bombay High Court has set aside a state order denying a six-year-old underprivileged child admission to a private school under the Right to Education (RTE) Act quota on account of breaching the eligibility rules regarding the distance between home and school.In a ruling expected to have a bearing on school admissions under the RTE, a single-judge bench of justice N J Jamadar observed that a “neighbourhood school” described under the Act cannot be construed in a “rigid and pedantic manner”.The court directed Balmohan Vidyamandir (BV) in Dadar to admit the child to Class 1 within a week, saying that a very rigid view on area limits under the RTE would “impinge upon the constitutional right of free and compulsory education”.In a metropolis like Mumbai, the court said, the state “could not have applied the barometer of distance…with exactitude,” especially when the chances of the child securing admission in any other private unaided school had diminished. The distance criterion stipulated in the RTE rules needs to be applied with “requisite flexibility” depending on the area’s geographical realities, it added.The court was hearing a petition filed by Karuna Kamble, a 38-year-old resident of the BDD Chawl in Worli. Kamble had challenged a decision by the Deputy Director of Education (DDE), Mumbai Region, in August to cancel the admission granted to her six-year-old daughter at Balmohan Vidyamandir under the 25% RTE quota for children from economically weaker sections (EWS) because their home address was beyond the prescribed distance from the school.Kamble said that her daughter had secured admission in Balmohan Vidyamandir through the RTE quota in April after submitting all the necessary documents. However, the school later “blatantly and brazenly” refused to admit her daughter without a reason, she claimed, adding that other EWS children, too, had been denied admission similarly.When the matter was escalated to the DDE, the school claimed that Kamble’s home was beyond 1 km from the school, thereby breaching the distance rule under the RTE quota. The DDE agreed with the school’s decision, prompting Kamble to approach the high court for relief.In her petition, Kamble said that while two other children whose homes were between 1 km and 3 km from the school were admitted by Balmohan Vidyamandir, the DDE cancelled her daughter’s admission on the basis of an education inspector’s report stating that her home was 4 km from the school. She also submitted that the cancelled admission would mean her daughter would lose an academic year.The state argued that its decision was in line with the rules under the RTE Act. It also alleged that Kamble had misrepresented the distance between her home and the school and misled the authorities, and had deliberately chosen schools far from her home. Balmohan Vidyamandir’s counsel said that the high court had previously, in a series of decisions, upheld the area restriction for admission under the RTE.The court noted that the distance between Kamble’s home and the school was 4 km. However, it pointed out that according to the Maharashtra Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Rules, 2011, enacted to enforce the RTE Act in the state, a “neighbourhood school” should be located within 3 km “as far as possible”.Justice Jamadar said that rules framed by different states under the RTE laid down distance criteria based on population density, literacy levels, and the need for a school. “There is, thus, an element of flexibility in the concept of neighbourhood,” the judge said, adding that it cannot be defined “with clinical precision or mathematical exactitude”.“In an era of time-space compression, the distance ceases to be an absolute inhibiting factor. Time is said to be the greatest distance between two places. In a metropolis like Mumbai, the concept of distance becomes even more relative. A number of variables come into play. The means of transport and easy accessibility become critical,” the judge added.

title: Aligarh road rage: Audi runs over injured motorcyclist, man dies | Hindustan Times
description: The case was registered at Banna Devi police station, and teams have been formed to arrest the absconding driver
content: In a suspected case of road rage, a man riding a motorcycle was killed after an Audi car allegedly rammed the two-wheeler from behind and then ran over him while he lay injured on the road in Aligarh on Tuesday night. Another man riding the motorcycle was injured. Police have registered cases of murder and attempt to murder after a video of the incident went viral.The case was registered at Banna Devi police station, and teams have been formed to arrest the absconding driver. According to reports, the car is registered in the name of Devraj Singh, a former BJP district unit president in Aligarh, and the absconding driver is said to be his nephew.Aligarh SP (City) Aditya Bansal said on Thursday evening that the police station received information on Wednesday about the incident, which took place on Tuesday night.“According to the complaint, the occupants of an Audi car deliberately hit the motorcycle, leaving both riders injured. The motorcyclist, identified as Manoj Kumar, later died, while the other rider, Kanhaiya, was injured,” Bansal said.A case was registered under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Section 103 for murder and Section 109 for attempt to murder, he said.According to Bansal, the statement of Kanhaiya, an eyewitness and the injured survivor, was recorded. He told police that an altercation had taken place between the two parties over honking before the incident. The Audi driver allegedly rammed the moving motorcycle from behind and then drove over Manoj, who had fallen on the road.“The CCTV footage has been preserved, the car has been seized, and the field unit has collected evidence. A technical inspection of the vehicle has also been conducted,” Bansal said.He added that the Audi was registered in the name of Devraj Singh, a resident of Raghuveer Puri under Banna Devi police station limits. The driver has been identified as Singh’s nephew, and police teams are working to arrest him.Manoj Kumar, who was in his late thirties, worked as a sweetmeat seller. He was married and had three children.The video of the incident, which has gone viral, purportedly shows the Audi hitting the motorcycle from behind and then running over one of the injured men. Some people at the scene are also seen throwing stones at the car as it drives away in the darkness.

title: How many drug peddlers released by police, SAD (PS) questions CM | Hindustan Times
description: Reacting to Mann’s reported remarks describing the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act as weak, Chandumajra said the chief minister, who also held the home portfolio, must clarify his claim that accused persons could obtain bail at police stations
content: Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit) senior leader Prem Singh Chandumajra on Thursday questioned the Punjab government’s anti-drug campaign, asking chief minister Bhagwant Mann to disclose how many of the 1.27 lakh people reportedly arrested under the drive were released from police stations.Reacting to Mann’s reported remarks describing the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act as weak, Chandumajra said the chief minister, who also held the home portfolio, must clarify his claim that accused persons could obtain bail at police stations. He alleged that such remarks could embolden drug traffickers.He questioned why the police had failed to identify the source of narcotics despite the large number of arrests. He also cited the arrest of an anti-drone unit employee with a large drug consignment, alleging that the incident raised questions about the campaign’s effectiveness.Chandumajra criticised Mann for travelling to France while people were protesting in Mansa over the murder of an anti-drug activist. He also questioned why the Punjab assembly session lasted only nine minutes despite the need for a serious debate on drugs.He urged Union home minister Amit Shah to investigate the chief minister’s remarks and demanded a CBI probe into whether drug traffickers had benefited from alleged lapses in law enforcement

title: Plot allotments at old land rates cost GMADA  ₹400 crore: ED probe | Hindustan Times
description: Plots under Punjab government’s oustee policy provided at 2018 rates until 2025 even as land prices rose nearly threefold in seven years, finds probe
content: The Enforcement Directorate’s ongoing money-laundering probe into alleged irregularities at the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) has revealed that officials continued to allot prime residential plots under the oustee policy at heavily discounted, outdated rates for seven years, costing the Punjab government nearly ₹400 crore.The irregularities came to light while compiling a comprehensive report last week, said Enforcement Directorate (ED) officials privy to the probe.Until 2025-26, allotment letters continued to be issued at the 2018 rate of ₹25,000 per square yard, even as land prices rose nearly threefold to ₹65,000 per square yard in seven years, the investigation has found.The oustee policy is intended to benefit landowners whose land was acquired for development projects. In exchange for acquired land, 441 plots were allotted between 2019 and 2026 — 100 in IT City’s Sector 82 Alpha and 341 in Sector 66 Beta. Another 169 applications remain pending, including 39 in Sector 82 Alpha and 130 in Sector 66 Beta.During a three-day search at GMADA’s Mohali office last month, the ED had seized records relating to the policy. The agency has separately alleged that manipulation of reserve prices for unsold land parcels could have caused a potential loss of nearly ₹10,000 crore to GMADA and the Punjab government.Under the oustee policy, notified by the Punjab government’s department of housing and urban development in May 2013, landowners whose property is acquired for residential, institutional, industrial or integrated mixed-land-use projects are provided monetary compensation for the acquired land.As an additional benefit, oustees are also allotted residential plots at prescribed rates.Under the 2013 policy, GMADA launched its first oustee plot scheme on August 26, 2013, followed by subsequent schemes in 2018 and 2021.According to the investigation, GMADA repeatedly revised the prevailing rates for residential plots under its jurisdiction, but estate officers continued issuing allotment letters for these schemes at old rates.The rate, which stood at ₹25,000 per square yard in 2018-19 and 2019-20, was increased to ₹32,500 in 2021-22, ₹39,000 in 2022-23, ₹42,900 in 2023-24, ₹51,500 in 2024-25 and ₹65,000 in 2025-26.Vikas Garg, principal secretary, Punjab’s department of housing and urban development, said he was unaware of the issue but would examine it after reviewing the records.Committee backed old rates in 2020Also under ED scrutiny is a June 2020 meeting of a committee comprising senior GMADA and PUDA officials, the Estate Officer (Plots) and the authority’s legal adviser, where allotment of plots to oustees and the applicable rates were discussed.GMADA had advertised a plot scheme for oustees on August 24, 2018, based on the prevailing rates for different schemes. The rates were subsequently revised on June 12, 2019.The committee took the view that beneficiaries allotted plots under the oustee quota in IT City’s Sector 82 Alpha and Sector 66 Beta should be charged ₹25,000 per square yard, as fixed by GMADA on June 12, 2019.The committee also noted that allotment letters for applications invited in 2018 had not been issued. It directed the then Estate Officer (Plots) to issue allotment letters to all successful applicants under the schemes launched in 2013 and 2018 within 15 days. However, ED’s official note records that the directions were not followed and allotment letters continued to be issued over subsequent years.The investigation has also flagged procedural shortcomings, including the inclusion of applicants in the draw of lots without proper scrutiny of their documents and failure to issue Letters of Intent (LOIs) within the timelines prescribed in the scheme brochures.

title: Raj Thackeray, Sanjay Raut post Modi-Adani documentary on X | Mumbai news
description: The 36-minute documentary, titled “How Adani and Modi stole India”, was created by Indian-American entrepreneur and Hotmail co-founder Sabeer Bhatia  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: Days after the Mumbai police issued notices to at least 24 X (formerly Twitter) users for sharing a controversial documentary on the ties between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani, Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray and Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Thursday also posted the video on their accounts and urged people to watch it.The 36-minute documentary, titled “How Adani and Modi stole India”, was created by Indian-American entrepreneur and Hotmail co-founder Sabeer Bhatia. It accuses Modi and Adani of corruption, collusion, and corporate cronyism, questioning business dealings, land allocations and government decisions over two decades.Thackeray shared the documentary on his X account on Thursday morning, along with a post in Marathi that said: “The government wants to make this documentary disappear from social media. You will understand the reason for this once you watch the documentary. So watch it before the government makes it disappear!”Raut also shared the video, tagging the handles of the Bharatiya Janata Party and its ideological fount, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. He wrote: “Patriots…And Blind devotees…And Friends…Do take a look…”Later in the day, he said, “There are attempts by the BJP and the government to suppress the video. They want to give Mumbai and many other infrastructure projects to Adani.”BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban said the documentary should be shown on one screen, and videos of Raj Thackeray welcoming the Adanis should be shown on an adjacent screen.Deputy commissioner of police (cyber crime) Bajrang Bansode declined to comment.The notices issued by the Mumbai police stated that the West Cyber police, Crime Branch and CID had received a complaint alleging that multiple X accounts had published “highly objectionable content targeting a well-known company”. The content allegedly lacked any apparent factual or lawful basis, causing serious harm to the company’s reputation, the notices said.

title: KEM Hospital chemist contract renewal faces dispute | Mumbai news
description: The proposal tabled at the Improvements committee on Thursday seeks to renew the contract of Parel Chemist from August 20, 2026, to August 19, 2031. Two corporators, Congress leader Ashraf Azmi and Meher Mohsin Haider have urged the BMC to invite fresh bids  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: A proposal to extend the contract of a medical store at KEM Hospital in Parel for another five years without inviting fresh tenders has come under scrutiny in the BMC. Opposition corporators have alleged that the arrangement increases the financial burden on poor patients due to poor discounts on medicines.The proposal tabled at the Improvements committee on Thursday seeks to renew the contract of Parel Chemist from August 20, 2026, to August 19, 2031. Two corporators, Congress leader Ashraf Azmi and Meher Mohsin Haider have urged the BMC to invite fresh bids.In a letter to the civic administration, Azmi alleged that patients pay more due to inadequate discounts on medicines. Both corporators allege that the discount offered by this chemist is 12.5% on the MRP, while at other major hospitals, including AIIMS, vendors must offer discounts of at least 30%, said Azmi.He also questioned the hospital’s practice of procuring medicines from the on-campus pharmacy rather than selecting suppliers through competitive processes based on prices and discounts. He alleged that delays in finalising the list of medicines available free to patients further increase their dependence on the store. Of approximately 2,500 medicines intended to be covered under free-medicine schedules, only around 800 had been finalised, he said.He has sought an inquiry into whether hospital authorities directed departments to purchase medicines from the on-campus pharmacy even though this was against regulations.Haider questioned the legal basis for the proposed renewal. In her representation, she said Clause 25(iii) of the existing contract allows an extension to be considered subject to satisfactory performance but does not give the contractor an automatic right to another term.Haider has sought an independent audit of discounts provided between 2021 and 2026, a comparative market study and an independent valuation of the premises to determine whether the proposed terms maximise public benefit.The proposal was not taken up at the improvements committee meeting and will come up for discussion again next month.

title: Maharashtra makes NOC from co-owners of joint property mandatory for sale | Mumbai news
description: MUMBAI: The Maharashtra government has tightened land registration rules to prevent the sale of jointly held land without other co-owners’ knowledge or consent  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: The Maharashtra government has tightened land registration rules to prevent the sale of jointly held land without other co-owners’ knowledge or consent. Under the new procedure, sellers must submit co-owners’ consent or no-objection certificates (NOCs) to register sale deeds involving land recorded under a common property card or 7/12 extract.A government circular issued by the state revenue department on October 19 now forbids sub-registrars to register sales deeds without the required documents. “The written consent of co-owners of jointly held properties must be obtained and made part of the document submitted for registration. If the written consent of the co-owners is not attached to the document, it will not be registered,” the circular states.However, if a co-owner attaches a measurement map of their part of the property, consent from other co-owners will not be mandatory. “If a co-owner of land recorded in joint names in the 7/12 extract (property card) intends to sell their share, and the seller attaches a copy of the measurement map obtained from the land records department showing the portion to be sold, the sub-registrar shall register the document without insisting on the written consent or NOC of the other co-owners recorded in the 7/12 extract,” the circular says.Section 44 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 permits a co-owner to transfer their own share without the consent of other co-owners, which has led to a rise in disputes and court petitions over the sale of jointly held land.Circular aims to curb unauthorised property transactions, protect ownership rights and prevent land disputesThe circular was brought out to solve the issue of the growing number of complaints and cases against registration offices for registering such transactions and causing hardship to affected parties. It aims to curb unauthorised transactions, protect ownership rights and prevent financial losses and land disputes.Also Read: Mumbai property registrations rise 5% YoY to 12,622 in September; Ganesh Chaturthi registrations jump 22%“The revised procedure was intended to reduce litigation and prevent disputes among co-owners arising from land transactions conducted without their knowledge,” said a senior revenue official.Also Read: ₹711 crore tower to ₹294 crore apartments: Mumbai’s sea-facing versus sea-view luxury homes premium explained">From a ₹711 crore tower to ₹294 crore apartments: Mumbai’s sea-facing versus sea-view luxury homes premium explained

title: Amid stiff opposition, BMC to dereserve Alexandra Cinema plot in Byculla for residential use | Mumbai news
description: The proposal, based on a recommendation from the state urban development department (UDD), was first placed before the committee on August 12. It was passed after two months under Section 64(3A) of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888,which provides for deemed approval of civic proposals if the relevant committee fails to decide on them within 45 days  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: The BMC Improvements Committee on Thursday passed a proposal to delete the cinema reservation on the 1,005-sq-m plot of the defunct Alexandra Cinema in Byculla-Nagpada, paving the way for residential development. The decision was taken amid strong opposition from Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) corporators, who had warned that the move could set a precedent for other closed cinemas across Mumbai.The proposal, based on a recommendation from the state urban development department (UDD), was first placed before the committee on August 12. It was passed after two months under Section 64(3A) of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888,which provides for deemed approval of civic proposals if the relevant committee fails to decide on them within 45 days.Congress corporator Meher Mohsin Haider alleged that the provision was being used to push through contentious proposals despite opposition. “This is how proposals are passed through the backdoor, as they are always strongly opposed,” she said.Haider expressed concern that removing the cinema reservation could open the floodgates to similar demands involving other defunct theatres. Mumbai’s Development Plan 2034 had 119 reservations for cinema halls and theatres, covering 3,09,284.08 sq m, she pointed out. “Where is the source of entertainment in Byculla for local residents?” she asked, questioning the rationale behind allowing residential development instead of exploring ways to revive the theatre.In a letter to Improvements’ Committee chairperson Sandhya Doshi in August, Haider had questioned why the reservation needed to be deleted altogether when the property could potentially be redeveloped for its original purpose. “If a dilapidated building can be reconstructed and a closed cinema modernised and restarted, why cancel the reservation altogether and clear the way for residential development?” she had asked.Shiv Sena (UBT) senior corporator and committee member Sachin Padwal had also opposed the proposal, pointing out that the theatre had been shut since 2007 and alleging that no serious efforts had been made to revive it. Following the proposal’s passage on Thursday, corporators from Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) staged a walkout in protest.According to the proposal submitted by the BMC administration, the plot is currently reserved for a cinema under the Development Plan. The administration has recommended deleting the reservation and permitting residential use following applications seeking a change in land use. “The theatre, which permanently shut in 2007, has remained unused for nearly two decades. The proposal is based on a recommendation from the state urban development department,” the administration stated.The proposal cites two requests to remove the cinema reservation: one by Maharashtra State Wakf Board representative Samir Gulamnabi Kazi to urban development minister Eknath Shinde on February 25, 2026, and another by Rafiq Patel, listed as the occupant of the plot, to the BMC’s development planning department on March 27. Following directions from the urban development department, the BMC submitted its report and recommendations on April 6, with the municipal commissioner’s prior approval.Congress corporator Ashraf Azmi said that Alexandra came under the Kamathipura cluster redevelopment project. “How can they individually dereserve it?” he asked. “Even if it was outside the cluster, we oppose it on the grounds that there is no means of entertainment for local residents.”The 105-year-old Alexandra was once among Mumbai’s prominent single-screen theatres. Founded by two of India’s film pioneers—the legendary Ardeshir Irani, who made India’s first talkie Alam Ara, and Abdulally Esoofally—it was known for screening Hollywood films and English-language classics. Like several old cinema houses, it struggled to remain viable amid changing viewing preferences, mounting financial pressures and the expansion of multiplexes, and by the early 2000s, shifted to screening low-budget and adult films. It shut down in 2007 and has remained unused since.With the cinema reservation now cleared, the decision paves the way for residential development on the strategically located 1,005-sq-m plot, bringing its long-standing association with cinema to an end.

title: HC warns slum dwellers littering streets of forfeiture of rehab rights | Mumbai news
description: The court was hearing a bunch of petitions over the continued dumping of municipal solid waste at the Kanjurmarg landfill  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: The Bombay High Court on Thursday warned that the right of slum dwellers in Mumbai to permanent alternate accommodation would be forfeited if they were found dumping garbage in public places, in violation of the court’s order for maintaining public hygiene.“This is a serious issue in Mumbai. Citizens think they can encroach on any land parcel, they will dirty the public places and will not coordinate with the civic body. They will threaten civic officials and the police,” said the division bench of justices GS Kulkarni and Dr Neela Gokhale.“What attitude is this,” the judges asked. “People are resisting even basic cleanliness. This isn’t acceptable at all. For slums, we will get their right to a permanent alternate accommodation forfeited. If you want to live in this city, follow basic principles. If you throw garbage anywhere and do not follow the rules, we will forfeit your rights.”The court was hearing a bunch of petitions over the continued dumping of municipal solid waste at the Kanjurmarg landfill, saying maintenance of public hygiene was a collective responsibility and required citizens to aid the municipal machinery.On Thursday, the court expressed concern over the indiscriminate dumping of garbage and said that slum dwellers could not dump “anywhere and everywhere”.“We understand that there is a government policy and these slum dwellers are a vote bank but still they need to be disciplined, they just cannot claim a right to accommodation or in situ accommodation etc,” the bench observed, saying the Slum Rehabilitation Authority (SRA) cannot increase the burden of the civic body and it must “control the slums”.The court appreciated efforts taken by local wards, and added, “We want every ward officer to follow the rules. Accountability ward wise must be set. Week to week feedback must be there.”THe court noted that littering on public roads infringes upon constitutional rights of citizens, guaranteed under the right to life.“We can’t have such unruly citizens. Their rights have to be forfeited else they will not learn a lesson. Let us be very clear, these slum dwellers will have to mend their ways. They cannot get everything for free. If they want to live in Mumbai they will have to mend their ways,” the bench said.The court said that the SRA would have to ensure that residents of rehabilitation facilities followed basic cleanliness rules.“They cannot say that they won’t adhere to the rules. We don’t recognise these types of citizens. We can’t have a situation wherein they create obstacles in the path of the civic body,” the bench said.

title: Punjab-origin landlord stripped of royal honour over squalid housing conditions | Hindustan Times
description: Nirpal Singh Riat’s name was on an updated UK cabinet office list issued this month among those whose Order of the British Empire (OBE) has been annulled
content: A British Indian landlord based in London has been stripped of his royal honour by King Charles III after being fined for renting out damp and squalid rooms.Nirpal Singh Riat’s name was on an updated UK cabinet office list issued this month among those whose Order of the British Empire (OBE) has been annulled.Riat, who was conferred the royal honour by the late Queen Elizabeth II in 2010 for “services to charity and to the Punjabi people”, was found to have brought the “honours system into disrepute”.“The King has directed that the appointment of Nirpal Singh Riat to be an officer of the civil division of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire, dated 31 December 2010, shall be cancelled and annulled and that his name shall be erased from the Register of the said Order,” reads the cabinet office statement.Riat, who denies some of the allegations levelled against him as “fabricated”, has been dubbed a rogue landlord after details of his business emerged in court around three years ago. According to local media reports, the businessman now in his 70s was given one of the biggest fines in west London of 300,000 pounds (around ₹3.8 crore) over illegally converting houses into flats and renting outbuildings to vulnerable people forced to live in “terrible conditions”. There were also reports of a previous fine over an illegal property conversion.The stripping of Riat’s honour follows a local councillor in Hounslow raising the matter with the Honours Forfeiture Committee. The Honours Forfeiture Committee is an advisory committee under the UK cabinet office that reviews cases where a person with a British honour may have brought the honours system into disrepute.The cancellation of a royal honour is rare and follows a similar move against another Indian-origin businessman in 2024. Lord Rami Ranger was stripped of his CBE conferred by the late Queen Elizabeth II in the New Year’s Honours list of December 2015 for services to British business and the Asian community after the Forfeiture Committee found that he had brought the “honours system into disrepute”.However, the British Indian peer challenged the revocation in court and earlier this month won the right to a judicial review of the annulment of his royal honour. His legal team is set to argue at a full hearing in the coming months that the stripping of his CBE was disproportionate and that due process had not been followed. In the UK honours system, a CBE (Commander of the Order of the British Empire) ranks higher than an OBE.

title: ‘Equal cancer care is top priority’, says UICC president-elect | Mumbai news
description: The UICC has the ability to connect governments, doctors, researchers, patients and civil society groups. Dr CS Pramesh said this strength should be used to turn research and evidence into policies that make a real difference to patients  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: Making cancer treatment and care more accessible will be a top priority for Dr CS Pramesh, the new president-elect of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC), which brings together more than 1,100 member organisations across 170 countries.“I have seen both the extraordinary progress we have made and the substantial inequities that persist. My focus will be on learning from successful approaches, sharing them across countries and turning the common goal of equal cancer care into better outcomes for patients,” said Dr Pramesh, director of Tata Memorial Hospital and professor and head of thoracic surgery at Tata Memorial Centre in Mumbai.He was elected president of the UICC for the 2026-2028 term during the organisation’s general assembly on October 20. The meeting also saw the appointment of its new board of directors for 2026-2028. While Dr Pramesh will be the UICC president-elect from 2026-28, he will be the organisation’s president from 2028-30.In an interaction with the Hindustan Times after his election, Dr Pramesh said he would bring cancer organisations, governments and healthcare professionals together to improve access to treatment, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.A surgical oncologist and researcher, Dr Pramesh is known for his work in clinical trials in cancer research and his role in establishing the national cancer grid. His clinical areas of interest include the treatment of oesophageal and lung cancers and minimally invasive surgery.For him, making cancer treatment affordable is not just about reducing the cost of medicines. It is also about ensuring that patients can access early diagnosis, quality treatment and the right medical advice without their financial condition or place of residence becoming a barrier. “I believe that cancer care should not depend on a person’s income, where they live, or their ability to navigate a complex health system,” he said.The UICC has the ability to connect governments, doctors, researchers, patients and civil society groups. Dr Pramesh said this strength should be used to turn research and evidence into policies that make a real difference to patients.He also believes that India has important lessons to share with the world, especially in building a cancer care system that works across different income groups and regions.India’s National Cancer Grid (NCG), which began with a relatively small group of cancer centres, has grown into a network of more than 420 cancer centres, research institutions, patient groups and professional organisations in India and abroad. Its member organisations treat more than 860,000 new cancer patients every year, accounting for around 60% of India’s cancer burden.Dr Pramesh said the importance of the network lies not only in its size but also in its approach to bringing institutions together. Through shared treatment guidelines, training, research, quality improvement and virtual tumour boards, the network helps hospitals improve treatment standards and reduce differences in the care patients receive. Such a model can also help make medical expertise available beyond large cities.As UICC president-elect, Dr Pramesh also wants to strengthen cooperation among member organisations and encourage countries to work towards universal health coverage. Sharing successful models between countries and adapting them to local conditions will be important in making progress, he said.He also sees potential in the UICC’s Access to Oncology Medicines (ATOM) initiative, which aims to improve access to affordable cancer medicines in regions where treatment remains difficult to obtain. Looking ahead to the end of his UICC presidency, Dr Pramesh’ hopes to see a shift from promises of equal cancer care to action on the ground.

title: Pursue goals with honesty, hard work, Mann exhorts schoolchildren | Hindustan Times
description: Interacting with students of Guru Gobind Singh International School, Faridkot, Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann urged them to dream big and pursue their ambitions through honesty and hard work
content: The Punjab Vidhan Sabha on Thursday opened its doors to schoolchildren, giving young minds a first-hand understanding of how laws are made, budgets are passed and elected representatives are held accountable.Interacting with students of Guru Gobind Singh International School, Faridkot, chief minister Bhagwant Mann urged them to dream big and pursue their ambitions through honesty and hard work, stressing that talent and merit, not influence or recommendations, must determine their future.“The youth are the greatest strength of Punjab and providing them with inspiration, opportunities and a progressive environment is essential for building a brighter future for Punjab. Never allow temporary setbacks to weaken your determination,” the chief minister told the students.The real measure of success lay not in where one came from, but in the honesty, hard work and commitment with which one pursued their goals, he said.Sharing his life experiences, Mann encouraged students aspiring to join the civil services or become advocates, doctors and defence officers to start working towards their goals today rather than waiting for the perfect moment.Quoting former president Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, Mann reminded the students, “True dreams are those that inspire a person to keep striving even when the world is asleep. Do not become disheartened by examination results or initial failures.”“I myself had lost my first election, but continued to work with determination. Setbacks are not the end of the journey. They are opportunities to learn, improve and return stronger.”The chief minister explained to the students the significance and functioning of the Punjab assembly. “Bills are introduced, debated and passed into law in the Vidhan Sabha and the state budget is also approved here. Institutions such as the Vidhan Sabha belong to the people,” Mann said.“Young citizens must understand how democracy functions, how decisions affecting their lives are made and how public representatives are accountable to the people,” he said.

title: BJP accuses National Conference of shying away from panchayat polls in J&K | Hindustan Times
description: Speaking in the assembly last month, chief minister Omar Abdullah, referring to panchayat polls, said he was adopting the same line as the BJP - that the elections would be held at an appropriate time.
content: Leader of Opposition in J&K assembly Sunil Sharma on Thursday accused the Omar Abdullah-led government of shying away from panchayat polls, saying the elections could have served as a litmus test for the National Conference (NC).Sharma’s remarks came a day after panchayat polls were announced in Ladakh.“Omar Abdullah has made it clear in the legislative assembly that his government won’t be holding panchayat polls in J&K. Even NC president Farooq Abdullah has said that panchayat polls won’t be held in the UT. They (NC) are aware that if panchayat polls are held, the ruling party will face its biggest setback since coming to power in 2024,” Sharma said, adding that people would teach the NC a lesson as the government has failed to fulfil its promises.“They haven’t fulfilled a single promise, whether it is free electricity, gas cylinders or reservations. So they are aware of the outcome of the polls,” he alleged.Speaking in the assembly last month, chief minister Abdullah, referring to panchayat polls, said he was adopting the same line as the BJP - that the elections would be held at an appropriate time.Jammu and Kashmir has a three-tier Panchayati Raj system. The term of the district development councils (DDCs) ended on February 24, leaving the region without elected grassroots representation at district level for the first time since the abrogation of Article 370 in August 2019.The terms of panchayats and block development councils (BDCs) ended two years ago. The last panchayat elections were held in 2018, while BDC polls took place in October 2019.

title: Sona Mohapatra doubles down on her statement on Daler Mehndi amid outpouring of support for singer; says empathy cannot replace accountability | Hindustan Times
description: Daler Mehndi was recently reprimanded by Uttarakhand Cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal over his performance. Sona Mohapatra responded to it.
content: Singer Daler Mehndi was recently reprimanded by Uttarakhand Cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal over his performance at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in New Tehri on Sunday. After allegations surfaced that he was under the influence of alcohol and unable to sing, there was an outpouring of support for him from the film and music fraternity. Sona Mohapatra, who also previously described her experience of watching Daler perform as less than ideal, doubled down on her statement.Sona Mohapatra doubles down on statement about Daler MehndiSona acknowledged in a long note on her Instagram that she feels something is ‘wrong with (her) wiring’ as she sees support pour in for Daler, even though she had claimed otherwise. “There was my perspective on the Daler Mehndi incident, and then there seemed to be almost an entire fraternity of artists speaking in the opposite direction. The contrast was impossible to miss,” she wrote, stating that it was exhausting not to go with the flow.Pointing out that performing artists are privileged to enjoy love, applause, beautiful hotels, good pay, and more, she questioned, “And yet, when did gratitude towards everything that makes all this possible become less important than protecting our own? When did empathy become a reason to abandon accountability?” Sona also added, “And why are we, especially in India, so easily swept away by sentimentality? We seem to place such a premium on being moved that we sometimes forget to think.” Sona also mentioned that one can feel compassion for someone without suspending judgment, adding that she’s happy for the people who took the time to understand the nuance of what she had written. What Sona Mohapatra said about Daler Mehndi in the pastWhen the controversy reached a boiling point on Wednesday, Sona recalled watching Daler perform at the second edition of the Sufi Heritage Festival. “From where we watched, Daler ji appeared disoriented, struggled to hold a note and kept repeating the same musical phrase. The overall production was also deeply disappointing. We watched audience members gradually leave, people who had paid good money and come with great expectations,” she wrote. This came amid contrasting support from Daler’s brother, Mika Singh, and others in the film and music fraternity. Denying that he drinks alcohol, it was claimed that he was unwell on the day. Speaking to PTI, Minister Uniyal said, “Such a big artiste, he should have informed us about this. This fact was revealed only when he was interrupted. If he was unwell, he should not have come to perform. We were asked to make full payment of ₹35 lakh in advance to the artiste; hotels were also booked in advance. I have nothing personal against Mehndi nor any intention to hurt him, but such a big artiste, knowing his condition, should have refused to perform.”

title: Anantnag: Omar asks officials to speed up devp works before winter | Hindustan Times
description: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said the government is committed to starting work on the mini-secretariat in the district once the decision was taken on its location.
content: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Thursday urged officials to take advantage of the fair weather and complete the developmental projects before the harsh winter sets in.Abdullah was in Anantnag district to review development works with cabinet ministers and MLAs.“Today projects worth ₹60 crore were either inaugurated or their foundation was laid. At least 11 water supply schemes were inaugurated while the foundation stones of several other developmental works were laid,” Abdullah said.He said the purpose of the meeting was to assess the progress of developmental works in the district.The chief minister said that the demands of almost every Anantnag MLA had been heard. “The demands of their constituents were reflected in the meeting. We will do our best to meet their demands,” he said, adding that the government is committed to starting work on the mini-secretariat in the district once the decision was taken on its location.“ I have asked the DC to consult the MLAs and civil society and decide where the mini-secretariat should be built. As soon as the land is identified, we will prepare the detailed project report (DPR),” he said.He also said work on the maternity hospital would begin once the location was finalised.

title: 4 held with 10kg heroin in Amritsar | Hindustan Times
description: The arrested suspects have been identified as Sukhraj Singh of Hargobind Avenue, Ajitpal Singh, alias Mota, of Khandwala, Anmolpreet Singh of Jawahar Nagar and Robin Gill of Chogawan village, all residents of Amritsar district
content: The counter intelligence (CI) wing of Punjab Police busted a cross-border narcotics smuggling network by arresting four persons and recovering 10kg of heroin from their possession, director general of police (DGP) Gaurav Yadav said on Thursday.The arrested suspects have been identified as Sukhraj Singh of Hargobind Avenue, Ajitpal Singh, alias Mota, of Khandwala, Anmolpreet Singh of Jawahar Nagar and Robin Gill of Chogawan village, all residents of Amritsar district. Along with the contraband, police teams impounded a motorcycle and a scooter that the suspects were using to transport the illicit cargo.Sharing details of the operation, the DGP said that the CI Amritsar team acted on a reliable intelligence input. The report indicated that the associates were operating under the direct instructions of a foreign-based handler, from whom they had retrieved a consignment of heroin to deliver to another party.A police team intercepted all four suspects near Dera Baba Darshan Singh in Ghanupur Kale village while they were travelling on their two-wheelers. A subsequent search led to the direct recovery of the 10kg heroin consignment.Preliminary investigations reveal that the accused were functioning as a local distribution arm for international drug smugglers, aiming to supply the contraband across various parts of the state.A case has been registered under Sections 21, 25, and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act at the state special operations cell (SSOC) police station in Amritsar.

title: Man unloading chickens dies in freak accident after tempo door hits BEST bus in Andheri | Mumbai news
description: MUMBAI: A 53-year-old man, Farid Ahmad Shaikh, died in a freak accident in MIDC, Andheri East on Wednesday after a stationary tempo door from which he was unloading chickens grazed a passing BEST bus and hit him  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: A 53-year-old man, Farid Ahmad Shaikh, died in a freak accident in MIDC, Andheri East on Wednesday after a stationary tempo door from which he was unloading chickens grazed a passing BEST bus and hit him. The MIDC police have registered a case against the bus driver.According to the police, the incident occurred at 10.15 am when the bus, operated by Mateshwari Urban Transport Solutions under a wet-lease arrangement with BEST, was travelling from Majas Depot towards Andheri. The bus driver in his statement said that a tempo was parked on the left side of the road, and a worker unloading chickens from it suddenly opened the tempo’s rear door.“The door struck the bus’s left rear corner before rebounding and hitting Shaikh, causing him to fall and sustain injuries,” said a BEST official. “The bus driver initially continued ahead but stopped after passengers informed him that a person had been injured in an incident involving the bus. Meanwhile, other workers from the chicken shop arrived on motorcycles and confronted the driver, informing him that the injured man had been taken to hospital.”According to BEST officials, the driver called the police to report the accident, after which police officials reached the spot and took both the bus and the tempo to MIDC police station for further inquiry. The driver and conductor were initially allowed to leave, with instructions to keep the bus at Majas Depot pending further action.Later that night, at around 9.45 pm, the police informed the driver over the phone that Shaikh had succumbed to his injuries. The driver was asked to report to the police station at 10 am on Thursday for further investigation. An accidental death report was registered on October 21, and the MIDC police subsequently registered an FIR against the bus driver under Sections 106(1), 281 and 125(B) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.The bus driver and conductor have been summoned for further investigation. The police are probing the circumstances leading to the accident, including the movement of the bus and the opening of the tempo’s rear door.

title: Jealousy over suspected affair: Airport security officer, 21, stabbed to death by ex in Nerul | Mumbai news
description: NAVI MUMBAI: A 21-year-old security officer at Navi Mumbai International Airport died on Wednesday, a day after she was allegedly stabbed multiple times by her former partner near Nerul railway station, in an attack police suspect was triggered by jealousy  | Mumbai news
content: NAVI MUMBAI: A 21-year-old security officer at Navi Mumbai International Airport died on Wednesday, a day after she was allegedly stabbed multiple times by her former partner near Nerul railway station, in an attack police suspect was triggered by jealousy. The accused, Danish Mohammad Ansari, 27, allegedly attacked Sadiya Sheikh in public on Tuesday morning after suspecting her of being involved with another man, police said.Sheikh had previously filed two non-cognisable (NC) complaints against Ansari — one with Navi Mumbai airport police and another with Antop Hill police — alleging repeated harassment and an attempt to assault her, according to information available in the case.The two became friends during the Covid-19 pandemic, and Ansari had reportedly told his family that he intended to marry her. However, over the past year, he allegedly began suspecting that she was in another relationship, leading to repeated confrontations.About six months ago, Ansari allegedly went to Sheikh’s workplace at the airport and demanded that she show him her mobile phone. When she refused, he allegedly assaulted her.Despite the earlier complaints, Ansari allegedly continued to pursue her. On Tuesday, around 6.45 am, Sheikh was on her way to work when he allegedly followed her to a bus stop on the eastern side of Nerul railway station and attacked her with a knife.He allegedly stabbed her multiple times in the back, abdomen, neck and chest before fleeing. Sheikh was initially taken to Meenatai Thackeray Hospital in Nerul and later shifted to Sion Hospital for further treatment. She succumbed to her injuries on Wednesday.Ansari, a driver residing in Antop Hill, Mumbai, allegedly went into hiding at his grandmother’s house in Ghansoli after the attack. Police tracked him using his mobile phone location and arrested him.Nerul police initially registered a case under Sections 109(1) (attempt to murder), 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack, including the earlier complaints filed by Sheikh against the accused.

title: Jhota murder case: 4 accused sent to 14-day judicial custody | Hindustan Times
description: The accused — pharmacy owner and prime accused Ashwani Kumar, his wife Neelam Rani, and Ashwani’s associates Vipin Kumar Garg and Laadi — were produced before the magistrate through video conferencing
content: A Mansa court on Thursday remanded all four accused in the murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh, alias Jhota, to 14 days of judicial custody. Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight on October 13, triggering widespread protests in Mansa.The accused — pharmacy owner and prime accused Ashwani Kumar, his wife Neelam Rani, and Ashwani’s associates Vipin Kumar Garg and Laadi — were produced before the magistrate through video conferencing. Mansa senior superintendent of police (SSP) Vaibhav Chaudhary confirmed that the court had sent them to jail till November 5.Officials said the district police informed the court that the Punjab government had transferred the investigation into the murder to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). Following the submission, the accused were remanded to judicial custody.On Tuesday, chief minister Bhagwant Mann announced that the murder investigation would be handed over to the CBI. The announcement came just hours before Union home Minister Amit Shah met Jhota’s family.Police officials said the accused were produced before the magistrate through video conferencing due to security concerns, as supporters of the slain activist continued their round-the-clock protests in large numbers in Mansa.Jhota was shot dead on October 13 inside Ashwani Kumar’s chemist shop in a busy locality near the level crossing in Mansa town. He was reportedly seen confronting Ashwani at the shop and accusing him of selling drugs to addicts without valid medical prescriptions.The incident sparked outrage among local residents and Jhota’s supporters, who have been demanding justice for the slain activist. The agitation has continued since the day of the shooting, with protesters insisting that their demands be met before they call off their protest.Statements of Jhota’s family recorded CBI teams met Jhota’s parents and widow at the local circuit house on Thursday and recorded their statements as part of the investigation. The agency also sent a team to the residences of Kumar and Garg as it began its inquiry into the case.The CBI registered a fresh murder case on Wednesday, naming Kumar as an accused and booking unidentified persons under various criminal charges. The agency is now investigating the circumstances surrounding the killing.Family vows to continue agitationJhota’s family said that the ongoing agitation, which began on October 13, would continue until their demands were fulfilled.His widow, Manpreet Kaur, said the family would give consent for the postmortem examination only after the Insaaf Committee approved it. She maintained that her husband had lost his life because of his commitment to fighting narcotics trafficking.Manpreet said any decision regarding the postmortem examination and cremation would be taken in consultation with Jhota’s supporters. The family’s decision reflects its insistence that the demands raised by the protesters be addressed before the next steps are taken.Financial aid for injured Giani Tek Singh Dhanaula, jathedar of Takht Damdama Sahib in Talwandi Sabo, Bathinda, handed over cheques for ₹5 lakh each to four people who sustained bullet injuries in the attack in which Jhota was killed.The jathedar was accompanied by Jhota’s father Bhim Singh during the distribution of financial assistance.

title: 23 booked for obstructing, manhandling cops probing garba sword scare in Titwala | Mumbai news
description: THANE: What began as a probe into a viral video of youths brandishing swords at a Varap garba event escalated into a high-voltage clash in Kamba, near Titwala  | Mumbai news
content: THANE: What began as a probe into a viral video of youths brandishing swords at a Varap garba event escalated into a high-voltage clash in Kamba, near Titwala. Acting on a tip-off, a Thane Rural Local Crime Branch team detained suspect Kaushal Hiranand Jha at a local hotel.Jha allegedly created a ruckus, while local politician Rajan Dubey intervened, asserting his political clout and warning officers that detaining Jha “will prove costly for them.” A crowd of 20 to 25 people gathered, jostled the policemen, and tried to block the detention. As officers transported Jha to Kalyan Taluka police station, Dubey and his associates pursued them in cars and on two-wheelers. Jha reportedly hurled abuses, threatened officers, and tried to injure himself inside the vehicle.Police have registered a separate case against Jha, Dubey and the others under sections 351(2) (criminal intimidation), 352 (intentional insult), 121 (voluntarily causing hurt), 190 (defines unlawful assembly), 191(2) (offense of rioting), 186(2) (unlawful procession) and 132 (use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) of the BNS.In a startling aftermath, senior police inspector Mukesh Dhage and an unidentified sub-inspector were abruptly transferred immediately after booking Dubey. The influential Dombivli leader holds strong ties across ruling and opposition parties. Additional superintendent of police Anmol Mittal confirmed the transfers were non-routine, citing several reasons, though he remained silent on any direct link to the case.

title: GMLR project puts 1,524 trees on chopping block, activists warn of irreversible consequences | Mumbai news
description: MUMBAI: The proposed felling of 1,524 trees for the Goregaon-Mulund Link Road (GMLR) project could further aggravate Mumbai’s rising heat and pollution, undermine its ecological balance and threaten the health of residents, environmental activists have warned, urging the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to withdraw the proposal  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: The proposed felling of 1,524 trees for the Goregaon-Mulund Link Road (GMLR) project could further aggravate Mumbai’s rising heat and pollution, undermine its ecological balance and threaten the health of residents, environmental activists have warned, urging the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to withdraw the proposal.In a letter to the BMC’s Tree Authority, the Watchdog Foundation, a civic and commuter rights non-governmental organisation (NGO), has objected to the proposed felling and transplantation of trees for the fourth phase of the GMLR, stretching from the Western Express Highway in Goregaon to Airoli Toll Naka in Mulund, as well as the improvement of the junction of the Eastern Express Highway and the GMLR.Trustees Nicholas Almeida and advocate Godfrey Pimenta said the loss of the trees could have irreversible consequences for the city’s environment, affecting biodiversity, air quality and urban temperatures.The foundation’s objection follows a Tree Authority notice published on October 22, inviting citizens to submit objections and suggestions on the proposal. Pointing to the unusually hot and humid conditions prevailing in Mumbai in October, the foundation said the city needed more green cover to combat rising temperatures and pollution, rather than infrastructure projects that would further deplete it. “Development cannot come at the cost of destroying the very environment that sustains us,” Pimenta stated, adding that the proposed loss of trees raised questions about the environmental cost of infrastructure development.The foundation has urged the civic administration to explore alternatives that minimise tree loss and protect the city’s remaining green cover. It has also appealed to elected corporators to oppose the proposal, arguing that the interests of the environment and residents must be safeguarded.According to the BMC notice, the proposal has been submitted by the executive engineer of the GMLR Bridge Department.However, a civic official from the BMC’s bridges department said the trees could not be saved as they stood in the way of the project. “These trees are coming in the way of the GMLR project and there is no option but to fell them. Nothing can be done to save them,” the official said.The civic body has invited objections and suggestions within seven days of the notice’s publication. A hearing has been scheduled for October 30, from 4.30pm to 6pm, at the office of the superintendent of gardens and tree officer in Byculla.

title: Uran to face twice-weekly water cuts from Oct 27 as Ransai dam runs low | Mumbai news
description: The restrictions follow the state government’s directive for a 10% water cut from October 16. Ransai dam’s water level is reportedly declining by around an inch daily, prompting MIDC to urge consumers to conserve water  | Mumbai news
content: NAVI MUMBAI: Uran’s water shortage is set to worsen, with the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) introducing twice-weekly water cuts from October 27 as falling levels at Ransai dam force rationing nearly two months earlier than last year. The cuts will affect Uran town, rural settlements and industrial establishments, amid deficient monsoon rainfall and an intensifying El Niño weather pattern.The restrictions follow the state government’s directive for a 10% water cut from October 16. Ransai dam’s water level is reportedly declining by around an inch daily, prompting MIDC to urge consumers to conserve water.“The state government has ordered a 10% water cut from October 16, but the restrictions for Uran residents will come into effect from October 27,” said Tanaji Kamble, deputy engineer, Uran MIDC.Last year, the dam overflowed three times during the monsoon, allowing regular supplies until December. This year, restrictions are beginning in October, raising concerns over the ability of existing reserves to sustain demand in the coming months.Uran requires around 41 million litres per day (MLD), while MIDC supplies approximately 30 MLD under normal conditions, leaving a daily deficit of 10-11 MLD despite supplementary sources. Of the overall demand, industry accounts for around 25 MLD, Uran town 4.5 MLD and rural areas supplied through the system 6.5 MLD.Ransai dam’s water level stands at 113 feet, against 116.6 feet at the same time last year. Storage has fallen from 10.018 million cubic metres to 9.212 million cubic metres year-on-year. Built by MIDC in 1971 at Dighode village, the dam was designed to store around 10 million cubic metres, but decades of silt accumulation have reportedly reduced its effective capacity to less than 7 million cubic metres.Villages face acute shortagesThe crisis is already severe in parts of rural Uran. Residents in the Chanje and Kegaon gram panchayat areas reportedly receive water for as little as 30 minutes once every 15 days, leaving households struggling to meet basic needs.Ten villages in eastern Uran, with around 35,000 residents, receive water from Punade dam, while Chirner, Koproli and Khopta depend on Cidco’s Hetawane dam.
