The different supply networks mean shortages vary across the taluka.Residents have flagged stalled village water-supply schemes, inadequate planning and alleged water theft as factors worsening the crisis. Uran municipal council president Bhavana Ghanekar has also alleged that five water reservoirs have not been cleaned, raising concerns over water quality.

title: Delhiwale: Is that a peepal or pilkhan | Latest News Delhi
description: A landmark Delhi book clocks an anniversary yearA book on Delhi need not always have a monument on every other page  | Latest News Delhi
content: A landmark Delhi book clocks an anniversary yearA book on Delhi need not always have a monument on every other page. Or paya-nihari, or chhole bhathure, for that matter. A book might also have a leaf. Pradip Krishen’s Trees of Delhi turns twenty this year.First published in 2006, this definitive field guide covers 252 species, helping the Delhiwale recognise trees they might have been passing for years without knowing what they were. Each entry is filled with photos and gives the tree’s scientific, common and desi names, its flowering seasons, and details of its leaves and fruit. There are also where-to-see directions: the Ridge for bistendu, Jahanpanah City Forest for kareel.A quick flip of the book from cover to cover sends the city trees passing beneath the reader’s fingers. A canopy fills a photo on one page, followed by close-ups of a bark, a flower, a fruit. The text alongside explains what to look for. Kosam, reettha, and imli follow one another as the pages turn.Some entries concern trees that are not at all associated with Delhi. The olive, for instance. Page 177 however cautions the reader against expecting the immensely gnarled, single-trunked olive trees in Mediterranean tourist brochures. The book locates Delhi’s oldest olive specimen at Lal Bahadur Shastri’s samadhi sthal in Vijay Ghat, with others at the Italian embassy (of course!) and the Vatican embassy.Since the book’s “Where to see it” directions for each tree species are two decades old, looking for them might hold a little suspense, though most are likely still there. The amaltas entry recommends heading to Amrita Shergil Marg, Shanti Path, Akbar Road and Shakti Sthal. It also warns that amaltas might one day become so common in Delhi that people cease to notice it. (But its summertime yellow flowers are too eye catching!)The book now has company in guides to the trees of other cities and regions,m. Among those published since are Fruiting Trees of Delhi, A Naturalist’s Guide to the Trees & Shrubs of India, Trees of Mumbai and Trees of South India. In 2013, Pradip Krishen himself ventured beyond Delhi with Jungle Trees of Central India. Here it ought to be pointed out that the first Delhi book of this kind arrived far back in the 1960s, Flora of Delhi by J K Maheshwari.Now the existential question. Twenty years from now, will someone still carry this book out to look for a tree? A mobile phone can already help identify one from a photograph.Meanwhile, this evening, in her Vasant Vihar drawing room, Lithuanian ambassador Diana Mickevičienė’s much-used copy of Trees of Delhi lies open at the kaniar entry, on pages 194 and 195. Pink slips protrude from the book, probably marking entries for trees that interest her. A real green leaf rests beside the printed leaves of kaniar. The ambassador’s ringed hand is steadying the page, see photo.

title: Ladakh administration defends in HC cancellation of land allotment to Wangchuk’s institute | Hindustan Times
description: In an affidavit filed in the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, the administration maintained that the 40-year lease allotment covering 1,076 kanals and 1 marla of land at Phyang Thang had “lapsed by operation of law” on May 5, 2019, due to the Himalayan Institute of Alternative Learning (HIAL)’s failure to execute a lease deed or deposit mandatory land premiums within the stipulated one-year period.
content: The Ladakh administration has defended cancelling land allotment to Sonam Wangchuk’s institute, citing the activist’s “disregard for the law”, and said the allotment automatically lapsed due to unpaid dues and an unexecuted lease deed.In an affidavit filed in the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, the administration maintained that the 40-year lease allotment covering 1,076 kanals and 1 marla of land at Phyang Thang had “lapsed by operation of law” on May 5, 2019, due to the Himalayan Institute of Alternative Learning (HIAL)’s failure to execute a lease deed or deposit mandatory land premiums within the stipulated one-year period.The affidavit running into 136 pages was filed by Leh deputy commissioner and CEO of LAHDC, Romil Singh Donk, in response to HIAL’s writ petition challenging the August 21, 2025, cancellation order of leased land to the institute.The affidavit said the writ petition is “misconceived, devoid of merit, and barred by delay and laches” and made it clear that the original allotment order issued on May 5, 2018, was conditional and explicitly stated that the lease would be deemed cancelled if the allottee failed to execute the deed within a year.The administration asserted that HIAL never deposited a single rupee towards land premium or ground rent and failed to secure formal possession through the Tehsildar as mandated.Furthermore, the higher education department of UT Ladakh certified in October 2026 that HIAL is not a recognised university, nor are its courses affiliated with the University of Ladakh or other statutory bodies, violating the core objective of setting up an alternative university.Bringing other context before the court, the affidavit highlighted the past conduct of HIAL’s founder Wangchuk and his organisation, the Students’ Educational and Cultural Movement of Ladakh (SECMOL), and said that SECMOL has occupied 124 kanals of state land at Phey for over three decades without formal allotment or payment of an assessed ₹80 lakh premium.The affidavit also references the violent protests in Leh in September 2025, which led to Union Home Ministry’s intervention, the cancellation of SECMOL’s FCRA registration, and Wangchuk’s brief detention under the National Security Act prior to its revocation in March 2026, as part of a consistent pattern of public order disruptions.When approached for comments, HIAL CEO Gitanjali Angmo denied the claims made by the Ladakh administration in its affidavit.Citing a September 25, 2025 order by the home ministry cancelling SECMOL’s FCRA registration, the affidavit said it was done due to multiple statutory violations which included accepting foreign funds from a Swedish donor to study the sovereignty of the nation deemed prejudicial to national interest.It said that local residents, the Phyang Welfare Society and village Nambardars have repeatedly petitioned authorities since 2018, alleging broken promises regarding the university project, unauthorised diversion of ancient irrigation streams for “Ice Stupa” experiments, and an alleged illegal encroachment of an additional 174 kanals beyond the boundary wall.The affidavit said the villagers complained that HIAL deceived them with false promises of a world-class university, blocked ancient pasture lands, and repeatedly diverted centuries-old natural irrigation streams for Ice Stupa projects, causing severe water shortage for local farmers.Urging the high court to dismiss the petition, the administration highlighted the antecedents of Wangchuk and SECMOL and submitted that the organisation and the petitioner are merely vehicles through which Wangchuk has repeatedly sought to hold public land on his own terms.The affidavit also said that HIAL had made false statements under oath in its petition by claiming it sent repeated reminders during the first year and deposited all requisite dues.It annexed official records showing zero written communications between May 2018 and March 2020, zero payments deposited, and suppressed letters written by HIAL in June 2020 seeking a complete waiver of both premium and ground rent, a request that was never granted.

title: AAP hits out at Congress over Warring’s freebie remarks | Hindustan Times
description: AAP state president and cabinet minister Aman Arora said Warring’s remarks about restricting electricity subsidies and financial assistance for women based on need raised serious questions about the Congress’s agenda for Punjab
content: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday criticised the Congress over its leader Amarinder Singh Raja Warring’s statement regarding free power, monthly allowance for women and other freebies, stating his remarks had exposed the party’s anti-people and feudal mindset.AAP state president and cabinet minister Aman Arora said Warring’s remarks about restricting electricity subsidies and financial assistance for women based on need raised serious questions about the Congress’s agenda for Punjab.He was reacting to Warring’s statements at an online talk show recently about limiting subsidies to genuinely deserving people.Addressing a press conference, Arora warned that if the Congress came to power in Punjab in 2027, it would snatch away free electricity, the ₹10 lakh Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna and financial assistance for women, while bringing back toll plazas and imposing higher electricity and canal water charges.“Congress wants to deny ordinary Punjabis welfare benefits while its own MPs, MLAs and former ministers continued to enjoy subsidies,” Arora said, asking the opposition party’s top leadership to clarify whether these schemes would continue under a Congress government.Challenging Congress leaders to lead by example, Arora asked why party leaders, former ministers, MLAs and their families continued to benefit from government subsidies instead of voluntarily surrendering them if they genuinely believed that those who did not need assistance should be excluded.“While the AAP government has been providing free electricity for four years and financial assistance to women for around six months, I have not seen Congress leaders publicly relinquish these benefits,” he said.Backing Arora’s criticism, AAP Punjab media in-charge Baltej Pannu said Warring’s statement exposed Congress’ anti-people agenda and its intention to burden ordinary Punjabis financially by taking away facilities that had brought relief to millions of families.“Warring’s statement reflects the direction in which the Congress wants to take Punjab. Chief minister Bhagwant Mann has repeatedly warned that traditional political parties will target the facilities provided to ordinary families if they returned to power. Warring has now placed that agenda before the public himself,” he said.Pannu said the people of Punjab would not allow the Congress to reverse the progress made in electricity, healthcare, women’s welfare, irrigation and education.

title: Baramulla: Two terror associates held with IEDs, pistols | Hindustan Times
description: The arrested men were identified as Tahir Ahmad Malik of Chinkipora, Sopore, and Waseem Sultan Beigh of Chinkipora, Sopore.
content: Police on Thursday arrested two suspected terror associates in Delina, Baramulla, and recovered arms, ammunition and explosives, including Turkish-made pistols, from their possession.The arrested men were identified as Tahir Ahmad Malik of Chinkipora, Sopore, and Waseem Sultan Beigh of Chinkipora, Sopore.“In a significant counter-terror operation, Baramulla police, in a joint operation with 52 Rashtriya Rifles (RR), apprehended two suspected terrorist associates from the Darpura Nursery area of Delina, Baramulla, based on credible intelligence inputs. During the operation, the joint team recovered arms, explosive materials and other items from their possession, including one Turkish-made CANIK pistol and one magazine containing 10 rounds. Two improvised explosive devices (IEDs) weighing approximately 15 kg and 7.5 kg, respectively, police said.Police also seized a scooty and ₹6,500 cash from the accused.“Preliminary investigation indicates that the accused were allegedly functioning as overground workers (OGWs) and may have been involved in facilitating the movement and supply of weapons and explosives to terrorist operatives. Their suspected role and the extent of their involvement are being investigated,” police spokesman said, adding that a case had been registered under relevant provisions of law.Both men have been arrested, and further investigation is underway to establish their backward and forward linkages, identify other individuals involved in the suspected network, and ascertain the source and intended destination of the recovered arms and explosive materials, police added.

title: PGIMS Rohtak relieves doctor following HC’s stay on re-employment | Hindustan Times
description: The move was challenged by Dr Anil Pannikker, who argued that the appointment violated university statutes prescribing an upper age limit of 58 years for the post and that the university’s executive council had no authority to relax the statutory condition
content: The Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS), Rohtak, has reportedly relieved Dr Kundan Mittal from its Department of Pediatric Pulmonology and Intensive Care after he submitted his resignation following the Punjab and Haryana high court’s interim stay on his re-employment as medical superintendent.Dr Mittal had earlier resigned from the medical superintendent’s post after the court stayed his re-employment, which had been challenged on the grounds that it violated the statutory age limit and appointment rules.On being contacted, Dr Mittal has confirmed the development. However, the institute officials said that Dr Mittal had submitted his resignation and it was under process.Dr Mittal retired on June 30, 2026, on attaining the age of superannuation. The Haryana government subsequently granted him a three-year service extension and re-employed him as medical superintendent.The move was challenged by Dr Anil Pannikker, who argued that the appointment violated university statutes prescribing an upper age limit of 58 years for the post and that the university’s executive council had no authority to relax the statutory condition.The matter came up before justice Harpreet Singh Brar on September 16. In an interim order, the court stayed the operation of the re-employment order dated August 3, 2026, and a subsequent executive council resolution dated August 6.The university was, however, left free to appoint a medical superintendent in accordance with the applicable statutes and rules.

title: 52 FIRs registered, 21 arrested for stubble burning in Haryana | Hindustan Times
description: While the environmental compensation is recovered from the farmer burning the paddy stubble, the red entry in revenue records prohibits the cultivator from selling his crop under the MSP in the next two crop cycles
content: The Haryana government on Thursday said that 52 first information reports (FIRs) have been registered and 21 people arrested for stubble-burning violations during the ongoing paddy harvesting season.The chairperson of the commission for air quality management (CAQM), Rajesh Verma, reviewed the enforcement measures being implemented by the state government to improve air quality. Haryana chief secretary Anurag Rastogi was also present in the meeting.Haryana’s director (agriculture) Amit Khatri said that Haryana has distributed 13,200 crop-residue management machines against a target of 9,000.He said that apart from lodging 52 FIRs and arresting 21 people for crop-residue burning related offences, the environmental compensation of ₹10,000 has also been recovered. “Red entries have also been made in farm records in cases related to stubble burning,” Khatri said in the meeting, according to an official spokesperson.While the environmental compensation is recovered from the farmer burning the paddy stubble, the red entry in revenue records prohibits the cultivator from selling his crop under the minimum support price (MSP) in the next two crop cycles.The official spokesperson said that the state is using a mobile application developed by the national remote sensing centre to verify burnt areas at the village level, helping authorities monitor incidents using satellite data.To promote the use of paddy residue as a resource, district-level agreements have been made with industries to utilise over 27 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) of paddy residue during the current season.It was informed in the meeting that biomass-based power projects had consumed over 7 LMT of paddy straw by September 30, while compressed biogas plants had consumed over 1 LMT.Verma appreciated the Haryana government for the continuous decline in stubble-burning incidents. He also commended the Jhajjar district administration for developing a model brick kiln in the Badli area that is utilising paddy stubble as fuel.Brick kilns in eight non-NCR districts are using paddy straw pellets as fuel, while Indira Gandhi Super Thermal Power Station has achieved 73% of its co-firing target.Shekhar Vidyarthi, chairman, Haryana State Pollution Control Board, said that 20 drones have been deployed in the first phase of surveillance, and another 30 are planned. These measures will help authorities monitor affected areas and identify incidents of stubble burning more effectively.Meeting with Punjab focuses on plan to curb farm firesA separate meeting with the Punjab government focused on the implementation of the state action plan aimed at preventing and controlling paddy stubble burning, as directed by CAQM on May 15, an official statement said.The commission reviewed on-ground enforcement measures, district-level preparedness, and monitoring mechanisms for effective paddy stubble management.Key topics included the availability, deployment, and effective use of crop residue management (CRM) machinery at both the district and farmer levels.The commission assessed gaps in machinery utilisation and arrangements for the collection, transportation, and use of paddy straw through in-situ and ex-situ management.The commission emphasised the need to strengthen the crop-residue supply chain and ensure effective utilisation of available machinery during the peak harvesting period.The meeting also covered field validation of burnt-area assessment through satellite-based fire alerts, along with District-wise deployment of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring stubble-burning incidents.Other points of discussion included compliance with a CAQM directive mandating the use of paddy straw-based biomass pellets and briquettes in brick kilns, along with progress towards targets for biomass co-firing in thermal power plants.

title: 2 held for firing at retd Haryana Police officer’s house in Faridabad | Hindustan Times
description: The accused allegedly fired three shots at the house before fleeing on a Bullet motorcycle; the incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed at the residence
content: Two men were arrested after they allegedly opened fire at the house of a retired Haryana Police sub-inspector in Faridabad in the early hours of Thursday, police said.The incident took place around 2.30am in Nagla Enclave Part-2 when the family of retired sub-inspector Sarjeet Bainsla was asleep, they said.The accused allegedly fired three shots at the house before fleeing on a Bullet motorcycle. The incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed at the residence, police said.A windowpane was shattered during the firing, while one bullet hit a wall. The third shot was fired into the air, according to police.Bainsla, who retired from the Haryana Police in 2023, said he did not recognise the attackers. He learnt about the incident after a neighbour informed him, following which he checked the CCTV footage, police said.A 59-second CCTV clip purportedly shows two men approaching the house on foot and opening fire. One of them was wearing a blue T-shirt with a cloth tied around his head, while the other was dressed in a white shirt.The footage also purportedly shows one of the men picking up an empty cartridge casing before the duo fled on a motorcycle, police said.The accused have been identified as Harsh and Ranjit. They are being questioned to ascertain the motive behind the firing, police added.“A case has been registered based on a complaint from the family. We have arrested two suspects and are questioning them to determine the motive behind the firing,” said inspector Hukum Singh, SHO of Saran police station.

title: Man accused of attack on influencer gets bail | Hindustan Times
description: Additional Sessions Judge SU Wadgaonkar noted that although 11 to 12 people were allegedly involved in the assault, the injuries included a small laceration and trauma to the back. The court said the circumstances prima facie did not indicate an intention or knowledge to cause death.
content: Pune: The Pune sessions court has granted bail to Rahul Sitaram Waghmare accused of attacking YouTube influencer and transport businessman Atharv Jagtap with a koyta during an alleged group assault outside a restaurant on Shirole Road on August 15. The court observed that the nature of the injuries and the circumstances did not prima facie establish an intention to kill.Additional Sessions Judge SU Wadgaonkar, in an order pronounced on Wednesday, noted that although 11 to 12 people were allegedly involved in the assault, the injuries included a small laceration and trauma to the back. The court said the circumstances prima facie did not indicate an intention or knowledge to cause death.Waghmare was granted bail on a personal bond of ₹25,000 and a surety of the same amount. The court directed him not to contact Jagtap or tamper with prosecution evidence.According to the FIR registered at Deccan Police Station, Jagtap had a dispute with Madhavi Kumbhar, whom he knew through social media, following a disagreement during Navratri in 2025. The dispute allegedly escalated after Kumbhar’s friend, Pratik Shinde, trolled one of Jagtap’s social media reels.The prosecution said Jagtap and his friends were leaving Cafe Flying Gypsy around 3.45 am on August 15 when they were confronted by Kumbhar, Snehal Sonke, Shardul Oval and six to eight unidentified persons.Jagtap allegedly retreated into the restaurant after becoming frightened. One of the attackers allegedly struck him on the head with a koyta after aiming for his neck. The group also allegedly kicked and punched him before fleeing when the restaurant manager raised an alarm.Jagtap was initially taken to Sassoon General Hospital and later shifted to Dinanath Mangeshkar Hospital for a CT scan. He was discharged after treatment and subsequently lodged a complaint.Seeking bail, Waghmare’s lawyer argued that the principal accused had already been granted bail, the investigation was largely complete and Waghmare had been in custody since August 15. The prosecution opposed the plea, alleging that he had played a key role in the assault and citing other criminal cases against him.The court held that the existence of other criminal cases, by itself, was insufficient to reject the application. It allowed the plea, subject to conditions.

title: Protecting farmers’ interests, dignity Centre’s top priority, says Chouhan | Hindustan Times
description: Chouhan called for a balance between modern agricultural practices and traditional knowledge to protect soil health while ensuring that farming remained economically viable
content: Union agriculture and farmers’ welfare minister Shivraj Chouhan on Thursday said protecting the dignity and self-respect of farmers and farming remained a top priority of the Centre, asserting that he considered himself a servant of farmers and would not allow their honour to be compromised.Addressing a Kisan Chaupal at Taraori in Haryana’s Karnal district, where he formally launched the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, in presence of Haryana agriculture and farmers welfare minister Shyam Singh Rana, the Union minister said serving farmers was his greatest form of worship.He called for a balance between modern agricultural practices and traditional knowledge to protect soil health while ensuring that farming remained economically viable.“This turban is a symbol of farmers’ honour and self-respect, and I will never allow it to be lowered,” he said, reiterating that the Centre, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, was committed to safeguarding the interests and dignity of farmers.Senior scientists from the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI), and a large number of progressive farmers attended the interaction.Emphasising the need to protect soil fertility, Chouhan cautioned farmers against excessive and indiscriminate use of chemical fertilisers. He clarified that the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ was not aimed at opposing any particular fertiliser but at promoting its balanced and scientific application.Comparing unnecessary fertiliser use to taking calcium supplements without a medical need, he said excessive application of chemicals could damage the soil’s fertility and increase cultivation costs.“Farmers must come out of the race of copying one another. If one farmer applies four bags of fertiliser, another should not feel compelled to apply four-and-a-half bags. Get the soil tested through a soil health card and apply only the nutrients required by the crop,” he said.Addressing farmers’ concerns about natural farming, Chouhan shared his personal experience, saying he cultivated vegetables, fruits and crops on his own farm and practised natural farming himself.He said natural farming should not be considered a loss-making proposition, provided farmers followed the prescribed scientific methods.Chouhan advised farmers owning three to five acres to begin natural farming on at least one acre, learn the complete process and assess its benefits before expanding it to the remaining land.Haryana gets ₹1,343 crore financial nod for 28,422 pucca housesAdditionally, in his capacity as Union minister for rural development, Chouhan handed over a letter of financial approval for ₹1,343.06 crore to the Haryana government, through for the construction of 28,422 pucca houses for poor families in Haryana under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G).The Union minister also praised Haryana’s farmers for the reported sharp decline in stubble-burning incidents this year, crediting their growing awareness and adoption of crop-residue management techniques, including the use of super seeders.

title: PM’s Pune visit deferred, metro inauguration date uncertain | Hindustan Times
description: Initially scheduled for completion in March 2025, the project has missed several deadlines due to construction delays and the clearance process
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s proposed visit to Pune district, scheduled for November 3, has been deferred, leaving the inauguration of the long-delayed Hinjewadi-Shivajinagar Metro Line 3 uncertain. November 16 is being considered as a possible revised date, but there is no official confirmation of the visit or the inauguration programme.Modi was scheduled to visit Baramati to inaugurate Prerna Sthal, a memorial on the premises of Vidya Pratishthan, an educational institution headed by Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar. The memorial features a statue of Lord Buddha and exhibits on other prominent personalities.Yugendra Pawar, Sharad Pawar’s grandnephew and a trustee of Vidya Pratishthan, confirmed on Thursday that the visit had been deferred. He said November 16 was a likely date but added that the institution had received no official communication confirming the revised schedule.The postponement has also cast uncertainty over the inauguration of the 23-km Hinjewadi-Shivajinagar Metro Line 3, which will connect Pune’s IT hub with the city centre.Officials of the Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA), which is implementing the project through a public-private partnership, did not respond to queries.Initially scheduled for completion in March 2025, the project has missed several deadlines due to construction delays and the clearance process. The first 12-km section received provisional clearance from the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (CMRS) in July. So far, 17 of the line’s 23 stations have received clearance.

title: Kejriwal questions Amit Shah over drug menace in BJP-ruled states | Hindustan Times
description: AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal challenged Shah to demonstrate results in Bihar, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Goa before making claims about Punjab
content: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday slammed Union home minister Amit Shah over the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP’s) “so-called campaign against drugs in Punjab”, questioning its failure to tackle drug menace in BJP-ruled states.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal challenged Shah to demonstrate results in Bihar, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Goa before making claims about Punjab. “Bihar, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Goa all have BJP governments. Why has the drug menace not been eradicated there? Have no deadlines been set for eliminating drugs in these states?” he posted on X, questioning the claims made by Shah at a public meeting in Delhi.The AAP leader asked the home minister whether he was now claiming that drugs would be eliminated in Punjab in the same way that he had supposedly eliminated them in Bihar. “Before speaking about Punjab, Shah must first demonstrate that he can eliminate drugs in BJP-ruled states,” he said.Kejriwal claimed that under the Bhagwant Mann government, the party had promised a safer Punjab, and was delivering on that promise. He said since 2022, more than 1.27 lakh arrests had been made in drug-related cases, 7,260 kilograms of heroin seized, and 1,288 criminal modules were busted. “This is only the beginning. We are committed to completely eliminating drugs and gangsters from Punjab,” he added.BJP ‘misusing’ drug issue ahead of polls: Sanjay SinghAAP Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh on Thursday accused the BJP of misusing central agencies and the drug issue for electoral gains while targeting the Bhagwant Mann government in Punjab.He said the BJP was attempting to divert attention from its own “failures” by politicising drugs ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.Singh was in Amritsar, where he appeared before a local court to record his statement in a defamation case filed by Shiromani Akal Dal (SAD) leader Bikram Singh Majithia.Launching an attack on opposition parties in Punjab, Singh said that the BJP was “systematically misusing” investigative agencies to win elections.

title: Stop overcooking your vegetables: Chef shares 7 tips to get the texture right | Hindustan Times
description: From steaming to uniformly chopping, check out these techniques which help you to avoid soggy or underdone veggies.
content: Overcooking is a common problem when preparing vegetables. You want to cook them well without turning them into a soggy, limp mess. Otherwise, a plate of vibrant veggies can become unappetising, even with the best of seasonings or a flavourful curry. This means you need to get the basics right, from choosing the right cooking method to knowing when to take them off the heat.ALSO READ: Are you cooking eggs the wrong way? Endocrinologist reveals the biggest mistake people makeWe asked a culinary expert for tips to make cooking vegetables easier. Most cooking advice often focuses on advanced techniques; the basics can get overlooked. Chef Ranveer Singh, a chef specialising in Indian and tandoor cuisine, shared simple tips to help you cook vegetables to the right texture without overdoing them.He said, “It's not necessary to cook vegetables until they are soft and lifeless. You should aim for those to be tender on the inside, a little bit crunchy and still tasty. However, it’s easy to forget the vegetables on the heat for just a couple of minutes more and end up with soggy broccoli, mushy asparagus, or limp beans. The trick to successful cooking of vegetables is knowing not only when to stop but also how to cook them.”Here are some of his hacks:1. Stop cooking by texture, not just by timeCooking times vary depending on the vegetable and the equipment used, so don't treat cookbook timings of cooking veggies for five to ten minutes as the standard.Start checking the vegetables early to avoid overcooking.A fork or knife should pierce a well-cooked vegetable easily, but it should also retain some firmness.2. Cut vegetables uniformlyCut vegetables into similar-sized pieces so they cook evenly. If a carrot is cut half the size of another carrot, the smaller piece may be cooked properly while the bigger piece may still remain hard.Smaller pieces cook faster; larger ones may remain hard.Uniform cuts help prevent some pieces from being overcooked and others remain underdone. 3. Blanch, then shockBlanching vegetables, including beans, peas, and broccoli, delivers a bright look with a fresh texture.After boiling the vegetables for a short period of time, throw them immediately into ice water so that the cooking process stops immediately.This retains the crunchiness of the vegetables by stopping the cooking process instead of cooking them with heat after boiling.4. Don't boil vegetables into submissionProlonged boiling can diminish the flavor, color and firmness of vegetables.Instead of letting them cook for a long time until soft, boil them just until they become tender.The vegetables should retain their own taste instead of tasting like something that has been boiled for thirty minutes.5. Use less water when appropriateUsing more water does not necessarily mean better cooking.When boiling vegetables, use just enough water to cover them rather than filling the pot unnecessarily.Consider steaming vegetables that do not need to be fully submerged in water.6. Try steamingSteaming vegetables is perhaps the easiest way to prepare them without soaking them in water.The process of steaming helps vegetables to maintain their original consistency and taste.Broccoli, carrots, cauliflower, and green beans can be steamed perfectly so that vegetables can become soft but still be firm. 7. Get your pan properly hot before sautéingAdding vegetables to a cold or just-warm pan will produce moisture from the vegetables, which will soften them.Start with a hot pan, add the oil first, and then the vegetables.A hot pan makes cooking fast and browning light while preventing the loss of crunchiness in vegetables.So, cooking vegetables well comes down to getting a few basics right. The chef's advice highlighted that it is important to watch for texture while cooking. With these expert-recommended tips, you cook vegetables better, and they taste better too, as all their flavours are intact.

title: Half of streetlights in Noida Sector 70 non-functional: Residents | Hindustan Times
description: Noida: Residents of Sector 70 have alleged that around half of the area’s streetlights, which cover about 800 houses, have remained dysfunctional for the past few months
content: Noida: Residents of Sector 70 have alleged that around half of the area’s streetlights, which cover about 800 houses, have remained dysfunctional for the past few months.They said the lack of adequate lighting has raised safety concerns, despite repeated complaints to the Noida authority. Officials, however, said repairs had begun and all faulty streetlights would be fixed by the end of the week.According to resident welfare association (RWA) officials, the sector has around 800 homes and comprises an estimated 2,500 residents. The sector has two RWAs representing different areas: one for blocks A and B, and the other representing the 5 per cent abadi plots in the area, a category of residential plots allotted to farmers whose land is acquired for development.Both RWA officials have raised concerns regarding this issue and said that repeated complaints to the authority over the past two to three months had yielded little progress.“The condition of streetlights in Sector 70 is very poor. The RWA team is exhausted from repeatedly lodging complaints with the authorities, yet the officials remain unwilling to listen,” claimed Amit Chauhan, president of the RWA representing blocks A and B.Janter Yadav, president of the 5 per cent RWA in Sector 70, said several high-mast lights in the area were also not functioning, leaving the neighbourhood in darkness at night.“The sector has three parks, most of the high-mast lights in the parks are also not working. It gets completely dark at night. We have complained to the Noida Authority multiple times over the past two to three months, but there has been no concrete resolution,” he claimed.Both RWAs have also sent multiple written complaints on the matter to the Noida Authority regarding the issue in early October, reviewed by HT.Responding to the complaints, Amarjit Singh, senior manager in the Noida authority’s electrical and mechanical department, said they were “looking into this matter.”An official, requesting anonymity, said the authority had received the complaints and repair work was already underway. Some streetlights had been repaired, and all faulty lights would be fixed by the end of the week, the official said, attributing the malfunction to voltage fluctuations.

title: Jakhar brings murder victim’s family outside assembly, seeks FIR | Hindustan Times
description: Jakhar was addressing journalists outside the Punjab Vidhan Sabha alongside Kumar’s mother and other family members, who had arrived to seek justice
content: Former Punjab BJP president Sunil Jakhar on Thursday demanded an impartial investigation into the murder of Ajay Kumar in Sant Nagar, Abohar, and the registration of an FIR against those responsible based on the statement the victim made to the police before his death.Jakhar was addressing journalists outside the Punjab Vidhan Sabha alongside Kumar’s mother and other family members, who had arrived to seek justice. The family staged a protest outside the assembly but was later detained by the police.Jakhar said he would bring the family to the assembly premises every day to ensure that their voices reached the ears of what he described as a “deaf government”. BJP leader Ashwani Kumar Sharma was also present.Kumar was shot in Sant Nagar, Abohar, on September 27. He remained under treatment for several days after sustaining critical injuries but died on October 19. His family has been staging protests in Abohar, demanding justice. According to the family, his postmortem examination has yet to be conducted.Kumar’s mother and other family members alleged that his brother had testified in the 2015 Bheem murder case, which led to Shiv Lal Doda and his nephew being sentenced to 20 years in prison. They further alleged that Kumar was murdered following Doda’s recent release on bail.

title: Man booked for abetment to suicide after 18-yr-old woman death | Hindustan Times
description: Noida: Months after an 18-year-old woman hanged herself at her relative’s home in a village located near Noida’s Sector 73 in May, a Kanpur-based man has been booked on charges of abetment to suicide over the death, police said on Thursday
content: Noida: Months after an 18-year-old woman hanged herself at her relative’s home in a village located near Noida’s Sector 73 in May, a Kanpur-based man has been booked on charges of abetment to suicide over the death, police said on Thursday.The step came as the victim family accused the suspect of sexual and mental harassment, said officials.According to police, the woman, originally from Kanpur Dehat, was a forensic science student at a Mathura university. She died on May 14 while staying at a relatives’ house in Sarfabad village where she had come to appear for an exam.In his police complaint, her father said, “My daughter was sexually and mentally harassed by a man, who introduced himself as a leader of a political party…She was befriended and pressurised for marriage by the suspect. In November 2025, I also received a message from her that the suspect assaulted her,” reads the FIR, seen by HT.The family has alleged that the suspect was pressuring her to marry after she turned 18, said officials.“On the day of the incident, the man approached our home to inform us that my daughter was going to end her life by hanging herself,” the victim’s father said in the FIR, adding, “Due to constant threat and fear, my daughter ended her life.”Officials said they have seized the victim’s phone and efforts are underway to retrieve its data.“We are waiting for data retrieval from the victim’s phone. Meanwhile, on the victim family’s allegations a case under section 108 (abetment to suicide) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita was registered against the suspect, and a team is being formed to nab him in Kanpur,” said Pramod Kumar Shukla, station house officer, Sector 113 police station.Police officials, however, said that they are yet to ascertain if the suspect is related to any political party and a team has been formed to arrest him from Kanpur while the investigation is underway.

title: Cheaper, faster learning accelerates commerce-first product launches | Mumbai news
description: MUMBAI: The future of product launches in India is decisively commerce-first, believes Sairam Ranganathan, head of e-commerce at WPP Media India  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: The future of product launches in India is decisively commerce-first, believes Sairam Ranganathan, head of e-commerce at WPP Media India. Product launches are no longer just campaign driven. Thanks to the emergence of e-commerce and quick-commerce, the landscape is dynamic, with these platforms becoming more than just points of transaction and turning into influential environments for product discovery, trials, conversion and other learnings on buying habits, Ranganathan said recently, while releasing a framework for new product launches in a digital world.The commerce-first launch playbook has been compiled in view of the unmistakable shift in consumer behaviour where shoppers are increasingly discovering and ordering products online. E-retail is expected to touch a Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) of $170 billion by 2030, up from $65 billion in 2025, the WPP Media playbook noted, adding that quick-commerce is already a mainline channel with 16-17% share of the e-commerce GMV.The advantage of commerce-first launches is that it helps identify and validate the opportunities early on as brands can test their propositions and learn from actual shopper behaviour, the playbook noted. Ranganathan said quick-commerce is the new sales touch point which further compresses the trial and learning cycle. Little surprise then that many companies, both in the direct-to-consumer segment as well as large, traditional FMCG firms are launching products only for quick-commerce platforms, he said.Content creators or social media influencers, retail media and quick-commerce are accelerating discovery, product trial and generating faster market feedback, he said. Once the learnings are in place, companies can scale whatever is working for them. With 90% of Indian retail still being offline, early analysis on the basis of digital demand and consumer endorsement of products segues into expanding them into general trade (neighbourhood kiranas) and modern trade (big box retail), he added.Adarsh Menon, partner at Fireside Ventures, an early-stage venture capital fund with sizeable investments in a portfolio of digital-first consumer brands, said that even legacy brands have re-sequenced their launches from general trade to digital first. “And these are traditional FMCG companies that are seeing and accepting it as a legitimate way to introduce new products,” said Menon. Several big companies have launched Modern Trade and e-commerce exclusive brand extensions in fabric conditioners, coffees and liquid detergents, for instance.The WPP Media playbook says that the time-poor, affluent, urban consumers are looking for convenience, premiumization and product relevance. For them, availability of a product at the point of need beats brand recall. But the next phase of e-retail growth is coming from well beyond the metros. What works for the tier 2 plus markets are the affordable entry packs, trust-first messaging through credible reviews and reach through local creator eco system and regional language content.Fireside’s Menon said the difference between old-school and new-age launches is that in the old school ways, product launch used to be an “enormous, almost irreversible, bet”. It required months of research, loads of inventory, distributor and retailer negotiations to stock products, building media etc with a commitment of huge capital. “Now a product launch is more of an experiment where a brand can list in a few 100 pin codes and then within a week can know if there is any traction,” he said.Besides, brands have more information that they can work with as digital platforms sit on real time shopping signals. But do platforms share the data? “It may not be complete data but it is still way better than what they ever got from their traditional distribution networks,” Menon said.“Online platforms definitely share more though I still call them walled gardens. Also, the platforms have realised the value of the data and they are now monetizing it through their analytics products for consumer brands to use,” Menon said.Clearly, digital product launches are not a quick-fix to all the problems “but there is a fundamental improvement in the cost and speed of learning which is good,” Menon said.Yet he warns of the pitfalls of blindly following sampling. “A sample size of 50,000 online consumers, for instance, doesn’t represent the whole country,” he said. So, this requires being mindful of that fact before scaling up operations. Secondly, a trial may be faster online but “trial isn’t traction”, Menon said. Brands still need to build repeat purchases for the long term. “No doubt it has become cheaper to discover whether you have a winner or not. But the platform or the discovery doesn’t convert a product into a winner. You still need a great product, great proposition, and all the other traditional blocks required to build a great brand such as good pricing and distribution as well,” Menon said.While the initial brand lessons can be learnt digitally, for scale, the product must go offline into general trade and modern trade outlets. “I like to repeat that today, the digital world is where brands are being born, but omnichannel (digital plus physical retail) is where they will grow up,” he said.Besides, brands born online should not be built keeping only a two- or five-year horizon in mind. “To create a lasting brand, you have to live in a consumer’s mind and not just on a shelf or a phone,” Menon said.

title: Thieves break into locked flat at upscale high-rise in Gr Noida | Hindustan Times
description: Greater Noida: Unidentified suspects allegedly burgled a locked flat of an upscale high-rise society in Greater Noida’s sector Zeta 1 late Wednesday night and made off with jewellery among other valuable things, police officials said on Thursday
content: Greater Noida: Unidentified suspects allegedly burgled a locked flat of an upscale high-rise society in Greater Noida’s sector Zeta 1 late Wednesday night and made off with jewellery among other valuable things, police officials said on Thursday.According to police, there were no signs of forced entry into the flat as the main door remained intact.“Prima facie, it appears that the suspect was aware of the jewellery and the keys… Of the three rooms, only one room had been checked (by suspects), where two almirahs were kept. The suspect touched one almirah to get the keys to another safe, where the jewellery was stored,” said an investigator.In her police complaint, seen by HT, the victim, a teacher by profession and resident of ATS Dolce society, said, “On Thursday, around 12.20am, when my daughter and I returned from our native place in Bihar, we found the almirah locks opened and the items including jewellery were missing from it.”Officials said the woman who lives with her parents in the flat in Tower 5, had gone to attend a family function in her native town in Bihar on October 17. “We were alerted by them about the theft on Thursday around 10am,” said the officer, adding that there were no CCTV cameras installed on the balcony or in the passage area leading to the flat.Investigation found that the family had hired a house help around three months ago who is being interrogated, said officials.The victim’s relative said, “The house help was hired through a society member. The estimated value of the jewellery would be revealed after my victim relative’s father, a retired government employee from Jamshedpur in Jharkhand, returns home on Friday. We found liquor bottles and two empty glasses in the room.”Police said a case of theft was registered at the Surajpur police station on Thursday and an investigation is underway and CCTV cameras installed in the vicinity are being scanned.

title: Gautam Budh Nagar: Liquor shops, bars to stay closed on Friday | Hindustan Times
description: GREATER NOIDA:All liquor shops, bars and other establishments selling alcoholic beverages in Gautam Budh Nagar district will remain closed on Friday, October 23, until the conclusion of polling for the 2026 biennial Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections
content: GREATER NOIDA:All liquor shops, bars and other establishments selling alcoholic beverages in Gautam Budh Nagar district will remain closed on Friday, October 23, until the conclusion of polling for the 2026 biennial Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections.The district administration has declared a dry day to ensure peaceful voting, officials said.The order applies to all licensed outlets selling liquor and other intoxicating substances, including country liquor shops, composite and model shops, bars and wholesale and retail liquor establishments. Military and paramilitary canteens will also have to suspend liquor sales during the restricted period.District magistrate Medha Roopam, acting as the licensing authority, issued the order under Section 59 of the United Provinces Excise Act and Section 135C of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.“The dry day has been declared on October 23, until the conclusion of polling, with the objective of maintaining public peace and ensuring free, fair and peaceful elections,” read the order issued late Wednesday.The directive follows the state government instructions to enforce a dry day on polling day across Uttar Pradesh, except Kanpur Nagar, Kanpur Dehat and Unnao.The restrictions also cover retail and wholesale liquor licences, including those for foreign liquor, country liquor and other specified intoxicating substances. Establishments holding licences to serve liquor at designated premises and those involved in the manufacture, storage and supply of liquor are also included.The administration has directed officials to prevent illegal sale and smuggling of liquor during the period. “Licensees shall ensure strict compliance with the closure order. No compensation or allowance will be paid on account of the closure,” the order stated.Violations will invite strict action against the licence holder concerned, the administration said.“We have been directed to ensure strict compliance with the dry-day order. We will also keep a check on illegal sale and smuggling of liquor during the period,” said Subodh Kumar, district excise officer.

title: FDA inspects all 102 methanol licence holders in Pune div; 15 licences cancelled | Hindustan Times
description: The Pune division emerged as a key focus because it has the highest concentration of methanol-related companies in Maharashtra.
content: Pune: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) inspected all 102 licensed methanol-related companies in the Pune division as part of a crackdown on violations involving the chemical’s storage, handling and sale, officials said on Thursday. Following the drive, 28 licences were suspended and 15 were cancelled.According to FDA officials, the state-wide inspection drive was launched after the Pune hooch tragedy. The Pune division emerged as a key focus because it has the highest concentration of methanol-related companies in Maharashtra. The FDA has been conducting inspections and tightening enforcement over the past four months, they said.Girish Hukare, Joint Commissioner, FDA (Drug) Pune division, said, “No cases of illegal methanol sales were found during the inspections. The 28 licence suspensions were linked to technical and documentation-related deficiencies, including issues with record keeping and the appointment of computer personnel. The 15 licence cancellations were related to violations involving the storage, handling and distribution of methanol.”As per officials, the existing rules already govern the purchase, sale, storage and handling of methanol. The FDA’s focus is on enforcing these provisions rather than framing new regulations, they said.“The inspection of all licensed establishments has been completed, but continued monitoring is necessary to ensure that the rules are followed consistently,” said Hukare.FDA officials added that inspections and verification would continue, and action would be taken against companies found to be violating the rules. They said the aim is to prevent methanol misuse and ensure compliance with safety requirements.

title: Yeida moves NCLT over  ₹1000 crore dues by Suraksha Group | Hindustan Times
description: Yeida has approached the NCLT, seeking intervention over the alleged delay by Suraksha Group in paying  ₹1,000 crore in hiked land compensation to farmers
content: The Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (Yeida) has approached the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), seeking intervention over the alleged delay by Suraksha Group in paying ₹1,000 crore in hiked land compensation to farmers, Yeida CEO RK Singh said Thursday.The total compensation amounts to ₹1,334 crore, representing a 64.7% raise promised to farmers whose land was acquired for development projects. Yeida said the group has paid ₹334 crore, leaving ₹1,000 crore outstanding.In 2013, Yeida promised farmers enhanced compensation for their acquired land. The amount was to be recovered from land allottees, including developers and individuals who purchased land from the authority."The resolution plan submitted by the Suraksha Group before the NCLT to take over Jaypee Infratech Limited projects provided for payment of ₹1,334 crore as hiked compensation. However, the group has delayed the payment of ₹1,000 crore. We have issued notices to the firm, but the dues are yet to be cleared. We have approached the NCLT to expedite the payment so that farmers get their money on time,” Singh said.Also Read: Suraksha Group completes construction of nearly 6,000 housing units at Jaypee's stalled Wish Town in NoidaFarmers from at least 40 villages are awaiting the hiked land compensationAbhijit Gohil, CEO of Suraksha Group, said, “We have paid ₹334 crore and the remaining amount will be paid soon. We are yet to get possession of some portions of farmers’ land. Once we get possession, we will start paying the remaining hiked compensation. We will comply with the resolution plan.”Suraksha Group took over Jaypee Infratech Limited in 2024 following an NCLT order and is developing the delayed Jaypee Wishtown housing projects.Also Read: ₹51 crore">LuLu leases hypermarket space at Greater Noida Mall for 15 years at nearly ₹51 crore

title: Ghaziabad: FIR filed over ‘obscene’ songs at dandiya event | Hindustan Times
description: Ghaziabad: An FIR has been registered against unidentified organisers of a Dandiya event for causing disturbance by allegedly playing “loud music and obscene songs” following a complaint filed by a resident of a high-rise in Wave City township in Ghaziabad, police officials said on Thursday
content: Ghaziabad: An FIR has been registered against unidentified organisers of a Dandiya event for causing disturbance by allegedly playing “loud music and obscene songs” following a complaint filed by a resident of a high-rise in Wave City township in Ghaziabad, police officials said on Thursday.Officials said they have booked unidentified organisers of the event that was allegedly held behind the residential tower of the complainant, a 39-year-old woman.In the FIR seen by HT, the woman alleged the loud music and objectionable songs caused her disturbance and also hurt her religious sentiments, forcing her to finally leave to stay at a hotel on October 18 night.“We registered an FIR on October 20 upon the complaint given by the woman. Police were also called to intervene while the loud music was being played but the event continued despite requests. Police have booked unidentified organisers in this connection,” said Priyashri Pal, assistant commissioner of police (ACP) of Wave City Circle.“Items, songs, and Bhojpuri songs were being played very loud on DJ console, and this hurt my religious sentiments. The loud DJ was being played since evening of October 18 during the Dandiya event. I called up the police and the organisers were asked to lower the sound. After police left, the loud music started again and continued till late night. The police were informed again… Finding no solution, I had to leave my flat and stay at a hotel,” the FIR stated citing her.The FIR was registered under the BNS section 296 (obscene acts and songs) at the Wave City police station.“An investigation is underway and legal action will be initiated in accordance with the law. The section in the FIR is bailable,” the ACP added.

title: Noida Sector 56 residents flag ‘2-week long’ water shortage | Hindustan Times
description: Noida: Residents of Noida’s Sector 56 have alleged they have been facing a water shortage for about a fortnight, with water pressure remaining quite low even when the supply is available
content: Noida: Residents of Noida’s Sector 56 have alleged they have been facing a water shortage for about a fortnight, with water pressure remaining quite low even when the supply is available.Officials of the Noida authority’s Jal Board, however, said the problem has existed for only last few days only and is actually related to annual maintenance.The sector has a population of approximately 10,000 people, residents said.Highlighting the persisting situation, Sanjay Mavi, president of the Sector 56 RWA, said, “Residents are forced to purchase water from private tankers to meet their daily needs. Even when water is supplied, the pressure is extremely low. Although we reside in Noida, described as one of the most developed cities, we lack access to water which is a basic necessity for survival.”Mavi alleged that the problem persists despite repeated complaints to the Noida authority.Jitendra Kumar, another resident, said the shortage had disrupted their daily life due to the inconvenience in household chores. “It is the festive season, and we are struggling for water, a basic requirement…Me and my wife had to seek held from our Sector 93 resident daughter for laundry. We visited her home over the weekend, carrying our dirty clothes with us,” he said.Kumar said he even got his water pipes repaired in the hope that it might help but to no avail.HT has seen request messages sent by residents to Noida authority officials on October 15 and as recently as Thursday, seeking a resolution to the issue.Meanwhile, Ashok Verma, senior manager at the Jal Board, explained that the Ganga water supply is halted for 15 to 29 days annually for regular maintenance, which can affect water supply. “I am aware of these concerns. The supply was stopped on October 20, so the issue has been going on for only a couple of days and shall be resolved soon,” he said, disputing residents’ claims that the shortage had persisted for about a fortnight.

title: 22 methanol firms appeal to minister against FDA action after Pune hooch deaths | Hindustan Times
description: The companies submitted a written representation to the minister last week. Sources said a few legislators also supported the move.
content: PUNE: Twenty-two methanol companies, whose licences were suspended or cancelled following the deaths of 22 people in a suspected spurious liquor tragedy in Pune in May, have appealed to Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) minister Narhari Zirwal, seeking relief from the action initiated by FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe.The companies submitted a written representation to the minister last week. Sources said a few legislators also supported the move.Zirwal, however, denied receiving any letters from legislators seeking to reverse the action against the companies. “No letters have been received from the elected members requesting the revocation of the cancellation or suspension of these companies’ licenses. The investigations are ongoing, and accordingly, action will be taken based on the probe’s findings,” Zirwal told the Hindustan Times on Thursday.He further said that filing appeals is part of the established procedure and that decisions would be made after examining the cases during hearings.“Eventually, in such cases, companies come together and approach the minister against the action. Filing an appeal is part of the process. Decisions are taken after due consideration during hearings. If there are serious irregularities, the methanol companies’ licences will remain suspended or cancelled,” the minister said.In the Pune division, 28 licences were suspended and 15 cancelled. Officials said hearings in some cases are underway, while others are pending.Under the appeal process, companies can challenge the FDA commissioner’s decisions before the minister. If their appeals are rejected, they may approach the Bombay high court.Following the hooch tragedy, Mundhe ordered inspections of methanol manufacturers and dealers across the state to check compliance with safety and regulatory requirements. The drive resulted in notices being issued to 405 companies. The licences of 309 companies were suspended for one month, while 69 companies had their licences cancelled.According to FDA officials, inspections revealed serious irregularities in the production, storage and sale of methanol at the 69 companies, prompting the permanent cancellation of their licences. Of these, 15 were in Pune, five in Nashik, 17 in Konkan, eight in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and 20 in Mumbai.Methanol, an industrial chemical, can cause fatal poisoning when consumed. The state government made it mandatory for producers to add a bittering agent and a colouring liquid to methanol to deter its use in illicit liquor production.According to a state government report, 446 people have died in toxic liquor incidents across Maharashtra to date.

title: After suspected dengue death of girl, PMC reviews preventive measures | Hindustan Times
description: At a special meeting on October 23, chaired by additional municipal commissioner Pavneet Kaur, officials reviewed hospital preparedness, diagnostic and treatment facilities, and measures to prevent mosquito breeding.
content: PUNE: The suspected dengue death of a nine-year-old girl from Lohegaon has prompted the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) to review its preparedness to tackle mosquito-borne diseases, including dengue and malaria. At a special meeting on Thursday, chaired by additional municipal commissioner Pavneet Kaur, officials reviewed hospital preparedness, diagnostic and treatment facilities, and measures to prevent mosquito breeding.Hindustan Times reported on Thursday that the girl, a Class 4 student from Khese Park in Lohegaon, died at Ruby Hall Clinic (RHC) on October 18 after her condition deteriorated rapidly. Her dengue test was positive on a non-ELISA NS1 antigen test. The death will be treated as a suspected dengue fatality until the PMC’s health audit committee establishes the cause. The civic body has sought her treatment records and test reports from the hospital for further investigation.According to PMC data, the city recorded 2,413 dengue cases between January 1 and October 20. Of these, 568 were reported in August, 726 in September and 553 in October.As part of its preventive drive, civic teams visited around 14 lakh homes and inspected 28,31,386 containers and water-storage points. Aedes mosquito larvae were detected in 18,885 containers across 13,000 homes. The civic body issued notices to 2,664 properties and collected fines totalling ₹6.3 lakh, officials said.At Thursday’s meeting, officials reviewed the availability of diagnostic tests and treatment facilities. Rapid diagnostic kits for free dengue testing have been made available at all PMC dispensaries. Free confirmatory tests are also available at sentinel centres at Dr Naidu Hospital, Dr Kotnis Hospital and Kamala Nehru Hospital, said Dr Nina Borade, the PMC’s health chief.All government and private hospitals have been directed to register patient details on the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) portal and avoid duplicate entries, civic officials said.Private hospitals have 8,400 beds, including 670 intensive care unit (ICU) beds, available for dengue patients. Civic hospitals have 333 beds, including six ICU beds. On average, around 50% of these beds are vacant, according to the civic body.Dr Naidu Hospital has reserved 50 beds exclusively for dengue patients, of which 10 to 15 are occupied daily. Treatment at the hospital is free. Officials have been directed to ensure that patients with severe symptoms receive immediate treatment at Dr Naidu or Kamala Nehru Hospital. The use of mosquito nets has also been made mandatory in dengue wards.The civic body has directed its teams to prioritise spraying and other preventive measures in areas reporting higher case numbers. Instead of indiscriminate fogging in open spaces, teams have been asked to carry out fogging for 20 minutes inside the homes of patients and in adjoining enclosed areas. Biological larvicides will also be used regularly to treat stored water, particularly in settlements where residents store water during supply cuts.“The PMC is also running an awareness campaign through audio messages played on garbage-collection vehicles. Audio files have been distributed to all 15 ward offices. Housing societies have been asked to keep water tanks and storage containers clean, while schools are conducting essay and drawing competitions to educate students. Residents should observe one dry day every week to prevent mosquito breeding,” Kaur said.Standing committee flags delay in spraying after child’s deathThe PMC’s review came amid criticism at Thursday’s standing committee meeting, where NCP corporator and committee member Suhas Tingre questioned delays in insecticide spraying and alleged inaction by the health department.Tingre said an eight-year-old girl, a close relative of his, died of malaria on Sunday. He also cited the case of a two-and-a-half-year-old girl from his ward who, he said, had spent eight days in the intensive care unit at Sassoon General Hospital after contracting dengue. According to Tingre, insecticide spraying had not been carried out at the child’s home even eight days after she was discharged.To highlight the issue, Tingre played a phone call from the child’s family over the meeting hall’s microphone. He alleged that the health department had previously cited the expiry of its spraying contract and a shortage of staff to explain its inability to act.“Reasons such as an expired contract and a shortage of manpower cannot be accepted when people’s lives are at risk,” Tingre said, demanding immediate preventive measures, regular spraying and adequate staffing.He warned that the civic body’s failure to act could trigger a wider protest. “The health of Pune’s citizens cannot be compromised. The administration must take concrete and immediate steps to control dengue and malaria,” he said.The PMC has appealed to residents to prevent water from stagnating, keep water tanks covered and cooperate with inspection teams. It has also urged people experiencing symptoms to seek medical advice promptly, maintaining that adequate hospital beds are available across the city.

title: Vegetable trader found dead after assault over onion prices | Hindustan Times
description: A 35-year-old vegetable trader was found dead at his home in Jamalpur on Wednesday morning, hours after he was allegedly assaulted by several men following an argument over onion prices in Manesar’s Kasan, police said on Thursday
content: A 35-year-old vegetable trader was found dead at his home in Jamalpur on Wednesday morning, hours after he was allegedly assaulted by several men following an argument over onion prices in Manesar’s Kasan, police said on Thursday.The deceased was identified as Atma Ram, who lived with his family in rented accommodation in Jamalpur.Police said Ram was selling vegetables in Kasan on Tuesday evening when he got into an argument with a customer over the price of onions. The customer allegedly called a few associates, who assaulted Ram.Ram returned home that night and told his family about the assault. Police said he had a visible injury on his leg but had dinner and gone to sleep as usual. His family found him dead the following morning.Sunil Kumar, station house officer of Bilaspur police station, said a medical board conducted the autopsy on Thursday.“The autopsy report on the exact cause of death is awaited. If doctors establish that he died of assault injuries, an FIR under Section 103(1) (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita will be registered and the suspects arrested,” he said.Police said they were questioning family members to establish the circumstances of the assault and its exact location.

title: Four held for assaulting family over garbage dumping dispute in Gurugram | Hindustan Times
description: Investigators said the woman from the victim family had allegedly repeatedly dumped kitchen waste on a vacant plot in front of the other family’s house
content: Three men were arrested and a minor was apprehended on Thursday for allegedly assaulting a couple and their two minor children over repeated garbage dumping on a vacant private land in Behrampur, Sector 59, said police.According to police, the accused included a 45-year-old man, his 75-year-old father, both residents of Behrampur, Sector 65 and their 28-year-old relative from Faridabad’s Bhaisrawali. The apprehended minor is the 45-year-old man’s 16-year-old son. The incident took place on the evening of October 16.Police said the daughter suffered a head injury and a deep cut on her forearm, while the other three sustained multiple fractures in their forearms and legs.Investigators said the woman had repeatedly dumped kitchen waste on a vacant plot in front of their house. The plot belonged to the neighbouring family, leading to disputes between the two sides in the past.On October 16, the woman’s son was on a motorcycle with her to deliver lunch to his father when their vehicle was involved in a minor collision with the neighbour’s son, who was also riding a motorcycle. An argument followed between the two sides.“Later that evening, the husband went to the neighbor’s house to complain about his son. A heated argument broke out, following which the man returned home,” said police.Police said the neighbours and others allegedly attacked him at the entrance of his house with rods and sticks. They also assaulted his wife and children when they tried to intervene before fleeing the spot. Neighbours rushed the injured family to a private hospital in Sector 57. They were discharged on Wednesday, police added.The injured man said he received six stitches on his head and suffered a fracture on his left forearm. “My son suffered fractures in both forearms and his right knee. My wife fractured her left leg, while my daughter sustained a severe head injury after being hit with a rod,” he said.“Our condition was critical and I could only give my statement to the police two days after the incident,” he said.Sandeep Turan, spokesperson, Gurugram police, said the incident was captured on a CCTV camera. “The three arrested men would be kept in lock-up overnight and granted bail on Friday,” he said.Based on the man’s complaint, an FIR was registered against the suspects for assault, wrongful restraint, rioting and criminal intimidation at Sector 65 police station on Sunday.

title: MSRTC divisional controllers to be held responsible for unclean toilets at ST stands | Hindustan Times
description: The move aims to improve sanitation standards and ensure better facilities for passengers at ST bus stations across Maharashtra
content: The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) has issued a warning that divisional controllers will be held directly responsible if toilets at bus stations are found unclean.The corporation charges passengers a ₹2 sanitation fee, making it essential to provide clean and hygienic facilities in return. The administration has made it clear that negligence in maintaining cleanliness will not be tolerated, and that responsibility will not be able to be shifted solely to contractors. The move aims to improve sanitation standards and ensure better facilities for passengers at ST bus stations across Maharashtra.The warning was issued on Thursday by state transport minister and MSRTC chairman Pratap Sarnaik during a cleanliness review meeting. Senior officials, including departmental heads, regional managers and divisional controllers, attended the meeting to review sanitation arrangements at bus stations.During the meeting, the minister stressed that providing clean toilet facilities to passengers is one of the corporation’s fundamental responsibilities. He pointed out that passengers pay a sanitation fee of ₹2 without raising objections and are therefore entitled to receive basic cleanliness facilities in return. He said that the corporation must fulfil the passengers’ legitimate expectations and ensure that sanitation standards are maintained across its bus stations.The minister also highlighted that poorly maintained toilets directly affect the public image of the MSRTC and instructed officials to remain vigilant about cleanliness. He directed them to carry out regular inspections of toilets, ensure consistent monitoring of sanitation arrangements and make contractors accountable for cleaning work as stipulated in their agreements.Emphasising that the responsibility for cleanliness extends beyond contractors, Sarnaik said, “Senior officials must personally monitor conditions at bus stations under their jurisdiction instead of shifting the entire burden to agencies hired for sanitation work. If passengers are denied clean facilities, the concerned divisional controllers will be held accountable.”

title: Anahat Singh beats sixth-seed Salma Hany in a thrilling match to reach Silicon Valley Open semifinals | Hindustan Times
description: The 18-year-old now will face Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam, who recently beat her in the Asian Games gold medal match.
content: Teenage squash star Anahat Singh continues her great run in the Silicon Valley Open in Redwood City (USA) on Friday. After upsetting world number three Egyptian Nour El Sherbini on Thursday to reach the quarterfinals, the 18-year-old Indian dispatched another Egyptian and sixth-seed Salma Hany in a thrilling match to reach the last-4.Anahat lost the first game in quick time 11-4, but after that, she made a superb comeback and won the next game, 11-8. Hany responded with another quick 11-4 win. Under pressure, Anahat upped her game big time and thrashed her opponent, ranked 14th in the world, in the next two games 11-2, 11-5 and took the contest 3-2.Anahat will now play Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam in the semis. The third seed Subramaniam recently beat the Indian 11-4, 11-4, 11-7 in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games gold medal match. Anahat, who picked up two medals in the Asian Games, will look to avenge that defeat for sure. "It feels great. Coming into the match, I had never played her before, so I did not really know what to expect. I have watched her play so many times, and she is highly experienced on the PSA World Tour. I was just looking forward to seeing how I would match up against her. I did not start off well. "The first game was 11-4, which was a pretty bad start. However, I wanted to find a way to make my way back into the match and put up a fight. Whether it resulted in a win or a loss, I did not want to let it go too easily. I gave it my all in the second game and tried to make it one-all. We kept winning games alternately, so it was quite a roller-coaster. I am happy I got through it," Ahahat said after winning her match.

title: 2016 drowning of 14 students at Murud beach: HC strikes down FIR against 17 people | Hindustan Times
description: MUMBAI: Ten years after 14 third-year students of a Pune college drowned at Murud beach, the Bombay High Court on Thursday quashed criminal proceedings against 17 people, including the institute’s chairman, principal, teachers and non-teaching staff, ruling that they cannot be held “criminally negligent for an unforeseeable event occurring beyond their direct control or operational purview”
content: MUMBAI: Ten years after 14 third-year students of a Pune college drowned at Murud beach, the Bombay High Court on Thursday quashed criminal proceedings against 17 people, including the institute’s chairman, principal, teachers and non-teaching staff, ruling that they cannot be held “criminally negligent for an unforeseeable event occurring beyond their direct control or operational purview”.A single-judge bench of justice Milind Jadhav said that third-year college students are mature and possess a reasonable degree of life experience. They are expected to understand the distinction between right and wrong and to appreciate the likely consequences of their actions, it added.The court also said that if vicarious liability can be foisted on the institute’s trustees, teaching and non-teaching staff members, similar liability can be imposed on state authorities, which are responsible for ensuring that all public beaches have adequate signage, warnings, and beach safety and rescue measures.The incident occurred on February 1, 2016, when 116 students, faculty, and staff members of the Abeda Inamdar Senior College of Arts, Science and Commerce in Pune went for a picnic to Murud beach in Raigad. In the afternoon, 41 third-year students entered the sea, and around 20 were swept away. Local residents managed to rescue six of them, but the remaining 14 drowned.On April 19, 2016, the Murud police registered an FIR against 17 people for causing death by negligence. Five office-bearers of the educational trust that runs the college, including chairman PA Inamdar, the principal, faculty members, and non-teaching staff accompanying the students, were among those booked.The 17 accused subsequently approached the high court, seeking to quash the criminal proceedings. They argued that there was no evidence to invoke the charge of causing death by negligence against the office bearers, teaching and non-teaching members of the college.Additional public prosecutor Rajeshree Newton opposed the petition, arguing that the accused were directly responsible for ensuring the students’ safety, and the death of the 14 students was a direct result of their negligence.
