Newton justified the registration of the FIR, stating that the accused ought to have taken precautionary measures, especially when a large number of students went to a spot where there were chances of life-threatening accidents.However, the court refused to accept Newton’s argument, saying that there was no evidence indicating negligence on the part of the staff members that could be said to have resulted in the drowning of the 14 students.The court noted that the third-year students had gone to the beach after lunch at a hotel while the two professors supervising them were resting. The students ventured into the sea, after which 20 of them were swept away by the sea current and 14 unfortunately lost their lives, it added.The bench also said that the mere occurrence of an accident resulting in death or the alleged absence of ordinary care does not by itself render them liable for an offence punishable under section 304A (causing death by negligence) of the Indian Penal Code.

title: Napa Valley's wineries feel Trump's tariff squeeze | Travel
description: Napa Valley's wineries feel Trump's tariff squeeze  | Travel
content: Napa Valley rocketed to international fame when its vintages shocked French rivals in a high-profile blind tasting contest that instantly turned the California corner into a wine-lovers' destination.Now, Donald Trump's unpredictable tariff policies and attacks on traditional allies are souring the area's relationship with the foreign tourists and international markets it has grown to depend on."Napa Valley is proudly one of the most global, if not the most global destination in the United States for wine," Linsey Gallagher, president of Visit Napa Valley, an organization representing the region's hotel industry, told AFP."But at the moment that piece of the business is a little bit challenged."Napa announced itself to the global wine-drinking public in dramatic fashion in 1976, when two of its vintages, a red and a white, won the Judgment of Paris, a blind tasting judged by nine experts, most of them French."Napa did not have any publicity, and then all of a sudden, the few journalists wrote articles, and Napa became a buzzing place," said Ivo Jeramaz, whose uncle, Mike Grgich, made the 1973 Chateau Montelena Chardonnay that was named best white at the competition."The wealthy clients started coming, money started pouring in."The region boomed, said Jeramaz, who now runs Grgich Hills Estate, and spends hours talking with visitors who come to taste his wines.But the excitement of the last few decades has cooled, he said, a situation exacerbated by tariffs that the US president has imposed on countries that buy California wine."Nobody is benefiting from tariffs," said Jeramaz, who blames them for raising production costs and hurting exports."We were selling over 1,000 cases, which is for us a good amount of wine, to Canada, and now we have zero since tariffs. So it's a big problem."Ottawa and Washington are locked in a deep trade dispute, exacerbated by Trump's frequent insults and claims that Canada will be taken over as a 51st US state.In response, some Canadian provinces have pulled US goods from their shelves and tourists who would otherwise have headed south have voted with their feet and stayed home."It's a big, big hit," said Jeramaz.- International component -About 20 percent of visitors to the region used to come from abroad, drawn by a Mediterranean-style climate, tranquil vineyards and lively towns full of restaurants and fashionable shops. That share has fallen to eight percent."The biggest impact for us comes from the decline in Canadian visitors," said Gallagher.In an effort to fill the gap, businesses have focused their advertising efforts on the domestic market.The strategy appears to be working for now.Last year the valley welcomed around 3.8 million people, up three percent from pre-pandemic tourism levels."But we're only going to be able to extract so much out of that domestic and local market. We won't fully recover until that international piece comes back," Gallagher warned.- Wellness, Napa-style -Changing consumption habits among younger generations are also weighing on Napa Valley, where more than 1,000 vineyards line a nearly 37-mile stretch traversed by a tourist train.Winemakers are trying to understand and adapt to these new customers who care more about environmental and social justice practices than about brands."When we get our wines in front of younger consumers and tell them the story of how they're made, how the grapes are grown, that it is a living, breathing, beautiful agricultural product, they're excited to discover something new," said Ali van Zyl, owner of the Belong Wine Company label.Another way to draw visitors is to highlight the valley's natural attractions and its food and hotel offerings.Tourism managers hope it could reposition Napa as a destination for people seeking a healthy lifestyle."Sharing a bottle of wine is a lot different than taking a bunch of tequila shots," said Laura Gabriel, van Zyl's partner in the River Club tasting house."It is a natural product and it's a part of well-lived life, with hiking and being outdoors and cooking," said Gabriel. "That's the Napa form of wellness."pr/mbt/smsThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Traffic on Old Delhi road to be blocked for four days for drain work | Hindustan Times
description: A GMDA spokesperson advised commuters to plan their journeys in advance and use alternative routes during the closure. Commuters have also been advised to follow traffic diversions and directions issued by the Gurugram Traffic Police
content: A stretch of Old Delhi Road near Sushil Aima marg, towards Atul Kataria Chowk, will remain closed from October 24 to 27 for drain construction, the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA) said on Thursday.A senior GMDA official said 30 metres of the road on each side would closed for construction of a reinforced cement concrete (RCC) box-type precast culvert and a box-type drain at Master Storm Water Drain Leg-I.“The culvert will be using precast girders to widen the drain, which is currently narrow beneath the road, restricting the flow of stormwater. The authority will also reconstruct the drain from Jwala Mill upto Rezangla Chowk. A fresh plan will be prepared in coordination with the Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL),” said a senior GMDA official.A GMDA spokesperson advised commuters to plan their journeys in advance and use alternative routes during the closure. Commuters have also been advised to follow traffic diversions and directions issued by the Gurugram Traffic Police.Meanwhile, GMDA CEO PC Meena on Thursday directed GMRL officials to coordinate with the Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited (HVPNL) and power distribution companies to set a timeline for shifting electricity substations and feeders along the proposed metro route.During a meeting at the GMDA office, officials said nine electricity feeders were affected by the proposed route, of which six have been relocated.The remaining feeders will be shifted in coordination with the departments concerned.Officials also said the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is constructing a new 66 kV substation, which is expected to be completed by December 2026. Once it becomes operational, the existing substation will be removed to clear the way for construction of the metro corridor.The GMDA spokesperson said no major hurdles involving basic infrastructure, including sewerage lines, drinking water pipelines or stormwater drains, had been identified along the metro route.

title: North zone inter-DPS football c’ship kicks off at Khanna: ‘Sports mirror life, help us negotiate highs & lows’ | Hindustan Times
description: Inaugurating the championship, Hindustan Times executive editor Ramesh Vinayak lauded the DPS society’s efforts to promote a sporting culture among students and expressed hope that the tournament would foster a friendly but robust competition
content: The whistle’s been blown, the boots are laced and the goal’s clear. Eighteen Delhi Public Schools have converged upon DPS Khanna for the North Zone Inter-DPS Football Championship, being held from October 22 to 24.The participating teams have been divided into four pools, with matches being played at the DPS football grounds as well as two other stadiums: Mohanpur and Bhamaddi.Inaugurating the championship, Hindustan Times executive editor Ramesh Vinayak lauded the DPS society’s efforts to promote a sporting culture among students and expressed hope that the tournament would foster a friendly but robust competition. “Sports mirror life and help us negotiate the highs and lows that confront us,” he said.Vinayak also highlighted India’s rich footballing legacy, recalling its achievements in the Asian Games and its qualification for the World Cup and Olympics in 1960. He observed that football enjoys a wide following in India, with enthusiasts passionately following major international tournaments and club-level matches. While motivating young players to hone their skills, he reminded them that Punjab has produced several legendary footballers, including Jarnail Singh and Inder Singh, whose achievements continue to inspire aspiring athletes.DPS Khanna chairman and former Punjab home secretary DS Bains said football inculcates team spirit, teaches discipline, encourages careful planning and rewards flawless execution- the very qualities that won England the Battle of Waterloo.Among the participating schools are DPS Abohar, Amritsar, Baramulla, Bathinda, Chandigarh, Greater Faridabad, Jhakri, Kanpur, Karnal, Katra, Khanna, Manali, Mohali, Pathankot, Patiala, Srinagar, Yamunanagar and Sangrur.

title: Five booked over drowning deaths of eight students at Diveagar beach | Hindustan Times
description: Police said that the FIR was registered following a complaint from Yuvraj Baburao Vahile, 42, a farmer from Kelgaon in Khed taluka of Pune district. His son, Rajveer, was among the eight students who died.
content: PUNE: Five people associated with Winners Academy, an Alandi-based coaching institute, were booked by Dighi Coastal Police on October 18 for alleged negligence in connection with the drowning deaths of eight students at Diveagar beach in Raigad district on October 1. Police had initially registered accidental death cases.The accused have been identified as academy founder Amar Gautam Adak, Mangal Suresh Narskhede, Saba Mahbub Inamdar, Shilpa Amar Adak and Vaishnavi Mangal Narskhede. They were booked under Sections 106(1) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), pertaining to causing death by negligence and acts committed by several persons with common intention, respectively.Police said on Thursday that the FIR was registered following a complaint from Yuvraj Baburao Vahile, 42, a farmer from Kelgaon in Khed taluka of Pune district. His son, Rajveer, was among the eight students who died.The complaint alleges lapses in supervising the students during the outing and questions the arrangements made for the trip and the responsibility of the accompanying adults. The allegations are yet to be established.Inspector Santosh Shripal Awati, the investigating officer, said, “The case was registered against all five accused under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The father has demanded action against those responsible for the deaths of the students. The probe is underway.”Winners Academy and Study Centre, Alandi, a private coaching institute established in 2022, had been operating without necessary permission, according to available information.The eight deceased students, all aged 16, were Tanmay Dattatray Vahile, Sumeet Bharat Ahire, Pranav Ramdas Bansode, Kaiwalya Satish Wasankar, Rajveer Yuvraj Vahile, Yash Kiran Wankhede, Soham Tukaram Bhandwalkar and Kaustubh Sandeep Dond.

title: Gurugram’s tilting building to undergo structural safety assessment | Hindustan Times
description: Gurugram's district admin has asked MCG officials to determine whether a five-storey ‘tilted’ building in Sushant Lok-3 should be declared unsafe and demolished
content: Gurugram:The district administration has asked Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) officials to determine whether a five-storey “tilted” building in Sushant Lok-3 should be declared unsafe and demolished.The building tilted dangerously following excavation work on an adjacent plot on October 19.The decision was taken during a meeting chaired by sub-divisional magistrate (Wazirabad) Sanjeev Singla, who discussed the matter with the building owners, neighbours evacuated from four adjoining buildings, and officials from the town and country planning department, PWD, local police, and civil defence.“We have asked the MCG to coordinate with the concerned officials to determine whether the building is structurally unsafe and requires demolition, or if it can be saved through retrofitting. In the meantime, traffic movement in front of the building has stopped, and nearby houses have been evacuated. As a preventive measure, SDRF personnel were brought in, and regular police teams have been deployed to monitor the situation,” said Singla.He added that two earth moving machines have also been deployed to support the tilted building. “A police case has also been registered in this matter and an investigation is under way,” he said.Families evacuatedOfficials said the concerned building, which has a stilt and four storeys, tilted dangerously to the right, damaging its internal structure. The Gurugram police evacuated four nearby buildings to ensure the safety of the 14 families residing there. The evacuated families have since been residing either in hotels or with relatives.According to a contractor working at the damaged building the incident occurred around 4 pm on October 19. “We immediately informed the police and the excavation work was halted. Around 40 workers were on site,” he said.Also Read: Gurugram’s senior living market gains ground as high-net-worth retirees and NRIs drive demandAmit Khosla, a neighbour who evacuated his house following the incident, said 14 families are currently facing uncertainty and are unable to return to their homes. “The building is unsafe, and if it rains, it could cause the structure to collapse, posing a serious safety risk to the surrounding area. The authorities should expedite a decision and find a permanent solution to this issue so the residents can safely return to their homes.”Also Read: Gurugram’s stilt-plus-four row: What changed, and what it means for homebuyers

title: NHAI deploys anti-smog guns, sprinklers across Delhi-NCR for dust control | Hindustan Times
description: NHAI officials have also been directed to monitor activities daily and submit progress reports with geo-tagged photographs.
content: Gurugram:The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) deployed anti-smog guns, water sprinklers and tankers, mechanised road-sweeping machines, and additional sanitation workers across Delhi-NCR as part of its dust-control measures, officials said on Thursday.According to NHAI officials, the authority has deployed around 60 water sprinklers and tankers, 14 anti-smog guns, 23 Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs), two tractor-mounted brooms and over 900 workers to support dust mitigation efforts on highways and expressways. In addition, 13 MRSMs are operating across 157 km of national highway stretches within Delhi NCR.The move comes as Delhi-NCR recorded poor air quality after Dussehra celebrations. On Thursday, Delhi recorded an air quality index of 223, while Noida registered 242, Greater Noida 219, Gurugram 193, and Faridabad 117.Alok Deepankar, Member (Technical), NHAI, reviewed the pollution-control measures and directed field teams to ensure full deployment of equipment, workforce, and water sprinkling; regular operation of anti-smog guns; and daily mechanical sweeping. “Strict compliance with norms established by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) in Delhi-NCR, which includes covering of construction materials, maintenance of dust-free road surfaces and intensified measures as per applicable GRAP stages, will be ensured,” he said.NHAI officials have also been directed to monitor activities daily and submit progress reports with geo-tagged photographs.Officials also said the highways authority planted around 980,000 saplings in NCR during FY 2025-26, against a target of 952,000, as part of its environmental initiatives.NHAI’s recent review also included decongestion projects like Urban Extension Road (UER)-II, Dwarka Expressway, Delhi Noida Direct (DND)–Sohna Expressway and Delhi–Dehradun Expressway, which are helping to reduce traffic congestion and vehicular emissions in Delhi-NCR.Officials said they will actively track progress on the proposed decongestion projects. Officials added that they will also promptly resolve citizens’ complaints received through the Green Delhi app and social media platforms.

title: Surajkund Diwali mela returns with 300 stalls, cultural shows | Hindustan Times
description: The fair will conclude on October 26, with Union minister Manohar Lal attending the closing ceremony as the chief guest, officials said.
content: Faridabad:The third edition of the Surajkund Diwali mela, being held at Faridabad, will begin on Friday, with Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini inaugurating the event, officials said.The mela, organised by the Haryana tourism department, will showcase culture, handicrafts, traditional attire, and regional delicacies, officials said.Around 300 stalls will be set up, showcasing the work of artisans from different states of the country, officials said.Haryana heritage and tourism minister Arvind Sharma said, “Surajkund Diwali mela is not merely an event for celebration and shopping, but also an important platform to preserve Indian culture, traditions and the skills of artisans.”The fair will conclude on October 26, with Union minister Manohar Lal attending the closing ceremony as the chief guest, officials said.According to officials, the four-day fair will feature a range of cultural performances, with Sufi and folk singer Kanwar Grewal among the key attractions. Folk artists from different states will also present traditional dances, folk songs and cultural performances.A large food court has been arranged at the venue, offering visitors a variety of traditional cuisines from different regions, officials said.Organisers said the venue will be under CCTV surveillance, with Faridabad police conducting patrols throughout the fair.Deputy commissioner of police (DCP) (NIT)Uttam said that more than 650 police personnel would be deployed on duty throughout the event. Special surveillance arrangements have been made at entry and exit gates, key locations, and crowded areas within the fairgrounds.“CCTV cameras have been installed, and a control room has been set up to monitor the footage, with police personnel deployed there to keep track of visitors entering and leaving the venue,”she said.A bomb disposal squad and a dog squad have also been deployed to strengthen security at the fair, officials added.
