title: Gurugram Sector 9A resident takes the lead on civic issues | Hindustan Times
description: According to Bhola, his work usually involves following up on complaints, meeting officials and pressing for action until results are visible.
content: Gurugram:When 46-year-old Lalit Suraj Bhola returned to India from the United States in 2003, he never thought that improving the civic infrastructure of a residential neighbourhood would become a defining part of his life. An IT engineer by profession, Bhola has spent years taking up residents’ complaints with civic authorities to make the sector a better place.In 2017, Bhola became the general secretary of the Sector 9A residents’ welfare association (RWA). He said his efforts to improve the neighbourhood started before he took up the formal responsibility. The sector’s low-lying terrain has long posed challenges, particularly during the monsoon due to inadequate drainage and waterlogging, he added.“I aimed to make Sector 9A one of the best sectors in Gurugram. Earlier, people looked down on the sector because it is one of the lowest-lying areas. Now, the sector has improved a lot,” he said.Over the years, Bhola said he has taken up several infrastructure-related demands with the authorities. He said his efforts helped secure additional water tanks at the Sector 9A boosting station, covering a sewage treatment plant (STP) drain to address persistent foul odour, and improved connectivity to the Dwarka Expressway.Bhola said he also worked to close a railway crossing and to install underground pipelines and stormwater drainage systems.According to Bhola, his work usually involves following up on complaints, meeting officials and pressing for action until results are visible. The responsibility does not end with forwarding a complaint to the relevant department. It requires monitoring whether the work is carried out and whether it addresses the problem on the ground, he added.“As citizens, we have to follow up with authorities time and again to make sure they take up our complaints. I keep meeting officials of different departments, and they have been kind enough to listen to our concerns,” said Bhola.Bhola said he has joined other RWA representatives in seeking greater recognition for residents’ associations and a stronger role in decisions concerning parks, community centres and civic maintenance. He has argued that residents, as the end users of these facilities, should have a say in how they are managed.“Residents continue to face civic service gaps, including sanitation-related concerns, requiring the RWA to keep engaging with the municipal corporation and other departments,” he said.

title: BJP mounts all-out voter outreach for UP MLC polls | Hindustan Times
description: With turnout traditionally low in these elections, the BJP deployed ministers, MLAs, district presidents and booth-level teams to contact eligible voters. The party set up control rooms in each constituency, shared voter lists with mandal units and launched a phone campaign to remind voters to cast their ballots.
content: The BJP intensified efforts to boost voter turnout ahead of Friday’s Uttar Pradesh legislative council elections, seeking to retain its six seats and make inroads into Opposition-held constituencies ahead of the 2027 assembly polls.Voting will be held for 11 seats — five graduates’ and six teachers’ constituencies — whose sitting members’ terms end on December 6. Of the 11 outgoing members, six are from the BJP, three from the Samajwadi Party (SP) and two are independents. The BJP’s focus is on retaining its six seats and wresting the seats held by the SP and independents.According to the state election office, polling will take place from 8 am to 4 pm in the designated districts. Counting is scheduled for October 27. Counting will take place on October 27 and results will shape the composition of the Upper House ahead of crucial 2027 assembly polls.The five graduates’ constituencies are Lucknow, Agra, Meerut, Varanasi and Bareilly-Moradabad, while the six teachers’ constituencies are Lucknow, Agra, Meerut, Varanasi, Bareilly-Moradabad and the Gorakhpur-Jhansi-Prayagraj zone.With turnout traditionally low in these elections, the BJP deployed ministers, MLAs, district presidents and booth-level teams to contact eligible voters. The party set up control rooms in each constituency, shared voter lists with mandal units and launched a phone campaign to remind voters to cast their ballots.“Graduate and teachers MLC elections have low turnout historically. Our challenge is to bring voters to the booth. We are doing door-to-door contact, calling up voters and arranging transport where needed,” a senior BJP functionary said.State BJP president and Union minister of state for finance Pankaj Chaudhary reviewed preparations with constituency in-charges and asked them to ensure contact with all eligible voters. The party also mobilised its teacher cell and educated youth wing to work as booth and polling agents.The BJP is confident of retaining at least five of its six seats but faces tough contests in two to three constituencies where the SP and Independent candidates have strong networks among teachers and graduates.The SP has fielded candidates backed by teachers’ associations and is seeking to capitalise on discontent among shiksha mitras, aided-school teachers and university staff over issues such as the old pension scheme, regularisation and honorarium.The two independent MLCs, meanwhile, have support among graduate voters in some urban pockets, making the contests triangular in certain constituencies.The BJP is also seeking to consolidate its support among professionals, lawyers, doctors and teachers aligned with Sangh-affiliated organisations such as the Akhil Bharatiya Rashtriya Shaikshik Mahasangh.Unlike general elections, voting in graduate and teacher constituencies is restricted to registered graduates and teachers. With turnout often below 50-60%, mobilising even a relatively small number of voters can swing the outcome.The BJP currently enjoys a majority in the legislative council, which is crucial for the passage of bills and for making MLCs ministers. Retaining six seats and gaining one or two more would further cement its dominance in the Upper House.The administration has made elaborate security arrangements for polling day with the deployment of police and sector magistrates. Voters must carry photo ID and registration slips.

title: Tourist bus fares to rise by 20-25%, hike in school bus fares from next academic year | Hindustan Times
description: Operators may be facing higher costs, but entire burden should not be passed on to passengers, say citizens
content: With the Pune Bus and Car Owners Association proposing a 20-25% hike in transportation charges for tourist buses in Pune with immediate effect and school bus fares set to increase from the next academic year, there are concerns among citizens relying on tourist buses and school buses over the affordability of essential transportation services.Announcing the decision at a press conference at Patrakar Bhavan on Thursday, Rajan Junavane, president of the Pune Bus and Car Owners Association, said, “Over the past five years, there has been no increase in bus transportation fares. However, during this period, the cost of purchasing vehicles and maintaining them has increased substantially. The prices of tyres, spare parts, batteries, fuel and lubricants have gone up, while expenses related to vehicle maintenance, repairs, insurance, drivers’ salaries and allowances have also increased. Toll charges, taxes and various government-mandated compliance costs have added to the financial burden on operators. Under these circumstances, providing transportation services at the existing rates has become extremely challenging. We have therefore been compelled to propose a fare revision of around 20-25% to ensure the sustainability of our operations.” Junavane said that the association comprises around 1,400 members involved in different segments of passenger transportation across Pune and its surrounding areas. The proposed revision covers vehicles ranging from 13-seater to 49-seater capacities including school buses, staff buses and tourist buses.Kiran Desai, a senior member of the association, said, “The revision is necessary to ensure that operators can continue providing services while meeting expenses related to vehicle upkeep, safety requirements and employee payments. The association believes that continuing to operate at the existing rates will put increasing financial pressure on vehicle owners and can affect the viability of passenger transport services.”Tushar Jagtap, secretary of the association, said, “Vehicle owners are facing increase across almost every major expense. The cost of vehicles has nearly doubled; tyre prices have increased significantly; and oil, batteries and spare parts have become considerably more expensive. In addition, drivers’ salaries and allowances; RTO passing and fitness charges; insurance premiums and government e-challan-related expenses have added to our costs. These are recurring expenses that operators cannot avoid. We have to maintain our vehicles and comply with the applicable regulations while continuing to provide services. The proposed fare revision has therefore become necessary to protect the business and livelihoods of people dependent on this sector.”Whereas Swati Makhija, a parent, said, “School bus fees are already a significant expense for parents, apart from school fees, books, uniforms and other educational costs. Any increase in transportation charges will further burden household budgets. Parents cannot easily discontinue school bus services, especially when both parents are working or when the school is far from home. The authorities and operators should consider the financial difficulties faced by families before increasing the charges.”Pune resident Kedar Mane said, “Prices of groceries, fuel and other essential items have already increased, and household expenses are becoming difficult to manage. Tourist buses are often a more practical option for families travelling together, particularly for religious trips and holidays. A 20-25% increase will make such travel more expensive. While operators may be facing higher costs, the entire burden should not be passed on to passengers. There should be some effort to keep these services affordable.”The association has proposed revised per-kilometre rates for buses ranging from 17-seater to 49-seater capacities. While the revised tourist bus rates are proposed to come into effect immediately, school transportation charges are proposed to be revised from the next academic year.

title: No let-up in commuters’ woes as buses stay off road in Ludhiana | Hindustan Times
description: Sukhwinder Singh, president of the PRTC and Punjab Roadways Union in Ludhiana, said the strike would continue indefinitely until the Punjab State Outsource Personnel Transmission to Contractual Engagement Act, 2026, was implemented
content: Passengers had to wait longer than usual for buses at the local bus stand on Thursday as more than half the fleet of the Punjab Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) and Punjab Roadways remained off road for the second consecutive day. Women, entitled to free travel on government buses, were among the worst affected.“Today, most of the buses on the road are private ones. They charge more than government buses. This particularly affects women like us, who can travel free on government buses,” said Rashmeet Kaur, who was waiting for a bus to Patiala.Another issue reported by passengers was that government buses generally operate on schedule, even when they are not full. “Private buses wait until they have a certain number of passengers, which can delay the journey. This affects us when we have to reach somewhere for work or an appointment,” said Puneet Arora, a private-sector professional waiting at the bus stand.Sukhwinder Singh, president of the PRTC and Punjab Roadways Union in Ludhiana, said the strike would continue indefinitely until the Punjab State Outsource Personnel Transmission to Contractual Engagement Act, 2026, was implemented.He said the Act proposes that outsourced workers who have completed more than five years of service be placed on direct contracts. The union expressed fear that the Election Commission would soon impose the Model Code of Conduct in the state ahead of the assembly elections, leaving the issue unresolved.“Who knows which government will come to power after the elections? The next government may not implement this. Therefore, it is imperative that the Act is implemented as soon as possible,” he added.Navraj Batish, general manager of the Punjab Roadways’ Ludhiana depot, said, “Around 40% of our fleet, operated by permanent workers or under the kilometre scheme, is still on the road. The issue raised by the outsourced workers will take time to resolve.”PRTC has a fleet of around 130 buses in Ludhiana, while Punjab Roadways has 96 buses.

title: Delivery exec’s death: Kin blame cops for failing to act in time | Latest News Delhi
description: Days after a 24-year-old delivery executive allegedly died by suicide following an assault and threats by a family over a torn  ₹10 note, his family on Thursday alleged that the Delhi Police failed to act in time  | Latest News Delhi
content: Days after a 24-year-old delivery executive allegedly died by suicide following an assault and threats by a family over a torn ₹10 note, his family on Thursday alleged that the Delhi Police failed to act in time.The 24-year-old man allegedly consumed a poisonous substance on October 5 after recording a video recounting his assault by two men over a torn currency note in east Delhi. He died on October 20, police said.The victim was allegedly assaulted by two residents of east Vinod Nagar on the night of October 4 after he refused to accept a torn currency note, according to police.A PCR call was received at 11.03 pm on October 4, with the victim reporting that he had been attacked by the accused, police said, adding that an FIR was registered at Kalyanpuri police station.In the video, the man said he went to deliver coffee to a customer who took 10-15 minutes to arrange payment before handing him cash, including a torn ₹10 note. When he objected, the customer allegedly told him to take it or leave it. He then offered to cancel the order and questioned why it had been placed if payment could not be made properly. He alleged that the customer abused him before another man arrived and slapped him multiple times. He also alleged that the man mocked him for his background.Police subsequently received information that he had been admitted to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital on October 5.He died on October 20, following which Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), pertaining to abetment of suicide, was added to the FIR, police said.The two accused were arrested on October 20 and were identified as Rakesh alias Bunti (30) and Rampal Singh (65), police said.The man’s uncle said, “He had simply asked them to give a fresh note or coin. But the old man slapped him. He had marks on his face for days. Then, the old man’s relative came and he picked up a rod and assaulted my nephew. My nephew told his manager everything and they went to the old man’s house. There, the family started using communal slurs and threatened us...”The family said the man was “dejected” as nobody was supporting him and the police also didn’t take any action before his death.Senior police officials said that they are verifying all the details.

title: Two shot at, another stabbed over old enmity Govindpuri | Latest News Delhi
description: New Delhi: Two men were shot at and a third was stabbed during a clash between two groups over old enmityin southeast Delhi’s Govindpuri area early on Thursday, police said  | Latest News Delhi
content: New Delhi: Two men were shot at and a third was stabbed during a clash between two groups over old enmityin southeast Delhi’s Govindpuri area early on Thursday, police said. The accused fled the spot after the attack and police teams are conducting raids to arrest them.According to police, a PCR call about gunfire and an assault was received around 1 a.m. The incident took place outside Asha Kiran apartments.The injured were identified as Sanju Bhesdhari, Mansoor Alam and Nitin Singh. Sanju sustained a gunshot wound and was admitted to Apollo Hospital in Sarita Vihar. Nitin also suffered a gunshot injury and was taken to AIIMS Trauma Centre. Alam, who sustained minor injuries, has been discharged, police said.DCP (southeast) Vineet Kumar said, “Preliminary probe revealed that a clash between two groups involved firing and knife attacks. Two empty cartridges and two knives were found at the spot. Legal action is being initiated and efforts are underway to identify, trace and apprehend the suspects.”Suman Singh, Nitin’s mother, said her son was having dinner on Wednesday night when he suddenly got up to leave. “When I asked him where he was going, he told me he would be back shortly. After some time, people informed me that someone stabbed and shot my son. Initially, I thought they were joking, but then they told me he had actually been injured,” she said.The incident took place near a venue where Durga Puja celebrations were being held. “I have not met my son yet. I have two sons and Nitin is the elder one. He is in the ICU,” she said, adding that her son worked in the private sector. She said the family was yet to ascertain the circumstances in which he sustained injuries.

title: 7 held in interstate drug racket bust, 8 kg heroin seized | Hindustan Times
description: New Delhi: Delhi Police has recovered over 8 kilograms of heroin worth crores and arrested seven people, who were allegedly part of a drug trafficking racket operating in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand, an officer said on Thursday
content: New Delhi: Delhi Police has recovered over 8 kilograms of heroin worth crores and arrested seven people, who were allegedly part of a drug trafficking racket operating in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand, an officer said on Thursday.Police seized the contraband during an operation that ran for about a month.Deputy Commissioner of Police (Rohini) Shashank Jaiswal said the racket surfaced with the arrest of Prakash Kumar, 31, a resident of Jharkhand’s Chatra district. Police said Kumar was allegedly involved in illegal cultivation of poppy on his agricultural land and supplied raw opium to other members of the gang.Police said following a tip-off on September 16, they intercepted a car and arrested its 58-year-old occupant, Laxman Hooda, with 300 grams of heroin and ₹3 lakh cash.A case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act was registered at the Begampur police station, and an investigation was launched to ascertain the source of the contraband and arrest other members in the network, police said.The probe led to the arrest of Anil Bhola, 51, with 501 grams of heroin; Bablu, 35, with 6.275 kg of the contraband; Ruksar Ali, 42, who ran a heroin manufacturing facility in Bareilly; Ajaj Ahmed, 38, with 501 grams of heroin; Mohammad Azhar, 20, with 551 grams of heroin and ₹9.81 lakh cash; and Prakash Kumar, 31, police added.

title: Ludhiana: Regular jobs, DA arrears, old pension scheme sought as employees protest at DC office | Hindustan Times
description: Their key demands include the release of 18% pending dearness allowance (DA), restoration of the old pension scheme, payment of a 2.59 multiplier to pensioners, restoration of the assured career progression (ACP) scheme, and reinstatement of 37 discontinued allowances, including the rural allowance
content: Government employees and teachers in Ludhiana took mass casual leave and staged a protest outside the deputy commissioner’s office on Wednesday and Thursday, accusing the Punjab government of failing to fulfill their long-pending demands.The protest was organised on the call of the Sanjha Mulazam Te Pensioner Manch Punjab and the Coordination Committee Punjab. Addressing the gathering, employee and teacher union leaders said repeated postponement of meetings had deepened dissatisfaction among staff.Their key demands include the release of 18% pending dearness allowance (DA), restoration of the old pension scheme, payment of a 2.59 multiplier to pensioners, restoration of the assured career progression (ACP) scheme, and reinstatement of 37 discontinued allowances, including the rural allowance.The protesters also demanded the withdrawal of government notifications dated July 15, 2015, and July 17, 2020, the transfer of computer teachers to the education department, regularisation of contractual employees, and a pay hike for Mid-Day Meal workers and other outsourced staff.Union leaders alleged that the chief minister had repeatedly cancelled scheduled meetings and failed to honour prior commitments. They emphasised that employees, who form the backbone of the administration, continue to face uncertainty over service conditions and financial benefits.Meanwhile, deputy commissioner Himanshu Jain said public services and emergency operations were functioning smoothly despite the agitation.Asked how the administration would ensure uninterrupted services if the protest persisted, Jain said, “So far, we have been managing with their support. Public dealing is going on, and emergency services are being handled.”Warning of an intensified agitation, union leaders said employees across Punjab had participated in district-level protests on October 21 and 22 by taking mass leave. They warned that the agitation would escalate if the government continues to ignore their demands.Several other employee representatives and union members were present at the demonstration.

title: Union minister Shah launches 43 projects aimed at Yamuna clean-up | Hindustan Times
description: New DelhiUnion home minister Amit Shah on Thursday inaugurated and laid the foundation for a slew of Delhi Jal Board (DJB) projects worth  ₹8,941
content: New DelhiUnion home minister Amit Shah on Thursday inaugurated and laid the foundation for a slew of Delhi Jal Board (DJB) projects worth ₹8,941.22 crore aimed at cleaning up the Yamuna by setting up wastewater treatment plants and improving water supply across Delhi.Officials aware of the details said that 10 projects worth ₹2,827.11 crore were commissioned and the foundation for 33 projects worth ₹6,114.11 crore was laid.Chief minister Rekha Gupta, who was accompanying Shah, said, “The focus is on intercepting drains, modernising old sewage treatment plants (STPs), setting up new STPs, laying sewer lines and connecting the sewer network to STPs.”Delhi water minister Parvesh Verma, who was also present, said the projects covered STPs, decentralised STPs, pumping stations, drains and water treatment plants. “Under the previous government, tenders were floated, cancelled and floated again. Files kept moving, but the work never started,” Verma said.One of the key projects pertains to interception and diversion of sewage from the Barapullah and Maharani Bagh drains—which used to flow straight into the Yamuna—to the Okhla STP through a new 35 million gallons per day (mgd) pumping station at Batla House. Eight existing STPs will be upgraded at a cost of ₹1,041 crore, raising their capacity from 78.2mgd to 140.8mgd, which will cover a population of around 7.85 million people, Verma said.Around ₹1,161 crore covers a 124mgd Okhla STP project and upgrades at Rithala and Kondli, the minister added.Twenty-nine of decentralised STPs and sewage pumping stations, worth ₹3,113.67 crore, will cover 358 unauthorised colonies and 113 villages, which house around 3.63 million people, in Narela, Bawana, Kanjhawala, Bijwasan, Tikri Kalan and nearby areas.“Sewage from these areas will be treated close to where it is produced, so it does not end up in the drains. Another ₹1,691 crore will be spent on 1,034km of sewer network for about 25.82 lakh people,” Verma said.A 2mgd recycling plant at Bawana, and a line carrying 4mgd of treated water from the Kapashera STP to Bijwasan for horticulture and other non-potable uses is set to ease the pressure on freshwater demand.“A new 477 million litre per day (mld) water treatment plant at Chandrawal, built at ₹298.3 crore, replaces plants set up in 1935 and 1955. It will serve about 22 lakh people in Sadar Bazar, Chandni Chowk, Matia Mahal, Ballimaran, Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar, Rajinder Nagar and New Delhi,” a government official said.

title: Ludhiana bizman shot dead at friend’s birthday party; nine booked | Hindustan Times
description: According to the FIR, Rahul closed his kulcha shop on College Road around 10 pm on Wednesday and told his father that he was going to attend the birthday party of his friend, Akhil Joshi, at the latter’s residence in Green World Homes
content: A 34-year-old businessman, belonging to the family that runs the decades-old Pandit Ji Chole Kulche eatery, was allegedly shot dead by a friend during an argument during a birthday celebration at an upscale residential complex on Pakhowal Road on Wednesday night. The incident took place at Green World Homes in Daad village.The deceased, Rahul Sharma, was rushed by friends to Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH), where he succumbed to his injuries. Police have registered a murder case against nine persons based on the statement of Rahul’s father, Kuldeep Kumar Sharma, 64. The prime suspect, Gagandeep Arora of Moga, allegedly opened fire from his licensed firearm. Four police teams have been constituted to trace and arrest the accused.Deputy commissioner of police (city) Alam Vijay Singh said the police received information about the shooting during the intervening night of Wednesday and Thursday. Describing it as an incident arising from an argument, he said eight to 10 men had gathered for a birthday celebration and that the killing did not appear to have been planned or targeted.Inspector Jagdev Singh, SHO of the Sadar police station, said a preliminary investigation indicated that Rahul had sustained two bullet wounds. “The exact details of what happened at the party will become clear only after the accused are arrested,” he said.Father learns of son’s death hours after partyAccording to the FIR, Rahul closed his kulcha shop on College Road around 10 pm on Wednesday and told his father that he was going to attend the birthday party of his friend, Akhil Joshi, at the latter’s residence in Green World Homes. Around 2 am, Kuldeep Kumar Sharma received a call informing him that his son had been admitted to the emergency ward at DMCH. He later learned that Rahul had died of bullet injuries.The FIR names Akhil Joshi, Gagandeep Arora, Amritpal, Gaurav, Gautam, Sagar, Karan, Saksham and Paramraj of Khanna as accused. The police have booked them under Sections 103(1) (murder), 191(3) (rioting), and 190 (unlawful assembly) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with Sections 25, 27, 54 and 59 of Arms Act.Police sources said Rahul was also involved in the real estate business and was allegedly discussing a business-related matter with Gagandeep, who owns a famous eatery brand, when an argument broke out and shots were fired. However, the police said the motive would be established only after the accused are apprehended and questioned. Rahul had been married for three years.Firing accidental, says hostAkhil Joshi, at whose birthday party the shooting took place, released a video message claiming that the gun went off accidentally. His statement came amid allegations that some of Rahul’s friends had left the hospital after bringing him there.In the video, Joshi claimed that the group heard a gunshot before Rahul suddenly collapsed. He said he questioned Gagandeep, who allegedly told him that a bullet had gone off while he was placing his revolver on a table and struck Rahul.Joshi further claimed that he and Gagandeep rushed Rahul to DMCH and remained there until members of Rahul’s family arrived. He said they left later because they were frightened, denying that they had abandoned Rahul or fled the hospital.The police have yet to establish the sequence of events leading to the shooting. The circumstances surrounding the discharge of the firearm, the cause of the argument, and the role of each accused remain under investigation.Second fatal shooting in a dayThis is the second fatal shooting in Ludhiana within 24 hours. Earlier in the day, a 31-year-old man from Panchkula, Haryana, was shot dead during a clash between two groups in the EWS Colony area near Tajpur Road after he accompanied his friends to confront a group suspected of vandalising their associate’s car. Police have arrested one suspect in connection with that case.Crime increasing, says MP WarringLudhiana MP Amrinder Singh Raja Warring wrote on X (formerly Twitter) that the incident was disturbing. “What is even more heartbreaking is that such incidents are becoming increasingly common in Punjab, raising serious concerns about the safety of our people. Whether it is a businessman, a trader or an ordinary citizen, every Punjabi deserves to live without fear for their life and their family,” the former Punjab Congress president stated.BJP state general secretary Anil Sarin demanded the immediate arrest of the accused, while former Union Minister Ravneet Singh Bittu visited the victim’s house.

title: Pune tops Maha in dog-bite cases, rabies deaths this year | Hindustan Times
description: Pune district has reported the highest number of dog-bite cases and rabies deaths in Maharashtra, with 77,286 dog bites and 14 rabies fatalities recorded between January and September 2026; according to the state health department
content: Pune district has reported the highest number of dog-bite cases and rabies deaths in Maharashtra, with 77,286 dog bites and 14 rabies fatalities recorded between January and September 2026; according to the state health department. However, the district recorded a lower number of dog-bite cases this year than the 95,535 such cases recorded last year. Whereas rabies deaths in Pune district rose from 10 in 2025 to 14 this year. The district also recorded 18,335 other animal (cats, rats and monkeys etc.) bites, taking the total number of animal-bite cases between January and September 2026 to 95,621.Among other districts, Thane reported 26,683 dog-bite cases and seven rabies deaths during the same period; Ahilyanagar recorded 30,413 dog-bite cases and eight rabies deaths; and Solapur reported 28,620 dog bites and six rabies deaths; officials said. Across Maharashtra, 480,206 dog-bite cases and 118,021 other animal bites were reported in the first nine months of 2026. The state recorded 59 rabies deaths during this period as compared to 33 during the corresponding period last year. The total number of animal-bite cases stood at 598,227 in 2026, down from 667,744 in 2025.The figures – compiled from the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) and case investigation forms (CIFs) – underline the continuing public health burden of animal bites and rabies across the state; officials said.Dr Madhavi Shinde, epidemic medical officer, Pune district, said that Pune district sees patients not just from the district but also from western Maharashtra due to the existence of numerous good hospitals. “Even if a patient from a district like Satara or Solapur comes to Sassoon Hospital and Naidu Hospital for treatment and dies, the death is reported as a rabies death in Pune district. A large number of patients are actually not from Pune,” she said.Pravin Tapkir, a resident of Pashan, said, “Pune’s dog bite figures and rabies deaths are alarming. The civic administration must strengthen stray dog management, ensure timely anti-rabies vaccination and treatment, and improve public awareness. Residents should not have to fear for their safety while walking in their own neighbourhoods. The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) must take preventive measures before more lives are put at risk.”Dr Sarika Funde-Bhosale, chief veterinary officer, PMC, said, “Dog-bite prevention requires a coordinated approach. The PMC is continuing its efforts to strengthen the Animal Birth Control (ABC) programme, including sterilisation and vaccination of stray dogs, along with measures to address public safety. We are also working to improve awareness and urge citizens to report dog-bite incidents promptly so that timely medical treatment can be provided. Besides, the work of stray dog shelters is underway and once completed, it is likely to reduce the number of dog-bite cases.”

title: HC grants interim protection to serving Indian Statistical Service officer in Solan FIR over matrimonial dispute | Hindustan Times
description: Petitioner seeks quashing of an FIR registered when her husband was SP Solan; cites contradictory claims over jewellery and pending matrimonial litigation
content: The Himachal Pradesh high court has granted interim protection from coercive action to a serving Indian Statistical Service officer in a criminal case registered at Solan Sadar police station on a complaint by her mother-in-law, amid a matrimonial dispute involving her husband, who was serving as superintendent of police, Solan, at the time.The court, in an order dated October 16, directed the state not to take coercive action against the woman officer in the FIR registered on May 18, 2025, under Sections 305, 331(3), 351(2) and 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The officer had approached the high court seeking the quashing of the FIR and consequential criminal proceedings. The petition alleges that the case was registered under the influence of her husband, an IPS officer, who was then serving as the SP of Solan.A single-judge bench of justice Chirag Bhanu Singh issued notice to the respondents on October 16. Deputy advocate general Prashant Sharma, appearing for the state, accepted notice and was granted two weeks to file a reply. Notices were also issued to the IPS officer and his mother.The matter has been listed for November 17.According to the petition, the woman officer married the IPS officer on February 16, 2023. The petition states that matrimonial differences developed between the couple and alleges domestic violence and dowry-related demands by her husband and his family.The petition states that a divorce petition was filed by her husband on December 23, 2024, before the family court in Agra, Uttar Pradesh. The Supreme Court, on October 8, 2025, shifted the case from Agra to the family court in Jaipur.She alleges that when she visited her matrimonial home in Solan on December 31, 2024, she was assaulted by her husband on the night of January 1, 2025, and he threatened to kill her using his service firearm. The woman subsequently filed a domestic violence complaint before the Jaipur court on February 10, 2025. The FIR under challenge was lodged by the IPS officer’s mother, on May 18, 2025, invoking provisions related to theft, trespass and intentional insult.

title: Emergency fund investment : రూ. 10లక్షల ఎమర్జెన్సీ ఫండ్.. ఎక్కడ ఇన్వెస్ట్​ చేయడం బెటర్? | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: ఉద్యోగం పోయినా, హఠాత్తుగా ఆసుపత్రి ఖర్చులు ముంచుకొచ్చినా ఆదుకునేది అత్యవసర నిధి (ఎమర్జెన్సీ ఫండ్). రూ.10 లక్షల ఎమర్జెన్సీ ఫండ్‌ను సేవింగ్స్ ఖాతా, ఎఫ్‌డీ, లిక్విడ్ ఫండ్లలో ఎలా విభజించుకోవాలో ఆర్థిక నిపుణులు చెబుతున్న సలహాలు మీకోసం..
content: ఉద్యోగాల్లో కోతలు, అకస్మాత్తుగా వచ్చే వైద్య అత్యవసర పరిస్థితి లేదా హఠాత్తుగా ఇంటి ఖర్చులు పెరగడం.. కారణం ఏదైనా ఆపద సమయంలో ఆర్థికంగా నిలబెట్టేది ఎమర్జెన్సీ ఫండ్ (అత్యవసర నిధి) మాత్రమే! అవసరానికి చేతిలో డబ్బులు ఉంటే అత్యవసర పరిస్థితుల్లో ఎక్కడా అప్పులు చేయాల్సిన అవసరమే ఉండదు. అయితే, చేతిలో రూ.10 లక్షల ఫండ్ ఉన్నప్పుడు, దానిని మొత్తాన్ని సాధారణ సేవింగ్స్ ఖాతాలోనే ఉంచితే వచ్చే వడ్డీ చాలా తక్కువ. పోనీ అని ఆ డబ్బునంతటినీ ఫిక్స్​డ్​ డిపాజిట్లు (ఎఫ్​డీ) లేదా మ్యూచువల్ ఫండ్లలో లాక్ చేస్తే, తక్షణమే అత్యవసరమైనప్పుడు నగదు ఉపసంహరణ కష్టమవుతుంది. మరి మన దగ్గర ఎమర్జెన్సీ ఫండ్​గా ఉన్న రూ. 10లక్షలను ఏం చేయాలి?ఇక్కడ ప్రధానంగా మూడు అంశాల మధ్య సమతుల్యత సాధించాలి:తక్షణ నగదు లభ్యత (లిక్విడిటీ)పెట్టుబడి భద్రత (క్యాపిటల్ సేఫ్టీ)మెరుగైన రాబడి (రిటర్న్స్)కేవలం ఎక్కువ రాబడి వస్తుందనే ఆశతో కాకుండా, ఆపద వచ్చినప్పుడు ఎంత వేగంగా డబ్బు చేతికి అందుతుందనే ప్రాతిపదికన ఈ రూ.10 లక్షలను ఎలా విభజించుకోవాలో పర్సనల్ ఫైనాన్స్ నిపుణులు వివరిస్తున్నారు.రూ.10 లక్షల నిధిని ఎలా కేటాయించాలి?ఫండ్స్‌ఇండియా.కామ్ సీఈఓ రిషభ్ గార్గ్ అభిప్రాయం ప్రకారం.. రూ.10 లక్షల అత్యవసర నిధిని మూడు భాగాలుగా విభజించుకోవడం ఉత్తమమైన పద్ధతి:సేవింగ్స్ ఖాతా: రూ.2 లక్షలు (1-2 నెలల ఇంట్లో అత్యవసర ఖర్చుల కోసం)లిక్విడ్ మ్యూచువల్ ఫండ్లు: రూ.4 లక్షలుఫిక్స్​డ్​ డిపాజిట్లు (ఎఫ్​డీ): రూ.4 లక్షలు (వేర్వేరు కాలపరిమితులతో)మరోవైపు డెజర్వ్ (Dezerv) సహ-వ్యవస్థాపకుడు సందీప్ జెత్వాని మరో వ్యూహాన్ని సూచిస్తున్నారు. ఆయన ప్రకారం:సేవింగ్స్ ఖాతా: రూ.1.5 లక్షలు (తక్షణ ఆసుపత్రి జాయినింగ్ లేదా అత్యవసర ఖర్చులకు)లిక్విడ్ మ్యూచువల్ ఫండ్లు: రూ.4.5 లక్షలుఅల్ట్రా-షార్ట్ డ్యూరేషన్ డెట్ ఫండ్: రూ.4 లక్షలుఆసుపత్రిలో చేరడం లేదా తక్షణ ముందస్తు చెల్లింపుల కోసం సేవింగ్స్ అకౌంట్ వెంటనే ఉపయోగపడుతుంది. తొలి నెలలో అవసరం పడని నిధులను అల్ట్రా-షార్ట్ డ్యూరేషన్ ఫండ్లలో ఉంచుకోవచ్చు. అయితే వీటి రాబడులు మార్కెట్ ఒడుదొడుకులకు లోబడి ఉంటాయని గుర్తుపెట్టుకోవాలి.ఉపసంహరణ సులభతరం.. భద్రత ఎందులో ఎక్కువ?ఈ మూడు మార్గాల్లో డబ్బు ఉపసంహరించుకునే వేగం, భద్రత వేర్వేరుగా ఉంటాయి:సేవింగ్స్ ఖాతా: యూపీఐ, డెబిట్ కార్డ్, నెట్ బ్యాంకింగ్ ద్వారా క్షణాల్లో డబ్బు వాడుకోవచ్చు.ఫిక్స్​డ్​ డిపాజిట్లు: గడువు తీరక ముందే ఎఫ్‌డీని రద్దు చేసుకోవచ్చు. కానీ బ్యాంకులు స్వల్ప పెనాల్టీ విధించవచ్చు లేదా వడ్డీ తగ్గించవచ్చు.లిక్విడ్ ఫండ్లు: దరఖాస్తు చేసిన మరుసటి పనిదినంలో డబ్బు బ్యాంక్ ఖాతాలో జమ అవుతుంది. కొన్ని స్కీమ్‌లు రోజుకు రూ.50,000 లేదా పెట్టుబడిలో 90 శాతం వరకు తక్షణ ఉపసంహరణ సదుపాయాన్ని అందిస్తున్నాయి."అన్ని లిక్విడ్ ఫండ్లూ ఇన్​స్టెంట్ రెడెంప్షన్ ఇవ్వవు. కాబట్టి ఈ సదుపాయం ఉన్న వేర్వేరు ఫండ్ హౌస్‌లకు చెందిన రెండు స్కీమ్‌లలో డబ్బును విభజించి పెట్టుబడి పెట్టడం మంచిది," అని సందీప్ జెత్వాని సలహా ఇచ్చారు.భద్రత విషయానికొస్తే, బ్యాంకు సేవింగ్స్ అకౌంట్లు, ఎఫ్‌డీలకు డిపాజిట్ ఇన్సూరెన్స్ అండ్ క్రెడిట్ గ్యారెంటీ కార్పొరేషన్ ద్వారా ఒక బ్యాంకులో ఒకరి పేరు మీద గరిష్ఠంగా రూ.5 లక్షల వరకు (అసలు + వడ్డీ) బీమా రక్షణ లభిస్తుంది. కానీ లిక్విడ్ మ్యూచువల్ ఫండ్లకు ఇటువంటి బీమా రక్షణ ఉండదు. ఇవి తక్కువ రిస్క్ ఉన్న స్వల్పకాలిక డెట్ సాధనాల్లో ఇన్వెస్ట్ చేసినప్పటికీ, రాబడికి హామీ ఉండదు.దీనిని నివారించేందుకు 'స్వీప్-ఇన్ ఎఫ్‌డీ' సదుపాయాన్ని లేదా చిన్న చిన్న మొత్తాలలో అనేక ఎఫ్‌డీలు చేయడం మేలని రిషభ్ గార్గ్ చెబుతున్నారు. స్వీప్-ఇన్ పద్ధతిలో సేవింగ్స్ ఖాతాలో అదనంగా ఉన్న సొమ్ము ఆటోమేటిక్‌గా ఎఫ్‌డీగా మారుతుంది. అవసరమైనప్పుడు దానంతట అదే సేవింగ్స్ ఖాతాలోకి వస్తుంది.రాబడి, పన్ను నిబంధనలు..రాబడి పరంగా సేవింగ్స్ ఖాతాలో తక్కువ వడ్డీ లభిస్తుంది. ఎఫ్‌డీలు నిర్ణీత కాలానికి స్థిరమైన వడ్డీని ఇస్తాయి. లిక్విడ్ ఫండ్ల రాబడులు మార్కెట్ వడ్డీ రేట్ల ఆధారంగా మారుతుంటాయి. ప్రస్తుతం లిక్విడ్ ఫండ్ పోర్ట్‌ఫోలియోలు ఖర్చులు పోను దాదాపు 6.2 శాతం నుంచి 6.6 శాతం వరకు వార్షిక రాబడి అంచనాలను చూపుతున్నాయి.పన్ను పరంగా పరిశీలిస్తే, సేవింగ్స్ అకౌంట్, ఎఫ్‌డీల నుంచి వచ్చే వడ్డీ మీ ఆదాయపు పన్ను స్లాబ్ రేటు ప్రకారం పన్నుకు గురవుతుంది. లిక్విడ్ ఫండ్ల లాభాలపై కూడా మీ పన్ను స్లాబ్ ప్రకారమే పన్ను పడుతుంది. అయితే మ్యూచువల్ ఫండ్లలో లాభాలను ఉపసంహరించుకున్న సమయంలో మాత్రమే పన్ను చెల్లించాల్సి ఉంటుంది. ఎమర్జెన్సీ ఫండ్‌ను కొన్నేళ్ల పాటు తాకకుండా ఉంచినప్పుడు ఈ పన్ను ప్రయోజనం ఇన్వెస్టర్లకు కలిసి వస్తుంది.ఒకే బ్యాంకులో మొత్తం దాచడం సురక్షితమేనా?రూ.10 లక్షల నిధి మొత్తాన్ని ఒకే బ్యాంకులో ఉంచడం వల్ల రిస్క్ పెరుగుతుంది. డీఐసీజీసీ బీమా పరిమితి రూ.5 లక్షలే కాబట్టి, అంతకు మించి ఒకే బ్యాంకులో ఉంచిన మొత్తంపై భద్రత ఉండదు. కాబట్టి ఈ నిధిని రెండు లేదా మూడు వేర్వేరు బ్యాంకులలో, అలాగే లిక్విడ్ ఫండ్లలో విభజించి ఉంచడం సురక్షితం.అత్యవసర సమయంలో ముఖ్యంగా వైద్య అత్యవసర పరిస్థితి ఏర్పడినప్పుడు భార్య లేదా కుటుంబ సభ్యులు ఆ డబ్బును సులభంగా తీసుకునేలా జాయింట్ అకౌంట్ లేదా నామినేషన్ నమోదు చేయడం అత్యంత ఆవశ్యకం. డబ్బు ఎక్కడ ఉంచారో కుటుంబ సభ్యులకు స్పష్టంగా తెలియజేయాలి.ఎమర్జెన్సీ ఫండ్ అనేది భారీ లాభాల కోసం ఉద్దేశించినది కాదు. ఆపద సమయంలో కుటుంబానికి ఆర్థిక స్థిరత్వాన్ని, ధైర్యాన్ని అందించడమే దీని ప్రాథమిక లక్ష్యం.(గమనిక- ఇది సమాచారం కోసం రూపొందించిన కథనం మాత్రమే. హిందుస్థాన్ టైమ్స్ తెలుగుకు ఎలాంటి సంబంధం లేదు. ఏదైనా ఆర్థికపరమైన నిర్ణయం తీసుకునే ముందు మీరు మీ ఫైనాన్షియల్ అడ్వైజర్​ని సంప్రదించడం శ్రేయస్కరం.)

title: HP cops trace nearly 89% of missing persons in nine months | Hindustan Times
description: Between January 1 and September 30, a total of 893 FIRs involving 1,328 missing persons were registered across the state.
content: In line with the Supreme Court’s directions, the Himachal Pradesh Police has strengthened its mechanism for reporting, investigating and tracing missing persons, particularly women and children.In a statement, the state police said that it had achieved an overall tracing rate of 88.7% during January–September 2026, reflecting sustained efforts to locate missing persons and reunite them with their families.In its judgment on May 22, 2026, the top court had emphasised the immediate registration of FIRs on receiving information about missing persons, without insisting upon any waiting period. Acting on these directions, the HP Police issued instructions to all field units on June 6, 2026, mandating immediate FIR registration, prompt search operations, special attention to missing children and regular supervisory monitoring.Between January 1 and September 30, a total of 893 FIRs involving 1,328 missing persons were registered across the state. Of these, 88.7% of missing persons have been successfully traced, while efforts continue to trace the remaining persons. Of the total missing persons reported, 61.6% were adults and 38.4% were children.The police have urged the parents, guardians and members of the public to approach the nearest police station or contact the emergency response support system (ERSS-112) without delay.

title: Himachal government clears policy to tackle malnutrition, anaemia | Hindustan Times
description: The policy envisages coordinated efforts by the departments of health and family welfare, women and child development, education, agriculture, horticulture, food and civil supplies, jal shakti, rural development, panchayati raj and other concerned departments.
content: The state government has approved the Himachal Pradesh Nutrition Policy, 2026, aimed at addressing malnutrition, anaemia, micronutrient deficiencies, poor dietary diversity and emerging diet-related diseases through a comprehensive and coordinated approach. The policy emphasises promoting traditional Himachali foods, seasonal fruits, pulses, millets, green leafy vegetables, dairy products and other locally available nutritious ingredients to improve public health and encourage healthy eating habits.The policy adopts a life-cycle approach to nutrition, with special emphasis on the first 1,000 days of life, maternal and child nutrition, adolescents and vulnerable sections of society. It seeks to ensure access to safe, nutritious and affordable food while promoting balanced, culturally acceptable diets that households can easily incorporate into their daily lives. Special attention will be given to people living in remote and tribal areas to improve access to nutrition and healthcare services.The policy envisages coordinated efforts by the departments of health and family welfare, women and child development, education, agriculture, horticulture, food and civil supplies, jal shakti, rural development, panchayati raj and other concerned departments.To strengthen interdepartmental coordination, planning, implementation and monitoring, it proposes the establishment of a state nutrition coordination cell (SNCC) and district nutrition coordination cells (DNCCS).To strengthen food safety infrastructure and surveillance, the policy envisages upgrading the composite testing laboratory (CTL) at Kandaghat and the establishment of four laboratories in the state. The process for establishing a new laboratory at Dharamshala has already been initiated.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said the state government is committed to building a healthy, well-nourished and empowered Himachal. “Nutrition is fundamental to human development and every child, woman and citizen must have access to safe, nutritious and affordable food. The policy provides a comprehensive framework to address nutritional challenges through the coordinated efforts of all concerned departments, with particular emphasis on vulnerable communities and people living in remote areas,” he said.Sinduri Pomegranates exported to DubaiAs many as 1.3 metric tonnes of Sinduri-variety pomegranates grown in Kullu district were exported to Dubai, Sukhu said on Thursday.He said the government was facilitating access to markets within the state and across the country to ensure remunerative prices for farmers’ produce. It was also extending all possible assistance to help them reach international markets.The regional office of the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), Chandigarh, facilitated the export of this consignment. The pomegranates were sourced from farmers in Kullu and the Bhuntar farmer producer organisation (FPO) based in Kullu. Around 600 farmers are associated with this organisation.

title: Horticulture minister inaugurates HP’s first agri monorail system in Mandi | Hindustan Times
description: The monorail project is one kilometre long. The project, established in Palhota-2 cluster, covers 28.44 hectares and is associated with 85 farmer families.
content: Horticulture minister Jagat Singh Negi on Thursday inaugurated the first agri monorail system to facilitate transportation of fruits and other agricultural produce grown in difficult terrain.The Himachal Pradesh Subtropical Horticulture, Irrigation and Value Addition (HPSHIVA) monorail project in Mandi district is constructed at a cost of approximately ₹20 lakh. The monorail project is one kilometre long. The project, established in Palhota-2 cluster, covers 28.44 hectares and is associated with 85 farmer families.Negi said the monorail project would be beneficial for farmers and horticulturists in the region.The facility will save time and labour of farmers and horticulturists while reducing transportation difficulties, a statement issued here said.The minister said the state government was continuously working to integrate modern technology into the horticulture sector, strengthen farmers’ economic condition and expand basic infrastructure in rural areas.Modern facilities such as monorail projects would play an important role in the development of horticulture in Himachal Pradesh, he added.The minister said the ₹1,292-crore HP SHIVA project, funded by the Asian Development Bank, was being implemented in seven districts -- Bilaspur, Hamirpur, Kangra, Mandi, Solan, Sirmaur and Una. The main objective is to increase the income of farming families.Keeping farmers’ interests in mind, the duration of the HP SHIVA project has been extended by two years, from June 2028 to June 2030, he noted.The minister said the first phase of HP SHIVA covering 3,000 hectares is scheduled to be completed by February 2027. Director of Horticulture Satish Sharma, HP SHIVA Project Director Sameer Singh Rana and other senior officers were present on the occasion.

title: Delhi census: Second phase of self-enumeration likely to begin Jan 10 | Latest News Delhi
description: Training will cover digital data collection, privacy concerns and security, while the questionnaire includes a caste question.  | Latest News Delhi
content: A 15-day self-enumeration phase of the 2027 census is likely to begin on January 10 in Delhi, followed by door-to-door visits by enumerators from January 25 to February 28, officials said on Thursday.The census is being carried out in two phases­­ – house-listing, which has already been done, and population enumeration, which started for snow-clad areas of Himalayan states after online self-enumeration closed on August 31. This is the first time in independent India that enumerators will ask a question on caste.The Directorate of Census Operations, Delhi, held a training session at the Delhi Secretariat on Thursday for district magistrates, additional district magistrates and sub-divisional magistrates, briefing them on the progress of the first phase and preparations for the next stage. Chief secretary Rajeev Verma had also held a meeting with district magistrates on October 13, directing them to sensitise the public.Also Read | Census house-listing phase ends in Delhi, covers 5.5 million households“The dates are still tentative, but we have been directed to start preparing for the exercise. The enumerators and supervisors who participated in the first phase will undergo training for the second phase. The training will be conducted at the district level,” an official said.The houselisting phase of the census was conducted in the MCD areas from May 16 to June 15 while in NDMC areas it went on April 16 to May 15. The self-enumeration and house visit phase of the census has already been conducted in the snow-bound regions of Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand between August 17 and September 30, 2026.The dates for other states and UTs are not known. Enumerators and supervisors are likely to undergo three-day training between November and December.More than 50,000 enumerators were deployed for the first phase, with Delhi divided into over 46,500 houselisting blocks. While the first phase was conducted in two stages — initially in the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) and Delhi Cantonment Board areas, followed by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) areas — the second phase will cover the entire Capital simultaneously, another official said.Also Read | MHA asks MCD for audit plan covering every building in city Census questions and data privacyIn August, the Union government notified 40 questions, including a query on caste for the first time in independent India, to be asked of respondents. The order from Registrar General of India Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan notified 11 questions more than the 2011 Census, the last time the exercise was conducted in India. Among the new questions were those asking for parental details, and others on passports, Aadhaar, Voter ID and mobile number, driving licence, and Covid-19 vaccination details, and permanent residential address –– which raised privacy concerns.The question on caste was listed as question number 10 in the notification – as “scheduled caste/scheduled tribe/caste” – in open-ended format, which means Census officers will record the caste of a person as declared, without any requirement to match it to pre-prepared lists.Originally scheduled for 2021, the census was initially postponed due to the Covid-19 pandemic. Data collection is targeted to conclude by March 1, 2027, but officials say the collation and publication of results will take two to three years. The exercise is likely to stamp India’s status as the world’s most-populous nation.Also Read | Census 2027: 93,000 persons submit details under self-enumeration in DelhiSecurity and public awarenessSenior police officers also attended Thursday’s training session and were directed to sensitise beat staff and police stations about the need to provide security to enumerators. Station house officers were asked to coordinate with charge officers and ensure security, wherever required.“Concerns were flagged about certain sensitive areas where people may be apprehensive about sharing details. It was advised that adequate security be deployed during the door-to-door exercise,” an official said.The Directorate of Census Operations will launch awareness campaigns through radio jingles, posters at metro stations, billboards and public announcements. Enumerators will also be trained to address residents’ concerns, particularly regarding the collection of personal information, including details about bank accounts.“People will be assured that their data will remain confidential and will not be leaked,” an official said.Also Read | Private teachers can be roped in for Census as Centre amends rulesInformation collected and digital toolsQuestions on education will cover literacy and digital literacy, attendance at educational institutions, highest educational qualification and stream or discipline. Respondents will also be asked about their employment status during the previous year, occupation, economic activity, industry or trade, nature of work and travel to their workplace.Census 2027 is being conducted using digital tools for the first time, with data collected through a dedicated mobile application while retaining the traditional door-to-door enumeration process.

title: Delhi gets LG nod to merge four govt hospitals into AIIMS-like institution | Latest News Delhi
description: The plan aims to share staff and facilities, improve referrals and expand medical education. The Delhi cabinet must approve the integration.  | Latest News Delhi
content: Decks have been cleared for the proposed merger of four major government hospitals in east Delhi – Guru Tegh Bahadur (GTB) Hospital, Delhi State Cancer Institute (DSCI), Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital (RGSSH) and the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences (IHBAS) – into a single autonomous, multi-speciality institution modelled on the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), health minister Pankaj Singh said on Thursday.The proposal, seen by HT, envisages dissolving the separate bodies currently governing the four hospitals in Dilshad Garden and its vicinity, and bringing them under a single entity with a unified administrative structure.Singh said the Delhi government had received lieutenant governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu’s approval for the integration and would soon invite tenders for the next stage of the process.Also Read | 7 years on, no sanctioned posts: Chandigarh Sector 48 hospital still depends on GMCH-32 medics“We have received the LG’s approval for the integration of the four hospitals. We will soon float the tender for the same. Now trans-Yamuna area will have a multispeciality AIIMS-like institution, that will provide direct benefit to around 6 million population of the area and subsequently to the larger Delhi residents,” Singh said, adding that work was progressing on a fast track to provide subsidised healthcare services.The LG’s office did not respond to HT’s requests for comment.Expected Benefits for Patients and Medical EducationAccording to the proposal document, the merger is intended to reduce duplication of services and make better use of existing infrastructure and staff. All specialities that are offered by these different hospitals will be consolidated under a single (and larger) banner, while patients will now be able to be cross-referred to the other units – something which isn’t possible right now.The proposal also envisages pooling teaching positions across the institutions to increase postgraduate medical seats and expanding infrastructure to accommodate more undergraduate MBBS seats. The government expects that sharing facilities, staff and teaching resources will help the hospitals treat patients more efficiently and expand medical education.Also Read | Putting patients, outcomes and clinical evidence firstGovernance and Next StepsAt present, the four institutions operate under different governance arrangements.GTB Hospital is run directly by the Delhi government and has an attached University College of Medical Sciences. The other three are governed by separate societies, according to the proposal.“The societies that are now governing these hospitals separately will be dissolved and there will be a formation of a new governing body, which will be on the same lines as the AIIMS Delhi governing system,” a senior government official said.The next step is to obtain approval from the Delhi cabinet, which the proposal estimates could take around six months. An administrative order formalising the integration would follow, the official said.Before that, the health department plans to appoint a transactional adviser and an infrastructure consultant through a tender. The consultants will assess how facilities can be shared, help frame rules and regulations for infrastructure use, develop the institutional framework and prepare the cabinet note required for the next round of approval, the official said.

title: Heated exchanges, mic-snatching: Delhi's MCD house sees clashes over ward funds, pollution and Yamuna clean-up | Latest News Delhi
description: Mayor Pravesh Wahi said the MCD’s disciplinary committee would take action against members involved in disruption, as councillors tore papers and threw water.  | Latest News Delhi
content: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi’s (MCD) House meeting on Thursday was marked by heated confrontations over nearly every issue, including ward-wise budgetary allocations, pollution preparedness, Yamuna clean-up, and the undisposed garbage in the city, including an attempt to snatch the microphone from the mayor and the throwing of paper.Addressing the disruption during the meeting at a press conference afterwards, mayor Pravesh Wahi said the MCD’s disciplinary committee would initiate action against the members involved.Also read: Chaos erupts at Delhi MCD house during debate, AAP alleges 'personal attack' on councillorAgenda Items Passed Without DeliberationIn the end, 23 items on the agenda were passed without deliberation. Among this was reclaiming land on the Okhla and Bhalswa dumpsites by processing legacy waste through bio-remediation and bio-mining, along with the development of waste-processing facilities with minimum capacities of 1,800 tonnes per day (TPD) at Bhalswa, 700 TPD at Shingola, 1,400 TPD at Okhla and 1,200 TPD at Narela-Bawana landfill sites, among others.Other proposals that were approved included temporarily allotting MCD land for a batching plant near Chandni Chowk Metro Station, establishing a 125-tonne-per-day (MTPD) dung-based compressed biogas (CBG) plant at Bhalswa Dairy, and implementing the Zero Waste Colony initiative in 12 zones of the corporation.The proposal to introduce garbage user charge was postponed for consideration later.Also read: ₹16-crore biogas plant in Najafgarh">Delhi CM inaugurates ₹16-crore biogas plant in NajafgarhDispute Over Ward-wise Budget AllocationsThe meeting started at 2:30pm and one of the first points of confrontation concerned the allocation of funds to individual ward councillors. This triggered a verbal spat between Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) members.Wahi announced that the allocation was being increased from the existing ₹50 lakh to ₹75 lakh.“The MCD is continuously undertaking new initiatives for the public good. As part of this, every councillor will be allocated ₹25 lakh for development projects in their respective wards, and 2,500 additional sanitation workers will be engaged for a period of three months to ensure improved cleanliness during the upcoming festive season,” he said in the house.However, Leader of the Opposition, councillor Ankush Narang criticised the allocation, saying the ruling BJP had promised ₹2 crore in funds for each councillor.“Even after seven months, only ₹50 lakh has been provided. With Diwali just around the corner, the BJP still has no concrete plan to release the remaining funds,” Narang said in the meeting.Also read: MHA asks MCD for audit plan covering every building in cityDisputes Over Pollution, Garbage and the YamunaDiscussion over pollution preparedness, undisposed garbage across the city, and the cleanliness of the Yamuna, further intensified the confrontation between members.Later, Naziya Danish, a councillor backed by the Congress party, criticised Shagufta Chaudhary Zubair, who was earlier associated with the Congress but joined AAP in 2024.During the ensuing altercation, they climbed the dais and attempted to snatch the microphone from Wahi. The confrontation escalated further, with members tearing papers and throwing water at one another.At around 4:00pm, after roughly 90 minutes the mayor announced that all agendas had been passed and adjourned the meeting.

title: ‘Security concerns’: Delhi Police denies permission for Diljit Dosanjh's Oct 30 concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium | Latest News Delhi
description: A hoax bomb threat email sent to Delhi schools on October 15 reportedly warned students against attending the concert, with pro-Khalistani slogans included.  | Latest News Delhi
content: Delhi Police has denied permission for Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh’s concert in the Capital on October 30, citing security concerns, according to a letter the police wrote to ticketing partner BookMyShow.However, as of Thursday evening, the ticketing partner had not removed the show listing from its app or website.Dosanjh’s Aura India Tour concert was scheduled at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. In a letter to BookMyShow, the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (South District) stated, “With reference to your application, I am to inform you that your request for organising Diljit Dosanjh’s Aura India Tour Delhi at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on 30.10.2026 has been examined by this office. In view of the specific threat-related inputs, coupled with the multifarious security and law and order commitments arising out of the ongoing festive season and other important law and order concerns, the same cannot be acceded to.”Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal confirmed that permission was not granted, but refrained from sharing more details.Also read: Many threats, only 1 traced: School hoax hunt flounders in DelhiThreat-related inputs and hoax emailA senior police officer, who did not wish to be named, said apart from the “festive rush”, one of the reasons is a hoax bomb threat e-mail received by multiple schools in Delhi on the morning of October 15. One such e-mail, seen by HT, warned students not to attend Dosanjh’s concert on October 30.The hoax e-mail also had pro-Khalistani slogans. Six schools received the e-mail, including The British School, Mount Carmel, Ahlcon International School, and Ahlcon Public School.Meanwhile, Dosanjh or his team has not yet commented on the development.Also read: Multiple schools across Delhi receive bomb threats; nothing suspicious, say policePolitical reactions to the decisionDosanjh held concerts on October 26 and October 27, 2024, at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, with each day drawing over 40,000.Meanwhile, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj took to social media to attack Delhi Police and the BJP-led Delhi government. “Real heroes like Diljit Dosanjh supported the farmers’ movement and spoke out against police violence against students. The government is biased against such brave Punjabis. It earlier banned his film Sutlej, which was based on Punjab police atrocities during the militancy,” Bharadwaj alleged on X.Also read: 'Were told can't land in Delhi due to security reasons': Frankfurt-Delhi Air India passengers recall hijacking scareResponding to the allegations, Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra accused AAP of doing petty politics. “Diljit Dosanjh had performed at numerous university-level shows as well as at the Indira Gandhi Stadium. Most importantly, after the farmers’ protest, he performed a grand show at the same Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on October 26-27, 2024,” Malhotra said.

title: ఆదిలాబాద్‌లో పత్తి క్వింటాలుకు రికార్డు స్థాయిలో రూ.9,260.. కనీస మద్దతు ధర రూ.8,667 కంటే ఎక్కువ! | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: తెలంగాణలో పత్తి ధర రికార్డులు సృష్టిస్తోంది. కనీస మద్దతు ధర దాటి పలుకుతోంది. డిమాండ్ ఎక్కువ ఉండటంతో వ్యాపారులు మంచి ధర పెడుతున్నారు.
content: ఆదిలాబాద్ వ్యవసాయ మార్కెట్ యార్డులో గురువారం పత్తి కొనుగోళ్లు ప్రారంభమయ్యాయి. మొదటి రోజే ప్రైవేటు వ్యాపారులు క్వింటాలు పత్తికి రికార్డు స్థాయిలో రూ.9,260 ధర చెల్లించారు. ఇది ప్రభుత్వం నిర్ణయించిన కనీస మద్దతు ధర (MSP) క్వింటాలుకు రూ.8,667 కంటే ఎక్కువ. ఈ పత్తిలో తేమ శాతం 8శాతంగా ఉంది.రాష్ట్రంలో పత్తి కొనుగోళ్లు ప్రారంభమైన మొదటి రోజున నమోదైన అత్యధిక ధర ఇదే కావచ్చు. జిల్లా కలెక్టర్ రాజర్షి షా మార్కెట్ యార్డులో పత్తి కొనుగోలు ప్రక్రియను లాంఛనంగా ప్రారంభించారు. ఆయన మార్కెట్ యార్డును పరిశీలించి, వ్యాపార లావాదేవీలు సజావుగా సాగేందుకు చేసిన ఏర్పాట్లను సమీక్షించారు. రైతులు తమ పత్తిని సులభంగా అమ్ముకునేందుకు వీలుగా జిల్లావ్యాప్తంగా 33 జిన్నింగ్ మిల్లులను, 18 పత్తి కొనుగోలు కేంద్రాలను ఏర్పాటు చేసినట్లు అధికార వర్గాలు తెలిపాయి.ఆదిలాబాద్ మార్కెట్ యార్డులో రైతులకు తాగునీరు వంటి కనీస సౌకర్యాలు కల్పించారు. అలాగే వారికి ప్రయోజనం చేకూర్చేలా రూపాయికే భోజనం పథకాన్ని కూడా అందుబాటులో ఉంచారు. జిల్లాలోని కొన్ని ప్రాంతాల్లో ఇంకా పత్తి ఏరే పని కొనసాగుతుండటంతో, రాబోయే రోజుల్లో వ్యాపార కార్యకలాపాలు మరింత ఊపందుకోనున్నాయి.రాష్ట్రంలో 2026-27 సీజన్‌కు గాను మద్దతు ధరతో పత్తి సేకరణ ప్రక్రియను కాటన్‌ కార్పొరేషన్‌ ఆఫ్‌ ఇండియా (CCI) అధికారికంగా వేగవంతం చేసింది. ఇందులో భాగంగా రాష్ట్రవ్యాప్తంగా తొలివిడతగా 157 కొనుగోలు కేంద్రాలను అందుబాటులోకి తీసుకువచ్చింది. సీసీఐ కేంద్రాల్లో పంటను విక్రయించేందుకు మొదటిరోజే 8,205 మంది రైతులు ఆన్‌లైన్‌లో స్లాట్ బుకింగ్ చేసుకున్నారు.ప్రస్తుతం బహిరంగ మార్కెట్‌లో పత్తికి మంచి ధర లభిస్తుండటంతో, ప్రారంభ రోజున సీసీఐ కేంద్రాలకు రైతుల రాక కొంత తక్కువగానే నమోదైంది. మరిన్ని కొనుగోలు కేంద్రాలను కూడా పూర్తిస్థాయిలో అందుబాటులోకి తీసుకురానున్నారు. రాష్ట్రవ్యాప్తంగా మొత్తం 356 జిన్నింగ్ మిల్లులు అందుబాటులో ఉండగా, ప్రభుత్వం ఇప్పటివరకు 30 జిల్లాల పరిధిలోని 335 జిన్నింగ్ మిల్లులను సీసీఐ కొనుగోలు కేంద్రాలుగా నోటిఫై చేస్తూ నిర్ణయం తీసుకుంది.ఈ ఏడాది రాష్ట్రవ్యాప్తంగా సుమారు 48.20 లక్షల ఎకరాల్లో రైతులు పత్తి పంటను సాగు చేశారు. ఎల్-నినో ప్రభావం, ప్రతికూల వాతావరణ పరిస్థితుల వల్ల ఈసారి పత్తి దిగుబడి తగ్గే అవకాశం ఉందని అంచనా వేస్తున్నారు. ఉత్పత్తి తగ్గి డిమాండ్ పెరగడంతో ప్రైవేటు వ్యాపారులు పోటీపడి పత్తిని కొనుగోలు చేస్తున్నారు. ఓపెన్ మార్కెట్‌లో మద్దతు ధర కంటే ఎక్కువ రేటు లభిస్తుండటంతో రైతులు కూడా ప్రైవేట్ వ్యాపారులకే విక్రయించేందుకు మొగ్గు చూపుతున్నారు.

title: పౌర్ణమి రోజు ధ్యానం ఎందుకు చేయాలి? ఆధ్యాత్మిక రహస్యాలివే | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: పౌర్ణమి వేళ ఆధ్యాత్మిక సాధకులు ధ్యానం చేయడానికి గల ప్రాముఖ్యతను ఆత్మన్ అవేర్‌నెస్ సెంటర్‌కు చెందిన శ్రీ శ్రీ గురూజీ సుందర్ వివరించారు. మనస్సును అంతర్ముఖం చేసుకోవడానికి ఈ సమయం ఎలా ఉపయోగపడుతుందో, ధ్యానం చేసే సరైన పద్ధతులను ఆయన పంచుకున్నారు.
content: సనాతన ఆధ్యాత్మిక సాంప్రదాయాల్లో పౌర్ణమికి ఎంతో విశిష్ట స్థానం ఉంది. లౌకిక జీవన పరుగుల నుంచి కాసేపు విరామం తీసుకుని, ధ్యానం ద్వారా తమ దృష్టిని అంతరంగం వైపు మరల్చడానికి పౌర్ణమి తిథిని సరైన అవకాశంగా సాధకులు భావిస్తారు. ఈ క్రమంలోనే 2026 అక్టోబర్ 26న రానున్న ఆశ్వయుజ పౌర్ణమి (హంటర్స్ మూన్) వేళ ధ్యానం వెనుక ఉన్న ఆధ్యాత్మిక అంతరార్థాన్ని ఆత్మన్ అవేర్‌నెస్ సెంటర్ అధిపతి శ్రీ శ్రీ గురూజీ సుందర్ హెచ్‌టీ ప్రతినిధితో పంచుకున్నారు.ఆశ్వయుజ పౌర్ణమి సమయంభారత కాలమానం ప్రకారం పూర్ణిమ అక్టోబర్ 25, ఆదివారం ఉదయం 11:55 గంటలకు ప్రారంభమవుతుంది. అక్టోబర్ 26, సోమవారం ఉదయం 9:41 గంటలకు పౌర్ణమి ముగుస్తుంది. అమెరికా ఈడీటీ కాలమానం ప్రకారం 2026 అక్టోబర్ 26న అర్ధరాత్రి 12:12 గంటలకు ఆశ్వయుజ పౌర్ణమి నిండు రూపానికి చేరుకుంటుంది.దైనందిన ఒత్తిళ్ల నుంచి ఉపశమనం పొంది, మౌనంగా ధ్యానం చేసుకోవడానికి ఈ సమయాన్ని ఒక అవకాశంగా మార్చుకోవచ్చని ఆధ్యాత్మిక వేత్తలు సూచిస్తున్నారు.ధ్యానానికి పౌర్ణమి ఎందుకు అనుకూలం?పౌర్ణమి వేళ ధ్యానం చేయడం వల్ల సాధకుల్లో అంతర్ చేతన పెరుగుతుందని గురూజీ సుందర్ చెప్పారు. నిత్య జీవితంలో ఎదురయ్యే గందరగోళం నుంచి దృష్టి మళ్లించి, అంతర్మథనం చేసుకోవడానికి ఈ తిథి సహకరిస్తుందని తెలిపారు."పౌర్ణమి రోజున ధ్యానం చేసే సాధకుడు ఎటువంటి ఆటంకాలు లేకుండా ప్రశాంతంగా తన అంతరంగ శూన్యంలోకి పయనించగలడు" అని గురూజీ వివరించారు. అయితే చంద్రుని ప్రభావం ధ్యానంపై నేరుగా పడుతుందనేది సైంటిఫిక్ నిరూపణ కాదని, ఇది పూర్తిగా ఆధ్యాత్మిక విశ్వాసాలకు సంబంధించిన అంశమని స్పష్టం చేశారు.పౌర్ణమి రోజు ధ్యానం చేసే విధానంధ్యానం ప్రారంభించడానికి ఎలాంటి సంక్లిష్ట పూజా విధానాలు లేదా ప్రత్యేక పరికరాలు అవసరం లేదని ఆత్మన్ అవేర్‌నెస్ సెంటర్ మార్గదర్శకాలు చెబుతున్నాయి. సరైన పద్ధతిలో ధ్యానం చేయడానికి కొన్ని సూచనలు..కృతజ్ఞతా భావం: మనకు సహకరించిన వ్యక్తులు, లభించిన మంచి అనుభవాలను గుర్తుచేసుకుంటూ కృతజ్ఞతతో ధ్యానాన్ని ప్రారంభించాలి.సౌకర్యవంతమైన ఆసనం: వెన్నుముకను నిటారుగా ఉంచి, ప్రశాంతంగా కళ్ళు మూసుకుని కూర్చోవాలి.ఆలోచనల పరిశీలన: మనస్సులో వచ్చే ఆలోచనలు, భావోద్వేగాలను మంచి-చెడు అని తీర్పులు చెప్పకుండా కేవలం గమనిస్తూ ఉండాలి.మౌనం పాటించడం: ప్రారంభంలో 15 నుంచి 30 నిమిషాల పాటు ప్రశాంతంగా, మౌనంగా కూర్చోవడం అలవాటు చేసుకోవాలి.ప్రార్థనతో ముగింపు: ధ్యానం ముగిసే సమయంలో సర్వేజనా సుఖినోభవంతు అనే భావనతో అందరి శ్రేయస్సు కోరుతూ ప్రార్థించాలి.కేవలం పౌర్ణమి నాడే ధ్యానం చేయాలా?ధ్యానం అనేది కేవలం పౌర్ణమి రోజుకే పరిమితం కాదని గురూజీ సుందర్ స్పష్టం చేశారు. నిర్దిష్ట రోజు లేదా సమయం కంటే సాధనలో ఉండే నిబద్ధత, నిరంతర అభ్యాసమే ముఖ్యమని చెప్పారు.ఈ సందర్భంగా సూఫీ సాధ్వి రబియా అల్ అడవ్యా జీవితంలోని ఒక సంఘటనను ఆయన గుర్తుచేశారు. ఒక పౌర్ణమి నాడు రబియా శిష్యులు బయట వెన్నెల అందాలను చూస్తూ మురిసిపోతుండగా, ఆమె మాత్రం ఇంట్లో కూర్చుని అంతర్గత సాధనపైనే దృష్టి పెట్టారు. బయటి భౌతిక అందాల కంటే అంతరంగంలో వెలిగే జ్ఞాన కాంతి వైపు దృష్టి మరల్చడమే ఆధ్యాత్మిక సాధన ముఖ్య ఉద్దేశమని ఈ కథ స్పష్టం చేస్తోంది. ప్రశాంతత అవసరమైన ఏ సమయంలోనైనా ధ్యానం, ప్రార్థన చేసుకోవచ్చని ఆయన వివరించారు.

title: Gunde Ninda Gudi Gantalu Today Episode: బాలు తల్లి ప్రేమ.. అరుణ్ సస్పెండ్.. శోభను గెంటేసిన బాలు.. శృతి సపోర్ట్ | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: Gunde Ninda Gudi Gantalu Serial October 23rd Episode: గుండె నిండా గుడి గంటలు సీరియల్ అక్టోబర్ 23 ఎపిసోడ్ లో బాలుని మీనా కాపాడుతుంది. ఇది గుణ పనే అని బాలు తెలుసుకుంటాడు. అటు చివర్లో ఇంట్లో చిచ్చు పెట్టడానికి వచ్చిన శోభను శృతి సపోర్ట్ తో బాలు గెంటేస్తాడు.
content: Gunde Ninda Gudi Gantalu Serial Today Episode: స్టార్ మా సీరియల్ గుండె నిండా గుడి గంటలు ఈరోజు ఎపిసోడ్ లో బాలు కారు, లైసెన్స్ తిరిగి రావడమే కాకుండా అరుణ్ సస్పెండ్ అవుతాడు. తనను మీనానే కాపాడటంతో ఆమెను దేవత అంటూ బాలు పొగుడుతాడు. అటు బాలు తల్లి ప్రేమ ఎలాంటిదో ఈ ఎపిసోడ్ కళ్లకు కట్టినట్లు చూపించింది.అరుణ్ బండారం బయటపెట్టిన కానిస్టేబుల్అరుణ్ బండారం కానిస్టేబుల్ బయటపెట్టే సీన్ తో సీరియల్ శుక్రవారం (అక్టోబర్ 23) ఎపిసోడ్ మొదలైంది. అరుణ్ సారే కావాలని కేసు పెట్టారని, బాలు కారు బ్రేకులు ఫెయిలయ్యాయని అతడు సీఐతో చెబుతాడు. తనకు కూడా గాయాలు అలా అయినవే అని అంటాడు.బాలు ఒకరి ప్రాణాలు కాపాడేవాడు తప్ప తీయడని, తన కూతురు, మనవడు ప్రాణాలతో ఉండటానికి కారణం బాలునే అని కానిస్టేబుల్ వెల్లడిస్తాడు. అరుణ్ సార్ కు బాలుపై ఉన్న వ్యక్తిగత కక్ష వల్లే ఇలా చేశాడని చెబుతాడు.అరుణ్ సస్పెన్షన్.. బాలుకి కారు కీస్ ఇచ్చి..దీంతో అరుణ్ పై సీఐ వారం పాటు సస్పెన్షన్ వేటు వేస్తాడు. వ్యక్తిగత కక్షలతో ఇలా చేసినందుకు మందలిస్తాడు. నీ వల్ల తనకు చీవాట్లు పడేవని అంటాడు. కానీ అరుణ్ మాత్రం ఈ బాలు వల్లే తనకు ప్రతిసారీ చెడు జరుగుతోందని అంటాడు. మరి నీవల్ల నాకు జరుగుతున్నదేంటని బాలు వాదిస్తాడు. చివరికి బాలు కారు కీస్, లైసెన్స్ ను అరుణ్ ద్వారానే బాలుకి సీఐ ఇప్పిస్తాడు. ఆ తర్వాత కానిస్టేబుల్ కు బాలు, మీనా థ్యాంక్స్ చెబుతారు. అటు అరుణ్ ఆవేశంతో రగిలిపోతుంటాడు.దేవత అంటూ మీనాపై బాలు ప్రశంసలుఆ తర్వాత బయటకు వచ్చి కారును చూసి బాలు ఎమోషనల్ అవుతాడు. ఇది లేకపోతే మనం ఏమైపోయేవాళ్లమో అని అంటాడు. మీనాను కూడా బండి వదిలేసి కారులో తనతోపాటే రమ్మంటాడు. మీనానే చూస్తూ డ్రైవ్ చేస్తుండటంతో రోడ్డు ముందుంది అని ఆమె అంటుంది. కానీ నా కళ్ల ముందు దేవత ఉందంటూ భార్యను పొగుడుతాడు. నీవల్లే ఈ కారు నాకు మళ్లీ దక్కింది.. నువ్వు ఆ గర్భవతికి సాయం చేయడం, ఆమె వచ్చి నిజం చెప్పడం వల్లే అసలు విషయం అందరికీ తెలసిందని బాలు అంటాడు.నా ఐదు లక్షలు పోయినప్పుడు మీరు కూడా నాకు సాయం చేశారు కదా..మనం భార్యాభర్తలం ఒకరికొకరం సాయం చేసుకోవాలి అని మీనా అంటుంది. అయినా మీరు కూడా మీ ప్రాణాలను పణంగా పెట్టి ఆమెకు ఏమీ కాకుండా చేశారు.. దీనికంతటికీ ఈ కంకణమే కారణం.. అదే మనల్ని కాపాడిందని మీనా అంటుంది. కారు బ్రేకులు ఎవరో కావాలనే తీశారని అన్నారు కదా అని మీనా అంటే.. అవును అదెవరో కనిపెట్టాలని బాలు అంటాడు.ఇంట్లో బాలు, మీనా ఒకరిపై మరొకరి పొగడ్తలు.. కుళ్లుకున్న ప్రభావతి, మనోజ్ఇటు ఇంట్లో బాలు, మీనా కోసం సత్యం ఎదురు చూస్తుంటాడు. ప్రభావతి మాత్రం తనదైన స్టైల్లో నోరు జారుతూనే ఉంటుంది. వాళ్లు ఇంటికి రాగానే అప్పుడే వదిలేశారా అంటుంది. అంత సులువుగా ఎలా బయటపడ్డావని మనోజ్ వెటకారంగా అడుగుతాడు. కారు, లైసెన్స్ రెండూ ఇచ్చారని, ఇదంతా మీనా వల్లే సాధ్యమైందని బాలు చెబుతాడు.దీంతో ప్రభావతి, మనోజ్ మరింత కుళ్లుకుంటారు. మీ పెంపకం, అమ్మమ్మగారి పెంపకంలో ఆయనకు అన్నీ మంచి లక్షణాలే వచ్చాయి.. ఓ గర్భిణి ప్రాణం పోకుండా కారును తీసుకెళ్లి పోలీసు బైకుకు ఢీకొట్టాడు.. అదే ఆయనను కాపాడింది అని మీనా అంటుంది. ఇద్దరి పొగడ్తలూ వినలేక ప్రభావతి, మనోజ్ ముఖాలు అదోలా పెడతారు. ఈ గ్యాప్ లో శృతి తనదైన స్టైల్లో మనోజ్, ప్రభావతిపై పంచులు వేస్తుంది. ఈ మధ్య నీకు బాగా వెటకారం ఎక్కువైందని ప్రభావతి అంటుంది.కారు బ్రేకులు మన ఇంట్లో వాళ్లే కావాలని తీసేశారన్న బాలు.. రోహిణిపై డౌట్అయితే కారు బ్రేకులు ఎవరో మన ఇంట్లో వాళ్లే కావాలని తీశారని బాలు చెప్పడంతో అందరూ షాకవుతారు. ముందు రోజు కేవలం మన ఇంట్లోనే కరెంట్ పోయిన విషయం గుర్తుందా అని మీనా అంటుంది. అప్పుడే రోహిణిపై అనుమానం కలిగేలా మనోజ్ మాట్లాడటంతో ఆమె షాక్ తింటుంది. ఆ రోజు కరెంటు పోవడం, నా దిండు కింద ఉన్న తాళాలు ఎక్కడో మూలన పడి ఉండటం చూస్తుంటే ఎవరో మన ఇంట్లో వాళ్లే ఈ పని చేసినట్లు కన్ఫమ్ అవుతుందని బాలు అంటాడు.మనోజ్ ఈ పని చేశాడా అని శృతి అంటే.. ఆ పిరికి సన్యాసికి అంత సీన్ లేదని బాలు అంటాడు. తర్వాత రోహిణి భయంతో వెళ్లి నీళ్లు తాగుతుంది. ఆమె చుట్టూ తిరుగుతూ అనుమానంగా చూస్తుంటే.. తాను అంత దుర్మార్గురాలిని కానని చెబుతుంది. చివరికి తల్లిని కూడా బాలు అనుమానంగా చూస్తాడు. ఈ మధ్య చింతామణిలాంటి వాళ్లతో సావాసం చేసి ఇలాంటివి చేస్తుందేమో అని అంటాడు. దీంతో వాడంటే ఇష్టం లేదు కానీ.. మరీ కన్న కొడుకును అలా చేసేంత రాక్షసురాలిని కాను అని ప్రభావతి అంటుంది.గుణ మనుషులే ఈ పని చేశారన్న బాలుఆ తర్వాత పైన గదిలోకి వెళ్లిన బాలుకి సడెన్ గా తన కారు వెంట రౌడీలు పడి తనను రెచ్చగొట్టిన సీన్ గుర్తుకు వస్తుంది. మీనా రాగానే ఆ విషయం చెబుతూ వాళ్లు గుణ మనుషులే అని, అంటే వాళ్లే ఈ పని చేశారని అంటాడు. వాళ్లు కావాలని కారు స్పీడు పెంచేలా రెచ్చగొట్టి తన ప్రాణం తీయాలని చూశారని చెబుతాడు. వాళ్లకు కారు తాళాలు ఇంట్లో వాళ్లే ఇచ్చి ఉంటారని అంటాడు. ఆ పని అత్తయ్యే చేశారని అనుకుంటున్నారా అని మీనా అంటుంది.తల్లిపై బాలు ఎనలేని ప్రేమఅదేం లేదు.. ఆమెకు నేనంటే ఇష్టం లేదు కానీ.. మరీ కన్న కొడుకును చంపేంత దుర్మార్గురాలైతే కాదు అని బాలు అంటాడు. మరి మీ తల్లిపై ఇంత ప్రేమ పెట్టుకొని ఎందుకు ఆమెతో ఊరికే గొడవ పడుతుంటారు.. నానా రకాల పేర్లు పెట్టి పిలుస్తారు అని మీనా అడుగుతుంది. చిన్నప్పటి నుంచి అమ్మ ప్రేమ లేకుండా పెరిగాను.. ఆమెను అలా ఆట పట్టిస్తూ, ఆమెతో అలా తిట్టించుకుంటూ తిరిగితే అలాగైనా కాస్త అమ్మతో గడిపిన ఫీలింగ్ కలుగుతుంది అని బాలు అంటాడు. మరి ఆమెను చింతామణితో పోల్చారని మీనా అడిగితే.. ఏదో సరదాకి అలా అన్నాను కానీ ఆ చింతామణికి, మా అమ్మకి పోలిక ఎక్కడ.. అని తల్లిపై తనకున్న ఎనలేని ప్రేమను చాటుకుంటాడు బాలు.శృతి తల్లి శోభ గొడవ.. తరిమేసిన బాలుచివర్లో ఇంట్లో వాళ్లందరూ కలిసి ఇల్లు దులుపుతుంటారు. అప్పుడే శృతి తల్లి శోభ వస్తుంది. శృతి కూడా ఓ పని మనిషిలా ఇల్లు దులపడం చూసి షాకవుతుంది. నువ్వు కూడా దులుపుతున్నావా.. నీకా కర్మేంటి అని అంటుంది. మేం వద్దన్నా.. సరదాగా ఉంటుందని ఆమే చేస్తోందని సత్యం అంటాడు. మీరూ దులిపి తరించండి అని బాలు వెటకారంగా అంటాడు.మీ నాన్న బస్సు డ్రైవర్ గా పని చేసి ఖాళీగా ఇంట్లో ఉన్నాడు కదా.. ఆయనతో దులిపించుకోండి అని శోభ అనడంతో శృతి కోప్పడుతుంది. ఇలాగే మాట్లాడే బాలు నిన్ను పలానాదాన్ని తరిమేసినట్లు తరుముతాడు అని అంటుంది. బాలు కూడా నిజంగానే శోభను ఇంట్లో నుంచి గెంటేసే ప్రయత్నం చేస్తాడు. అక్కడితో గుండె నిండా గుడి గంటలు సీరియల్ ఈరోజు ఎపిసోడ్ ముగుస్తుంది.

title: Norwegians fall for wild investment scam: Buying gold and leaving it in the forest | Trending
description: Swindlers have persuaded Norwegians into buying gold and leaving it in the forest as part of a growing investment fraud.  | Trending
content: Swindlers have persuaded Norwegians into buying gold and leaving it in the forest as part of a growing investment fraud, according to the country’s banking lobby. Several bank clients have spent large sums to purchase gold and then left it out in nature, following promises that “others will keep it safe while the value rises,” Finans Norge said in a statement Thursday, without specifying the amounts. The gold was subsequently stolen.Also Read: ₹1.5 lakh scam on X">Why is ‘Jay Singh Rathore’ trending? 5 things about the alleged ₹1.5 lakh scam on XIt said the scheme is one of three fraud methods that banks are “specifically warning against right now.” The first of such cases was registered in the spring, Gry Nergård, director of anti-fraud operations at Finans Norge, said by phone. Incidents had been reported in Oslo and towns around it but also in Bergen on the west coast, she added.Last year, the losses of Norwegian lenders and their customers from financial fraud totaled 962 million kroner ($100 million), the lobby group said. At the same time, the banks prevented fraud attempts amounting to over 3.5 billion kroner.Finans Norge is conducting an anti-fraud information campaign titled “NO WAY – you won’t fool me,” together with the country’s banks, aiming to increase the awareness of Norwegians about identifying and avoiding scam attempts.
