title: It’s GO time! Indian travellers share their most unforgettable moments | Hindustan Times
description: Dancing with the dead in Madagascar. Partying until dawn in Tehran. Communing with spirits in Benin. Indian travellers are going farther to experience what guidebooks leave out. The pay-off is epic. So are the risks
content: The island where the dead don’t stay buriedOne doesn’t simply stumble upon a Famadihana. The Turning Of The Bones ritual, practised by the Merina and Betsileo ethnic groups in Madagascar, involves a family exhuming the remains of their ancestors, rewrapping the corpses in fresh linens, invoking memories of the deceased through dance and music, and returning the bones and bodies to the tomb. Family members come from across the country, sometimes travelling for days, to attend. To those outside the community, it seems macabre. To Mohammad Anas (@TravelWithAK), 26, who first heard about it three years ago, it was a cultural celebration he knew he simply had to see. “Death does not mean the person is excluded from the family,” says the travel vlogger from Mumbai. “For them, passed on members live in their midst. The ceremony is a way of bringing them back and celebrating with them.”Anas visited in October 2023. Getting there took more than a little legwork. There are no direct flights between India and the island on the south-east edge of Africa. In the capital, Antananarivo, he asked locals about the ritual, “Because when there is Famadihana, the whole village and the locality knows that something like this is going to happen.” Then, he convinced an English-speaking driver to take him to a village hosting the ritual, nearly 80 kilometres away.Luckily, nearly eight hours and several pointed fingers later, they located the host family, the Raotozafys, and followed them to the celebration site. Anas watched as the family exhumed the bones of their relatives and re-bundled them with reverence. “Sometimes if the bodies have decomposed too much, two or three people are wrapped together to give the bundle more shape and strength,” he says. They placed photographs of the deceased on their respective bodies while a 20-piece band played Madagascar’s national anthem, followed by Christian prayers. They also brought their ancestors up-to-date on their lives. There was drinking (some of it was poured onto the wrapped bodies) music and dancing. “I saw a different side to the acceptance of death. Some mourn, the Malagasy celebrate. Culture belongs to the people, who am I to question it?” The party nation they don’t want to tell you aboutEven before war broke out in Iran, not too many Indians visited. Fewer than 10,000 Indian nationals would go there to study, work, or go on pilgrimage. All non-essential travel has been halted this year, which makes Pulkit Chaudhary’s memories of his December 2025 visit even more fond. The 26-year-old from Rajasthan (@TheTallTrotter) has posted YouTube videos, offering glimpses of everyday life in the capital Tehran, and the smaller cities of Rasht, Qazvin and Beheshti island.The Iranians love to party. “Contrary to what we are told, the culture is very European,” he says. “The people are open-minded, uninhibited, and modern.” There are no clubs, no bars in the Islamic republic, so they host parties at home – live music, cigarettes, families and all. Chaudhary’s Couchsurfing host, Maryam Zamyar, took him to one epic gathering in the Kerman province, 975 kilometres from Tehran. It was a 24 hour drive, with a stop at Isfahan, but it was worth it, he says. The people were celebrating Shab-e Yalda, the winter solstice and longest night of the year at the home of Zamyar’s childhood friend. “The kids were eating sweets and dancing, the youngsters were enjoying drinks and live music, older uncles were chilling and smoking shisha.”On the menu? Boz Ghormeh, their famous goat stew; Ash-e Kermani, a local soup of grains, legumes and herbs; and Zireh Polo, their version of jeera rice. For dessert, there was Kolucheh Kermani, a cookie filled with dates or nuts. There was lots of smoking, live music and lively chatter. “Music is a huge part of their culture and everyone knows how to play a regional instruments such as the sitar and daf, the frame drum,” he recounts. “Experiencing this unexpected side of Iran, to be invited as an outsider into their world was a heartwarming moment.” Where the spirits roam the city streetsBenin is tiny. The West-African nation is about the size of Telangana, with only half the population of the south Indian state. Barely 90 Indian or Indian-owned companies operate there, dealing in automobiles, textiles, and food processing.Few Indians visit. So, it was an eye-opener for Sharanya Iyer (@TrulyNomadly), 36, who went there in January, 2025. She was in the city of Ouidah during Vodun Days, a national celebration of the region’s ancient nature-focused religion.The excitement plays out right on the streets: Straw-covered spinning Zangbeto (night watchmen), ancestor worship, trance rituals and voodoo-like practices. “It’s super chaotic. There’s music, dancing, kids, adults. The energy is electric but overwhelming,” says Iyer.Snakes and reptiles, she says are her “biggest fear”. And yet, she couldn’t keep away from the Temple of Pythons, which honours the deity that embodies wisdom, protection and fertility. And she was determined to see the markets where priests prescribe specific rituals to infertility or marital problems. “Nobody’s allowed to film there because they’re sceptical of global perception of what they practise.” The cures can be as varied as a peacock feather or a dead monkey’s head or the carcass of an endangered species – in the belief that animals carry healing energy. “As travellers, we can only share what we experienced and felt. There is no room for judgment.” The frosty nation with a warm spot for IndiaVishnu Saha (@TheWanderingManiac), 27, knew he was going to be very far from his home, Hyderabad, when he visited Afghanistan in January this year. Temperatures there drop to below freezing, the wind makes it feel colder. But the locals, he says, were surprisingly warm.He stepped into a mobile shop in Kabul only to look for a tripod. But the moment the owners, brothers Jamshed and Jalal, found out he was Indian, everything changed. They declared, in Hindi, their undying love for Bollywood, with Jamshed even imitating SRK’s quintessential laugh. Before long, they’d invited Saha to dinner. “Refusal was not an option,” he says.They took him to Kabul’s popular restaurant, Ziyafat, which had traditional open spaces for groups of men and families to dine together. The restaurant, delighted to have an Indian guest, gave him a tour of the kitchen. “We had Kabuli pulao, Afghan naan, mutton karahi, grilled chicken, kebabs and dishes I can’t even remember,” Saha recalls. “I don’t think I had seen so much food in front of me before.” That meal must have cost at least ₹10,000 but his hosts refused to let him pay. “Countries like Afghanistan don’t see too many tourists, so when people do come, their hospitality is unmatched.”Locals told Saha that even though they didn’t like the government, they were glad to see the end of the war. It meant that Afghanistan was opening up to tourism and business, giving locals the opportunity to be seen for who they are. The road trip with a side of riskGarima Bakshi was on her second visit to Somaliland. She was there four years ago and was so taken in by the warmth of the Somalis, she knew she had to go back. This time around, in February 2026, she booked a four-day road trip from Hargeisa in Somaliland to Mogadishu, via Garowe, the capital of Puntland.The route runs through the Horn of Africa – forests, mountains, frankincense valleys, limestone valleys, pristine beaches. But it cuts through three separate governance systems, has passport controls, even currencies change along the way. “You travel through the bush in local buses which do not stop, except for a 30-minute lunch and toilet break,” says the 27-year-old who documents her trips on @WanderingWithPaint. “Foreigners rarely get permission to travel through all the areas on that route.”So, Bakshi disguised herself as a Somali woman. She put on an abaya, covering herself from head to toe and boarded the bus alone. Then three days in, when the bus stopped for lunch in a village controlled by Islamist militants, she ran into trouble. Someone had alerted them that there was a non-Somali woman on board. Bakshi was swiftly escorted off the bus by AK-47 wielding men. “They took me into a grocery shop -- the kind we see in movies – with a secret jail in the back.” They interrogated her for four hours about why she chose to smuggle herself via this route, searched her belongings and checked her passport. They only let her leave after taking the 350 USD (approx. ₹33,000) that she had on her, but spared her camera, phones and gadgets.Remarkably, the bus waited all this time. The passengers spent the night on board, in the middle of the desert. Bakshi reached her destination, and had a friend wire her enough money to get back to India. She says she booked her ride specifically to see how locals do it. “I can return to the comfort of my home. But this is real life for them. That’s quite humbling.”From HT Brunch, October 24, 2026Follow us on www.instagram.com/htbrunch

title: For these women tinkering with cyberdecks, all that glitters is code | Hindustan Times
description: Tech girlies, assemble! Women are making keychains that play music and plushies that record notes. What, like it’s hard?
content: When did tech get so boring? The 2000s had colourful Game Boys, Tamagotchis and phones shaped like burgers. Now, we’re stuck with black-and-grey rectangles that are aggressively functional, with the looming threat of AI stealing our jobs and drinking our water.Instagram girlies are rebelling by building gadgets with personality, no engineering degree needed. Their teacher: YouTube tutorials and Reddit’s r/cyberdecks. Their motor: Raspberry Pi (a credit-card-sized single-board computer). Their creations: Tiny computers that fit into powder compacts, pink dollhouses and dangly keychains. The mini-machines are designed to do specific things and do them well, be it run retro games, store music, or display ebook pages.This is about more than making computers cute. It’s a way for women to use tech for creativity and self-expression. Because, in the words of Elle Woods, who rocked a fuzzy pink cordless phone, “What, like it’s hard?” Fuzzy logicCyberdecks aren’t new. OGs cobbled together their own in the 1980s. The revival, however, is led by women, and draws from the early internet’s spirit of fun and experimentation.On Instagram, @RasPiManiax has fitted a cyberdeck (pearl embellishments, a mini compass, clock, screen and keyboard) inside her compact mirror. She uses it to plan yoga sequences and play downloaded music. When haters told @GaziSj to spend less time online and touch grass, she took the advice literally. Her cyberdeck is a wooden box, filled with actual grass and moss, along with a screen and keyboard for playing retro games.For 24-year-old Delhi-based UI/UX designer Mudita Singhal (@WithLuvAamo), the inspiration comes from the 1995 film Clueless (1995). Singhal says she was fascinated by the protagonist Cher Horowitz’s computerised wardrobe, which let her mix and match outfits for the day. “Every girl I knew wanted that technology. No one built it then, and we didn’t know at the time that we could do it ourselves.”Her latest cyberdeck (a tiny screen attached to a stuffed tiger she crocheted herself) is linked to a printer and prevents her ideas from languishing in her notes app. “Once a week, it automatically prints one idea that I just have to do, and the idea is then deleted from its memory.” DIY divasTech has long been a boys’ club. A 2026 survey by Akamai Technologies found that nearly 90% of women leave tech careers within a decade of starting them, while women account for less than a third of the global workforce in tech-related fields. Perhaps getting a safe space to tinker with tech on their own terms might help? “I don’t have a background in electrical engineering and I know nothing about hardware, but seeing other women on the internet do it made me think, maybe I can too,” says Singhal.Creators such as @SageCadence_, an electrical engineering student at Stanford, are making the process less intimidating, breaking cyberdeck-building down into five basic components: The Raspberry Pi (the brain), a screen, input devices such as keyboards and buttons, a power source, and an enclosure. The last is where things get fun. You can 3D-print a case, use acrylic or wood, or repurpose a vintage suitcase. Once the hardware works, it’s all about software customisation.Anjali Johan (@Pink.Progress.AJ), a 23-year-old computer engineer from Rajkot, Gujarat, knows how alienating the tech world can feel. “Even in my office, men would take up maximum space and equipment.” Her computer engineering course was dry and theoretical, not geared to build the fun stuff. Small, hands-on projects, she believes, can make learning the basics much more intuitive. Her own cyberdeck is an old smartwatch that plays music. “It’s like playing with Lego blocks. A YouTube video or ChatGPT and Gemini can tell you exactly which parts you’d need and how to program them.” Girl codeCyberdecks are just the beginning. @CovaCut has built a Tamagotchi-style flash drive, with a tutorial showing followers how to build and animate their own characters. @Ux_Deniza made a butterfly hairpin that records your voice and turns it into diary entries. Her step-by-step tutorial covers everything from the circuit board, mic and battery to the coding. She even shares the behind-the-scenes fails: Botched soldering jobs, wires that stuck out of the hairpin, and a last-minute decision to pretend they were part of the aesthetic. Meera Patil, 29, a firmware engineer at AMD in Canada, makes keychain charms embedded with NFC stickers that can play a voice note or song when tapped against a phone. She moulds them out of air-dry or polymer clay into tiny houses, flowers and letters tucked inside envelopes, then programs them using her phone. “It’s pretty simple. Even a layperson can do it.” Next on her list: Building a smartwatch that tracks UV exposure and tells you when it’s time to reapply sunscreen.Not everyone gets the vision. Singhal recalls a woman on Twitter who stitched together Raspberry Pis to make a corset, only to be flooded with comments from men asking, “What is this? You’re wasting so many Raspberry Pis.” Sigh. Some people do need to touch grass.From HT Brunch, October 24, 2026Follow us on www.instagram.com/htbrunch

title: Simone Biles breaks down in tears bidding farewell to Houston home that holds six years of memories | Hindustan Times
description: Simone Biles and her husband, NFL player Jonathan Owens, listed their Texas home for $1.275 million in September.
content: Simone Biles became emotional as she prepared to part ways with the Houston-area home she had lived in for six years. The Olympic champion revealed that the property attracted a buyer within only a few days.Simone Biles gets emotional while leaving homeOn Wednesday, October 21, the 29-year-old posted a heartfelt TikTok video, in which she was seen crying while getting ready to leave the house. In the caption, Biles shared that the property had sold soon after being listed.“Today is the first day the house is going to be on the market,” she said tearfully in the video.“Why the f--- am I boohoo crying? F---. This house will be on the market for the first time, and I don’t know why I’m boohoo crying,” she added.Also read | Travis Kelce, Taylor Swift buy Ohio lakefront home: Inside Chiefs star's new $5.35 million Bratenahl mansionBiles reflects on six years of memoriesBiles gave fans a look inside the property, showing rooms that had been emptied of furniture before taking them outside to the backyard, which featured a swimming pool.“I was here for six years, and I feel like there were just so many good memories, so many bad memories. But I feel like I grew up in this house. It’s made me a real adult, so I’m gonna miss it. Ugh, I didn’t think I’d be emotional about a house,” Biles mentioned.Near the end of the video, she became emotional once more as she expressed her hope that the house would hold the same special meaning for its new owners that it had for her. “Whoever buys this house, I hope it brings you as much joy as it did for me,” she concluded.Property finds buyer within four daysAs previously reported by In Touch, Simone Biles and her husband, NFL player Jonathan Owens, listed their Texas home for $1.275 million in September. The 3,998-square-foot property features four bedrooms, three-and-a-half bathrooms. The couple lived there while their nearby custom home was being built.Also read | Simone Biles reveals shocking health scare, support pours in: ‘Almost dying wasn’t on my…'The Houston Business Journal reported that the transaction was completed on October 15, with the sale price estimated to be between $1.08 million and $1.24 million. Biles purchased the house in 2020 and revealed in her caption that it found a buyer in just four days.

title: As the Hunter Moon arrives, a spiritual guru explains why the Full Moon is considered an auspicious day for spiritual seekers | Hindustan Times
description: According to a spiritual guru, the full Moon can offer spiritual seekers an opportunity to explore meditation more deeply. Here's how.
content: The October full Moon is a chance to pause, turn inward and make time for meditation. For many spiritual seekers, this lunar phase holds special meaning. Some believe it offers an opportunity to deepen their practice, while others use the night to reflect, pray and find calm.According to HH Guruji Sundar of Aathman Awareness Centre, the full Moon can offer spiritual seekers an opportunity to explore meditation more deeply. He explains why some people associate this day with inner stillness, while others may experience restlessness.Also Read What happens when you meditate in temples? A spiritual guru explainsWhen is the October full Moon in 2026?According to the Old Farmer’s Almanac, the October full Moon, known as the Hunter’s Moon, reaches its peak on October 26, 2026, at 12:11 a.m. EDT. In the United States, the exact local date and time can vary by time zone.The Hunter’s Moon gets its traditional name from seasonal hunting practices in the Northern Hemisphere. Beyond its place in the autumn sky, the full Moon also carries spiritual meaning for people who follow meditation and lunar traditions.Also Read Full Moon October 2026: Know the best time to witness the day in the US and its astrological meaningWhy is the full Moon considered auspicious for meditation?According to HH Guruji Sundar, spiritual seekers can use the full Moon as an opportunity to deepen their meditation practice.The spiritual guru tells HT that the Moon’s relationship with Earth holds spiritual significance for meditators. He believes that the day can help advanced seekers turn inward and experience a deeper state of awareness.As Guruji explains, “the meditator will have a graceful sail during meditation into their inner space.”Why do some people feel restless on the full moon day?Not everyone experiences meditation in the same way. Some people may find it easy to sit quietly, while others may struggle with racing thoughts or distractions.Guruji believes that a person’s ability to handle their inner energy influences how they experience the day. According to his teachings, regular meditation helps you observe your thoughts without letting them control your attention.Also Read Cleveland Clinic says you don’t have to be religious to meditate: Here's what beginners should knowHow to meditate on the October full MoonYou do not need a special room or elaborate ritual to begin. If you want to use the Hunter’s Moon as a moment for reflection, try these simple steps inspired by Aathman Awareness Centre’s guidance.Begin with gratitude: Spend a few moments thinking about the people and experiences you appreciate.Find a comfortable position: Sit with your back naturally straight and close your eyes gently.Observe your thoughts: Let thoughts and feelings come and go without fighting them or following every distraction.Sit in silence: Start with 10 to 15 minutes and gradually increase the time if you feel comfortable.End with a prayer: If prayer is part of your practice, offer a quiet wish for the well-being of others and yourself.You can practise these steps indoors. You do not need to look directly at the Moon or wait until it reaches its peak.Does full Moon meditation work on other days?According to Guruji, meditation does not depend on a particular date or hour. Sincerity and regular practice matter more than waiting for a specific lunar phase.He also shares a story about the Sufi mystic Rabi'a al-Adawiyya. When her disciples admired the beauty of the full Moon, she remained focused on her meditation and the divine presence she sought within.The story reflects a central idea in her spiritual tradition: looking beyond an external sight can help you reflect on your inner life.What should you remember about full Moon spirituality?The October full Moon can serve as a meaningful reminder to pause, reflect and reconnect with your spiritual practice. You can meditate, pray or spend a few quiet minutes away from daily distractions.As Guruji’s teachings suggest, the value lies not only in the lunar phase but also in the attention and sincerity you bring to your practice.Disclaimer: This article presents spiritual beliefs and practices for informational purposes only. Reader's discretion is advised.

title: Weekend Drive: Break the class ceiling | Hindustan Times
description: Kia’s Sorrento SUV is the first of its kind. It’s bigger than other SUVs. The middle-row seats shine. And it’s priced well, too
content: Kia isn’t dipping a toe into the premium SUV market with the Sorento. It’s diving in. There are two engines, front- or all-wheel drive, six- and seven-seater options and 32 versions to choose from. And starting at ₹27.99 lakh, it’s also priced to make rivals nervous.The Sorento is the biggest SUV in its class, yet it doesn’t feel that way from the outside. The vertically stacked headlights and neat, sharp detailing give it a crisp, expensive look, the kind German brands have long used to signal quality. A gently sloping roofline softens its bulk, so it seems more like a large, upmarket crossover than a traffic bully in the Fortuner mould. If you want a car that intimidates, look elsewhere. If you want one that will still look smart in five years, this is it. Step inside, and the Sorento really shines. Almost everything you touch is soft and well-finished, and the buttons click with a reassuring precision usually reserved for pricier cars. The touchscreen is refreshingly easy to use, with no hunting through menus to find what you need.The equipment list is long: Twin 12.3-inch screens, a head-up display, a 12-speaker Bose sound system, a panoramic sunroof, ventilated front seats, 10 airbags, a 360-degree camera and dashcams front and rear. There’s even an AI voice assistant.The best seats are in the middle row. In the six-seat version, these are plush, ventilated captain’s chairs with generous legroom and a lovely, airy view out. The third row is easy to reach but best left to children. Those low seats will leave adult knees pointing skywards. With all seats up, boot space is tight. Fold the last row, though, and it swallows plenty. The Sorento engine suits two very different buyers. The petrol hybrid is the city specialist. It glides through stop-go traffic and is officially rated at 19.6kpl. On the highway, however, it gets noisy and starts to feel stretched. The diesel is the long-distance champion. It pulls strongly, cruises effortlessly at highway speeds and is perfectly happy in town too. Its automatic gearbox is smooth. On long road trips, it may even be the more economical of the two.What surprised us most was the ride. The Sorento simply glides over broken roads. Around Udaipur we drove across badly damaged stretches without once needing to slow down. European rivals such as the Skoda Kodiaq and Volkswagen Tayron are sharper to drive. But Sorento buyers will care far more about comfort, and on that front Kia has nailed it. The lower and mid-range versions will put serious pressure on the Mahindra XUV 7XO, possibly luring some Toyota Innova Hycross buyers to the hybrid variant. Next to the Sorento, the Kodiaq and Tayron look overpriced and underequipped.There is one misstep. The top HTX version comes only with all-wheel drive, which pushes it to ₹37.49 to ₹40.19 lakh. That aside, the Sorento feels genuinely premium, close to luxury. It is loaded with features, rides beautifully and offers the right engine for every kind of driver. Kia has built another winner.From HT Brunch, October 24, 2026Follow us on www.instagram.com/htbrunch

title: Rude Food by Vir Sanghvi: Indian chefs are finally adding marrow to the menu | Hindustan Times
description: Chefs worldwide have been obsessed with cooking bone marrow. It’s now on Indian menus too. Have it spiced, in a crust, as a gravy, and soon on its own as well
content: Everything that happens in the world of food eventually gets to India. It may take a little time to reach us but sooner or later our chefs come to grips with it.Eight years ago, I wrote about bone marrow. We thought we knew about bone marrow, I wrote, but we were only used to goat marrow, a small quantity of which we were able to harvest from mutton bones. It was nice, but not really my thing. My fascination was with beef marrow, great big chunks of a delicate jelly-like substance with a light ethereal taste that did not have the offal-pungency of liver or other organ meats, none of which I eat. Marrow has been around forever, but it only became a staple of Western restaurant menus after the British chef Fergus Henderson popularised his version, in which he oven-roasted the marrow and served it with a little sea salt, sourdough toast and a parsley salad. Henderson’s version is still one of my favourite things to eat, though when I interviewed him about it in 2012, he was modest enough to give the credit to Rowley Leigh, another influential British chef whose ideas had influenced the dish.Anthony Bourdain fell in love with marrow, wanted it to be his last meal (which, sadly, it wasn’t) and championed Henderson’s style of cooking in the US. American chefs began doing even more interesting things with marrow, and at New York’s three-Michelin-starred Le Bernardin, Eric Ripert (who is, of course, French) paired it with sea urchin, a marriage made in heaven. The best bone marrow I had outside of the West was at 100 Mahaseth in Bangkok where the charcoal roasted version with perilla seeds became the signature dish of the chef Chalee Kader. I thought it would be hard for an Indian version to be as delicious until I had the marrow at London’s Hoppers. The Hoppers version is called Bone Marrow Varuval. South Indians can argue over whether it is actually a Varuval (I think not, but what do I know?) but Karan Gokani, the charismatic chef and food writer who runs Hoppers, has a very good recipe for it in his Hoppers: The Cookbook. Gokani calls it “the most popular curry at the restaurant. I reckon over the years we have had as many guests visit us for this dish as we have for our namesake hoppers”. All of this begged the obvious question: Why didn’t more restaurants make more marrow dishes in India?The answer was obvious if you thought about it. By the time marrow became a global craze, the anti-beef frenzy had started in India. You couldn’t do much with goat marrow (best for Nalli Nihari etc), which was too small. The real thing remained a problem.The first Indian chef I know who got around that problem was Hussain Shahzad at Mumbai’s O Pedro. This was long before Hussain became a superstar with Papa’s, and he was hardly ever written about in those days. Hussain had the bright idea of using buffalo marrow, which offended nobody’s religious sensibilities. And O Pedro, which was already my favourite restaurant in Mumbai, became my regular marrow haunt. In January 2019, I took Gaggan Anand and his kitchen team to O Pedro for dinner, and they were hugely impressed by the chef, loved his take on marrow and invited him to Bangkok to cook with them.Sadly, the pandemic intervened (as did Gaggan’s decision to open a new Gaggan). But by the time we emerged from Covid, Indian chefs were all in love with buffalo marrow.Now it’s not difficult to find great marrow dishes. At Restaurant Chef Pillai in Cochin a Malayali spiced-marrow dish is the star of the menu. It would be tempting to wonder if the eponymous chef-owner stole the idea from Hoppers, but the truth is that Suresh Pillai was the original head chef of the Marylebone branch of Hoppers. He left London (where he had also worked with the Panjabi sisters for years) to come back to Kerala. He soon became the best-known chef in Kerala and created a vast foodie empire. I asked Suresh whether his marrow dish has any origins in traditional Kerala cuisine. He was honest enough to say that it was a modern innovation. They do use marrow in cooking in Kerala but they use it in gravies and curries, not on its own. The exception, Pillai thinks, is a Muslim community near Wayanad, which uses marrow from large bovine bones. But that, he said, is not where his own dish comes from.Western-style marrow dishes now appear on lots of menus, even if most chefs who cook Indian food are less willing to be as adventurous as Suresh and Hussain. Will Aghajanian does two completely different marrow dishes at his two Mumbai restaurants: The Table and Kasper’s. Both are extremely popular. In Delhi, Jamsheed Bhote and Hanisha Singh have long experimented with bone marrow at Plats, the wonderful neighbourhood restaurant they run. Their bone marrow main course is outstanding. I asked Jamsheed when he put marrow on the menu. “The bone marrow has been on the menu for the past 6 months,” he responded. “We have used bone marrow in a crust over the tenderloin steak since the beginning of the restaurant seven years ago. We toyed with the idea of serving the marrow as a small plate for a bit and then finally put it on the menu six months back.”I suspect other chefs are also trying to work out how to put bone marrow on their menus. Indian chefs are good with goat marrow as an ingredient. At Nisaba, Manish Mehrotra transforms his raan with a bone marrow gravy. And at Raga, Rydo Anton makes the world’s least oily Nalli Nihari with marrow. But not many are ready to serve bovine marrow on its own. In Kochi, Suresh Pillai first freezes the marrow and then oven roasts it for ten minutes, which is similar to Fergus Henderson’s technique. He has thought about cooking the marrow gently in a warm tandoor but still has to figure out how to ensure that it doesn’t melt.I am sure he will work out the technique. Now that Indian chefs have come to grips with an ingredient it won’t be long before they master its complexity.From HT Brunch, October 24, 2026Follow us on www.instagram.com/htbrunch

title: Spectator by Seema Goswami: If you hate it, say it | Hindustan Times
description: Being polite isn’t always ideal. Sometimes, turning down an invite or a gift is the nicest thing you can do – for yourself
content: From the time we are children, one lesson is drilled into us by the adults around us: Be polite. Be polite no matter how irritated you are. Be polite no matter what the provocation. Be polite even if the other person is not. Be polite because good manners cost nothing. I could go on, but you get the general drift.It’s only when you grow up and become an adult in your own right, that you realise politeness is not always the answer no matter what the question. On the contrary, life throws up many occasions on which it does not pay to be polite at all – in fact, it has the opposite effect. Don’t believe me? Well, allow me to count the ways: · How do you react when you get a present you absolutely loathe? Well, if you are anything like me, you immediately go into ‘be polite’ mode. And that means responding with enthusiastic thanks and acting as if you love, love, love the gift. I even go to the extent of wearing the present or displaying it prominently in the presence of the person who gave it. You know what happens next, right? I get the same sort of thing year after year because the person in question now believes that he/she has cracked my taste. And I have nobody to blame for this sad state of affairs except myself.· We all get our share of invitations that strike terror in our hearts. My nightmare scenarios include Holi parties, Diwali milans, musical soirees where the hosts insist on performing, art exhibitions that are vanity projects for people with more money than talent, and so on. The default position when presented with these invitations is to ‘be polite’ and turn up for a short while to mark your attendance before making your escape. Well, I’m done wasting the time I have left on this planet on these tedious get-togethers. From now on, I am going to make my excuses and stay right at home. · When I visit people’s homes, I have absolutely no problem lying about the food the hostess has served up. Even if I absolutely hate it, I paste a smile on my face and pretend to love it. Hell, I even go back for seconds. But when it comes to restaurants, there is no point in doing the whole ‘be polite’ thing. Now, I don’t go out of my way to diss the chef if he is serving up slop, but if I am asked by the wait staff or the kitchen how I like the food, I am going to be honest. So, don’t ask the question if you don’t want the truth – polite or otherwise.From HT Brunch, October 24, 2026Follow us on www.instagram.com/htbrunch

title: Cell division: How to really pull the plug on your screen addiction | Hindustan Times
description: Everyone loves the idea of unplugging. No one really does it. Here’s what happened when four phone-obsessed people gave up screen time for real
content: Boomers call it a digital detox. Gen Z calls it analogue living. It’s the same old desire to unplug from tech and live outside the screen. “But we’re too anxiously attached to our devices,” says Mumbai businessman Siddharth Bhimani, 38. “It’s also impossible to completely disconnect because of all the things we need our phones for.” Turns out, there are reasonable boundaries that actually work. Here are some.Scroll to a haltThree years ago, Bhimani was looking to ways to switch off after his daughter — then five years old — complained that he was always on his phone. So, he got a Nokia flip phone to use on the weekends. He’d switch off his iPhone and only pick up emergency calls on that second number. It was instant “mental decluttering” over those two days, he says. “There’s something calming about knowing no one can contact you.” It also changed how he interacted with people. Bhimani learnt to cook new recipes from scratch with his daughter. When out with friends, he’d suggest playing games rather than having everyone be on their phones. He slowly stopped missing the dopamine rush of checking Instagram or Facebook even on his iPhone.For freelance music writer Harita Odedara, 23, the trigger for going analogue was the student protests in July. She lives in Himachal Pradesh and was on her phone for 12 hours a day, liking and sharing Reels in solidarity. The day she and her partner booked bus tickets to attend the protests, education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. “All of a sudden, I felt so empty.”Odedara downloaded an app that turned her phone black-and-white, so she would be dissuaded from looking at it. She restricted short-form video content and set “social media hours” during 6pm to 8pm. It freed up her hours dramatically, giving her time to sketch, read and connect with artists.Then, a challenge she still hasn’t accounted for: All the “uncomfortable emotions and feelings that come up when you aren’t looking at a screen,” she says. “We don’t talk enough about this side of digital detoxing — learning what to do with yourself when you’re not doomscrolling.” Pull the plugSome self-confessed phone addicts (aren’t we all?) have resorted to extreme measures. Business manager Ayan Modi, 26, was on a solo trip in Europe in 2023 when he realised that he was more focused on uploading photos and Reels than enjoying his grand adventure. Back in Mumbai, he experimented with going off his smartphone completely for seven days “just to see what happened”.He got a dumbphone, a Karbonn K140 Pop, began using cash for payments, and went MIA online. That one week turned to two, then a month. And before Modi knew it, he’d spent five months without a smartphone. He requested his boss to call him if a task was urgent. Because his job at the time involved tracking sales data and crunching numbers, all he needed was his work laptop to stay updated on developments in his field. “I felt more focused at work because my phone was not around to distract me.” Even after he returned to using his smartphone, the benefits carry over. He’d rather play music on a record player or the radio than pick up the phone. He’s more conscious about his spending and instead of idly scrolling, he tries to “actively consume only long-form content, such as 25-minute YouTube content or podcasts”.The clean break isn’t for everyone. Malvika Fulwani, a 34-year-old clinical dietician, averages 15 hours of screen time a day. Even after keeping her phone far away (or another floor of her house while she worked) the FOMO was real. “I had to get out of the spiral.” Her way out was 10-day Vipassana retreat in Nashik. No devices, no talking, no books, music, games, nothing. Just meditation.“When I came back, I realised I could leave my phone unattended for an hour or more. I now put it in DND mode from 10.30pm to 6am,” Fulwani says. “I still have to be on social media for work. But at least I’m no longer so attached to it.” Cut the cordBhimani, when he uses his Nokia, relies on his wife’s phone to make online payments or to use GPS or book tickets for events. He’s missed client calls and delivery OTPs. “Get a dumbphone only if you’re okay putting up with these inconveniences.” Missing work updates hurts less when you run your own business and aren’t reporting to a higher-up. It’s harder if your job requires you to be present online. It might be hardest for women who rely on online trackers to let loved ones know they are safe.Modi says he is no longer locked in on the latest memes or hip cafés. But going smartphone-free takes a village. When his friends were meeting, they’d call and let him know. His colleagues would book Ubers for him after post-work drinks. Work communication happened on Slack, not WhatsApp, so not having a smartphone didn’t matter.For those considering cutting down screen time, Bhimani advises starting small: Perhaps two hours after work, or just on Sundays. Get comfortable with leaving the phone at home for short outings. Or get a phone dock and hang it up on the wall like a landline. “The world isn’t going to end if you don’t check your notifications all the time,” he says.From HT Brunch, October 24, 2026Follow us on www.instagram.com/htbrunch

title: The Brunch round-up for October 24: The week and how it made us feel | Hindustan Times
description: This week, we’re hoping Virat Kohli gets hired, wondering what the Girls sequel will be like, getting locked up in Arkham and drooling over Emilio Sakraya
content: Thrilled to announce… that Virat Kohli is on LinkedIn. He signed up last week, headlined himself as Professional Athlete at Indian Cricket Team, and casually dropped a long note about his achievements. It’s viral ad campaign vibes, TBH. Because, honestly, is the job market so bad that star cricketers are Open To Work? Feeling sunburned. We were so excited about Taika Waititi’s film adap of Kazuo Ishiguro’s sci-fi novel, Klara and the Sun. Then, the peppy, colourful trailer dropped, and we deflated a little. But no one expected it to be as bad as it seems to be. The unsettling tale about humanoids and companionship has been reduced to a comedy. One-star reviews all around. Ugh. Just unplug. Completing the set. Remember when the US boyband Boy Throb was trying desperately to get Indian singer Darshan Magdum to join them abroad as their fourth member? It’s happened! Magdum got a visa this week after a year of trying, and got a Darshan Day welcome at a New Jersey mall. On their first performance as quartet, a fan commented, “Is this what the moon landing felt like?” It probably did. Cashing in. Look who’s swimming among the millionaires on Shark Tank: Mindy Kaling. Kelly Kapoor is in her investor phase. She’s supported a probiotic soda brand, a skincare brand and a clinic in the past. But please, let her not be the Shark who only supports women-centric businesses. That performative girlboss era is over. Girls’ girls. A Girls sequel is coming. We suspect the actors sprung for the show because they peaked with the HBO series. The world is in a worse mess than when Girls aired. Millennials are struggling, but in different ways. Greta Lee, then an extra, is now our queen. Where will the show go? Is Hannah a suburban mom blogger? Marnie, a failed wellness influencer? Jessa, an ironic tradwife? We’re staying tuned. Getting cheep thrills. We love a pointless hyperfixation. The internet gave us one via Kelly Clarkson’s feud with Brooklyn boutique Art of Play. Clarkson claims employees gave her the Pretty Woman treatment, refusing to sell her a $15,000 mechanical bird because they thought she was poor. The store says Molly was never for sale and that Clarkson’s claims “have put them in danger”. TL;DR: Molly is totally worth the drama. Hot and bothered. The screen adaptation of Rebecca Yarros’s Fourth Wing is on the way, with Emilio Sakraya playing Xaden, and Esther McGregor as Violet in the Prime Video series. Romantasy fans are already swooning over Sakraya’s biceps, abs and Instagram thirst traps. We’ve never seen the internet so unanimously approve of a casting choice. Suiting up. The Arkham Asylum graphic novel was creepy, chaotic, Lynchian and loaded with allegory. Batman, trapped in the Gotham madhouse, had to confront his demons while facing off against the Joker, Two-Face, Mad Hatter and Killer Croc. The landmark comic is getting a sequel set 1,000 years in the future. We have questions. We have chills.From HT Brunch, October 24, 2026Follow us on www.instagram.com/htbrunch

title: What we know about Todd Benzinger's family and children as 1990 World Series winner dies at 63 | Hindustan Times
description: Former MLB star Todd Benzinger, 63, has died. The 1990 World Series champion is survived by children, including basketball player Grant Benzinger.
content: Todd Benzinger, the former Cincinnati Reds and San Francisco Giants star, has passed away at the age of 63. The Reds announced his death in a statement on Thursday. A cause of death of the 1990 MLB World Series winner was not given."Todd will forever be remembered by Reds fans for catching the final out of the 1990 World Series, but those of us who had the privilege of knowing him will remember so much more," Rick Walls, the executive director of the Reds Hall of Fame Museum, said.The death of the former MLB World Series winner has revealed that there is very little documented detail on his family, especially his marriages and children. In this article, we will take a look at what is publicly documented over the years about the family of the late Todd Benzinger.What We Know About Todd Bezinger's FamilyAccording to the Society for American Baseball Research, Todd Benzinger was married to Kristi Wagers. While the SABR article only documents the name Kristi, a media guide of Wright State University basketball team's from 2014-15 documents their son, Grant Benzinger, as the "son of Todd Benzinger and Kristi Wagers."Grant Benzinger was a star guard for Wright State University and pursued a professional basketball career in Europe after college. Records show that Grant Benzinger stopped playing basketball professionally in 2021.Also read: Jamal Wallace suspended indefinitely by Utah amid rape and intimate video sharing allegationsThe Wright State University media guide documents that Grant Benzinger was born on March 1, 1996, and notes that he has "three sisters."Furthermore, a San Francisco Giants media guide from 1993 carrying a profile of Todd Benzinger states that at the time, Todd and Kristi has a daughter named Justine.The identities of Todd Benzinger's other children are not publicly documented.Texas Home Movie, an event videography studio, documents in a Facebook post from May 10, 2015, the marriage of Todd Benzinger to Nicole. However, there are no confirmed news reports documenting a second marriage for Todd Benzinger.Also read: Virginia's Sen. Louise Lucas indicted on drug and money laundering charges as FBI probe ‘marijuana enterprise’Grant Benzinger Was A College Basketball StarGrant Benzinger was a star at Wright State basketball, finishing with 1,451 points in 132 games across four seasons (2014 to 2018). An MLB.com news article from 2018 documents that Grant Benzinger was voted the MVP of the Horizon League Tournament that year.After college, Grant Benzinger moved to Germany, playing for the Uni Baskets Paderborn in the country's second-tier ProA League. He suffered an ACL tear in 2019 but stayed with the club till the 2020-21 season.

title: Trump calls LeBron James a ‘TOTAL DISGRACE’ accusing 76ers star of disrespecting US national anthem | Hindustan Times
description: Donald Trump’s remarks followed criticism from JD Vance a day earlier, when he called out WNBA players for leaving the court during the national anthem.
content: President Donald Trump had already made his stance toward LeBron James apparent in July, when he weighed in on the NBA’s GOAT debate and chose Michael Jordan over the 76ers star while calling the latter a “racist."Trump reignited his criticism of James on Thursday, accusing the NBA star of showing disrespect toward the US national anthem and branding him a “TOTAL DISGRACE.”Trump finds Lebron James’ behavior disrespectful“While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post alongside a video that showed James moving his body during the anthem.The clip showed James standing alongside his Philadelphia 76ers teammates, swinging his arms in a warm-up stretch and mimicking basketball shooting motions. “I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for! President DONALD J. TRUMP,” Trump’s post further read.Trump’s criticism follows JD Vance condemning WNBA playersTrump’s remarks followed criticism from Vice President JD Vance a day earlier, when he called out players from the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries for leaving the court during the national anthem ahead of WNBA Finals games.Also read | Enes Kanter Freedom sends message to Angel Reese while confirming WNBA Finals Game 3 attendanceVance condemned the move as “disgraceful,” arguing that athletes should not express opposition to a politician by “disrespecting the country writ large.”Trump and James’ long-running feudDonald Trump had previously taken aim at James in July while discussing his choice for basketball’s greatest player, naming Hall of Famer Michael Jordan over the Philadelphia 76ers star.During the remarks, Trump also suggested that James might be racist and speculated that the NBA star disliked him.“And I think LeBron is maybe he’s a racist, but maybe he doesn’t like Trump. I only like people who like me. So I would say Michael Jordan all the way,” the US president said.Also read | LeBron James’ courtside exchange with fan draws attention during 76ers vs Knicks clash: 'He’s been so irritated'Meanwhile, James is in his record 24th NBA season and has frequently criticized Trump while speaking out on issues such as racial justice, voting rights and education. title: Actor Tom Skerritt, star of 'Alien' and 'Top Gun,' dies at 93 | Hollywood
description: PEOPLE-TOM SKERRITT/ (PIX):Actor Tom Skerritt, star of 'Alien' and 'Top Gun,' dies at 93  | Hollywood
content: By Will DunhamOct 22 - Versatile actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in Hollywood megahits including the sci-fi classic "Alien," the war comedy "M*A*S*H," and the action drama "Top Gun," has died at the age of 93, his manager confirmed.Skerritt, a Detroit native whose Hollywood career spanned from the 1960s to the 2020s, died on Wednesday of natural causes, said ABC7, citing a statement from his family.Known for his rugged good looks and ability to shine in a variety of genres, Skerritt delivered memorable performances in leading and supporting roles in film and television.Skerritt's breakthrough role was a roguish US Army surgeon in director Robert Altman's 1970 Korean War black comedy "M*A*S*H," a film whose ensemble cast also included Donald Sutherland, Elliott Gould and Sally Kellerman. Skerritt played Southerner Duke Forrest as the doctors at the Mobile Army Surgical Hospital stitched up wounded troops.The film, whose popularity coincided with American unease over the Vietnam War, was nominated for five Academy Awards.In director Ridley Scott's claustrophobic 1979 sci-fi horror "Alien", Skerritt played Dallas, the captain of an ill-fated spacecraft whose crew encounters a deadly parasitic extraterrestrial creature with a surrealist look and a bad attitude. In the film's famous and bloody "chestburster" scene, Skerritt's character is seated next to cast mate John Hurt when a baby alien violently exits the torso of Hurt's character."Alien," an influential masterpiece whose ensemble cast also included Sigourney Weaver and Ian Holm, earned two Oscar nominations."It is spontaneity and impulse that make the difference, and that is what I felt we had with 'Alien.' Every one of us had that immediate rapport with each other - the respect that I had for the other actors and the respect that they had for me," Skerritt told interviewer Peter Sobczynski in 2019, while also lauding Scott's directorial brilliance."Alien" was one of several films in which Skerritt appeared that featured strong female characters, in this case Weaver's courageous character Ripley. That was considered pioneering at the time."When I read the script, one of the things that I liked most about it was that the woman becomes the hero. I loved that," Skerritt said."The sight of women being in positions of strength and fortitude to make the right connections and decisions was what appealed to me. I experienced that as well in 'Steel Magnolias,' with the women in that. I liked the idea of women being tough and strong and influential."In "Steel Magnolias" , Skerritt played Drum Eatenton, husband of Sally Field's M'Lynn Eatenton.Tony Scott, the brother of the "Alien" director, cast Skerritt in the key supporting role of naval aviation instructor Viper Metcalf in the 1986 blockbuster "Top Gun" that helped star Tom Cruise soar into Hollywood's stratosphere.Skerritt also played Shirley MacLaine's husband in director Herbert Ross's 1977 ballet drama "The Turning Point," and starred alongside another emerging star in Brad Pitt in Robert Redford's beautifully shot 1992 period drama "A River Runs Through It."Among other films in which he appeared were: "Harold and Maude" , "Ice Castles" , "The Dead Zone" , "Poltergeist III" , "Contact" , "Tears of the Sun" and "Ted" .On the small screen, Skerritt starred in the offbeat CBS series "Picket Fences" from 1992 to 1996, playing a Wisconsin town sheriff and claiming an Emmy as outstanding lead actor in a drama series in 1993.Born on August 25, 1933, in Detroit, Skerritt served in the US Air Force before becoming an actor, making his film debut in 1962 alongside a young Redford in "War Hunt." He was a father of five children and was married three times.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Red Bull advisor Marko slams Horner memoir as 'collection of untruths' | Hindustan Times
description: Red Bull advisor Marko slams Horner memoir as 'collection of untruths'
content: Former Red Bull advisor Helmut Marko launched a scathing attack on ex-team principal Christian Horner on Thursday, describing his newly-released memoir as a "collection of untruths".The 83-year-old Austrian, who was a senior figure in the racing team, said it was "an embarrassment" that the book was being published on October 22, the day of Red Bull founder Dieter Mateschitz's death in 2022.Horner, who led Red Bull to eight drivers' titles and six constructors' crowns, was sacked as team principal in July 2025, 17 months after he was accused by a woman colleague of "inappropriate behaviour".The Englishman was twice cleared over the claims by the Formula One team's parent company, Red Bull GmbH, and his wife, former Spice Girl Geri Halliwell, stood by him.But there were rumblings of discontent within the team, with several high-profile departures, while form on the track dipped. Horner was formally dismissed in September 2025 with a huge payoff estimated to be as much as £100 million.Marko said that Horner should have shown more loyalty."That's a collection of untruths," he told Sky Sports Germany."I don't even want to get into the level of discourse. Especially after the huge settlement he received, one would have expected some loyalty."I don't think he's even aware that his book is being published on the exact day Dietrich Mateschitz died."Marko had previously said that many of Horner's claims made in the book were not true.- 'Brutal' -Horner, meanwhile, has accused Marko of playing a role in his dismissal soon after his former partner, the mother of his daughter, had died of cancer.He also claims that Marko did not offer his condolences, a claim refuted strongly by the Austrian."The only thing I want to clarify is that I even sent him my condolences in writing, for his ex-partner, who died of cancer," said Marko, in a further interview with Austrian newspaper Kronen Zeitung. "That's all that matters to me."The pair worked together at Red Bull for more than 20 years.Horner, 52, told the Autosport Business Exchange conference in New York on Thursday that his departure from Red Bull was "pretty abrupt and quite brutal".He said he now reflected with pride on his achievements."I'm very proud of what we all did there and I feel privileged to have worked with some amazing drivers," he said.He also revealed that Red Bull shareholders had recently called him to show their appreciation of his part in the creation of Red Bull's own power unit, and its maiden victory with Max Verstappen at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia."It was an appreciated gesture," he said."For all the men and women involved, it was an incredible achievement at their 16th attempt to win a Grand Prix, which is very hard at the best of times."I was grateful to the shareholders who reached out and to Oliver Mintzlaff who thanked me as well. It was quite a different call than I had 15 months earlier."str/bsp/dmcThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Jamal Wallace suspended indefinitely by Utah amid rape and intimate video sharing allegations | Hindustan Times

content: Utah has indefinitely suspended senior defensive tackle Jamal Wallace following his arrest on a Class A misdemeanor charge related to the alleged “distribution of an intimate image”.Wallace is also the subject of a rape investigation, with allegations that videos connected to the incident were circulated on social media, ESPN reported.Utah suspends Jamal Wallace indefinitelyThe university addressed the matter in an official statement which read, "We were made aware of the situation with Jamal Wallace on Oct. 11 and he was immediately placed on an indefinite suspension from the program," the university said."We take these matters seriously. title: Wayne Rooney labels Manchester United players “selfish” after Bruno Fernandes criticism | Football News

title: Assembly pays tributres to Jhota; adjourns in 9 minutes | Hindustan Times
description: Following obituary references, the first day of the six-day session concluded in nine minutes and six seconds before Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan adjourned the House till Friday
content: The Punjab assembly on Thursday paid tributes to anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was killed last week by a medical store owner in Mansa, with the Speaker describing him as a “buland awaz” (strong voice) against those peddling poison in the form of drugs.The opening day of the assembly session began with the House paying tributes to prominent personalities who passed away since its previous sitting in August.Following obituary references, the first day of the six-day session concluded in nine minutes and six seconds before Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan adjourned the House till Friday.Those included in the obituary list were former deputy speaker and cabinet minister Chunni Lal Bhagat, former Rajya Sabha member Varinder Bajwa, former MLA Ranjeet Singh, noted orthopaedic surgeon Dr Rattan Lal Mittal, and Vidya Kaur, mother of AAP MLA Manjit Singh Bilaspur.The House also paid tribute to the eight VB-G RAM G workers who died in a road accident in Sangrur last week.Congress MLA Sukhwinder Singh Kotli also demanded that the name of the Sangrur man, who allegedly died by suicide last month, also be included in the obituary list.The House observed a two-minute silence in memory of the deceased after which the Speaker adjourned the sitting.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann, a number of cabinet ministers and MLAs stayed away from the session.Congress burns AAP govt’s effigy Before entering the assembly, Congress legislators burnt an effigy of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government, accusing it of failing to fulfil the aspirations of Punjab’s people.Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa, who led the party legislators, said the state government had failed on all fronts even as its five-year term was nearing its end. Congress legislators also raised anti-government slogans in the Vidhan Sabha gallery.Later, Punjab Pradesh Congress committee president and Jalandhar Cantt MLA Pargat Singh criticised the government for adjourning the session after nine minutes even as day-long official business, including question hour, calling attention motion and resolutions were listed to be taken up during the day’s proceedings.Instead of replying to questions on crucial issues, including the murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, the government chose to evade accountability and “run away” from the assembly, alleged Singh. “We wanted a debate on the law and order, farming and other issues in the House,” he said.Bajwa said the Speaker did not conduct the non-official business and claimed that the Opposition parties were not taken into confidence in this regard.Punjab Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Kewal Singh Dhillon also flayed the AAP government over the short session. “The session ended without discussing issues facing the state. This has resulted in a waste of public money worth crores,” said Dhillon here.

title: Min wages increased for workers in Noida, Greater Noida from Oct 1 | Hindustan Times
description: UP sets Gautam Budh Nagar minimum monthly wages at  ₹13,883 for unskilled and  ₹17,106 for skilled workers from October 2026 to March 2027.
content: NOIDA: Unskilled workers in Gautam Budh Nagar will get a minimum monthly wage of ₹13,883 while skilled workers will be entitled to ₹17,106 under the revised variable dearness allowance (VDA) rates, according to the UP labour department.The revision, applicable from October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027, comes months after widespread worker protests in Noida’s industrial areas in April for higher wages, better overtime payments and improved working conditions.Following the protests, unskilled workers’ wages were raised from ₹11,313 to ₹13,690, and skilled from ₹13,940 to ₹16,868.The protests followed Haryana’s announcement of a minimum-wage increase. Workers, including those employed in factories in Noida’s Phase 2 industrial area, raised concerns over wages and sought improvements in benefits, including weekly offs and bonuses. Following protests, the UP government announced an interim raise in minimum wages.The latest October adjustment reflects the VDA mechanism rather than a fresh, across-the-board wage settlement, said officials. The revised rates that cover unskilled, semi-skilled and skilled workers, are based on the average All India Consumer Price Index for January to June 2026, which stood at 431 points, officials said. In a statement on Thursday, additional labour commissioner Rakesh Dwivedi said the rates had been calculated using prescribed consumer price index.“The variable dearness allowance rates for the period from October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027, have been calculated on the basis of the average All India Consumer Price Index for January to June 2026, which stood at 431 points,” he said.The monthly wage for unskilled workers comprises a basic wage of ₹12,885 and VDA of ₹998.59, while semi-skilled workers will receive ₹15,271.41, including a basic wage of ₹14,173 and VDA of ₹1,098.41.For skilled workers, the revised monthly wage comprises a basic wage of ₹15,876 and VDA of ₹1,230.39.The corresponding daily wages have been fixed at ₹533.98 for unskilled workers, ₹587.36 for semi-skilled workers and ₹657.94 for skilled workers.The daily wage is calculated by dividing monthly wage by 26, with the calculation accounting for weekly rest days treated as paid holidays, said assistant labour commissioner Suyash Pandey.

title: Chiefs place left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve with a bulging disk in his lower back | Hindustan Times
description: Chiefs place left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve with a bulging disk in his lower back
content: KANSAS CITY, Mo. — The Kansas City Chiefs placed Josh Simmons on injured reserve because of a bulging disk in his lower back Thursday, guaranteeing their starting left tackle will be out at least four more weeks after having already missed the first five games of the season.Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will continue to protect the blind side of Patrick Mahomes. On the right side, Jaylon Moore remains in the concussion protocol, which means Joshua Ezeudu is expected to start at that tackle position on Sunday night in Seattle.The Chiefs chose Simmons in the first round of the 2025 draft in the hopes that he could be their franchise left tackle. He was coming off a serious knee injury at Ohio State, but the Chiefs believed he would be able to make a full recovery in time to play as a rookie.His knee has never been a problem. But other factors have kept him off the field.Simmons started the first five games last season before missing time to deal with personal matters. He returned to start in three more games before a fractured and dislocated hand landed him on IR for the remainder of the season.He showed up to training camp in late July feeling good, though, and Simmons hoped his injury issues were behind him. But on Aug. 17, he reported feeling some discomfort in his calf, and the Chiefs' training staff determined it was stemming from his back.Chiefs trainer Rick Burkholder obtained an MRI exam that confirmed the herniated and bulging disk, which was “higher up than we normally see in our offensive linemen, which complicated the case.”The Chiefs recommended a second opinion, and a back specialist in California believed that Simmons would be able to overcome the injury with rehabilitation rather than surgery.That is why the Chiefs had not put Simmons on injured reserve until Thursday.“Josh worked his tail off. He worked diligently with my staff every day, and he improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week,” Burkholder said. “However we feel he plateaued in the recovery process. ... He's just not there yet.”After discussing the situation with Simmons, his family and representatives, the decision was made to place him on IR.“It was decided and agreed upon by everybody,” Burkholder said, adding that surgery still is not in the forecast.Benson has surpassed all expectations at left tackle after the former Indiana offensive lineman stepped into role. And when pressed into duty against the Chargers last Sunday, Ezeudu faired well in Moore's place on the right side the rest of the way.Ezeudu was a third-round pick of the Giants in the 2022 draft. The Chiefs acquired him for a seventh-round pick in August.“He's played before,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said, “and when we brought him in, we knew that, and we knew he was a good player. So now, potentially, there's an opportunity to be in there and play, and I thought he did a nice job when he was in there this past weekend. So yeah, I think everybody around him has got confidence in him, too.”See ’s full NFL coverage hereThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Seahawks activate RB Zach Charbonnet from PUP list | Hindustan Times
description: FOOTBALL-NFL-SEA-CHARBONNET/
content: The Seattle Seahawks activated running back Zach Charbonnet from the physically unable to perform list on Thursday.To make room on the active roster, the team placed tight end Elijah Arroyo on injured reserve with a shoulder injury.Head coach Mike Macdonald said earlier this week that Charbonnet is not guaranteed to play Sunday night when the Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs ."Zach is going to have a full week's worth of reps, so that's exciting, and there's a possibility that you could see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that's exciting," Macdonald said on Monday.Charbonnet, 25, is nine months removed from tearing his ACL in the NFC divisional round win against San Francisco on Jan. 17. "I know he's had a certain date in mind, which is a really ambitious date. Those who have tried to come back from a significant knee surgery understand the undertaking that it takes. Zach's a beast. He looks great. It's not easy to say, 'All right, let's go.' So for him to have that courage to say that and work through the things he's worked through, you can't do anything but tip your cap to him."Charbonnet led the Seahawks in rushing touchdowns and was second in rushing yards last season. title: Exclusive| Bill Hader: Obsession director Curry Barker told me he watched me perform when he was a kid | Hindustan Times
description: Bill Hader says voice acting can be exhausting, but seeing children enjoy The Cat in the Hat makes it worthwhile
content: American actor, director, writer and comedian Bill Hader known for Saturday Night Live, his Emmy winning series Barry and many more projects talks to HTCity about lending his voice to Warner Bros animated film, The Cat in the Hat. The actor says most people don't realise "how exhausting" a job doing voice-overs really is but at the same time it's well worth it because the kids love it.Being a father yourself, how excited are your kids for the movie?I took my youngest daughter and her friends for an advance screening and they love it. They were laughing and even ended up crying at the end, they were so moved by it, so reaction is great.Was voice-overs for animation movies always part of the plan?I never planned on being in The Cat in the Hat. You just get a call or an email and I say, "That would be amazing." That's how it happened. I would certainly love to do more of this work.While we have seen you do the fun stuff on Saturday Night Live and in animation movies, on the other hand there's the award winning Barry where you played a hit man and also served in multiple roles including writer and director. How does one switch between extremes?I'm not somebody who has a specific process. I know actors like Robert De Niro really work hard on their craft; for me it's more intuitive. I really rely on my director to say- go this way or that, we discuss it and collaborate. Growing up, being an actor was something I never thought about, it was more about being a filmmaker. Being an actor opened doors so I could go on to direct Barry. I just feel very lucky about how things worked out.What SNL characters do people still talk to you about the most?There are so many! The Californians is one because I live in Los Angeles, people definitely remember the Californians. Stefon Meyers is another one people still enjoy. It comes and wades. It's interesting that people who are doing stuff now, grew up watching those characters. I met Obsession director Curry Barker at dinner and he told me "I watched you, as a kid" They were just little kids back then (laughs) that generation is now making great stuff. I was lucky I came up at a time where I had people like John Mulaney writing for me, who is now a great comedian himself. You've also spoken about real and relatable issues like anxiety.Once every month or two someone comes up to me and says “Thank you for speaking about anxiety; it helped me or helped my kid.” That's very meaningful.Any plans to visit India?I'd love to come to India, and I love films from India. I would absolutely come at some point. My friends who've been to the country love it and I want to experience it myself.

title: Rangers legend Ron Duguay dies at 69 after cancer battle as girlfriend shares heartfelt tribute | Hindustan Times
description: “It’s with a shattered heart, but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now. He fought so hard. Love never ends,” Sarah Palin, Duguay's girlfriend, tweeted.
content: Ron Duguay, the former NHL player and New York Rangers legend, has died at 69 following a battle with colon cancer. His girlfriend, Sarah Palin, announced his passing on social media Thursday.Duguay's girlfriend shares heartfelt tribute“It’s with a shattered heart, but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now. He fought so hard. Love never ends,” Palin wrote on X. Her post featured a smiling photograph of Duguay on the ice and confirmed that he “passed away peacefully on October 22, 2026 after a hard fought battle with cancer.”It also noted that details of “a celebration of life” would be shared at a later date.Rangers mourn loss of franchise iconDuguay spent eight seasons with the New York Rangers across two separate stints. His first run with the franchise lasted from 1977 to 1983 and included a trip to the 1979 Stanley Cup Final, where the Rangers fell to the Montreal Canadiens in five games. He returned for another two-season spell from 1986 to 1988.Across 499 games with New York, Duguay recorded 164 goals and 176 assists, totaling 340 points. The Rangers also issued a statement mourning the loss of the franchise icon and paying tribute to his legacy.“The New York Rangers organization mourns the loss of Ron Duguay, one of the most popular players in franchise history. Ron’s signature skating style—with his hair flowing as he moved down the ice—captivated The Garden Faithful, and his skill, tenacity, and charisma earned him the admiration of all New Yorkers,” the team said.Also read | Penguins' Ben Kindel hospitalized after medical episode on flight, details on what happened unclearThe statement concluded by extending condolences to Duguay’s family and friends.Duguay’s legacy with the RangersDuguay continues to share the Rangers’ franchise record for the quickest goal from the opening faceoff, scoring just nine seconds into a game against the Philadelphia Flyers on April 6, 1980.He thrived at Madison Square Garden, where his on-ice performances and magnetic personality helped him become a fan favorite and a well-known figure across New York.Trade to Detroit sparked career revivalThe Canadian's first stint with the Rangers ended in 1983 when Detroit acquired him in a trade as he was going through a dip in form. He became part of the Red Wings’ resurgence in the early 1980s under then-general manager Jimmy Devellano.During the 1983-84 season, Duguay ranked fourth on Detroit with 33 goals and 47 assists, finishing third on the team with 80 points. He improved the following year, placing second among the Wings with 38 goals, 51 assists and 89 points. His assist and point totals marked career highs.The Red Wings also issued a statement honoring Duguay following his passing.Also read | PAC cause of death: What we know about AEW star Benjamin Satterley’s passing as tributes pour in for WWE's NevilleAt the 1986 trade deadline, Detroit traded Duguay to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for Doug Shedden. He also went on to play for the Penguins and the Los Angeles Kings.Across 864 regular-season games in his NHL career, Duguay recorded 620 points, including 274 goals and 346 assists. He added 53 points, with 31 goals and 22 assists, in 89 Stanley Cup Playoff appearances.

title: It's never too early for some Christmas cake mixing- Here's how you can join in the fun | Hindustan Times
description: Hotels in Mumbai and Pune are beginning Christmas celebrations with cake-mixing ceremonies, where guests combine dried fruits, nuts, spices and spirits
content: Christmas might be months away, but festive cheer has already hit Mumbai and Pune. Cake mixing ceremonies, where dried fruits, nuts, spices, and spirits are blended to prepare the cakes, are bringing people together.An early start to Festive cheerChef Mihir Kane, director of culinary at Fairmont Mumbai, calls cake-mixing ceremony a “celebration of culinary heritage, craftsmanship and togetherness that signals the beginning of the festive season.” Kane asserts that Christmas cake is all about depth of flavour, with time playing a key role. “Soaking dried fruits in advance allows them to absorb the flavours of the chosen liquid, while the spices and other ingredients develop greater complexity as they come together.” Fairmont’s cake mixing event will take place in early November.Contact: 8097555901An early start to Festive cheerChef Mihir Kane, director of culinary at Fairmont Mumbai, calls cake-mixing ceremony a “celebration of culinary heritage, craftsmanship and togetherness that signals the beginning of the festive season.” Kane asserts that Christmas cake is all about depth of flavour, with time playing a key role. “Soaking dried fruits in advance allows them to absorb the flavours of the chosen liquid, while the spices and other ingredients develop greater complexity as they come together.” Fairmont’s cake mixing event will take place in early November.Contact: 8097555901Kickstarting the season of Shared ExperiencesThe Orchid Hotel, Mumbai, kicked off Yuletide festivities with the customary cake mixing ceremony on Thursday. The tradition gets everyone together and contribute to the preparation, making it a collective celebration rather than just a culinary activity, says Gaurav Shiva, General Manager.He adds, “The ingredients themselves come together to create something richer as a whole. In many ways, this reflects the spirit of Christmas, which is about bringing people together, celebrating relationships and creating memories.” Cake mixing at home -Use dark rum, brandy or whisky to add warmth and depth to the fruit mixture. For a non-alcoholic version, grape juice, apple juice or orange juice can be used, along with citrus zest. Since fruit juices are more perishable than spirits, the soaking time and storage conditions should be adjusted accordingly.-The ratio depends on the style of cake being prepared. As a starting point, go for approximately 70-75% dried and candied fruits, 20-25% nuts and around 2-5% mixed spices. The spices should enhance the natural sweetness of the fruits rather than overpower them.-Cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves and ginger add warmth, while orange or lemon zest brings freshness. Brown sugar or dark sugars can contribute caramel-like notes, and nuts add texture.-Be mindful as overmixing the batter can affect the cake’s texture, while opening the oven too frequently may cause uneven baking. Another common oversight is not allowing the cake to cool completely before storing it.Inputs by chef Avinash Kumar, Novotel, Juhu Beach Mumbai

title: Sri Lanka survive late drama to script record ODI chase against England despite Brook’s double ton | Cricket
description: Recovering from 24/2, Sri Lanka survived a tense finish to pull off the second-highest run chase in ODI cricket  | Cricket
content: England captain Harry Brook lit up Rawalpindi on Thursday with the fastest double century in ODI history. His 202 off 116 balls powered England to 429/4, but that extraordinary effort was eclipsed by a remarkable chase from Sri Lanka. Recovering from 24/2, they survived a tense finish to pull off the second-highest successful run chase in ODI cricket.Avishka Fernando provided the impetus with 97 off 83 balls, sharing a 166-run stand for the third wicket with Pavan Rathnayake, who struck 130 off 106 deliveries. Dasun Shanaka then shifted the momentum with a blistering 97 off 50 balls before Janith Liyanage applied the finishing touch with an unbeaten 61 off 21 deliveries.Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis would have had second thoughts about bowling first after Brook dismantled his team's attack.The England skipper reached his double century in just 114 balls, breaking the record set by India's Shubman Gill last month.Sri Lanka's chase suffered an early setback when Mendis was run out by Gus Atkinson without facing a ball in the fifth over, leaving the side at 24/2. Fernando and the middle order rebuilt the innings, but England refused to give up.Josh Tongue kept the contest alive in the final over, dismissing Dunith Wellalage and Eshan Malinga off consecutive deliveries. Sri Lanka were reduced to eight wickets down, needing seven runs from the final three balls.No.10 Asitha Fernando denied Tongue a hat-trick and took a single to bring the well-set Liyanage back on strike. Liyanage responded emphatically, launching the next delivery over long-off for six to seal a stunning victory with one ball to spare.It was the second-highest successful chase in the format, behind South Africa's 438/9 against Australia in 2006. The win also marked Sri Lanka's highest successful run chase in ODI cricket, surpassing their previous best of 322 against India at The Oval in 2017. Sri Lanka also registered the highest successful chase against England in ODIs, surpassing Australia's 352-run pursuit at Lahore last year.The victory was Sri Lanka's first in the ODI tri-series, which also features Pakistan. They had lost their opening match to Pakistan at the same venue on October 18. Pakistan have won both their games so far and will face England in Lahore on Sunday before taking on Sri Lanka at the same venue on Tuesday.
