title: CJP news highlights: Delhi HC reserves verdict in Neha Bora's petition, order likely to be pronounced tomorrow | India News
description: CJP news highlights: The High Court on Thursday commenced hearing AISA president Neha Bora’s petition challenging a Delhi Police notice directing her to furnish a personal bond of  ₹10,000 along with one surety to “maintain peace during the period of inquiry”. | India News
content: CJP news highlights: The live updates to the blog are closed. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will not appear before the Delhi Police Crime Branch for questioning on Thursday, as they have sought more time, ANI reported, citing sources.Earlier, in the day, the Crime Branch had Das and Ranka, asking them to appear at its Rajouri Garden office at 12 pm on Thursday. The summons comes a day after the two leaders were released from Tihar Jail, where they had been held in connection with protests against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Neha Bora plea to be heard in Delhi HC todayThe Delhi High Court said it would pass an order on AISA president Neha Bora’s plea challenging the police notice directing her to furnish a peace bond on Friday at 6 pm.Bora, who has been at the forefront of protests against alleged irregularities in the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, has sought the quashing of the notice and directions to the police not to take any coercive action against her.Das, Ranka renew demand for Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation after releaseHours after walking out of Tihar Jail late on Wednesday, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared in a video holding the Indian flag and reiterated their demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, signalling that their release had not brought an end to the broader campaign against the voter-roll overhaul.The two were released after spending more than a week in custody, amid heightened restrictions on protests over the contentious revision of electoral rolls.Das and Ranka had been lodged in Tihar Jail for allegedly violating peace bonds and trespassing at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site that has recently been stripped of its designated status.A Special Executive Magistrate ordered their release after accepting sureties on their behalf. The two also undertook not to organise further demonstrations at the site.

title: Himachal IPS officer booked over police fund ‘bungling’ | Hindustan Times
description: FIR follows constable’s claim that  ₹1.87 lakh spent on official works when Sanjeev Gandhi was Shimla SP were not reimbursed; officer dubs allegations false
content: Deputy inspector general of police (DIG) Sanjeev Kumar Gandhi has been booked on charges of cheating, financial irregularities and misappropriation of government funds, following a complaint by a police constable who claimed that he was denied reimbursement of ₹1.87 lakh spent on official arrangements.The charges relate to a period when Gandhi, a 2012-batch IPS officer, was serving as superintendent of police, Shimla, from 2023 to February 7, 2026. He was promoted to DIG in January this year.Gandhi has termed the allegations false and said he would respond through legal means.According to the complaint and findings of a preliminary examination of financial records, a case was registered at Shimla Sadar police station on Thursday under Sections 316(5), 314, 318, 336 and 340 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The complainant, a constable posted at Kaithu police lines in Shimla, alleged that he had been assigned responsibilities for official work and arrangements during 2024 and 2025. He claimed that he was asked to make the necessary arrangements using his personal funds and was assured that the expenditure would subsequently be reimbursed.According to the complaint, the constable spent a total of ₹1.87 lakh on the arrangements and submitted the relevant bills to the office. The bills were reportedly examined and approved for payment. The constable alleged that on February 6, 2026, Gandhi, who was then serving as SP, Shimla, called him to his office and obtained his signatures on payment-related vouchers by allegedly misleading him into believing that the signatures were required to complete the reimbursement process. However, the complainant claimed that despite signing the vouchers, he did not receive the approved amount.The complainant further stated that after he inquired in July, the accounts branch told him that the funds in question had already been withdrawn but had not been credited to his account.The police, in a statement, said that the relevant financial records were examined after the complaint was received.The investigation revealed that a total of ₹2.35 lakh had been illegally withdrawn from a district police fund over the two years.The police alleged that there is no record indicating the purpose for which Gandhi, then SSP, had used the funds.According to the records, when Gandhi was transferred to the department of personnel, he allegedly diverted the approved payment meant for the complainant to cover a shortfall in a fund.Reacting to the development, Gandhi said the FIR has been registered against him for questioning the utilisation of funds under the Himachal Pradesh Police Road Safety Fund. He demanded an independent audit and rejected the allegations of financial misappropriation.“I will respond to the allegations through legal means. The action against me is linked to my demand for an audit of the road safety fund,” he said.

title: Nurpur drug trafficker’s assets worth  ₹48 lakh forfeited | Hindustan Times
description: According to police, the assets comprise a residential house at Channi village in Indora tehsil in Kangra district, valued at  ₹45 lakh, and an amount totalling  ₹ 2.40 lakh recorded as drug money.
content: Nurpur police have achieved a significant breakthrough by taking legal action against illegally acquired assets worth ₹48 lakh belonging to a drug trafficker detained under the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PIT-NDPS) Act, officials said on Thursday.According to police, the assets comprise a residential house at Channi village in Indora tehsil in Kangra district, valued at ₹45 lakh, and an amount totalling ₹ 2.40 lakh recorded as drug money.Police officials said that the case pertains to a resident of Sirat village. On July 30, 2023, police recovered 10grams of heroin and ₹8,500 from his possession. An FIR was registered under Sections 21 and 25 of the NDPS Act. He had also been booked in two previous NDPS cases in 2022 involving recoveries of 8grams and 9 grams of heroin.In view of his continued involvement in drug trafficking, Nurpur police recommended the preventive detention of the trafficker under the PIT-NDPS Act.A spokesperson of the police department said that as part of further action, Nurpur police conducted a detailed financial investigation into his movable and immovable properties and identified assets. “A freezing order was issued on June 12, 2025, under Section 68F (1) of the NDPS Act and confirmed by the competent authority on July 9, 2025. Following the prescribed legal proceedings, the identified assets were forfeited in favour of the government,” police said.

title: BJP returning to power in Himachal in 2027: Anurag | Hindustan Times
description: Former Union minister and BJP MP Anurag Thakur was speaking on the sidelines of a felicitation function for representatives of Panchayati Raj institutions and urban local bodies in Theog constituency on Thursday
content: Former Union minister and BJP MP Anurag Thakur predicted that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will return to power in Himachal Pradesh in the 2027 assembly elections with “more than two-thirds majority”.Accusing the Congress state government of financial mismanagement, Thakur said, “The BJP is expected to get a decisive mandate in the 2027 Assembly elections. The BJP will win decisively in Himachal Pradesh, with a majority of more than two-thirds.”He was speaking on the sidelines of a felicitation function for representatives of Panchayati Raj institutions and urban local bodies in Theog constituency on Thursday. Thakur said that the Congress government in Himachal was facing discontent among employees, pensioners, unemployed youth, women, farmers and orchardists.Thakur criticised the Congress and other opposition parties over their objections to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and allegations concerning electronic voting machines (EVMs), accusing them of questioning constitutional institutions after losing elections.Thakur alleged that some opposition leaders had received support from foreign interests and accused them of attempting to undermine India’s democratic institutions through misinformation and political agitation.“When the Congress wins elections in Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Jharkhand or other states, the EVMs are fine. When it loses, the EVMs become faulty. Earlier, the Election Commission was acceptable to them; now they question it,” he said.Thakur accused the Congress of hypocrisy over electoral processes and cited its past political record to challenge its criticism of democratic institutions.Former chief minister and leader of the opposition, Jai Ram Thakur, said the results of the recent panchayat elections reflected a clear mandate against the Congress government.“In the upcoming Assembly elections, the people of Himachal Pradesh will completely wipe out the Congress and ensure the formation of a BJP government with an overwhelming majority,” he said.HP govt’s day numbered: ShrikantBJP Himachal in-charge and Mathura MLA Shrikant Sharma said that the Congress government was on its way out.He alleged that the Congress government had failed to address the concerns of various sections of society.“Young people were worried about employment opportunities, employees were struggling with their demands, and farmers and orchardists continued to face numerous challenges. Instead of resolving public grievances, the government remained preoccupied with political statements and controversies,” Sharma said.Turning to organisational matters, Sharma emphasised the importance of strengthening the party at the grassroots level. He said that “Apna Booth, Sabse Mazboot” was not merely a slogan but a guiding principle of the BJP’s organisational structure.

title: Shimla cops use water cannons, lathi-charge to stop protesters seeking rollback of UGC Act | Hindustan Times
description: The protesters marched to the secretariat after completing a 600-km, 21-day ‘Swarn Samaj Ashwamedh Nyay Yatra’, demanding the rollback of UGC provisions, enactment of a law for the protection of the Swarn Samaj and action on issues concerning social justice.
content: Police resorted to a lathi-charge and used water cannons on members of the Rashtriya Devbhoomi Party, who were protesting outside the secretariat in Shimla to demand the withdrawal of the University Grants Commission (UGC) Act.The protesters marched to the secretariat after completing a 600-km, 21-day ‘Swarn Samaj Ashwamedh Nyay Yatra’, demanding the rollback of UGC provisions, enactment of a law for the protection of the Swarn Samaj and action on issues concerning social justice.The protesters began their march from near the Inter-State Bus Terminus (ISBT) in Shimla, travelled through Khalini and Tolland before reaching the secretariat. They subsequently gathered outside the state government complex and sought to submit a memorandum to chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu.Police deployed at the secretariat stopped them and used force as they attempted to move towards the premises. The protesters were demanding that the government receive their memorandum and address their concerns.The march marked the culmination of the fourth phase of the nationwide Swarn Samaj campaign, which the organisers said began in Himachal Pradesh on October 2 and covered 600 kilometres over 21 days. Participants included representatives of social organisations from Himachal Pradesh and other states.RDP national president Rumit Singh Thakur said. “We have walked 600 kilometres over 21 days and have come here to place our demands before the government. Although the UGC issue does not fall directly within the state government’s jurisdiction, we want the government and opposition to raise our concerns.”

title: Omar inaugurates Kashmir Marathon Expo ahead of Sunday’s race | Hindustan Times
description: The J&K CM will be flagging off the marathon but will not be participating this year as he did in the first two editions.
content: Srinagar: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah inaugurated the three-day Kashmir Marathon Expo at Polo ground on Thursday.The final leg of preparations for the much-anticipated third edition of the event is scheduled to be held on Sunday.The chief minister expressed confidence that the Kashmir Marathon would attract runners from across the country and abroad, further strengthening its standing as a major sporting event in the region. “For the third time, the Kashmir Marathon is being organised. On Sunday, people will come to participate not only from different parts of the country but also from abroad. Every race has its own beauty, but the Kashmir Marathon’s surroundings are unmatched. The prize money offered is also significantly higher than that of many other races,” he said.Highlighting a new initiative aimed at encouraging local talent, the chief minister said a separate prize category had been introduced for local runners in response to their demands.“This year, keeping in view the demands of our local runners, prizes have been introduced for them as an incentive to participate in both the half marathon and the full marathon,” he said, adding that the initiative would encourage greater participation among local athletes.Recalling his participation in the first two editions of the Kashmir Marathon, Omar Abdullah expressed hope that this year’s event would witness enthusiastic participation from runners and sports enthusiasts.Urging people who had not yet registered to take advantage of the opportunity available at the exposition, the Chief Minister said, “For those who have not registered yet, there is still an opportunity to do so here. Come, register and participate in the marathon. Winning is not as important as participating. Take part and enjoy the marathon.”Omar inspected various stalls and counters set up by government departments, private sports firms and event partners, showcasing a wide range of sports gear, equipment and accessories aimed at promoting fitness, outdoor activities and a vibrant sporting culture. The exposition also features dedicated bib collection centres and on-the-spot registration counters for participants of the upcoming marathon.The chief minister also interacted with stall owners, athletes and volunteers, appreciating their efforts in promoting sports, fitness and outdoor activities in Jammu and Kashmir.On the occasion, he presented race bibs and merchandise to several runners participating in Sunday’s event, encouraging them to take part with enthusiasm and sporting spirit.mi

title: ‘Winnability, not fixed quotas’: SP snubs Cong push for 3-digit seat share | Hindustan Times
description: SP leaders ask Congress leadership to refrain from negotiating through media and instead form an alliance committee to initiate primary level discussions
content: LUCKNOW Setting clear boundaries ahead of the 2027 UP Assembly polls, the Samajwadi Party (SP) on Thursday pushed back against reports of the Congress eyeing a three-digit seat share in a pre-Diwali alliance pact, asserting that “winnability” will be the sole criterion for distributing tickets.Taking strong exception to statements regarding seat numbers, senior SP leaders asked the Congress leadership to refrain from negotiating through the media and instead form a formal alliance committee to initiate primary-level discussions.“Any kind of media statement regarding seat sharing is not in the interest of the alliance, and what individual leaders say or claim is of no importance to us,” said former MLC and senior SP leader Udaiveer Singh. “The Congress top leadership should first form an alliance committee to start primary-level discussions with counterparts in our party. Subsequent to that, issues will be discussed between the top leadership of both parties. It is unfortunate that some leaders are fixing alliance seats through media discussions. This is against the spirit of the alliance,” he added.Highly placed sources within the SP maintained that the party is closely analysing recent voting patterns, local organisational strength, and candidate viability rather than conceding a large block of seats based on the Congress’s national profile or its improved tally in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.SP president Akhilesh Yadav has repeatedly underlined this position. He stated that the successful 2024 INDIA bloc alliance with the Congress will continue for the 2027 Assembly polls, but candidate selection and seat-sharing will be decided solely on winnability.“Gathbandhan bhi hoga, gathbandhan ke saath challenge bhi, baat humare liye seat ki nahi hogi, jeetne wali seat ki hogi. Jo jeete woh seat le le” (there will be an alliance, and there will also be challenges with it. For us, it will not be about seats but about winnability, whoever can win a seat should get it),” Yadav said while launching the party’s campaign from Rae Bareli in September this year.Party sources indicated that the SP is analysing recent voting patterns, local organisational strength and candidate viability rather than conceding a large block of seats based on the Congress’s national profile or its improved showing in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. While the SP has in earlier reports been linked to offers in the range of around 60-65 seats, sources stressed that the final number will flow purely from winnability assessments, not fixed quotas.According to official EC data, in the 2022 UP Legislative Assembly polls (403 seats), the BJP won 255 seats with 41.29% of valid votes. The SP secured 111 seats with 32.06%. The Congress won just two seats with a 2.33% vote share, despite contesting the vast majority of constituencies. The Rashtriya Lok Dal (then allied with the SP) won eight seats, while the Bahujan Samaj Party managed only one seat despite a 12.88% vote share. The broader SP-led alliance finished with around 125 seats against the NDA’s roughly 273.In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in UP (80 seats), the picture shifted under a seat-sharing arrangement. The SP won 37 seats (approximately 33.8% vote share overall). The BJP took 33 seats (around 41.7%). The Congress, allotted 17 seats in the INDIA alliance, won six (overall vote share about 9.5%). The INDIA bloc finished with 43 seats to the NDA’s 36.“Data from the Election Commission does not lie,” another SP source said. “In 2022, the Congress’s statewide performance was minimal. In 2024, targeted seats delivered better results. For 2027, we will look at Assembly segments where any ally has proven strength, recent margins and candidate acceptability. Numbers for the sake of numbers help no one. As Akhilesh ji has said time and again, the alliance continues, but only winnability decides the seats,” he added.The SP’s emphasis on winnability has set a clear boundary. Party leaders maintain that an effective alliance against the BJP requires prioritising seats that can actually be won, rather than symbolic or inflated allocations.

title: How Anahat beat an 8-time world champion to script the biggest win of her career | Hindustan Times
description: The 18-year-old Indian stunned her icon Nour 3-0 (11-8, 11-8, 11-7) in the second round of the Silicon Valley Open
content: When young athletes step on to play an opponent they once looked up to, they often speak about enjoying the moment, relishing the opportunity and soaking in the experience.Anahat Singh did all of that in her first encounter with Nour El Sherbini. And, walked out a winner.In the biggest victory yet of her blossoming career, the 18-year-old Indian stunned Egypt's eight-time world champion 3-0 (11-8, 11-8, 11-7) in the second round of the Silicon Valley Open, a PSA gold event, in California's Redwood City.It's a remarkable result on several counts – not least the straight-games scoreline against the top seed.Anahat is at a career-high ranking of 15 while Nour, a former multiple-times world No.1, still sits at No.3. The Indian teen secured her first Asian Games individual medal, a silver, only last month while the 30-year-old Egyptian gobbled eight World Championships gold medals, the joint most by a woman with Malaysian legend Nicol David, between 2015 and 2025. When Nour became the youngest world junior champion in history in 2009, coincidentally on Indian soil, Anahat was one.“It feels unreal,” Anahat told PSA. “I grew up watching every single match of hers. I admire her so much."Putting that admiration aside, even if briefly, was a key pre-match topic between her and Harinder Pal Sandhu, India’s national coach accompanying Anahat at the tournament.“Sometimes when you play greats of the game, too much respect gets in the way. This match for Anahat was more about the mind than tactics,” Sandhu told HT from the US. “My conversations with her were about keeping Nour’s stature aside, and reminding her that you are the world junior champion and world No.15.”Starting the year outside the top 25, Anahat grabbed the biggest PSA title of her career at the Squash on Fire Open in February. Five months on, she became the first Indian to be crowned the world junior champion. Two months on, she became the first Indian woman to win an individual silver at the Asian Games. A month on, she scripted her career's biggest win.The Indian teen is not just routinely rubbing shoulders with the world's best now, she is also starting to get past them. Anahat won the Squash on Fire Open title defeating current world No.8 Georgina Kennedy in the final. At last month's London Squash Classic, she beat the then 11th-ranked Nele Gilis. At Aichi-Nagoya, she produced a memorable fightback against world No.6 Satomi Watanabe to confirm a historic medal. Even as most of India's Asian Games medallists basked in the celebration at home, Anahat was back to business in Egypt nine days after her last match in Japan.“This result, just after the Asian Games, is a very big achievement,” said Sandhu. “The most pleasing thing for me was that she did not allow her to stage a comeback.”At the Egyptian Squash Open, Anahat led world No.7 Fayrouz Aboelkheir by two games to one before Fayrouz turned it around. The Indian was wary of a similar fightback from a champion who has been there and done that for years and shares the same coach as her: former French world No.1 Gregory Gaultier. Flaunting the variety in her game that troubled Watanabe in Japan, Anahat frequently targeted the front corners against Nour.“The tactics were about not allowing Nour to dictate the pace, and playing to Anahat’s style rather than engaging in conventional long rallies,” said Sandhu.Almost fittingly, the 18-year-old capped off the clinical show with an angled backhand volley that died on an outstretched 30-year-old. Anahat turned around wearing a look of disbelief. A couple of seconds later, Nour walked across and gave her a hug. The child who grew up following a colossal of the sport had just outclassed her.

title: ₹12,000 crore project: Prayagraj metro DPR revised, airport link added; state nod awaited | Hindustan Times
description: The revised plan proposes two corridors: Shantipuram to Cheoki in Naini and Jhunsi to the airport via Bamrauli and the proposed Aero City area. The second corridor has been extended to the airport to improve connectivity.
content: A revised detailed project report (DPR) for a conventional metro rail network in Prayagraj has been submitted by RITES Limited, a PSU under the ministry of railways, to the Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation (UPMRC). The estimated ₹12,000 crore project awaits state government approval before being forwarded to the Centre for clearance, officials informed on Thursday.The revised plan proposes two corridors: Shantipuram to Cheoki in Naini and Jhunsi to the airport via Bamrauli and the proposed Aero City area. The second corridor has been extended to the airport to improve connectivity.A key feature is a proposed metro interchange at Parade, where the two corridors will intersect and connect with a ropeway station, creating a multimodal transport hub.The project has undergone several revisions. An initial DPR proposed a conventional metro system, followed by a MetroLite plan featuring 39 smaller stations and lighter infrastructure. Following suggestions from UPMRC, RITES conducted a fresh survey last year and prepared the revised DPR for a conventional metro network.Prayagraj Development Authority (PDA) vice-chairman Rishi Raj said the revised DPR includes extending the Jhunsi-Bamrauli corridor to the airport. The project will require state and central government approvals for clearance and funding, he added.

title: Honour your commitments in relationships: UP governor to students | Hindustan Times
description: Speaking at the seventh convocation of Maharishi University of Information Technology, Lucknow, Patel also advised students to rely on their own intelligence, discretion and creativity rather than becoming overly dependent on Artificial Intelligence (AI). She urged them to use their knowledge for the welfare of society and the country, and not to mislead people.
content: Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel on Thursday said there was nothing wrong with students having girlfriends, but stressed that they must honour their commitments if they chose to enter a relationship.Speaking at the seventh convocation of Maharishi University of Information Technology, Lucknow, Patel also advised students to rely on their own intelligence, discretion and creativity rather than becoming overly dependent on Artificial Intelligence (AI). She urged them to use their knowledge for the welfare of society and the country, and not to mislead people.Congratulating degree recipients and award winners, she said respecting parents, maintaining a positive outlook and using knowledge in the national interest were central to the purpose of education.Recalling her tenure as women and child welfare minister, Patel said decisions were taken to provide financial assistance to widows and empower women through property and housing schemes.The governor also visited the student project exhibition and appreciated innovations.Patel said state universities had adopted five villages each to work on education, sanitation and nutrition, covering around 200 villages. She added that 19 state universities had secured A+ and A++ grades from the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC).Higher education minister Yogendra Upadhyay, university chancellor Ajay Prakash Srivastava and vice-chancellor Prof B P Singh were present.

title: Pilibhit voter roll discrepancies: FIR against 2 SDMs, computer operator | Hindustan Times
description: Pilibhit district magistrate (DM) Alok Kumar confirmed the FIR and said preliminary investigations, conducted on the directions of Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa, found lapses on the part of Puranpur SDM Mayank Goswami and Amariya SDM Hemant Chaudhary.
content: An FIR has been registered against two sub-divisional magistrates (SDMs) and a computer operator over alleged irregularities in the electoral roll of Pilibhit Sadar assembly constituency, after an inquiry found discrepancies in 10,470 voter entries.Pilibhit district magistrate (DM) Alok Kumar confirmed the FIR and said preliminary investigations, conducted on the directions of Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa, found lapses on the part of Puranpur SDM Mayank Goswami and Amariya SDM Hemant Chaudhary. Both officers have been removed from their posts and attached to the district headquarters, while computer operator Anil Kumar has been dismissed. Departmental proceedings against the two SDMs have also been initiated.Rinwa said the district election officer’s report found that 13,779 Form-8 applications seeking changes to voter details had been entered between May 31 and August 29, 2026, without the corresponding forms or records being available in the office. Of these, 10,470 applications were approved and 3,309 rejected.The computer operator and the two electoral registration officers (EROs) responsible for the constituency during the periods ending July 16 and from July 17 to August 29 have been held responsible for the irregularities. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has directed legal action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and relevant provisions of the Indian Penal Code. The role of assistant electoral registration officers is also being investigated.The case has sparked a political controversy as Pilibhit Sadar is represented by state minister Sanjay Gangwar, who won the 2022 assembly election by 6,920 votes. The constituency has 3,48,937 registered electors, according to figures cited by the Congress.The ECI has ordered scrutiny of all Form-6 applications for enrolment and Form-7 applications for deletion processed by the computer operator between April 10, when the special intensive revision (SIR) concluded, and October 21. The district election officer (DEO) has been asked to submit a detailed report within a day.Electoral rolls across all assembly constituencies in Pilibhit are also to be examined, while correction of affected Form-8 entries is under way.

title: Pune’s festive vehicle registrations dips by 25.6% | Hindustan Times
description: Motor car registrations witnessed the steepest decline among the major vehicle categories, dropping 46.1 per cent from 4,813 to 2,595, while two-wheeler registrations fell 12 per cent from 8,007 to 7,046
content: During the festive season, new vehicle registrations in Pune dropped by 25.6%, according to data from the Pune Regional Transport Office (RTO). Registrations fell to 10,534 in October 2026, down from the 14,168 vehicles recorded in October 2025.Motor car registrations witnessed the steepest decline among the major vehicle categories, dropping 46.1 per cent from 4,813 to 2,595, while two-wheeler registrations fell 12 per cent from 8,007 to 7,046.According to Pune RTO data, motorcycle registrations dropped by 961. Registrations of auto-rickshaws fell sharply from 183 to 41, while tourist taxi registrations declined from 423 to 229. Goods vehicle registrations decreased from 577 to 507, and tractor registrations fell from 100 to 42. Bus registrations, however, increased marginally from 33 to 36, while the category listed as ‘others’ rose from 32 to 38.Swapnil Bhosale, deputy regional transport officer, Pune RTO, said, “The registration figures show a decline in the overall number of vehicles registered during the period under comparison. Purchasing decisions can be influenced by several factors.”“I had planned to buy a car this Dussehra, but the drought has affected our farming income, and we are not getting a good price for our produce. With uncertain earnings and expenses to manage, I felt it was not the right time to take on a big financial commitment,” said Bhagwandas Bhadale, a farmer from rural Pune.The data also reveals a contrasting trend in electric vehicle registrations. Electric motorcycle registrations increased from 1,152 to 1,182, while electric car registrations rose from 355 to 382. Total registrations in the electric vehicle category increased from 1,566 to 1,638, a rise of approximately 4.6 per cent. Electric goods vehicle registrations also climbed from 16 to 44, while electric auto-rickshaw registrations increased from 5 to 14. Tourist taxi registrations in the electric category, however, fell from 38 to 12. The figures suggest that the overall decline in vehicle registrations has not been accompanied by a fall in every electric vehicle category.

title: Solapur police crack down on sand mafia; 51 smugglers detained over two years | Hindustan Times
description: The move targets illegal sand extraction and sale, particularly in areas where no sand auctions have been carried out; and use of proceeds from the trade to finance criminal activities
content: Cracking down on the sand mafia, the Solapur district police have detained 51 sand smugglers and habitual offenders in Yerawada central prison under the Maharashtra Prevention of Dangerous Activities (MPDA) Act over the past two years from September 2024 to September 2026. The move targets illegal sand extraction and sale, particularly in areas where no sand auctions have been carried out; and use of proceeds from the trade to finance criminal activities.The crackdown follows incidents wherein sand smugglers allegedly rammed vehicles into government officials and attacked police personnel. Solapur superintendent of police Atul Kulkarni said that the police have compiled detailed records of habitual offenders and are using stringent preventive measures to curb the illegal trade. Proposals for action against 11 more habitual offenders, particularly sand smugglers, have been sent to the district collector. The police have also externed 45 criminal gangs comprising 175 members for offences including theft, attempted robbery and attempted murder; with action against 30 more gangs planned. Among the gangs targeted are those of Pankaj Kolekar, linked to sand smuggling; and other groups associated with criminal offences.“We have maintained detailed records of habitual offenders, particularly those involved in illegal sand extraction and sale, and are taking stringent action against them. Over the past two years, we have detained 51 sand smugglers and other habitual offenders under the MPDA Act and sent them to Yerawada central prison. We have also forwarded proposals for action against 11 more offenders to the district collector. Our objective is to prevent these individuals from continuing their illegal activities and using the proceeds to fund other crimes,” Kulkarni said.Those detained under the MPDA Act include Mahesh Shinde, Suraj Shinde, Ajinkya alias Bablu Rokade and Akshay Rokade from Pandharpur; Pappu Ingole, Sachin Ananda Kedar and Rohit Kadlaskar from Sangola; Pintu Patil from Akkalkot; Annasaheb Patil and Swapnil Kamble from Madha; and Sharad Koli from Mohol. The police have also detained Dattatraya Jadhav of Pandharpur, accused of milk adulteration that endangered public health; and Somnath alias Bapu Bhosale of Mohol.“In a wider campaign against organised crime, we have invoked the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against three gangs. These include a group allegedly led by Fayaz Sheikh, accused of operating an MD drug manufacturing unit in an industrial area; along with 17 members of the gang. Action has also been initiated against the gang associated with self-styled godman Manohar Bhosale in Karmala, with further investigation underway,” Kulkarni said.

title: Australia suffer first innings defeat in South Africa in 56 years as Temba Bavuma's team script stunning win | Cricket
description: Australia were beaten by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha, their first innings defeat on South African soil in 56 years.   | Cricket
content: After suffering a defeat in Durban in the first Test, South Africa roared back into the five-match Test Series by absolutely crushing Australia in the second Test at the St George's Park in Gqeberha. Crashing to an innings and 31-run loss in a breathtakingly dramatic Test match, the visitors suffered their first innings defeat on South African soil for the first time in 56 years.Not since the Johannesburg Test of 1970 - where Australia were routed by an innings and 129 runs - have they been beaten so comprehensively in the Rainbow Nation. This marks only the second time South Africa has inflicted an innings defeat on Australia since readmission, serving as a harsh echo of their famous victory in Hobart in 2016.Temba Bavuma’s masterclass rescues ProteasThe sheer magnitude of Australia's defeat is highlighted by the fact that at one point of the match, they looked most likely to take full control. Early in the match, the Australian bowling attack tore through the South African top order, reducing the hosts to a precarious 110/6.A monumental rescue mission orchestrated by South Africa captain Temba Bavuma followed. He hit an astounding innings of 179, guiding South Africa to 425/9 before they declared. The 315 runs added after the fall of the sixth wicket stand as one of the most remarkable lower-order turnarounds in recent Test history.At 36 years and 154 days old, Bavuma became the oldest captain to score a century against Australia in the World Test Championship, eclipsing the previous record held by India's Rohit Sharma. Additionally, his brilliant knock secured his place as the first-ever South African captain to register a Test century at St George’s Park. It also now stands as the second-highest individual Test score at the venue, sitting just behind Herschelle Gibbs' 196 in 2001.ALSO READ: Temba Bavuma, captaincy and the making of a batting starCatastrophic collapse and rare follow-onFaced with an imposing first-innings total, Australia's batting lineup completely disintegrated. The tourists suffered a catastrophic collapse, folding for a dismal 99 all out. Marco Jansen starred for South Africa with a 5-wicket haul.This was their third-lowest Test total in South Africa, behind only the infamous 47 at Cape Town in 2011 and 75 at Durban in 1950.Conceding a massive 326-run deficit, Australia were enforced a follow-on. This marked a generational low; it was only the third time in this century, and just the third time in the past 38 years, that an Australian Test team were forced to bat again.While their second innings offered slightly more resistance, the monumental deficit proved insurmountable, as they were bundled out for 296 in the second innings. Travis Head offered some fight by scoring a century, but to no avail. Kagiso Rabada was the star with the ball taking 4 wickets.

title: Are you ignoring this key nutrient while chasing protein? Nutritionist reveals an important link between protein and fibre | Health
description: Explore the essential balance of protein and fibre in your diet, understand their roles, and learn why nutrient diversity supports optimal health.  | Health
content: Protein has become nutrition’s favourite number. We add it to breakfast, look for it in snack bars, blend it into smoothies and mentally calculate whether we’ve had “enough” by dinner. Protein awareness has certainly come a long way, and that is a good thing. But as a nutritionist, I’d like people to ask another question alongside “Am I getting enough protein?” “Am I getting enough fibre too?” Because while our protein obsession has grown, protein was never meant to exist in a nutritional vacuum.What is protein digestibility?Imagine two options side by side, both offering roughly the same amount of protein. They may look identical at first glance, but their protein source, essential amino-acid profile, quality, digestibility, and other nutritional benefits can differ. That's where the protein + fibre conversation gets interesting. Protein and fibre tend to live in completely different wellness conversations. Protein gets the gym selfies. Fibre comes up when someone mentions their gut. Yet for everyday nutrition, we need to make room for both.Protein supplies essential amino acids needed to maintain and repair muscle. Fibre has a different job: certain fermentable fibres, including prebiotic fibres, feed our gut microbiota. So protein and fibre don't need to compete for attention; they play different roles in the same diet. Is 2 eggs a day too much protein?This matters especially when we intentionally add more protein to our day. Think about how easy it is to add protein: an extra protein-rich breakfast, a protein snack at your desk, or a shake after a long day. Increasing protein is one goal, but it shouldn't mean fibre-rich foods quietly disappear from the menu. What if I eat only protein and fibre?"So I prefer a simple rule: when you think protein, think fibre too. If your afternoon snack is protein-heavy, do you make room for fruits, vegetables, whole grains, or other fibre-containing foods? And when choosing packaged nutrition, look beyond the protein number to the overall nutritional composition," Nutritionist Madhuri Ruia tells Health Shots. Do we need fibre to absorb protein?Importantly, this isn't about claiming that fibre magically makes the body absorb more protein. The two nutrients have distinct roles. It is about moving away from single-nutrient thinking and toward a more balanced approach to everyday nutrition. Which is better for me, fermented yeast protein or whey protein?Protein choices themselves are evolving too. Whey and familiar food sources remain established choices, while sources like fermented yeast protein are expanding the landscape. Some yeast protein concentrates can provide all nine essential amino acids and, when processed properly, show good digestibility. For consumers, that means more ways to find quality protein that fits their dietary preferences and routines. Perhaps that is the real upgrade our protein routines need. Not necessarily another scoop, but a wider lens. We have done a good job of teaching people to look for protein. The next step is to think beyond protein alone; quality protein, fibre, and overall diet balance all deserve a place in the conversation. description: OTT Tamil: వర్సటైల్ యాక్టర్ 'మక్కల్ సెల్వన్' విజయ్ సేతుపతి కథానాయకుడిగా నటించిన తమిళ ఫీల్-గుడ్ కామెడీ ఎంటర్‌టైనర్ 'బత్తా' (Baththa) ఓటీటీ విడుదలకు సిద్ధమైంది. ప్రముఖ డిజిటల్ ఓటీటీ ప్లాట్‌ఫామ్ 'నెట్‌ఫ్లిక్స్' (Netflix) లో అక్టోబర్ 29 నుంచి ఈ సినిమా స్ట్రీమింగ్ కానుంది.
content: OTT Tamil: వైవిధ్యమైన పాత్రలతో దక్షిణాది చిత్ర పరిశ్రమలో తనకంటూ ప్రత్యేక స్థానాన్ని ఏర్పరుచుకున్న తమిళ నటుడు, 'మక్కల్ సెల్వన్' విజయ్ సేతుపతి (Vijay Sethupathi). విలక్షణమైన కథాంశాలను ఎంచుకుంటూ ప్రేక్షకులను అలరించే ఆయన లేటెస్ట్ ఫీల్-గుడ్ డ్రామా 'బత్తా' (Baththa). థియేటర్లలో విమర్శకుల ప్రశంసలతో పాటు ప్రేక్షకుల ఆదరణ పొందిన ఈ చిత్రం ఇప్పుడు డిజిటల్ వీక్షకులను అలరించేందుకు సిద్ధమైంది.ఈ చిత్ర డిజిటల్ హక్కులను ప్రముఖ దిగ్గజ ఓటీటీ ప్లాట్‌ఫామ్ నెట్‌ఫ్లిక్స్ (Netflix) దక్కించుకుంది. ఈ పండుగ సీజన్ కానుకగా అక్టోబర్ 29 నుంచి ఈ సినిమాను స్ట్రీమింగ్‌కు తీసుకువస్తున్నట్లు నెట్‌ఫ్లిక్స్ సంస్థ అధికారికంగా వెల్లడించింది. తమిళంతో పాటు తెలుగు, కన్నడ, మలయాళం, హిందీ భాషల డబ్బింగ్ వెర్షన్‌లు ఏకకాలంలో ఓటీటీ ఆడియెన్స్ కు అందుబాటులోకి రానున్నాయి.బత్తా.. 5 భాషల్లో గ్రాండ్ డిజిటల్ ఎంట్రీబత్తా మూవీ అక్టోబర్ 1న థియేటర్లలో రిలీజైంది. బాక్సాఫీస్ దగ్గర మంచి విజయం సాధించింది. అంతేకాదు ఐఎండీబీలో ఏకంగా 9.1 రేటింగ్ సొంతం చేసుకోవడం విశేషం. ఓ మంచి ఫీల్ గుడ్ కామెడీ ఎంటర్టైనర్ గా ఈ సినిమాను తమిళ ప్రేక్షకులు ఆదరించారు.అయితే పాన్-ఇండియా స్థాయిలో విజయ్ సేతుపతికి ఉన్న క్రేజ్‌ను దృష్టిలో ఉంచుకుని, ఈ సినిమాను కేవలం తమిళంలోనే కాకుండా తెలుగు, కన్నడ, మలయాళం, హిందీ భాషల్లో కూడా డబ్బింగ్ చేసి ఏకకాలంలో విడుదల చేస్తున్నారు. దీనితో తెలుగు ఓటీటీ ప్రియులు కూడా తమ సొంత భాషలో ఈ క్లాసిక్ కామెడీ ఎంటర్‌టైనర్‌ను ఆస్వాదించవచ్చు.ఈ చిత్రానికి బాలాజీ తరణీధరన్ (Balaji Tharaneetharan) దర్శకత్వం వహించారు. గతంలో విజయ్ సేతుపతితో 'నడువుల కొంజమ్ పక్కత కానోమ్' వంటి మైండ్ బ్లాకింగ్ కామెడీ హిట్‌ను అందించిన ఈ కాంబినేషన్ మళ్లీ సుదీర్ఘ విరామం తర్వాత 'బత్తా' చిత్రం ద్వారా ఒకే వేదికపైకి రావడం విశేషం.వినోదం, హృదయానికి హత్తుకునే కథాంశం'బత్తా' మూవీ కథా నేపథ్యం అత్యంత సహజ సిద్ధమైన హాస్యంతో, మనుషుల అనుబంధాల చుట్టూ తిరుగుతుంది. ఒక సాధారణ వ్యక్తి ఎదుర్కొనే విచిత్రమైన పరిస్థితులు, వాటిని అతడు తన అమాయకత్వం, తెలివితేటలతో ఎలా ఎదుర్కొన్నాడనేది సినిమాలో ఎంతో వినోదాత్మకంగా చూపించారు. సబ్‌టైటిల్స్ లేదా డబ్బింగ్‌తో పనిలేకుండా ప్రతీ సగటు ప్రేక్షకుడికి కనెక్ట్ అయ్యే హ్యూమర్ ఈ సినిమాలో ఉండటం ప్రధాన బలం.ఓ క్రిమినల్ ను 8 ఏళ్ల ఓ బాలుడు అనుకోకుండా ఓ బాత్రూమ్ లో వేసి తాళం వేస్తాడు. ఆ తర్వాత జరిగే పరిణామాలు, ఇద్దరి మధ్య ఏర్పడే బాండింగ్ చుట్టూ ఈ సినిమా తిరుగుతుంది.విజయ్ సేతుపతి నటన, ఆయన మార్క్ కామెడీ టైమింగ్, సహజమైన డైలాగ్ డెలివరీ ఈ చిత్రానికి బలంగా నిలిచాయని సినిమాను చూసిన సినీ విమర్శకులు పేర్కొన్నారు. ఇటీవల కాలంలో థ్రిల్లర్‌లు, యాక్షన్ సినిమాల మోజులో పడి నిజమైన 'ఫీల్ గుడ్' అండ్ ఫ్యామిలీ కామెడీ చిత్రాలు తగ్గడంతో, 'బత్తా' లాంటి సినిమాలు ఓటీటీ వీక్షకులకు మంచి రిఫ్రెష్‌మెంట్‌ను ఇస్తాయి. అక్టోబర్ 29 నుంచి నెట్‌ఫ్లిక్స్‌లో అందుబాటులోకి రానున్న ఈ చిత్రాన్ని మీ వాచ్‌లిస్ట్‌లో ఖచ్చితంగా చేర్చుకోండి.

title: Unshackled India turn 225 into target practice | Cricket
description: Samson and Abhishek scored at a rate that left little room for doubt who the eventual winners would be  | Cricket
content: For India, New Zealand chose to reserve their best. Glenn Phillips turned it on with an unbeaten 40-ball 82, Finn Allen carved 45 off 24 balls, before Bevon Jacobs left India high and dry with 31 off 16.But evidently, even 225 wasn’t enough as India orchestrated a fascinating chase in the first T20I at Christchurch to ride into the record books. Primarily because Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma responded by treating this target as an invitation to attack. So spectacular was their unshackled batting that even a middle-order collapse could not derail a chase completed with two balls to spare.The previous highest successful T20I chase by India was 209, against Australia at Visakhapatnam in 2023. That mark was surpassed with room to spare, the foundation was laid in a Powerplay that seemed to render the target almost irrelevant.Samson made 67 from 33 balls, Abhishek contributed 29 from 12, and the opening pair put on 93 before Abhishek was dismissed, all before the powerplay could be completed. Their assault yielded 15.66 runs an over, leaving India needing 132 from the remaining 14 overs. For a side chasing 226, this was the kind of luxury very few chasing teams get.“We just watch the ball and hit hard,” Samson said of his partnership with Abhishek, a wonderfully uncomplicated description of an approach that left New Zealand scrambling for answers. “We do have a lot of conversations happening in the middle, but nothing makes sense actually.”It was not quite as simple or senseless as Samson made it sound. The opener had to contend with movement from Matt Henry early in the innings, but responded with a crisp pull and a straight drive before taking on Adam Milne and Lockie Ferguson. Abhishek supplied the more explosive counterpoint, launching Henry over cover for six and pulling Milne for towering blows. Ferguson’s second over cost 22 runs, while the fourth yielded 26 as New Zealand’s lengths unravelled under pressure.Samson reached his half-century from 23 balls, with eight fours and four sixes, and India embarked on a start that made the chase appear likely to be completed long before the final over.“We just felt like keeping the shape and having a very positive intent in the Powerplay,” Samson said. “Once we got off to a flying start, we felt the match could be finished in the first half as well.”That confidence was not misplaced, but New Zealand’s spinners ensured the contest was not decided quite so early. Michael Bracewell removed Abhishek, caught at short third, before Mitchell Santner bowled Samson with an under-edge onto the stumps. Bracewell then dismissed Tilak Varma for six, and Santner had Ishan Kishan caught at long-on for one. India, having reached 93 without loss, were suddenly 122 for four.The collapse was a reminder that attacking intent doesn’t entirely eliminate risk; it merely changes the terms on which a team accepts it. New Zealand’s spinners took four wickets for 76 runs in eight overs, while the pace attack managed only two wickets for 154 runs in 11.4 overs at an economy rate of 13.2. The distinction was decisive. India’s openers had dismantled the seamers, but the middle order had to negotiate a more difficult phase against spin.Shreyas Iyer and Axar Patel did so with a 45-run partnership from only 24 balls. Axar struck a six and two fours before being caught at midwicket, but the stand restored some of the momentum lost in the middle overs.Where Samson and Abhishek had made the target look vulnerable, Naman Dhir ensured the late wobble did not become a crisis with an unbeaten 42 from 15 balls.Iyer credited the opening pair with setting up the pursuit, pointing to the importance of reaching 80 or 85 in the first six overs when chasing a total above 220. “That’s a tremendous start,” he said. “Once they get going, it’s just about the momentum they carry forward, and today was just an example of that.”His assessment also offered an explanation for New Zealand’s imposing total. India had initially found the pitch a little slow, with the ball holding in the surface, and their bowlers had missed the hard lengths they wanted to hit. As dew arrived, however, the surface became flatter and the ball skidded on more.Phillips exploited that with an 82 that acted as the innings’ centrepiece, with Allen and Jacobs providing the time-to-time push the innings needed.The total still appeared formidable, but the conditions that had helped New Zealand also benefited India’s batters. Iyer said the dew made the wicket skid and the ball come on to the bat more easily as the match progressed. India’s response was therefore not simply an exercise in hitting harder; it was a willingness to exploit the changing conditions while maintaining a scoring rate that left little room for doubt who the eventual winners would be.

title: CBFC says Sunny Deol’s Suryaa Ant Se Aarambh Tak not submitted for certification after IMA seeks review over portrayal of doctors | Bollywood
description: The clarification comes after the IMA wrote to Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting, raising concerns over the film’s promotional content.  | Bollywood
content: Sunny Deol's upcoming release has courted trouble before release. As per the latest update from news agency ANI, the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) has clarified that Sunny Deol’s upcoming film Suryaa Ant Se Aarambh Tak has not been submitted for certification, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B) said.What were the objections? The clarification comes after the Indian Medical Association (IMA) wrote to Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw, raising concerns over the film’s promotional content and its alleged portrayal of the medical profession.In its letter to the minister, the IMA objected to the “generalisation of corruption within healthcare” and the “depiction of violence against medical professionals”. It warned that such portrayals could have consequences for the safety of healthcare workers and the doctor-patient relationship. “We wish to express our serious concern regarding the portrayal of the medical profession in the film ‘SURYAA Ant Se Aarambh Tak’. Its promotional content raises concerns about the generalisation of corruption within healthcare, the depiction of violence against medical professionals, and the potential consequences for public trust and the safety of healthcare workers,” a part of the letter read.The IMA said the film’s promotional content could create the impression that corruption and unethical practices are widespread across the medical fraternity. While acknowledging that individual cases of professional misconduct must be investigated and punished, the association maintained that the actions of a few individuals should not tarnish the reputation of countless honest and dedicated doctors.The association also raised concerns about scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nursing staff and other hospital personnel, particularly when such acts appear to be presented as heroic or justified. According to the IMA, such portrayals risk normalising violence against healthcare professionals and could further endanger medical personnel who already face safety challenges in hospitals.“Scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nursing staff, and hospital personnel, particularly when presented as heroic or justified acts, risk normalising violence against those committed to saving lives. Doctors and healthcare personnel already face serious safety challenges in hospitals. Content that appears to glorify attacks on medical professionals may encourage hostility and further endanger those providing essential healthcare services,” it added.The IMA emphasised that it does not support corruption, unethical medical practices or professional misconduct, stating that any wrongdoing should be addressed through appropriate legal and disciplinary action.The association urged the Information and Broadcasting Ministry to conduct an impartial review of the film’s content and its portrayal of the medical profession. It also sought appropriate corrective measures from the filmmakers to address what it described as the generalisation of alleged misconduct and the depiction of violence against healthcare workers.Additionally, the IMA requested that the government consider a ban or other appropriate action if justified under applicable law.About the filmOpening against the backdrop of a deeply personal loss, the teaser establishes a man carrying the scars of his past before pulling him into a disturbing chain of events connected to the medical system. What initially appears to be personal soon begins to reveal something far bigger, as Suryaa starts questioning what others have accepted and uncovers a shocking truth buried beneath a seemingly legitimate system, as per the makers.Besides Sunny Deol in the lead role, ‘Suryaa’ also stars Ravi Kishan, Pragya Jaiswal, Tanushree Chakraborty, Manish Wadhwa, Tinu Anand, Virti Vaghani, Jisshu Sengupta, Khalid Siddiqui, Anoop Trivedi and Rohit Tiwari.It is scheduled to be released on November 20.

title: Hyunbaek-core is South Korea’s quiet luxury trend for people who want ‘rich girl’ aesthetic | Trending
description: “Hyunbaek” is a shortened name for Hyundai Department Store, with “core”, a term commonly used to describe the defining aesthetic of a particular style.  | Trending
content: A new fashion trend emerging in South Korea is drawing attention for its understated portrayal of wealth, with social media users describing it as “the style of a rich girl who has nothing left to buy, even when she goes shopping at a department store.”Known as “Hyunbaek-core,” the trend has gained traction among people in their 20s and 30s, as per a report by The Korea Times. It combines “Hyunbaek”, a shortened name for Hyundai Department Store, with “core”, a term commonly used to describe the defining aesthetic of a particular style.The aesthetic evokes the image of a wealthy young woman browsing a luxury department store without appearing particularly interested in shopping. It is characterised by an effortless sense of affluence, understated elegance and an air of indifference towards material possessions.Hyunbaek-core is closely associated with the concept of “quiet luxury”, which emphasises premium fabrics, refined silhouettes and subtle details instead of conspicuous designer logos. Materials such as silk and cashmere are central to this aesthetic, which communicates wealth without overtly displaying it.While the trend bears similarities to the “old money” aesthetic, which draws inspiration from traditional upper-class lifestyles and dressing, Hyunbaek-core has a more relaxed and effortless approach. Rather than emphasising formality, it seeks to convey the impression of someone who has grown up surrounded by luxury and does not feel the need to prove it.How Hyunbaek-core became popularUnlike earlier fashion trends such as “ballet-core” and “poet-core”, which take inspiration from particular professions, identities or cultural archetypes, Hyunbaek-core is built around a specific place: Hyundai Department Store.The trend’s emergence is closely linked to the retailer’s growing popularity among younger, affluent consumers. Hyundai Department Store has pursued a strategy to attract this demographic, particularly through its flagship store, The Hyundai Seoul, in Yeouido.The share of visitors in their 20s and 30s increased from 37% in 2020 to 46.7% in the first nine months of this year. This growing presence has helped establish the department store in the minds of younger consumers as a destination associated with wealth, luxury and an aspirational lifestyle. As a result, the department store has become more than a shopping destination, with its name now serving as shorthand for a particular social image and aesthetic.(Also Read: The ‘kinda chic’ trend is the internet’s new language for self-love)A growing fascination with inherited wealthThe popularity of Hyunbaek-core also reflects a broader shift in how young people view wealth and social mobility.As economic pressures mount and some younger consumers become less convinced that hard work alone can guarantee upward mobility, the lifestyle of people born into privilege has increasingly become an object of fascination.“Stories of self-made success and the rags-to-riches narrative have lost their persuasive power, and in their place, we are seeing an abstract longing for and admiration of inherited wealth,” Lee Jun-young, a professor in the Department of Economics and Finance at Sangmyung University, said.This yearning is reflected in the appeal of an aesthetic that suggests wealth is an inherent part of one’s life rather than something that needs to be displayed or acquired through visible symbols of success. Hyunbaek-core, therefore, is not simply about wearing expensive clothes. It is also about projecting the image of someone for whom luxury is ordinary rather than aspirational.Lee Eun-hee, a professor of consumer psychology at Inha University, described the trend as an example of the “panoplie effect”. The concept refers to how consumers use products associated with a particular social group to identify themselves with that group or signal a desired social identity. Lee attributed the trend to declining social mobility, suggesting that the appeal of such aesthetics is linked to people’s desire to associate themselves with a privileged class.
