title: Rethinking the MBA: Why domain expertise and practical learning matter more than ever | Hindustan Times
description: As industries transform, B-schools must equip students with practical skills, adaptability and cross-disciplinary knowledge to prepare them for emerging careers
content: A student entering a management programme today may graduate into a role that barely existed when the application was submitted. New technologies can transform industries within months, start-ups can disrupt established markets, and geopolitical or environmental developments can redraw business priorities almost overnight. In such a world, knowing how organisations worked yesterday is no longer enough; future managers must learn how to respond when the rules themselves are changing.This reality is reshaping management education. Aspirants are looking beyond a broad qualification towards programmes that provide specialised knowledge, meaningful industry exposure and opportunities to build new ventures. The World Economic Forum’s Future of Jobs Report 2025 estimates that 39% of workers’ core skills will change by 2030, making adaptability and continuous learning essential management capabilities.Coaching as Compensation: What the Red Fort scheme reveals about school educationFrom generic managerial roles to specialised expertiseOrganisations once hired management graduates for broad functional roles and developed their sectoral knowledge internally. Today, industries such as fintech, healthcare, sustainability and digital commerce increasingly require contextual expertise from the outset.A healthcare manager, for instance, must understand patient experience, regulation and digital health ecosystem being developed under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission alongside conventional operations. Similarly, a fintech professional in India must understand how UPI's scale shapes product design, how RBI's digital lending regulations shape compliance, and how a single data breach can erode customer trust. As industries become more complex, employers increasingly value candidates who can combine sound management fundamentals with sector-specific expertise.A New Vision for Higher Education: From academic knowledge to lifelong capabilityYet specialisation must coexist with cross-disciplinary learning because contemporary business problems rarely respect functional boundaries. Management programmes must therefore develop both domain depth and cross-disciplinary thinking. Future managers need not become experts in every discipline, but they must be able to collaborate across fields and evaluate the commercial, social and regulatory implications of their decisions. This combination can provide aspirants with clearer pathways into emerging careers without reducing management education to narrow vocational training.Why entrepreneurship programmes have taken offThe rise of entrepreneurship education must be viewed within India’s changing policy and business environment. Two decades ago, starting a venture was often perceived as a risky alternative to established employment. The environment is markedly different today. Initiatives such as Make in India and Startup India have brought entrepreneurship, innovation and domestic enterprise to the centre of the national development agenda. The scale of this shift is evident: from around 500 DPIIT-recognised start-ups in 2016, India crossed 2 lakh by the end of 2025. Incubators, accelerators, seed-funding avenues, tax incentives and institutional networks have made the ecosystem more enabling for aspiring founders.India’s Youth Dividend: The missing link between demographics and governanceTechnology has simultaneously democratised entrepreneurship. Digital payments, online marketplaces, cloud-based tools and social media have lowered entry barriers that once favoured established companies. A young venture can now identify a niche audience, test an offering and reach prospective customers without investing heavily in mass-media promotion. Although building a successful venture remains difficult, and failure is an inescapable possibility, developing a scalable enterprise, or even aspiring to create a unicorn, no longer appears as far-fetched as it did earlier.Entrepreneurship programmes must therefore extend beyond writing business plans. Students need to practise customer discovery, test assumptions, build minimum viable products, evaluate unit economics and learn from unsuccessful experiments. This reflects the logic of effectuation: beginning with available means, testing possibilities and adapting as uncertainty unfolds. The resulting entrepreneurial mindset is valuable not only to founders but also to family businesses, social enterprises and established organisations seeking innovation.Experiential learning as an employability imperativeIndustry increasingly expects graduates to possess an application-oriented mindset, the ability to recognise which ideas are relevant, adapt theoretical frameworks and conceptual models to unfamiliar situations and implement solutions within real organisational constraints. Live projects, internships, simulations and field immersion expose students to the complete problem-solving process. Instead of responding to neatly defined case-study questions, they must identify the actual problem, gather evidence, engage with stakeholders and revise their recommendations when confronted with operational realities.For recruiters, this experiential learning has tangible value. Graduates with prior exposure to real business situations may require less time to understand workplace expectations, reducing recruitment uncertainty, search costs and initial training efforts. Furthermore, it provides a richer signal of a student’s analytical ability, communication and professional judgement than grades alone.However, such experiences must be integrated into academic coursework rather than treated merely as resume-building activities. Faculty guidance, industry feedback, and structured reflection are essential for converting experiences into learning.Preparing managers for an interconnected worldB-schools must consequently rethink what being “industry-ready” means. The external environment is changing quickly, while the emerging Gen Z workforce brings different expectations regarding flexibility, purpose, technology, learning and career progression. Management education must respond to both transformations: the changing nature of industry and the changing nature of the workforce entering it.Alumni can be invaluable partners in this evolution. Working across sectors and career stages, they can help institutions identify emerging skill requirements, review programme structures, mentor students, and create opportunities for live projects and industry immersion.The future-ready B-school will not choose between theory and practice, or between general management and specialisation. It will integrate them. Its purpose will be to develop graduates who possess domain knowledge, practical judgement, entrepreneurial initiative and the ability to keep learning in a volatile world. That is what will prepare students not merely for their first managerial role, but for careers that will repeatedly require them to adapt, innovate and lead.(The author, Madhu Mandal, works as an Associate Professor, XLRI Delhi-NCR)

title: 'I don't know what will happen 5 years from now': Nikhil Kamath on whether he would marry someday | Trending
description: Nikhil Kamath said he finds people who are uncertain about their beliefs appealing, arguing that excessive certainty can prevent people from changing minds.  | Trending
content: Nikhil Kamath, co-founder of Zerodha, recently shared his views on marriage and having children, saying he does not know whether he would want to get married someday, as he prefers to keep his options open rather than make long-term commitments.Speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2026, Kamath was asked whether his decision not to marry or have children was temporary or a lifelong choice. “Nobody knows what they want for life. Like, we were speaking to the Swamiji right now. I think he’s an incredibly articulate man. He spoke so well. I don’t know what I want six months from now, let alone five years from now. And I think that’s true for all people,” Kamath said.He added that he finds people who are uncertain about their beliefs appealing, arguing that excessive certainty can prevent people from changing their minds. “The people I find appealing are people who are not certain. I think certainty is a problem. Too much of the world is trying to figure out what they believe in and then get so emotionally attached to that belief, and almost egoistic about that belief, that they’re never willing to change their mind,” he said.Kamath said he hopes to continue questioning certainty for as long as possible, adding that he does not know what his life will look like five years from now. “For now, I’m kind of optimising for freedom and peace of mind, and living life in a manner where I have the time to pursue different things and just be open,” he said.(Also Read: Zerodha exec calls Nikhil Kamath 'better looking', Kamath brothers' hilarious X exchange goes viral)Nikhil Kamath on not wanting childrenKamath has previously spoken about his reluctance to have children, questioning whether he would want to spend nearly two decades raising a child in the hope that they would look after him in his old age.“I’m going to ruin 18-20 years of my life babysitting this child and then if luck serves me right, the reverse will happen at some point. What if he says ‘scr** you’ at 18 and leaves anyway,” he said in a podcast.He also questioned the idea that people are more significant than they think they are, saying, “I think we all feel that we are more important than we actually are. You are born, and you die like every other animal on the planet, and then you are gone, and nobody remembers anybody.”

title: A beautiful home can still feel uncomfortable: Designer shares 4 interior mistakes to avoid | Hindustan Times
description: Did you know your well-decorated home can still feel uncomfortable? Learn from a designer the mistakes you need to avoid.
content: When you return from a long day at work or a regular day out, your home becomes a sanctuary for rest and relaxation. What makes a home comfortable? Contrary to popular opinion, an aesthetically pleasing home can also be uncomfortable. So, comfort is much more than how a room is decorated.ALSO READ: Can your home make you happier? 5 decor tips to create a space you loveWhat does an expert have to say about what determines a comfortable home beyond aesthetics? Priyanka Sinha, founder of The Opulence Interior Design Studio, reminded us that the rule of thumb is to take into account how people move around and use a room.She added, "A beautiful house doesn't necessarily equal a comfortable house; whether it's the colours, the furniture or the decor, everything can look appealing, but comfort is a touch more subtle than this.”Here are some of the mistakes the designer flagged:1. Choosing looks over functionChoose furniture and decor that serve a practical purpose, aside from looking good.Leave enough space around large pieces, such as sofas, to move comfortably.Check whether furniture is comfortable to sit on and easy to use before buying it.Pick designs that suit daily lifestyle and everyday routines. 2. Ignoring proportion and scaleChoose furniture that suits the size of your room. Oversized pieces can make small rooms feel cluttered. Undersized pieces can leave large rooms looking incomplete.Consider how each piece fits alongside walls, doors, windows, and open areas for visual balance.Measure space and furniture before buying, allowing enough room to walk around comfortably. 3. Using too many colours and patternsChoose a consistent base colour palette to create a cohesive look.A more harmonised style can be achieved by establishing a unifying base palette and then adding personality with tactful accents.Earthy neutrals, natural textiles and well-chosen colour combinations can add richness without being too stimulating. 5. Forgetting the importance of empty spaceHomeowners can tend to want to fill every nook and cranny of their house with furniture, accessories and ornamental objects.Empty space is also a design element in a room and provides the eye with a break while providing room for major items to make an impact.Open spaces help with mobility and create an airy feel to rooms. Homeowners should sometimes wonder what can be taken out or moved rather than what can be added to a space. In the end, the designer reiterated the value of a home that prioritises functionality alongside aesthetics. A well-designed space should accommodate your daily routines, allow easy movement and make you feel at ease. After a home should also feel good as much as it looks good.What defines a good design? She added, “Good design is not about aesthetics alone; it is about achieving a space that is intuitive, harmonious, individual and lasting, and when we are conscious of proportion, space, function, light, colour and breath, then our homes will feel good for us and not just look good.”

title: Bengal: Three Christian families allege assault, threats to abandon faith; police deployed in area | Kolkata
description: Bengal: Three Christian families allege assault, threats to abandon faith; police deployed in area  | Kolkata News
content: Kolkata, Three Christian families in West Bengal's Paschim Medinipur district have complained to police that they were threatened and assaulted by a group of people earlier this week to force them to renounce their faith, prompting the force to deploy its personnel in the area.The aggrieved families, which have been residing in the area for the past 30 years and converted to Christianity around 18 months ago, have also complained to police that they were forced to participate in certain religious rituals against their wishes, a senior officer told PTI on Thursday.She said police have registered a case based on the complaints.Nine members of the families, residing in Chandrakona, have claimed in their police complaint that the group on October 18 and 19 assaulted and threatened them with dire consequences if they did not recant Christianity, the officer told PTI."A woman of one family reportedly lost consciousness after assault. A girl of another family was also allegedly assaulted and threatened. They were also allegedly forced to participate in religious rituals against their wishes, she said, citing the police complaints.The police officer said the accused group had allegedly warned the families not to approach police over the matter."A case has been initiated against people named by the families in their complaint. We are unable to disclose the names for the sake of our investigation," she said, adding that all nine members of the aggrieved families were escorted to the police station where they lodged the complaint."They have gone back home, and police personnel have been posted in their area to prevent any untoward incident. The situation is totally under control," the police officer said.She said police were probing whether the incident stemmed from a local dispute, an old family feud or any other reason. "We are probing all possible angles. We do not know which political affiliation the accused people belong to. We will come out with every possible detail after the investigation is over," she added.Several calls and messages by PTI to District Magistrate Bijin Krishna seeking his comments on the allegations have gone unanswered.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Almonds may help you fall asleep sooner: Study links daily consumption to better rest and sleep quality | Health
description: Adults who ate almonds daily in a study reported quicker sleep onset and longer sleep than those given a calorie-matched snack.  | Health
content: Sleepless nights are a common problem today as people deal with stress and busy schedules that can make it difficult to unwind. Many familiar hacks and tips circulate, from cutting back on caffeine to limiting screen time before bed. Let's see what else you can add to your sleep-aid list to strengthen your counter for sleepless nights.ALSO READ: How to tell if you are getting fitter: Expert shares 5 everyday signs, from better sleep to faster recoveryIs there anything special that you can add to your diet that specifically improves sleep? A study published in Frontiers in Nutrition in July 2026 took a closer look at whether eating almonds daily could help people fall asleep sooner and improve their overall sleep quality.Almonds may not come as a surprise, given their longstanding association with brain health. Many Indian mothers give their children almonds with milk in the belief that they support memory. But how may almonds help improve sleep? Can almonds improve your sleep?The findings highlighted the potential role of almonds in supporting sleep quality. The study had 175 adults aged 21-55 who participated. They reported poor sleep quality and received 60g of almonds or a calorie-matched control snack, like chidva, khakra, or cracker.Now, the group that received almonds reported falling asleep sooner and sleeping longer. The benefits are simple: you fall asleep quicker and don't wake up in the middle of the night as much, which means reduced random wakefulness. Why do almonds help you sleep better?Let's take a closer look at the nutrients in almonds that may help support sleep. Sheela Krishnaswamy, nutrition and wellness consultant, explained, “Almonds contain several nutrients that are biologically relevant to normal nervous system function and overall health, including magnesium and tryptophan. Magnesium is involved in normal nervous system and muscle function, while tryptophan is used by the body to produce serotonin and melatonin.”Alongside unsaturated fats and antioxidants, almonds also naturally contain small amounts of melatonin, a hormone that helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle.That said, eating almonds alone is not a foolproof plan for better sleep. They should be part of a broader sleep-friendly routine that includes limiting caffeine in the evening, creating a comfortable sleeping environment, and maintaining consistent bedtimes. Note to readers: This article is for informational purposes only and not a substitute for professional medical advice.

title: Ticket Rates: దయచేసి టికెట్ల రేట్లు పెంచకండి.. అదే ప్రభుత్వం చేసే మంచి.. ఇండస్ట్రీలో ఎవరూ నిజం చెప్పరు: నిర్మాత ధీరజ్ | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: Ticket Rates: టాలీవుడ్ లో ప్రతి పెద్ద సినిమాకు టికెట్ల రేట్లు పెంపు, సినిమా రిలీజ్ లు వాయిదా పడుతుండటంపై నిర్మాత ధీరజ్ మొగిలినేని సంచలన కామెంట్స్ చేశారు. దయచేసి టికెట్ల రేట్లు పెంచొద్దని, అలాగే పెద్ద సినిమాలు ఒకసారి అనౌన్స్ చేసి వాయిదా వేయొద్దని కోరారు.
content: Ticket Rates: తెలుగు సినిమాల ఇండస్ట్రీలో చిన్న నిర్మాతల గోడు ఎవరూ పట్టించుకోవడం లేదన్న విమర్శలు, ఆరోపణలు ఎప్పటి నుంచో ఉన్నవే. తాజాగా టికెట్ల రేట్ల పెంపు, సినిమా రిలీజ్ ల వాయిదాపై నిర్మాత ధీరజ్ మొగిలినేని చేసిన కామెంట్స్ సంచలనం రేపుతున్నాయి. టికెట్ రేట్లు పెంచకపోవడమే ఇండస్ట్రీకి ప్రభుత్వం చేసే మంచి అని ఆయన అనడం గమనార్హం.మీరు మాకు చేసే మంచి అదే..సమ్మర్ హాలిడేస్ మూవీ ప్రమోషన్లలో భాగంగా ఈ మూవీ నిర్మాత ధీరజ్ మీడియాతో మాట్లాడారు. ఈ సందర్భంగా పెద్ద సినిమాలకు టికెట్ల రేట్లు పెంచడంపై స్పందించారు.“దయచేసి టికెట్ల రేట్లు పెంచొద్దు. రాజమౌళిగారి వారణాసిలాంటి ఒకటో రెండో సినిమాలు అయితే ఓకే కానీ ప్రతి సినిమాకు పెంచొద్దు. దీనివల్ల మాలాంటి చిన్న సినిమాల వారికి తీవ్ర నష్టం కలుగుతోంది. ప్రతి థియేటర్ పెద్ద సినిమానే వేస్తున్నారు. టికెట్ల రేట్ల పెంపు వల్ల వాళ్లకు అందులో ఎక్కువ లాభం వస్తోంది. చిన్న సినిమాలు వేస్తే ఏం రాదంటూ వాళ్లు థియేటర్లు, షోలు ఇవ్వడం లేదు. అందుకే ప్రభుత్వం దయచేసి టికెట్ల రేట్లు పెంచొద్దు. దీనివల్ల ఎవ్వడికీ లాభం లేదు. మీరు ఇండస్ట్రీకి టికెట్ రేట్లు పెంచకపోవడమే చేసే అతిపెద్ద మంచి” అని ధీరజ్ అనడం గమనార్హం.4 రోజుల ముందు వచ్చినా చూస్తారు.. మరి మేమేం కావాలి?ఇక ఆదర్శ కుటుంబంలాంటి పెద్ద సినిమాల రిలీజ్ లు వాయిదా పడటంపై ధీరజ్ ఘాటు కామెంట్స్ చేశారు. ఇండస్ట్రీలో నిర్మాతల మధ్య కమ్యూనికేషన్ గ్యాప్ లేకపోయినా.. ఎవరూ నిజం చెప్పరని అనడం గమనార్హం."వెంకటేష్ గారు, త్రివిక్రమ్ గారి కాంబినేషన్ అంటే ఒక బ్రాండ్. 'ఆదర్శ కుటుంబం' లాంటి సినిమా విడుదల తేదీకి కేవలం 4 రోజుల ముందు ప్రమోషన్లు మొదలుపెట్టినా థియేటర్లకు జనాలు భారీగా వస్తారు. కానీ చిన్న సినిమాలకు ఆ సౌలభ్యం ఉండదు. మేము అక్టోబర్ 30 విడుదల కోసం పబ్లిసిటీకి, డిస్ట్రిబ్యూటర్లతో అగ్రిమెంట్లకు ఇప్పటికే లక్షల్లో ఖర్చు చేశాం" అని ధీరజ్ పేర్కొన్నారు."ఇప్పుడు హఠాత్తుగా ఆదర్శ కుటుంబం అక్టోబర్ 30కి రావడంతో, వేరే దారి లేక మా సమ్మర్ హాలిడేస్ సినిమాను నవంబర్ 6కి వాయిదా వేసుకోవాల్సి వచ్చింది. మళ్లీ నవంబర్ 6 కోసం ప్రమోషన్లు చేయాలంటే కొత్తగా వడ్డీలకు అప్పులు తెచ్చి ఖర్చు పెట్టాలి. పెద్ద సినిమాల రూ. 50 లక్షల హెచ్చుతగ్గులు పెద్దగా ప్రభావం చూపకపోవచ్చు కానీ, చిన్న నిర్మాతలకు ఇది ప్రాణసంకటంగా మారుతుంది" అని స్పష్టం చేశారు.తమిళ ఇండస్ట్రీ నుంచి నేర్చుకోవాలిఇటీవల తమిళ చిత్ర పరిశ్రమలో జరిగిన ఒక ఉదాహరణను ధీరజ్ ఈ సందర్భంగా గుర్తుచేశారు. "తమిళంలో ధనుష్ తన సినిమాను నెల్సన్-రజనీకాంత్ ల 'జైలర్ 2' కోసం వాయిదా వేసుకుంటూనే, సూర్య సినిమా ప్రొడ్యూసర్లు ముందే డేట్ ఫిక్స్ చేసుకున్నందున వారికీ ఇబ్బంది కలగని విధంగా సరికొత్త తేదీని ఎంచుకున్నారు. అక్కడ పెద్ద హీరోలు, నిర్మాతలు ఒకరినొకరు గౌరవించుకుంటున్నారు" అని విశ్లేషించారు."టాలీవుడ్‌లో పెద్ద నిర్మాతలు కేవలం ఇతర పెద్ద సినిమాల మేకర్స్‌తో మాత్రమే కమ్యూనికేట్ అవుతున్నారు. చిన్న సినిమాల నిర్మాతల షెడ్యూళ్లను, వారి కష్టాలను అసలు పరిగణనలోకి తీసుకోకపోవడం వల్ల తీవ్రమైన కమ్యూనికేషన్ గ్యాప్ ఏర్పడుతోంది" అని ఆవేదన వ్యక్తం చేశారు.పరిశ్రమకు ఇది ఆరోగ్యకరం కాదుగతంలో కూడా 'లెనిన్' వంటి పలు చిత్రాల సమయంలో సరైన కమ్యూనికేషన్ లేకపోవడం వల్ల చిన్న నిర్మాతలు ఇబ్బంది పడ్డారు. గతంలో కింగ్ నాగార్జున కూడా బహిరంగంగానే పెద్ద సినిమాల మేకర్స్‌కు హితవు పలికారు."సినిమాలను సరైన సమయానికి పూర్తి చేసి పక్కా ప్లానింగ్‌తో రావాలి తప్ప, వాయిదాల పేరిట పరిశ్రమను ఇబ్బంది పెట్టకూడదు" అని సూచించారు.ఇలాంటి పరిస్థితులు ఇలాగే కొనసాగితే తెలుగు చిత్ర పరిశ్రమలో ఆరోగ్యకరమైన వాతావరణం దెబ్బతినడమే కాకుండా, బాక్సాఫీస్ కలెక్షన్లపై కూడా తీవ్ర ప్రతికూల ప్రభావం పడుతుందని సినీ విశ్లేషకులు భావిస్తున్నారు. పెద్ద నిర్మాతలు చిన్న సినిమాలను కూడా ఆదుకునేలా రీలీజ్ క్యాలెండర్ నిర్వహించాల్సిన అవసరం ఎంతైనా ఉంది.

title: SRFTI students allege denial of basic facilities amid ongoing protest | Kolkata
description: SRFTI students allege denial of basic facilities amid ongoing protest  | Kolkata News
content: Kolkata, SRFTI students, who are continuing their indefinite sit-in protest on campus despite being asked to vacate the premises, on Thursday alleged that the administration denied them access to basic facilities to stop their agitation.In a message issued on the occasion of Bijoya Dashami on Wednesday, the students said the institute mess had remained closed since October 17, while access to the gym, music room and New CRT, where students watch films, had also been "restricted by the administration".The students alleged that the "institute administration was resorting to measures that amounted to collective punishment by denying them access to basic facilities amid the ongoing agitation".The allegations come amid a prolonged standoff between students and the institute administration following a series of violent incidents on the campus.In a notice issued on October 16, the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute suspended regular academic activities in its Film and Electronic and Digital Marketing departments until November 13 and asked students to leave their hostels and vacate the premises within 24 hours.Refusing to leave, the students said they were continuing their indefinite sit-in protest and academic boycott, which had entered its 25th day, over concerns about campus security and accountability.The allegations come amid an extended standoff between students and the institute administration following a series of violent incidents on the campus.The agitation began after clashes on September 27 during an event organised by the Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat , which the students described as an RSS-linked organisation.The students subsequently sought written assurances on campus security, action against those allegedly involved in the violence and an independent investigation into the incidents.Tensions escalated further following another incident on October 4, when students alleged that stones, bricks and bottles were thrown towards the campus.The protesters later intensified their agitation, demanding accountability, withdrawal of disciplinary notices issued to protesting students and the resignation of Vice-Chancellor Santosh Ajmera.They have also alleged that the administration's response to the protest has compounded their difficulties, particularly over accommodation and access to essential facilities.The students have maintained that their agitation would continue until their concerns over safety, accountability and the administration's handling of the situation were addressed.An SRFTI official, however, alleged that a section of the protesting students had overstayed in the hostel for years despite the expiry of their terms and were "the troublemakers and instigating and preventing junior students from attending academic session since September 28".The official said six students were suspended on October 15 on disciplinary grounds over allegations ranging from attacks on faculty members and campus security personnel to writing obscene graffiti on campus walls.Sudip Chakraborty, spokesperson for the SRFTI students' union, denied the allegations and said the students would take legal action in response to the charges.He added that around 150 students, many of them from outside West Bengal, lived on the campus and in nearby areas, and warned that "any revengeful action by the institute authorities will inconvenience them".Chakraborty further alleged that the administration had prevented students participating in the sit-in from using a nearby washroom in the academic building, describing the move as a "basic denial of rights"."This had never happened before even during Covid by closing down our facilities," he claimed.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Document listing 200 trees for felling in Noida raises concerns | Hindustan Times
description: Divisional forest officer Rajni Kant said a request for tree felling was received in connection with a project
content: A forest department document listing 200 trees for felling and another 331 for transplantation at Noida’s Sector 91 Biodiversity Park reportedly linked to a proposed deer park has raised questions over the environmental safeguards being followed during development work in an existing green space.The move has brought the management of the city’s green spaces under scrutiny when Noida is grappling with deteriorating air quality ahead of winter. It has prompted questions about the need to remove established trees within a biodiversity park and the measures being taken to minimise ecological damage.The document contains species-wise details and measurements of trees covered under the felling and transplantation exercise.Forest department officials said that the department had granted permission for tree felling but was examining allegations that the work may have exceeded the approved limits.Divisional forest officer Rajni Kant said a request for tree felling was received in connection with a government project, and the department issued the necessary permissions. “Following a complaint alleging that some trees may have been felled beyond the scope of the permission granted, we are getting the matter investigated. If any violation is found, action will be taken as per the rules.”The deteriorating air quality ahead of winter has brought renewed attention to the protection of urban green spaces. Tree transplantation is among the measures used to retain vegetation during development. The survival of transplanted trees depends on the method used, subsequent maintenance and monitoring.Environmental activist Vikrant Tongad is among those who have raised concerns over the tree felling and sought clarity from the forest and horticulture departments on the permissions granted for the work and the measures being taken to safeguard the existing green cover. He said the authorities should make details of the proposed work and the steps being taken to protect the park’s trees public.“The authorities need to make the details of the project and the permissions obtained for tree felling public. When Noida is struggling with air pollution, the removal of trees from an established green space raises environmental concerns,” Tongad said.Tongad said he contacted forest department and horticulture department to seek information about the work. He added that a formal complaint was being prepared for submission.

title: Keerthy Suresh, Radhika Apte, Rana Daggubati, Huma Qureshi and Vetrimaaran: IFP announces its celeb lineup for Season 16 | Bollywood
description: Actors, filmmakers, writers and artists from across the country will come together for the 16th edition of IFP, scheduled for October 24 and 25 in Mumbai.  | Bollywood
content: Actors, filmmakers, writers and artists from across the country will come together for the 16th edition of IFP, scheduled for October 24 and 25 at Mehboob Studios in Mumbai. This year's line-up includes Keerthy Suresh, Radhika Apte, Rana Daggubati, Mrunal Thakur, Sobhita Dhulipala, Huma Qureshi, Nithya Menen and Pratik Gandhi, alongside National Award-winning filmmaker Vetrimaaran and several other names from the creative industries. Spread across two days, the festival will feature conversations, masterclasses and workshops covering cinema, streaming, writing, music, advertising and digital storytelling.Vetrimaaran, Rana Daggubati and Huma Qureshi to discuss their journeysFilmmaker Vetrimaaran will talk about his approach to cinema and the process of making films in a session titled Making of a Modern Auteur. Rana Daggubati will look beyond his work as an actor and discuss his efforts to support new talent in More Than a Star: On Nurturing the New Wave.Huma Qureshi will revisit the roles and career decisions that have shaped her as a performer in Many Lives of Huma Qureshi. Mrunal Thakur will also look back at her journey from television to Hindi and Telugu cinema in Making Her Mark, while Sobhita Dhulipala is among the actors set to feature at the festival.Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte will share the stage for On Playing Power Ft. AKKA. The conversation will focus on their characters in the upcoming Netflix series Akka and what it takes to portray women who hold power. Nithya Menen will discuss her approach to acting in Becoming Kanmani.Pratik Gandhi will explore the work that goes into building a character in The Actor at Work with Ratna Pathak Shah. Filmmaker Sujoy Ghosh will join another discussion, Subverting Expectations in Cinema, about finding new ways to tell stories instead of relying on familiar formulas. Juhi Chaturvedi, Varun Grover and Sonam Wangchuk among other speakersThe programme extends beyond films and acting, with sessions dedicated to writing, literature, sustainability, advertising and the impact of technology on art. Screenwriters Juhi Chaturvedi and Varun Grover will discuss their creative processes and writing across different formats in On Craft, Creativity & Writing Across Mediums.Sooni Taraporevala will appear on Anurag Minus Verma Podcast Live, while Satyanshu Singh will lead a session titled Killing Your Darlings. Craig Mazin, the acclaimed screenwriter, will take questions from audiences through a virtual AMA.Sonam Wangchuk will discuss practical ideas around sustainable living in How To Live Simply. Artist Raghava KK will examine how artificial intelligence and algorithms are changing creative work in Art After The Algorithm & AI. Actor Shefali Shah will join Saurabh Dwivedi for Pustakalay Ft. The Audacity of Being.Advertising filmmakers Prakash Varma and Amit Sharma will come together for What Makes a Good Ad? Other sessions will look at independent music, improvisation, photography, design and digital storytelling, making the festival a meeting point for people working across different creative fields.Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte share their excitement about AkkaSpeaking about IFP Season 16 and her upcoming Netflix and YRF series Akka, Keerthy Suresh shared, “What I love about IFP is that it brings together people who are genuinely passionate about storytelling, regardless of where they are in their creative journey. It's a space where new ideas, fresh voices and different forms of creativity come together under one roof. As someone who has grown through constantly exploring new characters and stories, I find that spirit of experimentation incredibly inspiring. I'm excited to be part of IFP 2026, connect with fellow creators and audiences, and have conversations about storytelling, craft, the evolving ways in which we tell stories today and talk about my upcoming series, Netflix and YRF’s - Akka.”Radhika Apte also spoke about what makes the festival special to her, linking its emphasis on creative exchange to her work on Akka. She said, "IFP has built a wonderful community of creators, storytellers and artists who are constantly pushing themselves to think differently and create fearlessly. What makes it special is the energy of people coming together to share ideas, challenge conventions and learn from one another. I've always believed that creativity thrives when diverse perspectives meet, and IFP is a great example of that. With Akka, my upcoming series with Netflix and Yash Raj Films, I've had the opportunity to be part of a distinctive story and a world shaped by compelling characters and complex dynamics. I'm looking forward to being part of IFP 2026, engaging with emerging talent and exchanging ideas on storytelling and performance." Huma Qureshi and Pratik Gandhi on the value of creative exchangeFor Huma Qureshi, IFP offers an opportunity to connect with fellow artists and encourage people who are just starting out. Sharing her thoughts on the upcoming edition, she said, “IFP has always felt like a space that celebrates creativity in its most honest and exciting form. What I love about the festival is the energy it creates around storytelling and the opportunity it gives artists to come together, exchange ideas and inspire one another. As someone who has constantly explored different forms of storytelling through acting, writing and production, I truly value spaces that encourage experimentation and new voices. I’m really looking forward to being part of IFP, meeting young and emerging creators, and having meaningful conversations around the creative process, cinema and the many possibilities that storytelling can open up.”Pratik Gandhi described the festival as a place where artists and audiences can engage with different forms of creative expression. He shared, “IFP represents an essential cultural intersection where diverse forms of storytelling, performance, and creative practice meet. Its strength lies in convening artists and audiences from varied backgrounds to spark discovery, exchange, and dialogue.” IFP Season 16: Dates, venue and scheduleIFP began in 2011 as a 50-hour filmmaking challenge. Since then, it has grown into a platform that brings together creators from different parts of the world and across a range of disciplines. Its 16th edition continues that approach, with a programme spanning films, streaming, writing, music, advertising and the arts.The festival will be held on October 24 and 25, 2026, at Mehboob Studios in Mumbai.

title: First NBA Store in India to Open in 2027 Through Expanded Merchandising Partnership With Suditi | Hindustan Times
description: The expanded collaboration will bring the NBA’s first physical store to India in 2027 and broaden the country’s official fanwear selection.
content: Mumbai, Maharashtra, IndiaSuditi Will Operate NBAStore.in, the League’s Official Online Store in IndiaSuditi Launches Widest Assortment of Officially Licensed NBA Fanwear Ever in the CountryThe National Basketball Association (NBA) and Suditi Sports Apparel Ltd. (Suditi), a long-time leader in apparel exports, today announced a multiyear expansion of their longstanding merchandising collaboration in India that will see Suditi open the first NBA Store in the country, operate the league’s official local online store at NBAStore.in, and launch the widest assortment of officially licensed NBA fanwear ever in the market.The first NBA Store in India will open in 2027 and mark the league’s first-ever physical retail location in the country. Additional details, including the store’s location, will be announced at a later date.Beginning this month, Suditi will begin operating NBAStore.in, providing fans across India with access to a comprehensive selection of official NBA merchandise, including current and former player jerseys, apparel, headwear, performance and casual footwear, basketballs, accessories, and more from major brands such as Nike, New Era, Mitchell & Ness, Wilson and NBA Fanwear by Suditi.As part of the expanded fanwear collection, Suditi will introduce casual shirts and lifestyle footwear to its offering that already includes t-shirts, jackets, sweatshirts, pants, headwear, accessories and more. The entire collection will be available at NBAStore.in, Suditi’s direct-to-consumer platform ShopTheArena.com, and select online and in-person retail channels across the country.“Extending our longstanding relationship with Suditi marks a meaningful step in accelerating the NBA’s retail growth in India,” said NBA Head of India Sunny Malik. “Together, we are making it easier than ever for fans to represent their favorite teams and players through the most comprehensive selection of official NBA merchandise across NBAStore.in and Suditi’s physical and online stores, alongside the historic opening of the first NBA Store in the country next year.”“Eight years ago, we began working with the NBA to bring officially licensed fanwear to India, and the business has grown significantly since,” said Tanuj Agarwal, Co-founder of Suditi Sports Apparel Ltd. “We are excited to now extend our merchandising partnership by operating NBAStore.in and launching the first NBA Store in India. With an assortment of leading brands offering official NBA merchandise, we are making it easier than ever for fans to connect with the game of basketball.”The 2026-27 NBA season is airing live in India on Prime Video and NBA League Pass, the league’s premium live game subscription service available via the NBA App. Fans in India can follow the NBA on Facebook (Facebook.com/NBAIndia), Instagram (@NBAIndia) and, for everything style related, (@NBAStyle_in) and X (@NBAIndia), and download the NBA App for the latest news, updates, scores, stats, schedules, videos and more.About the NBAThe National Basketball Association (NBA) is a global sports and media organization with the mission to inspire and connect people everywhere through the power of basketball. Built around five professional sports leagues: the NBA, WNBA, NBA G League, NBA 2K League and Basketball Africa League, the NBA has established a major international presence with games and programming available in 214 countries and territories in more than 50 languages, and merchandise for sale in more than 200 countries and territories on all seven continents. NBA rosters at the start of the 2026-27 season featured 125 international players from a record-tying 43 countries across six continents. The NBA’s digital assets include NBA TV, NBA.com, the NBA App and NBA League Pass. The NBA has created one of the largest social media communities in the world, with more than 2.5 billion likes and followers globally across all leagues, team and player platforms. The NBA’s Tap to Watch provides seamless access to local, national and global live game telecasts via the NBA App, NBA.com, third-party digital platforms and NBA partner platforms. NBA Cares, the NBA’s global social impact platform, drives change on issues facing fans and communities in the areas of health and wellness, civic engagement, social justice and inclusion, and sustainability.About SuditiSuditi Sports Apparel Ltd is a sports merchandise company engaged in the business of manufacturing, marketing and distribution of licensed sports apparel in India. It has partnerships with leading sports brands including the NBA and premier international football clubs and distributes its products across all leading e-commerce channels and over 500 offline point of sales.Media Contact DetailsJandric Lim, NBA Asia, jlim@nba.com, +63 939 904 6805Note to readers: This article is part of HT's paid consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. HT assumes no editorial responsibility for the content, including its accuracy, completeness, or any errors or omissions. Readers are advised to verify all information independently.

title: Allu Arjun reviews Jailer 2, says the film is a true showcase of the aura of Rajinikanth: ‘Only he can hit  ₹500 crore without getting his shirt torn’ | Hindustan Times
description: Rajinikanth-starrer Jailer 2 has emerged as a blockbuster within its first week of release. The film crossed  ₹575 crore worldwide.
content: Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 is a sensation at the box office. The Tamil film was released in theatres last week, and has since crossed the ₹300 crore mark at the Indian box office in its first week. Released in theatres on October 15, the sequel has become the highest-grossing Tamil film of 2026 so far and has also surpassed several major releases from the past two years. Actor Allu Arjun saw the film recently and took to his X account to share his review of the Nelson Dilipkumar directorial.Allu Arjun's review of Jailer 2In his new post, Arjun wrote, “#Jailer2 is (fire emoticons) A true showcase of @rajinikanth sir’s star power, swag & aura! A Commercial Entertainer that keeps the adrenaline pumping!”He went on to shower particular praise for music composer Anirudh Ravichander and wrote, “Brother… @anirudhofficial KILLED IT! All the artists, technicians & the producer have poured their hearts into this film. The Showman @Nelsondilpkumar garu delivers the coolest hit with a BANG!”“Only Rajinikanth can hit 500 crore+ without getting his shirt torn,” he concluded in Telugu, and congratulated the entire team of Sun Pictures. Jailer 2 managed to pull a net domestic collection of ₹317.20 crore in India, and ₹205 crore from overseas. It brings the worldwide gross of the sequel to ₹576.45 crore before the end of its first week in theatres. It has now surpassed the 20-day haul of Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam: The Conclusion, which has brought in ₹560 crore so far, making it the second-highest-grossing Indian film of 2026.About Jailer 2Jailer 2 is directed by Nelson and produced by Kalanithi Maran of Sun Pictures. Anirudh Ravichander, who’s soon to marry Kalanithi’s daughter, Kavya Maran, composed the music. Rajinikanth reprised his role as retired jailer Tiger Muthuvel Pandian with Ramya Krishnan, Mirnaa and Rithvik joining him. SJ Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu and Vidya Balan make up the new cast. Picking up from the first part, Jailer 2 sees retired jailer Tiger Muthuvel Pandian facing off against new foes from the idol-smuggling network. He is also trying to protect his family not just from new enemies, but from the reality about the death of his son in the first part. Jailer 2 received favourable reviews from critics and the audience alike.

title: Battlefield of the future: How AI is transforming warfare | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Gaurav Mehndiratta and Himanshu Suryavanshi.
content: Warfare has long been shaped by technologies that shorten the interval between observation and action. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is curtailing that interval further, but their significance depends as much on trustworthy data, joint institutions and domestic industry as on algorithms.The progression from industrial-age mass to precision weapons and network-centric battlefield has made information central to military advantage. AI adds the capacity to examine large volumes of information and flag patterns for human assessment. There are primarily three ways AI changes the character of war. First, it elevates the status of data from just a source of information to an instrument of power. Secondly, it changes the economics of mass, by giving an edge to the one who can field larger number of AI-assisted systems at a relatively cheaper cost. Lastly, it relocates the role of humans from analysing data to taking decisions.This transformation is best understood through the OODA loop: Observe, Orient, Decide and Act. AI can accelerate observation through sensor fusion, assist orientation through pattern recognition, support decision-making through predictive analytics and enable faster action through automated and integrated systems. The objective is not replacing military judgement but delivering reliable and timely decision advantage.At the strategic level, AI is reshaping cyber security, protection of critical infrastructure and national industrial capacity. The experience of Ukraine has demonstrated that cyber-attacks, information campaigns and kinetic operations increasingly occur simultaneously. Countries, therefore, require resilient data networks, secure digital infrastructure and robust cyber-defence capabilities.At the operational level, AI is transforming command and control (C2). Advanced decision-support systems can integrate inputs from land, air, maritime, cyber and space domains into a common operational picture (COP). For India, this aligns closely with ongoing reforms focused on jointness, integrated theatre commands and multi-domain exercises.At the tactical level, autonomous and semi-autonomous systems are changing battlefield dynamics. Drone swarms, loitering munitions and AI-enabled reconnaissance systems are increasing the speed and scale at which military forces can operate. The growing use of autonomous capabilities in Ukraine illustrates how AI is increasingly embedded across the sensor-to-shooter kill chain.For four days in May, last year, India was engaged in a conflict that looked a lot different from the ones that it had trained for and fought earlier. The Indian Army’s Akashteer, a fully indigenous, automated Air Defence Control and Reporting System, played a significant role in Operation Sindoor. As per a press release by the ministry of information & broadcasting, Akashteer had intercepted and neutralised every inbound projectile, and successfully defended the Indian airspace on May 9 and 10.Operation Sindoor offered a glimpse of the battlefield capabilities that India’s defence ecosystem must now aspire to build at scale. It also sharpened the questions the nation has long posed to its defence establishment about preparedness, integration, technological self-reliance, and future warfighting readiness: Are we building the ability to understand and adapt with evolving battlefield? Are we building at the pace, and in the shape that matches tomorrow’s battlefield demands?The answer, as evident in the last couple of years, is encouraging but incomplete.AI-related projects are being developed through DRDO, DPSUs, startups and private industry. In 2022, the launch of 75 AI-enabled defence products at India’s first AI in Defence symposium highlighted the breadth of ongoing efforts across surveillance, logistics, cybersecurity, and autonomous systems. The IndiaAI Mission has since invested ₹10,372 crore on affordable compute and a startup ecosystem. Additionally, the AIKosh data repository held more than 7,500 datasets and 273 models as of February 2026.In line with their vision of technological advancement by enhancing operational readiness, Indian armed forces have also established research centres specifically focusing on the development of AI for their use cases. The IAF Centre of Excellence for Artificial Intelligence under the aegis of UDAAN (Unit for Digitisation, Automation, Artificial Intelligence and Application Networking) was inaugurated in 2022. This was followed by the establishment of the Indian Navy Incubation Centre for Artificial Intelligence (INICAI) and the Indian Army AI Incubation Centre (IAAIIC), supported through collaboration with the broader defence technology ecosystem.In a battlefield, outcomes are increasingly being decided by algorithms and not just armour. It becomes even more pertinent for an Agrasar Bharat to make the right move across AI, indigenous manufacturing and procurement reforms parallelly.The rise of AI poses unforeseen risks. Military AI systems can inherit data biases, generate incorrect outputs, be vulnerable to cyber compromise and may have questionable accountability. Furthermore, diversification of data sources becomes imperative to minimise the injection of stale or error-infected data and increase reliability. The challenge for policymakers is to establish governance frameworks that encourage innovation while ensuring transparency, human supervision and compliance with international and domestic law.The future battlefield will reward countries capable of combining technological innovation, industrial resilience, military integration and strategic vision.For India, success will depend on building sovereign AI capabilities that support defence modernisation, strengthen indigenous manufacturing and preserve strategic autonomy. Seamless AI-integration into the defence ecosystem from data collection to delivering results will play a pivotal role. Therefore, military AI stack needs to be formalised for interoperability within the defence ecosystem.Military AI is at a relatively nascent stage of development across the globe. Successful establishment of a definitive or uncontested model for AI-powered warfare is still under progress. Major powers are testing the evolving technologies, operational concepts and governance frameworks. For India, this offers a unique window of opportunity to embed military AI factors into capability building, acquisition processes, and strategic doctrine from the outset. The objective is not merely to adopt AI, but to shape its use in a manner consistent with India’s security requirements and long-term national interests.Traditional measures of military power need to increasingly be complemented by new determinants of advantage: The ability to adapt rapidly, deploy affordable mass, operate effectively across multiple domains and integrate unmanned systems, AI, electronic warfare and space-enabled capabilities into a unified operational architecture.India does not lack intent, ambition, capital or talent for this shift. What it most definitely needs is sustained investment in the research and development of military AI; synchronisation between the armed forces that operate these systems, the research laboratories and manufacturers that build them, and the acquisition machinery that must procure them at the speed of relevance.That coordination is Agrasar Bharat’s need of the hour.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Gaurav Mehndiratta, partner and leader, Aerospace and Defence, and Himanshu Suryavanshi, associate partner, Aerospace, Defence, Shipbuilding & Space, KPMG, India.

title: Man conned of  ₹2.5 lakh in marriage scam in Beed district; new bride turns out to be minor | Mumbai news
description: Man conned of  ₹2.5 lakh in marriage scam in Beed district; new bride turns out to be minor  | Mumbai news
content: Beed, Police in Maharashtra's Beed district have launched an investigation after a man claimed he was cheated of ₹2.5 lakh in a matrimonial fraud, discovering his newly-wedded wife was actually a minor.The marriage crumbled within just two days when the bride revealed the entire alliance was a racket orchestrated to extort money and steal valuables, police said on Thursday.Acting on a complaint filed by the aggrieved man, a resident of Georai town in the central Maharashtra district, police initiated a probe and discovered the bride was actually a minor whose identity documents had been forged.The groom's family had contacted matchmakers based in Jafrabad town in Jalna district. On June 22, the young man's father shared his son's photograph and biodata via WhatsApp. The intermediaries subsequently shared a young woman's photograph and asked the family to meet in Jafrabad, police said.On October 1, the man and his parents travelled to Jafrabad to meet the prospective bride. During the meeting, the middlemen demanded ₹2.5 lakh to finalize the match. Desperate to arrange the wedding, the groom's family agreed to the demand, they said.On the evening of October 5, the bride's entourage arrived in Georai by car. As per the agreement, the groom's family transferred ₹25,000 each digitally to two designated mobile numbers and handed over the remaining ₹2 lakh in cash. A priest was summoned to solemnize the wedding rituals, following which the middlemen departed, leaving the bride behind, according to police."However, within 48 hours of the wedding, the bride began insisting on returning to her parental home. When the family assured her they would visit around Dussehra, she reportedly confessed the marriage was a sham orchestrated solely to siphon off cash and gold ornaments. When the groom contacted the intermediaries demanding an explanation, they dodged his calls and offered evasive replies," they said.The matter escalated to police, and on October 19, the girl recorded her statement. Investigations revealed that while a forged Aadhaar card reflected her age as 20 years, she was, in fact, a minor.In her statement, the girl claimed she had been brought to Georai without prior intimation and forcibly married off, alleging she had been duped as well, police said.Police promptly produced her before the Child Welfare Committee .Kishor Pawar, Inspector at the Georai Police Station, said, "We have received the complaint. Since the bride is a minor, appropriate legal procedure was followed and she has been shifted to a juvenile shelter home. A thorough probe into the racket was on."This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Marco Rubio’s visit: Catalyst for a new era of diplomacy | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Gouri Sankar Nag and Arpan Bhattacharya.
content: US secretary of State, Marco Rubio’s visit to India by passing Delhi has generated a distinct buzz within diplomatic circle in the subcontinent. His visit, this time the second one in last six months, seems quite focused based on intensive close door planning before resuming Iran strikes after the mid-term election in early November. The trip being one-of-a-kind is defined by its route to Jamnagar, the site of the Reliance refinery complex. The signal of urgency is conspicuous as Washington fast-tracks its approach to deal with India less as a capital to be courted and more as a set of economic assets. Needless to say, Delhi’s prompt appreciation of the change of format reflects how deeply it wanted the visit to succeed. The timing of the visit is significant. The US is trapped in the Iran conundrum., the conflict that moved into an uneasy lull leaving the home front in shambles where the adverse pressure renders politics murkier. The midterm elections on November 3 make it a fraught scenario for the Republicans facing a tough challenge before the campaign begins for the 2028 presidential race. The Iran episode produced no clear victory while fuel price hike remains a hot-button issue with voters. Before polling day, cheap and steady fuel is worth more to the administration than another confrontation. This is why Jamnagar matters. Its twin refineries process about 1.4 million barrels a day, the largest single-site operation in the world, and were built to handle the heavy, high-sulphur crude that most American refineries cannot. Since US forces seized Nicolás Maduro in January, Washington has controlled Venezuela’s oil industry and has been marketing its output abroad. Reliance is now the largest buyer of Venezuelan crude, and Rubio said openly in Mumbai that he would ask the company to refine more of it. With the Strait of Hormuz disrupted and Red Sea shipping obstructed, Jamnagar could emerge as a saviour to reduce American dependence on the Gulf. The Russian oil question shows the bargain more clearly. Just before Rubio left, President Trump took no time to pause the punitive tariffs on buyers of Russian oil authorised under the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a measure that would have hit India hard. Rubio conceded that India can’t and need not give up Russian oil overnight, and Washington has itself agreed to buy Russian diesel. New Delhi welcomed the pause as relief. Read the dates. A 60-day window from mid-October closes in mid-December, after the midterms. India keeps buying Russian crude at Washington’s discretion, and the price of that discretion is to take more American and Venezuelan oil and to close the trade deal Rubio describes as all but signed.The larger change is what can precisely be designated as diplomatic decentering. Hitherto the familiar model ran from capital to capital, through foreign ministries, joint statements and summits. Rubio’s itinerary followed refineries and boardrooms. Multilateral diplomacy continues, but private capital now sits inside it as a participant. The effect was pacifying for both sides. For India the gains are real even though several risks are discernible. The first is strategic. The second is political. Venezuelan oil flows from an American takeover of another country’s resources, and buying it is not a neutral commercial act for a country that has long defended sovereignty in the Global South. Closer energy alignment with Washington while the Iran conflict is unresolved also narrows India’s room with Tehran, including one on Chabahar.The third risk is the one least discussed. Jamnagar sits on the Gulf of Kutch beside India’s first Marine National Park. Heavier, sulphur-rich crude means more sulphur to strip out, more emissions, and more tanker traffic in fragile coastal waters. A single site that carries so much of India’s refining, and now part of American energy planning, can also turn into a single point of failure: a fire, a cyclone or a prolonged labour dispute there might ripple through two economies at once. Rubio’s visit can prove a turning point for India, but only if New Delhi sets the terms. It should take the investment and the energy, insist that serious diplomacy keeps its address in the capital, press for the sanctions pause to become durable rather than a temporary relief, and write environmental conditions into any expansion at Jamnagar. (The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Gouri Sankar Nag, professor & head, Department of Political Science, S-K-B University and Arpan Bhattacharya, assistant professor, Department of Political Science, Ramananda College, Bishnupur, West Bengal.
