title: Sai Pallavi says Ramayana co-star Ranbir Kapoor keeps himself updated on Tamil films; asked about Vijay Sethupathi's Maharaja, Baththa | Hindustan Times
description: At an event for Ramayana held in Chennai, Sai Pallavi revealed just how fond her co-star Ranbir Kapoor was of South Indian cinema.
content: The team of Ramayana was in Chennai on Wednesday evening for the audio launch of the Nitesh Tiwari film. The film’s leads, Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash, were present at the event where AR Rahman's songs were launched. Sai spoke about her co-star Ranbir’s fondness for Tamil films when she took to the stage, revealing how he discussed Vijay Sethupathi’s films with her.(Also Read: National Award-winning VFX expert Arun Kumar says criticism around Ramayana, Jailer 2 visuals based on growing confusion on CGI vs AI | HT Exclusive)Sai Pallavi says Ranbir Kapoor fond of South cinemaSai spoke about the film’s team when she took to the stage at the Ramayana event. Talking about Ranbir, she said, “Now, I’m going to speak about dear Ram. Every time he has met me, I've noticed I wouldn’t have watched a Tamil movie released that week or month. But he has updated himself, and he’ll ask me about it. He has watched Amaran, and we have discussed it. But even Maharaja or Baththa, he has stayed updated.”The actor also stated that Ranbir loves South Indian cinema, adding, “He makes it a point to watch it and pass his appreciation in some or the other form. Which, I think, is so kind. You don’t have to do that. But it’s so nice that you do that. It’s like he has a library for them in his mind.” Sai then spoke about Ranbir playing Ram, “We have seen him in Animal, Barfi and other films. Ram is a restrained and restricted character. He’s got some sort of inner peace in him that just radiates through his eyes. I am very happy, excited that I got to see you perform like that.” Sai also said at the event that she was a massive fan of Rahman, adding that his songs have been part of her childhood and have become the background score of her life. She also spoke about Yash and said that she has noticed Tamilians cheering for him, be it for KGF or Toxic, as if he had made a film in their language. She stated that they might be from different languages, but are bound by craft. About RamayanaRamayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. The film, based on Valmiki’s Ramayana, stars Ranbir as Ram, Sai as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Ravi Dubey, Sunny Deol, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan and Lara Dutt also star in it. The first part of Ramayana is releasing on November 5, while the second part will be released in 2027.

title: Osteoporosis in women: Doctors reveal how much calcium and vitamin D you really need | Health
description: Osteoporosis can develop without obvious symptoms and make bones more prone to fractures, particularly after menopause. Here's what experts suggest.   | Health
content: Osteoporosis means your bones are weak and fragile, making them more susceptible to fractures. It can be particularly common in women following menopause as estrogen levels fall and bone loss speeds up. Although you can't always avoid the effects of ageing and hormones, we can all help our bones by getting enough calcium and vitamin D and keeping active.Also Read | Hemato-oncologist warns untreated sleep apnea could be putting your liver at risk; suggests signs to look out for and treatmentIn an interview with HT Lifestyle, Dr Lalit Modi, director of orthopaedics and joint replacement at CK Birla Hospitals, Jaipur, and Dr Rakesh Rajput, director and HOD of orthopaedics at CK Birla Hospitals, CMRI Kolkata, explained why osteoporosis affects women more and how much calcium and vitamin D they really need.According to Dr Lalit, for women, attention should be paid not only to fracture prevention but also to the early detection of bone loss and its treatment. Dr Rakesh noted that for many women, the consequences may not be obvious until much later, as osteoporosis can develop without noticeable symptoms. “Calcium and vitamin D are important throughout life, but taking supplements without understanding how much the body needs is not the answer,” he added. Here's what both experts suggest:Calcium: building and maintaining strong bonesCalcium is the primary mineral for bone health, both Dr Lalit and Dr Rakesh stressed. “As a general rule, the amount of calcium that adult women need per day is around 1000 mg and increases to about 1200 mg for women over 50 years of age. But it can differ under specific conditions and in local clinical practice,” Dr Lalit specified.Whenever possible, calcium should be obtained through the diet, Dr Lalit stressed, recommending foods like milk, curd, paneer, and other calcium-rich foods. For women who avoid dairy, Dr Rakesh recommended including ragi, calcium-set tofu, sesame seeds, certain leafy greens, and calcium-fortified foods.“If required, additional calcium can be given as a supplement, although excess calcium intake beyond recommended levels does not necessarily prevent fractures,” Dr Lalit cautioned. Dr Rakesh warned that excessive supplementation can cause problems, such as kidney stones in some people; therefore, a doctor should help you figure out whether you need supplements and how much.Vitamin D: helping the body absorb calciumFor vitamin D, Dr Rakesh stressed that the commonly used recommendations for adults range from 600 to 800 IU daily, with needs varying by age and health status. “Women with a deficiency may need a different dose under medical supervision,” he added.Per Dr Rakesh's guidelines, while calcium provides the mineral structure that keeps bones strong, vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium from food. It is also crucial for maintaining proper function of muscles and bones.If either is consistently inadequate, the experts warned that maintaining bone strength becomes harder and that you will experience weaker bones, which can increase the risk of falls and fractures.Dr Lalit highlighted that vitamin D, which the body can produce when sunlight hits our skin, can be increased by getting sun each day (but too much is also unhealthy). Meanwhile, Dr Rakesh stressed that living in a sunny country does not guarantee adequate vitamin D; time spent indoors, clothing, sunscreen use, skin pigmentation, and limited sunlight exposure can all affect how much the body produces. “The correct dose you get depends on all of the above. Additionally, age, dietary intake, risk factors, and vitamin D levels (if measured) should be considered when testing. Do not use high-dose vitamin D supplementation without medical advice,” he cautioned.Consuming fortified foods and other vitamin D-rich foods, or taking a supplement, is an alternative. Dr Rakesh advises consuming foods such as oily fish, egg yolks, and fortified products, although diet alone may not always provide enough.Calcium and vitamin D on their own are not enoughLastly, calcium and vitamin D alone are not sufficient to treat established osteoporosis from an orthopaedic perspective, both experts stressed.“Weight-bearing exercise, strength training, fall prevention, and, if necessary, prescription medications are also part of the treatment plan,” Dr Lalit stated. Apart from these, Dr Rakesh advised brisk walking.“Menopausal women, patients with a history of fracture, or those with risk factors for osteoporosis should seek a discussion with their doctor for assessment of bone health. A bone density test (DEXA scan) can be considered based on age and risk. Healthy bones require more than supplements. Eat healthily, stay active, and get checked by a healthcare professional to keep bone loss at bay and protect yourself from fractures,” Dr Lalit advised.Note to readers: This article is for informational purposes only and not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always seek the advice of your doctor with any questions about a medical condition.

title: Delhi Police busts interstate heroin network, seizes 8.1 kg contraband worth  ₹60 crore | Latest News Delhi
description: Delhi Police busts interstate heroin network, seizes 8.1 kg contraband worth  ₹60 crore  | Latest News Delhi
content: New Delhi, The Delhi Police has busted an alleged interstate heroin manufacturing and supply network spanning Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand, arresting seven persons and recovering more than 8 kg of the contraband worth around ₹60 crore in the illicit market, officials said on Thursday.The operation has led to the arrest of an alleged raw opium supplier from Jharkhand's Naxal-affected Chatra district, allegedly involved in illegal cultivation of poppy on his agricultural land, police said.Police have also seized nearly 3.3 kg of chemicals and other raw materials used in heroin-manufacture, ₹12.81 lakh in cash, three SUVs, a motorcycle and equipment allegedly used in production of the contraband.Investigation has revealed that raw opium was allegedly sourced from Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh, processed into heroin at an illicit manufacturing unit in Lucknow and supplied through a network operating across Delhi-NCR and other states, police said.The operation began on September 16 when a Delhi Police team, acting on specific inputs, intercepted an SUV in Sector 32 of north-west Delhi's Begumpur and apprehended Laxman Hooda, 58, who had allegedly arrived to deliver a heroin consignment.Police recovered 300 grams of heroin and ₹3 lakh from the vehicle, which was seized.The next day, police apprehended an alleged supplier, Anil alias Bhola, 51, from Sonipat in Haryana and recovered 501 grams of heroin from his SUV.Anil has been previously involved in 12 criminal cases and was arrested in a narcotics case registered at Bhalswa Dairy police station in 2025. He allegedly failed to surrender after being granted interim bail and was subsequently declared a proclaimed offender by a court, police said.Further investigation, aided by technical surveillance and human intelligence, led the team to a heroin manufacturing facility in Lucknow, where Bablu, 35, was apprehended on October 4.The raid resulted in the recovery of 6.275 kg of freshly manufactured heroin, along with 2.5 kg of sodium, 787 grams of acetic anhydride and equipment, including a gas cylinder, mixer-grinder, tub, utensils, an electronic weighing machine and other material allegedly used in the manufacturing process.Acting on Bablu's disclosures, police traced and apprehended Ruksar Ali alias Raju, the alleged owner of the manufacturing facility, from Bareilly in Uttar Pradesh, officials said.On October 6, the team arrested Ajaj Ahmed, 38, from Bareilly with the help of technical surveillance. He allegedly supplied crude opium to Ruksar Ali. Police recovered 501 grams of heroin and a Royal Enfield motorcycle from him.The investigation subsequently led to the arrest of Mohammad Azhar, 20, from Badaun in Uttar Pradesh on October 16. He allegedly supplied heroin and crude opium to Ajaj Ahmed. Police recovered 551 grams of heroin, ₹9.81 lakh in cash and an SUV from him.The final link was traced to Chatra district of Jharkhand, where Prakash Kumar, 31, was arrested on October 18. He allegedly supplied raw opium to the accused and was involved in illegal cultivation of opium poppy on his agricultural land, police said.With these arrests, police claimed to have dismantled the alleged network spanning raw opium cultivation, procurement of raw materials, heroin manufacturing and distribution.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Asthma, influenza and the power of prevention | Hindustan Times
description: Authored by - Dr Randeep Guleria, chairman, Institute of Internal Medicine & Respiratory and Sleep Medicine and director, Medanta Medical School, Gurugram.
content: For people living with asthma, the flu is often more than just a few days of fever and fatigue. It can trigger worsening breathlessness, persistent coughing and severe asthma attacks that may require emergency treatment or hospitalisation. Preventing respiratory infections is therefore an important part of maintaining stable asthma control throughout the year.Asthma remains under-recognised in India despite affecting millions of people. Findings from the Indian Global Asthma Network study revealed that nearly 82% of individuals who experienced current wheeze remained undiagnosed, while about 70% of those with severe asthma symptoms had not been diagnosed with asthma. This means many people may be living with symptoms for years without understanding the underlying condition or the steps they can take to better protect their respiratory health.People who frequently wheeze during colds, use inhalers regularly, have a history of chest infections or pneumonia, or are older adults living with asthma should pay particular attention to respiratory infection prevention.One of the biggest concerns for people with asthma is not the infection itself, but what the infection can trigger. Influenza is a well-known cause of asthma flare-ups because it increases inflammation in already sensitive airways. Even individuals who usually have good symptom control can experience sudden worsening of asthma following influenza infection.These flare-ups can have consequences far beyond temporary discomfort. Severe asthma attacks may require oral steroids, unscheduled doctor visits, emergency care and hospitalisation. They can also take weeks to fully recover from, affecting quality of life-long after the infection has resolved. This is where prevention becomes especially important.While inhalers remain the foundation of asthma treatment, they cannot prevent influenza infection. Vaccination offers an additional layer of protection by helping reduce the likelihood of influenza and its impact on respiratory health. Research has shown that influenza vaccination substantially reduces the risk of influenza in people living with asthma. Importantly, evidence suggests that improving influenza vaccine uptake could help reduce influenza-triggered asthma attacks, one of the most common causes of symptom worsening and loss of asthma control. Respiratory infections can lead to increased airway inflammation, making asthma symptoms more difficult to manage and increasing the risk of severe exacerbations. While vaccination cannot prevent every respiratory illness, it can help reduce exposure to a trigger that frequently contributes to asthma flare-ups.For people living with asthma, avoiding exacerbations is often just as important as controlling day-to-day symptoms. Fewer influenza-triggered asthma attacks can mean less wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness and persistent cough. This may translate into reduced reliance on rescue medications, fewer unscheduled health care visits and a lower likelihood of hospitalisation. Beyond the clinical benefits, preventing flare-ups can help people stay engaged in their daily activities, whether at work, school or home, without the disruption that often accompanies worsening asthma symptoms.Asthma management is not only about treating symptoms when they occur; it is also about preventing the triggers that can lead to serious exacerbations. Along with prescribed medications, trigger avoidance, regular follow-up and healthy lifestyle habits, annual influenza vaccination should be viewed as an important component of preventive asthma care. Protecting against influenza helps strengthen a broader strategy aimed at maintaining stable asthma control throughout the year.Ultimately, the greatest benefit of influenza vaccination for many people with asthma may not simply be avoiding influenza itself, but avoiding the asthma flare-up that influenza can trigger. By helping reduce one of the most common causes of exacerbations, vaccination can support better long-term symptom control, fewer hospital visits and an improved quality of life, allowing people with asthma to live with greater confidence and stability year-round.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Dr Randeep Guleria, chairman, Institute of Internal Medicine & Respiratory and Sleep Medicine and director, Medanta Medical School, Gurugram.

title: Fadnavis inaugurates 3 new bridges in Mumbai, says infra push to cut city travel time | Mumbai news
description: Fadnavis inaugurates 3 new bridges in Mumbai, says infra push to cut city travel time  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Thursday said new infrastructure projects in Mumbai would help create seamless north-south and east-west connectivity, helping realise the vision of reducing travel time across the city to 50 to 60 minutes.Fadnavis was speaking after virtually inaugurating three new flyovers the railway overbridges at Sion in the island city and Vidyavihar in the eastern suburbs, and a flyover on the Goregaon-Mulund Link Road in the western suburbs."These infrastructure projects will be important in our plan to reach from one part of Mumbai to another in 50 to 60 minutes," he said, adding that improved traffic flow would facilitate better movement and enhance ease of living.The three projects aim to improve east-west connectivity, reduce travel time and ease traffic congestion at key junctions in the city.The reconstructed Sion railway overbridge has been built after demolishing the 112-year-old British-era structure, which was declared unsafe in 2019. The new flyover will facilitate the planned construction of the fifth and sixth railway lines between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and Kurla under the Mumbai Urban Transport Project .The new bridge will provide space for the additional railway lines, which are expected to improve suburban and long-distance train operations. The project, originally scheduled for completion in February 2027, was completed four months ahead of schedule, according to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.Fadnavis said it will improve traffic flow and facilitate the laying of the fifth and sixth railway lines under MUTP-II. The additional lines will help increase the number and frequency of suburban train services.The Vidyavihar bridge connects Ramchandra Chemburkar Marg in the east with Lal Bahadur Shastri Marg in the western part of Mumbai. It is expected to reduce travel time between the two sides from around 30 minutes to 10 minutes.CM Fadnavis said the new railway bridge will also ease the load on the Ghatkopar railway overbridge.The third flyover, measuring 1.26 km, has been constructed near Hotel Ratnagiri junction in Goregaon East as part of the GMLR project. It connects General Arun Kumar Vaidya Marg with Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari Road near Santosh Nagar.Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar, Maharashtra ministers Ashish Shelar and Mangal Prabhat Lodha and Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde also attended the inauguration ceremony.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: వైఎస్ ఫ్యామిలీలో వివాదం.. మేనకోడలి పెళ్లికి బెంగళూరు ప్యాలెస్ ఇచ్చేందుకు జగన్ నో! | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: వైఎస్ కుటుంబంలోని ఆస్తుల విషయంపై మరోసారి పెద్ద ఎత్తున చర్చ నడుస్తోంది. మేనకోడలి పెళ్లికి బెంగళూరు ప్యాలెస్ ఇచ్చేందుకు జగన్ నో చెప్పారని ప్రచారం నడుస్తోంది. దీనిపై షర్మిల స్పందించాల్సి ఉంది.
content: వైఎస్సార్ కుటుంబంలో ఆస్తుల వివాదం మరోసారి వెలుగులోకి వచ్చింది. వైఎస్సార్సీపీ అధినేత, మాజీ ముఖ్యమంత్రి వైఎస్ జగన్ మోహన్ రెడ్డి తమ కుటుంబానికి చెందిన బెంగళూరు యలహంక ప్యాలెస్‌లో మేనకోడలి వివాహానికి అనుమతించేందుకు నిరాకరించారని విశ్వసనీయ వర్గాల ద్వారా తెలుస్తోంది. ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ కాంగ్రెస్ అధ్యక్షురాలు వైఎస్ షర్మిల కుమార్తె వైఎస్ అంజలి రెడ్డి వివాహానికి సంబంధించిన ఈ విషయం ప్రస్తుతం తెలుగు రాష్ట్రాల రాజకీయాల్లో తీవ్ర చర్చనీయాంశంగా మారింది.విజయమ్మ చెప్పినా వినని జగన్!వైఎస్ షర్మిల కుమార్తె అంజలి రెడ్డికి, అమెరికాలో నివసిస్తున్న సోమల రఘురామిరెడ్డితో ఈ ఏడాది సెప్టెంబర్ 24న నిశ్చితార్థం జరిగిన సంగతి తెలిసిందే. ఈ క్రమంలో నవంబర్ 25వ తేదీన కుటుంబానికి ఎంతో ప్రత్యేకమైన బెంగళూరు యలహంక ప్యాలెస్‌లో వేడుకగా వివాహం జరిపించాలని షర్మిల నిర్ణయించుకున్నారు. అయితే ప్యాలెస్‌లో పెళ్లికి సంబంధించిన అనుమతి కోసం తల్లి వైఎస్ విజయమ్మ ద్వారా జగన్‌ను షర్మిల సంప్రదించగా.. అందుకు జగన్ అంగీకరించలేదని సమాచారం.ఈ ఆస్తి తన భార్య వైఎస్ భారతి రెడ్డి తల్లి పేరిట రిజిస్టర్ అయి ఉందని, అందుకే అక్కడ వివాహ వేడుకకు అనుమతించలేనని జగన్ తన తల్లికి స్పష్టం చేసినట్లు తెలుస్తోంది. విజయమ్మ ఎంత నచ్చజెప్పే ప్రయత్నం చేసినా జగన్ తన నిర్ణయాన్ని మార్చుకోలేదని సమాచారం.కొత్త వేదిక కోసం షర్మిల సెర్చింగ్ఇప్పటికే వైఎస్ షర్మిల బంధువులతో పాటు పలువురు రాజకీయ ప్రముఖులకు, సినీ, వ్యాపార రంగాల ప్రముఖులకు వెడ్డింగ్ కార్డ్స్ అందజేశారు. ఈ జాబితాలో కాంగ్రెస్ అధిష్టాన పెద్దలతో పాటు కర్ణాటక సీఎం డి.కె. శివకుమార్, తెలంగాణ ముఖ్యమంత్రి రేవంత్ రెడ్డి, తమిళనాడు మాజీ ముఖ్యమంత్రి, వైఎస్సార్ కుటుంబ శ్రేయోభిలాషులు, విఐపీలు ఉన్నారు. అకస్మాత్తుగా ప్యాలెస్ అందుబాటులో లేకపోవడంతో, విఐపీల భద్రత, రవాణా వసతులకు తగినట్లుగా మరొక ప్రత్యామ్నాయ వేదికను వెతికే పనిలో షర్మిల బృందం పడింది.యలహంక ఆస్తి వెనక అసలు వివాదం ఏమిటి?దివంగత ముఖ్యమంత్రి వైఎస్ రాజశేఖర్ రెడ్డి జీవించి ఉన్న సమయంలో తన కుమారుడు జగన్, కుమార్తె షర్మిల ఇద్దరికీ ఆస్తుల్లో సమాన వాటాలు ఉండాలని ఆకాంక్షించేవారని షర్మిల సన్నిహితులు చెబుతున్నారు. అందుకే హైదరాబాద్, బెంగళూరు, సొంత ఊరైన ఇడుపులపాయలలో ఇద్దరికీ చెరో నివాసాన్ని ఏర్పాటు చేశారు.హైదరాబాద్(లోటస్ పాండ్) ఒకే ప్రాంగణంలో పక్కపక్కనే రెండు నివాసాలు నిర్మించారు. షర్మిల ప్రస్తుతం తన నివాసంలోనే ఉంటున్నారు. ఇడుపులపాయలో కూడా ఇద్దరికీ వేర్వేరు గృహాలు ఉన్నాయి. బెంగళూరు (యలహంక)లో సుమారు 20 ఎకరాల విస్తీర్ణంలో రెండు పక్కపక్క ఇళ్లను నిర్మించారు. వైఎస్సార్ బెంగళూరు వచ్చినప్పుడల్లా ఇక్కడే విడిది చేసేవారు. జగన్ బెంగళూరు వెళ్లినప్పుడు తన ప్యాలెస్‌లోనే ఉంటారు.అయితే షర్మిలకు కేటాయించిన ఇల్లు ఆమె పేరిట అధికారికంగా రిజిస్టర్ కాకపోవడం, 2009 సెప్టెంబర్ 2న వైఎస్సార్ హెలికాప్టర్ ప్రమాదంలో అకస్మాత్తుగా మరణించడంతో ఆస్తుల పంపిణీ ప్రక్రియ అసంపూర్తిగా మిగిలిపోయింది. ఇది కాలక్రమేణా ఇద్దరి మధ్య వివాదానికి దారితీసింది. ఇవి కాకుండా మరికొన్ని కారణాలు ఉన్నాయని తెలుస్తోంది.ఐదేళ్లుగా కొనసాగుతున్న ఆస్తుల వివాదంగత ఐదేళ్లుగా జగన్, షర్మిల మధ్య సరస్వతి పవర్ అండ్ ఇండస్ట్రీస్ లిమిటెడ్ షేర్లతో పాటు పలు కుటుంబ ఆస్తుల వివాదం నడుస్తోంది. ఈ కేసు ప్రస్తుతం నేషనల్ కంపెనీ లా ట్రైబ్యునల్ విచారణలో ఉంది. జగన్ జైలులో ఉన్నప్పుడు షర్మిల వైఎస్సార్సీపీ తరఫున ఓదార్పు యాత్రలు చేశారు. 2019 ఎన్నికల ప్రచారంలోనూ కీలక పాత్ర పోషించారు. అయితే 2019లో జగన్ ముఖ్యమంత్రి అయిన తర్వాత ఆస్తుల పంపిణీ వ్యత్యాసాల వల్ల వీరి సంబంధాలు పూర్తిగా దెబ్బతిన్నాయి. అనంతరం షర్మిల తెలంగాణలో వైఎస్సార్‌టీపీ పెట్టి, ఆ తర్వాత కాంగ్రెస్‌లో విలీనం చేశారు. తర్వాత ఏపీ కాంగ్రెస్ అధ్యక్షురాలిగా బాధ్యతలు స్వీకరించి రాజకీయంగా తన సోదరుడిపై తీవ్ర విమర్శలు గుప్పిస్తున్న సంగతి తెలిసిందే.ఈ క్రమంలో షర్మిలను వైసీపీ సోషల్ మీడియా తీవ్రస్థాయిలో టార్గెట్ చేసింది. జగన్‌‌ను దెబ్బకొట్టేందుకు షర్మిలను కూటమి పార్టీలు ఉపయోగించుకుంటున్నాయని ఆరోపణలు వచ్చాయి. ఇప్పుడు మేనకోడలి పెళ్లికి ప్యాలెస్‌లో పర్మిషన్ ఇవ్వని విషయం కూడా పెద్ద ఎత్తున చర్చ నడుస్తోంది. ఇందులో అసలు విషయం తెలియాల్సి ఉంది. దీనిపై షర్మిల ఏం మాట్లాడుతారా అనే ఆసక్తి నెలకొంది. ఏదైనా రాజకీయ వేదిక మీద జగన్‌పై ఈ విషయం గురించి కచ్చితంగా షర్మిల కామెంట్స్ చేసే అవకాశం ఉంది.

title: How digital health can build a prevention-first India | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Dr Vikram Thaploo, CEO, Apollo TeleHealth.
content: A routine antenatal screening at a primary health care centre in Manipur recently identified syphilis in a pregnant woman. What made the intervention significant was not simply the diagnosis, but the fact that a condition with potentially serious consequences for both mother and child was identified during routine care, allowing treatment to begin in time. This is where the real promise of digital health lies, not merely in making a doctor accessible remotely, but in helping the healthcare system recognise risk earlier and act before a health problem becomes a crisis.India has made considerable progress in terms of improving digital access to health care. With teleconsultation patients do not have to rely on location or geography to speak to a specialist. The next step in terms of health should be more than just the consultation. A greater opportunity lies in creating a system that would determine risk levels, provide assistance and connect people to care throughout their treatment, especially in areas where distance, cost and availability affect health conditions.This shift is especially important as India confronts the growing burden of non-communicable diseases. Hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular disease and cancer often develop silently, with patients seeking medical attention only after symptoms become difficult to ignore. Prevention, therefore, cannot remain confined to occasional health camps or hospital visits. It has to become part of routine primary health care, supported by screening, diagnostics, follow-ups and timely referrals.Digital health can make this possible by turning the consultation into one part of a larger care pathway. Telemedicine can connect patients with doctors, while tele radiology and tele cardiology can extend specialised interpretation to locations where such expertise may not be physically available. Tele condition management can support patients after diagnosis, while connected devices and digitally enabled screening programmes can help health care teams identify changes in vital parameters before they become emergencies. Digital dispensaries, teleophthalmology, cancer screening and technology-enabled primary care models can further extend this continuum into communities.The impact of such an approach becomes clearer when viewed at scale. In Odisha, a digitally enabled health care initiative has crossed one million teleconsultations while facilitating more than 200,000 diagnostic tests and over 20,000 referrals for specialised care. The significance of these numbers is not simply the volume of consultations delivered. It is the ability to connect consultation with diagnostics, medicines and escalation of care, creating a pathway that does not end when the video call ends.The same principle applies to chronic disease management, where the consultation is only the beginning. The more difficult part begins afterwards: Taking medicines regularly, monitoring parameters, making lifestyle changes and recognising when the condition is deteriorating. Digital platforms can help healthcare teams maintain this connection through remote monitoring, scheduled follow-ups, health education and escalation protocols.India is also developing the digital foundations required to make this model more effective. Platforms such as the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and ABHA are creating the basis for more connected health records and greater interoperability. When combined with appropriate consent frameworks and strong data governance, this can help move healthcare from fragmented encounters towards a more continuous understanding of an individual’s health journey.Artificial Intelligence (AI) will add another layer to this transformation, particularly in areas such as risk stratification, image interpretation and clinical decision support. The objective, however, should not be to automate health care for its own sake. Technology must help clinicians identify patterns earlier, prioritise high-risk patients and make better informed decisions while keeping clinical judgement and patient needs at the centre of care.As for India, the real test of digital health will be determined by the outcomes on the ground. The nation requires digital health systems that will function equally well in rural and urban areas, assist health workers in the field, provide testing facilities at the right time, and ensure proper channels to higher levels of care if needed. While hospitals will always be critical in handling complex and serious situations, digital health can help patients reach them at the proper time instead of after their medical problem has progressed. The ultimate measure of digital health should consequently not be how many people are brought into a consultation. It should be how early disease is identified, how effectively people remain connected to care and, most importantly, how many serious complications can be prevented. If digital health can make health care more anticipatory rather than reactive, it can become more than an access solution. It can become one of the most important enablers of a prevention-first health care system for India.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Dr Vikram Thaploo, CEO, Apollo TeleHealth.

title: Report: Remembering Veenapani Festival 2026 | Hindustan Times
description: From musical storytelling performances to a classical Sanskrit play and a reimagination of a Shakespearean one, the event was a treat
content: Ferns and falling flowers, fruit laden trees, sultry summer temperatures, workers throwing their voices over a verdant campus; the artistic director cycling up and down the mud path fixing something or the other a few hours before the first show; volunteers abuzz with some help from their walkie-talkies; guests eating bajjis, burgers and dosas while waiting for the popsicle van to show up… These were some of the images that stayed in the mind well after the 12th edition of the Remembering Veenapani Festival (RVF) 2026 held from April 12 to 26 at the Adishakti Theatre Arts Campus near Auroville in Puducherry. RVF featured nine shows that collectively reflected the words of Adishakti Theatre’s founder, Veenapani Chawla: “Anything and everything is theatre.”Besides plays, music shows and dance theatre performances, the festival ran a documentary film series showcasing films on contemporary themes. Before the Third Bell, The Documentary Edition was curated by Aparna Sanyal of the Public Service Broadcasting Trust (PSBT). The festival’s first show was a musical storytelling performance, Mone Rekho, that had Soumik Datta, all through his sarod recital, recalling his relationship with his musical mentor, who constantly reminded him to “keep in mind” certain phrases of raags, salient features of classical music and the sacred tenets of being a student of classical music.Then, Sage for the Ages launched their album R-Evolution that stands with those struggling to keep the earth safe. Written by Kirtana Krishna, the songs speak of the problems of plastic, of “the earth being sold”, and of the yearning for home. Preethi Athreya’s Rubber Girl was a riveting dance theatre performance that delved into desire and the evolution of cabaret as a form in which women’s bodies are “packaged.” The performer’s research melded seamlessly into the storytelling.Jangama Collective’s Bob Marley from Kodihalli, directed by Lakshman K P, featured Shwetha Rani H K, Bharath Dingri and Chandrashekar K depicting caste oppression playing out over generations and across locations. To the credit of the performers, the Kannada play was completely understood and much appreciated by the Aurovillian audience. The Queen, written by Aditya Rawal and directed by Daniel Owen Dsouza, was spectacular in presentation and performance, with Puja Sarup playing the protagonist. Adishakti Theatre’s A Woman or Not to Be, written and directed by Vinay Kumar, skillfully reimagined Hamlet as a woman raging against her father while grieving the suspected murder of her mother. The ensemble of actors led by Nimmy Raphel (who played Hamlet) challenged every memorable scene from the famous play with new questions and perspectives.Something Like Truth, written by Shanta Gokhale and directed by Parna Pethe, was another hit that presented the female gaze and shone with feminine energy. Natanakairali’s Kutiyattam version of Śūdraka’s classic Mrcchakatikam was brought alive by Kapila Venu, Sooraj Nambiar and an ensemble of highly proficient actors under the seasoned directorial guidance of G Venu. The Vasu Dixit Collective then presented the grand finale. “It had the audience in tears,” said Adishakti’s artistic director Vinay Kumar. What marks the RVF out from other arts festivals is the sense of sanctuary it provides for artistes and the arts, without drawing a line between genres and forms. For actor, theatre educator and theatre-maker Puja Sarup, who first visited Adishakti for a workshop in 2004, returning for the festival is like a homecoming. “Since then, I have attended the Adishakti actor training workshop, watched performances, been part of productions, explorations, residencies and performed in other editions of the RVF. It is the people and the space that draw me. Every time I come here I feel held by both. It is one of those friendships where it doesn’t matter when the last meeting was. When you meet you just pick up from where you left off,” she says.It is a struggle to put up the sponsor-less festival year after year but the organizers have stubbornly kept it free and open to all in the hope of giving more audiences a chance to experience high quality theatre from across the world. Nimmy Raphel, managing trustee, Adishakti Theatre, says she has accepted that “it is not going to get any easier” but will “run the festival for as long as possible.” She points to the “transactional world” they have to negotiate while seeking corporate sponsorship and says, “I don’t know if arts can work that way.” Crowd-funding is not any easier but the approach of collaborations is helpful, she says adding that audiences have emphatically expressed “their special love for live performances”. Vinay Kumar and Nimmy Raphel point to the wholesome nature of theatre that makes it easy to include various forms rather than just plays. “Theatre is a very integrated form. It allows the possibility of having movement, music, mime, puppetry and more. In Adishakti, it is all part of our practice,” says Nimmy. Vinay Kumar stresses that defining only plays as theatre does not reflect an Indian aesthetic. “Dance and music are a very integral part of theatre-making in our tradition. Those forms already belong here in the theatre,” he says.The challenges notwithstanding, year after year, the Remembering Veenapani Festival demonstrates that theatre in all its fullness is more than an evening of recreation for those who choose to be steeped in it. It is a lifetime of showing up; sitting with an instrument, an empty stage, a sheet of paper, an ensemble of actors or with one’s own inadequacies and transforming all of that into something much more.Charumathi Supraja is a writer, poet and journalist based in Bengaluru.

title: Dussehra is over elsewhere, but in Himachal's Kullu, the festivities have just begun | Trending
description: Kullu in Himachal Pradesh celebrates Dussehra differently from much of India, with festivities beginning on Vijayadashami.  | Trending
content: While Dussehra celebrations conclude on Vijayadashami in much of India, a hill town in Himachal Pradesh follows a different tradition. Here, the festival begins on the very day it marks the end of celebrations elsewhere. The centuries-old custom has its roots in the region's royal history and distinctive religious practices.Why Kullu celebrates Dussehra after VijayadashamiThe tradition is linked to Raja Jagat Singh, who ruled Kullu in the 17th century. According to the Ministry of Tourism's Utsav portal, the king installed an idol of Lord Raghunath, a form of Lord Rama, brought from Ayodhya at the palace temple in Kullu.Lord Raghunath subsequently became the principal deity of the valley, and the festival developed around his worship. Unlike in many parts of India, where Dussehra celebrations culminate on Vijayadashami with the burning of Ravana's effigies, the day marks the beginning of Kullu's week-long festivities.(Also Read: Costco CEO Ron Vachris went from forklift driver to CEO following his father’s advice to ‘not chase a title’)The role of Lord Raghunath in Kullu DussehraLord Raghunath remains the central figure of the festival. The celebrations feature a grand Rath Yatra, during which his decorated wooden chariot is pulled by devotees to Dhalpur Maidan. The procession is joined by village deities carried on elaborately decorated palanquins, accompanied by priests, musicians and devotees.According to the official Kullu district administration website, the gathering reflects the region's deep-rooted religious beliefs and cultural traditions. The deities assemble to pay their respects to Lord Raghunath, bringing together communities from across the valley.The festival also includes traditional music, folk performances and Nati dances, along with exhibitions and local markets. These activities make Kullu Dussehra a cultural gathering as well as a religious celebration.How Kullu Dussehra differs from celebrations elsewhereIn many parts of India, Dussehra is associated with Ramlila performances and the burning of effigies of Ravana, symbolising the victory of good over evil. Kullu follows a different tradition, with the arrival and gathering of village deities forming the centrepiece of the celebrations.(Also Read: Rare egg of extinct giant moa bird to return to New Zealand after 60 years in US collection)The festival typically continues for seven days after beginning on Vijayadashami. In 2026, the official Kullu district website lists the International Kullu Dussehra celebrations from October 21 to 27.Over the years, the event has grown into a major cultural attraction, drawing visitors who want to experience Himachal Pradesh's religious traditions, folk arts and local heritage.

title: India’s turn to test the VC cycle | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Aditya Singh, co-founder and partner, All In Capital.
content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) can bring a change. Deep technology can be tactical. Indian people can increase consumption for years. People who bet their money on all three simultaneously can expect losses.The story of venture capital (VC) in history teaches us an unpleasant truth: Sometimes it’s the technology that is good but the time is bad.Indeed, the Internet changed the world. However, the American venture funds established at the peak of the dot com boom didn’t take benefits from that. Cambridge Associates commented that American VC funds created in 1999 continue to show a negative overall internal rate of return (IRR) even after years. It should be noted that 2021 and 2022 American VC funds established in the years of extreme supply of money and high valuations started to show median net IRRs of around 1% only now.Due to the fact that people have high technology in their hands does not mean that they will profit from their investments. The market price, competition, and follow-on financing are also important. It is concerning that India seems to be slipping into certain times of old, but this has nothing to do with the slowing down of Indian entrepreneurship. It should be kept in mind that three major developments – namely, AI, deep technology, and consumer brands – are taking place at the same time. All of these innovations are leading to the concentration of capital in their respective segments while requiring businesses to prove their high market value.In brief, AI is the first distortion in question.The debate about the reality of AI has ended, and now we only wonder whether the financing received by companies in the field is reasonable given their market price.As Sam Altman put it, investors are "over-excited about AI," even though he believes AI is one of the most revolutionary technologies of the last decades.Check out the situation of the American VC that rose to the occasion to check the status of where AI stood. In 2025, AI accounted for 65.5 % of the US VC deal volume. The remarkable figure of 88.8% of the US VC deal volume went to AI in Q1 2026. In 2025, the US invested around $222 billion in AI whereas the entire VC market of India in the same year stood at around $16 billion.We are trying to play a game where our entire ecosystem is smaller than a single component of the American ecosystem.The key takeaway from this is not that India can’t produce world-class AI companies. Instead, it has the potential to create world-class SaaS companies. At Bain's estimates, by 2022 around 14 Indian SaaS firms making more than $100 million in annual recurring revenue existed, whereas Freshworks earned $839 million in revenue in 2025.The lesson is more nuanced: Indian investors are unable to apply the model of fundraising for tech startups that has been successful in Silicon Valley to AI. Any generic AI app devoid of any proprietary data, advantageous distribution or workflow can be created in a very short time. At the same time, American companies have access to bigger rounds of financing, clients sitting nearby and an ecosystem in which money changes hands faster than it ever does in India. Even Indian venture firms are starting to look towards the West. According to ET, this year Peak XV, DeVC and Activate among others had increased their investments in AI companies based in the US. Peak XV, Accel and Elevation among them financed over ten US-based AI startups in 2025. The winners from the Indian side will not be companies that simply attach AI to their products.The situation could become worse and every company risks getting less profitable than companies with superior funding potential.The interesting aspect of deep tech is that it entails numerous contradictions. The fund of ₹1 lakh crore set up by the government is the most significant initiative in India's innovation history. It was developed to cover high-risk research by providing long-term, low-cost financing.However, good industrial policy and good venture investment do not mean the same thing.The government's goal is to create a strategic sector encompassing rockets and semiconductors as well as biotechnology, robotics, military and power technologies while the goal of VC funds is to make high profits within the lifespan of their investment project.Though the two objectives overlap, they do not refer to exactly the same thing. India has over 3,600 deep tech startups at this point. The new government capital, the newly launched specialised vehicles and the traditional-style VC investments have all started to flow into the industry. However, it generates a new risk – investments get allocated much faster than scientific talent becomes available. If a fund allocates its resources to searching for investable deep tech companies, it can no longer be afraid that good science will not receive support. The main risk is that mediocre science will get funding just because funds need to be invested somewhere. And science risk is not subject to due diligence in the manner similar to SaaS. SpaceX was set up in 2002 and successfully launched its first Falcon 1 rocket in 2008. Skyroot opened its doors in 2018 and launched Vikram S in 2022, but its most significant contract was concluded only in 2026, that is to say, eight years after the foundation of the company. These stories are impressive but serve as a reminder of the long way every deep-tech company needs to go before achieving satisfactory results. There is no doubt that deep tech can deliver venture returns. Market behavior provides an indication as to how deep tech might be able to perform better than ‘regular’ technology. However, this requires specialist underwriting as well as patient capital. Traditional VC structures typically have their fund life at more than 10 years, with issues around fund life constraints and the need for specialist expertise being mentioned directly by McKinsey as significant factors for deep tech investing.The ₹1 lakh crore RDI programme can be a boon for India and at the same time can create challenges for the investors who are unable to follow strict investment disciplines. These statements are not contradictory.Lastly, the consumer. In this case, the bubble has a different look.India’s consumption story could be making headlines nevertheless what worries me is the cost of creating numerous digitally native brands based largely on the same platforms for acquisition, the same marketplaces and similar consumer pools.Funding is abundant during the initial phase. However, funding during the subsequent stages is very selective.D2C funding in India peaked in 2022 at $1.6 billion, declined to $ 824 million in the following years and recovered to $ 898 million in 2025. However, the important number here is the 69% decline in funding in D2C companies in the late stage between 2022 to 2025, even as the funding at seed and early stage accounted for 70% of the total funding in the sector.We finance a large number of firms at the seed stage because modern technologies facilitate their emergence. Subsequently, they reach the Series A and B and require a lot of money in addition to that because they realize that just having access to the Meta platform is not enough, customer acquisition is expensive, COD and RTO are taking away all profits, and traditional offline distribution requires additional investments.The large consumer firms will survive this phase of development and the biggest labels in India could very well be born right now. However, while there is a prosperous consumer market, not every consumer startup is worthy of VC investments.The main concern is that this situation is only evident in three industries named above. This may be one of the most underreported implications of the current phase of economic development. Money has not disappeared, it has just changed its concentration level.In the US, it is AI that absorbs an increasing amount of venture funds. In India, AI and deep technologies have already started to dominate investment minds. Big funds are still on the rise along with well-established managers. Of course, many worthy businesses of such industries as healthcare, fintech, enterprise software, logistics, etc. may not be the trendiest sector and thus may fail to find VC.In the first half of 2026, India's investments in private equity (PE) and venture capital (VC) fell by 36% when compared to the previous year, even though the US reached the highest levels of venture capital investment. This isn't an ordinary winter; it's a monsoon, hitting three specific areas and remaining dry for the rest of the world.The cause of concern is precisely what makes such vintages more dangerous.Every bubble opens with the truth, which, in conjunction with other observations, validates it. Everything was true back in October 2000: The Internet and smartphones were true, software as a service was true, and so is AI in December 2023. India’s deep tech opportunity is true. The market for Indian consumption is perfectly valid.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Aditya Singh, co-founder and partner, All In Capital.

title: Kanpur man run over after being pinned to car roof; 2 held for murder | Hindustan Times
description: Kanpur man run over after being pinned to car roof; 2 held for murder
content: Kanpur , A 37-year-old man was allegedly pinned to the roof of a car with his hands trapped in its rear window panes and driven for around 1.5 km before being thrown onto the road and run over by the same vehicle in Kanpur, police said on Thursday.Commissioner of Police Raghubir Lal told PTI that two of the three accused named in the murder case have been arrested.The victim, Biru Singh Badauria, a salesperson with a food products company, was returning home after visiting a Dussehra fair when the incident took place in the Hanumant Vihar area on Tuesday night.According to a complaint filed by his father, Ram Shankar Singh, the accused intercepted Badauria and assaulted him. When he tried to flee, they allegedly hit him with their car, pinned him to its roof with his hands trapped in the rear window panes and drove at high speed for around 1.5 km.They then allegedly threw him onto the road and ran over him with the vehicle.Badauria was initially taken to a private hospital and later shifted to Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital, where he died during treatment on Wednesday.The family alleged that the attack stemmed from an earlier dispute between Badauria and two of the accused, Rajveer and Mewa Yadav, residents of Khadepur's Nai Basti.The victim's brother initially lodged a complaint describing the incident as a road accident, following which a case was registered. The victim's father later filed a separate complaint alleging murder and naming Rajveer, Mewa Yadav and Pintu, according to Lal.The police are examining CCTV footage and have recovered the vehicle involved in the incident, he said.Rajveer and Pintu have been arrested, while efforts are underway to trace the third accused, Lal said, adding that further action would be taken based on the evidence.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Jailer 2 Box Office Collection: దటీజ్ సూపర్ స్టార్.. తొలి వారమే జైలర్ 2 ఆల్ టైమ్ రికార్డు.. నాలుగో స్థానానికి.. | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: Jailer 2 Box Office Collection: రజనీకాంత్ - నెల్సన్ దిలీప్‌కుమార్ కాంబినేషన్‌లో వచ్చిన సంచలన చిత్రం 'జైలర్ 2' బాక్సాఫీస్ వద్ద రికార్డుల తుఫాను సృష్టిస్తోంది. తొలి వారంలోనే ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా రూ.576.45 కోట్ల గ్రాస్ కలెక్షన్లు సాధించి, ఆల్-టైమ్ అత్యధిక వసూళ్లు సాధించిన 4వ తమిళ చిత్రంగా నిలిచింది.
content: Jailer 2 Box Office Collection: తమిళ సినీ రంగానికి ఎప్పుడూ చక్రవర్తి అనిపించుకునే సూపర్ స్టార్ రజనీకాంత్ (Rajinikanth) తన బాక్సాఫీస్ స్టామినాతో మరోసారి ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా ప్రకంపనలు సృష్టిస్తున్నారు. 2023లో విడుదలై ఇండస్ట్రీ హిట్ కొట్టిన 'జైలర్' చిత్రానికి సీక్వెల్‌గా వచ్చిన 'జైలర్ 2' (Jailer 2) బాక్సాఫీస్ వద్ద సరికొత్త చరిత్రను లిఖిస్తోంది. దర్శకుడు నెల్సన్ దిలీప్‌కుమార్ తెరకెక్కించిన ఈ యాక్షన్ థ్రిల్లర్, థియేటర్లలోకి వచ్చిన తొలి రోజు నుంచే అత్యంత సానుకూల టాక్‌తో దూసుకుపోతోంది.నవరాత్రి, దసరా పండుగ సెలవుల కాలాన్ని సంపూర్ణంగా ఉపయోగించుకున్న 'జైలర్ 2', థియేటర్లలో ఏడు రోజులు (మొదటి వారం) పూర్తి చేసుకునే సరికే మైండ్ బ్లాకింగ్ కలెక్షన్లతో ఇండస్ట్రీ రికార్డులను ఒక్కొక్కటిగా బద్దలు కొడుతోంది. మణిరత్నం 'పొన్నియిన్ సెల్వన్ 1', రజనీకాంత్ గత చిత్రం 'కూలీ', అజయ్ దేవగన్ 'దృశ్యం: ది కన్‌క్లూజన్' లైఫ్‌టైమ్ వసూళ్లను ఈ సినిమా కేవలం వారంలోనే దాటేసింది.ఫస్ట్ వీక్ బాక్సాఫీస్ సునామీ: ఎన్ని కోట్లంటే?ట్రేడ్ వర్గాల అధికారిక సమాచారం ప్రకారం.. 'జైలర్ 2' ఇండియాలో రూ. 317.20 కోట్ల నెట్ వసూళ్లు సాధించగా, ఇండియా వైడ్ గ్రాస్ రూ. 371.45 కోట్లకు చేరింది. ఇక ఓవర్సీస్ నుంచి ఏకంగా రూ. 205 కోట్లకు పైగా గ్రాస్ రాబట్టింది. దీనితో కలిపి ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా కేవలం 7 రోజుల్లోనే రూ.576.45 కోట్ల గ్రాస్ కలెక్షన్‌ను సాధించింది.ఈ ఊహించని బాక్సాఫీస్ రన్ ద్వారా 2026 సంవత్సరంలో భారత్‌లో అత్యధిక వసూళ్లు సాధించిన రెండవ చిత్రంగా 'జైలర్ 2' నిలిచింది. ఇటీవల బాక్సాఫీస్ వద్ద రూ. 560 కోట్లు రాబట్టిన అజయ్ దేవగన్ 'దృశ్యం: ది కన్‌క్లూజన్' లైఫ్‌టైమ్ రికార్డును కేవలం వారంలోనే జైలర్ 2 అధిగమించడం విశేషం.ఎవరెవరి రికార్డులు అవుట్ అంటే..'జైలర్ 2' సృష్టించిన ఈ కలెక్షన్ల సునామీతో పలు దిగ్గజ తమిళ చిత్రాలు వెనకబడిపోయాయి.పొన్నియిన్ సెల్వన్ 1 (PS-1): మణిరత్నం డ్రీమ్ ప్రాజెక్ట్ PS-1 లైఫ్‌టైమ్ గ్రాస్ రూ. 488.36 కోట్లను 'జైలర్ 2' సునాయాసంగా దాటేసింది.కూలీ (Coolie): రజనీకాంత్ గత చిత్రం, లోకేష్ కనగరాజ్ దర్శకత్వంలో వచ్చిన 'కూలీ' సాధించిన రూ. 518 కోట్ల వసూళ్లను కూడా ఈ సీక్వెల్ దాటేసింది.దీనితో కోలీవుడ్ చరిత్రలోనే అత్యధిక వసూళ్లు సాధించిన నాలుగో చిత్రంగా 'జైలర్ 2' అవతరించింది. ప్రస్తుతం రజనీకాంత్ '2.0' (రూ. 691 కోట్లు), దళపతి విజయ్ 'లియో' (రూ. 605.90 కోట్లు), 'జైలర్' (రూ. 604.74 కోట్లు) మాత్రమే దీనికంటే ముందు వరుసలో ఉన్నాయి. వచ్చే రెండవ వారంలో ఇవి కూడా దాటే అవకాశం ఉందని సినీ విశ్లేషకులు భావిస్తున్నారు.టైగర్ ముత్తువేల్ పాండియన్ నెక్స్ట్ మిషన్ ఏంటి?సన్ పిక్చర్స్ బ్యానర్‌పై కళానిధి మారన్ అత్యంత భారీ బడ్జెట్‌తో నిర్మించిన ఈ చిత్రంలో రజనీకాంత్ రిటైర్డ్ జైలర్ 'టైగర్ ముత్తువేల్ పాండియన్' పాత్రలో తిరిగి అలరించారు. రమ్యకృష్ణ, మిర్నా, రిత్విక్ పాత పాత్రల్లో కనిపించగా.. ఎస్‌జే సూర్య, మిథున్ చక్రవర్తి, సూరజ్ వెంజరమూడు, విద్యా బాలన్ వంటి దిగ్గజ నటులు కొత్తగా వచ్చి చేరారు.మొదటి భాగం ముగిసిన దగ్గరి నుంచే ప్రారంభమయ్యే ఈ కథలో.. విగ్రహాల అక్రమ రవాణా చేసే అంతర్జాతీయ ముఠా నుంచి తన కుటుంబాన్ని కాపాడుకోవడం, మరియు కొడుకు మరణం గురించిన నిజాన్ని దాచడంలో ఎదురయ్యే సవాళ్లను రజనీకాంత్ తనదైన స్టైల్, యాక్షన్ ఎలిమెంట్స్‌తో మెప్పించారు. వీకెండ్స్ దాటినా కూడా వీక్‌డేస్‌లో థియేటర్లు హౌస్‌ఫుల్ కావడం రజనీకాంత్ మానియాకు నిదర్శనంగా నిలుస్తోంది.

title: Make universities India’s R&D engine | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by Shobhit Mathur, VC and co-founder and Yashowardhan Tiwari, VC’s office, Rishihood University.
content: Recently, the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, published its report titled Research & Development Statistics at a Glance 2025-26. The report stated that India’s gross expenditure on research and development (GERD) has more than tripled over a decade, rising from ₹79,355.89 crore in 2013-14 to ₹244,767.81 crore in 2023-24. India’s GERD reached an all-time high in 2023-24, touching 0.84% of the GDP, and the report predicted a continuation in its upward trajectory. While the milestone does highlight India’s progress in funding its science and tech innovation ecosystem, it needs a closer critical reflection to better grasp India’s digital innovation footprints and broader strides in science and technology R&D.India’s digital success is often measured by record-breaking payment volumes, and absolute stats are showcased as signs of technological leadership. However, the devil lies in the details. The report cited above also mentioned that GERD for 2023-24 was “mainly driven by the private sector industry (45.2%), central sector institutions/labs (30.9%), higher education institutions (12.6%), and public sector industry (4.1%)”, while the contributions of institutions under state government and scientific and industrial research organisations (SIROs) remained on the margins at 4.0% and 3.2% respectively. The limited R&D capacity of institutions at the federal level, and a consequent top-down percolation of scientific knowledge, is just one of the apparent problems towards generating avenues for decentralisation of R&D and generation-cum-application of localised knowledge.Diving into the report further reveals that DRDO alone accounted for a major chunk (32.7%) of India’s GERD by the central sector institutions for 2023-24, and has been consistently the largest contributor over the years. While defence spending is crucial to India’s superpower ambitions, there needs to be an equal push towards strategic investment in innovation in the other sectors. For instance, MeitY and the Department of Science & Technology barely account for 2.7% and 5% of the expenditure by the central sector for 2023-24. Similarly, industrial R&D for the private sector was absolutely dominated by transportation and drugs and pharmaceuticals, with a share of 32.6% and 21.4% respectively, while information technology (7.9%) and electricals & electronics (5.9%) remained relatively miniscule in their shares. The most worrying aspect of GERD trends is the rapid increase in percentage share of MNCs in total business R&D in India, going up from 49.9% in 2020-21 to 71.3% in 2023-24, with the composition of MNCs including 252 private sector Indian MNCs, 124 private sector foreign MNCs and 14 public sector Indian MNCs. In essence, tech R&D is either being outsourced to India for foreign consumption, or exported to foreign markets without ushering in a parallel transformation within the Indian society. The true test of India’s technological progress lies elsewhere: Whether innovation can improve productivity in a village, expand opportunity in a small town and strengthen public services where they matter most. This is not simply an argument for inclusion. It is an economic argument.Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu recently asked on X: Why can a Swiss school teacher buy an iPhone with days of income while her Indian counterpart must work for months? His thesis of rural development through research and development holds that deep technological capability determines the terms on which a society trades with the world, and therefore what it can afford to pay its teachers, nurses and farmers. The GERD numbers make his insight a prescription: raise research spending, spread it beyond a few agencies and multinational balance sheets, and deploy it where livelihoods are made.Higher education contributes just 12.6% of India’s GERD; its greatest untapped resource. Universities are the natural instrument of decentralised research: spread across districts, embedded in local languages and economies, generating and applying localised knowledge. Private universities, with their autonomy and agility, are the best bet for fast-tracking innovation, provided government and industry fund them as research partners through public grants and problem-driven industry laboratories. Agricultural universities can co-create technologies with farmers, engineering colleges can build multilingual, voice-first applications, and medical colleges can pilot telehealth with district hospitals.India’s GERD milestone deserves celebration; its composition demands correction. Route research funding through universities into villages and small towns, and innovation will reach the farmer, student and entrepreneur, serving both India and Bharat.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Shobhit Mathur, VC and co-founder and Yashowardhan Tiwari, VC’s office, Rishihood University.

title: India's consumption story has a real estate angle: How shopping malls are becoming an investment theme | Real Estate News
description: From fashion and dining to entertainment-led experiences, India's organised retail market is evolving beyond shopping.   | Real Estate News
content: A shopping mall today is no longer just a place to buy clothes, groceries or household essentials. It is increasingly a destination for dining, entertainment, socialising and discovering new brands. From experiential stores and speciality restaurants to gaming zones and family entertainment centres, retailers are rethinking the role of physical spaces in an increasingly digital marketplace.This transformation has implications beyond the retail industry. It is also reshaping the commercial real estate market, where the performance of a shopping centre depends on its ability to attract customers, retain tenants and generate sustainable rental income.For investors exploring Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), this creates an interesting intersection between India's consumption story and income-generating commercial property.The connection, however, is not as simple as higher consumer spending translating directly into higher property returns. Understanding the relationship requires looking at retail leasing trends, the changing role of shopping malls, tenant economics, and the way these factors influence the performance of a real estate portfolio.India's retail real estate market is changingThe scale of recent leasing activity highlights the continuing demand for organised retail space.According to JLL's India Retail Market Dynamics Q2 2026, published in September 2026, gross retail leasing across India's top seven markets reached 6.27 million square feet in the first half of 2026, representing a 10.5% increase over the corresponding period in 2025. Shopping mall leasing increased by 22.4% year-on-year, while malls accounted for 43.1% of overall gross retail leasing during the first half.The report also found that shopping mall vacancy across the seven markets declined from 11.60% in the first half of 2025 to 11.15% by the end of the first half of 2026.These figures suggest that demand for organised retail environments remains relevant to retailers expanding their physical presence. But the underlying story is about the kind of space businesses want and the experiences they seek to offer customers.Fashion and apparel accounted for 33% of retail leasing in the first half of 2026, followed by food and beverage at 18% and entertainment at 16%, according to JLL. The entertainment segment's share of leasing increased from 12% in the first half of 2025 to 16% a year later.For property owners, this changing tenant mix can influence how shopping centres are designed, operated and positioned in the market.From shopping destinations to experience-led spacesThe growth of e-commerce has changed the expectations associated with physical retail. Consumers can purchase many products online, making the in-person experience an increasingly important part of a retailer's proposition.Shopping centres are responding by bringing together multiple activities under one roof. A consumer may visit a mall for a particular purchase but also spend time at a restaurant, watch a film, visit a gaming centre or explore a new store.For retailers, such locations can provide visibility, customer engagement and opportunities to create experiences that are difficult to replicate through a digital storefront alone.For mall operators, the challenge is to create a tenant mix that encourages repeat visits while making efficient use of the available space. Dining, entertainment and leisure facilities can complement conventional retail stores, potentially extending customer visits and supporting demand for neighbouring outlets.CBRE India's India Retail Figures H2 2025 report, published in January 2026, identified experience-led retail, flagship stores and formats targeting younger consumers among the factors supporting leasing activity. It also highlighted the expansion of direct-to-consumer brands into physical retail as part of their broader growth strategies.However, experience-led retail is not a guarantee of commercial success. Entertainment facilities and other experiential formats require investment and effective management. Their contribution to a property's financial performance depends on tenant economics, leasing arrangements, operating costs and the ability to attract customers consistently.The relevant question for property investors is whether these changes strengthen the underlying business of the shopping centre over time.How consumer demand can influence a mall's rental incomeFor a retail property owner, the relationship between consumer activity and financial performance runs through the tenants occupying the space.Retailers assess locations based on factors such as customer footfall, spending patterns, brand positioning, rental costs and the potential to generate sales. A mall that attracts the right audience may be better placed to retain tenants and secure leasing commitments, although individual retailers' outcomes can vary.When a property maintains healthy occupancy, it can support rental receipts. Lease renewals, new tenant agreements and contractual rent escalations may also influence the growth of rental income.But occupancy alone does not tell the complete story. A property may have a high proportion of occupied space while facing pressure on rents, tenant incentives or operating expenses. Conversely, a mall investing in refurbishment or repositioning may experience temporary vacancies while preparing for a different tenant mix.The quality and durability of rental income therefore matter as much as the headline occupancy figure.For a retail-focused REIT, investors need to understand how the underlying properties generate cash, what it costs to operate them and how leasing trends affect the trust's financial results. The performance of an individual property portfolio may differ from broader retail market trends because of its location, tenant composition, lease structures and competitive position.Where REITs fit into the retail real estate storyDirect ownership of a shopping centre is beyond the financial reach of most individual investors and involves substantial operational responsibilities. Retail-focused REITs provide a different route to exposure to commercial property.Under India's regulatory framework, REITs pool investments into real estate assets and issue units to investors. Listed units can be bought and sold through stock exchanges, subject to market prices and liquidity. Investors do not directly own or manage the individual stores or shopping centres in the portfolio.The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates REITs through its SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, as amended. The framework establishes requirements relating to the structure, operation, disclosures, and distributions of these investment vehicles.For investors interested in retail property, the attraction lies in the possibility of participating in the financial performance of professionally managed assets without purchasing an entire commercial property.Yet exposure to retail real estate should not be confused with a direct investment in consumer spending. A retailer's sales may increase without producing an equivalent increase in the rent paid to a landlord. The terms of the lease, the tenant's financial position, and the property owner's costs all influence the relationship.Similarly, a mall's popularity does not automatically translate into higher REIT distributions or rising unit prices. Investors must assess the trust's actual financial performance and the valuation at which its units are trading.What investors should examineThe changing retail landscape makes it important to look beyond the number of people visiting a shopping centre or the pace of store openings. Several indicators can help investors assess the quality of a retail real estate portfolio.Occupancy and leasing trends: Examine how much of the available space is occupied, how occupancy has changed over time, and whether vacant units are being leased on competitive terms.Tenant mix and concentration: A combination of fashion, food and beverage, entertainment and other retailers can broaden a property's appeal. Investors should also understand the dependence on major tenants or particular retail categories, especially when changes in one sector could affect leasing demand.Lease expiries and rental growth: The timing of lease renewals can influence future income. Investors should review contractual rent escalations, upcoming expiries and the rents achieved on new agreements.Property investment and operating costs: Shopping centres may require ongoing spending on maintenance, refurbishment, amenities and new experiences. These investments can support competitiveness, but they also affect the cash available to the property owner.Financial performance and valuation: Rental receipts, operating expenses, borrowing and distributable cash flows should be assessed alongside the market price of REIT units and the disclosed value of the underlying assets.These factors help distinguish a favourable market environment from the performance of a specific investment.The risks behind the consumption opportunityIndia's organised retail market may benefit from changing consumer preferences and retailers' expansion plans, but the sector remains exposed to economic and operational risks.A slowdown in discretionary spending can affect retailers' sales and expansion decisions. Rising operating costs may put pressure on tenants, while new competing malls or changes in local shopping patterns can influence footfall and occupancy.The growth of online shopping and quick commerce also affects different retail categories in different ways. Some retailers may use physical stores to strengthen customer relationships and support omnichannel operations, while others may reconsider the amount or type of space they require.Supply is another consideration. When new retail developments enter a market, existing properties may face greater competition for tenants. The effect depends on the location, quality and positioning of the new and existing assets.For REIT investors, these risks can affect rental income, property valuations and the market price of listed units. Distributions are not guaranteed, and listed REITs are not substitutes for deposits or other products designed to provide assured returns.A careful assessment should therefore consider both the potential offered by changing retail demand and the risks associated with operating commercial property.Looking beyond the shopping experienceIndia's retail real estate market reflects a wider shift in how consumers use physical spaces. Shopping centres are competing not only on the range of products available but also on convenience, dining, entertainment and the overall experience they offer.For commercial property owners, these changes create opportunities to attract retailers and strengthen a property's position in the market. For investors, the important question is whether the demand for these spaces translates into durable rental income, effective property management, and sustainable cash flows.Retail-focused REITs offer one way to participate in the economics of commercial real estate, but the investment case ultimately rests on the underlying portfolio rather than the popularity of shopping malls alone.Understanding the tenant mix, occupancy, leasing terms, operating costs, financial disclosures, and valuation can help investors evaluate that distinction.The consumption story may draw people into shopping centres. For REIT investors, it is the quality and sustainability of the property income behind that activity that deserves closer attention.Primary research and regulatory sourcesJLL, India Retail Market Dynamics Q2 2026, September 2026: Read the report.
