title: From global capability centres to office demand: What India's commercial real estate boom means for REITs | Real Estate News
description: India's expanding global capability centres are driving demand for quality office space, creating new opportunities and challenges for commercial real estate.  | Real Estate News
content: India's office buildings are increasingly becoming more than workplaces. As multinational companies expand their technology, engineering, financial services and research operations in the country, commercial offices are emerging as an important part of India's evolving role in the global business ecosystem.At the centre of this shift are global capability centres (GCCs). Once associated largely with back-office support and cost efficiency, these centres are increasingly undertaking functions such as product development, data analytics, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and research. Their changing role is influencing not only the nature of employment in India but also the demand for modern commercial real estate.For investors looking at Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), this creates an important question: how does the expansion of corporate India translate into the performance of income-generating property?The answer lies in understanding the relationship between office leasing, tenant demand, occupancy, rental income and the quality of the assets held by a REIT.India's office market enters a new phaseThe scale of India's office market provides context for this shift. According to JLL's January 2026 report, India's Office Market Scales Unprecedented Highs, gross office leasing across the country's top seven cities reached 83.3 million square feet in 2025, an increase of 7.8% over the previous year. Net absorption, which measures the net change in occupied office space, reached 57 million square feet, the highest annual level recorded in the report.GCCs were an important contributor to this activity. JLL reported that these centres leased approximately 31.4 million square feet during 2025, accounting for 37.7% of gross office leasing. This represented an increase of 13.1% over 2024.The figures point to a commercial real estate market supported by more than one source of demand. Global businesses are expanding their Indian operations, while domestic companies and flexible workspace operators are also competing for office space.CBRE India's March 2026 report, Decoding the GCC Surge: Insights into India's Transforming Workspace Landscape, similarly identifies GCC expansion as a major influence on office demand. Its analysis found that GCCs leased more than 100 million square feet between 2022 and 2025, accounting for approximately 39% of total office leasing in 2025.For commercial property owners, the significance extends beyond the amount of space leased. The nature of occupier demand, the quality of buildings sought and the duration of leasing commitments can all influence the stability of a property's rental income.Why global capability centres need a different kind of workspaceThe evolution of GCCs is changing the conversation around office space.As these centres take on more specialised functions, companies may require facilities that support collaboration, technology infrastructure, security, employee experience and access to skilled talent. Location also matters, with businesses evaluating connectivity, the availability of suitable office buildings and proximity to relevant talent pools.This can create opportunities for owners of well-located, professionally managed office properties. However, the benefits are not distributed evenly across every building or market. Companies can choose between locations, negotiate lease terms and reconsider their space requirements as business conditions change.For REITs, the implications depend on the assets they own and their ability to attract and retain tenants.A property in a strong office market may still face challenges if it is poorly located, requires substantial investment or cannot meet occupiers' expectations. Conversely, an established building with competitive amenities, efficient operations and access to talent may be better positioned to attract businesses seeking long-term space.The key is to distinguish the broader growth of GCCs from the performance of an individual property portfolio. A growing sector creates potential demand, but it does not guarantee occupancy, rental growth or investment returns for every REIT.From office leasing to rental income: The connection investors should understandCorporate leasing activity is relevant to REIT investors because rent is one of the principal sources of income generated by commercial properties.When a company leases office space, the agreement establishes the contractual terms under which the property owner receives rent. The impact on a REIT's financial performance depends on factors such as the size of the lease, the agreed rental rate, the lease duration, rent escalation provisions and the costs associated with operating the property.Occupancy is an important indicator in this equation. Higher occupancy can support rental receipts, while vacancies may reduce income and increase the costs associated with finding replacement tenants. But occupancy should not be assessed in isolation: the rental rates secured, tenant quality, lease expiries and incentives offered to tenants also matter.Rental growth is another factor worth examining. Where market conditions permit, property owners may secure higher rents when new leases are signed or existing agreements are renewed. Yet rental growth can vary considerably between cities, micro-markets and buildings. A rise in average office rents across a city does not mean that every property will achieve the same increase.Investors should therefore examine the operating performance of the specific REIT rather than rely solely on headline office-market statistics.Quarterly results and annual reports can help establish whether leasing momentum is translating into sustained rental income, improved occupancy and stronger cash flows. They can also reveal whether performance is being affected by vacancies, operating expenses, capital expenditure or changes in tenant concentration.Why location continues to matterIndia's commercial real estate market is spread across several major office hubs, including Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Pune, Chennai and Kolkata. Each market has its own mix of occupiers, available supply, infrastructure and rental dynamics.JLL's 2025 office-market analysis found that Bengaluru accounted for 29% of annual gross leasing, followed by Delhi NCR at 20.9%. Mumbai and Hyderabad each accounted for 14% of the total. These figures illustrate the different contributions of major cities to the country's office market.For investors, city-level trends are only the starting point. Office performance can vary substantially within the same city, depending on connectivity, proximity to talent, competing supply and the quality of the commercial district.A REIT with properties across several locations may have exposure to different economic and leasing conditions. This can help diversify its sources of rental income, although diversification does not eliminate the risks associated with a downturn in office demand or changes in corporate leasing behaviour.The geographical composition of a portfolio should therefore be considered alongside its tenant mix, occupancy levels and lease maturity profile.What happens if office demand slows?The GCC story is encouraging for India's commercial real estate sector, but it should not be interpreted as a one-way growth trajectory.Corporate leasing decisions are influenced by business confidence, economic conditions, technology, workforce planning and the cost of occupying space. Companies may consolidate offices, delay expansion or redesign their workplaces. Changes in the use of artificial intelligence and other technologies may also influence future staffing and workspace requirements, although the scale and timing of these effects will vary by business.New office supply is another consideration. If additional space enters a market faster than occupier demand grows, landlords may face greater competition for tenants. This can influence occupancy, leasing incentives and rental growth.For REITs, the effect depends on the resilience of the existing portfolio and the trust's ability to manage vacancies, renew leases and maintain operating efficiency. Debt levels, financing costs and planned capital expenditure also affect how much cash is ultimately available to investors.These risks make it important to look beyond gross leasing figures. Market-wide demand may remain healthy even as individual buildings experience vacancies or pressure on rents.What should REIT investors track?Investors assessing the relationship between India's office-market growth and REIT performance can focus on five indicators.Occupancy levels: Are the properties maintaining or improving the proportion of space occupied by tenants? Persistent vacancies can affect rental receipts.Lease expiries and renewals: When do major leases expire, and how much rental income depends on a limited number of tenants? A concentrated expiry schedule may increase uncertainty around future cash flows.Rental growth: Are new leases and renewals being concluded at competitive rates? Headline city-wide rental growth should be compared with the performance disclosed by the individual trust.Tenant concentration: How dependent is the portfolio on a few large occupiers, sectors or geographical markets? A diversified tenant base can reduce dependence on any single company, although it cannot remove broader market risk.Financial performance and valuation: Are operating income and distributable cash flows developing sustainably? Investors should also assess borrowing, refinancing requirements, capital expenditure and the market price of units relative to the disclosed value of the underlying assets.These indicators help connect the macroeconomic story to the investment itself. The expansion of GCCs may support demand for quality offices, but the financial outcome for unitholders depends on the performance, management and valuation of the assets held by the REIT.The bigger picture: Commercial real estate as an evolving investment opportunityIndia's expanding role in global business operations is creating a new context for its office market. GCCs are taking on more sophisticated responsibilities, companies continue to evaluate their Indian footprints, and demand for suitable commercial space is influenced by changing business requirements.For the REIT market, this creates a potential opportunity to participate in the underlying economics of professionally managed commercial property through listed units rather than direct ownership.Yet the investment case is not simply that more companies need offices. Individual properties must attract tenants, secure competitive leases, manage costs, and sustain cash generation over time.That distinction is central to evaluating REITs. Strong office leasing can provide a favourable market backdrop, but it does not automatically translate into higher distributions or rising unit prices. Investors still need to examine the underlying portfolio, its financial performance, and the price at which they invest.As India's commercial real estate market evolves, the most useful question for investors is not just how much office space companies are leasing, but how effectively that demand is being converted into durable rental income and long-term property value.Primary research and regulatory sourcesJLL, India Office Market Dynamics Q2 2026, 31 August 2026: Read the research. title: Rental income without owning a property: Understanding the REIT investment proposition | Real Estate News
description: Listed Real Estate Investment Trusts offer investors a route into income-generating commercial real estate without the responsibilities of direct ownership.  | Real Estate News
content: For generations, owning property has been closely associated with financial security in India. A residential apartment that appreciates or a commercial unit that generates monthly rent can be an important part of a household's wealth. Yet direct property ownership comes with a significant financial commitment, ongoing maintenance and the responsibility of finding and managing tenants.For investors interested in real estate but looking for an alternative to purchasing and managing a property themselves, Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) offer a different approach.Listed REITs allow investors to buy units in a trust that owns or invests in income-generating real estate. Instead of purchasing an individual office space or retail property, investors gain exposure to a portfolio of assets managed professionally. The units trade on stock exchanges, making the investment accessible through the securities market, subject to prevailing prices and liquidity.The proposition is straightforward: participate in the economic activity generated by commercial property without taking on the responsibilities of being a direct landlord. Understanding how that proposition translates into investment returns, however, requires a closer look at how REITs operate.How does a REIT generate income?A REIT's underlying properties can generate revenue by leasing space to businesses and other tenants. Office buildings, business parks and retail properties, for instance, earn rental income through lease agreements.The cash generated by these assets does not automatically translate into an equivalent amount for investors. Property operating expenses, financing obligations, capital expenditure and other costs influence how much cash is available for distribution.In India, REITs operate under the regulatory framework established by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Under Regulation 18(16) of the SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, at least 90% of the net distributable cash flows of a REIT must be distributed to its unitholders, subject to applicable legal provisions. The regulations also prescribe distribution requirements at the underlying special-purpose vehicle and holding-company levels. SEBI's regulations and subsequent amendments set out the applicable framework.This requirement is an important feature of the REIT structure, but it should not be mistaken for a guaranteed income stream. The amount available for distribution depends on the cash generated by the assets and the expenses and obligations of the trust. If rental receipts weaken, costs rise or financing becomes more expensive, the cash available for distribution may be affected.The distinction between a regulatory distribution requirement and a guaranteed investment return is fundamental to understanding REITs.What do investors actually receive?Investors in listed REITs may receive periodic distributions from the trust. These payments can comprise different components, depending on the nature of the underlying cash flows and the applicable structure.A distribution is not necessarily equivalent to rental income from a property owned directly by an individual. In direct ownership, the landlord receives rent under a lease agreement, subject to vacancies, expenses and contractual terms. In a REIT, the investor's entitlement arises through the trust's distribution mechanism, which reflects the financial performance of the portfolio and the relevant regulatory requirements.Investors should therefore examine more than the headline amount distributed. The frequency of payments, the composition of distributions, the trust's financial position and its ability to sustain cash flows all matter.Tax treatment is another consideration. Different components of REIT distributions may be subject to different tax provisions, depending on their nature and the investor's circumstances. Investors should review the relevant disclosures and seek professional tax advice rather than assume that every distribution is taxed in the same way.Most importantly, a distribution should not be viewed in isolation from the price paid for the units. A trust may make distributions while its unit price declines. The investor's overall return depends on the distributions received and the change in the market value of the investment, after accounting for applicable costs and taxes.Rental income is only one part of the investment storyThe performance of a REIT is closely connected to the quality and financial productivity of its underlying properties.Occupancy is one indicator worth examining. Properties with a high proportion of occupied space may be better positioned to generate rental income, although occupancy alone does not establish the quality or sustainability of cash flows.Lease structures also matter. The duration of leases, the timing of expiries, contractual rent escalations and the concentration of tenants can influence the stability of income. A portfolio facing substantial lease expiries in a short period, for example, may be more exposed to changes in market rents or delays in securing replacement tenants.Property location and tenant demand are equally relevant. An office portfolio's performance can be affected by corporate leasing decisions, while retail assets may respond to tenant sales, footfall and consumer spending. Changes in the local supply of commercial space can also influence occupancy and rental growth.These factors explain why investors should look beyond the broad label of commercial real estate. Two REITs can have different risk profiles even if both invest in office properties, because their tenants, locations, lease terms, financing and valuations may differ.Quarterly financial results, annual reports and stock-exchange disclosures provide the information needed to assess these differences.REITs versus direct property ownershipThe choice between investing in a REIT and buying property depends on an investor's objectives, resources and willingness to manage risk.Direct ownership gives the individual control over a particular property and its use, subject to legal and contractual restrictions. It can also involve substantial upfront capital, transaction expenses, maintenance, vacancy risk and the time required to sell.REITs provide exposure to a portfolio rather than a single property. Investors do not need to manage tenants or oversee building maintenance themselves, and listed units can generally be traded through a stock exchange. However, the price at which units can be sold depends on market conditions and available liquidity.The two approaches also behave differently in terms of valuation. Direct property transactions can take time, with the eventual selling price influenced by local demand, negotiations and transaction costs. REIT units are marked to market through exchange trading, meaning prices can fluctuate from day to day as investors respond to interest rates, earnings expectations and broader market sentiment.Neither approach is inherently superior in every situation. Direct ownership may suit someone seeking control over a specific asset and able to manage the associated responsibilities. A REIT may be worth evaluating for someone seeking professionally managed exposure to commercial property through a listed investment.The relevant question is which structure better fits the investor's financial goals and risk tolerance.The risks investors should not overlookThe appeal of rental-backed cash flows should not obscure the risks associated with REITs.Interest-rate sensitivity: Changes in interest rates can affect borrowing costs, refinancing requirements and the relative attractiveness of income-generating securities. Higher financing expenses may put pressure on cash flows, while changes in market yields can influence unit valuations.Occupancy and rental risk: Vacancies, tenant departures, delayed leasing and weaker rental demand can reduce income. Even properties in established commercial locations are exposed to changes in business requirements and market conditions.Valuation risk: The market price of a REIT unit can differ from the estimated value of its underlying assets. Investors should review disclosed net asset value alongside market price, financial performance and the assumptions used in property valuations.Leverage: Borrowing can help finance real estate assets, but it also creates repayment and refinancing obligations. Investors should assess the trust's debt levels, financing costs and maturity profile.Liquidity and volatility: Listed units offer a route to buying and selling, but liquidity is not unlimited. Investors may need to accept an unfavourable price when selling during volatile market conditions or periods of low trading activity.SEBI's REIT regulatory framework provides the rules governing the structure, disclosures and operations of these investment vehicles. Investors should read the applicable regulations alongside the offer document and ongoing disclosures of the individual REIT they are considering.What should investors check before investing?A disciplined evaluation can begin with a few practical questions.First, what properties does the REIT own or invest in, and how diversified is the portfolio across locations and tenants? Second, are occupancy levels, leasing activity and rental income broadly stable? Third, what does the trust's distribution history reveal, and how does the composition of those payments affect the investor's understanding of income?Investors should also examine the market price relative to the disclosed net asset value, the trust's borrowing position, capital expenditure requirements and upcoming lease expiries. Comparing these indicators across periods can help distinguish recurring operating performance from one-off developments.The investor's own circumstances matter just as much. Money needed for near-term expenses may not be appropriate for an investment whose market price can fluctuate. Those already exposed to property through their home, business or other assets should also consider whether another real estate-linked investment genuinely improves portfolio diversification.The aim is not to find a REIT that promises the highest distribution, but to understand the relationship between the price paid, the cash flows generated, the risks undertaken and the investor's financial objectives.An income proposition that calls for careful evaluationREITs have introduced a listed route into commercial real estate for investors who may not want to purchase an entire property. Their structure combines exposure to rental-generating assets with professional management and a regulatory framework governing distributions and disclosures.But the underlying economics remain important. Rental income depends on tenants, occupancy and lease terms. Distributions depend on available cash flows and applicable obligations. Unit prices respond to both property fundamentals and wider market conditions.For investors considering this asset class, the starting point should be a clear understanding of how the trust generates cash, what it distributes and what could affect future performance.The appeal of participating in commercial real estate without becoming a landlord is understandable. Making an informed investment decision, however, requires looking beyond the promise of rental-backed income to the complete picture of valuation, risk and return.Primary sourcesSEBI, SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, last amended 18 April 2026: Read the regulations. Explains the framework for computing net distributable cash flows at REIT and underlying entity levels.SEBI, REIT investor education: Understanding REITs and InvITs. An introductory resource for understanding the investment structure and investor considerations.Note to the reader: This article has been produced on behalf of the brand by HT Brand Studio and does not have journalistic/editorial involvement of Hindustan Times.

title: Beyond gold and property: Could REITs find a place in India's festive investment portfolio? | Real Estate News
description: As investors revisit their financial goals during the festive season, listed REITs offer another way to access income-generating commercial property.  | Real Estate News
content: For many Indian households, the festive season is a time to celebrate, spend and make financial decisions. Gold purchases, property enquiries and fresh investments often become part of the annual conversation about wealth creation. But as investment choices expand, another question is emerging: can investors participate in the potential of real estate without committing a substantial sum to buying a property?Listed Real Estate Investment Trusts, or REITs, offer one possible route.Unlike traditional property ownership, which can require a large upfront investment and involve responsibilities such as maintenance, tenant management and resale, REITs allow investors to buy units in a trust that owns and operates income-generating real estate. The units are listed on stock exchanges, allowing investors to buy and sell them through the market, subject to prevailing prices and liquidity.According to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), REITs are pooled investment vehicles that enable investors to participate in real estate without directly owning physical property. Their listed structure provides an alternative for investors interested in the asset class but who may not wish to purchase an entire office building, business park or shopping centre themselves.For investors considering their festive-season financial decisions, the distinction is important. REITs change the way individuals can access commercial real estate, although they do not eliminate the risks associated with property markets or investing in listed securities.A different route into real estateReal estate has traditionally been associated with direct ownership. Buying a residential property or commercial unit can involve a significant financial commitment, transaction costs and ongoing responsibilities. Selling the property may also take time, depending on market conditions and buyer demand.A REIT offers a different structure. It pools investors' money into a trust that owns or invests in real estate assets, with a professional manager overseeing the portfolio. Investors purchase units representing their interest in the trust rather than acquiring an individual property.SEBI's investor education material explains that REIT units are listed and traded on stock exchanges, much like shares of listed companies. This gives investors an avenue to participate in real estate without managing a property themselves.The structure can also make the investment accessible at a lower initial amount than direct property ownership, depending on the unit price and the number of units purchased. However, accessibility should not be confused with safety. The value of listed units can fluctuate, and investors may receive less than their purchase price when they sell.Understanding where the returns come fromThe investment proposition of a REIT rests on the performance of its underlying assets and the financial structure through which those assets are held and managed.Commercial properties can generate rental income from tenants occupying office spaces, retail establishments and other eligible real estate assets. After accounting for relevant expenses and obligations, the trust may distribute income to its unitholders in accordance with applicable regulations.SEBI's REIT regulations prescribe distribution requirements for net distributable cash flows. Under the regulatory framework, a REIT is generally required to distribute at least 90% of its net distributable cash flows to unitholders, subject to the applicable provisions.This requirement is an important feature of the structure, but it should not be interpreted as a guarantee of a particular income amount or investment return. The cash available for distribution depends on the performance of the assets, rental receipts, expenses, financing costs and other relevant factors.Investors may also benefit from capital appreciation if the market price of their units rises. Conversely, units can lose value. Returns therefore depend on both the financial performance of the trust and the price at which an investor buys and sells.Why the festive season can be a moment to reassess investmentsThe festive season is not, in itself, a reason to expect better REIT returns. There is no assurance that purchasing units during Diwali or another festive period will produce superior performance.Its relevance is more practical. For many households, this period offers an opportunity to review annual spending, consider the use of bonuses or surplus savings, and revisit longer-term financial goals.For those exploring real estate exposure, REITs can broaden the conversation beyond buying a residential property. Direct property ownership may involve a substantial down payment, transaction costs, maintenance and a potentially lengthy resale process. Listed REIT units, by contrast, can be purchased through a demat and trading account, with the investment amount determined by the prevailing unit price and the quantity purchased.This accessibility does not make REITs risk-free or automatically suitable for every investor. A household saving for a near-term expense, for instance, has different requirements from someone building a long-term portfolio. The ability to sell listed units also depends on market liquidity and the price available at the time of sale.Investors should therefore consider their time horizon, cash requirements and tolerance for market fluctuations before making a decision.What should investors examine before buying?A closer look at the underlying assets and financial disclosures can help investors move beyond headline distribution figures and assess the investment more carefully.The underlying property portfolioInvestors should examine the type, location and quality of the assets held by a trust. An office-focused portfolio may respond differently to market conditions than one with significant retail exposure. Geographical concentration and dependence on a small number of large tenants can also influence risk.Occupancy and leasing trendsOccupancy levels, lease renewals and rental growth can offer insights into a property's income-generating capacity. Investors can review these indicators in a REIT's quarterly financial results, annual report and other exchange disclosures.Distributions and their compositionPast distributions provide useful context, but they are not a promise of future income. Investors should examine the amounts paid over time, the sources of those distributions and the applicable tax treatment. Different components may receive different tax treatment, so investors should consult current disclosures and seek professional tax advice where necessary.Valuation and borrowingA strong property portfolio does not automatically make its units attractive at every price. Investors should assess the market price alongside disclosed net asset value, financial performance and the trust's borrowing position. Higher financing costs or refinancing pressures can affect financial flexibility and the cash available for distribution.Liquidity and market riskListed units offer an avenue to buy and sell through an exchange, but the execution price may differ from an investor's expectations. Trading volumes, market conditions and price volatility matter, particularly when an investor may need the money at a specific time.SEBI's investor education resources and the disclosures published by individual REITs provide useful starting points for understanding the structure, regulatory requirements and risks associated with these investments.An alternative, not a replacement for every investmentGold, residential property, fixed-income products and equity investments serve different purposes in a household's financial plan. REITs should be evaluated in the same way: according to their role in the portfolio, rather than the popularity of a particular investment during the festive season.For an investor seeking exposure to commercial real estate, a listed REIT may offer a way to participate without the financial commitment and operational responsibilities of direct property ownership. For someone who needs predictable access to money in the near term, the market-linked nature of REIT units may be less appropriate.Diversification also requires looking at the risks that investments share. Someone whose income, business interests or existing assets are already closely tied to property may not necessarily gain meaningful diversification by adding another real estate-linked investment.The starting point, therefore, is not how much to invest during the festive season, but what the investment is intended to achieve.A more informed approach to festive investingREITs provide Indian investors with a regulated route to participate in commercial real estate without directly purchasing and managing an entire property. Their listed structure, underlying rental-generating assets and prescribed distribution framework distinguish them from direct property ownership, while their market-linked nature introduces risks that investors need to understand.The decision to invest should follow an assessment of the underlying assets, financial disclosures, valuation, distribution history and personal financial goals.Festive investing need not mean adding another product to a portfolio simply because the season encourages spending and financial activity. It can instead be an opportunity to understand unfamiliar asset classes, compare alternatives and make decisions with a clearer view of both potential returns and risks.For those considering REITs, the most useful festive investment may be the time spent understanding how the structure works before committing money to it.Primary source referencesSEBI Investor Education: Understanding REITs and InvITs — the structure of REITs, listed trading, potential income and investor considerations.SEBI: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, last amended on 18 April 2026 — regulatory framework, investment conditions and distribution requirements.SEBI: Master Circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts, 11 July 2025 — operational requirements and disclosures.SEBI: Investor Charter for Real Estate Investment Trusts, 12 June 2025 — investor rights and responsibilities.Note to the reader: This article has been produced on behalf of the brand by HT Brand Studio and does not have journalistic/editorial involvement of Hindustan Times.

title: High fees leaves over 800 MBBS seats vacant in deemed universities across TN, Puducherry | Hindustan Times
description: High fees leaves over 800 MBBS seats vacant in deemed universities across TN, Puducherry
content: Chennai, More than 800 medical seats remain vacant across deemed universities in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry after the final counselling held for NEET UG 2026, sources said on Thursday.High tuition fees have led to this situation, say educationists and industry experts.According to Medical Counselling Committee sources, of the total 837 unfilled MBBS seats across the country , 824 were vacant in deemed universities in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry alone.Educationists criticised the lack of a fee cap for deemed universities and pointed out that high-scoring NEET candidates are forced to forgo these seats simply because they cannot afford the exorbitant fees, thereby defeating the core purpose of conducting a merit-based national entrance examination.Senior educationist and State Platform for Common School System – Tamil Nadu general secretary P B Prince Gajendra Babu told PTI that the high scorer in NEET, whose financial position does not permit them to get admitted to such private institutions with a high fee, simply opts out. Such candidates do not apply for the counselling."The lesser scorer who is financially sound applies and secures the seat," he said, adding, "NEET failed in both of its objectives neither ensure merit nor curb commercialisation of medical education."He said all private medical education institutions, including those deemed to be universities that cannot reduce their fee structure and keep the seats unfilled, must be closed."The state governments should be encouraged to open an adequate number of medical colleges wherever needed," he added.Industry experts cite the excessive annual tuition fees as the main driver behind the low intake.A Srinath, a higher education career counsellor for the students in the city, claimed annual MBBS fees in deemed universities across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry range between ₹25 lakh and ₹35 lakh per year."The students have to pay hostel and mess fees between ₹1.2 lakh and ₹2.5 lakh per year in private institutions. In contrast, the average annual fee across other parts of India in private institutions stands at around ₹17 lakh, resulting in a substantial fee disparity over the four and a half year duration of the course," he said.With the seats remaining unfilled, an additional round of counselling may be expected. The MCC will take a decision in this regard. "However, it is unclear till now," he added.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: An open letter to Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Tamil Nadu's future | Hindustan Times
description: This article is authored by C Raj Kumar, Founding Vice Chancellor, OP Jindal Global University and President, World University Leaders Forum.
content: Dear Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, I am writing this letter as a Tamilian who was born and raised in Kanyakumari, educated in schools in Kanyakumari, Vellore, and Chennai, and had the privilege of studying at Loyola College, Madras. Later, I pursued my higher studies at the University of Delhi, University of Oxford, Harvard University and the University of Hong Kong. I left the city of Chennai more than 30 years ago for various educational and professional pursuits in India and around the world.Despite that, wherever I have lived and worked, I have always nurtured the hopes of Tamil Nadu and its people and society deep within me: The faith and emphasis on education, the historical commitment to contributing to human dignity, and the relentless pursuit of fulfilling aspirations that have created opportunities for every generation.I also write to you as a fellow Loyolite whose path crossed yours, albeit briefly. I joined Loyola in 1991 and completed my BCom degree in 1994. My time at Loyola briefly overlapped with your time studying visual communication. Yet the issues that I plan to discuss are matters of public importance. Let me begin by congratulating you on garnering the trust of the people of Tamil Nadu through a democratic process and assuming leadership as the Chief Minister (CM) of Tamil Nadu. Never before in the history of Tamil Nadu, and rarely in the history of India, has an elected CM who was not predicted to win gained that high office purely because of the mandate of the people of Tamil Nadu.Your readiness to shed the comfort and the natural security of a celebrated career needs to be appreciated. Your entry into public life required you to prepare yourself for intense scrutiny, uncertainty and onerous responsibility that your stardom and fame alone could never prepare you for. I would like to believe that this confidence will become the foundation for a government that earns trust through everyday administration and efforts to contribute to good governance.In this spirit, I am offering you four suggestions.Make integrity an institutional culture of governance: Throughout your campaign, you emphasised the need for a corruption-free government. The harder task now for you is this: After your victory, how will you run a government that will confront these practices, discourage the incentives, and undermine the vested interests that have allowed and enabled corruption as an accepted form of institutional governance? While personal integrity undoubtedly creates confidence in the leader, institutional integrity is the only way to ensure that decisions taken in government are fair and transparent, even when the leader is not present. For the people of Tamil Nadu, corruption most often attacks their personal dignity. This could take different forms and manifestations: unofficial payments for obtaining a birth certificate, a bribe to obtain a driving licence, an intermediary demanding payment for an entitlement, speed money to fast-track permissions, approvals or licences, or an unexplained delay that disappears when money changes hands.A credible and robust reform agenda must address these day-to-day encounters of ordinary citizens with the government machinery. You have a responsibility to make transparency a habit. You need to work towards making procurement transparent, appointments fair, and public services time-bound.There is a need to build robust, independent scrutiny while protecting whistleblowers and those who report wrongdoing. Publication of this information will enable citizens to monitor public expenditure and, in the process, help you and join hands with you in providing clean administration.This principle of accountability also needs to be shared with your colleagues in the party, partners in the political coalition, and other political appointees. The nature of coalition politics in a democracy will, on many occasions, require negotiations. I can only hope that they never lead you to walk away from the principles on which public trust has been reposed in you as you establish these important boundaries. The message that you want to convey is that proximity to the CM does not secure immunity from any form of scrutiny.Your greatest contribution, and indeed a significant legacy, could be the establishment of a culture of governance in which integrity and honesty become the natural way of government, guiding public institutions and government officials in the exercise of power.Become a more accessible CM: The past life you lived had indeed created a distance. Individuals saw you on theatre screens, watched your performances with admiration, and found hope and inspiration in the stories you brought to life. For many years, people knew you as a celebrated actor and admired you for the characters you portrayed on screen. Heroism is indeed powerful, but much of this admiration was experienced from a distance. The relationship between an actor and his admirers is fundamentally different from the relationship between a political leader and the people he represents. Democratic politics alters the contours of that relationship; the people of Tamil Nadu, who have entrusted you with power, naturally seek opportunities to speak. They want to be heard and to influence decisions that may be impacting their lives. Their dreams and aspirations now relate to employment, education, health, infrastructure, improved quality of governance in administration, and, most importantly, their ability to be heard by those who hold power. The fact of the matter is this: You won the election as the leader of a party. But after having become the CM of Tamil Nadu, you now serve as the CM for every person in your state, including those who did not vote for you and probably those who were not convinced about your politics. They have an equal claim on your attention. You want to create numerous concentric and related circles of engagement that transcend your closest colleagues; there is a case for drawing in elected representatives, scholars, media representatives, civil society, entrepreneurs, organisation officials, private sector representatives, farmers, workers and citizens across the political, economic, social and ideological constituencies. There are various ways by which this can be done. There is a case for consultations; visits to various districts with somewhat unscripted exchanges and conversations; more organised and accessible public hearings; reliable grievance redressal mechanisms; and opportunities to consult with all stakeholders, especially for important governance decisions. While digital forms of communication can broaden participation, please remember that there are people without connectivity or technological confidence who ought to have other opportunities, ways, and means to connect with your work. I recognise that no CM can meet everybody. At the same time, everybody should nevertheless feel that the government is reachable, that a petition sent will receive reasonable cognisance, at times a responsible reply, and on appropriate occasions a deliverable remedy.Citizens ought to have the freedom to share with you an uncomfortable truth, offer an unfamiliar idea, or even challenge a decision. Such candour can only strengthen your government. A reputation for accessibility gives your political leadership the moral foundations critical to democratic politics.Expand the intellectual foundations of your government:The future of Tamil Nadu will need substantive thought leadership about public finance, education and employment for youth, health and health infrastructure, urban planning and urban development, the development of new infrastructure, including transport and mobility, and environmental resilience. Your political commitments and electoral promises ought to set the direction of policy, led by you as the CM. You need to increase the intellectual gravitas of your government substantially. Please consider surrounding yourself with people who are capable of asking difficult questions, intellectually challenging a government's public policy choices, examining evidence, and explaining the various trade-offs the government will constantly have to make. This expertise ought to be welcomed even when it at times complicates a decision or delays a course of action.It is important for you to know that as you rise higher in political and public life, there are greater possibilities of being surrounded by people who are mostly going to agree with you, will endorse your decisions without question, and will work towards further reinforcing your own beliefs, ideas, and even convictions. I suggest that you consciously develop alternative channels of communication and even consultations, which may be, at times, informal and even private with individuals who are not necessarily found in the corridors of power or within the predictable and familiar circles of political, bureaucratic, and administrative influence. I believe that some of the most valuable and relevant perspectives might come from somewhat unconventional thinkers, academics, independent minds, and other individuals who have neither a position of power nor a favour to seek from you.You need people in your circle who have the intellectual independence and autonomy to speak their mind and the personal courage of conviction to tell you when they believe that you may not be right. These conversations, I believe, can help you challenge assumptions, at times even recognise mistakes, make course corrections, discover new possibilities, and also appreciate that formal structures of government may not always reveal the full truth.There is a case for you to consider the involvement of people beyond political party affiliations and ideological limitations. Individuals such as Professor Raghuram Rajan and Dr Palanivel Thiaga Rajan are great examples of the knowledge, experience, expertise, and intellect that Tamil Nadu can draw upon. Professor Rajan's intellectual leadership, scholarship, and central banking experience offer important perspectives that will be highly relevant to your government. Dr PTR's own contribution and experience in finance and government deserve strong engagement regardless of political differences.There is a need for looking beyond economics: Educators, scientists, technology specialists, public health professionals, lawyers, entrepreneurs, innovators, and experienced administrators who can contribute to better policy. There is a case for you to induct practitioners who understand why even the best public policy programs sometimes do not achieve their objectives and end up failing.At the level of delivery, the diasporic Tamilian expertise is not only limited to its locality and locale within the state of Tamil Nadu. People who may be working in other parts of India and internationally may be happy to welcome the opportunity to contribute to your leadership and vision. There is a need to build channels of communication through which their experience and expertise can serve your state without requiring political affiliation or physical relocation.Every department in your government needs to seek knowledge from outside, share experiences, and even recognise mistakes early so that the possibility for change remains not just an aspiration but a lived responsibility throughout the evolution of your administration. Technical expertise should help you strengthen democratic judgment, while the final responsibility will remain with you and your colleagues in your cabinet. There is a case for bringing new expertise even within the cabinet.Build partnerships in the private sector with a focus on education: You need to engage closely with enlightened businesses, thoughtful entrepreneurs, universities, and philanthropic institutions through transparent collaborations which are directed towards clearly defined public outcomes. In this regard, education provides a significant point of convergence. Connect with schools, colleges, and universities on research and development, emerging innovations and technologies, and well-established organisational practices.The emerging needs of business: Bring the students to the heart and centre of your governance. Bring together the young people of Tamil Nadu so that these partnerships improve, create internship opportunities, and establish an entrepreneurial environment that leads to meaningful employment.You need to prioritise accessibility and make it central to your reform agenda. A young person's aspiration to benefit from innovation should not depend solely on family income, location, disability, or, for that matter, familiarity with a particular language. There is a strong case for promoting scholarships, affordable programmes, educational accessibility, technological access, and robust pathways from rural institutions, which can help ensure that progress reaches those most likely to be suffering from exclusion. Build on institutions and initiatives that have worked well. There is a case for public and private institutions to come together to promote constructive dialogue, thereby establishing and benchmarking new standards of accountability. This ought to be done while your government retains the responsibility for equity, quality, and accountability.CM Vijay, these ideas and perspectives come from me because of the affection that I have for the state that shaped me, and I have hopes for the responsibilities you now carry. I believe the integrity you have demonstrated can protect public trust. Accessibility can deepen it, but only through expertise and purposeful collaboration can these ideas translate into lasting impact.More than 30 years after leaving Tamil Nadu, I still believe that its promise and its future are a personal responsibility. I fervently hope that your leadership will give that commitment a fuller and more meaningful expression. It will allow the citizens of Tamil Nadu to experience dignity and fairness in their interactions with the government and its instrumentalities, including government officials exercising power.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by C Raj Kumar, Founding Vice Chancellor, OP Jindal Global University and President, World University Leaders Forum.

title: Cafe owner death: Prime suspect model, 2 others brought to Lucknow from Nagpur | Hindustan Times
description: Cafe owner death: Prime suspect model, 2 others brought to Lucknow from Nagpur
content: Lucknow, Police brought model Shraddha Dubey, the prime suspect in the alleged murder of cafe owner Shiva Sharma, along with her sister Rashmi Dubey and driver Danish, to the Hazratganj police station in Lucknow, officials said on Thursday.The three were arrested in Nagpur on Tuesday and subsequently transported to Lucknow after a court there granted their transit remand to the Uttar Pradesh Police, officials said.Sharma died after allegedly falling from the balcony of an apartment in the Balu Adda area under the Hazratganj police station limits on October 9.His mother lodged a murder case against Shraddha, alleging that her son was assaulted and tortured before being thrown from the apartment.Initially, the police treated the incident as an accidental death, but they later registered a murder case following the family's allegations.Shraddha had been on the run since the incident and was arrested in Nagpur. The police had announced a reward of ₹50,000 for information leading to the arrest of Shraddha, her sister, and Danish.The police are questioning the three accused to ascertain the sequence of events leading to Sharma's death, officials said.In videos circulated on social media, Shraddha has denied involvement in Sharma's death and claimed that he jumped from the balcony after going into a bathroom at her residence. She has also alleged that he was under a debt of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh and had threatened to end his life if he failed to repay it.She has maintained that CCTV footage would establish what happened and denied allegations of assault or torture.An audio recording circulating on social media purportedly captures a conversation in which Sharma admits to taking and selling jewellery belonging to Shraddha. She is heard claiming that the jewellery was worth around ₹6 lakh and asking when the money would be returned.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: A daughter comes home, Bengalis celebrate, and the 48 minutes that mark a moment of divine power: The many emotions that make Durga Pujo special | Hindustan Times
description: Maa Durga arrives at her maternal home with her children, Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik and Ganesh. Legend says Mahadev follows her secretly because he misses her.
content: Durga Pujo is not just a festival but a rollercoaster of emotions, with Bengalis across the world experiencing joy, nostalgia and grief all at once. It is that time of the year when devotees wait for their daughter to come home for a few days, and during those days, time seems to stop. Everything else can wait; it’s time for Pujo - The network you are trying to reach is on a Pujo break.Maa Durga arrives at her maternal home with her children, Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik and Ganesh. There is also a popular belief that her husband, Mahadev, follows her without her knowledge because he misses her so much.ALSO READ: Is Karma always fair? 5 myths that might challenge what you think you know about karma, and why good actions matterAccording to popular folklore, the rituals begin with Maa Durga resting under a Bel tree before continuing her journey from Kailash to her maternal home. The folklore says that during her journey, she rests under the Bel tree on Shoshthi, the sixth day of Navratri. This is why the day is also known as Bel Shoshthi.On the day of Saptami, she is welcomed with delicacies, gifts, and everything that makes a daughter’s homecoming special. Basically, it is a celebration of a daughter being home, and no stone is left unturned. Devotees also perform aarti and offer bhog to Maa Durga.Then comes Ashtami, considered one of the most significant days of Durga Pujo. A 48-minute period, known as Sandhi Pujo, marks the transition from Maha Ashtami to Maha Navami. During this time, Maa Durga is worshipped in her fierce Chamunda form, one of the most powerful manifestations of the goddess. According to the Devi Mahatmya, when the demon generals Chanda and Munda attack the goddess, a fierce form emerges from her forehead and defeats them. Priests who perform Durga Pujo say that the rituals performed during this 48-minute period are believed to calm Maa Durga in her fierce Chamunda form.According to Bengali Shakta traditions, Sandhi Pujo is performed during the 48-minute period that includes the final 24 minutes of Maha Ashtami and the first 24 minutes of Maha Navami.Elaborating on the same, Sidhharrth S Kumaar, Chief Astrologer at NumroVani, adds, “Sandhi Pujo reminds us that real change begins within us. As Bengalis welcome Maa Durga home as their daughter, they also look to her for strength and courage. Praying to her is not just about seeking protection, but also finding the courage to face the truth and make a change.”ALSO READ: What does it mean when someone passes away on Mahalaya? The spiritual meaning of dying on Sarva Pitru AmavasyaOnce Sandhi Pujo is over, devotees know it is time to start preparing to bid farewell to their Maa. As Navami begins, the countdown to next year’s Pujo starts. Now, isn’t that an emotional rollercoaster?Navami Pujo concludes with a yagna, marking the end of Maa Durga’s stay at her maternal home and the beginning of her journey back to Kailash. The Kola Bou, or Nabapatrika, is immersed at a time determined each year by the tithi, according to the Bengali Phool Panjika. Yet devotees continue to worship the idol and extend the celebrations, as if they are not ready to let go of their daughter just yet. The feeling of longing is much like the emotion felt during a daughter’s bidaai.Then comes Bijoya Dashami, when Maa Durga is prepared for her journey back to Kailash and offered sindoor and sweets before she leaves for her husband’s home. This ritual is popularly known as Shidoor Khela, during which married women apply vermilion to each other.After Shidoor Khela, the idol is immersed in water, with the hope that, no matter what happens, Maa Durga will surely return the next year. After the immersion, everyone sits down with their loved ones, spends time together, shares good food and leaves with an unspoken promise: “Aashche bochhor abar hobe!”ALSO READ: What tantra really teaches about Shakti, fear, and the power within, a spiritual expert explainsDisclaimer: The religious stories and rituals described in this article reflect cultural traditions and beliefs that may vary across communities. They are presented for cultural understanding and should not be taken as scientifically established claims.

title: ఏఐ హవా, భౌగోళిక ఉద్రిక్తతలు.. ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా లోహాలకు ఫుల్ డిమాండ్ | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: ఆర్టిఫిషియల్ ఇంటెలిజెన్స్ (ఏఐ) డేటా సెంటర్ల విస్తరణ, భౌగోళిక రాజకీయ ఉద్రిక్తతల వల్ల కాపర్, అల్యూమినియం వంటి కీలక లోహాలకు ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా విపరీతమైన కొరత ఏర్పడుతోందని వుడ్ మెకెంజీ సంస్థ తాజా నివేదికలో వెల్లడించింది. రాబోయే రోజుల్లో వీటికి గిరాకీ మరింత పెరుగుతుందని స్పష్టం చేసింది.
content: ఆర్టిఫిషియల్ ఇంటెలిజెన్స్ (ఏఐ) విప్లవంతో డేటా సెంటర్ల నిర్మాణం వేగవంతం కావడం, భౌగోళిక రాజకీయ ఉద్రిక్తతలు, పెరిగిన విద్యుత్ అవసరాలు అంతర్జాతీయ లోహ రంగాన్ని తీవ్రంగా ప్రభావితం చేస్తున్నాయి. లండన్ కేంద్రంగా పనిచేసే ప్రముఖ పరిశోధనా సంస్థ 'వుడ్ మెకెంజీ' విడుదల చేసిన తాజా నివేదిక ప్రకారం.. కాపర్ (రాగి), అల్యూమినియం, నికెల్, లిథియం వంటి వ్యూహాత్మక లోహాలకు ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా డిమాండ్ రికార్డు స్థాయిలో పెరుగుతోంది.పెరుగుతున్న డిమాండ్‌కు అనుగుణంగా గనుల నుంచి తోడే ఉత్పత్తి ప్రక్రియ, కొత్త ప్రాజెక్టుల నిర్మాణం సాగకపోవడంతో భవిష్యత్తులో లోహాల కొరత మరింత తీవ్రమయ్యే ప్రమాదముందని నిపుణులు హెచ్చరిస్తున్నారు.ఏఐ డేటా సెంటర్లు.. భారీగా పెరిగిన విద్యుత్, లోహాల వినియోగంప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా ఏఐ డేటా సెంటర్ ప్రాజెక్టుల సామర్థ్యం 250 గిగావాట్లకు (GW) పైగా చేరింది. ఇది గతేడాదితో పోలిస్తే మూడింతలు ఎక్కువ కావడం గమనార్హం. ఈ డేటా సెంటర్ల నిర్మాణానికే కాకుండా, వాటికి విద్యుత్ అందించే ట్రాన్స్‌మిషన్ నెట్‌వర్క్‌లు, సబ్‌స్టేషన్లు, విద్యుత్ ఉత్పత్తి కేంద్రాలకు సాధారణ వసతుల కంటే 3 నుంచి 4 రెట్లు ఎక్కువ లోహాలు అవసరమవుతున్నాయి.ఏఐ డేటా సెంటర్ల విద్యుత్ డిమాండ్ 2025 నుంచి 2030 మధ్య ఐదింతలు పెరిగి, 2035 నాటికి 1,000 టెరావాట్ అవర్లను (TWh) దాటుతుందని అంచనా. ఆసియా పసిఫిక్ ప్రాంతంలో 2030 నాటికి ఈ డిమాండ్ దాదాపు మూడు రెట్లు పెరగనుంది. విద్యుత్ గ్రిడ్ సమస్యల వల్ల జపాన్ వంటి దేశాల్లో డేటా సెంటర్ ఆపరేటర్లు మైక్రోగ్రిడ్లు, ఆఫ్-గ్రిడ్ విద్యుత్ మార్గాల వైపు మొగ్గు చూపుతున్నారు.కాపర్ ధరలు పైపైకి.. రికార్డు స్థాయికి ధరలుఅంతర్జాతీయ మార్కెట్లో శుద్ధి చేసిన కాపర్ (రాగి) సరఫరా దెబ్బతినడంతో టన్ను కాపర్ ధర రికార్డు స్థాయిలో 14,759 డాలర్లకు (USD) చేరింది. అమెరికా తన దేశీయ అవసరాల కోసం నిల్వలను 170 రోజులకు పైగా పెంచుకోవడంతో మిగతా ప్రపంచంలో తీవ్ర కొరత ఏర్పడింది. ఇతర దేశాల్లో నిల్వలు కేవలం 48 రోజులకు సరిపడా మాత్రమే మిగిలాయి. ఫలితంగా అంతర్జాతీయంగా 4,60,000 టన్నుల కాపర్ లోటు ఏర్పడింది.2026లో చిలీ గనుల ఉత్పత్తి 5.2 శాతం తగ్గినప్పటికీ, వచ్చే ఏడాది ప్రపంచ గనుల ఉత్పత్తి 5 శాతం కంటే ఎక్కువ పెరిగే అవకాశముంది. అయితే రాబోయే దశాబ్దంలో ఏటా 8,50,000 టన్నుల కొత్త కాపర్ ఉత్పత్తి సామర్థ్యాన్ని సాధించాల్సి ఉంది. అనుమతుల జాప్యం, భౌగోళిక రాజకీయ ముప్పుల కారణంగా కొత్త ప్రాజెక్టుల నిర్మాణం నెమ్మదిస్తోంది.అల్యూమినియం, నికెల్ మార్కెట్ల పరిస్థితిమధ్యప్రాచ్యంలో జరిగిన దాడుల వల్ల ప్రపంచంలోనే అతిపెద్ద అల్యూమినియం స్మెల్టర్లలో రెండింటికి తీవ్ర నష్టం వాటిల్లింది. దీనివల్ల ప్రపంచ ప్రాథమిక ఉత్పత్తిలో దాదాపు 2 శాతం కోతపడి, 2026లో 10 లక్షల టన్నుల కొరత ఏర్పడింది. చైనా తన ఉత్పత్తి సామర్థ్యాన్ని 99 శాతానికి పెంచినప్పటికీ, ఇండోనేషియా 13 లక్షల టన్నులు ఉత్పత్తి చేసినప్పటికీ ఈ లోటు భర్తీ కాలేదు. అయితే 2027 నాటికి అల్యూమినియం మార్కెట్ మళ్లీ మిగులు స్థితికి చేరుకుంటుందని నివేదిక పేర్కొంది.మరోవైపు నికెల్ మార్కెట్‌లో 2026లో శుద్ధి చేసిన లోహ ఉత్పత్తి 2 శాతం తగ్గుతోంది. 2015 తర్వాత నికెల్ ఉత్పత్తి తగ్గడం ఇదే తొలిసారి. ఇండోనేషియా ప్రభుత్వం మైనింగ్ కోటాలను తగ్గించడం, మైనింగ్ ప్రాంతాల్లో కరువు పరిస్థితులు నెలకొనడం వల్ల క్లాస్-2 నికెల్ లభ్యత తగ్గుతోంది. కొరతను తట్టుకోవడానికి చైనాకు చెందిన స్టెయిన్‌లెస్ స్టీల్ పరిశ్రమలు స్క్రాప్ వినియోగాన్ని పెంచుతున్నాయి. 2030 నాటికి నికెల్ ధర టన్నుకు 19,000 డాలర్లకు చేరుకోవచ్చని అంచనా.లిథియం, బ్యాటరీ రంగంలో విప్లవాత్మక మార్పులులిథియం కార్బోనేట్ ధరలు 2025 మధ్యలో నమోదైన కనిష్ఠ స్థాయిల నుంచి 2026 నాటికి 130 శాతం వరకు పెరిగాయి. గత దశాబ్దకాలంలో లిథియం సరఫరా వ్యవస్థలో 60 బిలియన్ డాలర్ల పెట్టుబడులు వచ్చాయి. 2050 వరకు పెరిగే డిమాండ్‌ను అందుకోవడానికి మరో 150 బిలియన్ డాలర్ల నుంచి 250 బిలియన్ డాలర్ల పెట్టుబడులు అవసరమవుతాయని వుడ్ మెకెంజీ స్పష్టం చేసింది.ఈవీ (EV) బ్యాటరీ రంగంలో ఎల్ఎఫ్పీ (LFP) సాంకేతికత 2030 వరకు ఆధిపత్యం చెలాయించనుంది. చైనాకు చెందిన సీఏటీఎల్ (CATL) సంస్థ రూపొందించిన మూడో తరం 'షెన్షింగ్' బ్యాటరీ కేవలం 4 నిమిషాల్లోనే 10 నుంచి 80 శాతం ఛార్జింగ్ పూర్తయ్యే వెసులుబాటును తెచ్చింది. అలాగే సోడియం-అయాన్ బ్యాటరీ లభ్యత 2026 మూడో త్రైమాసికం నుంచి చైనాలో ఊపందుకుంది. 2035 నాటికి సోడియం-అయాన్, ఎల్ఎఫ్పీ బ్యాటరీల తయారీ వ్యయం సమాన స్థాయికి చేరుకుంటుందని నివేదిక అంచనా వేసింది.ముందున్న సవాళ్లు"డేటా సెంటర్లు ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా విద్యుత్ రంగానికి పెద్ద సవాలుగా మారాయి. అయితే పెరుగుతున్న డిమాండ్‌కు, క్లిష్టంగా మారుతున్న సరఫరా వ్యవస్థకు మధ్య వస్తున్న వ్యత్యాసమే అసలు సమస్య" అని వుడ్ మెకెంజీ మెటల్స్ అండ్ మైనింగ్ రీసెర్చ్ వైస్ ప్రెసిడెంట్ లిండ్సే గ్రాంట్ విశ్లేషించారు."ఉత్పత్తిని పెంచేందుకు వేగవంతమైన అనుమతులు, నిరంతర పెట్టుబడి కట్టుబాట్లు లేకపోతే భవిష్యత్తు ఎదుగుదలకు అవసరమైన గనుల సరఫరాను పరిశ్రమ అందించలేదు" అని ఆయన స్పష్టం చేశారు.

title: Exclusive | Delhi Police denies permission for Diljit Dosanjh's October 30 Delhi concert, cites security concerns | Hindustan Times
description: Authorities have denied security permission for Diljit Dosanjh’s October 30 concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, citing “threat-related inputs.”
content: Bad news for all Diljit Dosanjh fans in Delhi! If you had booked your tickets for his show happening in the city on October 30, here is an update. HT City has learnt that the show has been denied security permissions.In a letter addressed to BookMyShow, Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (South District) mentioned, "Sir, With reference to your application dated 14.10.2026 on the subject cited above, I am to inform you that your request for organizing "Diljit Dosanjh's Aura India Tour Delhi" at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, New Delhi, on 30.10.2026 has been examined by this office. In view of the specific threat-related inputs, coupled with the multifarious security and law & order commitments arising out of the ongoing festive season and other important law & order concerns, the same cannot be acceded to."This will come as a big blow to all those who were set for the live event.

title: 'Difficult to accept': IIT Bombay faculty writes to director after protesting students 'forcefully' removed | Mumbai news
description: The faculty members asked the administration to issue a clear statement explaining what happened and fix responsibility for the action.  | Mumbai news
content: A group of about 20 faculty members at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay) have questioned the institute’s role in allowing police on the campus on October 18 to clear a nearly month-long peaceful demonstration over the death of a student in September.In an email to IIT Bombay director Prof Shireesh B Kedare on Wednesday, the faculty members cited allegations that the police detained students and used force to disperse them and questioned the role of institute officials present during the incident. They asked the administration to issue a clear statement explaining what happened and fix responsibility for the action.While acknowledging that faculty members held differing views on the protest — some believed the protest had served its purpose while others saw its continuance crucial for reviewing student welfare -- the letter said they all agreed that the forceful removal of peaceful protesters was “difficult to accept”.The letter cited student allegations of physical assault, including claims of having their hair pulled, being kicked, and being throttled by police personnel.On Sunday, police dismantled ‘Justice Corner’, a spot at the entrance of the campus where they had been protesting for the past month over the death of a student who was found dead in his hostel room on September 18. The deceased’s parents, who visited the campus to pay homage to their son, were also briefly detained along with the students.The faculty members questioned whether any institute official authorised the police to enter the campus and detain the protesters. They also asked why a second round of police action took place, during which more than 20 students were reportedly detained. And why the institute did not help the students who were detained at the Powai police station.The letter called on the administration to file a formal complaint if the police acted without its approval. It also asked the administration to locate students’ personal belongings, including laptops, that were seized from the protest site but not returned.An IIT-B official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, claimed that the institute did not requisition police assistance to clear the protest site. The official said police entered the campus to check the route of a visiting Member of Parliament, and the action against the protesters took place during this visit.The students, who were protesting at the entrance of the campus, have shifted to a spot outside the director’s office, demanding the return of their laptops, medicines and other belongings, which they alleged were confiscated by the administration. An official said students had been told to collect their belongings as per the institute’s lost-and-found policy.
