Mahtab Alam Rizvi, a meeting was convened today with all the members of the high-level committee constituted on October 18, along with all Deans of Faculties, JMI; the Dean of Students’ Welfare; the Controller of Examinations; the Dean of Academic Affairs; the Chief Proctor; all Provosts; the Chief Public Relations Officer; and the Security Advisor, as per the release.The meeting deliberated on the recommendations of the high-level committee and its discussions with students and explored a way forward to restore peace and normalcy on campus.Following detailed discussion, JMI has announced and notified the constitution of a committee to draft the Constitution of Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU) in furtherance of Article 23(J)&(K) of the JMI Act, 1988. The Committee will consider the circumstances leading to the dissolution of JMISU in 2006, various rulings of Competent Courts in relation to JMISU, and recommendations of the Lyngdoh Committee (2007). The need for a comprehensive examination of the matter arises from the fact that the last Students’ Union at the University was dissolved in 2006.In the intervening two decades, several developments have taken place, making it necessary to review the issue in the light of the prevailing legal and institutional framework.The committee will examine the existing court orders concerning Students’ Union elections at JMI, the recommendations of the Lyngdoh Committee Report on student bodies and Students’ Union elections in universities, colleges and other institutions of higher education across India, as well as the applicable ordinances and statutes of Jamia Millia Islamia.As per the release, JMI remains committed to safeguarding students’ rights, upholding democratic values and restoring peace and normalcy on campus while protecting the University's academic environment, heritage and national and international standing.

title: Indian embassy issues advisory for nationals in France amid violent protests: ‘Remain vigilant and exercise caution’ | India News
description: The embassy also urged Indians to stay away from areas where demonstrations are taking place and follow directions issued by French authorities. | India News
content: The Indian embassy in Paris has issued an advisory for Indian nationals living in France and those planning to visit the country amid ongoing violent protests and clashes, urging them to stay alert and avoid large gatherings and crowded areas."In view of the recent developments and localised curfews imposed in France, please remain vigilant and exercise due caution,” the advisory issued on Wednesday evening read.The embassy also urged Indians to stay away from areas where demonstrations are taking place and follow directions issued by French authorities. It asked citizens to check official channels for updates on possible disruptions to transport services across French cities. “In case of any emergency, Indian nationals can contact: Embassy of India, Paris: +33 6 48 34 00 63 | cons.paris@mea.gov.in,” it said.Indian embassy in Italy issued advisory earlierEarlier this week, the Indian embassy in Italy had issued a safety advisory for Indian nationals amid protests over the rising cost of living and poor public services in the country.“Indian nationals are advised to exercise caution, avoid crowded areas and locations where protests are taking place, and follow local news about such events,” the advisory released on Monday said. France gripped by violent protestsFrance has recently seen some of its worst unrest in years. Protests over the rising cost of living, declining public services and concerns about education turned violent, with looting, arson and clashes with police reported in Paris, Marseille and Lyon, among other cities.High school students have raised concerns over a lack of funding for schools, poor facilities and staff shortages, especially in lower-income neighbourhoods. Some have also complained that school days, which often run from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., are exhausting. They have also questioned the complexity and fairness of the university admissions system.France has seen two consecutive nights of calm since the unrest over the weekend. Curfews remain in force in parts of several major cities, including limited areas of Paris.More protests are planned for Thursday and Saturday after calls from student unions and groups linked to the “yellow vest ” movement. The movement's demonstrations over fuel prices led to massive unrest in France in 2018 and 2019.Paris police said on Wednesday that they would prohibit a protest planned for Thursday in the French capital, citing concerns over public safety and the risk of damage to property.Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said on Wednesday that 174 of the 2,500 people detained during and after the protests had been jailed. A further 917 had been formally prosecuted, he added.Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met union representatives on Wednesday and said a “massive” security operation would be carried out on Saturday. The move aims to prevent a repeat of the violence caused by small groups of rioters, which had exposed gaps in security arrangements.With inputs from agencies

title: Sara Ali Khan turns heads in Gaurav Gupta and Manish Malhotra ensembles, showcasing her glamorous style | Fashion Trends
description: Sara Ali Khan makes a statement in Gaurav Gupta and Manish Malhotra creations, giving fashion lovers two looks to admire. Here's the breakdown of her outfits.  | Fashion Trends
content: In a set of pictures released recently, Sara Ali Khan wore two striking couture ensembles by designers Gaurav Gupta and Manish Malhotra, serving high-fashion glamour and offering plenty of style inspiration. Here’s a breakdown of her standout looks.​Also read | Yami Gautam serves ethnic fashion goals in an elegant purple saree for Ravan Dahan at Red FortSara Ali Khan in Gaurav Gupta coutureSara Ali Khan’s look is all about understated luxury, featuring a champagne-gold-embellished gown with a sculpted sweetheart neckline and an oversized satin train that creates a regal silhouette. The gown follows the body’s natural contours from the waist through the hips, then extends into a narrow, floor-length skirt. This creates a mermaid-inspired silhouette, which is particularly effective for formal eveningwear. The strapless bodice features a sweetheart neckline, defined by its gently curved, heart-shaped contour. Unlike a bright gold or silver gown, champagne gold reflects light more softly. This creates an elegant, almost liquid-metal effect that works beautifully under event lighting and in photographs.The gown features dense, all-over embellishments, with sequins and metallic embroidery catching the light at different angles.Jewellery and makeupGiven the gown's depth, Sara kept her accessories minimal. She chose to wear drop-style earrings in a light metallic finish. The earrings also frame the face and work particularly well with the pulled-back hairstyle. The hair is swept back into a loose, textured updo, with the bun positioned towards the back of the head.Sara’s makeup leans towards a classic evening-glam aesthetic. The dark, defined eyes with smoky shading and emphasis around the lash line create depth and definition. The base is smooth and polished, with subtle dimensions rather than an excessively sculpted finish, and the lip colour appears muted and neutral, allowing the eyes and gown to remain the main focus.Sara Ali Khan in Manish Malhotra coutureSara Ali Khan channelled the Navratri festive spirit with a stunning ensemble designed by Manish Malhotra, featuring the richness of Bandhani, reimagined in deeper hues of royal sapphire, amethyst, and plum. The beauty of this Indian textile is the artistry of handcrafted mirror work and the timelessness of tradition. Celebrating the spirit of Navratri and paying homage to the extraordinary heritage of Indian craftsmanship with colour, texture, and a new expression of festive dressing, this Manish Malhotra ensemble creates a regal vision. Jewellery and makeupThe outfit is complemented by statement gold jhumkas, a delicate maang tikka, and stacked bangles or a traditional hathphool. The hair is kept in a sleek low bun, with soft waves swept away from the face. Warm bronze eyes, softly defined eyeliner, sculpted cheeks, and a nude rose or muted berry lip round out the glam.

title: From eMudhra to Bank of Baroda: 5 major data breaches in recent times | India News
description: Here is a look at five recent data breaches and significant cybersecurity incidents linked to India | India News
content: A security flaw at Bengaluru-based digital certificate provider—eMudhra Ltd.—put global web security at risk after weak cryptographic keys linked to eight certificates prompted Google, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft to take “emergency action”.The keys could potentially have allowed attackers to create fraudulent certificates for websites and software, raising concerns about the security of systems that rely on digital authentication.The incident is among several major cybersecurity breaches and data exposures involving Indian organisations in recent years, affecting sectors ranging from banking and healthcare to technology and infrastructure. While some incidents involved customer information appearing on the dark web, others exposed sensitive corporate records or raised concerns about the security of digital systems. Here is a look at five recent data breaches and significant cybersecurity incidents linked to India: eMudhra: Weak cryptographic keys put global web security at riskeMudhra’s security incident came to light in October 2026, after a researcher identified weaknesses in private keys associated with eight intermediate certificates issued by the Bengaluru-based company.The weak keys were eMudhra’s own doing. In its replies to Mozilla, the company said its staff used them by mistake at a key generation ceremony in April 2025 and that “there were human errors in multiple steps of the process”.The private keys were meant to be sufficiently complex to prevent anyone from deriving them from the corresponding public keys. However, the affected keys were numbers that could be recovered by testing a small range of possibilities. This meant that attackers could use them to issue fraudulent certificates, impersonate websites, or sign software as though it came from a verified publisher.Google, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft took steps to block the affected certificates. “As this incident enables even technically unsophisticated individuals to easily recover the private keys for these intermediates, the impact of this incident could not be higher,” Mozilla wrote in its incident report.eMudhra said its infrastructure was not compromised and no data was breached. It said its Indian digital signature certificate and eSign businesses run on separate infrastructure and were unaffected.State Bank of India: 3,897 customer records identified in suspected Data ExposureThe State Bank of India (SBI) on October 21, 2026, informed the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange that it had suffered “an incident involving the loss of certain data,” with 3,897 customer records containing personal information identified within a larger trove of about 3.75 lakh records on the dark web.The exposed information reportedly included registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF (Customer Information File) identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata linked to loan records and other files. The bank said it learnt of the incident on October 16 through its threat intelligence provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In).SBI activated its incident-response protocols and engaged an independent CERT-In-empanelled agency to establish the authenticity, source and extent of the exposure. It said the incident was not expected to have a material impact on its core operations, financial performance or business continuity.The bank’s disclosure did not establish how the data had left its systems or what the remaining records in the larger dataset contained. The investigation is ongoing, and the full number of individuals potentially affected remains unclear.Bank of Baroda: Customer information and internal documents appear on dark webBank of Baroda confirmed a cybersecurity incident on July 27, 2026, after customer information and internal documents allegedly linked to the lender appeared on the dark web. The bank said the incident involved a compromised employee email account, resulting in unauthorised access to certain data.Cybersecurity researcher Srikanth L said the leaked material included customer details, identification documents, loan papers and internal audit records. The dataset was advertised on a dark-web site as containing more than 700GB of information, based on an analysis of the site’s metadata. The full volume and authenticity of the material were not independently established.The bank said the incident had been identified promptly and that containment measures had been implemented. It also said its core banking systems had not been accessed and remained secure. Bank of Baroda initiated a forensic investigation and said it was working with the relevant authorities.Reliance Group: Files linked to Kudankulam Nuclear Plant published onlineIn July 2026, a ransomware group published files it claimed were linked to the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu. The material reportedly included facility-related documents, supplier details and information about infrastructure systems.Reliance Group confirmed a partial data breach involving a server hosted by Indian data centre provider Yotta and said that the government had been informed. The group behind the leak claimed that the files were connected to the nuclear plant, but the authenticity and full scope of the material required careful verification.The incident drew attention to cybersecurity risks associated with third-party data storage and contractors working with strategically important infrastructure. The case highlighted the potential consequences of unauthorised access to corporate systems that hold information related to critical infrastructure.Vitraya Technologies: Alleged exposure of medical and insurance recordsVitraya Technologies—which operates a digital platform for health insurance claims— approached the Supreme Court in 2026 seeking a CBI probe into the alleged hacking and theft of personal and medical data of more than 1.5 lakh citizens stored by the companyThe petition filed by the company alleged a large-scale cyber intrusion involving unauthorised access to highly sensitive personal information, including medical records, insurance claim details, Aadhaar-linked information, and other personally identifiable data. Vitraya detected a coordinated cyberattack in February 2025 involving brute-force login attempts, mass downloading of confidential records, and the extraction of sensitive customer data from its digital infrastructure.Vitraya also alleged that it approached Punjab’s cybercrime police in March 2025. However, despite repeated representations and full cooperation during the preliminary inquiry, the police allegedly delayed registering an FIR for nearly six months. The Supreme Court agreed to examine the plea for a central investigation and issued notice in August 2026.The case highlighted concerns over the protection of sensitive medical and insurance information held by digital healthcare platforms, where unauthorised access can expose details about individuals’ health and financial circumstances.

title: OTT Thriller: నెగెటివ్ టాక్‌తోనూ థియేటర్లలో కోట్లు కొల్లగొట్టిన తమన్నా థ్రిల్లర్.. ఓటీటీలో స్ట్రీమింగ్ ఎప్పుడంటే? | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: OTT Thriller: హిందీలో బిజీగా మారిన మిల్క్ బ్యూటీ తమన్నా ఇప్పుడో మిస్టరీ థ్రిల్లర్ తో ఓటీటీలో ఎంటర్ టైన్ చేసేందుకు రెడీ అవుతోంది. ఆమె లేటెస్ట్ మూవీ ది వ్వాన్ ఓటీటీ రిలీజ్ డేట్ పై లేటెస్ట్ బజ్ వైరల్ గా మారింది. మరి ఈ చిత్రం గురించి పూర్తి వివరాలు ఇక్కడ చూసేయండి.
content: OTT Thriller: బాక్సాఫీస్ దగ్గర ఒక్కోసారి రివ్యూలకు, కలెక్షన్లకు అస్సలు సంబంధమే ఉండదు. నెగెటివ్ టాక్ తెచ్చుకున్నా కూడా కొన్ని సినిమాలు థియేటర్లలో కాసుల వర్షం కురిపిస్తుంటాయి. సరిగ్గా ఇదే కోవలోకి చెందుతుంది బాలీవుడ్ లేటెస్ట్ జానపద థ్రిల్లర్ 'ది వ్వాన్: ది ఫోర్స్ ఆఫ్ ది ఫారెస్ట్' (The Vvaan: The Force of the Forrest).ఓటీటీలోకి ది వ్వాన్మిల్కీ బ్యూటీ తమన్నా భాటియా, స్టార్ హీరో సిద్ధార్థ్ మల్హోత్రా జంటగా నటించిన ఈ ది వ్వాన్ మూవీ ఓటీటీలోకి రాబోతుంది. జానపద మిస్టరీ జోనర్లో తెరకెక్కిన ఈ చిత్రం థియేటర్లలో ప్రేక్షకులను ఆకట్టుకున్న తర్వాత, ఇప్పుడు డిజిటల్ స్క్రీన్‌పై అలరించేందుకు సిద్ధమైంది.అసలేంటి ఈ ఓటీటీ కండీషన్?ది వ్వాన్ సినిమా డిజిటల్ స్ట్రీమింగ్ హక్కులను ప్రముఖ ఓటీటీ సంస్థ అమెజాన్ ప్రైమ్ వీడియో సొంతం చేసుకుంది. తాజా సమాచారం ప్రకారం ఈ చిత్రం నవంబర్ 6, 2026 నుంచి ప్రైమ్ వీడియోలో స్ట్రీమింగ్ కానుంది. అయితే ఇక్కడే ఓ పెద్ద ట్విస్ట్ ఉంది. ఈ సినిమాను ప్రైమ్ సబ్‌స్క్రిప్షన్ ఉన్న వారు కూడా నేరుగా చూసే వీలు లేదు. ది వ్వాన్ మూవీని 'రెంటల్' (Rent) పద్ధతిలో ముందు అందుబాటులోకి తెస్తున్నారు. అంటే ప్రైమ్ మెంబర్‌షిప్ ఉన్నప్పటికీ, ఈ సినిమా చూడాలంటే విడిగా అదనపు డబ్బులు చెల్లించి రెంట్ కి తీసుకోవాల్సి ఉంటుంది. మరి ఈ పెయిడ్ విధానంలో సినిమాకు ఎలాంటి రెస్పాన్స్ వస్తుందో చూడాలి.అడవి నేపథ్యంలో సాగే మిస్టరీఈ చిత్రానికి ప్రముఖ దర్శకుడు దీపక్ కుమార్ మిశ్రా దర్శకత్వం వహించారు. అడవి నేపథ్యంలో సాగే ఒక పురాతన జానపద కథను, ఆధునిక సస్పెన్స్ ఎలిమెంట్స్‌తో ముడిపెట్టి ఈ థ్రిల్లర్‌ను తెరకెక్కించారు. తమన్నా, సిద్ధార్థ్ మల్హోత్రా కెరీర్‌లో ఇదొక డిఫరెంట్ అటెంప్ట్ అని చెప్పవచ్చు. బాలీవుడ్ దిగ్గజ నిర్మాతలు ఏక్తా కపూర్, శోభా కపూర్ అత్యంత ప్రతిష్టాత్మకంగా ఈ హిందీ చిత్రాన్ని నిర్మించారు.క్రేజీ కాస్ట్ఈ సినిమాలో లీడ్ పెయిర్‌తో పాటు మరికొందరు టాలెంటెడ్ నటీనటులు కీలక పాత్రలు పోషించారు. పాపులర్ నటీమణులు శ్వేతా తివారీ, ప్రముఖ కమెడియన్ సునీల్ గ్రోవర్, మనీష్ పాల్, సీనియర్ నటుడు అనూప్ సోని తమ నటనతో సినిమాకు అదనపు బలాన్ని చేకూర్చారు. థియేటర్లలో మిస్ అయిన వారు, భిన్నమైన జానపద థ్రిల్లర్ కథలను ఇష్టపడే వారు నవంబర్ మొదటి వారంలో అమెజాన్ ప్రైమ్ లో ఈ చిత్రాన్ని వీక్షించవచ్చు.

title: From a  ₹711 crore tower to  ₹294 crore apartments: Mumbai’s sea-facing versus sea-view luxury homes premium explained | Hindustan Times
description: Mumbai real estate: As marquee deals set new benchmarks, the real premium lies not just in owning a sea-facing home, but in securing an unobstructed view
content: In Mumbai’s luxury real estate market, a sea view is more than a lifestyle aspiration; it is a powerful marker of exclusivity, a coveted address, and often a decisive factor in determining a property’s worth. Yet, for discerning homebuyers, not all views of the Arabian Sea are created equal. The distinction between a sea-view apartment and a genuinely sea-facing residence, with an uninterrupted panorama of the coastline, can translate into a significant premium.As marquee transactions continue to set new benchmarks, one thing is becoming increasingly clear: in the city's ultra-luxury housing market, the real premium lies not merely in owning a home by the sea, but in securing a view that is difficult to replicate.Few transactions illustrate this distinction better than the purchase by Tanya Dubash, daughter of industrialist Adi Godrej, and her company, Shaula Real Estates Private Limited. According to property registration documents accessed by Zapkey, they acquired two additional luxury sea-facing apartments in Worli for over ₹294 crore, at approximately ₹2.53 lakh per sq ft.The transaction ranks among India’s most expensive residential property deals. The purchase follows Dubash’s acquisition of a luxury duplex in the same development in May 2025, for over ₹226 crore, reinforcing the enduring appeal of Mumbai’s most exclusive waterfront residences.The Worli address has already established its credentials in the upper echelons of the country’s residential property market.On May 28, 2025, Leena Gandhi Tewari, chairperson of pharmaceutical company USV, purchased two sea-facing duplex apartments in the same complex for ₹639 crore, at nearly ₹3 lakh per sq ft. With stamp duty and GST adding approximately ₹63.9 crore, the total outlay rose to around ₹703 crore, making it the most expensive residential property transaction recorded in India at the time.Such deals underscore the premium that affluent buyers are willing to pay for properties that combine expansive living spaces, prime locations and an enduring relationship with the sea. In a city where developable land is scarce and the coastline is one of its most valuable natural assets, unobstructed sea views have become an increasingly powerful differentiator in the luxury housing segment.The appeal extends beyond Worli. In South Mumbai, Godrej Properties Ltd has entered into a development agreement for a 2.5-acre land parcel in Marine Lines, where it plans to develop a luxury residential project with an estimated revenue potential of ₹6,000 crore, according to a regulatory filing dated September 28.With its heritage architecture, established neighbourhoods and proximity to the city’s principal business, cultural and lifestyle destinations, Marine Lines occupies a distinctive position in Mumbai’s residential landscape. Improved connectivity, particularly through the Coastal Road, has further enhanced its appeal among affluent homebuyers and end-users.The proposed redevelopment is expected to feature four- and five-bedroom residences, including sea-facing homes, catering to buyers seeking a combination of space, exclusivity and coastal views in one of South Mumbai’s most established locations.Meanwhile, another landmark transaction has put Juhu in the spotlight. Embassy Developments Limited has signed a memorandum of understanding with Dinesh Thakkar, founder, chairman and managing director of Angel One Limited, for the sale of an entire residential tower at Embassy Terazza for approximately ₹711 crore, according to a regulatory filing dated September 22.The company described the deal as India’s largest single residential unit transaction.Situated on Juhu Tara Road, an address favoured by prominent business families, industrialists and celebrities, Embassy Terazza is an ultra-luxury, low-density development spread across more than two acres.The project comprises approximately 50 residences across five towers and has an estimated gross development value exceeding ₹3,000 crore. Designed around exclusivity and expansive views, the development offers one residence per floor, panoramic vistas of the sea and city, landscaped internal gardens, carefully planned layouts and curated wellness and lifestyle amenities. The project is being developed under a development management model.Also Read: Mumbai real estate: Is an apartment overlooking the sea more expensive than a sea-view apartment? Read on to find outThat’s not all, Rekha Jhunjhunwala, wife of the late renowned investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala had purchased nearly all the units within a building for ₹118 crore to preserve the uninterrupted view of the Arabian Sea from her Malabar Hill abode almost two years ago.The difference between seeing the sea and facing itA sea-view apartment may offer glimpses of the coastline from select rooms or balconies, while a sea-facing home typically positions the sea as a central feature of the living experience. But even this distinction is not always straightforward. The orientation of the apartment, the floor on which it sits, the breadth of the panorama and the likelihood of future construction obstructing the view can all influence its market value.According to real estate experts, while both sea-view and sea-facing apartments offer a view of the sea, the permanence of that view, the property’s location and the possibility of future construction obstructing the vista can determine its value.Sea-view and sea-facing apartments are located across the west coast of Mumbai, including areas such as Marine Drive, Malabar Hills, Walkeshwar, Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Peddar Road, Worli, Dadar, Mahim, Bandra, Juhu, Vile Parle, Andheri, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali, among several others.A sea-facing apartment typically faces the sea directly, often offering an uninterrupted view of the waterfront. Marine Drive is a prominent example of Mumbai’s sea-facing residential market. A sea-view apartment, on the other hand, may be located farther from the coastline but offer a view of the sea from its windows or balcony. Such views may not be permanent, as future buildings could obstruct them.Sea view is something that is far from the sea but offers a view of the sea. But a sea view is temporary. If a tall structure comes up in front of an existing building, the sea view can go for a toss. On the other hand, a sea-facing apartment, as the name suggests, faces the sea and offers an uninterrupted view of the sea.How much premium do sea-facing apartments command?Real estate experts said sea-facing apartments in established luxury neighbourhoods such as Marine Drive, Malabar Hill, Walkeshwar, Worli, Bandra and Juhu command some of the highest prices in Mumbai’s residential market. In prime locations, prices can range from ₹1 lakh per sq ft to ₹2.8 lakh per sq ft, depending on the location, building and property specifications.Also Read: How much money do you need to buy an apartment in Worli Sea Face in Mumbai?Where can homebuyers find relatively affordable sea-view homes?For homebuyers seeking waterfront views at comparatively lower prices, several micro-markets offer alternatives to South Mumbai’s premium locations. In the Sewri-Wadala, Mazgaon belt, sea-view apartments are priced at around ₹35,000– ₹45,000 per sq ft, while select pockets of Bandra, Versova, Madh Island in Malad, Gorai, Dahisar offer creek-view homes at ₹30,000– ₹80,000 per sq ft.Also Read: 5 locations in the Mumbai real estate market offering affordable sea-view apartments"Beyond Mumbai’s core city limits, sea- or creek-facing apartments in Mira Road-Bhayandar are available at around ₹15,000– ₹20,000 per sq ft. Ulwe in Navi Mumbai offers sea-facing or open sea-view apartments at approximately ₹12,000– ₹18,000 per sq ft. These are the most affordable localities, which offer the view of the sea," said Bharat Singh, a Navi Mumbai based real estate consultant.

title: From Tiger Shroff shooting to Baba Siddique murder, UP links recur in Bishnoi gang probes | Hindustan Times
description: A UP link into alleged interstate firearms supply networks linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang has resurfaced after arrests were made in the Tiger Shroff case.
content: The Uttar Pradesh connection in investigations into alleged interstate firearms supply networks linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang has resurfaced, with two women originally from Sitapur and Azamgarh, who had been living in Haryana’s Sonipat, among four people arrested in connection with the October 18 firing at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai.UP Police are now verifying their backgrounds as investigators probe their alleged role in transporting a pistol and ammunition for the shooters.Radha, 30, from Sitapur, and Babita, 23, from Azamgarh, were arrested on Tuesday (October 20) along with Kunal, 21, and Sumit, 19, both from Haryana’s Sonipat. Investigators suspect the women acted as arms carriers in a supply chain allegedly coordinated by Anil Pandit, a US-based operative suspected of links to the Bishnoi gang.Also Read | Tiger Shroff shooting case: Shooters surveyed Salman, Aamir Khan and Ranbir Kapoor’s homes Sitapur superintendent of police Ankur Agarwal said Radha’s parents told police that she had married around 10 years ago and divorced about five years ago.She had been living in the National Capital Region (NCR) and working as a labourer at a private firm, he said. According to her parents, she visited her native village about once a year and was likely to return around Diwali. Police checked her background in her parental village, Agarwal added.Azamgarh SSP Anil Kumar said a joint team of Delhi and Mumbai police took Babita into custody from Kotiyar village for questioning. She had worked at a packaging unit around two to three years ago, he said.The arrests have renewed attention on UP’s presence in investigations into interstate gang operations, including the 2024 murder of former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique and separate firearms supply cases involving alleged suppliers from Lucknow and Gorakhpur. However, investigators have not established a common network connecting these cases.UP women allegedly ferried pistol to MumbaiAccording to investigators, Kunal, who had recently been released on bail, was introduced to Pandit through a friend from Harsana village in Haryana. On Pandit’s instructions, Kunal allegedly collected a pistol and 20 rounds of ammunition from Amritsar, accompanied by Sumit.Kunal subsequently persuaded Radha to travel to Mumbai with the weapon. On October 15, he allegedly took Radha and Babita to New Delhi railway station, with the pistol concealed in Radha’s bag. The women reached Mumbai’s Dadar railway station on October 17, where a minor boy allegedly collected the bag from Radha near their hotel.Three motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at Shroff’s car in Mumbai’s Juhu area the following evening. The actor escaped unhurt, while his driver was injured.Investigators said Pandit subsequently asked Kunal to arrange the shooters’ escape. Radha and Babita left Mumbai for Delhi on October 18 and were apprehended at New Delhi railway station on October 20. Kunal and Sumit were arrested in Sonipat. Maharashtra Police’s Crime Investigation Department subsequently obtained court permission to formally arrest the four and secured three days’ transit remand.Bahraich shooters in Siddique murderTwo alleged shooters in the October 12, 2024, murder of former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique — Shiv Kumar Gautam and Dharmaraj Kashyap — were from Bahraich district. Another accused, Gurmail Singh, was from Haryana. Investigators also examined allegations that a scrap dealer from Bahraich had supplied pistols to the shooters.The Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for Siddique’s murder, bringing the alleged role of UP-based shooters and arms suppliers under scrutiny in a high-profile interstate crime investigation.Lucknow, Gorakhpur arms casesIn November 2024, the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) arrested Lucknow resident Prince Kailash Vishwakarma and his alleged associate Sajjan Kumar alias Deepak, who was from Bahraich, in a separate firearms supply case. Both were arrested in Maharashtra with two pistols each. Maharashtra Police suspected links between the alleged supply network and criminal operations in Mumbai, including those associated with the Bishnoi gang. A direct connection with Siddique’s shooters was not established.Also Read | From Salman Khan, Baba Siddique to Tiger Shroff: The Lawrence Bishnoi gang hit list that keeps growingIn September 2025, the STF arrested five alleged members of an illegal arms network in Gorakhpur, recovering four .32-bore pistols, a revolver and five live cartridges. Investigators alleged that the network sourced weapons from Madhya Pradesh and Haryana for distribution across eastern UP. The case also involved scrutiny of alleged links between the key accused and gangsters Goldy Brar and Rohit Godara.Whether the latest case shares any operational links with the earlier firearms networks remains under investigation.

title: In 2024, Florida researchers developed a DNA test for four invasive snakes, including Burmese pythons, offering a new way to detect them in the wild | World News
description: In 2024, University of Florida researchers developed a DNA test that detects four invasive snakes in water and soil. Field testing is still to come.  | World News
content: Florida has a snake problem, and it’s hard to see. In 2024, University of Florida researchers reported a new DNA test for four invasive snakes. According to a study in Ecology and Evolution, is built to detect the DNA of Burmese pythons, northern African pythons, boa constrictors, and rainbow boas from environmental samples, and in early controlled tests it picked up Burmese python DNA in both water and soil. The University of Florida news release calls it a pioneering tool for showing where invasive species have been.Why invasive snakes are so hard to findMelissa Miller, the lead author and an invasion ecologist at the UF/IFAS Fort Lauderdale Research and Education Center, says once a nonnative species is established, it is often too late to get rid of it. From there, the news release notes, efforts shift to containment or long-term management, both of which can be costly for native wildlife and for funding. The study says Florida has more than 500 nonnative species, more than 50 established reptiles, and that $10.6 million was spent on Burmese python removal from 2004 to 2021. It also notes that visual surveys are estimated to detect less than 5 percent of Burmese pythons. Co-author Sergio Balaguera-Reina says secretive species like most snakes are hard to detect, even at high densities. How the four-in-one test worksThe test is called a tetraplex digital PCR assay. Brian Bahder, a senior author and associate professor of vector entomology at the same center, calls it essentially four tests in one. Each part detects one species without detecting the others. The study agrees, reporting no cross-amplification across species, and calls this the first tetraplex digital PCR assay for four invasive constrictor snakes. The release adds that Bahder usually works on detecting lethal bronzing in palm trees. He explains that the molecular testing works similarly across organisms because the main difference is the DNA sequence. The technique uses eDNA, or genetic material organisms shed into the environment.What the early tests revealedThe team then tested how well it performed. The release said known quantities of DNA were placed in water and concentrated onto a filter using a vacuum pump. They then put a Burmese python into water and took samples at set times. Water samples tested positive within five minutes of exposure. Soil from where a python had been resting also tested positive. All soil samples taken 24 hours, one week, and two weeks after the snake was removed contained python DNA. The test was meant to work in Florida’s varied environments, from the thick Everglades habitat to urban areas where nonnative constrictors have now been found.What’s next for the testThe researchers are cautious about the implications of the findings. Bahder said in the release that concentration estimates are only the first step and that more experiments are needed to understand how time, distance, and environmental factors affect detection. The study adds that field performance still needs to be evaluated and will be the subject of future research. Miller notes testing for many species in one sample could reduce survey costs, and she hopes the tool will help with early detection and rapid removal. Co-author Frank Mazzotti said in the release that the team’s first next step is adding more species to the assay, especially fish like Asian swamp eels and bullseye snakeheads, which would extend it beyond snakes. He also said the team plans to set up a regional sampling network to detect new invasions early and assess removal efforts across the area covered by the Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan.

title: Pregnancy : ప్రెగ్నెన్సీ ‘టు-డూ’ లిస్ట్.. మహిళలు ఇవి తెలుసుకుంటే చాలు! | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: గర్భం దాల్చిన తర్వాత ఏవి పాటించాలి, ఏవి మానాలి అనే విషయంలో చాలామంది గర్భిణులు అయోమయానికి గురవుతుంటారు. ప్రతీ విషయంలోనూ పరిపూర్ణంగా ఉండాలనే తాపత్రయంతో ఒత్తిడి పెంచుకోకుండా, తల్లి-బిడ్డ ఆరోగ్యాన్ని కాపాడే ప్రాథమిక అంశాలపై దృష్టి పెట్టాలని వైద్య నిపుణులు సూచిస్తున్నారు.
content: గర్భం దాల్చిన క్షణం నుంచి మహిళల జీవితంలో ఒక సరికొత్త అధ్యాయం మొదలవుతుంది. ఆసుపత్రి పరీక్షలు, రక్త పరీక్షలు, స్కాన్లు, ప్రత్యేక ఆహార నియమాలు, వ్యాయామాలు.. ఇలా ప్రతీ విషయాన్నీ సరిగ్గా చేయాలనే ఆరాటంలో చాలా మంది తల్లులు తీవ్రమైన మానసిక ఒత్తిడికి, అలసటకు గురవుతుంటారు. అయితే, కనిపించిన ప్రతీ సలహానూ పాటించాల్సిన అవసరం లేదని, ప్రాథమిక ఆరోగ్య సూత్రాలపై దృష్టి పెడితే చాలని వైద్య నిపుణులు స్పష్టం చేస్తున్నారు."ఈ ప్రయాణంలో ప్రతీ విషయంలోనూ పర్‌ఫెక్ట్‌గా ఉండాలని ప్రయత్నించడం వల్ల మానసిక అలసట పెరుగుతుంది. దానికి బదులు తల్లి, బిడ్డ ఆరోగ్యానికి అత్యంత ముఖ్యమైన కొన్ని ప్రాథమిక అలవాట్లను పాటిస్తే సరిపోతుంది," అని పూణెలోని మదర్‌హుడ్ ఆసుపత్రికి చెందిన ప్రముఖ స్త్రీవైద్య నిపుణులు డాక్టర్ రాఖీ వాఘ్ వెల్లడించారు.క్రమం తప్పకుండా ఆంటినాటల్ తనిఖీలు..గర్భధారణ సమయంలో వైద్యులు సూచించిన షెడ్యూల్ ప్రకారం ఆంటినాటల్ చెకప్‌లకు హాజరుకావడం అత్యంత ముఖ్యం. నిర్దేశిత వారాల్లో రక్తం పరీక్షలు, అల్ట్రాసౌండ్ స్కాన్లు, ఇతర స్క్రీనింగ్‌లు చేయించుకోవడం వల్ల కడుపులోని బిడ్డ ఎదుగుదలను ఎప్పటికప్పుడు పరిశీలించవచ్చు. ఏవైనా సమస్యలు ఉంటే ప్రారంభంలోనే గుర్తించి చికిత్స అందించేందుకు ఇవి దోహదపడతాయి.బ్యాలెన్స్​డ్​ ఆహారం, విటమిన్ల సప్లిమెంట్లు..గర్భధారణ సమయంలో శరీరానికి అదనపు పోషకాలు అవసరం. రోజువారీ ఆహారంలో తాజా కూరగాయలు, పండ్లు, తృణధాన్యాలు, పప్పుధాన్యాలు, పాలు, ప్రోటీన్ ఎక్కువగా ఉండే పదార్థాలను చేర్చుకోవాలి. వీటితో పాటు శరీరం పోషకాల లోపానికి గురికాకుండా ఉండటానికి డాక్టర్ సలహా మేరకు ఫోలిక్ యాసిడ్, ఐరన్, క్యాల్షియం, విటమిన్-డీ సప్లిమెంట్లను క్రమం తప్పకుండా వాడాలి.సురక్షితమైన శారీరక శ్రమ, తగినంత నిద్ర..వైద్యులు ప్రత్యేకంగా బెడ్ రెస్ట్ సూచించనంత వరకు రోజువారీ పనులతో పాటు చురుగ్గా ఉండటమే మంచిది. రోజూ తేలికపాటి నడక, గర్భిణులకు అనువైన స్ట్రెచింగ్ వ్యాయామాలు చేయడం వల్ల శరీరంలో శక్తి స్థాయిలు పెరుగుతాయి. ప్రసవ సమయంలో ఇవి ఎంతో సహాయపడతాయి. వ్యాయామంతో పాటు తగినంత విశ్రాంతి తీసుకోవడం కూడా అంతే ముఖ్యం. శరీరం అలసిపోయినట్లు అనిపిస్తే వెంటనే పనులు పక్కనబెట్టి నిద్రపోవాలి.సోషల్ మీడియా సలహాలు వద్దు.. పోలిక అసలే వద్దు!ప్రస్తుత డిజిటల్ యుగంలో సోషల్ మీడియా, ఇంటర్నెట్ గ్రూపుల నుంచి వచ్చే రకరకాల సలహాలను గుడ్డిగా పాటించకూడదు. "ఈ కఠినమైన డైట్ చేయాలి, ఈ మూలికలు వాడాలి" అంటూ వచ్చే ప్రచారాలను వైద్యుడితో మాట్లాడకుండా ప్రయత్నించవద్దు. అలాగే మీ గర్భధారణను మరొకరితో పోల్చి చూసుకోవడం ఆపేయాలి. స్కానింగ్ నివేదికలు, బరువు పెరిగే విధానం, ప్రసవ ప్రణాళికలు ఒకరికొకరు వేర్వేరుగా ఉంటాయి.ప్రసవానికి సిద్ధమవ్వడం.. అత్యవసర సంకేతాల గుర్తింపునొప్పులు రావడం, పాలివ్వడం, పసిపాప సంరక్షణపై ముందుగానే అవగాహన పెంచుకోవాలి. ప్రసవం అనుకున్న ప్రణాళిక ప్రకారం జరగకపోతే, అప్పటికప్పుడు వైద్యులు తీసుకునే నిర్ణయాలకు సహకరించేలా మానసికంగా సిద్ధంగా ఉండాలి.అదే సమయంలో కొన్ని ప్రమాదకర సంకేతాలను అస్సలు నిర్లక్ష్యం చేయకూడదు. కడుపులో తీవ్రమైన నొప్పి, అధిక రక్తస్రావం, ఉమ్మనీరు కారడం, తీవ్రమైన తలనొప్పి, కంటి చూపు మసకబారడం, హఠాత్తుగా కాళ్లలో వాపు రావడం, ఆయాసం, జ్వరం లేదా కడుపులో పిండం కదలికలు తగ్గడం వంటి లక్షణాలు కనిపిస్తే వెంటనే ఆసుపత్రికి వెళ్లాలి. 'పరిపూర్ణత' కంటే 'అవగాహన', సొంత శరీరం చెప్పే మాట వినడమే సురక్షితమైన ప్రసవానికి పునాది.(గమనిక- ఇది సమాచారం కోసం రూపొందించిన కథనం మాత్రమే. పూర్తి వివరాల కోసం మీరు మీ వైద్యుడిని సంప్రదించాల్సి ఉంటుంది.)

title: 4 devotees hit by speeding car on Chennai-Kolkata highway, die: Cops | India News
description: One of the injured devotees died while being shifted to a local hospital, the police officer said. | India News
content: Four devotees were killed and another was seriously injured after they were hit by a speeding SUV on the Chennai-Kolkata national highway (NH-16) in Andhra Pradesh’s Kakinada district in the early hours of Thursday, police said.The accident occurred at Kathipudi village under Prathipadu assembly constituency at around 6 am. The deceased were identified as Sirigidi Erraiah (38), Lingala Sitaram (45), Bonela Sathibabu (40) and Thatipudi Shivaprasad (40).According to Peddapuram deputy superintendent of police (DSP) A B G Tilak, a group of 40 devotees, who were on “Bhavani Deeksha,” were travelling from Denkada in Vizianagaram district to Vijayawada in a bus when the vehicle broke down near Sattibabu Pulao Centre at Kathipudi village. As the driver pulled over to facilitate repairs, some passengers got off the bus to have tea at a nearby shop.“As five devotees were walking along the roadside towards the shop, a speeding Mahidra Scorpio approaching from behind hit them. Three devotees died on the spot, while two others sustained injuries,” the DSP said.One of the injured devotees died while being shifted to a local hospital, while another is undergoing treatment and his condition is said to be stable, the police officer said.The police reached the accident site and began an investigation.Andhra Pradesh state transport minister Mandipalli Ramprasad Reddy said he spoke to transport officials to obtain details of the incident. He also conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families.The minister directed the concerned authorities to ensure the best possible medical treatment for those injured in the accident and to provide them with emergency medical care and necessary facilities.Kakinada district in-charge minister Ponguru Narayana also expressed grief over the deaths. After speaking to district officials, he conveyed his condolences to the victims' families and assured them that the government would stand by them during this difficult time.

title: Gujarat Govt tightens school entry rules; outsiders can't enter without permission | Education
description: The Edu Dept directed school authorities to prevent the collection, publication or circulation of students' photographs, videos and personal information.   | Education News
content: The Gujarat government on Wednesday directed schools to tighten their entry rules and bar outsiders from entering the premises without prior permission."Any external person shall obtain prior written permission from the principal or head of the Institution to enter the school premises. Only government officials who are duly authorised....to perform their official duties shall be exempted," a circular issued by the Office of the Commissioner of Schools stated.Gwalior’s Chirag Chopra overcomes family debt and academic setbacks to become bank officer through self-studyDetails of visitors must be recorded in the visitor register, it said.The Education Department also directed school authorities to prevent the collection, publication or circulation of students' photographs, videos and personal information in ways that could compromise their safety, dignity or privacy."Photography, videography, interviews, audio recording or live-streaming of students, teachers or school activities shall not be carried out without the prior written permission of the Principal. Such activities may be permitted only for lawful purposes," the circular stated.Allahabad HC rejects plea to include BTech graduates in UP Junior Analyst (Food) recruitment"No visitor shall collect information about an individual child or publish the child's identity or photograph without the prior written permission of the Principal, particularly where such activity is not in the best interests of the child and may affect the child's safety, dignity or privacy," it said.Access to classrooms, laboratories, libraries, hostels, playgrounds, toilets and other areas where student activities take place will require prior written permission. The visitor shall be accompanied by the principal, a teacher or an authorised school official in such cases.The circular also empowers principals to deny entry to visitors whose presence could affect school security, discipline, privacy or the academic environment.Nandan Nilekani pitches for AI generated question papers, nationwide CBT to avoid paper leaksAnyone who enters without permission, refuses to leave, attempts unauthorised photography or videography, or obstructs school activities must be reported immediately to the local police and education authorities, the circular said.The State Government, under the principle of 'In Loco Parentis' (responsibility equivalent to that of a parent) bears a special responsibility for the safety, dignity, privacy and welfare of all children studying in government schools, it stated.The circular also noted that Article 21 of the Constitution grants every child the right to life, dignity and privacy, and the Supreme Court, in its judgment in K S Puttaswamy (Retd) vs Union of India, has recognised the right to privacy as a fundamental right.In addition, the school safety policy and guidelines of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) emphasise that every school must provide a safe, secure and child-friendly environment for children and protect them from exploitation and privacy violations, it added.

title: కాకినాడ జిల్లాలో ఘోర రోడ్డు ప్రమాదం.. స్కార్పియో ఢీకొట్టి నలుగురు భవానీ భక్తులు మృతి | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: కాకినాడ జిల్లాలో ఘోర రోడ్డు ప్రమాదం జరిగింది. విజయవాడకు వెళ్తున్న భవానీ భక్తులను స్కార్పియో ఢీకొట్టంది. ఈ ఘటనలో నలుగురు మరణించారు.
content: విజయవాడ కనకదుర్గమ్మ దర్శనానికి వెళ్తున్న భవానీ భక్తులను మృత్యువు కబళించింది. కాకినాడ జిల్లా ప్రత్తిపాడు నియోజకవర్గం పరిధిలోని కత్తిపూడి జాతీయ రహదారిపై గురువారం తెల్లవారుజామున చోటుచేసుకున్న ఘోర రోడ్డు ప్రమాదంలో నలుగురు భవానీ మాలధారులు అక్కడికక్కడే ప్రాణాలు కోల్పోయారు. ఈ హృదయవిదారక ఘటన స్థానికంగా తీవ్ర విషాదాన్ని నింపింది.విజయనగరం జిల్లా డెంకాడ మండలానికి చెందిన దాదాపు 40 మంది భవానీ భక్తులు ప్రత్యేకంగా ఒక ప్రైవేట్ ట్రావెల్స్ బస్సును మాట్లాడుకుని విజయవాడ వైపు ప్రయాణమయ్యారు. కనకదుర్గమ్మను దర్శనం చేసుకునేందుకు వెళ్తున్నారు. అయితే వీరి బస్సు కాకినాడ జిల్లా కత్తిపూడి సమీపానికి చేరుకోగానే వాహనంలో సడన్‌గా సాంకేతిక సమస్య తలెత్తింది.దీంతో అప్రమత్తమైన బస్సు డ్రైవర్ వాహనాన్ని జాతీయ రహదారి పక్కగా సురక్షితంగా నిలిపివేశారు. బస్సు రిపేర్ అవుతుండటంతో, సుదీర్ఘ ప్రయాణంతో అలసిపోయిన కొందరు భక్తులు కాసేపు విశ్రాంతి తీసుకునేందుకు బస్సు దిగారు. ఇందులో భాగంగా కొందరు టీ తాగేందుకు రహదారి దాటి ఎదురుగా ఉన్న షాపు వైపు వెళ్లేందుకు ప్రయత్నించారు.సరిగ్గా అదే సమయంలో అత్యంత వేగంగా ఒక స్కార్పియో వాహనం రోడ్డు దాటుతున్న భక్తులను బలంగా ఢీకొట్టింది. ఢీకొట్టిన తీవ్రతకు భక్తులు గాల్లోకి లేచి దూరంగా పడిపోయారు. ఈ ప్రమాదంలో తీవ్ర గాయాలపాలైన ముగ్గురు భక్తులు ఘటన స్థలంలోనే రక్తమడుగులో ప్రాణాలు వదిలారు. తీవ్రంగా గాయపడిన మరో భక్తుడిని స్థానికులు, పోలీసులు వెంటనే గమనించి సమీపంలోని ఆసుపత్రికి తరలించే ప్రయత్నం చేశారు. అయితే ఆసుపత్రికి తరలిస్తుండగా మార్గమధ్యంలో పరిస్థితి విషమించి ఆయన కూడా మృతి చెందారు.ఈ దుర్ఘటనలో మరణించిన వారిని విజయనగరం జిల్లా డెంకాడకు చెందినవారిగా పోలీసులు గుర్తించారు. చిరికిడి ఎర్రయ్య (38), లింగాల సీతారాం (45), బోనెల సత్తిబాబు (40), తాటిపూడి శివప్రసాద్ (40) మరణించారు. ఒకే ప్రాంతానికి చెందిన నలుగురు భక్తులు దుర్మరణం పాలవడంతో డెంకాడ గ్రామంలో తీవ్ర విషాద ఛాయలు అలముకున్నాయి.ప్రమాద సమాచారం అందుకున్న వెంటనే పోలీసులు హుటాహుటిన ప్రమాద స్థలానికి చేరుకున్నారు. ప్రమాద స్థలాన్ని పరిశీలించి, మృతదేహాలను పోస్టుమార్టం నిమిత్తం ప్రభుత్వ ఆసుపత్రికి తరలించారు. ఈ మేరకు కేసు నమోదు చేసి దర్యాప్తు చేస్తున్నారు.ఈ ఘోర ప్రమాదంపై మంత్రి నారా లోకేశ్ స్పందించారు. 'కాకినాడ జిల్లా కత్తిపూడి వద్ద రోడ్డు ప్రమాదంలో విజయనగరం జిల్లా డెంకాడకు చెందిన భవానీ భక్తులు మృతి చెందడం చాలా బాధాకరం. మృతులకు నివాళులు అర్పిస్తున్నాను. వారి ఆత్మకు శాంతి కలగాలని ప్రార్థిస్తున్నాను. మృతుల కుటుంబాలను ప్రభుత్వం ఆదుకుంటుంది.' అని లోకేశ్ ఎక్స్‌లోపోస్ట్ చేశారు.

title: After attack on Tiger Shroff, Maharashtra govt cracks down on bike taxis | Mumbai news
description: Rapido said the individual linked to the Juhu shooting had not been active as a rider on its platform since October 14.  | Mumbai news
content: The state transport department is cracking down on bike taxis following Sunday’s Tiger Shroff shooting, after one of the accused was identified as a Rapido rider. On Wednesday, transport minister Pratap Sarnaik instructed aggregator companies to thoroughly vet their riders’ antecedents, adding that the state is stepping up enforcement of its bike taxi policy.“The incident involving Tiger Shroff has raised issues regarding passenger safety and recruitment policies of aggregator companies. It is our fault that they don’t ask for domicile proof and police verification of these drivers while registering them. By next week, we will announce stringent steps for aggregators to follow,” said Sarnaik.Also read: Tiger Shroff shooting case: Shooters surveyed Salman, Aamir Khan and Ranbir Kapoor’s homesGovernment reviews implementation of bike taxi policyThe government has been struggling to monitor the bike taxi policy ever since it was rolled out in September, Sarnaik has also instructed the transport commissioner to prepare a detailed report on how the policy is being implemented. In Sunday’s incident at Juhu, it was found that the shooters’ getaway man had been a Rapido rider. As he waited with a motorcycle on the sidelines, his associates fired at the actor’s car before fleeing the scene on the motorcycle.According to RTO officers, aggregators have not been thoroughly verifying their riders’ antecedents. Neither is proof of identity and residence sought and verified, nor is police verification undertaken, they said. Another key requirement is that riders must be domiciled in Maharashtra. The minister has directed aggregators to rigorously vet all applicants to make sure none has a criminal record. Also read: Monday Musings: In bike-taxi battle, Pune’s commuters are paying the priceAuto and taxi unions demand disclosure of enforcement actionMeanwhile, auto-rickshaw and taxi unions, which fear that bike taxis will cut into their business, are demanding that the transport department make public details of the action taken against bike taxis. They claim no information has been submitted by app-based companies to the transport department and question whether the policy remains on paper.Keshav Nana Kshirsagar, president of Maharashtra Kamgar Sabha, said, “There is a need to cancel the registration of bike taxis. If the companies employ people without adequate document verification, individuals with serious criminal backgrounds could potentially operate in major cities such as Mumbai for years. This is not merely a law-and-order issue but a national security concern.” He had demanded a high-level inquiry and strict action against those found responsible.Also read: Pune RTO turns up heat on illegal bike taxis, seeks police action against appsRapido says accused was inactive as a rider since October 14Rapido, for its part, had released a statement after Sunday’s incident, saying “the individual mentioned in media reports had been registered on its platform but had not been active as a captain since October 14”.A Rapido spokesperson said, “Individuals in India’s large gig economy commonly register on multiple platforms simultaneously. The individual had used its service as a customer on the day of the incident. The company said it was in constant contact with the authorities and cooperating with the investigation, adding that it had zero tolerance for violence or criminal activities.”The RTOs have been instructed to crack down on violations of the bike taxi policy. For instance, they will initiate action against two-wheelers other than electric bikes being used to ferry passengers.Also read: Tiger Shroff shooting accused had a short fuse, say neighboursProvisional licences expire as department checks complianceAggregators had been allowed to operate bike taxis under provisional licences for a month in mid-September, but these have since expired, RTO officials said. Aggregators were expected to obtain permanent licences but the department is examining compliance.Uber, Rapido and Ola had each registered around 50 electric bikes while seeking permits, even as thousands of petrol-driven two-wheelers are allegedly operating as taxis on the ground.“Simply having a policy in place doesn’t work if it is not thoroughly enforced. When the government allows private operators into the public domain, monitoring them is essential,” said AV Shenoy, transport expert and founding member of the Mumbai Mobility Forum.

title: Supreme Court directs mother to take 7-year-old daughter back to US by Dec 31 in custody dispute | India News
description: The Supreme Court has ordered a 7-year-old girl to return to the US by December 31 in a custody dispute, ruling that her welfare is best served there. | India News
content: The Supreme Court has ordered a seven-year-old girl to return to the United States nearly four years after her mother brought her to India in violation of a US court’s custody order, holding that the child’s best interests would be served by growing up and receiving her education in the country of which she is a citizen.A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan allowed the father’s appeal against a Karnataka high court judgment that had declined to direct the child’s return, ruling that the girl’s formative years in India with her mother did not establish that her welfare could be served only by remaining here.Also Read I ‘Children have a fundamental right to internet access, blanket bans disproportionate’: Supreme Court‘Welfare of child’ governing principleDirecting the mother to travel with the child to the US by December 31, 2026, the court said the decision rested primarily on the child’s welfare, while the circumstances in which she was brought to India and the need to respect the orders of a competent foreign court further supported the conclusion.“The welfare of the child has remained the governing consideration throughout,” said the bench, adding that the principle that a parent should not benefit from their own wrongdoing was relevant only after the child’s welfare had been fully considered. Senior advocates Mukul Rohatgi, along with advocate Prabhjir Jauhar, appeared for the father. In August 2022, a California court, after hearing both sides, granted them joint custody and shared parenting, with an equal division of time with the child. It restrained either parent from taking her out of California without other’s consent or a court order.Formative years in the USBarely two weeks later, on September 8, 2022, the mother left the US with the child and travelled to India. In December that year, the California court recorded a violation of its earlier order and directed the mother to return the child to the father’s physical custody in California.The father subsequently approached the Karnataka High Court seeking the child’s return. The high court dismissed his plea, reasoning, among other things, that the child was comfortable with her mother, had begun attending school in India and had not been shown to have suffered any harm in her care.The Supreme Court, however, found these considerations insufficient to conclude the girl’s welfare could be served only by remaining with her mother.Also Read I 'Don't meddle with powers of other agencies': Supreme Court to ED in case against Pinarayi Vijayan, stays probe for 7 daysThe bench acknowledged that the child had spent nearly four years in India and that her early formative years had unfolded here. But it said this did not establish that she could not be better served by returning to the US. “On the other hand, the child is a citizen of the United States and is entitled to all the benefits that such citizenship carries”.Importantly, the court made clear that it was not compelling the mother to relocate to the US against her wishes or to continue the marriage. But it said she could not insist that the child must also remain in India or deny the father the joint custody and shared parenting that had been granted to him.

title:
10 Windows laptops that could challenge your idea of what an everyday laptop should offer | Technology News
(HT Tech)
description: We'll be comparing 10 Windows laptops across productivity, portability, display quality and everyday performance to help you narrow down your next upgrade. | Technology News
content: Choosing a Windows laptop in current times is no longer just about picking a processor and checking the amount of RAM. Display quality, battery life, portability and the kind of work you do can make a massive difference to everyday use. An OLED screen may appeal to someone who spends hours reading or watching videos, while a business-focused laptop may be a better fit for office work, coding and frequent travel. AI-focused processors also feature in newer models, although their benefits depend on the applications you use. This article is going to bring together 10 Windows laptops from HP, Dell, ASUS, Lenovo and Samsung, ranging from slim OLED models to conventional productivity machines.Factors to consider when buying a Windows laptopProcessor and workload: For documents, browsing and video calls, a mainstream modern processor is usually sufficient. Coding, heavier creative applications and sustained multitasking may benefit from a more capable CPU. Check software compatibility if you are considering an ARM-based model.Display quality: OLED panels offer deep blacks and strong contrast, while IPS displays can be practical for office work. Also compare resolution, brightness, refresh rate and whether the screen supports touch.RAM and storage: Aim for at least 16GB RAM if you regularly keep multiple applications and browser tabs open. A 512GB SSD suits many users, while 1TB offers more room for large projects and offline files. Check whether memory can be upgraded later.Portability and battery life: A 14-inch laptop is usually easier to carry than a larger model, while a 15-inch screen gives you more working space. Compare official battery claims, charging options, weight and port selection before deciding.Top 3 features of Windows laptops An OLED display and a lightweight design are the main reasons to consider the HP OmniBook 5 for everyday computing. It is positioned for users who want a portable Windows laptop for office tasks, browsing, video calls and entertainment. This Amazon listing is associated with an OLED configuration, but interested buyers should confirm the exact processor and memory variant before ordering, particularly if they rely on specialist Windows applications. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Buyers generally praise the OmniBook 5 for its OLED display, lightweight design, smooth everyday performance and impressive battery life. Some remain cautious about ARM software compatibility, so users who depend on particular professional applications should check support before making a purchase.Why we picked itThe OmniBook 5 is worth considering if portability and OLED picture quality are higher priorities than gaming performance. It could suit students, office users and frequent travellers who want a laptop for everyday work and entertainment. The Dell 15 takes a practical approach to everyday productivity, pairing an Intel Core Ultra 5 225H processor with 16GB of DDR5 memory and a 512GB SSD. Its conventional laptop design and selection of ports suit desk-based work, office documents and multitasking. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Reviews highlight reliable everyday performance, a comfortable keyboard, useful ports and good thermal behaviour. However, buyers find the display less vibrant than they would like, and battery life is not considered one of its strongest points.Why we picked itThis Dell is worth comparing if you prefer a familiar 15.6-inch work laptop with a modern Intel processor, 16GB RAM and practical connectivity. It is geared towards office work and multitasking rather than specialised graphics workloads. The ASUS Vivobook S14 combines a compact 14-inch design with an OLED panel and AMD Ryzen AI processing. This configuration includes 16GB RAM and a 512GB SSD, giving it a sensible foundation for multitasking, research, video calls and everyday creative work. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Reviews praise the Vivobook S14 for its OLED screen, comfortable keyboard, long battery life, lightweight design and smooth multitasking. Brightness and reflections remain common complaints, however, so consider your working environment if you frequently use a laptop near windows or outdoors.Why we picked itThe Vivobook S14 brings an OLED display to a portable productivity laptop with AMD Ryzen AI processing. It is worth considering for students and professionals who want a compact machine for office tasks, browsing and visual content. The Dell Inspiron 3530 is a conventional productivity laptop built around the 13th Gen Intel Core i7-1355U processor, 16GB RAM and a 512GB SSD. Its 15.6-inch Full HD display offers a familiar workspace for spreadsheets, documents, web research and online meetings. It is a straightforward option for users who value everyday computing over a thin-and-light design or dedicated gaming hardware. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Reviews generally find the Inspiron capable of handling office work and everyday tasks. Its straightforward design and keyboard are seen as practical strengths, although sustained workloads can expose cooling limitations, which may matter to users who regularly run demanding applications for long periods.Why we picked itThe Inspiron 3530 is worth considering for buyers who need a familiar, full-size Windows laptop for office work, study and routine multitasking. Its Core i7 configuration is the main attraction for users who do not need a dedicated graphics card. The ASUS Zenbook 14 is aimed at buyers who want a premium, portable laptop without giving up a high-quality display. The UX3405CA-QL1014WS configuration uses an Intel Core Ultra 5 225H, while ASUS lists OLED display options, 16GB of memory and a 512GB SSD for this variant. Its compact build suits commuting and travel, and the port selection includes Thunderbolt 4 for compatible accessories. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Buyers describe the Zenbook 14 as lightweight and easy to carry, with positive feedback about coding, casual gaming and browsing. The display and sound quality also receive praise, while fast charging is appreciated. Overall, the supplied feedback describes it as worth the price.Why we picked itThe Zenbook 14 stands out for its portable design, OLED display options and Thunderbolt 4 connectivity. It is worth considering for professionals who move between workspaces and want a premium screen without carrying a larger 15- or 16-inch laptop. The Lenovo Yoga Slim 7 Aura Edition is a slim laptop for people who want portability without settling for a basic display. Lenovo's related Yoga Slim 7 configuration pairs the Core Ultra 5 226V with 16GB LPDDR5X memory, a 512GB SSD and a 14-inch OLED screen. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Buyers appreciate the Yoga Slim 7's display quality and battery life. Feedback also highlights its build quality, keyboard comfort and practical port selection, suggesting that users value it as a portable work machine rather than just a laptop for media consumption.Why we picked itThe Yoga Slim 7 Aura Edition is worth considering for buyers who want a slim productivity laptop with a quality screen and a portable build. It is particularly relevant for professionals who work across home, office and travel settings. The Samsung Galaxy Book6 combines a restrained design with a Windows laptop setup for everyday productivity. The laptop comes with 16GB RAM and a 512GB SSD. Samsung offers Galaxy Book6 configurations with Intel Core Ultra processors, a WUXGA display and Dolby Atmos audio. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Users praise the Galaxy Book6's premium design, sharp display, smooth everyday performance and battery endurance. Some find the chassis slightly heavy, while others feel the keyboard could use its available space more effectively. The overall feedback highlights design and everyday usability.Why we picked itThe Galaxy Book6 is worth considering if you want a modern Windows laptop with a clean design and practical connectivity. Its exact configuration matters, so confirm the processor and screen size before comparing it with other premium options here. A convertible laptop can be useful when your work moves between typing, reading and touchscreen interaction. The HP OmniBook X Flip OLED pairs a 360-degree hinge with an OLED touchscreen and an Intel Core Ultra 5 226V in the referenced configuration. It offers 16GB LPDDR5X memory and a 1TB SSD, giving it more storage than several other laptops in this list. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Reviews highlight the vibrant OLED screen, sharp resolution, smooth 120Hz refresh rate and versatile convertible design. The keyboard and speakers receive less enthusiastic feedback compared with the display and performance, so buyers should weigh the flexibility of the hinge against their everyday typing needs.Why we picked itThe OmniBook X Flip is worth considering if you want a laptop that can also serve as a touchscreen device for reading, presenting or sketching. Its convertible design and 1TB storage make it distinct from traditional clamshell options. The Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 is a practical option for everyday work, online classes and general home use, it has an Intel Core Ultra 5 322 processor. Lenovo's matching Slim 3i Gen 11 configuration offers a 15.3-inch WUXGA anti-glare display, 16GB DDR5 memory and a 512GB SSD. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Feedback around the IdeaPad Slim range highlights its clean design, comfortable everyday performance and useful display size. Buyers also appreciate its keyboard and portability, while graphics performance remains a limitation for users who expect to run demanding games or graphics-heavy applications.Why we picked itThe IdeaPad Slim 3 is worth considering if you need a straightforward laptop for study, office documents and everyday multitasking. Its larger screen and anti-glare panel make it relevant for people who spend long periods working with text. The Lenovo ThinkBook 14 is aimed at users who want a compact laptop for work, it comes with an AMD Ryzen 5 220 processor and 1TB storage. Its business-oriented positioning makes it worth comparing for office productivity, web-based tools and multitasking. What are buyers saying on Amazon?Available feedback highlights the ThinkBook's lightweight build, responsive everyday performance and useful business features. Buyers also value the listed 1TB storage, bright display and compact form factor for work. Check the exact listing configuration before using these impressions to compare variants.Why we picked itThe ThinkBook 14 is worth considering if you need a work-oriented laptop with generous storage in a compact form. title: 7 luggage myths I stopped believing after years of travelling across multiple destinations and transport options | Travel
description: From cabin trolleys to duffle bags, here are common luggage myths about weight, capacity, wheels, protection and packing worth ignoring.   | Travel
content: After travelling with more suitcases than I care to count, I have become slightly obsessed with how people pack. I notice the huge suitcase being dragged through the airport for a three-night trip, the tiny cabin bag that somehow weighs more than the person carrying it and the traveller trying to close an expandable case while sitting on it. I have done versions of all three myself. The funny thing about luggage is that we tend to shop for it by looking at the specifications first. How many litres does it hold? How many wheels does it have? Is it hard shell or soft shell? How many compartments are inside? Those details matter, but they do not always tell you how the bag will behave once you actually start travelling with it. After years of regular flights, I have found that some of the most common things we believe about luggage are only partly true. A larger suitcase does not necessarily mean more useful packing space, a lightweight bag is not automatically the most comfortable one and a duffle is not always the obvious choice for a strict cabin allowance.Myth 1: A bigger suitcase means you can pack moreTechnically, yes. Practically, not always. A large suitcase can hold a lot more than you need for a short trip, which sounds like a good thing until you remember that airlines have weight limits. You can have half the case empty and still be asked to pay for excess baggage if everything inside pushes you over the allowance.I have become much more conscious of this after travelling frequently. When I am packing for a short trip, I would rather have a case that makes me stop adding unnecessary things than one that gives me enough room to pack for every possible version of the holiday. The same applies to cabin luggage. A bag may have plenty of physical capacity, but if your airline allows only 7kg, that is still the number that matters at the airport. Myth 2: Hard shell luggage is always heavierThe material is only one part of a suitcase's weight. Wheels, handles, locks, frames and internal fittings can add quite a bit too, which is why two bags of a similar size can feel completely different on a luggage scale. I have used both hard and soft luggage extensively, and I would not choose between them simply by looking at the outer material. A hard shell can be useful when I am carrying something that needs protection, particularly electronics or other fragile items. A soft case can make more sense when most of what I am carrying is clothing, and I want some flexibility while packing. The empty weight is worth checking, but it should not be the only number you look at. Myth 3: A duffle is always better when your cabin allowance is only 7kgThis one has some truth behind it, which is why the myth survives. A simple fabric duffle can be considerably lighter than a wheeled cabin bag because it does not need wheels, a telescopic handle and the other hardware that comes with a trolley. If the airline gives you a strict weight limit, saving weight on the bag itself can leave more allowance for your clothes and other belongings.The catch becomes obvious when you actually carry a fully packed duffle through an airport. I have travelled with bags that felt perfectly manageable when I picked them up at home and considerably less charming after a long walk between gates. A trolley gives you wheels for a reason. So if I am taking a short trip with mostly soft clothing, a lightweight duffle can be a very sensible option. If I know I will be spending hours walking around an airport or changing between different forms of transport, I am much happier rolling my luggage. Myth 4: Four- or eight-spinner wheels are always betterFour- or eight-wheeled suitcases have completely changed how easy luggage can feel on a smooth airport floor. Being able to push a suitcase beside you rather than constantly pulling it behind you is particularly useful when you have another bag, a child or a coffee in your other hand.But airport floors are not the only surfaces you will encounter.Stairs, uneven pavements, station platforms and crowded public transport can all make a different wheel configuration more practical. Four wheels also add weight and occupy some space within the case, so the choice is not quite as simple as saying that more wheels equal better luggage. For someone who spends most of their travel time inside airports and hotels, spinner wheels can be brilliant. For someone who regularly lifts their luggage, uses public transport or walks on uneven surfaces, other designs can work just as well. Myth 5: Soft luggage does not protect your belongingsI think soft luggage gets judged a little unfairly here. It is not trying to do the same job as a rigid case. If I am packing clothes, shoes, toiletries and other things that can handle being squeezed together, flexible luggage can be extremely useful. It can fit into spaces where a rigid case cannot and is often forgiving when you have one awkwardly shaped item that refuses to sit neatly inside the bag.I would think differently if I were carrying fragile equipment. A rigid outer shell offers a level of protection that fabric simply cannot provide, and that can matter a lot when you are checking a bag into the hold. The contents should influence the luggage choice just as much as the size of the suitcase. Myth 6: An expandable suitcase gives you more airline allowanceI love expandable luggage for one very specific reason. It is brilliant when you come home with more than you left with. That extra space can be incredibly useful after shopping, especially when you have managed to squeeze everything into a smaller configuration on the way out. The mistake is assuming that the additional capacity somehow changes your baggage allowance. It does not.If your airline allows 15kg, an expanded suitcase weighing 18kg is still an 18kg suitcase. I have found it much more useful to think of expansion as extra volume rather than extra capacity in the airline sense. It gives you somewhere to put things. It does not permit you to add more weight. Myth 7: The lightest suitcase is always the best suitcaseThis is perhaps the myth I disagree with most. A lightweight suitcase can be a huge advantage, especially when you are travelling on a strict cabin allowance. If the empty bag weighs less, more of your allowance can go towards the things you actually want to take.But there comes a point where saving a few hundred grams is not worth compromising on everything else. I have had travel days where a good handle mattered more than the empty weight of the suitcase. I have walked long distances through airports where smooth wheels made a bigger difference than an extra bit of packing space. And when I am carrying electronics, I care far more about protection than saving the last few grams. After using so many different types of luggage, I have stopped looking for one perfect bag. The luggage that works for a quick work trip may not be what I want for a family holiday, and the bag that is brilliant for airport transfers may not be the one I want to carry on public transport. That is really the point of all these luggage myths. There is no universal winner.A duffle can make sense when weight is your biggest concern. A trolley can be far more comfortable when you have a long airport day ahead. A hard shell can be the sensible choice for fragile belongings, while a soft case may make packing clothing and odd-shaped items much easier. I now choose luggage based on the trip first and the specifications second. It is a small change, but after this many flights, I have found it saves me from buying a bag that looks perfect on paper and turns out to be completely wrong once I actually start travelling with it. title: LuLu Group plans  ₹2,500-crore investment, targets 25 outlets across Delhi-NCR by 2030 | Real Estate News
description: LuLu Group plans to invest  ₹2,500 cr to open 25 outlets across Delhi-NCR by 2030, including a 30,000-sq-ft store in Gurugram by the end of the financial year  | Real Estate News
content: UAE-based LuLu Group, which has opened a 1-lakh-sq-ft hypermarket in Greater Noida, is targeting an investment of ₹2500 crore to establish 25 outlets across Delhi-NCR by 2030. The outlets will comprise a mix of hypermarkets and smaller daily concept stores, depending on the catchment and population of each location, a senior company executive told Hindustan Times.The outlets will vary in size, with daily concept stores typically spanning around 30,000 sq ft and larger hypermarkets occupying larger spaces, said Jayakumar Gangadharan, Director – UP, Delhi NCR, and Telangana, LuLu Group, adding that the company is targeting the number of stores rather than a specific total retail area.The LuLu hypermarket in Greater Noida spans 1 lakh sq ft on the lower ground floor of I-Thum's Galleria Mall. The company sees its opening as an entry point into the wider Delhi-NCR market rather than a standalone expansion into Greater Noida.“We were targeting NCR as a region. We have signed up at other locations as well, including Gurugram, and are looking at more spaces. The projects are at different stages, and this one happened to be ready earlier. We got a bigger space here (Greater Noida), and I am glad we could start with a bigger concept,” Gangadharan said.The company has leased the Greater Noida property for 15 years. The hypermarket is expected to generate additional footfall for the mall, which currently receives around 8,000 visitors a day.Also Read: LuLu opens 1 lakh sq ft hypermarket in Greater Noida“We are expecting a 70-80% increase in the mall's footfall, and we are hoping to account for around 50% of the total footfall,” he said.LuLu's Gurugram plansLuLu Group is also planning to open a store spanning around 30,000 sq ft in a mall in Gurugram by the end of the current financial year. Fit-outs are expected to begin soon, with the project currently at the design and planning stage, the executive said.The company is looking at mall properties across Delhi-NCR, particularly in densely populated areas and emerging residential catchments. It is open to both larger hypermarket formats and smaller stores, typically ranging from 30,000 sq ft to 70,000 sq ft, depending on space availability and the location's potential.“We started in Uttar Pradesh with Lucknow, and Delhi-NCR was obviously the next market we wanted to penetrate and expand into. The NCR region is densely populated, and we see potential to have multiple stores in each city, including Delhi and Gurugram,” he said.The company is also exploring both outright purchases and leases for its expansion. Leasing space in existing malls allows it to use established retail infrastructure, while its own mall developments offer an opportunity to create an integrated retail environment, he said.Expansion in Lucknow and other citiesIn Lucknow, where the group first established its presence in Uttar Pradesh with a 22 lakh sq ft mall in 2022, LuLu is planning two additional stores, each around 30,000 sq ft, in Ashiyana and Aliganj. Both are mall properties, and fit-outs are nearly complete, Gangadharan said.The company is also gradually expanding its omnichannel and online services. These are expected to be introduced in Greater Noida in line with the model it operates in Lucknow.The Greater Noida hypermarket is expected to engage at least 1,500 people, directly and indirectly, according to the executive. In Lucknow, the group's operations have generated employment for around 12,000-15,000 people, including direct and indirect jobs.The retailer's product portfolio spans domestic and international offerings, with sourcing operations across 32 countries. Its stores offer a wide range of products across categories, Gangadharan said.India investment planIn 2022, LuLu Group announced plans to invest in India over four years across malls, hypermarkets and other businesses. The proposed investments covered several cities, including Gurugram, Noida, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai, as well as locations across Kerala.The Greater Noida outlet is the group's 23rd store, while projects in Ahmedabad and Visakhapatnam are at the design stage, the executive said, adding the company plans to invest nearly ₹2500 crore in NCR and UP.The group has also opened stores in Bengaluru and Chennai, including a 40,000-sq-ft outlet in Bengaluru and stores spanning around 1 lakh sq ft and 30,000 sq ft in Chennai, respectively, Gangadharan said.The company has also expanded through partnerships with metro rail operators. On October 12, it opened its first hypermarket in Chennai at Shenoy Nagar Metro Station on the Chennai Metro's Green Line, alongside a smaller LuLu Daily store at Chennai Central Metro Station. The Shenoy Nagar hypermarket spans around 1 lakh sq ft and includes a supermarket and department store, with LuLu Fashion Store and LuLu Connect outlets.Also Read: IKEA plans 30 India stores by 2030, bets on transit-linked locations where 'not everybody has to drive'With operations spanning more than 35 countries, LuLu Group has a retail network of more than 285 stores and 24 shopping malls across the Gulf Cooperation Council region, Egypt, India and the Far East, according to the company.

title: Govt asks TV channels to curb inflammatory debates, says mute, interrupt or cut the feed | India News
description: Centre has asked TV channels to exercise editorial control over debates, mute abusive panellists, avoid live anti-terror operation coverage, use verified facts. | India News
