content: The Union government has asked television channels to exercise stricter editorial control over debates and panel discussions to prevent communal, anti-national, derogatory or inflammatory content from being aired, directing them to mute speakers, interrupt programmes or cut feeds where necessary.In an advisory issued on Wednesday, the information and broadcasting ministry also cautioned broadcasters against live coverage of anti-terror operations and urged them to use verified facts, approved maps and artificial intelligence tools without compromising news accuracy.Also Read | IB ministry pulls up TV channels for ‘distasteful, disturbing & violent content’Government asks TV channels to curb inflammatory debates“Adequate editorial control (including, but not limited to careful selection and pre-sensitisation of the panellists/participants) should be exercised. Wherever necessary, immediate remedial measures such as muting, disclaimers, interruption or discontinuation of feed should be implemented in order to prevent airing of derogatory, abusive or inflammatory content,” the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting’s advisory released on Wednesday said.The advisory, which is addressed to all TV channels but is largely aimed at news broadcasters, also asks channels to stay away from live coverage of anti-terror operations, use only Survey of India-approved maps of the country in all their broadcasts and graphics, and limit artificial intelligence (AI) tools to an assisting role, without compromising the accuracy or authenticity of news.“The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has observed instances of non-compliance with the provisions of the Programme Code prescribed under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 and the Cable Television Network Rules, 1994 by various private satellite television channels,” the advisory said.Also Read | Centre asks BARC to resume TV ratings for news channelsAdvisory calls for verified reporting, approved maps, responsible use of AIThis follows a meeting of the Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), constituted under the Cable Television Networks (Amendment) Rules, 2021, which observed that several TV channels were not adhering to the Programme Code. The committee also emphasised that inappropriate behaviour or language should not be normalised on air.Channels were also told to show “due caution, responsibility and editorial discretion” while airing violent, graphic or disturbing visuals, so as not to offend good taste or decency or cause unnecessary distress to viewers. On crime and violence, the ministry said reports must be based on verified facts and be balanced, so that false insinuations and half-truths are not aired.Channels should avoid sensational reporting that may glorify or normalise unlawful or socially undesirable behaviour, and should not repeat or loop disturbing visuals excessively, the advisory said. “The use of appropriate blurring or masking techniques is suggested wherever warranted so as to not offend good taste and decency of the viewers,” it said.Special care is needed when showing visuals of crimes against women and children, the advisory said. Channels were also asked to strictly follow the Supreme Court’s repeated directions not to reveal the identities of victims of sexual offences.For natural calamities, disasters and major accidents, the ministry said visuals should be time-stamped where necessary to avoid unnecessary panic among viewers, and reporting should be based on verified facts.Broadcasters were also asked to tighten their editorial checks and make sure everyone involved in news gathering, editing, production and broadcast knows the Programme Code. They were encouraged to hold regular workshops and training sessions for their teams.

title: Video: Elephant carrying silver howdah panics at Karnataka Dasara celebration, damages vehicles before being tranquilised | Trending
description: Shivamogga's Dasara Jamboo Savari ended in chaos after Somanna, the elephant carrying the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari, panicked and ran amok.  | Trending
content: A silver howdah-bearing elephant panicked during a Dasara procession at Karnataka’s Shivamogga, running amok for over an hour and damaging multiple vehicles before veterinarians tranquilised it. The elephant, Somanna, lost its way in narrow lanes after getting frightened by the crowd. The officials confirmed no spectators were injured.What had happened?The Dasara procession started in a disciplined way without any chaos. Everyone was walking in an orderly fashion, including Somanna, who was carrying the Ambari, a silver howdah bearing the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari. There was also another elephant, Sagar, who was leading from the front.Also Read: Elephant runs amok in Varanasi, large-scale rescue bid launchedHowever, a small change in formation triggered chaos, leading to Somanna running amok, charging at vehicles, and ultimately being tranquilised by forest department officials.The locals claimed that the situation occurred after Somanna replaced Sagar this year. Every year, Sagar carries the Ambari, but this year Somanna was selected because the forest department relied on the elephant’s exceptional track record in rescue operations.According to eyewitnesses, Somanna got frightened when it was moved to the front. It got scared and panicked, then entered narrow lanes. Eventually, the animal became more aggressive and tried to topple the Ambari. In a panic, it rammed into a car, damaging the silver structure and several other vehicles. Reportedly, the elephant, in its scared state, also tried to lift a car.As the situation ran out of control, veterinarians tranquillised the elephant with a dart. Eventually, Somanna stopped trumpeting and stood still. The forest department staff acted quickly, removed the Ambari, and chained the Somanna to take it to a tent built for elephants. During this, the mahout who was trying to calm the elephant sustained injuries. What did the authorities say?“Fortunately, no one was injured. Another Utsava Murthy has been taken to Banni Mantapa, and the Dasara festivities are continuing. The reasons for the incident are being looked into,” Deputy Commissioner Prabhulinga Kavalikatti told ANI. The official called the incident “unexpected” and “accidental”.Also Read: Kerala temple elephant goes on rampage, flips car like toy in dramatic videoCCF said, "Somanna got scared and tried to return to its tethering place. It did not attack anyone, but damaged some vehicles in panic. The last-minute changes are not the reason. We are focusing on safely moving the elephant back."Amid all the chaos, Sagar, the other elephant, reportedly kept walking calmly.(With inputs from ANI)

title: Chetwode, Dinkar to a Field Marshal’s baton: How the Army chief’s office has changed | India News
description: It is the prerogative of an Army chief to shape the office to his own taste, people aware of the matter said. | India News
content: A corner of the Army chief’s office in New Delhi’s South Block has quietly evolved over the years, reflecting the choices of successive chiefs of the world’s second-largest army.From Chetwode’s ‘country first’ motto that hung on the wood-panelled wall for decades to Ramdhari Singh Dinkar’s stirring verses and now a Field Marshal’s ceremonial baton, each change has reinforced the office’s military character and gravitas, people aware of the matter said on Thursday.It is the prerogative of an Army chief to shape the office to his own taste, they added.The corner, which also displays a pair of elephant tusks, has long served as a favoured backdrop for successive Army chiefs to strike a pose with visiting dignitaries and exchange mementos. It has also been the setting for photographs of outgoing chiefs with their successors during the change of command.‘Country-first' mottoThe longest-standing fixture in the Army chief’s office was Field Marshal Philip W Chetwode’s motto, delivered by him at the inauguration of the Indian Military Academy in Dehradun in 1932.It read, “The safety, honour and welfare of your country come first, always and every time. The honour, welfare and comfort of the men you command come next. Your own ease, comfort and safety come last, always and every time.”Chetwode’s words remained on the wall for decades, including during General VP Malik’s tenure as Army chief from 1997 to 2000, Malik confirmed to HT.The two most recent Army chiefs added their own touch to the office.Dinkar's versesAfter General Upendra Dwivedi took over as Army chief in 2024, the Chetwode motto gave way to verses from Ramdhari Singh Dinkar’s poem Shakti Aur Kshama, which underscores that restraint and forgiveness must be backed by strength.Written in Hindi, it loosely translates to: “Truth be told, humility shines brightest when backed by the arrow; only the peace accord of those with strength is revered. The world values patience, forgiveness and compassion only when there’s true strength behind them.”Other changesDwivedi, who retired in June 2026, completed the corner’s makeover by installing portraits of Field Marshals Sam Manekshaw and KM Cariappa.Dinkar’s verses made way for the Field Marshal’s baton under the current Army chief, General Dhiraj Seth. Portraits of the two military legends have also been replaced with newer versions, recasting the corner as a tribute to India’s Field Marshals.Seth has made another change. In the adjacent Army chief’s lounge, the painting titled Karam Kshetra—Field of Deeds has been replaced by the Indian Army emblem. The Karam Kshetra artwork had replaced an iconic painting depicting the signing of the Instrument of Surrender at the end of the 1971 war with Pakistan, which led to the liberation of Bangladesh.Its removal in December 2024 sparked questions within sections of the defence establishment. The Mahabharata-inspired painting featured Arjuna riding his chariot driven by Lord Krishna, snow-capped mountains, Pangong Lake in eastern Ladakh and the ancient philosopher Chanakya, alongside modern military hardware, including tanks, infantry combat vehicles, light combat helicopters, Apache attack helicopters, multi-barrel rocket launchers and drones.Only a handful of senior officers, including Seth and Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, continue to work out of South Block—the defence ministry has relocated to Kartavya Bhavan-2. Both the South and North Blocks will eventually be transformed into the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, envisioned as the world’s largest museum, spanning 155,000 square metres.

title: BJP, Samajwadi Party brace for yet another numbers test in Uttar Pradesh MLC elections | Hindustan Times
description: Expected in November-December, the elections will see MLAs vote to elect members to the Upper House.
content: The political manoeuvring during the Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh earlier this month could find an echo in the upcoming polls to 10 Legislative Council seats, with the ruling BJP and the SP facing another test of numbers, candidate selection and the possibility of cross-voting ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Expected in November-December, the elections will see MLAs vote to elect members to the Upper House, bringing party strength and the management of legislators back into focus. The contest comes after the Rajya Sabha nominations brought the possibility of cross-voting and the risks associated with fielding additional candidates into focus. 10 MLCs in Upper HouseThe terms of the 10 sitting MLCs in the 100-member Upper House expire on January 30, 2027. ECI is expected to hold the polls one or two months earlier, with the model code of conduct for the Assembly elections likely to come into force in January.“The ECI will issue the notification for the elections to the 10 MLC seats under the Assembly areas well in advance and most likely in November, as it has done in case of Rajya Sabha seats and MLC seats under the teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies,” a senior BJP leader said.Based on the present Assembly strength, the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance could win eight of the 10 seats, while the SP could secure two.The seats were last contested in January 2021, when the BJP had 304 MLAs and the SP 47. With 31 first-preference votes required to win a seat at the time, the BJP won nine seats and the SP one.Also Read I Ahead of SSR, ECI bars transfer of officials involved in UP voter roll revisionThe BJP currently has 256 MLAs, while the SP has 101. Including its alliance partners, three unaffiliated MLAs and two legislators of Raja Bhaiya’s Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, the NDA’s effective strength is estimated at 294. The BSP has no representative in the Assembly following the recent death of its lone MLA.Nine of the 10 sitting MLCs whose terms are ending belong to the BJP and one to the SP.The Rajya Sabha polls earlier this month brought cross-voting concerns into focus, with the BJP and SP avoiding additional candidates. Whether they follow the same strategy in the MLC elections remains to be seen.

title: Mumbai doctor booked for allegedly issuing death certificate after viewing body on video call | Mumbai news
description: Police said four men allegedly mistook a 60-year-old municipal worker for a wild boar during a hunt in Sanjay Gandhi National Park.  | Mumbai news
content: A doctor from Mira Road has been booked for allegedly issuing a death certificate stating that the victim in the Sanjay Gandhi National Park poaching murder case died of a heart attack after viewing his body on a WhatsApp video call, without physically examining him.HT had reported on Wednesday how four men allegedly shot a 60-year-old municipal worker dead inside the premises of the Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP) mistaking him for a wild boar.Also read: Haryana man shot dead in clash over car vandalism in LudhianaDoctor allegedly declared victim dead without physical examinationDuring the investigation, police found that Dr Rajesh Pandurang Palande, 56, associated with Ashish Hospital in Kashigaon, had allegedly declared the victim dead after seeing his body on a video call. “The doctor issued a death certificate without physically examining the deceased, relying instead on a WhatsApp video call. We have booked him for allegedly issuing a false death certificate and helping the other accused cover up the murder,” said Rahul Chavan, deputy commissioner of police, Mira Road.The case came to light after Rahul Patil, senior police inspector at Kashigaon police station, received information that Vijay Sapte, a resident of Velkari Pada in Chena village, had been shot dead in a forest by people from his locality and that his body was subsequently cremated in the village.Also read: Civic worker shot dead as SGNP hunt goes awry; 4 arrestedGroup had gone hunting for wild boar in forest areaPatil met Rohit Vijay Sapte, 21, the deceased’s son, who revealed that his father had been injured by pellets fired from a gun. During a detailed inquiry, Rohit said that on Monday at around 4 pm, residents of Velkari Pada had gone to the Dabucha Ghat hill area to hunt wild boar.Those accompanying Vijay included Mahesh Anant Gaikar, 52, Kalpesh Bandu Dagla, 25, Kunal Prabhakar Shelar, 31, a municipal sanitation worker and Kathod Bistur Labad, 55. Rohit had also accompanied the group. Gaikar was carrying a shotgun, while Vijay and Labad had muzzle-loading guns.“While we were scattered throughout the forest, around 9.30 pm, a mobile phone torch was switched on. Mistaking the light for that of a wild animal, Gaikar fired his double-barrelled shotgun. The pellets struck my father on the left side of his chest and his leg. Shelar was struck on the upper arm, while Dagla was hit on the neck by the pellets, leaving them both injured as well,” Rohit told the police.Rohit said he and the others carried his injured father back to the village. However, after noticing that his father’s body had turned cold, Rohit said they suspected he had died.Also read: 3 suspected poachers shot dead in Karnataka forest; CM orders magisterial probeDoctor allegedly issued certificate after WhatsApp video callAccording to Rohit, Gaikar then initiated a WhatsApp video call with Dr Palande and showed him Vijay’s body. The doctor allegedly declared Vijay dead and asked for his Aadhaar card, proof of residence and other documents, promising to issue a death certificate, which Gaikar forwarded.Rohit then performed the last rites in the presence of relatives, and the body was cremated at the Chenegaon cremation ground at around 6 am.DCP Chavan said Dr Palande had allegedly issued the death certificate illegally without physically examining the deceased, relying instead on a WhatsApp video call. The police have booked Palande and the other accused in connection with the case.

title: Manipur violence: Protesters’ bid to storm CM's event foiled as tensions escalate | India News
description: The protesters demanded that the CM and home minister address the prevailing law and order situation instead of attending a sports event. | India News
content: A bandh called against the killing of a 45-year-old Kuki man the day before paralysed Kangpokpi district on Wednesday amid a spike in ethnic violence in Manipur. It coincided with the second and last day of a shutdown in Imphal Valley against the killing of three Meiteis in an ambush in Imphal East on Monday.Meanwhile, a protest against the killings in Imphal turned violent on Wednesday, with protesters attempting to storm the Khuman Lampak Indoor Stadium in Imphal West, where chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh and home minister Govindas Konthoujam were attending the inaugural function of the first Manipur State Poomsae Taekwondo Championship, with delegates from South Korea also present, officials said.Also Read I Shutdowns paralyse Manipur’s Meitei-dominated Imphal Valley, Kuki-majority KangpokpiProtestors press demandsThe protesters demanded that the CM and home minister address the prevailing law and order situation instead of attending a sports event while civilians were being killed. Security forces fired several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the mob, injuring at least three protesters. The injured were taken to a nearby hospital, officials said. Later, protesters gathered at Khurai Lamlong in Imphal East and made another attempt to press their demands. Police used several rounds of tear gas shells, smoke grenades and stun bombs to disperse them. Two people sustained injuries, including a woman reportedly hit by a stun grenade on her right foot, said police. The injured were taken to a nearby hospital, and tension remained in the area, officers requesting anonymity said.Militants ambushed 14 Meitei men collecting firewood in the Sunurok hills of Kangpokpi district on October 19, killing three of them. The families of the victims alleged that the attackers belonged to the Kuki community. Additional director general of police Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo said three people had been arrested in connection with the ambush. Two of them admitted to being part of the group that killed the three men, he said. “The role of the third arrested man in this heinous crime is being probed, and the investigation is on to identify the others who are involved in the case.”The Joint Action Committee (JAC), formed after the killings, said the bodies would not be accepted until the government booked all those involved. It announced a one-day cease-work protest on Thursday, with sit-ins at respective locations, and appealed to schools, colleges and other institutions to support the protest.Burnt effigies, dead bodiesOn Monday, protesters had left two bodies at the main gate of the chief minister’s residence to protest the failure to protect civilians. Security forces fired tear gas shells after the mob breached security and parked a truck carrying the bodies outside the residence.Normal life remained affected across the five Imphal Valley districts during a 48-hour shutdown called by the Native Peoples Committee Manipur against the killings. Markets remained closed, public transport stayed off the roads and educational institutions were shut.Protesters also burnt effigies of Rajya Sabha MP A Sharda Devi and Konthoujam at Khabeisoi in Imphal East.Also Read I Kharge questions Modi, Shah over failure to restore peace in ManipurMeira Paibi activists later gathered at Devi’s residence in Brahmapur to question her “silence” on the killings. They left after she assured them through a video call that their demands would be conveyed to the government.Meanwhile, around 15 abandoned houses were set ablaze at Khoikai village in Kamjong district on Wednesday. The village has been deserted since April following Naga-Kuki clashes.

title: DNA from a pangolin collected in 1836 helped confirm the Himalayan pangolin as a distinct species after nearly 190 years in a museum | World News
description: In 2026, DNA from an 1836 museum specimen confirmed the Himalayan pangolin as its own species, which could help conservation efforts and track poaching.  | World News
content: A pangolin specimen from 1836, now sitting in the Natural History Museum in London, has helped to solve a scientific mystery. According to the Communications Biology study, researchers used DNA from that nearly 190-year-old specimen to confirm the Himalayan pangolin, Manis aurita, as its own species. It is found in Nepal and northern India. Many scientists had believed it was a subspecies of the Chinese pangolin.A mammal under heavy pressurePangolins are medium-sized mammals native to Africa and Asia. Long, thick tails, huge curling claws, and armored bodies covered in overlapping, pinecone-like scales are their trademarks. According to the Field Museum, pangolins are poached for those scales, making them the most trafficked mammals in the world. This makes them highly vulnerable to extinction. The scales are thought to be a potent aphrodisiac in traditional Chinese medicine, and illegal poaching is a huge threat. Anderson Feijó, an assistant curator of mammals at the Field Museum and co-corresponding author of the study, says markets sell mostly scales, not whole animals. So it’s hard to know what species is being hunted.A name that was nearly lostThe name Manis aurita goes back to 1836, when it was described as a pangolin species. Later, it was downgraded to a subspecies of the Chinese pangolin. Then, in 2025, another group of scientists showed that Chinese pangolins were in fact two species. One lives mainly in China. The other lives in the foothills of the Himalayas, across parts of Nepal, India, Bhutan, and Myanmar. That group named the mountain species Manis indoburmanica, the Indo-Burmese pangolin. In science, the first name a species gets is the one that sticks. Feijó and his colleagues had been working on the pangolin family tree for a decade, analyzing physical traits and DNA. Kai He of Guangzhou University, a co-corresponding author, says this left a core riddle. Were indoburmanica and aurita the same species or different ones? The answer was in the ancient DNAThe Natural History Museum’s team sequenced DNA from the historical type specimen of aurita, the Nepalese subspecies. The DNA matched modern pangolins from the Himalayas. The species described as Manis indoburmanica in 2025 should be called Manis aurita, the Field Museum noted. In a few small but distinct ways, the Himalayan pangolin is different from the Chinese pangolin. It has a larger body, a longer tail, and smaller ears. The name aurita refers to its distinct ears. The two species also occupy separate areas that do not overlap. Narayan Koju of the Nepal Engineering College at Pokhara University, the study’s first author, says the finding caps more than five years of research that began in Nepal.Why this is important for conservationNew DNA analyses are helping conservation scientists identify which pangolin species are being poached. They can trace samples back to high-risk regions in illegal markets. The findings could also aid efforts to reintroduce pangolins to former ranges. Feijó notes that before, someone might have introduced Chinese pangolins into Nepal without knowing the difference. The clarification provides a basis for the conservation of this cryptic, endangered species, says co-corresponding author Yan Hua of the Guangdong Academy of Forestry. Museums were important as well. Because wild pangolins are so rare, collections give researchers access to more animals across the species’ range, says Feijó. The study involved scientists from institutions including Guangzhou University and the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. As Feijó put it, “we can’t protect what we do not know.”

title: Bombay high court raps BMC, MPCB over failure to enforce firecracker ban ahead of Diwali | Mumbai news
description: The court directed the Mumbai police commissioner to brief station heads on its orders and prepare an SOP to ensure compliance with restrictions.  | Mumbai news
content: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday pulled up the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) and the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) for failing to issue public notices regarding its recent order banning the bursting of firecrackers in public places, including streets, lanes and footpaths.“The wheels of the official machinery appear to be turning too slowly to comply even with the basic preliminary compliances as ordered by the court,” a division bench of justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said.The bench noted that neither authority had taken any steps to inform citizens about the firecracker ban through newspapers, electronic and social media, and other platforms, as directed by the court on October 15.Also read: ₹35,000 penalty">Mumbai air pollution: BMC cracks down on construction sites, issues stop-work notice and ₹35,000 penaltyJudges flag routine violations during religious processionsThe judges also expressed concern about the police’s failure to enforce restrictions on noise pollution, particularly during religious processions. “There appear to be routine violations of the orders passed by this court, particularly in relation to religious processions and burning of firecrackers on public streets,” the bench noted.The court directed the Mumbai police commissioner to convene a meeting with all officers in charge of police stations, bring to their attention the court’s orders, and prepare a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlining actions to be taken in response to the violations. It clarified that the officers are to be specifically instructed to ensure the meticulous implementation of the directions prohibiting processions that use sound systems without the appropriate licence being displayed.Also read: Lasers, firecrackers flout HC curbs during visarjan, alleges Awaaz Foundation“The officers shall also be apprised of the total ban imposed on the bursting of firecrackers during festivities on public streets, roads, etc., as directed in the order dated October 15, 2026,” the court said. It directed the police commissioner to file an affidavit assuring that the “court’s orders shall be implemented in letter and spirit”.“Unless the officers are duly apprised of the orders passed by the court, effective implementation of the orders cannot take place, thereby causing severe annoyance and disturbance to the public at large, apart from breach of their legal rights as observed by us,” the bench observed.Also read: Green only in colour: Firecrackers flood Delhi markets amid festive season, rising AQIHigh Court hearing suo motu petition on noise pollutionThe court was hearing a suo motu petition taken up in September concerning noise pollution caused by religious processions in Mumbai and other cities across Maharashtra.On October 15, the court had ordered a year-round ban on bursting firecrackers in public places, while directing the state government, BMC and MPCB to spread awareness about noise and air pollution through public announcements, notices and display boards on public transport. It had also urged citizens to use green, low-emission firecrackers.

title: Prez Murmu presents National Exhibition of Art awards; urges support for rural artists | India News
description: The awards recognised artists selected for the two events, which provide platforms for showcasing contemporary visual art and printmaking | India News
content: President Droupadi Murmu presented awards to artists at the 65th National Exhibition of Art and the 3rd Print Biennale India 2026 in New Delhi on Wednesday. The event was organised by the Lalit Kala Akademi under the Union ministry of culture.Union culture and tourism minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and culture ministry secretary Vivek Aggarwal attended the ceremony at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre, along with artists, senior officials and members of the cultural fraternity.The awards recognised artists selected for the two events, which provide platforms for showcasing contemporary visual art and printmaking. The ceremony also featured a film documenting the history of the Lalit Kala Akademi and the National Exhibition of Art, which began in 1955.Also Read: Bilaspur gears up for President Murmu’s Oct 6 visitAddressing the gathering, Murmu spoke about the role of art in reflecting India’s culture, traditions and civilisational history. She emphasised the importance of preserving traditional art forms and identified printmaking as a significant medium of artistic expression.The President also highlighted the role of exhibitions and biennales in facilitating interaction and the exchange of ideas among artists. She referred to the culture ministry’s efforts to expand opportunities for artists, increase public access to artworks and connect the arts with the creative economy.Shekhawat presented Murmu with a Gond painting as a token of appreciation. In his address, he said the Lalit Kala Akademi provided a national platform for artists to exhibit their work and represent the diversity of Indian art.The minister also discussed printmaking, describing it as a medium that combines technical skills with artistic experimentation. He said the National Exhibition of Art and the Print Biennale helped promote interaction among artists, build international connections and increase the visibility of Indian art.Referring to the government’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shekhawat highlighted the role of culture and creativity in the country’s development. He also noted that incorporating artwork sales into the programme could help expand income opportunities for artists and support the creative economy.Aggarwal outlined the history of the Akademi, established in 1954, and the National Exhibition of Art, whose first edition was held at Jaipur House in 1955 with approximately 1,200 entries.This year, the National Exhibition received 6,175 artworks submitted by 2,495 artists from 27 states and Union territories. Of these, 270 artworks were selected for display, and 20 artists were chosen for awards.Aggarwal also highlighted the Print Biennale’s role in encouraging experimentation in printmaking and facilitating engagement between Indian and international artists.Separately, the culture ministry will organise India Biennale 2026 from December 4, 2026, to March 21, 2027, at monuments and heritage sites across Delhi. The initiative is intended to bring contemporary artworks into historical settings and expand public engagement with art and heritage.

title: GRAP Stage 1 restrictions invoked in Delhi-NCR as AQI enters ‘poor’ category; real estate sector seeks targeted curbs | Real Estate News
description: GRAP 1 restrictions imposed in Delhi-NCR: Real estate sector calls for targeted curbs on pollution-intensive construction activities rather than a blanket ban   | Real Estate News
content: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked Stage 1 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR on October 21 after the capital’s air quality slipped into the ‘poor’ category. In response, real estate developers called for targeted curbs on pollution-intensive construction activities rather than a blanket ban on construction.The sector also stressed that restrictions limited to private construction projects in Delhi may not yield the desired results unless similar measures are implemented uniformly across the National Capital Region (NCR). A coordinated approach, backed by strict enforcement across all sources of pollution, is essential for sustained improvement in air quality, they said.“The deterioration in air quality across Delhi-NCR is a serious concern, and all stakeholders must work together to address the issue. Construction activities should follow prescribed dust-control measures, including water sprinkling, covering construction materials and proper management of debris. However, restrictions should be targeted at activities that contribute significantly to pollution rather than imposing a blanket approach across all construction work,” said Parveen Jain, president, NAREDCO.“Any restrictions must also take into account project timelines and the resulting impact on project completion, along with the livelihoods of daily-wage workers, developers and homebuyers. Moreover, restrictions limited to private construction projects in Delhi alone may not deliver the desired results unless similar measures are implemented uniformly across the NCR. A coordinated approach, backed by strict enforcement across all pollution sources, is essential for sustained improvement in air quality,” he said.GRAP 1 restrictions imposedThe CAQM’s decision followed a review by its GRAP Sub-Committee, which noted a sharp deterioration in Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI). The AQI rose from 179, in the ‘moderate’ category, on October 20 to 244 at 2 pm on October 21, entering the ‘poor’ category. Forecasts by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) indicated that air quality was likely to remain poor over the coming days, according to the order.Also Read: Delhi winter pollution plan: Real estate developers seek balanced approach, clear timelines for construction curbsThe sub-committee directed the implementation of all measures under Stage 1 of the existing GRAP across the entire NCR with immediate effect. What GRAP Stage 1 means for constructionUnder Stage 1, authorities are required to enforce dust-mitigation measures at construction and demolition (C&D) sites. Construction materials and waste must be stored properly, and they must be transported in covered vehicles.Meanwhile, Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa was quoted by agencies as saying that the government had introduced preventive measures to tackle winter pollution, including restrictions on polluting vehicles, staggered office timings and work-from-home arrangements.Sirsa said Delhi had invoked Stage 1 of GRAP later this year than in previous years, adding that nearly 30 agencies were working together under the government’s 11-point air pollution mitigation plan. Long-term measures include end-to-end carpeting of roads to curb dust, promoting electric vehicles and phasing out polluting fuel-based industries across Delhi-NCR, he said. Also Read: Delhi winter pollution curbs: Real estate developers seek balanced approach to construction bans, warn of project delays and rising costsThe government also plans to prohibit dust-generating demolition and outdoor civil construction activities from November 1 to January 31. A complete ban on construction and demolition activities is scheduled from December 10 to January 20.GRAP is a set of emergency measures implemented in stages to prevent further deterioration in air quality across Delhi-NCR once pollution levels cross specified thresholds.

title: జంతర్ మంతర్ వద్ద నిరసన చేయబోమని హామీ.. సీజేపీ నేతల విడుదల | Hindustan Times Telugu
description: జంతర్ మంతర్‌ను నిరసన ప్రదేశంగా ప్రభుత్వం మళ్లీ గుర్తించే వరకు అక్కడ ఎలాంటి ధర్నాలు చేపట్టబోమని హామీ ఇవ్వడంతో కాక్రోచ్ జనతా పార్టీ (సీజేపీ) కో-కన్వీనర్లు సౌరవ్ దాస్, అశుతోష్ రంకాలను ఢిల్లీ కోర్టు బుధవారం విడుదల చేసింది. రూ.50 వేల పూచీకత్తుతో వీరికి ముందస్తు షరతులతో విడుదల ఉత్తర్వులు ఇచ్చింది.
content: న్యూఢిల్లీ: జంతర్ మంతర్ వద్ద ఎలాంటి నిరసనలు, ధర్నాలు చేపట్టబోమని లిఖితపూర్వక హామీ ఇవ్వడంతో కాక్రోచ్ జనతా పార్టీ (సీజేపీ) కో-కన్వీనర్లు సౌరవ్ దాస్, అశుతోష్ రంకాలను ఢిల్లీ స్పెషల్ ఎగ్జిక్యూటివ్ మేజిస్ట్రేట్ (ఎస్ఈఎం) కోర్టు బుధవారం జుడీషియల్ కస్టడీ నుంచి విడుదల చేసింది. ఏడు రోజుల కస్టడీ అనంతరం రూ.50,000 చొప్పున వ్యక్తిగత బాండ్లు, పూచీకత్తులను సమర్పించాలని న్యాయస్థానం ఆదేశించింది. అక్టోబర్ 23న జరిగే తదుపరి విచారణకు పూచీకత్తుదారులతో సహా హాజరుకావాలని స్పష్టం చేసింది.శాంతిభద్రతలకు కట్టుబడి ఉంటాంన్యూఢిల్లీ డిస్ట్రిక్ట్ ఎస్ఈఎం, ఏసీపీ రితు రాజ్ ఎదుట నేతలు దాఖలు చేసిన హామీ పత్రంలో కీలక అంశాలను వెల్లడించారు. జంతర్ మంతర్‌ను చట్టబద్ధంగా మళ్లీ నిరసన ప్రాంతంగా నోటిఫై చేసేంత వరకు అక్కడ ఎలాంటి ఆందోళనలకు పిలుపునివ్వబోమని స్పష్టం చేశారు. శాంతిభద్రతలు, శాంతియుత వాతావరణ పరిరక్షణకు కట్టుబడి ఉంటామని తేల్చిచెప్పారు. రాజ్యాంగబద్ధమైన పరిమితుల లోపే తమ పోరాటాలు ఉంటాయని, న్యాయ వ్యవస్థపై తమకు పూర్తి నమ్మకం ఉందన్నారు.భారతీయ నాగరిక్ సురక్ష సంహిత (బీఎన్ఎస్ఎస్) సెక్షన్ 135(3) కింద ప్రజలకు ఎలాంటి ఇబ్బంది కలగకుండా ఉండేందుకు, నేతలు ఇచ్చిన హామీ పత్రాలు, బాండ్లు సరిపోతాయని, వీరిని కస్టడీలో ఉంచాల్సిన అవసరం లేదని మేజిస్ట్రేట్ వ్యాఖ్యానించారు.విడుదలపై ప్రాసిక్యూషన్ అభ్యంతరంఈ కేసులో సీజేపీ నేతల విడుదలను ప్రాసిక్యూషన్ తీవ్రంగా వ్యతిరేకించింది. వీరి నుంచి శాంతిభద్రతలకు ఇంకా ముప్పు పొంచి ఉందని, కస్టడీని మరో మూడు రోజులు పొడిగించాలని దర్యాప్తు అధికారి (ఐఓ) విజ్ఞప్తి చేశారు. నేతలు బయట ఇచ్చే ప్రకటనలు, మీడియా వ్యాఖ్యలు కోర్టులో ఇచ్చిన హామీలకు విరుద్ధంగా ఉన్నాయని ప్రాసిక్యూషన్ న్యాయవాదులు భైరవ్ దాస్, ప్రశాంత్ ప్రకాశ్ వాదించారు. గతంలో వీరు తిహార్ జైలుకు వెళ్తున్న సమయంలో అనుచరులు చేసిన వ్యాఖ్యలు ఎస్ఈఎం కోర్టు ప్రతిష్ఠను దిగజార్చేలా ఉన్నాయని ఆరోపించారు.అయితే సీజేపీ నేతల తరఫు న్యాయవాది అభీక్ చిమ్నీ ఈ వ్యాఖ్యలపై స్పందిస్తూ బేషరతుగా క్షమాపణలు చెప్పారు. భవిష్యత్తులో ఇలాంటి సంఘటనలు పునరావృతం కాబోవని కోర్టుకు హామీ ఇచ్చారు.అసలు కేసేంటి? నేపథ్యమిదే..శాంతిభద్రతల విచ్ఛిన్నానికి పూనుకుంటున్నారనే ఆరోపణలతో పార్లమెంట్ స్ట్రీట్ పోలీసులు బీఎన్ఎస్ఎస్ సెక్షన్లు 126, 170 కింద కేసు నమోదు చేశారు. అక్టోబర్ 12న జంతర్ మంతర్ వద్ద ఇనుప గేటు ఎక్కి లోపలికి ప్రవేశించిన ఆరోపణలపై సౌరవ్ దాస్, అశుతోష్ రంకాలను మరుసటి రోజు అరెస్టు చేశారు. అక్టోబర్ 14న వీరిని 5 రోజుల జుడీషియల్ కస్టడీకి పంపగా, సోమవారం నాటి విచారణలో మరో రెండు రోజులు కస్టడీ పొడిగించారు. పండుగల సీజన్ దృష్ట్యా వీరు బయటకు వస్తే మళ్లీ శాంతిభద్రతల సమస్య ఏర్పడే అవకాశం ఉందని పోలీసులు వాదించినప్పటికీ, ధర్మాసనం షరతులతో కూడిన విడుదలకు అంగీకరించింది.ప్రత్యేక సమగ్ర సవరణ (ఎస్ఐఆర్)లో అక్రమాలు జరిగాయంటూ ప్రధాన ఎన్నికల కమిషనర్ జ్ఞానేష్ కుమార్‌కు వ్యతిరేకంగా నిరసన తెలిపేందుకు సిద్ధమైన ఈ నేతలను అక్టోబర్ 10న పోలీసులు అదుపులోకి తీసుకున్నారు. ఆ మరుసటి రోజు (అక్టోబర్ 11న) ఒక సంవత్సరం పాటు శాంతికి భంగం కలిగించబోమని బాండ్ రాసిచ్చిన తర్వాత విడుదలయ్యారు. అయితే మరుసటి రోజే నిబంధనలు ఉల్లంఘించి జంతర్ మంతర్ వద్దకు చేరుకోవడంతో ఈ అరెస్టు చోటుచేసుకుంది. అక్టోబర్ 23న పోలీసులు సమర్పించే పూచీకత్తుల పరిశీలన నివేదిక ఆధారంగా తదుపరి చర్యలు ఉండనున్నాయి.

title: Country singer John Anderson dies at 71, leaves behind wife of 43 years and two daughters | Hindustan Times
description: The country music singer and Country Music Hall of Fame member has died at 71.
content: Country music singer John Anderson, known for hits including “Swingin’” and “Seminole Wind”, has died at the age of 71, his family announced on Wednesday, October 21. The Country Music Hall of Fame member leaves behind his wife Jamie Anderson, whom he married in 1983, and their two daughters, Brionna and Alexa.Anderson’s family announced his death in a statement shared on Instagram, remembering him as a beloved husband, father, grandfather and best friend. His cause of death was not disclosed in the initial reports.“It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend,” the family said.The statement described Anderson as a singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives, but said his role within the family meant much more than his musical achievements.“He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special,” the family said. The family also asked for thoughts and prayers as they grieve his death.John Anderson’s career and hit songsBorn in Apopka, Florida, in 1954, Anderson built a career spanning several decades, earning recognition for his distinctive voice and traditional country sound.He rose to prominence in the early 1980s with songs including “Wild and Blue”, “Swingin’” and “Black Sheep”. He later returned to the top of the country charts with “Straight Tequila Night” and “Money in the Bank”. His song “Seminole Wind” also became one of his best-known recordings.Anderson was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2014 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024, recognizing his contributions to country music.Health struggles and final public appearanceAnderson faced serious health problems in 2017 and 2018, including a benign tumor and hearing difficulties that affected his career. He eventually returned to recording, releasing the album Years in 2020.The singer attended the Country Music Hall of Fame’s Medallion Ceremony in Nashville on October 18, three days before his death.

title: Action ordered against officials after errors found in electoral rolls in UP's Pilibhit Sadar | India News
description: The action comes after the Congress alleged large-scale changes to the electoral roll in Pilibhit Sadar, claiming that 13,150 voters’ names were changed. | India News
content: Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) ordered legal action against officials responsible for errors in the electoral roll of Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency and directed their immediate removal from voter list duties, following a complaint that Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers were displaying details of other voters.The action comes after the Congress alleged large-scale changes to the electoral roll in Pilibhit Sadar, claiming that 13,150 voters’ names were changed while their EPIC numbers remained unchanged. The party has also sought the Supreme Court’s intervention in the matter.In a press release issued on Wednesday, the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, said the complaint was investigated through the District Election Officer, Pilibhit. Subsequent checks confirmed that searching certain voters’ EPIC numbers online displayed details of other voters. Taking a strict view of the discrepancies, the UP CEO’s office issued instructions to “immediately rectify such errors” and “forthwith remove the Electoral Registration Officer and VRC Operator of Assembly Constituency 127-Pilibhit from voter list duties.” It also directed officials to initiate legal action against them under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The office has sought a clear report on the responsibilities of the constituency’s Assistant Electoral Registration Officers.The District Election Officer, Pilibhit, has been directed to conduct a thorough review of voter lists across all Assembly constituencies in the district and submit a detailed report within two days.The allegationsAccording to allegations levelled by the Congress, 13,150 names were changed in the assembly between July and September, after the final electoral roll was published on April 10, without Form 6 or Form 7 applications. The party further claimed that 804 living voters were deleted and 2,600 names of people who did not reside in the constituency were added.Citing examples, Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate alleged that names such as Rashid were changed to Abdul, Mohammad Yusuf to Hasrat, Mohammad Waseem to Sher Mohammad, and Mohammad Shadab to Salim Khan. She claimed that most of the altered names belonged to Muslim men and alleged that voter details were changed through software.UP Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam alleged a conspiracy that could influence electoral outcomes, while MP Imran Masood said the party would pursue the issue “on the streets, in Parliament and in courts.”The final electoral roll in Uttar Pradesh was published on April 10 and contained 13.39 crore voters. More than 2.04 crore voters were removed, and over 84 lakh were added during the revision exercise.The post-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) rolls have faced further scrutiny after social media users flagged alleged duplicate entries involving electors with multiple voter IDs. The UP CEO’s office has said officials are working on deduplication to remove such entries.The statewide review ordered on Wednesday will now examine whether similar discrepancies between EPIC numbers and voter details exist in other constituencies across Uttar Pradesh.

title: Bruno Fernandes questions Michael Carrick’s tactics, Manchester United manager hits back after Como loss | Football News
description: Asked about the lack of cohesion while defending and pressing without the ball, Fernandes made it very clear that it was down to Carrick and his coaching staff.  | Football News
content: The 1-4 defeat to Como has added to Manchester United’s concerns, with the result once again causing a senior player to speak out after the match. It follows Lisandro Martinez’s criticism after the loss to Atletico Madrid. While Martinez took aim at the club’s sporting director over recruitment, Bruno Fernandes pointed to Michael Carrick’s coaching staff and their tactics after the defeat to Como.After the dismal performance, Manchester United are now winless in seven consecutive games across all competitions for the first time since an eight-match run between November and December 2015.When asked about United's lack of cohesion while defending and pressing without the ball, Fernandes made it very clear that it was down to Carrick and his coaching staff. The reasoning was that if you give the opposition time on the ball, they become more confident, and you end up with your own players frustrated and worn out."It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," Fernandes told TNT Sports after the match."But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."Also Read - Manchester United thrashed, Arsenal earn late draw vs Bayern Munich; Real Madrid beat RB LeipzigAsked whether United’s tactical approach contributed to the defeat against Como, Fernandes made it clear the responsibility lay with Carrick and his coaching staff, saying it was their job to identify and address the problem."That's on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me," said Fernandes."I just said, I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable - as they did to us."It was the second game in a row where Manchester United conceded a goal inside two minutes in the UCL. They were caught off guard in the first minute against Atletico, while Como scored in the second with Nico Paz breaching the defence.“I'm really angry”: CarrickResponding to Fernandes’s criticism, Carrick defended the tactical approach but pointed to United’s lack of effort off the ball as a bigger problem. The United manager said his side tried to press man-to-man in the second half but stressed no tactical setup would work without players tracking back."We half pressed man-to-man in the second half and ended up conceding a goal from that," Carrick told TNT Sports. "Whatever tactics you play, if you don't run back, you ain't going to win.""I'm really angry," he said. "For us to play in that way is not acceptable."United were completely outplayed by Como who, under Cesc Fabregas, have qualified for the UCL for the first time in their history. Como outperformed their xG of 2.04 (Opta Analyst) by scoring four goals, whereas United's xG of 1.05 was already quite poor for a UCL night.Carrick did admit he'd look at the coaching staff's role in the defeat but made it clear that Manchester United's lack of intensity and lack of commitment was just as much to blame."I'll definitely look at what we've done [as a coaching staff] or if it's the motivation and the intention and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football you have to bring," he said. "We didn't bring that today.“You can't turn it on and off and you can't choose when you want to perform or when you don't want to perform or when you give absolutely everything or when you maybe don't.”

title: Gurugram’s stilt-plus-four row: What changed, and what it means for homebuyers | Hindustan Times
description: Gurugram real estate: The stilt-plus-four row puts property registrations, revenue and buyer investments at risk amid uncertainty over building approvals
content: Gurugram’s stilt-plus-four (S+4) housing policy has become a flashpoint between urban development and infrastructure planning. What began as a way to increase the supply of independent residential floors has evolved into a wider debate over building permissions, parking, civic amenities and the legal certainty of property transactions.The stakes are considerable. In an affidavit before the Punjab and Haryana high court, the Haryana Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) said 32,024 permissions for S+4 construction had been granted in Gurugram up to April 2, 2026. The department has opposed a blanket halt to construction, arguing that individual violations should not invalidate every approval issued under the policy.The affidavit by DTCP director-general Dr J Ganesan was placed before a division bench of Acting Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor on October 14. The bench had issued notice on July 27 on an application filed by petitioner Sunil Singh in an ongoing public interest litigation challenging the policy.Here is what changed, why the dispute matters and what buyers need to know.What is the stilt-plus-four policy?The S+4 model allows a residential building to have four dwelling floors above a stilt level intended for parking. It has become popular in Gurugram’s plotted colonies, where independent floors offer an alternative to apartments in high-rise residential societies.The model allows plot owners and developers to create multiple independent homes on a single plot, potentially increasing the supply of housing and the number of units available for sale.However, residents’ welfare associations have raised concerns that additional dwelling units are increasing population density without adequate improvements in roads, water supply, sewerage, drainage and parking.Also Read: ₹1.38 lakh crore, despite fewer units; Bengaluru follows at ₹1.30 lakh crore">Gurugram tops luxury housing market by launch value at ₹1.38 lakh crore, despite fewer units; Bengaluru follows at ₹1.30 lakh croreComplaints have also included the alleged conversion of stilt parking into residential or commercial spaces and the operation of paying guest accommodations in areas with narrow roads. These concerns have put the policy under greater scrutiny.What changes has Haryana introduced?The policy has undergone several changes over the years.In March 2019, the state issued instructions allowing the fourth floor to be treated as an independent residential unit. Instructions issued in September 2019 also provided for the purchase of additional development rights.In February 2023, the government froze approvals under the S+4 policy and appointed an expert committee headed by retired bureaucrat P Raghavendra Rao to examine the implications of additional construction.Following the committee’s recommendations, the government revived the policy on July 2, 2024, with additional restrictions.One important safeguard concerned the use of stilt parking. Under Clause 8 of the 2024 instructions, building-plan approvals and occupation certificates could be withdrawn if the stilt area was enclosed, either fully or partially.The policy subsequently faced another setback. On April 2, 2026, the Punjab and Haryana high court stayed the operation of the July 2024 notification and restrained further approvals and occupation certificates under the policy. The dispute has since centred on the legality of the policy, the adequacy of civic infrastructure and the treatment of permissions already granted.How many buildings and buyers are affected?According to the DTCP affidavit, 32,024 permissions had been granted in Gurugram up to April 2, 2026. These included 18,719 building-plan approvals in private licensed colonies and 13,305 approvals in Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran sectors.In private licensed colonies in the Gurugram-Manesar Urban Complex, 15,447 building plans had been approved. Of these, 9,625 were sanctioned before July 2024, while 5,822 were approved between July 2, 2024, and the high court’s April 2 stay.The DTCP also reported that occupation certificates had been issued for 8,602 buildings.These figures cover different stages of development. Some buyers may own completed and occupied floors, others may have purchased properties under construction, while some may have paid advances for units awaiting approvals or completion.Their legal and financial positions will therefore vary according to the sanctioned building plan, construction status, occupation certificate, sale agreement and registration documents.What does the row mean for stamp duty and registration?The controversy has implications for property transactions and government revenue.In December 2024, Haryana increased stamp duty rates applicable to the registration of independent floors, alongside revisions in circle rates. The revised framework raised the rate used for floor registrations from ₹7,150 to ₹9,300 per square foot, according to published reports.For buyers, higher stamp duty increases the upfront cost of acquiring a property. For the government, registrations generate revenue, while additional construction also creates demands for investment in civic infrastructure.However, the current uncertainty is not simply a question of how much stamp duty a buyer must pay.Building-plan approval, an occupation certificate and registration of a sale deed are three distinct stages. Approval permits construction subject to applicable conditions; an occupation certificate concerns the building’s compliance and eligibility for occupation; registration records the property transaction in accordance with the law.The court’s interim directions have created uncertainty for transactions involving properties that have yet to secure the necessary clearances. Whether a particular sale deed can be registered depends on the property’s documents and the applicable directions of the authorities.The available information does not establish that every existing S+4 registration has been stopped or that all previously registered floors have become invalid.For the state, delays in eligible property transactions could affect stamp duty collections. The actual impact will depend on how many transactions are postponed, which properties remain eligible for registration and how the government implements the court’s directions.What does it mean for buyers who have already invested?For buyers who have paid substantial sums, the immediate concern is whether their property can be completed, occupied, registered or resold without complications.Those who own completed floors should verify the sanctioned building plan, occupation certificate, registered sale deed and legal status of their specific unit.Buyers of under-construction properties face different risks. Delayed approvals or occupation certificates could affect possession timelines, financing arrangements and resale plans. Where a transaction is incomplete, the terms of the sale agreement and the nature of the approvals already obtained become particularly important.A property should not automatically be treated as illegal merely because it falls under the S+4 category. Equally, an earlier building-plan approval should not be treated as proof that every subsequent construction activity complies with the sanctioned plan.What does the legal position mean for buyers?Advocate Ritu Bhariok, legal adviser to the Federation of Affordable Home Buyers, said the uncertainty surrounding the stilt-plus-four policy had highlighted the need for clear regulations that protect homebuyers while ensuring compliance with building norms. She said the authorities must clarify the status of existing approvals and occupation certificates, and provide legal certainty to buyers who had invested their savings in these properties. Any resolution, she said, must balance buyers’ interests with the need to ensure that civic infrastructure can support increased residential density.For buyers, the distinction between a blanket challenge to a policy and a finding against an individual property is important. The final outcome of the litigation and subsequent directions from the authorities will determine how different categories of properties are treated, she said.Affected purchasers should seek an independent legal review before making further payments, entering into resale agreements or assuming that pending documentation will automatically be resolved.Also Read: Gurugram’s senior living market gains ground as high-net-worth retirees and NRIs drive demandWhat lies ahead?The dispute ultimately concerns how Gurugram should accommodate growth without overwhelming its existing infrastructure.The DTCP has argued that alleged violations in individual buildings should be dealt with on a case-by-case basis rather than used to invalidate every S+4 permission. The broader challenge is to establish whether the existing infrastructure can support the additional population and what safeguards are necessary for future development.For residents, the priority is ensuring that additional housing is matched by adequate public services. For developers and investors, clarity on approvals and registrations is essential to restore confidence in the market.For the state, the challenge is to balance housing supply, property-related revenue and urban planning requirements while complying with the court’s directions.Until the legal position becomes clearer, buyers must distinguish between a sanctioned plan, a completed building, an occupation certificate and a registered property. In Gurugram’s S+4 market, that distinction could determine whether an investment remains a straightforward property purchase or becomes a prolonged legal and financial concern.

title: Chhattisgarh woman IPS officer's AK-47 firing at Dussehra ritual sparks safety debate | Hindustan Times
description: Chhattisgarh woman IPS officer's AK-47 firing at Dussehra ritual sparks safety debate
content: Raipur, A video of a senior woman IPS officer firing an AK-47 assault rifle into the air during a traditional weapon worship ritual on Dussehra in Chhattisgarh's Rajnandgaon city has gone viral, triggering a debate over safety, discipline and weapon handling protocols.While some social media users defended Rajnandgaon Superintendent of Police Ankita Sharma, saying she was merely following a tradition, others criticised her handling of the weapon.A traditional 'Shastra Puja' ritual was performed at Police Lines in Rajnandgaon on Tuesday on the occasion of Vijayadashami. Police weapons and vehicles were worshipped.The viral video showed Sharma, dressed in a saree, firing several rounds from an AK-47. Rajnandgaon Additional Superintendent of Police Kirtan Rathore was also seen firing an AK-47 after her in another video.Videos showing police personnel firing weapons after the ritual in other districts, including Raipur, Bilaspur, Raigarh, Durg, Kabirdham and Bastar, were also shared with the media on Tuesday.Asked about the video involving Sharma, Deputy Chief Minister Arun Sao said the government would take cognisance of the matter.Retired IPS officer R K Vij told PTI that firing should be carried out only at a safe location and with adequate precautions."The tradition is essentially about performing the worship of weapons, not firing them. Such firing carries the risk of accidents and should be avoided," he said.An IPS officer said on condition of anonymity that firing blank rounds, commonly known as 'awazi kartoos', is part of the Shastra Puja tradition which is followed across the state. Live ammunition is not used on such occasions, he said.Even a bullet fired into the air comes back down and can injure people in the vicinity, the officer added.Former Indian Army officer K J S Dhillon took to social media to raise concerns over the way the weapons were fired, as seen in the videos."Dangerously incorrect handling of a loaded weapon - All aspects of safety of weapon handling violated - Pointing a loaded weapon in all directions. Ppl in background are visibly terrified - Firing a service weapon for an unauthorised act in a non-authorised dress - Basic weapon handling drill taught in the...academies not adhered to - Such irresponsible action can cause death or hurt to self or others...," he wrote.Another social media user, identifying himself as Army veteran Colonel Deepak Kumar, also described the act as reckless and unprofessional, and questioned the woman officer's handling of the rifle after firing.Some users suggested that only blank ammunition should be used for ceremonial firing.Several social media users, however, defended Sharma, arguing that the incident should not overshadow her professional record.A handle with the name 'Former Major L S Choudhary', in a social media post, acknowledged that there were mistakes in the officer's weapon handling but said they should be corrected without discrediting her work in Chhattisgarh.Another user, Narendra Negi, defended Sharma, saying she was a trained IPS officer. The criticism targeting her partly stemmed from her firing the rifle while wearing a saree, he contended.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Delhi govt working to formulate policy to strengthen data management | Latest News Delhi
description: The policy seeks to establish a framework for the collection, processing, sharing, and protection of data  | Latest News Delhi
content: The Delhi government is working on a policy to strengthen data management across departments and ensure compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, passed in 2023 to regulate how organisations collect and use digital personal data, officials said on Thursday.The policy, described as a “compliance enabler”, seeks to establish a common framework for the collection, processing, sharing, protection and management of data at the Delhi government level. Officials said it is aligned with the DPDP Act, 2023, the DPDP Rules, 2025, which operationalised it, and the advisories of the National Data Governance Committee.The State Data Governance Committee (SDGC) will serve as the apex policy body for data governance in the Delhi government. The chief secretary will chair it and will include senior secretaries from departments, including finance, planning, urban development, health and family welfare, and education. The committee is to meet every quarter, according to the proposal.The policy proposes departmental data governance committees (DDGCs) headed by the respective heads of departments. These committees will be responsible for managing departmental datasets and implementing the state’s data governance framework, officials said.Delhi’s Department of Information Technology (DoIT) will act as the nodal agency. It will oversee operational components, including the state data exchange layer (SDEL), which allows data to be shared without duplication and the need for centralisation, the consent management system, state data catalogue and a central compliance dashboard, officials said.The framework envisions a team of data stewards handling areas such as data accuracy, processing permissions, metadata tagging, and citizen grievances.The proposed policy is built around nine thematic pillars: governance and institutional framework, privacy and security, legal and regulatory compliance, secure interoperability and data sharing, data lifecycle management and classification, citizen rights and multilingual grievance redressal, annual data quality index and monitoring, capacity building and change management, and AI and emerging technology governance.The government has proposed a series of immediate implementation measures, including circulars directing departments to comply with the DPDP framework, appointment of nodal officers and committees, adoption of standard data-sharing protocols, standard operating procedures and a state data exchange architecture.Under the compliance framework, every department must nominate a DPDP nodal/grievance officer and conduct a data mapping and inventory exercise. This will involve identifying the personal data collected by departments, its purpose, storage, and access.The policy envisions periodic audits, compliance reviews, monitoring and enforcement mechanisms, along with privacy-by-design principles.A separate state data exchange platform is proposed to facilitate inter-departmental data sharing, with integration planned with platforms including API Setu, DigiLocker, Entity Locker, NAPIX, BharatX, AI Kosh and NDAP. The integration target has been set for July 2027, officials said.

title: ‘I’ve spent my life educating people about trans lives… this film does it too’ | Hindustan Times
description: Aman, a short film directed by Rahul Roye won the best short film at the BFI London Film Festival. It gives voice to the unspeakable
content: Kabir Maan, the 34-year-old actor who plays the titular role of Aman—a film that won the best short film award at the recently-concluded British Film Institute (BFI) Film Festival—speaks to Hindustan Times about the taboos of trans representation, how he almost didn’t make it to the film’s world premiere because of the difficulty he faced in getting a passport, and why livelihood remains a precarious issue for transgender people, including him. Edited excerpts.Is this the first time you have acted in a film?Yes, this is my debut film!How did you come across this script and what did you think about it when you first came across it?I’ve been working in the education and social sector since 2018. I first spoke to Rahul Roye (the director) in 2024. That was a particularly tough time for me. I was dealing with heartbreak while also struggling to transition and establish my teaching career. When Rahul reached out, he told me about the role—they were looking for a pre-operative trans man on HRT (Hormone Replacement Therapy)—and asked for some photographs. When I sent them, he called me back the same day and said, ‘you’re it, the whole crew loves you’.The film shows a trans man, Aman, being intimate with a cis-gender man, and shortly before his gender affirming surgery, learns he is pregnant. These aren’t issues that we talk about at all in queer/trans spaces. Did the script make you pause?I mean, my whole life, I’ve been fighting for society to accept my identity and not see me as a girl. This character gets intimate with a man, has a sexual orientation different from mine, and gets pregnant—all of this made me wonder if, by doing this role, I would be enacting the roles society forced me to play. Then there was the fact that the film also showed my character in a binder, and binding, as you know, is such a sacred practice that we, as transmen, do behind closed doors. What would it be like showing it on screen? I thought a lot about it. I realised that I am a trans man, and I am doing the work of educating people, whether it is my parents and friends or the officials I encounter for getting my documents. So why not do this too? This is my chance to educate the wider world.What was the director’s reaction when you told him you’ll do the film?He asked me if I smoked. I said yes, but I was just about to quit. He immediately told me not to, because Aman is a chain smoker! When we started the acting workshops remotely, he would often call me Aman. At one point, I had to stop attending the workshops. Rahul told me to take my time but also said that he wouldn’t be able to find another Aman, and I had to come back and do the film because it was important. In general, trans lives are very challenging. Till the very last day, before I was supposed to fly to Kolkata to shoot, I wasn’t sure if my mental health would permit me to go. There is a scene in the film when I check if I’m pregnant with a pregnancy kit. I told Rahul that I needed 30 minutes to mentally prepare for this scene. I tried to recall all the bad incidents that have happened to me, and I realised that that’s 95% of my life. The 5% good is that I am alive.That’s method acting. Using the memory of an emotion to emote in a scene.I think ever since puberty hits, the life of a transgender person is a roller-coaster journey. After we shot the bathroom scene, I was crying, the dialect coach was crying, and Rahul entered the bathroom and hugged me and cried. That was the first time I realised that we all are doing something that had the potential to change [perceptions].After we wrapped shooting the film, I realised that each scene that required me to cry, I was actually crying. I wasn’t acting. And that was also very cathartic for me—this film gave me an opportunity to channelise my trauma and pain.You have been vocal about your struggle in getting appropriate documentation when the amended Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act was passed earlier this year. Can you please tell us a little bit about it.I am a trained teacher and special educator. Last year, the Kendra Vidyalaya opened some posts, for which I wanted to apply. At the same time, I applied to take the Central Teaching Eligibility Test.Now, to apply for the KV teacher’s post, I needed to supply my Class X board certificate. The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), which I studied under, has not corrected the documents of any trans person that I know of. Were I to provide my CBSE enrollment number, my deadname would come up. That’s what happened when I applied for the KV teacher’s post. I had to fill the form using my deadname and gender.The moment I added my transgender identity, the age relaxation that I am granted on the basis of my caste identity, is immediately nullified. So I had no choice but to fill the form with my deadname and gender identity. I spoke to a few friends, who advised me to write an application to the CBSE. I attached the Nalsa judgement, the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, but I have not got any response as yet.When I went for the CTET exam, the form once again had to go in my dead name and gender identity. At the exam centre, the head invigilator humiliated me. She told me, ‘don’t teach me about transgender issues’. She said my admit card and TG card were all very well, but she couldn’t fathom what to make of me. Finally they let me take the exam one hour late, and placed me in a different seat where someone could keep an eye on me. I passed the exam. The irony was that the Delhi Pride was taking place that very day barely two kilometres away.I faced a similar struggle when I tried to get my passport renewed to visit Toronto, when the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) in September.I applied for the passport in ‘Tatkal’, which they refused to give me because of the changes to my name and gender. When I gave them documents to show my gender change—the gazette notification, aadhaar card, PAN card—they asked for documents like my birth certificate to prove my male gender.One official asked me for a document from a doctor stating the date from which my gender changed. I spent over a month making several trips to the office, meeting at least 15 different officials, to convince them that they couldn’t ask me questions about my facial hair, or whether I have had bottom surgery. The trouble is that officials don’t have any knowledge [of trans people].

title: Heavy rain likely in Tamil Nadu for 2 more days: Schools shut in Tirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari and Tenkasi; Chennai on yellow alert | India News
description: Heavy to very heavy rainfall that began on Tuesday continued overnight, with Chennai’s MGR Nagar recording the highest rainfall of 15 cm. | India News
content: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Wednesday forecast more rainfall over Tamil Nadu for the next two days as a low-pressure area formed over the southwest Bay of Bengal, shutting down schools in several parts of the state.Schools will remain closed on October 22 in Tirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari and Tenkasi districts due to heavy rainfall. However, no school closure order has been issued for Chennai so far. All government and government-aided schools and private schools in Puducherry and Karaikal have been also declared a holiday on Thursday.Heavy to very heavy rainfall that began on Tuesday continued overnight, with Chennai’s MGR Nagar recording the highest rainfall at 15 cm. Several neighbourhoods in and around the state capital received between 10 cm and 15 cm of rain. The IMD has issued a yellow alert for Chennai amid the heavy showers.On October 22, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching speeds of 40-50 kmph at one or two locations, the IMD predicted, according to PTI news agency. The districts likely to experience such rainfall include Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli, Kanyakumari, Tenkasi, Virudhunagar, Ramanathapuram, Theni, Dindigul, Madurai, Coimbatore, the Nilgiris, Sivaganga, Pudukkottai, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai, along with Karaikal in Puducherry.On October 23, widespread rainfall is expected to continue. “Heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places with thunderstorm & lightning with gusty wind speed reaching 40-50 kmph at one or two places is likely to occur over Kanyakumari, Nilgiris and Coimbatore,” an IMD bulletin said.Meanwhile, schools were closed on October 21 in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu districts due to heavy rainfall. However, no orders directing school closures in these districts on October 22 had been issued so far.(With PTI inputs)
