He photographed the impressions and shared the picture in a Facebook group on Saturday, October 18, asking members whether they resembled dinosaur footprints.(Also read: Brothers in China stunned to learn their stepping stones are 190-million-year-old dinosaur fossils)Prathetsena said that the stream was relatively dry at the time, exposing the rocks which had the footprints. He did not report the discovery to park rangers at the time as his family was in a hurry. Instead, he later posted the picture on Facebook.Thailand’s Department of Mineral Resources responded in the comments section of his post, acknowledging the post and saying it would investigate the discovery. On October 19, park rangers visited the site to examine and measure the footprints.A day later, on October 20, the Department of Mineral Resources confirmed the discovery in a post on its official Facebook page, announcing that the impressions were genuine dinosaur footprints.More about the dinosaur footprintsThailand’s Department of Public Relations has said that “The find includes a single trail with a total of six prints on the Phu Phan formation, dating back approximately 120 million years to the Early Cretaceous period.”No skeletal remains were found at the site. However, under Thai law, fossil protection extends beyond bones and teeth to include “trace fossils”, like the dinosaur footprints in question. Consequently, the confirmed trail immediately gained legal protection.(Also read: 10-year-old’s curiosity leads to discovery of ancient dinosaur footprints on a beach)The prints were preserved in sandstone. Each print is about 29 cm long and 26 cm wide.Authorities have temporarily closed the area to protect the site from natural erosion and human interference, prohibiting unauthorised access. Geologists are inspecting the site, and the public has been urged not to dig, disturb or move any evidence.The measures are intended to preserve the footprints for further scientific study, with plans to develop the site into an educational attraction following the assessments.

title: Pilibhit roll row: After Oppn flags anomalies, ECI removes ERO and VRC operator | Hindustan Times
description: All DEOs of the state directed to take cognizance of Pilibhit matter and thoroughly examine voter lists of all assembly constituencies in their respective districts, says UP CEO
content: LUCKNOW The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Wednesday ordered the removal of two election officials and legal action against them following a preliminary inquiry that confirmed large-scale anomalies in the electoral rolls of the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency.Taking cognisance of complaints filed by the Opposition, the poll panel relieved the electoral registration officer (ERO) and the voter registration centre (VRC) operator of Pilibhit Sadar from all voter list preparation duties.UP chief electoral officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa said all district election officers (DEOs) of UP had been directed to take cognizance of the Pilibhit matter and thoroughly examine voter lists of all assembly constituencies in their respective districts and submit a report within two days in the CEO office.The district election officer had been directed to carry out immediate correction of the electoral roll of Pilibhit Sadar assembly constituency, he added.The ECI moved into action mode after the Samajwadi Party and Uttar Pradesh Congress on Wednesday alleged that voters’ names were being altered in the state’s electoral rolls to deprive people of their voting rights, citing “irregularities” involving 13,150 entries in the Pilibhit Sadar assembly constituency.Rinwa said legal action against erring officers will be taken under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code. The district election officer had been also directed to submit a report regarding responsibilities of assistant electoral registration officers (AERO) of the constituency, he said.The poll panel took cognizance of the complaint submitted by political parties regarding the EPIC number of voters registered in the voter list for the Pilibhit Sadar assembly constituency and directed district election officer to investigate the matter and submit a report immediately, he added.According to the report submitted by the DEO after an investigation into the voter list of the constituency, it was found that the details of other voters were displayed when the EPIC number of some voters was searched online, he added.The DEO, Pilibhit, had been directed to thoroughly examine voter lists of all assembly constituencies in Pilibhit district and submit a detailed report within two days, CEO said.

title: 6 months and 4 states later, Belgian mega machine on 240 wheels rolls into Kheri | Hindustan Times
description: The giant vessel—a cyclisation reactor—is the centrepiece of India’s first integrated sugar-to-bioplastic plant being set up at Balrampur Chini Mills in Kumbhi village of UP’s Kheri district
content: LAKHIMPUR KHERI In an extraordinary feat of heavy-haul engineering and cross-state coordination, a mammoth 240-wheel trailer carrying a 110-ft-long, 26-ft-wide reactor from Belgium rolled into Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri district on Wednesday, nearing the finish line of a gruelling six-month road journey across four states.The giant vessel—a cyclisation reactor—is the centrepiece of India’s first integrated sugar-to-bioplastic (Polylactic Acid, or PLA) plant being set up at Balrampur Chini Mills in Kumbhi village in UP’s Kheri district. Escorted by police personnel, three red-flagged pilot vehicles and a 40-member technical crew tasked with lifting overhead power cables and pruning roadside trees, the convoy was stationed at Chhauchh village along National Highway 730A on Wednesday before making its final push to Kumbhi on Thursday morning.Months before the vessel even left Odisha’s Paradip Port, engineers conducted an exhaustive route survey through Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh to identify choke points. Along every leg of the journey, district administrations coordinated with the Public Works Department (PWD), local municipalities, forest officials, and electricity boards to temporarily dismantle highway signboards and clear overhead bottlenecks.“Originally assembled with 308 wheels, the trailer’s wheel count had to be reduced to 240 in Jharkhand to negotiate difficult turns along the way,” a Kumbhi sugar mill official revealed. While the final logistics bill is still being tallied, senior mill officials pegged the transportation cost alone at ₹4 crore to ₹5 crore.Entering Kheri from Bahraich district via the Sisaiya crossing in Dhaurahra tehsil, the vessel drew crowds of onlookers along the highway. Kheri district magistrate Anjani Kumar Singh confirmed that all departments concerned had been placed on alert to ensure smooth final-mile navigation to the mill premises.Once the reactor reaches Kumbhi on Thursday morning and installation is completed, the landmark facility is expected to commence operations by next month, according to Sunil Kumar Yadav, general manager of the Balrampur sugar unit at Kumbhi.“The vessel is a cyclisation reactor, the key machine in producing polylactic acid (PLA), a completely biodegradable plastic,” Yadav explained. “Sugarcane-derived sugar will first be converted into lactic acid, which will then be processed into PLA granules and pellets,” he added.Calling it a globally unique facility, Yadav noted that its fully integrated model brings raw material processing and final biopolymer manufacturing under a single roof — offering a scalable green alternative to conventional petroleum-based plastic pollution.The groundwork for the mega project was laid on February 22 last year when chief minister Yogi Adityanath visited Gola Gokarnanath to lay the foundation stone for the ₹3,080-crore plant.Alongside the main plant, a 200-acre industrial park is also proposed to house downstream ancillary units that will mould the PLA pellets into everyday eco-friendly products.“When operational, the plant will add a new chapter to Kheri’s agriculture-based industrial development,” DM Anjani Kumar Singh said, adding that the project will steer the region towards sustainable industrial growth while unlocking substantial employment and entrepreneurial opportunities for local youth.

title: Iltija expresses solidarity with protesting forestry students | Hindustan Times
description: Interacting with the students, Iltija listened to their grievances and questioned the rationale behind recruitment rules that fail to adequately recognise specialised forestry qualifications
content: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) leader Iltija Mufti on Wednesday visited Benhama in Ganderbal to express solidarity with protesting students of Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-Kashmir) over the proposed recruitment rules for forester posts in the Jammu and Kashmir forest department.Iltija also expressed concern over the notice directing students to vacate their hostels amid the ongoing protest. Interacting with the students, Iltija listened to their grievances and questioned the rationale behind recruitment rules that fail to adequately recognise specialised forestry qualifications.The PDP leader said the protection and management of forests, flora and fauna, and the region’s fragile ecological resources require specialised technical knowledge, scientific understanding and practical field experience.She questioned how candidates without specialised forestry education, including those holding degrees in commerce or engineering, could be expected to discharge responsibilities requiring an in-depth understanding of forest ecosystems, biodiversity, wildlife and conservation, without the necessary domain-specific training.She emphasised that while every academic discipline has its own value, professional roles involving forest management must give due importance to the qualifications and expertise directly relevant to the job.Expressing concern over the notice asking protesting students to vacate their hostels, she said that the grievances of students should be addressed through dialogue rather than measures that add to their distress. She urged the university authorities to act sensitively and ensure that students are not penalised for raising legitimate concerns about their professional future.Calling upon the concerned authorities to reconsider the proposed recruitment framework, she demanded a fair and transparent policy that recognises specialised forestry education and safeguards the interests of qualified graduates.

title: J&K Police recover nearly 2kg narcotics in Arnia sector | Hindustan Times
description: Police registered a first information report (FIR) under Sections 8, 18, 21, 22, 27 and 27 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and investigation was taken up
content: Police on Wednesday recovered 804 grams of heroin and 1.1 kg of opium from Talhar, a border village along the Indo-Pak international border in the Arnia sector of Jammu district, during an investigation into a suspected narcotics smuggling module linked to a drone-dropping incident, officials said.The recovery was made during the investigation into a case linked to the alleged consumption of narcotics by 26-year-old Sunny Kumar, son of Tarsem Lal, a resident of Kotli Mirdian in Suchetgarh tehsil near a border ditch in his village, they said.Police registered a first information report (FIR) under Sections 8, 18, 21, 22, 27 and 27 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and investigation was taken up.“During the course of investigation and subsequent questioning, Kumar’s alleged involvement in a narcotics smuggling module linked to a drone-dropping incident came to light,” said a police spokesperson.“Acting on the leads, a police team, led by station house officer RS Pura, recovered 804gm of heroin and 1.114kg of opium from the Talhar area of sector Arnia,” he said.“Preliminary investigation has indicated a cross-border nexus involving the use of drones for smuggling narcotics into Indian territory. Police are investigating the backward and forward linkages of the module to identify the source of the consignment, its intended recipients and other persons involved in the narco-terror network,” he said.Further investigation was underway to establish the complete chain of the narcotics trafficking network and identify all those involved.

title: LG vows to eliminate terrorism from J&K, pays tributes to police martyrs | Hindustan Times
description: On the occasion, J&K DGP Nalin Prabhat read out Sinha’s message while remembering the courage, dedication and patriotism of the brave police men
content: Jammu and Kashmir lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha paid tributes to police martyrs on Wednesday and resolved not to rest until the region is free from separatist and terrorist elements.Sinha warned terrorists and their supporters within the UT that their days are over and even if they try to hide underground, they will be punished under the law.On the occasion, J&K DGP Nalin Prabhat read out Sinha’s message while remembering the courage, dedication and patriotism of the brave police men.Sinha said that their service and sacrifice remain an enduring source of inspiration for Jammu and Kashmir and the nation.“Our goal is to identify and root out terrorism and all associated elements in Jammu and Kashmir. Today, we resolve not to rest until this land is freed from separatist and terrorist elements. I warn anyone within Jammu and Kashmir who supports terrorism that your days are over. Even if you attempt to hide in the netherworld (Pataal), we will find you and ensure you are punished under the law,” he said.Sinha expressed gratitude to all police martyrs and conveyed deep respect and sympathy to their families, along with prayers and best wishes for their health and well-being.“While no recognition can compensate for the loss suffered by families, it is the responsibility of the nation to honour their sacrifice through meaningful support and care. I have always said that no honour or assistance can compensate a family for the pain of losing a loved one. Yet, it is the nation’s duty to honour their sacrifice not merely in words, but also through its conduct and responsibilities. I assure the entire J&K Police family that every possible effort will continue to be made to ensure a dignified life, welfare, and necessary support for the families of the martyrs,” he said.The LG acknowledged the contributions of the J&K Police, describing its history as one marked by courage, discipline and an unwavering commitment to duty. He said that from maintaining law and order and combating terrorism to assisting citizens during emergencies and natural disasters, the force has rendered distinguished service under challenging circumstances.“Thousands of personnel of the J&K Police have laid down their lives in the fight against terrorism. I believe the courage of the J&K Police is not confined to the borders of the Union territory but is a source of inspiration for the entire police system of the country. The nation will never forget the contribution of the immortal martyrs,” he said.The LG also observed that the police uniform symbolises service, responsibility and sacrifice. He said the true measure of policing lies in ensuring public safety, delivering justice to citizens and standing by society in times of need and crisis.“In the 79 years since Independence, India has faced numerous challenges. The Jammu and Kashmir Police, the Indian Army and the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) have protected the nation’s security and integrity in difficult circumstances. Today, India is moving resolutely towards its goal of becoming a developed nation. In this journey, peace, stability and progress in Jammu and Kashmir are of special importance, and the major responsibility of ensuring them rests on the shoulders of the Police, Army and CAPFs,” he said.The LG reaffirmed the government of India’s commitment to strengthening peace and progress in Jammu and Kashmir and called upon citizens to uphold unity, communal harmony and mutual trust, while remaining vigilant against forces seeking to disrupt peace and stability.

title: Two get 10-year jail term in 2017 heroin, ganja seizure case | Hindustan Times
description: NCB says 340 grams of heroin and 160 grams of ganja were seized from the convicts at Barabanki railway station; drugs were transported from Nagaland
content: A court in Barabanki has sentenced two drug traffickers to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment each in a 2017 case involving the seizure of 340 grams of heroin and 160 grams of ganja, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), Lucknow, said in a press release issued on Wednesday.The court of the additional district and sessions judge, Barabanki, convicted Shakeel and Rampyari on Monday for their involvement in drug trafficking, the NCB said.The case dates back to May 27, 2017, when the NCB’s Lucknow zonal unit, acting on specific intelligence, seized the contraband from black bags allegedly in the conscious possession of the two accused at Barabanki railway station.According to the agency, the two were travelling on the Avadh Assam Express and were getting off the train at the station when the seizure was made. The investigation revealed that the drugs had been transported from Dimapur in Nagaland to Barabanki, the press release said.During the trial, the prosecution sought stringent punishment, citing the gravity of drug trafficking and its adverse impact on society. After examining the evidence and circumstances of the case, the court sentenced both convicts to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment, the NCB said.The agency urged citizens to share information about drug trafficking through the MANAS national narcotics helpline 1933, assuring that informers’ identities would be kept confidential.

title: Lucknow Development Authority seeks to bring 662 revenue villages under its ambit | Hindustan Times
description: As many as 662 revenue villages are proposed to be brought under the Lucknow Development Authority’s (LDA) jurisdiction as the authority seeks to expand planned development beyond its existing limits of 1,082 square kilometres and bring additional rural and urban areas under its regulatory ambit
content: As many as 662 revenue villages are proposed to be brought under the Lucknow Development Authority’s (LDA) jurisdiction as the authority seeks to expand planned development beyond its existing limits of 1,082 square kilometres and bring additional rural and urban areas under its regulatory ambit.The LDA has sent a revised proposal to the Uttar Pradesh government seeking approval to expand its jurisdiction across the remaining urban and rural areas of Lucknow district, excluding the Lucknow Industrial Development Authority (LIDA) and cantonment areas.The move aims to check unplanned growth, improve infrastructure and bring unauthorised colonies under a planned development framework.LDA vice-chairman Prathamesh Kumar said the authority would take up development and regularisation work in the newly included areas after the government approves the proposal and issues the necessary notifications.“We have sent the proposal to the state government seeking approval. Once the approval is granted, regularisation and development works in the newly added areas will also become part of the LDA’s responsibilities,” Kumar said.He added that the authority planned to introduce new housing schemes, improve connectivity and upgrade infrastructure in the expanded areas. It would also explore the regularisation of unauthorised and illegal colonies, he said.Six blocks, 10 nagar panchayats in expansion planThe revised proposal covers the remaining areas of six development blocks including Sarojini Nagar, Kakori, Malihabad, Bakshi Ka Talab, Gosainganj and Mohanlalganj along with the entire Mal block.It also seeks to include 10 nagar panchayats: Mahona, Itaunja, Malihabad, Nagaram, Amethi, Kakori, Bakshi Ka Talab, Mohanlalganj, Banthra and Gosainganj.The proposal seeks to bring the remaining urban and rural areas within Lucknow district under the LDA’s jurisdiction while retaining the specified exclusions. The proposed expansion would extend the authority’s planning oversight beyond the existing notified development area.Proposal awaiting government approvalThe LDA board approved the revised proposal at its 181st meeting on July 5, 2024. The authority sent it to the state government on July 10, 2024.The government subsequently asked the LDA to provide a revised proposal addressing 11 points in its prescribed checklist. The authority submitted the required details on October 3, 2024.In March 2025, the government sought the authority’s comments on observations from the urban development and panchayati raj departments.New schemes, infrastructure and colony regularisation plannedThe proposed expansion could allow the LDA to plan housing schemes and connectivity improvements in areas currently outside its notified jurisdiction. The authority also intends to take up infrastructure development and examine the regularisation of unauthorised colonies after the government clears the proposal.The move follows directions issued after a meeting chaired by chief minister Yogi Adityanath on July 5, 2022, to review the functioning of development authorities.The meeting noted that more than 45 lakh people lived within the LDA’s jurisdiction at the time and that Lucknow was expanding year after year, with a considerable portion of its growth remaining unplanned. Officials were directed to consider expanding the authority’s jurisdiction to bring such development under a planned framework.

title: Panchayat elections in Ladakh on November 21 | Hindustan Times
description: The last date for filing nominations is November 2, while scrutiny of nomination papers will take place on November 3; candidates can withdraw their nominations until November 5
content: The State Election Commission (SEC) of Ladakh, on Wednesday, announced the schedule for the impending panchayat elections in the strategic Union territory, with polling scheduled for November 21 and the entire election process to be completed by November 30.The state election commissioner, Sudhanshu Pandey, said that the election notifications will be issued by the administrator and the SEC on October 26.The last date for filing nominations is November 2, while scrutiny of nomination papers will take place on November 3. Candidates can withdraw their nominations until November 5.The last general elections to panchayat halqas in Ladakh were held in November 2018, necessitating the constitution of new panchayat halqas.The schedule has been framed under Rule 7 of the Jammu and Kashmir Panchayati Raj Rules, 1996, as applicable to the Union territory of Ladakh.The provision requires the government to notify elections to panchayat halqas in consultation with the election authority. The model code of conduct has also come into force with immediate effect, directing candidates and political parties to comply strictly with the prescribed guidelines throughout the election process.Ladakh notifies 100 constituencies across 8 hill councilsOn Wednesday evening, the administration of UT Ladakh notified 100 elected constituencies across eight LAHDCs under the amended LAHDC Act, 1997: Leh (22), Kargil (21), Sankoo (13), Changthang (10), Nubra (9), Sham (9), Zanskar (9), and Drass (7).Earlier, the administration dissolved the erstwhile LAHDC Kargil with immediate effect following the reorganisation of districts. Ladakh LG Vinai Kumar Saxena on Tuesday notified the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Amendment) Regulation, 2026, paving the way for hill councils in all eight districts of the Union territory, including the newly created Sankoo district.

title: No invitation yet from MHA for fresh talks: Ladakh bodies | Hindustan Times
description: Soon after last week’s meeting concluded, the Ladakh leaders told media that they have been invited for another meeting in New Delhi that could take place on October 22
content: The proposed meeting between the Ladakh leadership and Union ministry of home affairs (MHA) officials, scheduled for Thursday in Delhi, is not taking place for the time being.The last round of talks between the Ladakh leadership and the high powered committee of the MHA in Leh last week remained inconclusive, with the Ladakh leadership rejecting the draft proposal submitted by the MHA for study.Those in the know said that the MHA has not sent a fresh invite to Ladakh leaders due to unknown reasons; however, there is every possibility that the meeting could be held in the coming days. “The meeting was scheduled for Thursday. Since no invitation was extended, there is every possibility the meeting could take place on any other date,” a senior leader of Leh Apex Body (LAB) said.Soon after last week’s meeting concluded, the Ladakh leaders told media that they have been invited for another meeting in New Delhi that could take place on October 22.The Ladakh leadership has been demanding statehood, Sixth Schedule, and a say in the appraisal of the chief secretary and other senior officers. However, so far, the MHA team has not agreed to these demands of the Ladakh leadership, especially those raised by the LAB and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA).On Saturday, Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra termed it “unfortunate” that the Ladakh leadership rejected the draft proposal within two hours.The LAB and KDA have held several rounds of talks with the MHA. “During negotiations on the Sixth Schedule, it was explained that this provision applies to states, particularly in the northeastern region, where a minority tribe needs protection against any discriminatory action by a majority tribe. Therefore, the Sixth Schedule has a different geographical, historical and cultural context, and its relevance in the case of Ladakh is not particularly significant in the same way,” Kundra had said.“After considerable deliberation, the MHA provided a 32-page document to the leaders of Ladakh on the morning of October 16. I want to make one thing very clear through you: the constitutional amendment and the kind of democratic structure the people of Ladakh want will emerge through discussion and deliberation. We do not want to submit a draft unilaterally. We want a framework that has the broad agreement of Ladakh’s leadership. We had expected this to happen in a positive manner. Naturally, nobody can read a 32-page document immediately and provide a response. We suggested that the leaders study it and that another meeting be convened after a week or 10 to 15 days,” he had said.

title: Landmark at 11,500 ft, regular high court hearings begin in Leh | Hindustan Times
description: Justice Parihar said that the 65 cases listed on the opening day represented an initial effort to streamline access for local litigants
content: A historic chapter in Indian judicial history unfolded on Wednesday as the high court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh commenced regular hearings at its newly established Leh bench. Located at an altitude of over 11,500 feet, it is the country’s highest high court bench.Chief justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Sanjay Parihar presided over the first regular division bench. Proceedings were conducted in a hybrid format, with chief justice Bhati attending virtually and justice Parihar presiding physically in Leh.The division bench cleared five listed matters before justice Parihar sat as a single bench to hear 60 individual cases.Justice Parihar said that the 65 cases listed on the opening day represented an initial effort to streamline access for local litigants. He said that establishing regular hearings in high-altitude terrain marks a milestone in national judicial infrastructure, ensuring geographical barriers do not impede justice.Earlier, litigants and lawyers from Leh, Kargil, and surrounding areas had to undertake arduous journeys to Srinagar or Jammu for high court proceedings.Kargil and Leh have a one-way road distance of around 220km, making it difficult for litigants to travel such a long distance. Addressing this issue, advocate Tashi Gyalson, former chief executive councillor of the Leh Hill Development Council said, “On the day of inauguration, CJI Justice Surya Kant stated that hearings will also be held virtually for litigants from far-off places like Zanskar and Nubra. Therefore, the same mode could be applied to litigants from Kargil.”When asked whether litigants can now file fresh petitions directly at the Leh bench or if it is currently limited to existing transferred cases, he confirmed that new cases are indeed being accepted. “Yes, fresh cases can also be filed at the high court bench in Leh. Otherwise, what purpose would this bench serve?” he added.The physical infrastructure for the bench at Melongthang, Leh, was formally inaugurated by the Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant, on October 18.

title: Sukhu, Vikramaditya reject BJP’s factionalism allegations | Hindustan Times
description: BJP had alleged that the absence of the CM and the Congress state president from the event reflected the growing internal contradictions within the Congress
content: Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Wednesday rejected the BJP’s allegations of factionalism within the Congress after skipping the recent unveiling of a statue of former chief minister Virbhadra Singh in Sarahan.Speaking to the media in Shimla, Sukhu said Congress leaders had come together to honour Virbhadra Singh’s legacy and asserted that the unveiling of his statue should not be linked to factionalism within the party.BJP had alleged that the absence of the CM and the Congress state president from the event reflected the growing internal contradictions within the Congress.Speaking to reporters at Sanjauli Heliport in Shimla, Sukhu said the BJP’s allegations of factionalism in the Congress were misplaced and accused the opposition party of being divided into several factions itself. “Why should there be factionalism? This is a wrong statement. The BJP itself is divided into five factions,” Sukhu told reporters.“The unveiling of his statue should not be linked with factionalism. It is wrong to interpret such an occasion as a sign of divisions within the Congress. When his statue was unveiled in Shimla, all Congress leaders including Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi were present,” Sukhu said.Meanwhile, public works and urban development minister Vikramaditya Singh also dismissed the factionalism allegations over the unveiling of former CM Virbhadra Singh’s statue.“It was a district-level function, and installing his statue at his birthplace was necessary, given the sentiments of the local people. We had invited everyone. Those who could attend came, while those who could not, did not. There is nothing to do with factionalism in this,” he told reporters in Shimla on Wednesday.CM launches helicopter service from Sanjauli to RampurThe CM on Wednesday launched a helicopter service from Sanjauli in Shimla to Rampur.The service, launched under the regional connectivity scheme (UDAN), will operate three days a week under the Heli-HOP Himachal Helicopter Service. The fare for Shimla-Rampur service is ₹3,637.Under the schedule, the helicopter will take off from Sanjauli at 9.55am and reach Rampur at 10.30am. It will then depart from Rampur for Reckong Peo at 10.50am, reaching there at 11.25am.The return flight from Reckong Peo will take off at 11.30am and reach Rampur at 12.05pm. The helicopter will then depart from Rampur for Sanjauli at 12.10pm and arrive at 12.45pm. The service will operate every Monday, Friday and Saturday.Speaking on the occasion, Sukhu said that the initiative was not merely a means of travelling from one place to another, but also a symbol of changing times, new thinking and immense development opportunities in the hill state. The CM said that the state government had set a target of connecting every corner of Himachal through helicopter services.Himachal to introduce moral science from Class 1 The CM on Wednesday presided over a meeting with senior officers of the education department and directed the introduction of moral science from Class 1 to inculcate ethical values, discipline, compassion, respect for elders and a sense of responsibility among children from an early age.Sukhu emphasised that education should focus not only on academic achievements but also on character-building and the overall development of students. During the meeting, he reviewed the implementation of the CBSE curriculum in government schools and stressed the need to ensure qualified teachers, adequate administrative staff and a conducive learning environment.

title: 2024 arithmetic may push SP, Congress to stick together | Hindustan Times
description: An analysis of assembly segment-wise leads in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections suggests that if the voting pattern is repeated, the INDIA bloc could pose a formidable challenge to the BJP. The BJP’s Lok Sabha tally in Uttar Pradesh fell from 62 seats in 2019 to 33 in 2024, while the SP and Congress together won 43 of the state’s 80 seats. The SP won 37 and the Congress six.
content: Seat-sharing differences may be straining the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, but the electoral arithmetic of 2024 offers both parties a compelling reason to stay together: their combined lead extended to more than 220 of the state’s 403 assembly segments.An analysis of assembly segment-wise leads in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections suggests that if the voting pattern is repeated, the INDIA bloc could pose a formidable challenge to the BJP. The BJP’s Lok Sabha tally in Uttar Pradesh fell from 62 seats in 2019 to 33 in 2024, while the SP and Congress together won 43 of the state’s 80 seats. The SP won 37 and the Congress six.Nationally, the Congress won 99 seats, emerging as the second-largest party, while the BJP retained its position as the largest party with 240 seats.The assembly segment-wise breakdown shows the SP-Congress alliance leading in more than 220 segments. The Trinamool Congress also led in one segment, taking the combined lead to 221.This was not the first time the SP and Congress had joined hands. The two parties contested the 2017 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections as alliance partners, but the arrangement failed to deliver the results they would have expected. The SP won 47 of the 311 seats it contested, securing 21.82% of the total valid votes. Its vote share in the seats it contested as the Congress’s alliance partner was 28.32%. The Congress contested 114 seats and won seven, securing 6.25% of the total valid votes and 22.09% of the votes polled in the seats it contested. Despite the alliance, candidates from both parties faced each other in some constituencies.The Congress had earlier allied with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) for the 1996 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, when the state was undivided. The Congress won 33 of the 126 seats it contested in the 425-member assembly, while the BSP won 67 of the 296 seats it contested. The Congress secured 8.35% of the total valid votes and 29.13% of the votes polled in the seats it contested. The BSP received 19.64% of the total valid votes and 27.73% of the votes polled in the seats it contested.The SP-BSP alliance too had failed to work in 2019 Lok Sabha elections. The SP won five seats with 18.11% of the total valid votes, while the BSP won 10 seats with 19.43%.Will the Congress and the SP eventually reach a seat-sharing agreement?“An alliance is very important for the Congress and the Samajwadi Party if they want to defeat the BJP. If the SP and the Congress decide to come together, they may pose a serious challenge to the BJP. Both parties may initially have differences over seat-sharing, but they will eventually realise its importance and come together if the prevailing political situation is taken into account,” said professor SK Dwivedi, former head of the political science department at Lucknow University.UP Congress president Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ said the INDIA bloc would perform better in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections than it did in the state in 2024.“We hope the central leadership of the two parties will soon reach a seat-sharing understanding. We are sure whatever decision is taken on the seat-sharing issue will be in accordance with the honour and feelings of the Congress and its workers,” said Mishra.Samajwadi Party chief spokesman and former minister Rajendra Chaudhary said both the parties were yet to begin talks for seat sharing. He said Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had already made it clear that the winnability of candidates, and not the number of seats, would be the main criteria for seat-sharing.

title: 2027 polls: Congress eyes 3-digit seat share in pre-Diwali deal with SP | Hindustan Times
description: Buoyed by the INDIA bloc’s performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and its recent campaigns against the BJP, including over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the Congress is signalling that it will no longer settle for a token share in the alliance.
content: Dismissing the Samajwadi Party’s (SP) “winnability over numbers” argument as a ploy to limit its share, the Congress is preparing to drive a hard bargain for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, demanding at least a three-digit seat share.Buoyed by the INDIA bloc’s performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and its recent campaigns against the BJP, including over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the Congress is signalling that it will no longer settle for a token share in the alliance.“Winnability is a deception and the victory of AAP candidates in Delhi is an example. In politics, most people vote for a party out of trust and our candidates will not be weak ones. Just as others plan to select strong candidates, we will do the same,” said Congress’s UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam on Wednesday, pushing back against the SP’s argument that seat allocation should be determined by electoral prospects rather than numbers.The Congress’s past assembly election performances are central to the SP’s argument. In 2017, the Congress contested 114 seats and won seven, while the SP won 47 of the 311 seats it contested. In 2022, the Congress contested 399 seats but won only two, while the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested.However, the message from the Congress camp is loud, “Past assembly defeats cannot be the sole yardstick for deciding its place in the alliance.”The party is preparing to put its own electoral calculations on the table and resist any attempt by the SP to dictate terms.Aradhana Mishra’s elevation as the state Congress chief was initially seen as a sign of the party’s conciliatory approach towards the SP. However, the Congress had two views on seat-sharing — one favouring a softer stance and the other advocating a more aggressive bargain. The latter approach has now received the green light from the party’s top leadership.The Congress’s demand for a three-digit seat share marks a departure from its relatively restrained approach in previous negotiations. The party also wants to avoid the uncertainty of last-minute seat-sharing arrangements that characterised previous election run-ups.A list of constituencies has emerged from consultations between Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and UP Congress leaders, the latest of which was held on October 19. Party sources said another meeting was planned for the end of the month, with the aim of concluding seat-sharing talks before Diwali.“Discussions have now begun. We have submitted a list of seats to our top leadership, and communication with alliance partners has also begun around constituencies. Formal face-to-face talks will soon be held,” Gautam said.The Congress won six of the 17 Lok Sabha seats it contested in Uttar Pradesh in 2024, while the SP won 37. The two parties contested the election as INDIA bloc allies.“Each seat is being analysed. Seat-sharing discussions will have Priyanka Gandhi as an integral part of the organisation,” Aradhana Mishra said.The state leadership has held at least two meetings with Priyanka Gandhi in New Delhi to discuss seat-sharing.The Congress is examining constituencies where it finished second in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, along with seats associated with prominent state leaders. The SP, however, is understood to be cautious about conceding a larger share to its ally. SP leaders have suggested that 50 seats would amount to a substantial concession, while party chief Akhilesh Yadav has stressed that winnability of candidates, rather than the number of seats, should determine the allocation.According to party sources, both sides are expected to press their claims based on past electoral performances and organisational strength.Meanwhile, the Congress held a meeting with office-bearers and former MPs and MLAs to discuss its upcoming campaign in Uttar Pradesh and the national capital.

title: Chandigarh: Wedding venue booking cancelled, consumer panel orders full refund | Hindustan Times
description: The case concerns Harvinder Pal, a Chandigarh resident from Manimajra, who booked the Panchkula Community Centre in Sector 6 for his daughter’s wedding scheduled for April 26, 2020
content: The district consumer disputes redressal commission, Chandigarh, has directed the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) to refund ₹9,900 withheld from a marriage venue booking cancelled during the Covid-19 lockdown, along with 9% annual interest and ₹5,000 as compensation for harassment, mental agony and litigation expenses.The case concerns Harvinder Pal, a Chandigarh resident from Manimajra, who booked the Panchkula Community Centre in Sector 6 for his daughter’s wedding scheduled for April 26, 2020. He had paid ₹74,900 for the booking on November 2, 2019.However, the wedding function could not be held at the venue due to the Covid-19 lockdown. Pal sought a refund of the entire amount on May 7, 2020, following which ₹65,000 was returned, leaving ₹9,900 unpaid.Despite repeated requests, the remaining amount was not refunded. In a letter dated September 29, 2025, the estate officer of the Haryana Shahari Vikas Pradhikaran (HSVP), Panchkula, rejected his claim, stating that the amount represented goods and services tax (GST) pertaining to the 2020-21 financial year and could not be adjusted in the 2024-25 financial year.Pal approached the consumer commission, submitting documents related to the booking and cancellation. He also cited another case in which the entire amount for a cancelled community centre booking had reportedly been refunded.While examining the matter, the commission observed that there was no material on record to establish that Pal was liable to forfeit the remaining ₹9,900 following the cancellation.It further noted that the authority’s explanation regarding GST and financial-year adjustments did not justify retaining the amount, particularly when the booking had been cancelled due to the pandemic and the facility had not been used.The commission held that administrative or accounting difficulties, by themselves, could not be a ground for withholding money collected from a consumer under these circumstances.

title: Haryana Police plan multi-prong strategy to curb crime networks | Hindustan Times
description: Strategy to target organised crime at multiple levels, local facilitators, and recruitment channels for youth, says Haryana Special Task Force
content: Keeping in view the continuous threat posed by gangsters operating from foreign countries and behind the bars, the Haryana Special Task Force (STF) has drawn up a three-pronged strategy to dismantle organised crime networks. The strategy targets gangsters orchestrating crimes from abroad and inside prisons, their local associates and intermediaries, and the networks that allegedly lure vulnerable youths into criminal gangs.When asked about the increasing number of criminal activities allegedly being operated by gangsters from jails and abroad, the inspector general of police STF Simardeep Singh said the task force was committed to dismantling organised crime networks operating in the state and was tracking not only gangsters based abroad but also criminals lodged in Haryana’s prisons and people who had come into contact with them.“We are not only focusing on gangsters sitting abroad and operating their gangs in Haryana but are also tracking the records of criminals lodged in jails across the state. We are examining the people who have come into contact with them, particularly those arrested for petty offences and lodged in jail for a couple of months,” Singh told Hindustan Times.The strategy seeks to target organised crime at multiple levels, including the gangsters allegedly directing operations, the local networks facilitating their activities and the recruitment channels through which young people are drawn into criminal gangs.The STF is examining the backgrounds and criminal records of people who may have been in jails for petty crimes and came into contact with established gangsters during their time in prison in the past several years. The focus on those arrested for relatively minor offences is aimed at identifying potential recruitment networks and preventing young people from being influenced by organised crime syndicates.According to the information, the agency also taking help of the national agencies to track gangsters operating from foreign countries who allegedly continue to coordinate criminal activities in Haryana through associates on the ground. At the same time, prison-based networks are under scrutiny to establish how criminals lodged in jails may continue to influence or direct operations outside.By identifying intermediaries and disrupting links between gangsters and potential recruits, the STF intends to weaken the local support structures that enable criminal gangs to sustain their activities and expand their reach.STF’s enforcement record shows that it has arrested 1,972 accused since 2024, including 369 most-wanted or wanted criminals, 1,063 gangsters and 540 accused involved in heinous crimes, according to the figures provided by the task force. The year-wise arrests of gang members indicate sustained action against organised crime. The STF arrested 323 gangsters in 2024, followed by 470 in 2025, while 270 had been arrested so far in 2026.The officials monitoring the gangsters settled in abroad claimed that they have tightened the grip over these criminals and in 2026 alone, 15 wanted criminals have been successfully deported and brought back to India with the help of technical surveillance, intelligence inputs, Interpol channels and coordination with other law enforcement agencies.In August, Haryana STF proposed a reward of US $10,000 on each of four foreign-based gangsters—Himanshu Bhau, Rohit Godara, Randeep Malik, and Anil Pandit, who claimed the responsibility of attack on bollywood actor Tiger Shroff.

title: Kullu Dussehra a living expression of Himachal’s rich ‘dev sanskriti’: Governor | Hindustan Times
description: The festivities began with the traditional Rath Yatra of Lord Raghunath, with more than 347 local deities from different parts of the Kullu Valley participating in the historic congregation
content: Kullu Dussehra was not merely a religious festival but a living expression of Himachal Pradesh’s rich Dev Sanskriti, folk traditions, collective faith and social harmony, said Himachal governor Kavinder Gupta on Wednesday while formally inaugurating the week-long International Kullu Dussehra Festival at the historic Dhalpur Ground in Kullu.The celebrations mark the beginning of one of the state’s most renowned cultural and religious celebrations.The festivities began with the traditional Rath Yatra of Lord Raghunath, with more than 347 local deities from different parts of the Kullu Valley participating in the historic congregation. Bindu Gupta, wife of the governor, was also present on the occasion.Extending his greetings to the people on the auspicious occasion, the governor said that the unique confluence of Dev and Lok Sanskriti makes Kullu Dussehra distinctive and gives it a special place on the cultural map of the country. He emphasised that traditions are not merely a legacy of the past but a source of strength and guidance for the present and the future. Preserving these traditions and transmitting them to younger generations, he said, was a collective responsibility.Referring to the message of Vijayadashami, the governor said that the life of Lord Shri Ram inspires society to follow the path of truth, duty, sacrifice, justice and righteousness. He called upon people to remain united against social evils including drug abuse, violence, corruption and forces that seek to create discord in society.Appealing to citizens to uphold the spirit of ‘nation first’, the governor said that national unity, integrity and social harmony were the collective responsibility of every citizen. “Our unity is our greatest strength,” he said, stressing the need to rise above differences and place national interest above all other considerations.

title: Haryana needs a ‘full-time CM’, not one ‘busy with Punjab politics’: Rao Narender | Hindustan Times
description: Haryana Congress says two years of BJP govt marred by anti-people policies, rising crime, corruption and unfulfilled promises
content: Haryana Congress on Wednesday launched a multi-barrel attack against the state government as it completed two years of its third consecutive term in power on October 17, with the principal opposition party demanding a “factual account” of the poll promises from chief minister Nayab Singh Saini.In a coordinated offensive akin to carpet bombing, senior Congress leaders held press conferences in 13 different locations with former chief minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda addressing the media in Delhi and the state party chief Rao Narender Singh in Sirsa.Taking a dig at chief minister Nayab Saini’s Punjab visits, the Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee (HPCC) chief said that the people of Haryana entrusted him with the responsibility of governing the state, but it appeared that Punjab politics was receiving greater priority in his political engagements than Haryana’s problems.“Haryana needs a full-time chief minister, not a part-time one, who remains present in the state, listens to the concerns of farmers, youth, traders, employees and ordinary citizens, and works to resolve them,” he said, raising a question mark over the state government’s performance and promises made ahead of October 2024 assembly elections.Accusing the state government of failing to maintain law and order and resolving farmers’ grievances, the HPCC chief alleged that “unemployment and corruption” were on the rise while the government was unable to deal with “alleged scams, drug abuse” and issues concerning health.“Instead of merely making claims about its achievements, the government must present a factual account of its election promises before the people,” Singh said, pointing out that people across the state are struggling with crime, unemployment, farmers’ problems, corruption and the poor state of public services.“During the assembly elections, the BJP made major promises to every section of society. The government must now explain how many promises have been fulfilled, how many are under implementation and what timelines have been set for completing the remaining commitments.”Referring to BJP’s claim about procurement of 24 crops at the minimum support price (MSP), the HPCC chief demanded that the government must publish details of procurement of each crop, the number of farmers who benefited and the status of payments. He said the government must explain how many of the 5 lakh urban and rural houses promised have been sanctioned, how many have been completed and how many have been handed over to beneficiaries.

title: Will challenge HERC’s decision to grant licence to pvt firm: Saini | Hindustan Times
description: The employees are opposing HERC’s decision granting a 25 year parallel electricity distribution licence to a 2025 incorporated company, Eleven Power for Gurugram and Nuh revenue districts
content: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Wednesday said the state government is standing firmly with power department employees and will strongly represent their case before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) against Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (HERC) decision to grant a private company, a licence to supply electricity in Gurugram and Nuh.Saini chaired a review meeting with administrative secretaries here to assess arrangements ahead of the three-day state-wide strike from, October 22 to 24, called by the Haryana Power Employees and Engineers Joint Struggle Front. Deputy commissioners (DCs) of all districts joined the meeting online, while energy minister Anil Vij, chief secretary Anurag Rastogi and director general of police (DGP) Ajay Singhal were also present.The employees are opposing HERC’s decision granting a 25 year parallel electricity distribution licence to a 2025 incorporated company, Eleven Power for Gurugram and Nuh revenue districts despite objections from the Haryana’s power distribution and transmission companies, power engineers, employee unions and public representatives.The chief minister warned that disturbances under the cover of the power employee unions’ strike will not be tolerated under any circumstances. “Strict legal action will be taken against any anti-social element attempting to damage a power station or power grid... such acts will amount to a waste of public money, which the government will not tolerate,” said Saini.The chief minister said that the government is ready to engage lawyers trusted by the power unions to pursue the case and reiterated that the government’s doors are always open for dialogue.Appealing to the unions to defer their strike in the public interest, Saini said the state government, along with the power unions, has opposed HERC’s decision.“In keeping with the demand of the power employee unions, the government has decided to challenge the decision before APTEL,” Saini said and reiterated that the government “stands firmly with power employees” on this issue and that government’s doors are always open for talks.He told the unions that, if they so wished, the state government is prepared to pursue the case through lawyers of their choice.He directed all deputy commissioners to ensure that the public does not face any inconvenience during the three-day statewide strike. Directions were issued to all departments to work proactively to prevent any disruption during the strike and ensure that no power installation is damaged. He also directed that drones be deployed to monitor sensitive installations.DCs to submit reports to high-level committeesThe DCs were also directed to constitute district-level committees to submit regular reports to the high-level committee headed by the chief secretary in Chandigarh. DCs will remain in contact with headquarters through hotline numbers, while separate control room numbers will be publicised to receive complaints from the public.Energy minister Anil Vij said that HERC is an independent regulator under the Central government. He said that the government had not invited applications for granting a licence to a private company to supply electricity in Haryana. HERC’s regulations provide for companies to apply for such a licence. He said the state government, along with the Engineers’ Association, has opposed the grant of a licence to the private company from the outset and will appeal against the decision.6,230 police personnel deployedDirector general of police (DGP) Ajay Singhal said that a total of 6,230 police personnel had been deployed at 1,015 locations across all districts. He said that police control rooms and helpline numbers have also been established in all districts and security arrangements are being reviewed continuously.Commissioner and secretary (energy department), Ashima Brar said that the department will enlist the services of retired employees and power employees from neighbouring states. She said that director-level officers will be stationed at the control room set up by the department.

title: UP govt nurses to stage sit-in at Lucknow health directorate | Hindustan Times
description: The 13-point charter of demands include the state government providing the old pension scheme to eligible nurses and ensuring home-district postings, as previously assured by the health minister.
content: In a bid to pressure the state government into accepting their 13-point charter of demands, government nurses who are members of the UP Rajkiya Nurses Sangh (UPRNS), a body representing nurses working in state government hospitals, abstained from work for two hours across several hospitals on Wednesday. They have also planned to stage a sit-in at the health directorate on Thursday.“We have been wearing black badges since October 9. Today (Wednesday), nurses protested with a two-hour work boycott. As part of the next phase, nurses will stage a sit-in at the health directorate in Lucknow tomorrow and hold a peaceful protest to draw the attention of the government and administration toward their pending issues and the 13-point charter of demands,” said Ashok Kumar, general secretary of UPRNS.The 13-point charter of demands include the state government providing the old pension scheme to eligible nurses and ensuring home-district postings, as previously assured by the health minister and state officials.The UPRNS also urged the government and administration to seriously consider all demands, take an early decision on those already agreed upon as well as the remaining pending issues, and issue necessary government orders to ensure justice for the nursing officers and employees who play a vital role in the state’s healthcare system.“If positive steps are not taken soon to resolve the demands, the ongoing two-hour work boycott could be converted into an indefinite one. The government and administration would be entirely responsible for any situation arising from such a development,” said Kumar.

title: Chandigarh: Mystery shrouds death of Chhattisgarh bizman at Sector 17 hotel room | Hindustan Times
description: He was identified as Deepak Mittal, director of Sanjay Grain Products Private Limited and a contractor with the Punjab government, who had arrived in Chandigarh on Tuesday for a meeting with Markfed officials scheduled for Wednesday
content: A 56-year-old businessman from Raipur, Chhattisgarh, died after being found unresponsive in his room at Hotel Taj in Sector 17 on Wednesday morning.He was identified as Deepak Mittal, director of Sanjay Grain Products Private Limited and a contractor with the Punjab government, who had arrived in Chandigarh on Tuesday for a meeting with Markfed officials scheduled for Wednesday, officials familiar with the matter said. Police said he had recently secured a contract for packaging of flour and pulses and the supply of ration kits.Police have ruled out foul play for now, stating that he was suffering from health complications. Some liquor bottles were also found at the spot.A woman had also allegedly visited him at the hotel on Tuesday night. Police say they have questioned her and cleared her of suspicion.An official, who questioned her, said that she had alerted the hotel staff that he was feeling unwell following which a waiter had come to check on him.Around 8 am, the staff found him lying “unconscious but breathing” in his room. He was rushed to Government Multi Speciality Hospital, Sector 16, where doctors declared him brought dead.Police say prima facie it appears he died of health complications, including hypertension, but maintained that the exact cause would be clear once the post-mortem reports are out. The procedure was carried out on Wednesday after his family arrived and gave their consent. The body was handed over to them after autopsy.Inquest proceedings have been initiated at the Sector 17 police station. A spokesperson of the hotel said, “We are saddened by this unfortunate incident and offer our deepest condolences. We are extending our support to the family and assisting the authorities.”

title: President Murmu likely to attend Nashik Kumbh flag hoisting after CM extends invitation | Mumbai news
description: Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis led a state delegation that included deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar to the Rashtrapati Bhavan to formally invite Murmu to the function, which will mark the start of the Kumbh Mela.  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: President Droupadi Murmu is likely to attend the Dhwajarohan (flag hoisting) ceremony of the Sinhastha Kumbh, scheduled for October 31, 2027 in Nashik.Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis led a state delegation that included deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar to the Rashtrapati Bhavan to formally invite Murmu to the function, which will mark the start of the Kumbh Mela.Murmu was also invited to attend the Godavari river aarti, the inauguration of the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Kumbh Mela Authority’s website, the launch of the Kumbh Mela theme song, and the unveiling of a coffee-table book and a commemorative postage stamp dedicated to the Kumbh, all scheduled for the flag-hoisting day.State officials said they were confident that Murmu would attend the event, one of the rare occasions when the President of India would be attending a religious function, even though a formal confirmation from Rashtrapati Bhavan is still awaited.Deputy CM Eknath Shinde said, “This is Trikhandi Kumbh and it comes after 65 years. The President has accepted the invitation.’’Food and civil supplies minister Chhagan Bhujbal, who was a member of the delegation that called on the President, said, “We went to Rashtrapati Bhavan to invite the President for the flag hoisting at Kumbh Mela. She will come, but an official confirmation is awaited. I think this is the first time that the President has been invited for the Kumbh flag hoisting, as chief ministers normally do it.”Commenting on the invitation, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut said, “Maharashtra is progressive, and it’s good that the state government has invited her.” Alluding to the Ayodhya Ram temple inauguration to which Murmu was reportedly not invited, Raut said, “That programme was in PM Modi’s hands. He didn’t want anyone else as the focus would have shifted to Murmu - an Adivasi lady.’’The state invitation presented to the President is based on a distinctive artistic concept. When opened, a box reveals a three-dimensional pop-up artwork depicting the mythological origins, spiritual significance and grandeur of the Kumbh Mela.Incorporating experiences associated with all five senses — sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch — the concept effectively highlights Nashik’s cultural heritage, the sacred significance of the Godavari River and the unique importance of the Kumbh in Indian traditions.The state delegation also presented Murmu a Paithani (a traditional art from the Nashik district) saree and a shawl, the officials said.

title: Fiscal squeeze: State curbs spending amid  ₹81,500-cr relief burden | Mumbai news
description: The state finance department, in a circular issued on Wednesday, cited the state’s limited resources and called for stricter expenditure controls  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: Amid mounting pressure on the state exchequer, the Maharashtra government has tightened the rules governing supplementary budgetary demands ahead of the winter session of the state legislature, restricting additional spending to urgent and essential requirements.The state finance department, in a circular issued on Wednesday, cited the state’s limited resources and called for stricter expenditure controls. “Considering the state’s limited resources, it is necessary to ensure proper planning of expenditure against budgetary allocations and to exercise control over expenditure provided for in the budget,” the circular states.The move assumes significance as the state government’s preliminary estimates suggest that its drought relief package alone could cost more than ₹45,000 crore. The substantial outlay threatens to put further pressure on the state’s finances, coming on top of the Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Shetkari Karjmukti Yojana 2026, the farm loan waiver scheme estimated to cost ₹36,585 crore. The relief burden currently amounts to more than ₹81,500 crore.The fiscal pressures come only months after chief minister Devendra Fadnavis presented a ₹7.69-lakh crore budget for 2026-27 in March. It also declared the state’s accumulated debt to be ₹11.03 lakh crore, with the debt-to-GSDP ratio touching 20.38%, its highest in recent years. In June, the state government tabled supplementary demands amounting to ₹97,706 crore, equivalent to 12.70% of the total budget outlay.Supplementary demands are sought to meet expenditure beyond provisions in the annual budget.Against this backdrop, the state finance department has made it clear that supplementary demands cannot be treated as an open-ended source of additional funding. Departments will have to demonstrate the urgency and necessity of their requests, with proposals subject to tighter scrutiny.“Proposals for supplementary demands should be considered only for highly urgent and essential committed expenditure, court-related matters, and expenditure relating to centrally sponsored schemes,” the circular states.The finance department has also prescribed thresholds for seeking additional allocations. For central and externally aided schemes, including centrally sponsored schemes, supplementary funds may be sought where no budgetary provision exists or where more than 50% of the existing allocation has been spent and additional funding is required.For other expenditure heads, departments may seek additional funds if more than 70% of the budgetary provision has been utilised, further funding is necessary and the shortfall cannot be met through reappropriation during the current financial year.“These conditions place the onus on departments to demonstrate that additional funding is essential and cannot be managed within existing allocations,” a senior finance official said.

title: Secretary tourism reviews functioning of directorate, key projects in Jammu | Hindustan Times
description: The presentation covered the progress of various tourism projects, development and promotion of emerging tourist destinations, adventure and sustainable tourism initiatives, organization of festivals and events
content: Secretary to the government, tourism department, J&K, Avny Lavasa (IAS) on Wednesday conducted a comprehensive review of the functioning of the directorate of tourism Jammu, taking stock of ongoing projects, proposed initiatives and various developmental and promotional activities being undertaken by the directorate.Welcoming the secretary tourism, Aijaz Qaiser (JKAS) joint director tourism, Jammu gave a detailed presentation highlighting the ongoing projects, upcoming initiatives, tourism infrastructure development, promotional activities and various proposals aimed at further strengthening the tourism sector in the Jammu region.The presentation covered the progress of various tourism projects, development and promotion of emerging tourist destinations, adventure and sustainable tourism initiatives, organization of festivals and events, as well as measures aimed at enhancing the overall tourist experience in the region. Upcoming initiatives for promotion of adventure tourism like Jammu marathon, paragliding accuracy cup and river rafting were discussed in detail.Secretary tourism Avny Lavasa reviewed the progress of various initiatives in detail and held extensive discussions with the officers on key areas requiring focused attention. She issued several directions for timely completion of ongoing projects, effective implementation of approved initiatives and further strengthening of tourism infrastructure and promotion across the Jammu region.She emphasised the need for close monitoring of projects, inter-departmental coordination and a result-oriented approach to ensure that tourism initiatives deliver tangible benefits to visitors as well as local communities.The secretary also stressed upon the officers to accord priority to the development of new tourism experiences and destinations, and directed the officers to institutionalise the annual initiatives and festivals of Jammu province so that they grow with each passing year thereby enriching the experience to participants in particular and public in general.

title: Cong to raise Jhota murder in House, seek CM’s resignation, says Bajwa | Hindustan Times
description: Bajwa, who met the deceased activist’s family, accused the Bhagwant Mann-led Punjab government of failing to curb narcotics trafficking and gangster activities, which he said had worsened the law-and-order situation in the state
content: Leader of Opposition in the Punjab assembly Partap Singh Bajwa on Wednesday said the Congress would raise the issue of the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh alias Jhota in the assembly session beginning Thursday.Bajwa, who met the deceased activist’s family, accused the Bhagwant Mann-led Punjab government of failing to curb narcotics trafficking and gangster activities, which he said had worsened the law-and-order situation in the state.“Law and order is a key issue as people from all walks of life feel unsafe. We will demand the resignation of the chief minister over Jhota’s murder as the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has failed on all fronts,” Bajwa said.He also questioned the BJP-led Union government’s failure to check drug trafficking with the help of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and other central agencies.Central probe a win for Punjab’s people: Giani HarpreetShiromani Akali Dal (Punar-Surjit) president Giani Harpreet Singh on Wednesday described the decision to hand over the murder case to the CBI as a victory for the family’s perseverance and the collective struggle of Punjab’s people.In a press statement, he said the resolve shown by Jhota’s family, particularly his elderly father, and the unity demonstrated by the people had compelled the government to heed their demand. “The development demonstrates that sustained public pressure can force the government to act,” he said.He called for turning Jhota’s anti-drug campaign into a mass movement at the village level, advocating a social boycott of drug traffickers and their complete isolation within the communities.

title: Neither gave nor took  ₹500 crore: Shinde seeks probe into Jarange’s allegations | Mumbai news
description: In response, Jarange-Patil said he would present evidence supporting his allegations at a press conference on Thursday  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde on Wednesday denied the ₹500-crore bribery allegations made against him by Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange-Patil, and sought an investigation into the matter. In response, Jarange-Patil said he would present evidence supporting his allegations at a press conference on Thursday.Jarange-Patil had sparked a political row while addressing a Dussehra rally in Beed on Tuesday, when he claimed that the Shiv Sena chief had told a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader that he had paid the activist ₹500 crore to pacify him during his agitation for Maratha reservation two years ago.Shinde responded to the allegations while speaking to the media in Delhi on Wednesday. “I have neither given nor taken ₹500 crore. Jarange-Patil must verify facts and then talk. He must give proof to investigative agencies, and this must be probed. Doodh ka doodh aur paani ka paani hona chahiye (The truth should come out). All of Maharashtra knows me and my work.”The former chief minister, who is also a Maratha, urged Jarange-Patil to continue working for the community and not engage in politics. “As chief minister, I had helped the Maratha community by giving them concessions and jobs. In the last 60 years, many CMs could not do anything [for Marathas]; I have given them reservation, and it is still in place. I have given justice to Marathas. Manoj Jarange-Patil must work for the community and not make it a political platform,” he said.Meanwhile, Jarange-Patil told reporters that he would hold a press conference on Thursday to present evidence supporting his allegations.As the activist’s allegations kicked up a political storm, Shiv Sena (UBT) lashed out at the Shiv Sena, with Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut saying that Shinde should have addressed the matter during his Dussehra rally on Tuesday, but instead kept talking about the Thackerays.“Who is the BJP leader who gave ₹500 crore to silence the Maratha agitation? The Enforcement Directorate should investigate it, and Eknath Shinde must get a summons. Why is [chief minister] Devendra Fadnavis quiet now? Jarange-Patil says he has proof. I think he never lies and speaks like a Shiv Sainik. Fadnavis must give this information [about the alleged bribe] to the ED and the Economic Offences Wing,” said Raut.Shiv Sena leaders have slammed Jarange-Patil and defended their party chief. At the party’s Dussehra rally, Sena leader Ramdas Kadam had said: “If you want to destroy Eknath Shinde, Marathas won’t spare you. You claim that you are on a hunger strike, but eat in the bathroom. Should we do an inquiry on how you have amassed wealth and roam around in expensive cars? You should be happy that Eknath Shinde gave reservation to Marathas. Eknath Shinde is worshipped by Marathas. If you speak ill of him, Maharashtra won’t tolerate it.”

title: Meet the retired cop who won’t stop finding missing persons | Mumbai news
description: Though he retired in February 2025, Rajesh Pandey has reunited 25 missing people with their families since then  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: Rajesh Pandey, a 60-year-old retired Mumbai police constable, was enjoying a cup of tea with his wife on the afternoon of October 8 when his phone rang. On the other end was a distraught doctor from Satara, Rajendra Mane, who told Pandey that his 22-year-old nephew, Dhanraj, had been missing since August 9.Pandey put down his cup and asked Mane to send him everything he knew about Dhanraj: his photograph, height, weight, clothes he was last seen wearing, medical details, interests and habits. Within minutes, he had circulated the information across nearly 1,000 WhatsApp groups related to finding missing persons. These groups comprise police officers, NGOs and other organisations, and civil society members from across the country.Three days later, Pandey received a call from the Bengaluru police informing him that Dhanraj had been spotted in the city. The same day, he boarded a train to Bengaluru with Mane. However, upon reaching the city, they learned that Dhanraj had later been spotted in Pondicherry. Undeterred, Pandey set off again the following day.The search continues, but Pandey is no stranger to such pursuits. Though he retired in February 2025, he has reunited 25 missing people with their families since then. He has taken neither a family vacation nor a day off during this period.“I get immense satisfaction when I see someone smile after reuniting with a lost loved one. That alone is my fee,” said Pandey, who lives in a 160-sq-ft home in the Naigaon police quarters in Dadar with his wife and two sons. Retirement has allowed him to devote himself entirely to tracing missing people, particularly children. “I travel at my expense to follow a lead or tag along with the police team when I get a tip-off,” he said.During his 32 years in uniform, Pandey helped solve nearly 3,000 missing-person cases. His methods have even acquired a name within the Mumbai police: the “Pandey Module”. For harrowed families desperately searching for loved ones, he remains the go-to man. His tenacity and skill in reuniting missing persons with their families remain unmatched, his former colleagues say.For Pandey, this remains his mission, which he now pursues without his khaki uniform and the moustache that once complemented it.Operation MuskaanPandey joined the Mumbai police in 1992 after his father’s death, hoping to support his four younger sisters. In 2011, while posted at Santacruz police station, he helped a woman trace her kidnapped child to her estranged husband. The experience, he said, sparked his passion for finding missing people.Since then, he has left no stone unturned and has not left any missing-person case pending throughout his career. Taking note of his commitment and style, in 2016, then Mumbai police commissioner Datta Padsalgikar launched Operation Muskan, an initiative to trace and rescue missing and trafficked children. According to Padsalgikar, the initiative, with Pandey’s help, traced 2,165 of 2,182 missing minors in 2025.Pandey has also been invited by various commissionerates to share his expertise—the Pandey Module—with young officers.“He is committed, and his experience helps and guides us,” said Rakesh Kalasagar, commissioner of Government Railway Police (GRP) Mumbai. “Six months ago, I had invited Pandey to share his experience and method of tracing missing people with my subordinates and new recruits to understand how to go about sensitive cases of missing children. His network across the country has helped us a lot.”Police commissionerates in Thane and Mira-Bhayander-Vasai-Virar, along with the Palghar district administration, have also sought his guidance.The Pandey ModuleAt the heart of Pandey’s approach is an extensive network of unlikely informants: tailors, cleaning staff at guest houses and hotels, bar employees, ashram workers and NGO volunteers. He doesn’t just rely on technology; he has a proven method that delivers results.“I find out every little detail about the missing person, along with his interests or even things that might seem unimportant to the family, like their hobbies, which might give me a lead,” he said.In April this year, Nitin Cheda, a 22-year-old businessman from Lokhandwala in Andheri West, disappeared after suffering heavy business losses. When the police search, which spanned several days, hit a dead end, Cheda’s brother contacted Pandey.Examining Cheda’s call records, Pandey noticed calls to a business directory service. He visited its Malad office and discovered that Cheda had enquired about “cheap hotels” in Panaji, Goa, hours before disappearing.Pandey travelled to Goa, rented a two-wheeler and spent three days searching with local police before spotting Cheda at Baga beach. He summoned Cheda’s brother to Goa, counselled the young man about repaying his loans, and urged him to return to his family.Another case took him to Varanasi.In June 2025, Pandey received a call from a desperate mother who had been looking for her four-year-old daughter since the child went missing from the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), one of India’s busiest railway stations, on May 20. He scanned through hours of CCTV footage and spotted a man walking with the child before they disappeared into the crowd.The trail eventually led Pandey to Varanasi, where a journalist told him about a girl speaking in Marathi at a Child Welfare Committee (CWC) centre. The child was reunited with her family.
