Pandey later learnt that the alerts he had circulated had apparently prompted the abductor to abandon her at Varanasi station, where she was rescued.Pandey’s phone is now crowded with two kinds of messages: photos of missing people from various WhatsApp groups, and messages from people thanking him for finding a lost loved one.His resolve remains steadfast, and his retirement has changed little. “I will continue this quest till my last breath,” he said.

title: Bumper paddy yield a procurement challenge in Punjab | Hindustan Times
description: Production of non-basmati paddy may exceed 220 lakh tonnes this season against 180-lakh tonne quota fixed by Centre
content: ChandigarhPunjab is heading towards a challenging paddy procurement season, with the state’s expected production likely to exceed the procurement quota of 180 lakh tonne fixed by the Union ministry of consumer affairs, food and public distribution.The state’s total non-basmati paddy production — which is procured by government agencies for the public distribution system — is expected to exceed 220 lakh tonnes this season. Given the historical trend of around 90% of the total production reaching mandis for procurement, the quantity arriving in the markets could surpass the Centre’s approved quota, putting pressure on the state’s procurement machinery and finances.“The procurement scenario seems tougher this season, as we have been signalled by the Union ministry that the crop beyond the defined quota will not be accepted. We hope to stay within the limits; otherwise, we will seek an extension,” a senior official in the Punjab food and civil supplies department said.Haryana experience raises concernsThe state government’s concerns have been heightened by the Centre’s handling of excess paddy procurement in Haryana during the previous season. Against a quota of 36 lakh tonnes, Haryana procured 62 lakh tonnes in 2025, exceeding its approved limit by 26 lakh tonnes. The Centre’s refusal to accept the additional quantity has served as a warning for Punjab, which is now preparing to manage a potentially similar situation.For the current season, Haryana has been allocated a procurement quota of 59 lakh tonnes.Punjab officials believe the Centre’s approach towards Haryana indicates that exceeding the approved procurement limit could create serious complications for the state.Initially, the Centre had fixed Punjab’s procurement target at 156 lakh tonnes, equivalent to the quantity procured during the previous season. Following representations by the state government, the Centre considered the average procurement over three years and revised the target to 171 lakh tonnes.The state food department subsequently sought a further increase, following which Punjab was permitted to procure 180 lakh tonnes.The state may have to approach the Centre again if the actual procurement exceeds the sanctioned limit. Such a request could involve revising the procurement quota and increasing the financial arrangements required to purchase the additional grain at the minimum support price (MSP).Paddy yield rises by nearly 9 quintals per hectare“According to the results of crop-cutting experiments, the production is 67.35 quintals against last season’s production of 58.6 quintals per hectare. We are expecting a bumper harvest of 220 lakh tonnes or maybe more,” Punjab agriculture director Gurjeet Singh Brar said.Punjab cultivated paddy over 32.76 lakh hectares during the current kharif season. Of this, approximately 6.5 lakh hectares were under premium basmati varieties, which are not procured by government agencies for the public distribution system. Consequently, around 26.25 lakh hectares fall under the non-basmati paddy area generally covered by government procurement at the MSP.Favourable factors for high yieldExplaining the increase in paddy production, former Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) vice-chancellor BS Dhillon said Punjab could witness higher crop output even during drought conditions because of several favourable factors.According to Dhillon, increased sunshine, reduced incidence of diseases, lower nutrient leaching and the availability of adequate irrigation water can contribute to higher yields despite deficient rainfall. He said the authorities would have to determine how best to procure and manage the additional grain generated by the bumper crop.PAU director of extension Makhan Singh Bhullar said increased paddy production creates additional challenges for the government.Existing rice stocks add to storage woesPunjab’s procurement concerns extend beyond the immediate challenge of purchasing the current crop. The state’s godowns already hold approximately 150 lakh tonnes of rice from the previous three seasons.With the current season’s procurement expected to generate at least another 120 lakh tonnes of rice, the total stock could increase substantially, adding to the pressure on storage facilities and grain management arrangements.Punjab has cash credit limit of ₹42,786 crTo facilitate procurement, Punjab has been sanctioned a cash credit limit (CCL) of ₹42,786.68 crore to purchase 180 lakh tonnes of paddy, pay farmers the MSP of ₹2,441 per quintal and meet administrative expenses.However, if arrivals exceed the approved procurement quantity, the state may have to seek an increase in the CCL to finance the purchase of additional paddy.According to Varinder Sharma, director of the Punjab food and civil supplies department, they have received an assessment from the agriculture department indicating that arrivals would remain within the approved limit, and arrangements were made accordingly.“We are taking all caution so that nothing from outside the state is allowed in Punjab mandis and the state farmers are able to sell their produce,” Sharma said.

title: Sangrur crash: Protest ends after govt assures  ₹10 lakh compensation, plots | Hindustan Times
description: Deputy commissioner Punamdeep Kaur said the administration had held a meeting with the committee and conveyed that their demands have been accepted by the government
content: The families of the victims and the members of the action committee seeking justice for eight workers killed in the October 18 crash ended their protest on Wednesday, following assurances from the administration that their demands would be met.The protesters have been demanding enhanced compensation for the families of the deceased and the injured in the mishap. Eight workers, including six women, were killed and 12 others sustained injuries after a car ran them over on a stretch of the Lehragaga-Jakhal road in Sangrur on Sunday. The workers were enrolled under the Viksit Bharat Guarantee Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin scheme.Deputy commissioner Punamdeep Kaur said the administration had held a meeting with the committee and conveyed that their demands have been accepted by the government.“The state has agreed to increase the compensation from ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh for the family of each deceased worker and for those who sustained serious injuries. Those with minor injuries will be given ₹2 lakh and their entire treatment will be provided free of cost,” the DC said, adding that the demand for 5-marla plots had also been accepted.“The sarpanch will pass a resolution to complete the process and fulfil the demand,” she added.Additional deputy commissioner (development) Sukhchain Singh Papra said that family members of the deceased would be employed as daily wagers in the forest department, and the process had been initiated.Bikker Singh, president of the action committee, confirmed the development and said 5-marla plots would be allotted to the families of both the deceased and injured. “The administration has also assured us that steps will be taken for the security and well-being of workers,” he said.The incident took place near Alisher village, where a group of more than 20 workers enrolled under VB-GRAMG were engaged in work. Some of them were sitting along the road when a speeding car mowed them down, police said.The driver of the Chevrolet Magnum car, identified as Pargat Singh, a resident of Raidhrana village, was arrested hours after the incident.An FIR under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 117(2) (voluntarily causing grievous hurt), and 324(4) (mischief causing property damage) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has been registered against the accused.Meanwhile, Jalandhar MP and former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi also met the protesters and assured them of his support.Taking a jibe at the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Channi said, “The rise in gangsterism and drug abuse has made life difficult for the common man.”

title: HC orders auction of five art works disputed by Mafatlal family | Mumbai news
description: MUMBAI: The Bombay High Court has ordered the auction of five paintings owned by Mafatlal Dyes and Chemicals Limited (MDCL), which went under liquidation in 2010  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: The Bombay High Court has ordered the auction of five paintings owned by Mafatlal Dyes and Chemicals Limited (MDCL), which went under liquidation in 2010. It held that the paintings, including works by MF Husain and FN Souza, belonged to the company and not members of the Mafatlal family including Atulya Mafatlal and his former wife Sheetal, who staked their claim to the art works.The paintings – two art works by MF Husain and one each by FN Souza, Biren De and Jogen Chowdhury – were among 44 caught in a legal battle between members of the business family including socialite Sheetal Mafatlal, her former husband Atulya, and Atulya’s brother Ajay, who was Aparna prior to gender reassignment.Unable to pay its debts, MDCL went into liquidation in 2010. To recover the company’s dues, the official liquidator filed three reports relating to the 44 paintings seized by the Mumbai Police in January 2014 following allegations of theft and other criminal offences made against each other by members of the Mafatlal family.The paintings were placed under the care of the Sir JJ School of Art by the company court. While family members squabbled over their ownership, five paintings were identified by the police as belonging to MDCL.On Wednesday, the high court noted that the company’s promoters were engaged in a three-way fight among Atulya, son of the late Yogindra Mafatlal, his brother Ajay, and Sheetal. Another sibling, Gayatri Jhaveri, who made her claims through Ajay and her parents, was also in the fray. The question before the court was whether the five paintings identified by the police belonged to MDCL and could be used to recover dues to its creditors, or whether they belonged to one of the feuding family members.A single-judge bench of Justice Somasekhar Sundaresan said, “In the teeth of the asset register, the purchase vouchers and the affidavits of the Mumbai Police, which make a clearly reasonable case for the (five) identified paintings to belong to the company, Sheetal and Atulya have chosen not to lead evidence and their conduct calls for adverse inference.”The paintings had been at the centre of a family dispute since August 2011, when Atulya’s daughter Marushka filed a police complaint against her stepmother Sheetal accusing her of stealing 35 paintings and moving them out of the Mafatlal bungalow. Sheetal, on the other hand, filed a complaint of dowry harassment, matrimonial cruelty and domestic violence against Marushka, Atulya and other members of the Mafatlal family.The police later found ten paintings in the house of Sheetal’s friend Yasmin Valibhoy, who she later fell out with. Yasmin had also questioned Sheetal’s claim to ownership of the paintings before the court.The family was referred to a mediator by the high court and they filed consent terms and arrived at a settlement in 2012. Sheetal relied on these consent terms to claim that she was allowed to retain possession of the paintings. She claimed that Atulya, Ajay and Marushka had consented not to claim them.The court, however, noted that the consent terms were filed with regard to 35 paintings that were the subject of Marushka’s complaint. Justice Sundaresan noted that in her statement to the police Sheetal had said she had moved 47 paintings and two artefacts out of the Mafatlal home.He said the consent terms did not cover all 44 paintings and “this, in no manner, could be dispositive of whether the company did or did not own the subject paintings and cannot bind the official liquidator, more so bearing in mind the consent terms were among members of the promoter family under whose watch the company had to move to liquidation,” the judge observed.“If the members of the Mafatlal family kept possession of paintings paid for by the company in the Mafatlal Bungalow and later fought over the said paintings, trading criminal charges, to eventually settle their fight among themselves, the consent terms cannot add weight to the question of whether the paintings belonged to the company or to anyone else,” the judge said.However, in October 2012, after the consent terms were filed, there was another twist. Sheetal moved a magistrate’s court seeking the return of 31 seized paintings. When they were handed over to her, she alleged the originals had been replaced by fakes and a fresh round of criminal proceedings began. She filed an FIR against Yasmin and two others which was later transferred to the CID.Yasmin told the Mumbai police that according to the asset register of the MDCL, the company owned the paintings. In January 2014, the CID found the 44 paintings in a premises rented by Sheetal in Princess Street. The police then filed a closure report in the case. When Sheetal challenged the closure report in the high court, it was dismissed in 2019 and the court permitted the police to prosecute her for making false statements. The Supreme Court too granted her no relief.The court said Sheetal contended that all paintings belonged to her. Gayatri claimed to be entitled to the remaining paintings and conceded that the five identified paintings belong to the liquidation estate of the company. Yasmin, who had fallen out with Sheetal, was interested in cross-examining Sheetal to prove her wrong.“Suffice it to say, none of the private parties has brought forth positive evidence to prove title,” Justice Sundaresan said. “There is nothing in Sheetal’s affidavit that asserts title. She has not adduced a single instrument even circumstantially in support of her title to the subject paintings,” the judge added.“What is crystal clear is that neither Sheetal nor any of the members of the Mafatlal family who signed the consent terms with her, has led any evidence as to title to the subject paintings in court. These parties may have engaged in a mutual dispute and arrived at consent terms among themselves, but how they can claim title to the subject paintings is a subject on which they present nothing in evidence,” the judge remarked

title: 24 ‘X’ accounts get Mumbai police notice to remove documentary on Modi, Adani | Mumbai news
description: The controversial documentary accuses Prime Minister Narendra Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani of corruption, collusion, and corporate cronyism.  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: The Mumbai police issued a notice to X (formerly Twitter) on October 18 to review 24 of its account holders and take appropriate action for sharing a Sabeer Bhatia documentary titled ‘How Adani and Modi stole India’, terming the content false and misleading. The platform subsequently forwarded the notice to the account holders for their response.The controversial documentary accuses Prime Minister Narendra Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani of corruption, collusion, and corporate cronyism. It gained attention after the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued takedown directives to platforms such as YouTube and Meta following court orders.The notice issued by the Mumbai police stated that the West Cyber police, Crime Branch and CID received a complaint alleging that multiple X accounts published and disseminated highly objectionable content targeting a well-known company. This content allegedly lacked any apparent factual or lawful basis, causing serious and continuing harm to the company’s reputation.It further stated that publishing and disseminating objectionable, false, misleading, and disparaging statements violates X’s rules and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) sections 352 and 356.Mumbai police requested X to urgently review the objectionable tweets posted through multiple handles and take appropriate action to remove or disable access to the content in accordance with applicable law and the platform’s policies.Meanwhile, Sabeer Bhatia, an Indian-American entrepreneur who co-founded the first free web-based email service, Hotmail.com (now Outlook.com) and who directed and uploaded the documentary in question, posted on X that he had deleted the video. A few X account holders also deleted the video while others posted the notice, claiming injustice.

title: Core sector growth rises to 7.9%, highest in new series | India News
description: Core sector industries output, as measured by the Index of Core Industries (ICI) stood at 7.9% in September, up from 5.9% in August, according to data released by Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Wednesday. September output was the highest growth in the new ICI series, which has 2022-23 as its base year. | India News
content: Core sector industries output, as measured by the Index of Core Industries (ICI) stood at 7.9% in September, up from 5.9% in August, according to data released by Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Wednesday. September output was the highest growth in the new ICI series, which has 2022-23 as its base year.Out of the nine industries in the index, six recorded expansion while the rest contracted. The industries that drove ICI growth were iron ore, electricity, coal, and refinery products. Iron ore output picked up pace in September, growing by 18.4% after rising by 5.5% in August. Since January this year, the sector has recorded double-digit growth in every month except February and August. Electricity, which has the highest weight of 31% in the index, grew by 11.4%, lower than the 13.2% recorded in the previous month. Coal output expanded by 10.7%, after contracting by 3.8% in the previous month. Refinery products, with the second-highest weight at 23%, also recorded a double-digit growth of 10.3% in September, compared with 5.6% in August. Cement and steel output grew by 4.9% and 9.8%, respectively.“Coal and iron ore output witnessed a meaningful pickup in their YoY growth rates in September 2026 compared to August 2026; while this was aided by a low base, the sequential uptick in coal was quite strong, amid low stocks at power plants,” said Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA Ltd. “Growth in electricity generation eased somewhat to 11.4% in September 2026 from 13.1% in August 2026, albeit remaining quite strong, as the monsoon deficit supported demand in the month,” Nayar added.The sub-sectors that contracted in August were fertilisers, natural gas and crude oil. Fertilisers output saw the deepest contraction of 11.7% in the index in August, though it has improved from 12.4% contraction observed in last month. Natural gas output contracted by 4.6%, followed by crude oil which contracted 1.4%. The contractions in both natural gas and crude oil output narrowed compared to August. The contraction in these three industries would likely be because of shortage of raw materials because of ongoing West-Asia war, as India imports these raw materials. To be sure, crude oil and natural gas output remained negative even before the war started. Out of the 30-month data available from April 2024 in the new series, crude oil and natural gas were in contraction in 28 and 27 months, respectively. While fertilisers output remained in contraction for only twelve months.The overall index recorded cumulative growth of 5.1% in the current fiscal year (April-September), up from 2.5% in the same period of the previous year.

title: Energy ties in focus as Ambani hosts Marco Rubio at Jamnagar | India News
description: Officials said Rubio was expected to discuss Venezuelan crude and RIL’s proposed refinery project in the US during the visit. | India News
content: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Wednesday toured Reliance Industries Ltd’s (RIL) complex at Jamnagar in Gujarat, home to the world’s largest single-site oil refinery, after telling reporters earlier in the day that conversations between US authorities and the conglomerate were aimed at identifying opportunities to partner and work together in energy.RIL chairman and managing director Mukesh Ambani and executive director Anant Ambani hosted Rubio, who also visited the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex and Vantara, the company’s animal rescue and conservation centre, and is staying overnight at the RIL township near Jamnagar. US ambassador to India Sergio Gor accompanied him.Officials said Rubio was expected to discuss Venezuelan crude and RIL’s proposed refinery project in the US during the visit. The US State Department said in a post on X that Rubio’s second visit to India this year, focused on Mumbai and Jamnagar, underscored Washington’s commitment to commercial investment, energy cooperation and the strategic partnership between the two countries. Before heading to Gujarat, Rubio met Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran in Mumbai. There were no formal readouts from the US side on these meetings.Asked by reporters before the visit whether he was seeking an investment commitment from Reliance or an agreement to refine more Venezuelan crude, Rubio said he aimed to have a “broader discussion about their presence globally at a time in which energy is featuring prominently in many of the geopolitical decisions that are being made”.Describing Reliance as a prominent energy company with a large investment in the US, he said: “This is a company…that has the capability to refine the heavy crude that’s produced in the western hemisphere, including from Venezuela…I think through our conversations, we’ll hopefully identify other opportunities to partner and work together.”On Tuesday, Rubio had described India as a “refining superpower” while speaking to reporters in Mumbai, and said RIL could process larger volumes of Venezuelan crude as the country’s oil production increased. “We will talk with Reliance about refining more Venezuelan crude,” he said.Rubio also met external affairs minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai on Tuesday and said the two countries were “very, very close” to finalising a bilateral trade deal.According to an RIL statement, the visitors toured the refinery, which can process 1.4 million barrels of crude a day and has a complexity index of 21.1, which the company describes as the world’s highest and which allows it to process even the heaviest crude oils.“The visit included wide-ranging discussions on the global energy landscape and opportunities for commercial partnerships across conventional and new energy,” the statement said. “The exchange covered reliable and affordable energy supplies, technological advances, resilient supply chains and the investment required to meet growing demand.”The visit comes as the Trump administration grapples with high diesel prices ahead of the US midterm elections on November 3. Days before Rubio’s visit, President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs under the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a week after announcing a deal with Russia to release roughly 5 million tonnes of Russian diesel onto the world market.Reliance has also backed the construction of a refinery at the Port of Brownsville in Texas, the first major new oil refinery in the US in about 50 years, according to Trump who made an announcement in March, describing it as a “historic $300 billion dollar deal” — a reference to its projected economic value.Gor highlighted the growth in energy trade between the two countries in a post on X. “Over the past year, India’s imports of US LPG have surged from under 10% to 67%, making the United States India’s largest LPG supplier,” he said, also describing RIL’s investment in the Texas refinery as an opportunity to expand American energy production and create jobs.India’s imports of Venezuelan crude averaged 190,000 barrels a day in 2026, with about 80% of the volumes delivered to Sikka port, which serves the Jamnagar refinery, according to an S&P Global Commodity Insights report. Kpler estimates cited by Bloomberg earlier this month projected India’s Venezuelan crude imports at 465,000 barrels a day in October, up from 196,000 barrels a day in September.

title: 30% of India’s croplands technically suitable for solar agrovoltaics: Pralhad Joshi | India News
description: Joshi also said the new PM-Kusum 2.0 includes a dedicated agrivoltaics component, with immense potential to expand India’s solar capacity while substantially benefiting farmers. | India News
content: An estimated 47.5 million hectares, or approximately 30%, of India’s 160 million hectares of cropland should be technically suitable for agrivoltaics—where solar panels are installed directly above existing farms, Union minister for new and renewable energy (MNRE) Pralhad Joshi said on Wednesday at the inauguration of the 7th edition of the AgriVoltaics World Conference (AWC) 2026 in Delhi’s Bharat Mandapam.Joshi also said the new PM-Kusum 2.0 includes a dedicated agrivoltaics component, with immense potential to expand India’s solar capacity while substantially benefiting farmers.“The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) has estimated 47.5 million hectares, or approximately 30% of India’s 160 million hectares of cropland, is technically suitable for agrivoltaics. One deployment scenario covering 16 million hectares estimates annual electricity generation of 12,775 TWh, potentially comparable to or exceeding India’s projected electricity demand of 5,250–10,020 TWh by 2050,” said Joshi, stating one of the world’s most ambitious agrivoltaic programmes would be launched under the next phase of PM-Kusum.“Elevated and tilted structures could make agrivoltaic plants 25–30% more expensive than conventional ground-mounted solar installations, and the government aims to bridge this cost gap by supporting AgriPV capacity creation,” the minister added.The conference was inaugurated alongside the agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan too, who said any AgriPV policy must be designed to meet the practical requirements of India’s small and marginal farmers, who constitute more than 85% of the farming community. Currently, coverage of ground-mounted solar panels is part of the existing PM Kusum scheme, which provides subsidies to farmers for both ground-mounted panels and solar pumps.“The average landholding in the country is only 0.96 hectares. Thus, agrivoltaics models must allow farmers to continue cultivation instead of replacing farming with solar power generation,” Chouhan said.The conference also saw the launch of a Decision-Making Tool developed by the India Agrivoltaics Alliance (IAA) – which allows farmers to assess the AgriPV potential of their land and the cost required for installation. An AgriPV policy handbook was also launched, which officials said should provide a base for further deliberations on the final policy. “The three-day conference will allow suggestions and further ideas to be incorporated into the final policy planned,” a senior official said.The conference has brought together over 1200 delegates, including international experts, policymakers, researchers, industry leaders, innovators, start-ups and development partners.

title: Punjab to crack down on illegal Pregabalin sales, says Dr Balbir | Hindustan Times
description: The minister said the health department was keeping a close watch on around 35,000 chemist shops across the state to check the alleged over-the-counter sale of Pregabalin, a prescription medicine
content: Amid growing concerns over the misuse of the habit-forming drug, Pregabalin, health minister Dr Balbir Singh on Wednesday warned that action would be taken against pharmacies found violating prescription and sale regulations.The minister said the health department was keeping a close watch on around 35,000 chemist shops across the state to check the alleged over-the-counter sale of Pregabalin, a prescription medicine.“Pregabalin is a drug for patients with diabetes, or those who require pain relief. It is an excellent lifesaving drug. The misuse of the drug has earned it a bad name. The majority of chemists follow the law, but some are violating the rules. We will identify them and take action against them,” the minister said.He also directed the drug wing of the Food and Drug Administration to ensure regular inspections with the assistance of the police so that no medicine dealer operated without a valid licence or sold life-saving medicines without a doctor’s prescription.Pregabalin is a prescription-only medication for the treatment of nerve pain and seizures in certain adults. Doctors may also recommend it for treating anxiety.The minister said the Union government had included Pregabalin under Schedule H1 of the Drugs Rules, 1945, on May 13, 2026. The new provision is scheduled to come into effect on November 12.Last year, the Punjab government had banned the sale and stocking of Pregabalin tablets with a strength exceeding 75mg.The habit-forming medicine continues to find favour among drug users because it is inexpensive, readily available and can be used to get high, relieve anxiety and intensify the effects of heroin, experts said.Data accessed by HT shows that, between April 1, 2025, and August 31, 2026, Pregabalin-containing formulations worth ₹2 crore were seized from 71 firms for violations of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the Drugs Rules, 1945. The licences of 15 firms were cancelled, 42 firms were suspended, and court proceedings were initiated in four cases, officials said.A recent study by the Government Medical College (GMC), Patiala, titled “A Hospital Multicentric Observational Study Across Different Regions of Punjab and the Union Territory of Chandigarh”, flagged high use of the drug among younger patients, particularly those who had begun using substances at an early age.Dr Rohit Garg, professor in the department of psychiatry at GMC, Patiala, said many users initially turned to Pregabalin as an alternative to heroin but eventually became dependent on both substances.“Most addicts started taking the tablets as an alternative to chitta (heroin). However, they are now addicted to both chitta and Pregabalin. We see drug addicts taking 10-15 tablets every day,” he said.He added that no medication has been specifically approved for Pregabalin dependence, unlike opioid dependence, for which drugs such as buprenorphine or methadone are used.

title: Parliament’s Central, Library halls gear up to host 12th BRICS forum next week | India News
description: The event will discuss key issues such as ethical digital transformation, global governance reform and parliamentary diplomacy and feature cultural snapshots from different states and local cuisine. | India News
content: Two iconic parts of the Parliament complex—the Central Hall and the Library Hall (formerly the Chamber of Princes)—are being decked up to host the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum next week, officials said. The event will discuss key issues such as ethical digital transformation, global governance reform and parliamentary diplomacy and feature cultural snapshots from different states and local cuisine.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has planned various programmes and a Culture Bazar in the Parliament complex. Craftsmen and artisans from different states, including Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, will display their works for the BRICS’ guests, according to an official. “Banquets would be hosted by Birla and Vice President CP Radhakrishnan, and guests will be given guided tours of the Parliament complex, New Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur,” a senior official told HT.The Central Hall will be the venue of the forum on October 26 and 27. The Library Hall of the Chamber of Princes, which was used as a reading room for MPs, would be used for an international event for the first time.“After Parliament shifted to the new building, the Library Hall lost its purpose. Now it is being refurbished for the BRICS Speakers’ Summit,” said a second official.Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will attend the event for an interaction with delegates.Eleven countries, including India, China, Russia and Brazil, are members of the BRICS. Another 10 countries, including Belarus, Malaysia and Uzbekistan, are partners of this global alliance. A senior official said that all 21 countries are expected to attend the event.Speaker Birla will chair the inaugural session and also deliver the valedictory speech. His office has also lined up bilateral meetings between Birla and his counterparts. Union ministers, MPs, state-level presiding officers and global parliamentary leaders are also set to attend the programme.The themes centre around “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development, featuring high-level sessions on institutional resilience, ethical AI/digital transformation, global governance reform, sustainability, parliamentary diplomacy, and capacity-building.The forum is expected to adopt a joint declaration covering all these issues.

title: Weak web IDs and a decade-old PHP flaw. The week the internet's plumbing showed its cracks | HT Explainers
description: A Bengaluru firm's guessable keys and critical flaws in the code behind much of the web have shown how much rests on parts few people check. | HT Explainers
content: Within hours of each other, serious cracks were exposed in two pieces of the internet's hidden plumbing. A researcher found that eMudhra, a Bengaluru-based certificate authority, had made the keys behind eight of its security certificates so weak that one of them was simply the number 4. Then came the revelation from developers of PHP, the programming language behind a large share of the world's websites, who disclosed two critical flaws. Finland and a number of government agencies across the world public-facing internet services offline as a precaution.Most people never think about either. Few know which company vouches for the websites they visit, or what language those sites run on, and that invisibility makes both problems harder to fix.eMudhra and the identity cardsEvery website whose address begins with "https" carries a certificate, a digital identity card that lets a browser confirm the site is genuine before it shows a padlock. Several dozen certificate authorities issue these cards, and any one of them can vouch for any website in the world.The keys eMudhra used to sign its cards should each have been a random number about 116 digits long. They were 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237, small enough for a computer to find by counting. Anyone who worked them out could have forged an identity card for any website, and Mozilla, which makes the Firefox browser, said "the impact of this incident could not be higher". Browsers were protected because they accept a certificate only if it appears in public logs, where a forgery would have been spotted. Google, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft also blocked the certificates within days. Apps, routers and other devices that skip those checks will keep trusting the keys until someone updates them.PHP, the software under much of the webPHP runs on web servers, the computers that host websites, and assembles each page at the moment a visitor asks for it. Wiz, the Alphabet-owned security company that found the flaws, estimates the problems affect around 70% of the internet."PHP is everywhere," the security company Huntress wrote. "It quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood."Both flaws scored 9.2 on CVSS, the industry's 10-point scale for how dangerous a software bug is. The EU's cybersecurity response team, CERT-EU, said that score pointed to a risk of remote code execution without any login. In plain terms, an attacker anywhere on the internet might be able to make a vulnerable server run commands of their choosing. The web host GoDaddy said that could mean stolen data, defaced websites or a complete takeover of the server. CERT-EU and Australia's cybersecurity agency said every version of PHP from version 5 onward could be affected, though PHP had not said which versions were vulnerable.Also read: The two kinds of AI attacker CERT-In flagged, and the weaknesses they exploitedWhy governments pulled the plugCERT-EU told organisations that could not patch immediately to consider taking affected sites offline, and Britain's National Cyber Security Centre gave similar advice. Some governments did not wait. Finland took all its public-facing internet services offline, and Dutch national and local government sites went down. According to Dutch news agency ANP, more than 100 Dutch municipalities, provinces and water boards were affected because they use a service from one software supplier, Notubiz. The universities of Vienna and Freiburg pulled their sites too.Going offline is the bluntest protection available.The race after the patchPHP's developers released four patches on Wednesday and told users to update immediately. A published patch can also help attackers work out what was broken, and security experts warned they would move quickly against servers that had not yet been fixed.That race may already be under way. Dane Knecht, chief technology officer of the web security company Cloudflare, wrote on X that Cloudflare was "seeing early attacks emerging" and had added protections for customers, which he called a "STOPGAP only". Australia's cybersecurity agency said it was "currently not aware of active exploitation".Fixing PHP takes deliberate effort. Wordfence, which makes a popular WordPress security plugin, warned that WordPress's automatic updates would not apply the fix, because PHP is installed on the server underneath. Site owners need to find out who updates PHP for them, whether that is a hosting company, a developer or themselves.A decade-old flaw, found by AIWiz said it found the flaws with several AI tools, working with OpenAI and the security firm Calif, and estimated that they had gone undetected for more than a decade. "With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work," it said.The PHP Foundation, which oversees the language, said a researcher had spotted the first signs of one flaw in 2024, but the issue was "theorized, but no concrete vectors were found". It called the delay "a structural failure".Also read: Cyberattack targets refrigerators at French supermarkets: Why nothing is un-hackableWhat the two flaws have in commonBoth affect parts of the internet that users never see and never chose. eMudhra's keys could have been used to impersonate websites that had never been its customers. PHP is buried in so much software that, as Huntress put it, "the number of places you have to go looking to identify vulnerable PHP versions gets very big, very fast".Both flaws stayed hidden for a long time: 18 months in eMudhra's case, and more than a decade in PHP's by Wiz's estimate. Both also had early warning signs that did not lead to a fix. In May 2025, revocation lists eMudhra published for six of the certificates failed signature checks, and the company told Mozilla it had resolved the problem by re-signing them "with flawed keys". PHP's 2024 lead was judged theoretical and set aside for more pressing issues.AI figures in both stories. eMudhra says the researcher may have used AI-assisted techniques, and a Mozilla engineer wrote that AI agents he tested recovered the keys "on their first attempt with a simplistic prompt". Wiz credits AI with finding PHP's flaws in a week. Tools that help researchers find old bugs fast are available to attackers too.And both fixes depend on people acting. Browsers update themselves, but many devices and apps will keep trusting eMudhra's keys until someone updates them, and every PHP server has to be patched by whoever runs it.Where they differeMudhra's flaw was in the internet's trust system, which tells a browser who a website is. PHP's flaws are in the software that runs the website itself. eMudhra's weak keys came from one company's mistakes at a single key-making session in April 2025, while PHP's flaws were bugs in widely shared code.The attacks differ too. Using eMudhra's website keys required an attacker to intercept a victim's connection, on a café's Wi-Fi or at an internet provider, and browsers had a safety net that would have exposed forgeries. PHP's flaws can be attacked directly over the internet, and most sites have no comparable protection other than patching, which helps explain why some governments chose to take their sites offline.What to doOrdinary users should update their browsers, phones and computers, and never click past a warning that a website's certificate is not valid. Website owners should find out who maintains PHP on their sites and make sure the fix is applied. If they cannot patch, CERT-EU advises considering taking the site offline until they can.

title: Insult to Opposition leaders: Mallikarjun Kharge hits out at Kiren Rijiju for replying to PM Modi letter | India News
description: Kharge had written to Modi on October 16 to demand an all-party meeting regarding the government’s new delimitation proposals, and warned against rushing a Constitutional Amendment Bill (One Hundred and Thirty First Amendment Bill, 2026) without consultation. | India News
content: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday took an exception to parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju replying to his letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and accused the PM of insulting Opposition leaders by not writing back to them directly.“He [Rijiju] has not been given that much power. He is being used as a front, just as they are using Gyanesh Kumar. Similarly, they are using Rijiju. He [PM Modi] does not reply to anyone himself. We write to him, and he gets someone else to draft the reply. What does this mean?” Kharge said during an interaction in Bengaluru.“He (Modi) is insulting opposition leaders. He is insulting all the opposition parties, and why are they not coming? You should reply. You should take cognisance of what we say. Are you above the law? Are you above the Constitution? You are one MP among 543, and you are number one among them. That does not mean that you can do whatever you want,” Kharge added.Kharge had written to Modi on October 16 to demand an all-party meeting regarding the government’s new delimitation proposals, and warned against rushing a Constitutional Amendment Bill (One Hundred and Thirty First Amendment Bill, 2026) without consultation. The government is pushing for the passage of the bill along with the delimitation bill to roll out 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha and state assemblies, as well as expand the Lok Sabha.In a detailed letter on Monday, Rijiju had written to Kharge over the government’s plan to again push the delimitation-related Constitution amendment bill, which could not be passed in April as the NDA could not muster two-third majority in the House.Rijiju had said there was no impropriety or irregularity in Parliament not being prorogued since the monsoon session ended in August as there was “no constitutional requirement” prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die.Tthe minister also said that he had reached out to the Congress unsuccessfully and added that consultations were held with a number of other opposition parties, including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and Samajwadi Party.In his October 16 letter, Kharge had also reiterated that the law introduced by the Modi government in 2023, which grants legal protection to the Election Commissioner and immunity, should be repealed.“All the irregularities that have occurred so far have been through Gyanesh Kumar. The question is—why did the government grant him such immunity? If the Modi government wants fair elections, it must adhere to the constitutional framework, remove Gyanesh Kumar, and overhaul the entire system,” Kharge said, reiterating the demand that ballot papers must replace the EVM system.

title: Delhiwale: Jawed and Lucy | Latest News Delhi
description: Most of the day, she is lying silently on the pavement, her head flopped down  | Latest News Delhi
content: Most of the day, she is lying silently on the pavement, her head flopped down. Behind her, over the same hours, he stays super-busy rustling out one round of tea after another. The young man stands by his gas burner, his arms a blur with the stirring and pouring of chai for his customers. While she occasionally curls deeper into herself, lowering her face towards her paws. Neither looks at the other. But it seems each might miss the other if one were not there.The dog is Lucy. The tea man is Jawed. All the other people living and/or working on this stretch of a Central Delhi road-side call her Lucy too. Jawed thinks she must be around two. The tea stall anyway is new. Jawed opened it this month, having earlier worked as an attendant in a chicken shop. His open-air establishment consists of a table, a bench, and a gas cylinder. The stall also serves boiled eggs and chatpata Maggi noodles. This evening, a peeled egg is resting on a steel plate covering a saucepan. On the egg crate, rose petals are arranged among a smattering of tomatoes and green chillies. The roses are drying.It has to be admitted that Jawed and Lucy are not fast friends. They do not engage in much batcheet. He calls her only when he has something for her to eat or drink. She understands the words “khana” and “pani.” Every day, Jawed collects chicken feet from the area’s meat shops for Lucy’s khana.He also feeds three other dogs in the vicinity—Jeny, Lawrence and Sheru. Although Jeny hangs out at the nearby stall of “Shahnaz Chai Wali,” Jawed says, much as Lucy at his.That said, Lucy has no particular place reserved for her. The pavement in front of Jawed’s stall remains mostly clear of passers-by and garbage, and so she lies there. Indeed, at four in the morning, when Jawed opens the stall, she is already around. At 11 at night, when he closes, she accompanies him part of the way to his home nearby. Beyond a certain point, she stops. The dogs there are possessive about their area, Jawed explains.Recently, a fight with another dog left Lucy injured at the back of her neck. Jawed says he brought “engine oil” from a car repair workshop and applied it to the wound. He credits it with her recovery.“Lucy never bites,” Jawed says. Sometimes she does bark when somebody kicks her. Now, being photographed, Lucy suddenly raises her head, bares her teeth and growls. Jawed makes kissing sounds. She at once calms down, withdrawing beneath a row of parked scooters. Only her face and paws are showing.Later, a customer is lingering beside the tea stall bench. Lucy quietly approaches him, sniffs his backside, and returns to her usual place in front of Jawed’s stall. See photo.

title: Work hit as govt employees in Punjab go on two-day mass casual leave | Hindustan Times
description: The protesters are demanding the restoration of the old pension scheme (OPS), release of pending dearness allowance (DA) instalments and arrears, regularisation of contractual workers and fulfilment of other long-pending demands
content: Government employees across Punjab stayed away from work on Wednesday as part of a two-day mass casual leave agitation, disrupting administrative functioning in several districts.The protesters are demanding the restoration of the old pension scheme (OPS), release of pending dearness allowance (DA) instalments and arrears, regularisation of contractual workers and fulfilment of other long-pending demands.The agitation, organised under the banner of the Punjab Employees and Pensioners’ Joint Front and the Joint Employees’ Platform Punjab, witnessed demonstrations at district administrative complexes and tehsil offices. Nearly three-lakh employees reportedly participated in the mass leave programme, according to Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh.Pargat criticised the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government, saying the large-scale participation reflected growing dissatisfaction among government employees. He urged the government to address their grievances through dialogue rather than allowing the situation to escalate.The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) also extended its support to the two-day statewide strike by government employees. Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon accused the AAP government of being anti-employee, alleging that it had neglected employees’ concerns for the past four-and-a-half years.In the Doaba region, employees staged protests in Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur, Kapurthala and Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar districts. Many wore black badges to register their opposition to the government’s alleged failure to honour its commitments.Tejinder Singh Nangal, an activist of the Joint Coordination Committee, alleged that the government had failed to resolve employees’ concerns despite meetings with representatives. He said the OPS remained unimplemented despite a notification and also raised concerns over the non-implementation of the Punjab and Haryana high court’s decision regarding DA.In Hoshiarpur, the Sanjhi Talmel Committee organised a rally outside the district administrative complex. The protesters demanded revision of pension benefits using a multiplication factor of 2.59, regularisation of temporary and outsourced employees and removal of anomalies in the Pay Commission’s report.Their demands also included regularisation of mid-day meal, anganwadi and ASHA workers, restoration of 37 discontinued allowances, withdrawal of notifications concerning central pay scales and the three-year probation period, and restoration of the cashless health scheme.Employee and pensioner leaders accused the state government of neglecting their concerns and prioritising publicity over resolving public grievances.In Bathinda and other districts of the south Malwa region, clerical staff remained absent from offices, affecting routine government services and inconveniencing people visiting district headquarters.The unions warned of intensifying their protests if the government failed to initiate meaningful dialogue and take concrete steps to fulfil their demands.(With PTI inputs)

title: Monitor debates, be ready to mute panellists, Centretells TV channels | India News
description: Channels should choose panellists carefully, brief them in advance, and be ready to mute them, interrupt, run disclaimers or cut the feed if a participant’s comments turn derogatory, abusive or inflammatory, said the advisory. | India News
content: The government on Wednesday asked TV channels to keep a close watch on debates and panel discussions so that they do not promote communal or anti-national attitudes. Channels should choose panellists carefully, brief them in advance, and be ready to mute them, interrupt, run disclaimers or cut the feed if a participant’s comments turn derogatory, abusive or inflammatory, said the advisory.“Adequate editorial control (including, but not limited to careful selection and pre – sensitisation of the panellists/participants) should be exercised. Wherever necessary, immediate remedial measures such as muting, disclaimers, interruption or discontinuation of feed should be implemented in order to prevent airing of derogatory, abusive or inflammatory content,” said the ministry of information and broadcasting’s advisory released Wednesday.The advisory, which is addressed to all TV channels but is largely aimed at news broadcasters, also asks channels to stay away from live coverage of anti-terror operations, use only Survey of India-approved maps of the country in all their broadcasts and graphics, and limit artificial intelligence (AI) tools to an assisting role, without compromising the accuracy or authenticity of news.“The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has observed instances of non-compliance with the provisions of the Programme Code prescribed under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 and the Cable Television Network Rules, 1994 by various private satellite television channels,” noted the advisory.This follows a meeting of the Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), constituted under the Cable Television Networks (Amendment) Rules, 2021, which observed that several TV channels were not adhering to the Programme Code. The committee also emphasised that inappropriate behaviour or language should not be normalised on air.Channels were also told to show “due caution, responsibility and editorial discretion” while airing violent, graphic or disturbing visuals, so as not to offend good taste or decency or cause unnecessary distress to viewers. On crime and violence, the ministry said reports must be based on verified facts and be balanced, so that false insinuations and half-truths are not aired.Channels should avoid sensational reporting that may glorify or normalise unlawful or socially undesirable behaviour, and should not repeat or loop disturbing visuals excessively, said the government. “The use of appropriate blurring or masking techniques are suggested wherever warranted so as to not offend good taste and decency of the viewers,” it said.Special care is needed when showing visuals of crimes against women and children, the advisory said. Channels were also asked to strictly follow the Supreme Court’s repeated directions on not revealing the identity of victims of sexual offences.For natural calamities, disasters and major accidents, the ministry said visuals should be time-stamped where necessary to avoid unnecessary panic among viewers, and reporting should rest on verified facts.Broadcasters were also asked to tighten their editorial checks and make sure everyone involved in news gathering, editing, production and broadcast knows the Programme Code. They are encouraged to hold regular workshops and training sessions for their teams.

title: Will US national VanDyke return to India? Court to hear case linked to Myanmar drone warfare on Friday | India News
description: NIA has alleged the seven accused imparted training to members of Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups. | India News
content: With the next hearing in an alleged conspiracy case involving seven foreign nationals who trained ethnic militias in Myanmar after travelling there via India scheduled for Friday, all eyes are on whether US national Mathew Aaron VanDyke will return to India.People close to VanDyke, who did not want to be named, said he would return to India and join the court proceedings on Friday since he had already booked his return ticket from the US. However, the National Investigation Agency (NIA), which is probing the case, is waiting for a confirmation from VanDyke.“He is expected to come back and attend the next court date - set on Friday,” one of them said.Also read | No UAPA in NIA chargesheet against US national VanDyke, his Ukrainian associates arrested in IndiaHT is trying to get in touch with VanDyke’s family in the US.VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals – arrested in March this year under stringent provisions of the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act or UAPA that were later dropped by the agency in its charge sheet filed in September – were allowed by a Delhi court to return to their countries in the last week of September for a month on a condition that they will rejoin the investigations. The seven accused were only charged under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, which is a compounding offence, by NIA in its charge sheet.The federal agency did not press for their physical presence in India despite keeping its UAPA probe against them open, and agreed on their travel back home after they furnished personal undertakings, and provided their residential address and contact details.Also read | NIA did not press for US national VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to stay in India; UAPA probe stays openVanDyke was arrested on March 13 at Kolkata airport under section 18 of the UAPA, which relates to conspiracy, advocacy, abetment or incitement to commit a terrorist act. The six Ukrainians – Hurba Petro, Taras Slyviak, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Marian Stefankiv, Maksim Honcharuk and Viktor Kaminskyi – were arrested at Delhi and Lucknow airports the same day.NIA had earlier alleged the seven accused had illegally entered Myanmar through Mizoram without valid travel documents and participated in a pre-scheduled training programme for Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups targeting the Myanmar military junta.Also read | After release of US citizen Van Dyke, Delhi court grants default bail to 6 Ukrainians in Myanmar arms training caseThe US national is being represented by advocates Rohit Gour and Rohit Dandriyal. They are yet to comment on his return.NIA has alleged that for nearly three months, the seven accused imparted training in drone warfare, drone operations, assembly and jamming technology to members of Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups, including the Chin National Front (CNF) and the Kachin Independence Army (KIA).It has also claimed that VanDyke and others received logistical support from the members of CNF and the mission was financed through funds arranged by a commander of a Myanmar-based rebel group.NIA has so far not commented on the return of the accused to their countries.

title: Land case backlog puts Prayagraj revenue officials in the dock | Hindustan Times
description: Divisional commissioner Lokesh M issued these directives on Monday following a performance review of revenue officials, which he deemed “unsatisfactory.”
content: The divisional commissioner has ordered disciplinary action against tehsildars and naib tehsildars in Prayagraj and Pratapgarh after finding that over 1,500 land dispute cases in the former and 712 in the latter have exceeded the mandatory six-month disposal deadline.Official records indicate a widespread delay across the region. In addition to the backlog in Prayagraj and Pratapgarh, 271 cases remain pending beyond the deadline in Kaushambi, while Fatehpur reports 245 such cases.Divisional commissioner Lokesh M issued these directives on Monday following a performance review of revenue officials, which he deemed “unsatisfactory.” Despite previous instructions to expedite case resolutions, officials responsible for the files have failed to clear the backlog.The review also highlighted shortcomings in grievance redressal. While officials were asked to ensure an 80% satisfaction rate for complaints filed through the Integrated Grievance Redressal System (IGRS) and a 90% complainant-contact rate, the targets remain unmet. Satisfaction levels currently stand at 63.92% in Prayagraj, 59.03% in Kaushambi, 55.25% in Fatehpur and 59.19% in Pratapgarh. The rate of contacting complainants is 79.98% in Prayagraj, 79.08% in Kaushambi, 75.02% in Fatehpur and 75.98% in Pratapgarh.The commissioner also flagged delays in uncontested succession cases, which must be resolved within seven days. The number of pending uncontested succession cases is 230 in Prayagraj and 271 in Pratapgarh. Mutation cases, which must be decided within 90 days, have also piled up, with 707 pending in Prayagraj, 618 in Pratapgarh, 182 in Kaushambi and 185 in Fatehpur beyond the prescribed period.Inspections in Kunda and Chail tehsils also revealed that record-keeping protocols for encroachment cases and grievance registers were not being followed. Consequently, the divisional commissioner has directed the district magistrates of all four affected districts to initiate formal disciplinary proceedings against the concerned ADMs, SDMs, tehsildars, naib tehsildars and other relevant revenue personnel.

title: Punbus, PRTC contractual workers continue strike as talks with govt fail | Hindustan Times
description: The strike, which began on the evening of October 20, has disrupted public transport services across Punjab and Chandigarh, leaving commuters struggling to find alternatives
content: Talks between striking contractual employees of Punbus and the Pepsu Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) and minister Harpal Singh Cheema and transport secretary Varun Roojam remained inconclusive in Chandigarh on Wednesday, with unions refusing to call off their indefinite strike until their demands are met.The strike, which began on the evening of October 20, has disrupted public transport services across Punjab and Chandigarh, leaving commuters struggling to find alternatives. Nearly 2,000 state-run buses have been taken off the roads, affecting services operated by the Punjab Roadways and PRTC.Around 40% of Punjab Roadways’ fleet of nearly 600 buses remained off the roads, while PRTC’s 1,800 buses stayed off the roads. Only regular employees continued operating select services according to their duty rosters.According to a government release issued later in the day, Cheema directed the transport department to take immediate, result-oriented action on the legitimate demands of PUNBUS workers, prompting the department to initiate the redressal process.Following the minister’s directions, the Punjab State Bus Stand Management Company Limited (PUNBUS) has decided to convene a high-level review meeting on October 29 under Cheema’s chairmanship.The meeting will focus on finalising rules for regularising contractual PUNBUS employees on the pattern of PRTC, reviewing the transition of outsourced employees to contractual status under the Punjab State Outsourced Personnel (Transition to Contractual Engagement) Act, 2026, and examining demands for withdrawing police cases registered against workers during previous agitations.Ahead of the meeting, PUNBUS management directed depot managers across the state to expedite verification of outsourced employees eligible for contractual engagement. Depots must verify the service records of personnel with up to five years of service, based on the May 30, 2026, cut-off date, and submit compliance reports by October 26. Officials have been warned that delays, negligence or discrepancies could invite departmental action.PRTC Union president Resham Singh Gill said the strike would continue until the government fulfilled its commitments.He accused the government of failing to honour its earlier assurance to issue a notification addressing the employees’ demands by October 15.“The transport minister had given us time until October 15 to issue the notification, but the government failed to do so. Now, we have been given another date, October 29. We will call off the strike only when our demands are met,” Gill said.The employees are demanding regularisation of around 6,500 contractual workers, direct contractual employment for outsourced staff, abolition of private recruitment agencies and implementation of equal pay for equal work.They also opposed the expansion of the private kilometre scheme, under which private operators supply buses for specified routes, arguing that it threatens employment opportunities in state transport undertakings. The unions are further seeking unconditional withdrawal of police cases against 30 employees booked during previous protests.Protests were held at bus stands in Bathinda and adjoining districts, as well as at district headquarters across Punjab. Union leaders are planning demonstrations outside the Punjab Vidhan Sabha and an indefinite dharna near the chief minister’s official residence if the deadlock continues.

title: Police forces should unite to make India drug-free: Amit Shah | India News
description: Shah, who was addressing police officers at the National Police Memorial in Delhi on the occasion of Police Commemoration Day, also lauded the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) for conducting elections peacefully in West Bengal. | India News
content: Union home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday urged all police forces across the country to work towards the government’s goal of making India drug-free by 2029.Shah, who was addressing police officers at the National Police Memorial in Delhi on the occasion of Police Commemoration Day, also lauded the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) for conducting elections peacefully in West Bengal.During his address, Shah also said that while India’s three internal security hotspots—J&K, the Northeast, and areas with Left Wing Extremism (LWE)—are peaceful and seeing development, the focus should be on cracking down against drug smuggling. “The country is still not completely free from problems. We still face many challenges. The home ministry has decided to wage a united fight against drugs in the remaining three and a half years—2026, 2027, 2028, and 2029—and to rid the country of the drug problem by December 31, 2029,” he said, asking all forces to join this battle. The home minister also said that West Bengal, which has a history of electoral violence and killings, reported no such incidents during elections this year.“While the country succeeded in eliminating electoral violence in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, electoral violence had persisted in Bengal for a long time. In the recently concluded Bengal Assembly elections, our security personnel achieved great success in completing the elections without a single loss of life, and in doing so, the Central Security Forces have set a new standard. Today, the entire country believes that the country is free from electoral violence,” he said.Shah also said that the year 2026 is a very important year for the Indian Police, because the war against Naxals was won on March 31, 2026.Addressing a press conference, Home Secretary Govind Mohan said around 2,000 artists from 126 Naxal-affected districts across the country will participate in this year’s Ekta Diwas parade in Gujarat’s Kevadia as part of a special programme celebrating national unity and the end of armed Naxalism. “The parade has been a regular part of all Ekta Diwas celebrations but this year it will feature all the forces from CAPFs and state police, who have been at the forefront of the struggle against armed Naxalism. During the parade when each contingent passes in front of Honourable PM, a short film will be displayed on a number of LED screens which will summarise their salient achievements against this fight.”Mohan also said that the National School of Drama(NSD) will present a drama through an array of 2,000 artists—all drawn from 126 districts across the country that at some point witnessed the menace of Naxalism. “These 2000 artists will through their performance, replay live examples of what they went through when armed Naxalism was rampant and how their lives and properties were threatened by militants belonging to Naxal elements day in and day out,” he said.Project Karmaveer launchedShah also announced the launch of ‘Project Karmaveer’, wherein former police and CAPF personnel and widows of martyrs from these forces will operate 400 common service centres across the country.In a post on X, Shah said, “Our police personnel and jawans of the Central Armed Police Forces are true karmaveers, who hold duty above all, even at the cost of their lives. In their honour, on the occasion of Police Commemoration Day today, ‘Project Karmaveer’ is being launched, under which the brave widows of martyrs and former personnel will operate 400 Common Service Centres across the country. Through these centres, they will be able to earn a respectable livelihood by providing pension, banking, and citizen services.”

title: Amritsar:Three juveniles among seven nabbed with 3kg heroin, grenade & 2 pistols | Hindustan Times
description: The police recovered one hand grenade, two .30-bore pistols along with 29 live cartridges and 3.4 kg heroin from their possession, director general of police Gaurav Yadav said on Wednesday
content: The Amritsar rural police have busted two networks involved in drug trafficking, illegal arms and explosives smuggling, apprehending seven individuals, including three juveniles, in two separate operations. The police recovered one hand grenade, two .30-bore pistols along with 29 live cartridges and 3.4 kg heroin from their possession, director general of police Gaurav Yadav said on Wednesday.Those arrested in the first operation were identified as Ajay, 28, a resident of Mudh Khokhar, and Robin Masih alias Noni, 22, a resident of Sultanwind. Those apprehended in the second operation were identified as Gurlal Singh, 20 and Rashpal Singh, 18, both residents of Lopoke, along with three 17-year-old juveniles. Police have also impounded an unregistered motorcycle from the accused.DGP Yadav said a preliminary investigation had revealed that the arrested accused were allegedly in contact with foreign-based smugglers and were smuggling illegal weapons for further distribution among criminal elements. Further investigation is underway to uncover the entire network and establish its backward and forward linkages, he said.Sharing details of the first operation, inspector general of police, border range, Gurpreet Singh Bhullar said the police had received a reliable input that suspect Ajay has been procuring drone-dropped heroin and illegal firearms from across the border to supply them further on the directions of foreign-based gangsters.“Acting swiftly, the police, in coordination with a central agency, set up a special checkpoint in the Manawala area and intercepted Ajay along with his accomplice Robin Masih while they were riding a motorcycle. A search of the bag carried by the pillion rider led to the recovery of nearly 3.4 kg heroin and one .30-bore pistol along with 19 live rounds,” he said.In the second operation, the IGP said a joint team of the CIA and SHO, Lopoke, while patrolling during the Dussehra festival, received a tip-off about a cross-border smuggler pushing consignments of arms and explosives through local youth. Acting on the input, police intercepted the group during checking and recovered one live hand grenade, one .30-bore pistol along with 10 live rounds from the accused.Amritsar rural senior superintendent of police Kanwalpreet Singh Chahal said Ajay was a drug addict and a habitual criminal facing at least five cases, including four under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and one under the Arms Act.Two separate FIRs under Sections 21 and 25 of the NDPS Act, Section 25 of the Arms Act, and Sections 3, 4, and 5 of the Explosive Substances Act have been registered at the Chatiwind and Lopoke police stations, officials said.

title: Amit Shah’s likely Lucknow visit on October 30 may sharpen BJP’s 2027 campaign | Hindustan Times
description: “Union home minister Amit Shah is expected to visit Lucknow on October 30 to attend the proposed two-day state executive committee’s meeting,” a senior BJP leader holding an organisational post said. He, however, added that there was no official programme yet on Shah’s visit or the meeting itself.
content: Union home minister Amit Shah is likely to visit Lucknow on October 30 to attend a proposed two-day meeting of the BJP’s state executive committee, an event that could give fresh impetus to the party’s preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.The meeting, proposed for October 30 and 31, is expected to focus on the party’s electoral strategy, organisational preparedness and measures to strengthen its network at the grassroots level.“Union home minister Amit Shah is expected to visit Lucknow on October 30 to attend the proposed two-day state executive committee’s meeting,” a senior BJP leader holding an organisational post said. He, however, added that there was no official programme yet on Shah’s visit or the meeting itself.The proposed visit assumes significance as the BJP seeks to consolidate its organisational machinery well ahead of the polls in the state. Shah’s address could set the tone for the BJP’s campaign in the state.“In the proposed meeting, the party is expected to deliberate on strengthening its booth-level organisation, increasing workers’ participation and ensuring that the achievements and welfare schemes of the state and Central governments reach voters,” the BJP leader said.The proposed meeting comes against the backdrop of the BJP’s reduced tally in Uttar Pradesh in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, when the Samajwadi Party emerged as the state’s largest party in terms of seats won. The results prompted renewed attention to the BJP’s organisational strategy and its outreach among different sections of voters.

title: ₹162-crore road project put on back burner in Ludhiana | Hindustan Times
description: The MC had issued a request for proposal (RFP) and received bids in response, but senior officials familiar with the matter said the state government has stalled progress for now
content: Administrative delays have stalled the World-Class Roads project, with the municipal corporation Ludhiana putting the ₹162-crore initiative on the back burner ten months after its announcement as it awaits a formal go-ahead from the state government.The MC had issued a request for proposal (RFP) and received bids in response, but senior officials familiar with the matter said the state government has stalled progress for now.“We have bids. But we can’t take it forward yet as the government has paused the project for now,” an official said.Superintendent engineer of the buildings and road (B&R) cell, Sham Lal Gupta, said, “As we get the necessary go-ahead from the higher-ups, we will take the project forward.”MC commissioner Ankur Mahindroo said, “I have just joined two days back. It will take a few days for me to get to know about the projects. I am not in a position to comment on this yet.”Unveiled by then industries and local bodies minister Sanjiv Arora on January 25, the project was aimed at transforming Ludhiana’s urban landscape into a benchmark of safe, inclusive, sustainable, and smart mobility. The initiative sought to reimagine the city’s streets as vibrant public spaces rather than mere traffic corridors. Under the project, 15 kilometres of roads across 10 critical city corridors were to be redeveloped following a complete street approach, prioritising pedestrians, cyclists, public transport users, and street vendors alongside vehicular traffic.Key features of the stalled project included 5.3 km of accessible footpaths, 15.7 km of cycle lanes, 250 organised vending spaces, 40 rain and sun shelters, 10 public toilets, and 36 water ATMs. Emphasising green infrastructure, the plan assured zero tree cutting, alongside the planting of 3,633 new trees and the establishment of 54 rainwater harvesting pits, along with new stormwater drains, LED street lighting, landscaping, and junction improvements.Piloted by the Punjab Infrastructure Development Board, the project was to be executed under a hybrid annuity model to ensure high-quality construction and long-term maintenance, with the concessionaire responsible for upkeep at an estimated annual cost of 2.5% of construction value.Arora had earlier highlighted barrier-free design elements, including kerb ramps, tactile paving, zebra crossings, and tabletop crossings to ensure universal accessibility, with specific corridors such as Sherpur Chowk to Jagraon Bridge, Model Town Road, and Gill Canal Bridge to Gill Village featuring unique design themes reflecting Ludhiana’s heritage and future aspirations.

title: Digital Census 2027: Ludhiana MC gears up for self-enumeration from Nov 16 | Hindustan Times
description: Officers directed to expedite preparations and sensitise residents; online window open till Nov 30, followed by door-to-door enumeration scheduled for Dec1 to Jan 4
content: With the online self-enumeration window for Digital Census 2027 set to open on November 16, the municipal corporation (MC) has directed its charge officers to complete all preparatory arrangements in advance and sensitise residents about submitting their household details online.MC commissioner-cum-principal Census officer Ankur Mahindroo reviewed the preparations at a meeting with charge officers at the MC’s Zone D office in Sarabha Nagar on Wednesday. He stressed the need for advance planning and wider public awareness to facilitate the exercise.The online self-enumeration facility will remain available from November 16 to 30, allowing residents to submit their details from home. Those who do not complete the process online will be covered during the subsequent door-to-door enumeration, scheduled from December 1, 2026, to January 4, 2027.Mahindroo said the concerned staff had been directed to ensure that all necessary arrangements were in place well before the exercise begins. He also appealed to residents to make use of the online facility and cooperate with enumerators during the door-to-door process.The meeting was attended by charge officers overseeing the census exercise, including joint commissioner Amanpreet Singh; assistant commissioners Gurpal Singh and Jasdev Singh Sekhon; superintending engineers Sham Lal Gupta, Ekjot Singh, Praveen Singla, Ranjit Singh and Harkiranjit Singh; and Census superintendent Tarun Goyal, among others.

title: Noida Elevated Road shut after second cave-in in a month, repairs underway | Hindustan Times
description: The Noida authority expects to complete repairs within two days and is considering an IIT Delhi safety audit to assess the road’s condition.
content: The Noida authority has closed the carriageway from Sector 61 towards Sector 18 and started repairs on the six-lane Noida Elevated Road, days after a 2x2-foot section near Sector 33 caved in, officials said on Wednesday.The latest incident came to light on Monday morning after a passer-by reported the damage. Officials initially barricaded the affected patch but allowed traffic to continue. On Wednesday, however, the damaged section widened, prompting authorities to shut the entire carriageway between Sectors 61 and 18, officials said.Also read: Noida elevated road closed from Sector 61 to Sector 18 after section caves in, traffic divertedTraffic diverted to Maharaja Agrasen Marg during repairsTraffic has been diverted to Maharaja Agrasen Marg, which runs parallel to the elevated road. The closure will remain in place until repairs are completed, the traffic police said.“We are also probing to ascertain the reason for this cave-in and if this is linked to the previous incident,” said Vandana Tripathi, additional chief executive officer of the Noida authority.Officials said they expect to complete repairs within two days. It is also planning to engage IIT Delhi to conduct a safety audit of the elevated road, which opened to the public in 2017, officials said.Also read: Noida sets October 31 deadline for road repairEarlier cave-in reported near Vishwa Bharti Public School in SeptemberThe incident comes barely a month after a 10x5-foot section, around three feet deep, caved in near Vishwa Bharti Public School on September 15.
