The authority is investigating whether the two incidents are connected.Built at a cost of ₹480 crore, the elevated road connects Sector 18 with Sector 61 and adjoining sectors, providing a key route between Noida, Ghaziabad and Delhi via the DND Flyway. Nearly 150,000 commuters use it on weekdays, according to traffic department data.The road underwent repair and restoration work costing ₹14.55 crore in March 2024 after cracks developed on its surface and layers eroded at several locations.

title: Ludhiana: Education institution head, associate booked in bid to usurp plot | Hindustan Times
description: The complaint was lodged by Rajesh Verma, a commission agent residing in Janta Enclave, Basant Avenue, Ludhiana, who claimed ownership of the plot for the past 17 years
content: The Doraha police have booked the head of an educational institution in Doraha and his associate for allegedly attempting to usurp a 287.5-square-yard plot by damaging its gate and seeking to secure a sale deed wrongfully, according to a complaint.The accused have been identified as Har Partap Singh, who heads the institution, and Gurdev Singh, his associate. The complaint was lodged by Rajesh Verma, a commission agent residing in Janta Enclave, Basant Avenue, Ludhiana, who claimed ownership of the plot for the past 17 years.Verma told the police that he had purchased the property from Swaroop Singh and Jasvir Kaur. He said the plot was enclosed by a boundary wall and fitted with a gate when he bought it. He alleged that the accused had since damaged the gate and were attempting to take over the property by wrongfully getting a sale deed registered and challenging his ownership.The complainant further stated that the sellers were relatives of Har Partap Singh and that Singh and Gurdev Singh had facilitated the property transaction.Assistant sub-inspector Harjit Singh, the investigating officer, said, “A case has been registered against the two accused under Sections 318(4) (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property), 329(3) (punishment for criminal trespass), 62 (attempt to commit offences), 324(4) (mischief causing property damage) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with Section 82 of the Registration Act.”

title: CM Fadnavis to inaugurate 3 flyovers on Oct 22 | Mumbai news
description: The three bridges, constructed by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), are expected to improve east-west connectivity, reduce travel time and ease congestion at some of the city’s busy traffic junctions.  | Mumbai news
content: osama.rawal@hindustantimes.comMumbai: The city will get two railway overbridges and one flyover today, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis set to virtually inaugurate the reconstructed Sion and Vidyavihar railway overbridges (ROBs) and a flyover on the Goregaon-Mulund Link Road (GMLR) at 1pm. Deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar and Mumbai mayor Ritu Tawde will also be present. Live screenings of the inauguration will be arranged at all three locations.The three bridges, constructed by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), are expected to improve east-west connectivity, reduce travel time and ease congestion at some of the city’s busy traffic junctions.Sion ROBThe Sion railway overbridge (ROB) replaces a 112-year-old structure declared unsafe. Its reconstruction was necessary to facilitate Central Railway’s plan to lay the fifth and sixth railway lines between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) and Kurla under the Mumbai Urban Transport Project (MUTP-2). The pillars supporting the old bridge between the railway tracks were obstructing the expansion. The new bridge, which does away with these intermediate pillars, will allow the railway authorities to undertake the track expansion while improving the movement of suburban and long-distance trains.The project finished four months ahead of its February 2027 deadline, despite challenges involving shifting water pipelines and other utilities, tree-related interventions, and reconstructing civic amenities. While Central Railway constructed the main bridge over the tracks, the BMC’s Bridges Department rebuilt and strengthened the approach roads.The bridge provides an important east-west link between Dharavi, Bandra, the Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) and Kurla on one side, and Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Road and the Eastern Express Highway on the other. Pedestrian infrastructure has also been improved, with a new subway beneath Lal Bahadur Shastri (LBS) Marg opened in February 2026 and a relocated subway beneath Sant Rohidas Marg reopened in July.Vidyavihar ROB The Vidyavihar ROB will provide another crucial east-west connection, linking Ramchandra Chemburkar Marg on the eastern side with LBS Marg on the western side. Currently, commuters travelling between these stretches often face congestion around Ghatkopar station and its flyover. The new bridge is expected to reduce the travel time between the two sides from approximately 30 minutes to 10 minutes, easing pressure on the existing Ghatkopar station flyover.Spread across a 650-metre stretch, the bridge has separate approaches on either side of the railway tracks. The project involved two phases: shifting railway utilities, constructing the main bridge, building service roads on both sides, and widening Somaiya Nullah. The second phase was completed on September 30. The bridge also provides direct pedestrian access to Vidyavihar railway station along with ticket counters.GMLR flyoverThe 1.26-km Goregaon-Mulund Link Road (GMLR) flyover is expected to ease congestion in Goregaon East, particularly around the Hotel Ratnagiri junction. Extending from General Arunkumar Vaidya Marg to Santosh Nagar on Film City Road, the six-lane flyover is part of the BMC’s larger GMLR project, which aims to connect the Western Express Highway with the Eastern Express Highway.The flyover will allow vehicles to bypass several congested stretches, including Dindoshi Court, Hotel Ratnagiri junction and Walbhat River Chowk. It will also serve as an important surface-level connection to the twin underground tunnels planned as part of the larger GMLR project, providing an alternative east-west route for motorists travelling between Mumbai’s western and eastern suburbs.

title: How pollution in Delhi surged on Dussehra night | India News
description: A similar surge may come in the weeks ahead as Diwali approaches., especially with firecrackers given the green light by the Supreme Court. | India News
content: Hour-by-hour readings show the pollution level in Delhi started surging on Tuesday evening, as Dussehra effigies burned, while the two previous nights of similar weather produced no such spike.A similar surge may come in the weeks ahead as Diwali approaches. The burning of firecrackers may be allowed more widely this year, going by the Supreme Court’s observations earlier this month.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant said it wanted a “pragmatic and practical” way to regulate them, and warned that people would see a restrictive order as coercion. It tied the Delhi-NCR case to the national one before Justice MM Sundresh, whose bench cleared “next-generation” laris, or joint crackers, across the country on September 30.Also Read | Green only in colour: Firecrackers flood Delhi markets amid festive season, rising AQI What the readings showedBecause the weather changed little from the two nights before, Dussehra night gives a rough measure of what one evening of celebrations does to Delhi’s air. Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) in the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) 4pm bulletin rose from 179 on Dussehra, Tuesday October 20, to 245 on Wednesday, the season’s highest and one point below July 13’s 246; the 66-point jump was the third-largest after Dussehra since 2015.The data cannot say how much came from the effigy burning itself, firecrackers, other fires, traffic or chemistry in the damp air, but makes evident a link between the celebrations and the surge in PM2.5 levels.At the median of 45 long-running stations, the one-hour PM2.5 sub-index, CPCB’s 0-500 score for fine particles, was 300 or more (about 120 micrograms per cubic metre, µg/m³) for 14 hours from 10pm, peaking at 346 at 2am, when 35 of 41 stations were above 300. At the peak hour of each earlier spike this month, no more than 18 were above this level.Between 6pm and 11pm on Tuesday, the median PM2.5 reading across the long-running stations rose by 86 µg/m³, about three times as much as on the two evenings before (29 and 27). Carbon monoxide and nitrogen dioxide, largely from traffic and other burning, rose by similar amounts on all three evenings.From 10pm to 6am the median PM2.5 reading was 167 µg/m³, against 67 and 90 on the two nights before, while the coarse part (PM10 minus PM2.5) was 121 µg/m³, against 120 on Monday night. At the typical station, PM2.5 readings were about 58% of PM10 readings, against 41-42% on the two nights before and 29-35% in the dust-led spike that opened the month.By 4pm on Wednesday PM2.5 was back to Tuesday afternoon’s 69 µg/m³. The 245 bulletin, a 24-hour average, records the surge that played out overnight.All three nights had calm or near-calm surface winds, mist by 9.30pm and the strongest temperature inversions since at least October 7, with 7.6°C, 5.6°C and 7.2°C of warming aloft at 4.30am on October 19, 20 and 21. Wednesday’s inversion was lower, at about 160 metres against 240-250 m, with almost no wind beneath it. What they suggestThe celebrations drove the surge, and the weather made it worse. Wednesday’s lower, stiller inversion accounts for only part of the jump, since calm, damp nights under strong inversions, one of them stronger than Wednesday’s, held PM2.5 at 67-90 µg/m³ on the two nights before. Nearly all the extra pollution was fine particles while traffic emissions rose about as much as on the two evenings before, which points to the effigy burnings. Crop smoke cannot on their own explain such strong jump: fire detections in Punjab and Haryana fell from 121 on October 18 to 22 on Dussehra, and the north-westerly winds that could carry it to Delhibrought no spike the two previous nights.The reasoningMost PM2.5 comes from burning, as smoke or as particles that form from combustion gases, while dust is mostly coarse, so a fine share that climbs while the coarse part holds steady means the extra pollution was fine particles. Carbon monoxide and nitrogen dioxide, a gauge of how much traffic exhaust the still air held, rose by similar amounts on all three evenings, while PM2.5 rose about three times as much on Tuesday, so whatever was added between 6pm and 11pm was far richer in particles than exhaust -- particularly since there would have been no evening peak hour traffic on a festival holiday.A lower inversion squeezes a night’s emissions into less air, but packing Monday night’s 90 µg/m³ into Wednesday’s two-thirds depth gives roughly 135-140, short of 167. And that PM2.5 was back at Tuesday afternoon’s level by 4pm on Wednesday marks a one-off release, since a build-up across the region would have left Wednesday afternoon dirtier.For figures from earlier in the month, HT converted CPCB’s index scores into concentrations using the board’s own table. Checked against CPCB’s measured values for October 18-21, the conversion was within 0.1 µg/m³ at the typical station-hour.What the data cannot sayBesides the split between sources, the readings cannot rule out humidity making some monitors over-read particulate concentration, and damp air also speeds the conversion of gases into particulate matter. The level of PM2.5 kept rising after the burnings ended at 11pm, to about 180 µg/m³ at 2am and 3am; late burning or smoke drifting in from elsewhere in the city could explain that, though a settling inversion or damp-air chemistry may have added to it.Nor can the data exclude a small crop-smoke share, since satellites miss fires lit between their passes. CPCB’s real-time figures are also provisional, and the board can revise them.

title: Space crunch at CSMT slows down CR’s platform extension for 15-car trains | Mumbai news
description: To expand the carrying capacity from 12-car to 15-car, two more platforms need to be extended by around 45-50 metres.  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: A lack of space at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) has stalled Central Railway’s plan to run 54 services of 15-car locals, augmented on August 15, as only one platform, Platform 7, can currently accommodate these longer trains.To expand the carrying capacity from 12-car to 15-car, two more platforms need to be extended by around 45-50 metres. CR authorities identified platforms 5-6 at CSMT for expansion. However, the process requires technical intervention from engineers because it involves extensive track realignment and changes to signalling systems, which could potentially affect the speed of trains entering the station.“The biggest concern is that the extension could force trains approaching CSMT to slow down, with speed restrictions potentially increasing from the existing 40 kmph to 20-25 kmph due to changes in track alignment and the positioning of points and signals,” said a CR official.He added that the work would require shifting tracks and railway points at 10-12 locations, besides modifying signal alignment and straightening up the tracks by upto seven degrees.“There are 10-12 track points at CSMT that would need to be shifted. This will enable us to extend the length of platforms by 45-50 meters. However, the impact will be seen towards Masjid as the tracks will have to be shifted further north leaving little space for trains between the two stations,” the official explained.“This could necessitate lower speed limits, potentially affecting train movements on the already congested approach to the terminus. We will also have to plan the work carefully as changes to the existing infrastructure could disrupt fast local services entering CSMT.”Railway sources said they intend to carry out the platform extension work after Diwali. At present, minor works are underway at the ends of platforms 5-6, with concrete slabs being stacked on the floors.The proposed platform extensions are crucial to any further expansion of 15-car services on the Main Line. Once the infrastructure is upgraded, CR could potentially increase the number of 15-car services from the current 54 to around 150, significantly enhancing passenger-carrying capacity on the CSMT-Kasara/Karjat/Khopoli corridor.

title: Doctor shows how to make green fish with spicy ginger oil: A one-pot recipe loaded with 57g protein | Hindustan Times
description: Dr Rupy Aujla's one-pot green fish recipe can be part of a simple everyday meal that is healthy, indulgent, and easy to prepare.
content: If you are looking for a recipe that will help you hit your protein goal but is different from the desi dishes that you try every day, London-based physician Dr Rupy Aujla has the perfect dish for you to try.Also Read | Fitness influencer shares how to make a truly eggless omelette that is loaded with 40g proteinTaking to Instagram on October 2, the doctor shared his one-pot green fish with spicy ginger oil recipe, a dish which he described as perfect for a midweek dinner and that is loaded with 57 grams of protein in each serving.“This recipe has saved me more times than I can count when I get home tired, hungry and need dinner fast,” wrote Dr Aujla in the caption. “And it still ticks all my boxes: high in protein, high in fibre and full of plants!”The quantities of ingredients listed below are sufficient for two servings. The detailed steps to make the dish are presented as follows. Ingredients for one-pan green fish with spicy ginger oil2–3 tbsp olive oil20g ginger, peeled and julienned1 tsp cumin seeds1 tsp brown mustard seeds1 tsp fennel seeds1 tsp red chilli flakes (optional)120g peas (frozen)120g spinach (frozen)30g coriander1 green chilli, deseeded and roughly chopped400ml fish stock1 tbsp fish sauce1 can chickpeas (can), drained and rinsed400g cod filletMethod of preparationHeat the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add the spices and ginger. Cook for three to four minutes until the ginger is golden, and the spices are beginning to pop.Drain into a small bowl and set aside. (This is to prevent the ginger from burning in the residual heat.)Place the peas, frozen spinach, coriander, green chilli, fish stock and fish sauce into a blender and blend until smooth.Pour into the pan, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook for five to six minutes, until thickened.Add the chickpeas to the pan and bring back to a gentle simmer.Once it is bubbling, add the fish to the pan, spoon some sauce over, cover, and cook for seven to eight minutes, until the fish is cooked through. Uncover several times during this period to give a gentle stir and make sure no greens stick to the bottom.Serve in bowls with the sizzled ginger and spices. (If desired, you can add some of the spiced oil you previously drained) Enjoy.Note to readers: This report is based on user-generated content from social media. HT.com has not independently verified the claims and does not endorse them.This article is for informational purposes only.Dr Rupy Aujla, MBBS, BSc, MRCGP, MSc, is a London-based doctor, specialising in general practice and emergency medicine, a nutritionist and founder of The Doctor’s Kitchen.

title: Three youths electrocuted during Durga idol immersion in Gkp | Hindustan Times
description: The injured were rushed to Nehru Hospital at Baba Raghav Das (BRD) Medical College, where three youths were declared dead
content: : Three youths, including two real brothers, were electrocuted and seven others sustained burn injuries after an iron rod mounted on a trolley carrying a Durga idol came into contact with an 11,000-volt high-tension wire during an immersion procession on Wednesday evening.The injured were rushed to Nehru Hospital at Baba Raghav Das (BRD) Medical College, where three youths were declared dead. Five of the seven injured are reportedly critical.The deceased were identified as Lucky, 17, Vicky, 19, and Chandan, 21, all residents of Jungle Ayodhya Prasad village. Gulriha SHO Jagdish Prasad Pal said Lucky and Vicky were brothers.The accident occurred near Rajhi crossing under Gulriha police station limits while the idol was being taken for immersion.Preliminary findings suggest power supply had been disconnected as a precaution during the procession but was restored before the trolley passed beneath the overhead wire.The incident triggered outrage, with residents staging a protest and blocking traffic outside BRD Medical College for several hours. They demanded an FIR against power corporation officials, alleging negligence.Circle Officer Ravi Kumar Singh said police were investigating the circumstances of the accident and traffic was restored after officers spoke to the protesters.Investigators are examining why the power supply was restored while the procession was still underway. title: Ludhiana: Commuters hit as indefinite transport strike begins | Hindustan Times
description: Over 90% of buses at the Ludhiana depot remained off the road, according to Praveen, general secretary of the contract workers’ union, leaving students, working women and job seekers who rely on affordable public transport to contend with disrupted journeys and steeper commuting costs
content: Permanent and contractual employees of Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC launched an indefinite strike on Wednesday to press for their long-pending demands, throwing government bus services in Ludhiana into disarray and leaving daily commuters scrambling for alternatives.Over 90% of buses at the Ludhiana depot remained off the road, according to Praveen, general secretary of the contract workers’ union, leaving students, working women and job seekers who rely on affordable public transport to contend with disrupted journeys and steeper commuting costs.More than 300 permanent and contractual transport workers gathered at the Ludhiana Inter-State Bus Terminal (ISBT) around 10 am and began the protest after a meeting with the government failed to resolve their grievances. The unions announced plans to stage another protest outside the transport minister’s residence in Dirba on Thursday (October 22).With government buses largely off the roads, commuters were left to seek alternatives to reach colleges, workplaces and other destinations. Although private buses continued to operate, travelling by them or hiring an auto-rickshaw or cab meant additional expenditure for passengers already managing tight budgets.For students and working women who travel daily, even a modest increase in commuting costs can add up over the month.“I depend on government buses because they are affordable. When these buses do not run, we have to find other options and spend more money. Not everyone can afford to pay extra for daily travel,” said Jashan, a college student.Shreya, a working woman, said the disruption had made her daily commute difficult. “We have to reach our workplaces on time. We cannot simply stay at home because buses are not running, so we have to find another way to travel even if it costs more,” she said. Job seekers travelling for interviews and other work have also been inconvenienced, as delays or difficulty finding transport can disrupt their plans.Over 70 meetings held over their demandsAddressing protesters at the Ludhiana depot, union leaders Satnam Singh and Jatinder Singh Soni accused the government of failing to honour its commitments to employees and address their long-pending demands. They said that despite 70 to 75 meetings with the government, no concrete solution had emerged.The union claimed that no transport employee had been regularised under the present government and that no new government bus had been added to the fleet in the past five years. It also opposed the kilometre-scheme model of bus operations, alleging that it promoted privatisation and undermined employment opportunities for young people.The workers are demanding the regularisation of contractual employees, an end to the contractor system, equal pay for equal work and greater employment security. They have also sought the withdrawal of cases registered against employees during protests and reiterated their opposition to the kilometre-scheme model.Union vice-president Gurpreet Singh and Sukhwinder Singh Babbu said the government had introduced a bill in 2026 to facilitate the contractual appointment of outsourced employees, but alleged that its implementation had been delayed. They also demanded that employees who had completed the required process and had been working on contract for 11 years be regularised under the applicable service rules.The union further alleged that employees were facing mental and physical harassment because of the failure to implement service rules. It claimed that cases had been registered against protesting workers to suppress their agitation.The workers have urged the government to implement the 2026 legislation, regularise contractual employees under the applicable service rules, withdraw cases registered against protesters and issue the necessary notifications without further delay.Praveen, general secretary of the contract workers’ union, said the workers would continue their agitation until their demands were addressed.The strike has left daily commuters bearing the immediate cost of the impasse.Calls and texts made to Navraj Batish, Punjab Roadways general manager, yielded no response.

title: Bakhtawar Chowk double decker structure design may need more tweaks | Hindustan Times
description: Gurugram:The design of the proposed double-decker flyover and underpass at Bakhtawar Chowk is likely to take more time to finalise, as the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA) has sought further amendments to the revised design submitted by the Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL)
content: Gurugram:The design of the proposed double-decker flyover and underpass at Bakhtawar Chowk is likely to take more time to finalise, as the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA) has sought further amendments to the revised design submitted by the Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL).GMDA officials said the authority wants to utilise the available space at the junction more efficiently to ensure adequate space for the proposed six-lane underpass and smooth traffic movement between Sector 47 and Medanta Medicity.The authority plans to construct the underpass at Bakhtawar Chowk to cater to the expected increase in traffic due to commercial developments coming up in Sector 47 and adjoining areas.On October 1, the GMRL submitted a revised design after GMDA CEO directed it to make provisions for a six-lane underpass at the junction. In a letter to GMDA, the GMRL said necessary changes had been made and revised drawings submitted for approval. “The Medicity-Satpaul Mittal Marg has a right of way of 50 metres and it was desired that GMRL propose a central pier for the double-decker structure, with provision for a six-lane underpass along this road,” the letter read.A senior GMRL official said the agency had revised the design as directed by the GMDA but was facing practical difficulties because of the limited width of the road connecting Sector 47 to Medicity“The width at the junction is sufficient for six lanes, but the roads on either side are not wide enough to accommodate them. We are trying to fix the design to provide for six lanes,” the official said.According to the GMRL, the double-decker structure will have an elevated road on the first level, with three lanes on each side. The second level will have a metro viaduct and station at Bakhtawar Chowk.The design will also have provision for a future underpass to be built by the GMDA, connecting Sector 47 with the Medanta hospital road. At ground level, two service lanes on each side will facilitate traffic movement.A senior GMDA official said, “The location of the piers and other structures needs to be placed in such a manner that sufficient room is available for the six-lane underpass.”

title: DTCP demolishes illegal shops on green belt in Gurugram’s DLF Phase 3 | Hindustan Times
description: The enforcement wing of the department of town and country planning (DTCP) on Wednesday demolished unauthorised structures on a green belt along Moulsari Avenue Road in DLF Phase 3, saying they were obstructing traffic entering the area from NH-48
content: The enforcement wing of the department of town and country planning (DTCP) on Wednesday demolished unauthorised structures on a green belt along Moulsari Avenue Road in DLF Phase 3, saying they were obstructing traffic entering the area from NH-48.Amit Madholia, district town planner (enforcement), said the structures included a scrap shop, an eatery, three motorcycle repair workshops, four small vending stalls, a meat shop, a car paint workshop and a car wash station.“These unauthorised structures were on a green area earmarked in the approved layout plan of DLF Phase 3. They created a bottleneck at the entrance to Moulsari Avenue Road, congesting traffic entering from NH-48. Their removal has freed up carriageway space and will ease traffic movement,” Madholia said.In separate drives on Wednesday, DTCP’s enforcement wing demolished structures in three unauthorised colonies in Bohra Kalan, Kharkhari and Jamalpur villages with assistance from Gurugram police.In Bohra Kalan, the team demolished three boundary walls and dug up the entire earthen road network in a colony spread over about 1.5 acres, officials said.In Kharkhari, five plinths, two under-construction structures and the entire earthen road network were demolished in a colony spread over about 1.25 acres.In Jamalpur, the team demolished an under-construction structure and the road network in a colony being developed across five acres.

title: Gurugram on outage alert ahead of power workers’ strike | Hindustan Times
description: Four unions leading the strike opposed the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (HERC) decision to grant Eleven Power Private Limited a parallel distribution licence in Gurugram and Nuh, citing concerns over job security and privatisation
content: Residents in Gurugram were warned that power faults could go unattended during a three-day statewide strike by Haryana power-sector unions, scheduled to begin at 10pm on Wednesday.Four unions leading the strike opposed the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (HERC) decision to grant Eleven Power Private Limited a parallel distribution licence in Gurugram and Nuh, citing concerns over job security and privatisation.The 25-year licence allows domestic, commercial and industrial consumers to switch from Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) to the private supplier, subject to feasibility, once it develops its distribution infrastructure in phases, officials said.DHBVN field employees alerted residents through WhatsApp groups about possible supply disruptions and the unavailability of repair services during the strike.“Employees across all ranks, including contractual staff and those engaged through third-party vendors, are participating in the strike,” a senior official said. He said no staff would be available to repair faults during outages, and residents had been warned.Sunil Sareen, deputy convenor, Dwarka Expressway Gurugram Development Association, and a resident of Emaar Imeprial Gardens in Sector-102, said DHBVN field officials had alerted several societies.“As consumers, we welcome multiple power suppliers because they give us a choice. Competition will push DHBVN to improve its services and infrastructure,” he said.Officials identified the four bodies leading the strike as the Haryana Power Engineers Association, All Haryana Power Corporation Workers Union, Haryana Electricity Board Workers Union, and Haryana Power Corporation SC-ST and BC Workers Union. Several other unions were also supporting the strike, they said.Ravinder Ghanghas, general secretary of the Haryana Power Engineers Association, said the protest was against the parallel licensing system.“In other cities where private discoms operate, they are assigned specific areas for power distribution, mainly to domestic consumers,” he said.Ghanghas said this was the first time Gurugram and Nuh had been opened in their entirety to parallel electricity distribution by a private firm.“This is effectively pushing the public sector towards privatisation, and we oppose it. We have all seen what happened to BSNL,” he said, adding that a further decision on the strike would be taken on Saturday.Suresh Ruhil, the association’s Gurugram district president, said Gurugram generated ₹450-500 crore in monthly revenue for DHBVN.“The discom is already making a profit, so why the haste to privatise it?” he said.Officials said high-level talks had been held between the Haryana government and unions to avert the strike.On Wednesday, Haryana energy minister Anil Vij, clarifying the government’s position, said no application has been sought from any private firm for electricity supply. “HERC rules allows any firm to apply for licence,” he said.They said Vij had invited the unions to a meeting at 3pm on Wednesday, but the associations declined, saying last-minute talks would serve no purpose.Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, on Wednesday, said the goverment will appeal against the HERC’s order granting the licence and before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity. “The goverment is ready to hire a battery of lawyers as per unions’ choice to contest the appeal,” he said, adding the Haryana goverment is completely in support of the unions on the issue and they are always welcome for negotiation on the matter. Saini directed the officials to ensure that the strike does not cause trouble to the common masses amid the festive season.

title: Devotees bid farewell to Goddess Durga in Lko | Hindustan Times
description: Since morning, pandals at Bengali Club, Ravindrapalli, Model House, Chowk, Boys Anglo among others recorded rituals of Darpan Visarjan and Sindoor Khela before idols were taken out for immersion.
content: : Amid the beats of dhak and dhunuchi dance devotees bid an emotional adieu to Goddess Durga on Wednesday, marking the end of Durga Puja festivities across the city.Since morning, pandals at Bengali Club, Ravindrapalli, Model House, Chowk, Boys Anglo among others recorded rituals of Darpan Visarjan and Sindoor Khela before idols were taken out for immersion.At Ramakrishna Math, the six-day Durga Puja concluded with religious rituals and devotional programmes under the guidance of president Swami Muktinathanand Maharaj. Setting an example in environmental conservation, the Math immersed the idol not in the Gomti but in a pond at village Bakkas, to prevent river pollution.At Ravindrapalli, women applied vermillion to the Goddess and to each other amid the beats of dhols. Later, after Darpan Visarjan, the idol was immersed at Jhulelal Ghat.At Bengali Club, vice-president Enakshi Sinha said immersion was carried out as per tradition. After morning puja, Darpan Visarjan and pran visarjan by shaking the kalash were performed, followed by Sindoor Khela by women. In the evening, the idol was immersed in the permanent pond inside the club premises, while the main kalash was immersed in Gomti.In Gomtinagar, Darpan Visarjan was performed after special puja and Pushpanjali on Dashami. Committee member Ansh said around 350 to 400 women participated in Sindoor Khela held from morning till 2:30 pm, dancing to the beats of dhunuchi after offering sindoor to the Goddess. The idol was later immersed at Jhulelal Ghat.

title: Govt offices wear deserted look as Ludhiana employees join mass leave | Hindustan Times
description: Members of the DC Office Employees Union, employee and pensioner associations, the Democratic Teachers Front, PSPCL and health workers participated in the protest under the banner of the Joint Action Committee Punjab
content: Government employees and pensioners from several departments joined the two-day mass leave protest in Ludhiana on Wednesday, holding demonstrations outside the deputy commissioner’s office to force action on unresolved demands. The agitation will continue on Thursday, October 22.Members of the DC Office Employees Union, employee and pensioner associations, the Democratic Teachers Front, PSPCL and health workers participated in the protest under the banner of the Joint Action Committee Punjab.The protesters raised slogans against the state government over unresolved issues concerning salaries, pensions and service conditions.The unions are demanding restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), release of pending dearness allowance (DA) instalments, regularisation of contractual employees, full salaries during the probation period and restoration of withdrawn allowances. They have also sought the withdrawal of orders affecting the salaries of employees recruited after 2020, including those appointed on compassionate grounds, and regular recruitment to fill vacant posts across government departments.Addressing the gathering, union leaders accused the state government of failing to honour its commitments to employees and pensioners. They warned that the agitation would be intensified if their demands remained unaddressed. The leaders also said employees and pensioners could campaign against the ruling Aam Aadmi Party if chief minister Bhagwant Mann failed to resolve their grievances.Protest in KhannaIn Khanna, employees, teachers and pensioners from Khanna, Samrala, Machhiwara and Doraha gathered at Prem Bhandari Park on Wednesday after taking collective leave. The gathering was followed by a protest march through the town.The protesters highlighted the delay in releasing pending DA instalments, the continued non-restoration of OPS, delays in regularising contractual and outsourced employees, the withdrawal of allowances and vacancies across government departments.Women employees and teachers, along with pensioners and workers from various departments, participated in the demonstration.The unions warned that they would consider further action if the government failed to address their demands.

title: 103 protected birds, reptiles rescued from illegal pet trade at West Delhi shop | Latest News Delhi
description: New DelhiAt least 103 protected birds and reptiles were rescued and confiscated on Tuesday from a pet shop in west Delhi’s Moti Nagar, where they were illegally put up for sale, police said on Wednesday  | Latest News Delhi
content: New DelhiAt least 103 protected birds and reptiles were rescued and confiscated on Tuesday from a pet shop in west Delhi’s Moti Nagar, where they were illegally put up for sale, police said on Wednesday.Police were tipped off and accompanied by environmentalists and wildlife rescuers, including 25-year-old Punjab-based activist Sahil Sharma, officers aware of the matter said.“The recovered birds and reptiles included 52 rose-ringed parakeets, two Alexandrine parakeets, three Indian star tortoises, two Indian flapshell turtles, three Indian tent turtles, 28 Indian roofed turtles and 13 black-spotted pond turtles,” Sharma told HT, adding that he has helped carry out nearly two dozens similar raids across seven states over the past seven months.An FIR was filed under sections 9,39, and 51 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act on the complaint of activist Manjira Banerjee, who was present throughout the raid, Sharma said.A senior police officer, who asked not to be identified, confirmed the registration of the FIR and said no arrest was made in the case until Wednesday evening. “We have informed the wildlife and forest department officials about the case and further action will be taken by them,” the officer added.A forest and wildlife official, who requested not to be named, said, “The FIR has been registered. We will seek permission from the concerned magistrate to release the rescued protected birds and reptiles into suitable natural habitats.”Sharma said he had been receiving several social media complaints from people regarding alleged illegal wildlife trade in Delhi’s Moti Nagar and Chandni Chowk.“Over the past several months, I received hundreds of complaints through Instagram regarding the alleged illegal wildlife trade in Moti Nagar. After gathering credible information about the presence of protected animals at the shop, I travelled from Punjab to Delhi to coordinate the raid with Delhi Police and local animal lovers,” he said.All the rescued birds and reptiles were handed over to the wildlife department for veterinary examination and further legal proceedings.

title: US orders some embassy staff to leave Saudi Arabia as drone debris kills two near oilfield; Indian national among injured | World News
description: The move comes as Saudi Arabia confirmed that two people were killed after debris from an intercepted drone fell near the Shaybah oilfield.  | World News
content: The United States on Wednesday ordered non-emergency government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia to leave the country amid escalating attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels.In a post on X, State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott wrote, "The U.S. Department of State issued an ordered departure for non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia."Pigott added, "Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions."The move comes as Saudi Arabia confirmed that an Indian national was among two people injured after debris from an intercepted drone fell near the Shaybah oilfield in the kingdom’s southeastern region on Wednesday. A Nepali national and a Filipino national were killed in the incident, while a Pakistani national was also injured. Drone debris sparks fire near Saudi oilfieldSaudi Arabia's Ministry of Defence said in a press release Wednesday that the falling debris from an intercepted drone fell on a contractor's vehicle at the Shaybah oil field, located just 10 km south of the border to Abu Dhabi, and started a fire. The incident comes amid a slew of drone attacks from the Houthis as the Houthis and the Saudi coalition continue to fight in Yemen, after their UN-administered four-year truce fell through in July this year."An official source at the Ministry of Energy stated that Saudi air defences intercepted a drone attempting to target a processing facility at Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province on Wednesday morning," the press release stated.Also read: Elon Musk responds after Kara Swisher says he could be probed if Trump loses midterms: 'Message received'"The incident resulted in a fire in a vehicle belonging to a contractor operating at the oil field, outside the facility’s perimeter, with no impact on operations. The source explained that the relevant authorities responded to the incident and took the necessary measures."The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others, a Pakistani and an Indian, due to falling debris following the interception," it added. “The source extended sincere condolences and sympathy to the families of the deceased and wished the injured a speedy recovery.”US issues security warning across West AsiaOn Sunday, US diplomatic missions across West Asia issued security advisories urging American citizens to remain vigilant amid rising regional tensions and prepare for possible travel disruptions.The advisories covered 12 countries: Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Jordan, Bahrain, Oman, Iran, Qatar, Iraq, Lebanon, Yemen and Israel."Be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions," the advisory said, adding that "the hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area.""Iran and groups supportive of Iran may target other US interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including US businesses and other institutions," it said.With inputs from AP.

title: Mumbai suburbs sizzle at 37.4°C, highest in Maha | Mumbai news
description: The coastal belt along Konkan and Goa has been experiencing higher temperatures, said Dr Bikram Singh, head scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Mumbai  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: The mercury climbed to 37.4°C in Santacruz on Wednesday, making Mumbai’s suburbs the hottest district in Maharashtra. The maximum temperature was 3.4°C above normal, while the Mumbai city region recorded 36.6°C, a departure of 3.1°C from normal.The coastal belt along Konkan and Goa has been experiencing higher temperatures, said Dr Bikram Singh, head scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Mumbai.Temperatures have risen again after easing over the past few days, Singh said, adding that some relief could be on the way. The drop in temperatures across north India is expected to gradually influence north Maharashtra and other parts of the state.“This year, the pattern has been different from earlier years with heatwaves,” he said. The heat came alongside moderate air pollution, with Mumbai recording an AQI of 113 on Wednesday. BKC was the most polluted location among the areas cited, with an AQI of 158, followed by Navy Nagar at 150. Kandivali West recorded the cleanest air at an AQI of 66, while Borivali East followed at 73.Wind patterns played a key role in the hazy conditions, Singh said. “With south-easterly winds being dominant, the haziness and dullness were seen. However, as northerly and north-easterly winds strengthen, they will bring down the temperatures and the resultant pollution levels,” he said.Doctors said the combination of heat and pollution was leaving more people with persistent respiratory symptoms. Dr Harish Chafle, senior consultant and bronchoscopist at Gleneagles Hospital, said even people with no previous history of asthma were experiencing asthma-like symptoms that were taking longer to subside.“Exposure to particulate matter in the atmosphere leads to swelling of the airways, making it difficult for people to breathe. It can worsen existing conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), along with other respiratory ailments,” he said.Chafle said symptoms that would usually ease within four to five days were now lasting for more than two weeks in some patients. Chronic cough, a runny nose and body ache were also taking longer to resolve.With some patients not responding to their usual medication, doctors were increasingly having to prescribe inhalers and steroids to control inflammation, he said.

title: Delhi govt sanctions  ₹25.6cr to resolve waterlogging hotspot at Chhatarpur | Latest News Delhi
description: New DelhiThe Delhi government on Wednesday granted administrative approval and expenditure sanction of  ₹25  | Latest News Delhi
content: New DelhiThe Delhi government on Wednesday granted administrative approval and expenditure sanction of ₹25.6 crore for a modern drainage network and two pump houses at Mandi Road and Bandh Road in south Delhi’s Chhatarpur, in a bid to resolve waterlogging at one of the city’s perennial hot spots.The project comprises a 1.4km precast drain along Mandi Road, a 1.9 km precast drain along Bandh Road, two pump houses to clear stormwater and relaying the entire Mandi Road.A site inspection of the impacted stretch was carried out by the Public Works Department (PWD) minister Parvesh Verma in July, when heavy rainfall inundated the stretch. “Earlier, this road was under the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). The responsibility has now been brought under PWD, enabling faster decisions, a single point of accountability and integrated planning of road and drainage works.Financial bids for the project have been opened and the work will be awarded shortly,” a PWD official said.Mandi Road connects CDR Chowk to the Delhi-Haryana border via Jaunapur village, and the area is naturally low-lying. Rainwater once drained through a natural channel into Haryana, but rapid urbanisation closed that outlet. Since then, every monsoon has brought knee-deep water, traffic jams and damaged roads, while temporary pumping has offered only short-lived relief. The work, once completed, is expected to bring relief to residents of Sultanpur, Gadaipur village, Jaunapur village and nearby areas, who have had to wade through flooded roads every monsoon.Minister Verma said, “When I visited Mandi Road, residents told me clearly that waterlogging had made their lives difficult for years and that it must be fixed on priority. For too long, the people of Sultanpur, Gadaipur, Jaunapur and nearby areas were told to simply live with this problem.”“Every monsoon, the same pumps came out and the same promises were made. Under ‘One Government, One Governance’, PWD has taken charge of this road, and with ₹25.60 crore sanctioned, we are building precast drains on both sides of Mandi Road, a drain along Bandh Road and two pump houses. This is a permanent solution, not a temporary patch,” he said.Officials said that the precast drain technology allows faster construction with minimal disruption to residents and traffic.

title: Haryana man shot dead in clash over car vandalism in Ludhiana | Hindustan Times
description: Police say the victim, a driver by profession, had accompanied his friends to confront the suspected vandals when the clash broke out
content: A 31-year-old man from Panchkula, Haryana, was shot dead during a clash between two groups in the EWS Colony area near Tajpur Road in the early hours of Wednesday after he accompanied his friends to confront a group suspected of vandalising their associate’s car.Police said the two groups had also clashed on Tuesday evening over another issue before a fresh confrontation later that night led to the fatal shooting.The deceased, identified as Dilbara Singh, alias Harry, sustained a bullet injury to his chest and succumbed to his injuries at a private hospital on Wednesday morning. A driver by profession, Harry had been living with his wife in rented accommodation in Ludhiana for the past six to seven months.Deputy commissioner of police (Rural) Gursewak Singh said, “Preliminary investigations revealed that Harry and his associates had clashed with a rival group near Tajpur Road on Tuesday evening. The two groups assembled again later that night, resulting in another confrontation during which one of the accused opened fire.”“The victim’s group outnumbered the rival faction. Realising that they could be overpowered, one of the accused, identified as Jonty, pulled out a firearm and opened fire and a bullet struck Harry in the chest,” the DCP said.According to Harry’s wife, Rajwinder Kaur, a homemaker, the couple was at their rented residence on Tuesday night when some of his friends arrived and informed him that their associate Vikas’s car had been vandalised. Harry accompanied them to confront those suspected of damaging the vehicle.Rajwinder said she received a call from one of her husband’s friends around 3 am informing her that Harry had been shot. She also claimed that her husband had been assaulted by a group of youngsters the previous weekend and suspected that the same individuals might have been responsible for the fatal attack.Harry’s friends alleged that some residents of the locality, whom they accused of involvement in criminal activities, had vandalised Vikas’s car. They said the group had gathered to question those responsible for the damage when an altercation broke out and shots were fired. Harry was rushed to a private hospital, where he later died.The DCP said investigators were probing whether a longstanding dispute existed between the two groups, as preliminary findings suggested that they had been involved in previous confrontations.“A probe to establish the nature of the firearm, whether it was licensed or illegal, used in the shooting is underway. A hunt is on to nab the accused, the officer added.Shop owner, father attacked with baseball bat over parking disputeA man reportedly attacked a shop owner and his father with a baseball bat and allegedly threatened them with a revolver outside their shop over a parking dispute in Purani Madhopuri on Wednesday.The elderly man sustained a head injury and was taken to civil hospital for treatment.According to shop owner Sanchit, a car parked outside his shop obstructed the opening of its shutter. When his father asked the car owner, theirneighbour, to move the vehicle, the latter allegedly hurled abuses and manhandled him before pulling out a revolver and threatening those present.The accused then took a baseball bat from his car and struck both Sanchit and his father before fleeing. While Sanchit sustained minor injuries, his father suffered a head wound that required stitches.Inspector Gurjit Singh, station house officer of Division No. 3 police station, said the police had asked the victim to submit a formal complaint before registering an FIR and investigators were examining CCTV footage from the area to verify the allegations.

title: 3 years before polls, Sena, BJP spar over CM’s post | Mumbai news
description: At the annual Dussehra rally of the party on Tuesday, Sena ministers Pratap Sarnaik and Gulabrao Patil, along with former minister Ramdas Kadam, openly backed their party chief and deputy chief minister Shinde for the top post  | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: With three years to go before the next assembly elections, the battle over who should be Maharashtra’s next chief minister has already begun within the ruling Mahayuti alliance, with the Shiv Sena and BJP staking their claims. Sena leaders are pitching for Eknath Shinde’s return as chief minister, while BJP leaders are insisting that chief minister Devendra Fadnavis will continue to lead the alliance.At the annual Dussehra rally of the party on Tuesday, Sena ministers Pratap Sarnaik and Gulabrao Patil, along with former minister Ramdas Kadam, openly backed their party chief and deputy chief minister Shinde for the top post. Their remarks signalled that the leadership question remains alive within the ruling alliance, reviving memories of the prolonged stand-off between a sulking Shinde and an unyielding Fadnavis after the two leaders switched roles after the Mahayuti swept to power in the 2024 assembly elections.On Tuesday, Patil even sought divine blessings for Shinde’s return, declaring that the Sena would increase its tally to pave the way for his elevation. “We pray to Lord Ram and Goddess Jagdamba to make Eknath Shinde saheb the chief minister of Maharashtra once again and bring back good days for farmers,” he said.He claimed the Sena had 60 MLAs, a combined strength of 73 legislators when MLCs were included, and a total 85-86 representatives when MPs were counted. “If every MLA ensures the election of one MLA from a neighbouring constituency, Eknath Shinde will become the next chief minister,” Patil said.State transport minister Pratap Sarnaik said Shinde’s return as chief minister was the hope of party leaders and grassroots workers. “Whether it is Pratap Sarnaik, Anand Paranjape or an ordinary Shiv Sainik, everyone wants Eknath Shinde saheb to become chief minister once again. However, numbers are very important when it comes to becoming the chief minister,” he told the media on Tuesday.“Today, Eknath Shinde saheb is deputy chief minister because we do not have the numbers. But in the next assembly election, we will increase our strength,” he added.Referencing the standoff between Shinde and Fadnavis nearly two years ago, Kadam said, “Eknath Shinde saheb was a rightful claimant to the chief minister’s post. However, what happened later is something only Shinde Saheb himself knows well.”The BJP, however, was quick to reaffirm its position. Party MLC Parinay Fuke, a close confidant of the chief minister, said the Mahayuti would contest the next assembly elections under Fadnavis, signalling that the BJP intends to retain him as the face of the alliance.“Given the way Fadnavis saheb is taking Maharashtra forward on the development front, we will contest the next election under his leadership. Not only that, we will also achieve greater success than in the previous election,” said Fuke.Claiming that the alliance currently has around 240 seats, Fuke said the Mahayuti would aim to cross the 250-seat mark in the 288-member assembly during the next election.Seizing on the remarks, the opposition Shiv Sena (UBT) questioned the BJP’s claim that all is well within the ruling Mahayuti coalition. Former MP Priyanka Chaturvedi said the public statements reflected underlying tensions among the alliance partners.“I want to ask the BJP if they approve such remarks. I have been repeatedly saying that everything is not well in this three-party alliance. We keep hearing about boycotts of meetings. When farmers are badly affected by drought, the three ruling parties are busy deciding who will become chief minister, MLA, MLC, among others,” she said.

title: Building tilt upends lives: Evacuated families face uncertain wait to return home | Latest News Delhi
description: A dozen families evacuated from three residential buildings after an under-construction building tilted following deep excavation on an adjoining plot said they had no clarity on when they could return home  | Latest News Delhi
content: A dozen families evacuated from three residential buildings after an under-construction building tilted following deep excavation on an adjoining plot said they had no clarity on when they could return home.The five-storey building, C1770, tilted by 2.5 inches on Monday evening. Authorities deployed two cranes to support it, sealed the area and evacuated three neighbouring buildings as a precaution. Residents left with little more than daily essentials, clothes and medicines.Avani, who vacated her flat in C1768 on Tuesday, said she and her friend barely had time to pack a bag. “We don’t even know whom to contact for updates or when we can return to our normal lives,” she said.Tarun Chopra, who left the same building with his wife, minor son and elderly mother, questioned who would pay their hotel bills.“This crisis arose from the plot owner’s negligence. It may take up to a month before we can return home, but the fear will remain,” he said.Gaurav Rampall, who vacated his flat in C1771 with his wife and two children, said they initially considered a hotel in Gurugram but moved to his parents’ home in Saket, Delhi.“Our personal and professional lives have been badly affected. My son, who attends LKG at a school in Sector 62, and our seven-month-old daughter are the worst affected. His travel time to school has doubled overnight,” he said.Rampall said he expected a resolution to take at least 15–20 days. The affected families were pressing the plot owner for a permanent solution, he added.Police and district administration officials said excavation to a depth of 8.5 feet at C1769 had exposed the entire foundation of the adjoining building. A Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) inspection found that the plot owner lacked permission for excavation to that depth, they said.“The excavation needed to be only four to five feet deep and carried out in phases, with measurements to avoid exposing the entire foundation at once. Instead, an 8.5-foot-deep trench was dug along the building’s entire length using a JCB machine, damaging it,” said a police official, citing DTCP engineers.Two DTCP engineers inspected the site and seized construction materials, including rebars, to prevent further excavation or construction without clearance.Officials suspected the owner was planning a basement and had rushed the excavation to avoid detection.Shakti Thakral, owner of the damaged building, said finishing work was underway and one family had planned to move in before Diwali.“Now, we don’t know when we will be able to move in. I cannot undertake any work on my property until disaster management and DTCP officials give clearance,” he said.Thakral said a dilapidated three-storey building on the adjoining plot had recently been demolished to make way for a new one.“I had my building constructed without damaging the old property. But its owner did not even alert me before carrying out deep excavation negligently,” he said.Anshul Gogia, the owner of the plot on which the tilted building stands, said that all the construction and excavation work at the site was being carried out with due permission. Refuting the allegations of deep excavation, Gogia said that trench they dug was only five feet and two inches deep. “DTCP engineers will inspect the site and inform us about what had made the building tilt,” he added.

title: After blood centre lapses, UP pushes for extra safety checks on transfusion | Hindustan Times
description: The move follows inspections of 208 blood centres in March 2026, which led to the suspension of licences of 55 centres.
content: : Uttar Pradesh has proposed mandatory quality checks on blood units procured in bulk from other states after inspections found serious lapses at blood centres, raising concerns over infection screening, transportation and documentation.The Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration (UPFSDA), in a proposal sent by commissioner Roshan Jacob to the National Blood Transfusion Council (NBTC), has recommended testing at least 1% of every consignment, or a minimum of one unit, whichever is higher, at a government blood centre in the presence of a drug inspector.The move follows inspections of 208 blood centres in March 2026, which led to the suspension of licences of 55 centres.Inspectors found missing infection-test reports, donor forms, transportation temperature records and inadequate labelling, making it difficult to verify the safety and source of blood units, particularly packed red blood cells (PRBC).Unsafe blood transfusions can transmit HIV and hepatitis B and C. Under existing guidelines, supplier centres conduct infection screening, while recipient centres check compatibility before transfusion.UPFSDA has also proposed mandatory advance intimation to drug inspectors, clear labelling of transferred units, transportation temperature records and documentation tracing each unit from donor to recipient.Assistant commissioner FSDA Brijesh Singh said donor and recipient records, including prescribed Aadhaar details and linked mobile numbers, must be maintained. Pilot-tube segments and patient blood samples must be preserved for at least seven days.Under the NBTC guidelines issued on October 28, 2015, supplier blood centres are generally responsible for infection testing, while recipient centres conduct cross-matching to establish compatibility before transfusion. The transfer framework also requires appropriate transportation and storage conditions, donor consent for use beyond the original centre, and maintenance of traceability records. UPFSDA’s proposal seeks to reinforce these safeguards.

title: Cracks repair work force closure of RTR flyover, triggers traffic snarls | Latest News Delhi
description: The repair is expected to be completed by October 26, while vehicular movement on the flyover is likely to start by October 27.  | Latest News Delhi
content: New Delhi:The old Rao Tula Ram (RTR) flyover on the Outer Ring Road, heading towards Vasant Vihar from Delhi airport, has been closed to traffic for repair work after cracks appeared at two locations, spilling traffic onto alternate routes and causing massive snarls.The Public Works Department (PWD) began the repair work on Wednesday, and an officer said the Delhi Traffic Police issued a traffic advisory.The repair is expected to be completed by October 26, while vehicular movement on the flyover is likely to start by October 27.Until then, traffic from Delhi airport, Gurugram, and Dwarka heading to Vasant Vihar and Chirag Delhi has been diverted onto the service road adjoining the RTR flyover and other alternate routes, the officer said.“The flyover has been closed for repair work, and the entire traffic has been diverted onto the adjoining service road. Consequently, traffic is heavy, and the queue is extending considerably behind the flyover. The flyover will remain closed until completion of the work, and traffic on this road is expected to remain heavy, especially during peak hours,” the advisory read.Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi Traffic Range) Vikas Kumar said that on Tuesday, traffic personnel observed cracks at two locations on the flyover and immediately informed the PWD, seeking necessary repairs as a precautionary measure.“The repairs of the patches required the closure of the flyover. Considering public safety, it was not possible to keep even part of it open. The flyover closure has led to traffic congestion. To address the situation, we have taken measures, including updating Google Maps to mark the flyover as closed and show the alternate route via the service road. We have also increased deployment of traffic personnel to ensure smooth traffic flow,” the DCP added.Meanwhile, many commuters took on to social media to draw attention to the traffic chaos.“Entire Rao Tula Ram Marg is choked since morning! Stuck at the junction for 30mins coming from the airport. Please do something!,” a commuter posted on X.Another commuter posted, “Taking 2.5 hours to reach from Gurugram to central Delhi because the Vasant Vihar flyover is closed. Please help.”Delhi Police said PWD officials, in coordination with Delhi Traffic Police, are working to restore the flyover as soon as possible to ensure safe movement for commuters.“The repair work is expected to be completed by October 26 morning, after which the flyover is expected to reopen for commuters, subject to completion of the work and safety clearance,” a statement read.PWD officials said they observed deterioration of the concrete, visible cracking, and exposed reinforcement in the gap slab section of the old RTR flyover.

title: JMI forms panel to draft students’ union constitution, protesters demand poll dates | Hindustan Times
description: New Delhi: Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) on Wednesday notified the formation of a five-member committee to draft the students’ union constitution amid protests over its restoration, suspended since 2006
content: New Delhi: Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) on Wednesday notified the formation of a five-member committee to draft the students’ union constitution amid protests over its restoration, suspended since 2006.The development comes nearly 10 days after five students went on a hunger strike, followed by a series of on-campus protests demanding the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU).However, the protesting students rejected the order of panel constitution, demanding notification of the students’ union election to call off the strike.According to the notification, the committee will also conduct a detailed study into the circumstances that led to the dissolution of the JMISU and submit its report by December 20.“On the recommendation of the high-level committee, constituted on October 18, the vice-chancellor has constituted a committee to draft the constitution of JMISU under the JMI Act, 1988,” the notification signed by registrar Mahtab Alam Rizvi stated.Zubair Meenai will chair the five-member panel, with four members: Luqman Ahmed Khan, Aslam Khan, M Amarjeet Singh, and Neelofar Afzal. All are professors at the university.“The committee will consider the circumstances leading to the dissolution of JMISU, various rulings of competent courts in relation to JMISU, and recommendations of the Lyngdoh committee in 2007,” the university said.It further stated that the panel will reach out to all stakeholders, including students and submit the draft by December 20, 2026.In a separate notification, the JMI administration announced it would review disciplinary action taken against students involved in protests between October 12 and 21. The university had suspended three students in connection with the ongoing agitation.Meanwhile, the protesting students issued a release demanding that JMISU elections be held through a student-constituted election commission, that the university revoke in writing all disciplinary action connected with the ongoing protest, that it remove the chief Proctor and the security advisor, and that it ensure medical monitoring, ambulance access, and protection from intimidation for the students on hunger strike. “The students of Jamia will not be intimidated by deadlines or threats. Our protest is peaceful and democratic, and the hunger strike continues,” the release stated.

title: DTC wins three national awards for urban transport initiatives | Latest News Delhi
description: New Delhi:The Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) has been selected for three national Awards of Excellence in Urban Transport by the Union housing and urban affairs ministry for its initiatives in digital mobility, smart bus management and data-driven route planning  | Latest News Delhi
content: New Delhi:The Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) has been selected for three national Awards of Excellence in Urban Transport by the Union housing and urban affairs ministry for its initiatives in digital mobility, smart bus management and data-driven route planning.The awards will be presented at the valedictory session of the 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026 in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, on October 24, officials said on Wednesday.The three initiatives recognised are the Pink Saheli National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) programme, the Integrated Smart Bus Management System and the DEVI Bus Routes Initiative.The Pink Saheli NCMC Card programme has facilitated the issuance of over 2 million cards for free bus travel to eligible women and transgender passengers under the applicable scheme. It has been recognised in the Excellence in Innovation and Smart Mobility Solutions category.The Integrated Smart Bus Management System has been selected for the City with the Best Public Transport System award. It uses GPS-based tracking, CCTV surveillance and performance dashboards to monitor bus operations.The DEVI Bus Routes Initiative, implemented in coordination with IIT Delhi, has been recognised in the Best Use of Big Data Analytics for Operations and Evidence-Based Transport Planning category. The initiative uses data analytics and scientific route planning to improve neighbourhood connectivity and first- and last-mile access.Delhi transport minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said the awards reflected the government’s commitment to modernising public transport through technology and inclusive mobility.“These recognitions are an encouragement to further strengthen Delhi’s public transport system. Our focus is on using technology and data to make bus services more efficient, accountable and accessible, while ensuring better last-mile connectivity,” Singh said.The awards come as the Delhi government seeks to improve public transport connectivity, operational efficiency and passenger services through technology-led interventions and better route planning, added officials.

title: Toxic froth returns to Yamuna, AAP alleges tender irregularities in anti-froth drive | Latest News Delhi
description: AAP Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj said the tendering process for treating the Yamuna Froth near Kalindi Kunj was still underway and the financial bid had not yet been opened.  | Latest News Delhi
content: New Delhi:A thick layer of toxic white froth has once again covered stretches of the Yamuna near Kalindi Kunj as falling temperatures and the churning of water falling from barrage intensify foaming on the river’s surface.With Chhath Puja less than a month away, the Delhi government agencies have started preparations for an anti-froth drive along the heavily polluted Kalindi Kunj-Okhla stretch, officials said.The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), however, has alleged irregularities in the tendering process for the deployment of an agency to spray the defoaming agent.A senior government official said preparations for the anti-froth drive ahead of Chhath puja had begun. “Multiple agencies are being hired for procurement of chemicals to treat the froth. Only food-grade chemicals will be used to ensure safety. Separate bids have been invited for the deployment of sprinkling unit,” official added.AAP Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj said the tendering process for treating the Yamuna Froth near Kalindi Kunj was still underway and the financial bid had not yet been opened.“However, the contractor had already set up tents and equipment at the site. Earlier, we exposed corruption in PWD road construction and now this is corruption in DJB,” Bharadwaj posted on X. He also shared a video showing a tent set up by a private contractor near Kalindi Kunj.Former deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia alleged that another scam was taking place in the Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government in the name of cleaning Yamuna. He said a company was awarded the work before the tender was opened.Delhi Jal Board (DJB) spokesperson did not respond to the allegations.The froth forms when surfactants include detergents from untreated domestic sewage, industrial pollutants, wastewater from dhobi ghats, and organic matter released by decomposing water hyacinth trapped near the Okhla barrage, DJB officials said.The river’s deteriorating condition has once again drawn attention around Saraswati Puja, when devotees gather along its banks for idol immersion, he added.

title: Cuffe Parade marina plan stalled over proposed bridge | Mumbai news
description: The issue came up at an MCZMA meeting on September 24, according to minutes uploaded last week. Members noted that the MMRDA had received clearance in August for the bridge project in the same or a nearby location and deferred the marina proposal pending clarification on whether the two projects would overlap or obstruct each other  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: A proposed marina off Cuffe Parade has hit a hurdle after the Maharashtra Coastal Zone Management Authority (MCZMA) asked its developer, Rashmi Development Private Limited, to obtain an NOC from the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) confirming that the project will not clash with a proposed bridge linking Nariman Point with Colaba and Cuffe Parade.The issue came up at an MCZMA meeting on September 24, according to minutes uploaded last week. Members noted that the MMRDA had received clearance in August for the bridge project in the same or a nearby location and deferred the marina proposal pending clarification on whether the two projects would overlap or obstruct each other.Raj Pradhan, owner of Rashmi Development Private Limited, said the company had obtained an NOC from the MMRDA.The company plans to develop an inland water transport terminal and marina at Cuffe Parade, with a promenade, immigration centre, jetty, yacht ramp, breakwater, navigational channel and turning circle. The proposal also includes an anchored cruise ship that would function as a floating hotel.The proposal was discussed at three MCZMA meetings in March, April and June and received a recommendation on July 1. The company later withdrew it and submitted a fresh proposal in August. Plans for the private marina and floatel are yet to be finalised.Meanwhile, the Mumbai Port Authority has invited global bids for a separate ₹922.67-crore marina and integrated waterfront development at Victoria Dock, named the Viksit Bharat Mumbai Marina.The project will be developed on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) basis, with a 45-year concession. The marina is planned across a protected water area of 37.3 hectares, with capacity for 604 yachts and 424 berths in its first phase.The selected company will develop the shore-side facilities, expand berthing in later phases and operate the marina for 45 years before transferring the assets to the port authority. The planned amenities include a marina terminal, sailing school, yacht club, repair yard at Haji Bunder, fuel station, five-star hotel, tourism business centre, restaurants, retail outlets and a venue for boat shows and events.The bidder offering the highest share of profits to the port authority will win the contract. Bids must be submitted by December 15.M Angamuthu, Chairperson, Mumbai Port Authority, said, “The Marina will open a part of the city’s working harbour for organised marine tourism, sailing and waterfront services, while keeping port operations and safety at the centre.” He said the port authority was executing the marine works and had the necessary clearances.

title: ₹20-crore hostel proposal offers little relief as RMLNLU row simmers | Hindustan Times
description: The administration’s figures show six water coolers for 260 undergraduate boys and six for 200 postgraduate boys
content: : A dispute between students and the administration of Dr Ram Manohar Lohiya National Law University (RMLNLU) has intensified, with students on Wednesday rejecting the university’s response to their October 12 representation and warning that their protest would continue if their concerns remained unresolved.The administration uploaded its reply on October 20, following a discussion with students on October 13. Students alleged that several issues remained unaddressed and that assurances given during the meeting were not reflected in the response.Overcrowding in the girls’ hostel remains a major flashpoint. Students proposed shifting some residents to the university’s Type-5 residences, while the administration said a proposal for a new hostel, estimated to cost ₹20 crore, had been sent to the government six months ago, with approval expected shortly.Students also flagged drinking water and electrical safety concerns. The administration’s figures show six water coolers for 260 undergraduate boys and six for 200 postgraduate boys. The girls’ hostel, with 42 rooms, also has six coolers, reportedly serving 70-80 students per cooler.Students said joint registrar Sanjay Diwakar’s assurance that engineers would inspect water quality and cooler safety on October 14 remained unfulfilled even after seven days.The administration cited two doctors working four-hour shifts, a psychologist visiting twice weekly and a 24-hour ambulance. Students, however, demanded clarity on nursing cover and tetanus availability.On Friday, students plan to submit their proposed student body constitution to vice-chancellor Amar Pal Singh, registrar Keshav Kumar and joint registrar Sanjay Diwakar, seeking fresh talks. They warned of continuing their protest if dialogue was denied or their recommendations rejected.University spokesperson Shashank Shekhar said, “The University administration remains open to constructive dialogue with students. Their concerns and proposals will receive due consideration in accordance with applicable rules and procedures.

title: Lasers, firecrackers flout HC curbs during visarjan, alleges Awaaz Foundation | Mumbai news
description: The foundation recorded noise levels ranging from 82 to 110.8 dB(A) across several neighbourhoods, including Mahim, Dadar West, Prabhadevi and Cuffe Parade. It also flagged laser lights directed at traffic and residential buildings  | Mumbai news
content: Mumbai: Noise levels touched 110.8 decibels during Devi visarjan procession in Mahim on Tuesday night, as firecrackers, loudspeakers and laser lights were allegedly used in violation of Bombay high court restrictions, Awaaz Foundation has alleged. The organisation has written to chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking action against violators and stricter enforcement of the court’s orders.The foundation recorded noise levels ranging from 82 to 110.8 dB(A) across several neighbourhoods, including Mahim, Dadar West, Prabhadevi and Cuffe Parade. It also flagged laser lights directed at traffic and residential buildings.Mahim recorded the highest readings, between 94.4 and 110.8 dB(A), while Dadar West registered 82 to 102.6 dB(A). At Prabhadevi, firecrackers and loudspeakers generated readings of 88 to 103.1 dB(A). Cuffe Parade recorded 87.2 to 100.4 dB(A), with horn-type loudspeakers and lasers in use.The foundation, led by Sumaira Abdulali, also reported smoke from firecrackers in Dadar West and explosions in the distance at Worli and near Babulnath. At Haji Ali, laser lights from a moving procession were allegedly directed towards home and traffic.In her letter to Fadnavis on Wednesday, Abdulali said the violations raised concerns about compliance with the Bombay high court’s restrictions on firecrackers in public spaces, including roads and footpaths, during festivals in 2026. The court’s directions also require police to measure noise levels and take appropriate action.The latest communication is the foundation’s fourth formal alert to the state government in less than a month. It had earlier flagged loudspeakers, firecrackers and laser beams during the Ganpati festival in emails sent on September 26, September 28 and October 13. Some laser beams were allegedly directed into homes and towards traffic.The foundation also alleged that several violations during Ganpati festivities occurred in the presence of police personnel, without visible deployment of decibel meters.
